During binaural sound localization, the sighted control group showed decreased cerebral blood flow in the occipital lobe, which was not observed in early-blind individuals. In contrast, during monaural sound localization (one ear plugged), a subgroup of early-blind subjects who were behaviorally superior at sound localization displayed two activation foci in the occipital cortex. This effect was not seen in blind individuals who did not demonstrate superior monaural sound localization abilities, nor in sighted individuals. Notably, the degree of activation of one of these foci was strongly correlated with sound localization accuracy across the entire group of blind subjects. These findings suggest that the occipital cortex is specifically involved in the use of monaural cues for auditory localization in blind individuals who perform better than sighted individuals. Our results shed light not only on intermodal compensatory mechanisms but also on individual differences in these mechanisms and on inhibitory patterns that differ between sighted individuals and those deprived of vision early in life.

title: High-Infiltration of Tumor-Associated Macrophages Predicts Unfavorable Clinical Outcome for Node-Negative Breast Cancer
text: The tumor microenvironment in breast cancer is composed of various cell types, including tumor cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune cells. These cells can either promote or inhibit tumor growth and progression. The aim of this retrospective study was to investigate the density of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in breast cancer and its correlation with clinicopathological parameters. The study included 172 breast cancer patients, and the researchers analyzed paraffin-embedded tissue samples and clinical data, including up to 5 years of follow-up information. The study used immunohistochemical staining to evaluate the density of TAMs in the tumor stroma. The results showed that TAMs were significantly more frequent in high-grade breast cancer patients. Additionally, breast cancer patients with a high density of TAMs had lower rates of disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival compared to patients with low density of TAMs. Furthermore, high infiltration of TAMs was associated with worse survival rates in node-negative breast cancer patients. Overall, the study found that the number of TAMs in the tumor stroma is an independent predictor of survival time for breast cancer patients, and high infiltration of TAMs is a significant unfavorable prognostic factor for patients with invasive breast cancer.

title: Murine Dishevelled 3 Functions in Redundant Pathways with Dishevelled 1 and 2 in Normal Cardiac Outflow Tract, Cochlea, and Neural Tube Development
text:
Dishevelled (Dvl) proteins play critical roles in both the canonical beta-catenin/Wnt pathway and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, which regulate cell proliferation, patterning, and polarity in developing tissues. While three mammalian Dvl genes have been identified, their developmental functions have been poorly understood. Here, we investigate the roles of Dvl3 in development and demonstrate functional redundancy among the three murine Dvls.
We found that Dvl3(-/-) mice die perinatally with cardiac outflow tract abnormalities, including double outlet right ventricle and persistent truncus arteriosis. These mutants also display a misoriented stereocilia in the organ of Corti, which is enhanced in the presence of a single allele of the PCP component Vangl2/Ltap (LtapLp/+). Although neurulation appears normal in both Dvl3(-/-) and LtapLp/+ mutants, combined mutants display incomplete neural tube closure.
Our findings show that many of the roles of Dvl3 are also shared by Dvl1 and Dvl2. In contrast, more severe phenotypes are observed in Dvl3 mutants with the deficiency of another Dvl, and increasing Dvl dosage genetically with Dvl transgenes demonstrates the ability of Dvls to compensate for each other to enable normal development. Interestingly, global canonical Wnt signaling appears largely unaffected in the double Dvl mutants, suggesting that low Dvl levels are sufficient for functional canonical Wnt signals.
In summary, we demonstrate that Dvl3 is required for cardiac outflow tract development and describe its importance in the PCP pathway during neurulation and cochlea development. Additionally, we establish several developmental processes in which the three Dvls are functionally redundant.

title: Dynamics of adherens junctions in epithelial establishment, maintenance, and remodeling
text:
The epithelial cadherin (E-cadherin)-catenin complex forms a mature adherens junction (AJ) by interacting with various cytoskeletal components and regulatory/signaling molecules. This dynamic structure not only physically connects adjacent epithelial cells but also couples intercellular adhesive contacts to the cytoskeleton, thereby defining each cell's apical-basal axis. The coordinated activities of E-cadherin and its associated molecules are crucial for the proper formation, polarity, and function of epithelial cells. Recent advances in live-cell imaging have shed light on the dynamic nature of E-cadherin turnover at junctions, which plays a critical role in both junction formation and the maintenance of epithelial integrity during tissue homeostasis and remodeling.
In this context, Rho family GTPases and Par polarity proteins are among the key regulators of adherens junction formation and integrity. However, the full extent of E-cadherin turnover at junctions has only recently been appreciated, thanks to the development of live-cell imaging techniques. This turnover plays a vital role in maintaining the proper functioning of adherens junctions and the overall integrity of epithelial tissues.

title: Long-term outcome of patients with asystole induced by head-up tilt test.
text:
AIMS: To evaluate the long-term outcomes of patients who presented with asystole during head-up tilt testing, one of the largest reported cohorts of patients with this condition.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Since 1990, 1322 patients with syncope of unknown origin underwent head-up tilt testing. Of these, 330 patients (24%) exhibited an abnormal response (syncope or pre-syncope), and 58 patients (5%) experienced asystole (> or = 3000 ms) during the test. The duration of asystole ranged from 3 to 90 seconds, with a median duration of 10 seconds (interquartile range: 4-19 seconds). Two different tilting protocols (Westminster [60 degrees] and isoproterenol [80 degrees]) were used, and the time to the syncopal episode and the duration of asystole were compared. The results showed that the time to the syncopal episode was significantly shorter in the Westminster protocol group (13 minutes vs 2 minutes, P=0.0005), but the duration of asystole was not significantly different between the two groups. During the follow-up period of 40 months (17 months for patients without asystole and 66 months for patients with asystole), 12 patients with asystole experienced syncopal recurrences, and 34 patients without asystole presented syncopal episodes. The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the mean time free of recurrence was 92 months for patients with asystole and 82 months for patients without asystole (P=ns). The number of previous syncopes was found to have a significant relationship with recurrences (P=0.002), but not with gender, age, asystole occurrence, asystole duration, or timing to asystole during head-up tilt testing. There were no cardiac-related deaths.
CONCLUSIONS:
1. Asystole during head-up tilt testing does not necessarily imply a malignant outcome, as the incidence of syncopal recurrences is low.
2. Pacemaker or drug therapy do not significantly influence the outcome, which is correlated with the previous number of syncopal episodes but not with gender, age, asystole occurrence, asystole duration, or timing to asystole during head-up tilt testing.
3. The tilting protocol (angle) may influence the time to and incidence of asystole during head-up tilt testing.

title: ZINC 15 – Ligand Discovery for Everyone
text: Many questions about the biological activity and availability of small molecules remain unanswered for researchers who could greatly benefit from their answers. To bridge the gap between chemistry and biology, we have developed a suite of tools for ligand annotation, purchasability, target identification, and biological association, which are integrated into ZINC and designed for investigators who are not computer specialists. The latest version contains over 120 million "drug-like" compounds, of which a quarter are available for immediate delivery. ZINC connects these compounds to high-value ones, such as metabolites, drugs, natural products, and annotated compounds from the literature. Researchers can access these compounds through their gene annotations as well as their major and minor target classes. The new version offers user-friendly analysis tools that are accessible to non-experts, while still providing advanced features for specialists. ZINC retains its original 3D structure, with all molecules available in biologically relevant, ready-to-dock formats. ZINC is freely available at <http://zinc15.docking.org>.

title: Condensin-mediated remodeling of the mitotic chromatin landscape in fission yeast
text: The eukaryotic genome is composed of DNA molecules significantly longer than the cells that harbor them. During mitosis, these DNA molecules undergo a process known as chromosome condensation, where they reach their maximum compactness. This process is facilitated by the protein condensin, a member of the structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) family. Despite the importance of chromosome condensation, the spatial organization of mitotic chromosomes and the mechanisms by which condensin shapes chromatin architecture remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, we employed chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) techniques in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Our findings revealed that the interphase chromatin landscape, characterized by small chromatin domains, is replaced by fewer but larger domains during mitosis. Condensin achieves this by establishing longer-range, intrachromosomal DNA interactions, which compact and individualize chromosomes. Concurrently, local chromatin contacts are constrained by condensin, leading to profound implications for local chromatin function during mitosis. Our results underscore the crucial role of condensin in transforming the chromatin landscape as cells prepare for cell division.

title: Efficacy of the 6-month thrice-weekly regimen in the treatment of new sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis under clinical trial conditions.
text:
BACKGROUND: Under the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme of India, patients with new smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis are treated with a thrice-weekly regimen of antitubercular drugs (2H(3)R(3)Z(3)E(3)/4H(3)R(3)) for 6 months. In this retrospective analysis, we evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of this regimen in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis under clinical trial conditions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from 268 patients treated with the control regimen (2H(3)R(3)Z(3)E(3)/4H(3)R(3)) in two clinical trials conducted at the National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis, Chennai, India between 2001 and 2006.
RESULTS: Of the 249 patients with available data, 238 (96%) had a favourable status at the end of treatment. Treatment failure occurred in 11 patients, of whom 7 had initial drug susceptibility and 4 had initial drug resistance. Among the 238 patients with a favourable status at the end of treatment, 14 (6%) had recurrence of tuberculosis during the following 24 months. In the intention-to-treat analysis, 245 (94%) of 262 patients had a favourable status at the end of treatment. Of the 28 patients with initial drug resistance, 24 (86%) had a favourable outcome. Only 4 of these 24 patients had recurrence of tuberculosis in the following 2 years. Among the 221 patients initially infected with drug-susceptible organisms, drug resistance did not develop in any of the 7 patients in whom the treatment failed or the 10 who had recurrence of tuberculosis. Further, 5 of the 7 patients in whom the treatment failed continued to excrete drug-susceptible bacilli at 6 months. Adverse drug reactions were observed in 38 (14%) of the 262 patients, with only 3 (1.1%) requiring modification in treatment.
CONCLUSION: This thrice-weekly 6-month regimen of antitubercular drugs, when administered under full supervision, is associated with a high rate of favourable treatment outcomes in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. The regimen shows few adverse drug reactions, and none of the patients developed drug resistance.

title: Curcumin attenuates inflammatory response in IL-1beta-induced human synovial fibroblasts and collagen-induced arthritis in mouse model.
text:
Curcumin, a key component of turmeric, has been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of curcumin in reducing collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) in mice and its impact on the activation of fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs).
We used DBA/1 mice that were immunized with bovine type II collagen (CII) and treated with curcumin every other day for two weeks after the initial immunization. We evaluated the incidence of arthritis and used an arthritis index based on paw thickness. In addition, we examined the proliferation of CII- or concanavalin A-induced splenic T cells in vitro using interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) production as a marker. We also measured the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) in the mouse ankle joint and serum, as well as the expression levels of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in human FLSs.
Our results showed that curcumin treatment significantly reduced the clinical arthritis score in CIA mice compared to untreated mice. Additionally, curcumin inhibited the proliferation of splenic T cells, reduced the expression of TNF-alpha and IL-1beta in the ankle joint, and decreased the levels of IgG2a in serum. Furthermore, curcumin altered the transcription activity of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) in FLSs, leading to a decrease in PGE2 production, COX-2 expression, and MMP secretion.
These findings suggest that curcumin can effectively suppress the inflammatory response by inhibiting pro-inflammatory mediators and regulating humoral and cellular immune responses.

title: Loss of IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb impairs myogenic differentiation.
text: In recent years, there has been growing interest in the actions of protein products resulting from alternative splicing of the Igf1 gene. However, the significance and functional relevance of these observations remain poorly defined. To investigate the functions of IGF-I splice variants, we examined the impact of loss of IGF-IEa and IGF-IEb on the proliferation and differentiation of cultured mouse myoblasts. Our results showed that RNA interference-mediated reductions in total IGF-I, IGF-IEa alone, or IGF-IEb alone had no effect on cell viability in growth medium. However, cells lacking total IGF-I or IGF-IEa alone proliferated significantly slower than control cells or cells lacking IGF-IEb in serum-free media. Simultaneous loss of both or specific loss of either splice variant significantly inhibited myosin heavy chain (MyHC) immunoreactivity by 70-80% (P < 0.01) under differentiation conditions (48 h in 2% horse serum) as determined by Western immunoblotting. This loss in protein was associated with reduced MyHC isoform mRNAs, as reductions in total IGF-I or IGF-IEa mRNA significantly reduced MyHC mRNAs by approximately 50-75% (P < 0.05). Loss of IGF-IEb also reduced MyHC isoform mRNA significantly, with the exception of Myh7, but to a lesser degree (∼20-40%, P < 0.05). Interestingly, provision of mature IGF-I, but not synthetic E peptides, restored Myh3 expression to control levels in cells lacking IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb. These findings suggest that IGF-I splice variants may regulate myoblast differentiation through the actions of mature IGF-I and not the E peptides.

title: Antimicrobial peptide pleurocidin synergizes with antibiotics through hydroxyl radical formation and membrane damage, and exerts antibiofilm activity.
text:
Background: Pleurocidin, a 25-mer antimicrobial peptide (AMP), has been shown to exhibit bactericidal activity. However, the mechanisms underlying its synergistic activity when combined with conventional antibiotics and its antibiofilm effects are not well understood.
Methods: To investigate the interaction between pleurocidin and antibiotics, we employed a checkerboard assay. To elucidate the mechanisms involved in their synergism, we detected hydroxyl radical formation using 3'-(p-hydroxyphenyl) fluorescein, measured the NAD(+)/NADH ratio by NAD(+) cycling assay, observed changes in bacterial viability with the hydroxyl radical scavenger thiourea, and investigated cytoplasmic membrane damage using propidium iodide. Additionally, we examined the antibiofilm effect of pleurocidin using a tissue culture plate method.
Results: Our findings revealed that pleurocidin exhibited synergistic activity with antibiotics against various bacterial strains (fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) ≤ 0.5), except for Enterococcus faecium treated with a combination of pleurocidin and ampicillin (FICI = 0.75). We found that pleurocidin alone and in combination with antibiotics induced hydroxyl radical formation, which was caused by a transient NADH depletion. The addition of thiourea prevented bacterial death, particularly in the case of the combined treatment of pleurocidin and ampicillin, which showed synergistic effects. Furthermore, the combination of pleurocidin and erythromycin increased the permeability of bacterial cytoplasmic membrane. Additionally, pleurocidin exhibited a potent inhibitory effect on preformed biofilm of bacterial organisms.
Conclusion: Our results suggest that pleurocidin synergizes with antibiotics through hydroxyl radical formation and membrane-active mechanisms, and exhibits antibiofilm activity. These findings imply that pleurocidin may be a promising therapeutic agent and adjuvant for antimicrobial chemotherapy.

title: Outcome of pregnancy in women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency.
text:
Background: Pregnant women with mild preexisting renal disease typically experience few complications during pregnancy, but the risks of maternal and obstetrical complications in women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency remain unclear.
Methods: We investigated the frequency and types of maternal and obstetrical complications, as well as outcomes of pregnancy, in 67 women with primary renal disease (82 pregnancies). All participants had initial serum creatinine concentrations of at least 1.4 mg/dL (124 mumol/L) and gestations that continued beyond the first trimester.
Results: Our findings showed a significant increase in mean serum creatinine concentration from 1.9 ± 0.8 mg/dL (168 ± 71 mumol/L) in early pregnancy to 2.5 ± 1.3 mg/dL (221 ± 115 mumol/L) in the third trimester. The frequency of hypertension rose from 28% at baseline to 48% in the third trimester, and that of high-grade proteinuria (urinary protein excretion > 3000 mg/L) from 23% to 41% during the same period. Among the 70 pregnancies (57 women) for which data were available during pregnancy and immediately postpartum, pregnancy-related loss of maternal renal function occurred in 43%. Eight of these pregnancies (10% of the total) were associated with rapid acceleration of maternal renal insufficiency. Obstetrical complications included a high rate of preterm delivery (59%) and growth retardation (37%). The infant survival rate was 93%.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that among pregnant women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency, the rates of complications due to worsening renal function, hypertension, and obstetrical complications are increased. However, the fetal survival rate remains high. Further research is needed to better understand the risks and outcomes of pregnancy in this population.

title: High-mobility group box-1 protein induces osteogenic phenotype changes in aortic valve interstitial cells.
text:
Objective:
Calcific aortic valve (AV) disease is an inflammation-related condition, and high-mobility group box-1 (HMGB1) protein and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) have been implicated in various inflammatory diseases. This study aimed to investigate the involvement of the HMGB1-TLR4 axis in calcific AV disease and to evaluate the effect of HMGB1 on the pro-osteogenic phenotype change of valvular interstitial cells (VICs).
Methods:
Expression of HMGB1 and TLR4 in human calcific AVs was analyzed using immunohistochemical staining and immunoblotting. Cultured VICs were used as an in vitro model, and the effects of HMGB1 on VICs were examined with and without TLR4 small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA), c-Jun N-terminal kinase mitogen-activated protein kinase (JNK MAPK), and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) inhibitors.
Results:
Enhanced accumulation of HMGB1 and TLR4 was observed in calcific valves. HMGB1 induced high levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine production and promoted the osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs. Additionally, HMGB1 induced phosphorylation of JNK MAPK and NF-κB. However, these effects were significantly suppressed by siRNA silencing of TLR4. Furthermore, blockade of JNK MAPK and NF-κB phosphorylation prevented HMGB1-induced production of pro-osteogenic factors and mineralization of VICs.


Conclusion:
The HMGB1 protein may promote osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs through the TLR4-JNK-NF-κB signaling pathway, contributing to the development of calcific AV disease.

title: RiboSys, a high-resolution, quantitative approach to measure the in vivo kinetics of pre-mRNA splicing and 3'-end processing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: In this study, we present methods for obtaining a quantitative description of RNA processing at the molecular level in budding yeast. As a model organism for gene expression studies, we constructed tetON (for induction studies) and tetOFF (for repression, derepression, and RNA degradation studies) yeast strains harboring a series of reporter genes integrated in the genome under the control of a tetO7 promoter. We adapted reverse transcription and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) techniques to determine the average number of mRNA copies per cell in a population. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) measurements of transcript numbers in individual cells validated the RT-qPCR approach for the average copy-number determination, despite the variability in transcript levels within a population of cells. Additionally, RT-qPCR was used to identify and quantify the products of different splicing events in the reporter transcripts, and methods were developed to map and quantify 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation. This system enables the quantitative monitoring of pre-mRNA production, splicing, 3'-end maturation, and degradation with unprecedented resolution, making it suitable for mathematical modeling. By employing this approach, we demonstrate that reporter transcripts are spliced prior to their 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation, occurring cotranscriptionally.

title: Generation of mice with a conditional allele for the p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor gene.
text: The p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor has been linked to various biological and pathological processes, although significant progress has been made in understanding its physiological function, many details and aspects remain unclear. This is partly due to the limitations of the two existing knockout mouse models (Exons 3 or 4 deleted, respectively), which display inconsistencies that hinder definitive conclusions. To address this issue, we generated mice carrying a conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) created by flanking Exons 4-6, which encode the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, using loxP sites. To validate this novel conditional allele, we generated both neural crest-specific p75(NTR) /Wnt1-Cre mutants and conventional p75(NTR) null mutants. Both mutant lines displayed abnormal hind limb reflexes, indicating that loss of p75(NTR) in neural crest-derived cells leads to a peripheral neuropathy similar to that observed in conventional p75(NTR) mutants. This novel conditional p75(NTR) allele will provide new opportunities to investigate the role of p75(NTR) in specific tissues and cells.

title: A Triple-Stain Flow Cytometric Method to Assess Plasma- and Acrosome-Membrane Integrity of Cryopreserved Bovine Sperm Immediately after Thawing in Presence of Egg-Yolk Particles1
text: Simultaneously evaluating the viability and acrosome integrity of spermatozoa using flow cytometry could be a valuable tool in both research and clinical settings. In this study, a new triple-stain combination was developed to evaluate the viability and acrosome integrity of bovine sperm processed in egg yolk-based extenders using flow cytometry. The combination of SYBR-14, propidium iodide (PI), and phycoerythrin-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PE-PNA) enabled the distinction between sperm cells, egg yolk, and debris particles, which is crucial for flow cytometric analysis of frozen-thawed bovine sperm. Unlike traditional methods that require washing to remove egg yolk, this combination eliminates the need for this step. Additionally, PE-PNA was used to identify acrosome-damaged/reacted sperm cells from acrosome-intact cells. Repeatability was evaluated using two processed ejaculates from 10 bulls, with three straws per batch analyzed in duplicate measurements. The method-agreement analysis between the SYBR-14/PE-PNA/PI and fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated PNA staining was performed on 14 frozen-thawed semen samples, with FITC-PNA/PI staining performed immediately after thawing and after a 3-h incubation at 37°C. The British Standards Institution repeatability index of the SYBR-14/PE-PNA/PI combination was 2.6%. In contrast, the FITC-PNA/PI method showed an average 6.3% overestimation of the live and acrosome-intact sperm cell subpopulation. Overall, the new triple-stain combination is highly repeatable and easy to use in routine applications, providing a more accurate estimate of the rate of sperm cells with intact head membranes and acrosomes compared to the commonly used and validated FITC-PNA/PI staining method.

title: Universal voluntary HIV testing with immediate antiretroviral therapy as a strategy for elimination of HIV transmission: a mathematical model.
text:
BACKGROUND
Approximately 3 million individuals worldwide were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) at the end of 2007, yet an estimated 6.7 million were still in need of treatment, and a further 2.7 million individuals became infected with HIV in 2007. Prevention efforts may reduce HIV incidence, but they are unlikely to eliminate the disease entirely. In this study, we investigated a theoretical strategy of universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate treatment with ART, and examined the conditions under which the HIV epidemic could be driven towards elimination.
METHODS
We employed mathematical models to explore the impact on the case reproduction number (stochastic model) and long-term dynamics of the HIV epidemic (deterministic transmission model) of testing all individuals in our test-case community (aged 15 years and older) for HIV every year and starting people on ART immediately after they are diagnosed HIV positive. We used data from South Africa as the test case for a generalized epidemic, and assumed that all HIV transmission was heterosexual.
FINDINGS
Our studied strategy could significantly accelerate the transition from the present endemic phase, in which most adults living with HIV are not receiving ART, to an elimination phase, in which most are on ART, within 5 years. It could reduce HIV incidence and mortality to less than one case per 1000 people per year by 2016, or within 10 years of full implementation of the strategy, and reduce the prevalence of HIV to less than 1% within 50 years. We estimate that in 2032, the yearly cost of the present strategy and the theoretical strategy would both be US$1.7 billion; however, after this time, the cost of the present strategy would continue to increase, whereas that of the theoretical strategy would decrease.
INTERPRETATION
Universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate ART, combined with present prevention approaches, could have a significant impact on severe generalized HIV/AIDS epidemics. This approach merits further mathematical modeling, research, and broad consultation.

title: Common variants in DGKK are strongly associated with risk of hypospadias
text: Hypospadias, a common congenital malformation of the male external genitalia, has been the focus of a genome-wide association study (GWAS) using pooled DNA from 436 individuals with hypospadias (cases) and 494 controls of European descent. The study identified several potential risk genes, including DGKK, which encodes diacylglycerol kinase κ. To further investigate the association between DGKK and hypospadias, individual genotyping was performed on two SNPs (rs1934179 and rs7063116) in the discovery sample of 133 cases and their parents, as well as in additional samples from the Dutch (133 cases and 402 controls) and Swedish (266 cases and 402 controls) populations. The results showed a significant association between the risk allele of rs1934179 and hypospadias in all three populations, with an allele-specific odds ratio (OR) of 2.5 in the discovery sample, 3.9 in the Dutch sample, and 2.5 in the Swedish sample. Similarly, the risk allele of rs7063116 was associated with hypospadias in all three populations, with an OR of 2.3 in the discovery sample, 3.8 in the Dutch sample, and 2.2 in the Swedish sample. Expression studies also showed that DGKK is expressed in preputial tissue from both cases and controls, and that the risk allele of rs1934179 was associated with lower expression in carriers. Based on these findings, the authors propose that DGKK is a major risk gene for hypospadias.

title: Neutrophils Suppress Intraluminal NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Cell Clearance and Enhance Extravasation of Disseminated Carcinoma Cells.
text:
UNLABELED
Immune cells play a crucial role in the initial stages of cancer metastasis, but their functions in facilitating progression through the later stages of the invasion-metastasis cascade are poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the novel functions of neutrophils in promoting intraluminal survival and extravasation at sites of metastatic dissemination.
We demonstrate that CD11b(+)/Ly6G(+) neutrophils enhance metastasis formation through two distinct mechanisms. First, they inhibit natural killer cell function, leading to an increase in the intraluminal survival time of tumor cells. Subsequently, they facilitate extravasation of tumor cells through the secretion of IL1β and matrix metalloproteinases.
Our findings identify neutrophils as key regulators of intraluminal survival and extravasation in the context of cancer metastasis. By suppressing natural killer cell activity and increasing extravasation of tumor cells, neutrophils play a crucial role in facilitating the progression of cancer metastasis.
This study provides important insights into the systemic contributions of neutrophils to cancer metastasis, highlighting their role in intermediate steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade. Our findings have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting neutrophils in cancer treatment.
In conclusion, our study demonstrates the critical role of neutrophils in promoting cancer metastasis, highlighting their involvement in both intraluminal survival and extravasation. These findings underscore the importance of targeting neutrophils in cancer treatment, and suggest that strategies aimed at modulating neutrophil function may be effective in preventing or slowing the progression of cancer metastasis.

title: High Km soluble 5'-nucleotidase from human placenta. Properties and allosteric regulation by IMP and ATP.
text: A human placental soluble "high Km" 5'-nucleotidase has been isolated and purified from a mixture of "low Km" 5'-nucleotidase and nonspecific phosphatase using AMP-Sepharose affinity chromatography. The enzyme was purified 8000-fold to a specific activity of 25.6 μmol/min/mg. The subunit molecular mass is 53 kDa, and the native molecular mass is 210 kDa, indicating a tetrameric structure. The enzyme exhibits high activity towards IMP and GMP, with IMP being hydrolyzed 15 times faster than AMP. The enzyme has a virtually absolute requirement for magnesium ions and is regulated by them. Purine nucleoside 5'-triphosphates, such as dATP, ATP, and GTP, strongly activate the enzyme, with the potency order being dATP > ATP > GTP. 2,3-Diphosphoglycerate also activates the enzyme as potently as ATP. The enzyme's activity is modified by the concentration of ATP, with higher concentrations leading to a sigmoidal activation curve at low IMP concentrations and a hyperbolic activation curve at high IMP concentrations. Inorganic phosphate shifts the hyperbolic substrate velocity relationship for IMP to a sigmoidal one. Under physiological conditions (3 mM ATP, 1-4 mM Pi, 150 mM KCl, pH 7.4), the enzyme is 25-35 times more active towards 100 μM IMP than towards 100 μM AMP. These data suggest that the enzyme coexists in human placenta with the low Km enzyme, is regulated by IMP, ATP, and Pi levels, and has complex interaction of the associated binding sites.

title: Histones are incorporated in trans during reassembly of the yeast PHO5 promoter.
text: In yeast, the remodeling of the PHO5 promoter chromatin upon activation is accompanied by temporary increases in histone acetylation and subsequent removal of histones from the promoter region. During the process of repression, nucleosomes must be reassembled on the promoter. By using a strain with two differently tagged and regulated versions of histone H3, we were able to determine where the histones for reassembling the inactive promoter chromatin come from. Our findings show that the incorporated histones originate from outside the chromatin fraction. Promoter closure occurs rapidly, and the histone chaperones Asf1 and Hir1, as well as the SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling complex, play important roles in the rapid reassembly of nucleosomes at the PHO5 promoter.

title: National study of physician awareness and adherence to cardiovascular disease prevention guidelines.
text:
Background:
Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. However, few studies have investigated the adherence of physicians to CVD prevention guidelines based on physician specialty or patient characteristics, particularly gender.
Methods and Results:
An online survey of 500 randomly selected physicians (300 primary care physicians, 100 obstetricians/gynecologists, and 100 cardiologists) used a standardized questionnaire to assess physician awareness, adoption, and barriers to national CVD prevention guidelines by specialty. An experimental case study design was used to evaluate physician accuracy and determinants of CVD risk level assignment and application of guidelines among high-, intermediate-, or low-risk patients. The study found that intermediate-risk women were significantly more likely to be assigned to a lower-risk category by primary care physicians than men with identical risk profiles (P<0.0001), and similar trends were observed among obstetricians/gynecologists and cardiologists. The assignment of risk level significantly predicted recommendations for lifestyle and preventive pharmacotherapy. After adjusting for risk assignment, the impact of patient gender on preventive care was not significant except for less aspirin (P<0.01) and more weight management recommended (P<0.04) for intermediate-risk women. Physicians rated themselves as less effective in their ability to help patients prevent CVD. Additionally, fewer than 1 in 5 physicians were aware that more women than men die each year from CVD.
Conclusions:
The primary factor associated with CVD preventive recommendations was perception of risk. Gender disparities in recommendations for preventive therapy were largely explained by the lower perceived risk despite similar calculated risk for women versus men. Educational interventions for physicians are needed to improve the quality of CVD preventive care and lower morbidity and mortality from CVD for men and women.

title: TECHNICAL ADVANCE Floral dip: a simplified method for Agrobacterium-mediated
text: The Agrobacterium vacuum infiltration method has enabled the transformation of Arabidopsis thaliana without the need for plant tissue culture or regeneration. In this study, the effectiveness of this method was evaluated and a significantly modified transformation protocol was developed. The labor-intensive vacuum infiltration process was replaced by a simpler dipping method involving the immersion of developing floral tissues in a solution containing Agrobacterium tumefaciens, 5% sucrose, and 500 microliters per liter of surfactant Silwet L-77. Sucrose and surfactant were crucial for the success of the floral dip method. Plants inoculated when they had numerous immature floral buds and few siliques produced transformed progeny at the highest rate. The use of plant tissue culture media, hormone benzylamino purine, and pH adjustment was found to be unnecessary, and Agrobacterium could be applied to plants at a range of cell densities. Repeated applications of Agrobacterium improved transformation rates and overall yield of transformants by approximately twofold. Covering plants for one day to retain humidity after inoculation also increased transformation rates by twofold. The modified method should facilitate high-throughput transformation of Arabidopsis for applications such as T-DNA gene tagging, positional cloning, or attempts at targeted gene replacement.

title: Pathway connectivity and signaling coordination in the yeast stress-activated signaling network
text:
Stressed cells coordinate a complex response involving multiple physiological pathways. Despite significant progress in understanding the stress-activated regulatory network, key aspects of the complete network and principles of signal integration remain unclear. To address this gap, we developed a combined experimental and computational approach to integrate available protein interaction data, gene fitness contributions, and transcriptome profiles of salt-stressed yeast cells. This allowed us to infer the salt-responsive signaling network in yeast, revealing novel insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying cellular stress responses.
Our approach identified new regulators, uncovered previously unappreciated crosstalk between known pathways, and highlighted previously unknown "hubs" of signal integration. We validated these predictions by showing that Cdc14 phosphatase is a central hub in the network and that modification of RNA polymerase II coordinates induction of stress-defense genes with reduction of growth-related transcripts. This work has important implications for understanding stress biology, as the orthologous human network is enriched for cancer-causing genes.
In summary, our study demonstrates the power of integrating multiple types of data to gain a comprehensive understanding of cellular stress responses. By combining experimental and computational approaches, we were able to identify novel regulators, uncover hidden patterns of crosstalk, and highlight key nodes in the stress-activated regulatory network. These findings have important implications for both basic research and disease diagnosis and treatment.

title: Premigratory and migratory neural crest cells are multipotent in vivo.
text: The neural crest (NC) is an embryonic stem cell population that gives rise to a wide range of cell types, including peripheral neurons, myelinating Schwann cells, and melanocytes. However, there has been a long-standing debate about whether individual NC cells are truly multipotent or if they are composed of a heterogeneous mixture of lineage-restricted progenitors. To resolve this controversy, we used in vivo fate mapping of single trunk NC cells in the R26R-Confetti mouse model, which allows for the tracking of individual cells throughout development. By combining quantitative clonal analyses with definitive markers of differentiation, we found that the vast majority of individual NC cells are multipotent, with only a few clones contributing to a single derivative. Interestingly, this multipotency is maintained in migratory NC cells. Our findings provide conclusive evidence for the in vivo multipotency of both premigratory and migrating NC cells in the mouse.

title: Implementing the ESHRE 'poor responder' criteria in research studies: methodological implications.
text: The Bologna criteria for defining poor ovarian response (POR) during IVF offer a valuable framework for new research in the field of assisted conception. However, designing studies around the European Society for Human Reproduction and Embryology (ESHRE) POR criteria can be methodologically challenging due to the inclusion of various POR subpopulations with distinct baseline characteristics and unknown clinical prognosis. When conducting randomized controlled trials (RCTs), potential bias may arise if women from each subpopulation are not evenly allocated between intervention groups. In the case of small or moderate-sized RCTs, a single-sequence randomization method may not ensure balanced allocation between groups. Stratified randomization methods provide an alternative methodological approach that can help address these challenges. Depending on the chosen methodology, the reporting of patient characteristics and outcomes within each intervention group may be more accurate and informative when grouped according to relevant subpopulations.

title: Generation of gene-edited rats by delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 protein and donor DNA into intact zygotes using electroporation
text: The use of the CRISPR/Cas9 system to generate gene-edited animals through microinjection is inefficient, time-consuming, and requires high technical skills. In contrast, our study demonstrates the optimization of an electroporation method for intact rat zygotes using sgRNAs and Cas9 protein in combination or not with ssODNs (~100 nt). This approach resulted in a high frequency of knockouts, ranging from 15 to 50% of analyzed animals. Notably, the use of ssODNs as a donor template led to precise knock-in mutations in 25-100% of analyzed animals, which is comparable to microinjection. Interestingly, electroporation of long ssDNA or dsDNA donors, which have been used successfully in microinjection in the past, did not lead to the generation of genome-edited animals, despite the visualization of dsDNA within zygotes. Therefore, the simultaneous electroporation of a large number of intact rat zygotes is a rapid, simple, and efficient method for generating a variety of genome-edited rats.

title: Uridylation of miRNAs by HEN1 SUPPRESSOR1 in Arabidopsis
text: HEN1-mediated 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect plant microRNAs (miRNAs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) as well as animal piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) from degradation and 3' terminal uridylation [1-8]. However, the enzymes responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs, siRNAs, or piRNAs in hen1 have remained unknown. In this study, a genetic screen identified a second-site mutation, hen1 suppressor1-2 (heso1-2), that partially suppresses the morphological phenotypes of the hypomorphic hen1-2 allele and the null hen1-1 allele in Arabidopsis. HESO1 encodes a terminal nucleotidyl transferase that preferentially adds untemplated uridine to the 3' end of RNA, which is completely abolished by 2'-O-methylation. The heso1-2 mutation affects the profile of u-tailed miRNAs and siRNAs and increases the abundance of truncated and/or normal-sized ones in hen1, leading to increased total amounts of miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. In contrast, overexpressing HESO1 in hen1-2 causes more severe morphological defects and less accumulation of miRNAs. These findings demonstrate that HESO1 is an enzyme responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. These observations also suggest that uridylation may destabilize unmethylated miRNAs through an unknown mechanism and compete with 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease activities in hen1. These findings have implications for piRNA uridylation in hen1 in animals.

title: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to Prevent HIV Infection: Current Status, Future Opportunities and Challenges
text:
As the global incidence of HIV continues to exceed 2 million new infections annually, there is an urgent need for effective interventions to reduce HIV transmission. Randomized, placebo-controlled studies have demonstrated that daily oral antiretroviral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with a fixed-dose combination tablet containing tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine can significantly reduce HIV incidence among diverse at-risk populations. However, several challenges remain in implementing PrEP, including low awareness and utilization among at-risk individuals, uncertainty about adherence in real-world settings, inadequate training of healthcare providers, limited data on potential adverse effects, high costs, and stigma associated with PrEP use and the behaviors that would warrant its use.
Innovative pharmacological approaches could help address these challenges. For example, less-than-daily oral dosing regimens and long-acting injectable medications could reduce pill burdens and facilitate adherence, while local delivery of PrEP medications to genital compartments via gels, rings, and films may limit systemic drug exposure and potential toxicities. As the portfolio of chemoprophylactic agents and delivery systems expands, it is hoped that antiretroviral chemoprophylaxis could become an acceptable, feasible, and highly effective addition to existing HIV prevention strategies, providing a much-needed solution to the ongoing HIV epidemic.

title: Prepregnancy BMI and the risk of gestational diabetes: a systematic review of the literature with meta-analysis.
text: The aim of this study is to assess and quantify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) based on prepregnancy maternal body mass index (BMI). The study design is a systematic review of observational studies published in the last 30 years. Four electronic databases were searched, yielding 1745 citations, of which 70 studies (including 671,945 women) were included (59 cohorts and 11 case-controls). The majority of studies were of high or medium quality. Compared to women with a normal BMI, the unadjusted pooled odds ratio (OR) for underweight women developing GDM was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.69-0.82). The ORs for overweight, moderately obese, and morbidly obese women were 1.97 (95% CI 1.77-2.19), 3.01 (95% CI 2.34-3.87), and 5.55 (95% CI 4.27-7.21), respectively. For every 1 kg/m² increase in BMI, the prevalence of GDM increased by 0.92% (95% CI 0.73-1.10). The study findings highlight the positive association between prepregnancy BMI and the risk of GDM, providing valuable information for counseling women planning a pregnancy.

title: Multiple risk behaviour: increasing socio-economic gap over time?
text: BACKGROUND: Unhealthy behaviors often co-occur, and this study aimed to investigate the relationship between education and lifestyle, defined as a cluster of risk behaviors, over time. METHODS: Cross-sectional data from the Belgian Health Interview Surveys in 1997, 2001, and 2004 were analyzed, including individuals aged ≥ 15 years with information on health behaviors and education (n = 7431, n = 8142, and n = 7459, respectively). A lifestyle index was created based on the sum of four unhealthy behaviors: smoking, risky alcohol use, sedentary behavior, and poor diet. The lifestyle index was dichotomized as low (0-2) or high (3-4). Socio-economic inequalities in multiple risk behavior were assessed using logistic regression and Relative Index of Inequality (RII), stratified by sex. RESULTS: Approximately 7.5% of the adult population combined three to four unhealthy behaviors. Lower educated men were found to be at the highest risk. The odds ratio (OR) among men significantly increased from 1.6 in 2001 to 3.4 in 2004 (P = 0.029), while the increase in the OR among women was less pronounced. However, the RII did not show any gradient, neither for men nor for women. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that lower educated individuals are more likely to engage in multiple risk behaviors. The findings also indicate an increasing polarization in socio-economic inequalities among men, highlighting the need for targeted health promotion programs to address these behaviors simultaneously.

title: Variations and Trends in Health Burden of Visual Impairment Due to Cataract: A Global Analysis.
text:
The purpose of this study is to assess the global trends in the health burden of people with visual impairment due to cataract, measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and to investigate the correlations between national levels of socioeconomic development and these DALYs.
Methods:
The study used data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2015 to estimate global, regional, and national DALY numbers, crude rates, and age-standardized rates of cataract vision loss by age and sex. The study also obtained data on human development index (HDI), per capita gross domestic product (GDP), and other country-level data from international open databases. Regression analysis was used to assess the correlations between age-standardized DALY rate and socioeconomic variables.
Results:
The study found that the global DALY numbers of cataract vision loss increased by 89.42%, from 2048.18 thousand in 1990 to 3879.74 thousand in 2015 (P < 0.001). Females had higher DALY numbers and crude rates compared to males, with an age-standardized DALY rate of 315.83 and crude rate of 38.29, respectively (all P < 0.001). The study also found that the age-standardized DALY rate was higher in countries with low HDI, with 91.03 for low HDI, 81.67 for medium HDI, 55.89 for high HDI, and 17.10 for very high HDI countries (P < 0.01), respectively. The national age-standardized DALY rates in 2015 were negatively associated with both HDI (R2 = 0.489, P < 0.001) and per capita GDP (R2 = 0.331, P < 0.001). Stepwise multiple regression showed that HDI was significantly correlated with national age-standardized DALY rates in 2015 after adjusting for other confounding factors (P < 0.001).

Conclusions:
The study concluded that the global health burden of vision loss due to cataract increased between 1990 and 2015 despite efforts to address the issue. The study also found that the burden of cataract vision loss was significantly associated with national levels of socioeconomic development, with countries with lower HDI and lower per capita GDP having higher DALY numbers. These findings suggest that addressing the socioeconomic determinants of health, such as poverty and inequality, may be crucial in reducing the burden of cataract vision loss globally.

title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR/Cas systems.
text: To elucidate the functional effects of genetic variants and elements, advanced genome editing tools are essential. The Type II prokaryotic CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats)/Cas system has been shown to facilitate RNA-guided site-specific DNA cleavage with precision. We developed and tested two different Type II CRISPR/Cas systems, demonstrating that Cas9 nucleases can be directed by short RNAs to cleave endogenous genomic loci in human and mouse cells with accuracy. Additionally, we found that Cas9 can be converted into a nicking enzyme, allowing for homology-directed repair with minimal mutagenic activity. Furthermore, multiple guide sequences can be encoded in a single CRISPR array, enabling simultaneous editing of multiple sites within the mammalian genome, highlighting the ease and versatility of the RNA-guided nuclease technology.

title: Transformation of intact yeast cells treated with alkali cations.
text: Intact yeast cells were treated with alkali cations, leading to their competence for DNA uptake. Among the alkali cations tested, Li+, Cs+, Rb+, K+, and Na+ were found to be effective in inducing competence in Saccharomyces cerevisiae D13-1A cells. The optimal conditions for transformation of these cells with plasmid YRp7 were investigated in detail using CsCl. The results showed that the most effective incubation time was 1 hour, and the most optimal cell concentration was 5 x 107 cells per ml. Additionally, the optimum concentration of Cs+ was found to be 1.0 M. Transformation efficiency increased with increasing concentrations of plasmid DNA, and the presence of polyethylene glycol was essential for efficient uptake. Heat pulse and various polyamines or basic proteins were also found to stimulate the uptake of plasmid DNA. Interestingly, circular DNA was taken up by Cs+-treated yeast cells, although the uptake efficiency was lower compared to linear plasmid DNA. The transformation efficiency with Cs+ or Li+ was found to be comparable to conventional protoplast methods for a plasmid containing the ars1 gene, although not for plasmids containing a 2 microns origin replication.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life as Measured with EQ-5D among Populations with and without Specific Chronic Conditions: A Population-Based Survey in Shaanxi Province, China
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of chronic conditions and other risk factors on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in a distributed sample of individuals located in Shaanxi Province, China, using the EQ-5D instrument. The study employed a multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method to select participants, and EQ-5D was used to measure HRQoL. The study found that the most frequently reported problems involved pain/discomfort (8.8%) and anxiety/depression (7.6%). Nearly half of the respondents who reported problems in any of the five dimensions were chronic patients. The study also identified factors associated with EQ VAS, including male gender, higher level of education, employment, younger age, urban residence, access to free medical service, and higher levels of physical activity. The three leading risk factors were cerebrovascular disease, cancer, and mental disease. The study's findings highlight the importance of managing chronic diseases and improving HRQoL, and suggest that longitudinal studies are needed to monitor changes in HRQoL and evaluate the outcomes of chronic disease intervention programs.

title: Memory and Modularity in Cell-Fate Decision Making
text: Cells that are genetically identical and share the same environment can exhibit distinct phenotypes, often due to a combination of chance, external cues, and cellular attempts to exert autonomous behaviors. By observing thousands of cells over hundreds of generations under constant conditions, we investigate the stochastic decision-making process that leads to the transition between a solitary, motile state and a chained, sessile state in Bacillus subtilis. Our findings reveal that the motile state is "memoryless," meaning it lacks autonomous control over the time spent in this state, while the time spent as connected chains of cells is tightly regulated, ensuring coordination among related cells in the multicellular state. We show that the three-protein regulatory circuit governing this decision is modular, with initiation and maintenance of chaining being genetically separable functions. Additionally, we find that stimulation of the same initiating pathway can trigger biofilm formation, suggesting that autonomous timing allows cells to make a "trial commitment" to multicellularity that external signals can extend.

title: Lpd depletion reveals that SRF specifies radial versus tangential migration of pyramidal neurons
text: During corticogenesis, the majority of cortical neurons (pyramidal neurons) arise from the ventricular zone and undergo a series of transformations to become bipolar. These neurons then migrate to their proper positions within the cortex, remaining attached to their glial substrate as they pass through the subventricular and intermediate zones. These regions are rich in tangentially migrating interneurons and axon fibre tracts. In order to understand the role of lamellipodin (Lpd), a homologue of a key regulator of neuronal migration and polarization in Caenorhabditis elegans, in corticogenesis, we examined its function. We found that Lpd depletion causes bipolar pyramidal neurons to adopt a tangential, rather than radial-glial, migration mode without affecting their cell fate. Mechanistically, Lpd depletion reduces the activity of SRF, a transcription factor regulated by changes in the ratio of polymerized to unpolymerized actin. Therefore, Lpd depletion exposes a role for SRF in directing pyramidal neurons to select a radial migration pathway along glia rather than a tangential migration mode.

title: Identification of p18 INK4c as a tumor suppressor gene in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: Genomic alterations leading to uncontrolled activation of cyclin/cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) complexes are a key driver of many common human tumor types, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). In GBM, these alterations are most frequently due to homozygous deletion of the p16(INK4a) gene and less commonly involve genomic amplifications of genes encoding cyclins or CDKs. We have identified a novel genetic alteration in GBM, involving deletion of the p18(INK4c) CDK inhibitor gene. This deletion occurs in combination with homozygous deletion of p16(INK4a) in 43% of GBM primary tumors examined by immunohistochemistry. Restoration of p18(INK4c) expression in p18(INK4c)-deficient GBM cells using lentiviral vectors led to G(1) cell cycle arrest, indicating that p18(INK4c) functions as a tumor suppressor gene in GBM. These findings highlight an additional mechanism by which cyclin/CDK activity is aberrantly activated in GBM, underscoring the importance of targeting these pathways for therapeutic intervention.

title: Two-stage control of an oxidative stress regulon: the Escherichia coli SoxR protein triggers redox-inducible expression of the soxS regulatory gene.
text: Escherichia coli responds to the redox stress caused by generators of superoxide, such as paraquat, by activating the synthesis of up to 80 polypeptides. The expression of a key group of these inducible proteins is regulated at the transcriptional level by the soxRS locus (the soxRS regulon). A two-stage control system was proposed for soxRS, in which an intracellular redox signal triggers the SoxR protein as a transcriptional activator of the soxS gene, leading to increased levels of SoxS protein and subsequent activation of transcription of the various soxRS regulon genes. To monitor soxS transcription, operon fusions of the E. coli lac genes were constructed to the soxS promoter. Expression from the soxS promoter is strongly inducible by paraquat in a manner dependent on a functional soxR gene. Other superoxide-generating agents, such as phenazine methosulfate, also trigger soxR(+)-dependent soxS expression, and the inductions by paraquat and phenazine methosulfate were dependent on the presence of oxygen. In contrast, other oxidative stress agents, such as H2O2, gamma rays, and heat shock, failed to induce soxS expression. Aerobic growth of superoxide dismutase-deficient bacteria, on the other hand, triggered soxR-dependent soxS expression. These results suggest a specific redox signal for soxS induction. Furthermore, direct binding of the SoxR protein to the soxS promoter was demonstrated through band-shift and DNase I footprinting experiments, indicating a role for SoxR in the activation of the soxS gene. The binding mode of SoxR to DNA is similar to that of its homolog MerR, with the SoxR footprint spanning the -10 to -35 region of the soxS promoter.

title: Air pollution and cardiovascular disease: a statement for healthcare professionals from the Expert Panel on Population and Prevention Science of the American Heart Association.
text: Air pollution is a diverse and intricate mixture of gases, liquids, and solid particles. Epidemiological studies have consistently shown an elevated risk of cardiovascular events associated with both short-term and long-term exposure to current levels of ambient particulate matter. Various plausible mechanisms have been proposed, including enhanced coagulation and thrombosis, a propensity for arrhythmias, acute vasoconstriction of the arteries, systemic inflammatory responses, and the long-term promotion of atherosclerosis. The purpose of this statement is to provide healthcare professionals and regulatory agencies with a comprehensive review of the literature on air pollution and cardiovascular disease, as well as to address the implications of these findings in terms of public health and regulatory policies. Practical recommendations for healthcare providers and their patients are also outlined. Finally, suggestions for future research are made to address several remaining scientific questions.

title: Non-invasive ventilation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: helmet versus facial mask
text: The present study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a novel interface, the helmet, in improving the success rate of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). A prospective, controlled, randomized study with a cross-over design was conducted in 10 patients. The study compared the gas exchange, inspiratory effort, patient-ventilator synchrony, and patient tolerance of NIV delivered via the helmet and conventional facial mask. Both interfaces were used in a random order, with each trial preceded by periods of spontaneous unassisted breathing. The primary outcome measures included arterial blood gases, inspiratory effort, duration of diaphragm contraction, and ventilator assistance. The results showed that both interfaces were effective in improving gas exchange and inspiratory effort, with no significant differences in patient comfort. However, the helmet was less efficient than the mask in reducing inspiratory effort and worsened patient-ventilator synchrony, as evidenced by longer delays to trigger on and cycle off mechanical assistance, and a higher number of ineffective efforts. These findings suggest that while the helmet may offer some advantages in terms of patient comfort, it may not be the most effective interface for NIV in patients with COPD.

title: Case Management and Client Access to Health and Social Services in Outpatient Substance Abuse Treatment
text: A primary objective of case management in substance abuse treatment is to coordinate services across various settings and integrate these services with other community resources, such as housing, mental health, medical, and social services. However, case management is a multifaceted construct that encompasses several key dimensions, including the extent of coverage, the degree of management of the referral process, and the location of case management activity (on-site, off-site, or both). This study investigates the relationship between specific dimensions of case management and the utilization of health and ancillary social services in outpatient substance abuse treatment. Overall, the findings suggest that more comprehensive case management during the referral process and providing case management both on-site and off-site are most consistent with predictions of greater use of health and ancillary social services by substance abuse clients. However, these effects are specific to general health care and mental health services, and case management appears to have little impact on use of social services or aftercare plans.

title: Evidence that the Ipl1-Sli15 (Aurora Kinase-INCENP) Complex Promotes Chromosome Bi-orientation by Altering Kinetochore-Spindle Pole Connections
text: The attachment of sister kinetochores to microtubules from opposite spindle poles during mitosis (bi-orientation) remains poorly understood. In yeast, the ortholog of the Aurora B-INCENP protein kinase complex (Ipl1-Sli15) may play a crucial role in this process, as it is necessary to prevent sister kinetochores from attaching to microtubules from the same spindle pole. To investigate the function of Ipl1 in this process, we studied cells that cannot replicate their chromosomes but still duplicate their spindle pole bodies (SPBs). We found that kinetochores detach from old SPBs and reattach to old and new SPBs with equal frequency in cells with intact Ipl1 function, but remain attached to old SPBs in ipl1 mutants. These findings suggest that Ipl1-Sli15 may facilitate bi-orientation by promoting the turnover of kinetochore-SPB connections until tension in the surrounding chromatin pulls sister kinetochores towards opposite spindle poles.

title: CRITICAL REVIEW Cutaneous Vasculitis Update: Diagnostic Criteria,
text:
Vasculitis, an inflammatory condition that affects the blood vessels, can lead to various complications such as hemorrhage, aneurysm formation, infarction, or stenosis, which can cause tissue ischemia. The skin, due to its large vascular bed and exposure to cold temperatures, is particularly susceptible to vasculitis. There are many different types of vasculitic syndromes that affect the skin, ranging from localized and self-limited to generalized and life-threatening with multi-organ involvement.
To accurately diagnose cutaneous vasculitis, a biopsy is necessary to confirm the presence of acute or chronic signs of vasculitis, such as fibrinoid necrosis or endarteritis obliterans, as well as past signs of healed arteritis. Additionally, extravascular findings such as patterned fibrosis or collagenolytic granulomas should be noted. While vasculitis can be classified based on its etiology, many cases have no identifiable cause, and a single etiologic agent can lead to multiple distinct clinicopathologic expressions of vasculitis. Therefore, a morphological approach to classification is best, which involves determining the size of the vessels and the principal inflammatory response. These histologic patterns roughly correlate with the pathogenic mechanisms that can be further confirmed through direct immunofluorescent examination, ANCA status, and findings from the work-up for systemic disease.
This review focuses on the diagnostic criteria, classification, epidemiology, etiology, pathogenesis, and evaluation of the cutaneous vasculitis patient. By understanding these aspects, healthcare professionals can provide more accurate diagnoses and effective treatments for patients with cutaneous vasculitis.

title: E2F-dependent histone acetylation and recruitment of the Tip60 acetyltransferase complex to chromatin in late G1.
text: E2F proteins play a crucial role in regulating gene expression by either activating or repressing transcription. Following mitogenic stimulation, E2F4-p130-histone deacetylase complexes dissociate, while activating E2F1, -2, and -3 species associate with target promoters. The acetylation of histones H3 and H4 is a critical step in this process, but it remains unclear whether this is a prerequisite or a consequence of E2F binding. To investigate the role of E2F in histone acetylation, we examined the effect of overexpressing a dominant-negative (DN) E2F1 mutant in serum-stimulated T98G cells. Our results showed that DN E2F1 blocked all E2F binding, H4 acetylation, and, albeit partially, H3 acetylation. Additionally, target gene activation and S-phase entry were also impaired by DN E2F1. Conversely, ectopic activation of E2F1 led to a rapid induction of H3 and H4 acetylation, indicating a direct role for E2F in these events. E2F1 was previously shown to interact with histone acetyltransferases (HATs) p300/CBP and PCAF/GCN5. In our study, we found that ectopically expressed E2F1 also bound the unrelated HAT Tip60 and induced the recruitment of five subunits of the Tip60 complex (Tip60, TRRAP, p400, Tip48, and Tip49) to target promoters in vivo. Furthermore, we observed that E2F-dependent recruitment of Tip60 to chromatin occurred in late G(1) following serum stimulation. Our findings suggest that the activities of multiple HAT complexes may contribute to E2F-dependent acetylation, transcription, and S-phase entry.

title: Chemical approaches to stem cell biology and therapeutics.
text: Small molecules have the potential to unlock the full therapeutic potential of stem cells by modulating their fate and function. By using rational design and screening, researchers have identified useful compounds to study the fundamental mechanisms of stem cell self-renewal, differentiation, and reprogramming. These findings have enabled the development of cell-based therapies and drugs targeting endogenous stem and progenitor cells for repair and regeneration. This lecture will discuss recent advances in stem cell biology and regenerative medicine, as well as new perspectives and future challenges in using chemical approaches to modulate stem cell fate and function.

title: Genome-wide maps of chromatin state in pluripotent and lineage-committed cells
text: In this study, we leverage single-molecule-based sequencing technology to conduct high-throughput profiling of histone modifications in mammalian cells. By generating over four billion bases of sequence data from chromatin immunoprecipitated DNA, we generate genome-wide chromatin-state maps of mouse embryonic stem cells, neural progenitor cells, and embryonic fibroblasts. Our findings reveal that lysine 4 and lysine 27 trimethylation are effective in distinguishing genes that are actively expressed, poised for expression, or stably repressed, thereby reflecting the cell state and lineage potential. Additionally, we identify lysine 36 trimethylation as a marker for primary coding and non-coding transcripts, facilitating gene annotation. Furthermore, we detect trimethylation of lysine 9 and lysine 20 at satellite, telomeric, and active long-terminal repeats, and observe that these modifications can spread into proximal unique sequences. Finally, we demonstrate that chromatin state can be read in an allele-specific manner by using single nucleotide polymorphisms, providing a framework for the application of comprehensive chromatin profiling towards characterizing diverse mammalian cell populations.

title: Oncofetal long noncoding RNA PVT1 promotes proliferation and stem cell-like property of hepatocellular carcinoma cells by stabilizing NOP2.
text:
Abstract:
This study investigated the expression profiles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in fetal and adult liver tissues from mice, as well as their potential role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Our findings revealed that many lncRNAs are up-regulated in fetal liver tissues, including lncRNA-mPvt1, which was found to promote cell proliferation, cell cycling, and the expression of stem cell-like properties in murine cells. Interestingly, we observed that human lncRNA-hPVT1 is up-regulated in HCC tissues and is associated with a poor clinical prognosis. Our results also showed that lncRNA-hPVT1 up-regulates a series of cell cycle genes in HCC cells and binds to the RNA-binding protein NOP2, leading to the stabilization of NOP2 proteins. Our findings suggest that the regulation of the lncRNA-hPVT1/NOP2 pathway may have beneficial effects on the treatment of HCC.
Introduction:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a primary liver cancer that is a major health problem worldwide. Early detection and diagnosis of HCC are crucial for improving patient outcomes, but current diagnostic markers have limitations. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been implicated in the development and progression of HCC, but their expression profiles in fetal and adult liver tissues have not been well-characterized. In this study, we aimed to investigate the expression profiles of lncRNAs in fetal and adult liver tissues from mice and to identify potential diagnostic markers for HCC.
Methods:
We used microarray analysis to compare the expression profiles of lncRNAs in fetal and adult liver tissues from mice. We also analyzed the expression of lncRNA-hPVT1 in HCC tissues and its association with clinical outcomes in human HCC patients. To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the protumorigenic effects of lncRNA-hPVT1, we used gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments, as well as RNA pulldown and mass spectrum experiments to identify RNA-binding proteins that interact with lncRNA-hPVT1.
Results:
Our microarray analysis revealed that many lncRNAs are up-regulated in fetal liver tissues, including lncRNA-mPvt1, which was found to promote cell proliferation, cell cycling, and the expression of stem cell-like properties in murine cells. Interestingly, we observed that human lncRNA-hPVT1 is up-regulated in HCC tissues and is associated with a poor clinical prognosis. Our results also showed that lncRNA-hPVT1 up-regulates a series of cell cycle genes in HCC cells and binds to the RNA-binding protein NOP2, leading to the stabilization of NOP2 proteins.
Discussion:
Our findings suggest that the expression of many lncRNAs is up-regulated in early liver development and that the fetal liver can be used to search for new diagnostic markers for HCC. LncRNA-hPVT1 promotes cell proliferation, cell cycling, and the acquisition of stem cell-like properties in HCC cells by stabilizing NOP2 protein. Regulation of the lncRNA-hPVT1/NOP2 pathway may have beneficial effects on the treatment of HCC. Our study highlights the potential of lncRNAs as diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for HCC.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study demonstrates that the expression of many lncRNAs is up-regulated in early liver development and that the fetal liver can be used to search for new diagnostic markers for HCC. LncRNA-hPVT1 promotes cell proliferation, cell cycling, and the acquisition of stem cell-like properties in HCC cells by stabilizing NOP2 protein. Regulation of the lncRNA-hPVT1/NOP2 pathway may have beneficial effects on the treatment of HCC. Further studies are needed to validate our findings and to explore the potential of lncRNAs as diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for HCC.

title: Candida albicans, a distinctive fungal model for cellular aging study
text:
Unicellular eukaryotic organisms, including Candida albicans, serve as popular model systems for understanding aging in eukaryotes. While Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe have long been established as aging model organisms, the addition of Candida albicans as a distinctive unicellular aging model provides further insight into the aging process. Notably, Candida albicans exhibits two distinct cell forms: yeast (blastospore) and hyphal (filamentous). Surprisingly, these two cell forms have similar replicative lifespans, allowing for the study of aging in both cell forms.
Old Candida cells display an accumulation of glycogen and oxidatively damaged proteins, which can be used to determine cellular age. Deletion of the SIR2 gene leads to a decrease in lifespan, while insertion of an extra copy of SIR2 extends lifespan, indicating that Sir2 regulates cellular aging in Candida albicans similarly to its role in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Interestingly, Sir2 deletion does not result in the accumulation of extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules, but rather influences the retention of oxidized proteins in mother cells, suggesting that extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules may not be directly associated with cellular aging in Candida albicans.
This novel aging model, which enables efficient large-scale isolation of old cells, may facilitate biochemical characterizations and genomics/proteomics studies of cellular aging, and help to verify aging pathways observed in other organisms, including Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

title: ANKTM1, a TRP-like Channel Expressed in Nociceptive Neurons, Is Activated by Cold Temperatures
text: Mammals use specialized neurons in their peripheral nervous system to detect temperature. Research has identified four TRPV-class channels that are involved in detecting heat, and one TRPM-class channel that detects cold. The range of temperatures that activate these channels covers the majority of the physiological spectrum sensed by most mammals, with a notable exception in the range of noxious cold temperatures. In this study, we investigate the characteristics of ANKTM1, a cold-activated channel with a lower activation temperature compared to the cold and menthol receptor, TRPM8. ANKTM1 is a distant relative of TRP channels with little amino acid similarity to TRPM8. We find that ANKTM1 is expressed in a subset of nociceptive sensory neurons, where it is co-expressed with TRPV1/VR1 (the capsaicin/heat receptor), but not with TRPM8. Consistent with the expression of ANKTM1, we identify noxious cold-sensitive sensory neurons that also respond to capsaicin but not to menthol.

title: Plasma vitamin D metabolites and risk of colorectal cancer in women.
text:
OBJECTIVE:
Evitamin D and its precursor, 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], have shown promise in preventing colorectal cancer through experimental evidence. To investigate this further, we examined the relationship between plasma concentrations of these vitamin D metabolites and colorectal cancer risk in a nested case-control study among women in the Nurses' Health Study.
METHODS: We identified 193 colorectal cancer cases, aged 46-78 years, diagnosed up to 11 years after blood collection. Two controls were matched per case on year of birth and month of blood draw. We calculated odds ratios (OR) using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for factors such as body mass index, physical activity, smoking, family history, hormone replacement therapy use, aspirin use, and dietary intakes.
RESULTS: We found a significant inverse association between plasma 25(OH)D and colorectal cancer risk (P = 0.02). Women in the highest quintile had an OR of 0.53 (95% CI: 0.27-1.04). This association remained strong when limited to women aged 60 years or older at blood collection (P = 0.006) but was not apparent among younger women (P = 0.70). The benefit of higher 25(OH)D concentrations was observed specifically for cancers at the distal colon and rectum (P = 0.02), but not for those at the proximal colon (P = 0.81). In contrast, we did not observe an association between 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and colorectal cancer, although risk was elevated among women in the highest quintile who were also in the lower half of the 25(OH)D distribution (OR = 2.52; 95% CI: 1.04-6.11).
CONCLUSION: Our findings support the hypothesis that higher plasma levels of 25(OH)D are associated with a lower risk of colorectal cancer in older women, particularly for cancers at the distal colon and rectum.
