Our results demonstrate that binding affinity is a critical parameter governing system-wide signaling fidelity for bacterial signal transduction proteins. Specifically, we found that preferential binding affinity is the basis for signaling fidelity in bacterial two-component systems. These findings have important implications for our understanding of bacterial signal transduction and may lead to the development of novel strategies for modulating bacterial signaling pathways.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study provides a system-wide approach to understanding the specificity of HK-RR pairs in M. xanthus. Our findings demonstrate that binding affinity is a critical parameter governing signaling fidelity in bacterial two-component systems and highlight the importance of considering the specificity of protein-protein interactions in the design and development of novel therapeutics.

title: hnRNP A1 associates with telomere ends and stimulates telomerase activity.
text: Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme complex that replicates the telomere's 3' end by reverse-transcribing an RNA template. However, the presence of G-quadruplex structures in the DNA substrate can hinder telomerase's extension. We discovered that hnRNP A1, a protein previously linked to telomere length regulation, binds to both single-stranded and structured human telomeric repeats. In the latter case, it disrupts their higher-order structure. Using an in vitro telomerase assay, we found that depleting hnRNP A/B proteins from 293 human embryonic kidney cell extracts significantly reduced telomerase activity, which was fully restored upon addition of purified recombinant hnRNP A1. This suggests that hnRNP A1 functions as an auxiliary, if not essential, factor in the telomerase holoenzyme. Furthermore, we found through chromatin immunoprecipitation that hnRNP A1 associates with human telomeres in vivo. We propose that hnRNP A1 facilitates telomere elongation by unwinding G-quadruplex or G-G hairpin structures that form at each translocation step.

title: Rapamycin passes the torch: a new generation of mTOR inhibitors
text: Mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) is an unusual protein kinase that regulates growth and metabolism in response to nutrients, growth factors, and cellular energy levels. Dysregulation of mTOR is frequently observed in cancer and metabolic disorders. Rapamycin, an allosteric inhibitor of mTOR, was approved as an immunosuppressant in 1999. Recently, there has been growing interest in its potential as an anticancer drug. However, the performance of rapamycin and its analogues (rapalogues) has been underwhelming despite isolated successes in certain cancer subsets. It is clear that the full therapeutic potential of targeting mTOR remains untapped. A new generation of ATP-competitive inhibitors that directly target the mTOR catalytic site display potent and comprehensive mTOR inhibition and are currently in early clinical trials.

title: Dynamic capsule restructuring by the main pneumococcal autolysin LytA in response to the epithelium
text: Bacterial pathogens produce complex carbohydrate capsules to evade the host's immune system. However, this very capsule can actually make the bacteria more susceptible to antimicrobial peptides found on the surface of epithelial cells. Here, we demonstrate that when pneumococci are exposed to these peptides, they can quickly remove the capsule from the cell surface within minutes through a process mediated by the suicidal amidase enzyme LytA. In contrast to classical bacterial autolysis, during capsule shedding, LytA promotes bacterial survival and is distributed around the cell in a circular pattern. Both autolysis and capsule shedding rely on the enzymatic activity of LytA. Removing the capsule greatly enhances the bacteria's ability to invade epithelial cells, and this process is the primary mechanism by which pneumococci reduce their surface-bound capsule during early acute lung infection in mice. The unexpected role of LytA in removing capsule to counteract antimicrobial peptides may explain why nearly all clinical isolates of pneumococci retain this enzyme despite the lethal selective pressure of antibiotics.

title: The mammalian Scribble polarity protein regulates epithelial cell adhesion and migration through E-cadherin
text: Scrib (Scrib) is a crucial polarity protein in Drosophila melanogaster that plays a vital role in synaptic function, neuroblast differentiation, and epithelial polarity. Additionally, it has been implicated as a tumor suppressor in various studies. In contrast, its role in rodent systems has been primarily associated with receptor recycling and planar polarity, with limited information available on its involvement in apical/basal polarity. Our current findings demonstrate that depletion of Scrib leads to disruptions in adhesion between Madin–Darby canine kidney epithelial cells, resulting in a mesenchymal appearance, increased migration, and loss of directionality. Although the assembly of tight junctions is delayed, confluent monolayers retain their polarity. These effects are distinct from those observed with Rac activation or Scrib binding to βPIX and are instead attributed to Scrib's role in regulating E-cadherin–mediated cell–cell adhesion. Notably, the morphological and migratory changes induced by Scrib depletion are recapitulated in E-cadherin knockdown cells, and partial rescue of adhesion is achieved through expression of an E-cadherin–α-catenin fusion protein. These findings suggest that Scrib stabilizes the interaction between E-cadherin and the catenins, thereby contributing to the maintenance of epithelial cell adhesion and migration, which are crucial for tumor suppression in mammalian systems.

title: Histone acetylation and DNA demethylation of T cells result in an anaplastic large cell lymphoma-like phenotype.
text: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) is characterized by the repression of the T-cell expression program, despite its T-cell origin. The underlying mechanisms for this phenomenon remain unclear. To investigate the role of epigenetic mechanisms in the loss of the T-cell phenotype, we treated ALCL and T-cell lymphoma/leukemia cell lines with epigenetic modifiers to induce DNA demethylation and histone acetylation. Global gene expression analysis revealed that combined treatment with DNA demethylation and histone acetylation was unable to restore the T-cell phenotype in ALCL cells. Instead, the treatment led to the up-regulation of ALCL-specific genes, such as ID2, LGALS1, and c-JUN, and a near complete loss of the T-cell phenotype, including CD3, LCK, and ZAP70. Furthermore, we found that histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) was suppressed in ALCL cells, which is consistent with its absence in primary tumor samples as demonstrated by immunohistochemistry. Our findings suggest that epigenetically activated suppressors, such as ID2, contribute to the down-regulation of the T-cell expression program in ALCL, which is maintained by H3K27me3.

title: YEASTRACT: providing a programmatic access to curated transcriptional regulatory associations in Saccharomyces cerevisiae through a web services interface
text: The YEASTRACT database (<http://www.yeastract.com>) was created to support the analysis of transcriptional regulation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Last updated in June 2010, the database contains over 48,200 regulatory associations between transcription factors (TFs) and target genes, including 298 specific DNA-binding sites for 110 characterized TFs. To enhance the database, the developers revisited and added detailed information on the experimental evidence supporting these associations, categorizing them as direct or indirect. This update allows users to restrict their queries to associations with experimental evidence for the direct action of TFs in the promoter region of their target genes. Additionally, the database is now accessible through a machine-readable web service interface, providing users with greater flexibility in querying, retrieving, and exploiting the data. To further facilitate the use of the curated data, several computational tools have been developed. Since its launch in 2006, YEASTRACT has been widely used by researchers worldwide, and we anticipate that the new data and services will continue to support yeast biologists and systems biology researchers in their work.

title: Mechanisms that Specify Promoter Nucleosome Location and Identity
text: The chromatin structure of eukaryotic gene promoters is typically characterized by a region without nucleosomes (NFR) flanked by at least one H2A.Z variant nucleosome. However, computational predictions of nucleosome positions based on the thermodynamic properties of DNA-histone interactions have had limited success. Here, we demonstrate that the action of the essential RSC remodeling complex in S. cerevisiae helps explain the discrepancy between theory and experiment. In RSC-depleted cells, NFRs shrink, causing the average positions of flanking nucleosomes to move towards predicted sites. Additionally, the essential Myb family proteins Abf1 and Reb1, whose binding sites are enriched in NFRs, are required for nucleosome positioning at distinct subsets of promoters. In contrast, H2A.Z deposition is dispensable for nucleosome positioning. By regulating H2A.Z deposition using a steroid-inducible protein splicing strategy, we show that NFR establishment is necessary for H2A.Z deposition. These findings suggest a sequential pathway for the assembly of promoter chromatin architecture.

title: HIV seropositivity and tuberculosis in a large general hospital in Malawi.
text: The prevalence of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) in Malawi is significantly higher in Central Africa. Since tuberculosis (TB) is an initial manifestation of the disease, consecutive patients admitted to the TB wards of Zomba General Hospital, Malawi, were asked for permission to undergo an HIV antibodies test. Two additional studies were conducted: all medical in-patients clinically suspected of immune deficiency from September 1986 and all blood donors from April 1988 were tested for HIV seropositivity. Of the TB patients who volunteered, 26% were seropositive. In the high-risk age groups (20-40 years), this percentage increased to 32%. The seropositivity among medical in-patients suspected of immune deficiency rose significantly from April 1987 to October 1988. Finally, among blood donors tested, 20% were seropositive.

title: Determinants of neonatal mortality in Indonesia
text:
In Indonesia, neonatal mortality accounts for approximately 40% of under-five child mortality. To identify the determinants of neonatal mortality and inform evidence-based interventions, this study analyzed data from a nationally representative sample of births in Indonesia between 1997 and 2002.
The study found that neonatal mortality rates varied significantly across different communities in Indonesia. Infants born in East Java had significantly higher odds of neonatal death compared to the lowest mortality regions, while infants born in North, Central, and Southeast Sulawesi and Gorontalo combined also had higher odds of neonatal death.
The study also found that various individual and household-level factors were associated with neonatal mortality. For example, infants born to mothers and fathers who were employed had higher odds of neonatal death, while infants born to unemployed fathers had lower odds. Similarly, infants born to mothers with a history of delivery complications had higher odds of neonatal death, while infants born to mothers who had received postnatal care were significantly protected from neonatal death.
The study's findings suggest that public health interventions in Indonesia should address community, household, and individual-level factors that influence neonatal mortality. These interventions should include strategies to improve access to skilled birth attendance and postnatal care, particularly in areas with high neonatal mortality rates. Additionally, the study highlights the importance of addressing low birth weight and short birth interval infants, as well as perinatal health services factors in reducing neonatal mortality in Indonesia.

title: High density mapping of the MHC identifies a shared role for HLA-DRB1*01:03 in inflammatory bowel diseases and heterozygous advantage in ulcerative colitis
text: Genome-wide association studies of related inflammatory bowel diseases, such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, have revealed strong evidence of association with the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). This region encodes numerous immune-related genes, including classical HLA molecules. Previous studies in IBD have identified multiple associations at both HLA and non-HLA genes, but lacked the statistical power to fully understand the genetic architecture of these diseases. To address this limitation, we performed high-density SNP typing of the MHC in over 32,000 IBD individuals, implicating multiple HLA alleles, with a primary role for HLA-DRB1*01:03 in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Interestingly, differences were observed between these diseases, such as a predominant role for class II HLA variants and a heterozygous advantage in ulcerative colitis, suggesting an important adaptive immune response in the colonic environment in the pathogenesis of IBD.

title: High-Threshold Mechanosensitive Ion Channels Blocked by a Novel Conopeptide Mediate Pressure-Evoked Pain
text: Little is known about the molecular mechanisms underlying somatosensory mechanotransduction in mammals. To address this gap in knowledge, we screened a library of peptide toxins for their effects on mechanically activated currents in cultured dorsal root ganglion neurons. One conopeptide analogue, termed NMB-1, stood out for its selective inhibition of sustained mechanically activated currents in a subset of sensory neurons. Biotinylated NMB-1 retained its activity and selectively bound to peripherin-positive nociceptive sensory neurons. Unlike NMB-1, the tarantula toxin GsMTx-4, which inhibits stretch-activated ion channels, had no effects on mechanically activated currents in sensory neurons. In behavioral assays, NMB-1 only inhibited responses to high intensity, painful mechanical stimulation, with no effects on low intensity mechanical stimulation or thermosensation. Surprisingly, NMB-1 was also found to be an inhibitor of rapid FM1-43 loading (a measure of mechanotransduction) in cochlear hair cells. These findings demonstrate that distinct channels respond to different types of mechanical stimuli and suggest that mechanically activated sustained currents underlie noxious mechanosensation. NMB-1 thus provides a novel diagnostic tool for identifying the molecular channels involved in hearing and pressure-evoked pain.

title: Hyperactive Neuroendocrine Secretion Causes Size, Feeding, and Metabolic Defects of C. elegans Bardet-Biedl Syndrome Mutants
text:
Bardet-Biedl Syndrome (BBS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a range of clinical manifestations, including polydactyly, retinopathy, hyperphagia, obesity, short stature, cognitive impairment, and developmental delays. The disorder is caused by disruptions in the BBS proteins, which are essential for cilia formation and function. In various organisms, including the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans, BBS proteins are expressed in ciliated sensory neurons and play a critical role in regulating cilia-associated signaling pathways.
In contrast to other cilia-defective mutants, C. elegans bbs mutants exhibit unique phenotypes, including increased release of dense-core vesicles and altered body size, feeding, and metabolic abnormalities. These findings suggest that BBS proteins also regulate dense-core vesicle exocytosis, and that some features of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome may be caused by excessive neuroendocrine secretion.
In this study, we show that abrogating the enhanced secretion of dense-core vesicles in bbs mutants can correct some of their organism-wide phenotypes, including body size, feeding, and metabolic abnormalities, without correcting their ciliary defects. These findings expand the role of BBS proteins and suggest that some features of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome may be caused by excessive neuroendocrine secretion.

title: Fiji: an open-source platform for biological-image analysis
text: Fiji is a specialized distribution of the widely-used open-source software ImageJ, tailored towards biological image analysis. By leveraging modern software engineering techniques, Fiji seamlessly integrates cutting-edge software libraries with an array of scripting languages, enabling lightning-fast prototyping of image processing algorithms. This allows developers to quickly turn innovative ideas into functional ImageJ plugins that can be easily shared with end users through an in-built update system. We propose Fiji as a powerful platform for fostering collaborative efforts between computer science and biology researchers.

title: Pharmacologic characterization of a potent inhibitor of class I phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases.
text:
Extensive evidence suggests that activation of the lipid phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway plays a key role in the development and progression of various types of cancer. As a result, PI3K inhibitors have significant potential as cancer therapies. Here, we provide details on the pharmacological properties of a prototype compound from a new series of class I PI3K inhibitors, PI103.
PI103 is a potent inhibitor with low micromolar IC50 values against recombinant PI3K isoforms p110α (2 nmol/L), p110β (3 nmol/L), p110δ (3 nmol/L), and p110γ (15 nmol/L). It also inhibited the TORC1 protein kinase by 83.9% at 0.5 micromol/L and showed an IC50 value of 14 nmol/L against DNA-PK. Notably, PI103 displayed a high degree of selectivity for the PI3K family, with no activity against a panel of 70 other protein kinases.
In vitro, PI103 potently inhibited the proliferation and invasion of a wide range of human cancer cell lines. Additionally, it modulated biomarkers consistent with inhibition of PI3K signaling. In vivo, PI103 was rapidly distributed to tissues and tumors, leading to tumor growth delay in eight different human cancer xenograft models with various PI3K pathway abnormalities. Decreased phosphorylation of AKT was observed in U87MG gliomas, consistent with drug levels achieved. Furthermore, PI103 inhibited invasion in orthotopic breast and ovarian cancer xenograft models, and showed anti-angiogenic activity. Despite its rapid in vivo metabolism, PI103 is a valuable tool compound for exploring the biological function of class I PI3K and represents a lead for further optimization of this novel class of targeted molecular cancer therapeutics.

title: Optimized CRISPR/Cas tools for efficient germline and somatic genome engineering in Drosophila.
text: The recently developed type II CRISPR/Cas system has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating the genomes of various organisms. In this study, we present a toolbox for high-efficiency genome engineering of Drosophila melanogaster, consisting of transgenic Cas9 lines and versatile guide RNA (gRNA) expression plasmids. Through systematic evaluation, we identify Cas9 lines with either ubiquitous or germ-line-restricted patterns of activity. We also demonstrate that different U6 snRNA promoters can result in differential activity of the same gRNA, with the U6:3 promoter exhibiting the most potent effect. By combining Cas9 and gRNA, we are able to target both essential and nonessential genes with transmission rates ranging from 25-100%. Additionally, we demonstrate that our optimized CRISPR/Cas tools can be used for offset nicking-based mutagenesis, and that they allow for precise genome editing through homology-directed repair with rates that make selection markers unnecessary. Finally, we show a novel application of CRISPR/Cas-mediated technology in revealing loss-of-function phenotypes in somatic cells following efficient biallelic targeting by Cas9 expressed in a ubiquitous or tissue-restricted manner. Our CRISPR/Cas tools will facilitate the rapid evaluation of mutant phenotypes of specific genes and the precise modification of the genome with single-nucleotide precision. Our results also pave the way for high-throughput genetic screening with CRISPR/Cas.

title: Cost-effectiveness of 10-Year Risk Thresholds for Initiation of Statin Therapy for Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease.
text:
The American College of Cardiology and American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines for cholesterol treatment have significant implications for treating adults without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) with statins. To assess the cost-effectiveness of different 10-year ASCVD risk thresholds, we developed a microsimulation model using a US societal perspective, 3% discount rate, and lifetime time horizon.
Our results indicate that the current 10-year ASCVD risk threshold of 7.5% or higher (which is associated with 48% of adults treated with statins) has an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of $37,000/quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained. More lenient thresholds of 4.0% or higher (61% of adults treated) and 3.0% or higher (67% of adults treated) have ICERs of $81,000/QALY and $140,000/QALY, respectively. Shifting from a 7.5% or higher threshold to a 3.0% or higher threshold would be associated with an additional 161,560 cardiovascular disease events averted.
Our findings were sensitive to changes in patient preferences, statin price, and the risk of statin-induced diabetes. Using a cost-effectiveness threshold of $100,000/QALY, there was a higher than 93% chance that the optimal ASCVD threshold was 5.0% or lower.
In conclusion, the current 10-year ASCVD risk threshold used in the ACC/AHA guidelines has an acceptable cost-effectiveness profile, but more lenient thresholds would be optimal. The optimal threshold was sensitive to patient preferences and other factors.

title: Biochemical Properties of Highly Neuroinvasive Prion Strains
text: Prions, infectious proteins, propagate from peripheral entry points into the central nervous system (CNS), leading to progressive neurodegeneration and ultimately death. However, the pathogenesis of prion diseases can vary significantly depending on the strain, or conformational variant of the aberrantly folded and aggregated protein, PrP(Sc). While most prion strains invade the CNS, some strains fail to gain entry and do not cause clinical symptoms of disease. The basis for this remarkable variation in pathogenesis among strains remains unclear. Using mouse-adapted prion strains, we demonstrate that highly neuroinvasive prion strains primarily form diffuse aggregates in the brain, are non-congophilic, conformationally unstable in denaturing conditions, and lead to rapidly lethal disease. These neuroinvasive strains efficiently generate PrP(Sc) over short incubation periods. In contrast, weakly neuroinvasive prion strains form large fibrillary plaques and are stable, congophilic, and inefficiently generate PrP(Sc) over long incubation periods. Our findings suggest that the most neuroinvasive prion strains are also the least stable, supporting the idea that the efficient replication and unstable nature of the most rapidly converting prions may be linked to their efficient spread into the CNS.

title: The twin-arginine translocation (Tat) protein export pathway
text: The twin-arginine translocation (Tat) protein export system is prevalent in the cytoplasmic membranes of most bacteria and archaea, boasting the unique ability to transport fully formed proteins across the membrane. To achieve this, the system must create a transmembrane pathway of sufficient size to accommodate diverse, structured macromolecular substrates while maintaining the impermeability of the membrane to ions. In the Gram-negative bacterium Escherichia coli, this challenging task is accomplished using just three small membrane proteins: TatA, TatB, and TatC. This Review provides an overview of recent advances in our understanding of how this remarkable machine functions.

title: New developments in the ATSAS program package for small-angle scattering data analysis
text:
New advancements have been made in the program package ATSAS (version 2.4) for the processing and analysis of isotropic small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering data. These developments include:
1. Multi-platform data manipulation and display tools, enabling users to access and visualize data from various sources and platforms.
2. Automated data processing and calculation of key parameters, streamlining the analysis process and improving accuracy.
3. Enhanced usage of high- and low-resolution models from other structural methods, allowing for more comprehensive structural analysis.
4. Novel algorithms for constructing three-dimensional models from weakly interacting oligomeric systems and complexes, providing improved accuracy and resolution.
5. Enhanced tools for analyzing data from mixtures and flexible systems, facilitating the analysis of complex systems and improving the accuracy of results.
The new ATSAS release includes installers for major platforms (Windows, Linux, and Mac OSX) and provides updated and improved user documentation. Additionally, web-related developments, such as a user discussion forum and expanded online access to run ATSAS programs, are also presented.

title: The First Myriapod Genome Sequence Reveals Conservative Arthropod Gene Content and Genome Organisation in the Centipede Strigamia maritima
text: Myriapods, such as centipedes and millipedes, exhibit a simple homonomous body plan relative to other arthropods. While all members of the class are terrestrial, they achieved terrestriality independently of insects. Notably, the class Myriapoda is the only arthropod group without a sequenced genome. To address this gap, we conducted an analysis of the genome of the centipede Strigamia maritima. Our study reveals a compact genome that has undergone less gene loss and rearrangement compared to previously sequenced arthropods, and retains many orthologous genes from the bilaterian ancestor that have been lost in insects. We identify numerous genes located in conserved macro-synteny contexts, as well as small-scale examples of gene clustering. Furthermore, we observe several instances where S. maritima has evolved unique solutions to problems encountered by insects, such as the absence of an olfactory receptor gene family and the use of alternative splicing mechanisms to generate coding sequence diversity. Interestingly, the lack of photosensory proteins in S. maritima is linked to the absence of canonical circadian clock genes. The phylogenetic position of myriapods allows us to infer the origin of various molecular mechanisms and traits in arthropod evolution. For example, we propose that juvenile hormone signaling evolved alongside the emergence of the exoskeleton in arthropods, and that RR-1 containing cuticle proteins evolved in the lineage leading to Mandibulata. Additionally, we identify specific times and mechanisms of gene expansions and losses throughout arthropod evolution. The genome of S. maritima provides a unique window into the ancestral arthropod genome, while also showcasing adaptations tailored to its distinct life history.

title: Genetic and Functional Diversification of Small RNA Pathways in Plants
text:
Multicellular eukaryotes, including plants, produce small RNA molecules (approximately 21-24 nucleotides) of two main types: microRNA (miRNA) and short interfering RNA (siRNA). These small RNAs function as sequence-specific guides to regulate or silence genes, transposons, viruses, and chromatin structure. The formation or activity of small RNAs requires factors from gene families that encode DICER (or DICER-LIKE [DCL]) and ARGONAUTE proteins, as well as, in some cases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RDR) proteins. Unlike animals, plants have multiple DCL and RDR proteins.
Using a series of insertion mutants of Arabidopsis thaliana, unique functions for three DCL proteins in miRNA (DCL1), endogenous siRNA (DCL3), and viral siRNA (DCL2) biogenesis were identified. One RDR protein (RDR2) was required for all endogenous siRNAs analyzed. The loss of endogenous siRNA in dcl3 and rdr2 mutants was associated with the loss of heterochromatic marks and increased transcript accumulation at some loci. Defects in siRNA-generation activity in response to turnip crinkle virus in dcl2 mutant plants correlated with increased virus susceptibility.
Our findings suggest that the proliferation and diversification of DCL and RDR genes in plants during evolution contributed to the specialization of small RNA-directed pathways for development, chromatin structure, and defense.

title: Immunosuppressant FTY720 inhibits thymocyte emigration.
text: The thymus plays a crucial role in providing mature T cells to the peripheral immune system, but the mechanisms underlying T cell export from the thymus are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the effect of a novel immunosuppressive agent, FTY720, on T cell export from the thymus. We found that daily administration of FTY720 at a dose of 1 mg/kg resulted in a significant decrease in the number of peripheral T lymphocytes. In contrast, long-term daily administration of FTY720 in the thymus led to a three- to fourfold increase in the proportion of mature medullary thymocytes (CD4+CD8- and CD4-CD8+) and a slight decrease in the double-positive cell ratio (CD4+CD8+). Phenotypic analysis revealed that these increased subsets represent possible recent thymic emigrants, and high levels of L-selectin expression on these cells suggest that they were prevented from leaving the thymus. Intrathymic labeling with fluorescein isothiocyanate revealed that only one-fourth of labeled cells could be detected in the lymph nodes and spleen of FTY720-treated mice compared to control mice. These results suggest that the immunosuppressive action of FTY720, at least in part, may be due to its inhibitory effect on T cell emigration from the thymus to the periphery.

title: Validating a conceptual model for an inter-professional approach to shared decision making: a mixed methods study
text:
RATIONALE:
In recent years, there has been growing interest in the use of inter-professional (IP) healthcare teams to engage patients in decision-making processes. To address this, we developed a conceptual model for an IP approach to shared decision making (SDM) in primary care. This model was validated with stakeholders in Canada.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES:
Our aim was to assess the validity of the IP-SDM model with stakeholders in Canada. Specifically, we sought to:
1. Identify changes that stakeholders would propose to the IP-SDM model;
2. Determine barriers and facilitators to the model's implementation in clinical practice; and
3. Evaluate the model using a theory appraisal questionnaire.
METHODS:
We conducted 15 individual interviews and 7 group interviews with 79 stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, patients, and family members. Participants were asked to provide feedback on the IP-SDM model, including suggestions for changes, barriers to implementation, and facilitators of successful implementation. We analyzed the transcripts thematically and descriptively analyzed the questionnaires.
RESULTS:
Stakeholders emphasized the importance of placing the patient at the center of the model and expanding the concept of family to include significant others. They also highlighted the need to clarify outcomes, emphasize the concept of time, and integrate the micro, meso, and macro levels into a single model. The most common barriers identified were time constraints, insufficient resources, and an imbalance of power among healthcare professionals. The most common facilitators were education and training in inter-professionalism and SDM, motivation to achieve an IP approach to SDM, and mutual knowledge and understanding of disciplinary roles. The majority of stakeholders found the concepts and relationships between them to be clear and logical, and considered the model to be relevant to inter-professional collaboration, SDM, and primary care.
CONCLUSIONS:
Stakeholders validated the IP-SDM model for primary care settings and proposed few modifications. Future research should assess the model's effectiveness in implementing SDM in IP clinical practice.

title: Glutaminolysis activates Rag-mTORC1 signaling.
text:
Amino acids, specifically glutamine, play a crucial role in controlling cell growth by activating the highly conserved kinase TORC1. Glutamine is a key player in cell growth regulation and metabolism, but its exact mechanism of action in TORC1 activation remains unclear. Glutamine is metabolized through glutaminolysis to produce α-ketoglutarate, which is a critical intermediate in cellular metabolism.
Our findings demonstrate that glutamine, in combination with leucine, activates mammalian TORC1 (mTORC1) by enhancing glutaminolysis and α-ketoglutarate production. Inhibition of glutaminolysis, on the other hand, prevents the loading of RagB and lysosomal translocation, ultimately leading to the suppression of mTORC1 activity. Interestingly, constitutively active Rag heterodimers can also activate mTORC1 in the absence of glutaminolysis. Conversely, enhanced glutaminolysis or exposure to a cell-permeable α-ketoglutarate analog leads to increased lysosomal translocation and activation of mTORC1.
Furthermore, our study reveals that glutaminolysis regulates not only mTORC1 activity but also cell growth and autophagy, two processes that are tightly linked to mTORC1 function. These findings suggest that glutamine and leucine activate mTORC1 via glutaminolysis and α-ketoglutarate production upstream of Rag, which may provide an explanation for the addiction of cancer cells to glutamine.
In summary, our research uncovers the molecular mechanism by which glutamine and leucine control cell growth through the activation of TORC1. By elucidating the role of glutaminolysis in this process, our findings provide new insights into the regulation of cellular metabolism and its impact on cell growth and autophagy.

title: microRNA-31/factor-inhibiting hypoxia-inducible factor 1 nexus regulates keratinocyte differentiation.
text:
Notch plays a crucial role in the transition from cell proliferation to differentiation in the epidermis and corneal epithelium. Dysregulation of Notch signaling has been implicated in various skin diseases, including psoriasis, eczema, non-melanoma skin cancer, and melanoma, where differentiation and proliferation are disrupted. While much is known about the downstream effects of Notch signaling, the factors that regulate Notch receptor signaling after ligand activation are not fully understood. Notch can undergo hydroxylation by factor-inhibiting hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (FIH-1), but the biological significance of this process is unclear.
Our study reveals that FIH-1 expression is upregulated in diseased epidermis and corneal epithelium. Elevating FIH-1 levels in primary human epidermal keratinocytes (HEKs) and human corneal epithelial keratinocytes (HCEKs) impairs differentiation in both submerged cultures and a three-dimensional organotypic raft model of human epidermis, in part, by reducing Notch signaling. Conversely, knockdown of FIH-1 enhances keratinocyte differentiation. In vivo, loss of FIH-1 leads to increased Notch activity in the limbal epithelium, resulting in a more differentiated phenotype.
We also identify microRNA-31 (miR-31) as an endogenous regulator of FIH-1 expression that promotes keratinocyte differentiation by Notch activation. Ectopic expression of miR-31 in an undifferentiated corneal epithelial cell line leads to differentiation and recapitulates a corneal epithelium in a three-dimensional raft culture model. Our findings establish a novel mechanism for keratinocyte fate decisions, where Notch signaling potential is partially controlled through a miR-31/FIH-1 axis.

title: Advantages of larval control for African malaria vectors: Low mobility and behavioural responsiveness of immature mosquito stages allow high effective coverage
text:
Based on sensitivity analyses of the MacDonald-Ross model, it has been suggested that targeting adult female mosquitoes with insecticides is the most effective way to reduce malaria transmission. However, these analyses have overlooked a crucial biological difference between mosquito adults and their immature stages: adults are highly mobile flying insects that can easily evade intervention measures, while mosquito eggs, larvae, and pupae are confined to small aquatic habitats and cannot escape control measures. We hypothesize that targeting adult mosquitoes may be less effective due to their ability to avoid interventions, such as excito-repellent insecticides.
To test this hypothesis, we developed a simple model of intervention avoidance by mosquitoes and demonstrated that it can significantly reduce the proportion of the vector population covered by control measures and overall impact on malaria transmission. We also reviewed historical evidence showing that larval control of African malaria vectors can be effective, and found that the only limitations to its effectiveness are practical rather than fundamental. Therefore, we conclude that larval control strategies against malaria vectors in sub-Saharan Africa have the potential to be highly effective, complementary to adult control interventions, and should be prioritized for further development, evaluation, and implementation as an integral part of the Rolling Back Malaria initiative.

title: The Arabidopsis Chromatin-Modifying Nuclear siRNA Pathway Involves a Nucleolar RNA Processing Center
text: In the plant species Arabidopsis thaliana, small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) direct the cytosine methylation of endogenous DNA repeats through a complex pathway involving two forms of nuclear RNA polymerase IV (Pol IVa and Pol IVb), RNA-dependent RNA polymerase 2 (RDR2), DICER-LIKE 3 (DCL3), ARGONAUTE4 (AGO4), a chromatin remodeler called DRD1, and the de novo cytosine methyltransferase DRM2. We found that RDR2, DCL3, AGO4, and the largest subunit of Pol IVb (NRPD1b) colocalize with siRNAs within the nucleolus, while Pol IVa and DRD1 are located outside of the nucleolus and interact with endogenous repeat sequences. When we disrupted the pathway proteins, their downstream partners mislocalized, revealing their order of action. Our data suggest that Pol IVa acts first, and its localization is RNA-dependent, implying the presence of an RNA template. Based on these findings, we propose that the maintenance of the heterochromatic state in Arabidopsis involves the transcription of Pol IVa-specific genes, followed by the production and assembly of AGO4- and NRPD1b-containing silencing complexes within nucleolar processing centers.

title: Peripheral arterial disease in the elderly: The Rotterdam Study.
text: To determine the age- and sex-specific prevalence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and intermittent claudication (IC) in an elderly population, we conducted a population-based study among 7715 subjects (40% men, 60% women) aged 55 years and older. We measured the ankle-arm systolic blood pressure index (AAI) to diagnose PAD and used the World Health Organization/Rose questionnaire to diagnose IC. PAD was defined as an AAI of <0.90 in either leg. The prevalence of PAD was 19.1% (95% CI: 18.1%-20.0%), with higher rates among men (16.9%) than women (20.5%). Approximately 1.6% of the study population (2.2% among men, 1.2% among women) reported symptoms of IC. Among those with PAD, 6.3% experienced symptoms of IC (8.7% among men, 4.9% among women), while in 68.9% of those with IC, an AAI of <0.90 was found. Subjects with an AAI <0.90 were more likely to be smokers, have hypertension, and have symptomatic or asymptomatic cardiovascular disease compared to those with an AAI of 0.90 or higher. The authors conclude that the prevalence of PAD in the elderly is high, while the prevalence of IC is relatively low, although both prevalences increase with advancing age. The majority of PAD patients experience no symptoms of IC.

title: Antioxidants attenuate the plasma cytokine response to exercise in humans.
text: Exercise causes an increase in plasma levels of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6, but the specific stimuli and sources of these cytokines remain largely unknown. To investigate the role of oxidative stress and the potential contribution of monocytes in this cytokine response, we conducted a study on six healthy non-athletes who performed two 45-min bicycle exercise sessions at 70% of their maximum oxygen uptake (Vo(2 max)) before and after taking antioxidants (vitamins E, A, and C for 60 days; allopurinol for 15 days; and N-acetylcysteine for 3 days). Blood samples were collected at baseline, immediately after exercise, and 30 and 120 minutes later. We measured plasma cytokine levels using ELISA and monocyte intracellular cytokine levels using flow cytometry. Before taking the antioxidants, exercise caused a 60% increase in TNF-alpha, a threefold increase in IL-1beta, and a sixfold increase in IL-6 compared to baseline (P < 0.05). After taking the antioxidants, plasma IL-1beta became undetectable, the TNF-alpha response to exercise was abolished, and the IL-6 response was significantly blunted (P < 0.05). Exercise did not increase the percentage of monocytes producing these cytokines or their mean fluorescence intensity. Our findings suggest that in untrained humans, oxidative stress is the major stimulus for exercise-induced cytokine production, and monocytes play no role in this process.

title: Relation between colonic proglucagon expression and metabolic response to oligofructose in high fat diet-fed mice.
text: Several studies suggest that fermentable dietary fiber, specifically short chain fructo-oligosaccharide (OFS), may play a role in controlling obesity and associated metabolic disorders. To investigate this further, we conducted a study in mice fed a standard diet and two distinct high-fat diets that induce metabolic disorders associated with obesity. Our findings confirm previous results in rats fed a standard diet enriched with OFS, including increased total and empty caecum weight, decreased epididymal fat mass, and increased colonic and portal plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels. Interestingly, when OFS was added to the two different high-fat diets, it had different effects on energy intake, body weight gain, glycemia, and epididymal fat mass. Specifically, OFS decreased these parameters only when added to the high-fat-carbohydrate-free diet, where it promoted colonic proglucagon expression and insulin secretion. Our results suggest an association between increased proglucagon expression in the proximal colon and OFS's effects on glycemia, fat mass development, and/or body weight gain. Overall, our findings support the idea that dietary oligosaccharides, such as OFS, may constitute an interesting class of dietary fibers that promote endogenous GLP-1 production, leading to beneficial physiological consequences. However, further human studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Aurora B phosphorylates spatially distinct targets to differentially regulate the kinetochore-microtubule interface.
text: Chromosome segregation during cell division relies on the precise regulation of interactions between kinetochores and microtubules. However, the mechanisms by which plasticity is achieved to correct diverse attachment defects remain unclear. In this study, we investigate the role of Aurora B kinase in regulating kinetochore-microtubule attachments. We demonstrate that Aurora B phosphorylates three distinct targets within the conserved outer kinetochore KNL1/Mis12 complex/Ndc80 complex network (KMN), which plays a crucial role in kinetochore-microtubule attachments. The combinatorial phosphorylation of the KMN network generates graded levels of microtubule-binding activity, with full phosphorylation significantly impairing microtubule binding. Notably, the spatial distribution of these targets along the kinetochore axis leads to their differential phosphorylation in response to changes in tension and attachment state. Our findings suggest a mechanism for the tension-dependent fine-tuning of kinetochore-microtubule interactions, rather than generating exclusively binary changes in microtubule binding.

title: Prognostic importance of 6-mercaptopurine dose intensity in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text:
In this study, the authors investigated the prognostic value of various factors, including dose intensity of oral 6-mercaptopurine (6MP) and methotrexate, in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treated with a continuation therapy protocol. The study included 182 children who achieved remission and received weekly methotrexate 40 mg/m2 parenterally and daily oral 6MP, interrupted every 6 weeks during the first year by pulse chemotherapy. The authors measured the levels of methotrexate polyglutamates (MTXPGs) and thioguanine nucleotides (TGNs) in the red blood cells (RBCs) of these children and analyzed the relationship between these levels and event-free survival (EFS).
The results showed that higher dose intensity of oral 6MP and weekly methotrexate were significant predictors of overall EFS in univariate analysis. In multivariate analysis, only higher dose intensity of oral 6MP remained a significant predictor of EFS, with lower thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) activity tending to associate with better outcome. Additionally, the authors found that dose intensity of oral 6MP was associated with EFS among children with a homozygous wild-type TPMT phenotype. However, increasing the intensity of therapy to the point where neutropenia precludes chemotherapy administration may be counterproductive.
In conclusion, the study suggests that increased dose intensity of oral 6MP is an important determinant of EFS in ALL, particularly among children with a homozygous wild-type TPMT phenotype. However, it is crucial to balance the dose intensity of therapy with the risk of neutropenia to ensure optimal treatment outcomes.

title: Orai1 and STIM1 are critical for breast tumor cell migration and metastasis.
text: Tumor metastasis is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, and uncovering the molecular mechanisms underlying this process is crucial for the development of effective cancer therapies. By investigating the underlying molecular mechanisms, we may identify potential drug targets that can be targeted to prevent or slow down tumor metastasis. In this study, we investigate the role of Orai1 and STIM1, two proteins involved in store-operated calcium entry, in breast tumor cell migration and metastasis. Our findings demonstrate that these proteins are essential for breast tumor cell migration in vitro and tumor metastasis in vivo. Moreover, we show that inhibition of Orai1 or STIM1 using RNA interference or pharmacological inhibitors of store-operated calcium channels leads to a decrease in tumor metastasis in animal models. These results suggest that targeting store-operated calcium entry channels may be a promising strategy for cancer therapy, particularly in highly metastatic human breast cancer cells.

title: Mouse Spermatogenic Stem Cells Continually Interconvert between Equipotent Singly Isolated and Syncytial States
text: The identity and behavior of mouse spermatogenic stem cells have been a long-standing area of interest. In the traditional view, stem cell function is believed to be restricted to a small population of isolated (As) spermatogonia. However, by examining the single-cell dynamics of GFRα1+ stem cells in vivo using live imaging and pulse labeling, we challenge this prevailing hypothesis and propose an alternative model. Our findings show that, through fragmentation, syncytial spermatogonia also contribute to stem cell function in homeostasis. We demonstrate that the entire GFRα1+ population comprises a single stem cell pool, in which cells continually interconvert between As and syncytial states. By developing a minimal biophysical model that only relies on the rates of incomplete cell division and syncytial fragmentation, we are able to precisely predict the stochastic fates of GFRα1+ cells during steady-state spermatogenesis and postinsult regeneration. Our results provide a new and dynamic understanding of spermatogenic stem cell function in the mouse testis.

title: Pseudoknots: RNA Structures with Diverse Functions
text: RNA molecules perform a wide range of functions within cells, including transferring genetic information from DNA to protein and catalyzing chemical reactions. These simple linear molecules can form complex three-dimensional structures, with certain structures being commonly adopted by RNA molecules. One such structure is the pseudoknot, which is composed of two helical segments connected by single-stranded regions or loops. The H-type fold of the pseudoknot involves the bases in the loop forming intramolecular pairs with bases outside of the stem, resulting in a second stem and loop. This creates a quasi-continuous helix with one continuous and one discontinuous strand. The single-stranded loop regions often interact with the adjacent stems, forming hydrogen bonds and contributing to the overall structure of the molecule. Pseudoknots are structurally diverse and play a variety of roles in biology, including forming the catalytic core of ribozymes, self-splicing introns, and telomerase. They also play critical roles in altering gene expression by inducing ribosomal frameshifting in many viruses.

title: An essential role for interferon gamma in resistance to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection
text: Tuberculosis, a significant health concern in developing countries, has resurfaced in recent years in many industrialized nations. The heightened susceptibility of immunocompromised individuals to tuberculosis has been demonstrated through numerous experimental studies, which highlight the crucial role of T cell-mediated immunity in resistance. Interferon gamma (IFN-gamma), a key lymphokine, is believed to play a pivotal role in macrophage activation and resistance to intracellular pathogens. To investigate the role of IFN-gamma in tuberculosis, mice have been generated that lack the gene for IFN-gamma (gko). These mice fail to produce IFN-gamma upon infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, resulting in impaired production of reactive nitrogen intermediates and inability to restrict bacillary growth. In contrast to control mice, gko mice exhibit exacerbated tissue necrosis and succumb to a rapid and fatal course of tuberculosis that can be delayed, but not prevented, by administration of exogenous recombinant IFN-gamma.

title: Malignancies, prothrombotic mutations, and the risk of venous thrombosis.
text: In this study, we aimed to identify individuals with cancer who are at an increased risk of developing venous thrombosis. We analyzed data from 3220 patients with cancer and 2131 control participants without cancer, all of whom were recruited from anticoagulation clinics in the Netherlands. We found that patients with cancer had a significantly higher risk of venous thrombosis compared to controls, with an odds ratio of 6.7. The risk was highest in patients with hematological malignancies, followed by lung cancer and gastrointestinal cancer. Additionally, we found that patients with cancer who had distant metastases had a higher risk of venous thrombosis compared to those without distant metastases. Carriers of the factor V Leiden mutation who also had cancer had a 12-fold increased risk of venous thrombosis compared to individuals without cancer and factor V Leiden. Similar results were observed for the prothrombin 20210A mutation in patients with cancer. These findings suggest that patients with cancer are at a high risk of venous thrombosis, particularly in the first few months after diagnosis and in the presence of distant metastases. Carriers of prothrombotic mutations may also be at an increased risk.

title: The Hippo signaling pathway restricts the oncogenic potential of an intestinal regeneration program.
text: Although the role of Hippo signaling in organ size control is well established, the mechanisms underlying its involvement in tissue regeneration are largely unexplored. To address this gap in knowledge, we employed a colonic regeneration model induced by dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) and investigated the involvement of Yes-associated protein (YAP) in this process. Our findings reveal that regenerating crypts exhibit elevated YAP levels. Inactivation of YAP has no observable defects under normal homeostasis but significantly impairs DSS-induced intestinal regeneration. Conversely, overactivation of YAP leads to widespread early-onset polyp formation following DSS treatment. These findings underscore the critical role of YAP in tissue regeneration, requiring precise control to balance compensatory proliferation and prevent the intrinsic oncogenic potential of the regenerating tissue.

title: The essence of SNPs.
text:
Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are a common form of genetic variation, distinguished from rarer variations by the requirement that the least abundant allele have a frequency of at least 1%. The study and use of SNPs have the potential to greatly benefit a wide range of genetic disciplines. The recent surge of interest in SNPs can be attributed to the convergence and maturation of several research areas, including:
1. Large-scale genome analysis and related technologies, which have enabled the high-throughput detection and characterization of SNPs.
2. Bio-informatics and computing, which have facilitated the analysis and interpretation of the vast amounts of data generated by genome-wide SNP studies.
3. Genetic analysis of simple and complex disease states, which have revealed the importance of SNPs in disease susceptibility and progression.
4. Global human population genetics, which has provided insights into the distribution and evolution of SNPs across different populations.
As the number of known SNPs continues to grow, there is an increasing focus on exploring the most effective ways to harness the potential of this upcoming "revolution." Major questions are being asked in all areas, including how to:
1. Identify and prioritize the most informative SNPs for disease risk prediction and personalized medicine.
2. Develop and apply computational tools for SNP analysis and interpretation.
3. Integrate SNP data with other types of genomic and clinical data to improve disease understanding and treatment.
4. Address ethical and regulatory issues related to the use of SNP data in research and clinical settings.
The ongoing discovery of SNPs is expected to yield hundreds of thousands of new SNPs in the coming years, further propelling the field forward and raising new challenges and opportunities for researchers and clinicians alike.

title: Combination inhibition of PI3K and mTORC1 yields durable remissions in orthotopic patient-derived xenografts of HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases
text: Brain metastases pose the most significant clinical challenge in the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer. To address this challenge, we have developed and characterized orthotopic patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) of HER2-expressing breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM). These PDXs were used to identify targeted combination therapies, with a focus on inhibition of the PI3K and mTOR signaling pathways. Our results demonstrate that combined inhibition of PI3K and mTOR resulted in durable tumor regressions in three of five PDXs, and this therapeutic response was correlated with a reduction in the phosphorylation of 4EBP1, an mTORC1 effector. In contrast, the two nonresponding PDXs exhibited hypermutated genomes with enrichment of mutations in DNA-repair genes, suggesting an association between genomic instability and therapeutic resistance. These findings support the idea of conducting a biomarker-driven clinical trial of a PI3K inhibitor in combination with an mTOR inhibitor for patients with HER2-positive BCBM.

title: Activation of Frontal Neocortical Areas by Vocal Production in Marmosets
text: Primate species frequently rely on vocal communication to facilitate social interactions. Although significant progress has been made in understanding the acoustic structure of primate vocalizations and their social context, the neocortical control of audio-vocal interactions in primates remains inadequately explored, with most knowledge derived from lesion studies in squirrel monkeys and macaques. To elucidate the neocortical areas involved in vocal control in a New World primate species, the common marmoset, we employed a method previously employed in other vertebrate species: the analysis of the expression of the immediate early gene Egr-1 in freely behaving animals. The distribution of Egr-1 immunoreactive cells in the neocortex of three marmosets exposed to the playback of conspecific vocalizations and vocalizing spontaneously (H/V group) was compared to data from three other marmosets that heard the playback but did not vocalize (H/n group). Our findings revealed a higher number of Egr-1 immunoreactive cells in the anterior cingulate cortex, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex in the H/V group. These results provide conclusive evidence that the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, which is equivalent to Broca's area in humans and has been linked to auditory processing of species-specific vocalizations and orofacial control in macaques, is actively involved in vocal output in marmosets. Our findings support the notion that the network of neocortical areas related to vocal communication in marmosets is remarkably similar to that of Old World primates. The role of these areas in vocal production and their contribution to the evolution of speech in primates are discussed.

title: Familial hiatal hernia in a large five generation family confirming true autosomal dominant inheritance.
text:
Background: Hiatal hernia is a relatively rare condition, and its familial occurrence has been rarely documented.
Aims: To describe the pattern of inheritance of familial hiatal hernia within an affected family.
Methods: We investigated 38 members of a family across five generations, using a combination of interviews and barium meal examinations to identify any evidence of a hiatal hernia.
Results: Twenty-three of the 38 family members had radiological evidence of a hiatal hernia. Notably, no individual born to unaffected parents developed a hiatal hernia, suggesting that the condition may be inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. In one case, direct male-to-male transmission was observed, further supporting an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance.
Conclusions: Our findings indicate that familial inheritance of hiatal hernia does occur, and direct male-to-male transmission suggests an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance.

title: An Excitatory Loop with Astrocytes Contributes to Drive Neurons to Seizure Threshold
text: In focal epilepsies, seizures are fueled by a highly synchronized neuronal activity that originates at specific brain sites and then spreads to larger areas of the brain. Despite extensive research, the early cellular events that trigger and sustain a focal seizure are still not well understood. Identifying these events is crucial to comprehend the pathophysiology of focal epilepsies and to develop novel pharmacological treatments for drug-resistant forms of epilepsy. Recent evidence suggests that astrocytes play a prominent role in the initiation of seizures. To investigate the relationship between astrocytes and neurons in focal seizures, we employed simultaneous patch-clamp recording and calcium imaging techniques in a novel in vitro model of focal seizures induced by local applications of N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) in rat entorhinal cortex slices. Our findings revealed that a rise in calcium levels in astrocytes correlates with both the initial development and the maintenance of a focal, seizure-like discharge. Additionally, we observed a delayed astrocyte activation during ictal discharges in other models, including the whole in vitro isolated guinea pig brain, in which the site of seizure generation cannot be precisely monitored. In contrast, interictal discharges were not associated with calcium changes in astrocytes. By selectively inhibiting or stimulating astrocyte calcium signaling, we found that neurons engage astrocytes in a recurrent excitatory loop, possibly involving gliotransmission, which promotes seizure initiation and sustains the ictal discharge. This neuron-astrocyte interaction may represent a novel target for developing effective therapeutic strategies to control seizures.

title: Diminished performance on neuropsychological testing in late life depression is correlated with microstructural white matter abnormalities.
text:
Background: Traditional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) does not provide specific information on the extent of underlying white matter structural abnormalities in late-life depression (LLD). Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) offers a unique opportunity to investigate these abnormalities, but has been limited by examining only a subset of regions of interest (ROI) and by confounds common to the study of an elderly population, including comorbid vascular pathology. Furthermore, comprehensive correlation of DTI measurements, including axial and radial diffusivity measurements, has not been demonstrated in the LLD population.
Methods: In this study, 51 depressed and 16 non-depressed elderly subjects underwent traditional anatomic T1 and T2-weighted MRI, as well as DTI. The DTI data were skeletonized using tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), and both regional and global analyses were performed.
Results: Widespread structural abnormalities within white matter were detected in the LLD group, accounting for age, gender, and education and matched for cerebrovascular risk factors and global T2 white matter hyperintensities (T2WMH). Regional differences were most prominent in the uncinate and cingulate white matter, and were generally characterized by an increase in radial diffusivity. Age-related changes were more advanced in individuals with LLD relative to controls in the cingulate bundle. Regression analysis demonstrated significant correlations of regional fractional anisotropy and radial diffusivity with five different neuropsychological factor scores. TBSS analysis demonstrated a greater extent of white matter abnormalities in LLD that were not responsive to treatment, compared to controls.
Conclusions: White matter integrity is compromised in late-life depression, primarily manifested by increased radial diffusivity in specific regions, suggesting underlying myelin injury. A possible mechanism for underlying myelin injury is chronic white matter ischemia related to intrinsic cerebrovascular disease. In some regions, such as the cingulate bundle, the white matter injury related to late-life depression appears to be independent of and compounded by age-related changes. The correlations with neuropsychological testing indicate the essential effects of white matter injury on functional status. Lastly, response to treatment may depend on the extent of white matter injury, suggesting a need for intact functional networks.

title: The atypical antipsychotic olanzapine causes weight gain by targeting serotonin receptor 2C.
text: Olanzapine, a type of antipsychotic medication, is known to cause excessive weight gain and increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. However, the underlying mechanisms of these metabolic changes are not well understood. To investigate, we used an experimental model of olanzapine-induced hyperphagia and obesity in female C57BL/6 mice. Our findings revealed that olanzapine treatment acutely increased food intake, impaired glucose tolerance, and altered physical activity and energy expenditure in mice. Interestingly, we found that olanzapine-induced hyperphagia and weight gain were significantly reduced in mice lacking the serotonin 2C receptor (HTR2C). Furthermore, treatment with a specific agonist of the HTR2C receptor, lorcaserin, suppressed olanzapine-induced hyperphagia and weight gain. Lorcaserin treatment also improved glucose tolerance in olanzapine-fed mice. Taken together, our results suggest that olanzapine exerts some of its metabolic side effects by antagonizing the HTR2C receptor.

title: Case-control study of endogenous steroid hormones and endometrial cancer.
text: The study investigated the relationship between hormone levels and the risk of developing endometrial cancer in premenopausal and postmenopausal women. The study included 68 case patients and 107 control subjects among premenopausal women, and 208 case patients and 209 control subjects among postmenopausal women. The study found that high levels of androstenedione were associated with a 3.6-fold and 2.8-fold increased risk of endometrial cancer among premenopausal and postmenopausal women, respectively, after adjusting for other factors. Additionally, high levels of estrone were associated with an increased risk of endometrial cancer, although adjusting for other risk factors reduced the effect. However, high levels of sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) were associated with a reduced risk of endometrial cancer among postmenopausal women. The study suggests that high levels of unopposed estrogen may not be the sole underlying biologic pathway for all risk factors for endometrial cancer, as the relationship between hormone levels and risk varied by menopausal status. Further research should focus on alternative endocrinologic mechanisms and the biologic relevance of the increased risk associated with androstenedione in both premenopausal and postmenopausal disease.

title: FOXO4 is necessary for neural differentiation of human embryonic stem cells.
text: Maintaining proper protein function is crucial for cellular health, and proteostasis (the regulation of protein levels and activity) may play a significant role in the immortality of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Interestingly, hESCs exhibit an unusually high level of active proteasomes, a key component of the proteostasis network. The insulin/IGF-1 responsive transcription factor FOXO4 regulates proteasome activity in hESCs, and we have found that decreasing FOXO4 levels reduces the ability of hESCs to differentiate into neural cell types. This suggests that FOXO4 transcends evolutionary boundaries and connects hESC function to the regulation of longevity in invertebrates.

title: Gestational protein restriction affects trophoblast differentiation.
text: The impact of gestational protein restriction (PR) on placental development and function remains unexplored. To investigate the hypothesis that PR affects trophoblast differentiation during mid- and late pregnancy, rats were fed a 20% or isocaloric 6% protein diet from Day 1 to 14 or 18 of pregnancy. The effects of PR on trophoblast differentiation were evaluated by analyzing changes in the expressions of genes associated with trophoblast lineages. At Day 18 of pregnancy, PR increased the expressions of Esrrb, Id1, and Id2 (trophoblast stem cell markers), decreased the expression of Ascl2 (spongiotrophblast cell marker), and Prl2c1 (trophoblast giant cell marker), but did not affect the expressions of Gjb3 and Pcdh12 (glycogen cell markers) in the junctional zone (JZ). In the labyrinth zone (LZ), PR did not alter the expressions of Prl2b1 (trophoblast giant cell marker), Gcm1, and Syna (syncytiotrophoblast cell markers), but decreased the expression of Ctsq (sinusoidal trophoblast giant cell marker). These findings suggest that PR impairs the differentiation of trophoblast stem cells into spongiotrophoblast and trophoblast giant cells in the JZ, and the formation of sinusoidal trophoblast giant cells in the LZ.

title: In vitro characterization of the anti-PD-1 antibody nivolumab, BMS-936558, and in vivo toxicology in non-human primates.
text: The programmed death-1 (PD-1) receptor acts as an immune checkpoint, preventing excessive tissue damage and the development of autoimmune diseases during inflammatory responses. PD-1 is expressed on activated T cells, which it downregulates by binding to its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, on antigen-presenting cells. In cancer, the expression of PD-1 on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes hinders antitumor immunity, making PD-1 blockade a promising cancer immunotherapy approach. This report details the development and characterization of nivolumab, a fully human IgG4 (S228P) anti-PD-1 receptor-blocking monoclonal antibody. Nivolumab binds to PD-1 with high affinity and specificity, inhibiting the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands. In vitro assays showed that nivolumab can potently enhance T-cell responses and cytokine production in mixed lymphocyte reactions and stimulation assays with superantigens or cytomegalovirus. No antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity or complement-dependent cytotoxicity was observed with nivolumab and activated T cells as targets. Treatment with nivolumab did not induce adverse immune-related events in cynomolgus macaques at high concentrations, regardless of circulating anti-nivolumab antibodies. These findings provide a comprehensive preclinical characterization of nivolumab, whose antitumor activity and safety have been demonstrated in human clinical trials across various solid tumors.

title: Combined Impact of Lifestyle-Related Factors on Total and Cause-Specific Mortality among Chinese Women: Prospective Cohort Study
text:
Background: Although cigarette smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity, and other unhealthy lifestyle habits have been linked to an increased risk of various chronic diseases and premature mortality, the combined impact of these factors on mortality outcomes, particularly among non-Western populations, remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify the overall effect of lifestyle-related factors beyond active cigarette smoking and alcohol consumption on all-cause and cause-specific mortality in Chinese women.
Methods and Findings: The study used data from the Shanghai Women's Health Study, a population-based prospective cohort study in China. Participants were 71,243 women aged 40-70 years who never smoked or drank alcohol regularly. A healthy lifestyle score was created based on five lifestyle-related factors associated with mortality outcomes, including normal weight, lower waist-hip ratio, daily physical activity, non-exposure to spouse's smoking, and higher daily fruit and vegetable intake. The score ranged from 0 (least healthy) to 5 (most healthy) points. During an average follow-up of 9 years, 2,860 deaths occurred, including 775 from cardiovascular disease (CVD) and 1,351 from cancer. Adjusted hazard ratios for mortality decreased progressively with an increasing number of healthy lifestyle factors. Compared to women with a score of 0, hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for women with 4-5 factors were 0.57 (0.44-0.74) for total mortality, 0.29 (0.16-0.54) for CVD mortality, and 0.76 (0.54-1.06) for cancer mortality. The inverse association between the healthy lifestyle score and mortality was observed consistently regardless of chronic disease status at baseline. The population attributable risks for not having 4-5 healthy lifestyle factors were 33% for total deaths, 59% for CVD deaths, and 19% for cancer deaths.
Conclusions: This study, to our knowledge, quantified the combined impact of lifestyle-related factors on mortality outcomes in Chinese women. A healthier lifestyle pattern, including being of normal weight, lower central adiposity, participation in physical activity, non-exposure to spousal smoking, and higher fruit and vegetable intake, was associated with reductions in total and cause-specific mortality among lifetime nonsmoking and nondrinking women. These findings support the importance of overall lifestyle modification in disease prevention.

title: Aptamer-functionalized lipid nanoparticles targeting osteoblasts as a novel RNA interference–based bone anabolic strategy
text: Currently, significant concerns persist regarding the safety and efficacy of RNA interference (RNAi)-based bone anabolic strategies due to the lack of direct delivery systems for osteogenic siRNAs specifically targeting osteoblasts. To address this challenge, we employed cell-SELEX to identify an aptamer, CH6, that selectively targets both rat and human osteoblasts. We then developed CH6 aptamer-functionalized lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) encapsulating osteogenic pleckstrin homology domain-containing family O member 1 (Plekho1) siRNA (CH6-LNPs-siRNA). Our findings demonstrate that CH6 facilitates in vitro osteoblast-selective uptake of Plekho1 siRNA through macropinocytosis and enhances in vivo osteoblast-specific Plekho1 gene silencing, leading to improved bone formation, microarchitecture, mass, and mechanical properties in both osteopenic and healthy rodents. These results suggest that osteoblast-specific aptamer-functionalized LNPs could serve as a novel RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy, significantly improving the targeted delivery and selectivity of osteogenic siRNAs at the cellular level.

title: High abundance of plasma cells secreting transglutaminase 2–specific IgA autoantibodies with limited somatic hypermutation in celiac disease intestinal lesions
text: Celiac disease is an immune-mediated disorder characterized by the generation of mucosal autoantibodies against the enzyme transglutaminase 2 (TG2) in response to the ingestion of gluten in individuals who express human leukocyte antigen HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8. To investigate the IgA anti-TG2 response in celiac disease, we used a comprehensive and non-biased approach to analyze the antibody repertoire of ex vivo-isolated intestinal antibody-secreting cells (ASCs). Our findings revealed that TG2-specific plasma cells are significantly expanded within the duodenal mucosa in individuals with active celiac disease. These plasma cells produced high-affinity TG2-specific antibodies that did not undergo somatic mutations, suggesting a germline repertoire with high affinity for TG2. Interestingly, the TG2-specific antibodies did not inhibit enzymatic activity and instead served as substrates for TG2-mediated crosslinking when expressed as IgD or IgM, but not as IgA1 or IgG1. This may explain why the antibody response to TG2 exhibits signs of a primary immune response despite the chronic nature of the disease.

title: Alterations of white matter integrity in adults with major depressive disorder: a magnetic resonance imaging study.
text:
Objective:
Our study aimed to investigate alterations in white matter integrity in adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
Methods:
We conducted diffusion tensor imaging with a 3T MRI scanner on 45 patients with major depression and 45 healthy controls matched for age, sex, and education. Voxel-based analysis measured fractional anisotropy (FA), and differences between the patient and control groups were investigated. Correlations between microstructure abnormalities of white matter and symptom severity, age of illness onset, and cumulative illness duration were also examined.
Results:
We found a significant decrease in FA in the left hemisphere, including the anterior limb of the internal capsule and the inferior parietal portion of the superior longitudinal fasciculus, in patients with MDD compared to healthy controls. Diffusion tensor imaging measures in the left anterior limb of the internal capsule were negatively related to the severity of depressive symptoms, even after controlling for age and sex.
Conclusion:
Our findings provide new evidence of microstructural changes in white matter in non-late-onset adult depression. Our results complement those observed in late-life depression and support the hypothesis that the disruption of cortical-subcortical circuit integrity may be involved in the etiology of major depressive disorder.

title: [Clinical study on the therapeutic effect of acupuncture in the treatment of post-stroke depression].
text:
Objective: To evaluate the therapeutic effectiveness of "Xingnao Kaiqiao Zhenfa" (Acupuncture Technique for Restoring Consciousness) in the treatment of post-stroke depression.
Methods: A total of 256 stroke patients were randomly assigned to either an acupuncture group (n = 180) or a medication group (n = 76) based on their hospital visit sequence. Acupoints used in the acupuncture group included Neiguan (PC 6), Renzhong (GV 26), Baihui (GV 20), Yintang (EX-HN 3), and Sanyinjiao (SP 6, the affected side). The needles were retained for 20 minutes per session, twice daily, for one month. Medication group patients received Amitriptyline (50 mg/d initially, then 200 mg/d). The therapeutic effectiveness was evaluated using Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) and Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD) after one month of treatment.
Results: After one month of treatment, 31 (17.2%) and 13 (17.1%) patients in the acupuncture and medication groups, respectively, were cured, and 73 (40.6%) and 18 (23.7%) had a marked improvement in their depression state. The acupuncture group had a significantly higher markedly effective rate (56.6%) and total effective rate (72.8%) compared to the medication group (35.1% and 50.0%, respectively). The total scores of SDS and HRSD, as well as the severity index, decreased significantly in both groups after treatment, but the therapeutic effects of the acupuncture group were significantly better than those of the medication group in reducing SDS, HRSD, and severity index (P < 0.05). Additionally, the decreased values of depression, pessimistic mood, and irritability in the acupuncture group were significantly larger than those in the medication group (P < 0.05). No significant difference was found between the two groups in the decreased value of insomnia (P > 0.05).
Conclusion: The results of this study suggest that "Acupuncture Technique for Restoring Consciousness" is an effective treatment for post-stroke depression. The therapeutic effect of acupuncture is markedly superior to that of medication, with a significantly higher markedly effective rate and total effective rate in the acupuncture group. These findings provide evidence for the use of acupuncture as a complementary treatment for post-stroke depression.

title: 30 Years of NF-κB: A Blossoming of Relevance to Human Pathobiology
text: Thirty years ago, NF-κB was first identified as a rapidly inducible transcription factor with a broad role in gene induction across diverse cellular responses, particularly within the immune system. Since then, extensive research has elucidated the complex regulatory pathways involving this transcription factor. By leveraging recent discoveries in human genetic diseases, we will provide a comprehensive overview of specific proteins within their relevant medical and biological contexts.

title: Increased gene expression of brown fat uncoupling protein (UCP)1 and skeletal muscle UCP2 and UCP3 in MAC16-induced cancer cachexia.
