The study also finds that reducing presumptive treatment through improved diagnosis can significantly reduce the number of treatment courses required per clinical episode averted in lower-transmission settings, although some loss of overall impact on transmission occurs. Additionally, the study suggests that ACT partner drugs and non-artemisinin regimens with longer prophylactic times could result in a larger impact in higher-transmission settings, although their long-term benefit must be evaluated in relation to the risk of developing parasite resistance.
In summary, the study suggests that ACTs have the potential to significantly reduce transmission of Plasmodium falciparum malaria, particularly in lower-transmission settings, and that reducing presumptive treatment through improved diagnosis can help maximize the impact of ACTs. Additionally, the study highlights the importance of evaluating the long-term benefit and risk of developing parasite resistance when using non-artemisinin regimens in higher-transmission settings.

title: Systems metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli for L-threonine production
text: Historically, the development of amino acid-producing microorganisms has relied on random mutagenesis due to the complexity and strict regulation of the metabolic network. However, we have successfully engineered an Escherichia coli strain to overproduce L-threonine using systems metabolic engineering. By removing feedback inhibitions and transcriptional attenuation regulators, we increased the biosynthesis of Thr. We also deleted pathways involved in Thr degradation and manipulated the expression levels of additional target genes identified through transcriptome profiling and in silico flux response analysis. Our engineered E. coli strain produced Thr with a high yield of 0.393 g per gram of glucose and 82.4 g/l Thr in fed-batch culture, demonstrating the potential of this approach for producing other bioproducts.

title: Association Between ADHD and Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
text: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and obesity/overweight through a meta-analysis of existing research. METHODS: A comprehensive search of various databases was conducted through August 31, 2014, including both published and unpublished studies. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess study quality. Random-effects models were employed to analyze the data. RESULTS: Forty-two studies with a total of 728,136 participants (48,161 ADHD subjects and 679,975 comparison subjects) were included in the analysis. The results showed a significant association between obesity/overweight and ADHD for both children and adults. The pooled prevalence of obesity was found to be increased by approximately 70% in adults with ADHD compared to those without ADHD, and by approximately 40% in children with ADHD compared to those without ADHD. The association remained significant after adjusting for potential confounding factors, diagnosing ADHD through direct interview, and using directly measured height and weight. Gender, study setting, study country, and study quality did not moderate the association between obesity/overweight and ADHD. Additionally, ADHD was found to be significantly associated with overweight. The use of medication for ADHD was not found to increase the risk of obesity. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence for a significant association between ADHD and obesity/overweight through a meta-analysis of existing research. Further research is needed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and the long-term effects of ADHD treatments on weight in individuals with both ADHD and obesity.

title: Amyloid-DNA Composites of Bacterial Biofilms Stimulate Autoimmunity.
text: Research on the human microbiome has revealed that both beneficial and harmful bacteria can influence various diseases, including obesity, cancer, and autoimmune disorders, through mechanisms that are not yet fully understood. In our study, we discovered that a component of bacterial biofilms, called curli, forms irreversible fibers with bacterial DNA during biofilm formation. This interaction accelerates amyloid polymerization and creates immunogenic complexes that activate immune cells, such as dendritic cells, to produce cytokines like type I interferons, which are harmful in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). When we administered curli-DNA composites to lupus-prone and wild-type mice, we observed immune activation and production of autoantibodies in both groups. However, the infection of lupus-prone mice with curli-producing bacteria led to higher autoantibody titers compared to curli-deficient bacteria. These findings provide a potential mechanism by which the microbiome and biofilm-producing enteric infections may contribute to the progression of SLE, and suggest a potential target for treating autoimmune diseases.

title: Comprehensive genomic characterization defines human glioblastoma genes and core pathways
text: Human cancer cells typically exhibit multiple chromosomal abnormalities, nucleotide substitutions, and epigenetic modifications that drive malignant transformation. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) pilot project aims to evaluate the value of large-scale, multi-dimensional analysis of these molecular characteristics in human cancer and provide the data rapidly to the research community. In this study, we present an interim integrative analysis of DNA copy number, gene expression, and DNA methylation aberrations in 206 glioblastomas, the most common type of primary adult brain cancer, and nucleotide sequence aberrations in 91 of these glioblastomas. This analysis provides new insights into the roles of ERBB2, NF1, and TP53, uncovers frequent mutations in the phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase regulatory subunit gene PIK3R1, and reveals a network view of the pathways altered in the development of glioblastoma. Furthermore, integration of mutation, DNA methylation, and clinical treatment data reveals a link between MGMT promoter methylation and a hypermutator phenotype consequent to mismatch repair deficiency in treated glioblastomas, an observation with potential clinical implications. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and power of TCGA, showing that it can rapidly expand knowledge of the molecular basis of cancer.

title: LY2405319, an Engineered FGF21 Variant, Improves the Metabolic Status of Diabetic Monkeys
text:
Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a novel metabolic regulator that holds promise as a potential treatment for various metabolic disorders. In animal models, administration of recombinant wild-type FGF21 has been shown to significantly improve glycemia and other systemic measures of metabolic health. In this study, we investigate the pharmacological effects of a recently described FGF21 analogue, LY2405319 (LY), in diabetic non-human primates.
Methods:
Diabetic rhesus monkeys were treated subcutaneously with LY once daily for a period of seven weeks, with escalating doses of 3, 9, and 50 mg/kg. Metabolic parameters, including glucose, body weight, insulin, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels, were measured at 2, 4, 6, and 8 weeks following the final LY dose. Circulating profiles of adipokines were also analyzed, with a focus on adiponectin and leptin, to determine the direct action of FGF21 on adipose tissue.
Results:
LY therapy resulted in a rapid and significant lowering of various metabolic parameters, including glucose, body weight, insulin, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels, at all doses tested. Notably, we observed favorable changes in circulating profiles of adipokines, with increased adiponectin and reduced leptin, indicative of direct FGF21 action on adipose tissue. Importantly, these findings demonstrate that FGF21-based therapy has metabolic efficacy in an animal model with late-stage diabetes, with partial attenuation of its glycemic efficacy but full preservation of its lipid-lowering effect.
Discussion:

These findings support the continued exploration of the FGF21 pathway as a potential treatment for metabolic disease. The observed metabolic efficacy of LY in diabetic non-human primates suggests that FGF21-based therapies may be viable options for patients with advanced disease progression. The preservation of LY's lipid-lowering effect despite partial attenuation of its glycemic efficacy highlights the potential for FGF21-based therapies to address multiple aspects of metabolic dysregulation. Further studies are warranted to fully elucidate the mechanisms of FGF21 action and to determine the safety and efficacy of FGF21-based therapies in humans.

title: Epigenetic Control of Stem Cell Potential during Homeostasis, Aging, and Disease.
text: Stem cell decline is a crucial cellular phenomenon that underlies the aging process in various tissues. Epigenetic regulation plays a central role in maintaining stem cell function, and recent research has implicated epigenetic dysregulation as a key contributor to the altered potential of stem cells during aging. Unlike terminally differentiated cells, epigenetic dysregulation in stem cells has far-reaching consequences, as alterations can be transmitted to differentiated progeny and perpetuated within the stem cell pool through self-renewal divisions. This Review focuses on recent studies examining the epigenetic regulation of tissue-specific stem cells in homeostasis, aging, and aging-related diseases.

title: Host–Parasite Interactions and the Evolution of Gene Expression
text: The interactions between hosts and parasites create a continuous source of selection that drives the evolution of various traits in both species. To investigate how gene expression patterns evolve at genetic loci involved in host resistance and parasite infection, we developed a mathematically explicit model. Our findings reveal a striking yet intuitive conclusion: gene expression in host resistance loci tends to evolve towards co-expression of alleles, while parasite infection loci evolve towards expressing only a single allele. This occurs because hosts that co-express resistance alleles can recognize and clear a greater diversity of parasite genotypes, while parasites that co-express antigen or elicitor alleles are more likely to be recognized and cleared by the host, leading to the expression of only a single allele. Our model provides testable predictions that can help interpret existing data on expression levels for genes involved in host-parasite interactions, shedding light on the complex dynamics of this intriguing relationship.

title: A crucial role for interleukin (IL)-1 in the induction of IL-17–producing T cells that mediate autoimmune encephalomyelitis
text: Recent research has shown that interleukin (IL)-23-driven IL-17-producing T cells (ThIL-17 cells) play a key role in the pathology of certain autoimmune diseases. Our study found that the induction of antigen-specific ThIL-17 cells is impaired in mice lacking the IL-1 receptor type I (IL-1RI−/−), and this correlates with a lower incidence of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) in these mice. However, EAE can still be induced in IL-1RI−/− mice by transferring autoantigen-specific ThIL-17 cells from wild-type mice. Interestingly, IL-23 alone does not induce IL-17 production by T cells from IL-1RI−/− mice, but IL-1α or IL-1β can enhance IL-23-induced IL-17 production even in the absence of T cell receptor stimulation. Our findings suggest that IL-1 functions upstream of IL-17 to promote pathogenic ThIL-17 cells in EAE. Additionally, we found that phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, nuclear factor κB, and novel protein kinase C isoforms play essential roles in IL-1 and IL-23-mediated IL-17 production, and tumor necrosis factor α synergizes with IL-23 to enhance IL-17 production, which is IL-1 dependent.

title: Aberrant luminal progenitors as the candidate target population for basal tumor development in BRCA1 mutation carriers
text: Basal-like breast cancers that arise in women carrying mutations in the BRCA1 gene are thought to originate from the mammary stem cell. To investigate early changes that occur in BRCA1 mutation carriers, we isolated and characterized distinct epithelial subpopulations from normal mammary tissue and preneoplastic samples from individuals carrying a BRCA1 mutation. We identified three epithelial subsets: basal stem/progenitor cells, luminal progenitor cells, and mature luminal cells. Surprisingly, we found that breast tissue from BRCA1 mutation carriers contains an expanded population of luminal progenitor cells that exhibit factor-independent growth in vitro. Additionally, gene expression profiling revealed that breast tissue from BRCA1 mutation carriers and basal breast tumors are more similar to normal luminal progenitor cells than any other subset, including the stem cell-enriched population. The c-KIT tyrosine kinase receptor (encoded by KIT) was identified as a key marker of luminal progenitor cells and was found to be more highly expressed in BRCA1-associated preneoplastic tissue and tumors. Our findings suggest that an aberrant luminal progenitor population is a target for transformation in BRCA1-associated basal tumors.

title: Getting to the site of inflammation: the leukocyte adhesion cascade updated
text: Leukocyte recruitment, including neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte trafficking, relies on the ability of these cells to adhere and migrate through blood vessel walls. The traditional three-step model of leukocyte adhesion, consisting of rolling, activation, and firm adhesion, has been expanded and refined to include additional steps. These include slow rolling, adhesion strengthening, intraluminal crawling, paracellular and transcellular migration, and a second activation pathway in neutrophils that does not require signaling through G-protein-coupled receptors. This review focuses on recent advances in our understanding of the leukocyte adhesion cascade, a central paradigm in inflammation and immunity.

title: Genome-wide loss of 5-hmC is a novel epigenetic feature of Huntington's disease.
text: The epigenetic modification of cytosine, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5-hmC), has been implicated in various biological processes, including neurodevelopment. However, the genomic distribution and functional significance of 5-hmC in neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington's disease (HD) remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the genomic distribution of 5-hmC in HD mouse brains and found a significant reduction in the 5-hmC signal in the striatum and cortex compared to age-matched wild-type (WT) mice. This reduction was observed in both disease-specific (YAC128) and WT mice. We also identified disease-specific differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhMRs) and found that the acquisition of DhmRs in gene bodies is a positive epigenetic regulator for gene expression. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) of genotype-specific DhMR-annotated genes revealed that alterations in canonical pathways involved in neuronal development/differentiation (Wnt/β-catenin/Sox pathway, axonal guidance signaling pathway) and neuronal function/survival (glutamate receptor/calcium/CREB, GABA receptor signaling, dopamine-DARPP32 feedback pathway, etc.) may contribute to the onset of HD. Our findings suggest that loss of the 5-hmC marker is a novel epigenetic feature in HD, and that this aberrant epigenetic regulation may impair neurogenesis, neuronal function, and survival in HD brain. Our study also opens up a new avenue for HD treatment, as re-establishing the native 5-hmC landscape may have the potential to slow or halt the progression of HD.

title: Planning for Postdisaster Resiliency
text: The central theme of this article is the importance of planning for resilience in the aftermath of a catastrophe. The authors first present their understanding of planning for resilience as a crucial objective for communities recovering from disasters, highlighting the benefits of such planning in creating more resilient environments. They then delve into the challenges associated with planning for post-disaster recovery, including obstacles posed by federal and state governments, the potential of compact urban form models to guide rebuilding, and the lack of citizen involvement in the planning process. Finally, the authors draw on lessons learned from previous research and offer policy recommendations to foster pre-disaster recovery planning for resilient communities.

title: Increased stress-induced inflammatory responses in male patients with major depression and increased early life stress.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the activation of the innate immune system in response to psychosocial stress in patients with major depression who experienced early life stress. The researchers compared the levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), lymphocyte subsets, and DNA binding of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kB) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells between medically healthy male subjects with current major depression and increased early life stress (n=14) and non-depressed male comparison subjects (n=14) before and after completing the Trier Social Stress Test.
The results showed that the Trier Social Stress Test led to greater increases in IL-6 and NF-kB DNA-binding in major depression patients with early life stress, and these increases were correlated with the severity of depression but not early life stress. Additionally, the study found that the percentage of natural killer (NK) cells increased following stress, but there were no differences between the groups, and no correlation between NK cell percentage and stress-induced NF-kB DNA-binding or IL-6.
The study's findings suggest that male patients with major depression who experienced early life stress exhibit enhanced inflammatory responsiveness to psychosocial stress, providing preliminary evidence of a link between major depression, early life stress, and adverse health outcomes in diseases associated with inflammation.

title: KIF3A/B: a heterodimeric kinesin superfamily protein that works as a microtubule plus end-directed motor for membrane organelle transport
text: In this study, we cloned and characterized a new member of the murine brain kinesin superfamily, KIF3B, and found that it shares a high degree of homology with KIF3A, but not identity. KIF3B is expressed in various organ tissues and developing neurons of mice, where it accumulates with anterogradely moving membranous organelles after nerve axon ligation. Using immunoprecipitation assays, we found that KIF3B forms a complex with KIF3A and three other high molecular weight (approximately 100 kD)-associated polypeptides, called KAP3. In vitro reconstruction using baculovirus expression systems revealed that KIF3A and KIF3B directly bind to each other in the absence of KAP3. We also showed that KIF3B has motor activity in vitro, when combined with a chimeric motor protein (KIF3B head and KIF3A rod tail). Subcellular fractionation of mouse brain homogenates revealed that the native KIF3 complex is associated with membrane fractions other than synaptic vesicles. Immunoprecipitation and electron microscopic studies also showed that KIF3 is associated with membranous organelles. Our findings suggest that KIF3B forms a heterodimer with KIF3A and functions as a new microtubule-based anterograde translocator for membranous organelles, and that KAP3 may determine functional diversity of the KIF3 complex in various kinds of cells in vivo.

title: A genetic screen identifies an LKB1–MARK signalling axis controlling the Hippo–YAP pathway
text: The Hippo-YAP pathway is a newly discovered signaling cascade involved in the regulation of stem cell activity and organ size. To identify its components, we performed an RNAi-based kinome screen in human cells. Our screen revealed several kinases not previously linked to Hippo signaling that control various cellular processes. One of the hits, LKB1, is a well-known tumor suppressor whose mechanisms of action are only partially understood. We found that LKB1 acts through its substrates in the microtubule affinity-regulating kinase family to regulate the localization of the polarity determinant Scribble and the activity of the core Hippo kinases. Our data also suggest that YAP is crucial for the tumor-suppressive effects of LKB1. Our findings identify a signaling axis linking YAP activation to LKB1 mutations and have implications for the treatment of LKB1-mutant human cancers. Additionally, our research sheds light on upstream signals in the Hippo-YAP signaling cascade.

title: Beyond melanoma: inhibiting the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway in solid tumors.
text: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have been recognized as a breakthrough treatment for melanoma, exhibiting remarkable response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade. This success is likely to extend to other cancers, as hundreds of clinical trials are currently underway or proposed to investigate this promising modality of therapy in various malignancies. While immune checkpoint inhibitors have been extensively studied in melanoma and more recently in lung cancer, there is limited knowledge on their effectiveness in other cancers. This review aims to shed light on the tumor immune microenvironment, PD-1/PD-L1 expression, and the potential of immune modulation through PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors in patients with head and neck, prostate, urothelial, renal, breast, gastrointestinal, and lung cancers.

title: Partitioning the symptoms of hypoglycaemia using multi-sample confirmatory factor analysis
text: The allocation of hypoglycaemic symptoms to either autonomic or neuroglycopenic groups tends to occur on an a priori basis, rather than based on scientific evidence. However, given the practical need for clear symptom markers of hypoglycaemia, more rigorous scientific approaches must be pursued. Our studies, involving 295 insulin-treated outpatients and 303 additional insulin-treated diabetic outpatients, provide substantial evidence for a three-factor model of hypoglycaemic symptomatology. This model is based on statistical associations discovered among symptoms reported by diabetic patients and includes autonomie (sweating, palpitation, shaking, and hunger), neuroglycopenic (confusion, drowsiness, odd behavior, speech difficulty, and incoordination), and malaise (nausea and headache) factors. Confirmatory factor analyses validated the three-factor model in both groups, indicating that the relative loadings of symptoms on factors were equal and the residual variance for each symptom was identical across groups. These findings suggest that the results may be used in future research and clinical practice to provide valid groupings of symptoms.

title: Extracellular vesicles from human cardiac progenitor cells inhibit cardiomyocyte apoptosis and improve cardiac function after myocardial infarction.
text:
Introduction:
Recent research has suggested that cardiac progenitor cells (CPCs) may play a crucial role in improving cardiac function after injury. However, the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood, and the specific mediators of these effects are still unknown. Exosomes and other secreted membrane vesicles, collectively referred to as extracellular vesicles (EVs), have been identified as potential paracrine signaling mediators. In this study, we investigate the role of EVs secreted by human CPCs in cardioprotection.
Methods and Results:
CPCs were derived from atrial appendage explants from patients undergoing heart valve surgery. The conditioned medium (CM) from these CPCs was found to inhibit apoptosis in mouse HL-1 cardiomyocytic cells and enhance tube formation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. These effects were abrogated when the CM was depleted of EVs. The same effects were reproduced when EVs secreted by CPCs were added to the cells, but not when EVs secreted by human dermal fibroblasts were used. Transmission electron microscopy and nanoparticle tracking analysis revealed that the EVs were primarily 30-90 nm in diameter, similar in size to exosomes. MicroRNAs most highly enriched in EVs secreted by CPCs compared to fibroblasts included miR-210, miR-132, and miR-146a-3p. miR-210 downregulated its known targets, ephrin A3 and PTP1b, inhibiting apoptosis in cardiomyocytic cells. miR-132 downregulated its target, RasGAP-p120, enhancing tube formation in endothelial cells. Injecting infarcted hearts with EVs secreted by CPCs, but not by fibroblasts, resulted in less cardiomyocyte apoptosis, enhanced angiogenesis, and improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) compared to injecting control medium (0.8 ± 6.8 vs. -21.3 ± 4.5%; P < 0.05).
Conclusion:
Our findings suggest that EVs are the active component of the paracrine secretion by human CPCs. As a cell-free approach, EVs may circumvent many of the limitations of cell transplantation. Further research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms of cardioprotection mediated by EVs secreted by CPCs, but these findings provide a promising avenue for the development of new therapeutic strategies for cardiovascular disease.

title: Increased Adipocyte O2 Consumption Triggers HIF-1α, Causing Inflammation and Insulin Resistance in Obesity
text: Obesity-related adipose tissue hypoxia and inflammation have been implicated as causal factors in insulin resistance. Our study found that early in the course of high-fat diet (HFD) feeding and obesity, adipocyte respiration becomes uncoupled, leading to increased oxygen consumption and relative adipocyte hypoxia. These events trigger the induction of HIF-1α, setting off a chronic inflammatory response in adipose tissue that characterizes obesity. At the molecular level, these events involve the stimulation of adenine nucleotide translocase 2 (ANT2), an inner mitochondrial membrane protein, which leads to an uncoupled respiratory state. Inhibition of ANT2 or HIF-1α can prevent or reverse these pathophysiological events, restoring insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance. Our findings reveal the sequential series of events in obesity-induced inflammation and insulin resistance.

title: Lpcat3-dependent production of arachidonoyl phospholipids is a key determinant of triglyceride secretion
text: The role of specific phospholipids (PLs) in lipid transport has been challenging to assess due to the inability to selectively manipulate membrane composition in living organisms. However, recent studies have shown that the phospholipid remodeling enzyme lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 3 (Lpcat3) plays a critical role in triglyceride (TG) secretion. Lpcat3's unique ability to incorporate arachidonate into membranes is essential for TG secretion, and mice lacking Lpcat3 in the intestine fail to thrive during weaning and exhibit enterocyte lipid accumulation and reduced plasma TGs. Additionally, mice lacking Lpcat3 in the liver show reduced plasma TGs, hepatosteatosis, and secrete lipid-poor very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) lacking arachidonoyl PLs. Mechanistic studies have revealed that Lpcat3 activity impacts membrane lipid mobility in living cells, providing a biophysical basis for the requirement of arachidonoyl PLs in lipidating lipoprotein particles. These findings identify Lpcat3 as a key factor in lipoprotein production and demonstrate how manipulation of membrane composition can be used as a regulatory mechanism to control metabolic pathways.

title: Characterization of a single-stranded DNA-binding protein from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.
text: Single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB) plays a crucial role in DNA metabolism, including DNA replication, repair, and recombination, and is essential for cell survival. To investigate the ssDNA-binding properties of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 SSB (PaSSB), we employed fluorescence quenching measurements and electrophoretic mobility shift analysis (EMSA). Our results revealed that PaSSB exists as a stable tetramer in solution, and bound 22-32 nucleotides (nt) per tetramer depending on salt concentration. Using EMSA, we characterized the stoichiometry of PaSSB complexed with a series of ssDNA homopolymers, and determined the size of the binding site to be 29 ± 1 nt. Furthermore, our findings indicated that the dissociation constants of PaSSB for the first tetramer were lower than those for the second tetramer. Based on these biophysical analyses, the ssDNA binding mode of PaSSB is expected to be noncooperative.

title: Primary cilia and coordination of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signalling.
text: Primary cilia are microtubule-based organelles that play a crucial role in coordinating signaling pathways during various cellular processes, including cell cycle regulation, migration, differentiation, and tissue homeostasis. Defects in primary cilia assembly or function have been linked to a wide range of developmental disorders and diseases collectively known as ciliopathies. This review aims to summarize the current understanding of the role of primary cilia in regulating receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways and explore potential mechanisms of signaling crosstalk and networking within the primary cilium. Additionally, we will discuss how defects in ciliary RTK signaling contribute to human diseases and disorders.

title: Detecting and targeting tumor relapse by its resistance to innate effectors at early recurrence
text: Tumor recurrence poses a significant clinical challenge. Our findings reveal that emerging recurrent tumors exhibit a distinct phenotype compared to their primary tumors, allowing them to evade the host's innate immune response triggered by the progression from minimal residual disease (MRD) to actively growing recurrence. By screening for this innate response, we were able to accurately predict which mice would experience recurrence. Premature induction of recurrence also resensitized MRD to the primary therapy, suggesting a potential shift in the clinical treatment of dormant disease. By combining screening with second-line treatments targeting innate insensitivity, we were able to cure up to 100% of mice that would have otherwise relapsed. These findings may lead to new strategies for early detection and targeted treatment of tumor recurrence, regardless of tumor type or initial treatment.

title: Forces in Tissue Morphogenesis and Patterning
text:
During development, mechanical forces play a crucial role in shaping the growth and organization of tissues. These forces can cause changes in the size, shape, number, and position of cells, as well as alter gene expression patterns. As a result, mechanical forces are essential for any process of morphogenesis, or the formation and development of tissue shape.
Two key mechanisms drive tissue morphogenesis: force generation by actin-myosin networks and force transmission through adhesive complexes. These self-organizing processes allow tissues to adapt and change in response to mechanical forces, leading to large-scale shape changes.
In addition to these local forces, long-range force transmission and mechanosensing within tissues also coordinate and integrate forces to produce tissue-wide shape changes. This interplay between tissue mechanics and biochemical signaling orchestrates the complex processes of tissue morphogenesis and patterning during development.
Extrinsic mechanical forces, such as those generated by the movement of cells or the stretching of tissues, can also modulate cell fate specification and differentiation, further controlling tissue patterning. In this way, the interplay between mechanical forces and biochemical signaling is essential for the proper formation and organization of tissues during development.

title: CD169+ MACROPHAGES PRESENT LIPID ANTIGENS TO MEDIATE EARLY ACTIVATION OF INVARIANT NKT CELLS IN LYMPH NODES
text: Invariant natural killer T cells (iNKT cells) play a crucial role in the host defense against microbial infections. While it is known that iNKT cells recognize glycolipids presented by CD1d, the exact mechanisms of how they encounter antigen in vivo have remained unclear. To investigate this, we employed multiphoton microscopy to visualize the dynamics and activation of iNKT cells in lymph nodes. Our findings revealed that after antigen administration, iNKT cells become confined in a CD1d-dependent manner near subcapsular sinus CD169(+) macrophages. These macrophages retain, internalize, and present lipid antigen, which is essential for iNKT cell activation, cytokine production, and population expansion. Our results demonstrate that CD169(+) macrophages can function as true antigen-presenting cells, controlling early iNKT cell activation and promoting the rapid initiation of immune responses.

title: Oxygen Metabolism Causes Chromosome Breaks and Is Associated with the Neuronal Apoptosis Observed in DNA Double-Strand Break Repair Mutants
text: Cells lacking a crucial DNA repair pathway (nonhomologous DNA end joining, or NHEJ) experience an increase in spontaneous chromosome breaks, but the origin of these breaks has remained a mystery. Our study reveals that reducing cellular oxygen levels partially suppresses these breaks, while overexpressing an antioxidant enzyme (superoxide dismutase 1, or SOD1) in transgenic mice leads to an increase in chromosome breaks. The effect of SOD1 can be modulated by cellular oxygen tension. Remarkably, the increased chromosome breakage in SOD1-overexpressing mice correlates with a significant increase in neuronal cell death, particularly in embryos lacking the Ku86 gene. These findings suggest that oxygen metabolism plays a central role in the genomic instability observed in NHEJ-deficient cells and, by extension, in all cells.

title: Insertional mutagenesis in gene therapy and stem cell biology.
text:
The purpose of this review is to discuss recent findings on the mechanisms of insertional mutagenesis, which occur when genes are inserted into chromosomal DNA of hematopoietic cells, potentially leading to clonal competition and the development of leukemia or sarcoma. The use of gene vectors for advanced hematopoietic cell therapies has raised concerns about biosafety, and this review aims to provide novel insights into the underlying mechanisms.
Recent studies have shown that the insertion pattern of various retroviral gene vector systems can be explained by the properties of the viral integrase and associated cellular cofactors. Cell culture assays and animal models, including disease-specific and cancer-prone mouse models, have revealed the contributions of vector features and systemic factors to the induction of clonal imbalance. Additionally, databases summarizing vector insertion sites in dominant hematopoietic clones are emerging as new tools to identify genes that regulate clonal homeostasis.
Overall, these findings have important implications for the fields of hematology, oncology, and regenerative medicine. Mechanistic studies of insertional mutagenesis will lead to improved tools for advanced hematopoietic cell therapy, while simultaneously providing fascinating insights into gene networks that regulate cell fitness.

title: Markets, voucher subsidies and free nets combine to achieve high bed net coverage in rural Tanzania
text:
In Tanzania, there is a well-established network of commercial ITN retailers. In 2004, the government introduced a voucher subsidy for pregnant women, and in mid-2005, distributed free nets to under-fives in a limited number of districts, including Rufiji on the southern coast, during a child health campaign. The study assessed the contributions of these multiple delivery strategies existing simultaneously in a poor rural community to net coverage.
The study used a cross-sectional household survey in 31 rural villages of Rufiji district, Southern Tanzania, covering 1,752 households and 6,331 members. The survey collected information on net use, treatment status, and delivery mechanism through a questionnaire administered to every consenting respondent.
The study found that 62.7% of the population used insecticide-treated nets (ITNs), with higher coverage among infants (87.2%), young children (81.8%), and older children (54.5%) compared to adults (59.6%). About 30.2% of all nets had been treated six months prior to the survey. The main sources of nets for infants were purchase from the private sector with a voucher subsidy (41.8%), while half of nets used by young children and over a third of those used by older children were obtained free of charge through the vaccination campaign. Amongst the population overall, commercial purchase was the largest source of nets (45.1% use), and it was the primary means of protecting adults (60.2% use).
The study found that all delivery mechanisms, including sale of nets at full market price, under-served the poorest, but there was no difference in equity observed between voucher-subsidized and freely distributed nets. The study concluded that all three delivery strategies enabled the community to achieve high net coverage, reaching their respective target groups. The study showed that these approaches are complementary rather than mutually exclusive, highlighting the importance of multiple delivery strategies in achieving universal coverage.

title: Human chorionic gonadotropin levels in maternal blood in late pregnancy: relation to birthweight, sex and condition of the infant at birth.
text: A total of 527 blood samples were collected from an unselected population of women aged 36-40 weeks gestation. Serum levels of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) were measured using a specific radioimmunoassay that detects the beta 1-subunit of hCG. The study found that serum hCG levels were higher in women who were pregnant for the first time (primigravidae) and in those carrying female fetuses. Additionally, there was a correlation between serum hCG levels and the birthweight of the child, as well as the occurrence of fetal distress.

title: Brain-Specific Phosphorylation of MeCP2 Regulates Activity-Dependent Bdnf Transcription, Dendritic Growth, and Spine Maturation
text:
Mutations or duplications in the MECP2 gene are associated with Rett and Rett-like syndromes, which are neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by cognitive impairments, motor dysfunction, and behavioral abnormalities. MECP2 is expressed in various mammalian tissues and functions as a global transcriptional repressor; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying how MECP2 dysfunction leads to the specific neural phenotypes of RTT remain inadequately understood.
Our study reveals that neuronal activity and subsequent calcium influx trigger the de novo phosphorylation of MECP2 at serine 421 (S421) through a CaMKII-dependent mechanism. Notably, we find that S421 phosphorylation is specifically induced in the brain in response to physiological stimuli. These findings suggest that S421 phosphorylation plays a crucial role in regulating the ability of MeCP2 to control dendritic patterning, spine morphogenesis, and the activity-dependent induction of Bdnf transcription. These findings imply that neuronal activity regulates a specific program of gene expression that mediates the maturation of the nervous system, and that disruption of this process in individuals with MeCP2 mutations may underlie the neural-specific pathology of RTT.

title: A Candidate Gene Approach Identifies the TRAF1/C5 Region as a Risk Factor for Rheumatoid Arthritis
text:
Kurreeman FAS, Padyukov L, Marques RB, Schrodi SJ, Seddighzadeh M, et al. (2007) A Candidate Gene Approach Identifies the TRAF1/C5 Region as a Risk Factor for Rheumatoid Arthritis. PLoS Med 4(9): e278. doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.0040278
In Table 1, the allele ratio in column eight (Allele Ratiosb: Cases, Controls) refers to allele A: allele B and not allele1:allele2 as described in footnote b, with Allele A being the Susceptibility Allele as denoted in column seven. The footnote should read:
bNumber of alleles were compared in cases versus controls: allele A: allele B cases, allele A: allele B controls. Allele A refers to the susceptibility alleles as given in column seven.

title: Potential use of γ-secretase modulators in the treatment of Alzheimer disease.
text: Despite significant advances in our understanding of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis over the past 20 years, we have yet to identify disease-modifying therapies that can meaningfully alter the clinical course of this prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. In this brief review, we examine two clinically tested approaches - γ-secretase inhibition and γ-secretase modulation - and highlight the distinct differences between these therapeutic strategies. Additionally, we discuss potential genetic and biomarker-based translational and clinical trial models that may help in the development of a successful therapeutic agent.

title: Rational design of a flavivirus vaccine by abolishing viral RNA 2'-O methylation.
text: Viruses that replicate in the cytoplasm are unable to access the host's nuclear capping machinery, so they have evolved viral methyltransferases to methylate the N-7 and 2'-O caps of their RNA. Alternatively, they "steal" host mRNA caps to form the 5' end of their viral RNA. The purpose of 2'-O methylation of viral RNA caps is to mimic cellular mRNA and evade the host's innate immune system. A cytoplasmic virus lacking 2'-O methylation is replicative but lacks 2'-O methylation on its RNA, making it recognized and eliminated by the host immune response. Such a mutant virus could be engineered as a live attenuated vaccine. Here, we use Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), a significant mosquito-borne flavivirus, to demonstrate this novel vaccine concept. We find that JEV methyltransferase is responsible for both N-7 and 2'-O cap methylations as well as evading the host's innate immune response. A recombinant virus completely defective in 2'-O methylation was stable in cell culture after being passaged for over 30 days. The mutant virus was attenuated in mice, elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses, and retained the engineered mutation in vivo. A single dose of immunization induced full protection against lethal challenges with JEV strains in mice. Mechanistically, the attenuation phenotype was attributed to the enhanced sensitivity of the mutant virus to the antiviral effects of interferon and IFIT proteins. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of using 2'-O methylation-defective virus as a vaccine approach, which should be applicable to other flaviviruses and non-flaviviruses that encode their own viral 2'-O methyltransferases.

title: Fruit consumption and risk of type 2 diabetes: results from three prospective longitudinal cohort studies
text:
Objective: To investigate whether different types of fruits are associated with a lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
Design: Prospective longitudinal cohort study.
Setting: Health professionals in the United States.
Participants: 66,105 women from the Nurses' Health Study (1984-2008), 85,104 women from the Nurses' Health Study II (1991-2009), and 36,173 men from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study (1986-2008) who were free of major chronic diseases at baseline in these studies.
Main Outcome Measure: Incident cases of type 2 diabetes, identified through self-report and confirmed by supplementary questionnaires.
Results: During 3,464,641 person-years of follow-up, 12,198 participants developed type 2 diabetes. After adjusting for personal, lifestyle, and dietary risk factors for diabetes, the pooled hazard ratio for every three servings of total whole fruit consumption per week was 0.98 (95% confidence interval 0.97 to 0.99). With mutual adjustment of individual fruits, the pooled hazard ratios of type 2 diabetes for every three servings per week were 0.74 (0.66 to 0.83) for blueberries, 0.88 (0.83 to 0.93) for grapes and raisins, 0.89 (0.79 to 1.01) for prunes, 0.93 (0.90 to 0.96) for apples and pears, 0.95 (0.91 to 0.98) for bananas, 0.95 (0.91 to 0.99) for grapefruit, 0.97 (0.92 to 1.02) for peaches, plums, and apricots, 0.99 (0.95 to 1.03) for oranges, 1.03 (0.96 to 1.10) for strawberries, and 1.10 (1.02 to 1.18) for cantaloupe. The pooled hazard ratio for the same increment in fruit juice consumption was 1.08 (1.05 to 1.11). The associations with the risk of type 2 diabetes differed significantly among individual fruits (P < 0.001 in all cohorts).
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that the associations between individual fruit consumption and the risk of type 2 diabetes are heterogeneous. Greater consumption of specific whole fruits, particularly blueberries, grapes, and apples, is significantly associated with a lower risk of type 2 diabetes, whereas greater consumption of fruit juice is associated with a higher risk.

title: OncomiR-196 promotes an invasive phenotype in oral cancer through the NME4-JNK-TIMP1-MMP signaling pathway
text:
Background: MicroRNA-196 (miR-196) has been found to be highly up-regulated in oral cancer cells, and its significance in oral cancer has not been fully elucidated.
Methods: To investigate the functional impact of miR-196 in oral cancer, we examined cellular responses to miR-196 modulation, including cell growth, migration, invasion, and radio/chemosensitivity. An algorithm-based approach was used to identify the regulatory target of miR-196. The miR-196 target gene and downstream molecular mechanisms were confirmed through RT-qPCR, western blot, luciferase reporter, and confocal microscopy analyses. miR-196 expression was also determined in paired cancer and adjacent normal tissues from oral cancer patients.
Results: Our results showed that both miR-196a and miR-196b were highly over-expressed in cancer tissues and correlated with lymph node metastasis (P = 0.001 and P = 0.006, respectively). Functional assays revealed that miR-196 promoted cell migration and invasion without affecting cell growth. Mechanistic studies revealed that miR-196 inhibited NME4 expression and activated p-JNK, suppressed TIMP1, and augmented MMP1/9.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that miR-196 contributes to oral cancer by promoting cell migration and invasion. Clinically, miR-196a/b was significantly over-expressed in cancer tissues and correlated with lymph node metastasis. These findings provide new insights into the underlying mechanisms of cancer metastasis and may serve as a promising marker for better oral cancer management.

title: Reverse engineering of TLX oncogenic transcriptional networks identifies RUNX1 as tumor suppressor in T-ALL
text: The TLX1 and TLX3 transcription factor oncogenes play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL). By employing reverse engineering of global transcriptional networks, we uncovered the oncogenic regulatory circuit controlled by TLX1 and TLX3. This systems biology analysis designated T cell leukemia homeobox 1 (TLX1) and TLX3 as master regulators of an oncogenic transcriptional circuit governing T-ALL. Interestingly, a network structure analysis of this hierarchical network revealed RUNX1 as a crucial mediator of T-ALL induced by TLX1 and TLX3, and predicted a tumor-suppressor role for RUNX1 in T cell transformation. Consistently, we found recurrent somatic loss-of-function mutations in RUNX1 in human T-ALL. These findings position TLX1 and TLX3 at the apex of an oncogenic transcriptional network controlling leukemia development, highlight the power of network analyses to identify key elements in the regulatory circuits governing human cancer, and designate RUNX1 as a tumor-suppressor gene in T-ALL.

title: The Impact of the New WHO Antiretroviral Treatment Guidelines on HIV Epidemic Dynamics and Cost in South Africa
text:
Since November 2009, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends that adults infected with HIV should start antiretroviral therapy (ART) at CD4+ cell counts of ≤350 cells/µl, rather than ≤200 cells/µl. However, South Africa has only adopted this strategy for pregnant and tuberculosis (TB) co-infected patients. To assess the impact of fully implementing the new WHO guidelines on the HIV epidemic dynamics and associated costs, we used a model of HIV transmission and control in a specified population in Hlabisa subdistrict, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
We found that under the new guidelines, there will be a 7% increase in annual investments during the first five years, resulting in 28% more patients receiving treatment. However, there will be a more significant impact on HIV incidence, leading to lower annual costs after seven years. The cumulative net costs will reach a break-even point after approximately 16 years.
Our findings support the WHO recommendation of starting ART at ≤350 cells/µl for all HIV-infected patients. Apart from the benefits associated with many life-years saved, a modest frontloading of treatment appears to lead to net savings within a limited time-horizon. This finding is robust to alternative assumptions and foreseeable changes in ART prices and effectiveness. Therefore, South Africa should aim to rapidly expand its healthcare infrastructure to fully embrace the new WHO guidelines.

title: ER-associated mitochondrial division links the distribution of mitochondria and mitochondrial DNA in yeast
text: Mitochondrial division is crucial for the proper distribution and function of mitochondria within cells. Recent research has shown that ER-mitochondria interactions are important for mitochondrial division sites, but the molecular mechanisms behind these interactions are not fully understood. In this study, we investigate the role of the ER-mitochondria tethering complex, ERMES, and the highly conserved Miro GTPase, Gem1, in ER-associated mitochondrial division in yeast. Our findings reveal that Gem1 acts as a negative regulator of ER-mitochondria contacts, which is essential for the proper distribution and function of newly generated mitochondrial tips following division. Previous studies have shown that ERMES localizes to a subset of actively replicating mitochondrial nucleoids. Our results demonstrate that mitochondrial division is spatially linked to these nucleoids, and that a majority of these nucleoids segregate before division, resulting in their distribution into newly generated tips in the mitochondrial network. Therefore, we propose that ER-associated mitochondrial division plays a crucial role in linking the distribution of mitochondria and mitochondrial nucleoids in cells. DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.7554/eLife.00422.001.

title: BMI-1 Autoantibody as a New Potential Biomarker for Cervical Carcinoma
text: In this study, we investigated the potential of BMI-1 autoantibodies as a biomarker for cervical carcinoma. We analyzed the levels of BMI-1 autoantibodies in serum samples from 67 patients with cervical carcinoma and 65 controls using ELISA and immunoblot. Our results showed that BMI-1 autoantibody levels were significantly higher in patient sera than in normal sera, and the levels increased gradually during the tumor progression. We also found that the BMI-1 autoantibody level could be used as a biomarker for cervical carcinoma with a sensitivity of 0.78 and specificity of 0.76, and an area under the ROC curve of 0.922. These findings suggest that measuring BMI-1 autoantibody levels in patients with cervical cancer may have clinical prognostic value and could potentially be used as a non-tissue specific biomarker for neoplasms expressing BMI-1.

title: MicroRNAs can generate thresholds in target gene expression
text: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small, highly conserved non-coding RNA molecules that regulate gene expression by repressing protein production in a sequence-specific manner. To investigate the dynamics of miRNA-mediated regulation at the single-cell level, we employed quantitative fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry to monitor the expression of a target gene in the presence and absence of miRNA regulation. Our findings reveal that, although the average level of repression is in line with previous population-based measurements, the degree of repression varies significantly among individual cells. Specifically, we demonstrate that miRNAs establish a threshold level of target mRNA below which protein production is severely repressed. Near this threshold, protein expression exhibits a sensitive response to changes in target mRNA input, consistent with a mathematical model of molecular titration. These results demonstrate that miRNAs can function both as a binary switch and as a fine-tuner of gene expression.

title: Oncogenic mTOR signaling recruits myeloid-derived suppressor cells to promote tumor initiation
text: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) play a crucial role in both primary and metastatic cancer progression. However, the regulation of MDSCs is highly variable even among patients with the same type of malignancy, and the underlying mechanisms are largely unexplored. To investigate this phenomenon, we integrated human tumor genomics and syngeneic mammary tumor models, revealing that mTOR signaling in cancer cells dictates the ability of a mammary tumor to recruit MDSCs through regulating G-CSF. Inhibiting this pathway or its activators, such as FGFR, impairs tumor progression, which is partially rescued by restoring MDSCs or G-CSF. Tumor-initiating cells (TICs) exhibit elevated G-CSF levels, and MDSCs reciprocally increase TIC frequency through activating Notch in tumor cells, forming a feedforward loop. Our findings in primary breast cancers and patient-derived xenografts corroborate these mechanisms in patients, demonstrating a non-canonical oncogenic role of mTOR signaling in recruiting pro-tumorigenic MDSCs. These findings also reveal how defined cancer subsets may evolve to promote and depend on a distinct immune microenvironment.

title: Management of women who have a genetic predisposition for breast cancer.
text: The management of women with a genetic predisposition to breast cancer necessitates meticulous planning. Women with BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations are at a higher risk of developing breast cancer and other cancers, such as ovarian cancer. Common strategies used in the management of these patients include screening, prophylactic surgery, and chemoprevention. However, there are no randomized prospective trials that have evaluated the effectiveness of these strategies specifically in mutation carriers. It is important to inform all patients that these measures have the potential to cause harm as well as provide benefit.

title: Astrocytes from Familial and Sporadic ALS Patients are Toxic to Motor Neurons
text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder that primarily affects motor neurons. While astrocytes have been implicated in the pathology of ALS, their role in the disease is not fully understood, particularly in the majority of sporadic cases (SALS) that account for over 90% of all ALS patients. Using postmortem astrocytes derived from both familial (FALS) and sporadic ALS patients, we demonstrate that astrocytes from both patient groups are toxic to motor neurons. Additionally, we show that the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene, which accounts for less than 2% of all ALS cases, is a viable target for SALS, as its knockdown significantly attenuates astrocyte-mediated toxicity towards motor neurons. Our findings highlight the non-cell autonomous nature of SALS and provide an in vitro model system to investigate common disease mechanisms and evaluate potential therapies for both FALS and SALS.

title: High-intensity functional exercise program and protein-enriched energy supplement for older persons dependent in activities of daily living: a randomised controlled trial.
text: The purpose of this randomized controlled trial was to investigate the impact of a high-intensity functional exercise program on balance, gait ability, and lower-limb strength in older adults who are dependent in activities of daily living. The study also aimed to determine whether consuming a protein-enriched energy supplement immediately after exercise sessions enhances the effects of the training. A total of 191 older adults living in residential care facilities and with a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of ≤10 were randomly assigned to either a high-intensity functional exercise program or a control activity, and to either a protein-enriched energy supplement or a placebo. The participants underwent assessments of Berg Balance Scale, self-paced gait speed, and one-repetition maximum lower-limb strength at three and six months, and the data were analyzed using 2 x 2 factorial ANCOVA with the intention-to-treat principle. The results showed that the exercise group exhibited significant improvements in self-paced gait speed at three months compared to the control group (mean difference 0.04 m/s, p = 0.02), and at six months, there were significant improvements favoring the exercise group for Berg Balance Scale (1.9 points, p = 0.05), self-paced gait speed (0.05 m/s, p = 0.009), and lower-limb strength (10.8 kg, p = 0.03). No interaction effects were observed between the exercise and nutrition interventions. In conclusion, the study found that a high-intensity functional exercise program has positive long-term effects on balance, gait ability, and lower-limb strength in older adults who are dependent in activities of daily living. The addition of a protein-enriched energy supplement after exercise sessions did not appear to enhance the effects of the training.

title: Inhibition of fatty acid oxidation modulates immunosuppressive functions of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and enhances cancer therapies
text: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) promote tumor growth by suppressing T-cell immunity and fostering malignant cell proliferation and migration. Despite the potential of blocking MDSC in tumors, their heterogeneity, plasticity, and resistance to various chemotherapy agents have limited therapeutic approaches. Recent studies have highlighted the role of energy metabolic pathways in the differentiation and function of immune cells, yet the metabolic mechanisms regulating MDSC remain unclear. To investigate, we aimed to identify the energy metabolic pathway(s) employed by MDSC, assess its impact on their immunosuppressive function, and evaluate whether inhibition of this pathway enhances antitumor therapies. Using various mouse tumor models, we found that tumor-infiltrating MDSC (T-MDSC) exhibited increased fatty acid uptake and activated fatty acid oxidation (FAO). This was accompanied by elevated mitochondrial mass, upregulation of key FAO enzymes, and increased oxygen consumption rate. Pharmacological inhibition of FAO in T-MDSC blocked immune inhibitory pathways and functions, decreased production of inhibitory cytokines, and significantly delayed tumor growth in a T-cell-dependent manner. In addition, FAO inhibition combined with low-dose chemotherapy completely inhibited T-MDSC immunosuppressive effects and induced a substantial antitumor effect. Interestingly, similar increases in fatty acid uptake and FAO-related enzyme expression were observed in human MDSC in peripheral blood and tumors. These findings support the potential of testing FAO inhibition as a novel approach to block MDSC and enhance various cancer therapies.

title: Predicting mortality of patients hospitalized for acutely exacerbated chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
text:
Purpose: To identify factors that influence the short-term prognosis of patients with acutely exacerbated chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Patients and Methods: Retrospective analysis of 590 patients with COPD hospitalized in a university hospital's pulmonology unit between 1981 and 1990. A standardized protocol for treating acute COPD exacerbations was used for all patients. Two observers collected 23 clinical and laboratory variables defining the patients' status on admission, including age and arterial gas data. Interobserver reproducibility was evaluated using kappa statistics and Spearman's rank correlation for dichotomous and continuous variables, respectively. Univariate analysis and logistic regression analysis were used to assess the relationship between clinical and laboratory factors and mortality.
Results: Mortality rate was 14.4%. Logistic regression analysis identified four independent predictors of death: age (odds ratio [OR] 1.07; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04 to 1.11), alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient greater than 41 mm Hg (OR 2.33; 95% CI 1.39 to 3.90), ventricular arrhythmias (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.10 to 3.31), and atrial fibrillation (OR 2.27; 95% CI 1.14 to 4.51).
Conclusions: Patients with acutely exacerbated COPD at high risk of death can be identified at admission. Heart dysfunction variables are important predictors of this risk. Among pulmonary function data, only alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient contributes to the predictive model.

title: Clathrin is required for the function of the mitotic spindle
text: Clathrin plays a crucial role in the formation of vesicles that transport membranes and proteins throughout the cell. However, its function goes beyond this, as it also stabilizes the fibers of the mitotic spindle during cell division. In non-dividing cells, clathrin forms coated vesicles continuously, but during mitosis, it concentrates at the spindle apparatus. Here, we show that clathrin directly binds to the spindle fibers through its amino-terminal domain, which helps to align chromosomes during metaphase. Depletion of clathrin heavy chain using RNA interference leads to destabilization of kinetochore fibers, resulting in defective congression of chromosomes and persistent activation of the spindle checkpoint. Interestingly, the unique structure of clathrin is essential for its function in stabilizing kinetochore fibers, as only the triskelia (a structural subunit of clathrin) can rescue normal mitosis. The importance of clathrin in mitosis may have implications for understanding human cancers that involve gene fusions of clathrin heavy chain.

title: The origin and neuronal function of in vivo nonsynaptic glutamate.
text:
In vivo, basal levels of glutamate in the extracellular space outside the synaptic cleft are present in micromolar concentrations, but the origin and function of this glutamate are unknown. This study investigated the contribution of nonvesicular glutamate release from the cystine-glutamate antiporter to in vivo extracellular glutamate levels in the rat striatum.
Blockade of glutamate release from the cystine-glutamate antiporter resulted in a significant decrease (60%) in extrasynaptic glutamate levels, while blockade of voltage-dependent Na+ and Ca2+ channels produced relatively minimal changes (0-30%). These findings suggest that the primary source of in vivo extrasynaptic glutamate in the striatum is nonvesicular release from the cystine-glutamate antiporter.
To further investigate the mechanism of nonvesicular glutamate release, the study measured [35S]cystine uptake and found that it was negatively regulated by group II metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR2/3) via a cAMP-dependent protein kinase mechanism. Extracellular glutamate derived from the antiporter was shown to regulate extracellular levels of glutamate and dopamine. Infusion of the mGluR2/3 antagonist (RS)-1-amino-5-phosphonoindan-1-carboxylic acid (APICA) increased extracellular glutamate levels, and previous blockade of the antiporter prevented the APICA-induced rise in extracellular glutamate. These results suggest that glutamate released from the antiporter is a source of endogenous tone on mGluR2/3. Blockade of the antiporter also produced an increase in extracellular dopamine that was reversed by infusing the mGluR2/3 agonist (2R,4R)-4-aminopyrrolidine-2,4-dicarboxlylate, indicating that antiporter-derived glutamate can modulate dopamine transmission via mGluR2/3 heteroreceptors.
In conclusion, this study demonstrates that nonvesicular release from the cystine-glutamate antiporter is the primary source of in vivo extracellular glutamate and that this glutamate can modulate both glutamate and dopamine transmission.

title: Disease-associated functions of IL-33: the new kid in the IL-1 family
text: Interleukin-33 (IL-33), a recently identified member of the IL-1 family, is produced by a wide range of cells in response to pro-inflammatory stimuli and is believed to be released upon cell lysis. The IL-33 receptor, consisting of the ST2 receptor and the IL-1 receptor accessory protein, is ubiquitously expressed, with particularly high levels on T helper 2 (TH2) cells and mast cells. IL-33 has been shown to be host-protective against helminth infection and reduces atherosclerosis by promoting TH2-type immune responses. However, IL-33 can also contribute to the pathogenesis of various diseases, such as asthma, by expanding TH2 cells and mediating joint inflammation, atopic dermatitis, and anaphylaxis through mast cell activation. As such, IL-33 represents a potential new target for therapeutic intervention across a broad spectrum of diseases.

title: Interferon alpha therapy for hepatitis C: treatment completion and response rates among patients with substance use disorders
text:
Individuals with a history of substance use disorders (SUDs) are at increased risk of contracting hepatitis C viral infection (HCV). However, few studies have examined the treatment responses of these individuals empirically. This study aimed to assess the completion and response rates of interferon alpha therapy (IFN) among patients with HCV who had a history of comorbid SUDs.
Using a medical record database, information was retrospectively collected on 307,437 veterans seen in Veterans Integrated Service Network 20 (VISN 20) of the Veterans Healthcare Administration (VHA) between 1998 and 2003. The study compared the IFN completion and response rates among patients with a history of SUD (SUD+ Group) and patients without a history of SUD (SUD- Group).
The results of the study revealed that the odds ratio analyses showed that the SUD+ Group was equally likely to complete IFN therapy if they had genotypes 2 and 3 (73.1% vs. 68.0%) and if they had genotypes 1 and 4 (39.5% vs. 39.9%). Within the sample of all patients who began IFN therapy, the SUD- and SUD+ groups were similarly likely to achieve an end of treatment response (genotypes 2 and 3, 52.8% vs. 54.3%; genotypes 1 and 4, 24.5% vs. 24.8%) and a sustained viral response (genotypes 2 and 3, 42.6% vs. 41.1%; genotypes 1 and 4: 16.0% vs. 22.3%).
The conclusion of the study suggests that individuals with and without a history of SUD responded to antiviral therapy for HCV at similar rates. These findings imply that patients who have co-morbid SUD and HCV diagnoses can successfully complete a course of antiviral therapy.

title: Association between infection with Helicobacter pylori and risk of gastric cancer: evidence from a prospective investigation.
text:
Objective: To investigate the association between gastric cancer and prior infection with Helicobacter pylori.
Design: A case-control study comparing the prevalence of IgG antibodies to H pylori in blood samples collected prospectively before diagnosis of gastric cancer in cases.
Subjects: 29 men with a subsequent diagnosis of gastric cancer and 116 aged-matched controls selected from over 22,000 middle-aged men participating in two ongoing cohort studies (the British United Provident Association study and the Caerphilly Collaborative Heart Disease Study), who provided blood samples during 1975-1982.
Results: Of the 29 cases (69%), 54 of the 116 controls (47%) were positive for H pylori-specific antibody. The median specific IgG concentration was significantly higher in the cases than controls (90 micrograms/ml vs 3.6 micrograms/ml, p < 0.01). The estimated odds ratio for the risk of gastric cancer in those with a history of infection with H pylori was 2.77 (95% confidence interval 1.04-7.97, p = 0.039).
Conclusions: H pylori infection may be an important cause of gastric cancer, with between 35% and 55% of all cases associated with such an infection.

title: Oncostatin M and leukemia inhibitory factor do not use the same functional receptor in mice.
text: Oncostatin M (OSM) and leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) are members of the interleukin-6 (IL-6) cytokine subfamily that utilize a common signal transducer, gp130. Human OSM (hOSM) and LIF share a high-affinity receptor composed of gp130 and LIF receptor beta subunit (LIFRbeta). However, the receptor structure of murine OSM (mOSM) remained unknown until the recent cloning of its cDNA. Using recombinant mOSM, we investigated its biological activity and receptor structure in various cell lines. Murine hematopoietic cell lines M1 and DA1.a, an embryonic stem cell line CCE, and Ba/F3 transfectants expressing gp130 and LIFRbeta responded to murine LIF (mLIF) and hOSM with equal sensitivity, while they responded to mOSM only at a 30- to 100-fold higher concentration than mLIF and hOSM. In contrast, NIH3T3 cells responded to mOSM, but not to mLIF and hOSM. Scatchard plot analyses revealed that mOSM bound to gp130 with low affinity (Kd = 2.8-4.2 nmol/L), and the binding affinity did not increase in the presence of LIFRbeta. However, mOSM bound to NIH3T3 cells with high affinity (Kd = 660 pmol/L), whereas mLIF did not bind to NIH3T3 cells at all. These findings indicate that mOSM and mLIF do not share the same functional receptor, and mOSM signals through its unique receptor complex. Further studies in mice will elucidate the physiological roles of OSM.

title: Multifunctional in vivo vascular imaging using near-infrared II fluorescence
text: In vivo real-time epifluorescence imaging of mouse hind limb vasculatures in the second near-infrared region (NIR-II) is performed using single-walled carbon nanotubes as fluorophores, achieving both high spatial (∼30 μm) and temporal (<200 ms per frame) resolution for small-vessel imaging at 1–3 mm deep in the hind limb. This is made possible by the beneficial NIR-II optical window, which provides deep anatomical penetration and low scattering, allowing for unattainable spatial resolution by traditional NIR imaging (NIR-I) or microscopic computed tomography, and far exceeding scanning microscopic imaging techniques in terms of temporal resolution. Arterial and venous vessels are differentiated using a dynamic contrast-enhanced NIR-II imaging technique based on their distinct hemodynamics. Furthermore, the deep tissue penetration and high spatial and temporal resolution of NIR-II imaging enable precise quantifications of blood velocity in both normal and ischemic femoral arteries, surpassing the capabilities of ultrasonography at lower blood velocities.

title: Colorectal cancer survival in socioeconomic groups in England: variation is mainly in the short term after diagnosis.
text:
This study aimed to investigate differences in cancer survival rates between socioeconomic groups in England, with a particular focus on short-term survival.
The study population consisted of individuals diagnosed with colorectal cancer between 1996 and 2004 in England, identified through cancer registry records. The study examined five-year cumulative relative survival and excess death rates in the first month and subsequent periods after diagnosis.
The results showed that there was a high excess death rate in the first month of follow-up for colon cancer, with the highest rates observed in socioeconomically deprived groups. In subsequent periods, excess mortality rates were lower, and there was less variation in socioeconomic groups. A similar pattern was observed in rectal cancer, although the socioeconomic difference in death rates persisted for a longer period of time.
If the excess death rates in the entire colorectal cancer patient population were the same as those observed in the most affluent socioeconomic quintile, the annual reduction in deaths would be 360 in colon cancer and 336 in rectal cancer patients. These deaths occurred primarily in the first month and first year after diagnosis.
The findings of this study provide strong support for the use of short-term cancer survival as an operational measure of variation and progress in cancer control, as recent developments in the national cancer control agenda have emphasized the importance of outcome measures.

title: Cardiac myocyte remodeling mediated by N-cadherin-dependent mechanosensing.
text: Cell-to-cell adhesions play a crucial role in maintaining the structural and functional integrity of cardiac cells. While most studies have focused on cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, this study investigates the direct role of intercellular adhesion in the morphology and internal organization of neonatal ventricular cardiac myocytes. The results show that cadherin-mediated cell attachments can elicit a cytoskeletal network response similar to that of integrin-mediated force response and transmission, affecting myofibrillar organization, myocyte shape, and cortical stiffness. Traction forces mediated by N-cadherin were found to be comparable to those sustained by ECM, and the mechanical sensitivity of N-cadherin was higher than that of ECM. The cytoskeletal architecture of myocytes on an N-cadherin adhesive microenvironment was found to be different from that on an ECM environment, suggesting that the two mechanotransductive cell adhesion systems may play both independent and complementary roles in myocyte cytoskeletal spatial organization. These findings indicate that cell-to-cell-mediated force perception and transmission are involved in the organization and development of cardiac structure and function.

title: NEAT1: A novel cancer‐related long non‐coding RNA
text: Aberrant expression of the long non-coding RNA NEAT1 (nuclear paraspeckle assembly transcript 1) has been observed in various types of solid tumors, including lung, oesophageal, colorectal, and hepatocellular carcinoma, where it is associated with poor prognosis. In contrast, NEAT1 is downregulated in acute promyelocytic leukemia, where it promotes leukocyte differentiation. This review aims to provide an overview of the current evidence regarding the oncogenic role and potential clinical applications of NEAT1. Further research is needed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of NEAT1 overexpression.

title: The Function and Therapeutic Potential of Long Non-coding RNAs in Cardiovascular Development and Disease
text: The advent of genome-wide analysis and RNA sequencing has led to a groundbreaking discovery: a significant portion of the human genome, though transcribed, does not encode proteins. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as crucial regulators of gene expression in both healthy and diseased states. By studying lncRNAs in the heart, along with gene association studies, we have found that these molecules are regulated during cardiovascular development and disease. Some lncRNAs have been implicated in cardiac pathophysiology and hold promise as therapeutic targets. Here, we review the current understanding of the function of lncRNAs in the cardiovascular system, with a focus on cardiovascular development and biology, and their implications in hypertension, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, ischemia, and heart failure. We also discuss the challenges of lncRNA research and provide directions for future studies with translational focus.

title: Oct4 links multiple epigenetic pathways to the pluripotency network
text: Oct4 is a transcription factor of paramount importance in stem cell self-renewal, pluripotency, and somatic cell reprogramming. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying Oct4's regulatory activities remain poorly understood due to a lack of information on its associated protein complexes and intrinsic protein-protein interactions. To address this knowledge gap, we employed an improved affinity purification approach combined with mass spectrometry to investigate Oct4 protein complexes in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Our findings uncovered a multitude of novel Oct4 partners that play critical roles in the self-renewal and pluripotency of mESCs. Of particular note, we discovered that Oct4 interacts with multiple chromatin-modifying complexes, some of which have been previously implicated in stem cell maintenance and somatic cell reprogramming, while others represent novel findings. Our study provides a solid biochemical foundation for understanding the genetic and epigenetic regulation of stem cell pluripotency and offers a framework for exploring alternative factor-based reprogramming strategies.

title: Tet1 is dispensable for maintaining pluripotency and its loss is compatible with embryonic and postnatal development.
text: The Tet family of enzymes (Tet1/2/3) plays a crucial role in the conversion of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). mESCs exhibit high levels of Tet1 expression, which is essential for maintaining pluripotency and lineage commitment. However, the precise function of Tet1 in development remains unclear. To elucidate the role of Tet1 in pluripotency and development, we generated Tet1 mutant mESCs and mice. Our findings reveal that Tet1(-/-) ESCs have reduced levels of 5hmC and subtle changes in global gene expression, and are still pluripotent and capable of generating live-born mice in tetraploid complementation assays. However, Tet1 mutant mice display a slight reduction in body size at birth and a bias towards trophectoderm differentiation in vitro. Our results suggest that Tet1 loss leads to a partial reduction in 5hmC levels without compromising pluripotency in ESCs, and is compatible with embryonic and postnatal development.

title: LDL-cholesterol concentrations: a genome-wide association study
text: The background of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol has a significant role in the development of cardiovascular disease. To gain a deeper understanding of the biological mechanisms that regulate LDL cholesterol, we conducted a genome-wide association study of LDL-cholesterol concentrations in up to 11,685 participants. Our study identified two novel genetic variants (rs599839 and rs4970834) associated with LDL cholesterol at chromosomal locus 1p13.3. Subsequent analyses revealed a third statistically associated SNP (rs646776) at the same locus. Meta-analysis of data from all studies showed that these SNPs were significantly associated with LDL-cholesterol concentrations, explaining around 1% of the variation in circulating LDL-cholesterol concentrations and being associated with about 15% of an SD change in LDL cholesterol per allele. These findings provide new insights into the biological mechanisms that regulate LDL cholesterol and may lead to the discovery of novel therapeutic targets for cardiovascular disease.

title: Population Density, Water Supply, and the Risk of Dengue Fever in Vietnam: Cohort Study and Spatial Analysis
text: Background: Aedes aegypti, the primary vector of dengue viruses, frequently breeds in water storage containers utilized by households without access to tap water, and exhibits a high prevalence in densely populated urban areas. To identify geographic regions at highest risk of dengue fever outbreaks, we conducted an individual-level cohort study in a population of 75,000 geo-referenced households in Vietnam over the course of two epidemics, using dengue hospital admissions (n = 3,013). Methods and Findings: We employed space-time scan statistics and mathematical modeling to confirm our findings.
