Furthermore, the stimulatory effects of neuron-conditioned medium on glial glutamate transporter expression are attenuated in the presence of PACAP-inactivating antibodies or the PACAP receptor antagonist PACAP 6-38. In contrast, vasoactive intestinal peptide promotes glutamate transporter expression at higher concentrations, suggesting that PACAP exerts its effects on glial glutamate turnover via PAC1 receptors. While PKA activation is sufficient to promote GLAST expression, both PKA and PKC activation are required to optimize GLT-1 expression. The existence of multiple PAC1 receptor isoforms that activate PKA and PKC to different levels suggests a complex mechanism by which PACAP regulates glial glutamate transport and metabolism. Disturbances in these regulatory mechanisms may contribute to glutamate-associated neurological and psychiatric disorders.

title: Factors influencing B lymphopoiesis after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
text: In 93 allograft recipients, the correlation between the numbers of marrow B-cell precursors on days 80 and 365 and the counts of circulating B cells suggested that the post-transplantation B-cell deficiency is at least partially due to insufficient B lymphopoiesis. To investigate the factors that may affect B lymphopoiesis, the study evaluated the number of marrow B-cell precursors on days 30, 80, and 365 in patients with different grades of acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and extensive chronic GVHD. The results showed that the number of B-cell precursors was significantly lower in patients with grade 2 to 4 acute GVHD compared to those with grade 0 to 1 acute GVHD, and was 18-fold lower in patients with extensive chronic GVHD compared to those with no or limited chronic GVHD. The study concluded that post-transplantation B-cell deficiency is likely due to inhibition of B lymphopoiesis by GVHD and/or its treatment. The study did not find any significant relationship between B-cell precursor numbers and other factors such as CD34 cell dose, type of transplant (marrow versus blood stem cells), donor age, or patient age.

title: Genetic variants rs1994016 and rs3825807 in ADAMTS7 affect its mRNA expression in atherosclerotic occlusive peripheral arterial disease
text:
Introduction:
PeriPeripheral artery disease (PAD) is a vascular condition that affects the circulation in the peripheral regions of the body. Recent genome-wide association studies have identified a relationship between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in ADAMTS7 (a disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin motif 7) and atherosclerosis. This study aimed to investigate the expression of ADAMTS7 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the frequency of ADAMTS7 SNPs in a sample of Turkish patients with PAD, as well as to evaluate the association between matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) levels and PAD development.
Methods:
This case-control study included 115 PAD patients and 116 healthy controls. ADAMTS7 mRNA and protein expression was determined using reverse transcription quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot, respectively. The frequencies of ADAMTS7 SNPs (rs1994016 and rs3825807) were determined by real-time PCR in both groups. Plasma levels of nine MMPs were measured using a multiplex immunoassay system.
Results:
ADAMTS7 mRNA levels were significantly higher in PAD patients than in controls (t=-2.75, P=.007). There was no significant difference in the frequencies of ADAMTS7 SNPs between PAD patients and controls (P>.05). In PAD patients, ADAMTS7 mRNA levels were significantly increased for the CC genotype of rs1994016 (t=-2.31, P=.026) and TT genotype of rs3825807 (t=-2.23, P=.032). Furthermore, plasma levels of MMP-1, MMP-3, MMP-7, MMP-10, MMP-12, and MMP-13 were significantly higher in PAD patients than in controls (P<.05).
Conclusion:
This study is the first to investigate the relationship between PAD and ADAMTS7 expression, as well as the effects of ADAMTS7 SNPs on PAD development. Our findings suggest that ADAMTS7 may be associated with PAD development. Additionally, our study highlights the importance of MMP levels in the development of PAD.

title: Distinct Parietal and Temporal Pathways to the Homologues of Broca's Area in the Monkey
text:
In a recent study, the author investigated the connections between the ventrolateral frontal cortex and the parietal and temporal association areas in the macaque monkey. The study used the autoradiographic method to trace the pathways of axons from various cortical areas in the intermediate superolateral temporal region, inferior parietal lobule, and caudal superior temporal sulcus to the homologues of Broca's region in the macaque monkey.
The results showed that there are two main streams of axons that project to Broca's region: a ventral temporo-frontal stream that originates from auditory, multisensory, and visual association cortical areas in the intermediate superolateral temporal region, and a dorsal stream that originates from cortical areas in the inferior parietal lobule and the adjacent caudal superior temporal sulcus. The ventral stream targets area 45 more strongly than area 44, while the dorsal stream targets both areas 44 and 45.
The cortex of the most rostral part of the inferior parietal lobule was found to be preferentially linked with the ventral premotor cortex (ventral area 6), which controls the orofacial musculature. The cortex of the intermediate part of the inferior parietal lobule was linked with both areas 44 and 45. These findings demonstrate the posterior parietal and temporal connections of the ventrolateral frontal areas in the macaque monkey, which are similar to the connections found in the human brain.
The study provides new insights into the prelinguistic precursor circuitry of Broca's region and highlights the functional interactions between Broca's ventrolateral frontal region and posterior parietal and temporal association areas. The results suggest that these areas were adapted for language production in the human brain, and provide a basis for understanding the evolution of language in the primate brain.

title: MIRA-seq for DNA methylation analysis of CpG islands
text:
Objective:
To develop a reliable method for comprehensive genome-wide analysis of DNA methylation.
Materials and Methods:
Whole-genome analysis of DNA methylation involves techniques that utilize affinity-based approaches, such as enrichment using methyl-CpG-binding proteins. One such method, the methylated-CpG island recovery assay (MIRA), is based on the high affinity of the MBD2b-MBD3L1 complex for CpG-methylated DNA. Here, we provide a detailed description of MIRA and its combination with next-generation sequencing platforms (MIRA-seq).
Results:
We evaluated the performance of MIRA-seq and compared the data with whole-genome bisulfite sequencing.

Conclusion:
MIRA-seq is a reliable, genome-scale DNA methylation analysis platform for detecting DNA methylation differences at CpG-rich genomic regions. The method is not limited by primer or probe design and is cost-effective.

title: How many images are in an auditory scene?
text: If an auditory scene contains multiple spatially separated sound sources, how many of these sources can the auditory system process? Experiment I aimed to determine the maximum number of speech sources that listeners can localize simultaneously on the azimuth plane. Participants were presented with different words played from multiple loudspeakers, and reported the total number of sound sources and their individual locations. In experiment II, the accuracy of localizing a single speech source in a mixture of multiple speech sources was investigated. An additional sound source was added to a pre-existing set of sound sources, and participants were asked to localize this extra source. The results showed that the maximum number of sound sources that listeners can perceive is approximately four spatially separated speech signals, and three for tonal signals. As the total number of sound sources increases, localization errors also increase. When four or more speech sources are already present, the accuracy in localizing an additional source is near chance.

title: Mobilization of intracellular copper stores by the ctr2 vacuolar copper transporter.
text: Copper plays a crucial role in various cellular processes, including signaling, transcription, protein transport, iron mobilization, neuropeptide maturation, and development. While much is known about the intracellular transport of ions like calcium, little is understood about how eukaryotic cells mobilize their intracellular copper stores. This study uncovers a mechanism by which the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ctr2 protein releases bioavailable copper by mobilizing intracellular copper reserves. Contrary to its structural similarity to the Ctr1 plasma membrane copper importer, Ctr2 is localized to the vacuole membrane through microscopic and biochemical fractionation analyses. Our findings demonstrate that Ctr2 mobilizes vacuolar copper stores in a manner dependent on conserved amino acid residues shared by the Ctr1 and Ctr2 copper transport family, resulting in ctr2 Delta mutants accumulating excessive vacuolar copper. Moreover, a Ctr2 mutant with mislocalization to the plasma membrane stimulates extracellular copper uptake, supporting a direct role for Ctr2 in copper transport across membranes. These studies reveal a novel copper mobilization mechanism and suggest that organisms cope with copper deficiency by utilizing intracellular vesicular stores.

title: Peroxisomes Are Signaling Platforms for Antiviral Innate Immunity
text: For years, peroxisomes have been recognized as key players in regulating various metabolic processes in mammalian cells. These organelles work in conjunction with mitochondria to control lipid and reactive oxygen species metabolism. However, while mitochondria have been shown to play a crucial role in antiviral signal transduction, the role of peroxisomes in immune defense remained unexplored. Here, we investigate the distribution of the RIG-I-like receptor (RLR) adaptor protein MAVS on peroxisomes and mitochondria. Our findings reveal that peroxisomal and mitochondrial MAVS act in a sequential manner to establish an antiviral cellular state. Upon viral infection, peroxisomal MAVS triggers the rapid expression of defense factors without inducing interferon, while mitochondrial MAVS activates an interferon-dependent signaling pathway with delayed kinetics, which amplifies and sustains the antiviral response. The interferon regulatory factor IRF1 plays a crucial role in regulating MAVS-dependent signaling from peroxisomes. These results demonstrate that peroxisomes are a vital site of antiviral signal transduction.

title: Two-sided confidence intervals for the single proportion: comparison of seven methods. Stat. Med
text:
Simple interval estimate methods for proportions often exhibit poor coverage and can produce inappropriate intervals. When evaluating these methods, consider the following criteria:
1. Closeness of the achieved coverage probability to its nominal value.
2. Whether intervals are located too close to or too distant from the middle of the scale.
3. Expected interval width.
4. Avoidance of aberrations such as limits outside [0,1] or zero width intervals.
5. Ease of use, whether through tables, software, or formulae.

Seven methods for estimating a single proportion are evaluated on 96,000 parameter space points. Intervals based on tail areas and simpler score methods are recommended for use. In each case, methods are available that aim to align either the minimum or the mean coverage with the nominal 1 -alpha.

title: Nuclear accumulation of HDAC4 in ATM deficiency promotes neurodegeneration in ataxia-telangiectasia
text:
Ataxia telangiectasia (AT) is a neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the Atm gene. Our study reveals that ATM deficiency leads to the accumulation of histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) in the nucleus of neurons, which in turn promotes neurodegeneration. HDAC4 binds to chromatin and interacts with myocyte enhancer factor 2A (MEF2A) and cAMP-responsive element binding protein (CREB), leading to altered neuronal gene expression. Inhibition of HDAC4 activity or its nuclear accumulation ameliorates the neurodegenerative changes and restores behavioral abnormalities in ATM-deficient mice. However, complete rescue of the neurodegeneration requires the presence of HDAC4 in the cytoplasm, suggesting that the AT phenotype results from both the loss of cytoplasmic HDAC4 and its nuclear accumulation. Our findings highlight the critical role of HDAC4's cellular localization in the events leading to AT neurodegeneration.

title: Regulation and function of the E-cadherin/catenin complex in cells of the monocyte-macrophage lineage and DCs.
text: E-cadherin, a key adhesion molecule, plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of epithelial tissues and regulating immune cell functions. In epithelial cells, E-cadherin interacts with catenins and other intracellular signaling molecules, influencing signaling pathways involved in cell adhesion, migration, and survival. Recent research has also uncovered a novel role for E-cadherin in regulating mononuclear phagocyte functions, including the maturation and migration of Langerhans cells and the induction of tolerance in bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (DCs). The functionality of β-catenin in these processes may be instrumental in determining the balance between immunogenicity and tolerogenicity of DCs in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, E-cadherin ligands CD103 and KLRG1 are expressed on DC-, T-, and NK-cell subsets and contribute to their interaction with E-cadherin-expressing DCs and macrophages. This review aims to discuss the regulation, function, and implications of E-cadherin expression in these central immune cells.

title: Polymorphism and ligand dependent changes in human glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) function: allosteric rescue of loss of function mutation.
text: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a crucial role in regulating insulin secretion and is a major therapeutic target for the treatment of type II diabetes. However, the regulation of GLP-1R function is complex, involving multiple endogenous peptides and exogenous agonists. In this study, we investigated the effects of 10 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the GLP-1R on ligand binding, cell surface receptor expression, and signaling pathways. We found that specific SNPs had ligand- and pathway-specific effects, with the most significant effect observed in the Met¹⁴⁹ variant, which showed selective loss of peptide-induced responses across all pathways examined, but preservation of response to the small molecule compound 2. In contrast, the Cys³³³ variant showed preservation of peptide responses but attenuated response to compound 2. Interestingly, the loss of peptide function at the Met¹⁴⁹ receptor variant could be allosterically rescued by compound 2, providing evidence that allosteric drugs could be used to treat patients with this loss of function variant.

title: Neuronal circuitry mechanism regulating adult quiescent neural stem cell fate decision
text: Adult neurogenesis arises from neural stem cells within specialized niches, and neuronal activity and experience regulate various stages of this process, including proliferation, new neuron maturation, synaptic integration, and survival. While the impact of local neuronal circuitry on adult neural stem cells is unclear, our study reveals that quiescent radial glia-like neural stem cells (RGLs) in the adult mouse hippocampus respond to the neurotransmitter GABA through γ2-subunit-containing GABAA receptors. Clonal analysis of individual RGLs showed that their rapid exit from quiescence and enhanced symmetrical self-renewal are linked to the deletion of γ2. RGLs are close to terminals expressing 67-kDa glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67) of parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) interneurons, and they respond tonically to GABA released from these neurons. Optogenetic control of the activity of dentate PV+ interneurons, but not that of somatostatin-expressing or vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP)-expressing interneurons, can dictate the RGL choice between quiescence and activation. Furthermore, PV+ interneuron activation restores RGL quiescence after social isolation, an experience that induces RGL activation and symmetrical division. Our study identifies a niche cell–signal–receptor trio and a local circuitry mechanism that control the activation and self-renewal mode of quiescent adult neural stem cells in response to neuronal activity and experience.

title: Global vitamin D levels in relation to age, gender, skin pigmentation and latitude: an ecologic meta-regression analysis
text:
A meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies on serum 25(OH)D status globally was conducted. The mean serum 25(OH)D level was 54 nmol/l (95% CI: 52–57 nmol/l), with higher levels observed in women than men and in Caucasians than non-Caucasians. No significant trend in serum 25(OH)D levels was observed with latitude. However, after adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity, a significant decline in 25(OH)D levels was observed in Caucasians but not in non-Caucasians with increasing latitude. A global vitamin D insufficiency was observed, with a widespread prevalence compared to proposed threshold levels.
In this study, we conducted a meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies on serum 25(OH)D status globally. The mean serum 25(OH)D level was 54 nmol/l (95% CI: 52–57 nmol/l), with higher levels observed in women than men and in Caucasians than non-Caucasians. No significant trend in serum 25(OH)D levels was observed with latitude. However, after adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity, a significant decline in 25(OH)D levels was observed in Caucasians but not in non-Caucasians with increasing latitude. A global vitamin D insufficiency was observed, with a widespread prevalence compared to proposed threshold levels.
The study included 394 studies retrieved from Pubmed, Embase and Web of Science using the terms “serum”, “25-hydroxy-vitamin D”, “cholecalciferol”, and “human”. The mean 25(OH)D level was 54 nmol/l (95% CI: 52–57 nmol/l), with higher levels observed in women than men and in Caucasians than non-Caucasians. No significant trend in serum 25(OH)D levels was observed with latitude. However, after adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity, a significant decline in 25(OH)D levels was observed in Caucasians but not in non-Caucasians with increasing latitude. A global vitamin D insufficiency was observed, with a widespread prevalence compared to proposed threshold levels.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel monocyte/macrophage differentiation-dependent gene that is responsive to lipopolysaccharide, ceramide, and lysophosphatidylcholine.
text: A novel differentiation-dependent mRNA (DIF-2) has been identified in human mononuclear phagocytes through the differential display technique. The full-length cDNA was cloned and sequenced, revealing a protein composed of 156 amino acids with a predicted isoelectric point of 8.84. Analysis of mRNA expression in freshly isolated monocytes revealed a significant downregulation upon differentiation. A similar differentiation-dependent downregulation was observed in normal hepatocytes compared to undifferentiated HepG2 cells. The mRNA expression in monocytes was found to be sensitive to lipopolysaccharide, ceramide, and lysophosphatidylcholine, with strong induction of DIF-2 transcription by lipopolysaccharide and ceramide, and weaker induction by lysophosphatidylcholine. A homologous gene in mouse fibroblasts has been previously identified as a serum growth factor-inducible immediate early gene, suggesting that DIF-2 represents a gene regulated in differentiation processes and responsive to specific signaling molecules.

title: A Novel 3-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase That Regulates Reproductive Development and Longevity
text: Endogenous small molecules, known as metabolites, that regulate animal longevity are emerging as a novel means to influence health and lifespan. In the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans, bile acid-like steroids called dafachronic acids (DAs) have been shown to regulate developmental timing and longevity through the conserved nuclear hormone receptor DAF-12, which is homologous to mammalian sterol-regulated receptors LXR and FXR. Using metabolic genetics, mass spectrometry, and biochemical approaches, we have identified new activities in DA biosynthesis and characterized an evolutionarily conserved short chain dehydrogenase, DHS-16, as a novel 3-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase. Our findings demonstrate that DHS-16 controls DAF-12 activity and governs longevity in response to signals from the gonad, providing insight into the regulation of longevity in other animals. Our elucidation of the C. elegans bile acid biosynthetic pathway has also revealed the possibility of novel ligands and striking biochemical conservation to other animals, which could lead to the identification of new targets for manipulating longevity in metazoans.

title: An Argonaute transports siRNAs from the cytoplasm to the nucleus.
text: Ribonucleoprotein complexes consisting of Argonaute-like proteins and small regulatory RNAs play a wide range of roles in cellular biology. Many of these small RNAs are thought to act within the nucleus, and we used a genetic screen in Caenorhabditis elegans to identify factors essential for RNA interference (RNAi) in nuclei. Our study identified the Argonaute protein NRDE-3 as a key player in nuclear RNAi. In the absence of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), NRDE-3 resides in the cytoplasm, but when siRNAs are present, NRDE-3 binds to them and redistributes to the nucleus. This nuclear redistribution requires a functional nuclear localization signal and is necessary for efficient nuclear RNAi. Our findings suggest that specific Argonaute proteins can transport specific classes of small regulatory RNAs to distinct cellular compartments, allowing them to regulate gene expression in a targeted manner.

title: Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-Bisphosphate Functions as a Second Messenger that Regulates Cytoskeleton–Plasma Membrane Adhesion
text: The interactions between the plasma membrane and the cytoskeleton play a crucial role in regulating various cellular functions, including cell shape, formation of cell processes, cell movement, and endocytosis. Using optical tweezers, we have measured the tethering forces between the plasma membrane and the cytoskeleton and found that plasma membrane phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) acts as a second messenger that regulates the adhesion energy between the cytoskeleton and the plasma membrane. Our study shows that receptor stimuli that hydrolyze PIP2 reduce the adhesion energy, a process that can be mimicked by expressing PH domains that sequester PIP2 or by targeting a 5'-PIP2-phosphatase to the plasma membrane to selectively lower the concentration of PIP2 in the plasma membrane. Our findings suggest that plasma membrane PIP2 plays a key role in controlling dynamic membrane functions and cell shape by locally regulating the adhesion between the actin-based cortical cytoskeleton and the plasma membrane.

title: Tissue-resident memory T cells: local specialists in immune defence
text: T cells play a vital role in defending against infection and cancer. The movement of memory T cells throughout the body is crucial for their ability to provide immune protection, but recent studies have shown that specializing some memory T cells into distinct tissue-resident subsets can enhance local immunity. In recent years, significant progress has been made in understanding the development and function of tissue-resident T cells, revealing mechanisms that could inform rational vaccine design. This Review summarizes the major advances and emerging concepts in this field, discusses the differentiation and protective functions of tissue-resident memory T cells in various tissues throughout the body, and highlights remaining questions that need to be addressed.

title: Defective replication stress response inhibits lymphomagenesis and impairs lymphocyte reconstitution
text:
DNA replication stress can lead to genetic instability in cancer, but the role of the replication stress response in cancer development remains unclear. One key protein involved in the replication stress response is SMARCAL1, which helps stabilize DNA replication forks and prevent replication fork collapse, leading to DNA breaks and apoptosis. While the functions of SMARCAL1 in fork regression and remodeling have been studied, its in vivo functions in replication stress and cancer are not well understood.
To investigate the role of SMARCAL1 in cancer development, we used a gamma radiation-induced replication stress T-cell lymphoma mouse model. Our results showed a significant inhibition of lymphomagenesis in mice lacking one or both alleles of Smarcal1. Remarkably, about a quarter of the Smarcal1-deficient mice did not develop tumors. Additionally, we found that hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) and developing thymocytes in Smarcal1-deficient mice exhibited increased DNA damage and apoptosis during the proliferation burst following radiation and an impaired ability to repopulate the thymus after radiation. Furthermore, mice lacking Smarcal1 showed significant HSPC defects when challenged to respond to other replication stress stimuli.
Our findings reveal the crucial function of the DNA replication stress response, particularly SMARCAL1, in hematopoietic cell survival and tumor development. Our results also provide important insights into the immunodeficiency observed in individuals with mutations in SMARCAL1 by suggesting that it is an HSPC defect.

title: Human DNA methylomes at base resolution show widespread epigenomic differences
text:
DNA cytosine methylation is a crucial epigenetic modification that plays a central role in various cellular processes, including genome regulation, development, and disease. In this study, we present the first genome-wide, single-base-resolution maps of methylated cytosines in a mammalian genome, obtained from both human embryonic stem cells and fetal fibroblasts. We also conducted comparative analyses of messenger RNA and small RNA components of the transcriptome, several histone modifications, and sites of DNA-protein interaction for several key regulatory factors.
Our findings revealed significant differences in the composition and patterning of cytosine methylation between the two genomes. Approximately one-quarter of all methylation identified in embryonic stem cells occurred in a non-CG context, suggesting that these cells may employ distinct methylation mechanisms to regulate gene expression. Methylation in non-CG contexts showed enrichment in gene bodies and depletion in protein binding sites and enhancers. Interestingly, non-CG methylation disappeared upon induced differentiation of the embryonic stem cells, and was restored in induced pluripotent stem cells.
We identified hundreds of differentially methylated regions proximal to genes involved in pluripotency and differentiation, and observed widespread reduced methylation levels in fibroblasts, which were associated with lower transcriptional activity. These reference epigenomes provide a valuable foundation for future studies exploring the role of DNA cytosine methylation in human disease and development.

title: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis in patients with chronic abdominal pain: a blinded randomised controlled multi-centre trial.
text:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis for chronic abdominal pain is a controversial and evidence-free procedure. To investigate whether laparoscopic adhesiolysis provides significant pain relief and improves quality of life in patients with adhesions and chronic abdominal pain, we conducted a randomized controlled trial.
METHODS: We enrolled 116 patients with chronic abdominal pain attributed to adhesions, and excluded other causes for their pain. Patients underwent diagnostic laparoscopy, and those with confirmed adhesions were randomly assigned to either laparoscopic adhesiolysis or no treatment. Treatment allocation was concealed from patients and assessors, and pain was assessed using visual analogue score (VAS), pain change score, analgesic use, and quality of life score at 1-year follow-up. Analysis was by intention to treat.
FINDINGS: Of the 100 patients randomly allocated, there was no significant difference in pain relief and quality of life between the laparoscopic adhesiolysis (52 patients) and no treatment (48 patients) groups (mean change from baseline of VAS score at 12 months: difference 3 points, p=0.53; 95% CI -7 to 13).
INTERPRETATION: Although laparoscopic adhesiolysis provides relief from chronic abdominal pain, it is not more beneficial than diagnostic laparoscopy alone. Therefore, laparoscopic adhesiolysis cannot be recommended as a treatment for adhesions in patients with chronic abdominal pain.

title: Insulin Signaling and Dietary Restriction Differentially Influence the Decline of Learning and Memory with Age
text:
One of the most detrimental aspects of aging is memory loss, which can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. While research has identified factors that promote longevity, the impact of these factors on learning and memory is still unknown. Our study aimed to investigate the effects of longevity-promoting factors on memory performance in the nematode worm, Caenorhabditis elegans.
We found that mutants of the Insulin/IGF-1 receptor, daf-2, exhibited improved memory performance in early adulthood and maintained learning ability better with age. However, surprisingly, these mutants did not demonstrate an extension in long-term memory with age. In contrast, mutants of the Dietary Restriction (DR) gene, eat-2, showed impaired long-term memory in young adulthood but maintained this level of memory longer with age.
Our results also showed that crh-1, the C. elegans homolog of the CREB transcription factor, is essential for long-term associative memory, but not for learning or short-term memory. Interestingly, the expression of crh-1 declines with age and differs in the longevity mutants, and CREB expression and activity correlate with memory performance.
Our findings suggest that specific longevity treatments have both acute and long-term effects on cognitive functions that decline with age by regulating rate-limiting genes required for learning and memory. These results provide valuable insights into the complex interplay between aging and cognitive function and highlight the potential of longevity-promoting factors in maintaining cognitive health.

title: Unique response pathways are established by allosteric interactions among nuclear hormone receptors
text: Heterodimerization is a common mechanism among eukaryotic transcription factors, where two different receptors form a complex to regulate gene expression. The 9-cis retinoic acid receptor (RXR) is a common heterodimerization partner for several nuclear receptors, including the thyroid hormone receptor (T3R) and retinoic acid receptor (RAR). This raises the question of whether these complexes have dual hormonal responsiveness. To investigate, we developed a strategy to examine the transcriptional properties of each receptor individually or when tethered to a heterodimeric partner. Our findings reveal that the intrinsic binding properties of RXR are masked in T3R-RXR and RAR-RXR heterodimers. In contrast, RXR is active as a non-DNA-binding cofactor with the NGFI-B/Nurr1 orphan receptors. Heterodimerization of RXR with constitutively active NGFI-B/Nurr1 creates a novel hormone-dependent complex. These findings suggest that allosteric interactions among heterodimers create complexes with unique properties, highlighting the critical role of allostery in generating diversity in hormone response networks.

title: Midlife and Late‐Life Vascular Risk Factors and White Matter Microstructural Integrity: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study
text:
BACKGROUND: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) measures of white matter (WM) microstructural integrity have been found to provide earlier indications of WM injury than WM hyperintensities. However, the risk factors for poor WM microstructural integrity in late life have not been well established. This study aims to investigate the association between vascular risk factors in midlife and late life with measures of late-life WM microstructural integrity.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed data from 1851 participants in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC) who underwent 3-T magnetic resonance imaging, including DTI, as part of the ARIC Neurocognitive Study (ARIC-NCS). We examined the association between lipids, glucose, and blood pressure measures from the baseline ARIC visit (1987-1989, ages 44-65, midlife) and regional and overall WM mean diffusivity and fractional anisotropy obtained at ARIC visit 5 (2011-2013, ages 67-90, late life) with ARIC participants. We also considered whether these associations were independent of or modified by WM hyperintensity volumes. Our findings showed that elevated blood pressure in both midlife and late life, as well as elevated glucose in midlife but not late life, were associated with worse late-life WM microstructural integrity. These associations were independent of the degree of WM hyperintensity, and the association between glucose and WM microstructural integrity was stronger for those with the least WM hyperintensity. There was limited support for an adverse association between lipids and WM microstructural integrity.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that hypertension in both midlife and late life, as well as elevated glucose in midlife, are associated with worse WM microstructural integrity in late life. These findings highlight the importance of addressing vascular risk factors in midlife to preserve WM integrity in late life.

title: KRAS gene amplification and overexpression but not mutation associates with aggressive and metastatic endometrial cancer
text:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial carcinomas are a common type of gynecological cancer, with approximately three quarters of cases being diagnosed at an early stage. However, despite advances in systemic therapies, approximately 15-20% of patients experience recurrence. Homo sapiens v-Ki-ras2 Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogenes homologue (KRAS) mutations have been implicated in the development and progression of various human cancers, but there is limited understanding of their clinical significance in endometrial carcinomas.
METHODS: In this study, we conducted a comprehensive and integrated analysis of genome-wide expression related to KRAS mutations and copy-number alterations in primary and metastatic endometrial carcinoma lesions, using a primary investigation set and clinical validation set consisting of 414 primary tumors and 61 metastatic lesions.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed that amplification and gain of KRAS were present in 3% of primary lesions and 18% of metastatic lesions, and were significantly associated with poor outcome, high International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage, non-endometrioid subtype, high grade, aneuploidy, receptor loss, and high KRAS mRNA levels. In contrast, KRAS mutations were present in 14.7% of primary lesions with no increase in metastatic lesions, and were significantly associated with endometrioid subtype, low grade, and obesity.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that KRAS amplification and KRAS mRNA expression, which increase from primary to metastatic lesions, are relevant for endometrial carcinoma disease progression.

title: Hyperhomocysteinemia and atherosclerotic vascular disease: pathophysiology, screening, and treatment. off.
text:
Recent research has highlighted hyperhomocysteinemia as a significant risk factor for atherosclerotic vascular disease. This review aims to provide an in-depth analysis of homocysteine metabolism, the causes of hyperhomocysteinemia, the pathophysiological implications of this disorder, and the epidemiological evidence linking homocysteine levels to vascular disease. We also discuss the importance of screening for hyperhomocysteinemia in patients at high risk for vascular disease or with abnormalities in homocysteine metabolism, and provide evidence-based recommendations for treatment.
Trecommendations for treatment include administering a folic acid supplement (400-1000 microg) and a high-potency multivitamin containing at least 400 microg of folate. In some cases, higher doses of folic acid and cyanocobalamin supplements may be necessary. Until more definitive clinical trial data becomes available, these conservative recommendations offer a safe, effective, and evidence-based approach to the diagnosis, evaluation, and management of patients with hyperhomocysteinemia.

title: Best--worst scaling: What it can do for health care research and how to do it.
text: Statements like "quality of care is more highly valued than waiting time" cannot be supported or refuted using traditional discrete choice experiments (DCEs) because they rely on utility parameters that do not capture the nuances of quality of care. However, best-worst scaling tasks can overcome this limitation by asking respondents to make different choice decisions. While the nature of the best-worst task is generally understood, there are several issues related to the design and analysis of such experiments that require further explanation. This paper provides guidance on how to aggregate and analyze these data, and demonstrates through a quality of life pilot study how richer insights can be gained by using best-worst tasks.

title: Genetic variants and non-genetic factors predict circulating vitamin D levels in Hispanic and non-Hispanic White women: the Breast Cancer Health Disparities Study.
text:
Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several common polymorphisms in or near genes, including GC, CYP2R1, CYP24A1, and NADSYN1/DHCR7, which are associated with circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) in European populations. To replicate these findings in a different population, we examined six selected polymorphisms from these regions and their relationship with circulating 25(OH)D levels in 1,605 Hispanic women (629 U.S. Hispanics and 976 Mexicans) and 354 non-Hispanic White (NHW) women. Additionally, we assessed potential interactions between these variants and known non-genetic predictors of 25(OH)D levels, including body mass index (BMI), sunlight exposure, and vitamin D intake from diet and supplements.
Our results showed that the minor alleles of the two GC polymorphisms (rs7041 and rs2282679) were significantly associated with lower 25(OH)D levels in both Hispanic and NHW women. We also found a significant association between the CYP2R1 polymorphism, rs2060793, and 25(OH)D levels in both groups. However, we did not observe any significant associations for the polymorphisms in the CYP24A1 gene. In Hispanic controls, 25(OH)D levels were significantly associated with the rs12785878T and rs1790349G haplotype in the NADSYN1/DHCR7 region. Furthermore, we identified significant interactions between the GC rs2282679 and BMI and between the rs12785878 and time spent in outdoor activities. These findings provide additional support for the role of common genetic variants in determining individual variability in circulating 25(OH)D levels and highlight the importance of considering non-genetic factors in the interpretation of genetic associations.

title: Generation and characterization of methyl-lysine histone antibodies.
text:
This chapter describes the development and characterization of rabbit polyclonal antibodies specific to methylated histone H3-K9, named histone. The protocols outlined provide a detailed approach for designing peptides, immunizing rabbits, and quality controlling the generated methyl-lysine histone antibodies. Following in vivo characterization using indirect immunofluorescence (IF) on inter- and metaphase chromatin in wild-type (WT) and histone methyltransferase (HMTase)-deficient mouse cells, the study highlights the importance of developing high-quality, position-specific methyl-lysine histone antibodies for decoding epigenetic information. A comparative analysis of available methyl-lysine histone antibodies reveals significant differences in specificity and avidity, emphasizing the need for rigorous quality controls to ensure accurate experimental interpretation.
In summary, this chapter presents a systematic approach to generating and characterizing methyl-lysine histone antibodies, with a focus on their in vivo application in epigenetic research. The study underscores the need for high-quality antibodies and highlights the potential of these tools for decoding epigenetic information.

title: The Hallmarks of Aging
text: Aging is characterized by a progressive decline in physiological function, leading to increased vulnerability to death and the development of various pathologies, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. Recent advances in aging research have shed light on the genetic and biochemical mechanisms that control the aging process, revealing that the rate of aging is influenced by evolutionarily conserved pathways and processes. This review highlights nine tentative hallmarks of aging that are common to different organisms, with a particular focus on mammalian aging. These hallmarks include genomic instability, telomere shortening, epigenetic alterations, loss of protein function, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, stem cell exhaustion, and altered intercellular communication. Elucidating the interconnectedness between these hallmarks and their relative contributions to aging is a major challenge, with the ultimate goal of identifying pharmaceutical targets to improve human health during aging, with minimal side effects.

title: A sensitive mass spectrometry platform identifies metabolic changes of life history traits in C. elegans
text: Abnormal nutrient metabolism is a hallmark of aging, and recent advances in the field have led to a better understanding of the underlying genetic and nutritional framework, particularly in the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans. However, the direct metabolic consequences of perturbations in the life history of C. elegans remain to be fully elucidated. To address this gap, we have optimized and validated a sensitive mass spectrometry (MS) platform for identifying major metabolite classes in worms and applied it to study age- and diet-related changes. Using this platform, which allowed for the detection of over 600 metabolites in a sample of 2500 worms, we observed significant changes in fatty acids, amino acids, and phospholipids during different stages of worm life history, which were independent of the germ line. Our findings revealed a striking shift in lipid metabolism after early adulthood in worms, which was at least partially controlled by the metabolic regulator AAK-2/AMPK. Additionally, we found that most amino acids peaked during development, except for aspartic acid and glycine, which accumulated in aged worms. Dietary intervention also influenced worm metabolite profiles, with specific regulation depending on the metabolite class. These MS-based methods have proven to be powerful tools for performing worm metabolomics studies on aging and metabolism.

title: Characterisation of antibiotic prescriptions for acute respiratory tract infections in Danish general practice: a retrospective registry based cohort study
text: Inappropriate use of antibiotics is contributing to the growing problem of antimicrobial resistance. Despite guidelines issued in Denmark to promote rational antibiotic prescribing for acute respiratory tract infections in general practice, it is unclear if these recommendations are being followed. To investigate antibiotic prescription patterns for acute respiratory tract infections in Danish general practice, researchers analyzed electronic prescriptions labeled with clinical indications. They found that acute respiratory tract infections accounted for 456,532 antibiotic prescriptions between July 2012 and June 2013, with pneumonia being the most common indication (39%). Penicillin V was the most commonly prescribed antibiotic agent (58%), followed by macrolides (18%) and amoxicillin (15%). The use of second-line agents increased with age for all indications, and comprised more than 40% of prescriptions in patients aged >75 years. Women were also more likely to be prescribed antibiotics, regardless of clinical indication. The study highlights the need for strategies to improve the quality of antibiotic prescribing, particularly for pneumonia, acute otitis media, and acute rhinosinusitis. The overuse of antibiotics, including so-called "second-line" agents such as amoxicillin, increases resistance and may lead to a potentially catastrophic scenario where antibiotics are no longer effective. Further analysis of prescriptions given by out-of-hours clinics is also warranted.

title: Lack of Skeletal Muscle IL-6 Affects Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Activity at Rest and during Prolonged Exercise
text: The enzyme pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) plays a crucial role in regulating the utilization of substrates in skeletal muscle during exercise. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is produced in skeletal muscle during exercise in a duration-dependent manner and has been shown to increase whole-body fatty acid oxidation, muscle glucose uptake, and decrease PDHa activity in skeletal muscle of fed mice. The aim of the current study was to investigate whether muscle IL-6 contributes to the regulation of PDH during exercise in skeletal muscle. Skeletal muscle-specific IL-6 knockout (IL-6 MKO) mice and floxed littermate controls (controls) were subjected to a single bout of treadmill exercise for 10, 60, or 120 minutes, with rested mice of each genotype serving as basal controls. The respiratory exchange ratio (RER) was found to be higher in IL-6 MKO mice during the 120-minute exercise bout compared to controls, while RER decreased during exercise regardless of genotype. Additionally, phosphorylation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) increased with exercise regardless of genotype. PDHa activity was found to be higher in IL-6 MKO mice at rest and 60 minutes of exercise compared to controls, and remained unchanged in IL-6 MKO mice during exercise. Furthermore, neither PDH phosphorylation nor acetylation could explain the genotype differences in PDHa activity. These findings suggest that skeletal muscle IL-6 contributes to the regulation of PDH at rest and during prolonged exercise, and that muscle IL-6 normally dampens carbohydrate utilization during prolonged exercise via effects on PDH.

title: Clinical and pathologic characteristics of patients with BRCA-positive and BRCA-negative breast cancer.
text:
The purpose of this study was to investigate whether tumor pathological features and clinical characteristics differ in patients with and without BRCA mutations. We analyzed the medical records of 491 women with breast cancer who underwent genetic testing for BRCA mutations between 1997 and 2006. We retrospectively reviewed the medical records to gather clinical information such as ethnicity, age, clinical stage at diagnosis, age at parity, number of full-term pregnancies, use of oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy, and BRCA mutation status. We also reviewed the tumor pathology to determine the histological type, tumor grade, and expression of estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER-2/neu.
Of the 491 patients with breast cancer, 391 were BRCA-negative and 86 were BRCA-positive. Triple-negative breast cancer (i.e., those with negative estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER-2/neu status) was diagnosed in 57.1% of the BRCA1-positive patients, 23.3% of the BRCA2-positive patients, and 13.8% of the BRCA-negative patients. BRCA1 mutation carriers had higher nuclear grade tumors than the other two groups (P < .001). In contrast, BRCA2 mutation carriers were older at diagnosis than BRCA1 mutation carriers and noncarriers (P < .01).
Our findings suggest that breast cancers associated with BRCA1 mutations may be divided into two distinct groups: triple-negative and non-triple-negative groups. Future studies should aim to determine whether patients with BRCA1 mutations and triple-negative breast cancer respond better to treatment than BRCA-negative patients with similar tumor pathology.

title: Interferons: Success in anti-viral immunotherapy.
text: Interferons (IFNs) are glycoproteins with potent antiviral properties that form a crucial part of the host's defense against invading pathogens. These proteins are categorized into three groups, Type I, II, and III IFNs, based on the structure of their receptors on the cell surface. Due to their ability to modulate immune responses, IFNs have emerged as promising therapeutic options for controlling chronic virus infections. In combination with other drugs, Type I IFNs are currently considered the standard of care for suppressing Hepatitis C (HCV) and Hepatitis B (HBV) infections, while Type III IFN has shown encouraging results as a treatment for HCV infection in phase III clinical trials. However, while IFNs are effective, their use as a treatment is not without caution. As powerful cytokines, IFNs can affect a wide range of cell types, leading to unpleasant symptoms in many patients. As a result, constant monitoring is necessary for patients receiving IFN therapy to achieve the treatment goals of suppressing virus infection while maintaining quality of life.

title: Genetic analysis of human obesity in an Italian sample.
text: An investigation into the genetic factors contributing to obesity was conducted on a sample of nuclear families from Aosta Valley, North Italy. The sample consisted of the parents and siblings of obese elementary school children identified during a preliminary screening, as well as a similar number of non-obese children and their nuclear families. The total number of families analyzed was 67 for the obese group and 112 for the non-obese group. Various tests were applied to determine the genetic influence on obesity, with a particular focus on identifying a dominant major gene with a weak effect. Our findings indicate that genetic factors are indeed present, and several analyses suggest the presence of a dominant major gene with a subtle impact.

title: The non-coding RNA landscape of human hematopoiesis and leukemia
text: Non-coding RNAs, once considered inconsequential, have emerged as vital regulators of gene expression and cell fate decisions in the human hematopoietic system. However, their expression patterns and regulatory functions during both normal and malignant hematopoiesis remain inadequately understood. To address this knowledge gap, we present a comprehensive resource that defines the non-coding RNA landscape of the human hematopoietic system. By generating highly specific non-coding RNA expression profiles for each blood cell population, we identify unique fingerprint non-coding RNAs, such as LINC00173 in granulocytes, and assign them to critical regulatory circuits involved in blood homeostasis. When we incorporate acute myeloid leukemia samples into this landscape, we uncover prognostically relevant non-coding RNA stem cell signatures shared between leukemic blasts and healthy hematopoietic stem cells. Our findings underscore the importance of the non-coding transcriptome in the formation and maintenance of the human blood hierarchy, highlighting the need for further investigation into the role of long non-coding RNAs in haematopoiesis and leukemogenesis. While microRNAs have been well-established regulators of hematopoiesis and leukemogenesis, the mechanisms by which long non-coding RNAs contribute to these processes remain unclear. Our study provides a comprehensive resource that sheds light on the non-coding RNA expression landscape of the human hematopoietic system, underscoring their critical role in the formation and maintenance of the human blood hierarchy.

title: Incidence and risk of central nervous system metastases as site of first recurrence in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer treated with adjuvant trastuzumab.
text:
BACKGROUND: Central nervous system (CNS) disease as the site of first relapse after exposure to adjuvant trastuzumab has been reported in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. To determine the risk of CNS metastases as the first site of recurrence in these patients, we conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis of randomized trials that evaluated the use of adjuvant trastuzumab.
METHODS: We included eligible studies that randomized patients with HER2-positive breast cancer to receive adjuvant trastuzumab for 1 year, and reported CNS metastases as the first site of disease recurrence. We used fixed-effects inverse variance and random-effects models to calculate the incidence, relative risk (RR), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of CNS metastases as the first site of recurrence in trastuzumab-treated patients compared to control arms without trastuzumab therapy.
RESULTS: A total of 9020 patients were included in our analysis. The incidence of CNS metastases as the first site of disease recurrence in HER2-positive patients receiving adjuvant trastuzumab was 2.56% (95% CI 2.07% to 3.01%) compared to 1.94% (95% CI 1.54% to 2.38%) in HER2-positive patients who did not receive adjuvant trastuzumab. The RR of the CNS as the first site of relapse in trastuzumab-treated patients was 1.35 (95% CI 1.02-1.78, P = 0.038) compared to control arms without trastuzumab therapy. The ratio of CNS metastases to total number of recurrence events was 16.94% (95% CI 10.85% to 24.07%) and 8.33% (95% CI 6.49% to 10.86%) for the trastuzumab-treated and control groups, respectively. No significant differences were found based on trastuzumab schedule or median follow-up time. No evidence of publication bias was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that adjuvant trastuzumab is associated with an increased risk of CNS metastases as the site of first recurrence in HER2-positive breast cancer patients. These results have important implications for the management of these patients and highlight the need for further research into the mechanisms underlying this association.

title: Neutrophils in the activation and regulation of innate and adaptive immunity
text: Neutrophils have traditionally been perceived as the final line of defense in an acute inflammatory response, with a primary function in eliminating extracellular pathogens. However, recent research has expanded their role beyond this initial function. The evolving arsenal of neutrophil effector molecules now includes a diverse array of cytokines, extracellular traps, and humoral immune molecules. In addition, neutrophils play a key role in regulating and activating both innate and adaptive immune cells, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of a wide range of diseases, including infections caused by intracellular pathogens, autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammation, and cancer.

title: Functions of DNA methylation: islands, start sites, gene bodies and beyond
text: DNA methylation is commonly characterized as an epigenetic mark that silences gene expression, a function that was first proposed in the 1970s. However, recent advances in genome-scale mapping of methylation have allowed us to investigate the role of DNA methylation in various genomic contexts, including transcriptional start sites without CpG islands, gene bodies, regulatory elements, and repeat sequences. Our findings indicate that the function of DNA methylation is context-dependent and more complex than initially thought. As we continue to uncover the intricacies of DNA methylation, it is essential to improve our understanding of its functions in order to interpret changes in this mark that occur in diseases such as cancer.

title: Metaplasia and transdifferentiation: from pure biology to the clinic
text: Transformation from one tissue type to another is a well-established phenomenon that can be explained by the principles of developmental biology. Although these transformations are rare in nature, the possibility of deliberately reprogramming cells from one tissue type to another through the manipulation of transcription factors is now within reach. This approach has the potential to generate new therapies for a wide range of human diseases.

title: Pioglitazone Use and Risk of Bladder Cancer and Other Common Cancers in Persons With Diabetes.
text:
The study examines the association between pioglitazone use and the risk of various cancers in individuals with diabetes. The study design includes a cohort and nested case-control analysis, with a bladder cancer cohort of 193,099 individuals aged 40 years or older who were followed until December 2012. The study also includes a cohort analysis of 10 additional cancers in 236,507 individuals aged 40 years or older who were followed until June 2012. The exposure of interest is pioglitazone use, and the main outcomes are incident cancer, including bladder, prostate, female breast, lung/bronchus, endometrial, colon, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreas, kidney/renal pelvis, rectum, and melanoma.
The study found that pioglitazone use was not associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, although the study could not exclude a small increased risk. However, the study did find an increased risk of prostate and pancreatic cancer associated with ever use of pioglitazone, with a statistically significant association observed for prostate cancer. The study also found no clear patterns of risk for any cancer associated with time since initiation, duration, or dose of pioglitazone use. The study's findings suggest that the increased prostate and pancreatic cancer risks associated with pioglitazone use may merit further investigation to assess whether they are causal or due to chance, residual confounding, or reverse causality.

title: Embryonic stem cell lines from human blastocysts: somatic differentiation in vitro
text: This study describes the derivation of pluripotent embryonic stem (ES) cells from human blastocysts. Two diploid ES cell lines were cultivated in vitro for extended periods, maintaining expression of markers characteristic of pluripotent primate cells. The human ES cells express the transcription factor Oct-4, which is essential for the development of pluripotential cells in the mouse. When grafted into SCID mice, both lines gave rise to teratomas containing derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers. Both cell lines were also found to differentiate in vitro into extraembryonic and somatic cell lineages. Additionally, neural progenitor cells could be isolated from differentiating ES cell cultures and induced to form mature neurons. The derivation of ES cells provides a valuable model for studying early human embryology, as well as an investigational tool for the discovery of novel growth factors and medicines. Furthermore, ES cells have the potential to serve as a source of cells for use in transplantation therapy.

title: Multipoint Kras oncogene mutations potentially indicate mucinous carcinoma on the entire spectrum of mucinous ovarian neoplasms
text: The Kras mutation is a common occurrence in various human neoplasms, including ovarian mucinous tumors. In this study, we aimed to investigate the prevalence of Kras mutations along the histological continuum of normal ovaries, benign, borderline, and malignant ovarian mucinous neoplasms. We analyzed 7 cases of normal ovarian tissue, 7 cases of benign mucinous tumors, 10 cases of borderline mucinous tumors, and 41 cases of malignant mucinous ovarian tumors. The prevalence of Kras mutations in normal ovaries was 0%, while the prevalence in benign, borderline, and malignant mucinous neoplasms was 57.14%, 90%, and 75.61%, respectively. We identified six cases with novel Kras mutations not previously reported in the COSMIC database, including A11V, V14I, and A11T in mucinous carcinomas, and A11V and V14I in mucinous borderline tumors. Our findings suggest that Kras mutation is a crucial event in the progression of ovarian mucinous adenoma-borderline tumor-carcinoma sequence, with increased numbers of Kras mutations being the strongest predictor of unequivocal malignancy in ovarian mucinous neoplasms.

title: Identification and distinct regulation of yeast TATA box-containing genes.
text: Despite being one of the earliest identified eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory elements, the native TATA box sequence remains enigmatic. Using criteria associated with TATA boxes, we analyzed several Saccharomyces genomes and identified a consensus TATA(A/T)A(A/T)(A/G) sequence. Approximately 20% of yeast genes contain a TATA box. Interestingly, TATA box-containing genes are more likely to respond to stress, are highly regulated, and preferentially utilize the SAGA complex rather than TFIID compared to TATA-less promoters. The mechanisms of transcriptional regulation in yeast appear to be bipolar, possibly reflecting a need to balance inducible stress-related responses with constitutive housekeeping functions.

title: IL6 derived from cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes chemoresistance via CXCR7 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
text:
Various factors and cellular components within the tumor microenvironment play a crucial role in drug resistance in many types of cancer. In particular, we investigated the factors involved in chemoresistance in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Our findings revealed that interleukin 6 (IL6), primarily derived from cancer-associated fibroblasts, held the most significant sway in chemoresistance by upregulating C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 7 (CXCR7) expression through the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/nuclear factor-κB signaling pathway.
We discovered that CXCR7 knockdown significantly inhibited IL6-induced proliferation and chemoresistance in ESCC cells. Moreover, silencing CXCR7 led to a decrease in gene expression associated with stemness, chemoresistance, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, as well as a suppression of the proliferation ability of ESCC cells in three-dimensional culture systems and angiogenesis assays.
In clinical samples, ESCC patients with high expression of CXCR7 and IL6 exhibited significantly poorer overall survival and progression-free survival after receiving cisplatin following surgery. These results suggest that targeting the IL6-CXCR7 axis may provide a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of ESCC.

title: Myelodysplastic syndromes: revisiting the role of the bone marrow microenvironment in disease pathogenesis
text: Myelodysplastic syndromes are a diverse group of diseases characterized by defective blood cell production. These disorders are prone to developing into leukemia, and their underlying mechanisms are complex and involve the interplay between abnormal hematopoietic cells and their microenvironment. While the role of niche cells in disease progression is not fully understood, recent advances in animal models and the characterization of the hematopoietic stem cell niche have provided valuable insights into the potential involvement of the microenvironment in myelodysplasia and myeloproliferative disorders. These findings support the idea that targeting mesenchymal-hematopoietic interactions may offer a promising therapeutic approach for these diseases.

title: SMC complexes differentially compact mitotic chromosomes according to genomic context
text: Structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) protein complexes are crucial determinants of chromosome conformation. By employing Hi-C and polymer modeling techniques, we investigated the role of cohesin and condensin, two highly conserved SMC complexes, in organizing chromosomes in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae during mitosis. While cohesin is conventionally known for co-aligning sister chromatids, our findings reveal a novel function for the complex in compacting mitotic chromosome arms independently of sister chromatid cohesion. Polymer simulations suggest that this role can be fully accounted for through cis-looping of chromatin. In contrast, condensin is generally dispensable for compacting chromosome arms, and instead, it plays a targeted role in compacting the rDNA proximal regions and promoting resolution of peri-centromeric regions. Our results imply that the conserved mechanism of SMC complexes is to form chromatin loops, and that distinct SMC-dependent looping activities are selectively deployed to appropriately compact chromosomes.

title: Patterns of chlamydia testing in different settings and implications for wider STI diagnosis and care: a probability sample survey of the British population
text: In the UK, there has been a shift towards testing for chlamydia in non-specialist and community settings, with many individuals receiving a chlamydia test without being offered comprehensive STI and HIV testing. To better understand the sexual behaviors of these individuals, a probability sample survey of the British population was conducted between 2010 and 2012. The survey found that of the 26.8% of women and 16.7% of men who reported receiving a chlamydia test in the past year, the majority (28.4% of women and 41.2% of men) tested in genitourinary medicine (GUM) settings. However, a significant proportion (41.1% of women and 20.7% of men) tested in general practice (GP) and other non-GUM settings. Women who tested outside of GUM were more likely to be older, in a relationship, and to live in rural areas, and reported fewer risk behaviors. Additionally, individuals who tested outside of GUM were less likely to report an HIV test in the past 5 years. These findings suggest that while there has been an increase in chlamydia testing in non-GUM settings, there is still a need to provide pathways to comprehensive STI care for individuals at higher risk.

title: Treatment of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: role of AMPK.
text: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has emerged as a global health crisis, with a significant impact on the development of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and hepatic cellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite the prevalence of NAFLD, current treatments are limited to lifestyle interventions such as exercise and weight loss. Recent studies have shown that experimental compounds have improved NAFLD in preclinical animal models, and many of these therapeutics have been found to increase the activity of the cellular energy sensor AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). AMPK activity is reduced by inflammation, obesity, and diabetes, making it a promising therapeutic strategy for NAFLD. In this review, we propose three primary mechanisms by which AMPK activation may improve NAFLD, and examine the mechanisms by which AMPK is activated. We also identify 27 studies that have used AMPK activators to reduce NAFLD, and highlight future considerations for studies examining the relationship between AMPK and NAFLD.

title: Microenvironment-dependent growth of pre-neoplastic and malignant plasma cells in humanized mice
text: The majority of human cancers, including multiple myeloma, are preceded by a precursor state. However, there is a significant lack of in vivo models to study the interaction between human pre-cancerous cells in the bone marrow microenvironment and non-malignant cells. To address this gap, we developed a novel approach by genetically humanizing mice to allow the growth of primary human pre-neoplastic and malignant plasma cells alongside non-malignant cells in vivo. Our findings showed that growth was predominantly confined to the bone marrow, mirroring the pattern observed in patients with myeloma. Xenografts generated from these tumors captured the genomic complexity of the parental tumors and revealed additional somatic changes. Moreover, xenografts derived from patients with preneoplastic gammopathy displayed progressive growth, suggesting that the clinical stability of these lesions may, in part, be due to growth controls extrinsic to tumor cells. These results demonstrate the potential of our novel approach to investigate the full spectrum of human plasma cell neoplasia and highlight the utility of humanized models for understanding the functional diversity of human tumors.

title: Effect of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function in patients with paraquat poisoning.
text: The current study retrospectively analyzed 19 patients diagnosed with paraquat (PQ) poisoning to investigate the impact of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function and PQ elimination. The findings revealed that 7 patients died and 12 survived, with non-oliguric renal failure occurring in all deceased patients. Among the surviving patients, 10 had normal renal function, while 2 developed non-oliguric renal failure. A linear correlation was observed between plasma and urine PQ concentrations before and during activated charcoal hemoperfusion, with the equation parameters and correlation coefficient being as follows: Y=0.5820+1.7348X (R2=0.678; F=35.768; P<0.0001) before hemoperfusion, and Y=0.6827+1.2649X (R2=0.626; F=50.308; P<0.0001) during hemoperfusion. These findings suggest that in patients with normal renal function, the elimination kinetics of PQ by the kidneys are solely associated with plasma PQ concentrations. However, activated charcoal hemoperfusion had limited effectiveness in preventing acute kidney injury in patients with severe PQ poisoning.

title: Diabetes-induced effects on cardiomyocytes in chick embryonic heart micromass and mouse embryonic D3 differentiated stem cells.
text: Diabetes mellitus during pregnancy poses significant medical challenges due to increased risks of morbidity and mortality for both the fetus and pregnant woman. The etiology of diabetic embryopathy is complex, involving various teratogenic factors that can lead to congenital malformations. In this study, we investigated the potential cardiotoxic effects of hyperglycemia and hyperketonemia on embryonic cardiomyocytes using two in vitro models: primary chick embryonic cardiomyocytes and stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. Our findings revealed adverse effects in both systems, including changes in beating activity, cell activity, protein content, ROS production, DNA damage, and differentiating stem cell migration. The diabetic formulae used produced an increase in DNA damage and a decline in cell migration in mouse embryonic stem cells. These results provide valuable insights into the adverse effects of gestational diabetes mellitus and suggest that expectant mothers and maternity staff should monitor glycaemic levels months ahead of conception to minimize risks. Additionally, this study supports the recommendation of using antioxidants during pregnancy to prevent DNA damage caused by ROS production, which may lead to heart defects and other developmental anomalies.

title: Motion magnification
text:
We present Motion Magnification, a novel technique that serves as a visualization tool for subtle motion phenomena in video sequences. By amplifying minute deformations that would otherwise remain undetectable, Motion Magnification enables the visualization of motion patterns that are not visible to the naked eye. To achieve this, we employ a multi-stage approach that involves accurate motion measurement, grouping of pixels, and a novel motion similarity metric.
The first stage involves image registration, which allows us to measure the motion of pixels across frames in a video sequence. We then analyze the trajectories of feature points to determine the motion of individual pixels. This is followed by a segmentation step, where pixels are grouped based on their position, color, and motion similarity. A novel motion similarity metric is used to group even very small motions based on their temporal correlation, which often reveals physical causes.
In the next stage, we identify outliers using an outlier mask, which marks pixels that do not fit within our layered motion model. These pixels are then reproduced from the original registered observations. The final stage involves motion magnification, where the motion of a selected layer can be amplified by a user-specified amount. Texture synthesis is used to fill in any unseen "holes" revealed by the amplified motions.
The resulting motion-magnified images can reveal or emphasize small motions in the original sequence, as demonstrated through applications in the analysis of load-bearing structures, subtle motions or balance corrections of people, and the deformation of "rigid" structures under hand pressure. Our technique offers a powerful tool for visualizing and analyzing minute motion phenomena in video sequences, with potential applications in fields such as biomechanics, robotics, and computer vision.

title: Human TRPML1 channel structures in open and closed conformations
text: Transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) is a Ca2+-releasing cation channel that plays a crucial role in regulating calcium signaling and homeostasis within lysosomes. Mutations in TRPML1 have been linked to mucolipidosis type IV, a severe lysosomal storage disorder. In this study, we have determined the high-resolution structures of full-length human TRPML1 using electron cryo-microscopy, revealing two distinct conformations: an apo structure at pH 7.0 with a resolution of 3.72 Å and an agonist-bound structure at pH 6.0 with a resolution of 3.49 Å. Our findings reveal a hydrophobic cavity in pore helix 1, helices S5 and S6, and a neighboring subunit that forms a binding site for agonists, distinct from that found in TRPV1, a TRP channel from a different subfamily. Additionally, we observe a distinct opening of TRPML1, associated with dilations of its lower gate and a slight movement of pore helix 1. This study provides valuable insights into the regulatory mechanism of TRPML channels and contributes to a better understanding of TRP channel activation, shedding light on the molecular basis of mucolipidosis type IV pathogenesis.

title: Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV): high-performance genomics data visualization and exploration
text: Data visualization is a crucial aspect of genomic data analysis, but the sheer size and diversity of data sets generated by modern sequencing and array-based profiling techniques pose significant challenges to visualization tools. To address these challenges, the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) is a high-performance viewer that seamlessly handles large, diverse data sets while providing an intuitive and user-friendly experience at various levels of genome resolution. A distinctive feature of IGV is its focus on integrative genomics, supporting both array-based and next-generation sequencing data, as well as the integration of clinical and phenotypic information. Although IGV is commonly used to visualize public genomic data, its primary objective is to facilitate researchers' ability to visualize and explore their own data sets or those from colleagues. To achieve this, IGV offers flexible loading of local and remote data sets and is optimized for high-performance data visualization and exploration on standard desktop systems. IGV is freely available for download from <http://www.broadinstitute.org/igv> under a GNU LGPL open-source license.

title: Can genome engineering be used to target cancer-associated enhancers?
text:
Transcriptional misregulation is a key factor in the development of many diseases, including cancer. Distal regulatory elements, such as enhancers, play a crucial role in determining cell-specific transcription patterns in both healthy and diseased tissues. As enhancers are involved in the regulation of gene expression in a cell-specific manner, targeting these elements for therapeutic intervention may offer a more specific and effective approach to treating diseases. By modulating gene regulation mediated by cell type-specific enhancers, it is possible to restore normal epigenetic patterning in affected tissues with fewer side effects than seen with treatments that employ more nonspecific inhibitors, such as epigenetic drugs.
New technologies, such as genomic nucleases and site-specific epigenetic regulators, are being developed to enable precise genome engineering at enhancers. These methods use either artificial DNA-binding proteins or RNA-DNA interactions to target specific genomic regions, allowing for more precise control over gene expression. While this field is still in its early stages, the potential for precise genome engineering at enhancers holds great promise for the treatment of diseases. However, further refinements are needed to increase specificity and efficiency in order to fully realize the therapeutic potential of this approach.

title: Long‐Term Follow‐up of CD19 CAR Therapy in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
text:
In a phase 1 clinical trial, researchers investigated the safety and efficacy of Background CD19-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells in adults with relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The study was conducted at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) and involved 53 patients.
The results of the study showed that the Background CD19-CAR T cells induced high rates of initial response among patients with relapsed ALL, with 83% of patients achieving complete remission after infusion. However, the treatment was associated with severe cytokine release syndrome in 26% of patients, with one patient dying as a result.
The study also found that patients with a low disease burden (<5% bone marrow blasts) before treatment had significantly longer remission duration and survival compared to those with a higher disease burden (≥5% bone marrow blasts or extramedullary disease). Specifically, patients with a low disease burden had a median event-free survival of 10.6 months (95% CI, 5.9-not reached) and a median overall survival of 20.1 months (95% CI, 8.7-not reached), compared to a median event-free survival of 5.0-11.5 months (95% CI) and a median overall survival of 8.7-23.4 months (95% CI) among patients with a higher disease burden.
In conclusion, the study demonstrated that Background CD19-CAR T cells are effective in inducing complete remission in patients with relapsed ALL, with a median overall survival of 12.9 months in the entire cohort and 20.1 months in patients with a low disease burden. However, the treatment was associated with severe side effects, including cytokine release syndrome, and patients with a higher disease burden had a greater incidence of these side effects and shorter long-term survival.

title: Periosteum contains skeletal stem cells with high bone regenerative potential controlled by Periostin
text: Bone regeneration relies on the activation of poorly characterized skeletal stem cells (SSCs) residing in the periosteum, according to our study. Unlike bone marrow stromal cells/skeletal stem cells (BMSCs), periosteal cells (PCs) exhibit greater clonogenicity, growth, and differentiation potential in mice.
