During bone repair, PCs can efficiently contribute to cartilage and bone formation and integrate long-term after transplantation. Our molecular profiling revealed genes encoding Periostin and other extracellular matrix molecules associated with the enhanced response to injury of PCs. Periostin gene deletion impairs PC functions and fracture consolidation, and periostin-deficient periosteum cannot reconstitute a pool of PCs after injury, indicating the presence of SSCs within the periosteum and the requirement of Periostin in maintaining this pool. Our findings underscore the importance of analyzing the periosteum and PCs to comprehend bone phenotypes.

title: Metabolism strikes back: metabolic flux regulates cell signaling.
text: Mammalian cells rely on growth factor signaling to absorb essential nutrients, yet the synchronization of glucose and glutamine uptake has remained a puzzle. In this issue of Genes & Development, Wellen and colleagues (pp. 2784-2799) uncover a crucial mechanism where glucose flux through the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway regulates growth factor receptor glycosylation, allowing glutamine consumption. This process ensures that cells do not overindulge in anabolic metabolism when nutrients are scarce, highlighting the significance of substrate availability in modulating cell signaling.

title: Association of Pembrolizumab With Tumor Response and Survival Among Patients With Advanced Melanoma.
text:
The study investigated the effectiveness and safety of the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody pembrolizumab in treating advanced melanoma. The study included 655 patients with advanced or metastatic melanoma who were enrolled in open-label, multicohort, phase 1b clinical trials between December 2011 and September 2013. The patients were aged 18 years or older and were randomly assigned to receive pembrolizumab at different doses and schedules. The primary endpoint of the study was the objective response rate (ORR) in patients with measurable disease at baseline, and secondary endpoints included toxicity, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival.
The study found that pembrolizumab administration was associated with an overall ORR of 33%, 12-month progression-free survival rate of 35%, and median overall survival of 23 months. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 14% of patients, and 4% of patients discontinued treatment due to a treatment-related AE. There were no drug-related deaths. The study concluded that pembrolizumab administration was effective and well-tolerated in treating advanced melanoma, with an overall ORR of 33% and a median overall survival of 23 months.

title: Inflammatory signaling in human Tuberculosis granulomas is spatially organized
text: Granulomas are a defining feature of tuberculosis (TB), yet their function and mechanisms of formation remain poorly understood. To investigate the role of granulomas in TB, we conducted an unbiased analysis of the proteomes of granulomas from TB-infected individuals. Using laser-capture microdissection, mass spectrometry, and confocal microscopy, we generated detailed molecular maps of human granulomas. Our findings revealed that the centers of granulomas have a pro-inflammatory environment characterized by the presence of antimicrobial peptides, reactive oxygen species, and pro-inflammatory eicosanoids. In contrast, the surrounding tissue has an anti-inflammatory signature. These findings were consistent across a set of six human subjects and in rabbits. Interestingly, we found that the balance between systemic pro- and anti-inflammatory signals within each granuloma is crucial to TB disease outcome, but these signals are physically segregated within each granuloma. Based on the protein and lipid snapshots of human and rabbit lesions analyzed here, we hypothesize that the pathologic response to TB is shaped by the precise anatomical localization of these inflammatory pathways during the development of the granuloma.

title: Suppression of interferon-mediated anti-HBV response by single CpG methylation in the 5′-UTR of TRIM22
text:
Objective: Interferons (IFNs) play a crucial role in the early host immune response against viral infections, including hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, the effectiveness of IFN therapy for HBV infection is lower compared to other viral infections. This study aimed to investigate the cellular targets of HBV in response to IFNs using a proteome-wide screening approach.
Methods: We used liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to identify proteins downregulated and upregulated by IFN treatment in HBV X protein (HBx)-stable and control cells. We also investigated the mechanism by which HBV evades the host innate immune system through the suppression of IFN-stimulated genes.
Results: Our results showed that IFN treatment downregulated several genes, including TRIM22, which is known to have antiretroviral activity. We found that HBx suppresses the transcription of TRIM22 through a single CpG methylation in its 5'-untranslated region (UTR), leading to a reduction in the binding affinity of IFN regulatory factor-1 (IRF-1) and subsequent suppression of TRIM22 induction by IFN.
Conclusion: We verified our findings using a mouse model, primary human hepatocytes, and human liver tissues. Our data provide insight into the mechanism by which HBV evades the host innate immune system, highlighting the potential for targeting this mechanism for the development of novel antiviral therapies.

title: Developmental Analysis of Bone Marrow Neutrophils Reveals Populations Specialized in Expansion, Trafficking, and Effector Functions
text:
Summary:
Neutrophils are specialized white blood cells that require constant replenishment from bone marrow (BM) precursors due to their short lifespan. Although it is known that neutrophils originate from the granulocyte-macrophage progenitor (GMP), the specific pathways involved in their differentiation are not well understood. Using mass cytometry (CyTOF) and cell-cycle-based analysis, researchers identified three distinct neutrophil subsets within the BM: a committed proliferative neutrophil precursor (preNeu), which differentiates into non-proliferating immature neutrophils and mature neutrophils. Transcriptomic profiling and functional analysis revealed that preNeu require the C/EBPε transcription factor for their generation from GMP and their proliferative program is replaced by a gain of migratory and effector functions as they mature. preNeus expand under microbial and tumoral stress, and immature neutrophils are recruited to the periphery of tumor-bearing mice. In summary, the study identifies specialized BM granulocytic populations that ensure supply under homeostasis and stress responses.

title: TAK1-mediated autophagy and fatty acid oxidation prevent hepatosteatosis and tumorigenesis.
text:
The TGFβ-activated kinase kinase TAK1 is activated by various inflammatory cytokines, including TLRs, IL-1, TNF, and TGFβ. In turn, TAK1 activates the IKK-NF-κB and JNK signaling pathways, which regulate cell survival, growth, tumorigenesis, and metabolism. TAK1 signaling also enhances AMPK activity and autophagy. In this study, we investigated the role of TAK1 in regulating autophagy, lipid metabolism, and tumorigenesis in the liver.
We found that mice lacking TAK1 in hepatocytes exhibited severe hepatosteatosis and increased mTORC1 activity, which suppressed autophagy compared to their wild-type counterparts. TAK1-deficient hepatocytes showed decreased AMPK activity and autophagy in response to starvation or metformin treatment, but ectopic activation of AMPK restored autophagy in these cells. Additionally, we found that PPARα target genes and β-oxidation, which regulate hepatic lipid degradation, were also suppressed in hepatocytes lacking TAK1.
Interestingly, a high-fat diet challenge aggravated steatohepatitis in mice with hepatocyte-specific deletion of Tak1. Notably, inhibition of mTORC1 restored autophagy and PPARα target gene expression in TAK1-deficient livers, suggesting that TAK1 acts upstream of mTORC1. Furthermore, mTORC1 inhibition also suppressed spontaneous liver fibrosis and hepatocarcinogenesis in animals with hepatocyte-specific deletion of Tak1. These findings indicate that TAK1 regulates hepatic lipid metabolism and tumorigenesis via the AMPK/mTORC1 axis, affecting both autophagy and PPARα activity.

title: Formins at the Junction.
text: At the cell-cell interface between epithelial cells, the actin cytoskeleton and adhesion junctions are intimately linked through physical and functional interactions. The actin regulatory complex Arp2/3 has been shown to play a crucial role in the turnover of junctional actin, while the role of formins, the largest group of actin regulators, is less well understood. Formins are key players in shaping the actin cytoskeleton and have a range of functions within cells. In this review, we will discuss recent advances in our understanding of how formins regulate actin dynamics at cell-cell contacts and highlight their important functions during polarized protein traffic, which is essential for epithelialization.

title: CRISPR adaptation biases explain preference for acquisition of foreign DNA
text: CRISPR-Cas (clustered, regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats coupled with CRISPR-associated proteins) is a bacterial immune system that protects against invading phages or plasmids. During the CRISPR adaptation process, short pieces of DNA (spacers) are acquired from foreign elements and integrated into the CRISPR array. It has remained a mystery how spacers are selectively acquired from foreign DNA while self chromosome is avoided. Our study reveals that spacer acquisition is replication-dependent, and DNA breaks formed at stalled replication forks promote spacer acquisition. Chromosomal hotspots of spacer acquisition were found to be confined by Chi sites, which are sequence octamers highly enriched on the bacterial chromosome. These sites limit spacer acquisition from self DNA, and the avoidance of self is mediated by the RecBCD double-stranded DNA break repair complex. Our results suggest that in Escherichia coli, the acquisition of new spacers largely depends on RecBCD-mediated processing of double-stranded DNA breaks occurring primarily at replication forks, and the preference for foreign DNA is achieved through the higher density of Chi sites on the self chromosome, in combination with the higher number of forks on the foreign DNA. This model explains the strong preference to acquire spacers both from high copy plasmids and from phages.

title: High-resolution mapping of open chromatin in the rice genome.
text: Gene expression is regulated by the intricate interaction of transcription factors binding to specific DNA elements. One common feature of regions associated with regulatory proteins is their sensitivity to DNase I digestion. To investigate the genomic landscape of gene regulation in rice (Oryza sativa), we generated high-resolution maps of DNase I hypersensitive (DH) sites in both seedling and callus tissues. Surprisingly, only approximately 25% of the DH sites were found in putative promoters, indicating that the majority of gene regulatory elements in rice are not located in these regions. We observed a significant increase in DH sites in the callus compared to the seedling (58% more). Within the DH sites detected in both tissues, 31% showed altered DNase I sensitivity levels between the two tissues. Genes associated with these differentially expressed DH sites were frequently found in both tissues. The DNA sequences within the DH sites were hypomethylated, consistent with active gene regulatory elements. Interestingly, tissue-specific DH sites located in promoters had higher DNA methylation levels than the average methylation level of all DH sites in promoters. A distinct enrichment of H3K27me3 was observed at intergenic DH sites. These findings suggest that epigenetic modifications play a role in the dynamic changes in the number and DNase I sensitivity of DH sites during development.

title: Prospective study of body fat distribution and the risk of endometrial cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies have shown that overall obesity is positively associated with the risk of endometrial cancer (EC). However, there is limited research on the relationship between body fat distribution and EC risk.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 51,948 women in the Nurses' Health Study who reported their waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference in 1986. We calculated the waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and followed the women for 24 years, during which time 449 incident invasive EC cases were diagnosed.
RESULTS: In our analysis, we found that in the absence of adjustment for body mass index (BMI), the relative risks (RRs) for EC were 2.44 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.72-3.45) for WC and 1.69 (95% CI=1.20-2.40) for WHR. However, after adjusting for BMI, these positive associations were significantly attenuated and no longer reached statistical significance; RR=1.08 (95% CI=0.69-1.67) for WC and 1.15 (95% CI=0.81-1.64) for WHR, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In our prospective cohort study, we found no independent association between body fat distribution and the risk of EC after adjusting for BMI.

title: Breast cancer clusters in the northeast United States: a geographic analysis.
text: High breast cancer mortality rates have been reported in the northeastern region of the United States, with recent attention focused on Long Island, New York. In this study, the authors investigate whether the high breast cancer mortality is evenly distributed across the Northeast or if there are specific areas with statistically significant clusters of deaths. They analyzed demographic data and age-specific breast cancer mortality rates for 244 counties in 11 northeastern states and the District of Columbia over the period of 1988-1992. The study used a newly developed spatial scan statistic that searches for clusters of cases without specifying their size or location ahead of time, and tests for their statistical significance while adjusting for multiple testing. The analysis was adjusted for age, and further analyses were conducted to examine the impact of race, urbanicity, and parity as confounding variables. The results showed a statistically significant and broad cluster of breast cancer deaths in the New York City-Philadelphia, Pennsylvania metropolitan area, with a 7.4% higher mortality rate than the rest of the Northeast. Four smaller subclusters within this area were also found to be statistically significant: Philadelphia with suburbs, Long Island, central New Jersey, and northeastern New Jersey. The elevated breast cancer mortality on Long Island may be part of a larger pattern involving large parts of the New York City-Philadelphia metropolitan area. The study could not adjust for all potential risk factors, including age at first birth, age at menarche, age at menopause, breastfeeding, genetic mutations, and environmental factors, which may explain the detected cluster.

title: CD200R/CD200 Inhibits Osteoclastogenesis: New Mechanism of Osteoclast Control by Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Human
text: Homeostasis of the bone is maintained by the balance between bone-forming osteoblasts and bone-degrading osteoclasts. Osteoblasts originate from mesenchymal cells, while osteoclasts belong to the myeloid lineage. Communication between osteoclasts and osteoblasts occurs through the secretion of soluble factors, cell-bone interactions, and cell-cell contact, which modulate their activities. CD200, an immunoglobulin superfamily member, is expressed on various cell types, including mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). The CD200 receptor (CD200R) is expressed on myeloid cells such as monocytes/macrophages. We hypothesize that CD200 may be involved in the regulation of osteoclastogenesis and play a role in MSC-osteoclast communication in humans. In this study, we demonstrate that soluble CD200 inhibits the differentiation and maturation of osteoclast precursors in vitro, as well as the RANKL signaling pathway and the expression of osteoclast markers such as OSCAR and NFATc1. Moreover, MSCs inhibit osteoclast formation through cell-cell contact and CD200 expression on their surface. Our results clearly show that MSCs play a major role in regulating bone resorption and bone physiology, and that the CD200-CD200R couple may be a new target for controlling bone diseases.

title: Tumor-specific Th17-polarized cells eradicate large established melanoma.
text: CD4+ T cells can differentiate into multiple effector subsets, but their potential roles in anti-tumor immunity have not been fully explored. To investigate the impact of CD4+ T cell polarization on tumor rejection in a model mimicking human disease, we generated a new MHC class II-restricted, T-cell receptor (TCR) transgenic mouse model in which CD4+ T cells recognize a novel epitope in tyrosinase-related protein 1 (TRP-1), an antigen expressed by normal melanocytes and B16 murine melanoma. In vitro, we could robustly polarize CD4+ T cells into Th0, Th1, and Th17 subtypes based on cytokine, chemokine, and adhesion molecule profiles and surface markers, suggesting the potential for differential effector function in vivo. Contrary to the current view that Th1 cells are most important in tumor rejection, we found that Th17-polarized cells were more effective in destroying advanced B16 melanoma, with their therapeutic effect dependent on interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) production. In contrast, depletion of interleukin (IL)-17A and IL-23 had little impact. These findings suggest that the appropriate in vitro polarization of effector CD4+ T cells is crucial for successful tumor eradication, a principle that should be considered in designing clinical trials involving adoptive transfer-based immunotherapy of human malignancies.

title: Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study.
text:
Background: In assessing the severity of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), the modified British Thoracic Society (mBTS) rule identifies patients with severe pneumonia but does not identify those who may be suitable for home management. To develop a practical severity assessment model for stratifying adults hospitalized with CAP into different management groups, a multicenter study was conducted.
Methods: Data from three prospective studies of CAP conducted in the UK, New Zealand, and the Netherlands were combined. A derivation cohort comprising 80% of the data was used to develop the model, and the final model was tested against the validation cohort. Prognostic variables were identified using multiple logistic regression with 30-day mortality as the outcome measure.
Results: A total of 1068 patients were studied (mean age 64 years, 51.5% male, 30-day mortality 9%). Age ≥65 years and albumin <30 g/dl were independently associated with mortality over and above the mBTS rule (OR 5.2, 95% CI 2.7 to 10). A six-point score based on information available at initial hospital assessment enabled patients to be stratified according to increasing risk of mortality: score 0, 0.7%; score 1, 3.2%; score 2, 3%; score 3, 17%; score 4, 41.5%; and score 5, 57%. The validation cohort confirmed a similar pattern.
Conclusions: A simple six-point score based on confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age can be used to stratify patients with CAP into different management groups.

title: Mitochondrial iron chelation ameliorates cigarette-smoke induced bronchitis and emphysema in mice
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is linked to both smoking and genetic factors. We have previously identified iron-responsive element-binding protein 2 (IRP2) as a key gene associated with COPD susceptibility, and found that IRP2 protein levels are elevated in the lungs of individuals with COPD. In this study, we investigated the role of IRP2 in COPD development using mice. We found that mice lacking IRP2 were protected from cigarette smoke (CS)-induced experimental COPD. By using RNA immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (RIP-seq), RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and gene expression and functional enrichment clustering analysis, we identified IRP2 as a regulator of mitochondrial function in the lungs of mice. Specifically, we found that IRP2 increases mitochondrial iron loading and levels of cytochrome c oxidase (COX), leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and COPD. Interestingly, mice lacking the synthesis of cytochrome c oxidase, which have reduced COX, were protected from CS-induced pulmonary inflammation and impairment of mucociliary clearance (MCC). Mice treated with a mitochondrial iron chelator or fed a low-iron diet were also protected from CS-induced COPD. These findings suggest that targeting the mitochondrial-iron axis may be a promising therapeutic strategy for COPD.

title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Neutralize the Anti-tumor Effect of CSF1 Receptor Blockade by Inducing PMN-MDSC Infiltration of Tumors.
text: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) play a crucial role in promoting tumor progression. Targeting CSF1R, a key regulator of TAM function, has shown limited anti-tumor potential. Our study uncovered the mechanism that hinders the effectiveness of CSF1R-targeted therapy. We found that carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) are the primary sources of chemokines that attract granulocytes to the tumor microenvironment. Tumor cells produce CSF1, which inhibits the expression of granulocyte-specific chemokines in CAF through HDAC2-mediated mechanisms, thereby limiting the migration of these cells to the tumor site. Treatment with CSF1R inhibitors disrupts this crosstalk, leading to a significant increase in granulocyte recruitment to the tumor. Combining CSF1R inhibitors with a CXCR2 antagonist, which blocks granulocyte infiltration, resulted in strong anti-tumor effects.

title: Phenotypic deficits in the HIV-1 envelope are associated with the maturation of a V2-directed broadly neutralizing antibody lineage
text:
The emergence of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) against HIV-1 is a crucial goal of vaccine development, as it can provide long-term protection against the virus. However, the evolution of HIV-1 envelopes (Env) can lead to the development of resistance to bnAbs through a process of virus escape and antibody adaptation. To better understand this process and design effective vaccines, it is essential to identify the properties of Env that are capable of eliciting bnAb responses.
In this study, we investigated the evolution of the V2 apex directed bnAb lineage VRC26 in the HIV-1 subtype C superinfected donor CAP256. We analyzed the phenotypic changes of the virus populations circulating before and during the early phases of bnAb induction, and found that substantial phenotypic changes in Env occurred coinciding with early resistance to VRC26. Specifically, we observed a switch in Env properties, decreased sensitivity of superinfecting (SU) virus to VRC26, and reduced infectivity, altered entry kinetics, and lower sensitivity to neutralization after CD4 attachment. Notably, VRC26 maintained neutralization activity against cell-associated CAP256 virus, indicating that escape through the cell-cell transmission route is not a dominant escape pathway.
Our findings highlight the phenotypic plasticity of HIV-1 Env in evading bnAb pressure and the need to consider phenotypic traits when selecting and designing Env immunogens. We propose that combinations of Env variants with differential phenotypic patterns and bnAb sensitivity, as we describe here for CAP256, may maximize the potential for inducing bnAb responses by vaccination. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the mechanisms of HIV-1 resistance to bnAbs and informs the development of effective vaccine strategies.

title: High somatic mutation and neoantigen burden are correlated with decreased progression-free survival in multiple myeloma
text: Tumor-specific mutations can give rise to immunogenic neoantigens, which have been found to be associated with responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors in certain types of cancer. However, early clinical trials of single-agent checkpoint inhibitors in multiple myeloma (MM) have yielded disappointing results. To investigate the relationship between mutational burden and neoantigen landscape in MM patients and their response to therapy, we analyzed interim data from the MMRF CoMMpass study (NCT01454297) on 664 MM patients. Our findings revealed a positive linear correlation between somatic and missense mutation loads and neoantigen burdens (R2=0.862). On average, predicted neoantigen loads were 23.52 neoantigens, with an average of 9.40 expressed neoantigens per patient. Survival analysis showed that patients with higher somatic missense mutation loads and predicted expressed neoantigen loads had significantly shorter progression-free survival (PFS) compared to those with lower loads (P=0.0023 and P=0.0028, respectively). This pattern held true when analyzing the data by disease stage and cytogenetic abnormalities. Our findings suggest that high tumor mutation and neoantigen loads are clinically relevant risk factors that negatively impact survival of MM patients under current treatment standards.

title: Postmarket Safety Events Among Novel Therapeutics Approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Between 2001 and 2010
text:
Novel pharmaceuticals and biologics approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) often experience postmarket safety events, including withdrawals due to safety concerns, incremental boxed warnings, and safety communications, after initial regulatory approval. This study aimed to characterize the frequency of postmarket safety events among novel therapeutics approved between 2001 and 2010 and to identify potential predictors of these events.
The study included 222 novel therapeutics approved by the FDA during this period, of which 71 (32%) were affected by a postmarket safety event during a median follow-up period of 11.7 years. The median time from approval to the first postmarket safety event was 4.2 years, and the proportion of novel therapeutics affected by a postmarket safety event at 10 years was 30.8%. Multivariable analysis revealed that biologics, therapeutics indicated for psychiatric disease, those receiving accelerated approval, and those with near–regulatory deadline approval were statistically significantly associated with higher rates of postmarket safety events. Conversely, novel therapeutics with regulatory review times less than 200 days were associated with lower rates of events.
The findings of this study highlight the need for continuous monitoring of the safety of novel therapeutics throughout their life cycle, particularly for biologics, psychiatric therapeutics, and those approved through accelerated or near–regulatory deadline pathways. These results have implications for the regulatory approval process and clinical practice, as they suggest that postmarket safety events can occur even after initial regulatory approval and may require ongoing monitoring and management.

title: Who is where at risk for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease? A spatial epidemiological analysis of health insurance claims for COPD in Northeastern Germany
text:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a prevalent condition in Germany, with a projected increase in incidence in the coming years. Despite a comprehensive understanding of individual-level risk factors, there is limited knowledge on the spatial heterogeneity and population-based risk factors of COPD. An analysis of the broader, population-based processes could inform the development of more targeted healthcare and prevention strategies. This study aims to investigate the variation in COPD prevalence across municipalities and urban districts in northeastern Germany and identify location-specific population-based risk factors using health insurance claims from the AOK Nordost.
METHODS: To visualize the spatial distribution of COPD prevalence at the smallest possible scale, we employed a conditional autoregressive Besag-York-Mollié (BYM) model. Geographically weighted regression modeling (GWR) was applied to identify ecological risk factors for COPD at the population level.
RESULTS: The sex- and age-adjusted COPD prevalence was 6.5% in 2012, with significant variation across northeastern Germany. Population-based risk factors included the proportion of insurants aged 65 and older, insurants with migration background, household size, and area deprivation. The GWR model revealed that the population at risk for COPD varies substantially across northeastern Germany.
CONCLUSION: Area deprivation has both direct and indirect influences on COPD prevalence. Individuals residing in socially disadvantaged areas are at a higher risk of developing COPD, even if they are not directly affected by deprivation on an individual level. This highlights the importance of considering the impact of area deprivation on health when planning healthcare. Additionally, our findings indicate that certain subpopulations, such as insurants with migration background and individuals living in multi-person households, are at elevated risk of COPD in specific areas of the study region.

title: Large intergenic non-coding RNA-RoR modulates reprogramming of human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: The transition of lineage-committed cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) through reprogramming is accompanied by a comprehensive remodeling of the epigenome, resulting in altered patterns of gene expression. In this study, we investigate the transcriptional reorganization of large intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) during the derivation of human iPSCs and identify lincRNAs whose expression is associated with pluripotency. Among these, we identify ten lincRNAs whose expression is elevated in iPSCs compared to embryonic stem cells, suggesting that their activation may contribute to the emergence of iPSCs. Our findings indicate that these lincRNAs are direct targets of key pluripotency transcription factors, and using loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches, we demonstrate that one such lincRNA (lincRNA-RoR) plays a critical role in reprogramming. This study provides the first evidence for the functional importance of lincRNAs in the derivation of pluripotent stem cells.

title: Extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization: toward clinical application.
text: Two main types of extracellular vesicles (EVs), exosomes and shed microvesicles (sMVs), have been identified, each with distinct size distributions and protein/RNA profiles. EVs play a crucial role in cell-cell communication, both locally and systemically, and can be isolated from cell culture media and body fluids using various strategies. This review discusses the characteristics of EV subtypes, methods for isolating and quantifying EVs, as well as proteins selectively enriched in exosomes and sMVs that could be used as markers to distinguish between EV subtypes. Additionally, the review explores the potential applications of EVs in clinical diagnosis.

title: Up-regulated NRIP2 in colorectal cancer initiating cells modulates the Wnt pathway by targeting RORβ
text:
Colorectal cancer remains one of the most common types of cancer worldwide, and colorectal cancer initiating cells (CCICs) are a small subpopulation responsible for the malignant behaviors of colorectal cancer. However, the underlying mechanisms of CCIC self-renewal are not well understood. Recently, we identified Nuclear Receptor-Interacting Protein 2 (NRIP2) as a novel interactor of the Wnt pathway in enriched colorectal cancer colosphere cells. Our study found that NRIP2 is significantly up-regulated in CCICs from both cell lines and primary colorectal cancer tissues, and its overexpression increases Wnt activity, while silencing of NRIP2 attenuates Wnt activity.
We also found that the transcription factor RORβ is a key target through which NRIP2 regulates Wnt pathway activity. RORβ is a transcriptional enhancer of inhibitor HBP1 of the Wnt pathway, and NRIP2 prevents RORβ from binding with downstream HBP1 promoter regions, reducing the transcription of HBP1. This, in turn, attenuates the HBP1-dependent inhibition of TCF4-mediated transcription.
Our findings suggest that NRIP2 plays a critical role in CCIC self-renewal via the Wnt pathway, and its interactions with RORβ and HBP1 mediate a new mechanism for CCIC self-renewal. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer and may lead to the development of new therapeutic strategies for colorectal cancer treatment.

title: Speed Limits for Nonvesicular Intracellular Sterol Transport.
text: Sterol transport between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and plasma membrane (PM) occurs through non-vesicular mechanisms that require sterol transport proteins (STPs). We investigate the hypothesis that transport is enhanced at membrane contact sites where the ER is closely associated with the PM. Our findings suggest that sterol desorption from the membrane, rather than STP-mediated diffusion, is the rate-limiting step in the cellular context, indicating that there is no advantageous kinetic benefit to having STP-mediated sterol transfer occur at contact sites. Instead, contact sites may function to compartmentalize lipid synthesis or transport machinery, providing opportunities for regulatory control.

title: Misunderstandings in prescribing decisions in general practice: qualitative study.
text:
Objectives:
To identify and describe the misunderstandings that occur between patients and doctors during prescribing decisions in general practice.
Design: Qualitative study.
Setting: 20 general practices in the West Midlands and south east England.
Participants: 20 general practitioners and 35 consulting patients.
Main Outcome Measures: Misunderstandings between patients and doctors that have the potential or actual adverse consequences for taking medication.
Results: 14 categories of misunderstandings were identified, including patient information unknown to the doctor, doctor information unknown to the patient, conflicting information, disagreement about attribution of side effects, failure of communication about the doctor's decision, and relationship factors. All of these misunderstandings were associated with a lack of patients' participation in the consultation, in terms of voicing expectations and preferences or voicing responses to doctors' decisions and actions. They were all associated with potential or actual adverse outcomes, such as non-adherence to treatment. Many of these misunderstandings were based on inaccurate guesses and assumptions. In particular, doctors seemed unaware of the relevance of patients' ideas about medications for successful prescribing.
Conclusions: Patients' participation in the consultation and the adverse consequences of a lack of participation are crucial. The authors are developing an educational intervention that builds on these findings.

title: Phase-plate cryo-EM structure of a biased agonist-bound human GLP-1 receptor–Gs complex
text: The class B glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) G protein-coupled receptor is a key therapeutic target for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with both endogenous and synthetic GLP-1 peptides exhibiting unique functional selectivity. Here, we report the high-resolution structure of the human GLP-1 receptor in complex with the G protein-biased peptide exendin-P5 and a Gαs heterotrimer, at a global resolution of 3.3 Å. Comparing this structure to previous GLP-1 receptor structures reveals distinct differences in the organization of extracellular loop 3 and proximal transmembrane segments, as well as variations in the angle of Gαs–α5 helix engagement and the rate of conformational reorganization of the Gαs protein. These findings provide valuable insights into the molecular basis of biased agonism and its potential for improving therapeutic outcomes.

title: Therapeutic equivalence of alendronate 70 mg once-weekly and alendronate 10 mg daily in the treatment of osteoporosis. Alendronate Once-Weekly Study Group.
text:
Dosing convenience is a crucial factor in the effective management of chronic diseases, particularly osteoporosis. Less frequent dosing can enhance patient compliance, leading to better treatment outcomes. Animal studies have shown that once-weekly dosing with alendronate (70 mg) may provide similar efficacy to daily dosing (10 mg) due to its long duration of effect in bone. Additionally, dog studies suggest that the potential for esophageal irritation associated with daily oral bisphosphonates may be reduced with once-weekly dosing.
We conducted a one-year, double-blind, multicenter study of postmenopausal women (ages 42 to 95) with osteoporosis to compare the efficacy and safety of oral once-weekly alendronate 70 mg (N=519), twice-weekly alendronate 35 mg (N=369), and daily alendronate 10 mg (N=370). The primary endpoint was the comparability of increases in lumbar spine BMD, using strict pre-defined equivalence criteria. Secondary endpoints included changes in BMD at the hip and total body, as well as rate of bone turnover, assessed by biochemical markers. All three dosing regimens satisfied the equivalence criteria relative to daily therapy. Mean increases in lumbar spine BMD at 12 months were 5.1% (95% CI 4.8, 5.4) in the 70 mg once-weekly group, 5.2% (4.9, 5.6) in the 35 mg twice-weekly group, and 5.4% (5.0, 5.8) in the 10 mg daily treatment group. Increases in BMD at the total hip, femoral neck, trochanter, and total body were similar among the three groups. All three treatment groups similarly reduced biochemical markers of bone resorption (urinary N-telopeptides of type I collagen) and bone formation (serum bone-specific alkaline phosphatase) into the middle of the premenopausal reference range. All treatment regimens were well tolerated, with a similar incidence of upper GI adverse experiences. There were fewer serious upper GI adverse experiences, and a trend toward a lower incidence of esophageal events in the once-weekly dosing group compared to the daily dosing group. Clinical fractures, captured as adverse experiences, were similar among the groups.
Based on these findings, we conclude that the alendronate 70 mg once-weekly dosing regimen provides patients with increased convenience and may enhance compliance and long-term persistence with therapy, leading to improved treatment outcomes.

title: Association of Toll-Like Receptor 4 on Human Monocyte Subsets and Vulnerability Characteristics of Coronary Plaque as Assessed by 64-Slice Multidetector Computed Tomography.
text:
Background: Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR-4) is involved in monocyte activation in patients with rapidly progressing atherosclerosis, but its relationship with coronary plaque vulnerability has not been well-studied. We aimed to investigate this relationship in patients with stable angina pectoris (SAP) using 64-slice multidetector computed tomography (MDCT).
Methods and Results: We enrolled 65 patients with SAP who underwent MDCT. We measured the expression of TLR-4 on three monocyte subsets (CD14++CD16-, CD14++CD16+, and CD14+CD16+) using flow cytometry. Intracoronary plaques were assessed by 64-slice MDCT, and their vulnerability was defined based on the presence of positive remodeling (remodeling index >1.05) and/or low CT attenuation (<35 HU). We found that the circulating CD14++CD16+monocytes more frequently expressed TLR-4 than the other two subsets (P<0.001). Moreover, the relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+monocytes was significantly higher in patients with vulnerable plaques compared to those without (10.4 [4.1-14.5] % vs. 4.5 [2.8-7.8] %, P=0.012). Additionally, the relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+monocytes positively correlated with the remodeling index (r=0.28, P=0.025) and negatively correlated with CT attenuation value (r=-0.31, P=0.013).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that upregulation of TLR-4 on CD14++CD16+monocytes may be associated with coronary plaque vulnerability in patients with SAP.

title: Expandable Cardiovascular Progenitor Cells Reprogrammed from Fibroblasts.
text: Stem cell-based approaches to cardiac regeneration are gaining traction as potential treatments for heart failure. However, generating sufficient and functional autologous cells for transplantation remains a significant challenge. In this study, we isolated a cell population with remarkable proliferation capacity and limited cardiovascular differentiation potential during cardiac transdifferentiation of mouse fibroblasts. These induced expandable cardiovascular progenitor cells (ieCPCs) exhibited extensive proliferation in chemically defined conditions, with 10,000 starting fibroblasts producing 10 million ieCPCs. Notably, ieCPCs expressed cardiac signature genes and readily differentiated into functional cardiomyocytes (CMs), endothelial cells (ECs), and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) in vitro, even after prolonged expansion. When transplanted into mouse hearts following myocardial infarction, ieCPCs spontaneously differentiated into CMs, ECs, and SMCs and improved cardiac function for up to 12 weeks after transplantation. These findings demonstrate the potential of ieCPCs as a valuable system for studying cardiovascular specification and providing strategies for regenerative medicine in the heart.

title: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function
text: The thyroid hormone (TH) plays a crucial role in maintaining cellular homeostasis during stress responses, but its involvement in lung fibrosis remains unclear. Our study found that the activity and expression of iodothyronine deiodinase 2 (DIO2), an enzyme that activates TH, were significantly higher in the lungs of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis compared to healthy individuals, and were correlated with disease severity. We also discovered that DIO2-knockout mice were more susceptible to bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. Intriguingly, aerosolized TH delivery improved survival and resolved fibrosis in two mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis, and the TH mimetic, sobetirome, also attenuated bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. Our findings suggest that TH's antifibrotic properties are linked to its ability to protect alveolar epithelial cells and restore mitochondrial function. Notably, TH did not blunt fibrosis in mice lacking PPARGC1A or PINK1, implying that these pathways are essential for its antifibrotic effects. Overall, our study suggests that TH may represent a potential therapeutic approach for pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Tenomodulin promotes human adipocyte differentiation and beneficial visceral adipose tissue expansion.
text: Proper regulation of energy storage in adipose tissue is crucial for maintaining insulin sensitivity, and the molecular mechanisms underlying this process are not yet fully understood. Our study reveals that the type II transmembrane protein tenomodulin (TNMD) is upregulated in adipose tissue from insulin-resistant individuals compared to insulin-sensitive individuals, despite matching for body mass index (BMI). We found that TNMD expression increases in human preadipocytes during differentiation, and silencing TNMD inhibits adipogenesis. In mice fed a high-fat diet, overexpression of TNMD leads to increased epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) mass, and preadipocytes derived from TNMD-transgenic mice show enhanced proliferation. In these mice, lipogenic genes are upregulated in eWAT, and Ucp1 is upregulated in brown fat, while liver triglyceride accumulation is attenuated. Despite increased eWAT, TNMD-transgenic mice display improved systemic insulin sensitivity, reduced collagen deposition and inflammation in eWAT, and enhanced insulin stimulation of Akt phosphorylation. Our findings suggest that TNMD acts as a protective factor in visceral adipose tissue, alleviating insulin resistance in obesity.

title: Evidence for a limit to human lifespan
text: Since the 19th century, technological advancements have significantly increased human life expectancy. Demographic evidence reveals a consistent decline in mortality rates among the elderly and an increase in the maximum age at death, which may contribute to extended human longevity. These findings are supported by observations in various animal species, where lifespan can be influenced by genetic or pharmaceutical interventions. However, by analyzing global demographic data, we found that improvements in survival rates with age decline after the age of 100, and the world's oldest person's age of death has remained unchanged since the 1990s. Our results suggest that the maximum human lifespan is fixed and subject to natural constraints.

title: Effect of Oral Semaglutide Compared With Placebo and Subcutaneous Semaglutide on Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial
text: The article compares the effects of oral semaglutide with placebo and open-label subcutaneous semaglutide on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes. The study was a randomized, parallel-group, dosage-finding trial conducted over 26 weeks at 100 sites in 14 countries. A total of 1106 participants were assessed, of which 632 with type 2 diabetes and insufficient glycemic control were randomized. The study found that oral semaglutide resulted in better glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks, with significant reductions in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels. The study also found that body weight reductions were greater with oral semaglutide and subcutaneous semaglutide compared to placebo. Adverse events were common across all groups, with mild to moderate gastrointestinal events being the most common. The findings support the use of oral semaglutide for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, and suggest that longer-term and clinical outcomes studies are warranted.

title: Fast and accurate short read alignment with Burrows–Wheeler transform
text:
Motivation: The massive amount of short DNA sequencing reads generated by recent technologies necessitates the development of fast and accurate read alignment software. A first-generation of hash table-based methods have been created, including MAQ, which is accurate, feature-rich, and fast enough to align short reads from a single individual. However, MAQ does not support gapped alignment for single-end reads, making it unsuitable for aligning longer reads where indels occur frequently. Additionally, the speed of MAQ becomes a concern when scaling up the alignment to resequencing hundreds of individuals.
Results: To address these limitations, we developed Burrows-Wheeler Alignment (BWA), a new read alignment package that leverages backward search with Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT) to efficiently align short sequencing reads against a large reference sequence, such as the human genome, allowing for mismatches and gaps. BWA supports both base space reads, like those from Illumina sequencing machines, and color space reads from AB SOLiD machines. Evaluations on both simulated and real data demonstrate that BWA is approximately 10-20 times faster than MAQ while maintaining similar accuracy. Moreover, BWA outputs alignment in the standard SAM (Sequence Alignment/Map) format, making it easier to perform downstream analyses using the open-source SAMtools software package.
Availability: BWA is available for download at <http://maq.sourceforge.net>.

title: The financial cost of doctors emigrating from sub-Saharan Africa: human capital analysis
text:
Objective: To estimate the economic loss incurred by sub-Saharan African countries due to the migration of domestically educated doctors to Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
Design: A human capital cost analysis using publicly accessible data.
Setting: Nine sub-Saharan African countries with a high HIV prevalence or a large number of people living with HIV/AIDS and at least one medical school (Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe).
Participants: The study included doctors who migrated from the nine source countries to the four destination countries.
Main Outcome Measures: The study measured the financial cost of educating a doctor, calculated by converting the government-subsidized cost of education to US dollars using current country-specific interest rates. The study also calculated the cost of educating doctors in each source country and the savings to destination countries from receiving trained doctors.
Results: The estimated government-subsidized cost of educating a doctor in the nine source countries ranged from $21,000 in Uganda to $58,700 in South Africa. The overall estimated loss of returns from investment for all doctors currently working in the destination countries was $2.17 billion (95% confidence interval $2.13 billion to $2.21 billion), with costs ranging from $2.16 million (1.55 million to 2.78 million) for Malawi to $1.41 billion (1.38 billion to 1.44 billion) for South Africa. The ratio of the estimated compounded lost investment to gross domestic product was highest for Zimbabwe and South Africa. The study found that the benefit to destination countries of recruiting trained doctors was highest for the United Kingdom ($2.7 billion) and the United States ($846 million).
Conclusions: The study found that the emigration of domestically educated doctors from sub-Saharan African countries to Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States results in significant economic loss for the source countries. The study suggests that destination countries should invest in measurable training for source countries and strengthen their health systems to address this issue.

title: Chromatin modifying enzymes as modulators of reprogramming
text: The generation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) through somatic cell reprogramming involves a comprehensive reorganization of epigenetic marks. Although several proteins have been identified as regulators of chromatin-associated epigenetic states, the specific role of chromatin-modifying enzymes in the reprogramming process remains unclear. To investigate the contribution of these enzymes, we employed short hairpin RNAs (shRNAs) to target genes involved in DNA and histone methylation pathways, and identified positive and negative modulators of iPSC generation. Our findings reveal that inhibition of core components of the polycomb repressive complex 1 and 2, including the histone 3 lysine 27 methyltransferase EZH2, reduces reprogramming efficiency. Conversely, suppression of SUV39H1, YY1, and DOT1L enhances reprogramming. Specifically, inhibition of DOT1L by shRNA or small molecule treatment accelerates reprogramming, significantly increasing the yield of iPSC colonies, and substitutes for KLF4 and c-Myc (also known as MYC). Early inhibition of DOT1L leads to an increase in two alternative factors, NANOG and LIN28, which play essential roles in reprogramming. Genome-wide analysis of H3K79me2 distribution reveals that fibroblast-specific genes associated with the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition lose H3K79me2 in the initial phases of reprogramming. DOT1L inhibition facilitates the loss of this mark from genes that are fated to be repressed in the pluripotent state. These findings implicate specific chromatin-modifying enzymes as barriers or facilitators of reprogramming, and demonstrate how modulation of these enzymes can be exploited to more efficiently generate iPSCs with fewer exogenous transcription factors.

title: Natural variation in the parameters of innate immune cells is preferentially driven by genetic factors
text: The analysis of circulating immune cells provides valuable insights into human health and disease. To investigate the interplay between environmental and genetic factors on immune cell parameters in healthy individuals, we combined standardized flow cytometry of blood leukocytes with genome-wide DNA genotyping of 1,000 unrelated individuals of Western European ancestry. Our findings revealed that smoking, age, sex, and latent infection with cytomegalovirus were the primary non-genetic factors influencing immune cell variation. Using genome-wide association studies, we identified 15 loci associated with disease-related variants in immunophenotypes. Our results also showed that innate immune cell parameters were more strongly influenced by genetic factors, while adaptive cell parameters were primarily driven by environmental exposures. This study establishes a valuable resource for generating new hypotheses in immunology and highlights the importance of innate immunity in susceptibility to common autoimmune diseases. Both environmental and genetic factors play a role in shaping human immunity, and our findings leverage data from the Milieu Intérieur Consortium to comprehensively understand the complex interplay between lifestyle, environment, and genetics on human immune function.

title: The transcriptional program, functional heterogeneity, and clinical targeting of mast cells
text: Mast cells are a distinct population of immune cells that reside in various tissues and are capable of responding rapidly to a wide range of extracellular stimuli, including antigen-IgE complexes, bacteria, viruses, cytokines, hormones, peptides, and drugs. Despite their relatively small population in tissues, mast cells play a crucial role in both health and disease, thanks to their ability to rapidly release stored and newly synthesized mediators. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of mast cell biology, including their regulation, differentiation, survival, and novel functions beyond their traditional role in IgE-mediated allergic responses and antiparasitic activities. The review also highlights recent advances in mast cell research, such as the development of new mouse models and the identification of regulatory mechanisms that control mast cell functions. Finally, the article discusses current and future therapeutic opportunities for modulating mast cell activities in inflammatory diseases.

title: LIN28B enhanced tumorigenesis in an autochthonous KRASG12V-driven lung carcinoma mouse model
text: LIN28B is an RNA-binding protein that predominantly regulates let-7 microRNAs, which play crucial roles in inflammation, wound healing, embryonic stem cells, and cancer. LIN28B expression is linked to tumor initiation, progression, resistance, and poor outcomes in various solid cancers, including lung cancer. However, the specific function of LIN28B in non-small cell lung adenocarcinomas remains unclear. To investigate this, we employed LIN28B transgenic overexpression in an autochthonous KRASG12V-driven mouse model. Our findings revealed that LIN28B overexpression significantly increased the number of CD44+/CD326+ tumor cells, upregulated VEGF-A and miR-21, and promoted tumor angiogenesis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) accompanied by enhanced AKT phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of c-MYC. Moreover, LIN28B accelerated tumor initiation and proliferation, leading to a shorter overall survival. In addition, we analyzed lung adenocarcinomas from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and found that LIN28B expression was present in 24% of KRAS-mutated cases, underscoring the relevance of our model.

title: Cost-effectiveness comparison between topical silver sulfadiazine and enclosed silver dressing for partial-thickness burn treatment.
text:
The standard treatment for partial-thickness burns typically involves topical silver products, such as silver sulfadiazine cream and enclosed dressings containing silver-impregnated foam or silver-laden sheets (Mepilex Ag; Molnlycke Health Care, Gothenburg, Sweden or Aquacel Ag; ConvaTec, Skillman, NJ). However, the current healthcare system is limited by resource constraints, with a focus on evidence-based outcomes and cost-effective treatments. To compare the cost-effectiveness of enclosed silver dressings versus silver sulfadiazine (SSD) in treating partial-thickness burns with a total body surface area (TBSA) of less than 20%, a decision analysis was conducted using an incremental cost-utility ratio.
A comprehensive literature review was conducted to identify relevant health states in partial-thickness burn patients, including successful healing, infection, and noninfected delayed healing requiring either surgical or conservative management. Probabilities of these health states were combined with Medicare CPT reimbursement codes (cost) and patient-derived utilities obtained through visual analog scale assessments during patient interviews. Expected costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were calculated using the roll-back method, resulting in an incremental cost-utility ratio of $40,167.99/QALY.
One-way sensitivity analysis of complication rates confirmed the robustness of the model, and assuming a maximum willingness to pay $50,000/QALY, the complication rate for SSD must be 22% or higher for enclosed silver dressing to be cost-effective. Two-way sensitivity analysis demonstrated the cost-effectiveness of using enclosed silver dressings at most complication rates for both treatment modalities.
In conclusion, enclosed silver dressings are a cost-effective treatment option for partial-thickness burns.

title: Randomized clinical study of Hydrofiber dressing with silver or silver sulfadiazine in the management of partial-thickness burns.
text:
In this randomized controlled study, the authors compared the use of AQUACEL Ag Hydrofiber dressings with silver (n = 42) versus silver sulfadiazine (n = 42) for the management of partial-thickness burns covering 5% to 40% of the body surface area (BSA). The study found that the AQUACEL Ag dressing protocol was associated with several advantages over silver sulfadiazine, including:
* Less pain and anxiety during dressing changes
* Less burning and stinging during wear
* Fewer dressing changes
* Less nursing time
* Fewer procedural medications

In contrast, silver sulfadiazine was associated with greater flexibility and ease of movement. Although there were no significant differences in adverse events between the two treatment groups, the AQUACEL Ag dressing protocol had lower total treatment costs (Dollars 1040 vs. Dollars 1180) and a greater rate of re-epithelialization (73.8% vs 60.0%), resulting in cost-effectiveness per burn healed of Dollars 1,409.06 for AQUACEL Ag dressing and Dollars 1,967.95 for silver sulfadiazine. Overall, the study suggests that a protocol of care using AQUACEL Ag dressings may provide clinical and economic benefits compared to silver sulfadiazine in patients with partial-thickness burns.

title: Hepatitis C virus and blood transfusion: past and present risks.
text: Since the early 1980s, the risk of transmitting hepatitis C virus (HCV) through blood and blood products has significantly decreased. Various measures have contributed to this reduction, including the use of non-remunerated donors, rigorous donor selection to prevent HIV transmission, surrogate testing in some regions, and the introduction of anti-HCV testing. As a result, ALT surrogate testing has become obsolete. Currently, the residual risk of HCV transmission due to donations during the anti-HCV window period is approximately 1 in 100,000 transfusions of cellular products, and transmission of HCV through plasma products treated with modern inactivation methods, such as solvent-detergent treatment, has not been reported. Hemovigilance programs, which are being implemented, will provide more data on the safety of blood transfusion. In the near future, the introduction of HCV nucleic acid amplification technology (NAT) as a quality control measure for plasma products or blood donor screening by minipools is anticipated in many European countries. Moreover, NAT testing of individual blood donations may become available within the next two years. The further reduction of the residual risk through NAT testing will become cost-effective in comparison with other public health measures.

title: p62/SQSTM1 by Binding to Vitamin D Receptor Inhibits Hepatic Stellate Cell Activity, Fibrosis, and Liver Cancer.
text: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) play a crucial role in liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Activation of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) in HSCs inhibits liver inflammation and fibrosis. Our findings reveal that p62/SQSTM1, a protein upregulated in liver parenchymal cells and downregulated in HCC-associated HSCs, negatively regulates HSC activation. Total body or HSC-specific ablation of p62 enhances inflammation, fibrosis, and HCC progression. p62 directly interacts with VDR and RXR, promoting their heterodimerization and critical for VDR:RXR target gene recruitment. Loss of p62 in HSCs impairs the repression of fibrosis and inflammation by VDR agonists, demonstrating that p62 is a negative regulator of liver inflammation and fibrosis through its ability to promote VDR signaling in HSCs, whose activation supports HCC.

title: Developing criteria for evaluation of geroprotectors as a key stage toward translation to the clinic
text:
In the forthcoming decades, a significant transformation in the aging population will have profound social and economic implications globally. To mitigate this trend, accelerating the development of geroprotectors, substances that slow aging, repair age-related damage, and extend healthy lifespan, or healthspan, is crucial. While over 200 geroprotectors have been identified in model organisms and some are used in human applications for specific diseases, the path to determining their impact on aging in humans remains unclear. The obstacle in translating these findings to the clinic is primarily due to the lack of a standardized framework for defining, selecting, and categorizing these substances, given the complexity of the aging process and its vast diversity in mechanisms of action. To address this challenge, there is an urgent need for a scientific consensus on the following aspects:
1. Definition of 'geroprotector': A clear and universally accepted definition of geroprotectors is essential to ensure consistency in selection and classification.
2. Selection criteria for geroprotectors: Establishing a set of criteria for selecting geroprotectors will facilitate the identification of promising candidates and streamline the translation process.
3. Comprehensive classification system: A standardized classification system will help categorize geroprotectors based on their mechanisms of action, efficacy, and safety, enabling a more efficient analysis of their potential.
4. Analytical model: Developing an analytical model will provide a framework for evaluating the effectiveness and safety of geroprotectors in a clinical setting.
In this review, we will discuss current approaches to selection and propose our own suggested selection criteria to standardize the process of identifying and evaluating geroprotectors. By establishing a scientific consensus on these aspects, we can accelerate the translation of geroprotectors from bench to bedside, ultimately leading to improved health outcomes for the aging population.

title: β-Catenin Signaling and Roles in Liver Homeostasis, Injury, and Tumorigenesis.
text: β-catenin (encoded by CTNNB1) is a key component of the cell surface cadherin protein complex, which functions as an intracellular signal transducer in the WNT signaling pathway. Alterations in β-catenin activity have been linked to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and other liver diseases. In addition to WNT, other signaling pathways can also converge on β-catenin. β-catenin interacts with transcription factors such as T-cell factor, forkhead box protein O, and hypoxia inducible factor 1α to regulate the expression of target genes. The role of β-catenin in the metabolic zonation of the adult liver will be discussed. β-catenin also regulates the expression of genes involved in glucose, nutrient, and xenobiotic metabolism, and alterations in its activity may contribute to the pathogenesis of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Activation of hepatic stellate cells, which is required for fibrosis, is another consequence of alterations in β-catenin signaling. Many hepatic tumors, including hepatocellular adenomas, hepatocellular carcinomas, and hepatoblastomas, have mutations in CTNNB1 that result in constitutive activation of β-catenin. Therefore, this molecule could be a potential therapeutic target. The contribution of alterations in β-catenin activity to liver disease will be discussed, along with its potential use in diagnosis and prognosis, as well as the development of therapeutics.

title: The global burden of dengue: an analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013.
text:
The background of dengue fever is significant, with the World Health Organization (WHO) estimating that it is the most common arbovirus infection globally. However, the actual burden of dengue is poorly quantified, and there is a need for accurate estimates to inform public health policies and interventions.
In this study, we aimed to estimate the mortality, incidence, and burden of dengue fever using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013. We used a combination of vital registration, verbal autopsy, and surveillance data to model mortality, and officially reported cases to estimate incidence. We also accounted for under-reporting of cases using expansion factor estimates.
Our findings indicate that there were an average of 9221 dengue deaths per year between 1990 and 2013, with a peak of 11 302 deaths in 2010. This translates to a total of 576 900 years of life lost to premature mortality attributable to dengue in 2013. The incidence of dengue increased greatly between 1990 and 2013, with the number of cases more than doubling every decade. We estimate that there were 58·4 million apparent cases of dengue in 2013, with 566 000 years lived with disability attributable to dengue. Considering both fatal and non-fatal outcomes, dengue was responsible for 1·14 million disability-adjusted life-years in 2013.
While our estimates are lower than some other studies have suggested, they offer further evidence that the true symptomatic incidence of dengue is likely within the commonly cited range of 50 million to 100 million cases per year. Our mortality estimates are lower than those presented elsewhere, and we suggest that these estimates should be considered in light of the totality of evidence suggesting that dengue mortality might be substantially higher.
This study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Formin-mediated actin polymerization at cell–cell junctions stabilizes E-cadherin and maintains monolayer integrity during wound repair
text: Cadherin-mediated cell-cell adhesion is crucial for maintaining the integrity of epithelial tissues in both homeostasis and during development. However, the mechanisms that regulate actin polymerization at cell-cell junctions, which is essential for E-cadherin stability, are poorly understood. To investigate this, we examined the role of formin-mediated actin polymerization at epithelial junctions. Our findings identify mDia1 and Fmnl3 as key factors that enhance actin polymerization and stabilize E-cadherin at cell-cell junctions. Fmnl3 localizes to adherens junctions downstream of Src and Cdc42, and its depletion leads to a decrease in F-actin and E-cadherin at junctions, resulting in weakened cell-cell adhesion. Interestingly, Fmnl3 expression is up-regulated and junctional localization increases during collective cell migration. Depletion of Fmnl3 or mDia1 in migrating monolayers leads to the dissociation of leader cells and impaired wound repair. In summary, our results demonstrate that formin activity at epithelial cell-cell junctions is essential for maintaining adhesion and epithelial cohesion during dynamic processes such as wound repair.

title: A mechanically active heterotypic E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion enables fibroblasts to drive cancer cell invasion
text: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) facilitate tumor invasion and metastasis by applying a physical force on cancer cells, which enables their collective invasion. We demonstrate that this force transmission is mediated by a heterophilic adhesion involving N-cadherin on the CAF membrane and E-cadherin on the cancer cell membrane. This adhesion is mechanically active, and when subjected to force, it triggers β-catenin recruitment and adhesion reinforcement through an α-catenin/vinculin interaction. Disruption of the E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion abrogates CAFs' ability to guide collective cell migration and inhibits cancer cell invasion. Additionally, N-cadherin mediates the repolarization of CAFs away from cancer cells, and this process is dependent on afadin. Heterotypic junctions between CAFs and cancer cells are observed in patient-derived material, highlighting the cooperative nature of these interactions. Our findings reveal that a mechanically active heterophilic adhesion between CAFs and cancer cells enables collaborative tumor invasion.

title: Long non-coding RNA HOTTIP promotes BCL-2 expression and induces chemoresistance in small cell lung cancer by sponging miR-216a
text: Despite progress in the treatment of small cell lung cancer (SCLC), its inherent chemoresistance and poor prognosis remain a significant challenge. To address this, we conducted a global analysis of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in SCLC, using microarray data, in vitro and in vivo assays. Our findings revealed that HOTTIP, a lncRNA frequently amplified in SCLC, was associated with SCLC cell chemosensitivity, proliferation, and poor prognosis in patients. Mechanistic investigations showed that HOTTIP functions as an oncogene in SCLC progression by binding to miR-216a and abrogating its tumor-suppressive function in this context. Additionally, HOTTIP increased the expression of anti-apoptotic factor BCL-2, another target gene of miR-216a, and together they enhanced chemoresistance of SCLC cells. Our study establishes a role for HOTTIP in SCLC progression and chemoresistance, suggesting its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for clinical management of SCLC.

title: GSDS 2.0: an upgraded gene feature visualization server
text:
Title: Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) 2.0: An Upgraded Platform for Visualizing and Analyzing Genes
Abstract:
The Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) has been widely used by over 60,000 users since its initial release in 2007. To further enhance the platform, we have now upgraded GSDS to version 2.0, which includes several new features and improvements. These updates enable biologists to investigate the structure and function of genes in an intuitive and user-friendly manner.
Introduction:
Visualizing the structure and annotated features of genes is crucial for understanding their function and evolution. The Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) has been developed to facilitate this process, providing a user-friendly platform for biologists to explore and analyze genes. In this paper, we describe the upgraded version of GSDS, which includes a newly designed interface, support for additional types of annotation features and formats, and an integrated visual editor for editing the generated figure.
Features of GSDS 2.0:

* Newly designed interface: The upgraded GSDS features a modern and intuitive interface, making it easier for users to navigate and analyze genes.
* Support for additional types of annotation features and formats: GSDS 2.0 supports a wider range of annotation features and formats, including but not limited to gene ontology, KEGG, and Pfam.
* Integrated visual editor: Users can now edit the generated figure directly within the platform, allowing for greater flexibility and control over the visualization of their data.
* User-specified phylogenetic tree: GSDS 2.0 allows users to add a user-specified phylogenetic tree to facilitate further evolutionary analysis.

Availability and Implementation:

The web server and source code of GSDS 2.0 are freely available at <http://gsds.cbi.pku.edu.cn>.


Contact Information: For any inquiries or suggestions, please contact gaog@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn or gsds@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn.


Supplementary Information: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: SLP-65 regulates immunoglobulin light chain gene recombination through the PI(3)K-PKB-Foxo pathway
text: Although the crucial role of the adaptor protein SLP-65 in pre-B cell differentiation has been established, the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. In this study, we uncover a connection between SLP-65-dependent signaling and the phosphoinositide-3-OH kinase (PI(3)K)-protein kinase B (PKB)-Foxo pathway. We demonstrate that the forkhead box transcription factor Foxo3a promotes light chain rearrangement in pre-B cells. Our findings suggest that PKB inhibits light chain recombination by phosphorylating Foxo proteins, whereas restoration of SLP-65 function counteracts PKB activation and enhances Foxo3a and Foxo1 activity in pre-B cells. These data shed light on the molecular function of SLP-65 and reveal a key role for Foxo proteins in the regulation of light chain recombination, receptor editing, and B cell selection.

title: A case-mix classification system for explaining healthcare costs using administrative data in Italy.
text:
BACKGROUND: The Italian National Health Service (NHS) provides universal coverage to all citizens, offering primary and hospital care with a copayment system for outpatient and drug services. The financing of Local Health Trusts (LHTs) is based on a capitation system adjusted only for age, gender, and area of residence. To address the complexity of healthcare costs, we employed a risk-adjustment system, specifically the Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) System, using routinely collected administrative data in the Veneto Region of North-eastern Italy.
METHODS: We conducted a regional study on all residents in the Veneto Region in 2015. The ACG system was applied to classify the population based on the following information sources: hospital discharges, emergency room visits, chronic disease registry for copayment exemptions, ambulatory visits, medications, home care database, and drug prescriptions. Simple linear regressions were employed to contrast an age-gender model with more comprehensive risk measures aimed at predicting healthcare costs.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed that a simple age-gender model could only explain 8% of the variance in total costs in 2015. Incorporating diagnosis-related variables led to a 23% increase in explained variance, while pharmacy-based variables provided an additional 17% increase. The adjusted R-squared of the comprehensive model was found to be 6 times higher than the simple age-gender model.
CONCLUSIONS: The ACG System significantly improves the prediction of healthcare costs when compared to simple age-gender adjustments. Aging alone is not the primary determinant of the increase in healthcare costs, which is better explained by the accumulation of chronic conditions and resulting multimorbidity.

title: EpCAM-regulated intramembrane proteolysis induces a cancer stem cell-like gene signature in hepatitis B virus-infected hepatocytes.
text:
Background & Aims:
Hepatocytes infected with the hepatitis B virus (HBV) exhibit loss of the chromatin modifying polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), leading to the re-expression of specific, cellular PRC2-repressed genes. Epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) is one such gene, normally expressed in hepatic progenitors but re-expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) stem cells (hCSCs). In this study, we aimed to investigate the functional significance of EpCAM re-expression in HBV-mediated hepatocarcinogenesis.
Methods:
We employed molecular approaches, including transfections, fluorescence-activated cell sorting, immunoblotting, and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), to investigate the role of EpCAM-regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP) in HBV replicating cells in vitro and in liver tumors from HBV x/c-myc mice and chronically HBV-infected patients.
Results:
EpCAM undergoes RIP in HBV replicating cells, leading to the activation of canonical Wnt signaling. Transfection of Wnt-responsive plasmids expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) identified a GFP+ population of HBV replicating cells, which exhibited cisplatin- and sorafenib-resistant growth, similar to hCSCs, and increased expression of pluripotency genes NANOG, OCT4, SOX2, and hCSC markers BAMBI, CD44, and CD133. These genes are referred to as the EpCAM RIP and Wnt-induced hCSC-like gene signature. Interestingly, this gene signature is also overexpressed in liver tumors of x/c-myc bitransgenic mice. Clinically, a group of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinomas was identified, exhibiting elevated expression of the hCSC-like gene signature and associated with reduced overall survival post-surgical resection.
Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that the hCSC-like gene signature may serve as a prognostic tool for classifying subtypes of HBV-induced HCCs. Since EpCAM RIP and Wnt signaling drive the expression of this hCSC-like signature, inhibition of these pathways may offer a potential therapeutic strategy for this subtype of HBV-associated HCCs.

title: Parathyroid Hormone Directs Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Cell Fate.
text: Intermittent PTH administration has been shown to promote bone mass and prevent fractures, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. To investigate this further, we genetically deleted the PTH/PTHrP receptor (PTH1R) in mesenchymal stem cells using Prx1Cre. Our findings revealed that the absence of PTH1R led to reduced bone formation, increased bone resorption, and an accumulation of adipose tissue in the bone marrow (BMAT). Bone marrow adipocytes were found to express classic adipogenic markers and high levels of receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (Rankl), which is involved in the regulation of bone metabolism. Interestingly, RANKL levels were elevated in both bone marrow supernatant and serum, but were undetectable in other adipose depots. We also observed that Pref1+RANKL+ marrow progenitors were twice as abundant in mutant mice compared to controls. Notably, intermittent PTH administration to control mice significantly reduced BMAT. Similar findings were observed in male osteoporotic patients. These studies suggest that marrow adipocytes play a key role in PTH's therapeutic effects by directing mesenchymal cell fate and regulating bone metabolism.

title: Metformin attenuates blood-brain barrier disruption in mice following middle cerebral artery occlusion
text:
Background:
Metformin, a widely used hypoglycemic drug, has been shown to reduce the incidence of stroke and alleviate chronic inflammation in clinical trials. However, the effect of metformin on ischemic stroke is not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the effect of metformin on ischemic stroke in mice and explored the possible underlying mechanisms.
Methods:
We conducted a study using 98 adult male CD-1 mice that underwent 90-minute transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO).
