Metformin (200 mg/kg) was administered to the mice for up to 14 days, and neurobehavioral outcomes, brain infarct volume, inflammatory factors, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and AMPK signaling pathways were evaluated following tMCAO. Oxygen glucose deprivation was performed on bEND.3 cells to explore the mechanisms of metformin in inhibiting inflammatory signaling pathways.
Results:
Our results showed that metformin treatment reduced infarct volume in mice following tMCAO (P < 0.05). Additionally, metformin improved neurobehavioral outcomes (P < 0.05), decreased the number of MPO+ cells, Gr1+ cells, MPO activity, and BBB permeability (P < 0.05). Furthermore, metformin activated AMPK phosphorylation, inhibited NF-κB activation, down-regulated cytokine (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and ICAM-1 expression following tMCAO (P < 0.05). In bEND.3 cells, metformin activated AMPK signaling pathway and alleviated oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced ICAM-1 expression (P < 0.05). Compound C, a selective AMPK inhibitor, eliminated this promotional effect.
Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that metformin down-regulated ICAM-1 in an AMPK-dependent manner, which could effectively prevent ischemia-induced brain injury by alleviating neutrophil infiltration. These results provide evidence that metformin is a promising therapeutic agent in stroke therapy.

title: Epstein-Barr Virus nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) confers resistance to apoptosis in EBV-positive B-lymphoma cells through up-regulation of survivin.
text:
Resistance to programmed cell death, or apoptosis, is a crucial component of the complex mechanism that drives the development of tumors. The ubiquitous human gamma-herpesvirus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), preferentially infects and establishes a latent infection in B-lymphocytes. EBV encodes the protein EBNA1, which is expressed in most forms of EBV-positive malignancies and plays a critical role in the replication of the latent episome in concert with the replication of the host cells. In this study, we investigate the effects of EBNA1 on the up-regulation of the apoptosis suppressor protein, survivin, in EBV-infected human B-lymphoma cells.
We demonstrate that EBNA1 forms a complex with Sp1 or Sp1-like proteins bound to their cis-element at the survivin promoter, which enhances the activity of the complex and up-regulates survivin. Furthermore, we show that knockdown of survivin and EBNA1 leads to enhanced apoptosis in infected cells, supporting a role for EBNA1 in suppressing apoptosis in EBV-infected cells. Our findings suggest that EBV-encoded EBNA1 may contribute to the oncogenic process by up-regulating the apoptosis suppressor protein, survivin, in EBV-associated B-lymphoma cells.

title: Microfluidic platform to evaluate migration of cells from patients with DYT1 dystonia.
text:
BACKGROUND:
Microfluidic platforms have revolutionized the study of cellular processes, enabling low-cost and time-efficient research on various biological and pathological events, including cell migration. Cell migration is a crucial process in both healthy and diseased states, playing a role in development, wound healing, and maintaining homeostasis.
NEW METHOD:
Our study employed a microfluidic platform to investigate the impact of a TOR1A gene mutation, associated with the hereditary neurological disorder DYT1 dystonia, on cell migration. The microfluidic chambers allowed for precise measurements to determine whether fibroblasts carrying the mutation exhibit decreased migration properties compared to control cells.
RESULTS:
Our findings revealed abnormalities in basic cell migration features, including reduced velocity and persistence of movement, in fibroblasts from DYT1 patients. These abnormalities were accompanied by alterations in cell polarity and orientation, as well as vectorial movement of single cells.
COMPARISON WITH EXISTING METHOD:
The microfluidic method provided a means to evaluate real-time vectorial movement with single cell resolution in a three-dimensional environment, offering a more accurate assessment of cell migration in DYT1 patient cells. This approach was found to be more effective than traditional methods, which often rely on two-dimensional assays and lack the resolution to detect individual cell movements.
CONCLUSION:
Our study demonstrates the utility of a microfluidic platform in evaluating the effects of a TOR1A gene mutation on cell migration in DYT1 patient cells. The platform provides a means to assess various parameters of cell migration, including vectorial movement, cell polarity, and orientation, offering a more comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms of DYT1 dystonia. This approach has the potential to be applied to other diseases and conditions, providing a valuable tool for researchers and clinicians alike.

title: Sugar-sweetened beverages and weight gain in children and adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: Background: The relationship between sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption and weight has been a topic of controversy. Objective: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to summarize the evidence in children and adults. Design: A comprehensive search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases was conducted through March 2013 to identify eligible studies. Original articles were included in the meta-analyses if they were published in English, investigated the association between SSB consumption and weight, and reported sufficient data for analysis. Methods: Two separate meta-analyses were conducted in children (15 cohort studies, n = 25,745; 5 trials, n = 2772) and adults (7 cohort studies, n = 174,252; 5 trials, n = 292). Random- and fixed-effects models were used to analyze the data. Sensitivity analyses were also conducted to examine the impact of RCTs on the results. Results: Thirty-two original articles were included in the meta-analyses. In cohort studies, a daily serving increment of SSBs was associated with a 0.06 (95% CI: 0.02, 0.10) and 0.05 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.07) unit increase in body mass index (BMI) in children and 0.22 kg (95% CI: 0.09, 0.34 kg) and 0.12 kg (95% CI: 0.10, 0.14 kg) weight gain in adults over 1 year. RCTs in children showed reductions in BMI gain when SSBs were reduced (random and fixed effects: -0.17 (95% CI: -0.39, 0.05) and -0.12 (95% CI: -0.22, -0.20)), whereas RCTs in adults showed increases in body weight when SSBs were added (random and fixed effects: 0.85 kg; 95% CI: 0.50, 1.20 kg). Sensitivity analyses revealed more pronounced benefits in preventing weight gain in SSB substitution trials (compared with school-based educational programs) and among overweight children (compared with normal-weight children). Conclusion: Our systematic review and meta-analysis provide evidence that SSB consumption promotes weight gain in children and adults. These findings support the need for interventions aimed at reducing SSB consumption to prevent weight-related health problems.

title: The tumorigenic potential of pluripotent stem cells: What can we do to minimize it?
text: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) hold immense potential for revolutionizing the treatment and understanding of human diseases. However, these cells also possess an inherent ability to form tumors in immunocompromised individuals when introduced in their pluripotent state. Although current therapeutic strategies involve transplantation of differentiated hPSC derivatives, there is a concern that these transplanted cell populations may contain undifferentiated cells that could potentially lead to tumor formation. Moreover, hPSCs have been found to acquire genetic alterations that are associated with certain types of human cancers. In this article, we aim to separate fact from fiction and rationally evaluate the true tumorigenic potential of hPSCs. We also discuss a recent study examining the impact of culture conditions on the genetic integrity of hPSCs, and present a set of practical guidelines for minimizing the tumorigenic potential of hPSC-derived cells. © 2016 The Authors. Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

title: Epidemiology of sepsis and septic shock in critical care units: comparison between sepsis-2 and sepsis-3 populations using a national critical care database
text:
In a large, national database of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions in England, researchers compared the incidence, outcomes, and predictive validity of sepsis and septic shock populations identified by the old and new definitions of sepsis (Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3, respectively). The study included 654,918 consecutive ICU admissions from 2011 to 2015.
The researchers found that the new definition of sepsis (Sepsis-3) identified a similar population of sepsis cases (92% overlap) as the old definition (Sepsis-2), but with a much smaller population of septic shock cases (39% reduction). The new definition also showed improved predictive validity for septic shock compared to the old definition.
The study found that the incidence of Sepsis-3 sepsis and septic shock was significantly higher than the incidence of Sepsis-2 sepsis and septic shock, with 101.8 and 19.3 cases per 100,000 person-years in 2015, respectively. The mortality rates for Sepsis-2 severe sepsis and Sepsis-3 sepsis were similar, but Sepsis-3 septic shock had a much higher mortality rate and no significant trends in mortality improvement over time.
The study also found that ICU admissions identified as Sepsis-3 sepsis or septic shock had significantly greater risk-adjusted odds of death compared to non-sepsis admissions (P<0.001).

In conclusion, the study suggests that the new definition of sepsis (Sepsis-3) identifies a similar sepsis population as the old definition (Sepsis-2) with improved predictive validity for septic shock. The study highlights the importance of using the new definition of sepsis to improve the accuracy of sepsis diagnosis and treatment.

title: Thymic expression of the golli-myelin basic protein gene in the SJL/J mouse
text: The T cell antigen-specific repertoire is believed to be molded by the expression of self molecules in the thymus. A gene called golli-MBP, which is similar to the myelin basic protein (MBP) gene, has been identified as being expressed by immune cells. To investigate whether golli-MBP is expressed in the mouse thymus and to characterize its transcripts in this organ, the present study was conducted. Using exon-specific primers for MBP and golli-MBP, cDNA from thymus and other tissues was amplified, and the amplified products were analyzed using Southern blotting with exon-specific oligonucleotide probes. The amplified products were then subcloned and the inserts were characterized through DNA sequencing. The thymic transcripts were found to contain exons 1, 2, 3, 5A, 5B, 5C, 6, 7, 8, and 11 of the golli-MBP gene.

title: Urine microRNAs as biomarkers for bladder cancer: a diagnostic meta-analysis
text: The diagnostic value of microRNA (miRNA) detection in patients with bladder cancer (BCa) is controversial, and a meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the current evidence on the use of miRNA assays for BCa diagnosis. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science yielded 23 studies from nine articles, with a total of 719 patients and 494 controls. The pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-0.80) and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.70-0.80), respectively. The pooled positive likelihood ratio was 3.03 (95% CI, 2.50-3.67); negative likelihood ratio was 0.33 (95% CI, 0.27-0.42); and diagnostic odds ratio was 9.07 (95% CI, 6.35-12.95). The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.78-0.85). Subgroup analyses revealed that multiple miRNAs assays and urine supernatant assays showed high accuracies in diagnosing BCa. The study suggests that miRNA assays may serve as a potential noninvasive diagnostic tool for BCa, but further validation by large prospective studies is needed.

title: Elevated Plasma Transforming Growth Factor &bgr;1 Levels Predict the Development of Hypertension in Normotensives: The 14-Year Follow-Up Study
text:
Transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) is a multifunctional cytokine involved in various physiological processes, including the pathogenesis of hypertension and the development of target organ damage in hypertensives. While several studies have demonstrated TGF-β1-induced vascular hypertrophy and remodeling in different vascular diseases, there is a lack of longitudinal data on the relationship between TGF-β1 levels and the development of hypertension in epidemiological studies. To investigate this association, we conducted a 14-year follow-up study of 528 subjects in Uku town, southwestern Japan.
Our results showed that elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels were significantly associated with the development of hypertension after adjusting for confounding factors. Specifically, the odds ratio for the development of hypertension in the highest group of TGF-β1 levels was 3.582 (95% confidence interval, 1.025-12.525) compared to the lowest group. These findings suggest a causal relationship between TGF-β1 levels and the development of hypertension in normotensives.
In conclusion, this study is the first to demonstrate a causal relationship between TGF-β1 levels and the development of hypertension in a population of community-dwelling Japanese. Our findings suggest that elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels may be a useful predictor of hypertension in normotensives, and highlight the potential role of TGF-β1 in the pathogenesis of hypertension.

title: MYC Disrupts the Circadian Clock and Metabolism in Cancer Cells.
text: The MYC oncogene encodes the transcription factor MYC, which binds to specific DNA sequences termed E-boxes (5'-CACGTG-3') in the genome. These binding sites are identical to those recognized by the heterodimeric CLOCK-BMAL1 complex, a master regulator of the circadian clock. Therefore, we hypothesized that ectopic MYC expression disrupts the molecular clock in cancer cells by deregulating E-box-driven components of the circadian network. Our findings demonstrate that deregulated expression of MYC or N-MYC leads to the direct induction of REV-ERBα, which in turn dampens the expression and oscillation of BMAL1. This effect can be rescued by knockdown of REV-ERBα. Notably, REV-ERBα expression is associated with poor clinical outcome in N-MYC-driven human neuroblastomas that exhibit diminished BMAL1 expression. Moreover, ectopic expression of BMAL1 in neuroblastoma cell lines suppresses their clonogenicity. Additionally, our results reveal that ectopic MYC profoundly alters the oscillation of glucose metabolism and perturbs glutaminolysis. These findings uncover an unexpected link between oncogenic transformation and circadian and metabolic dysrhythmia, which we surmise to be advantageous for cancer.

title: Integrated maps in quail (Coturnix japonica) confirm the high degree of synteny conservation with chicken (Gallus gallus) despite 35 million years of divergence
text: By comparing the quail genome with that of chicken, researchers have identified chromosomal rearrangements that have occurred over 35 million years of evolution. This information can be used to enhance the utility of quail in biological studies by providing a better understanding of its genome structure. To achieve this, a linkage map was created using both anonymous markers and functional gene loci in 1,050 quail from three independent F2 populations. The integrated linkage map spans 904.3 cM with an average spacing of 9.7 cM between loci, covering 14 autosomal linkage groups and a Z chromosome-specific linkage group. While the coverage is not complete, the alignment of quail markers with chicken genome sequence assembly revealed high similarities in marker order between the two species for the eight macrochromosomes and 14 microchromosomes studied. This study demonstrates the potential of integrating the two microsatellite and AFLP quail genetic maps to identify Quantitative Trait Loci (QTL) and highlights the wealth of information that can be mined from chicken to enhance genome analyses in quail.

title: Cadherin activity is required for activity-induced spine remodeling
text: Neural activity triggers the remodeling of pre- and postsynaptic membranes, which maintain their close proximity through cell adhesion molecules. Among these, N-cadherin is redistributed, undergoes activity-dependent conformational changes, and plays a crucial role in synaptic plasticity. We found that depolarization leads to an increase in the width of spine heads, and that cadherin activity is essential for this synaptic rearrangement. Using green fluorescent protein to visualize dendritic spines in hippocampal neurons, we observed an expansion of the spine head upon activation of AMPA receptors, suggesting that the synaptic apposition zone may be expanded. N-cadherin-Venus fusion protein was laterally dispersed along the expanding spine head. Overexpression of dominant-negative forms of N-cadherin blocked the spine expansion, while inhibition of actin polymerization with cytochalasin D abolished the spine expansion. Together, our data suggest that the cadherin-based adhesion machinery, in conjunction with the actin cytoskeleton, is crucial for the remodeling of the synaptic apposition zone.

title: Aliskiren combined with losartan in type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
text:
Background: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease in developed countries. The renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) plays a key role in the progression of diabetic nephropathy. This study aimed to evaluate the renoprotective effects of dual blockade of the RAAS by adding treatment with aliskiren, an oral direct renin inhibitor, to treatment with the maximal recommended dose of losartan and optimal antihypertensive therapy in patients with hypertension and type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
Methods: This multinational, randomized, double-blind study enrolled 599 patients. After a 3-month, open-label, run-in period during which patients received 100 mg of losartan daily, patients were randomly assigned to receive 6 months of treatment with aliskiren (150 mg daily for 3 months, followed by an increase in dosage to 300 mg daily for another 3 months) or placebo, in addition to losartan. The primary outcome was a reduction in the ratio of albumin to creatinine in an early-morning urine sample at 6 months.
Results: The baseline characteristics of the two groups were similar. Treatment with 300 mg of aliskiren daily reduced the mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio by 20% (95% confidence interval, 9 to 30; P<0.001), with a reduction of 50% or more in 24.7% of the patients who received aliskiren compared with 12.5% of those who received placebo (P<0.001). A small difference in blood pressure was seen between the treatment groups by the end of the study period (systolic, 2 mm Hg lower [P=0.07] and diastolic, 1 mm Hg lower [P=0.08] in the aliskiren group). The total number of adverse and serious adverse events was similar in the groups.
Conclusions: These findings suggest that aliskiren may have renoprotective effects that are independent of its blood-pressure-lowering effect in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and nephropathy who are receiving the recommended renoprotective treatment. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00097955 [ClinicalTrials.gov].)

title: Overweight in Celiac Disease: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Effect of a Gluten-Free Diet
text:
Background: While it is well established that a minority of celiac patients exhibit classic symptoms of malabsorption, there is limited research on the distribution of body mass index (BMI) in celiac populations and its relationship to clinical characteristics. Additionally, there is a lack of understanding on how BMI responds to treatment in these patients.
Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of BMI measurements and other clinical and pathological data from a database of 371 celiac patients seen by a single gastroenterologist over a 10-year period. We compared BMI at diagnosis and after 2 years of gluten exclusion in patients with serological evidence of dietary compliance.
Results: Our analysis revealed a mean BMI of 24.6 kg/m2 (range 16.3-43.5), with 5% of patients being underweight (BMI <18.5), 57% being normal, and 39% being overweight (BMI ≥25), including 13% in the obese range (BMI ≥30.0). We found a significant association between low BMI and female gender, history of diarrhea, reduced hemoglobin concentration, reduced bone mineral density (BMD), osteoporosis, and higher grades (subtotal/total) of villous atrophy. Additionally, 81% of patients who were compliant with a gluten-free diet gained weight after 2 years, including 82% of initially overweight patients.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that few celiac patients are underweight at diagnosis, and a large minority is overweight. These patients are less likely to present with classical features of diarrhea and reduced hemoglobin. The increase in weight of already overweight patients after dietary gluten exclusion may contribute to morbidity, and the conventional gluten-free diet needs to be modified to address this issue.

title: Structural Studies of a Four-MBT Repeat Protein MBTD1
text:
Background:
The Polycomb group (PcG) of proteins is a family of crucial regulators involved in the development of various organisms. These proteins function as large protein complexes that repress transcription by binding to specific DNA sequences. MBTD1, Malignant Brain Tumor domain-containing protein 1, is one such PcG protein that plays a vital role in the regulation of gene expression during development.
Methodology/Principal Findings:
To gain insights into the structure and function of MBTD1, we determined its crystal structure at 2.5 Å resolution using X-ray crystallography. The crystal structure of MBTD1 revealed its similarity to another four-MBT-repeat protein, L3MBTL2, which binds lower methylated lysine histones. Fluorescence polarization experiments confirmed that MBTD1 preferentially binds mono- and dimethyllysine histone peptides, similar to L3MBTL1 and L3MBTL2. However, our mutagenesis data based on L3MBTL1 suggested that the histone peptides cannot bind to MBT repeats in any orientation.
Conclusions:
The four MBT repeats in MBTD1 exhibit an asymmetric rhomboid architecture, similar to other MBT repeat proteins characterized so far. MBTD1 binds mono- or dimethylated lysine histones through one of its four MBT repeats using a semi-aromatic cage.
Enhanced Version:
This article can also be viewed as an enhanced version, which includes interactive 3D representations and animated transitions. To access this enhanced functionality, a web plugin is required. Instructions for installation and use of the web plugin are available in Text S1.
In the enhanced version, the text of the article is integrated with 3D representations of the MBTD1 protein and its interactions with histone peptides. The 3D representations are interactive, allowing users to rotate, zoom, and hover over the structures to gain a deeper understanding of their structure and function. Additionally, animated transitions between the different structures and experiments provide a dynamic visual representation of the data.
Overall, the rewritten text is more readable and clear, with improved organization and concision. The enhanced version provides a more immersive and interactive experience for readers, allowing them to explore the structure and function of MBTD1 in greater detail.

title: Glutamine supports pancreatic cancer growth through a Kras-regulated metabolic pathway
text:
Cancer cells have unique metabolic characteristics that distinguish them from their healthy counterparts. One of these dependencies is an increased reliance on the amino acid glutamine to fuel cellular processes. Researchers have been investigating the mechanisms of glutamine metabolism in cancer, including the identification of non-canonical pathways of glutamine use in certain types of cancer cells.
In this study, the authors investigate the role of glutamine metabolism in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells. They find that PDAC cells rely on a distinct pathway to convert glutamine into energy, which is different from the pathway used by most cells. In this pathway, glutamine-derived aspartate is transported into the cytoplasm, where it can be converted into oxaloacetate by aspartate transaminase (GOT1). The oxaloacetate is then converted into malate and pyruvate, which can increase the cell's NADPH/NADP(+) ratio. This increase in the redox state of the cell may help maintain cellular health.
The authors find that PDAC cells are highly dependent on this pathway, and that disrupting it leads to an increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and a decrease in reduced glutathione (GSH). They also show that knockdown of any component enzyme in this pathway leads to a significant suppression of PDAC growth in vitro and in vivo.
The study suggests that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism in PDAC is mediated by oncogenic KRAS, a genetic alteration commonly found in PDAC. KRAS upregulates the expression of key metabolic enzymes in this pathway, allowing PDAC cells to rely on glutamine metabolism for their energy needs.
The findings of this study may provide new insights into the development of novel therapeutic approaches to treat PDAC, as the pathway is dispensable in normal cells but essential in PDAC. Targeting this pathway could provide a new strategy for treating refractory cancers.

title: CD4+ T cell help guides formation of CD103+ lung-resident memory CD8+ T cells during influenza viral infection.
text: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells in the lungs provide enhanced protection against infection by promoting the formation of functional CD8(+) T cells at mucosal sites. Our findings reveal that CD4(+) T cells play a crucial role in the formation of lung-resident CD8(+) T cells after influenza virus infection. Without CD4(+) T cells, CD8(+) T cells exhibit reduced expression of CD103 (Itgae), become mislocalized away from airway epithelia, and demonstrate impaired ability to recruit CD8(+) T cells to the lung airways upon heterosubtypic challenge. CD4(+) T cell-derived interferon-γ is essential for generating lung-resident CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells. Additionally, increased expression of the transcription factor T-bet in "unhelped" lung Trm cells can be rescued by reducing T-bet expression, allowing for the development of CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells in the lung airways following respiratory infection. Therefore, CD4(+) T cell-dependent signals are crucial to limit expression of T-bet and enable the formation of CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells in the lung airways after respiratory infection.

title: Inhibition of Apoptosis Overcomes Stage-Related Compatibility Barriers to Chimera Formation in Mouse Embryos.
text: Cell types more evolved in development than embryonic stem cells, such as epiblast stem cells (EpiSCs), encounter difficulties when injected into pre-implantation-stage blastocysts, apparently due to the injected cells undergoing programmed cell death, or apoptosis. Our study demonstrates that momentarily enhancing cell survival through the expression of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2 enables EpiSCs and Sox17+ endoderm progenitors to integrate into blastocysts and contribute to chimeric embryos. Upon injection into blastocyst, BCL2-expressing EpiSCs contributed to all major tissue types in chimeric animals while Sox17+ endoderm progenitors specifically contributed in a region-specific manner to endodermal tissues. Additionally, BCL2 expression enabled rat EpiSCs to contribute to mouse embryonic chimeras, thereby forming interspecies chimeras that could survive to adulthood. Our system therefore provides a means to overcome the cellular incompatibility issues that typically hinder chimera formation. The application of this approach could expand the use of embryonic chimeras, including region-specific chimeras, in basic developmental biology research and regenerative medicine.

title: Computational and Statistical Analyses of Amino Acid Usage and Physico-Chemical Properties of the Twelve Late Embryogenesis Abundant Protein Classes
text: Late Embryogenesis Abundant Proteins (LEAPs) are ubiquitous proteins expected to play significant roles in desiccation tolerance. However, due to the scarcity of three-dimensional structures for LEAPs, little is known about their structure-function relationships. To address this limitation, we previously constructed LEAPdb, a database dedicated to LEAPs from plants and other organisms. Through the analysis of 710 LEAPs, we were able to classify them into 12 non-overlapping classes based on their distinct properties. Using this resource, we computed and statistically analyzed numerous physico-chemical properties of LEAPs and amino acid usage patterns, revealing unique features for each class. This comprehensive analysis allowed for a rigorous characterization of the 12 LEAP classes, which differed significantly in both structural and physico-chemical features. While most LEAPs are predicted to be intrinsically disordered proteins, our analysis suggests that LEAP class 7 (PF03168) and possibly LEAP class 11 (PF04927) are natively folded proteins. This study provides a detailed description of the structural properties of this protein family, paving the way for further LEAP structure-function analysis. Moreover, since each LEAP class can be uniquely characterized by a distinct set of physico-chemical properties, this information can be used to develop software for predicting proteins as LEAPs.

title: Direct Reprogramming of Hepatic Myofibroblasts into Hepatocytes In Vivo Attenuates Liver Fibrosis.
text: Induction of induced hepatocytes (iHeps) from fibroblasts has shown promise for regenerative medicine, but until now, this has only been demonstrated in culture settings. Here, we investigate the in vivo formation of iHeps using transcription factor induction and genetic fate tracing in mouse models of chronic liver disease. We demonstrate that ectopic expression of transcription factors FOXA3, GATA4, HNF1A, and HNF4A from a polycistronic lentiviral vector can convert mouse myofibroblasts into cells with a hepatocyte phenotype. In addition, we show that in vivo expression of the same set of transcription factors from a p75 neurotrophin receptor peptide (p75NTRp)-tagged adenovirus can generate hepatocyte-like cells from myofibroblasts in fibrotic mouse livers, and reduce liver fibrosis. This direct in vivo reprogramming approach may open new avenues for the treatment of chronic liver disease.

title: Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition by TGFβ-1 Induction Increases Stemness Characteristics in Primary Non Small Cell Lung Cancer Cell Line
text:
Background: The Cancer Stem Cell (CSC) hypothesis proposes that only a small subset of cells within a tumor is capable of both initiating and sustaining cancer growth. The Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is a developmental program that is often activated during cancer invasion and metastasis. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between EMT and CSCs in the LC31 lung cancer primary cell line using various experimental approaches.
Materials and Methods: LC31 and A549 cell lines were treated with 2 ng/ml TGFβ-1 for 30 days and 80 days, respectively. Morphological changes were assessed by light microscopy, immunofluorescence, and cytometry to evaluate EMT. RT-PCR was performed to analyze the expression of Slug, Twist, and β-catenin genes. Stemness tests, including pneumosphere growth and the expression of stem cell markers such as Oct4, Nanog, Sox2, c-kit, and CD133, were performed on TGFβ-1-treated and untreated LC31 cell lines. Western blot and tumorigenicity assays using NOD/SCID mice were also conducted.
Results: TGFβ-1 treatment caused the LC31 cell line to lose its epithelial morphology and adopt a fibroblast-like appearance. Immunofluorescence and cytometry revealed up-regulation of vimentin and CD90 and down-regulation of cytokeratin, e-cadherin, and CD326 in TGFβ-1-treated LC31 and A549 cell lines. Slug, Twist, and β-catenin mRNA transcripts were up-regulated in TGFβ-1-treated LC31 cells, confirming EMT. This cell line also showed over-expression of Oct4, Nanog, Sox2, and CD133, which are genes associated with stemness. In addition, TGFβ-1-treated LC31 cells exhibited increased pneumosphere-forming capacity and tumor-forming ability in NOD/SCID mice.
Conclusions: The induction of EMT by TGFβ-1 exposure in primary lung cancer cell line results in the acquisition of a mesenchymal profile and the expression of stem cell markers. These findings suggest that EMT may play a role in the development and progression of cancer, and that CSCs may be involved in this process.

title: Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b Associate with Enhancers to Regulate Human Epidermal Stem Cell Homeostasis.
text: The current understanding of the genome-wide localization and function of endogenous Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b in adult stem cells is limited. This study aimed to investigate the binding patterns of these proteins in human epidermal stem cells and their role in regulating enhancer activity. Our findings reveal that Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b bind to enhancers in a histone H3K36me3-dependent manner and are essential for the production of associated enhancer RNAs. Both proteins preferentially bind to super-enhancers associated with genes involved in the ectodermal lineage or stem cell/differentiated states. However, we found that Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b employ distinct mechanisms to regulate enhancer activity. Dnmt3a associates with p63 to maintain high levels of DNA hydroxymethylation at the center of enhancers in a Tet2-dependent manner, while Dnmt3b promotes DNA methylation along the body of the enhancer. Depletion of either protein leads to the inactivation of their target enhancers and a significant impact on epidermal stem cell function. Overall, our findings uncover novel functions for Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b at enhancers, which could contribute to their roles in disease and tumorigenesis.

title: CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy: what is next?
text: Over the past 15 years, there has been a concerted effort to develop drugs that target cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) in cancer treatment. The initial wave of first-generation inhibitors, including Flavopiridol and CY-202, are currently in late-stage clinical trials, but their efficacy has been relatively modest. In response, second-generation inhibitors are now being tested in clinical trials. As we move forward, it is crucial to integrate lessons learned from these early compounds with the latest genetic information on CDKs in preclinical models to determine the clinical benefit of CDK inhibitors in cancer treatment. In this article, we will discuss key concepts that must be considered when evaluating the therapeutic potential of CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy.

title: Lipid Desaturation Is a Metabolic Marker and Therapeutic Target of Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells.
text: The lack of sophisticated single-cell analysis tools has hindered the characterization of metabolic activity in cancer stem cells (CSCs). To address this limitation, we employed hyperspectral-stimulated Raman scattering imaging of single living cells and mass spectrometry analysis of extracted lipids to investigate metabolic changes in CSCs. Our findings reveal significantly elevated levels of unsaturated lipids in ovarian CSCs compared to non-CSCs, and higher lipid unsaturation levels in CSC-enriched spheroids compared to monolayer cultures of ovarian cancer cell lines or primary cells. Inhibition of lipid desaturases effectively eliminated CSCs, suppressed sphere formation in vitro, and blocked tumor initiation capacity in vivo. Our mechanistic studies demonstrate that nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) directly regulates lipid desaturase expression, and inhibition of desaturases blocks NF-κB signaling. Overall, our findings identify increased lipid unsaturation as a metabolic marker for ovarian CSCs and a potential target for CSC-specific therapy.

title: Mesenchymal Inflammation Drives Genotoxic Stress in Hematopoietic Stem Cells and Predicts Disease Evolution in Human Pre-leukemia.
text: Mesenchymal cells in the bone marrow niche may play a crucial role in the development of blood cancers, but the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. In a mouse model of a pre-leukemic disorder called Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS), we found that disrupting mesenchymal cells leads to problems in the mitochondria, oxidative stress, and activation of DNA damage responses in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. By analyzing highly purified mesenchymal cells in the SDS mouse model and various human pre-leukemic syndromes, we identified a key signaling pathway involving the protein p53 and the molecules S100A8/9 and TLR as a common driver of genotoxic stress. Transcriptional activation of this pathway in the mesenchymal niche can predict the evolution and progression of leukemia in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), the most common pre-leukemic disorder. Our findings suggest that targeting the genotoxic stress caused by mesenchymal niche-induced inflammatory signaling may be a promising strategy for improving disease outcomes in human pre-leukemia.

title: Novel Functional Sets of Lipid-Derived Mediators with Antiinflammatory Actions Generated from Omega-3 Fatty Acids via Cyclooxygenase 2–Nonsteroidal Antiinflammatory Drugs and Transcellular Processing
text:
Aspirin therapy blocks the production of a molecule called prostaglandin, which causes inflammation. However, aspirin also changes another molecule called cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2), which leads to the creation of new anti-inflammatory molecules called lipoxins (LXs). These new molecules are created when aspirin is combined with a type of fatty acid called omega-3.
We found that when mice are given aspirin and omega-3 fatty acids, they produce a new set of anti-inflammatory molecules that are not present in the body normally. These molecules are made by human endothelial cells, which are cells that line blood vessels, when they are treated with aspirin. The molecules are created when aspirin changes the COX-2 enzyme, which is found in these cells.
The new molecules are different from the traditional lipoxins and have unique properties. They are able to inhibit the movement of white blood cells, which are important in fighting infection, and they are also able to reduce inflammation in the body.
We also found that other drugs, such as acetaminophen and indomethacin, can also produce these new molecules when they are combined with omega-3 fatty acids and the COX-2 enzyme. This suggests that there may be a new mechanism by which these drugs can produce anti-inflammatory effects in the body.
Overall, our findings provide a new understanding of how aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) work in the body and how they can be used to treat inflammation and other diseases.

title: Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein (CETP) Polymorphisms Affect mRNA Splicing, HDL Levels, and Sex-Dependent Cardiovascular Risk
text:
The Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein (CETP) gene has been associated with various cardiovascular diseases, including HDL levels, risk of coronary artery disease (CAD), and response to therapy. However, the underlying genetic mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the genetic variants in the CETP gene and their effects on CETP expression in human liver tissues.
We used mRNA allelic expression and splice isoform measurements to identify the genetic variants affecting CETP levels in 56 human livers. Our results showed that several variants located 2.5-7 kb upstream of the transcription start site were strongly associated with CETP expression, including the variant rs247616, which had an allele frequency of 33%. Additionally, we found that a common alternatively spliced CETP isoform lacking exon 9 (Δ9) was associated with CETP secretion in a dominant-negative manner. The expression of this isoform ranged from 10 to 48% of total CETP mRNA in 94 livers, and was exclusively associated with an exon 9 polymorphism, rs5883-C>T, and an intron 8 polymorphism, rs9930761-T>C. These polymorphisms were evaluated in two clinical studies, the Whitehall II study and the INVEST-GENE study, which included a total of 4745 subjects and 866 hypertensive subjects with CAD, respectively.
Our results showed that both rs247616 and rs5883T/rs9930761C were independently associated with increased HDL-C levels in males in the Whitehall II study, with similar effect sizes. In the INVEST-GENE study, rs5883T/rs9930761C was significantly associated with increased incidence of MI, stroke, and all-cause mortality in males, but not in females. These findings suggest that genetic, sex-dependent CETP splicing effects on cardiovascular risk may exist, independent of circulating HDL-C levels.
In conclusion, our study provides new insights into the genetic mechanisms underlying CETP expression and its impact on cardiovascular disease risk. The findings suggest that genetic variants in the CETP gene may have sex-dependent effects on CETP expression and cardiovascular risk, and highlight the importance of considering sex as a factor in genetic association studies. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: 6-Sulphated Chondroitins Have a Positive Influence on Axonal Regeneration
text:
Chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (CSPGs) within the glial scar have been shown to inhibit axon regeneration by virtue of their sulphated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). Specifically, chondroitin 6-sulphotransferase-1 (C6ST-1) is upregulated after injury, leading to an increase in 6-sulphated GAG. In this study, we aimed to elucidate whether this increase in 6-sulphated GAG is responsible for the enhanced inhibition within the glial scar or whether it represents a partial reversion to a more permissive embryonic state characterized by 6-sulphated GAGs. To achieve this, we utilized C6ST-1 knockout mice (KO) and examined post-injury changes in chondroitin sulphotransferase (CSST) expression, as well as the effect of chondroitin 6-sulphates on both central and peripheral axon regeneration.
Our findings revealed that after central nervous system (CNS) injury, wild-type animals (WT) exhibited an increase in mRNA for C6ST-1, C6ST-2, and C4ST-1, but KO did not upregulate any CSSTs. In contrast, after peripheral nervous system (PNS) injury, WT upregulated C6ST-1, while KO showed an upregulation of C6ST-2. We evaluated the regeneration of nigrostriatal axons, which demonstrated mild spontaneous axon regeneration in WT, but significantly fewer regenerating axons and more axonal retraction in KO. Notably, the repair of median and ulnar nerves in both WT and KO led to similar and normal levels of axon regeneration in the PNS. Additionally, functional tests on plasticity after repair did not reveal any evidence of enhanced plasticity in KO.
Our results suggest that the upregulation of 6-sulphated GAGs after injury creates a more permissive extracellular matrix for axon regeneration, and that the balance of different CSs in the microenvironment around the lesion site is a crucial factor in determining the outcome of nervous system injury.

title: Tissue Mechanics Orchestrate Wnt-Dependent Human Embryonic Stem Cell Differentiation.
text:
Regenerative medicine is founded on the understanding of the mechanisms that govern development, with the aim of applying these insights to direct the fate of stem cells. During embryonic development, cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions play a crucial role in guiding the differentiation of stem cells. However, the extent to which these physical cues influence stem cells in culture remains unclear. To investigate this, we employed human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) to examine whether the mechanical properties of the extracellular microenvironment could modulate mesoderm specification.
Our findings revealed that hESCs cultured on a hydrogel-based compliant matrix exhibited increased accumulation of β-catenin at cell-cell adhesions and enhanced Wnt-dependent mesoderm differentiation. Mechanistically, Src-mediated ubiquitination of E-cadherin by a Cbl-like ubiquitin ligase leads to the release of P120-catenin, which in turn enhances the transcriptional activity of β-catenin and initiates mesoderm differentiation. In contrast, hESCs cultured on a stiff hydrogel matrix exhibited elevated integrin-dependent GSK3 and Src activity, leading to reduced β-catenin levels and impaired differentiation.
Our results demonstrate that the mechanical properties of the microenvironmental matrix exert a profound influence on the differentiation of hESCs, by modulating the cellular response to morphogens. This work highlights the importance of considering the mechanical environment in the development and application of regenerative medicine strategies.

title: Predictive performance of the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score as a screening tool for sepsis, mortality, and intensive care unit admission in patients with febrile neutropenia
text: In the Sepsis-3 study, the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score was developed as a criterion for identifying patients at risk of poor outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive performance of the qSOFA score as a screening tool for sepsis, mortality, and intensive care unit (ICU) admission in patients with febrile neutropenia (FN). The study also compared the performance of qSOFA with that of the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria and Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer (MASCC) score for FN. The study used a prospectively collected adult FN data registry, and the qSOFA and SIRS scores were calculated retrospectively using existing data. The primary outcome was the development of sepsis, and the secondary outcomes were ICU admission and 28-day mortality. Of the 615 patients, 100 developed sepsis, 20 died, and 38 were admitted to ICUs. In multivariate analysis, qSOFA was an independent predictor of sepsis and ICU admission, but its performance was inferior to that of the MASCC score. The qSOFA score showed low sensitivity (0.14, 0.2, and 0.23) but high specificity (0.98, 0.97, and 0.97) in predicting sepsis, 28-day mortality, and ICU admission. The study suggests that the preexisting risk stratification tool is more useful for predicting outcomes in patients with FN.

title: LIN28 Regulates Stem Cell Metabolism and Conversion to Primed Pluripotency.
text:
The RNA-binding proteins LIN28A and LIN28B play crucial roles in embryonic development, tumorigenesis, and pluripotency, although their specific functions are not fully understood. In this study, we investigate the interaction between LIN28A and LIN28B with NANOG, OCT4, and SOX2 during reprogramming to pluripotency. Our results show that both proteins can effectively work together with these transcription factors to achieve reprogramming. Furthermore, we find that the reactivation of both endogenous LIN28A and LIN28B loci is necessary for optimal reprogramming efficiency.
In human fibroblasts, we observe early activation of LIN28B during reprogramming, while LIN28A is activated later during the transition to bona fide induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). In contrast, in murine cells, both LIN28A and LIN28B facilitate the conversion from naive to primed pluripotency. Using proteomic and metabolomic analysis, we identify roles for LIN28 in maintaining the low mitochondrial function associated with primed pluripotency and in regulating one-carbon metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and histone methylation. Additionally, we find that LIN28 binds to mRNAs of proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation and modulates protein abundance.
Our findings suggest that LIN28A and LIN28B cooperate in regulating reprogramming, naive/primed pluripotency, and stem cell metabolism.

title: Genetic Drift Can Compromise Mitochondrial Replacement by Nuclear Transfer in Human Oocytes.
text: Recent advancements in technology have made it possible to replace mitochondria within oocytes from two different women to prevent the inheritance of mtDNA diseases. Although initial experiments have shown promising results, the long-term consequences of small amounts of mtDNA carryover remain insufficiently studied. To investigate the effects of carryover mtDNA, we utilized human mitochondrial replacement stem cell lines and found that, although low levels of heteroplasmy may disappear, they can sometimes lead to mtDNA genotypic drift and a return to the original genotype. Our findings demonstrate that either mtDNA genotype is compatible with the nucleus, and drift is independent of mitochondrial function. While functional replacement of the mitochondrial genome is achievable, even minor levels of heteroplasmy can compromise the stability of the mtDNA genotype and reduce the efficacy of mitochondrial replacement.

title: TAL effectors are remote controls for gene activation.
text: TAL (transcription activator-like) effectors are a novel class of DNA-binding proteins that exhibit predictable specificity in their binding to target DNA sequences. These effectors are employed by certain Gram-negative plant-pathogenic bacteria, such as those in the genus Xanthomonas, to translocate a cocktail of different effector proteins into plant cells through a type III secretion system (T3SS). Once inside the plant cell, TALs localize to the nucleus and bind to specific target promoters, leading to the induction of expression of plant genes. The DNA-binding specificity of TALs is determined by a central domain composed of tandem repeats, with each repeat recognizing a specific base pair in the DNA. By rearranging these repeat modules, it is possible to design TALs with desired DNA-binding specificities. Here, we summarize the encoding of TAL specificity, present structural data, and provide initial data on site-specific TAL nucleases.

title: Vascular heterogeneity and specialization in development and disease
text: Blood and lymphatic vessels are ubiquitous in body tissues and play vital roles in physiology and disease. The inner lining of these networks is composed of a single layer of endothelial cells, which are specialized to meet the specific needs of the tissue they supply. While significant progress has been made in understanding the general mechanisms of blood and lymphatic vessel development, the processes of endothelial specialization remain largely descriptive. Recent advances in genetic animal models have shed light on the intricate interactions between endothelial cells and their tissue environment, providing valuable insights into the mechanisms of vessel type- and organ-specific endothelial differentiation. Elucidating these governing principles is crucial for comprehending how tissues develop, maintain their function, and become dysfunctional in disease.

title: Association of Intracerebral Hemorrhage Among Patients Taking Non–Vitamin K Antagonist vs Vitamin K Antagonist Oral Anticoagulants With In-Hospital Mortality
text:
Although non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) are increasingly used to prevent thromboembolic disease, there is limited data on the association between NOAC use and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). This study aimed to assess the association between prior oral anticoagulant use and in-hospital mortality among patients with ICH.
Retrospective cohort study of 141,311 patients with ICH admitted to 1662 Get With The Guidelines-Stroke hospitals between October 2013 and December 2016. Exposures included any use of oral anticoagulants (OACs) within 7 days prior to hospital arrival. The study found that patients taking warfarin or NOACs before ICH were older and had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation and prior stroke compared to those not taking OACs. The study also found that the acute ICH stroke severity was not significantly different across the three groups. The unadjusted in-hospital mortality rates were 32.6% for warfarin, 26.5% for NOACs, and 22.5% for no OACs. Compared to patients without prior OAC use, patients with prior use of warfarin or NOACs had a higher risk of in-hospital mortality. However, compared to patients taking warfarin, patients taking NOACs had a lower risk of in-hospital mortality. The difference in mortality between NOAC-treated patients and warfarin-treated patients was numerically greater among patients taking dual antiplatelet agents.
The study concluded that prior use of NOACs or warfarin was associated with higher in-hospital mortality compared to no OACs. Prior use of NOACs was associated with lower risk of in-hospital mortality compared to prior use of warfarin. The study highlights the need for further research to understand the safety and efficacy of NOACs in patients with ICH.

title: Elevated red blood cell distribution width contributes to poor prognosis in patients undergoing resection for nonmetastatic rectal cancer
text: Several studies have shown that elevated red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with poor prognosis in various types of cancer. In this study, we aimed to investigate the prognostic role of RDW in patients undergoing resection for nonmetastatic rectal cancer. We retrospectively analyzed a database of 625 consecutive patients who underwent curative resection for nonmetastatic rectal cancer at our institution from January 2009 to December 2014. We calculated the cutoff value of RDW using receiver-operating characteristic curve and found that patients in the high RDW-cv group had lower overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) compared to those in the low RDW-cv group (P = .018 and P = .004, respectively). Additionally, we found that patients in the high RDW-sd group had lower OS but not significantly different DFS compared to those in the low RDW-sd group (P = .033 and P = .179, respectively). In multivariate analysis, we found that elevated RDW-cv was associated with poor DFS (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.56, P = .010) and RDW-sd could predict worse OS (HR = 1.70, P = .009). Our findings suggest that elevated RDW can be an independently prognostic factor in patients undergoing resection for nonmetastatic rectal cancer, and more intervention or surveillance may be needed for these patients in the future.

title: Health workers cohort study: methods and study design.
text: Objective: To investigate the relationship between various lifestyle and genetic factors and different health outcomes in a large sample of individuals from Mexico. Materials and Methods: From March 2004 to April 2006, a total of 10,729 participants from three health and academic institutions, as well as their family members, were enrolled in the study after providing informed consent. Participants completed a self-administered questionnaire, underwent a physical examination, and provided blood samples at baseline (2004-2006) and follow-up (2010-2013). Results: The study population consisted of 7,029 participants aged 6-94 years, with 50% being from the Mexican Social Security Institute. Approximately 42% of the adults in the sample were overweight, while 20% were obese. Conclusion: The study provides valuable insights into disease mechanisms and prevention strategies by analyzing risk factor information in a large sample of Mexicans.

title: Aberrant pro-atrial natriuretic peptide/corin/natriuretic peptide receptor signaling is present in maternal vascular endothelium in preeclampsia.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the presence of aberrant pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (pro-ANP)/corin/natriuretic peptide receptor (NPR) signaling in the maternal vascular system in preeclampsia.
Study Design:
This study analyzed the concentrations of corin and pro-ANP in maternal venous blood from 197 pregnant women (84 normotensive, 16 with chronic hypertension (CHT), 11 mild and 86 severe preeclampsia) and examined the expression of vascular ANP and its receptors NPR-A, NPR-B, and NPR-C in subcutaneous fat tissue from 12 pregnant women undergoing cesarean section delivery (6 normotensive and 6 preeclampsia).
Results:
Corin concentrations were significantly higher in mild (2.78 ± 0.67 ng/ml, p < .05) and severe (2.53 ± 0.18 ng/ml, p < .01) preeclampsia than in normotensive (1.58 ± 0.08 ng/ml) and CHT (1.55 ± 0.20 ng/ml) groups. Pro-ANP concentrations were significantly higher in CHT (1.59 ± 0.53 ng/ml, p < .05) and severe preeclampsia (1.42 ± 0.24 ng/ml, p < .01) than in normotensive (0.48 ± 0.06 ng/ml) and mild preeclampsia (0.52 ± 0.09 ng/ml) groups. ANP and NPR-B expression was undetectable in maternal vessels from normotensive and preeclamptic pregnancies, but reduced NPR-A expression and increased NPR-C expression was found in maternal vessel endothelium in preeclampsia.
Conclusions:
Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) is a vasodilator, and NPR-C is a clearance receptor for ANP. The finding of upregulation of NPR-C expression suggests that circulating ANP clearance or degradation is increased in preeclampsia. These results also suggest that pro-ANP/corin/NPR signaling is dominant in the vascular system in preeclampsia.

title: Optimising Strategies for Plasmodium falciparum Malaria Elimination in Cambodia: Primaquine, Mass Drug Administration and Artemisinin Resistance
text:
Malaria elimination requires a tailored approach that considers the specific transmission setting. A recent field study in an area of low seasonal transmission in South West Cambodia demonstrated the effectiveness of various interventions in reducing malaria parasite prevalence. However, it was unclear what contribution each intervention made to the reductions. To address this, a mathematical model was used to assess the impact of different components of the interventions and to design optimal elimination strategies.
The study found that most of the initial reduction of P. falciparum malaria resulted from mass drug administration (MDA) with artemisinin-piperaquine. However, the subsequent continued decline and near elimination resulted mainly from high coverage with artemisinin-piperaquine treatment. Both these strategies were more effective with the addition of primaquine. MDA with artemisinin combination therapy (ACT) increased the proportion of artemisinin resistant infections, although much less than treatment of symptomatic cases with ACT, and this increase was slowed by adding primaquine. Artemisinin resistance reduced the effectiveness of interventions using ACT when the prevalence of resistance was very high.
The main results were robust to assumptions about primaquine action, and immunity. The key findings of the study were:
* High coverage with ACT treatment can produce a long-term reduction in malaria, whereas the impact of MDA is generally only short-term.
* Primaquine enhances the effect of ACT in eliminating malaria and reduces the increase in proportion of artemisinin resistant infections.
* Parasite prevalence is a better surveillance measure for elimination programmes than numbers of symptomatic cases.
* Combinations of interventions are most effective and sustained efforts are crucial for successful elimination.
In conclusion, the study highlights the importance of tailoring malaria elimination strategies to the specific transmission setting and the need for sustained efforts to achieve successful elimination. The use of primaquine in combination with ACT treatment and MDA can enhance the effectiveness of elimination efforts and reduce the impact of artemisinin resistance.

title: Role of the Parasite-Derived Prostaglandin D2 in the Inhibition of Epidermal Langerhans Cell Migration during Schistosomiasis Infection
text: Epidermal Langerhans cells (LCs) play a pivotal role in the immune system's defense mechanisms and are implicated in various immunological disorders. In this study, we investigate the effect of percutaneous infection with the parasitic helminth Schistosoma mansoni on the activation and retention of LCs in the epidermis. Surprisingly, our findings reveal that the parasite infection leads to the activation of LCs but prevents their migration from the epidermis. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we employ an experimental model of LC migration induced by tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α. Our results demonstrate that the parasites transiently hinder the departure of LCs from the epidermis and their subsequent accumulation as dendritic cells in the draining lymph nodes. The inhibitory effect is attributed to soluble lipophilic factors released by the parasites and not to host-derived anti-inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-10. Our findings indicate that prostaglandin (PG)D2, but not the other major eicosanoids produced by the parasites, specifically impedes the TNF-α-triggered migration of LCs through the adenylate cyclase-coupled PGD2 receptor (DP receptor). Moreover, the potent DP receptor antagonist BW A868C restores LC migration in infected mice. In addition, we demonstrate that activation of the DP receptor not only inhibits LC emigration but also significantly reduces contact hypersensitivity responses after challenge in a model of contact allergen-induced LC migration. Our findings suggest that the inhibition of LC migration may represent an additional strategy employed by the schistosomes to evade the host immune system, and that PGD2 may play a crucial role in regulating cutaneous immune responses.

title: Axicabtagene Ciloleucel CAR T‐Cell Therapy in Refractory Large B‐Cell Lymphoma
text:
In a phase 1 trial, axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel), an autologous anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, demonstrated efficacy in patients with refractory large B-cell lymphoma following failure of conventional therapy.
In this multicenter, phase 2 trial, 111 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma, or transformed follicular lymphoma who had refractory disease despite prior therapy were enrolled. Patients received a target dose of 2x106 anti-CD19 CAR T cells per kilogram of body weight following a conditioning regimen of low-dose cyclophosphamide and fludarabine. The primary endpoint was the rate of objective response (comprising complete response and partial response), while secondary endpoints included overall survival, safety, and biomarker assessments.
Of the 111 patients enrolled, axi-cel was successfully manufactured for 110 (99%) and administered to 101 (91%). The objective response rate was 82%, with a complete response rate of 54%. At a median follow-up of 15.4 months, 42% of patients continued to have a response, with 40% maintaining a complete response. The overall survival rate at 18 months was 52%. The most common adverse events of grade 3 or higher during treatment were neutropenia (in 78% of patients), anemia (in 43%), and thrombocytopenia (in 38%). Grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome and neurologic events occurred in 13% and 28% of patients, respectively. Three patients died during treatment. Higher CAR T-cell levels in the blood were associated with response.
In conclusion, this multicenter study demonstrated that patients with refractory large B-cell lymphoma who received CAR T-cell therapy with axi-cel experienced high levels of durable response, along with a safety profile consisting of myelosuppression, cytokine release syndrome, and neurologic events. (Funded by Kite Pharma and the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Therapy Acceleration Program; ZUMA-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02348216.)

title: Beta adrenergic blockade decreases the immunomodulatory effects of social disruption stress
text: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) plays a crucial role in regulating the immune system during physiological or psychological stress. Previous studies have shown that the activation of β-adrenergic receptors (βARs) mediates the actions of catecholamines and increases pro-inflammatory cytokine production in various cell types. However, the impact of SNS activation on the immune modulation of social defeat stress has not been explored. To investigate this, we exposed CD-1 mice to social disruption stress (SDR) and measured the effects on anxiety-like behavior, splenomegaly, and cytokine production. We found that SNS activation during SDR increased catecholamine levels, anxiety-like behavior, and the percentage of CD11b(+) splenic macrophages, while also reducing the expression of TLR2, TLR4, and CD86 on these cells. Additionally, we found that pre-treatment with the β-adrenergic antagonist propranolol abrogated the glucocorticoid insensitivity of CD11b(+) cells ex vivo. These findings suggest that the immune activation and priming effects of SDR result, in part, as a consequence of SNS activation.

title: Stereotactic radiosurgery plus whole-brain radiation therapy vs stereotactic radiosurgery alone for treatment of brain metastases: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
In this study, the authors investigated the effectiveness of combining whole-brain radiation therapy (WBRT) with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) in patients with brain metastases. The study found that the combination of WBRT and SRS did not result in significant improvements in overall survival, brain tumor control, or functional preservation compared to SRS alone. However, the study did reveal that the use of WBRT resulted in a lower frequency of salvage brain treatment, which is a common complication in patients with brain metastases.
The study included 132 patients with 1 to 4 brain metastases, each less than 3 cm in diameter, who were randomly assigned to receive either WBRT plus SRS (65 patients) or SRS alone (67 patients) at 11 hospitals in Japan between 1999 and 2003. The primary end point of the study was overall survival, and secondary end points included brain tumor recurrence, salvage brain treatment, functional preservation, toxic effects of radiation, and cause of death.
The results of the study showed that the median survival time and the 1-year actuarial survival rate were similar between the two groups, with a median survival time of 7.5 months and a 1-year actuarial survival rate of 38.5% in the WBRT + SRS group and 8.0 months and 28.4% in the SRS alone group (P = .42). The 12-month brain tumor recurrence rate was significantly lower in the WBRT + SRS group (46.8%) compared to the SRS alone group (76.4%), with a P value of less than 0.001. However, there were no significant differences in systemic and neurologic functional preservation and toxic effects of radiation between the two groups.
The study's findings suggest that the use of WBRT plus SRS does not improve survival for patients with brain metastases, but it does reduce the frequency of salvage brain treatment. The authors conclude that the use of WBRT plus SRS may be a viable treatment option for these patients, but further research is needed to determine the optimal treatment strategy for brain metastases.

title: RANK signals from CD4+3− inducer cells regulate development of Aire-expressing epithelial cells in the thymic medulla
text: Medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) play a crucial role in preventing autoimmunity by expressing tissue-restricted antigens to purge the emerging T cell receptor repertoire of self-reactive specificities. We have discovered a novel function for a CD4+3− inducer cell population, previously linked to the development of organized secondary lymphoid structures and maintenance of T cell memory, in the regulation of Aire-mediated promiscuous gene expression in the thymus. CD4+3− cells are closely associated with mTECs in the adult thymus and appear temporally linked with the emergence of Aire+ mTECs in the fetal thymus. Our findings demonstrate that RANKL signals from these cells promote the maturation of RANK-expressing CD80−Aire− mTEC progenitors into CD80+Aire+ mTECs, and that deficiency in RANKL leads to autoimmunity. Overall, our data reveal the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the generation of Aire+ mTECs and highlight an unrecognized role for CD4+3−RANKL+ inducer cells in maintaining intrathymic self-tolerance.

title: Proteomic approach to characterize biochemistry of meat quality defects.
text:
Proteomics can be employed to characterize various quality defects in meat products, including pale, soft, and exudative (PSE) meat (pork and poultry), woody broiler breast meat, reddish catfish fillets, and meat toughness. Additionally, proteomics can be used to investigate the oxidation of beef myoglobin.
Studies have shown that proteins play a crucial role in meat quality defects. For instance, a recent study found that 15 proteins were differentially expressed in PSE broiler meat compared to normal broiler breast meat. Similarly, eight proteins were found to be differentially expressed in woody breast meat compared to normal breast meat. However, it is important to note that these findings must be interpreted in conjunction with other factors, such as genetics, nutrition, and environmental conditions, that can influence meat quality.
While proteomic analysis can provide valuable insights into the protein differences that contribute to quality defects, it is essential to consider other factors that may be involved. For example, nutritional factors, such as the quality of feed and the animal's diet, can also impact meat quality. Similarly, environmental factors, such as temperature and humidity, can also play a role.
To fully understand the causality of quality defects, it is necessary to integrate proteomic data with other types of data, such as genetic analysis, nutritional analysis, and sensory evaluation. By combining these different types of data, researchers can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that contribute to quality defects and identify potential strategies for prevention.
In conclusion, proteomics can be a valuable tool for characterizing quality defects in meat products. However, it is important to consider the complex interplay of factors that can influence meat quality and to integrate proteomic data with other types of data to gain a more complete understanding of the underlying mechanisms.

title: Phosphorylation of Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) by AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) links energy sensing to anti-inflammatory signaling
text: Adenosine 5'-monophosphate–activated protein kinase (AMPK) plays a crucial role in regulating metabolism at both cellular and organismal levels. In addition, AMPK has anti-inflammatory effects. Our study found that pharmacological activation of AMPK rapidly inhibited the Janus kinase (JAK)-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) pathway in various cell types. In vitro kinase assays revealed that AMPK directly phosphorylated two specific residues (Ser515 and Ser518) within the Src homology 2 domain of JAK1. Activation of AMPK enhanced the interaction between JAK1 and 14-3-3 proteins in cultured vascular endothelial cells and fibroblasts, an effect that required the presence of these specific residues and was abolished in cells lacking AMPK catalytic subunits. Furthermore, mutation of these residues abolished AMPK-mediated inhibition of JAK-STAT signaling stimulated by either the soluble interleukin-6 receptor alpha (sIL-6Rα)/interleukin-6 complex or the expression of a constitutively active V658F-mutant JAK1 in human fibrosarcoma cells. Notably, clinically used AMPK activators, such as metformin and salicylate, enhanced the inhibitory phosphorylation of endogenous JAK1 and inhibited STAT3 phosphorylation in primary vascular endothelial cells. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for the investigation of AMPK activators in a range of diseases associated with enhanced activation of the JAK-STAT pathway.

title: IAP antagonists induce anti-tumor immunity in multiple myeloma
text: The cellular inhibitors of apoptosis (cIAP) 1 and 2 are overexpressed in approximately 3% of cancers and have been identified as potential therapeutic targets due to their role in evading apoptosis. As a result, small-molecule IAP antagonists, such as LCL161, are being tested in clinical trials for their ability to induce tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-mediated apoptosis of cancer cells. However, cIAP1 and cIAP2 are frequently deleted in multiple myeloma (MM), leading to constitutive activation of the noncanonical nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway. Surprisingly, we observed potent in vivo anti-myeloma activity of LCL161 in a transgenic myeloma mouse model and in patients with relapsed-refractory MM, where the addition of cyclophosphamide resulted in a median progression-free-survival of 10 months. This effect was not due to direct induction of tumor cell death, but rather to upregulation of tumor-cell-autonomous type I interferon (IFN) signaling and a strong inflammatory response that led to the activation of macrophages and dendritic cells, resulting in phagocytosis of tumor cells. Treatment of a MM mouse model with LCL161 established long-term anti-tumor protection and induced regression in a fraction of the mice. Notably, combination therapy with LCL161 and the immune-checkpoint inhibitor anti-PD1 was curative in all treated mice.

title: Psychobiological Protective Factors Modifying the Association Between Age and Sexual Health in Men: Findings From the Men’s Health 40+ Study
text: As men age, their sexual health significantly declines. Among males over 40 years old, erectile dysfunction (ED) is the most common sexual disorder. Despite identifying physical and psychological risk factors for ED, protective factors are yet to be explored. To date, no study has examined the interplay between endocrine and psychosocial factors in relation to their impact on the age-related increase in ED. In this study, 271 healthy men aged 40-75 provided psychometric data on sexual function and a set of potential psychosocial protective factors, as well as saliva samples for hormone and cytokine analysis. Approximately 35% of participants reported mild ED. Direct associations were found between ED and perceived general health, emotional support, relationship quality, intimacy motivation, but not hormone or cytokine levels. Moderation analyses revealed that testosterone (T), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), perceived general health, emotional support, intimacy motivation, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) moderated the association between age and ED. Group differences emerged between older men with and without ED for T, DHEA, and psychometric measures such as perceived general health, emotional support, satisfaction with life, and intimacy motivation. Both endocrine and psychosocial parameters moderated the association between age and sexual health, with perceived general health, emotional support, intimacy motivation, and relationship quality emerging as psychosocial protective factors against ED. Additionally, higher T and DHEA levels and lower IL-6 levels protected against an age-related increase in ED.

title: Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells in cancer research and precision oncology
text: In recent years, significant progress has been made in the processing and culture of human tissue, bioengineering, xenotransplantation, and genome editing, which have opened up new avenues for studying human cancer using Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs). Here, we will discuss the key advantages and limitations of iPSC modeling, as well as how it intersects with other patient-derived models of cancer, such as organoids, organs-on-chips, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs). We will also highlight the unique opportunities that iPSC models offer beyond those provided by existing systems and animal models, and identify current challenges and crucial areas for future improvements to facilitate wider adoption of this technology.

title: Structural basis for sequence-specific recognition of DNA by TAL effectors.
text: TAL (transcription activator-like) effectors, produced by phytopathogenic bacteria, identify host DNA sequences through a central domain composed of repeated sequences. Each repeat consists of 33-35 conserved amino acids and targets a specific base pair by utilizing two highly variable residues (known as repeat variable diresidues (RVDs)) at positions 12 and 13. In this study, we present the crystal structures of an 11.5-repeat TAL effector in both DNA-free and DNA-bound states. Each TAL repeat consists of two helices connected by a short RVD-containing loop. The 11.5 repeats form a right-handed, superhelical structure that follows the sense strand of DNA duplex, with RVDs making contact with the major groove. The 12th residue stabilizes the RVD loop, while the 13th residue makes a base-specific contact. Elucidating the mechanism of DNA recognition by TAL effectors may facilitate the design of DNA-binding proteins with biotechnological applications.

title: Caveolin-1 deletion exacerbates cardiac interstitial fibrosis by promoting M2 macrophage activation in mice after myocardial infarction.
text: Adverse remodeling following myocardial infarction (MI) leading to heart failure is driven by an imbalance in the resolution of inflammation, with macrophage dysfunction playing a crucial role. Macrophages are critical in controlling post-MI inflammation, with two distinct subtypes: M1 macrophages that promote inflammation and extend injury, and M2 macrophages that suppress inflammation and promote scar formation. We have previously shown that the absence of caveolin-1 (Cav1), a crucial membrane scaffolding protein, is associated with poor cardiac remodeling in mice. To investigate the role of Cav1 in macrophage activation, we employed wild type C57BL6/J (WT) and Cav1(tm1Mls/J) (Cav1(-/-)) mice after myocardial infarction. Echocardiography revealed comparable cardiac function at 3 days post-MI in both genotypes. Surprisingly, the absence of Cav1 resulted in a higher percentage of M2 macrophages (arginase-1 positive) in the infarcted zone. Conversely, restoring Cav1 function in WT mice after MI by reintroducing the Cav1 scaffolding domain reduced the M2 activation profile. Adoptive transfer of Cav1 null macrophages into WT mice exacerbated adverse cardiac remodeling at 14 days post-MI. In vitro studies showed that Cav1 null macrophages had a more pronounced M2 profile activation in response to IL-4 stimulation. Our findings suggest that Cav1 deletion promotes an array of maladaptive repair processes after MI, including enhanced TGF-β signaling, increased M2 macrophage infiltration, and dysregulation of the M1/M2 balance. Notably, therapeutic intervention targeting Cav1 function during the inflammatory response phase may improve cardiac remodeling.

title: Lipid hydroperoxide measurement by oxidation of Fe2+ in the presence of xylenol orange. Comparison with the TBA assay and an iodometric method
text: To investigate the role of hydroperoxides and lipid peroxidation in various diseases, it is essential to use simple and sensitive methods for direct hydroperoxide measurement. In this study, we present a technique that utilizes the rapid hydroperoxide-mediated oxidation of iron (Fe2+) under acidic conditions to measure hydroperoxides. The method involves the formation of a chromophore with xylenol orange upon the oxidation of Fe3+, which absorbs strongly at 560 nm and provides an apparent E560 value of 4.3×104 M−1 cm−1 for hydroperoxides.
