We validated the assay in a study of liposomal lipid peroxidation and found that it provided results comparable to those obtained using an iodometric method or by measuring conjugated dienes. In contrast, the assay that uses thiobarbituric acid underestimates lipid peroxidation and does not measure hydroperoxides directly.

title: Roles of exosomes in cardioprotection.
text: Exosomes, which originate from endosomal cells, have recently been recognized as crucial mediators of intercellular communication. All major cardiac cell types, including cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts, release exosomes that modulate cellular functions. Of particular interest is the fact that exosomes released from human cardiac progenitor cells (CPCs) have been shown to be cardioprotective and improve cardiac function after myocardial infarction to a degree comparable to that of their parent cells. These exosomes are enriched in cardioprotective microRNAs, such as miR-146a-3p. Additionally, circulating exosomes have been found to mediate remote ischaemic preconditioning. Furthermore, they are currently being investigated as diagnostic markers. The discovery that cell-derived extracellular signaling organelles can transmit the paracrine effects of stem cells suggests that cell-free strategies may one day replace cell transplantation. This review focuses on the emerging roles of exosomes in cardiovascular physiology, with a particular emphasis on the cardioprotective activities of CPC-derived exosomes.

title: The rate of change in declining steroid hormones: a new parameter of healthy aging in men?
text:
Research on healthy aging in men has recently shifted towards examining age-related hormonal changes, with a particular focus on testosterone (T) decline. However, other sex steroids, such as dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), estradiol (E2), and progesterone (P), have been largely overlooked. Despite this, an integrated hormone parameter reflecting aging processes in men has yet to be identified.
To address this gap, we recruited 271 healthy men between the ages of 40 and 75 and collected both psychometric data and saliva samples for hormone analysis. Our findings revealed negative associations between age and the four sex steroids (T, DHEA, E2, and P). We then used principal component analysis (PCA) to identify a principal component that unified the variance of these hormones. Subsequent PCA revealed a principal component of declining steroid hormones (DSH), which was significantly associated with age.
We also found that psychosocial factors such as depression, chronic stress, and perceived general health moderated the association between age and DSH. In conclusion, our results provide further evidence that sex steroids decline in aging men and that DSH and its rate of change can be used as biomarkers for healthy aging in men. Additionally, the negative association of age and DSH is moderated by psychosocial factors.

title: Development of a novel helper-dependent adenovirus-Epstein-Barr virus hybrid system for the stable transformation of mammalian cells.
text: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) episomes are maintained stably in permissive proliferating cell lines due to the EBV nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA-1) protein's ability to mediate replication and segregation. Previous studies have demonstrated the capacity of EBV episomes to confer long-term transgene expression and correct genetic defects in deficient cells. To achieve quantitative delivery of EBV episomes in vitro and in vivo, we developed a binary helper-dependent adenovirus (HDA)-EBV hybrid system. This system consists of one HDA vector for the expression of Cre recombinase and a second HDA vector containing all the sequences for the EBV episome flanked by loxP sites. Upon coinfection of cells, Cre expressed from the first vector recombines the loxP sites on the second vector, resulting in circular EBV episomes that express a transgene and contain the EBV-derived family of repeats, an EBNA-1 expression cassette, and 19 kb of human DNA that functions as a replication origin in mammalian cells. This HDA-EBV hybrid system transformed 40% of cultured cells, and transgene expression in proliferating cells was observed for over 20 weeks under conditions that selected for the expression of the transgene. In the absence of selection, EBV episomes were lost at a rate of 8 to 10% per cell division. Successful delivery of EBV episomes in vivo was demonstrated in the liver of transgenic mice expressing Cre from the albumin promoter. This novel gene transfer system has the potential to confer long-term episomal transgene expression without insertional mutagenesis and with reduced vector-related toxicity.

title: Spliceosome assembly pathways for different types of alternative splicing converge during commitment to splice site pairing in the A complex.
text: Differential splice site pairing is a mechanism that generates multiple mRNA isoforms by establishing alternative splicing patterns. This process is carried out by the spliceosome, an intricate complex of five core snRNPs that undergo sequential structural rearrangements to activate splice site pairing. To investigate the timing of splice site pairing, we conducted kinetic trap experiments using pre-mRNAs that exhibit alternative 5' splice site selection or alternative exon inclusion. Our findings reveal that splice site pairing commitment occurs in the A complex, a stage characterized by the ATP-dependent association of the U2 snRNP with the branch point. Interestingly, the timing of splice site pairing is independent of the intron or exon recognition modes of splice site recognition. Using ATPgammaS, we demonstrated that ATP hydrolysis is essential for splice site pairing, independent of U2 snRNP binding to the pre-mRNA. These results identify the A complex as the spliceosomal assembly step dedicated to splice site pairing and suggest that ATP hydrolysis stabilizes splice sites in a specific splicing pattern after U2 snRNP association with the branch point.

title: Transcripts of the MHM region on the chicken Z chromosome accumulate as non-coding RNA in the nucleus of female cells adjacent to the DMRT1 locus
text: The male hypermethylated (MHM) region, located near the middle of the short arm of the Z chromosome in chickens, consists of approximately 210 tandem repeats of a BamHI 2.2-kb sequence unit. The cytosines of the CpG dinucleotides in this region are highly methylated in male chickens, but much less methylated in female chickens, after fertilization around the 1-day embryonic stage. The MHM region is transcribed only in females, from a specific strand, into a heterogeneous, high molecular-mass, non-coding RNA that accumulates near the DMRT1 locus in the nucleus. The transcriptional silencing of the MHM region in males is likely due to CpG methylation, as treatment with 5-azacytidine can lead to hypomethylation and active transcription of this region in male embryonic fibroblasts. In ZZW triploid chickens, the MHM regions are hypomethylated and transcribed on both Z chromosomes, while in ZZZ triploid chickens, they are hypermethylated and transcriptionally inactive on all three Z chromosomes, suggesting a possible role of the W chromosome in regulating the state of the MHM region.

title: Macropinocytosis of protein is an amino acid supply route in Ras-transformed cells
text: Macropinocytosis is a highly conserved endocytic process by which cells internalize extracellular fluid and its contents into large, heterogeneous vesicles called macropinosomes. Oncogenic Ras proteins have been shown to stimulate macropinocytosis, but the functional contribution of this uptake mechanism to the transformed phenotype remains unclear. Our study reveals that Ras-transformed cells use macropinocytosis to transport extracellular protein into the cell, which undergoes proteolytic degradation and releases amino acids, including glutamine, that can enter central carbon metabolism. As a result, the dependence of Ras-transformed cells on free extracellular glutamine for growth can be suppressed by macropinocytic uptake of protein. Consistent with macropinocytosis playing a critical role in nutrient uptake in tumors, pharmacological inhibition of this process compromises the growth of Ras-transformed pancreatic tumor xenografts. These findings identify macropinocytosis as a mechanism by which cancer cells support their unique metabolic needs and suggest the potential for exploiting this process in the development of anticancer therapies.

title: Linking Splicing to Pol II Transcription Stabilizes Pre-mRNAs and Influences Splicing Patterns
text:
RNA processing occurs close to the site of transcription, suggesting a regulatory relationship between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing. Using an in vitro transcription/splicing assay, we demonstrate that the association of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription and pre-mRNA splicing is essential for efficient gene expression. Pol II-synthesized RNAs containing functional splice sites are protected from nuclear degradation, likely due to the high local concentration of splicing machinery, which ensures their association over interactions with nucleases. Additionally, transcription influences alternative splicing of newly synthesized pre-mRNAs, a process that is RNA Pol II-specific. We propose that the connection between transcription by Pol II and pre-mRNA splicing guarantees an extended half-life and proper processing of nascent pre-mRNAs.
Some minor changes I made include:
* Changing "RNA processing is carried out" to "RNA processing occurs close to the site of transcription" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "suggesting a regulatory link between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing" to "suggesting a regulatory relationship between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "Using an in vitro transcription/splicing assay, we demonstrate that an association of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription and pre-mRNA splicing is required for efficient gene expression" to "Using an in vitro transcription/splicing assay, we demonstrate that the association of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription and pre-mRNA splicing is essential for efficient gene expression" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "Pol II-synthesized RNAs containing functional splice sites are protected from nuclear degradation, presumably because the local concentration of the splicing machinery is sufficiently high to ensure its association over interactions with nucleases" to "Pol II-synthesized RNAs containing functional splice sites are protected from nuclear degradation, likely due to the high local concentration of splicing machinery, which ensures their association over interactions with nucleases" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "Furthermore, the process of transcription influences alternative splicing of newly synthesized pre-mRNAs" to "Additionally, transcription influences alternative splicing of newly synthesized pre-mRNAs" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "Because other RNA polymerases do not provide similar protection from nucleases, and their RNA products display altered splicing patterns" to "Other RNA polymerases do not provide similar protection from nucleases, and their RNA products display altered splicing patterns" to make the sentence more concise and clear.
* Changing "We propose that the connection between transcription by Pol II and pre-mRNA splicing guarantees an extended half-life and proper processing of nascent pre-mRNAs" to "We propose that the connection between transcription by Pol II and pre-mRNA splicing guarantees an extended half-life and proper processing of nascent pre-mRNAs" to make the sentence more concise and clear.

title: The emerging role of skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodelling in obesity and exercise.
text:
New research suggests that remodeling of the extracellular matrix in skeletal muscle may play a key role in the development of obesity and metabolic dysfunction. Exercise training has been shown to improve muscle function in obesity, and recent studies suggest that this may be mediated by regulatory effects on the muscle extracellular matrix. This review examines the available literature on skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodeling during obesity and the effects of exercise training.
A non-systematic literature review of 37 studies from humans and animals published between 1970 and 2015 on PubMed found that obesity is associated with increased gene and protein expression of various types of collagen, growth factors, and enzymatic regulators in skeletal muscle. However, only two studies investigated the effects of exercise on skeletal muscle extracellular matrix during obesity, and both suggested that exercise has a regulatory effect on the muscle extracellular matrix.
The effects of exercise on muscle extracellular matrix remodeling seem to be influenced by the duration and type of exercise training, with variable effects from a single session compared to longer durations of exercise. Further research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms behind skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodeling during obesity and the effects of exercise training.
In summary, this review highlights the potential of skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodeling as a new feature associated with obesity and metabolic dysfunction, and suggests that exercise training may play a regulatory role in this process. Further research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms involved and to determine the optimal exercise program for improving muscle function in obesity.

title: Effect of specific exercise strategy on need for surgery in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome: randomised controlled study
text:
Objective: To compare the effectiveness of a specific exercise strategy targeting the rotator cuff and scapula stabilizers with unspecific exercises in improving shoulder function and reducing pain in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome, thereby reducing the need for arthroscopic subacromial decompression.
Design: Randomized, participant and single assessor blinded, controlled study.
Setting: Department of orthopaedics in a Swedish university hospital.
Participants: 102 patients with long-standing (>6 months) persistent subacromial impingement syndrome who had failed earlier conservative treatment, recruited through orthopaedic specialists.
Interventions: The specific exercise strategy consisted of strengthening eccentric exercises for the rotator cuff and concentric/eccentric exercises for the scapula stabilizers in combination with manual mobilization. The control exercise program consisted of unspecific movement exercises for the neck and shoulder. Patients in both groups received five to six individual guided treatment sessions over 12 weeks. In between these supervised sessions, the participants performed home exercises once or twice a day for 12 weeks.
Main Outcome Measures: The primary outcome was the Constant-Murley shoulder assessment score evaluating shoulder function and pain. Secondary outcomes were patients' global impression of change due to treatment and decision regarding surgery.
Results: Most (97%, 95% CI 93-99%) of participants completed the 12-week study. There was a significantly greater improvement in the Constant-Murley score in the specific exercise group compared to the control exercise group (24 points, 95% CI 19-28.0 vs 9 points, 5-13; mean difference between groups: 15 points, 8.5-20.6). Significantly more patients in the specific exercise group reported successful outcome (defined as large improvement or recovered) in the patients' global assessment of change due to treatment: 69% (35/51) vs 24% (11/46); odds ratio 7.6, 3.1-18.9; P<0.001. A significantly lower proportion of patients in the specific exercise group subsequently chose to undergo surgery: 20% (10/51) vs 63% (29/46); odds ratio 7.7, 3.1-19.4; P<0.001.
Conclusion: A specific exercise strategy focusing on strengthening eccentric exercises for the rotator cuff and concentric/eccentric exercises for the scapula stabilizers is effective in reducing pain and improving shoulder function in patients with persistent subacromial impingement syndrome. By extension, this exercise strategy reduces the need for arthroscopic subacromial decompression within the 3-month timeframe used in the study.
Trial Registration: Clinical Trials NCT01037673.

title: Nucleotide sequence of an avian sarcoma virus oncogene (src) and proposed amino acid sequence for gene product
text: The gene (src) of avian sarcoma virus (ASV) and adjacent regions of the viral genome have been isolated through molecular cloning of viral DNA. The nucleotide sequence encompasses the full src gene and a portion of the gene env that encodes gp37, one of two glycoproteins found in the viral envelope. Src encodes a single, hydrophobic protein with structural features consistent with previous descriptions of the gene product (pp60src). It appears that a single viral protein is responsible for both initiating and maintaining neoplastic transformation by ASV. Unlike other viral oncogenes and their encoded proteins, src and its product do not exhibit any obvious structural similarities. Src is flanked by a repeated nucleotide sequence that may facilitate frequent deletion of the gene from the viral genome.

title: Issues in design and interpretation of MDR-TB clinical trials: report of the first Global MDR-TB Clinical Trials Landscape Meeting
text: In December 2014, sixty international experts on multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) convened in Washington D.C. and Cape Town, South Africa to address the suboptimal current treatment regimen for MDR-TB, which affects millions of people worldwide annually. The Global MDR-TB Clinical Trials Landscape Meeting aimed to strategize the coordination of research and development of new treatment regimens through a comprehensive approach that includes standardization of definitions, clinical trial capacity building, and optimization of regimens to improve compliance, prevent resistance, and have clinical relevance for special populations, such as children and those co-infected with HIV. The meeting also focused on generating a sufficient evidence base to facilitate regulatory approval and improved normative guidance. Participants discussed ongoing Phase 2B and Phase 3 trials of treatment combinations, as well as promising new regimens and combinations that may be evaluated in the near future, including all-oral and shorter duration treatment regimens. The ultimate goal of the meeting was to accelerate progress towards effective, non-toxic treatments that can be programmatically implemented.

title: Para-aortic splanchnopleura from early mouse embryos contains B1a cell progenitors
text: The definitive emergence of erythropoiesis in birds originates from stem cells that arise in the splanchnopleural mesoderm near the embryonic aorta, according to studies 1-4. In contrast, the yolk sac is traditionally believed to be the sole provider of haematopoietic stem cells during mammalian development (5). However, there may be alternative intraembryonic sources of stem cells in the mouse fetus (6,7). To investigate this possibility, we grafted intraembryonic splanchnopleura from 10- to 18-somite mouse embryos into immunodeficient SCID mice. Our findings reveal significant amounts of donor-derived serum IgM, normal numbers of IgM-secreting plasma cells, and the Bla (IgMa brightB220dullCD5+) cell subset being fully reconstituted by donor progenitors 3-6 months after engraftment. Moreover, our experiments uncover a previously unrecognized site of haematogenesis, with the earliest colonization occurring 12 hours before fetal liver involvement.

title: Establishment in culture of pluripotential cells from mouse embryos
text: Pluripotent cells are present in a mouse embryo until at least an early post-implantation stage, as evidenced by their ability to contribute to the formation of chimeric animals and teratocarcinomas. Until now, it has been difficult to establish continuous cultures of these cells in vitro, and cell lines have only been obtained through teratocarcinoma formation in vivo. We report here the establishment of pluripotent cell lines derived directly from in vitro cultures of mouse blastocysts. These cells are capable of differentiating either in vitro or after inoculation into a mouse as a tumor in vivo, and have a normal karyotype.

title: MHC class II interaction with CD4 mediated by a region analogous to the MHC class I binding site for CD8
text: The interactions between major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules and the CD4 or CD8 coreceptors play a crucial role in the selection of mature T cells in the thymus. On mature T cells, each of these two glycoproteins is associated with a specific bias in recognizing MHC molecules by the T-cell receptor. CD4+ T cells recognize antigens in association with MHC class II molecules, while CD8+ T cells recognize antigens in association with MHC class I molecules. Physical interactions between CD4/MHC class II molecules and CD8/MHC class I molecules have been demonstrated through cell adhesion assays, and a binding site for CDS on class I molecules has been identified. Here, we demonstrate that a specific region in the MHC class IIβ-chain β2 domain, which is structurally similar to the CDS-binding loop in the MHC class I α3 domain, is essential for the function of both mouse and human CD4.

title: Instability and decay of the primary structure of DNA
text: Although DNA is the bearer of genetic information, it exhibits limited chemical stability. In vivo, DNA is susceptible to degradation through hydrolysis, oxidation, and non-enzymatic methylation at significant rates. These processes are countered by specialized DNA repair mechanisms. The spontaneous degradation of DNA is likely to play a crucial role in the development of mutations, cancer, and aging, as well as in limiting the recovery of DNA fragments from fossilized remains.

title: Single-cell proteomic analysis of S. cerevisiae reveals the architecture of biological noise
text: A primary objective of biology is to quantitatively describe cellular behavior. However, this task has been hindered by the challenge of measuring protein abundances and their fluctuations. Here, we present a strategy that combines high-throughput flow cytometry with a library of GFP-tagged yeast strains to monitor protein levels at the single-cell level with unprecedented precision. By analyzing the bulk protein abundance of over 2,500 proteins in rich and minimal media, we gain a comprehensive understanding of the cellular response to these conditions and identify changes not detected by DNA microarray analyses. Our single-cell data reveal that the noise in protein expression is primarily driven by the stochastic production and degradation of messenger RNAs. Interestingly, we find that protein-specific differences in noise are strongly correlated with a protein's mode of transcription and function. For instance, proteins that respond to environmental cues exhibit higher noise levels, while proteins involved in protein synthesis are relatively quiet. These findings reveal a striking structure to biological noise and suggest that protein noise levels may have evolved to balance the costs and benefits of variation.

title: Direct conversion of fibroblasts to functional neurons by defined factors
text:
Cellular differentiation and lineage commitment are generally considered to be irreversible processes during development. However, recent research has shown that mouse and human fibroblasts can be reprogrammed to a pluripotent state using a combination of four transcription factors. This raised the question of whether transcription factors could directly induce other defined somatic cell fates, beyond simply an undifferentiated state.
We hypothesized that combinatorial expression of neural-lineage-specific transcription factors could directly convert fibroblasts into neurons. Starting from a pool of nineteen candidate genes, we identified a combination of only three factors, Ascl1, Brn2 (also known as Pou3f2), and Myt1l, that efficiently convert mouse embryonic and postnatal fibroblasts into functional neurons in vitro. These induced neuronal (iN) cells express multiple neuron-specific proteins, generate action potentials, and form functional synapses.
The ability to generate neurons from non-neural lineages has significant implications for studies of neural development, neurological disease modeling, and regenerative medicine. This breakthrough could potentially lead to the generation of neurons for use in transplantation therapies, or the development of new treatments for neurological disorders.

title: Inflammasome-mediated dysbiosis regulates progression of NAFLD and obesity
text:
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the most common form of liver disease worldwide and is closely linked to metabolic syndrome. In fact, approximately 20% of individuals with NAFLD will develop a more severe form of the disease, known as non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), which can lead to cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite significant research efforts, the mechanisms underlying the progression from NAFLD to NASH remain unclear.
Our study reveals that two key inflammatory pathways, the NLRP6 and NLRP3 inflammasomes, and the effector protein IL-18, play a crucial role in regulating the progression of NAFLD/NASH. We found that these pathways not only modulate the gut microbiota but also have a direct impact on multiple aspects of metabolic syndrome.
Using mouse models, we found that a deficiency in the NLRP3 and NLRP6 inflammasomes leads to changes in the composition of the gut microbiota, which in turn exacerbate hepatic steatosis and inflammation. This occurs through an increase in the influx of TLR4 and TLR9 agonists into the portal circulation, leading to enhanced hepatic TNF-α expression and NASH progression.
Furthermore, our findings suggest that altered interactions between the gut microbiota and the host, resulting from defective NLRP3 and NLRP6 inflammasome sensing, play a central role in the pathogenesis of multiple metabolic syndrome-associated abnormalities. This highlights the importance of the microbiota in the development and progression of seemingly unrelated systemic auto-inflammatory and metabolic disorders.
In conclusion, our study provides new insights into the complex interplay between the gut microbiota and the host in the development and progression of NAFLD/NASH. These findings have significant implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of this common and often severe disease.

title: Chromatin remodelling at promoters suppresses antisense transcription
text: Chromatin plays a crucial role in compacting DNA within eukaryotic cells, enabling efficient transcriptional regulation. To elucidate the mechanisms underlying chromatin structure control across the Saccharomyces cerevisiae genome, we investigated the function of the ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex Isw2 in positioning nucleosomes. Our findings indicate that Isw2 is primarily localized adjacent to promoter regions, where it repositioned nucleosomes at the interface between gene-rich and gene-poor sequences. The directional repositioning of nucleosomes by Isw2 leads to increased occupancy of the intergenic region, resulting in proper transcriptional regulation. Conversely, loss of Isw2 activity leads to inappropriate transcription, resulting in the generation of both coding and noncoding transcripts. Our study demonstrates that Isw2 repositions nucleosomes to enforce directionality in transcriptional initiation, thereby preventing transcriptional initiation from cryptic sites. These findings provide insights into the global organization of chromatin and advance our understanding of transcriptional regulation.

title: The Human Mitochondrial DEAD-Box Protein DDX28 Resides in RNA Granules and Functions in Mitoribosome Assembly.
text: Human mitochondrial ribosomes are specialized organelles responsible for the synthesis of 13 essential proteins, which are integral components of the oxidative phosphorylation system. Despite significant progress in understanding the pathway of mitoribosome biogenesis, the compartmentalization of this process, and the factors involved, the mechanisms underlying the biogenesis of the mitoribosome large subunit (mt-LSU) remain largely elusive. In this study, we identified the DEAD-box protein DDX28 as a critical component of RNA granules involved in the early stages of mt-LSU biogenesis. DDX28 interacts with the 16S rRNA and the mt-LSU, and its silencing via RNA interference (RNAi) in HEK293T cells leads to a range of consequences, including reduced levels of 16S rRNA and mt-LSU proteins, impaired mt-LSU assembly, and a complete shutdown of mitochondrial protein synthesis. These findings highlight the essential role of DDX28 during the early stages of mt-LSU biogenesis, which primarily occurs in the compartment defined by RNA granules near the mitochondrial nucleoids.

title: Conversion of Adult Pancreatic α-cells to β-cells After Extreme β-cell Loss
text: Pancreatic insulin-producing beta-cells exhibit a remarkable ability to maintain their functional capacity throughout an individual's lifetime, with minimal replication occurring under normal conditions. However, in response to increased metabolic demand or injury, beta-cells display enhanced self-duplication. The capacity for adult mammals to differentiate (regenerate) new beta-cells from precursor cells or alternative sources after complete or extreme beta-cell loss, as observed in diabetes, remains a topic of investigation. Our findings in a transgenic model of acute selective near-total beta-cell ablation via diphtheria-toxin suggest that beta-cell regeneration is indeed possible, as mice that received insulin exhibited augmented beta-cell mass over time. Utilizing lineage-tracing techniques to identify the origin of regenerated beta-cells, we discovered that a significant proportion of these cells originated from glucagon-producing alpha-cells, highlighting an unappreciated level of plasticity within the pancreatic endocrine system. This uncovered capacity for inter-endocrine cell conversion could be harnessed to develop novel strategies for generating beta-cells for diabetes therapies, either through in vitro differentiation settings or through induced regeneration.

title: Driver mutations in histone H3.3 and chromatin remodelling genes in paediatric glioblastoma
text: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor that exhibits significant differences in genetic alterations between adult and pediatric cases. To investigate the underlying genetic events, we performed exome sequencing on 48 pediatric GBM samples. Our findings revealed somatic mutations in the H3.3-ATRX-DAXX chromatin remodeling pathway in 44% of tumors (21/48), with recurrent mutations in H3F3A, which encodes the replication-independent histone 3 variant H3.3, observed in 31% of tumors (13/48). These mutations led to specific amino acid substitutions in the histone tail, including K27M and G34R/G34V, which are involved in key post-translational modifications. Additionally, we identified mutations in ATRX (α-thalassaemia/mental retardation syndrome X-linked) and DAXX (death-domain associated protein), which encode two subunits of a chromatin remodeling complex required for H3.3 incorporation at pericentric heterochromatin and telomeres, in 31% of samples overall and in 100% of tumors with G34R or G34V H3.3 mutations. Furthermore, somatic TP53 mutations were identified in 54% of all cases and in 86% of samples with H3F3A and/or ATRX mutations. Notably, screening of a large cohort of gliomas of various grades and histologies (n = 784) revealed that H3F3A mutations are specific to GBM and highly prevalent in children and young adults. Moreover, the presence of H3F3A/ATRX-DAXX/TP53 mutations was strongly associated with alternative lengthening of telomeres and specific gene expression profiles. Our findings highlight the recurrent mutations in a regulatory histone in humans and suggest that defects in the chromatin architecture underlie the pathogenesis of paediatric and young adult GBM.

title: Translational control of intron splicing in eukaryotes
text: Most eukaryotic genes are interrupted by non-coding introns that must be precisely removed from pre-messenger RNAs to produce functional mRNAs. Splicing is guided locally by short conserved sequences, but genes typically contain multiple potential splice sites, and the mechanisms that determine the correct sites are not well understood. In most organisms, short introns cannot be efficiently predicted based solely on sequence motifs. In multicellular eukaryotes, long introns are recognized through exon definition, leading to the production of multiple mRNA variants through alternative splicing. The nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway can further shape the observed sets of variants by selectively degrading those containing premature termination codons, which are frequently produced in mammals. Our findings show that the small introns of the ciliate Paramecium tetraurelia are under strong selective pressure to cause premature termination of mRNA translation in the event of intron retention, and that the same bias is observed among the short introns of plants, fungi, and animals. By knocking down the two P. tetraurelia genes encoding UPF1, a protein crucial in NMD, we demonstrate that the intrinsic efficiency of splicing varies widely among introns and that NMD activity can significantly reduce the fraction of unspliced mRNAs. These results suggest that, regardless of alternative splicing, species with large intron numbers universally rely on NMD to compensate for suboptimal splicing efficiency and accuracy.

title: Alternatively activated macrophages produce catecholamines to sustain adaptive thermogenesis
text:
All homeotherms (warm-blooded animals) rely on thermogenesis to maintain their core body temperature, ensuring that cellular functions and physiological processes can continue in cold environments. According to the prevailing model of thermogenesis, when the hypothalamus detects cold temperatures, it triggers the release of noradrenaline (norepinephrine) in brown adipose tissue and white adipose tissue. The β(3)-adrenergic receptors on these cells then activate lipolysis in white adipocytes and stimulate the expression of thermogenic genes, such as PPAR-γ coactivator 1a (Ppargc1a), uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), and acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 1 (Acsl1), in brown adipocytes. However, the specific identity of all the cell types involved in this efferent loop is not yet fully understood.
In mice, we have discovered an unexpected requirement for the interleukin-4 (IL-4)-stimulated program of alternative macrophage activation in adaptive thermogenesis. Exposure to cold temperatures rapidly triggers alternative activation of adipose tissue macrophages, which then secrete catecholamines to induce thermogenic gene expression in brown adipose tissue and lipolysis in white adipose tissue. Surprisingly, the absence of alternatively activated macrophages impairs metabolic adaptations to cold, while administration of IL-4 increases thermogenic gene expression, fatty acid mobilization, and energy expenditure, all in a macrophage-dependent manner. Therefore, we have uncovered a crucial role for alternatively activated macrophages in the regulation of an important mammalian stress response: the response to cold.

title: Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres Mediated by Mitotic DNA Synthesis Engages Break-Induced Replication Processes.
text: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a telomerase-independent mechanism of telomere maintenance that is observed in a subset of cancers. Through the analysis of telomerase-positive cells and their human TERC knockout-derived ALT cell lines, we have found that ALT cells exhibit more fragile telomeres, indicative of telomere replication problems. These replication defects lead to mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS) at telomeres in a RAD52-dependent, but RAD51-independent, manner. Telomeric MiDAS is a conservative DNA synthesis process, potentially mediated by break-induced replication, similar to the type II ALT survivors in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Replication stresses induced by ectopic oncogenic expression of cyclin E, G-quadruplexes, or R-loop formation can facilitate the ALT pathway and lead to telomere clustering, a hallmark of ALT cancers. The TIMELESS/TIPIN complex suppresses telomere clustering and telomeric MiDAS, while the SMC5/6 complex promotes them. In summary, ALT cells exhibit more telomere replication defects that result in persistent DNA damage responses at telomeres, leading to the engagement of telomeric MiDAS (spontaneous mitotic telomere synthesis) that is triggered by DNA replication stress, potentially driving genomic duplications in cancer.

title: Light acts directly on organs and cells in culture to set the vertebrate circadian clock.
text: The expression of clock genes in vertebrates is widespread and not limited to traditional clock structures. In zebrafish, the expression of the Clock gene exhibits a robust circadian oscillation in various tissues both in vivo and in vitro, indicating that endogenous oscillators exist in peripheral organs. A defining characteristic of circadian clocks is their ability to be synchronized or entrained to the local time, typically through exposure to environmental light-dark cycles. An intriguing question is whether peripheral oscillators are entrained by signals from central pacemakers such as the eyes or are they directly light-responsive. Our findings demonstrate that the clocks in peripheral organs of zebrafish are set by light-dark cycles in culture, and we also show that a zebrafish-derived cell line contains a circadian oscillator that is directly light-entrained.

title: Small molecule inhibition of the KRAS–PDEδ interaction impairs oncogenic KRAS signalling
text: The KRAS oncogene product is a prominent target in anticancer drug discovery, yet direct interference with KRAS signaling has not led to clinically effective drugs. The proper localization and signaling of farnesylated KRAS are regulated by the prenyl-binding protein PDEδ, which maintains the spatial organization of KRAS by facilitating its diffusion in the cytoplasm. Our study reveals that disrupting the binding of mammalian PDEδ to KRAS using small molecules provides a novel opportunity to suppress oncogenic RAS signaling by altering its localization to endomembranes. Through biochemical screening and structure-based hit optimization, we identified inhibitors of the KRAS-PDEδ interaction that selectively bind to the prenyl-binding pocket of PDEδ with nanomolar affinity, inhibit oncogenic RAS signaling, and suppress the proliferation of human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells that rely on oncogenic KRAS. Our findings may inspire the development of novel drugs targeting oncogenic RAS.

title: Evolution of novel cooperative swarming in the bacterium Myxococcus xanthus
text: Cooperation among individuals is crucial for evolutionary advancements to higher levels of biological organization. During these transitions, groups of individuals at one level (such as single cells) collaborate to form more complex units at a higher level (such as multicellular organisms). While observing the evolution of cooperation in higher eukaryotes can be challenging, microorganisms offer a unique opportunity for study. In this report, we investigate the evolution of novel cooperative behavior in experimental lineages of the bacterium Myxococcus xanthus. Wild-type strains of M. xanthus exhibit socially dependent swarming across soft surfaces through a mechanism known as 'S-motility,' which requires the presence of extracellular type IV pili. However, in lineages of M. xanthus unable to produce pili, a new mechanistic basis for cooperative swarming evolved. This evolved swarming is mediated, at least in part, by increased production of an extracellular fibril matrix that binds cells together. Although costly to individuals, fibril production significantly enhances population expansion in groups of interconnected cells. These findings demonstrate that fundamental transitions to primitive cooperation can easily occur in bacteria, highlighting the potential for cooperation to drive evolutionary advancements.

title: Exon duplication and divergence in the human preproglucagon gene
text:
Glucagon is a 29-amino acid pancreatic hormone that counteracts the blood glucose-lowering action of insulin by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. The structure of the hamster pancreatic glucagon precursor has recently been determined through the sequencing of a cloned cDNA. The hamster preproglucagon protein consists of 180 amino acids and contains five functional regions: a signal or pre-peptide, an NH2-terminal peptide (also called glicentin-related pancreatic peptide, GRPP), glucagon, and two carboxy-terminal glucagon-like peptides (GLP-1 and GLP-2). The sequences of two non-allelic anglerfish pancreatic glucagon precursors have also been determined, and their organization is similar but not identical to the hamster protein, lacking the polypeptide segment corresponding to hamster GLP-2. The presence of three regions possessing internal homology, that is, glucagon, GLP-1, and GLP-2, within proglucagon, and the absence of GLP-2 in the anglerfish precursors suggest that the structure of the preproglucagon gene may provide insight into the evolution of this polyprotein.
We have isolated and sequenced the human preproglucagon gene and found that the organization of the human precursor deduced from this sequence is identical to the hamster protein. The gene contains at least three intervening sequences that divide the protein-coding portion of the gene into four regions corresponding to the signal peptide and part of the NH2-terminal peptide, the remainder of the NH2-terminal peptide, and glucagon, GLP-1, and GLP-2. These findings suggest that triplication and subsequent sequence divergence of an exon encoding glucagon or a glucagon-like peptide produced this polyprotein precursor.

title: BH1 and BH2 domains of Bcl-2 are required for inhibition of apoptosis and heterodimerization with Bax
text: BCL-2 was identified as a gene located at the t(14;18) chromosomal breakpoint in follicular B-cell lymphoma (1-3). BCL-2 has a unique oncogenic function by prolonging cell survival by inhibiting multiple forms of programmed cell death (4-13). A related family of proteins, including BAX, share two highly conserved regions known as Bcl-2 homology 1 (BH1) and 2 (BH2) domains (Fig. 1). These domains were found to serve as novel dimerization motifs through site-specific mutagenesis (14-20). Specifically, substitution of Gly 145 in the BH1 domain or Trp 188 in the BH2 domain completely abrogated BCL-2's death-repressor activity in response to interleukin-3 deprivation, γ-irradiation, and glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis. Mutations that affected BCL-2's function also disrupted its heterodimerization with BAX, yet still allowed for BCL-2 homodimerization. These findings establish a functional role for the BH1 and BH2 domains and suggest that BCL-2 exerts its effects through heterodimerization with BAX.

title: KAP1 controls endogenous retroviruses in embryonic stem cells
text: More than 40% of the mammalian genome is composed of retroelements, including approximately one-quarter that are endogenous retroviruses (ERVs). Some of these ERVs are still active, such as the highly polymorphic early transposon (ETn)/MusD and intracisternal A-type particles (IAP) in mice. ERVs are silenced during early embryogenesis through histone and DNA methylation, although the mechanisms behind this process are not fully understood. KAP1 (KRAB-associated protein 1, also known as tripartite motif-containing protein 28, TRIM28), a protein that represses genes by recruiting histone methyltransferases, is involved in this process. Two lines of evidence suggest that KAP1-mediated repression may play a role in controlling ERVs: first, KAP1 can trigger permanent gene silencing during early embryogenesis, and second, a KAP1 complex silences the retrovirus murine leukaemia virus in embryonic cells. Our study shows that KAP1 deletion leads to a significant increase in the expression of ERVs, particularly IAP elements, in mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells and early embryos. We also demonstrate that KAP1 acts synergistically with DNA methylation to silence IAP elements, and that it is enriched at the 5′ untranslated region (5′UTR) of IAP genomes. Our findings establish that KAP1 plays a crucial role in controlling endogenous retroelements during early embryonic development.

title: The TOR signalling pathway controls nuclear localization of nutrient-regulated transcription factors.
text: The rapamycin-sensitive TOR signaling pathway in Saccharomyces cerevisiae activates a cell growth program in response to nutrients such as nitrogen and carbon. The TOR1 and TOR2 kinases (TOR) regulate cytoplasmic protein synthesis and degradation through the conserved TAP42 protein. Upon phosphorylation by TOR, TAP42 binds and potentially inhibits type 2A and type-2A-related phosphatases, but the mechanism by which TOR controls nuclear events such as global repression of starvation-specific transcription remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TOR prevents transcription of genes expressed upon nitrogen limitation by promoting the association of the GATA transcription factor GLN3 with the cytoplasmic protein URE2. The binding of GLN3 to URE2 requires TOR-dependent phosphorylation of GLN3, which is also dependent on the TOR effector TAP42. Phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of GLN3 are antagonized by the type-2A-related phosphatase SIT4. In addition, TOR inhibits expression of carbon-source-regulated genes by stimulating the binding of the transcriptional activators MSN2 and MSN4 to the cytoplasmic 14-3-3 protein BMH2. Therefore, the TOR signaling pathway broadly controls nutrient metabolism by sequestering several transcription factors in the cytoplasm.

title: Inhibition of pluripotential embryonic stem cell differentiation by purified polypeptides
text: Murine embryonic stem (ES) cells are derived directly from early embryos and possess the ability to differentiate into all adult tissue types, including the germ cell lineage, after re-incorporation into the normal embryo. These cells serve as both a cellular vector for generating transgenic animals and a valuable system for identifying polypeptide factors that control differentiation processes in early development. In particular, medium conditioned by Buffalo rat liver cells contains a polypeptide factor, ES cell differentiation inhibitory activity (DIA), which specifically inhibits the spontaneous differentiation of ES cells in vitro, allowing them to grow as homogeneous stem cell populations without the need for heterologous feeder cells. ES cell pluripotency, including the ability to produce functional gametes, is maintained during prolonged culture in Buffalo rat liver media as a source of DIA. Further investigation reveals that purified DIA is structurally and functionally related to recently identified haemopoietic regulatory factors, including human interleukin for DA cells and leukaemia inhibitory factor. These findings suggest that DIA and human interleukin DA/leukaemia inhibitory factor are multifunctional regulatory factors with distinct biological activities in both early embryonic and haemopoietic stem cell systems.

title: Pancreatic cancer genomes reveal aberrations in axon guidance pathway genes
text: Pancreatic cancer is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited effective treatment options. To gain a deeper understanding of the genomic alterations driving this disease, we performed exome sequencing and copy number analysis on a prospectively accrued clinical cohort of early-stage (I and II) sporadic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (n = 142). Our analysis of 99 informative tumors revealed significant heterogeneity, with 2,016 non-silent mutations and 1,628 copy-number variations identified. We identified 16 significantly mutated genes, including known mutations in KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A, SMAD4, MLL3, TGFBR2, ARID1A, and SF3B1, as well as novel mutations in genes involved in chromatin modification (EPC1 and ARID2), DNA damage repair (ATM), and other mechanisms (ZIM2, MAP2K4, NALCN, SLC16A4, and MAGEA6). Integrative analysis of in vitro functional data and animal models provided supportive evidence for the potential roles of these genetic aberrations in carcinogenesis. Pathway-based analysis of recurrently mutated genes revealed clustering in core signaling pathways in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and identified new mutated genes in each pathway. Additionally, we found frequent and diverse somatic aberrations in genes traditionally involved in embryonic axon guidance, including SLIT/ROBO signaling, which was also observed in murine Sleeping Beauty transposon-mediated somatic mutagenesis models of pancreatic cancer. These findings provide further support for the potential involvement of axon guidance genes in pancreatic carcinogenesis.

title: Rejuvenation of aged progenitor cells by exposure to a young systemic environment
text:
The decline in tissue regenerative potential is a hallmark of aging and may be attributed to age-related changes in tissue-specific stem cells. Specifically, a decrease in skeletal muscle stem cell (satellite cell) activity due to a loss of Notch signaling leads to impaired regeneration of aged muscle tissue. Similarly, a decline in hepatic progenitor cell proliferation, resulting from the formation of a complex involving cEBP-α and the chromatin remodeling factor brahma (Brm), inhibits the regenerative capacity of aged liver tissue.
To investigate the influence of systemic factors on aged progenitor cells from these tissues, we established parabiotic pairings (i.e., a shared circulatory system) between young and old mice (heterochronic parabioses), exposing old mice to factors present in young serum. Notably, heterochronic parabiosis restored the activation of Notch signaling as well as the proliferation and regenerative capacity of aged satellite cells. In vitro exposure of satellite cells from old mice to young serum enhanced the expression of the Notch ligand (Delta), increased Notch activation, and enhanced proliferation. Furthermore, heterochronic parabiosis increased aged hepatocyte proliferation and restored the cEBP-α complex to levels seen in young animals. These findings suggest that the age-related decline in progenitor cell activity can be modulated by systemic factors that change with age.

title: Continuous single-cell imaging of blood generation from haemogenic endothelium
text:
Despite decades of research, the identity of the cells responsible for generating the first haematopoietic cells in mammalian embryos remains unknown. The debate continues as to whether blood cells arise from mesodermal cells, mesenchymal progenitors, bipotent endothelial-haematopoietic precursors, or haemogenic endothelial cells. However, recent advances in imaging and cell-tracking technologies have allowed researchers to shed light on this mystery.
Using cutting-edge techniques, the authors of this study were able to show that embryonic endothelial cells are capable of giving rise to blood cells. By continuously observing single cells over long periods of time, the researchers were able to detect haemogenic endothelial cells that give rise to blood cells. This was achieved by simultaneously detecting the morphology and multiple molecular and functional markers of both endothelial and haematopoietic cells.
The study found that detachment of nascent blood cells from the endothelium is not directly linked to asymmetric cell division, and haemogenic endothelial cells are specified from cells already expressing endothelial markers. These findings provide new insights into the developmental origin of mammalian blood and the potential generation of haematopoietic stem cells from embryonic stem cells.
In summary, the study demonstrates that embryonic endothelial cells have the potential to give rise to blood cells, resolving the long-standing debate about the origin of the first haematopoietic cells in mammalian embryos. The findings also highlight the importance of advanced imaging and cell-tracking technologies in shedding light on the complex processes involved in the development of the immune system.

title: Formation of germ-line chimaeras from embryo-derived teratocarcinoma cell lines
text: The recent availability of embryo-derived pluripotent cells with a normal karyotype and high differentiative potential has prompted us to investigate their ability to form functional germ cells after injection into chimaeric mice. We report the results of blastocyst injection studies using three independently isolated XY embryo-derived cell lines (EK.CP1, EK.CC1.1, and EKCC1.2), which yielded a high proportion (>50%) of live-born chimaeric animals. Of these, seven male chimaeric mice have been found to be functional germ-line chimaeras.

title: Chloroquine resistance not linked to mdr-like genes in a Plasmodium falciparum cross
text: Chloroquine is believed to combat falciparum malaria by accumulating in the acidic vesicles of the parasite and disrupting their function (1-4). However, parasites resistant to chloroquine rapidly expel the drug in its original form, reducing its accumulation in the vesicles (5). The discovery that verapamil can partially reverse chloroquine resistance in vitro led to the suggestion that efflux may involve an ATP-driven P-glycoprotein pump, similar to those found in mammalian multidrug-resistant (mdr) tumor cell lines (6). Indeed, Plasmodium falciparum contains at least two mdr-like genes (7,8), one of which has been implicated in conferring chloroquine resistance (CQR) (7,9,10). To investigate the genetic basis of chloroquine resistance, we performed a genetic cross between CQR and chloroquine-susceptible (CQS) clones of P. falciparum, examining 16 independent recombinant progeny. Our findings indicate that the genetic locus governing chloroquine efflux and resistance is independent of the known mdr-like genes.

title: Identification of a cold receptor reveals a general role for TRP channels in thermosensation
text: The intricate mechanisms by which our bodies perceive cold temperatures are still not fully understood. However, recent breakthroughs have been made through the use of pharmacological agents, such as menthol, which can elicit a cooling sensation when applied to the skin. By studying the effects of menthol on sensory neurons, researchers have identified and cloned a receptor called CMR1, which is responsible for detecting both cold and menthol stimuli. This receptor, a member of the TRP family of excitatory ion channels, is found in trigeminal sensory neurons and plays a key role in transmitting cold sensations to the brain. These findings, along with previous discoveries of heat-sensitive channels VR1 and VRL-1, demonstrate that TRP channels are the primary temperature sensors in the mammalian peripheral nervous system, capable of detecting a wide range of temperatures.

title: Surface mechanics mediate pattern formation in the developing retina
text: The formation of biological structures involves organizing different types of cells into a specific spatial arrangement. In this study, we investigate the underlying physical mechanisms of biological patterning in the Drosophila retina in vivo. We find that E- and N-cadherins play a crucial role in mediating adhesion between retinal epithelial cells. Specifically, the differential expression of N-cadherin within a subpopulation of retinal cells (cone cells) leads to their unique shape, which minimizes their surface contact with surrounding cells. Remarkably, the packing of these cells resembles the way soap bubbles cluster together, demonstrating a remarkable similarity between the physical properties of biological systems and the behavior of soft matter. Our findings reveal that simple patterned expression of N-cadherin can give rise to complex spatial patterns of cells through the mechanics of cellular surfaces.

title: Role of inscuteable in orienting asymmetric cell divisions in Drosophila
text: Drosophila neuroblasts and epithelial cells in the procephalic neurogenic region undergo perpendicular division, segregating proteins Numb and Prospero into the basal daughter cell. Our study reveals that the proper orientation of the mitotic spindle and the localization of Numb and Prospero in these cells depend on the Inscuteable gene. In addition, ectopic expression of Inscuteable in other epithelial cells leads to reorientation of the mitotic spindle. Notably, Inscuteable localizes to the apical cell cortex before mitosis, suggesting that it plays a crucial role in establishing polarity during asymmetric cell division.

title: Specific interference by ingested dsRNA.
text: A genetic phenomenon known as interference has been observed in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, where the expression of a single gene can be specifically reduced through the injection of a corresponding fragment of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). One notable aspect of this process is the spreading effect, where interference is observed in a wide region of the animal following the injection of dsRNA into the extracellular body cavity. Here, we demonstrate that C. elegans can respond to dsRNA encountered in the environment in a gene-specific manner. C. elegans typically feed on bacteria, ingesting and digesting them in the pharynx and then absorbing bacterial contents in the gut. Interestingly, we find that Escherichia coli bacteria expressing dsRNAs can produce specific interference effects on nematode larvae that feed on them.

title: Bacterial RNA and small antiviral compounds activate caspase-1 through cryopyrin/Nalp3
text: Missense mutations in the CIAS1 gene have been linked to three autoinflammatory disorders: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, Muckle–Wells syndrome, and neonatal-onset multiple-system inflammatory disease. The CIAS1 gene encodes cryopyrin, a member of the NOD-LRR protein family that plays a crucial role in the activation of intracellular host defense signaling pathways. Cryopyrin forms a multi-protein complex called the inflammasome, which consists of apoptosis-associated speck-like protein (ASC) and caspase-1. The inflammasome promotes caspase-1 activation and the processing of pro-interleukin (IL)-1β. Our study demonstrates the importance of cryopyrin in inflammasome function and immune responses. Cryopyrin and ASC are essential for caspase-1 activation and IL-1β and IL-18 production in response to bacterial RNA and the imidazoquinoline compounds R837 and R848. In contrast, the secretion of tumor-necrosis factor-α and IL-6, as well as the activation of NF-κB and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), were found to be unaffected by cryopyrin deficiency. Additionally, our findings reveal that Toll-like receptors and cryopyrin regulate the secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 through distinct intracellular signaling pathways. These results provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of autoinflammatory syndromes and highlight the critical role of cryopyrin in host defense through bacterial RNA-mediated activation of caspase-1.

title: Control of cortical GABA circuitry development by Nrg1 and ErbB4 signalling
text:
Schizophrenia is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder that affects cognitive and social functioning, typically manifesting during late adolescence or early adulthood. While the clinical features of the disorder have been extensively studied, recent research has identified neuregulin 1 (NRG1) and its receptor ERBB4 as important risk genes for schizophrenia. However, the precise mechanisms underlying their involvement in the disease process remain unclear.
Our study aimed to investigate the role of NRG1 and ERBB4 signaling in the development of inhibitory circuitries in the mammalian cerebral cortex. We found that ErbB4 expression in the mouse neocortex and hippocampus is primarily confined to certain classes of interneurons, including parvalbumin-expressing chandelier and basket cells. ErbB4 localizes to axon terminals and postsynaptic densities receiving glutamatergic input, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments suggest that it cell-autonomously promotes the formation of axo-axonic inhibitory synapses over pyramidal cells. Additionally, ErbB4 expression in GABA-containing interneurons regulates the formation of excitatory synapses onto these cells. In contrast, ErbB4 is dispensable for excitatory transmission between pyramidal neurons.
Our findings provide a new perspective on the involvement of NRG1 and ERBB4 in the aetiology of schizophrenia, suggesting that their role is primarily in the wiring of GABA-mediated circuits in the postnatal cortex. These findings have important implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of schizophrenia.

title: Obesity as a medical problem.
text:
Obesity has become a widespread issue worldwide, surpassing undernutrition and infectious diseases as the leading cause of ill health. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), obesity is defined as a body-mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or higher, but this measurement does not account for the severe health consequences associated with less extreme degrees of overweight. The global obesity epidemic is attributable to a combination of genetic susceptibility, increased access to high-calorie foods, and decreased physical activity in modern society. Obesity is no longer a mere cosmetic concern, but a major public health threat that affects millions of people globally.
Obesity is linked to various serious health problems, including diabetes mellitus, coronary heart disease, specific types of cancer, and sleep-breathing disorders. The detrimental effects of excess body fat, particularly intra-abdominal fat, are not fully captured by BMI alone. The WHO notes that even moderate degrees of overweight can have significant negative impacts on health, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive approach to address this global epidemic.
In conclusion, obesity is a complex issue that requires a multifaceted solution. It is essential to recognize obesity as a public health crisis that affects individuals, communities, and societies worldwide. By adopting a proactive and coordinated approach to address this epidemic, we can work towards reducing the burden of obesity-related health problems and promoting global well-being.

title: Nonlinear Elasticity in Biological Gels
text: Unlike most synthetic materials, biological materials often become stiffer when deformed. This nonlinear elastic response, crucial for the physiological function of certain tissues, has been observed since at least the 19th century, but the molecular structure and design principles behind it remain unknown. Current models require complex, geometrically ordered structures unique to each material. In this article, we demonstrate that a much simpler molecular theory can account for strain stiffening in a wide range of biopolymer gels composed of purified cytoskeletal and extracellular proteins. This theory shows that systems of semi-flexible chains, such as filamentous proteins arranged in an open, cross-linked meshwork, inherently stiffen at low strains without the need for specific architectures or multiple elements with different intrinsic stiffnesses.

title: Live-cell delamination counterbalances epithelial growth to limit tissue overcrowding
text: The maintenance and development of epithelial tissues require a delicate balance between cell growth and death. However, the underlying mechanisms that regulate this balance and prevent tumorigenesis are poorly understood. To address this gap in knowledge, we used the fruit fly notum as a model system to investigate a novel process of cell delamination that occurs in response to crowding. In crowded regions of the tissue, some cells undergo a loss of cell-cell junctions and a progressive loss of apical area, leading to their eventual expulsion by neighboring cells. This process of delamination is recapitulated in a simple computational model of epithelial mechanics, which shows that stochastic cell loss can relieve overcrowding and restore equilibrium to the system. Our findings reveal a previously unknown mechanism that maintains the balance of epithelial tissues and may have important implications for understanding the early stages of cancer development.

title: Broad antiretroviral defence by human APOBEC3G through lethal editing of nascent reverse transcripts
text: Viral replication typically requires the overcome of the body's natural defenses within cells, a task often accomplished by specialized viral proteins. The HIV virion infectivity factor (Vif) protein is essential during the late stages of viral production to counteract the antiviral activity of APOBEC3G (apolipoprotein B mRNA-editing enzyme, catalytic polypeptide-like 3G; also known as CEM15), a protein expressed at high levels in T lymphocytes. When produced in the presence of APOBEC3G, vif-defective viruses are non-infectious. APOBEC3G is related to APOBEC1, a central component of an RNA-editing complex that deaminates a cytosine residue in apoB messenger RNA. Members of the APOBEC family also have the ability to mutate DNA through deamination of cytosine residues, although it is unclear whether this editing potential plays a role in HIV inhibition. Our study demonstrates that it does, as APOBEC3G exerts its antiviral effect during reverse transcription to trigger G-to-A hypermutation in the emerging retroviral DNA. Additionally, we find that APOBEC3G can act on a wide range of retroviruses, including HIV, suggesting that hypermutation through editing is a general innate defense mechanism against these pathogens.

title: Generation of cell polarity in plants links endocytosis, auxin distribution and cell fate decisions
text:
Dynamically polarized membrane proteins, specifically the PIN family of efflux carriers, play a crucial role in intercellular communication and development in multicellular organisms. The polar localization of PINs determines the direction of intercellular auxin flow, but the mechanisms underlying this polarity are not well understood. Here, we investigate the endocytosis-dependent mechanism of PIN polarity generation and its developmental implications.
Using real-time PIN tracking, we found that PINs are initially delivered to the plasma membrane in a non-polar manner and their polarity is established through endocytic recycling. We demonstrate that interference with PIN endocytosis, either through auxin or manipulation of the Arabidopsis Rab5 GTPase pathway, prevents PIN polarization. Our results show that failure to establish PIN polarity leads to alterations in asymmetric auxin distribution during embryogenesis and an increase in the local auxin response in apical embryo regions. This, in turn, leads to ectopic expression of auxin pathway-associated root-forming master regulators in embryonic leaves and promotes homeotic transformation of leaves to roots.
Our findings reveal a two-step mechanism for the generation of PIN polar localization, with endocytosis playing a crucial role in this process. Additionally, we highlight the link between endocytosis-dependent polarity of individual cells and auxin distribution-dependent cell fate establishment for multicellular patterning. These findings have important implications for our understanding of the mechanisms underlying cell-cell communication and the establishment of cellular polarity in multicellular organisms.

title: Congenital leptin deficiency is associated with severe early-onset obesity in humans.
text: The extreme obesity observed in ob/ob mice is due to genetic mutations affecting the leptin gene, a protein produced by adipocytes that plays a crucial role in regulating appetite and energy expenditure. While we have identified no similar evidence in humans, we examined two severely obese children from a consanguineous family and found that their serum leptin levels were significantly lower despite their elevated fat mass. Moreover, both children carried a homozygous frame-shift mutation involving the deletion of a single guanine nucleotide in codon 133 of the leptin gene. These findings provide the first genetic evidence that leptin plays a critical role in regulating energy balance in humans, and suggest that leptin deficiency may contribute to the development of severe obesity in humans.

title: Targeting of cell-surface β-amyloid precursor protein to lysosomes: alternative processing into amyloid-bearing fragments
text:
The progressive deposition of the amyloid β-peptide is an early and consistent feature of Alzheimer's disease. The β-peptide is derived from the β-amyloid precursor protein (βAPP), a transmembrane glycoprotein expressed in most mammalian cells. The normal secretion of βAPP involves a cleavage in the β-peptide region, resulting in the release of a soluble extramembranous portion and the retention of a 10K C-terminal fragment in the membrane. However, this secretory pathway precludes the formation of β-amyloid, prompting us to investigate alternative proteolytic processing pathways that may generate β-peptide-bearing fragments from full-length βAPP.
Using living human endothelial cells, we observed reinternalization of mature βAPP from the cell surface and its targeting to endosomes/lysosomes after incubation with a βAPP antibody. Following cell-surface biotinylation, we recovered full-length biotinylated βAPP inside the cells. Purification of lysosomes directly revealed the presence of mature βAPP and a diverse array of β-peptide-containing proteolytic products. Our findings establish a second processing pathway for βAPP and suggest that it may be responsible for generating amyloid-bearing fragments in Alzheimer's disease.

title: A keratin cytoskeletal protein regulates protein synthesis and epithelial cell growth
text: Cellular growth, or an increase in mass and size, is a tightly regulated cellular process. The Akt/mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) signaling pathway plays a central role in controlling protein synthesis and thus cell growth, tissue growth, and organism growth. A notable example of a physiological context requiring rapid cell growth is tissue repair in response to injury. Here, we demonstrate that keratin 17, an intermediate filament protein, regulates cell growth by binding to the adaptor protein 14-3-3σ. In mouse skin keratinocytes lacking keratin 17, protein translation is impaired, resulting in smaller cell size and decreased Akt/mTOR signaling activity. Interestingly, other signaling kinases remain unchanged, indicating a specific defect. Two amino acid residues in the amino-terminal head domain of keratin 17 are essential for the serum-dependent relocalization of 14-3-3σ from the nucleus to the cytoplasm and the subsequent stimulation of mTOR activity and cell growth. These findings reveal a novel and unexpected role for the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in regulating cell growth and size by modulating protein synthesis.

title: Co-crystal structure of the HNF-3/fork head DNA-recognition motif resembles histone H5
text: The three-dimensional structure of the HNF-3/fork head DNA-recognition motif complexed with DNA has been resolved through X-ray crystallography at a resolution of 2.5 Å. This α/β protein binds B-DNA as a monomer through interactions with the DNA backbone and both direct and water-mediated major and minor groove base contacts, resulting in a 13° bend in the DNA molecule. The transcription factor fold exhibits a striking similarity to the structure of histone H5, with the amino-terminal half comprising three tightly packed α-helices that present the third helix towards the major groove. The remaining portion of the protein consists of a twisted, antiparallel β-structure and random coil regions that interact with the minor groove.

title: A Mechanism Linking Extra Centrosomes to Chromosomal Instability
text:
Chromosomal instability (CIN) is a hallmark of many tumors and is often associated with the presence of extra centrosomes. However, a direct mechanistic link between extra centrosomes and CIN has not been established. It has been proposed that extra centrosomes can lead to CIN by promoting multipolar anaphase, a highly abnormal cell division that results in three or more aneuploid daughter cells.
Using long-term live-cell imaging, we have found that cells with multiple centrosomes rarely undergo multipolar cell divisions, and the progeny of these divisions are typically inviable. This suggests that multipolar divisions cannot explain the observed rates of CIN. In contrast, we have observed that CIN cells with extra centrosomes routinely undergo bipolar cell divisions, but display a significantly increased frequency of lagging chromosomes during anaphase.
To investigate the mechanism underlying this mitotic defect, we generated cells with varying centrosome numbers. Our findings show that extra centrosomes are sufficient to promote chromosome missegregation during bipolar cell division. These segregation errors are caused by cells passing through a transient "multipolar spindle intermediate" in which merotelic kinetochore-microtubule attachment errors accumulate before centrosome clustering and anaphase.
Our findings provide a direct mechanistic link between extra centrosomes and CIN, two common characteristics of solid tumors. We propose that this mechanism may be a common underlying cause of CIN in human cancer.

title: Haematopoietic stem cells and early lymphoid progenitors occupy distinct bone marrow niches
text: Although haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are commonly believed to reside within a specialized microenvironment, or niche, most experimental manipulations of the HSC niche have actually affected diverse restricted progenitors. This raises the question of whether HSCs and restricted progenitors occupy distinct, specialized niches or share a common niche. To investigate, we examined the physiological sources of the chemokine CXCL12, which is important for HSC and restricted progenitor maintenance. Using Cxcl12(DsRed) knock-in mice, which express DsRed under the control of the Cxcl12 locus, we found that CXCL12 is primarily produced by perivascular stromal cells, endothelial cells, osteoblasts, and some haematopoietic cells. Conditional deletion of CXCL12 from haematopoietic cells or nestin-cre-expressing cells had little or no effect on HSCs or restricted progenitors. In contrast, deletion of CXCL12 from endothelial cells depleted HSCs but not myeloerythroid or lymphoid progenitors. Deletion of CXCL12 from perivascular stromal cells depleted HSCs and certain restricted progenitors and mobilized these cells into the circulation. Deletion of CXCL12 from osteoblasts depleted certain early lymphoid progenitors but not HSCs or myeloerythroid progenitors, and did not mobilize these cells into the circulation. Our findings suggest that different stem and progenitor cells reside in distinct cellular niches within the bone marrow: HSCs occupy a perivascular niche, while early lymphoid progenitors reside in an endosteal niche.

title: Broad neutralization coverage of HIV by multiple highly potent antibodies
text: The development of broadly neutralizing antibodies against highly variable viral pathogens is a crucial goal for the treatment and protection against global circulating viruses. In this study, we investigated the neutralizing antibody repertoires of four human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-infected donors, who displayed remarkable breadth and potency of neutralizing responses. Through the rescue of 17 new monoclonal antibodies, we were able to identify antibodies that neutralize broadly across different clades of HIV. Notably, many of these new monoclonal antibodies exhibit a 10-fold or greater increase in potency compared to previously described broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, such as PG9, PG16, and VRC01. Furthermore, the monoclonal antibodies isolated in this study largely recapitulate the neutralization breadth observed in the corresponding donor serum, and many recognize novel epitopes on the envelope (Env) glycoprotein gp120, providing new insights into the design of vaccines. Analysis of the neutralization capabilities of the full complement of anti-HIV broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies available now reveals that certain combinations of antibodies offer significantly more favorable coverage of the diverse range of global circulating viruses, and these combinations may be useful in active or passive immunization regimens. Overall, the isolation of multiple HIV broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies from multiple donors, which together provide broad coverage at low concentrations, is a highly encouraging finding for the development of an effective antibody-based HIV vaccine.

title: Coordination of Rho GTPase activities during cell protrusion
text:
The GTPases Rac1, RhoA, and Cdc42 play a crucial role in regulating cytoskeleton dynamics, particularly during cell migration. Recent biosensor studies have shown that all three GTPases are activated at the leading edge of migrating cells, suggesting a possible regulatory relationship between them. While it is known that Cdc42 can activate Rac1 and RhoA is mutually inhibitory with Rac1, the spatiotemporal coordination of these GTPases at the seconds and single-micrometre scales during individual protrusion events remains unexplored.
To investigate the coordination of GTPase activity in mouse embryonic fibroblasts, we employed a combination of simultaneous visualization of two GTPase biosensors and a 'computational multiplexing' approach that enabled the relationships between multiple protein activities observed in separate experiments to be defined. Our findings revealed that RhoA is activated at the cell edge in synchrony with edge advancement, whereas Cdc42 and Rac1 are activated 2 micrometers behind the edge with a delay of 40 seconds. This suggests that Rac1 and RhoA operate in an antagonistic manner through spatial separation and precise timing, with RhoA playing a role in the initial stages of protrusion and Rac1 and Cdc42 activating pathways involved in reinforcement and stabilization of newly expanded protrusions.

title: Understanding mechanisms underlying human gene expression variation with RNA sequencing
text:
Understanding the genetic mechanisms underlying natural variation in gene expression is a crucial objective of both medical and evolutionary genetics. To achieve this goal, studies of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) have become a valuable tool. Although all eQTL studies to date have relied on measuring messenger RNA levels using expression microarrays, recent advances in RNA sequencing have enabled the analysis of transcript variation at unprecedented resolution.
