Additionally, analysis of approximately 500,000 DNA metagenomic reads from 12 fecal samples revealed that the earliest microbiome was enriched in genes facilitating lactate utilization, and that functional genes involved in plant polysaccharide metabolism were present before the introduction of solid food, priming the infant gut for an adult diet. The introduction of table foods led to a sustained increase in the abundance of Bacteroidetes, elevated fecal short chain fatty acid levels, enrichment of genes associated with carbohydrate utilization, vitamin biosynthesis, and xenobiotic degradation, and a more stable community composition, all of which are characteristic of the adult microbiome. This study suggests that the seemingly chaotic shifts in the microbiome are associated with life events, but further experiments are needed to determine how different infants respond to similar events.

title: gamma-tocopherol, the major form of vitamin E in the US diet, deserves more attention.
text:
Gamma-tocopherol, the primary form of vitamin E in plant seeds and a significant component of the US diet, has historically received less attention than its counterpart, alpha-tocopherol, which is predominant in tissues and supplements. However, recent studies have shown that gamma-tocopherol may play a crucial role in human health, boasting unique features that differentiate it from alpha-tocopherol.
Gamma-tocopherol has been found to be a more effective trap for lipophilic electrophiles than alpha-tocopherol, and it is well absorbed and accumulates in significant amounts in certain human tissues. Upon metabolism, gamma-tocopherol is converted into 2,7,8-trimethyl-2-(beta-carboxyethyl)-6-hydroxychroman (gamma-CEHC), which is primarily excreted in the urine. Interestingly, gamma-CEHC possesses natriuretic activity, a property not observed in the corresponding metabolite derived from alpha-tocopherol. Additionally, both gamma-tocopherol and gamma-CEHC, but not alpha-tocopherol, have been shown to inhibit cyclooxygenase activity, thereby exhibiting anti-inflammatory properties.
Epidemiological studies have found that plasma concentrations of gamma-tocopherol are inversely associated with the incidence of cardiovascular disease and prostate cancer. These findings suggest that gamma-tocopherol may play a significant role in human health, a possibility that warrants further investigation. It is worth noting that high doses of alpha-tocopherol can deplete plasma and tissue gamma-tocopherol, whereas supplementation with gamma-tocopherol leads to increased levels of both.
In conclusion, this review aims to provide an overview of the bioavailability, metabolism, chemistry, and non-antioxidant activities of gamma-tocopherol, as well as epidemiological data on its relation to cardiovascular disease and cancer. The unique features of gamma-tocopherol and its potential health benefits make it a compelling area of research, with implications for the development of novel vitamin E supplements and therapies.

title: Disclosure of APOE genotype for risk of Alzheimer's disease.
text:
Background: The apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype has been shown to be a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. However, the genotyping of patients and their family members has been discouraged due to concerns about the potential psychological impact of disclosing this information. In this study, we aimed to investigate the effects of disclosing APOE genotyping results on the psychological outcomes of asymptomatic adults with a parent with Alzheimer's disease.
Methods: We conducted a prospective, randomized, controlled trial in which 162 participants were randomly assigned to receive either the results of their own APOE genotyping (disclosure group) or not to receive such results (nondisclosure group). Participants were assessed for symptoms of anxiety, depression, and test-related distress at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 1 year after disclosure or nondisclosure. Additionally, we conducted secondary comparisons between the nondisclosure group and a subgroups of participants who were positive for the APOE epsilon4 allele (which is associated with increased risk).
Results: We found no significant differences between the disclosure and nondisclosure groups in terms of changes in time-averaged measures of anxiety, depression, or test-related distress. However, we did observe a significant difference in test-related distress between the epsilon4-negative subgroup and the epsilon4-positive subgroup. Specifically, the epsilon4-negative subgroup had lower levels of test-related distress than the epsilon4-positive subgroup. Additionally, we found that baseline scores for anxiety and depression were strongly associated with post-disclosure scores of these measures.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that disclosing APOE genotyping results to adult children of patients with Alzheimer's disease does not result in significant short-term psychological risks. However, we did observe a reduction in test-related distress among those who learned that they were epsilon4-negative. Individuals with high levels of emotional distress before undergoing genetic testing were more likely to have emotional difficulties after disclosure. These findings have implications for the genetic testing of individuals at risk for Alzheimer's disease. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00571025.)

title: Blood pressure and incidence of twelve cardiovascular diseases: lifetime risks, healthy life-years lost, and age-specific associations in 1·25 million people
text: The study aimed to investigate the associations between blood pressure and different types of cardiovascular disease in a contemporary population. The study analyzed data from over 1.2 million patients aged 30 or older, who were free of cardiovascular disease at the start of the study. The study found that the lowest risk for cardiovascular disease was in people with systolic blood pressure of 90-114 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure of 60-74 mm Hg, with no evidence of a J-shaped increased risk at lower blood pressures. The study also found that the effect of high blood pressure varied by cardiovascular disease endpoint, with strongest associations for intracerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and stable angina, and weakest associations for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Additionally, the study found that raised systolic blood pressure had a greater effect on angina, myocardial infarction, and peripheral arterial disease, whereas raised diastolic blood pressure had a greater effect on abdominal aortic aneurysm than raised systolic pressure. The study also found that people with hypertension (blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg or those receiving blood pressure-lowering drugs) had a lifetime risk of overall cardiovascular disease at 30 years of age of 63.3% compared to 46.1% for those with normal blood pressure, and developed cardiovascular disease 5 years earlier. The study emphasizes the need for new blood pressure-lowering strategies and will help inform the design of randomized trials to assess them. The study was funded by the Medical Research Council, National Institute for Health Research, and Wellcome Trust.

title: Can Online Consumers Contribute to Drug Knowledge? A Mixed-Methods Comparison of Consumer-Generated and Professionally Controlled Psychotropic Medication Information on the Internet
text:
Online health searches often exclude consumer-generated content from search returns, despite a lack of evidence demonstrating its inferiority compared to professionally controlled content. However, a recent study aimed to investigate the effects of two popular psychotropic medications, escitalopram and quetiapine, as reported by both professionally controlled websites and consumer-generated websites.
The study analyzed 960 consumer reviews from six websites, including four professionally controlled websites (WebMD, Revolution Health, Askapatient, and Crazymeds) and two consumer-generated websites (Askapatient and Crazymeds). The researchers found that both drugs were consistently ranked as top-selling agents in their respective drug classes, and had various off-label uses beyond their approved indications.
The study's findings revealed that consumers most frequently reported symptom improvement or worsening, changes in sleep and weight, and changes in daily routines. However, there were some differences in the way these effects were reported between professionally controlled and consumer-generated websites. For example, more consumers posting on professionally controlled websites reported symptom improvement, while more consumers posting on consumer-generated websites reported symptom worsening on quetiapine. Additionally, professional descriptions were more likely to list physical adverse effects and warnings about suicidal ideation, while consumer reviews provided richer descriptions of effects in context.
The study suggests that current strategies for filtering online health searches may inappropriately address the challenge of identifying quality health sources on the internet. While professionally controlled websites offer a concise and comprehensive listing of drug effects, consumer reviews provide valuable context and situational examples of how effects may manifest in various combinations and to varying degrees. The dispersion of consumer reviews across websites limits their integration, but a brief browsing strategy on the two target medications can retrieve representative consumer content.
In conclusion, the study highlights the importance of considering both professionally controlled and consumer-generated content when searching for health information online. By integrating these sources, individuals can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the effects of psychotropic medications and make more informed decisions about their health.

title: Effect of supplemental zinc on the growth and serum zinc concentrations of prepubertal children: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
text:
Background: Numerous studies have investigated the impact of zinc supplementation on the growth of children. However, the results of these studies have been inconsistent, and the underlying factors responsible for these varied outcomes remain unclear.
Objective: To conduct meta-analyses of randomized controlled intervention trials to assess the effect of zinc supplementation on the physical growth and serum zinc concentrations of prepubertal children.
Design: A total of 33 suitable studies were identified through MEDLINE searches and other methods. Weighted mean effect sizes (expressed in SD units) were calculated using random-effects models to assess the changes in height, weight, weight-for-height, and serum zinc concentration in response to zinc supplementation. Meta-regression techniques were employed to explore factors associated with effect sizes.
Results: Zinc supplementation produced highly significant and positive responses in height and weight increments, with effect sizes of 0.350 (95% CI: 0.189, 0.511) and 0.309 (0.178, 0.439), respectively. There was no significant effect of zinc on weight-for-height indexes, with a weighted mean effect size of -0.018 (-0.132, 0.097). Zinc supplementation resulted in a large increase in the children's serum zinc concentrations, with an effect size of 0.820 (0.499, 1.14). Growth responses were greater in children with low initial weight-for-age z scores and in those aged >6 mo with low initial height-for-age z scores.
Conclusions: The findings of this meta-analysis suggest that interventions to improve children's zinc nutriture should be considered in populations at risk of zinc deficiency, particularly in areas with elevated rates of underweight or stunting. The population mean serum zinc concentration may serve as a useful indicator of the successful delivery and absorption of zinc supplements in children.

title: Mechanisms of Age-Related Macular Degeneration
text: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD), a debilitating condition that affects up to 90% of patients and is the leading cause of blindness in the elderly globally, has two forms: wet and dry. The classification of these forms is based on the presence or absence of disruptive blood vessels in the retina. Recent advances in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying wet AMD have led to FDA-approved therapies, while there are currently no treatments for dry AMD. This review provides insight into the critical effector pathways involved in each form of the disease, highlighting a recurring theme of defective immune modulation in the immune-privileged ocular environment. Additionally, the latest research on AMD has revealed common molecular pathways with other neurodegenerative disorders, underscoring the potential for therapeutic intervention at key mechanistic steps in AMD pathogenesis.

title: The N-end rule pathway regulates pathogen responses in plants.
text: To effectively counteract pathogens, plants rely on a sophisticated system of immune responses that are tightly regulated to timely activate, appropriately duration, and adequately amplify defense programs. The coordination of plant immune response requires the activity of the ubiquitin/proteasome system, which controls protein stability in eukaryotes. Specifically, we demonstrate that the N-end rule pathway, a subset of the ubiquitin/proteasome system, regulates defense against a wide range of bacterial and fungal pathogens in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. Our findings show that this pathway positively regulates the biosynthesis of plant-defense metabolites, such as glucosinolates, as well as the biosynthesis and response to the phytohormone jasmonic acid, which plays a crucial role in plant immunity. Additionally, our results suggest that the arginylation branch of the N-end rule pathway regulates the timing and amplitude of the defense program against the model pathogen Pseudomonas syringae AvrRpm1.

title: H3K9 demethylase KDM4E is an epigenetic regulator for bovine embryonic development and a defective factor for nuclear reprogramming.
text: Aberrant epigenetic reprogramming in somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) embryos often leads to developmental defects during embryonic genome activation (EGA). In bovine eight-cell SCNT embryos, global hypermethylation of histone H3 lysine 9 tri- and dimethylation (H3K9me3/2) has been observed, but the underlying cause remains unclear. Our study reveals that two histone H3 lysine 9 demethylase genes, lysine-specific demethylase 4D (KDM4D) and 4E (KDM4E), play a crucial role in active H3K9me3/2 demethylation in in vitro fertilized (IVF) embryos and are deficiently expressed in cloned embryos at the time of EGA. Furthermore, we found that KDM4E is more essential in IVF and SCNT embryonic development, and overexpression of KDM4E can restore the global transcriptome, improve blastocyst formation, and increase the cloning efficiency of SCNT embryos. Our results suggest that KDM4E functions as a crucial epigenetic regulator of EGA and an internal defective factor responsible for persistent H3K9me3/2 barriers to SCNT-mediated reprogramming. Additionally, we found that interactions between RNA and KDM4E are essential for H3K9 demethylation during EGA. These findings advance our understanding of incomplete nuclear reprogramming and have important implications for transgenic cattle production.

title: Risk of gestational hypertension in relation to folic acid supplementation during pregnancy.
text: The study aimed to investigate the association between folic acid supplementation and gestational hypertension in a population of women in the United States and Canada. The study population consisted of women who had given birth to healthy infants between 1993 and 2000 and were participating in the Slone Epidemiology Center Birth Defects Study. The women were interviewed within 6 months after delivery regarding their sociodemographic and medical factors, including the occurrence of hypertension with or without preeclampsia, and their use of multivitamins during pregnancy. The relative risk of developing gestational hypertension during the month after folic acid supplementation, compared to not using folic acid during that same month, was estimated using Cox regression models. The study found that among 2,100 women, 204 (9.7%) reported gestational hypertension. The multivariate-adjusted relative risk of developing gestational hypertension during the month after folic acid supplementation was 0.55 (95% confidence interval: 0.39, 0.79), suggesting that folic acid-containing multivitamins may reduce the risk of gestational hypertension.

title: Aire regulates negative selection of organ-specific T cells
text:
Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a recessive genetic disorder caused by mutations in the AIRE gene, leading to a spectrum of organ-specific autoimmune diseases. The exact mechanisms underlying APS-1 are not fully understood, but studies in transgenic mice have shed light on the role of AIRE in tolerance mechanisms.
In these studies, we traced the fate of autoreactive CD4+ T cells with high affinity for a pancreatic antigen in mice with an AIRE mutation. Our findings revealed almost complete failure of the thymus to delete organ-specific cells in the presence of AIRE deficiency. These results suggest that APS-1 is caused by a failure of a specialized mechanism for deleting forbidden T cell clones, establishing a central role for this tolerance mechanism in the development of the disease.
In summary, APS-1 is a recessive Mendelian disorder resulting from mutations in the AIRE gene, which leads to a spectrum of organ-specific autoimmune diseases due to defects in tolerance mechanisms. The study of transgenic mice with an AIRE mutation has revealed a central role for this tolerance mechanism in the development of APS-1.

title: Extracellular Acidic pH Activates the Sterol Regulatory Element-Binding Protein 2 to Promote Tumor Progression.
text: The tumor microenvironment plays a crucial role in cancer progression, with conditions such as hypoxia and nutrient starvation being well-studied. However, the impact of acidic extracellular pH on cancer progression has received less attention. Our research shows that acidic pH (pH 6.8) triggers the activation of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2), leading to its nuclear translocation and binding to its targets. This activation leads to the upregulation of cholesterol biosynthesis-related genes, and inhibition of SREBP2 suppresses this upregulation. Additionally, we found that acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2 (ACSS2), a direct SREBP2 target, provides a growth advantage to cancer cells under acidic pH. Furthermore, acidic pH-responsive SREBP2 target genes were associated with reduced overall survival of cancer patients. Our findings suggest that SREBP2 is a key transcriptional regulator of metabolic genes and progression of cancer cells, particularly in response to extracellular acidification.

title: Mutation of the Human Circadian Clock Gene CRY1 in Familial Delayed Sleep Phase Disorder
text: The daily patterns of human activity are regulated by an intrinsic circadian clock that exhibits a 24-hour rhythm in various behavioral and physiological processes. However, in individuals with delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD), a common form of insomnia, the sleep-wake cycle is disrupted and shifted to later times, leading to misalignment with societal norms. In this study, we investigate a hereditary form of DSPD associated with a dominant coding variation in the core circadian clock gene CRY1. This variant results in a gain-of-function CRY1 protein with enhanced affinity for circadian activator proteins Clock and Bmal1, leading to reduced expression of key transcriptional targets and lengthened circadian molecular rhythms. The frequency of this allele is up to 0.6%, and reverse phenotyping of unrelated families reveals late and/or fragmented sleep patterns in carriers, suggesting that it affects sleep behavior in a significant portion of the human population.

title: Lateral Hypothalamic Signaling Mechanisms Underlying Feeding Stimulation: Differential Contributions of Src Family Tyrosine Kinases to Feeding Triggered Either by NMDA Injection or by Food Deprivation
text: In rats, researchers have found multiple ways to experimentally trigger feeding, including food deprivation and acute microinjection of the neurotransmitter glutamate (Glu) or its receptor agonist N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) into the lateral hypothalamic area (LHA). Under both conditions, the NMDA receptor (NMDA-R) in the LHA appears critical for transmitting signals encoded by Glu and stimulating feeding. However, the underlying intracellular mechanisms are unknown. To investigate, researchers examined the role of protein-tyrosine kinases (PTKs) in these mechanisms. They found that injections of PTK inhibitors into the LHA significantly suppressed feeding elicited by NMDA injection (up to 69%) but only mildly suppressed deprivation feeding (24%). These results suggest that PTKs may play a less critical role in signals underlying this feeding behavior. In contrast, food deprivation, but not NMDA injection, led to significant increases in the activity of Src PTKs and the expression of Pyk2, an Src-activating PTK. When considered together, the behavioral and biochemical results demonstrate that food deprivation can readily drive PTK activity in vivo, possibly due to greater recruitment of PTKs by neurotransmitter receptors activated during deprivation-elicited feeding. These findings highlight the importance of using multiple feeding stimulation paradigms to reveal the true contributions of signaling molecules to pathways underlying feeding behavior in vivo.

title: Relationship between advanced glycation end‐product accumulation and low skeletal muscle mass in Japanese men and women
text:
The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between advanced glycation end-product (AGE) accumulation and skeletal muscle mass among middle-aged and older Japanese men and women.
METHODS: A total of 132 participants enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Skin autofluorescence was assessed as a measure of AGEs. Appendicular skeletal muscle mass was measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, and skeletal muscle index was calculated by dividing appendicular skeletal muscle mass by height squared. Participants were divided into two groups (low skeletal muscle index and normal skeletal muscle index) using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia's skeletal muscle index criteria for diagnosing sarcopenia. Multivariate logistic regression analysis and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were used to determine significant factors associated with low skeletal muscle index.
RESULTS: Participants consisted of 70 men (mean age 57 ± 10 years) and 62 women (mean age 60 ± 11 years). There were 31 and 101 participants in the low and normal skeletal muscle index groups, respectively. Skin autofluorescence was significantly higher in the low skeletal muscle index group compared with the normal skeletal muscle index group (P < 0.01). Skin autofluorescence was a significant independent factor associated with low skeletal muscle index based on multivariate logistic regression analysis (odds ratio 15.7, 95% confidence interval 1.85-133.01; P = 0.012). The cut-off for skin autofluorescence was 2.45 arbitrary units, with a sensitivity of 0.75 and specificity of 0.91.
CONCLUSIONS: Skin autofluorescence was an independent factor associated with low skeletal muscle index among middle-aged and older Japanese men and women. This finding suggests that skin autofluorescence may be a useful marker for identifying individuals at risk of low skeletal muscle mass. Geriatr Gerontol Int 2017; 17: 785-790.

title: Large-Scale Profiling Reveals the Influence of Genetic Variation on Gene Expression in Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.
text: In this study, we leveraged whole-genome sequencing and gene expression profiling of 215 human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines from diverse donors to identify genetic variants associated with RNA expression for 5,746 genes. By predicting causal variants for these expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) that disrupt transcription factor binding, we validated a subset of them experimentally. Moreover, we identified copy-number variant (CNV) eQTLs, including those that affect gene expression by altering the copy number of intergenic regulatory regions. Additionally, we uncovered effects of rare genic CNVs and regulatory single-nucleotide variants on gene expression, and found that reactivation of gene expression on the X chromosome depends on the position of the gene within the chromosome. Our findings underscore the utility of iPSCs for genetic association analyses and provide a valuable resource for investigating the genetic regulation of gene expression in pluripotent cells.

title: Ethanol extract of Allium fistulosum inhibits development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
text:
Background/Objectives:
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a leading cause of chronic liver disease and is closely associated with metabolic syndrome. The present study aimed to investigate the effect of ethanol extract of Allium fistulosum (EAF) on NAFLD and explore its potential as a natural product for the development of a treatment for NAFLD.
Materials/Methods:
The preventive effect of EAF on hepatic lipid accumulation was evaluated in vitro using an oleic acid (OA)-induced NAFLD model in HepG2 cells, and in vivo in obese mice fed a Western diet (high-fat high-sucrose; WD) in the presence or absence of EAF supplementation. The study included three groups of animals (n = 7): normal diet (ND) group, WD group, and WD plus 1% EAF group.
Results:
EAF significantly reduced OA-stimulated lipid accumulation in HepG2 cells without causing cellular cytotoxicity, and blocked transcriptional activation of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 and fatty acid synthase genes. In vivo, EAF supplementation in mice fed either ND or WD attenuated increases in body weight, liver weight, epididymal fat weight, and hepatocellular lipid accumulation induced by the WD, and these effects were observed in comparison to the normal diet controls.
Conclusions:
The present study demonstrates that EAF attenuates the development of NAFLD, and its anti-lipogenic activity in the liver suggests its potential as a promising candidate for the prevention and treatment of NAFLD. These findings provide a basis for further investigations into the therapeutic potential of EAF in the development of novel drugs or drug combinations for NAFLD.

title: Cardiovascular risk factors in childhood and carotid artery intima-media thickness in adulthood: the Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study.
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the text with some changes to improve readability and clarity:
Context: Exposure to cardiovascular risk factors during childhood and adolescence may lead to the development of atherosclerosis later in life.
Objective: To investigate the relationship between cardiovascular risk factors measured in childhood and adolescence and common carotid artery intima-media thickness (IMT), a marker of preclinical atherosclerosis, measured in adulthood.
Design, Setting, and Participants: Population-based, prospective cohort study conducted at 5 centers in Finland among 2229 white adults aged 24 to 39 years who were examined in childhood and adolescence at ages 3 to 18 years in 1980 and reexamined 21 years later, between September 2001 and January 2002.
Main Outcome Measures: Association between cardiovascular risk variables (levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and triglycerides; LDL-C/HDL-C ratio; systolic and diastolic blood pressure; body mass index; smoking) measured in childhood and adulthood and common carotid artery IMT measured in adulthood.
Results: In multivariable models adjusted for age and sex, IMT in adulthood was significantly associated with childhood LDL-C levels (P =.001), systolic blood pressure (P<.001), body mass index (P =.007), and smoking (P =.02), and with adult systolic blood pressure (P<.001), body mass index (P<.001), and smoking (P =.004). The number of risk factors measured in 12- to 18-year-old adolescents, including high levels (ie, extreme age- and sex-specific 80th percentile) of LDL-C, systolic blood pressure, body mass index, and cigarette smoking, were directly related to carotid IMT measured in young adults at ages 33 through 39 years (P<.001 for both men and women), and remained significant after adjustment for contemporaneous risk variables. The number of risk factors measured at ages 3 to 9 years demonstrated a weak direct relationship with carotid IMT at ages 24 to 30 years in men (P =.02) but not in women (P =.63).
Conclusions: Risk factor profile assessed in 12- to 18-year-old adolescents predicts adult common carotid artery IMT independently of contemporaneous risk factors. These findings suggest that exposure to cardiovascular risk factors early in life may induce changes in arteries that contribute to the development of atherosclerosis.

title: MicroRNA-29 induces cellular senescence in aging muscle through multiple signaling pathways
text: The underlying mechanisms of muscle atrophy associated with aging are unclear, but recent studies have shed light on the role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in this process. By analyzing microRNA arrays and individual quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in muscles of aged rodents compared to young ones, we found a significant up-regulation of miR-29. This increase in miR-29 was found to impair the proliferation of muscle progenitor cells (MPCs) by interacting with the 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) of p85α, IGF-1, and B-myb, thereby suppressing their translation. In vivo, electroporation of miR-29 into muscles of young mice recapitulated the aging-induced responses in muscle, including increased levels of cellular arrest proteins and suppressed proliferation of MPCs. We also found that exogenous Wnt-3a stimulated miR-29 expression in primary cultures of MPCs, suggesting that Wnt-3a may play a role in the activation of miR-29 in aging muscles. Our findings provide a potential mechanism for aging-induced muscle senescence, which contributes to sarcopenia. The increase in miR-29 levels may play a key role in the development of muscle atrophy associated with aging.

title: Rictor, a Novel Binding Partner of mTOR, Defines a Rapamycin-Insensitive and Raptor-Independent Pathway that Regulates the Cytoskeleton
text: The mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) pathway integrates signals from nutrients and growth factors to regulate cell growth, which involves the accumulation of mass and an increase in cell size. mTOR is a large protein kinase that is targeted by rapamycin, an immunosuppressant with potential anticancer applications. mTOR interacts with the raptor and GbetaL proteins to form a complex that is sensitive to rapamycin. Our study reveals that mTOR is also part of a distinct complex defined by the novel protein rictor (rapamycin-insensitive companion of mTOR). Rictor shares homology with proteins from yeast, flies, and yeast, including AVO3p, which is part of a rapamycin-insensitive TOR complex that does not contain the yeast homolog of raptor and signals to the actin cytoskeleton through PKC1. Interestingly, the rictor-containing mTOR complex contains GbetaL but not raptor and does not regulate the mTOR effector S6K1 or bind FKBP12-rapamycin. Our findings suggest that the rictor-mTOR complex modulates the phosphorylation of PKCalpha and the actin cytoskeleton, indicating that this aspect of TOR signaling is conserved between yeast and mammals.

title: Activation of the estrogen receptor through phosphorylation by mitogen-activated protein kinase.
text: The phosphorylation of human estrogen receptor (ER) serine residue 118 is crucial for the full activation of the ER activation function 1 (AF-1). This Ser118 is phosphorylated by mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) in vitro and in vivo upon treatment with epidermal growth factor (EGF) and insulin-like growth factor (IGF) in cells. Overexpression of MAPK kinase (MAPKK) or the guanine nucleotide binding protein Ras, which activates MAPK, enhances estrogen-induced and antiestrogen (tamoxifen)-induced transcriptional activity of wild-type ER, but not that of a mutant ER with an alanine in place of Ser118. Therefore, the activity of the amino-terminal AF-1 of the ER is modulated by the phosphorylation of Ser118 through the Ras-MAPK cascade of the growth factor signaling pathways.

title: Regulation of the antimicrobial response by NLR proteins.
text: Nucleotide-binding, oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) proteins constitute a crucial component of the innate immune system, playing a central role in the recognition and response to microbial infections. Dysregulation of NLR function has been implicated in both mouse and human models, leading to increased susceptibility to infection and the development of autoinflammatory diseases. Despite significant progress in understanding NLR function and interactions, many aspects of their mechanisms of sensing, downstream signaling pathways, and in vivo functions remain incompletely understood. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of key NLR family members, including their activation by diverse microorganisms, downstream effector functions, and interactions with other innate sensor protein families. Additionally, the role of NLR-mediated microbial sensing in the activation of the adaptive immune response, which collaborates in the antimicrobial defense, will be discussed.

title: Acetylcysteine for prevention of acute deterioration of renal function following elective coronary angiography and intervention: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
The study investigated the effectiveness of oral acetylcysteine in preventing deterioration in renal function in patients with moderate renal insufficiency undergoing elective coronary angiography. The study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at the Grantham Hospital in Hong Kong from May 2000 to December 2001.
Two hundred Chinese patients aged 68 years on average (6.5 years) with stable moderate renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <60 mL/min) were enrolled in the study. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either oral acetylcysteine (600 mg twice daily; n = 102) or matching placebo tablets (n = 98) on the day before and the day of angiography. All patients received a low-osmolality contrast agent.
The primary outcome measure was the occurrence of a more than 25% increase in serum creatinine level within 48 hours after contrast administration. Secondary outcome measures included changes in creatinine clearance and serum creatinine levels.
The results showed that 12 control patients (12%) and 4 acetylcysteine patients (4%) developed a more than 25% increase in serum creatinine level within 48 hours after contrast administration (relative risk, 0.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.10-0.96; P =.03). Serum creatinine was lower in the acetylcysteine group (1.22 mg/dL [107.8 micromol/L]; 95% CI, 1.11-1.33 mg/dL vs 1.38 mg/dL [122.9 micromol/L]; 95% CI, 1.27-1.49 mg/dL; P =.006) during the first 48 hours after angiography. Acetylcysteine treatment significantly increased creatinine clearance from 44.8 mL/min (0.75 mL/s) (95% CI, 42.7-47.6 mL/min) to 58.9 mL/min (0.98 mL/s) (95% CI, 55.6-62.3 mL/min) 2 days after the contrast administration (P<.001). The increase was not significant in the control group (from 42.1 to 44.1 mL/min [0.70 to 0.74 mL/s]; P =.15). The benefit of acetylcysteine was consistent among various patient subgroups and persistent for at least 7 days. There were no major treatment-related adverse events.
The study concluded that acetylcysteine protects patients with moderate chronic renal insufficiency from contrast-induced deterioration in renal function after coronary angiographic procedures, with minimal adverse effects and at a low cost.

title: DNA Methylation in the Human Cerebral Cortex Is Dynamically Regulated throughout the Life Span and Involves Differentiated Neurons
text: The role of DNA cytosine methylation, an epigenetic regulator of chromatin structure and function, in normal and pathological brain development and aging remains unclear. To investigate, we analyzed the DNA methylation status at 50 loci, encompassing genes related to central nervous system (CNS) growth and development, in temporal neocortex samples from 125 subjects spanning a range of ages from fetal development to old age. Two psychiatric disease cohorts, defined by chronic neurodegeneration (Alzheimer's) or lack thereof (schizophrenia), were included. Our findings revealed a robust and progressive increase in DNA methylation levels across the lifespan for 8 of the 50 loci, typically accompanied by decreasing levels of the corresponding mRNAs. Additionally, 16 loci exhibited a sharp rise in DNA methylation levels within the first few months or years after birth. Disease-associated changes were limited to 2 of the 50 loci in the Alzheimer's cohort, which appeared to reflect an acceleration of the age-related change in normal brain. Furthermore, methylation studies on sorted nuclei revealed bidirectional methylation events in cortical neurons during the transition from childhood to advanced age, as reflected by significant increases at 3 and a decrease at 1 of 10 loci. Finally, we found that the DNMT3a de novo DNA methyl-transferase was expressed across all ages, including a subset of neurons residing in layers III and V of the mature cortex. Taken together, our results demonstrate that DNA methylation is dynamically regulated in the human cerebral cortex throughout the lifespan, involves differentiated neurons, and affects a substantial portion of genes by an age-related increase.

title: Mulberry leaves (Morus alba L.) ameliorate obesity-induced hepatic lipogenesis, fibrosis, and oxidative stress in high-fat diet-fed mice
text: Obesity is intricately linked with a myriad of chronic diseases, including fatty liver, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and severe metabolic syndrome. The onset of obesity is characterized by metabolic impairment, which manifests as excessive lipid accumulation and fibrosis in hepatic tissue, as well as an increase in oxidative stress. To investigate the potential of mulberry leaf (Morus alba L.) extract (MLE) in mitigating obesity-induced oxidative stress, lipogenesis, and fibrosis in the liver, MLE was administered to high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice for 12 weeks. The results demonstrated that MLE treatment significantly ameliorated the expression of liver X receptor alpha (LXRα), which is involved in lipogenesis, and reduced the levels of hepatic fibrosis markers, such as α-smooth muscle actin. Moreover, MLE up-regulated the expression of lipolysis-associated markers, including lipoprotein lipase, in the HFD-fed mice. Additionally, MLE normalized the activities of antioxidant enzymes, including heme oxygenase-1 and glutathione peroxidase, and reduced the levels of 4-hydroxynonenal, a marker of oxidative stress, in the HFD-fed mice. The findings suggest that MLE has a beneficial impact on obesity-related fatty liver disease by modulating hepatic lipid metabolism, fibrosis, and antioxidant defense systems. The supplementation of MLE may serve as a potential therapeutic approach for obesity-related diseases, including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and the risk of hip fractures in elderly patients.
text: Recent animal studies have shown that 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) lipid-lowering drugs (statins) significantly increase bone formation, but it is unknown whether this effect translates to humans. To investigate whether statin use is associated with a reduced risk of hip fracture in older adults, we conducted a case-control study of 6110 Medicare-enrolled individuals aged 65 years or older. We found that use of statins in the 180 days or 3 years prior to hip fracture surgery was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hip fracture, even after controlling for various demographic and clinical factors. In contrast, use of nonstatin lipid-lowering agents was not associated with a reduction in hip fracture risk. Our findings support an association between statin use and reduced hip fracture risk, although controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

title: The quality of modern cross-sectional ecologic studies: a bibliometric review.
text:
Despite its limitations, the ecological study design is commonly used by epidemiologists. However, there is a lack of understanding on how well researchers address the challenges of this design in their studies. To address this gap, a bibliometric review was conducted to evaluate the characteristics, statistical methods, and reporting of results of modern cross-sectional ecological studies.
A search of six major epidemiology journals identified 125 cross-sectional ecological studies published since January 1, 2000, and these studies were assessed using standardized criteria. The results showed that a significant number of studies used unreliable methods or contained statistical oversights. For instance, 64% of studies that adjusted their outcomes for age or sex did so improperly, and 20% of regression models had potential issues related to statistical validity. Simple linear regression was the most common analytic approach used (31%). Moreover, many authors omitted important information when discussing the ecological nature of their study (31%), the choice of study design (58%), and the susceptibility of their research to the ecological fallacy (49%).
These findings suggest that there is a need for internationally recognized guidelines that standardize reporting on ecological studies. Additionally, more attention should be given to the relevant biostatistical literature to improve the quality of ecological research.

title: Efficacy of Beta1 Integrin and EGFR Targeting in Sphere-Forming Human Head and Neck Cancer Cells
text:
Resistance to radiation therapy remains a significant challenge in the treatment of cancer, including head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Recent studies have shown that targeting both β1 integrin and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) simultaneously has a higher radiosensitizing potential than monotherapy in most HNSCC models. However, the mechanisms underlying this resistance are not fully understood.
In this study, we investigated the efficacy of targeting β1 integrin and EGFR in combination with X-ray irradiation on the behavior of sphere-forming cells (SFC), which are thought to play a key role in therapy resistance and recurrence. We used HNSCC cell lines (UTSCC15, UTSCC5, Cal33, and SAS) and plated them for primary and secondary sphere formation under non-adhesive conditions, which are believed to enrich for SFC and their self-renewal capacity. Treatment involved inhibitory antibodies against β1 integrin (AIIB2) and EGFR (Cetuximab) as well as X-ray irradiation (2-6 Gy single doses). We also analyzed the expression of TIC markers, cell cycling, and DNA repair protein expression and phosphorylation using flow cytometry and Western blotting.
Our results showed that SAS cells had higher primary and secondary sphere forming capacity compared to other HNSCC cell lines, which was consistent with their higher tumor up-take rates. However, AIIB2 and Cetuximab administration had minimal cytotoxic and radiosensitizing effects on SFC. Interestingly, secondary SAS spheres showed enhanced radiosensitivity compared to primary spheres, despite showing no difference in basal sphere forming capacity and radiosensitivity. Additionally, we observed an increased accumulation of G0/G1 phase cells in secondary SAS spheres, but no significant differences in DNA double strand break repair.
Our findings suggest that sphere-forming conditions select for cells that are resistant to both anti-β1 integrin and anti-EGFR inhibitory antibodies. Furthermore, primary and secondary sphere formation appear to involve distinct survival strategies, independent of β1 integrin and EGFR. These results highlight the need for further research to better understand the mechanisms underlying SFC survival and enrichment, and to identify novel, druggable cancer targets in these cells.

title: Anxiety
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of routinely administered psychiatric questionnaires on the recognition, management, and outcome of psychiatric disorders in non-psychiatric settings.
Data Sources: Embase, Medline, PsycLIT, Cinahl, Cochrane Controlled Trials Register, and hand searches of key journals.
Methods: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials examining the administration and routine feedback of psychiatric screening and outcome questionnaires to clinicians in non-psychiatric settings. A narrative overview of key design features and endpoints, along with a random effects quantitative synthesis of comparable studies.
Main Outcome Measures: Recognition of psychiatric disorders after feedback of questionnaire results; interventions for psychiatric disorders; and outcome of psychiatric disorders.
Results: Nine randomized studies were identified that examined the use of common psychiatric instruments in primary care and general hospital settings. Studies compared the effect of the administration of these instruments followed by the feedback of the results to clinicians, with administration with no feedback. Meta-analytic pooling was possible for four of these studies (2457 participants), which measured the effect of feedback on the recognition of depressive disorders. Routine administration and feedback of scores for all patients (irrespective of score) did not increase the overall rate of recognition of mental disorders such as anxiety and depression (relative risk of detection of depression by clinician after feedback 0.95, 95% confidence interval 0.83 to 1.09). Two studies showed that routine administration followed by selective feedback for only high scorers increased the rate of recognition of depression (relative risk of detection of depression after feedback 2.64, 1.62 to 4.31). This increased recognition, however, did not translate into an increased rate of intervention. Overall, studies of routine administration of psychiatric measures did not show an effect on patient outcome.
Conclusions: The routine measurement of outcome is a costly exercise. Little evidence shows that it is of benefit in improving psychosocial outcomes of those with psychiatric disorder managed in non-psychiatric settings.

title: The challenges of overcoming antibiotic resistance: Plant extracts as potential sources of antimicrobial and resistance modifying agents
text: The issue of antibiotic resistance, which has limited the use of affordable and older antibiotics, has prompted the need for continued research and development of new antimicrobial compounds. Understanding the mechanisms of resistance is crucial in the creation of strategies to address this problem. Bacteria can acquire or develop intrinsic resistance to antibiotics through various mechanisms, including active efflux of drugs, alteration of target sites, and enzymatic degradation. Multi-drug resistance (MDR) pumps, which can recognize and expel a variety of structurally unrelated compounds from the bacterial cell and confer resistance to a wide range of antibiotics, have been identified in many gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens, including Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and more recently, mycobacteria. Additionally, some chemical compounds (called MDR inhibitors or resistance modifying agents) have been observed to modify the resistance phenotype in bacteria by working synergistically with antibiotics in vitro. These compounds have the potential to be combined with antibiotics in the treatment of drug-resistant infections, providing an alternative to overcoming the problem of resistance in bacteria. Crude extracts of medicinal plants stand out as a rich source of potential resistance modifying agents, with the African biosphere holding particular promise due to its diverse plant species.

title: The effect of N-acetylcysteine in the nucleus accumbens on neurotransmission and relapse to cocaine.
text:
Background: Relapse to cocaine seeking has been linked to low glutamate levels in the nucleus accumbens core (NAcore), which can potentiate synaptic glutamate transmission from the prefrontal cortex (PFC) afferents. Systemic N-acetylcysteine (NAC) has been shown to restore glutamate homeostasis, reduce relapse to cocaine seeking, and depotentiate PFC-NAcore synapses. This study aims to investigate the effects of NAC applied directly to the NAcore on relapse and neurotransmission in PFC-NAcore synapses, as well as the involvement of metabotropic glutamate receptors 2/3 (mGluR2/3) and 5 (mGluR5).
Methods: Rats were trained to self-administer cocaine for two weeks and received either intra-accumbens NAC or systemic NAC 30 or 120 minutes prior to reinstatement with a conditioned cue or a combined cue and cocaine injection. Postsynaptic currents were recorded using in vitro whole cell recordings in acute slices, and cystine and glutamate uptake was measured in primary glial cultures.
Results: NAC microinjection into the NAcore inhibited the reinstatement of cocaine seeking. In slices, a low concentration of NAC reduced the amplitude of evoked glutamatergic synaptic currents in the NAcore in an mGluR2/3-dependent manner, while high doses of NAC increased amplitude in an mGluR5-dependent manner. Both effects depended on NAC uptake through cysteine transporters and activity of the cysteine/glutamate exchanger. Finally, it was shown that blocking mGluR5 potentiated the inhibition of cocaine seeking by NAC.
Conclusions: The effect of NAC on relapse to cocaine seeking depends on the balance between stimulating mGluR2/3 and mGluR5 in the NAcore, and the efficacy of NAC can be improved by simultaneously inhibiting mGluR5.

title: A phospholipid transfer function of ER-mitochondria encounter structure revealed in vitro
text: As phospholipids are primarily synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondrial inner membranes, it is essential for cells to efficiently distribute specific phospholipids to various cellular membranes to maintain organelle-specific phospholipid compositions. Although the ER-mitochondria encounter structure (ERMES) has been proposed to facilitate phospholipid transfer between these organelles, its role in this process remains controversial and requires experimental verification. To address this issue, we developed a novel in vitro assay system using isolated yeast membrane fractions to monitor phospholipid exchange between the ER and mitochondria. Our findings revealed that phospholipid transport between these organelles depends on the integrity of the membranes, rather than energy sources such as ATP, GTP, or the membrane potential across the mitochondrial inner membrane. Additionally, we found that the ERMES component plays a crucial role in phosphatidylserine transport from the ER to mitochondria, but not in phosphatidylethanolamine transport from mitochondria to the ER. This in vitro assay system provides a valuable tool for investigating non-vesicular phospholipid transport between the ER and mitochondria.

title: An integrin β3–KRAS–RalB complex drives tumour stemness and resistance to EGFR inhibition
text:
Cancer cells with stem-like properties are highly aggressive and often resistant to drug treatment. We have discovered that the protein integrin αvβ3 serves as a marker for breast, lung, and pancreatic cancers that exhibit stem-like properties and are resistant to receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as erlotinib. This was observed in laboratory experiments using cancer cells and in mice bearing patient-derived tumor xenografts, as well as in clinical samples from lung cancer patients who had progressed on erlotinib.
Our findings reveal that αvβ3, when unliganded, recruits KRAS and RalB to the tumor cell plasma membrane, leading to the activation of TBK1 and NF-κB. In fact, αvβ3 expression and the resulting KRAS-RalB-NF-κB pathway are both necessary and sufficient for tumor initiation, independence from the extracellular matrix, self-renewal, and resistance to erlotinib.
Interestingly, we found that pharmacological targeting of this pathway with bortezomib can reverse both tumor stemness and erlotinib resistance. These findings not only identify αvβ3 as a marker/driver of carcinoma stemness but also provide a potential therapeutic strategy to sensitize such tumors to receptor tyrosine kinase inhibition.
In summary, our study reveals that integrin αvβ3 is a key player in the development and resistance of cancer stem cells, and targeting this pathway with bortezomib may provide a new therapeutic approach to overcome resistance to receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors in cancer treatment.

title: Gain of toxic Apolipoprotein E4 effects in Human iPSC-Derived Neurons Is Ameliorated by a Small-Molecule Structure Corrector
text: Efforts to develop drugs for Alzheimer's disease (AD) have shown promise in animal studies, yet have failed in human clinical trials, highlighting the need to investigate AD in human model systems. Using human neurons derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that express the apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) variant of the APOE gene, we investigated the effects of ApoE4 on AD pathology. Our findings revealed that ApoE4-expressing neurons exhibit higher levels of tau phosphorylation, unrelated to increased production of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides, and display GABAergic neuron degeneration. Interestingly, ApoE4 increased Aβ production in human neurons, but not in mouse neurons. We also found that converting ApoE4 to ApoE3 through gene editing rescued the detrimental phenotypes, indicating the specific effects of ApoE4. Notably, neurons lacking APOE exhibited similar behavior to those expressing ApoE3, and the introduction of ApoE4 expression recapitulated the pathological phenotypes, suggesting a gain of toxic effects from ApoE4. Finally, treatment of ApoE4-expressing neurons with a small-molecule structure corrector ameliorated the detrimental effects, demonstrating that correcting the pathogenic conformation of ApoE4 is a viable therapeutic approach for ApoE4-related AD.

title: LncRNA NEAT1/let-7a-5p axis regulates the cisplatin resistance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma by targeting Rsf-1 and modulating the Ras-MAPK pathway.
text: The long non-coding RNA nuclear paraspeckle assembly transcript 1 (NEAT1) was found to be upregulated in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and associated with oncogenic growth and drug resistance. However, the underlying mechanisms of NEAT1 in drug resistance remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the expressions of NEAT1, let-72-5p, and Rsf-1 mRNA in NPC cells and examined their effects on cell proliferation and cisplatin resistance. We also analyzed the protein levels of Ras, p-Raf1, Raf1, p-MEK1, MEK1, p-ERK1/2, and ERK1/2 using western blot analysis. Our results showed that NEAT1 was upregulated and let-7a-5p was downregulated in NPC tissues and cell lines, and inhibition of NEAT1 significantly repressed cisplatin resistance in NPC cells. We found that NEAT1 interacted with let-7a-5p and that NEAT1 reversed the inhibitory effect of let-7a-5p on cisplatin resistance in NPC cells. Additionally, NEAT1 knockdown inhibited the Ras-MAPK pathway in NPC cells and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. These findings suggest that the NEAT1/let-7a-5p axis regulates cisplatin resistance in NPC by targeting Rsf-1 and modulating the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway.

title: Antibacterial peptide microcin J25 inhibits transcription by binding within and obstructing the RNA polymerase secondary channel.
text: The antibacterial peptide microcin J25 (MccJ25) has been shown to inhibit transcription by bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP). Biochemical studies have revealed that this inhibition occurs at the level of NTP uptake or NTP binding by RNAP, while genetic studies have indicated that inhibition of transcription requires a significant determinant, consisting of over 50 amino acid residues, within the RNAP secondary channel (also known as the "NTP-uptake channel" or "pore"). Biophysical experiments have further revealed that inhibition of transcription involves the binding of MccJ25 within the RNAP secondary channel. Molecular modeling studies have additionally shown that binding of MccJ25 within the RNAP secondary channel obstructs the RNAP secondary channel, thereby inhibiting transcription. These findings suggest that MccJ25 acts as a "cork in a bottle" by binding within and obstructing the RNAP secondary channel, providing an attractive target for drug discovery.

title: Exploring and exploiting the systemic effects of deregulated replication licensing.
text: Maintaining the accurate transmission and proper functioning of genetic material is crucial for proper cellular development and overall wellbeing. The replication licensing machinery plays a vital role in ensuring that replication occurs once per cell cycle, and its regulation is tightly controlled to prevent re-replication, which can lead to genomic instability and the development of cancer. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms underlying deregulation of the replication licensing apparatus and its systemic effects, including its role in carcinogenesis and various genetic syndromes. Additionally, recent findings have revealed that the replication licensing factor Cdc6 acts as a global transcriptional regulator above a certain threshold, providing new avenues for research. The role of the putative replication licensing factor ChlR1/DDX11, mutated in the Warsaw Breakage Syndrome, in cancer is also discussed. Finally, we explore the potential therapeutic advantages of targeting replication licensing factors, particularly Cdc6, and the future perspectives in this area of research.

title: Regulatory principles of pluripotency: from the ground state up.
text: Pluripotency is the remarkable ability of a single cell to generate all the specialized cell types of an adult organism. This property can be maintained indefinitely through the derivation of self-renewing embryonic stem cells (ESCs), providing an invaluable platform for investigating cell fate decisions and disease. Recent advances have shown that manipulating specific signaling cues can reprogram ESCs into a uniform "ground state" of pluripotency, more closely resembling the pluripotent naive epiblast. In this discussion, we will explore the external and internal regulatory mechanisms that govern pluripotency and examine the emerging spectrum of pluripotent states.

title: Neonatal Mortality Levels for 193 Countries in 2009 with Trends since 1990: A Systematic Analysis of Progress, Projections, and Priorities
text:
Background:
Historically, childhood mortality has been the primary focus of research, with a particular emphasis on infant and under-five mortality rates. However, neonatal mortality (deaths within the first 28 days of life) has received relatively little attention, despite accounting for approximately 41% of all child deaths. To provide a more comprehensive understanding of progress in reducing child mortality, we developed annual estimates of neonatal mortality rates (NMRs) and neonatal deaths for 193 countries from 1990 to 2009, with forecasts for the future.
Methods and Findings:
We compiled a database of mortality rates in neonates and children (<5 years) from 3,551 country-years of data. Reliable civil registration data were available for 38 countries from 1990 to 2009, and a statistical model was developed to estimate NMRs for the remaining 155 countries, of which 17 had no national data. Country consultation was conducted to identify data inputs and review estimates. In 2009, an estimated 3.3 million babies died in the first month of life, compared to 4.6 million neonatal deaths in 1990. More than half of all neonatal deaths occurred in five countries (44% of global livebirths): India (27.8%, 19.6% of global livebirths), Nigeria (7.2%, 4.5%), Pakistan (6.9%, 4.0%), China (6.4%, 13.4%), and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (4.6%, 2.1%). Between 1990 and 2009, the global NMR declined by 28% from 33.2 deaths per 1,000 livebirths to 23.9. The proportion of child deaths that occur in the neonatal period increased in all regions of the world, and globally, neonatal deaths now account for 41% of all child deaths. While NMRs decreased in some regions, Africa's NMR only dropped by 17.6% (43.6 to 35.9).
Conclusions:
Neonatal mortality has declined in all world regions, although progress has been slowest in regions with high NMRs. To achieve the Millennium Development Goal 4 (two-thirds reduction in child mortality), global health programs must address neonatal deaths more effectively.

title: Neuroprotective Effects of Four Phenylethanoid Glycosides on H2O2-Induced Apoptosis on PC12 Cells via the Nrf2/ARE Pathway
text: Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) serves as a crucial transcription factor in protecting against oxidative stress and neurodegenerative disorders. Phenylethanoid glycosides (PhGs), including salidroside, acteoside, isoacteoside, and echinacoside, exhibit antioxidant and neuroprotective properties. This study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective effect and underlying molecular mechanism of PhGs. Our findings revealed that PhGs pre-treatment significantly suppressed hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂)-induced cytotoxicity in PC12 cells by promoting the nuclear translocation of Nrf2 and reversing the downregulated expression of heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1), NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1), glutamate cysteine ligase-catalytic subunit (GCLC), and glutamate-cysteine ligase modifier subunit (GCLM). Silencing Nrf2 or inhibiting HO-1 using zinc protoporphyrin (ZnPP) diminished the neuroprotective effect of PhGs. Our results suggest that PhGs may interact with the Keap1-activated Nrf2/ARE pathway, with the more glycoside-rich PhGs exhibiting enhanced effects.

title: Mortality risk attributable to high and low ambient temperature: a multicountry observational study
text:
Background:
While various studies have provided estimates of premature deaths attributable to either heat or cold in specific countries, a comprehensive assessment of the total mortality burden attributable to non-optimum ambient temperature across different climates remains unexplored. This study aimed to quantify the total mortality burden attributable to non-optimum ambient temperature and the relative contributions from heat and cold, as well as moderate and extreme temperatures, in a large sample of locations worldwide.
Methods:
We collected data for 384 locations in 12 countries (Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, Thailand, UK, and USA) and fitted a standard time-series Poisson model for each location, controlling for trends and day of the week. We estimated temperature-mortality associations using a distributed lag non-linear model with 21 days of lag and pooled them in a multivariate metaregression that included country indicators and temperature average and range. We calculated attributable deaths for heat and cold, defined as temperatures above and below the optimum temperature, which corresponded to the point of minimum mortality, as well as for moderate and extreme temperatures, defined using cutoffs at the 2·5th and 97·5th temperature percentiles.
Findings:
We analyzed 74,225,200 deaths in various periods between 1985 and 2012. In total, 7·71% (95% empirical CI 7·43-7·91) of mortality was attributable to non-optimum temperature in the selected countries within the study period, with substantial differences between countries, ranging from 3·37% (3·06 to 3·63) in Thailand to 11·00% (9·29 to 12·47) in China. The temperature percentile of minimum mortality varied from roughly the 60th percentile in tropical areas to about the 80-90th percentile in temperate regions. More temperature-attributable deaths were caused by cold (7·29%, 7·02-7·49) than by heat (0·42%, 0·39-0·44). Extreme cold and hot temperatures were responsible for 0·86% (0·84-0·87) of total mortality.
Interpretation:
Our findings suggest that most of the temperature-related mortality burden was attributable to the contribution of cold. The effect of days of extreme temperature was substantially less than that attributable to milder but non-optimum weather. These results have important implications for the planning of public-health interventions to minimize the health consequences of adverse temperatures and for predictions of future effects in climate-change scenarios. Funding: This study was funded by the UK Medical Research Council.

title: Survivin is not required for the endomitotic cell cycle of megakaryocytes.
text: Survivin, a component of the chromosome passenger complex, plays a crucial role in the alignment, separation, and cytokinesis of chromosomes. Although survivin is essential for the proliferation and survival of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, its role in the endomitosis of megakaryocytes remains debated. To investigate the necessity of survivin for polyploidization, we analyzed mice with a megakaryocyte-specific deletion of survivin. PF4-Cre/survivin(fl/fl) mice displayed normal platelet counts and megakaryocytes with comparable ploidy levels to control littermates. The CD41(+) cells within these animals showed minimal excision but increased annexin V staining, suggesting that survivin is necessary for the survival of megakaryocyte progenitors in vivo. Contrary to this, megakaryocytes isolated from survivin-deficient mice exhibited robust excision and a higher degree of polyploidization when cultured ex vivo. These findings demonstrate that survivin is essential for the survival of megakaryocyte progenitors, but is not required for the polyploidization of committed megakaryocytes.

title: β1 integrin mediates an alternative survival pathway in breast cancer cells resistant to lapatinib
text:
Introduction:
The overexpression of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) in approximately 20% of breast cancers has led to the widespread use of HER2-targeted therapies, such as trastuzumab (T) and lapatinib (L). However, despite the success of these drugs, their efficacy is limited in patients whose tumors demonstrate de novo or acquired resistance to treatment. The β1 integrin, which resides on the membrane of breast cancer cells, has been implicated in the progression of breast tumors by activating various elements of breast tumor progression, including proliferation and survival.
Methods:
To investigate the role of β1 integrin in L and LT resistance, we developed a panel of HER2-overexpressing cell lines resistant to L, T, and the potent LT combination through long-term exposure and validated these models in 3D culture. Parental and L/T/LT-resistant cells were subjected to HER2 and β1 integrin inhibitors in 3D and monitored for 12 days, followed by quantification of colony number. Parallel experiments were conducted where cells were either stained for Ki-67 and Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) or harvested for protein analysis by immunoblot. Results were subjected to statistical testing using analysis of variance and linear contrasts, followed by adjustment with the Sidak method.
Results:
Our findings reveal that in L and LT resistance, where phosphorylation of EGFR/HER1, HER2, and HER3 is strongly inhibited, downstream kinases, including focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and Src, are up-regulated. Blockade of β1 by the antibody AIIB2 abrogates this up-regulation and achieves significant growth inhibition of L and LT resistant cells in 3D, without dramatically affecting the parental cells. SiRNA against β1 as well as pharmacologic inhibition of FAK also achieve the same growth inhibitory effect. In contrast, trastuzumab-resistant cells, which retain high levels of phosphorylated EGFR/HER1, HER2, and HER3, are only modestly growth-inhibited by AIIB2.
Conclusions:
Our data suggest that HER2 activity, which is suppressed in resistance involving L but not T alone, dictates whether β1 mediates an alternative pathway driving resistance. Our findings justify clinical studies investigating the inhibition of β1 or its downstream signaling moieties as strategies to overcome acquired L and LT resistance.

title: Incidence and Trends of Sepsis in US Hospitals Using Clinical vs Claims Data, 2009-2014
text: The study aimed to estimate the national incidence of sepsis and trends in the US using detailed clinical data from electronic health records (EHRs) of diverse hospitals. The study included 409 academic, community, and federal hospitals and identified 173,690 sepsis cases among 2.9 million adults admitted in 2014. The incidence of sepsis was 6.0%, with 26,061 (15.0%) dying in the hospital and 10,731 (6.2%) being discharged to hospice. The study found that the incidence of sepsis using clinical criteria was stable from 2009-2014, while the incidence per claims increased. In-hospital mortality using clinical criteria declined, but there was no significant change in the combined outcome of death or discharge to hospice. In contrast, mortality using claims declined significantly, as did death or discharge to hospice. The study also found that clinical criteria were more sensitive in identifying sepsis than claims, with comparable positive predictive value. The findings suggest that EHR-based clinical data provide more objective estimates than claims-based data for sepsis surveillance.

title: Body-mass index and risk of 22 specific cancers: a population-based cohort study of 5·24 million UK adults
text: In this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between body mass index (BMI) and the risk of developing various types of cancer. We analyzed data from over 5 million individuals in the UK and found that BMI was associated with the risk of 17 out of 22 common cancers, with the strongest associations observed for cancers of the uterus, gallbladder, kidney, cervix, thyroid, and leukemia. We found that BMI was positively associated with liver, colon, ovarian, and postmenopausal breast cancers, but inversely associated with prostate and premenopausal breast cancer. The study also showed that assuming causality, approximately 41% of uterine and 10% or more of gallbladder, kidney, liver, and colon cancers could be attributable to excess weight. Overall, our findings suggest that BMI is a significant predictor of cancer risk and that population-level interventions to reduce BMI could have a substantial impact on cancer incidence.

title: Cryo-EM structure of a herpesvirus capsid at 3.1 Å
text: Human herpesviruses are among the most expansive and intricate viruses at a molecular level, as evidenced by their structural and genetic composition. Utilizing cutting-edge cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) techniques with an optimized image reconstruction strategy, we have successfully determined the capsid structure of herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) at an unprecedented resolution of 3.1 angstroms. This structure is composed of approximately 3000 proteins organized into three distinct types of hexons (central, peripentonal, and edge), pentons, and triplexes. The major capsid protein, VP5, is present in both hexons and pentons, while VP26 proteins are exclusively found in hexons. Triplexes, on the other hand, are composed of VP23 and VP19C proteins. These proteins serve as core organizers, forming extensive intermolecular networks through multiple disulfide bonds (approximately 1500 in total) and noncovalent interactions. These interactions not only contribute to the stability and assembly of the capsid but also give rise to 46 distinct conformers that coalesce into a massive quasisymmetric shell, showcasing the remarkable structural and functional complexity of HSV.

title: Asymptotic and resampling strategies for assessing and comparing indirect effects in multiple mediator models.
text: In the behavioral sciences, hypotheses involving mediation are prevalent. Mediation occurs when a predictor influences a dependent variable indirectly through at least one intervening variable, or mediator. Despite the need for methods to assess mediation involving multiple simultaneous mediators, little attention has been given to this topic in the methodological literature. We aim to provide an overview of simple and multiple mediation and explore three approaches to investigate indirect processes. Additionally, we will discuss methods for contrasting two or more mediators within a single model. To illustrate these concepts, we present an example of assessing and contrasting potential mediators of the relationship between the helpfulness of socialization agents and job satisfaction. To facilitate the use of these methods in applications, we also provide SAS and SPSS macros, as well as Mplus and LISREL syntax.

title: Distinct Metabolomic Signatures Are Associated with Longevity in Humans
text: Alterations in metabolism have been shown to impact lifespan in experimental models, but there is a lack of data on this topic in humans. To investigate, we used liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry to quantify 217 plasma metabolites and examine their relationship to longevity in a large cohort of men and women followed for up to 20 years. Our findings reveal that higher concentrations of the citric acid cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and the bile acid, taurocholate, are associated with lower odds of reaching 80 years of age. In contrast, higher concentrations of isocitrate, but not taurocholate, are linked to worse cardiovascular health at baseline and an increased risk of future cardiovascular disease and death. Notably, none of the metabolites identified were associated with cancer risk. These findings suggest that some, but not all, metabolic pathways involved in human longevity are linked to the risk of common causes of death.

title: The expanding problem of adipose depot remodeling and postnatal adipocyte progenitor recruitment.
text: The increasing prevalence of obesity and related metabolic disorders has heightened the need to comprehend all aspects of adipose tissue biology. This involves understanding the functions of adipocytes, how adipose tissue expands in obesity, and how enlarged adipose tissues in adults impact physiology. Recent research has highlighted the significance of de novo adipocyte differentiation in adipose tissue expansion in both humans and animals. We will discuss recent efforts to identify adipose precursor populations that contribute to the physiological postnatal recruitment of white, brown, and beige adipocytes in mice, and provide an overview of the complex adipose tissue development process in vivo.

title: Clonal competition in BcrAbl-driven leukemia: how transplantations can accelerate clonal conversion
text:
BACKGROUND: Clonal competition in cancer refers to the process where the offspring of a cancer cell clone either outcompete or succumb to other competing clones due to differences in their functional characteristics, often resulting from subsequent mutations. Although the patterns of these mutations have been well-studied in many tumors, the dynamic process of clonal selection remains underappreciated.
METHODS: To investigate the dynamics of clonal competition in BcrAbl-induced leukemia, we used a γ-retroviral vector library encoding the oncogene in conjunction with genetic barcodes. We analyzed the growth dynamics of transduced cells at the clonal level both in vitro and in vivo in transplanted mice.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed moderate changes in clonal abundances in vitro, but surprisingly, we observed monoclonal leukemias in 6/30 mice after transplantation, caused by only two distinct BcrAbl clones. To elucidate the reasons behind this observation, we developed a mathematical model of hematopoietic tissue maintenance, which suggested that a differential engraftment capacity of these two dominant clones could explain our findings. These conclusions were further supported by additional transplantation experiments and increased BcrAbl transcript levels in both clones.
CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that clonal competition is not a strictly mutation-based process, but rather highly dependent on selection mechanisms in a given environmental context.

title: Open Babel: An open chemical toolbox
text:
Background:
The conversion of chemical structures between different formats is a recurring challenge in computational modeling. While standard interchange formats, such as Chemical Markup Language (CML), and de facto standards, such as the SMILES format, exist, the need to interconvert formats persists due to the diversity of application areas in chemistry, the differences in data stored by various formats (e.g., 0D versus 3D), and the competition between software vendors.
Results:
We present Open Babel, an open-source chemical toolbox that supports multiple formats for chemical data interconversion. Version 2.3 of Open Babel can convert over 110 formats, requiring a comprehensive library of cheminformatics algorithms to handle a wide range of chemical and molecular data, including partial charge assignment, aromaticity detection, bond order perception, and canonicalization. We provide a detailed description of the implementation of Open Babel, highlight key advancements in the 2.3 release, and outline various uses of the software, including scientific research and software development.
Conclusions:
Open Babel offers a solution to the proliferation of multiple chemical file formats and provides a range of useful utilities, such as conformer searching, 2D depiction, filtering, batch conversion, and substructure and similarity searching. For developers, it can be used as a programming library to handle chemical data in areas such as organic chemistry, drug design, materials science, and computational chemistry. Open Babel is freely available under an open-source license from <http://openbabel.org>.

title: Young adolescents' nutrition assessment on computer (YANA-C)
text:
Objective: To evaluate the relative validity and acceptability of the computerized 24-hour recall tool, Young Adolescent's Nutrition Assessment on Computer (YANA-C), in assessing the dietary intakes of young adolescents.
Design: The study compared the food and nutrient intakes assessed using YANA-C with those obtained through food records (study 1) and 24-hour dietary recall interviews (study 2).
Main Outcome Measures: The study evaluated the intakes of various food groups (fruits, fruit juice, vegetables, potatoes, bread, cereals, milk, cheese, other milk products, soft drinks, diet soft drinks, sugar/sweets, pastry/cookies, savory snacks, butter/sauces, eggs, fish, meat) and nutrients (energy, carbohydrates, protein, fat, fiber, calcium, vitamin C, and iron).
Subjects and Setting: A total of 237 pupils (ages 11-14) from two primary and four secondary schools in Belgium-Flanders participated in the study.
