The concentration of Ang-2 was inversely correlated with RH-PAT (r = -0.38, P < 0.0001) and positively correlated with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels (r = 0.57, P < 0.0001) and the degree of organ failure (sequential organ failure assessment score) (r = 0.58, P < 0.0001). The correlation between Ang-2 and RH-PAT persisted after controlling for sepsis severity. In a longitudinal mixed-effects model, recovery of RH-PAT over time was associated with a decline in Ang-2 levels.
Discussion:
Our findings suggest that Ang-2 levels are elevated in proportion to sepsis severity and are inversely correlated with endothelial NO bioavailability. These data suggest that impaired endothelial NO bioavailability may contribute to increased endothelial cell release of Ang-2, endothelial activation, and capillary leak in sepsis. Agents that increase endothelial NO bioavailability or inhibit WPB exocytosis and/or Ang-2 activity may have therapeutic potential in sepsis.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study demonstrates that Ang-2 levels are elevated in sepsis and inversely correlated with endothelial NO bioavailability. These findings suggest that impaired endothelial NO bioavailability may play a key role in the pathogenesis of sepsis-induced endothelial activation and capillary leak. Further investigation into the mechanisms underlying endothelial NO dysfunction in sepsis may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for this life-threatening condition.

title: Ecologic versus individual-level sources of bias in ecologic estimates of contextual health effects.
text: Several authors have attempted to justify ecological (aggregate) studies by arguing that their goal is to estimate contextual or group-level effects rather than individual-level effects. However, critics point out that these estimates are often used as estimates of individual effects, despite disclaimers. A more subtle issue is that ecological estimates of contextual effects can be biased due to the distribution of individual effects in the ecological data. This bias is plausible and common in studies of ecosocial factors and health outcomes, as social context is not randomly assigned to analysis units (administrative regions). Ecological data only provide marginal information on the joint distribution of individually defined confounders and outcomes, which means they cannot identify either contextual or individual-level effects. While ecological studies can still be useful with appropriate caveats, their limitations are better addressed by multilevel study designs, which collect and analyze both individual-level and group-level data. However, these studies may still face challenges related to inappropriate aggregation and changes in covariate distributions over time.

title: Left–right asymmetry in the vertebrate embryo: from early information to higher-level integration
text: Although vertebrates appear to be bilaterally symmetrical on the surface, there are numerous internal asymmetries in the arrangement and positioning of organs during embryonic development. These asymmetries are established through complex epigenetic and genetic pathways during embryogenesis. Recent studies in various model organisms have made significant progress in elucidating the mechanisms by which this laterality information is generated and transmitted to large regions of the embryo. Both commonalities and differences are emerging in the strategies employed by different vertebrates in left-right axis specification. Additionally, recent findings offer intriguing links between the establishment of left-right asymmetries and the symmetrical elongation of the anterior-posterior axis.

title: Obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cancer: the insulin and IGF connection.
text: Epidemiological research has shown a strong correlation between obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and an increased risk of cancer and cancer-related mortality. Insulin resistance, high insulin levels, elevated IGF levels, steroid and peptide hormone imbalances, and inflammation are believed to contribute to this association. Medications used to treat T2D, such as metformin and exogenous insulin, may also impact cancer risk and mortality. Innovative therapies targeting the insulin and IGF1 systems are being developed for use in cancer treatment.

title: Non-coding RNAs: Functions and applications in endocrine-related cancer.
text:
A substantial portion of the human genome is transcribed into non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), which have challenged the traditional central dogma of molecular biology. The non-coding transcriptome plays a crucial role in regulating gene expression through transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms. Recent research has shown that many ncRNAs are dysregulated in cancer, and there is a growing interest in using this knowledge to develop cancer biomarkers and anti-cancer drugs. In particular, endocrine-related cancers have relatively low survival rates, making the discovery of ncRNAs with clinical implications in these cancers a pressing need.
In this review, we aim to summarize the current state of knowledge on ncRNAs in endocrine-related cancers affecting both sexes. We focus on recent studies that have shed light on the roles and clinical implications of long ncRNAs, PIWI-interacting RNAs, tRNA- and Y RNA-derived ncRNAs, and small nucleolar RNAs in cancer. We also discuss the challenges and future directions in ncRNA research, including the potential of these unconventional transcripts as diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets. While significant progress has been made in the field, further work is necessary to realize the full potential of ncRNAs in cancer diagnosis and treatment.

title: NMR structural and kinetic characterization of a homeodomain diffusing and hopping on nonspecific DNA.
text: Protein-DNA interactions are inherently dynamic and involve both diffusion of the protein along the DNA and hopping of the protein from one DNA molecule or segment to another. Understanding how gene regulatory proteins interact nonspecifically with DNA in terms of both structure and dynamics is challenging due to the rapidly exchanging states of the experimental observables. To characterize the structural and kinetic aspects of the interaction of the HoxD9 homeodomain with a nonspecific, 24-bp DNA duplex, we employed a range of NMR spectroscopic techniques, including relaxation analysis, paramagnetic relaxation enhancement, and residual dipolar couplings. Our data revealed that HoxD9 binds to nonspecific DNA with the same binding mode and orientation as observed in the specific complex. However, the mobility of arginine side chains contacting the DNA was found to be higher in the nonspecific complex compared to the specific one. Additionally, we analyzed the kinetics of intermolecular translocation between two different nonspecific DNA molecules and found that direct transfer from one complex to another occurs without passing through the intermediate of free protein at high DNA concentrations, such as those present in vivo. This mechanism allows for more effective sampling of available DNA sites as the protein jumps from one segment to another, potentially accelerating the target search in vivo.

title: MHC Haplotype Matching for Unrelated Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation
text: Currently, the selection of unrelated donors for hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is based on matching for the alleles of each human leukocyte antigen (HLA) locus within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). However, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a significant and potentially life-threatening complication even after HLA-identical unrelated HCT. The MHC contains over 400 genes, but the total number of transplantation antigens is still unknown. To identify genes that influence transplantation outcome, linkage disequilibrium (LD)-mapping approaches could be used if the extended MHC haplotypes of the unrelated donor and recipient could be defined.

title: The SIR2/3/4 complex and SIR2 alone promote longevity in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by two different mechanisms. Genes Dev 13
text: The SIR genes in yeast play a crucial role in determining lifespan. Our findings indicate that the Sir proteins' role in life span regulation is unrelated to their involvement in non-homologous end joining. The short lifespan of sir3 or sir4 mutants is caused by the simultaneous expression of a and alpha mating-type information, which leads to increased rDNA recombination and likely results in the production of extrachromosomal rDNA circles. Similarly, the short lifespan of sir2 mutants is due to a direct failure to repress recombination generated by the Fob1p-mediated replication block in the rDNA. Sir2p is a limiting factor in promoting yeast longevity, and increasing the gene dosage extends the life span in wild-type cells. These findings suggest a possible role for the conserved SIR2 protein in mammalian aging.

title: Meta-analysis identifies common variants associated with body mass index in East Asians
text: In a recent study, researchers conducted a meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in east Asian populations to identify genetic loci associated with body mass index (BMI) and obesity. The study analyzed approximately 2.4 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 27,715 individuals and identified ten BMI-associated loci at a genome-wide significance level of P < 5.0 × 10(-8). Of these, seven loci (FTO, SEC16B, MC4R, GIPR-QPCTL, ADCY3-DNAJC27, BDNF, and MAP2K5) had previously been identified in GWAS of European populations, while three novel loci were found in or near the CDKAL1, PCSK1, and GP2 genes. In addition, three other loci nearly reached the genome-wide significance threshold, including two previously identified loci in the GNPDA2 and TFAP2B genes and a newly identified signal near PAX6. These findings may provide insight into novel pathways involved in obesity and highlight the importance of conducting genetic studies in non-European populations.

title: Phosphorylation of histone H3(T118) alters nucleosome dynamics and remodeling
text:
Nucleosomes, the basic building blocks of chromatin, play a crucial role in regulating various DNA processes such as transcription, replication, and repair. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of histone proteins within nucleosomes can modulate these processes. Among these modifications, phosphorylation of histone H3 at position T118 (H3(T118ph)) has been implicated in the regulation of transcription and DNA repair.
To investigate the influence of H3(T118ph) on nucleosome dynamics, we expressed and purified the modified histone and analyzed its effects on DNA-histone binding, nucleosome mobility, and DNA accessibility near the dyad region. Our results show that H3(T118ph) reduces DNA-histone binding by approximately 2 kcal/mol, increases nucleosome mobility by 28-fold, and increases DNA accessibility near the dyad region by 6-fold. Furthermore, we found that H3(T118ph) enhances the rate of hMSH2-hMSH6 nucleosome disassembly and enables nucleosome disassembly by the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler. These findings suggest that H3(T118ph) may directly enhance and potentially reprogram chromatin remodeling reactions.

title: Mechanosignaling through YAP and TAZ drives fibroblast activation and fibrosis.
text: Pathological fibrosis is fueled by a self-reinforcing cycle involving the fibrotic extracellular matrix (ECM) and fibroblast activation. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), transcriptional effectors of the Hippo pathway, as key regulators of fibroblast activation and ECM synthesis. YAP and TAZ are specifically expressed in fibrotic lung tissue, with pronounced nuclear expression of TAZ in spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells. In culture, both YAP and TAZ accumulate in the nucleus of fibroblasts grown on stiff matrices, but not on compliant matrices. Knockdown of YAP and TAZ inhibits fibroblast functions, including matrix synthesis, contraction, and proliferation, and this effect is specific to stiff matrices. We also demonstrate that the profibrotic effects of YAP and TAZ are, in part, mediated by their transcriptional target plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), which is regulated by matrix stiffness independent of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling. Immortalized fibroblasts conditionally expressing active YAP or TAZ mutant proteins can overcome soft matrix limitations on growth and promote fibrosis when transferred to the murine lung, highlighting the ability of fibroblast YAP/TAZ activation to drive a profibrotic response in vivo. Together, these findings identify YAP and TAZ as key regulators of the matrix-driven feedback loop that perpetuates and amplifies fibrosis.

title: Control of cellular cholesterol efflux by the nuclear oxysterol receptor LXR alpha.
text: LXR alpha is a nuclear receptor that has been previously shown to regulate the metabolic conversion of cholesterol to bile acids. In this study, we investigate the role of LXR alpha in the control of cellular cholesterol efflux. We demonstrate that retroviral expression of LXR alpha in NIH 3T3 fibroblasts or RAW264.7 macrophages, or treatment of these cells with oxysterol ligands of LXR, leads to a 7- to 30-fold induction of the mRNA encoding the putative cholesterol/phospholipid transporter ATP-binding cassette (ABC)A1. In contrast, the induction of ABCA1 mRNA in response to oxysterols is attenuated in cells that constitutively express dominant-negative forms of LXR alpha or LXR beta that lack the AF2 transcriptional activation domain. We further demonstrate that expression of LXR alpha in NIH 3T3 fibroblasts and/or treatment of these cells with oxysterols is sufficient to stimulate cholesterol efflux to extracellular apolipoprotein AI. The ability of oxysterol ligands of LXR to stimulate efflux is significantly reduced in Tangier fibroblasts, which carry a loss of function mutation in the ABCA1 gene. These findings suggest that cellular cholesterol efflux is, at least in part, controlled at the level of transcription by a nuclear receptor-signaling pathway. Specifically, activation of LXRs by oxysterols in response to cellular sterol loading leads to the induction of the ABCA1 transporter and the stimulation of lipid efflux to extracellular acceptors. These findings have important implications for our understanding of mammalian cholesterol homeostasis and suggest new opportunities for pharmacological regulation of cellular lipid metabolism.

title: Circadian regulation of intracellular G-protein signalling mediates intercellular synchrony and rhythmicity in the suprachiasmatic nucleus
text: In the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), the body's internal clock, thousands of cellular clocks exhibit synchronous oscillations, which are coordinated through a poorly understood mechanism of cell-cell communication. Here, we uncover that the amount of RGS16 (regulator of G protein signalling 16), a protein that inhibits Gαi, increases at a specific circadian time, allowing for time-dependent activation of intracellular cyclic AMP signalling in the SCN. Gene ablation of Rgs16 leads to a decrease in the circadian production of cAMP and consequently lengthens the circadian period of behavioral rhythm. The temporally precise regulation of the cAMP signal by clock-controlled RGS16 is crucial for the dorsomedial SCN to maintain its normal phase relationship with the ventrolateral SCN. Therefore, RGS16-dependent temporal regulation of intracellular G protein signalling coordinates the intercellular synchrony of SCN pacemaker neurons and establishes the 24-hour rhythm in behavior.

title: MDC1 collaborates with TopBP1 in DNA replication checkpoint control
text: Human TopBP1 plays a crucial role in regulating the DNA replication checkpoint. In this study, we identified MDC1, a key checkpoint protein involved in the cellular response to DNA double-strand breaks, as a TopBP1-associated protein. The interaction between TopBP1 and MDC1 is mediated by the fifth BRCT domain of TopBP1 and the Ser-Asp-Thr (SDT) repeats of MDC1. Furthermore, we demonstrated that TopBP1 accumulation at stalled replication forks is enhanced by the H2AX/MDC1 signaling cascade. Additionally, MDC1 is essential for ATR-dependent Chk1 activation in response to replication stress. Our findings suggest that MDC1 plays a critical role in multiple aspects of the cellular DNA damage response and the DNA replication checkpoint.

title: Deregulated DNA polymerase β strengthens ionizing radiation-induced nucleotidic and chromosomal instabilities
text:
DNA polymerase β (Pol β) is an error-prone enzyme that has been found to be overexpressed in various human tumors. By using two different recombinant CHO cell lines, we discovered that cells overexpressing Pol β are significantly more sensitive to ionizing radiation (IR) treatments, leading to increased apoptosis. Additionally, the surviving cells displayed a hypermutator phenotype, which could be attributed to different pathways involving Pol β, such as:
1. Enhanced incorporation of mutagenic dGTP analog, 8-oxo-dGTP, one of the most abundant purine-derived nucleotides exposed to γ-irradiation.
2. Induction of IR-induced DNA breaks and accumulation of chromosome aberrations.
Our findings suggest that alteration of Pol β expression in irradiated cells strengthens both cell death and genetic changes associated with a malignant phenotype, providing new insights into the cellular response to radiation and its carcinogenic consequences.

title: Chromosome 7 gain and DNA hypermethylation at the HOXA10 locus are associated with expression of a stem cell related HOX-signature in glioblastoma
text:
Background: HOX genes are a family of developmental genes that are typically not expressed in the developing forebrain or normal brain. However, recent studies have shown that aberrant expression of a HOX gene-dominated stem-cell signature in glioblastoma is associated with increased resistance to chemo-radiotherapy and sustained proliferation of glioma initiating cells. In this study, we aim to elucidate the epigenetic and genetic alterations that contribute to the expression of this signature in glioblastoma.
Results: Our findings reveal prominent hypermethylation of the HOXA locus at 7p15.2 in glioblastoma compared to non-tumoral brain. This hypermethylation is associated with a gain of chromosome 7, a hallmark of glioblastoma, and may function as a rescue mechanism by preventing undue gene expression due to tumor-driven gene dosage. We identify an alternative promoter in the HOXA10 gene that escapes hypermethylation in HOX-high glioblastoma. An additive effect of gene copy gain at 7p15.2 and DNA methylation at key regulatory CpGs in HOXA10 is significantly associated with HOX-signature expression. Furthermore, we observe concordance between methylation status and the presence of active or inactive chromatin marks in glioblastoma-derived spheres that are HOX-high or HOX-low, respectively.
Conclusions: Based on our findings, we propose that co-evolution and interaction between gene copy gain, which is associated with a gain of chromosome 7, and additional epigenetic alterations are key mechanisms that trigger a coordinated, but inappropriate, HOX transcriptional program in glioblastoma.

title: Probing the phenomenon of trained immunity in invertebrates during a transgenerational study, using brine shrimp Artemia as a model system
text: The study on the invertebrate Artemia revealed that its innate immune system exhibits adaptive features, termed trained immunity. However, the mechanisms behind this phenomenon and the memory characteristics of the innate immune system remain unclear. To investigate, we conducted a transgenerational study on Artemia, examining the presence or absence of enduring memory against homologous and heterologous antigens (Vibrio spp.) in the progenies of ancestors exposed to the bacteria. Our findings showed that the immune system of Artemia exhibits memory and partial discrimination, as evidenced by increased resistance to a homologous bacterial strain for three successive generations. This increased resistance was associated with elevated levels of heat shock protein 70 (hsp70) and high mobility group box 1 (hmgb1) signaling molecules, as well as alterations in the expression of key innate immunity-related genes. Additionally, we observed stochastic patterns in the acetylation and methylation levels of histones H4 and H3K4me3, respectively, in the progenies of ancestors challenged with the bacteria. Our results suggest that the innate immune responses in invertebrates have the capacity to be trained, and epigenetic reprogramming of selected innate immune effectors is likely to play a central role in the mechanisms leading to trained immunity.

title: Using Structural Information to Change the Phosphotransfer Specificity of a Two-Component Chemotaxis Signalling Complex
text: Two-component signal transduction pathways, comprising histidine protein kinases (HPKs) and their response regulators (RRs), are widely used by bacteria to respond to environmental challenges. These pathways are highly specific, with over 150 different pathways identified in some bacteria, each with tightly controlled phosphotransfer reactions to prevent unwanted crosstalk. One of the best understood two-component signaling pathways is the chemotaxis pathway, and our study presents the 1.40 Å crystal structure of the histidine-containing phosphotransfer domain of the chemotaxis HPK, CheA(3), in complex with its cognate RR, CheY(6). We identified a methionine finger on CheY(6) that nestles in a hydrophobic pocket in CheA(3) as crucial for the interaction, and found that this methionine occurs only in the cognate RRs of CheA(3), CheY(6), and CheB(2). Site-directed mutagenesis of this methionine, along with two adjacent residues, abolished binding, as shown by surface plasmon resonance studies, and phosphotransfer from CheA(3)-P to CheY(6). Interestingly, introducing this methionine and an adjacent alanine residue into non-cognate CheYs led to dramatic changes in their specificity, allowing protein interaction and rapid phosphotransfer from CheA(3)-P. Our structure-based approach identified specificity determinants for the CheA-CheY interaction, enabling successful reengineering of phosphotransfer signaling. In summary, our findings provide valuable insights into how cells control specificity in one of the most ubiquitous signaling pathways in biology, two-component signal transduction.

title: Combination varenicline and bupropion SR for tobacco-dependence treatment in cigarette smokers: a randomized trial.
text: The study investigated the effectiveness and safety of combining varenicline and bupropion sustained-release (SR) in treating tobacco dependence, compared to varenicline monotherapy. The study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial conducted at three midwestern clinical research sites between October 2009 and April 2013. A total of 506 adult cigarette smokers were randomly assigned to receive either varenicline and bupropion SR, varenicline and placebo, or placebo. The primary outcome measures were abstinence rates at 12 weeks, defined as prolonged (no smoking from 2 weeks after the target quit date) abstinence and 7-day point-prevalence (no smoking past 7 days) abstinence. Secondary outcomes were abstinence rates at 26 and 52 weeks. The results showed that the combination of varenicline and bupropion SR resulted in higher abstinence rates at 12 and 26 weeks compared to varenicline monotherapy, but not at 52 weeks. Specifically, 53.0% of the combination therapy group achieved prolonged smoking abstinence and 56.2% achieved 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence at 12 weeks, compared to 43.2% and 48.6% in varenicline monotherapy. However, neither outcome was significantly different at 52 weeks. The study also found that participants receiving combination therapy reported more anxiety and depressive symptoms compared to those receiving varenicline monotherapy. Overall, the study suggests that combining varenicline and bupropion SR may be more effective in treating tobacco dependence than varenicline monotherapy, but further research is needed to confirm these findings.

title: Effect of a C/EBP gene replacement on mitochondrial biogenesis in fat cells.
text: CCAAT/enhancer-binding proteins, C/EBPalpha and C/EBPbeta, play a crucial role in the differentiation and maturation of fat cells. Earlier studies demonstrated that replacing C/EBPalpha with C/EBPbeta in mice, resulting in the beta/beta genotype, impedes lipid accumulation in white adipose tissue (WAT). In this investigation, beta/beta mice exhibited increased energy expenditure and a longer lifespan compared to their control counterparts, likely due to enhanced WAT energy metabolism. The WAT of beta/beta mice was found to be rich in metabolically active, thermogenic mitochondria, which are capable of burning energy. The beta/beta allele exerted its effect by elevating the expression of the G protein alpha stimulatory subunit (Galphas) in WAT. Overexpression of Galphas in fat-laden 3T3-L1 cells was observed to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis, similar to the effect seen in the WAT of beta/beta mice, and significantly reduce the stored lipid pool.

title: Variable breakpoints target PAX5 in patients with dicentric chromosomes: a model for the basis of unbalanced translocations in cancer.
text: The search for genes involved in unstable chromosomal abnormalities has been challenging due to the variable breakpoints of these rearrangements. However, using the example of dicentric chromosomes in B cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia, we have identified specific gene loci that are targeted through various mechanisms. By using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and molecular copy number counting, we were able to delineate the breakpoints and clone the fusion genes. Our analysis revealed five fusion gene partners with PAX5: LOC392027 (7p12.1), SLCO1B3 (12p12), ASXL1 (20q11.1), KIF3B (20q11.21), and C20orf112 (20q11.1). All of these fusion proteins contained the DNA-binding paired domain of PAX5. Quantitative PCR confirmed that both deletion and fusion events led to underexpression of PAX5, which in turn affected the expression of its target genes, including EBF1, ALDH1A1, ATP9A, and FLT3. Additionally, we found that the homologous PAX5 allele was deleted or mutated in all cases, further supporting the key role of PAX5 in cancer pathogenesis. Our findings suggest that specific gene loci may be targeted by heterogeneous translocation breakpoints in human cancer, and this approach may be applicable to the identification of cancer genes in solid tumors, where unbalanced chromosomal rearrangements are more common and fewer genes have been identified. This strategy may also reveal that similar mechanisms operate in cancer pathogenesis in general.

title: Copyright � 1996, American Society for Microbiology Endotoxin-Induced Enhancement of Glucose Influx into
text: Hypoglycemia is one of the most harmful metabolic disorders caused by endotoxemia. In animal studies using lipopolysaccharide (LPS), there is a significant increase in glucose consumption in organs rich in macrophages. However, the direct effect of LPS on macrophage glucose uptake has not been fully understood. To investigate this, we conducted a study using murine peritoneal exudate macrophages in culture. Our results show that LPS stimulation accelerates glucose uptake by two to threefold, reaching a plateau after 20 minutes and remaining at the maximum as long as LPS is present. Using northern (RNA) blot analysis with cDNA probes for five known isoforms of glucose transporter (GLUT), we found that macrophage responses to LPS are supported by a rapid and sustained glucose influx via the GLUT1 isoform. The amount of GLUT1 mRNA was increased by LPS stimulation, suggesting that this is a key factor in the development of systemic hypoglycemia during prolonged endotoxemia.

title: Factors associated with American Board of Medical Specialties member board certification among US medical school graduates.
text: In this study, the authors investigated the factors associated with American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) member board certification among US medical school graduates. The study included a national cohort of 1997-2000 graduates, grouped by specialty choice at graduation and followed up through March 2, 2009. The authors found that graduates in all specialty categories who achieved high scores on the US Medical Licensing Examination Step 2 Clinical Knowledge were more likely to be board certified. However, the odds of board certification varied by specialty category, with the lowest odds for emergency medicine and the highest odds for radiology. Additionally, the authors found that graduates who identified as underrepresented racial/ethnic minorities were less likely to be board certified, except in the pediatrics category. The authors also found that each $50,000 unit increase in debt was associated with a decrease in the likelihood of board certification among graduates choosing obstetrics/gynecology, while a higher likelihood of board certification was observed among graduates choosing family medicine. These findings suggest that demographic and educational factors are important predictors of ABMS member board certification among US medical school graduates, and may have implications for medical education and residency programs.

title: Body-mass index and mortality in Korean men and women.
text:
BACKGROUND: Obesity has been linked to various health risks, but the role of body weight as a predictor of death remains controversial. To investigate this association, we conducted a 12-year prospective cohort study of 1,213,829 Koreans aged 30-95 years. We examined 82,372 deaths from any cause and 48,731 deaths from specific diseases (including 29,123 from cancer, 16,426 from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and 3362 from respiratory disease) in relation to body mass index (BMI).
METHODS: We analyzed the association between BMI and the risk of death in both sexes. The average baseline BMI was 23.2, and we found a J-shaped association between BMI and the risk of death from any cause, regardless of smoking history. The lowest risk of death from any cause was observed among individuals with a BMI of 23.0-24.9. In contrast, the risk of death from respiratory causes was higher among individuals with a lower BMI, while the risk of death from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or cancer was higher among those with a higher BMI. The relative risk of death associated with BMI decreased with increasing age.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that both underweight and overweight individuals had higher rates of death compared to those of normal weight. The association between BMI and death varied by cause of death and was influenced by age, sex, and smoking history. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining a healthy weight throughout life to reduce the risk of death from various causes.

title: Human iPSC-based modeling of late-onset disease via progerin-induced aging.
text: Reprogramming somatic cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) effectively "rewinds" their identity to an embryonic stage, posing a challenge for modeling late-onset disorders. In this study, we explore a strategy to introduce aging-related features in human iPSC-derived cell lines and apply it to the modeling of Parkinson's disease (PD). We achieve this by expressing progerin, a truncated form of lamin A associated with premature aging, in iPSC-derived fibroblasts and neurons. This leads to the manifestation of multiple aging-related markers and characteristics, including dopamine-specific phenotypes such as neuromelanin accumulation. By inducing aging in PD iPSC-derived dopamine neurons, we uncover disease features that require both aging and genetic susceptibility, including pronounced dendrite degeneration, progressive loss of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression, and enlarged mitochondria or Lewy-body-precursor inclusions. Our findings suggest that progerin-induced aging can be leveraged to reveal late-onset age-related disease features in iPSC-based disease models.

title: SNAREs — engines for membrane fusion
text: Since the late 1980s, SNARE proteins have been identified as crucial components of protein complexes that facilitate membrane fusion. Despite their genetic diversity, SNARE proteins share a conserved mechanism that enables them to adapt to various fusion reactions, including those involved in cell growth, membrane repair, cytokinesis, and synaptic transmission. As research continues to uncover the intricacies of these nanomachines, a fascinating picture is emerging of their remarkable capabilities.

title: Maintaining the norm: T-cell homeostasis
text: For many years, immunologists have been fascinated by the persistence of naive and memory T cells. Despite significant progress in understanding the factors that influence T-cell survival and homeostasis, the underlying mechanisms that regulate these subsets have remained largely elusive. Recently, however, it has become clear that the homeostasis of both naive and memory T-cell populations is remarkably dynamic and tightly regulated by internal stimuli, including cytokines and self-peptide–MHC ligands for the T-cell receptor. These homeostatic mechanisms may have a profound impact on the ability of the T-cell pool to respond to both foreign and self-antigens.

title: Cell type of origin influences the molecular and functional properties of mouse induced pluripotent stem cells
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been generated from various somatic cell populations through the introduction of specific factors. However, it remains unclear whether iPSCs derived from different cell types are similarly molecular and functionally characterized. In this study, we investigated the transcriptional and epigenetic profiles of iPSCs derived from mouse fibroblasts, hematopoietic cells, and myogenic cells. Our results show that these iPSCs exhibit distinct patterns of gene expression and epigenetic marks, which are influenced by their cellular origin. Furthermore, we found that the in vitro differentiation potential of iPSCs into embryoid bodies and various hematopoietic cell types is also influenced by their cellular origin. Interestingly, continuous passaging of iPSCs largely abolishes these differences, suggesting that early-passage iPSCs retain a transient epigenetic memory of their somatic cell origins. These findings have important implications for the use of iPSCs in disease modeling and potential therapeutic applications, as they may allow for the enhancement of differentiation into desired cell lineages.

title: Spatiotemporal control of mitosis by the conserved spindle matrix protein Megator
text: A hypothetical spindle matrix has been proposed to regulate chromosome movement, but its existence and function remain uncertain. In this study, we demonstrate that Megator (Mtor), the Drosophila counterpart of the human nuclear pore complex protein translocated promoter region (Tpr), and the spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) protein Mad2 form a conserved complex that localizes to a nuclear-derived spindle matrix in living cells. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching experiments reveal that Mtor is retained around spindle microtubules, displaying distinct dynamic properties. Mtor/Tpr promotes the recruitment of Mad2 and Mps1 but not Mad1 to unattached kinetochores (KTs), ensuring normal mitotic duration and SAC response. At anaphase, Mtor plays a role in spindle elongation, influencing chromosome movement. We propose that Mtor/Tpr functions as a spatial regulator of the SAC, ensuring efficient recruitment of Mad2 to unattached KTs at the onset of mitosis and proper spindle maturation. Additionally, enrichment of Mad2 in a spindle matrix helps confine the action of a diffusible "wait anaphase" signal to the vicinity of the spindle, promoting proper chromosome movement.

title: Randomized trial of folic acid supplementation and serum homocysteine levels.
text:
BACKGROUND: Lowering serum homocysteine levels through folic acid supplementation has been shown to reduce mortality from ischemic heart disease. While it is known that maximum homocysteine reduction occurs at a dosage of 1 mg/d, the effect of lower doses, relevant to food fortification, is unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a randomized controlled trial in which 151 patients with ischemic heart disease were assigned to receive 1 of 5 dosages of folic acid (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, or 1.0 mg/d) or placebo. Fasting blood samples for serum homocysteine and serum folate analysis were taken at baseline, after 3 months of supplementation, and 3 months after folic acid discontinuation.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed a dose-dependent decrease in median serum homocysteine levels with increasing folic acid dosage, with the maximum reduction observed at 0.8 mg of folic acid per day (2.7 micromol/L, 23%). The response to folic acid was found to be greater in individuals with higher initial serum homocysteine levels. Additionally, serum folate levels increased linearly with increasing folic acid dosage (5.5 nmol/L for every 0.1 mg of folic acid). However, within-person fluctuations in serum homocysteine levels over time were found to be large in the placebo group, indicating that monitoring the reduction in an individual is impractical.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that a dosage of folic acid of 0.8 mg/d is necessary to achieve the maximum reduction in serum homocysteine levels across the range of homocysteine levels in the population. Current US food fortification levels will only achieve a small proportion of the achievable homocysteine reduction.

title: Adherens junctions in Drosophila retinal morphogenesis.
text: Adherens junctions, comprised of classic cadherins and other core molecular components, play a crucial role in animal morphogenesis. Although the importance of cadherins in development is widely acknowledged, the mechanisms that regulate adherens junction function during morphogenesis are still the subject of ongoing research. Adherens junctions are involved in the formation of simple cell patterns, as well as more complex cell shape changes and movements that depend on the dynamic regulation of adherens junctions.

title: Multiple roles of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in skeletal development, growth, and repair.
text:
Chapter Summary: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) in Skeletal Morphogenesis
This chapter explores the crucial roles of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) in the development of skeletal tissues. Research has shown that VEGF regulates osteoclastic differentiation, migration, and activity, making it a central coordinator of the entire process. VEGF is essential for osteoclastic activity during both the formation of the primary ossification center and later stages of bone growth. Additionally, studies have identified VEGF as a critical factor for the survival of chondrocytes. Various factors that regulate bone formation, such as Prostaglandins E1 and E2, BMP-4, BMP-6, BMP-7, FGF-2, TGF-β, endothelin-1, IGF-1, and vitamin D3, can induce VEGF expression in osteoblasts through multiple signaling pathways.
The similarity between the embryonic bone development and the repair of fractured bones, combined with the finding that VEGF is expressed at sites of bone fracture, suggests that VEGF plays a role in bone repair as it does in bone development. Bone fractures can heal in two distinct ways, similar to the two ways of forming bone during embryonic development, with stabilized fractures healing through intramembranous ossification and unstable fractures undergoing endochondral ossification.
Future research directions in this field may include investigating the specific mechanisms by which VEGF regulates osteoclastic activity and chondrocyte survival, as well as exploring the potential therapeutic applications of VEGF in bone repair and regeneration. Despite the significant progress that has been made in understanding the roles of VEGF in skeletal morphogenesis, there are still challenges to be addressed, such as the complex interplay of signaling pathways involved in VEGF expression and the need for further studies to fully elucidate the mechanisms underlying bone repair and regeneration.

title: Effectiveness of thigh-length graduated compression stockings to reduce the risk of deep vein thrombosis after stroke (CLOTS trial 1): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial
text:
Background: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism are common complications after stroke. While graduated compression stockings (GCS) have been shown to reduce the risk of DVT in small trials of patients undergoing surgery, their effectiveness in stroke patients is uncertain. National stroke guidelines have extrapolated from these trials and recommend the use of GCS in stroke patients, despite a lack of sufficient evidence. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of thigh-length GCS in reducing DVT after stroke.
Methods: This outcome-blinded, randomized controlled trial enrolled 2518 patients who were admitted to hospital within one week of an acute stroke and were immobile. Patients were randomly assigned to either routine care plus thigh-length GCS (n=1256) or routine care plus avoidance of GCS (n=1262). A technician who was blinded to treatment allocation performed compression Doppler ultrasound on both legs at days 7-10 and, when practical, again at 25-30 days after enrollment. The primary outcome was the occurrence of symptomatic or asymptomatic DVT in the popliteal or femoral veins. Analyses were conducted by intention to treat.
Findings: All patients were included in the analyses. The primary outcome occurred in 126 (10.0%) patients allocated to thigh-length GCS and in 133 (10.5%) allocated to avoid GCS, resulting in a non-significant absolute reduction in risk of 0.5% (95% CI -1.9% to 2.9%). Skin breaks, ulcers, blisters, and skin necrosis were significantly more common in patients allocated to GCS than in those allocated to avoid their use (64 [5%] vs 16 [1%]; odds ratio 4.18, 95% CI 2.40-7.27).
Interpretation: These findings do not support the use of thigh-length GCS in patients admitted to hospital with acute stroke. National guidelines for stroke may need to be revised based on these results. Funding: Medical Research Council (UK), Chief Scientist Office of Scottish Government, Chest Heart and Stroke Scotland, Tyco Healthcare (Covidien) USA, and UK Stroke Research Network.

title: Streptococcus pneumoniae early response genes to human lung epithelial cells
text:
Background: Streptococcus pneumoniae infection begins with colonization of the host respiratory tract, where the bacteria interact with respiratory tract epithelial cells. To investigate the genes involved in the early stage of interaction with host epithelial cells, we used TIGR (JCVI) microarray technology to study the transcriptional responses of an encapsulated pathogenic pneumococcal strain TIGR4 upon exposure to human lung epithelial cells A549 for 0.5 and 1 hour time periods.
Findings: Our analysis revealed different transcriptional profiles at the two incubation time points, with most genes showing down-regulation at 0.5 hours and up-regulation at 1 hour. Specifically, genes involved in ribonucleotide biosynthesis were down-regulated at both time points, while genes related to cell envelope, energy metabolism, transport, and protein synthesis were mostly up-regulated at 1 hour. Additionally, we compared these profiles to the transcriptomes of a TIGR4-derived strain in response to human macrophages for the same time periods. We found a set of genes that exhibited similar expression changes upon exposure to both types of host cells, including bgaA (SP0648) and nanA (SP1693), as well as uncharacterized gene clusters such as SP1677-SP1680 and SP1688-SP1690.
Conclusion: These findings suggest that at the early stage of interaction with host epithelial cells, a complex gene regulation and expression change occur in bacteria. Some of these genes may play an essential role during pathogen-host interactions and for the establishment of infection.

title: Proteomic identification of a novel isoform of collapsin response mediator protein-2 in spinal nerves peripheral to dorsal root ganglia.
text: In this study, we employed a proteomic approach to investigate the polarity of primary afferent fibers in the spinal cord. We used lumbar spinal nerve segments, both central and peripheral to the dorsal root ganglion (DRG), from 5-week-old Wistar rats and subjected them to large-scale two-dimensional electrophoresis (2-DE) at a pH of 5-6. A total of approximately 800 protein spots were detected in the central and peripheral fractions, and one of the unique spots in the peripheral fraction with a molecular weight (MW) of 60 kDa and isoelectric point (pI) of 5.6 was identified as an isoform of collapsin response mediator protein-2 (CRMP-2) through matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) and Western blotting with anti-CRMP-2 antibodies that recognize residues 1-17 and 486-528. Notably, this novel spot was only detected in the peripheral fraction, but not in the central fraction, DRG, or other regions of the brain, and was therefore named periCRMP-2. In contrast, the C-terminal fragment of CRMP-2 was not detected in periCRMP-2 by MS analyses. Furthermore, our results showed that expression of periCRMP-2 decreased following sciatic nerve injury. These findings suggest that periCRMP-2 is a C-terminal truncated isoform that is specifically polarized in the peripheral side of spinal nerves and may play a role in nerve degeneration and regeneration.

title: Empirical statistical estimates for sequence similarity searches
text: The FASTA package of sequence comparison programs has been updated to provide more accurate statistical estimates for local sequence similarity scores with gaps. These estimates are derived from the distribution of similarity scores of unrelated sequences and corrected for the expected effect of library sequence length. This approach allows for accurate estimates to be calculated for both FASTA and Smith-Waterman similarity scores for protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and protein/translated-DNA comparisons. The accuracy of the statistical estimates is evaluated for 54 protein families using FASTA and Smith-Waterman scores. Probability estimates calculated from the distribution of similarity scores are generally conservative, and probabilities calculated using the Altschul-Gish lambda, kappa, and eta parameters are also found to be accurate. The performance of several alternative methods for correcting similarity scores for library-sequence length is evaluated using 54 protein superfamilies from the PIR39 database and 110 protein families from the Prosite/SwissProt rel. 34 database. The results show that both regression-scaled and Altschul-Gish scaled scores perform significantly better than unscaled Smith-Waterman or FASTA similarity scores. When the Prosite/SwissProt test set is used, regression-scaled scores perform slightly better, while when the PIR database is used, Altschul-Gish scaled scores perform best. Therefore, length-corrected similarity scores improve the sensitivity of database searches. Statistical parameters derived from the distribution of similarity scores from the vast number of unrelated sequences encountered in a database search provide accurate estimates of statistical significance that can be used to infer sequence homology.

title: Steroid hormone signalling links reproduction to lifespan in dietary-restricted Caenorhabditis elegans.
text: Dietary restriction (DR) has been shown to increase healthspan and longevity in various species, including primates. However, it is often accompanied by impaired reproductive function. The relationship between signals associated with the reproductive system and DR-mediated lifespan extension has not been fully elucidated. In this study, we investigate the role of cytochrome P450 DAF-9/CYP450 and the steroid hormone Δ(7)-dafachronic acid (DA) in Caenorhabditis elegans subjected to DR. Our findings demonstrate that DA signalling through the non-canonical nuclear hormone receptor NHR-8/NHR and the nutrient-responsive kinase let-363/mTOR is essential for DR-mediated longevity in C. elegans. Moreover, we show that steroid signalling affects germline plasticity in response to nutrient deprivation and this is required to achieve lifespan extension. These data highlight the central role of let-363/mTOR in integrating signals derived from nutrients and steroid hormones in mediating the relationship between germline physiology and lifespan in response to DR.

title: Regulation and effects of hypothalamic galanin: relation to dietary fat, alcohol ingestion, circulating lipids and energy homeostasis.
text: Galanin (GAL) is known to stimulate feeding behavior, differentiating it from other feeding stimulants such as neuropeptide Y and agouti-related protein. Unlike these peptides, GAL in the hypothalamus is relatively unresponsive to food deprivation and changes in corticosterone, glucose utilization, dietary carbohydrate, and leptin. This suggests that GAL is not essential under conditions of food scarcity or low-energy, high-carbohydrate diets. Contrary to this, recent findings indicate that GAL in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) functions in close relation to dietary fat and alcohol. Specifically, it mediates adaptive functions that allow animals to cope with conditions of positive energy balance involving excess consumption of these nutrients. GAL in the PVN is stimulated by a high-fat diet and alcohol, rising after a fat-rich meal or alcohol consumption and increasing food and alcohol consumption when centrally injected. Moreover, it produces a stronger feeding response in rats maintained on a fat-rich diet, promoting alcohol intake. These findings support the existence of non-homeostatic, positive feedback circuits between GAL and both dietary fat and alcohol, contributing to large meal sizes, over-consumption of alcohol, and obesity associated with fat-rich foods.

title: Evidence-based interventions for improvement of maternal and child nutrition: what can be done and at what cost?
text: According to recent research, maternal undernutrition is responsible for approximately 800,000 neonatal deaths annually, with stunting, wasting, and micronutrient deficiencies contributing to nearly 3.1 million child deaths each year. Since the publication of The Lancet Series on Maternal and Child Undernutrition in 2008, progress has been made through the implementation of various interventions at scale, and the evidence for their effectiveness has grown. An updated analysis of interventions to address undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in women and children was conducted, using standard methods to assess emerging new evidence for delivery platforms. The study found that if populations have access to ten evidence-based nutrition interventions at 90% coverage, the number of deaths in children younger than 5 years can be reduced by 15%. Additionally, improving access to iodised salt can alleviate iodine deficiency and improve health outcomes. The estimated total additional annual cost involved for scaling up access to these ten direct nutrition interventions in the 34 focus countries is approximately Int$9.6 billion per year. Investing in nutrition-specific interventions that reach poor segments of the population at greatest risk, in conjunction with nutrition-sensitive approaches such as women's empowerment, agriculture, food systems, education, employment, social protection, and safety nets, can greatly accelerate progress in countries with the highest burden of maternal and child undernutrition and mortality.

title: FGF regulates TGF-β signaling and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition via control of let-7 miRNA expression.
text: Maintaining normal endothelial function is crucial for various aspects of blood vessel health, but the regulatory mechanisms underlying this process are not well understood. Our study reveals that disrupting baseline fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling to the endothelium leads to a significant decrease in let-7 microRNA levels, which, in turn, enhances expression of transforming growth factor (TGF)-β ligands and receptors and activates TGF-β signaling, ultimately resulting in endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (Endo-MT). We also found that Endo-MT plays a pivotal role in neointima formation in a murine transplant arteriopathy model and in rejection of human transplant lesions. The decline in endothelial FGF signaling is attributed to the emergence of an FGF resistance state characterized by inflammation-induced reduction in FGF signaling components and their expression. These findings establish FGF signaling as a critical factor in maintaining endothelial homeostasis and highlight an unexpected role of Endo-MT in vascular disease.

title: Nuclear Receptors, RXR, and the Big Bang
text: The isolation and analysis of genes encoding receptors for steroids, retinoids, vitamin D, and thyroid hormone revealed a conserved template for nuclear hormone receptors. This discovery led to the identification of numerous related proteins, termed orphan receptors. Characterization of these orphan receptors, particularly the retinoid X receptor (RXR), positioned nuclear receptors at the center of the "Big Bang" of molecular endocrinology. This Review provides a personal perspective on nuclear receptors and explores their integrated and coordinated signaling networks, which are essential for multicellular life, highlighting the RXR heterodimer and its associated ligands and transcriptional mechanism.

title: A genome-wide short hairpin RNA screening of jurkat T-cells for human proteins contributing to productive HIV-1 replication.
text: Short interfering RNAs (siRNAs) have been employed to hinder HIV-1 replication. However, the persistent inhibition of HIV-1 replication through RNA interference has been hindered by a high mutation rate when viral sequences are targeted and by cytotoxicity when cellular genes are knocked down. To identify cellular proteins that contribute to HIV-1 replication that can be chronically silenced without significant cytotoxicity, we utilized a shRNA library that targets 54,509 human transcripts. We employed this library to select a comprehensive population of Jurkat T-cell clones, each expressing a single discrete shRNA. The Jurkat clones were then infected with HIV-1. Clones that survived viral infection represent moieties silenced for a human mRNA needed for virus replication, but whose chronic knockdown did not cause cytotoxicity. Overall, 252 individual Jurkat mRNAs were identified. Twenty-two of these mRNAs were secondarily verified for their contributions to HIV-1 replication. Five mRNAs, NRF1, STXBP2, NCOA3, PRDM2, and EXOSC5, were studied for their effect on steps of the HIV-1 life cycle. Our findings are compared to results from other investigators who used siRNA-based screenings in HeLa or 293T cells.

title: UNR facilitates the interaction of MLE with the lncRNA roX2 during Drosophila dosage compensation.
text: Dosage compensation is a regulatory mechanism that adjusts the expression of genes on the X chromosome between males (XY) and females (XX). In Drosophila, this process relies on non-coding RNAs and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), whose functions are not yet fully understood. Our study reveals that the Drosophila RBP UNR plays a crucial role in directing the male-specific-lethal complex to the X chromosome by facilitating the interaction of two essential subunits: the RNA helicase MLE and the long non-coding RNA roX2.

title: BMP/SMAD1 signaling sets a threshold for the left/right pathway in lateral plate mesoderm and limits availability of SMAD4.
text:
Bistability in developmental pathways refers to the generation of binary outputs from graded or noisy inputs. In the context of vertebrate embryonic development, bistability plays a crucial role in the specification of the left/right (LR) axis. The expression of transforming growth factor beta (TGFbeta) member NODAL in the left lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) is a bistable process, controlled by feed-forward and feedback loops. We have found that bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)/SMAD1 signaling sets a repressive threshold in the LPM, which is essential for the integrity of LR signaling.
Conditional deletion of Smad1 in the LPM led to precocious and bilateral pathway activation, indicating that the mutant LPM is sensitive to noisy input from the LR system. In vitro, BMP signaling inhibited NODAL pathway activation and formation of its downstream SMAD2/4-FOXH1 transcriptional complex. Interestingly, activity was restored by overexpression of SMAD4, and in embryos, elevated SMAD4 in the right LPM robustly activated LR gene expression, an effect that was reversed by superactivated BMP signaling.
Our findings suggest that BMP/SMAD1 signaling sets a bilateral, repressive threshold for NODAL-dependent Nodal activation in LPM, limiting the availability of SMAD4. This repressive threshold is essential for the bistable output of the LR system. In summary, bistability in developmental pathways refers to the generation of binary outputs from graded or noisy inputs, and is a critical aspect of LR axis specification in vertebrate embryonic development. The repressive threshold set by BMP/SMAD1 signaling in the LPM is essential for maintaining the bistable output of the LR system.

title: Human Macrophages Infected with a High Burden of ESAT-6-Expressing M. tuberculosis Undergo Caspase-1- and Cathepsin B-Independent Necrosis
text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infects lung macrophages, manipulating the host cells to create an environment conducive to its own replication and spread. The role of host cell death in Mtb infection is controversial, as the bacteria can both prevent apoptosis and induce necrosis. To investigate the mechanisms of cell death, we examined the role of the NLRP3 inflammasome in Mtb-infected macrophages. We found that Mtb infection at a high multiplicity of infection (MOI) leads to enhanced release of IL-1β, while a low MOI does not. Infected macrophages were analyzed for cell viability, and we found that infection at an MOI of 10, but not 1, led to extensive DNA fragmentation, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, loss of plasma membrane integrity, and HMGB1 release over two days. While we observed plasma membrane permeabilization and IL-1β release from infected cells, the cell death induced by Mtb was not dependent on caspase-1 or cathepsin B. Instead, it was found to be dependent on mycobacterial expression of the ESAT-6 protein. Our findings suggest that as the number of Mtb bacilli inside the human macrophage reaches a threshold, ESAT-6-dependent necrosis occurs, leading to caspase-1 activation.

title: Differentiation of Human Induced-Pluripotent Stem Cells into Smooth-Muscle Cells: Two Novel Protocols
text: Conventional methods for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into smooth muscle cells (SMCs) often result in inefficient and inconsistent outcomes, with a lack of specific SMC phenotypes (i.e., contractile or synthetic SMCs). To address this limitation, we present two novel hiPSC-SMC differentiation protocols that yield SMCs with predominantly contractile or synthetic phenotypes. Flow cytometry analysis of smooth muscle actin (SMA) expression revealed that approximately 45% of the cells obtained with each protocol exhibited an SMC phenotype, and the populations could be purified to ~95% via metabolic selection. Additionally, assessments of cellular mRNA and/or protein levels showed that SMA, myosin heavy chain II, collagen 1, calponin, transgelin, connexin 43, and vimentin expression in the SMCs obtained via the Contractile SMC protocol and in SMCs differentiated via a traditional protocol were similar, while SMCs produced via the Synthetic SMC protocol expressed lower levels of calponin, higher levels of collagen 1, and higher levels of connexin 43. Furthermore, functional assessments revealed that the two SMC populations exhibited distinct differences in response to carbachol treatment, with Contractile SMCs exhibiting a more extensive decline in two-dimensional surface area (to 12% of the original size) and Synthetic SMCs exhibiting greater cell migration and proliferation. These findings demonstrate that our novel differentiation protocols can efficiently generate SMCs from hiPSCs with specific phenotypes.

title: Conserved Histone Variant H2A.Z Protects Euchromatin from the Ectopic Spread of Silent Heterochromatin
text: The presence of boundary elements appears to hinder the spread of heterochromatin, yet these sites do not fully account for the preservation of adjacent euchromatin. Histone variant H2A.Z (Htz1 in yeast) replaces conventional H2A in many nucleosomes, and microarray analysis has revealed that HTZ1-activated genes are clustered near telomeres. Interestingly, the reduced expression of most of these genes in htz1Delta cells was found to be reversed by the deletion of SIR2 (sir2Delta), suggesting that H2A.Z antagonizes telomeric silencing. Other HTZ1-activated genes are located near the silent HMR mating-type locus, and their requirement for Htz1 can be bypassed by sir2Delta or by a deletion encompassing the silencing nucleation sites in HMR. In htz1Delta cells, Sir2 and Sir3 spread into flanking euchromatic regions, leading to changes in histone H4 acetylation and H3 4-methylation that are indicative of ectopic heterochromatin formation. Notably, Htz1 is enriched in these euchromatic regions and acts synergistically with a boundary element to prevent the spread of heterochromatin. These findings suggest that euchromatin and heterochromatin each contain components that antagonize switching to the opposite chromatin state.

title: COMMD proteins, a novel family of structural and functional homologs of MURR1.
text: MURR1 is a multifunctional protein that inhibits nuclear factor kappaB (NF-κB), a transcription factor with diverse regulatory functions in innate and adaptive immunity, apoptosis, cell cycle control, and oncogenesis. In this study, we report the identification of a novel family of proteins homologous to MURR1. These proteins, designated as COMMD or COMM domain-containing proteins, are characterized by the presence of a conserved and unique motif termed the COMM (copper metabolism gene MURR1) domain, which mediates protein-protein interactions. Similar to MURR1, several members of this family have been found to associate with and inhibit NF-κB. The COMMD proteins are highly conserved across multicellular eukaryotes, defining a novel family of structural and functional homologs of MURR1. The prototypical member of this family, MURR1/COMMD1, suppresses NF-κB activity by a novel mechanism involving chromatin interaction, distinct from the classical nuclear localization and cognate motif binding mechanisms.

title: Occurrence of chromosome 9 and p53 alterations in multifocal dysplasia and carcinoma in situ of human urinary bladder
text: To investigate the genetic changes in flat urothelial lesions, including carcinoma in situ (CIS) and moderate dysplasias (DII), we analyzed chromosomal regions frequently involved in bladder cancer using dual color fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) analyses. We studied 33 CIS and 16 DII from 21 patients and found nearly identical deletion frequencies on chromosomes 9 and 17 for CIS (86% and 84%, respectively) and DII (75% and 53%, respectively). A high correlation was observed between the results of FISH and LOH analyses. p53 mutations were detected in 12 of 15 patients (72% in CIS and 67% in DII). In three of 16 patients with multifocal tumors, oligoclonal lesions were identified by LOH analyses, supported by sequencing of p53, which revealed two different p53 deletions in two cases. Our findings suggest that chromosome 9 deletions cannot be used as a marker for papillary growth, as they are found in both types of flat lesions of the urothelium. The similar distribution and lower amount of genetic changes in DII suggest that DII may be a precursor lesion of CIS.

title: Fresh meat and further processing characteristics of ham muscles from finishing pigs fed ractopamine hydrochloride.
text:
Ractopamine hydrochloride (RAC) has consistently shown an advantage in improving carcass cutting yields in finishing pigs, and it remains a common feed additive in US finishing pig diets. However, there is limited information on its effect on further processing characteristics. Some studies have reported that RAC-fed pigs have higher ultimate pH in their muscles, which could potentially lead to better protein interaction and improved textural properties in further processed hams. To investigate this, an experiment was conducted to determine if RAC-fed pigs yielded hams with higher ultimate pH, and if so, whether this advantage improved the textural properties and water retention of further processed hams.
Two hundred hams from barrows and gilts were selected based on their body weight, and were either fed RAC or a control diet. The hams were then fabricated into 5 separate pieces to determine cutting yields, and 6 muscles were evaluated for ultimate pH. The hams were then processed to make cured and smoked hams. The results showed that RAC increased cutting yields of the whole ham, inside, outside, and knuckle by 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4%, respectively, when expressed as a percentage of chilled side weight (P < 0.0001). Additionally, the ultimate pH of the rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, and semitendinosus muscles were found to be 0.06 pH units higher (P < 0.05) in RAC-fed pigs compared to control pigs. No significant differences were detected in binding strengths or protein fat-free values between RAC-fed and control hams.
Overall, the study found that RAC increased cutting yields, total weight of cured hams, and ultimate muscle pH. These findings suggest that RAC can be fed to pigs to achieve desired growth characteristics and cutting yields without affecting further processed ham characteristics.

title: Translocated LPS Might Cause Endotoxin Tolerance in Circulating Monocytes of Cystic Fibrosis Patients
text:
Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is an inherited, pleiotropic disease caused by genetic abnormalities in the gene that codes for a chloride channel. The lungs of CF patients are chronically infected with various pathogens, but bacteremia (the presence of bacteria in the bloodstream) is rare in this condition. However, CF patients exhibit a unique phenomenon known as endotoxin tolerance (ET), where their circulating monocytes show a significant reduction in their inflammatory response to bacterial stimuli. Despite previous studies on this phenomenon, the underlying cause of ET in CF patients remains unknown.
In this study, we investigated the possibility that microbial/endotoxin translocation from a localized infection in the lungs to the bloodstream may play a role in inducing ET in CF patients. We analyzed the plasma of fourteen CF patients and found high levels of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) compared to healthy volunteers and patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). In vitro experiments using monocytes from healthy controls showed that endotoxin concentrations found in CF plasma were sufficient to induce an ET phenotype. Importantly, we failed to detect any bacterial DNA in the plasma of CF patients, suggesting that the endotoxin present in their bloodstream is derived from the lungs.
Our findings suggest that soluble endotoxin in the bloodstream of CF patients causes endotoxin tolerance in their circulating monocytes, which may contribute to the chronic inflammation and lung damage characteristic of CF. These results provide new insights into the pathogenesis of CF and may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies to target endotoxin tolerance in CF patients.

title: Effect of mammographic screening from age 40 years on breast cancer mortality in the UK Age trial at 17 years' follow-up: a randomised controlled trial.
text: The UK Age trial, which compared the effects of age-specific mammographic screening on breast cancer mortality, has been followed up for 17 years. The trial found that there was no significant difference in mortality between the groups after 10 years of follow-up, but there was a significant reduction in breast cancer mortality in the intervention group (women aged 40-49 years who received annual mammography screening) in the first 10 years after diagnosis. However, this reduction was not sustained beyond the first decade. The overall breast cancer incidence during the 17-year follow-up was similar between the intervention group and the control group. These findings support an early reduction in mortality from breast cancer with annual mammography screening in women aged 40-49 years, but further data are needed to fully understand the long-term effects. The study was funded by the National Institute for Health Research Health Technology Assessment programme and the American Cancer Society, with past funding from the Medical Research Council, Cancer Research UK, the UK Department of Health, and the US National Cancer Institute.

title: Concordance, disease progression, and heritability of coeliac disease in Italian twins.
text:
Background and Aims:
The aim of this study was to investigate the genetic and environmental factors contributing to the development of coeliac disease (CD) using a twin design. Specifically, we sought to determine the concordance rate of CD among monozygotic (MZ) and dizygotic (DZ) twin pairs, and to estimate the heritability of CD using an additive genetic, common, and unshared environmental (ACE) model.
Methods:
We recruited 23 MZ and 50 DZ twin pairs from the Italian Twin Registry, of which at least one member had CD. Zygosity was determined using DNA fingerprinting, and HLA-DQ and DR alleles were genotyped. CD status was ascertained through antiendomysial, anti-human tissue transglutaminase antibodies, and bowel biopsy.
Results:
Our results showed a significantly higher concordance rate of CD among MZ twin pairs (83.3% probandwise and 71.4% pairwise) compared to DZ twin pairs (16.7% probandwise and 9.1% pairwise). The concordance rate was not affected by sex or HLA genotype of the co-twin. Being MZ was significantly associated with the occurrence of CD (Cox adjusted hazard ratio 14.3, 95% confidence interval 4.0-50.3). In 90% of concordant pairs, the discordance time was ≤2 years. MZ and DZ co-twins had 70% and 9% cumulative probability of having symptomatic or silent forms of CD, respectively, within five years. Using the ACE model, we estimated heritability of CD to be 87% and 57%, respectively, with CD population prevalences of 1/91 and 1/1000.

Conclusion:
Our findings suggest that MZ twin pairs have a high probability of being concordant for CD, regardless of sex or HLA genotype. Most of the affected co-twins receive a diagnosis within two years, and a significant proportion of the phenotypic variance is due to genetic factors. These results provide evidence for the importance of genetic factors in the development of CD and support the use of twin studies in the investigation of complex diseases.

title: A literature review of the safety of medical body area network devices in magnetic resonance imaging
text:
In today's society, electro-magnetic fields and wireless technology are an integral part of our daily lives. The use of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machines to visualize internal human structures and functions in healthcare is becoming more prevalent. However, the rapid development of wireless devices, their miniaturization, and their application as clinical tools is creating an expanding intersection zone where safety concerns may arise. Although safety standards for devices in MRI machines have been previously published, it is unclear whether newer wireless technologies, including those used in Medical Body Area Networks (MBAN), have been adequately tested or disclosed.
To address this issue, we conducted a review of the clinical scientific literature and the United States Food and Drug Administration adverse events database. Our findings revealed a lack of published studies specifically addressing the safety of wireless devices potentially used in MBAN in MRI machines. We propose the addition of a research track to investigate the safety of these devices in MRI machines. By informed design of current and future MBAN components, devices, and systems, we can prevent potential patient adverse events resulting from the unintended consequences of concurrently using these technologies in MRI machines.

title: Synaptic glutamate release by ventromedial hypothalamic neurons is part of the neurocircuitry that prevents hypoglycemia.
text: The significance of neuropeptides in the hypothalamus has been experimentally confirmed. However, due to challenges in assessing function in living organisms, the roles of the rapidly acting neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA are largely unknown. Synaptic vesicular transporters, such as VGLUTs for glutamate and VGAT for GABA, are necessary for the vesicular uptake and release of neurotransmitters. Ventromedial hypothalamic (VMH) neurons are primarily glutamatergic and express VGLUT2. To investigate the role of glutamate release from VMH neurons, we generated mice lacking VGLUT2 selectively in SF1 neurons, a major subset of VMH neurons. These mice exhibit hypoglycemia during fasting due to impaired fasting-induced increases in the glucose-raising pancreatic hormone glucagon and impaired induction in the liver of mRNAs encoding PGC-1alpha and the gluconeogenic enzymes PEPCK and G6Pase. Similarly, these mice have defective counterregulatory responses to insulin-induced hypoglycemia and 2-deoxyglucose (an antimetabolite). Therefore, glutamate release from VMH neurons plays a crucial role in the neurocircuitry that helps prevent hypoglycemia.

title: c-Src and cooperating partners in human cancer.
text: The proto-oncogene c-src is infrequently mutated in human cancers, and when overexpressed in normal cells, its oncogenic potential is weak or non-existent. These findings have led some to question its involvement in the development of human tumors. However, more recent research has revealed that c-Src, a non-receptor tyrosine kinase, exhibits elevated protein levels and activity in a wide range of human cancers. In addition, it has been shown to play a critical role in multiple signaling pathways that regulate cell proliferation, survival, metastasis, and angiogenesis, making it an attractive therapeutic target.

title: Type 1 diabetes-associated IL2RA variation lowers IL-2 signaling and contributes to diminished CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cell function.
text: Numerous studies have shown that regulatory T cells (Tregs) from individuals with various human autoimmune diseases, including type 1 diabetes, exhibit impaired ability to control autologous pro-inflammatory responses compared to healthy controls. Treg dysfunction may be either a primary cause or a result of immune system perturbations during disease development. Genetic variations in genes involved in Treg function, such as IL2RA, have been linked to an increased risk of autoimmune diseases. However, the relationship between these genetic variations and Treg function has not been fully explored. To address this, we investigated the impact of an IL2RA haplotype associated with type 1 diabetes on Treg fitness and suppressive function in healthy human subjects. Our findings showed that the presence of this haplotype was associated with diminished IL-2 responsiveness in activated CD4+ T cells, reduced FOXP3 expression by Tregs, and a decrease in their ability to suppress T cell proliferation. These data provide a molecular and cellular mechanism by which genetic variations in the IL-2RA gene may contribute to the susceptibility to autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.

title: Hematopoietic stem cells and other hematopoietic cells show broad resistance to chemotherapeutic agents in vivo when overexpressing bcl-2.
text:
Objective:
Chemotherapeutic agents induce apoptosis, and their effectiveness depends on the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins in cells. However, determining whether overexpression of single genes is prognostic for increased resistance in tumors has been challenging due to the complex interactions of many proteins involved. To address this, we investigated the influence of bcl-2 overexpression on resistance to chemotherapeutics in a transgenic mouse model.
Methods:
We used H2K-bcl-2 transgenic and wild-type (WT) mice to study the contribution of increased bcl-2 levels to the response to various chemotherapeutics in vivo. Populations were enumerated using flow cytometry, and hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) were studied using FACS purification and long-term reconstitution assays in vivo. Resistance was confirmed by short-term proliferation assays with different amounts of chemotherapeutics in vitro.
Results:
bcl-2 overexpression protected many cell types, although protection levels varied between populations and agents. However, even sensitive populations returned to pre-treatment levels faster in transgenic mice. bcl-2 overexpression also prevented the dramatic changes in HSC following 5-FU treatment (downregulation of c-kit, upregulation of Lin, less efficient long-term reconstitution). In vitro studies demonstrated increased resistance of bcl-2 overexpressing HSC to chemotherapeutic agents.

Conclusions:
Increased expression of bcl-2 in HSC and their progeny endows these cells with broad resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. The ability to differentially regulate sensitivity to apoptosis of bystander and tumor cells is clinically important.

title: Direct sensing of systemic and nutritional signals by hematopoietic progenitors in Drosophila
text:
The Drosophila lymph gland is a hematopoietic organ that exhibits similarities to the mammalian myeloid lineage. Progenitor cells in the lymph gland, which are most closely related to common myeloid progenitors in mammals, proliferate and differentiate into three mature cell types: plasmatocytes, crystal cells, and lamellocytes. These cell types have functions similar to those of mammalian myeloid cells. During the early stages of larval development, the lymph gland contains only progenitor cells, while in the third instar, a medial region of the primary lobe called the medullary zone contains these progenitors, and maturing blood cells are found in a peripheral region designated the cortical zone. A third group of cells, referred to as the posterior signaling center, functions as a haematopoietic niche. Similarly to mammalian myeloid cells, Drosophila blood cells are able to respond to multiple stresses, including hypoxia, infection, and oxidative stress. However, the mechanisms by which systemic signals regulate cell fate determination in these progenitors have not been well characterized.
