This suggests that some genes may be individually compensated, and that a less-than-global pattern of dosage compensation, such as local or temporal, exists on the avian Z chromosome.
To investigate the pattern of sex-biased gene expression on the Z chromosome, we conducted global gene expression profiling in males and females for both somatic and gonadal tissue at various stages of the chicken life cycle. While average fold-change differences between males and females varied among tissue time-point combinations, embryonic brain samples had the smallest gene dosage effects, while adult gonadal tissue had the largest degree of male bias. Notably, there were no consistent patterns of overall dosage compensation along the Z chromosome.
Our findings suggest that dosage compensation on the Z chromosome is regulated on a gene-by-gene basis, and can vary depending on the tissue type and stage of development. This regulation may be a reflection of the criticality of each gene's function, with essential genes being tightly regulated to avoid disrupting important pathways and networks with differential expression levels in males and females.

title: Hormone replacement therapy prevents bone loss in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
text:
Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at an increased risk of developing osteoporosis, with high rates of spinal bone loss. While hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has been shown to be effective in the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, there is limited research on its use in patients with IBD. To address this gap, a two-year prospective study was conducted in 47 postmenopausal women with ulcerative colitis (25) or Crohn's disease (22), aged 44-67 years.
The study employed single photon absorptiometry and quantitative computed tomography to measure bone density in the radial and spinal regions annually. The results showed a significant annual increase in radial bone density of +1.42% (95% CI: +0.58 to +2.26; p < 0.005) and spinal bone density of +2.60% (95% CI: +1.06 to +4.15; p < 0.005). No significant correlation was found between the rates of change in bone density at the two sites, or between the rates of change and initial bone density in either the radius or spine. Additionally, the use of prednisolone during the study did not result in significantly different rates of change in spinal bone density compared to those who did not receive corticosteroids.
The study found that there were no significant differences in the rates of bone density change between patients with ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. Furthermore, the change in bone density did not correlate with the patients' age or number of years after menopause.
The study's findings suggest that HRT is effective in preventing bone loss in postmenopausal women with IBD. These results provide valuable insights into the management of osteoporosis in this patient population and highlight the need for further research in this area.

title: Disruption of the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction significantly improves the erythroid defect in a mouse model for Diamond-Blackfan anemia
text:
Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a congenital erythroid hypoplasia caused by haploinsufficiency of genes encoding ribosomal proteins (RPs). Previous studies have shown that perturbed ribosome biogenesis in DBA leads to a p53-mediated ribosomal stress response. However, the mechanisms of p53 activation and its relevance to the erythroid defect remain unclear.
To investigate the mechanisms of p53 activation in DBA, we employed a mouse model of RPS19-deficient DBA and crossed it with Mdm2C305F knock-in mice, which have a disrupted 5S ribonucleoprotein particle (RNP)–Mdm2 interaction. Upon induction of the Rps19 deficiency, Mdm2C305F reversed the p53 response and improved the expansion of hematopoietic progenitors in vitro and ameliorated the anemia in vivo. Unexpectedly, disruption of the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction also led to a selective defect in erythropoiesis.
Our findings highlight the sensitivity of erythroid progenitor cells to aberrations in p53 homeostasis mediated by the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction. Furthermore, we provide evidence indicating that physiological activation of the 5S RNP-Mdm2-p53 pathway may contribute to a functional decline of the hematopoietic system in a cell-autonomous manner over time.
In summary, our study reveals that the 5S RNP-Mdm2-p53 pathway plays a critical role in regulating erythroid cell function and that disruptions in this pathway can lead to the development of DBA. Our findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying this disease and may have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for its treatment.

title: Pharmacist participation on physician rounds and adverse drug events in the intensive care unit.
text:
The participation of a pharmacist on medical rounds in an intensive care unit (ICU) significantly reduces the rate of preventable adverse drug events (ADEs) caused by ordering errors, according to a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA). The study compared the rate of ADEs in an ICU where a pharmacist participated in rounds with one where they did not, and found that the rate of preventable ADEs decreased by 66% in the intervention group.
The study included 75 patients randomly selected from each of three groups: all admissions to the study unit during the baseline period, all admissions to the study unit during the postintervention period, and 50 patients selected at random from a control unit during the baseline period. The intervention involved a senior pharmacist making rounds with the ICU team and remaining available for consultation throughout the day.
The study found that the pharmacist made 366 recommendations related to drug ordering, of which 362 (99%) were accepted by physicians. The rate of preventable ADEs decreased from 10.4 per 1000 patient-days (95% confidence interval [CI], 7-14) before the intervention to 3.5 (95% CI, 1-5; P<.001) after the intervention in the intervention group, while the rate remained essentially unchanged in the control unit.
The study's authors concluded that the presence of a pharmacist on rounds as a full member of the patient care team in a medical ICU was associated with a substantially lower rate of ADEs caused by prescribing errors. Nearly all the changes were readily accepted by physicians.

title: Ligand-target interactions: what can we learn from NMR?
text: The conformation of a ligand in complex with a macromolecular target can be investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy in solution, regardless of the strength of the interaction between the ligand and the target. In the weak binding regime (k(off) > 10(4) Hz), the structure of the bound ligand is accessible for larger complexes (>100 kDa) than in the tight binding regime, making NMR studies possible. Here, I will review the current state-of-the-art NMR methodology used for screening ligands and investigating the structural properties of bound ligand conformations in both tight and weak binding regimes. I will also discuss the advantages and limitations of each approach. Recent advances in NMR methodology have expanded the possibilities for investigating transiently forming complexes, allowing for a more detailed understanding of ligand-target interactions. I will thoroughly review novel methods for determining the bound ligand conformation, such as transferred cross-correlated relaxation, and their advantages compared to established methodology, using the epothilone-tubulin complex as a primary example.

title: MotifMap: integrative genome-wide maps of regulatory motif sites for model species
text:
Background:
Unlocking the secrets of gene regulation on a genome-wide scale is a central challenge in biology. Despite significant progress in characterizing regulatory elements, only a small fraction of these have been identified, and computational methods are needed to systematically map and understand their relationships. However, the sheer size of non-coding regions and the complex spatial organizations of regulatory elements and interactions pose significant challenges to these efforts. Currently, there are no comprehensive genome-wide catalogs of regulatory elements for all model species.
Results:
To address these challenges, we have developed MotifMap, a system that uses databases of transcription factor binding motifs, refined genome alignments, and a comparative genomic statistical approach to generate comprehensive maps of candidate regulatory elements in the genomes of model species. We used MotifMap to derive new genome-wide maps for yeast, fly, worm, mouse, and human, resulting in a total of 519,108 sites for 570 matrices with a False Discovery Rate of 0.1 or less. We assessed the accuracy and coverage of the maps using high-throughput experimental ChIP-seq data and AUC statistics, providing strong evidence for their validity.
Conclusions:
MotifMap provides a foundation for analyzing gene regulation on a genome-wide scale and for automatically generating regulatory pathways and hypotheses. We demonstrate the power of this approach by using the P53 apoptotic pathway and the Gli hedgehog pathways as examples. By integrating MotifMap with other types of omic data, we can gain a deeper understanding of the complex networks that govern gene expression and their role in disease. MotifMap is available at http://motifmap.igb.uci.edu/, providing a valuable resource for the scientific community.

title: Inhibition of apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter as a novel treatment for diabetes.
text: Bile acids have been recognized as metabolic modulators, and the present study aimed to investigate the effects of a potent Asbt inhibitor (264W94) on glucose homeostasis in Zucker Diabetic Fatty (ZDF) rats. The study found that oral administration of 264W94 for two weeks increased fecal bile acid concentrations and elevated non-fasting plasma total Glp-1 levels. Treatment with 264W94 significantly decreased HbA1c and glucose levels, and prevented the typical drop in insulin levels seen in ZDF rats. An oral glucose tolerance test revealed up to two-fold increases in plasma total Glp-1 and three-fold increases in insulin levels in 264W94-treated ZDF rats at doses sufficient to achieve glycemic control. Tissue mRNA analysis showed a decrease in farnesoid X receptor (Fxr) activation in small intestines and the liver, but co-administration of a Fxr agonist did not attenuate the glucose-lowering effects of 264W94. The study suggests that inhibition of Asbt increases bile acids in the distal intestine, promotes Glp-1 release, and may offer a new therapeutic strategy for type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Early chromatin unfolding by RUNX1: a molecular explanation for differential requirements during specification versus maintenance of the hematopoietic gene expression program.
text:
At the cellular level, development progresses through a series of distinct regulatory states, each characterized by a unique gene expression profile. However, the molecular mechanisms that control the initial activation and subsequent maintenance of gene expression within a specific developmental pathway are still poorly understood. To address these questions, the hematopoietic system serves as a powerful experimental model, and in this study, we have focused on a key regulatory circuit involved in myelopoiesis: the transcription factor PU.1, its target gene colony-stimulating-factor 1 receptor (Csf1r), and upstream regulators such as RUNX1.
Our findings reveal that during development, the unfolding of chromatin precedes the establishment of active histone marks and the formation of stable transcription factor complexes at the PU.1 locus. We demonstrate that chromatin remodeling in this process is mediated by the transient binding of RUNX1 to specific cis-elements in the PU.1 locus. In contrast, the reorganization of the Csf1r locus requires the prior expression of PU.1 and the binding of RUNX1 to specific cis-elements. Once the full hematopoietic program is established, stable transcription factor complexes and active chromatin can be maintained without the presence of RUNX1.
Our experiments demonstrate how individual transcription factors function in a stage-specific manner to differentially regulate the initiation and maintenance of a developmental program. Specifically, we show that PU.1 and RUNX1 play distinct roles in the regulation of myelopoiesis, with PU.1 controlling the initial activation of gene expression and RUNX1 maintaining the program once it is established. This study provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms that control the regulation of gene expression during development and highlights the importance of stage-specific regulation in the establishment and maintenance of a developmental program.

title: Whole-genome fingerprint of the DNA methylome during human B cell differentiation
text: We employed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and high-density microarrays to investigate the DNA methylome of ten distinct B cell subpopulations across the entire differentiation program. Our findings revealed that non-CpG methylation was eliminated during B cell commitment, whereas CpG methylation exhibited a dynamic pattern of change during maturation, with an accumulative effect and affecting approximately 30% of all measured CpG sites. Early differentiation stages primarily displayed enhancer demethylation, which was associated with the upregulation of key B cell transcription factors and impacted multiple genes involved in B cell biology. In contrast, late differentiation stages showed extensive demethylation of heterochromatin and methylation gain at Polycomb-repressed areas, with genes exhibiting apparent functional impact in B cells remaining unchanged. This methylation signature, which has been linked to aging and cancer, was particularly pronounced in mature cells with an extended lifespan. By comparing B cell neoplasms with their normal counterparts, we identified that these neoplastic cells frequently acquire methylation changes in regions that are already undergoing dynamic methylation during normal B cell differentiation.

title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7 suppression
text: LIN28B regulates various developmental processes by modulating microRNAs (miRNAs) of the let-7 family. Although a role for LIN28B in cancer has been proposed, its in vivo significance has yet to be established. Our study reveals that LIN28B exhibits genomic aberrations and extensive overexpression in high-risk neuroblastoma compared to other tumor entities and normal tissues. High LIN28B expression serves as an independent risk factor for unfavorable outcomes in neuroblastoma. LIN28B represses the let-7 miRNAs, leading to elevated MYCN protein expression in neuroblastoma cells. This LIN28B–let-7–MYCN signaling pathway inhibits the differentiation of normal neuroblasts and neuroblastoma cells. Our findings have been recapitulated in a mouse model, in which LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage leads to the development of neuroblastomas characterized by low let-7 miRNA levels and high MYCN protein expression. Targeting this pathway may offer potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor expression correlates with tumour angiogenesis and prognosis in non-small-cell lung cancer.
text: Angiogenesis has recently been identified as a prognostic factor in non-small-cell lung cancer. Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PD-ECGF), which is shown to be enzymatically converted to thymidine phosphorylase (TP), has been found to induce angiogenesis in both in vitro and in vivo settings. High levels of TP within cancer cells have been associated with increased chemosensitivity to pyrimidine antimetabolites. In this study, the expression of PD-ECGF/TP was evaluated immunohistochemically in surgically resected tumor specimens from 107 patients with operable non-small-cell lung cancer using the P-GF,44C monoclonal antibody. The results showed that high expression of PD-ECGF/TP was present in 25% of cases and was significantly associated with high vascular grade (P = 0.01). Furthermore, the study found that positive expression of PD-ECGF/TP was more frequent in T2-staged cases than in T1 cases (P = 0.04). While overall survival was not significantly affected (P = 0.09), a worse prognosis was observed in node-negative patients with positive PD-ECGF/TP expression (P = 0.04). These findings suggest that PD-ECGF/TP may play an important role in angiogenesis in non-small-cell lung cancer, and that assessment of vascular grade and PD-ECGF/TP expression should be taken into account in the design of randomized trials evaluating the role of adjuvant chemotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer.

title: The association between psychological distance and construal level: evidence from an implicit association test.
text:
According to construal level theory (Liberman, Trope, & Stephan, in press; Trope & Liberman, 2003), people tend to adopt a more abstract and high construal level when evaluating, perceiving, and predicting more psychologically distant targets. This means that they perceive more abstract targets as being more psychologically distant. The current research further explored this phenomenon by demonstrating that the association between higher construal level and greater psychological distance also holds on a purely conceptual level.
Eight experiments using the Implicit Association Test (IAT; Greenwald, McGhee, & Schwartz, 1998) showed that there is a connection between words related to construal level (low vs. high) and words related to four dimensions of distance (proximal vs. distal): temporal distance, spatial distance, social distance, and hypotheticality. These findings not only confirm the link between level of construal and psychological distance but also support the idea that all four dimensions of psychological distance are related to level of construal in a similar manner. This supports the notion that they are all forms of psychological distance.

title: A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks
text: The performance of gene modules in intricate synthetic circuits is often unpredictable. When combining modules to form a circuit, downstream elements (such as binding sites for a regulatory protein) impose a burden on upstream modules, which can negatively impact circuit function. To address this issue, we developed a genetic device called a load driver, which mitigates the adverse effects of load on circuit function. Our design principle, timescale separation, involves the fast phosphotransfer processes of the load driver, which restore the ability of a slower transcriptional circuit to respond to time-varying input signals even in the presence of significant load. Without the load driver, we observed circuit behavior with a 76% delay in response time and a 25% decrease in system bandwidth due to load. In contrast, the addition of a load driver almost completely restored circuit performance. Load drivers will serve as fundamental building blocks in the construction of complex, higher-level genetic circuits.

title: Inflammatory monocyte/macrophage modulation by liposome-entrapped spironolactone ameliorates acute lung injury in mice.
text:
Objective: To investigate the therapeutic and preventive potential of liposome-encapsulated spironolactone (Lipo-SP) in acute lung injury (ALI) and fibrosis.
Materials and Methods: Lipo-SP was prepared using the film-ultrasonic method and physicochemical and pharmacokinetic characterization was performed for oral administration (10 and 20 mg/kg for SP-loaded liposome; 20 mg/kg for free SP) in a mouse model of bleomycin-induced ALI.
Results: Lipo-SP significantly enhanced the bioavailability of spironolactone and improved lung pathology. Mechanistically, spironolactone-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism contributed to the modulation of inflammatory monocyte/macrophage activity via an inhibitory effect on Ly6C(hi) monocytosis-directed M2 polarization of alveolar macrophages. Additionally, Lipo-SP at a lower dose (10 mg/kg) showed greater improvement in body weight gain.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that Lipo-SP has therapeutic and preventive potential for ALI and fibrosis, highlighting its promise as a promising approach for the treatment of these conditions.

title: Passive Surveillance for I. scapularis Ticks: Enhanced Analysis for Early Detection of Emerging Lyme Disease Risk
text: Lyme disease (LD) is expanding its geographic range in Canada due to the northward spread of the tick vector, Ixodes scapularis (Say). Early detection of emerging LD hotspots is crucial for effective public health responses, but current methods for identifying these areas at a local scale are limited. Passive tick surveillance has been ongoing in Canada since 1990, but this method lacks specificity in identifying areas where tick populations are established due to bird-borne tick dispersal from established LD risk areas. To address this limitation, we developed a logistic regression model using data from 70 field sites in Quebec, which estimated the risk of I. scapularis population establishment based on the number of ticks submitted in passive surveillance and an environmental suitability index derived from the model. Sensitivity-specificity plots were used to select an optimal threshold value of the linear predictor from the model as the signal for tick population establishment. This value was used to create an "Alert Map" identifying areas where passive surveillance data suggested ticks were establishing in Quebec. The Alert Map predictions were validated through field surveillance at 76 sites, revealing a significant difference in prevalence of established I. scapularis populations between high-risk areas predicted by the Alert Map (29 out of 48) and moderate-risk areas (4 out of 30) (P < 0.001). This study demonstrates that "Alert Maps" created using this approach can provide a useful, rapid, and accurate tool for identifying emerging areas of LD risk at a geographic scale suitable for local disease control and prevention activities.

title: Reduction of transmission from malaria patients by artemisinin combination therapies: a pooled analysis of six randomized trials
text:
Background: Artemisinin combination therapies (ACTs) are increasingly being used to treat Plasmodium falciparum malaria, and they have shown greater effectiveness against sexual stage parasites (gametocytes) compared to previous first-line antimalarials. This potential to reduce parasite transmission is significant, especially in areas with high transmission rates.
Methods: Data from six antimalarial trials conducted in The Gambia and Kenya were pooled, including 3,174 patients. Multivariable regression analysis was used to investigate the impact of ACT versus non-artemisinin antimalarial treatment, treatment failure, pre-treatment gametocytes, and submicroscopic gametocytaemia on transmission to mosquitoes and the area under the curve (AUC) of gametocyte density during the 28-day follow-up period.
Results: ACT treatment was associated with a significant reduction in the probability of being gametocytaemic on the day of transmission experiments (odds ratio [OR] 0.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.16-0.26), transmission to mosquitoes by slide-positive gametocyte carriers (OR mosquito infection 0.49, 95% CI 0.33-0.73), and AUC of gametocyte density (ratio of means 0.35, 95% CI 0.31-0.41). Treatment failure did not account for the difference between ACT and non-artemisinin impact. The presence of slide-positive gametocytaemia prior to treatment significantly reduced ACT impact on gametocytaemia (p < 0.001). Accounting for submicroscopic gametocytaemia reduced estimates of ACT impact in a high transmission setting in Kenya but not in a lower transmission setting in The Gambia.
Conclusion: Treatment with ACT significantly reduces the infectiousness of individual patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria compared to previous first-line treatments. Rapid treatment of cases before gametocytaemia is well developed may enhance the impact of ACT on transmission.

title: Skeletal Myogenic Progenitors Originating from Embryonic Dorsal Aorta Coexpress Endothelial and Myogenic Markers and Contribute to Postnatal Muscle Growth and Regeneration
text: In vertebrates, skeletal muscle is derived from somites, which are structures of the paraxial mesoderm. However, there have been numerous reports of myogenic cells appearing in non-somite tissues, suggesting either transdifferentiation or the persistence of a multipotent progenitor. Here, we provide evidence that clonable skeletal myogenic cells are present in the embryonic dorsal aorta of mouse embryos. Through a detailed clonal analysis of different tissue anlagen at various developmental stages, we found that these myogenic cells exhibit the same morphology as satellite cells derived from adult skeletal muscle and express a range of myogenic and endothelial markers. Interestingly, these markers are also expressed by adult satellite cells. Furthermore, we were able to clone myogenic cells from limbs of mutant c-Met-/- embryos, which lack appendicular muscles but have a normal vascular system. When transplanted, these cells participate in postnatal muscle growth and regeneration and fuse with resident satellite cells. Our findings suggest that the vascular system may have the potential to generate skeletal muscle cells, which could explain observations of nonsomite skeletal myogenesis and raise the possibility that a subset of satellite cells may originate from the vascular system.

title: Mapping of a gene for severe pediatric gastroesophageal reflux to chromosome 13q14.
text:
Title: Genetic Analysis of Severe Pediatric Gastroesophageal Reflux (GER)
Background: Gastroesophageal reflux (GER) is a common condition characterized by the backflow of stomach contents into the esophagus. While GER is often considered an adult condition, it can also affect children, and in some cases, it can be severe and persistent. Despite its prevalence, the genetic basis of severe pediatric GER has not been well understood.
Objective: To identify a genetic locus that cosegregates with a severe pediatric GER phenotype in families with multiple affected members.
Methods: We conducted a genome-wide scan of families with multiple affected members using polymorphic microsatellite markers spaced at an average of 8 centimorgans (cM). We then performed haplotyping and linkage analyses using the identified markers. The study included 5 families with multiple individuals affected by severe pediatric GER, identified through a patient support group.
Results: Our results showed that severe pediatric GER follows an autosomal dominant hereditary pattern with high penetrance. We were able to map the gene for severe pediatric GER to a 13-centimorgan region on chromosome 13q between the microsatellite markers D13S171 and D13S263. A maximum multifamily 2-point lod score of 5.58 and a maximum multifamily multipoint lod score of 7.15 were obtained for marker D13S1253 at map position 35 cM when presumptively affected persons were modeled as unknown. When presumptively affected persons were modeled as unaffected, a maximum multipoint score of 4.88 was obtained.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that a gene for severe pediatric GER maps to chromosome 13q14. These data provide the first evidence of a genetic component to severe pediatric GER and have important implications for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to identify the specific genetic mutation responsible for this condition.

title: Accelerating Policy Decisions to Adopt Haemophilus influenzae Type b Vaccine: A Global, Multivariable Analysis
text:
The adoption of new and underutilized vaccines by national immunization programs is crucial to reduce child mortality. However, policy decisions to adopt these vaccines in low- and middle-income countries often lag behind those in high-income countries. This study aims to identify the factors that contribute to these delays using the case of Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine.
Using data from 147 countries over a 17-year period, the study analyzed the relationship between country-level economic, epidemiological, programmatic, and policy-related factors and the time it takes for countries to make decisions to adopt Hib vaccine. The findings revealed that the receipt of support from the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI Alliance) significantly accelerated the time to decision, with a factor of 0.37 (95% CI 0.18-0.76) or 63%. The presence of two or more neighboring country adopters also accelerated decisions to adopt by a factor of 0.50 (95% CI 0.33-0.75). On the other hand, a 1% increase in vaccine price resulted in a delay of 1.02 (95% CI 1.00-1.04) in decisions to adopt. Global recommendations and local studies were not associated with the time to decision.
The study's findings suggest that supply- and demand-side factors, such as GAVI eligibility and neighboring country decisions, play a significant role in the adoption of new vaccines. The study's results provide evidence to support the idea that approaches to support the adoption of new vaccines should consider these factors. The study highlights the importance of addressing the economic and programmatic barriers to vaccine adoption, such as vaccine price, in order to accelerate the adoption of new and underutilized vaccines and reduce child mortality.

title: Haemolysin coregulated protein is an exported receptor and chaperone of type VI secretion substrates.
text: Secretion systems in bacteria rely on high-fidelity mechanisms to distinguish between the vast pool of cytoplasmic proteins. The type VI secretion system (T6SS) of Gram-negative bacteria, a common pathway that translocates effector proteins into target cells, has not had its substrate recognition factors defined. We have discovered that Haemolysin Coregulated Protein (Hcp), a ring-shaped hexamer secreted by all T6SSs, selectively binds to cognate effector molecules. Electron microscopy analysis of an Hcp-effector complex from Pseudomonas aeruginosa revealed the effector bound to the inner surface of Hcp. Subsequent studies demonstrated that interaction with the Hcp pore is a general requirement for the secretion of diverse effectors, including several enzymatic classes. Contrary to previous models depicting Hcp as a static conduit, our findings suggest that it acts as both a chaperone and receptor for substrates. These unique functions of a secreted protein highlight significant differences between the export mechanism of T6 and other characterized secretory pathways.

title: Long-term effects of continuing adjuvant tamoxifen to 10 years versus stopping at 5 years after diagnosis of oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer: ATLAS, a randomised trial
text: In this study, researchers investigated the effects of continuing tamoxifen treatment beyond 5 years in women with early breast cancer. The study included 12,894 women with early breast cancer who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen treatment, and were randomly assigned to either continue treatment for an additional 5 years (10 years in total) or stop at 5 years (control group). The researchers found that among women with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer, continuing tamoxifen treatment to 10 years significantly reduced the risk of breast cancer recurrence, mortality, and overall mortality compared to stopping at 5 years. The reduction in adverse breast cancer outcomes appeared to be less extreme before than after year 10. The study also found that treatment allocation had no effect on breast cancer outcomes among women with ER-negative disease, and an intermediate effect among women with unknown ER status. The study suggests that continuing tamoxifen treatment for 10 years can approximately halve breast cancer mortality during the second decade after diagnosis.

title: Roles for MicroRNAs in Conferring Robustness to Biological Processes
text: Biological systems employ a range of mechanisms to maintain their functions in the face of environmental and genetic changes. Recent research suggests that microRNAs (miRNAs), which play a crucial role in post-transcriptional gene regulation, help to ensure the robustness of biological processes by reinforcing transcriptional programs and dampening aberrant gene expression. In some cases, miRNAs may also help to suppress random fluctuations in transcript copy number. These activities have significant implications for normal development, physiology, disease, and evolution. In this discussion, we will explore examples and principles of how miRNAs contribute to robustness in animal systems.

title: Six-Year Follow-Up of Impact of Co-proxamol Withdrawal in England and Wales on Prescribing and Deaths: Time-Series Study
text:
Background: The analgesic combination of paracetamol and dextropropoxyphene (co-proxamol) has been associated with a significant number of fatal poisonings in the UK. In response to concerns regarding its safety and effectiveness profile, as well as its widespread use for suicidal poisoning, co-proxamol was withdrawn from the market in the UK in 2005, with partial withdrawal between 2005 and 2007, and full withdrawal in 2008. This study aimed to assess the association between co-proxamol withdrawal and prescribing patterns, as well as deaths involving single analgesics, in England and Wales between 1998 and 2010.
Methods: The study used prescribing data from the NHS Health and Social Care Information Centre (England) and Prescribing Services Partneriaeth Cydwasanaethau GIG Cymru (Wales), as well as mortality data from the Office for National Statistics. An interrupted time-series analysis was conducted to examine changes in prescribing patterns and deaths involving single analgesics during the study period.
Findings: The reduction in prescribing of co-proxamol following its withdrawal in 2005 was associated with increases in prescribing of several other analgesics (co-codamol, paracetamol, codeine, co-dydramol, tramadol, oxycodone, and morphine) during 2005-2010 compared to 1998-2004. These changes were associated with major reductions in deaths due to poisoning with co-proxamol receiving verdicts of suicide and undetermined cause, of -21 deaths (95% CI -34 to -8) per quarter, equating to approximately 500 fewer suicide deaths (-61%) over the 6 years 2005-2010, and -25 deaths (95% CI -38 to -12) per quarter, equating to 600 fewer deaths (-62%) when accidental poisoning deaths were included. There was little observed change in deaths involving other analgesics, apart from an increase in oxycodone poisonings, but numbers were small. Limitations of the study included the fact that it was based on deaths involving single drugs alone, and changes in deaths involving prescribed morphine could not be assessed.
Conclusions: The study found that following the withdrawal of co-proxamol in the UK, there was a significant reduction in poisoning deaths involving this drug, without a corresponding increase in deaths involving other analgesics. These findings suggest that the withdrawal of co-proxamol may have contributed to a reduction in poisoning deaths in England and Wales. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings and to explore the potential mechanisms underlying the observed changes in prescribing patterns and deaths involving single analgesics.

title: Apolipoprotein E genotype and concussion in college athletes.
text:
Objective: To investigate the association between apolipoprotein E (APOE) polymorphisms (E2, C/T Arg158Cys; E4, T/C Cys112Arg; and promoter, g-219t) and the history of concussion in college athletes. We hypothesized that individuals carrying one or more APOE rare (or minor) alleles would be more likely to report a history of concussion.
Design: Multicenter cross-sectional study.
Setting: University athletic facilities.
Participants: One hundred ninety-six male football (n = 163) and female soccer (n = 33) college athletes volunteered.
Interventions: Written concussion history questionnaire and saliva samples for genotyping.
Main Outcome Measures: Self-reported history of a documented concussion and rare APOE genotype (E2, E4, promoter).
Results: There was a significant association (Wald χ² = 3.82; P = 0.05; odds ratio = 9.8) between carrying all APOE rare alleles and the history of a previous concussion. Additionally, there was a significant association (Wald χ² = 3.96, P = 0.04, odds ratio = 8.4) between carrying the APOE promoter minor allele and experiencing 2 or more concussions.
Conclusions: Carriers of all 3 APOE rare (or minor) alleles assessed in this study were nearly 10 times more likely to report a previous concussion and may be at a greater risk of concussion versus noncarriers. Promoter minor allele carriers were 8.4 times more likely to report multiple concussions and may be at a greater risk of multiple concussions versus noncarriers. Further research involving larger samples of individuals with multiple concussions and carriers of multiple APOE rare alleles is warranted.

title: Plasma soluble corin and N-terminal pro-atrial natriuretic peptide levels in pregnancy induced hypertension.
text:
Objective:
One of the theories implicated in the pathogenesis of pregnancy-induced hypertension involves salt and water retention. To investigate this further, we aimed to measure the proenzyme convertase corin, which is responsible for cleaving pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) to active ANP, in the plasma of hypertensive pregnant females.
Study Design:
Sixty pregnant females suffering from pregnancy-induced hypertension in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy were compared to twenty-eight healthy pregnant females of the same gestational period. Concurrent urine and plasma samples were collected for the determination of various biochemical parameters. Plasma soluble corin and N-terminal (NT) pro-ANP (1-98) values were measured in both groups using enzyme immunoassays.
Results:
Plasma soluble corin mean value was significantly higher in the patient group compared to the control group. When the patient group was divided according to blood pressure, plasma NT pro-ANP showed significantly higher mean values in the group with blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg compared to the group with blood pressure <140/90 mmHg and the control group.

Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that high plasma soluble corin and NT pro-ANP values are particularly pronounced in hypertensive pregnant females with blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg, which may indicate an ANP receptor/post-receptor signaling defect that exacerbates the pregnancy-induced hypertensive state.

title: GATA-4 and GATA-6 modulate tissue-specific transcription of the human gene for P450c17 by direct interaction with Sp1.
text:
The cytochrome P450c17 enzyme catalyzes two distinct activities: steroidogenic 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase. The expression of the P450c17 gene is regulated by various factors, including cAMP, tissue specificity, developmental programming, and species-specific differences. The binding of transcription factors Sp1, Sp3, and NF1-C to the P450c17 promoter is crucial for basal transcription in human NCI-H295A adrenal cells. However, human placental JEG-3 cells do not express the P450c17 gene even when transfected with a vector expressing steroidogenic factor 1 (SF-1). Therefore, other factors are necessary for basal expression of P450c17 in these cells.
Deoxyribonuclease I footprinting and EMSAs identified a GATA consensus site at -64/-58 and an SF-1 site at -58/-50 in the P450c17 promoter. RT-PCR analysis identified GATA-4, GATA-6, and SF-1 in NCI-H295A cells and GATA-2 and GATA-3, but not GATA-4, GATA-6, or SF-1 in JEG-3 cells. Cotransfection of either GATA-4 or GATA-6 without SF-1 activated the P450c17 promoter in JEG-3 cells, while cotransfection of GATA-2 or GATA-3 with or without SF-1 did not. Surprisingly, mutation of the GATA binding site in the P450c17 promoter increased GATA-4 or GATA-6-induced activity, while mutation of the Sp1/Sp3 site decreased it. Furthermore, promoter constructs including the GATA site but excluding the Sp1/Sp3 site at -196/-188 were not activated by GATA-4 or GATA-6. These results suggest an interaction between Sp1/Sp3 and GATA-4 or GATA-6. Glutathione-S-transferase pull-down experiments and coimmunoprecipitation demonstrated interaction between GATA-4 or GATA-6 and Sp1, but not Sp3. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays confirmed that this GATA-4/6 interaction with Sp1 occurred at the Sp site in the P450c17 promoter in NCI-H295A cells. Demethylation with 5-aza-2-deoxycytidine permitted JEG-3 cells to express endogenous P450c17, SF-1, GATA-4, GATA-6, and transfected -227/LUC. Therefore, GATA-4 or GATA-6 and Sp1 together regulate expression of P450c17 in adrenal NCI-H295A cells, and methylation of P450c17, GATA-4, and GATA-6 silences the expression of P450c17 in placental JEG-3 cells.

title: Performance of an abbreviated version of the Lubben Social Network Scale among three European community-dwelling older adult populations.
text:
Purpose:
There is a need for brief and reliable scales to assess social networks and social support systems and screen for social isolation in older individuals.
Design and Methods:
The present study is a cross-national and cross-cultural evaluation of the performance of an abbreviated version of the Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) in identifying social isolation among community-dwelling older adult populations in three European countries. We defined clinical cut-points based on the concept of lack of redundancy of social ties to identify individuals at risk of social isolation.
Results:
The LSNS-6 and two subscales (Family and Friends) demonstrated high internal consistency, stable factor structures, and high correlations with criterion variables across all three samples. The proposed clinical cut-points showed good convergent validity, and classified 20% of respondents in Hamburg, 11% of those in Solothurn (Switzerland), and 15% of those in London as at risk for social isolation.
Implications:

We conclude that brief scales like the LSNS-6 should be considered for inclusion in practice protocols of gerontological practitioners. Screening older individuals based on the LSNS-6 provides quantitative information on their family and friendship ties and identifies individuals at increased risk for social isolation who might benefit from in-depth assessment and targeted interventions.

title: The PneuCarriage Project: A Multi-Centre Comparative Study to Identify the Best Serotyping Methods for Examining Pneumococcal Carriage in Vaccine Evaluation Studies
text:
Background:
The pneumococcus is a highly diverse pathogen with over 90 different serotypes, and the nasopharynx is its primary niche. Understanding pneumococcal carriage is crucial for evaluating the impact of pneumococcal vaccines. However, traditional serotyping methods are cumbersome and insufficient for detecting multiple serotype carriage, and there is a need for new methods that have been developed over the past decade. To address this gap, we established the PneuCarriage project, a large, international multi-centre study to identify the best pneumococcal serotyping methods for carriage studies.
Methods and Findings:
We distributed reference sample sets to 15 research groups for blinded testing, and 20 pneumococcal serotyping methods were used to test 81 laboratory-prepared (spiked) samples. The top-performing methods were then used to test 260 nasopharyngeal (field) samples collected from children in six high-burden countries. Sensitivity and positive predictive value (PPV) were determined for the test methods and the reference method (traditional serotyping of >100 colonies from each sample). The overall sensitivity ranged from 1% to 99% (reference method 98%), and PPV from 8% to 100% (reference method 100%), when testing the spiked samples. Fifteen methods had ≥70% sensitivity to detect the dominant (major) serotype, while only eight methods had ≥70% sensitivity to detect minor serotypes. For the field samples, the overall sensitivity ranged from 74.2% to 95.8% (reference method 93.8%), and PPV from 82.2% to 96.4% (reference method 99.6%). The microarray had the highest sensitivity (95.8%) and high PPV (93.7%).
Limitations:
The major limitation of this study is that not all of the available alternative serotyping methods were included.
Conclusions:
Most methods were able to detect the dominant serotype in a sample, but many performed poorly in detecting the minor serotype populations. Microarray with a culture amplification step was the top-performing method. The results of this comprehensive evaluation will inform future vaccine evaluation and impact studies, particularly in low-income settings where pneumococcal disease burden remains high.

title: Ribosome-Mediated Specificity in Hox mRNA Translation and Vertebrate Tissue Patterning
text: Historically, the ribosome was thought to be a simple machine responsible for protein synthesis, without any regulatory capacity in mRNA translation. However, our recent findings challenge this view by revealing that the ribosome is actually a complex system with regulatory functions. We have identified mutations in the Ribosomal Protein L38 (Rpl38) gene in mice that lead to surprising tissue-specific patterning defects, including pronounced homeotic transformations of the axial skeleton. Interestingly, global protein synthesis is unchanged in these mutant embryos, but the translation of a specific subset of Homeobox mRNAs is perturbed. Our data suggest that RPL38 acts as a regulatory component of the ribosome, facilitating 80S complex formation on these mRNAs and conferring transcript-specific translational control. Furthermore, we found that Rpl38 expression is enriched in regions of the embryo where loss-of-function phenotypes occur. Surprisingly, a ribosomal protein (RP) expression screen revealed dynamic regulation of individual RPs within the vertebrate embryo, suggesting that RP activity may be highly regulated to impart a new layer of specificity in the control of gene expression and mammalian development. Overall, these findings challenge our previous understanding of the ribosome's function and highlight the importance of regulatory mechanisms in controlling gene expression and development.

title: Growth and invasion of human melanomas in human skin grafted to immunodeficient mice.
text: In this study, researchers developed an orthotopic model of human melanoma by injecting malignant cells into human skin grafted onto nude and SCID mice. The melanoma cells proliferated and invaded the human skin grafts in a characteristic pattern, with three of six tumors growing as multiple nodules and infiltrating the grafts without significant architectural changes in the dermis. The other three tumors invaded the dermis along collagen fibers, with prominent endothelial vessels. In contrast, when melanoma cells were inoculated into mouse skin, they grew as diffuse, expanding nodules that did not invade the murine dermis. In the human skin grafts, the melanoma cells were angiogenic for human blood vessels, but murine vessels were only found at the periphery of the grafts. The tumor cells also invaded the human vessels, and four out of seven cell lines metastasized to the lungs, suggesting that this model is useful for studying the interactions between normal and malignant human cells in vivo.

title: Myeloperoxidase: friend and foe.
text: Neutrophilic polymorphonuclear leukocytes (neutrophils) are specially designed to engulf and destroy microorganisms through a process called phagocytosis. When coated with opsonins (usually complement and/or antibody), microorganisms bind to specific receptors on the surface of the phagocyte and are internalized through invagination of the cell membrane, resulting in the incorporation of the microorganism into an intracellular phagosome. This process leads to an increase in oxygen consumption, with most of the excess oxygen being converted into highly reactive oxygen species (ROS). Additionally, the cytoplasmic granules release their contents into the phagosome, ultimately leading to the death of the ingested microorganism. One of the antimicrobial systems formed in the phagosome is a complex consisting of myeloperoxidase (MPO), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and a halide (usually chloride). The initial product of this system is hypochlorous acid, which can then undergo further chemical reactions to form chlorine, chloramines, hydroxyl radicals, singlet oxygen, and ozone. These toxic agents can be released to the outside of the cell, potentially harming normal tissue and contributing to disease. This review will examine the potential sources of H2O2 for the MPO-H2O2-halide system, the toxic products of the MPO system, the evidence for MPO involvement in microbicidal activity, the involvement of MPO-independent antimicrobial systems, and the role of the MPO system in tissue injury. It is concluded that the MPO system plays a crucial role in the microbicidal activity of phagocytes.

title: Role of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 in the facilitation of angiogenesis and the healing of gastric ulcers.
text: The significance of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) in various physiological events underscores the importance of understanding the role of PGE synthases (PGESs) in vivo. However, there has been no investigation into the functional relevance of microsomal PGES-1 (mPGES-1) in the physiological healing processes of gastric ulcers and angiogenesis, which is crucial for ulcer healing. To address this gap in knowledge, we evaluated the role of mPGES-1 in the healing of gastric ulcers and angiogenesis using mPGES-1 knockout (mPGES-1 KO) mice and their wild-type (WT) counterparts. Gastric ulcers were induced by applying 100% acetic acid to the serosal surface, and the areas of the ulcers were measured subsequently. We found that mPGES-1 and cyclooxygenase-2 were upregulated in the granulation tissues compared to normal stomach tissues. The healing of acetic acid-induced ulcers was significantly delayed in mPGES-1 KO mice compared to WT, accompanied by reduced angiogenesis in the ulcer granulation tissues, as evidenced by decreased CD31 mRNA levels determined by real-time PCR and microvessel density in granulation tissues. Moreover, the mRNA levels of proangiogenic growth factors, such as transforming growth factor-β, basic fibroblast growth factor, and connective tissue growth factor, in the ulcer granulation tissues were also reduced in mPGES-1 KO mice compared to WT. Our findings suggest that mPGES-1 plays a crucial role in enhancing the ulcer-healing processes and angiogenesis indispensable to ulcer healing. Therefore, a selective mPGES-1 inhibitor should be used with caution in patients with gastric ulcers.

title: Echocardiographic Evidence of Innate Aortopathy in the Human Intracranial Aneurysm
text:
Background: Intracranial aneurysm (IA) is more prevalent in patients with coarctation of the aorta or bicuspid aortic valve compared to the general population, suggesting a common underlying pathophysiology. To investigate this further, we analyzed the echocardiographic aortic root dimension (ARD) in patients with IA.
Methods: We studied 260 patients with IA who underwent echocardiography at our institution between 2008 and 2010. We divided the patients into two groups based on their ARD: an eccentric group (patients aged <55 years with at least one ruptured aneurysm, an aneurysm ≥7 mm in size, or multiple aneurysms) and a non-eccentric group. We compared the clinical, angiographic, and echocardiographic findings of the two groups.
Results: We found that the eccentric group had significantly larger ARDs than the non-eccentric group (P = 0.049). This difference was confirmed by multivariable analysis (P = 0.02). In a subgroup analysis of patients aged <55 years, we found similar results for ARD (P = 0.03). However, hypertension was more common in the non-eccentric group (P = 0.01). Additionally, we found that height was inversely related to aneurysm size after adjusting for age, sex, weight, ARD, smoking status, and number of aneurysms (P = 0.004).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that a subset of patients with IA share a common intrinsic wall defect with aortopathy. This common origin may explain the observed association between IA and aortopathy.

title: Aortic and large artery compliance in end-stage renal failure.
text: In this study, the authors measured pulse wave velocity (PWV) in the aorta, right leg, and arm of 90 healthy control subjects (CS) and 92 hemodialysis patients (HD). They found that aortic PWV was significantly higher in HD patients (1113 ± 319 cm/sec) compared to CS (965 ± 216 cm/sec; P = 0.0016). Additionally, the aortic diameters were larger in HD patients at the root of the aorta (32.7 ± 4 mm vs. 28.2 ± 2.8 mm; P < 0.0001) and aortic bifurcation (16.9 ± 3.1 mm vs. 14.6 ± 2.2 mm; P < 0.0001). The pulse pressure was also significantly higher in HD patients (76.6 ± 23.7 mm Hg vs. 63.9 ± 22 mm Hg; P = 0.007). Furthermore, the authors found that aortic PWV increased with age (P < 0.0001) and mean arterial pressure (P < 0.0001) in both populations. The presence of aortic calcification showed a borderline relationship with the increase in aortic PWV (P = 0.050 in CS and P = 0.069 in HD). These results suggest that the aortic wall compliance is decreased in HD patients, resulting in an increase in the pulsatile component of arterial pressure.

title: The DNA polymerase λ is required for the repair of non-compatible DNA double strand breaks by NHEJ in mammalian cells
text: DNA polymerase lambda (polλ) is a recently discovered DNA polymerase whose cellular function remains unclear. Our study reveals that polλ plays a crucial role in repairing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) in mammalian cells through non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). We found that expressing a catalytically inactive form of polλ (polλDN) decreases the frequency of NHEJ events in response to I-Sce-I-induced DSB, while inactive forms of its homologues polβ and polμ do not. Only events that require DNA end processing before ligation are affected, and this defect leads to large deletions near the induced DSB. Additionally, polλDN-expressing cells are more sensitive to ionizing radiation and exhibit increased genomic instability, similar to NHEJ-defective cells. Our findings suggest that polλ plays a crucial role in repairing a specific subset of DSBs in genomic DNA, thereby contributing to the maintenance of genetic stability through the NHEJ pathway.

title: Angina with "normal" coronary arteries: sex differences in outcomes.
text:
BACKGROUND:
Several studies have shown that women with non-obstructive coronary disease have a higher rate of subsequent investigations, rehospitalizations for recurrent chest pain, and repeat coronary angiography compared to men. However, the sex-specific differences in these findings are not well understood. To address this gap, we conducted an evaluation of sex differences in rehospitalization rates for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or chest pain in patients with "angiographically normal" coronaries.
METHODS:
We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected angiographic and clinical data on all patients in British Columbia, Canada, who presented for their first cardiac catheterization with suspected ischemic heart disease but angiographically normal coronaries.
RESULTS:
Our analysis included 32,856 patients, of which 7.1% were men and 23.3% were women. Notably, women were older and more likely to have hypertension, prior stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and peripheral vascular disease compared to men, but the Canadian Cardiovascular Society class of angina did not vary by sex. Within 1 year, 1.0% of patients died (19 women and 18 men), and 0.6% had a stroke (13 women and 9 men), with no significant differences between sexes. However, readmission to hospital for ACS or chest pain requiring catheterization was significantly higher in women compared to men (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-14.31).
CONCLUSIONS:
Our findings suggest that women with angiographically normal coronaries are at higher risk of rehospitalization for ACS or chest pain compared to men, with important social and economic implications. These findings highlight the need for alternative diagnostic approaches for women, as traditional methods may not be optimal for this gender.

title: Keratin-dependent regulation of Aire and gene expression in skin tumor keratinocytes
text: The expression of the intermediate filament protein keratin 17 (K17) is significantly increased in inflammatory skin diseases and many tumors originating in stratified and pseudostratified epithelia. We have found that autoimmune regulator (Aire), a transcriptional regulator, is inducibly expressed in human and mouse tumor keratinocytes in a K17-dependent manner, and is necessary for the timely onset of Gli2-induced skin tumorigenesis in mice. The induction of Aire mRNA in keratinocytes depends on a functional interaction between K17 and the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein hnRNP K. Additionally, K17 colocalizes with Aire protein in the nucleus of tumor-prone keratinocytes, and each factor is bound to a specific promoter region featuring an NF-κB consensus sequence in a relevant subset of K17- and Aire-dependent proinflammatory genes. These findings provide novel insights into the role of keratin intermediate filaments and Aire in disease, as well as a molecular basis for the K17-dependent amplification of inflammatory and immune responses in diseased epithelia.

title: Flow-Dependent Regulation of Kruppel-Like Factor 2 Is Mediated by MicroRNA-92a.
text:
Background:
Upregulated by atheroprotective flow, the transcription factor Krüppel-like factor 2 (KLF2) plays a crucial role in maintaining endothelial function. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), non-coding small RNAs, have been shown to regulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level. In this study, we investigate the role of miRNAs, particularly miR-92a, in the atheroprotective flow-regulated KLF2.
Methods and Results:
We examined the effect of miRNAs on KLF2 expression in human umbilical vein endothelial cells using Dicer knockdown, which increased KLF2 mRNA levels. In silico analysis predicted that miR-92a could bind to the 3' untranslated region of KLF2 mRNA. Overexpression of miR-92a decreased KLF2 and its target genes, endothelial nitric oxide synthase and thrombomodulin, at both mRNA and protein levels. Conversely, inhibition of miR-92a increased KLF2 and its target genes. Subsequent studies revealed that atheroprotective laminar flow downregulated miR-92a precursor levels, leading to increased KLF2 expression. This flow-induced KLF2 was found to be reduced by miR-92a precursor. Additionally, miR-92a levels were lower in human umbilical vein endothelial cells exposed to atheroprotective pulsatile shear flow compared to atheroprone oscillatory shear flow. Immunoprecipitation coupled with real-time polymerase chain reaction revealed that pulsatile shear flow decreased the functional targeting of miR-92a precursor/KLF2 mRNA in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Consistently, mice receiving miR-92a precursor exhibited impaired vasodilatory response to flow.
Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that atheroprotective flow patterns decrease miR-92a levels, leading to increased KLF2 expression and maintenance of endothelial homeostasis.

title: Effectiveness of a diabetes education and self management programme (DESMOND) for people with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus: three year follow-up of a cluster randomised controlled trial in primary care
text:
Objective: To assess the sustainability of the benefits of a structured education and self-management program for individuals with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus over a three-year period.
Design: A three-year follow-up of a multicentre cluster randomized controlled trial conducted in primary care settings in the United Kingdom.
Setting: 207 general practices in 13 primary care sites.
Participants: Of the original 824 participants, 731 were eligible for follow-up, with biomedical data collected on 604 (82.6%) and questionnaire data on 513 (70.1%) participants.
Intervention: A structured group education program delivered in the community by two trained healthcare professional educators compared to usual care.
Main Outcome Measures: The primary outcome was glycated hemoglobin (HbA(1c)) levels, and secondary outcomes included blood pressure, weight, blood lipid levels, smoking status, physical activity, quality of life, beliefs about illness, depression, emotional impact of diabetes, and drug use at three years.
Results: At three years, HbA(1c) levels had decreased in both groups, but the difference was not significant after adjusting for baseline and cluster (difference -0.02, 95% confidence interval -0.22 to 0.17). The groups did not differ for the other biomedical and lifestyle outcomes and drug use. However, sustained improvements were observed in four out of five health beliefs in the intervention group compared to the control group (P<0.01). Depression scores and quality of life did not differ at three years.
Conclusion: A single structured education and self-management program for individuals with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus did not show significant differences in biomedical or lifestyle outcomes at three years, although there were sustained improvements in some illness beliefs.
Trial Registration: Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN17844016.

title: Acetylation of Histone H3 Lysine 56 Regulates Replication-Coupled Nucleosome Assembly
text:
Chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1) and Rtt106 play a crucial role in the deposition of newly synthesized histones onto replicating DNA to form nucleosomes. This process is essential for maintaining genome stability and inheriting functionally specialized chromatin structures in proliferating cells. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the acetylation of newly synthesized histones in this DNA replication-coupled nucleosome assembly pathway remain unclear.
Our study reveals that histone H3 acetylated at lysine 56 (H3K56Ac) is incorporated onto replicating DNA and enhances the ability of CAF-1 and Rtt106 to assemble DNA into nucleosomes. Genetic analysis indicates that H3K56Ac acts in a nonredundant manner with the acetylation of the N-terminal residues of H3 and H4 in nucleosome assembly. These findings uncover a regulatory mechanism by which H3K56Ac modulates replication-coupled nucleosome assembly mediated by CAF-1 and Rtt106.
In summary, our study provides insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying the deposition of newly synthesized histones onto replicating DNA to form nucleosomes, highlighting the importance of H3K56Ac in this process. These findings have significant implications for our understanding of the mechanisms that maintain genome stability and inheritance of functionally specialized chromatin structures in proliferating cells.

title: Selective inhibition of Ras-dependent cell growth by farnesylthiosalisylic acid.
text: S-trans,trans-Farnesylthiosalicylic acid (FTS) is a novel farnesylated carboxylic acid derivative that acts as a potent competitive inhibitor of the enzyme prenylated protein methyltransferase (PPMTase) in cell-free systems, with a Ki value of 2.6 microM. PPMTase methylates the carboxyl-terminal S-prenylcysteine in a wide range of prenylated proteins, including Ras. In contrast to cell-free systems, relatively high concentrations of FTS (50-100 microM) are required to inhibit protein methylation in intact cells, indicating that FTS is a weak inhibitor of methylation in these systems. Despite this, FTS reduces the levels of Ras in cell membranes and inhibits Ras-dependent cell growth in vitro, independently of methylation. The drug also inhibits the growth of human Ha-ras-transformed cells (EJ cells) and reverses their transformed morphology in a dose-dependent manner. Interestingly, FTS does not interfere with the growth of cells transformed by v-Raf or T-antigen, but inhibits the growth of ErbB2-transformed cells and blocks the mitogenic effects of epidermal and basic fibroblast growth factors. These results suggest that FTS may specifically interfere with the interaction of Ras with a farnesylcysteine recognition domain in the cell membrane, and raise the possibility that FTS may be a useful tool for modulating Ras growth signaling.

title: NADPH oxidase controls phagosomal pH and antigen cross-presentation in human dendritic cells.
text: The phagocyte NADPH oxidase (NOX2) plays a crucial role in the bactericidal activity of phagocytic cells and is a key component of innate immunity. Recent studies have shown that NOX2 activity in mouse dendritic cells (DCs) prevents the acidification of phagosomes, thereby promoting antigen cross-presentation. To investigate the role of NOX2 in the regulation of phagosomal pH in human DCs, we analyzed the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and phagosomal/endosomal pH in monocyte-derived DCs and macrophages (M(diameter)s) from healthy donors and patients with chronic granulomatous disease (CGD). Our findings revealed that human M(diameter)s are more efficient at acidifying their phagosomes than human DCs, which is accompanied by higher expression of the vacuolar proton ATPase (V-H(+)-ATPase). Interestingly, despite the lower pH in M(diameter)s, phagosomal ROS production was higher in these cells due to increased gp91phox expression and recruitment to phagosomes. In contrast, in the absence of NOX2 activity, the phagosomal and endosomal pH decreased. Moreover, impairment of antigen cross-presentation was observed in both the presence of a NOX2 inhibitor and in DCs derived from patients with CGD. These results suggest that NOX2 activity plays a critical role in regulating the phagosomal and endosomal pH in human DCs and is essential for efficient antigen cross-presentation.

title: Activation of fast skeletal muscle troponin as a potential therapeutic approach for treating neuromuscular diseases
text: The limited neural input in neuromuscular diseases leads to muscle weakness due to a reduction in the density of muscle innervation, the rate of neuromuscular junction activation, or the efficiency of synaptic transmission. To address this issue, we have developed a small-molecule fast-skeletal-troponin activator, CK-2017357, which amplifies the muscular response when neural input is diminished. By selectively binding to the fast-skeletal-troponin complex, CK-2017357 slows the rate of calcium release from troponin C and sensitizes muscle to calcium, resulting in a leftward shift of the force-calcium relationship and the force-frequency relationship of nerve-muscle pairs. This leads to an increase in muscle force production at sub-maximal nerve stimulation rates. Notably, we have demonstrated that sensitization of the fast-skeletal-troponin complex to calcium improves muscle force and grip strength immediately after administration of single doses of CK-2017357 in a model of the neuromuscular disease myasthenia gravis. Our findings suggest that troponin activation may represent a promising new therapeutic approach to enhance physical activity in diseases where neuromuscular function is compromised.

title: Cortactin regulates cofilin and N-WASp activities to control the stages of invadopodium assembly and maturation
text: Invadopodia are protrusions on the surface of invasive cancer cells that degrade the surrounding matrix. The mechanisms controlling their formation and maturation are not well understood. By dissecting the stages of invadopodium assembly and maturation, we found that cortactin phosphorylation plays a crucial role in these processes. Specifically, cortactin phosphorylation regulates cofilin and Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin polymerization. Cortactin directly binds cofilin and inhibits its severing activity, but phosphorylation releases this inhibition, allowing cofilin to sever actin filaments and create barbed ends at invadopodia. After barbed end formation, cortactin is dephosphorylated, which stabilizes invadopodia by blocking cofilin severing activity. These findings reveal novel mechanisms of actin polymerization in invadopodia and define four distinct stages of invadopodium assembly and maturation: invadopodium precursor formation, actin polymerization, stabilization, and matrix degradation.

title: Calreticulin exposure dictates the immunogenicity of cancer cell death
text: Anthracyclin-treated cancer cells are particularly effective in triggering an immune response against the tumor, whereas other drugs like etoposide and mitomycin C do not induce the same immune response. We found that anthracyclins cause the rapid surface exposure of a protein called calreticulin (CRT) on cancer cells. When CRT is blocked or reduced, the ability of dendritic cells to engulf and present anthracyclin-treated cancer cells to the immune system is impaired, and their immunogenicity is lost in mice. We discovered that the anthracyclin-induced CRT translocation can be mimicked by inhibiting a protein complex called protein phosphatase 1/GADD34. Treating cancer cells with recombinant CRT or inhibitors of protein phosphatase 1/GADD34 restored the immunogenicity of cell death induced by etoposide and mitomycin C in mice, and enhanced their antitumor effects. These findings identify CRT as a crucial factor in determining the immune response to cancer cells and suggest a potential strategy for immunogenic chemotherapy.

title: In vivo disruption of Xenopus U3 snRNA affects ribosomal RNA processing.
text: DNA oligonucleotides complementary to sequences in the 5' third of U3 snRNA were injected into Xenopus oocyte nuclei to disrupt endogenous U3 snRNA. The effect of this treatment on rRNA processing was then examined. Our findings revealed that some toads have a single rRNA processing pathway, while in others, two pathways can coexist within a single oocyte. Disruption of U3 snRNA in toads with a single rRNA processing pathway led to a reduction in 20S and '32S' pre-rRNA. In contrast, in toads with two rRNA processing pathways, an increase in '36S' pre-rRNA of the second pathway was observed. This study provides the first in vivo evidence that U3 snRNA plays a role in rRNA processing. Cleavage site #3 is located at the boundary of ITS 1 and 5.8S, and it links all of the affected rRNA intermediates. 20S and '32S' are the products of site #3 cleavage in the first pathway, while '36S' is the substrate for cleavage at site #3 in the second pathway. Based on our findings, we propose that U3 snRNP folds pre-rRNA into a conformation that dictates correct cleavage at processing site #3.

title: A genome-wide siRNA screen reveals diverse cellular processes and pathways that mediate genome stability.
text: Signaling pathways that respond to DNA damage are crucial for maintaining genome stability and are implicated in various diseases, including cancer. To identify additional genes involved in genome stabilization, we conducted a genome-wide siRNA screen by monitoring phosphorylation of the histone variant H2AX, an early marker of DNA damage. Our findings revealed hundreds of genes whose downregulation led to increased levels of H2AX phosphorylation (gammaH2AX), and we uncovered links to cellular complexes and genes with unclassified functions. We discovered a widespread role for mRNA-processing factors in preventing DNA damage, which in some cases is caused by aberrant RNA-DNA structures. Furthermore, we found that elevated gammaH2AX levels are associated with the neurological disorder Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) syndrome, and we identified a role for several CMT proteins in the DNA-damage response. These results demonstrate that preserving genome stability is mediated by a broader network of biological processes than previously appreciated.

title: Alphavbeta6-Fyn signaling promotes oral cancer progression.
text:
In our previous research, we demonstrated that the integrin beta6 is overexpressed in invasive oral squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and is correlated with the progression of oral tumors. However, the mechanism by which beta6 promotes oral cancer progression is not well understood. To investigate this, we aimed to determine whether integrin beta6 signaling activates Fyn and contributes to oral SCC progression.
Our study found that upon binding of beta6 to fibronectin, beta6 complexes with Fyn and activates it. This activation of Fyn recruits and activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK) to the complex. This complex is essential for activating the Shc protein and coupling beta6 signaling to the Raf-ERK/MAPK pathway. This pathway ultimately leads to the transcriptional activation of the matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) gene, promoting oral SCC cell proliferation and experimental metastasis in vivo.
Our findings suggest that integrin beta6 signaling activates Fyn, which in turn promotes oral cancer progression. This discovery provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying oral cancer development and may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of this disease.

title: miRNA-dependent gene silencing involving Ago2-mediated cleavage of a circular antisense RNA.
text:
MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that typically bind to the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of target messenger RNAs (mRNAs) in the cytoplasm, leading to mRNA degradation and translational repression. However, recent studies have shown that miRNAs can also regulate gene expression by targeting non-coding antisense transcripts. In this study, we investigate the role of miRNAs in regulating gene expression by targeting antisense transcripts in human cells.
We demonstrate that miR-671 directs the cleavage of a circular antisense transcript of the Cerebellar Degeneration-Related protein 1 (CDR1) locus in an Ago2-slicer-dependent manner. The resulting downregulation of circular antisense has a concomitant decrease in CDR1 mRNA levels, independent of heterochromatin formation. Our findings provide the first evidence for non-coding antisense transcripts as functional miRNA targets and a novel regulatory mechanism involving a positive correlation between mRNA and antisense circular RNA levels.
In summary, our study shows that miRNAs can regulate gene expression by targeting non-coding antisense transcripts, providing a new mechanism for miRNA-mediated regulation of gene expression.

title: Regulation of Serum Amyloid A3 (SAA3) in Mouse Colonic Epithelium and Adipose Tissue by the Intestinal Microbiota
text: The gut microbiota has been implicated as an environmental factor that contributes to the development of metabolic and inflammatory diseases in mammals. Recent studies have shown that gut bacteria-derived lipopolysaccharide (LPS) can trigger obesity and insulin resistance in mice, but the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. Hepatic serum amyloid A (SAA) proteins are markers of inflammation that have been found to be elevated in the serum of insulin-resistant mice, and adipose tissue-derived SAA3 has been shown to have monocyte chemotactic activity, suggesting a role in metabolic inflammation. To investigate the potential link between the gut microbiota and the induction of proinflammatory host factors, we performed molecular analyses of germ-free, conventionally raised, and genetically modified mouse models. Our results showed that SAA3 expression was significantly increased in adipose and colonic tissue in response to the presence of intestinal microbes. In the colon, we found that SAA3 expression was partially regulated by the Toll-like receptor (TLR)/MyD88/NF-κB signaling axis. We identified epithelial cells and macrophages as the main cellular sources of SAA3 in the colon, and found that colonic epithelial expression of SAA3 may be part of an NF-κB-dependent response to LPS from gut bacteria. In vitro experiments showed that LPS treatments of both epithelial cells and macrophages led to increased SAA3 expression. Our data suggest that LPS, and potentially other products of the gut microbiota, may contribute to chronic low-grade inflammation observed in obesity by elevating cytokine expression in tissues.

title: Reversing the tide — diagnosis and prevention of T2DM in populations of African descent
text:
Populations of African descent are disproportionately affected by the global epidemic of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Delayed diagnosis exacerbates the burden of the disease, leading to preventable complications and reduced health outcomes. Early detection and intervention could significantly reduce the prevalence of undiagnosed T2DM, improve disease statistics, and allocate resources more effectively. However, a crucial factor hindering accurate diagnosis in these populations is the suboptimal performance of screening tests, such as fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c, in detecting hyperglycaemia. To address this challenge, combining tests or incorporating non-fasting markers like glycated albumin may be a viable solution.
However, it is important to recognize that individuals of African, Caribbean, or African-American descent exhibit distinct differences in diet, exercise, body mass index (BMI), environmental factors, gene-environment interactions, and sickle cell trait, which impact the effectiveness of diagnostic tests and interventions. While intensive lifestyle interventions have been shown to be effective in primary prevention of T2DM in the African-American population, they have not been as successful in secondary prevention. The lack of health literacy and poor glycemic control in Africa and the Caribbean underscores the need for customized lifestyle interventions that can achieve both primary and secondary prevention.
In conclusion, diagnosis and prevention of T2DM require tailored strategies that take into account the unique characteristics of populations of African descent. By developing innovative approaches that account for this diversity, we can improve health outcomes and reduce the burden of T2DM in these communities.

title: Biofeedback and relaxation in the treatment of migraine headaches: comparative effectiveness and physiological correlates.
text: Twenty-seven patients with migraine headaches were divided into three groups and received different types of biofeedback training: thermal biofeedback, frontalis EMG biofeedback, or relaxation training. The training was conducted under "massed" practice conditions (nine sessions per week) and consisted of 18 training sessions and six test-generalization sessions. While improvements in headaches were observed in all groups, the thermal biofeedback group exhibited the most significant improvements, with almost complete elimination of migraine attacks by the end of training and maintenance of that performance for at least six months after training.
