Analysis of skin temperature and EMG changes in the three groups throughout the training period also suggests a relationship between skin temperature control and reduction in migraine headache symptoms, and warrants further investigation.

title: Fine-scale chromatin interaction maps reveal the cis-regulatory landscape of human lincRNA genes
text: High-resolution methods based on chromosome conformation capture have revolutionized our understanding of the three-dimensional (3D) organization of genomes, but are limited by their reliance on restriction enzymes. Here, we present a novel approach called DNase Hi-C, which utilizes DNase I for chromatin fragmentation, resulting in significantly improved efficiency and resolution compared to traditional Hi-C methods. By combining DNase Hi-C with DNA-capture technology, we have developed a high-throughput approach for targeted mapping of fine-scale chromatin architecture. We applied this method to investigate the 3D organization of 998 large intergenic noncoding RNA (lincRNA) promoters in two human cell lines. Our findings reveal that the expression of lincRNAs is tightly regulated by complex mechanisms involving both super-enhancers and the Polycomb repressive complex. Our study provides the first comprehensive view of the cell type-specific 3D organization of lincRNA genes.

title: BASOPHILS AND THE T HELPER 2 ENVIRONMENT CAN PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF LUPUS NEPHRITIS
text: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), self-reactive antibodies can target the kidney (lupus nephritis), leading to functional failure and possible mortality. Our study reveals that the activation of basophils by autoreactive IgE leads to their migration to lymph nodes, promoting the differentiation of T helper type 2 (T(H)2) cells and enhancing the production of self-reactive antibodies that cause lupus-like nephritis in mice lacking the Src family protein tyrosine kinase Lyn (Lyn(-/-) mice). Individuals with SLE also exhibit elevated serum IgE, self-reactive IgEs, and activated basophils that express CD62 ligand (CD62L) and the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecule human leukocyte antigen-DR (HLA-DR), which are associated with increased disease activity and active lupus nephritis. Furthermore, basophils were found in the lymph nodes and spleen of subjects with SLE. Our findings suggest that in Lyn(-/-) mice, basophils and IgE autoantibodies amplify autoantibody production that leads to lupus nephritis, and in individuals with SLE, IgE autoantibodies and activated basophils are factors associated with disease activity and nephritis.

title: Behavioral treatment of obesity in patients encountered in primary care settings: a systematic review.
text:
In 2011, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) approved intensive behavioral weight loss counseling for obese patients in primary care settings. This counseling involved 14 face-to-face sessions lasting 10-15 minutes each over a period of 6 months, delivered by physicians or other primary care practitioners.
Our systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of behavioral counseling for overweight and obese patients recruited from primary care settings, delivered by primary care practitioners working alone or with trained interventionists. We searched multiple databases for randomized controlled trials published between 1980 and 2014, meeting specific inclusion criteria.
Our findings revealed 12 trials involving 3893 participants, with intervention groups showing weight changes ranging from a loss of 0.3 kg to 6.6 kg at 6 months, while control groups showed a range of weight changes from a gain of 0.9 kg to a loss of 2.0 kg. Weight loss generally decreased with longer follow-up periods (12-24 months). Interventions that included both reduced energy intake and increased physical activity, along with traditional behavioral therapy, were found to produce larger weight loss than interventions without these components. Additionally, more treatment sessions, delivered in person or by telephone by trained interventionists, were associated with greater mean weight loss and likelihood of patients losing 5% or more of their baseline weight.
Our findings suggest that primary care practitioners could potentially play a role in delivering intensive behavioral counseling for obese patients, with trained interventionists delivering counseling in person or by telephone. However, there is a need for more research on the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Guanylate binding protein 1 is a novel effector of EGFR-driven invasion in glioblastoma
text: Although GBP1 (guanylate binding protein 1) was one of the first interferon-inducible proteins identified, its function remains largely unknown. However, recent studies have shown that EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor) activation is a common genetic alteration in various human tumors, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). GBM is characterized by a combination of features, including extensive invasion into normal brain tissue, rapid growth, necrosis, and angiogenesis. In this study, we found that EGFR activation increases GBP1 expression in GBM cell lines through a signaling pathway involving Src and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase. We also identified YY1 (Yin Yang 1) as the downstream transcriptional regulator that regulates EGFR-driven GBP1 expression. GBP1 is required for EGFR-mediated MMP1 (matrix metalloproteinase 1) expression and glioma cell invasion in vitro. Interestingly, deregulation of GBP1 expression does not affect glioma cell proliferation, but overexpression of GBP1 enhances glioma cell invasion through MMP1 induction, which is independent of its GTPase activity. Furthermore, reducing GBP1 levels by RNA interference in invasive GBM cells significantly inhibits their ability to infiltrate the brain parenchyma of mice. GBP1 expression is high and positively correlated with EGFR expression in human GBM tumors and cell lines, particularly those of the neural subtype. These findings suggest that GBP1 may be a previously unknown link between EGFR activity and MMP1 expression, and nominate it as a potential therapeutic target for inhibiting GBM invasion.

title: ATP binding to PAN or the 26S ATPases causes association with the 20S proteasome, gate opening, and translocation of unfolded proteins.
text: The archaeal ATPase complex PAN, a homolog of the eukaryotic 26S proteasome-regulatory ATPases, was shown to transiently associate with the 20S proteasome upon binding of ATP or ATPgammaS, but not ADP. Using electron microscopy (EM), PAN was observed as a two-ring structure capping the 20S proteasome, resembling two densities in the 19S complex. The N termini of the archaeal 20S alpha subunits were found to function as a gate that restricts the entry of seven-residue peptides while allowing the entry of tetrapeptides. Upon association with the 20S particle, PAN stimulates gate opening. Although degradation of globular proteins requires ATP hydrolysis, the PAN-20S complex with ATPgammaS can translocate and degrade unfolded and denatured proteins without hydrolyzing ATP. Interestingly, rabbit 26S proteasomes were also found to degrade these unfolded proteins upon binding of ATP, without hydrolyzing ATP. These findings suggest that unfolding of proteins requires energy from ATP hydrolysis, but ATP binding alone is sufficient to support the association of the ATPase with the 20S particle, gate opening, and the translocation of unfolded substrates into the proteasome, which can occur through facilitated diffusion through the ATPase.

title: Cytokines and anti-cytokine biologicals in autoimmunity: present and future.
text: The growing recognition of cytokines' crucial role in autoimmune disorders, particularly the central part played by tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFalpha) in the inflammatory and destructive processes common to various human autoimmune diseases, has led to the development of a new generation of therapeutics: TNFalpha blocking agents. In this article, we will examine the current understanding of cytokines' role in autoimmunity, as revealed by both laboratory and clinical studies. We will also discuss the potential future directions of anti-TNFalpha therapy, which may involve combination therapy with other anti-cytokine or anti-T cell agents, or the use of small molecules targeting molecules involved in TNFalpha production, such as NF-κB and p38 MAPK. The future developments in anti-TNFalpha and anti-cytokine therapy are likely to be exciting.

title: Vegetarian dietary patterns and mortality in Adventist Health Study 2.
text: The study investigated the relationship between vegetarian dietary patterns and mortality in a large North American cohort of Seventh-day Adventist men and women. The study found that individuals who followed a vegetarian diet had a lower risk of death from all causes, as well as from specific causes such as cardiovascular disease, non-cardiovascular non-cancer disease, renal disease, and endocrine disease, compared to non-vegetarians. The association between vegetarian diets and lower mortality was found to be more pronounced in men than in women. The study suggests that vegetarian diets may be a useful strategy for reducing the risk of death from various causes.

title: TEAD mediates YAP-dependent gene induction and growth control.
text: The transcriptional coactivator YAP (Yes-associated protein) has been linked to cancer development, with amplification observed in various human tumors. Recent research has shown that YAP is phosphorylated and inhibited by the Hippo tumor suppressor pathway. Our study uncovers the essential role of the TEAD family of transcription factors in mediating YAP-dependent gene expression. TEAD is also crucial for YAP-induced cell growth, oncogenic transformation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. We identify CTGF (connective tissue growth factor) as a direct YAP target gene involved in cell growth. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the functional relationship between YAP and TEAD is conserved in Drosophila Yki (the YAP homolog) and Scalloped (the TEAD homolog). Our study reveals TEAD as a critical component of the Hippo pathway, playing essential roles in mediating the biological functions of YAP.

title: Direct isolation of human central nervous system stem cells.
text: Stem cells, which possess the unique ability to self-renew and differentiate into multiple cell types, hold great promise for repairing or replacing damaged tissue. We have successfully isolated and characterized clonogenic human central nervous system stem cells (hCNS-SC) from fresh human fetal brain tissue using antibodies and fluorescence-activated cell sorting. These hCNS-SC are identified as 5F3 (CD133)(+) cells, which are negative for CD34, CD45, and CD24. Further analysis revealed that single 5F3(+) cells can initiate neurosphere cultures and give rise to both neurons and glial cells. Remarkably, when single 5F3(+) cells were replated as single cells, they were able to reestablish neurosphere cultures, indicating their self-renewal potential. Following transplantation into immunodeficient neonatal mice, the sorted/expanded hCNS-SC demonstrated potent engraftment, proliferation, migration, and neural differentiation.

title: p53 mutation in breast cancer. Correlation with cell kinetics and cell of origin.
text:
Several studies have investigated the expression of cytokeratins (CKs), vimentin, the epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR), the oestrogen receptor (ER), and the progesterone receptor (PgR) in breast cancer, but no study has directly compared p53 mutations with these phenotypic and differentiation markers in the same case. To address this gap in knowledge, the present study was designed to evaluate the expression of p53 and bcl-2 proteins in relation to phenotypic characteristics and cellular kinetic parameters (mitotic index and apoptotic index) in 37 cases of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and 27 cases of infiltrating ductal carcinoma (IDC) of the breast. In addition, p53 gene mutation was examined by polymerase chain reaction single strand conformation polymorphism (SSCP) analysis.
The results of the study showed that 13 cases (eight DCIS and five IDC) expressed CK8, CK14, CK18, vimentin, and EGFR, indicating a stem cell phenotype. In contrast, 44 cases (27 DCIS and 17 IDC) expressed CK8 and CK1, with weak or negative expression of CK18, and were negative for vimentin and EGFR, indicating a luminal cell phenotype. DCIS and IDC cases with a stem cell phenotype were ER/PgR negative and intermediate or poorly differentiated, while the cases with a luminal cell phenotype were ER/PgR positive and well or intermediate differentiated. The study also found that intermediate or poorly differentiated cases with a stem cell phenotype had higher proliferative activity (percentage of MIB-1 positive cells) than intermediate or well-differentiated cases with a luminal cell phenotype. Both DCIS and IDC cases with a stem cell phenotype were p53 positive and bcl-2 negative by immunohistochemistry. In IDC, p53 expression was associated with a reduction in both mitotic index and apoptotic index compared to DCIS. Most of the tumors showing a more differentiated phenotype (luminal) were p53 negative and bcl-2 positive. In these cases, cell kinetic parameters increased from DCIS to IDC. These findings suggest that there are subsets of DCIS and IDC that, due to their phenotypic characteristics, may be derived from subpopulations of normal breast cells with different control mechanisms of cell proliferation and neoplastic progression. However, the occurrence of p53 mutations by chance during neoplastic transformation cannot be excluded.

title: Cardiorespiratory fitness and body mass index as predictors of cardiovascular disease mortality among men with diabetes.
text:
Background: Despite the established relationship between cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) and reduced cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, questions persist regarding the impact of CRF on CVD mortality in overweight and obese individuals with diabetes. This study aimed to investigate the independent and joint associations of CRF and body mass index (BMI) with CVD mortality in men with diabetes.
Methods: This prospective observational study utilized data from the Aerobics Center Longitudinal Study, which included 2316 men with no prior history of stroke or myocardial infarction and diagnosed with diabetes (mean age: 50 years; SD: 10 years). Participants underwent a maximal exercise test and had their BMI calculated. The main outcome measure was CVD mortality across different levels of CRF, with stratification by BMI.
Results: During a mean follow-up period of 15.9 years (SD: 7.9 years), 179 CVD deaths were identified. In a multivariate model adjusted for age, examination year, fasting glucose level, systolic blood pressure, parental history of premature CVD, total cholesterol level, cigarette smoking, and abnormal resting and exercise electrocardiograms, men with a low CRF level were found to have a significantly higher adjusted risk of mortality compared to normal weight men with a high CRF level (hazard ratio: 2.7; 95% confidence interval: 1.3-5.7). This association persisted across different BMI categories, including normal weight (hazard ratio: 2.7; 95% confidence interval: 1.4-5.1), overweight (hazard ratio: 2.7; 95% confidence interval: 1.4-5.1), and class 1 obese (hazard ratio: 2.8; 95% confidence interval: 1.4-5.1).
Conclusion: This study found that low CRF level was associated with an increased risk of CVD mortality within normal weight, overweight, and class 1 obese weight categories in men with diabetes. These findings suggest that CRF may play a crucial role in reducing CVD mortality in overweight and obese individuals with diabetes, highlighting the importance of regular physical activity in this population.

title: Effect of screening on cervical cancer mortality in England and Wales: analysis of trends with an age period cohort model.
text: In 1997, the number of women dying from cervical cancer was 7% lower than in 1996, and had decreased by over 25% since 1992. This significant decline is likely due to the implementation of cervical screening programs, although other factors such as cohort effects may also play a role. To better understand the impact of cervical screening on cervical cancer mortality, we analyzed mortality data from England and Wales, taking into account the effects of age and year of birth. We modeled the data using a statistical model that accounted for the age-specific mortality rate being the product of a smoothly varying age effect, birth cohort effect, and age-dependent effect. By doing so, we were able to estimate the beneficial effects of cervical screening on cervical cancer mortality. Our analysis revealed that mortality rates have been declining since 1993, with a 4% upward adjustment made to account for changes in cause of death classification. Overall, our findings suggest that cervical screening has had a significant impact on reducing cervical cancer mortality in England and Wales.

title: The regulation of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors by Src kinase.
text: Src family kinases (SFKs) play a crucial role in regulating various cellular functions by interacting with growth factors, G-protein-coupled receptors, and ligand-gated ion channels. Recent research has shown that SFKs serve as a convergence point for multiple signaling pathways, influencing N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in the central nervous system. Multiple SFK molecules, such as Src and Fyn, bind to their substrate, NMDA receptors, through both indirect and direct mechanisms. The NMDA receptor is part of an SFK signaling complex consisting of SFKs, protein tyrosine phosphatase α, and C-terminal Src kinase. Early studies have demonstrated that intramolecular interactions within the SH2 or SH3 domain can lock SFKs in a closed conformation. Disrupting these interdomain interactions can lead to the activation of SFKs, involving multiple signaling pathways in the regulation of this process. The enzyme activity of SFKs exhibits a graded response, with different levels corresponding to activation states. It has also been proposed that the SH2 and SH3 domains may enhance the catalytic activity of protein tyrosine kinases, such as Abl. Recent findings have shown that the stability of neuronal Src protein is associated with its enzyme activity, and that the SH2 and SH3 domain interactions not only regulate the activation of neuronal Src but also influence the enzyme activity of active neuronal Src. These discoveries reveal novel mechanisms underlying the regulation of SFKs.

title: The art and design of genetic screens: RNA interference
text: The revolutionary gene knockdown technique of RNAi has unlocked novel opportunities for genetic screens in model organisms and human cells. In this article, we will discuss the current state-of-the-art for RNAi screening and the significance of carefully designed assays and sophisticated analytical approaches for large-scale screening experiments, ranging from high-throughput screens using simplified homogeneous assays to microscopy and whole-animal experiments. Similarly to classical genetic screens of the past, the success of extensive RNAi surveys hinges on the development of precise phenotypic assays and their interpretation within a meaningful biological context.

title: Computer assisted learning in undergraduate medical education.
text:
It is widely acknowledged that the education of undergraduate medical students will be enhanced through the use of computer-assisted learning. Access to a wide range of online options, as illustrated in the figure, is expected to make learning more exciting, effective, and likely to be retained. However, this assumption is not necessarily correct and requires careful consideration.
Box 1: Why fund computer-assisted learning?
Computer-assisted learning is an inevitable trend in medical education. Individual lecturers and departments are already introducing various computer-based applications, often in a haphazard manner. Planned and coordinated development is preferable to indiscriminate expansion.
1. Convenience and flexibility: Computer-assisted learning applications can reduce the need for face-to-face lectures and seminars, making it easier for students at peripheral hospitals or primary care centers to participate.
2. Unique presentational benefits: Computer-based presentations are particularly suited to visually intensive, detail-oriented, and difficult-to-conceptualize subjects, such as complex biochemical processes or microscopic images. Additionally, "virtual" cases can reduce the need for animal or human tissue in learning.
3. Personalized learning: Each learner can progress at their own pace, repeating, interrupting, and resuming as needed, which can be particularly beneficial for weaker students.
4. Economies of scale: Once an application is set up, the incremental cost of offering it to additional students is relatively small.
5. Competitive advantage: A "leading edge" virtual campus may attract top students, as they value the quality of information technology in their education.
6. Achieves the ultimate goal of higher education: The goal of higher education is to link people into learning communities. Computer applications, especially the internet and world wide web, are an efficient way of doing this.
7. Expands pedagogical horizons: The most controversial argument for computer-assisted learning is that it can expand the pedagogical horizons of medical education, allowing for new and innovative teaching methods that were previously impossible.

title: Combined Impact of Health Behaviours and Mortality in Men and Women: The EPIC-Norfolk Prospective Population Study
text:
BACKGROUND: There is overwhelming evidence that health behaviors have a significant impact on an individual's health, but the cumulative effect of these behaviors on mortality in the general population is not well understood. To address this gap in knowledge, we aimed to quantify the combined impact of four health behaviors on mortality in men and women living in the general community.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a prospective study of 20,244 men and women aged 45-79 years who were free of cardiovascular disease and cancer at the baseline survey in 1993-1997. Participants were followed up to 2006, with an average follow-up period of 11 years. We assessed four health behaviors: current non-smoking, physical activity, moderate alcohol consumption (1-14 units per week), and fruit and vegetable intake (plasma vitamin C level >50 mmol/l indicating intake of at least five servings per day). Participants were awarded a score of one point for each health behavior they engaged in, with a maximum score of four. We found that the age-, sex-, body mass-, and social class-adjusted relative risks (95% confidence intervals) for all-cause mortality (1,987 deaths) were significantly higher for individuals who had three, two, one, and zero compared to four health behaviors. Specifically, the relative risks were 1.39 (1.21-1.60), 1.95 (1.70-2.25), 2.52 (2.13-3.00), and 4.04 (2.95-5.54), respectively. These trends were consistent across subgroups stratified by sex, age, body mass index, and social class, and after excluding deaths within the first two years of follow-up. The strongest trends were observed for cardiovascular causes of death. Our findings suggest that the combination of four health behaviors predicts a 4-fold difference in total mortality in men and women, equivalent to being 14 years younger in chronological age.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides evidence that the combination of four health behaviors has a significant impact on mortality in the general population. Specifically, we found that individuals who engaged in four health behaviors had a 4-fold lower risk of mortality compared to those who engaged in none. These findings highlight the importance of promoting multiple health behaviors to reduce the burden of premature mortality in the general population.

title: Increased Cell Bond Tension Governs Cell Sorting at the Drosophila Anteroposterior Compartment Boundary
text:
The division of proliferating tissues into compartments is a conserved strategy throughout animal development (1-6). Signals across these boundaries can lead to the local expression of secreted proteins, which in turn organize growth and patterning of tissues. The presence of sharp and straight interfaces between compartments is crucial for maintaining the position of these organizers and ensuring the accurate implementation of body plans. However, the mechanisms that maintain boundaries in proliferating tissues are not well understood.
In this study, we used quantitative analysis of cell morphology and the response to laser ablation of cell bonds in the vicinity of the anteroposterior compartment boundary in developing Drosophila wings to investigate the mechanisms that maintain boundaries in proliferating tissues. We found that cell bonds along this compartment boundary exhibit approximately 2.5-fold higher mechanical tension compared to the remaining tissue. In addition, we found that the tension in cell bonds is reduced in the presence of Y-27632, an inhibitor of Rho-kinase, whose main effector is Myosin II. Using simulations using a vertex model, we demonstrated that a 2.5-fold increase in local cell bond tension is sufficient to guide the rearrangement of cells after cell division to maintain compartment boundaries.
Our findings provide a physical mechanism by which the local increase in Myosin II-dependent cell bond tension directs cell sorting at compartment boundaries, highlighting the importance of this mechanism in maintaining tissue organization and patterning during animal development.

title: Plant products as antimicrobial agents.
text: The surge in the use of plant-based drugs and dietary supplements has gained momentum in recent years, with ethnopharmacologists, botanists, microbiologists, and natural-products chemists working together to uncover phytochemicals and "leads" that could be developed into treatments for infectious diseases. While approximately 25-50% of current pharmaceuticals are derived from plants, none are used as antimicrobials. Traditional healers have long relied on plants to prevent or cure infectious conditions, and Western medicine is now seeking to replicate their successes. Plants are rich in a diverse array of secondary metabolites, including tannins, terpenoids, alkaloids, and flavonoids, which have been shown to have antimicrobial properties in vitro. This review aims to provide an overview of current botanical screening efforts, as well as in vivo studies of their effectiveness and toxicity. The structure and antimicrobial properties of phytochemicals are also discussed. As the use of these compounds is increasingly popular among the public, clinicians must consider the potential consequences of patients self-medicating with unregulated botanical preparations.

title: Nature, Nurture, or Chance: Stochastic Gene Expression and Its Consequences
text: Gene expression is inherently probabilistic, with random fluctuations in transcription and translation leading to cell-to-cell variations in mRNA and protein levels. This variability is observed across a wide range of organisms, from microbes to complex multicellular organisms, and is influenced by both the physical parameters that govern gene expression and the structure of the gene network. Stochastic gene expression has significant consequences for cellular function, with both beneficial and detrimental effects depending on the context. For example, it can be beneficial in situations such as the stress response, metabolism, development, the cell cycle, circadian rhythms, and aging.

title: Nuclear Hormone Receptor NHR-49 Controls Fat Consumption and Fatty Acid Composition in C. elegans
text: Mammalian nuclear hormone receptors (NHRs), such as liver X receptor, farnesoid X receptor, and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), play a crucial role in regulating energy metabolism. However, a comprehensive understanding of the regulatory networks involved in fat metabolism has been limited due to the lack of suitable experimental systems. Here, we investigate the role of NHRs in the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans and find that deletion of the NHR gene nhr-49 leads to increased fat content and shortened lifespan. Using a quantitative RT-PCR screen, we identify 13 genes involved in energy metabolism that are regulated by nhr-49. We find that nhr-49 acts as a key regulator of fat usage, modulating pathways that control fat consumption and fatty acid saturation. Interestingly, we observe two distinct phenotypes in the nhr-49 knockout: a high-fat phenotype due to reduced expression of enzymes involved in fatty acid β-oxidation, and a shortened adult life span resulting from impaired expression of a stearoyl-CoA desaturase. Despite their sequence similarity to mammalian hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 receptor, the biological activities of nhr-49 are most similar to those of mammalian PPARs, suggesting an evolutionarily conserved role for NHRs in regulating fat metabolism. Our findings provide novel insights into the coordinated regulation of NHR regulatory networks in governing fat metabolism.

title: Folate and vitamin B6 from diet and supplements in relation to risk of coronary heart disease among women.
text:
Title: High Intake of Folate and Vitamin B6 May Reduce Risk of Coronary Heart Disease Among Women
Background: Hyperhomocysteinemia, caused by genetic and lifestyle factors, including low intake of folate and vitamin B6, has been linked to an increased risk of CHD. However, there is limited data on the association between these nutrients and CHD risk in prospective studies.
Objective: To investigate the relationship between folate and vitamin B6 intake and the incidence of nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI) and fatal CHD among women.
Methods: This was a prospective cohort study of 80,008 women from the Nurses' Health Study who completed a detailed food frequency questionnaire to assess their usual intake of folate and vitamin B6. During 14 years of follow-up, 658 cases of nonfatal MI and 281 cases of fatal CHD were documented.
Results: After controlling for cardiovascular risk factors, including smoking and hypertension, and intake of alcohol, fiber, vitamin E, and saturated, polyunsaturated, and trans fats, the researchers found that women in the highest quintile of folate intake had a 31% lower risk of CHD compared to those in the lowest quintile. Similarly, women in the highest quintile of vitamin B6 intake had a 37% lower risk of CHD compared to those in the lowest quintile. The association between folate and vitamin B6 intake and CHD risk was strongest among women who did not regularly use multiple vitamins.
Conclusion: These findings suggest that high intake of folate and vitamin B6 may be important in the primary prevention of CHD among women.

title: Control of oocyte meiotic maturation and fertilization.
text: Sexual reproduction relies on meiosis to generate haploid gamete nuclei, which then fuse after fertilization to form a diploid zygote. In most animal species, oocytes undergo meiotic arrest during prophase and complete meiosis in response to intercellular signaling, a process known as meiotic maturation. This process is characterized by the transition between diakinesis and metaphase of meiosis I, accompanied by nuclear envelope breakdown, reorganization of the cortical cytoskeleton, and meiotic spindle assembly. Therefore, meiotic maturation is crucial for meiosis and prepares the oocyte for fertilization. In Caenorhabditis elegans, the processes of meiotic maturation, ovulation, and fertilization are temporally coupled, with sperm utilizing the major sperm protein as a hormone to trigger oocyte meiotic maturation, and the maturing oocyte signaling its own ovulation to facilitate fertilization. This chapter highlights recent advances in understanding the signaling mechanisms and gametic interactions required for fertilization.

title: From Cell Differentiation to Cell Collectives: Bacillus subtilis Uses Division of Labor to Migrate
text: The arrangement of cells, arising from cell-cell interactions, can lead to collective properties that are adaptive when cells work together to face environmental challenges. One crucial challenge for microorganisms is migration. In this study, we demonstrate how flagellum-independent migration is driven by the division of labor of two cell types that emerge during Bacillus subtilis sliding motility. Cell collectives self-organize into tightly aligned cell chains, forming filamentous loops at the colony edge. These loops migrate by pushing themselves away from the colony, a process that depends on the synergistic interaction of surfactin-producing and matrix-producing cells. We propose that surfactin-producing cells reduce friction between cells and their substrate, allowing matrix-producing cells to form bundles. The folding properties of these bundles determine the rate of colony expansion. Our findings highlight the importance of simple cell arrangements in yielding a strong ecological advantage, underscoring the diverse origins of multicellularity.

title: Tissue-resident macrophages self-maintain locally throughout adult life with minimal contribution from circulating monocytes.
text: Despite long-held beliefs, our research has revealed that tissue macrophages in the steady state are actually maintained locally, rather than being derived from monocytes. Using parabiosis and fate-mapping techniques, we found that monocytes do not significantly contribute to tissue macrophages in the steady state. Instead, we discovered that after depletion of lung macrophages, the majority of repopulation occurs through stochastic cellular proliferation in situ, dependent on macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-Csf) and granulocyte macrophage (GM)-CSF. Additionally, we found that host macrophages can expand and replace donor macrophages after bone marrow transplantation, even when the development of donor macrophages is compromised. This expansion is functional and prevents the development of alveolar proteinosis in mice transplanted with GM-Csf-receptor-deficient progenitors. Together, these results suggest that tissue-resident macrophages and circulating monocytes should be classified as distinct mononuclear phagocyte lineages that are maintained independently in the steady state.

title: Registration and real-time visualization of transcranial magnetic stimulation with 3-D MR images
text:
This paper presents a novel method for real-time registration and visualization of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) results on corresponding anatomical locations in magnetic resonance images (MRI) of the brain. The method involves three main steps:
1. The patient's scalp is digitized in physical space using a magnetic-field digitizer, following a specific digitization pattern.
2. A registration process minimizes the distance between the digitized points and a segmented scalp surface extracted from the MRI. This allows the physician to track the change in coil position in real-time and adjust it to the desired anatomical location.
3. The amplitude of motor evoked potentials is projected onto the segmented brain to create functional brain maps. The registration method achieves subpixel accuracy in simulations and a point-to-surface root-mean-square error of 1.17/spl plusmn/0.38 mm in a 24-subject study.
By combining these steps, the method enables accurate and efficient registration and visualization of TMS results in real-time, which can help improve the accuracy and effectiveness of TMS treatments.

title: Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
text: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAs) are characterized by a robust fibroinflammatory response, which generates elevated interstitial fluid pressures (IFPs) that exceed those previously measured or theorized for solid tumors. These high IFPs lead to vascular collapse and create significant barriers to the perfusion, diffusion, and convection of small molecule therapeutics. We identify hyaluronan, or hyaluronic acid (HA), as the primary matrix determinant of these barriers and demonstrate that systemic administration of an enzymatic agent can ablate stromal HA from autochthonous murine PDA, normalize IFP, and re-expand the microvasculature. In combination with the standard chemotherapeutic, gemcitabine, this treatment permanently remodels the tumor microenvironment and consistently achieves objective tumor responses, resulting in a near doubling of overall survival.

title: Circulating adiponectin, leptin and adiponectin-leptin ratio and endometrial cancer risk: Evidence from a meta-analysis of epidemiologic studies.
text:
In this meta-analysis, we investigated the associations between circulating adiponectin, leptin, and adiponectin-leptin (A/L) ratio and endometrial cancer risk by analyzing 14 manuscripts with 13 studies (five nested case-control and eight case-control studies) involving 1,963 endometrial cancer cases and 3,503 noncases. We used random-effects models to estimate summary odds ratios (SOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations. Our findings showed that:
* Compared to individuals with circulating concentrations of adiponectin, leptin, and A/L ratio in the bottom tertile, those in the top tertile had a significantly reduced risk of endometrial cancer (SOR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.34-0.65; I(2) = 63.7%; n = 13).
* There was an 18% reduction in risk for each 5 μg/mL increment in circulating adiponectin concentrations (SOR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.74-0.90; I(2) = 49%; n = 8).
* Stratifying by study characteristics and whether these studies considered or adjusted for potential confounders, the findings were robust in the analyses of circulating adiponectin and leptin.
* No evidence of publication bias was detected.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that increased circulating adiponectin and A/L ratio or decreased leptin concentrations are associated with a reduced risk of endometrial cancer. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: CDE-1 Affects Chromosome Segregation through Uridylation of CSR-1-Bound siRNAs
text: We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of the function of the conserved germline-specific nucleotidyltransferase protein, CDE-1, in the regulation of RNA interference (RNAi) and chromosome segregation in the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans. Our findings indicate that CDE-1 localizes specifically to mitotic chromosomes in embryos, a process that requires the interaction with the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase EGO-1 and the Argonaute protein CSR-1. We discovered that CDE-1 plays a crucial role in the uridylation of CSR-1-bound small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), and that in the absence of CDE-1, these siRNAs accumulate to inappropriate levels, leading to defects in both meiotic and mitotic chromosome segregation. Notably, elevated siRNA levels are associated with erroneous gene silencing, likely due to the inappropriate loading of CSR-1 siRNAs into other Argonaute proteins. Based on our findings, we propose a model in which CDE-1 functions to restrict specific EGO-1-generated siRNAs to the CSR-1-mediated, chromosome-associated RNAi pathway, thereby separating it from other endogenous RNAi pathways. The conserved nature of CDE-1 suggests that similar sorting mechanisms may operate in other animals, including mammals.

title: Localized diacylglycerol drives the polarization of the microtubule-organizing center in T cells
text: The reorientation of the T cell's microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) towards the antigen-presenting cell enables the directional secretion of cytokines and lytic factors. By using single-cell photoactivation of the T cell antigen receptor, we found that MTOC polarization is driven by the local accumulation of diacylglycerol (DAG). MTOC reorientation was preceded by the production of DAG and the recruitment of the microtubule motor protein dynein. Blocking DAG production or disrupting its localization impaired MTOC recruitment. Localized DAG accumulation was also necessary for cytotoxic T cell-mediated killing. Furthermore, photoactivation of DAG itself was sufficient to induce transient MTOC polarization. Our data reveal a DAG-dependent signaling pathway that controls microtubule polarity in T cells through the dynein protein.

title: Dual roles of plcA in Listeria monocytogenes pathogenesis.
text: The plcA gene of Listeria monocytogenes encodes a secreted phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C (Pl-PLC), which has been shown to play a crucial role in the pathogenesis of this bacterium. Recent studies have demonstrated that mutations within the plcA gene can result in avirulence in mice and pleiotropic effects when examined in tissue-culture models of infection. Genetic analysis has revealed that many of these effects are due to the loss of readthrough transcription from plcA into the downstream gene prfA, which encodes an essential transcription factor that regulates numerous virulence genes of L. monocytogenes. In contrast, construction of an in-frame deletion within plcA had no effect on expression of prfA, allowing for a direct assignment of the role of Pl-PLC in pathogenesis. Furthermore, Pl-PLC was shown to play a significant role in mediating escape of L. monocytogenes from phagosomes of primary murine macrophages, with this defect manifesting itself specifically in the liver but not in the spleen of infected mice.

title: Fine-tuning in regulation of Clp protein content in Bacillus subtilis.
text: Clp-controlled proteolysis in Bacillus subtilis plays a significant role, particularly under stressful conditions. Using calibrated Western blot analyses, the approximate number of heat-inducible Clp molecules per cell was estimated. These analyses revealed that the different Clp ATPases do not compete for the proteolytic subunit ClpP. Coimmunoprecipitation experiments showed specific interactions between ClpX and ClpP, ClpC and ClpP, and ClpE and ClpP. Notably, ClpE and ClpX were rapidly degraded in wild-type cells during prolonged heat stress, while they remained stable in a clpP mutant, suggesting that ClpP plays a role in their degradation. Furthermore, ClpCP appeared to be involved in the degradation of the short-lived ClpE ATPase, indicating a negative "autoregulatory" circuit for this particular Clp ATPase at the posttranslational level. The half-life of stress-inducible clp mRNAs was analyzed during exponential growth and heat shock, revealing precise regulation of Clp protein synthesis at the posttranscriptional level to meet the needs of B. subtilis.

title: A C-Type Lectin Collaborates with a CD45 Phosphatase Homolog to Facilitate West Nile Virus Infection of Mosquitoes
text: West Nile virus (WNV) is the most common arthropod-borne flavivirus in the United States, but the specific ligands involved in its infection are unknown. However, our study reveals that an Aedes aegypti C-type lectin called mosGCTL-1 is induced by WNV, interacts with the virus in a calcium-dependent manner, and facilitates infection in both in vivo and in vitro experiments. We also identify a mosquito homolog of human CD45 in A. aegypti, designated mosPTP-1, which recruits mosGCTL-1 to enable viral attachment to cells and enhance viral entry. In vivo experiments demonstrate that mosGCTL-1 and mosPTP-1 function together in a critical pathway for WNV infection of mosquitoes. This finding is further supported by observations in Culex quinquefasciatus, a natural vector of WNV. In addition, we show that blocking WNV infection in vivo with mosGCTL-1 antibodies during the mosquito blood-feeding process can effectively prevent the virus from spreading. Our study provides a molecular understanding of the interactions between flaviviruses and their arthropod vectors, which may lead to strategies for controlling viral dissemination in nature.

title: Use of human embryonic stem cells to model pediatric gliomas with H3.3K27M histone mutation
text: Over 70% of diffuse intrinsic pediatric gliomas, a highly aggressive brainstem tumor, exhibit heterozygous mutations that result in a K27M amino acid substitution (methionine replacing lysine 27) in the tail of histone H3.3. The mechanisms underlying the H3.3K27M mutation's role in tumorigenesis are not yet fully understood. To investigate, we employed a human embryonic stem cell-based model. Our findings indicate that H3.3K27M expression, when combined with p53 loss and PDGFRA activation in neural progenitor cells derived from human embryonic stem cells, leads to neoplastic transformation. Genome-wide analyses revealed a reversion of the transformed precursors to a more primitive stem cell state, marked by significant alterations in histone marks at key regulatory genes. In addition, we identified a compound targeting the protein menin as an inhibitor of tumor cell growth in vitro and in vivo.

title: Basis for avid homologous DNA strand exchange by human Rad51 and RPA.
text: Human Rad51 (hRad51), a member of a conserved family of recombinases, has been shown to exhibit exceptional ability in joining homologous DNA molecules and facilitating highly efficient exchange of paired DNA strands over long distances (>5.4 kilobase pairs). The efficiency of this process is found to be significantly dependent on the presence of a heterotrimeric single-stranded DNA binding factor called hRPA, and optimal conditions that minimize the interaction between the homologous duplex and the hRad51-single-stranded DNA nucleoprotein filament. This homologous DNA pairing and strand exchange system provides valuable insights into the mechanism of hRad51 function and the interactions between hRad51 and other recombination factors.

title: A multiple indicators multiple causes model of late-life depression in Latin American countries
text:
BACKGROUND: The Euro-D depression scale is composed of symptom clusters that may vary in their relationship to demographic and cognitive characteristics in older adults. It is crucial to investigate this hypothesis and determine the extent to which measurement bias affects conclusions regarding the Euro-D.
METHOD: A sample of 10,405 community-dwelling older adults from six Latin American countries were analyzed using a Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes (MIMIC) model to investigate measurement bias and the association between Euro-D symptom clusters and background variables.
RESULTS: The factorial validity of Euro-D, with a two-dimensional structure of affective suffering and motivation disturbance, was consistently supported across all countries. Although complete measurement invariance could not be assumed across countries, measurement bias was minimal. Both Euro-D factors were unrelated to age but related to gender, as well as to impairment in memory and verbal fluency. Gender differences were larger for affective suffering than for motivation disturbance, while differences in verbal fluency impairment were more strongly related to motivation disturbance.
LIMITATIONS: The current study was limited to examining invariance at the level of indicator thresholds, and the generalizability of findings to clinical populations needs to be further examined. Additionally, a wider range of cognitive tests is required to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the factors contributing to Euro-D scores across countries.
CONCLUSION: The current study provides evidence for the construct validity of Euro-D and the potential differential association of depression symptom clusters with gender and verbal fluency in older adults. Understanding the heterogeneity of late-life depression may have important clinical implications for the diagnosis and treatment of depression in old age.

title: Microvesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells stimulated by hypoxia promote angiogenesis both in vitro and in vivo.
text: Although mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been increasingly investigated as a potential treatment for various diseases, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we explored the mechanisms of MSC therapy by examining the release of membrane microvesicles (MVs) upon hypoxic stimulation. We found that MSCs released a large quantity of MVs upon hypoxic stimulation, which were similar in size and phenotype to the parent MSCs, except that they were negative for the receptor of platelet-derived growth factor. Using a DiI-labeling assay, we observed that MSC-MVs could be internalized into human umbilical cord endothelial cells (UC-ECs) within 8 hours of exposure. Additionally, we found that MVs promoted the proliferation of UC-ECs in a dose-dependent manner using carboxyfluorescein succinimidyl ester-labeling technique and MTT test. Furthermore, MVs enhanced in vitro capillary network formation of UC-ECs in a Matrigel matrix. In a rat hindlimb ischemia model, both MSCs and MSC-MVs significantly improved blood flow recovery compared to the control medium (P<0.0001), as assessed by laser Doppler imaging analysis. These findings suggest that MV release is one of the major mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of MSC therapy by promoting angiogenesis.

title: Evaluation of oxidative status and depression-like responses in Brown Norway rats with acute myeloid leukemia
text: A recent study has found that oxidative stress is significantly higher in rats with leukemia that are also depressed, suggesting a potential link between oxidative stress and the development of depression in cancer patients. To investigate this further, the study divided rats into two groups: those with leukemia and those without, and evaluated their behavior in a forced swim test. The rats were then killed and their brains, spleens, and other tissues were examined for signs of oxidative stress, including reduced glutathione levels, increased malondialdehyde levels, and changes in the expression of certain enzymes involved in the antioxidant system. The study also used radioligand binding assays to assess the effect of leukemia on cortical receptors. The results showed that leukemia significantly impaired locomotory activity and forced swim test behavior, and that signs of oxidative stress were observed in all stages of leukemia development. Additionally, the study found that the potency of the neurotransmitter glycine to bind to N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) receptors was significantly increased in the cortical homogenates of leukemic rats, which is a hallmark of depression. Upregulation of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) receptors was also observed in the cortex of leukemic rats, but only in the early stages of leukemia development. These findings suggest that disturbances in the antioxidant system in the brain cortex are accompanied by an activation of glycine sites of the NMDA receptor complex, which are characteristic of depression. Overall, the study provides evidence for the link between glutamatergic activity, oxidative stress, and leukemia, and highlights the potential role of oxidative stress in the development of depression in cancer patients.

title: Distinct roles for DNA-PK, ATM and ATR in RPA phosphorylation and checkpoint activation in response to replication stress
text: DNA damage encountered by DNA replication forks poses the risk of genome instability, a precursor to cancer. Damage checkpoint systems cause cell cycle arrest, promote repair, and induce programmed cell death when damage is severe. Checkpoints are critical components of the DNA damage response network that prevent cancer. DNA damage and disruption of replication machinery leads to replication stress, characterized by the accumulation of single-stranded DNA bound by replication protein A (RPA), which triggers the activation of ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3 related (ATR) and the phosphorylation of the RPA32 subunit of RPA. This leads to the activation of Chk1 and cell cycle arrest. DNA-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit (DNA-PKcs), a kinase related to ATM and ATR, has well-characterized roles in DNA double-strand break repair but poorly understood roles in replication stress-induced RPA phosphorylation. Our findings show that DNA-PKcs mutant cells fail to arrest replication following stress, and mutations in RPA32 phosphorylation sites targeted by DNA-PKcs increase the proportion of cells in mitosis, impair ATR signaling to Chk1, and confer a G2/M arrest defect. Inhibition of ATR and DNA-PK (but not ATM), mimics the defects observed in cells expressing mutant RPA32. Cells expressing mutant RPA32 or DNA-PKcs show sustained H2AX phosphorylation in response to replication stress that persists in cells entering mitosis, indicating inappropriate mitotic entry with unrepaired damage.

title: The essential Schizosaccharomyces pombe Pfh1 DNA helicase promotes fork movement past G-quadruplex motifs to prevent DNA damage
text:
Background:
G-quadruplexes (G4s) are stable, non-canonical DNA secondary structures composed of stacked arrays of four guanines, held together by Hoogsteen hydrogen bonds. These structures are found throughout the genomes of both bacteria and eukaryotes, with sequences capable of forming G4s termed G4 motifs. The budding yeast Pif1 DNA helicase, as well as several bacterial Pif1 family helicases, have been shown to robustly unwind G4 structures in vitro and suppress G4-induced DNA damage in vivo.
Results:
We investigated the genomic distribution and evolutionary conservation of G4 motifs in four fission yeast species, and examined the relationship between G4 motifs and Pfh1, the sole Pif1 family helicase in S. pombe. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation combined with deep sequencing, we found that many G4 motifs in the S. pombe genome were associated with Pfh1. Depletion of Pfh1 led to increased fork pausing and DNA damage near G4 motifs, as indicated by high DNA polymerase occupancy and phosphorylated histone H2A levels, respectively. Notably, G4 motifs were underrepresented in genes, but Pfh1-associated G4 motifs were located on the transcribed strand of highly transcribed genes more frequently than expected, suggesting a potential function of Pfh1 in replication or transcription at these sites.
Conclusions:
In the absence of functional Pfh1, unresolved G4 structures may cause fork pausing and DNA damage, similar to that observed in human tumors. These findings suggest that Pfh1 plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the genome by resolving G4 structures, particularly in regions of high transcriptional activity.

title: Wnt7a signaling promotes dendritic spine growth and synaptic strength through Ca²⁺/Calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II.
text: The balance between excitatory and inhibitory synapses is essential for proper brain function, and Wnt proteins play a crucial role in regulating this balance by promoting synapse formation. However, it remains unclear whether Wnt signaling differentially regulates the formation of excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Our study demonstrates that Wnt7a preferentially stimulates the formation of excitatory synapses, as evidenced by an increase in the number of excitatory synapses in hippocampal neurons and an increase in the frequency and amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs). In contrast, inhibitory synapses are unaffected by Wnt7a. We also found that Wnt7a increases the density and maturity of dendritic spines, and that the absence of Wnt7a leads to defects in spine morphogenesis and mossy fiber-CA3 synaptic transmission in the hippocampus. Using a postsynaptic reporter for Ca(2+)/Calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) activity, we demonstrated that Wnt7a rapidly activates CaMKII in spines. Importantly, inhibition of CaMKII abolishes the effects of Wnt7a on spine growth and excitatory synaptic strength. These findings suggest that Wnt7a signaling is critical for regulating spine growth and synaptic strength through the local activation of CaMKII at dendritic spines. Therefore, altered Wnt7a signaling may contribute to neurological disorders characterized by disrupted excitatory signaling.

title: Bitter taste receptors and α-gustducin regulate the secretion of ghrelin with functional effects on food intake and gastric emptying.
text:
The hormone ghrelin, which has gastroprokinetic properties, is secreted by the stomach, but the factors that control its release are unknown. Bitter taste receptors (T2R) and gustatory G proteins, including α-gustducin (gust) and α-transducin, are expressed in the gut and play a role in the sensation of nutrients. This study aimed to investigate the effect of T2R-agonists on ghrelin release and food intake, as well as gastric emptying, in mice.
The stomach of mice contains two populations of ghrelin-producing cells, each containing either octanoyl or desoctanoyl ghrelin, which colocalize with α-gustducin and α-transducin. When mice were given T2R-agonists via gavage, plasma levels of octanoyl ghrelin increased in wild-type (WT) mice, but the effect was reduced in gust(-/-) mice. Intragastric administration of T2R-agonists increased food intake in WT mice during the first 30 minutes, but not in gust(-/-) or ghrelin receptor knockout (KO) mice. This increase in food intake was accompanied by an increase in the expression of agouti-related peptide in the hypothalamus of WT mice, but not in gust(-/-) mice. The temporary increase in food intake was followed by a prolonged decrease (next 4 hours), which correlated with an inhibition of gastric emptying. The delay in emptying, which was only partially counteracted by ghrelin, was not mediated by cholecystokinin or GLP-1, but involved a direct inhibitory effect of T2R-agonists on gastric contractility.
This study provides the first functional evidence that activation of bitter taste receptors stimulates ghrelin secretion. Modulation of endogenous ghrelin levels by tastants may offer novel therapeutic applications for the treatment of weight and gastrointestinal motility disorders.

title: Ca2+-permeable AMPA receptors regulate growth of human glioblastoma via Akt activation.
text: New evidence suggests that glioblastoma cells release and exploit glutamate through autocrine or paracrine loops by activating Ca2+-permeable AMPA-type glutamate receptors. Our findings reveal that Ca2+ signaling through AMPA receptors regulates the growth and motility of glioblastoma cells by activating Akt. Specifically, Ca2+ influx through AMPA receptors phosphorylates Akt at Ser-473, promoting cell proliferation and mobility. In contrast, a dominant-negative form of Akt inhibited cell proliferation and migration, while the introduction of a constitutively active form of Akt rescued tumor cells from apoptosis induced by the conversion of Ca2+-permeable AMPA receptors to Ca2+-impermeable receptors. These findings suggest that Akt functions as a downstream effector of Ca2+ signaling mediated by AMPA receptors in glioblastoma cells. This novel pathway may contribute to the aggressive and invasive growth of human glioblastoma, making it a potential therapeutic target.

title: The Extracellular Surface of the GLP-1 Receptor Is a Molecular Trigger for Biased Agonism
text:
Ligand-directed signal bias has the potential to revolutionize drug development by enabling the creation of safer and more effective therapeutics. To harness this power, it is crucial to comprehend the intricate molecular mechanisms underlying ligand binding and intracellular signaling. Class B G protein-coupled receptors are activated by the interaction of the peptide N terminus with the receptor core, and understanding these interactions is key to unlocking the full potential of signal bias.
To gain insight into the molecular events that drive signaling, we have employed advanced analytical techniques that allow for the separation of pathway-specific signaling from those that modify agonist affinity. By mapping the functional consequences of receptor modification onto three-dimensional models of receptor-ligand complexes, we have gained valuable molecular insights into the initiation of receptor activation and the mechanistic basis for biased agonism.
Our findings reveal that peptide agonists can engage different elements of the receptor extracellular face to achieve effector coupling and biased signaling, providing a solid foundation for the rational design of biased agonists. This knowledge has the potential to revolutionize drug development by enabling the creation of safer and more effective therapeutics, and we are eager to continue exploring the vast possibilities offered by signal bias.

title: A local macrophage chemokine network sustains protective tissue-resident memory CD4 T cells
text: CD8 tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are crucial for local control of viral infections, but the role of CD4 TRM is less understood. To investigate, we used parabiotic mice and found that a preexisting pool of CD4 TRM cells in the genital mucosa was essential for full protection against a lethal herpes simplex virus 2 (HSV-2) infection. Chemokines produced by a network of macrophages in the vagina maintained the presence of CD4 TRM cells in memory lymphocyte clusters (MLCs), independent of circulating memory T cells. Within these MLCs, CD4 TRM cells were enriched in clones that expanded in response to HSV-2. Our findings underscore the importance of developing vaccine strategies that promote the establishment of TRM cells for protection against sexually transmitted viruses, and provide insights into how such a pool might be established.

title: Influence of smoking and plasma factors on patency of femoropopliteal vein grafts.
text:
Objective: To determine the effects of smoking, plasma lipids, lipoproteins, apolipoproteins, and fibrinogen on the patency of saphenous vein femoropopliteal bypass grafts at one year.
Design: Prospective study of patients with saphenous vein femoropopliteal bypass grafts enrolled in a multicenter trial.
Setting: Surgical wards, outpatient clinics, and home visits coordinated by two tertiary referral centers in London and Birmingham.
Patients: 157 patients (mean age 66.6 ± 8.2 years), including 113 with patent grafts and 44 with occluded grafts one year after bypass.
Main Outcome Measure: Cumulative percentage patency at one year.
Results: The following markers were significantly higher in patients with occluded grafts:
* Blood carboxyhemoglobin concentration (p < 0.05)
* Plasma thiocyanate concentration (p < 0.01)
* Plasma concentrations of fibrinogen (p < 0.001) and apolipoproteins AI (p < 0.04) and (a) (p < 0.05)
* Serum cholesterol concentrations were significantly higher in patients with grafts that remained patent one year after bypass (p < 0.005).
Analysis of smoking markers revealed that approximately one-quarter of patients (40) were untruthful about their smoking habits.
* Patency of grafts in smokers was significantly lower at one year by life table analysis than in non-smokers (63% vs 84%, p < 0.02).
* Patency was significantly higher by life table analysis in patients with a plasma fibrinogen concentration below the median than in those with a concentration above (90% vs 57%, p < 0.0002).
* Increased plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentration was significantly associated with improved patency at one year (85% at values above the median vs 68% at values in the lower half of the range, p < 0.02).

Conclusions: Plasma fibrinogen concentration was the most important variable predicting graft occlusion, followed by smoking markers. A more forceful approach is needed to stop patients smoking, and therapeutic measures to improve patency of vein grafts should focus on decreasing plasma fibrinogen concentration rather than serum cholesterol concentration.

title: No effect of dietary fat on short-term weight gain in mice treated with atypical antipsychotic drugs
text: Background: Atypical antipsychotic drugs (AAD) are known to cause significant weight gain in female C57BL/6J mice. However, the impact of dietary fat on this effect is unknown. Objectives: To investigate whether the obesigenic effects of AAD are greater in the presence of a high-fat diet. Methods: Female C57BL/6J mice were treated with AAD (olanzapine, quetiapine, or risperidone) for 3 weeks and fed either a low-fat or high-fat diet (4.6% or 15.6% fat by weight, respectively). Food intake, body weight, body composition, and serum lipid concentrations were measured during treatment with optimized doses of each drug. Energy intake and feed efficiency were calculated, and group differences in change were analyzed using repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). Results: AAD treatment resulted in significant weight gain compared to controls (P < 0.001). Treatment and diet had significant effects on food intake and energy efficiency over time (P < 0.001). AAD-treated mice had higher feed efficiency than controls (P < 0.05), but there was no significant interaction between drug and diet (P = 0.65). Risperidone low-fat mice gained significantly more absolute fat mass than placebo low-fat mice (P < 0.05). All treatment groups, except quetiapine low-fat and olanzapine high-fat, gained significantly more absolute lean mass than placebo controls (P < 0.05). Cholesterol levels were significantly lower in quetiapine and risperidone than placebo (P < 0.05). Risperidone low-fat mice had significantly higher triglyceride levels than placebo and risperidone high-fat mice (P < 0.05). Conclusions: The results of this study suggest that a high-fat diet does not exacerbate AAD-induced weight gain in female mice during a 3-week treatment period.

title: The role of free radicals in cold injuries.
text:
Cold injury is a type of tissue damage caused by exposure to cold temperatures. Even brief exposure to a cold and windy environment can lead to this type of injury. When frozen tissue is rewarmed, it is associated with the generation of free oxygen radicals, which play a crucial role in the mechanism of action of cold injury.
During ischaemia (decreased blood flow), energy stores are depleted, leading to the accumulation of adenine nucleotides and the breakdown of lipid membranes. On rewarming, these broken down lipids release free fatty acids, which are metabolized through cyclo-oxygenase and adenine nucleotides are metabolized through the xanthine oxidase pathway. These processes may generate free oxygen radicals, which can further damage tissue.
Leukocytes (white blood cells) may also contribute to the development of cold injury. Oxygen radical scavengers, such as superoxide dismutase and catalase, can help reduce cold-induced injury, but their effectiveness is limited due to their inability to cross the plasma membrane easily. Lipid-soluble antioxidants are more effective at scavenging free oxygen radicals because they are present in cell membranes, where peroxidative reactions can be stopped.
In summary, cold injury is caused by exposure to cold temperatures and is associated with the generation of free oxygen radicals during rewarming. The accumulation of adenine nucleotides and the breakdown of lipid membranes during ischaemia can lead to the release of free fatty acids, which may contribute to the development of cold injury. Leukocytes may also play a role in the pathogenesis of cold injury, and oxygen radical scavengers may help reduce the damage. However, the effectiveness of these scavengers is limited due to their inability to cross the plasma membrane easily. Lipid-soluble antioxidants are more effective at scavenging free oxygen radicals in cell membranes.

title: SIRT1 deacetylase in SF1 neurons protects against metabolic imbalance.
text: Chronic consumption of high-calorie diets leads to obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), which affect a staggering number of individuals worldwide. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms that protect against metabolic imbalances induced by diet is of utmost medical significance. Our study reveals that mice lacking SIRT1 in steroidogenic factor 1 (SF1) neurons are more susceptible to diet-induced obesity due to impaired energy expenditure. Additionally, these mice are more likely to develop T2DM due to insulin resistance in skeletal muscle. Conversely, mice overexpressing SIRT1 in SF1 neurons are better protected against diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance, with increased energy expenditure and enhanced insulin sensitivity in skeletal muscle. Our findings highlight the crucial role of SIRT1 in SF1 neurons in preventing metabolic imbalances caused by diet.

title: mTOR supports long-term self-renewal and suppresses mesoderm and endoderm activities of human embryonic stem cells.
text: Despite recent advances in understanding the transcriptional regulatory circuitry of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), the intracellular signaling pathways that govern their pluripotency remain largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate the role of the serine/threonine protein kinase mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) in regulating the long-term undifferentiated growth of hESCs. Our results demonstrate that mTOR plays a crucial role in maintaining hESC pluripotency, as inhibition of mTOR impairs cell proliferation and enhances mesoderm and endoderm activities. Using genome-wide microarray analysis, we identify a subset of developmental and growth-inhibitory genes that are repressed by mTOR, which is necessary for the maintenance of hESC pluripotency. These findings uncover a novel signaling mechanism by which mTOR regulates fate decisions in hESCs, and may contribute to the development of effective strategies for tissue repair and regeneration.

title: Intrinsic genetic characteristics determine tumor-modifying capacity of fibroblasts: matrix metalloproteinase-3 5A/5A genotype enhances breast cancer cell invasion
text: This study investigated the role of stromal fibroblasts in tumor invasion and the impact of genetic variations in matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) genes on this process. The study found that tumor-derived fibroblasts exhibited higher levels of invasion than normal fibroblasts, and that the MMP-3 5A/5A genotype was associated with enhanced invasion in the presence of recombinant MMP-3. In contrast, normal fibroblasts showed no variation in invasion in relation to MMP genotype. These findings suggest that more complex changes occur in tumor-derived fibroblasts, which may be epigenetic in nature, and that a high-expressing MMP-3 genotype may promote tumor progression more effectively in women with breast cancer.

title: Hallmarks of Cancer: The Next Generation
text:
The hallmarks of cancer, which consist of six biological capabilities acquired during the multi-step development of human tumors, serve as a unifying principle for understanding the complexities of neoplastic disease. These hallmarks include:
1. Sustaining proliferative signaling: Cancer cells have developed mechanisms to maintain and amplify growth signals, leading to uncontrolled cell division.
2. Evading growth suppressors: Cancer cells can bypass or disable mechanisms that normally regulate cell growth, such as tumor suppressor genes.
3. Resisting cell death: Cancer cells can evade or disable mechanisms that trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis), allowing them to continue to proliferate unchecked.
4. Enabling replicative immortality: Cancer cells can bypass or disable mechanisms that limit the number of cell divisions possible, allowing them to continue to proliferate indefinitely.
5. Inducing angiogenesis: Cancer cells can stimulate the formation of new blood vessels, which provides them with oxygen and nutrients.
6. Activating invasion and metastasis: Cancer cells can invade surrounding tissues and enter the bloodstream or lymphatic system, leading to the formation of secondary tumors in other parts of the body.
Underlying these hallmarks are genome instability, which generates the genetic diversity that expedites their acquisition, and inflammation, which fosters multiple hallmark functions. In the last decade, two emerging hallmarks of potential generality have been identified: reprogramming of energy metabolism and evading immune destruction. In addition to cancer cells, tumors also contain a repertoire of recruited, ostensibly normal cells that contribute to the acquisition of hallmark traits by creating the "tumor microenvironment." Recognition of the widespread applicability of these concepts will increasingly inform the development of new means to treat human cancer.

title: BCR/ABL oncogenic kinase promotes unfaithful repair of the reactive oxygen species-dependent DNA double-strand breaks.
text:
The oncogenic BCR/ABL tyrosine kinase in Philadelphia chromosome (Ph)-positive leukemia cells induces constitutive DNA damage through the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROSs). These ROSs cause chronic oxidative DNA damage, leading to the formation of double-strand breaks (DSBs) in both the S and G(2)/M cell cycle phases. The BCR/ABL-stimulated homologous recombination repair (HRR) and nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) mechanisms are responsible for repairing these lesions. However, a high mutation rate is observed in HRR products in BCR/ABL-positive cells, but not in normal counterparts. In addition, exclusive to BCR/ABL cells are large deletions found in NHEJ products.
We propose that the following sequence of events may contribute to the genomic instability of Ph-positive leukemias: BCR/ABL activation --> ROS generation --> oxidative DNA damage --> DSBs in proliferating cells --> unfaithful HRR and NHEJ repair.

title: Cancer risks attributable to low doses of ionizing radiation: assessing what we really know.
text:
High doses of ionizing radiation have well-established harmful effects on humans, including an increased risk of cancer. However, the situation is less clear at low radiation doses, and the risks of low-dose radiation are of significant societal concern in areas such as cancer screening, nuclear power, occupational radiation exposure, frequent-flyer risks, manned space exploration, and radiological terrorism.
We review the challenges in quantifying the risks of low-dose radiation and address two specific questions. First, what is the lowest dose of X- or gamma radiation at which there is strong evidence of increased cancer risks in humans? Epidemiological data suggest that this dose is approximately 10-50 millisieverts (mSv) for an acute exposure and 50-100 mSv for a prolonged exposure. Second, how can we extrapolate cancer risk estimates to even lower doses? While a linear extrapolation of cancer risks from intermediate to very low doses appears to be the most appropriate methodology, this approach may result in an underestimate of some radiation-induced cancer risks and an overestimate of others.
In summary, high doses of ionizing radiation have well-established harmful effects on humans, but the risks of low-dose radiation are less clear and of significant societal concern. We review the challenges in quantifying these risks and address two specific questions related to cancer risk estimates at low doses.

title: Laparoscopic uterosacral nerve ablation for alleviating chronic pelvic pain: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
Chronic pelvic pain is a prevalent condition that significantly impacts an individual's quality of life, productivity, and healthcare utilization. Laparoscopic uterosacral nerve ablation (LUNA) is a treatment option for patients with chronic pelvic pain. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of LUNA in improving pain outcomes and quality of life among women with chronic pelvic pain.
The study included 487 women with chronic pelvic pain lasting over 6 months, with minimal endometriosis, adhesions, or pelvic inflammatory disease. Participants were recruited from 18 UK hospitals and were randomly assigned to either bilateral LUNA or laparoscopy without pelvic denervation (no LUNA). The primary outcome measures were pain, assessed through visual analogue scales for the worst pain level experienced, noncyclical pain, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia. Secondary outcome measures included health-related quality of life, measured using the EuroQoL EQ-5D and EQ-VAS.
The study found that there were no significant differences in pain outcomes between the LUNA and no LUNA groups. Specifically, the visual analogue pain scales did not show any significant improvements in the worst pain level, noncyclical pain, dysmenorrhea, or dyspareunia. Similarly, there were no differences observed in quality of life outcomes between the two groups.
The results of this study suggest that LUNA may not be an effective treatment for improving pain outcomes and quality of life among women with chronic pelvic pain. These findings are consistent with previous studies that have shown limited efficacy of LUNA in managing chronic pelvic pain. Further research is needed to identify alternative treatment options for this debilitating condition.
This study was registered at controlled-trials.com with the identifier ISRCTN41196151.

title: Identification of bone and liver metastases from breast cancer by measurement of plasma alkaline phosphatase isoenzyme activity.
text: Plasma alkaline phosphatase isoenzyme activities were investigated in patients with breast cancer to diagnose and monitor bone and liver metastases. Our findings revealed that bone alkaline phosphatase activity was elevated in 42% of 50 patients (21/50) with radiologically confirmed bone metastases, whereas total alkaline phosphatase activity was increased in only 20% (10/50) of patients. Additionally, liver alkaline phosphatase activity was elevated in 48% (12/25) of patients with liver metastases, with all patients having concurrent bone metastases. Notably, bone alkaline phosphatase activity was significantly higher in patients with symptomatic bone disease. Isoenzyme determination provided valuable additional information that would have influenced patient management in five of 20 patients who were monitored serially. Our study demonstrates that measurement of alkaline phosphatase isoenzyme activity, although less sensitive than imaging techniques, can effectively screen for and detect a significant proportion of bone and liver metastases, and provide useful objective evidence of their response to treatment.

title: Recommendations on how to ensure the safety and effectiveness of biosimilars in Latin America: a point of view
text:
The use of biotechnology-derived medicines has significantly increased in recent decades, with biosimilars undergoing rigorous characterization and clinical studies to demonstrate their safety and effectiveness. However, these highly complex molecules can be susceptible to small changes in the purification and production process, which can have major implications for their safety and effectiveness profile. In Latin America, regulatory authorities are establishing well-defined and standardized pathways for the commercial licensure of biosimilars. To ensure that biosimilars reach their full potential in real-world clinical use, a comprehensive post-licensing monitoring system is essential. This system allows regulatory authorities to track the performance of biosimilars in the marketplace and determine their true similarity to the original biologic.
