Using normal mode analysis, we identify two dominant mechanisms of AMPAR NTD motion: intraprotomer clamshell motions and interprotomer counter-rotations, as well as the ability to interconvert between AMPAR and mGluR conformations. Additionally, we detect electron density for a potential ligand in the GluA2 interlobe cleft, which may trigger lobe motions. These findings support a dynamic role for the AMPAR NTDs, expanding the allosteric landscape of the receptor and providing a novel target for ligand development.

title: A complex secretory program orchestrated by the inflammasome controls paracrine senescence
text: Oncogene-induced senescence (OIS) plays a crucial role in tumor suppression by inducing senescent cells to release a complex pro-inflammatory response known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). This response reinforces senescence, activates immune surveillance, and paradoxically also has pro-tumorigenic properties. Here, we provide evidence that the SASP can also induce paracrine senescence in normal cells both in vitro and in vivo. By combining quantitative proteomics with small-molecule screens, we identified multiple SASP components involved in paracrine senescence, including TGF-β family ligands, VEGF, CCL2, and CCL20. Of these, TGF-β ligands are particularly important in regulating the expression of p15(INK4b) and p21(CIP1). The expression of the SASP is controlled by inflammasome-mediated IL-1 signaling, which is activated in senescent cells and can reproduce the SASP activation, leading to senescence. Our findings demonstrate that the SASP can cause paracrine senescence and have a significant impact on tumor suppression and senescence in vivo.

title: Prospective Study of One Million Deaths in India: Rationale, Design, and Validation Results
text: Over 75% of India's estimated 9.5 million annual deaths occur at home, with the majority lacking a certified cause. India and other developing countries urgently require reliable data on the causes of death. This report outlines the rationale, design, and implementation of the world's largest prospective study to identify the causes and risk factors of mortality. Nearly 14 million people in 2.4 million households across India will be monitored, with a well-validated verbal autopsy (VA) instrument used to collect data on vital status and causes of death. This study will provide reliable information on both the underlying cause of death and key risk factors, including behavioral, physical, environmental, and genetic factors. The study offers a globally replicable model for estimating cause-specific mortality using VA and strengthens India's mortality monitoring system. While misclassification is expected, the new cause-of-death data will be significantly better than previously available. [PLoS Medicine, February 2006.]

title: Genome-wide identification of genes directly regulated by the pleiotropic transcription factor Spx in Bacillus subtilis
text: The transcriptional regulator Spx plays a crucial role in maintaining the redox homeostasis of Bacillus subtilis cells under disulfide stress. Previous studies have shown that defects in Spx lead to altered gene expression, but the direct and indirect regulatory effects could not be distinguished. To investigate the regulatory mechanisms of Spx, we used chromatin immunoprecipitation to identify 283 potential binding sites of the Spx-RNA polymerase (Spx-RNAP) complex on the Bacillus subtilis chromosome. We found that three-quarters of these sites were located near Sigma(A)-dependent promoters, and upon treatment with diamide, the fraction of the Spx-RNAP complex increased, parallel to the number and occupancy of DNA sites. Correlation analysis of Spx-RNAP-binding sites with gene expression in wild-type and Spx-deficient strains exposed or not to diamide revealed that 144 transcription units comprising 275 genes were potentially under direct Spx regulation. Spx-controlled promoters exhibited an extended -35 box, and nucleotide composition at the -43/-44 positions strongly correlated with observed activation. In vitro transcription assays confirmed the activation of seven newly identified promoters, including one that was also activated by reduced Spx. Our study provides a global characterization of the Spx regulatory network, revealing its role in the basal expression of some genes and its complex interplay with other stress responses.

title: Expression of interleukin-18 in human atherosclerotic plaques and relation to plaque instability.
text:
BACKGROUND: Interleukin (IL)-18 is a proinflammatory cytokine with potential atherogenic properties, but its expression and role in atherosclerosis are not well understood.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, we investigated the presence and expression of IL-18 in stable and unstable human carotid atherosclerotic plaques retrieved by endarterectomy using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Western blot, and immunohistochemical techniques. Our findings showed that IL-18 was highly expressed in atherosclerotic plaques compared to control normal arteries, and was mainly localized in plaque macrophages. Additionally, the IL-18 receptor was upregulated in plaque macrophages and endothelial cells, suggesting potential biological effects. To determine the role of IL-18 in atherosclerosis, we examined the relation between IL-18 mRNA expression and signs of plaque instability using real-time quantitative PCR. Our results showed that significantly higher levels of IL-18 mRNA were found in symptomatic (unstable) plaques compared to asymptomatic (stable) plaques (P<0.01), suggesting a major role for IL-18 in atherosclerotic plaque destabilization and acute ischemic syndromes.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide, for the first time, evidence of a significant role for IL-18 in atherosclerotic plaque destabilization and acute ischemic events, highlighting the potential of IL-18 as a therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerosis-related diseases.

title: US-SOMO HPLC-SAXS module: dealing with capillary fouling and extraction of pure component patterns from poorly resolved SEC-SAXS data
text:
Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) coupled with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is a powerful analytical technique that allows for the direct collection of monodisperse sample data. However, issues such as capillary fouling and non-baseline-resolved peaks can hinder its effectiveness. To address these challenges, the UltraScan solution modeler (US-SOMO) HPLC-SAXS module provides a comprehensive framework for analyzing SAXS data, including simple linear baseline correction and symmetrical Gaussian decomposition tools.
In addition to these existing features, substantial improvements have been made to the module, including the evaluation of results using advanced statistical tools. A novel integral baseline-correction procedure has been developed, based on the assumption that the effect of capillary fouling on scattering increases monotonically with the intensity scattered by the material within the X-ray beam. This approach allows for more accurate correction of overlapping peaks, which are often skewed due to sample interaction with the column matrix.
As an example, the analysis of a polydisperse solution of aldolase is demonstrated. Heavily convoluted peaks are accurately decomposed using non-symmetrical modified Gaussian functions, allowing for the extraction and reliable modeling of individual SAXS profiles of tetramers, octamers, and dodecamers.

title: Determination of Malaria Epidemiological Status in Iran’s Malarious Areas as Baseline Information for Implementation of Malaria Elimination Program in Iran
text:
According to the willingness of the Ministry of Health of Iran and the presence of suitable conditions for disease elimination, the national malaria control program conducted a research study in 2007 to determine the malaria status and provide necessary information for the elimination program. This review was based on the vision of the national malaria elimination program in 2025, which began in 2010.
The study analyzed data at the district level using various variables. All districts in the three southeastern provinces where malaria is transmitted locally were included in the study. Malaria cases were determined and studied based on the national malaria surveillance system.
Findings revealed that vivax malaria is prevalent in Sistan & Baluchestan Province, with approximately equal numbers of vivax and malaria positive cases. Nikshahr district in this province had the highest number of local vivax cases, and Sarbaz district reported the maximum number of falciparum cases. In Hormozgan Province, no autochthonous falciparum cases were detected, except in Bandar Jask and one case in Minab. Additionally, there were no autochthonous falciparum cases in Kerman Province, except in Kahnoj and Ghale Ganj, with one case each in 2007.
The study suggests that the number of locally transmitted malaria cases in Iran has been increasing in recent years before the start of the malaria elimination plan. With the return of Afghan refugees to their home country, the main source of reporting of imported malaria cases has reduced, allowing local cases to be more clearly demonstrated.

title: Local neuroinflammation and the progression of Alzheimer’s disease
text: Postmortem immunohistochemical studies have revealed a state of chronic inflammation confined to affected areas of the brain in Alzheimer's disease. Key players in this inflammation include activated microglia (brain macrophages), proteins of the classical complement cascade, pentraxins, cytokines, and chemokines. Unlike the adaptive immune system, which is not involved in this inflammation, the innate immune system, which is phylogenetically older, appears to be the primary source of inflammation in the brain. Chronic inflammation can cause damage to host tissue, and the brain may be particularly susceptible due to its postmitotic nature, making it vulnerable to inflammation. Many inflammatory mediators are produced locally and selectively elevated in affected regions of Alzheimer's brain. Similar local innate immune reactions have been observed in other degenerative conditions, such as atherosclerosis and infarcted heart. Epidemiological and limited clinical evidence suggests that nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs may delay the onset and progression of Alzheimer's disease, but these drugs only target peripheral inflammation. More effective results may be achieved by developing drugs that inhibit microglial activation or the complement system in the brain, and combining drugs targeting different inflammatory targets may be more effective than using a single agent.

title: BLAST+: architecture and applications
text:
Here is a possible rewrite of the text with a more formal and objective tone:
Background: Sequence similarity searching is a crucial bioinformatics task that has gained significant importance in recent years. While Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST) has been widely used for this purpose due to its heuristics-based approach, the current software has limitations in terms of speed, particularly for long queries or database sequences. Additionally, the user interface of the command-line applications could be improved.
Results: In this study, we describe the development of a revised BLAST software and the introduction of new command-line applications. To address the issue of slow run times for long queries, we implemented a chunking approach for processing long sequences. This resulted in significantly shorter run times for searches against long databases of contigs or chromosomes. Furthermore, we developed a new feature that allows the retrieval of masking information for database sequences from the BLAST databases. Additionally, we created a modular software library that can access subject sequence data from arbitrary data sources.
Conclusion: The new BLAST command-line applications demonstrate substantial improvements in speed for long queries and chromosome length database sequences compared to the current tools. Moreover, the user interface of the command-line applications has been improved. These advancements in the BLAST software will enable researchers to perform sequence similarity searches more efficiently and effectively, thereby accelerating the discovery of new biological insights.

title: Intrauterine environments and breast cancer risk: meta-analysis and systematic review
text:
INTRODUCTION: Perinatal factors, including birth weight, birth order, maternal age, gestational age, twin status, and paternal smoking, have been postulated to influence breast cancer risk in offspring by altering the hormonal environment of the developing mammary glands during fetal development. Despite a biologically plausible relationship, epidemiological studies have yielded conflicting results. To investigate the associations between perinatal factors and breast cancer risk, we conducted meta-analyses of published studies.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed breast cancer studies published between January 1966 and February 2007 that reported data on birth weight, birth order, maternal age, gestational age, twin status, and maternal or paternal smoking. We employed random effect models to perform meta-analyses and summarize the results.
RESULTS: Our findings indicate that higher birth weights are associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. Specifically, studies categorizing birth weights into five groups revealed odds ratios (ORs) of 1.24 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04 to 1.48) for birth weights of 4,000 g or more and 1.15 (95% CI 1.04 to 1.26) for birth weights of 3,500 g to 3,999 g compared to a birth weight of 2,500 to 2,599 g. These findings did not support a J-shaped relationship between birth weight and breast cancer risk. Additionally, we found support for an association between birth weight and breast cancer risk across three and two birth weight categories, respectively. Women born to older mothers and twins were also found to be at some increased risk, although the results were heterogeneous across studies and publication years. Birth order, prematurity, and maternal smoking were unrelated to breast cancer risk.
CONCLUSION: Our findings provide some support for the hypothesis that in utero exposures reflective of higher endogenous hormone levels may influence the development of breast cancer in adulthood.

title: Epidemiologic studies on Dengue in Santiago de Cuba, 1997.
text:
In January 1997, a small outbreak of dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome (DHF/DSS) caused by dengue virus type 2 (DEN-2) occurred in Santiago de Cuba, an island in Cuba. A total of 205 DHF/DSS cases were reported, all in individuals over the age of 15. All but three of these individuals had a prior dengue infection, with the only known opportunity being the islandwide DEN-1 epidemic in 1977-1979. Complete clinical and laboratory surveillance was conducted on all reported cases of overt disease.
Between December 1997 and January 1998, a random sample of 1,151 individuals from 40 residential clusters in Santiago was tested for DEN-1 and DEN-2 neutralizing antibodies. The prevalence of DEN-2 antibodies in children under the age of 15, born after the 1981 DEN-2 epidemic, was used to estimate the 1997 DEN-2 infection rate. This was adjusted to account for observed cases, resulting in an estimated infection rate of 4.3%.
Using this estimated infection rate, the attack rate for dengue fever and DHF/DSS was calculated based on the number of primary and secondary DEN-2 infections. Only 3% of the 13,116 primary infections were overt, and the DHF/DSS attack rate for adults of all ages was 420 per 10,000 secondary DEN-2 infections.

title: Prognostic and Predictive Value of KRAS Mutations in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
text: The prognostic and predictive implications of KRAS mutations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain unclear. To investigate, we conducted a retrospective analysis of the prognostic and predictive value of KRAS mutations in patients with advanced NSCLC. Our study included 484 patients with available results for both KRAS and EGFR mutations, of whom 39 (8%) had KRAS mutations and 182 (38%) had EGFR mutations, with two cases having both mutations. We found that the median overall survival for patients with KRAS mutations, EGFR mutations, or both wild types was 7.7, 38.0, and 15.0 months, respectively (P < 0.001). KRAS mutation was identified as an independent poor prognostic factor in the multivariate analysis (hazard ratio = 2.6, 95% CI: 1.8-3.7). Furthermore, response rates and progression-free survival (PFS) were inferior in the KRAS mutation group when treated with pemetrexed-based regimen compared to the KRAS wild type group (14% vs. 28%, 2.1 vs. 3.9 months, respectively). However, there was no significant difference in treatment outcomes between the KRAS mutation and wild type groups when treated with gemcitabine-based chemotherapy or taxane-based regimen. Although the clinical outcomes to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) appeared better in patients with KRAS wild type than those with KRAS mutations, there was no statistical difference in response rates and PFS according to KRAS mutation status when EGFR mutation status was considered. Interestingly, two patients with both KRAS and EGFR mutations showed partial response to EGFR TKIs. G12D mutation, which is a subtype of KRAS mutation, was found to occur more frequently in never smokers, but there was no significant difference in clinical outcomes according to KRAS genotypes. Overall, our findings suggest that KRAS mutations have an independent prognostic value but a limited predictive role for EGFR TKIs or cytotoxic chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC.

title: A Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Covariance Matrix Estimator And A Direct Test For Heteroskedasticity
text: This paper proposes a parameter covariance matrix estimator that is consistent even when the residuals of a linear regression model exhibit heteroskedasticity. Unlike traditional estimators that rely on a specific model of heteroskedasticity, this new estimator is model-free and does not make any assumptions about the structure of the heteroskedasticity. By comparing the elements of the new estimator to those of the traditional estimator, one can directly test for heteroskedasticity. In the absence of heteroskedasticity, the two estimators will be approximately equal, but will generally diverge otherwise. The test has a convenient least squares interpretation.

title: Two Subsets of Naive T Helper Cells with Distinct T Cell Receptor Excision Circle Content in Human Adult Peripheral Blood
text: During aging, the thymus becomes less efficient in producing new T cells, leading to a decline in the number of naive T cells in the peripheral blood. To compensate for this deficit, the peripheral T cell pool must expand and replenish itself, at least in part. We have found that this expansion occurs in two distinct subsets of naive T cells, each with a different history of proliferation. T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are highly enriched in a subset of naive T cells, indicating that these cells have undergone more rounds of cell division. In contrast, another subset of naive T cells has a much lower TREC content, suggesting that they have not undergone as much proliferation. Interestingly, we have found that the subset of T cells with a lower TREC content is more prone to losing the protein CD31, which is a marker of naive T cells. As people age, the percentage of CD31-expressing naive T cells increases, while the percentage of CD31-negative naive T cells decreases. We hypothesize that T cell receptor (TCR) triggering is necessary for the homeostatic expansion of naive T cells in the peripheral blood. In support of this idea, we have found that TCR engagement in vitro leads to the loss of CD31 expression on T cells. Overall, our findings suggest that the peripheral T cell pool in aging individuals is dynamic and undergoes changes in response to the decline in thymic function.

title: A Role for the Vacuolating Cytotoxin, VacA, in Colonization and Helicobacter pylori–Induced Metaplasia in the Stomach
text: The carriage of Helicobacter pylori strains producing more active forms of the VacA toxin (s1/i1) is strongly linked to gastric adenocarcinoma. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the effects of different polymorphic forms of VacA on inflammation and metaplasia in the mouse stomach. Our findings show that bacteria producing the less active s2/i2 form of VacA colonize mice more efficiently than mutants lacking VacA or producing more active forms of it, providing the first evidence of a positive role for the minimally active s2/i2 toxin. In contrast, strains producing more active toxin forms induce more severe and extensive metaplasia and inflammation in the mouse stomach compared to strains producing weakly active (s2/i2) toxin. Additionally, we examined the association between VacA polymorphism and precancerous intestinal metaplasia in human gastric biopsy specimens, controlling for cagPAI status. Our results show that the vacA i1 allele is strongly associated with precancerous intestinal metaplasia, with almost complete absence of intestinal metaplasia in subjects infected with i2-type strains, even in a vacA s1, cagA(+) background.

title: Systematic review of role of bisphosphonates on skeletal morbidity in metastatic cancer.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of bisphosphonates in reducing skeletal morbidity in cancer patients with bone metastases through a comprehensive literature review.
Data Sources: Electronic databases, reference lists, and consultation with experts and pharmaceutical companies. Foreign language papers were included.
Study Selection: Randomized controlled trials comparing bisphosphonates, placebo, or standard care with at least one outcome of skeletal morbidity in patients with malignant disease and bone metastases.
Results: A total of 95 articles were identified, of which 30 studies met the inclusion criteria. Bisphosphonates significantly reduced the odds ratio for fractures (vertebral: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.57-0.84, P < 0.0001; non-vertebral: 0.65, 0.54-0.79, P < 0.0001; combined: 0.65, 0.55-0.78, P < 0.0001), radiotherapy (0.67, 0.57-0.79, P < 0.0001), and hypercalcaemia (0.54, 0.36-0.81, P = 0.003), but not for orthopaedic surgery (0.70, 0.46-1.05, P = 0.086) or spinal cord compression (0.71, 0.47-1.08, P = 0.113). The reduction in orthopaedic surgery was significant in studies lasting over a year (0.59, 0.39-0.88, P = 0.009). Use of bisphosphonates significantly increased time to first skeletal-related event but did not affect survival. Subanalyses showed that most evidence supports intravenous aminobisphosphonates.
Conclusions: In patients with metastatic bone disease, bisphosphonates significantly reduce skeletal morbidity, except for spinal cord compression and increased time to first skeletal-related event. Treatment should start when bone metastases are diagnosed and continue until it is no longer clinically relevant.

title: Rodent Models of Depression: Neurotrophic and Neuroinflammatory Biomarkers
text: Rodent models are a crucial tool for investigating the etiology and progression of depression. The interconnected systems of neurotrophic factors and cytokines play a central role in regulating normal brain plasticity, and impairments in these systems underlie the development of cerebral pathologies, including mental disorders. This review focuses on the various experimental rodent models of depression induced by different stressors (exteroceptive and interoceptive) during early life (including prenatal period) or adulthood, with an emphasis on changes in neurotrophic factors and neuroinflammatory indices in the brain. These parameters are closely linked to behavioral depression-like symptoms and impairments in neuronal plasticity, and are influenced by both gender and genotype. Stress-related changes in the expression of neurotrophins and cytokines in the rodent brain are region-specific, and different laboratories may obtain contradictory results due to variations in stress paradigms or experimental conditions. While these experimental models are simplifications of clinical depression states, they provide valuable insights into the involvement of neurotrophic factors and cytokines in the pathogenesis of the disease. These major regulatory systems may serve as promising targets for therapeutic interventions and drug development.

title: The docking domain of histone H2A is required for H1 binding and RSC-mediated nucleosome remodeling
text: Histone variants within the H2A family exhibit significant divergence in their C-terminal regions. In this study, we investigate the role of these divergences, with a particular focus on the H2A COOH-terminus docking domain, in the structural and functional properties of the nucleosome. Using a combination of biochemical techniques and advanced imaging methods, including Atomic Force Microscopy and Electron Cryo-Microscopy, we demonstrate that the H2A docking domain is a crucial structural feature within the nucleosome. Deletion or replacement of this domain with the incomplete docking domain from the variant H2A.Bbd leads to significant structural alterations in the nucleosome, including increased accessibility to nucleases, un-wrapping of ∼10 bp of DNA from each end of the nucleosome, and changes in the entry/exit angle of DNA ends. These structural modifications are associated with a reduced ability of the chromatin remodeler RSC to both remodel and mobilize the nucleosomes, as well as abrogation of linker histone H1 binding in nucleosomes containing the incomplete docking domain of H2A.Bbd. Our findings highlight the unique role of the H2A-docking domain in coordinating the structural-functional aspects of nucleosome properties, and suggest that incorporation of a 'defective' docking domain may be a primary structural role of H2A.Bbd in chromatin.

title: Regulation of poly(A) site choice of several yeast mRNAs
text: Several yeast genes produce multiple transcripts with distinct 3' ends, according to recent research. Of these, four genes have been identified to produce truncated transcripts that terminate within the coding sequence of longer transcripts: CBP1, AEP2/ATP13, RNA14, and SIR1. It has been demonstrated that the amount of the truncated CBP1 transcript rises during the switch to respiratory growth while the amount of the full-length transcript decreases. To determine whether this phenomenon is unique to CBP1, northern blot analysis was used to determine whether the levels of other truncated transcripts are similarly regulated by carbon source. The levels of the shortest transcripts of AEP2/ATP13 and RNA14 increased during respiration, while the shortest SIR1 transcript remained unchanged. However, two longer SIR1 transcripts were regulated reciprocally by carbon source. By sequencing partial cDNA clones, the 3' ends of each transcript were mapped, revealing multiple 3' ends for each transcript. Examination of the sequences surrounding the 3' ends of the induced transcripts failed to identify a consensus sequence, but weak putative 3' end formation signals were found in all of the transcripts. Similarly, no consensus sequence was found when the sequences surrounding the 3' ends of the longest transcripts were compared, but weak putative 3' end formation signals were identified. These findings suggest that carbon source regulation of alternative poly(A) site choice may occur in yeast.

title: Circular RNA and miR-7 in cancer.
text: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play a crucial role in fine-tuning gene expression and are often dysregulated in cancer. Recent discoveries have revealed that competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs) play important roles in regulating miRNA activity, adding complexity to the regulatory networks involving non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Of particular interest is the newly identified circRNA ciRS-7, which functions as a designated miR-7 inhibitor/sponge, revolutionizing our understanding of miRNA networks. As miR-7 regulates the expression of several oncogenes, elucidating the regulation of miR-7 activity could shed light on various cancer etiologies. In this review, we discuss the current knowledge on the ciRS-7/miR-7 axis in cancer-related pathways and propose possible models to explain the significance of coexpressing miR-7 alongside a circRNA inhibitor.

title: Angiotensin II Evokes Angiogenic Signals within Skeletal Muscle through Co-ordinated Effects on Skeletal Myocytes and Endothelial Cells
text: Muscle overload triggers the expression of angiogenic factors, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2, leading to the growth of new capillaries. We found that the overload-induced increase in angiogenesis, as well as the expression of VEGF, MMP-2, and MT1-MMP transcripts, was significantly reduced in muscle-specific VEGF knockout (VEGF KO) mice, indicating the critical role of myocyte-derived VEGF in this process. The upstream mediators that contribute to overload-induced VEGF production have yet to be identified. Our findings suggest that muscle overload increases angiotensinogen expression, a precursor of angiotensin (Ang) II, and that Ang II signaling plays a crucial role in basal VEGF production in C2C12 cells. Moreover, matrix-bound VEGF released from myoblasts can activate endothelial cells, as evidenced by elevated phospho-p38 levels. Interestingly, exogenous Ang II can also enhance VEGF expression and MMP-2 transcript levels in C2C12 myotubes, and this response is observed in skeletal muscle endothelial cells as well. Our studies demonstrate the requirement for muscle-derived VEGF in overload-induced angiogenesis and highlight a role for Ang II in basal VEGF production in skeletal muscle. However, while Ang II signaling is activated following overload and contributes to muscle VEGF production, inhibition of this pathway is not sufficient to halt overload-induced angiogenesis, suggesting that AT1-independent signals maintain VEGF production in losartan-treated muscle.

title: A specific loop in human DNA polymerase mu allows switching between creative and DNA-instructed synthesis
text: Human DNA polymerase mu (Polμ) is a member of the DNA polymerase family X, possessing both terminal transferase and DNA-templated polymerization activities. Despite its unconventional selection of template information, Polμ exhibits its maximum catalytic efficiency in DNA-templated reactions. The terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) domain of Polμ, containing a specific loop (loop1), confers its terminal transferase activity upon the enzyme. Deletion of loop1 from Polμ leads to a loss of TdT activity but enhances DNA binding and template-dependent polymerization. Interestingly, the insertion of loop1 from TdT into Polμ (replacing its cognate loop1) results in a chimeric enzyme with TdT activity, preferentially inserting dGTP residues, but with a significantly reduced template-dependent polymerization capacity. This suggests that a specialized loop in Polμ, capable of adopting alternative conformations, endows the enzyme with a dual functional capacity: (i) the ability to create new DNA information independently of the template, in which loop1 plays a key role as a 'pseudotemplate'; and (ii) the ability to polymerize DNA using the template strand. Recent in vivo and in vitro studies suggest that this dual capacity may be advantageous in resolving microhomology-mediated end-joining reactions.

title: Dnmt1-Independent CG Methylation Contributes to Nucleosome Positioning in Diverse Eukaryotes
text: Dnmt1, an epigenetic enzyme, propagates symmetrical CG methylation in many eukaryotes. However, their genomes typically lack CG dinucleotides due to imperfect repair of deaminated methylcytosines. Surprisingly, we found that many species lacking Dnmt1 still exhibit symmetrical CG methylation, which is catalyzed by a different DNA methyltransferase family, Dnmt5. Our survey of diverse organisms that diverged over a billion years ago revealed that Dnmt5-containing species often display clustered methylation, specifically in nucleosome linkers. These clusters occur at unprecedented densities and disfavor nucleosomes, contributing to nucleosome positioning between clusters. Notably, these species have small, transcriptionally active nuclei that approach the physical limits of chromatin compaction. Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated genome architecture, in which dense methylation influences nucleosome positions, potentially facilitating nuclear processes under extreme spatial constraints.

title: The Immunogenicity and Safety of the Live-attenuated SA 14-14-2 Japanese Encephalitis Vaccine Given with a Two-dose Primary Schedule in Children
text:
Effective and tolerable vaccination is a crucial strategy to prevent Japanese encephalitis (JE) in areas where the disease is prevalent. Although the live attenuated SA 14-14-2 JE vaccine (LAJEV) has been widely used since its introduction, there is a lack of systemic data on its safety and immunogenicity in Korea. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted an open-label, prospective cohort study to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of LAJEV in a two-dose primary series.
Participants
Ninety subjects were enrolled in the study, and LAJEV was administered in a 12-month interval. Neutralizing antibody titers were measured before and after each vaccination, and active monitoring for adverse events was conducted.
Immunogenicity
After the first dose, 91.1% of subjects demonstrated seroprotection with a geometric mean titer (GMT) of 40.9. Seroprotection rates after the second dose were 97%, and GMT showed an increase of 6.5-fold.
Safety
Most adverse events following immunization were self-limited, and no serious adverse events were reported until 42 days after each dose.
Conclusion
Our findings suggest that the two-dose administration of LAJEV in the primary immunization schedule is highly immunogenic and safe. These results provide valuable insights into the use of LAJEV in preventing JE in endemic areas.

title: Centrosome-dependent asymmetric inheritance of the midbody ring in Drosophila germline stem cell division
text: Many stem cells, including Drosophila germline stem cells (GSCs), exhibit asymmetric division, resulting in one stem cell and one differentiating daughter cell. However, the extent to which this asymmetry in cell division correlates with cell fate and has functional implications has been poorly explored. To address this question, we investigated the segregation of the midbody ring (MR) during GSC divisions in a centrosome age-dependent manner. Our findings reveal that male GSCs, which inherit the mother centrosome, exclude the MR, while female GSCs, which we demonstrate inherit the daughter centrosome, inherit the MR. Furthermore, we found that stem cell identity correlates with the mode of MR inheritance. Taken together, our data suggest that the MR does not inherently determine stem cell identity, although its stereotypical inheritance is under the control of stemness and potentially provides a platform for asymmetric segregation of certain factors.

title: Penile Curvature Incidence in Hypospadias: Can It Be Determined?
text: The study aimed to retrospectively determine the actual incidence of congenital penile curvature in various forms of hypospadias, in order to inform intraoperative assessment and correction of curvature. The study analyzed 842 patients with hypospadias who underwent surgery between 2003 and 2010, divided into two groups. The first group was routinely checked for curvature during surgery, while the second group had curvature assessed primarily in cases of severe hypospadias. The results were analyzed using Fisher's and chi-square tests. A total of 238 cases (28.3%) of associated curvature were confirmed. Curvature was found to be significantly more common in the first group, particularly in regards to hypospadias in general (P < 0.01), as well as distal (P < 0.05) and midshaft forms (P < 0.01). The study found that penile curvature is a common feature in hypospadias, particularly in distal forms. The study suggests that intraoperative testing for associated curvature should be considered a routine procedure in hypospadias repair.

title: Home birth and barriers to referring women with obstetric complications to hospitals: a mixed-methods study in Zahedan, southeastern Iran
text:
Background:
One significant factor contributing to high maternal mortality rates in developing countries is the delay in seeking emergency obstetric care (EmOC) facilities. This study aimed to identify the factors that hinder midwives and parturient women from utilizing hospitals when complications arise during home births in Sistan and Baluchestan province, Iran, where 23% of deliveries take place outside of hospital settings.
Methods:
A mixed-methods approach was employed in this study, combining both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis techniques. In the quantitative phase, the researchers compared existing health sector data with World Health Organization (WHO) standards for the availability and use of EmOC services. In the qualitative phase, interviews were conducted with midwives and traditional birth attendants, as well as in-depth interviews with 21 mothers. The data collected in this phase were managed according to qualitative data analysis principles.
Results:
The study findings revealed that three primary factors contribute to indecisiveness and delays in seeking EmOC among midwives and mothers: socio-cultural and familial reasons, apprehension about being insulted by physicians, and the need to protect professional integrity in front of patients. Additionally, the low quality and cost of EmOC, as well as the mothers' lack of health insurance, also contribute to delays in referral.
Conclusions:
Women who choose to give birth at home accept the risk of complications arising. Training midwives and persuading mothers and significant others to refer women to hospitals in the event of life-threatening complications is crucial in increasing the use of available hospitals. Hospitals must be safe, comfortable, and culturally sensitive environments for childbirth, and appropriate consideration should be given to ethical and cultural concerns. Addressing financial and insurance-related issues can also help midwives and mothers make informed decisions when complications arise.

title: ATPase-Dependent Control of the Mms21 SUMO Ligase during DNA Repair
text:
The modification of proteins by SUMO (Small Ubiquitin-like Modifier) is crucial for maintaining genome integrity, particularly during DNA replication. The Mms21-branch of the SUMO pathway counteracts recombination intermediates at damaged replication forks, facilitating sister chromatid disjunction. The Mms21 SUMO ligase docks with the arm region of the Smc5 protein in the Smc5/6 complex, which cooperates in recombinational DNA repair. However, the mechanism controlling the activity of the SUMO ligase remains unclear.
Our study reveals that the activity of the SUMO ligase and the chromosome disjunction functions of Mms21 depend on its docking to an intact and active Smc5/6 complex. This suggests that the Smc5/6-Mms21 complex operates as a large SUMO ligase in vivo. Although the E3 and nucleotide-binding domains of Smc5/6 are physically distant, Mms21-dependent sumoylation requires the binding of ATP to Smc5, which is a step in the ligase mechanism that assists Ubc9 function. This communication is enabled by a conserved disruption in the coiled coil domain of Smc5, suggesting potential conformational changes that activate the SUMO ligase.
Scanning force microscopy of the Smc5-Mms21 heterodimer reveals that the molecule is physically remodeled in an ATP-dependent manner. Our results demonstrate that the ATP-binding activity of the Smc5/6 complex is coordinated with its SUMO ligase, through the coiled coil domain of Smc5 and the physical remodeling of the molecule, to promote sumoylation and chromosome disjunction during DNA repair.

title: Cadherins in brain morphogenesis and wiring.
text: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion molecules that play crucial roles in animal development, particularly in the formation and maintenance of tissue architecture. Over the past decade, significant progress has been made in understanding the functions of cadherin-related molecules in the nervous system. These molecules not only regulate cell adhesion but also influence cell proliferation and planar cell polarity, and are essential for the proper development and function of the nervous system. In this review, we will discuss the roles of cadherins and related molecules in neural development and function in the vertebrate brain.

title: Autocrine WNT signaling contributes to breast cancer cell proliferation via the canonical WNT pathway and EGFR transactivation
text: De-regulation of the Wingless and Integration Site Growth Factor (WNT) signaling pathway through mutations in the Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC) and Axin proteins, which target β-catenin for degradation, has been linked to various types of human cancer. However, these genetic alterations are rarely observed in breast tumors. Nonetheless, there is evidence to suggest that WNT signaling may also be dysregulated in breast cancer. Most breast tumors exhibit hypermethylation of the promoter region of Secreted Frizzled-related Protein 1 (sFRP1), a negative WNT pathway regulator, leading to decreased expression of sFRP1 and enhanced WNT signaling. We previously demonstrated that, in addition to the canonical WNT/β-catenin pathway, WNT signaling activates the Extracellular Signal-Regulated Kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) pathway in mouse mammary epithelial cells via Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) transactivation. Using WNT modulators, sFRP1 and short interfering RNA-mediated Dishevelled (DVL) knockdown, we interfered with autocrine WNT signaling at the ligand-receptor level. The impact on proliferation was measured by cell counting, YOPRO, and the MTT (3-[4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl]-2,5-diphenyl-tetrazolium bromide) assay; β-catenin, EGFR, ERK1/2 activation, and Poly (ADP-ribose) Polymerase (PARP) cleavages were assessed by Western blotting after treatment of human breast cancer cell lines with conditioned media, purified proteins, small-molecule inhibitors, or blocking antibodies. Phospho-DVL and stabilized β-catenin are present in many breast tumor cell lines, indicating autocrine WNT signaling activity. Interfering with this loop decreases active β-catenin levels, lowers ERK1/2 activity, blocks proliferation, and induces apoptosis in MDA-MB-231, BT474, SkBr3, JIMT-1, and MCF-7 cells. The effects of WNT signaling are mediated partly by EGFR transactivation in human breast cancer cells in a metalloprotease- and Src-dependent manner. Furthermore, Wnt1 rescues Estrogen Receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer cells from the anti-proliferative effects of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-HT) and this activity can be blocked by an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Our data suggest that interference with autocrine WNT signaling in human breast cancer reduces proliferation and survival of human breast cancer cells and rescues ER+ tumor cells from 4-HT by activation of the canonical WNT pathway and EGFR transactivation. These findings suggest that interference with WNT signaling at the ligand-receptor level in combination with other targeted therapies may improve the efficiency of breast cancer treatments.

title: Alternative Markers of Hyperglycemia and Risk of Diabetes
text:
Objective: Fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-anhydroglucitol (1,5-AG) have been proposed as potential markers of short-term glycemic control in patients with diabetes. However, their associations with diabetes risk are not well understood.
Design and Methods: We conducted a cohort study using data from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study (2005-2006) to investigate the associations between fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-AG and the incidence of diabetes. Participants (n=1,299) were free of diabetes at baseline and were followed up for a median of 3.3 years. Incident diabetes was self-reported during annual telephone calls.
Results: During the follow-up period, 119 new cases of diabetes were identified. Compared to the lowest quartile, the fourth quartile of fructosamine and glycated albumin were significantly associated with an increased risk of diabetes (hazard ratio [HR] 3.99 [95% CI 1.93-8.28] and 5.22 [2.49-10.94], respectively). In contrast, the fourth quartile of 1,5-AG was associated with a significantly lower diabetes risk (0.27 [0.14-0.55]). These associations remained significant after adjustment for hemoglobin A(1c) (A1C) or fasting glucose.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-AG may be useful markers of diabetes risk, independently of baseline A1C and fasting glucose. These alternative biomarkers may provide valuable insights into the development of diabetes and help identify individuals at risk for the disease.

title: ROR-γ drives androgen receptor expression and represents a therapeutic target in castration-resistant prostate cancer
text: The androgen receptor (AR) is overexpressed and hyperactivated in human castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), yet the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. In this study, we discovered that retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor γ (ROR-γ) is overexpressed and amplified in metastatic CRPC tumors, and it plays a crucial role in driving AR expression. ROR-γ recruits nuclear receptor coactivator 1 and 3 (NCOA1 and NCOA3, also known as SRC-1 and SRC-3) to an AR-ROR response element (RORE) to stimulate AR gene transcription. We found that ROR-γ antagonists suppress the expression of both AR and its variant AR-V7 in prostate cancer (PCa) cell lines and tumors, and they significantly diminish genome-wide AR binding, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) abundance, and expression of the AR target gene network. Moreover, ROR-γ antagonists exhibit potent anti-tumor activity in multiple AR-expressing, but not AR-negative, xenograft PCa models, and they effectively sensitize CRPC tumors to enzalutamide without evident toxicity in mice. These findings establish ROR-γ as a key regulator of AR in CRPC and a promising therapeutic target for advanced PCa.

title: affy--analysis of Affymetrix GeneChip data at the probe level.
text:
MOTIVATION: The processing of Affymetrix GeneChip data has been a recent area of focus for data analysts. In response to the limitations of the traditional methodology, several alternative approaches have been proposed and are now widely used.
RESULTS: The affy package is an R software package designed to facilitate the analysis of oligonucleotide arrays manufactured by Affymetrix. In its second release, the package offers a high degree of flexibility in the analysis of probe intensity data, allowing for extensive manipulation and modification of the data. In this paper, we provide an overview of the primary classes and functions within the package and demonstrate their application in processing probe-level data. Additionally, we highlight the significance of probe-level analysis in the context of Affymetrix GeneChip technology.

title: Inducible caspase-9 suicide gene controls adverse effects from alloreplete T cells after haploidentical stem cell transplantation.
text: To assess the feasibility of a single T-cell manipulation to eliminate alloreactivity while preserving antiviral and antitumor T cells, we infused 12 haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients with increasing numbers of alloreactive haploidentical T cells expressing the inducible caspase 9 suicide gene (iC9-T cells). We evaluated whether the iC9-T cells could produce immune reconstitution and if any resulting graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) could be controlled by administering a chemical inducer of dimerization (CID; AP1903/Rimiducid). All patients who received >10(4) alloreactive iC9-T cells per kilogram experienced rapid reconstitution of immune responses towards 5 major pathogenic viruses and concurrent control of active infections. Four patients received a single dose of AP1903. CID infusion eliminated 85% to 95% of circulating CD3(+)CD19(+) T cells within 30 minutes, with no recurrence of GVHD within 90 days. In one patient, symptoms and signs of GVHD-associated cytokine release syndrome (CRS-hyperpyrexia, high levels of proinflammatory cytokines, and rash) resolved within 2 hours of AP1903 infusion. One patient with varicella zoster virus meningitis and acute GVHD had iC9-T cells present in the cerebrospinal fluid, which were reduced by >90% after CID. Notably, virus-specific T cells recovered even after AP1903 administration and continued to protect against infection. Therefore, alloreactive iC9-T cells can reconstitute immunity post-transplant and administration of CID can eliminate them from both peripheral blood and the central nervous system (CNS), leading to rapid resolution of GVHD and CRS. This approach may be useful for the rapid and effective treatment of toxicities associated with the infusion of engineered T lymphocytes. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT01494103.

title: Clonal analysis of epiblast fate during germ layer formation in the mouse embryo.
text: In this study, the fate of cells in the epiblast at the prestreak and early primitive streak stages of mouse embryos was investigated by injecting horseradish peroxidase (HRP) into individual cells in situ and tracking the labelled descendants up to the neural plate stage. The results showed that ectodermal cells were derived from epiblast progenitors located anterior to the primitive streak, while embryonic mesoderm was derived from cells throughout the epiblast, with the most anterior mesoderm cells originating from the posterior part of the streak. Endodermal cells were derived from a region that included, but extended beyond, the region producing the head process. The study also found that clonal descendants were not confined to a single germ layer or to extraembryonic mesoderm, indicating that these lineages are not separated at the beginning of gastrulation. Additionally, the population doubling time of labelled cells was 7.5 hours, and 43% of the cells were in or had completed a fourth cell cycle. The results suggest that while individual cells in the epiblast sheet behave independently, morphogenetic movement during germ layer formation is coordinated in the population as a whole. The fate map obtained in this study is similar to those of other vertebrates, indicating that topological fate relationships are conserved among them.

title: Effects of a High-Intensity Functional Exercise Program on Dependence in Activities of Daily Living and Balance in Older Adults with Dementia
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of a high-intensity functional exercise program on independence in activities of daily living (ADLs) and balance in older individuals with dementia, with a focus on differences between various types of dementia.
Design: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (UMDEX study) conducted in residential care facilities in Umeå, Sweden.
Participants: 186 individuals aged 65 and older with a dementia diagnosis, Mini-Mental State Examination score of 10 or greater, and dependence in ADLs were randomly assigned to either a high-intensity functional exercise program (n=93) or a seated control activity (n=93).
Measurements: Blinded assessors evaluated ADL independence using the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) and Barthel Index (BI) and balance using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) at baseline and 4 (directly after intervention completion) and 7 months.
Results: Linear mixed models revealed no significant between-group effect on ADL independence at 4 (FIM=1.3, 95% CI=-1.6-4.3; BI=0.6, 95% CI=-0.2-1.4) or 7 (FIM=0.8, 95% CI=-2.2-3.8; BI=0.6, 95% CI=-0.3-1.4) months. However, a significant between-group effect in favor of exercise was observed on balance at 4 months (BBS=4.2, 95% CI=1.8-6.6). Interaction analyses revealed that exercise effects differed significantly between dementia types, with positive exercise effects observed in participants with non-Alzheimer's dementia according to the FIM at 7 months, BI and BBS at 4 and 7 months.
Conclusion: A 4-month high-intensity functional exercise program appears to slow decline in ADL independence and improve balance in older individuals with mild to moderate dementia living in residential care facilities, with the exercise program having a greater impact on participants with non-Alzheimer's dementia.

title: Effect of Health Literacy on Quality of Life amongst Patients with Ischaemic Heart Disease in Australian General Practice
text:
Background:
Patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) must have a good understanding of their health information to manage their risk factors and improve their quality of life. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between health literacy and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with ischaemic heart disease (IHD) and to identify potential confounding variables.
Methods:
This cross-sectional study included 587 patients with IHD recruited from a stratified sample of general practices in two Australian states (Queensland and South Australia) between 2007 and 2009. Health literacy was assessed using a validated questionnaire and classified as inadequate, marginal, or adequate. The physical and mental components of HRQoL were evaluated using the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form (SF12) questionnaire. Multiple linear regression analyses were used to adjust for confounding variables (sociodemographic variables, clinical history of IHD, number of CVD comorbidities, and CVD risk factors).
Results:
The study included 76.8% male patients, with an average age of 72.0±8.4 years. Health literacy showed a mean of 39.6±6.7 points, with 14.3% (95%CI 11.8-17.3) classified as inadequate. Scores for the physical component of HRQoL were 39.6 (95%CI 37.1-42.1), 42.1 (95%CI 40.8-43.3), and 44.8 (95%CI 43.3-46.2) for inadequate, marginal, and adequate health literacy, respectively (p-value for trend = 0.001). This association persisted after adjustment for confounders. Health literacy was not associated with the mental component of HRQoL (p-value = 0.482). Advanced age, lower educational level, disadvantaged socioeconomic position, and a larger number of CVD comorbidities adversely affected both health literacy and HRQoL.

Conclusion:
Inadequate health literacy was found to be a contributing factor to poor physical functioning in patients with IHD. Increasing health literacy may improve HRQoL and reduce the impact of IHD among patients with this chronic CVD.

title: in
text: Transglutaminase 2 (TGase 2) is a calcium-dependent enzyme that catalyzes both intracellular and extracellular cross-linking reactions by transamidation of specific glutamine residues. TGase 2 is involved in the membrane-mediated events required for glucose-stimulated insulin release from pancreatic beta cells. Our study shows that disrupting TGase 2 impairs glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. TGase 2-deficient mice exhibit glucose intolerance after intraperitoneal glucose loading and a tendency to develop hypoglycemia after exogenous insulin administration, which is attributed to enhanced insulin receptor substrate 2 (IRS-2) phosphorylation. The increased peripheral sensitivity to insulin in these mice partially compensates for the defective secretion. The TGase 2-deficient mouse phenotype resembles that of maturity-onset diabetes of young (MODY) patients. During screening for the human TGase 2 gene in Italian subjects with MODY-like clinical features, we identified a missense mutation (N333S) in the active site of the enzyme. These findings implicate TGase 2 as a potential candidate gene in type 2 diabetes.

title: Chromatin structure and gene expression programs of human embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells.
text: The knowledge of the global chromatin structure and gene expression programs of human embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) can provide a robust means to evaluate whether the genomes of these cells have similar pluripotent states. Recent studies have suggested that ESCs and iPSCs represent different pluripotent states with distinct gene expression profiles. In this study, we compare global chromatin structure and gene expression data for a panel of human ESCs and iPSCs. Genome-wide maps of nucleosomes with histone H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 modifications reveal little difference between ESCs and iPSCs in these marks. Gene expression profiles confirm that the transcriptional programs of ESCs and iPSCs show few consistent differences. Although some variation in chromatin structure and gene expression was observed in these cell lines, these variations did not enable the distinction between ESCs and iPSCs.

title: Myeloid Cells Expressing VEGF and Arginase-1 Following Uptake of Damaged Retinal Pigment Epithelium Suggests Potential Mechanism That Drives the Onset of Choroidal Angiogenesis in Mice
text: While data suggests both myeloid cell accumulation during choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and complement activation, no clear explanation exists for the angiogenic drive that promotes pathological angiogenesis. One possible explanation is the early and specific conditioning and activation of the myeloid cell infiltrate. Using a laser-induced CNV murine model, we found that the recruitment of macrophages derived from monocytes and microglia prior to angiogenesis and contemporaneous with lesional complement activation may be a driving force behind pathological angiogenesis. Early recruited CD11b(+) cells expressed a distinct gene signature of selective inflammatory mediators, including a pronounced Arg-1 expression. Activated macrophages from the retina and peripheral blood were found to express enhanced VEGF expression, and this occurred prior to exaggerated VEGF expression from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) or the earliest stages of angiogenesis. These initial events, including distinct VEGF (+) Arg-1(+) myeloid cells, subsided when CNV was established and RPE-VEGF expression was maximal. Depletion of inflammatory CCR2-positive monocytes confirmed the origin of infiltrating monocyte Arg-1 expression, and following depletion, Arg-1 signal was lost, and CNV was suppressed. In vitro data also supported a mechanism whereby myeloid cells uptake damaged RPE or its derivatives, leading to the generation of VEGF (+) Arg-1(+) phenotype in vivo. Our findings reveal a potential early driver of angiogenesis via myeloid-derived VEGF drive following uptake of damaged RPE, providing an explanation for why CNV develops during any stage of macular degeneration and offering a therapeutic target for future interventions.

title: Monitoring Tumorigenesis and Senescence In Vivo with a p16INK4a-Luciferase Model
text: Monitoring cancer and aging in living organisms remains a challenging task. Here, we present a luciferase knockin mouse (p16(LUC)) that accurately reflects the expression of p16(INK4a), a tumor suppressor and aging biomarker. By assessing luminescence in p16(+/LUC) mice over their lifespan, we observed an exponential increase in luminescence with aging, which varied significantly among a group of contemporarily housed, syngeneic mice. Contrary to expectations, expression of p16(INK4a) with aging did not predict cancer development, suggesting that the accumulation of senescent cells is not the primary determinant of cancer-related death. In all 14 tumor models tested, expression of p16(LUC) was focally activated by early neoplastic events, allowing for sensitive visualization of tumors with greater sensitivity than other imaging modalities. Activation of p16(INK4a) was observed in both the emerging neoplasm and surrounding stromal cells. This work suggests that p16(INK4a) activation is a universal characteristic of all emerging cancers, making the p16(LUC) allele a sensitive and unbiased reporter of neoplastic transformation.

title: The Bacteroides sp. 3_1_23 Pif1 protein is a multifunctional helicase
text: ScPif1 DNA helicase, a prototypical member of the 5'-to-3' helicase superfamily, has been conserved across bacteria to human and plays a crucial role in maintaining genomic homeostasis. While extensive research has been conducted on eukaryotic Pif1 helicases, including those from yeast and humans, the functional and biochemical properties of prokaryotic Pif1 helicases remain largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate the expression, purification, and biochemical characterization of Pif1 helicase from Bacteroides sp. 3_1_23 (BsPif1). Our results demonstrate that BsPif1 binds to a wide range of DNA substrates, including partial duplex DNAs with 5'-overhangs, fork-like substrates, D-loop structures, and flap-like substrates, indicating that BsPif1 may play a role in resolving stalled DNA replication forks and enhancing Okazaki fragment maturation. Additionally, BsPif1 resolves R-loop structures and unwinds DNA-RNA hybrids, similar to its eukaryotic homologues. Furthermore, BsPif1 efficiently unfolds G-quadruplexes and disrupts nucleoprotein complexes. These findings suggest that prokaryotic Pif1 helicases may play a crucial role in resolving common issues that arise during DNA transactions. Interestingly, our results reveal that BsPif1 is distinct from yeast Pif1 but shares similarities with human Pif1 in terms of substrate specificity, helicase activity, and mode of action. These findings have important implications for understanding the functional roles of prokaryotic Pif1 helicases in vivo.

title: Netting neutrophils in autoimmune small-vessel vasculitis
text: Small-vessel vasculitis (SVV) is a chronic autoinflammatory condition associated with antineutrophil cytoplasm autoantibodies (ANCAs). Our findings indicate that chromatin fibers, known as neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), are released by ANCA-stimulated neutrophils and contain the targeted autoantigens proteinase-3 (PR3) and myeloperoxidase (MPO). The deposition of NETs in inflamed kidneys and the presence of circulating MPO-DNA complexes suggest that NET formation plays a key role in triggering vasculitis and promoting the autoimmune response against neutrophil components in individuals with SVV.

title: Control of Nutrient Stress-Induced Metabolic Reprogramming by PKCζ in Tumorigenesis
text: Cancer cells exhibit heightened metabolic activity and adaptability to survive and proliferate under nutrient-scarce conditions. We found that PKCζ deficiency fosters the plasticity necessary for cancer cells to reprogram their metabolism to utilize glutamine through the serine biosynthetic pathway when glucose is limiting. PKCζ suppresses the expression of key enzymes in this pathway, PHGDH and PSAT1, and phosphorylates PHGDH to inhibit its activity. Notably, mice lacking PKCζ exhibit enhanced intestinal tumorigenesis and increased levels of these enzymes, while patients with low PKCζ levels have a poor prognosis. Additionally, PKCζ and caspase-3 activities are correlated with PHGDH levels in human intestinal tumors, indicating that PKCζ is a crucial metabolic tumor suppressor in both mice and humans.

title: XRCC4's interaction with XLF is required for coding (but not signal) end joining
text:
XRCC4 and XLF are structurally related proteins that play critical roles in DNA Ligase IV function. XRCC4 forms a stable complex with DNA Ligase IV, while XLF interacts directly with XRCC4. Both XRCC4 and XLF form homodimers that can polymerize into heterotypic filaments independently of DNA Ligase IV. Recent structural and biochemical data suggest that XRCC4 and XLF cooperate to generate a filamentous structure that facilitates DNA bridging. Our findings indicate that reducing XRCC4's affinity for XLF leads to DNA repair deficits, including a surprising defect in VDJ coding, but not signal end joining. These data support a model where XRCC4/XLF complexes maintain DNA ends together, a requirement for coding end joining, but not for signal end joining. Additionally, our data suggest that DNA-PK phosphorylation of XRCC4/XLF complexes disrupts DNA bridging in vitro, implying a regulatory role for DNA-PK's phosphorylation of XRCC4/XLF complexes.
In summary, XRCC4 and XLF are essential proteins for DNA Ligase IV function, and their interaction generates a filamentous structure that promotes DNA bridging. Reducing XRCC4's affinity for XLF leads to DNA repair deficits, and DNA-PK phosphorylation of XRCC4/XLF complexes disrupts DNA bridging.

title: Loss of imprinting in colorectal cancer linked to hypomethylation of H19 and IGF2.
text: Epigenetic alterations in human cancers, including global DNA demethylation, gene-specific hypomethylation, and promoter hypermethylation, as well as loss of imprinting (LOI) of the insulin-like growth factor-II gene (IGF2), have been well-documented. Previous studies have proposed a mechanism for LOI involving hypermethylation of a differentially methylated region (DMR) upstream of the H19 gene, leading to the activation of the normally silent maternal allele of IGF2. However, our findings challenge this model, as we have found that colorectal cancers exhibit hypomethylation of both the H19 DMR and a DMR upstream of exon 3 of IGF2. This hypomethylation is present in both cancerous tissues and normal mucosa from the same patients, as well as in cell lines with somatic cell knockout of DNA methyltransferases DNMT1 and DNMT3B. These data suggest that hypomethylation may play a role in LOI, and that the traditional IGF2-H19 enhancer competition model for IGF2 imprinting may not be applicable to the human colon. Instead, an alternative model for LOI may involve a transcriptional repressor acting on the normally silent maternal allele of IGF2.

title: Management of patients with sore throats in relation to guidelines: An interview study in Sweden
text:
Objective:
This study aimed to investigate how Swedish general practitioners (GPs) manage patients with sore throats in relation to current guidelines, as expressed through semi-structured interviews.
Design:
Qualitative content analysis was used to analyze the interviews.
Setting:
The study was conducted in Swedish primary care.
Subjects:
A strategic sample of 25 GPs was selected.
Main Outcome Measures:
The study focused on the GPs' perceived management of sore throat patients, including their knowledge of current guidelines and their adherence to them.
Results:
The study found that nine of the interviewed GPs were adherent to current guidelines for sore throat management, while 16 were non-adherent. The two groups differed in their knowledge of guidelines, with adherent GPs sharing knowledge within their primary care team, while non-adherent GPs relied on idiosyncratic knowledge. Adherent GPs had a more restrictive approach to antibiotic use, while non-adherent GPs believed that any bacterial infection should be identified and treated with antibiotics. Adherent GPs also had a more thorough approach to patient history and examination, while non-adherent GPs often relied on redundant examination. Non-adherent GPs reported difficulties in getting patients to abstain from antibiotics, while adherent GPs did not encounter such problems.
Conclusion:
The study found that while two-thirds of the GPs were non-adherent and had a liberal attitude towards antibiotics, one-third were guideline adherent with a restricted view on antibiotics. Non-adherent GPs had significant knowledge gaps, and adherent GPs had discussed guidelines within their primary care team. The study suggests that knowledge shared within the team promotes guideline implementation.

title: Catch and release: how do kinetochores hook the right microtubules during mitosis?
text: Sport fishermen employ tension on their lines to prevent hooked fish from escaping. Similarly, at the molecular level, a mechanism similar to this angling technique is employed at kinetochores to ensure accuracy during mitosis. The mitotic spindle attaches randomly to chromosomes and then stabilizes these attachments through tension exerted by opposing microtubules. Unstable attachments, lacking tension, are quickly released, allowing for another chance at proper biorientation. This principle of stabilization through tension is not limited to mitosis, but also applies to other physiological contexts such as cell adhesion, motility, hemostasis, and tissue morphogenesis. Here, we review models for the stabilization of kinetochore attachments with an eye towards emerging models for other force-activated systems. Although the mitosis field has primarily focused on one kinase-based mechanism, it is possible that multiple mechanisms work together to stabilize properly bioriented kinetochores, and principles governing other tension-sensitive systems may also apply to kinetochores.

title: Label-free in vivo imaging of myelinated axons in health and disease with spectral confocal reflectance microscopy
text: We have developed a novel technique for high-resolution in vivo imaging of myelinated axons in the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerve without the need for fluorescent labeling. This method, based on spectral confocal reflectance microscopy (SCoRe), leverages a conventional laser-scanning confocal system to generate images by combining the simultaneously reflected signals from multiple lasers of different wavelengths. Unique color patterns are generated that allow for the identification and tracing of individual myelinated fibers in dense axonal areas, including nodes of Ranvier and Schmidt-Lanterman incisures. These patterns can be used to detect various myelin pathologies. Using SCoRe, we have achieved chronic brain imaging up to 400 μm deep, capturing the de novo myelination of mouse cortical axons in vivo. Additionally, we have demonstrated the feasibility of imaging myelinated axons in the human cerebral cortex. SCoRe represents a significant addition to the evolving toolbox for imaging myelination in living animals and has the potential to be applied in humans.

title: Applicability of current staging/categorization of α-synuclein pathology and their clinical relevance
text: In Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the distribution of alpha-synuclein (alphaS) pathology is predictable and follows a specific topographic pattern. Currently, two staging/categorization systems, Braak's and McKeith's, are used to assess the severity and probability of related clinical symptoms, such as dementia and extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS). In a cohort of 226 alphaS-positive individuals, we evaluated the applicability of these systems and the frequency of dementia and EPS. Our results showed that 83% of subjects had a distribution pattern compatible with the current staging/categorization systems. Notably, around 55% of subjects with widespread alphaS pathology (Braak's PD stages 5-6) did not display clinical signs of dementia or EPS, while 48% of subjects who fulfilled the McKeith criteria for diffuse neocortical category and had mild Alzheimer's disease-related pathology were demented and 54% displayed EPS. Additionally, 17% of subjects deviated from the suggested caudo-rostral propagation, suggesting alternative routes of progression. Our findings confirm that current staging/categorization systems can be applied to most subjects with alphaS pathology, but highlight the need to reassess the actual disease process, as around half of subjects with abundant alphaS pathology remain neurologically intact.

title: Batf is important for IL-4 expression in T follicular helper cells
text: Other than T helper (Th)-2 cells, T follicular helper (Tfh) cells are a prominent subset of IL-4-producing T cells, crucial for the regulation of type 2 humoral immunity; however, the transcriptional control of IL-4 production in Tfh cells remains largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate the role of the basic leucine zipper transcription factor ATF-like, Batf, in IL-4 expression in Tfh cells. Our findings reveal that Batf plays a pivotal role in IL-4 production in Tfh cells, rather than in canonical Th2 cells. Specifically, Batf, in collaboration with interferon regulatory factor (IRF) 4, Stat3, and Stat6, directly binds to and activates the CNS2 region in the IL-4 locus, leading to IL-4 production in Tfh cells. Additionally, Batf-to-c-Maf signaling is a critical determinant of IL-4 expression in Tfh cells. Notably, Batf deficiency impairs the generation of IL-4-producing Tfh cells, resulting in protection against allergic asthma. Our results thus demonstrate a positive role of Batf in promoting the generation of pro-allergic IL-4-producing Tfh cells.

title: Autocrine VEGF Signaling Synergizes with EGFR in Tumor Cells to Promote Epithelial Cancer Development
text: It has been established that tumor-derived VEGF acts on endothelial cells to promote angiogenesis and tumor growth. Our findings demonstrate that in K5-SOS-dependent mouse skin tumors, autocrine VEGF is essential for tumor cell proliferation in a cell-autonomous and angiogenesis-independent manner. VEGF is upregulated in SOS-expressing tumors, and its deletion in epidermal cells delays tumorigenesis by suppressing angiogenesis and tumor cell proliferation. Epidermis-specific Flt1 deletion also impairs tumorigenesis and proliferation. Interestingly, complete tumor inhibition occurs in the absence of VEGF in EGFR mutant mice, suggesting that VEGFR and EGFR cooperate in promoting tumor growth. Our findings reveal that K5-SOS upregulates VEGF, Flt1, and Neuropilin-1 in an Erk-dependent manner, leading to an autocrine proliferation loop. Conversely, EGFR inhibits tumor cell apoptosis. Moreover, Flt1 is upregulated in human squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and its inhibition in SCC cells impairs proliferation. These findings highlight the importance of VEGF as a growth factor for epidermal tumors, beyond its role in angiogenesis.

title: Discovery and development of the Polo-like kinase inhibitor volasertib in cancer therapy
text: The Polo-like kinase (Plk) family, particularly Plk1, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in oncology due to their crucial involvement in cell cycle regulation. Recent years have seen the development of several Plk1 inhibitors, with some agents showing encouraging results in early-phase clinical trials. This review focuses on volasertib (BI 6727), a potent and selective Plk inhibitor, which has shown promising activity in various cancer cell lines and xenograft models of human cancer. Trials to date have demonstrated that volasertib has clinical efficacy in a range of malignancies, with the most promising results seen in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Notably, recent phase II data have shown that volasertib combined with low-dose cytarabine (LDAC) was associated with higher response rates and improved event-free survival than LDAC alone in patients with previously untreated AML. Given the encouraging results and manageable safety profile of volasertib, it is currently in phase III development as a potential treatment for patients with AML who are ineligible for intensive remission induction therapy. This area of major unmet need is particularly relevant, as many patients with AML are of an older age and frail. This review discusses the biologic rationale for Plk1 inhibitors in cancer, the clinical development of volasertib to date in solid tumors and AML, and the future identification of biomarkers that might predict response to volasertib and help determine the role of this agent in the clinic.

title: Babies driving robots: self-generated mobility in very young infants
text: Infants' ability to generate their own mobility through locomotion is crucial for their cognitive, social, and motor development. For some children with special needs, this mobility can only be achieved through assistive technology such as power wheelchairs. Historically, infants under 24 months of age were not considered candidates for power mobility training. However, recent research has shown that younger infants can learn to use their reaching and grasping abilities to operate power mobility devices. This interdisciplinary study combines previous work in motor development and learning in infants with special needs, and the application of robot technology for rehabilitation, to determine whether young infants can learn to drive a mobile robot without formal training. The study focused on two infants who participated in the most sessions and found that they increased their total session time, percentage of session time spent driving, and total path length. These results suggest that young infants can independently move themselves using a mobile robot, providing a foundation for further training studies to advance the self-generated mobility of infants with special needs. Future studies will explore various training and technology combinations to reduce barriers to exploration and promote the general development of infants with special needs.

title: Effects of Abciximab on the architecture of platelet-rich clots in patients with acute myocardial infarction undergoing primary coronary intervention.
text:
BACKGROUND: Abciximab, when combined with aspirin, has been shown to improve the TIMI 3 flow rate of the infarct-related artery in patients undergoing either percutaneous coronary intervention or thrombolysis. The present study aimed to investigate whether the reperfusion efficacy of abciximab is related to changes in the structure of blood clots in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS AND RESULTS: In a double-blind trial, 23 AMI patients received either abciximab or a placebo before primary stenting. Ex vivo platelet-rich clots (PRC) were analyzed before and after the administration of abciximab or placebo, and the viscoelastic (G' in dyne/cm2) and morphological (mean platelet aggregate surface area [SAG] in micrometer(2)) indexes of the clots were assessed. Abciximab administration significantly reduced G' by 63% (P=0.0001) and SAG by 65% (P=0.0007), compared to the placebo group. These changes were observed in all patients, regardless of whether they had previously received heparin.
CONCLUSIONS: Abciximab significantly reduces the size of platelet aggregates and increases the accessibility of fibrin to ex vivo PRC in AMI patients. These modifications may contribute to the improved coronary artery patency observed with abciximab.

title: Natural Mutagenesis of Human Genomes by Endogenous Retrotransposons
text: Two dominant classes of mobile genetic elements, Alu and L1 elements, continue to insert themselves into human genomes, generating millions of new retrotransposon insertions in individual human genomes worldwide. However, current technologies are limited in their ability to detect these young insertions, making it challenging to assess the true extent of germline mutagenesis caused by endogenous human retrotransposons. Here, we describe novel methods for detecting these young retrotransposon insertions and demonstrate that they are indeed abundant in human populations.
