In contrast, the platelet counts of the 107 patients without malaria ranged between 10,000 and 150,000/dL, with a mean value of 58,000/dL (SD ± 54,000) and a median of 50,000/dL.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that the presence of thrombocytopenia may serve as a predictor of malaria in adult patients.

title: AMPA receptor ligand binding domain mobility revealed by functional cross linking.
text: Glutamate receptors are primarily mediators of excitatory synaptic transmission in the central nervous system (CNS). The AMPA-type receptor subtype has rapid kinetics, with activation, deactivation, and desensitization occurring on a millisecond timescale or faster. Crystallographic, biochemical, and functional studies have revealed that GluR2 Cys mutants, which form intermolecular disulfide cross-links between the lower D2 lobes of the ligand binding core, can be trapped in a desensitized state. Using multi-channel rapid perfusion techniques, we investigated the state dependence of cross-linking in these mutants under both reducing and oxidizing conditions. Our findings show that both wild-type GluR2 and the G725C and S729C mutants exhibit normal activation and desensitization kinetics under reducing conditions, but the Cys mutants can be efficiently trapped in nonconducting states when oxidized. In contrast, the I664C mutant is only partially inactivated under oxidizing conditions. We also observed spontaneous trapping of receptors in the absence of agonist, which is due to two motions: spontaneous breaking of the D1 dimer interface and hyperextension of the lower lobes of the ligand binding core. These data suggest that the glutamate binding domains are surprisingly mobile in the absence of ligand, which could influence receptor activity in the brain.

title: Ncf1 (p47phox) Is Essential for Direct Regulatory T Cell Mediated Suppression of CD4+ Effector T Cells
text:
Background:
The mechanisms underlying the suppression of CD4+ effector T cells (Teffs) by CD4+FOXP3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) are complex and multifaceted. While several mechanisms have been proposed, none have been shown to fully explain the observed suppression. Previous studies have suggested that Tregs may modulate the microenvironment redox state, which could potentially contribute to their ability to suppress Teffs.
Methodology/Principal Findings:
To test the hypothesis that oxidants may mediate the direct suppression of Teffs by Tregs, we isolated Tregs and Teffs from wild-type (WT) C57BL/6 mice or Ncf1(p47phox)-deficient C57BL/6 mice, which lack NADPH oxidase function. We then co-cultured Teffs with unlabeled Tregs at varying Treg:Teff ratios in the presence of anti-CD3/CD28-coated beads for 3 days in suppression assays. Treg-mediated suppression was quantified by flow cytometric analysis of CFSE dilution in Teffs. The presence of the antioxidants n-acetylcysteine (NAC) or 2-mercaptoethanol or inhibitors of NADPH oxidase (diphenyleneiodonium and VAS-2870) resulted in reduced WT Treg-mediated suppression. The observed suppression was in part dependent on TGFβ, as it was partially blocked with neutralizing antibodies. The suppression of Teff proliferation induced by exogenous TGFβ treatment could be overcome with NAC. Ncf1-deficient Teff were slightly but significantly less sensitive than WT Teff to suppression by exogenous TGFβ. Ncf1-deficient Tregs suppressed Ncf1-deficient Teff very poorly compared to wild-type controls. There was partial but incomplete reconstitution of suppression in assays with WT Tregs and Ncf1-deficient Teff.
Conclusions/Significance:
Our findings provide evidence that NADPH oxidase-derived ROS plays a role in the direct Treg-mediated suppression of CD4+ effector T cells. The suppression is blocked by thiol-containing antioxidants, NADPH oxidase inhibitors, or a lack of Ncf1 expression in Tregs and Teffs. These results suggest that oxidants may represent a potential new target for therapeutic modulation of Treg function.

title: Oxidative damage targets complexes containing DNA methyltransferases, SIRT1, and polycomb members to promoter CpG Islands.
text: Cancer cells exhibit simultaneous global losses and gains in DNA methylation. We demonstrate that exposure to cellular oxidative stress through hydrogen peroxide treatment recruits DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) to damaged chromatin. DNMT1 becomes part of a complex(es) containing DNMT3B and members of the polycomb repressive complex 4 (PRC4). Hydrogen peroxide treatment causes the relocalization of these proteins from non-GC-rich to GC-rich areas. Key components are similarly enriched at gene promoters in an in vivo colitis model. Although high-expression genes enriched for members of the complex display histone mark and nascent transcription changes, CpG island-containing low-expression genes undergo promoter DNA methylation. This oxidative stress-induced process may explain cancer-specific aberrant DNA methylation and transcriptional silencing.

title: Expression profiles during dedifferentiation in newt lens regeneration revealed by expressed sequence tags
text:
The purpose of this research is to gain insights into the molecular mechanisms of dedifferentiation in the adult newt, specifically in regards to lens regeneration. To achieve this, the researchers obtained sequence resources for a newt lens regeneration study and analyzed the dedifferentiation process at the molecular level.
To obtain the sequence resources, the researchers purified mRNA from the dorsal iris during dedifferentiation and constructed a cDNA library. From this library, the researchers sequenced and analyzed 10,449 clones, resulting in the annotation of 780 contigs and 1,666 singlets.
The analysis revealed the presence of cancer- and apoptosis-related genes during newt dedifferentiation, as well as several candidate genes that may participate in reprogramming during this process. These findings suggest that the expression of cancer- and apoptosis-related genes may be hallmarks of dedifferentiation.
The expression sequence tag (EST) resource generated in this study provides a valuable tool for future research on newt dedifferentiation, and the sequence information is now available in GenBank (accession numbers FS290155-FS300559).

title: In vivo proliferation and cell cycle kinetics of long-term self-renewing hematopoietic stem cells.
text: A rare subset of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), known as long-term self-renewing HSC (LT-HSC), must undergo a substantial expansion to generate mature blood cells. The phenotypic isolation of LT-HSC from mice allows for the direct measurement of their proliferation kinetics. In this study, we analyzed the proliferation and cell cycle kinetics of LT-HSC in normal adult mice. Our findings revealed that approximately 5% of LT-HSC were in the S/G2/M phases of the cell cycle, while an additional 20% were in the G1 phase at any given time. BrdUrd incorporation was used to determine the rate at which different cohorts of HSC entered the cell cycle over time. Our results showed that approximately 50% of LT-HSC incorporated BrdUrd by 6 days, and >90% incorporated BrdUrd by 30 days. By 6 months, 99% of LT-HSC had incorporated BrdUrd. Using nested reverse transcription-PCR analysis, we found that cyclin D2 was expressed in a significant proportion of LT-HSC. Although approximately 75% of LT-HSC are quiescent in G0 at any one time, all HSC are recruited into the cell cycle on a regular basis, with 99% of LT-HSC dividing on average every 57 days.

title: The role of the tissue omega-6/omega-3 fatty acid ratio in regulating tumor angiogenesis
text: Angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, is a crucial step in tumor growth and metastasis. It is well established that metabolites derived from omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids, which must be obtained through the diet and cannot be synthesized de novo in mammals, have distinct effects on cellular processes. Omega-6 fatty acid (n-6 FA)-derived metabolites promote angiogenesis by increasing growth factor expression, while omega-3 fatty acids (n-3 FA) exhibit anti-angiogenic and antitumor properties. However, most studies have overlooked the role of the n-6 FA/n-3 FA ratio in angiogenesis and instead focused on the absolute levels of n-6 and n-3 FA. This review highlights the biochemical interactions between n-6 and n-3 FA and emphasizes the importance of considering the n-6/n-3 FA ratio in tissues for modulating tumor angiogenesis. We propose that future research should incorporate the n-6/n-3 FA ratio as a key element in experimental design and analysis. Moreover, we recommend that clinical interventions aim to both reduce n-6 metabolites and simultaneously increase n-3 FA intake to effectively modulate tumor angiogenesis.

title: The Natural Statistics of Audiovisual Speech
text:
Humans, like other living beings, are constantly exposed to a wide range of dynamic, multimodal, extended, and time-varying stimuli. Our sensory systems must process and transmit these signals to the brain, which then uses statistical regularities to guide the selection of appropriate actions. However, there is still much to be learned about how the brain processes complex multisensory signals, such as human speech. While some studies have investigated the statistical properties of unimodal signals and natural scenes, little is known about the natural statistics of audiovisual speech.
In this study, we aimed to fill this knowledge gap by identifying the major statistical features of audiovisual speech. We found several interesting patterns, including:
1. Robust correlations and close temporal correspondence between the area of the mouth opening and the acoustic envelope.
2. Strongest correlation between the area of the mouth opening and vocal tract resonances.
3. Temporal modulation of both the area of the mouth opening and the voice envelope in the 2-7 Hz frequency range.
4. Consistent timing of mouth movements relative to the onset of the voice, ranging from 100 to 300 ms.

These findings are consistent with recent neural theories of speech, which suggest that speech communication is a reciprocally coupled, multisensory event. The outputs of the signaler are matched to the neural processes of the receiver, allowing for more effective and efficient communication.
In summary, our study provides new insights into the natural statistics of audiovisual speech, shedding light on the complex processes involved in speech perception and production. These findings have important implications for our understanding of how the brain processes multisensory information and how speech communication works.

title: Establishment of human iPSC-based models for the study and targeting of glioma initiating cells
text:
Glioma tumour-initiating cells (GTICs) can arise from the transformation of neural progenitor cells (NPCs). Research on GTICs has primarily focused on isolating and studying primary tumors, as well as using human embryonic tissue. However, recent studies have also reported on the genomic landscape of human gliomas, revealing dysregulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) and tumor suppressor protein p53 in approximately 90% and 86% of primary tumors, respectively.
In this study, we investigate the use of human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to model gliomagenesis. We find that dysregulation of RTK and p53 signaling in hiPSC-derived NPCs (iNPCs) recapitulates GTIC properties in vitro. When these transformed iNPCs are transplanted into mice, they form highly aggressive tumors containing undifferentiated stem cells and their differentiated derivatives. Notably, metabolic modulation compromises the viability of GTICs.
To identify compounds specifically targeting GTICs, we screened a library of 101 anti-cancer drugs. Our results show that three molecules selectively target transformed iNPCs and primary GTICs, highlighting the potential of hiPSCs for studying human tumorigenesis.
In summary, our findings demonstrate the utility of hiPSCs for modeling gliomagenesis and identifying potential therapeutic targets for GTICs.

title: Thyroid Hormone Receptor Repression Linked to Type I Pneumocyte Associated Respiratory Distress Syndrome
text: Although the lung is a defining feature of air-breathing animals, the pathway regulating the formation of type I pneumocytes, which are responsible for gas exchange, remains poorly understood. In contrast, the glucocorticoid receptor and its cognate ligand have been well-studied in promoting the maturation of type II pneumocytes. However, our study reveals that mutations in the nuclear co-repressor SMRT in mice (SMRTmRID) lead to a previously unidentified respiratory distress syndrome caused by premature differentiation of type I pneumocytes. Interestingly, these mice are unresponsive to glucocorticoids, but can be fully rescued by treatment with anti-thyroid hormone drugs. Our findings suggest an unexpected role for the thyroid hormone receptor (TR) in lung development, as TR and SMRT control type I pneumocyte differentiation through the transcription factor Klf2. Moreover, mice lacking lung Klf2 fail to develop mature type I pneumocytes and die shortly after birth, mirroring the SMRTmRID phenotype. These results identify TR as a second nuclear receptor involved in lung development, specifically type I pneumocyte differentiation, and suggest a potential new therapeutic approach for treating respiratory distress syndrome that is unresponsive to glucocorticoids.

title: Assessing the ceRNA hypothesis with quantitative measurements of miRNA and target abundance.
text: Recent research has suggested that competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) can act as sponges for microRNAs (miRNAs) by binding to their target sites, and changes in ceRNA abundance can modulate miRNA activity. To better understand this hypothesis, it would be beneficial to determine the quantitative relationship between a miRNA and its endogenous target sites. In this study, we manipulated the abundance of an miR-122 target site in hepatocytes and livers and observed the effects on miR-122 target genes. We found that target repression was released in a threshold-like manner at high target site abundance (≥1.5 × 10(5) added target sites per cell), and this threshold was insensitive to the effective levels of the miRNA. Additionally, we found that global target site abundance in hepatocytes did not change significantly in response to extreme metabolic liver disease models, suggesting that modulation of miRNA target abundance is unlikely to have a significant impact on gene expression and metabolism through a ceRNA effect.

title: Immunological mechanisms for desensitization and tolerance in food allergy
text:
Food allergy is a significant public health concern in Western countries, affecting approximately 5% of children and 3-4% of adults. Currently, allergen-specific immunotherapy is being actively investigated as a potential treatment for food allergy, but it remains experimental. Researchers are working to determine the optimal protocol for food immunotherapy, including the route of administration, maintenance dose, duration of therapy, and ideal patient candidates. The mechanisms underlying successful food desensitization are not yet fully understood, as there is no standard immunotherapy protocol. However, possible mechanisms include:
* Suppression of mast cells and basophils
* Development of food-specific IgG4 antibodies
* Reduction in the food-specific IgE/IgG4 ratio
* Expansion and up-regulation of natural or inducible regulatory T cells
* Shift from a Th2 to a Th1 immune profile
* Development of anergy or deletion in antigen-specific cells

Additional research is needed to better understand these mechanisms and identify valuable biomarkers for monitoring food allergic patients on immunotherapy.

title: Prodromal non-motor symptoms of Parkinson’s disease
text: The motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), including bradykinesia, muscular rigidity, and tremor, are caused by the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Recent studies have shown that Lewy bodies, a hallmark of PD, accumulate in various neuronal cell types throughout the brain, with an ascending gradient of pathological involvement from the medulla oblongata to the neocortex. This suggests that PD is no longer considered a disease characterized by selective damage to dopaminergic neurons in the mesencephalon, but rather a severe multisystemic neurodegenerative disorder. Furthermore, neuropathological alterations outside the substantia nigra are closely linked to non-motor symptoms of PD, such as autonomic disturbances, olfactory dysfunctions, depression, and sleep disorders (including REM-sleep behavior disorder). As a result, there is growing interest in identifying prodromal non-motor symptoms of PD, which may serve as an early diagnostic marker. Indeed, studies suggest that these symptoms may appear before the onset of motor symptoms, and could potentially be used to evaluate the effectiveness of neuroprotective agents in the future. Several tests are available to detect these prodromal symptoms, which could contribute to an earlier diagnosis of PD.

title: Erythroid Krüppel-Like Factor Directly Activates the Basic Krüppel-Like Factor Gene in Erythroid Cells �
text: The Sp/Krüppel-like factor (Sp/Klf) family consists of approximately 25 zinc finger transcription factors that recognize CACCC boxes and GC-rich elements. We investigated basic Krüppel-like factor (Bklf/Klf3) and found that its expression in erythroid tissues is highly dependent on another family member, erythroid Krüppel-like factor (Eklf/Klf1). Our results show that Bklf mRNA is significantly reduced in erythroid tissues from Eklf-null murine embryos. We discovered that Bklf is driven by two promoters: a ubiquitously active GC-rich upstream promoter, 1a, and an erythroid downstream promoter, 1b. Transcripts from these promoters encode identical proteins, and both promoters are dependent on Eklf in erythroid cells. Interestingly, Eklf also activates both promoters in transient assays. Using an inducible form of Eklf, we demonstrated activation of the endogenous Bklf gene in the presence of an inhibitor of protein synthesis. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays confirmed that Eklf associates with both Bklf promoters. Eklf is typically an activator of transcription, while Bklf is known to repress transcription. Our findings support the hypothesis that feedback cross-regulation occurs within the Sp/Klf family in vivo.

title: Noncanonical Wnt Signaling Promotes Obesity-Induced Adipose Tissue Inflammation and Metabolic Dysfunction Independent of Adipose Tissue Expansion
text:
Dysfunction in adipose tissue has a pivotal role in the development of insulin resistance in obese individuals, as suggested by cell culture and gain-of-function mouse studies. However, there is limited genetic evidence supporting a role for endogenous Wnt proteins in adipose tissue dysfunction, and the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway remains largely unexplored. This study provides evidence from human, mouse, and cell culture studies that Wnt5a-mediated noncanonical Wnt signaling contributes to metabolic dysfunction in obesity by increasing adipose tissue inflammation.
Wnt5a expression is significantly upregulated in human visceral fat compared to subcutaneous fat in obese individuals. In obese mice, Wnt5a ablation improves insulin resistance, along with reductions in adipose tissue inflammation. Conversely, Wnt5a overexpression in myeloid cells exacerbates adipose tissue inflammation and leads to greater impairments in glucose homeostasis. Wnt5a ablation or overexpression does not affect fat mass or adipocyte size. Mechanistically, Wnt5a promotes the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines by macrophages in a Jun NH2-terminal kinase-dependent manner, leading to defective insulin signaling in adipocytes. Exogenous interleukin-6 administration restores insulin resistance in obese Wnt5a-deficient mice, suggesting a central role for this cytokine in Wnt5a-mediated metabolic dysfunction. Taken together, these results demonstrate that noncanonical Wnt signaling contributes to obesity-induced insulin resistance independent of adipose tissue expansion.

title: A cluster of ribosome synthesis factors regulate pre-rRNA folding and 5.8S rRNA maturation by the Rat1 exonuclease
text: The enzyme Rat1 is responsible for degrading pre-rRNA spacer fragments and processing the 5'-ends of the 5.8S and 25S rRNAs. UV crosslinking studies have revealed multiple binding sites for Rat1 across the pre-rRNA, consistent with its known functions. Interestingly, the major 5.8S 5'-end is generated by Rat1 digestion of the internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) spacer from cleavage site A(3). This processing requires the 'A(3)-cluster' proteins, including Cic1, Erb1, Nop7, Nop12, and Nop15, which show interdependent pre-rRNA binding. Surprisingly, these A(3)-cluster factors were not crosslinked close to site A(3), but instead bound sites around the 5.8S 3'- and 25S 5'-regions, which are base paired in mature ribosomes, and in the ITS2 spacer that separates these rRNAs. In contrast, Nop4, a protein required for endonucleolytic cleavage in ITS1, binds the pre-rRNA near the 5'-end of 5.8S. Additionally, ITS2 was reported to undergo structural remodeling, and in vivo chemical probing suggests that A(3)-cluster binding is required for this reorganization, potentially regulating the timing of processing. Furthermore, we predict that Nop4 and the A(3) cluster establish long-range interactions between the 5.8S and 25S rRNAs, which are subsequently maintained by ribosomal protein binding.

title: Synergistic activity of the histone deacetylase inhibitor suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid and the bisphosphonate zoledronic acid against prostate cancer cells in vitro.
text: Bisphosphonates are widely used medications for treating malignant bone diseases, as they inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and have direct effects on cancer cells. In this study, we investigated whether the anticancer activity of the third-generation bisphosphonate zoledronic acid (ZOL) could be enhanced by combining it with the histone deacetylase inhibitor suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA). We found that ZOL and SAHA worked together to induce cell death in prostate cancer cell lines LNCaP and PC-3, resulting in a synergistic effect as shown by combination index isobologram analysis. The combination of ZOL and SAHA led to the dissipation of the mitochondrial transmembrane potential, activation of caspase-3, and DNA fragmentation, indicating that the two agents initiated apoptosis. Since ZOL inhibits the mevalonate pathway, which is essential for protein prenylation, we investigated whether the mevalonate pathway was also the target of the cooperative action of ZOL and SAHA. Our findings showed that geranylgeraniol, but not farnesol, significantly reduced ZOL/SAHA-induced cell death, indicating that the synergistic action of the agents was due to the inhibition of geranylgeranylation. Consistently, a direct inhibitor of geranylgeranylation, GGTI-298, synergized with SAHA to induce cell death, whereas an inhibitor of farnesylation, FTI-277, had no effect. Additionally, SAHA synergized with mevastatin, an inhibitor of the proximal enzyme in the mevalonate pathway. These in vitro findings provide a rationale for exploring the potential of combining SAHA and ZOL, or other inhibitors of the mevalonate pathway, as a promising strategy for anticancer therapy.

title: The Immune Response to Melanoma Is Limited by Thymic Selection of Self-Antigens
text: The expression of melanoma-associated antigens (MAA) is limited to normal melanocytes and melanomas, making them ideal targets for immunotherapy and melanoma vaccines. However, the immune responses to MAA may be limited by thymic tolerance, as MAA are derived from self. The extent to which self-tolerance prevents efficient immune responses to MAA remains unknown. The autoimmune regulator (AIRE) controls the expression of tissue-specific self-antigens in thymic epithelial cells (TECs), and the level of antigens expressed in TECs determines the fate of auto-reactive thymocytes. Deficiency in AIRE leads to an enlarged autoreactive immune repertoire in both humans (APECED patients) and mice. In this study, we found increased IgG levels to melanoma cells in APECED patients, correlating with autoimmune skin features. Additionally, the enlarged T cell repertoire in AIRE(-/-) mice enables them to mount anti-MAA and anti-melanoma responses, as shown by increased anti-melanoma antibodies and enhanced CD4(+) and MAA-specific CD8(+) T cell responses after melanoma challenge. We also found that thymic expression of gp100 is under the control of AIRE, leading to increased gp100-specific CD8(+) T cell frequencies in AIRE(-/-) mice. On the other hand, TRP-2 (tyrosinase-related protein) is absent from TECs, resulting in the presence of TRP-2-specific CD8(+) T cells in both AIRE(-/-) and AIRE(+/+) mice. This study highlights the importance of investigating thymic expression of self-antigens before including them in vaccination and immunotherapy strategies.

title: Murine embryonic stem cell differentiation is promoted by SOCS-3 and inhibited by the zinc finger transcription factor Klf4.
text: Embryonic stem (ES) cells homozygous for a Shp-2 mutation (Shp-2(Delta46-110)) exhibit hypersensitivity to leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) and increased phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT3) upon LIF stimulation. We hypothesized that LIF-responsive genes in Shp-2(Delta46-110) cells might harbor potential candidates for molecules essential for ES cell self-renewal. Using microarray analysis, we identified 41 genes whose expression was modulated by LIF in Shp-2(Delta46-110) ES cells. Validation of the top two up-regulated genes, suppressor of cytokine signaling-3 (SOCS-3) and Kruppel-like factor 4 (Klf4), through Northern blotting revealed that overexpression of SOCS-3 led to enhanced differentiation of ES cells into hematopoietic progenitors, while overexpression of Klf4 resulted in increased self-renewal capacity of ES cells as evidenced by secondary embryoid body (EB) formation. Notably, Klf4-transduced d6 EBs displayed higher levels of Oct-4, suggesting that Klf4 promotes ES cell self-renewal. These findings confirm the negative role of SOCS-3 in LIF signaling and uncover a novel function for Klf4 in ES cell biology.

title: MicroScope—an integrated microbial resource for the curation and comparative analysis of genomic and metabolic data
text:
MicroScope is a comprehensive platform designed to streamline the process of updating microbial genome annotations and conducting comparative analysis. The platform provides a wealth of data from ongoing and completed genome projects, including automatic and expert annotations, as well as data from post-genomic experiments such as transcriptomics and mutant collections. This enables researchers to refine and enhance their understanding of gene functions.
MicroScope boasts a range of tools and graphical interfaces for analyzing genomes and manually curating gene annotations in a comparative context. Since its initial launch in January 2006, the system has undergone continuous development, with new data content and analysis tools being added regularly. The most recent update of MicroScope was published in 2009 in the Database journal.
Today, the resource contains data for over 1600 microbial genomes, of which approximately 300 are manually curated and maintained by biologists. Expert annotations are continuously gathered in the MicroScope database, with around 50,000 added each year, contributing to the improvement of microbial genome annotations.
The platform has been significantly redesigned to be more user-friendly, with improved data browsing and searching tools, as well as original tools specifically developed and integrated for expert annotation. Furthermore, as part of the European project Microme (Framework Program 7 Collaborative Project), MicroScope is becoming a resource for the curation and analysis of both genomic and metabolic data.
The increasing focus on environmental bacterial (meta)genomes that can metabolize a wide range of chemical compounds with industrial relevance has led to an increasing number of projects being conducted on the platform.

title: Comparison of Maximal Oxygen Consumption Between Black and White Prepubertal and Pubertal Children
text: The purpose of this study was to determine if there were any differences in maximal oxygen consumption (VO2max) between two groups of black and white children, and if so, to determine if these differences were related to hematologic profiles, body composition, and/or physical activity/inactivity level. Forty-five prepubertal and 42 pubertal, clinically normal black and white children participated in the study. Body composition was measured using dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry, and visceral adipose tissue and s.c. adipose tissue were assessed using computed tomography scans of the abdomen. Daily physical activity/inactivity was assessed through questionnaires. The results showed that black prepubertal and pubertal children had lower VO2max values compared to white children (prepubertal: 28.8 ± 7.8 vs. 35.0 ± 6.5 mL/kg/min, p < 0.01; pubertal: 33.7 ± 6.4 vs. 40.4 ± 10.2 mL/kg/min, p < 0.05). Additionally, black children had lower hemoglobin (Hb) concentrations and hematocrits than white children (prepubertal: 12.1 ± 0.5 vs. 12.8 ± 0.9 g/dL, p < 0.001; 35.6 ± 1.4 vs. 37.4 ± 2.3%, p < 0.01, respectively; pubertal: 13.0 ± 0.9 vs. 13.6 ± 0.7 g/dL, p < 0.05; 37.7 ± 2.5 vs. 39.5 ± 2.1%, p < 0.05, respectively). These findings suggest that black prepubertal and pubertal children had lower VO2max compared to their white peers matched for age, pubertal stage, and body mass index, which may be attributed at least in part to their lower Hb concentrations and more sedentary lifestyle. Further investigations could explore the relationship between Hb flow rate (a function of Hb × maximal cardiac output) and VO2max in black and white children.

title: Retinoic acid inhibits Th17 polarization and enhances FoxP3 expression through a Stat-3/Stat-5 independent signaling pathway.
text: CD4(+) helper T (Th) cells play a crucial role in maintaining a delicate balance between host defense and autoimmune disease. Two key populations of helper T cells are the pro-inflammatory, interleukin-17 (IL-17)-producing (Th17) cells and the anti-inflammatory forkhead box P3-positive (FoxP3(+)) T regulatory (Treg) cells. Here, we demonstrate that all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) and other agonists of the retinoic acid receptor alpha (RARalpha) inhibit the formation of Th17 cells and promote FoxP3 expression. Conversely, inhibition of retinoic acid signaling hinders transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta1) induction of FoxP3. The ATRA-mediated effect occurs independently of IL-2, signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 (Stat5) and Stat3, revealing a novel mechanism for FoxP3 induction in CD4 T cells. As previous studies have shown that vitamin A derivatives are protective in animal models of autoimmune disease, the current findings suggest a previously unappreciated role for RARalpha in the regulation of CD4(+) T-cell differentiation and provide a mechanism for the anti-inflammatory effects of retinoic acid.

title: British Journal of Nutrition (2003), 89, 295–301 q The Authors 2003 DOI: 10.1079/BJN2002776 Plasma homocysteine concentration is decreased by dietary intervention*
text: High plasma total homocysteine (tHcy) concentrations have been linked to an increased risk of vascular diseases. To investigate the impact of a high intake of natural folate from food on tHcy levels, we conducted a crossover dietary intervention study with 37 healthy female participants. The study consisted of a baseline period and two 5-week diet periods (low- and high-folate diets) with a 3-week washout in between. The low-folate diet contained one serving of vegetables and fruit per day, while the high-folate diet included at least seven servings of vegetables, berries, and citrus fruit per day. We measured serum and red blood cell (RBC) folate, serum vitamin B12, and plasma tHcy concentrations at the beginning and end of each diet period. Our results showed that the mean concentrations of serum and RBC folate were 11.0 (SD 3.0) nmol/l and 412 (SD 120) nmol/l at the end of the low-folate diet, and 78 (95% CI 62, 94%) and 14 (95% CI 8, 20%) higher in response to the high-folate diet (P<0.001). The serum concentration of vitamin B12 remained unchanged during the intervention. The mean plasma tHcy concentration was 8.0 pmol/l at the end of the low-folate diet, and decreased by 13 (95% CI 9, 18%)% in response to the high-folate diet (P<0.001). In conclusion, consuming a diet rich in fresh berries, citrus fruit, and vegetables significantly increases serum and RBC folate levels and decreases plasma homocysteine concentrations.

title: Achieving increased resolution and more pixels with Superresolution Optical Fluctuation Imaging (SOFI)
text: Superresolution Optical Fluctuation Imaging (SOFI) was initially demonstrated to enhance imaging resolution by a factor of the square root of 2. Here, we explore ways to further improve the resolution of SOFI images by re-weighting the Optical Transfer Function (OTF) and exploiting cross-cumulants to obtain a good approximation of the underlying Point-Spread Function (PSF). We demonstrate a two-fold increase in resolution (beyond the diffraction limit) of near-infrared quantum dot-labeled tubulin networks of 3T3 fibroblasts.

title: Evaluation of reagent strips in detecting asymptomatic bacteriuria in early pregnancy: prospective case series.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the performance of reagent test strips in detecting asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnant women during their first antenatal clinic visit.
Design: Prospective case series.
Setting: Antenatal clinic of a large inner city maternity hospital.
Subjects: All women attending their first antenatal clinic. Exclusion criteria included patients taking antibiotics and those with urinary tract symptoms.
Intervention: A midstream urine specimen was divided into two samples: one was sent for microscopy and bacteriological culture, while the other was tested with a commercial reagent strip for the presence of blood, protein, nitrite, and leucocyte esterase.
Main Outcome Measures: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of the reagent strips in diagnosing asymptomatic bacteriuria (defined as 10(5) colony forming units/ml urine).
Results: The sensitivity of the reagent strips was low, ranging from 33% when all four tests were combined. Specificity was high, with values of 99% or more. Positive predictive value reached a maximum of 69%, while negative predictive value was typically 95% or more.
Conclusion: The study found that urine reagent strips are not sufficiently sensitive to detect asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnant women, resulting in many patients being missed. Given the potential serious consequences of this condition in pregnant women, the authors recommend that formal bacteriological investigation remain the investigation of choice in this patient population.

title: Wnt5a functions in planar cell polarity regulation in mice.
text: Planar cell polarity (PCP) refers to the polarization of cells within a single plane of a cell layer. In vertebrates, a distinctive epithelial PCP is observed in the uniform orientation of stereociliary bundles of sensory hair cells in the mammalian cochlea. PCP is also essential for convergent extension (CE), a polarized cellular movement that occurs during neural tube closure and cochlear extension. Studies in Drosophila and vertebrates have revealed a conserved PCP pathway, including Frizzled (Fz) receptors. Using the cochlea as a model system, we investigate the involvement of known ligands of Fz, Wnt morphogens, in PCP regulation. We find that Wnt5a forms a reciprocal expression pattern with a Wnt antagonist, secreted frizzled-related protein 3 (Sfrp3 or Frzb), along the axis of planar polarity in the cochlear epithelium. We also demonstrate that Wnt5a antagonizes Frzb in regulating cochlear extension and stereociliary bundle orientation in vitro, and that Wnt5a(-/-) animals have a shortened and widened cochlea. Furthermore, we show that Wnt5a is required for proper subcellular distribution of a PCP protein, Ltap/Vangl2, and that Wnt5a interacts genetically with Ltap/Vangl2 for uniform orientation of stereocilia, cochlear extension, and neural tube closure. Together, these findings demonstrate that Wnt5a functions in PCP regulation in mice.

title: The RNA Polymerase “Switch Region” Is a Target for Inhibitors
text: The alpha-pyrone antibiotic myxopyronin (Myx) inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP) by interacting with the RNAP "switch region" - the hinge that regulates the opening and closing of the RNAP active center cleft. Through a combination of genetic, biochemical, and structural approaches, we demonstrate that Myx binds to the RNAP switch region and prevents the interaction of RNAP with promoter DNA, thereby inhibiting transcription initiation. We identify the specific contacts between Myx and RNAP and evaluate the effects of Myx on RNAP conformation, suggesting that Myx functions by interfering with the opening of the RNAP active-center cleft during transcription initiation. Additionally, we show that structurally related alpha-pyrone antibiotics, such as corallopyronin (Cor) and ripostatin (Rip), also target the RNAP switch region and function analogously to Myx. Notably, the RNAP switch region is distinct from the targets of previously characterized RNAP inhibitors, and Myx, Cor, and Rip do not exhibit cross-resistance with these inhibitors. The RNAP switch region represents an attractive target for the identification of new broad-spectrum antibacterial therapeutic agents.

title: How reliable are light traps in estimating biting rates of adult Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Diptera: Culicidae) in the presence of treated bed nets?
text: In a study conducted in southern Sierra Leone, the efficiency of light traps in capturing mosquitoes relative to human bait catches was compared in two types of communities: those where most people slept under treated bed nets and those where most people slept without bed nets. The study found that the number of female Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes caught in these communities using light traps was strongly correlated (r > or = 0.72) with corresponding human biting catches performed on the same or adjacent nights. However, the relative sampling efficiency of light traps varied slightly but significantly with mosquito abundance in villages with treated bed nets, but not in those without them. Despite this variation, the relationship between relative sampling efficiency and mosquito abundance did not differ significantly between the two types of village. Overall, the study found that there was insufficient evidence to suggest that the presence of treated nets altered the relative efficiency of light traps, and any bias was slight and unlikely to be of practical importance. Therefore, the study concluded that light traps can be used as a surrogate for human bait catches in estimating the biting rates of A. gambiae mosquitoes in these communities.

title: Development of a novel mouse glioma model using lentiviral vectors
text:
Introduction:
Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive and malignant brain tumor that is difficult to treat. Developing a reliable and efficient model for studying GBM is crucial for understanding its pathogenesis and identifying potential therapeutic targets. In this study, we aimed to develop a novel method for inducing GBM in adult immunocompetent mice using Cre-loxP–controlled lentiviral vectors expressing oncogenes.
Methods:
We used Cre-loxP–controlled lentiviral vectors to deliver oncogenes to fewer than 60 glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)-positive cells in the hippocampus, subventricular zone (SVZ), or cortex of mice heterozygous for the Tp53 gene. The expression of activated forms of the oncoproteins Harvey-Ras and AKT was examined in the transduced cells. The tumorigenic potential of the transduced cells was evaluated by transplanting them into naive recipient mouse brain and observing the formation of GBM-like tumors.
Results:
Our results showed that mice developed GBM when transduced either in the SVZ or hippocampus. However, tumors were rarely detected when the mice were transduced in the cortex. In addition, we found that brain tumor cells transplanted into naive recipient mouse brain formed GBM-like tumors that contained CD133+ cells, formed tumorspheres, and could differentiate into neurons and astrocytes.
Discussion:
Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of using Cre-loxP–controlled lentiviral vectors to generate a region- and cell type-specific GBM model in adult mice. This novel approach allows for the precise control of oncogene expression in a limited number of cells, which is critical for studying the early stages of GBM development. The ability of the transplanted cells to form tumorspheres and differentiate into different cell types suggests that they have a high tumorigenic potential. These results have important implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies for GBM treatment.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, we have developed a novel method for inducing GBM in adult immunocompetent mice using Cre-loxP–controlled lentiviral vectors expressing oncogenes. This approach allows for the precise control of oncogene expression in a limited number of cells, which is critical for studying the early stages of GBM development. The ability of the transplanted cells to form tumorspheres and differentiate into different cell types suggests that they have a high tumorigenic potential. These results have important implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies for GBM treatment.

title: Research Letters
text: We present a case of preclinical variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (vCJD) in an individual who passed away from an unrelated medical condition 5 years after receiving a blood transfusion from a donor who later developed vCJD. Using western blot, paraffin-embedded tissue blot, and immunohistochemistry, we detected the presence of protease-resistant prion protein (PrP(res)) in the spleen, but not in the brain. Additionally, immunohistochemistry for prion protein was positive in a cervical lymph node. The patient was a heterozygote at codon 129 of the PRNP gene, indicating that susceptibility to vCJD infection is not limited to individuals with the methionine homozygous PRNP genotype. These findings have significant implications for future estimates and surveillance of vCJD in the UK.

title: Swi1Timeless Prevents Repeat Instability at Fission Yeast Telomeres
text: Genomic instability caused by DNA replication stress is linked to cancer and genetic disorders in humans. If left unchecked, replication stress, such as fork stalling and collapse, can occur at natural barriers throughout the genome. The fork protection complex (FPC) is thought to play a crucial role in stabilizing stalled replication forks at specific locations, including eukaryotic ribosomal DNA genes and the mating-type locus in fission yeast. However, little is known about the FPC's role at other natural barriers, such as telomeres. Telomeres are challenging to replicate due to the presence of repetitive GT-rich sequences and telomere-binding proteins. The mechanism that regulates telomere replication is not fully understood. In this study, we investigate the role of the fission yeast Swi1(Timeless) protein, a subunit of the FPC, in telomere replication. We find that loss of Swi1 leads to telomere shortening in a telomerase-independent manner. Our epistasis analyses suggest that heterochromatin and telomere-binding proteins are not significant obstacles to telomere replication in the absence of Swi1. Instead, repetitive DNA sequences impair telomere integrity in swi1Δ mutant cells, leading to the loss of repeat DNA. In the absence of Swi1, telomere shortening is accompanied by an increased recruitment of Rad52 recombinase and more frequent amplification of telomere/subtelomeres, similar to the behavior of tumor cells that utilize the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) pathway to maintain telomeres. These findings suggest that Swi1 ensures telomere replication by suppressing recombination and repeat instability at telomeres. Our study may also provide insights into the potential role of Swi1 in regulating telomere stability in cancer cells.

title: Prediction of guide strand of microRNAs from its sequence and secondary structure
text: In this study, we developed and tested support vector machine (SVM) models for predicting the guide strands of microRNAs (miRNAs). Our approach used various features, including mono-, di-, and tri-nucleotide composition, split nucleotide composition, and binary pattern, to distinguish the guide strand from the passenger strand. We achieved high accuracy scores using these features, with the best performance achieved when integrating secondary structure information with binary pattern (0.719). We also developed a hybrid model that combined various features and achieved an accuracy of 0.799. Our method outperformed other siRNA-designing methods on both miRNA and siRNA datasets. Overall, our study demonstrates the potential of using SVM models to predict guide miRNA strands and improve RNA silencing technology. A web server has been developed based on the SVM models described in this study (http://crdd.osdd.net:8081/RISCbinder/).

title: NIPBL, encoding a homolog of fungal Scc2-type sister chromatid cohesion proteins and fly Nipped-B, is mutated in Cornelia de Lange syndrome
text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a multifactorial disorder characterized by distinctive facial features, cognitive impairment, growth delays, and limb abnormalities. Recently, we identified and investigated a novel gene, NIPBL, which is mutated in individuals with CdLS. Our findings revealed the structure and homology of the NIPBL protein, which we named Delangin, across various species, including mammals, birds, and insects. Delangin shares significant similarity with orthologs in flies, worms, plants, and fungi, including Scc2-type sister chromatid cohesion proteins, and D. melanogaster Nipped-B. We propose that dysfunctional Delangin may disrupt the proper regulation of DLX genes, leading to proximodistal limb patterning defects in CdLS. Genetic analyses typically reveal individual Delangin or Nipped-B-like orthologs in diploid animal and plant genomes. The evolution of an ancestral sister chromatid cohesion protein to acquire a role in developmental gene regulation suggests a connection between CdLS and Roberts syndrome.

title: Impaired FANCD2 monoubiquitination and hypersensitivity to camptothecin uniquely characterize Fanconi anemia complementation group M.
text: FANCM is a component of the Fanconi anemia (FA) core complex, and a patient with biallelic mutations in FANCM (EUFA867) has been described. Interestingly, EUFA867 also carries biallelic mutations in FANCA. When we corrected the FANCA defect in EUFA867 lymphoblasts, we generated a "clean" FA-M cell line that was hypersensitive to mitomycin C. Unlike cells defective in other core complex members, FANCM(-/-) cells were proficient in monoubiquitinating FANCD2 and were sensitive to the topoisomerase inhibitor camptothecin, a feature shared only with the FA subtype D1 and N. Additionally, FANCM(-/-) cells were sensitive to UV light. We found that both FANCM and a C-terminal deletion mutant could rescue the cross-linker sensitivity of FANCM(-/-) cells, while a FANCM ATPase mutant did not. Our results suggest that FANCM functions in an FA core complex-dependent and -independent manner.

title: Vesicular Glycolysis Provides On-Board Energy for Fast Axonal Transport
text: Fast axonal transport (FAT) relies on a steady supply of energy over long distances to fuel the molecular motors that transport vesicles. We found that glycolysis provides the necessary ATP for FAT to occur. Although inhibiting ATP production in mitochondria did not affect vesicle motility, inhibiting the glycolytic enzyme GAPDH reduced transport in cultured neurons and Drosophila larvae. GAPDH localizes on vesicles through a huntingtin-dependent mechanism and is transported on fast-moving vesicles within axons. Purified motile vesicles showed GAPDH enzymatic activity and produced ATP. Our results demonstrate that vesicular GAPDH is necessary and sufficient to provide on-board energy for fast vesicular transport. When GAPDH was detached from vesicles, transport was reduced, but targeting GAPDH to vesicles was sufficient to promote FAT in GAPDH-deficient neurons. This suggests that a specifically localized glycolytic machinery can supply constant energy, independent of mitochondria, to fuel the processive movement of vesicles over long distances in axons.

title: RB loss in resistant EGFR mutant lung adenocarcinomas that transform to small-cell lung cancer
text: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors are effective treatments for non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLCs) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, but relapse typically occurs after an average of 1 year of continuous treatment. In a subset of these resistant cancers, a fundamental histological transformation from NSCLC to small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) occurs, but the molecular changes associated with this transformation remain unknown. Analysis of tumor samples and cell lines derived from resistant EGFR mutant patients revealed that Retinoblastoma (RB) is lost in 100% of SCLC transformed cases, but rarely in those that remain NSCLC. Additionally, these resistant cancers exhibit increased neuroendocrine marker expression and decreased EGFR expression, as well as greater sensitivity to BCL2 family inhibition compared to resistant NSCLCs. These findings suggest that this subset of resistant cancers may ultimately adopt many of the molecular and phenotypic characteristics of classical SCLC.

title: Periostin Deficiency Increases Bone Damage and Impairs Injury Response to Fatigue Loading in Adult Mice
text: The removal of bone damage and the formation of calluses in response to fatigue loading are crucial to prevent fractures. Periostin, a matricellular protein, plays a significant role in the adaptive response of cortical bone to loading. However, the extent to which periostin influences the injury response to fatigue remains unclear. To investigate this, we subjected Postn(-/-) and Postn(+/+) mice to axial compression of their tibia, causing fatigue damage. In Postn(+/+) mice, we observed an increase in the number of cracks and surface area (CsNb, CsS) within the first hour after fatigue, accompanied by a decrease in strength compared to non-fatigued tibia. At 15 days, the fatigued tibia showed a woven bone response, with increased tissue volume (CtTV) and bone volume (CtBV), in 75% of the fatigued bones. Additionally, cortical porosity and remodeling significantly increased in the fatigued tibia of Postn(+/+) mice. Interestingly, at 30 days, the fatigued tibia showed a similar strength to the non-fatigued tibia, indicating continuous removal of cortical damage. In contrast, Postn(-/-) mice exhibited detectable cracks even in the absence of fatigue, along with decreased collagen crosslinks and tissue hardness compared to Postn(+/+). Fatigue significantly increased CsNb and CsS in Postn(-/-), but was not associated with changes in CtTV and CtBV, indicating that only 16% of the fatigued bones formed woven bone. Moreover, cortical porosity and remodeling did not increase in Postn(-/-), and the level of damage remained high even after 30 days, resulting in compromised strength. Unlike Postn(+/+), osteocytic lacunae in Postn(-/-) showed no change in anisotropy (DA) after fatigue. These findings suggest that periostin plays a crucial role in influencing bone material properties, damage accumulation, and repair, including local modeling/remodeling processes in response to fatigue. Our results imply that the level of periostin expression may influence the propensity to fatigue fractures.

title: Preferential occupancy of histone variant H2AZ at inactive promoters influences local histone modifications and chromatin remodeling.
text: The histone variant H2AZ (Htz1) has been implicated in various cellular processes, including transcription activation, the prevention of ectopic heterochromatin spread, and genome integrity. Our genome-wide localization analysis revealed that Htz1 is distributed throughout the genome in an SWR1-dependent manner, with a nonrandom pattern of occupancy in intergenic regions compared to coding regions. Interestingly, we found that Htz1 occupancy is inversely proportional to transcription rates and the enrichment of RNA polymerase II under different growth conditions. While Htz1 does not directly regulate transcription repression genome-wide, its presence under inactive conditions is essential for optimal activation of a subset of genes. Furthermore, Htz1 is not primarily responsible for nucleosome positioning, even at promoters where it is highly enriched. Using biochemical approaches, we demonstrated that Htz1 incorporation into nucleosomes inhibits the activities of histone modifiers associated with transcription, such as Dot1, Set2, and NuA4, and reduces nucleosome mobilization driven by chromatin remodeling complexes. These findings suggest that Htz1 may serve to mark quiescent promoters for proper activation.

title: Genomic organisation and transcription characterisation of the gene encoding Leishmania (Leishmania) amazonensis arginase and its protein structure prediction.
text: The genomic organization of the gene encoding Leishmania (Leishmania) amazonensis arginase, as well as its flanking regions, was investigated. The transcribed RNA size was determined, allowing for the identification of genomic sites signaling for RNA trans-splicing and putative polyadenylation regions. The organization of this gene was compared to that of other proteins encoded by organisms of the Trypanosomatid family, and the complete nucleotide sequence of the arginase open reading frame was obtained. The three-dimensional structure of the enzyme was inferred through a computational analysis of the deduced amino acid sequence, based on the established crystal structure of Rattus norvergicus arginase. The human liver arginase sequence was also analyzed in the same way, and the comparison of the presumed structure of both the Leishmania and human enzymes revealed some differences that may be exploited in chemotherapeutic studies.

title: Endometrial carcinoma risk among women diagnosed with endometrial hyperplasia: the 34-year experience in a large health plan
text: Classifying endometrial hyperplasia (EH) based on the severity of glandular crowding (simple hyperplasia (SH) vs complex hyperplasia (CH)) and nuclear atypia (simple atypical hyperplasia (SAH) vs complex atypical hyperplasia (CAH)) may predict the risk of subsequent endometrial carcinoma, but there is a lack of data on the progression of these conditions. Our nested case-control study of EH progression included 138 cases diagnosed with EH and subsequently with carcinoma (1970-2003) at least one year later, and 241 controls individually matched on age, date, and follow-up duration and counter-matched on EH classification. After centralized pathology panel and medical record review, we calculated rate ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusted for treatment and repeat biopsies. Compared to disordered proliferative endometrium (DPEM) as the referent, atypical hyperplasia (AH) significantly increased the carcinoma risk (RR=14, 95% CI: 5-38). The risk was highest within the first 5 years after AH (RR=48, 95% CI: 8-294), but remained elevated 5 or more years after AH (RR=3.5, 95% CI: 1.0-9.6). The progression risks for SH (RR=2.0, 95% CI: 0.9-4.5) and CH (RR=2.8, 95% CI: 1.0-7.9) were substantially lower and only slightly higher than the progression risk for DPEM. The higher progression risks for AH may support the development of management guidelines based on the distinct progression risks for atypical vs non-atypical EH.

title: Redefining the Genetic Hierarchies Controlling Skeletal Myogenesis: Pax-3 and Myf-5 Act Upstream of MyoD
text: We investigated the roles of Pax-3 (splotch), Myf-5, and their homozygous mutants in skeletal myogenesis using mice. Our analysis revealed distinct perturbations in myogenic progenitor cells and early muscle defects in splotch and Myf-5 homozygous embryos. Remarkably, double homozygous mutants for splotch and Myf-5 exhibited a striking phenotype, with complete absence of body muscles. MyoD rescue experiments showed that activation of this gene is dependent on either Pax-3 or Myf-5, indicating that these genes define two distinct myogenic pathways. Interestingly, this genetic hierarchy does not appear to operate for head muscle formation.

title: Assessment of Volume Depletion in Children with Malaria
text:
Background: The extent of volume depletion in severe malaria is currently unknown, although knowledge of fluid compartment volumes can aid in treatment. To help manage severely ill children and test the hypothesis that changes in fluid compartment volumes reflect disease severity, we measured body compartment volumes in Gabonese children with malaria.
Methods and Findings: We estimated total body water volume (TBW) and extracellular water volume (ECW) in children with severe or moderate malaria and in convalescence using tracer dilution with heavy water and bromide, respectively. Intracellular water volume (ICW) was calculated from these parameters. Bioelectrical impedance analysis estimates of TBW and ECW were calibrated against dilution methods, and bioelectrical impedance analysis measurements were taken daily until discharge. Sixteen children had severe and 19 moderate malaria. Severe childhood malaria was associated with a significant depletion of TBW (mean [SD] of 37 [33] ml/kg, or 6.7% [6.0%]) relative to measurement at discharge, which is equivalent to mild dehydration in other conditions. ECW measurements were normal on admission in children with severe malaria and did not increase in the first few days of admission. Volumes in different compartments (TBW, ECW, and ICW) were not related to hyperlactataemia or other clinical and laboratory markers of disease severity. Moderate malaria was not associated with a depletion of TBW.

title: NSOM/QD-Based Direct Visualization of CD3-Induced and CD28-Enhanced Nanospatial Coclustering of TCR and Coreceptor in Nanodomains in T Cell Activation
text: Direct imaging of the nanoscale relationship between T cell receptor (TCR)/CD3 and CD4 or CD8 co-receptors before and after activation of primary T cells has not been reported. Our recent innovation of near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM) and immune-labeling quantum dots (QD) enabled us to image the Ag-specific TCR response during in vivo clonal expansion. We upgraded the NSOM/QD-based nanotechnology by dipole-polarization and dual-color imaging, allowing us to scan cell-membrane molecules with unprecedented best-optical lateral resolution. Our findings revealed that CD3, CD4, or CD8 molecules were distributed as single QD-bound molecules or nano-clusters equivalent to 2-4 QD fluorescence-intensity/size on the cell membrane of unstimulated primary T cells. Approximately 6-10% of CD3 molecules were found to co-cluster with CD4 or CD8 as 70-110 nm nano-clusters without forming nano-domains. The ligation of TCR/CD3 on CD4 or CD8 T cells led to CD3 nanoscale co-clustering or interaction with CD4 or CD8 co-receptors, forming 200-500 nm nano-domains or >500 nm micro-domains. This intrinsic event of TCR/CD3 ligation was found to be driven by Lck phosphorylation and was not limited to MHC engagement. Importantly, CD28 co-stimulation significantly enhanced TCR/CD3 nanoscale co-clustering or interaction with CD4 co-receptor within nano- or micro-domains on the membrane. In contrast, CD28 co-stimulation did not enhance CD8 clustering or CD3-CD8 co-clustering in nano-domains, although it increased the molecular number and density of CD3 clustering in the enlarged nano-domains. These findings provide new insights into the TCR/CD3 interaction with CD4 or CD8 co-receptor in T-cell activation.

title: Hoxa9 transforms primary bone marrow cells through specific collaboration with Meis1a but not Pbx1b.
text: Hoxa9, Meis1, and Pbx1 are proteins that play a role in leukemic transformation in both mice and humans. These proteins interact with each other and bind to specific DNA sequences. In this study, we investigated whether Hoxa9 could transform hemopoietic cells in collaboration with either Pbx1 or Meis1. We used primary bone marrow cells that were retrovirally engineered to overexpress Hoxa9 and Meis1 simultaneously. When these cells were transplanted into syngenic mice, they induced growth factor-dependent oligoclonal acute myeloid leukemia within 3 months. In contrast, overexpression of Hoxa9, Meis1, or Pbx1 alone, or a combination of these genes, failed to transform hemopoietic cells within 6 months post-transplantation. Similar results were obtained when FDC-P1 cells, which were engineered to overexpress these genes, were transplanted to syngenic recipients. These findings demonstrate a specific collaboration between a member of the Hox family and one of its DNA-binding partners in the transformation of hemopoietic cells.

title: Tyr26 phosphorylation of PGAM1 provides a metabolic advantage to tumours by stabilizing the active conformation
text: The mechanisms by which oncogenic signaling regulates glycolysis and anabolic biosynthesis in cancer cells are not fully understood. Recently, we discovered that the glycolytic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) regulates anabolic biosynthesis by controlling intracellular levels of its substrate 3-phosphoglycerate and product 2-phosphoglycerate. In this study, we uncover a novel mechanism by which Y26 phosphorylation enhances PGAM1 activation through the release of an inhibitory subunit, E19, which blocks the active site. We also determine the crystal structure of H11-phosphorylated PGAM1 and find that phospho-H11 activates PGAM1 by promoting substrate 3-phosphoglycerate binding. Furthermore, we find that Y26 phosphorylation of PGAM1 is common in human cancer cells and contributes to the regulation of 3-phosphoglycerate and 2-phosphoglycerate levels, promoting cancer cell proliferation and tumor growth. Since PGAM1 is a negative transcriptional target of TP53, and is therefore commonly upregulated in human cancers, these findings suggest that Y26 phosphorylation represents an additional mechanism underlying PGAM1 upregulation.

title: Spatial and Temporal Clustering of Dengue Virus Transmission in Thai Villages
text:
The transmission of dengue viruses (DENV), the leading cause of arboviral disease worldwide, varies over time and space due to a combination of factors related to the human host, virus, mosquito vector, and environment. Understanding the patterns of variation in transmission is crucial for conducting surveillance and implementing effective disease prevention strategies. To test the hypothesis that DENV transmission is focally distributed, we compared the spatial and temporal characteristics of DENV transmission within Thai villages where transmission is occurring and not occurring.
We conducted cluster investigations within 100 meters of homes where febrile children with acute dengue lived during two seasons of peak transmission. Data on human infection and mosquito infection/density were analyzed to define the spatial and temporal dimensions of DENV transmission, correlate these factors with variation in transmission, and determine the burden of inapparent and symptomatic infections. Among 556 village children enrolled as neighbors of 12 dengue-positive and 22 dengue-negative index cases, all 27 DENV infections (4.9% of enrollees) occurred in positive clusters (p < 0.01; attributable risk [AR] = 10.4 per 100; 95% confidence interval 1-19.8 per 100]. In positive clusters, 12.4% of enrollees became infected over a 15-day period, and DENV infections were concentrated near the homes of index cases. As only one of 217 pairs of serologic specimens tested in positive clusters revealed a recent DENV infection that occurred before cluster initiation, we attribute the observed DENV transmission after cluster investigation to recent transmission activity. Of the 1,022 female adult Ae. aegypti collected, all eight (0.8%) dengue-infected mosquitoes came from houses in positive clusters; none from control clusters or schools. Distinguishing features between positive and negative clusters were greater availability of piped water in negative clusters (p < 0.01) and greater number of Ae. aegypti pupae per person in positive clusters (p = 0.04). During primarily DENV-4 transmission seasons, the ratio of inapparent to symptomatic infections was nearly 1:1 among child enrollees.
Study limitations included the inability to sample all children and mosquitoes within each cluster and reliance on serologic rather than virologic evidence of interval infections in enrollees due to restrictions on blood collection frequency in children. Our findings reveal the remarkably focal nature of DENV transmission within a hyperendemic rural area of Thailand. These data suggest that active school-based dengue case detection prompting local spraying could contain recent virus introductions and reduce the longitudinal risk of virus spread within rural areas. Our results encourage future cluster studies to explore how host immune and behavioral aspects may impact DENV transmission and prevention strategies. Cluster methodology could serve as a useful research tool for investigating other temporally and spatially clustered infectious diseases.

title: Secondary T cell–T cell synaptic interactions drive the differentiation of protective CD8+ T cells
text: Immunization leads to the differentiation of CD8+ T cells, which acquire effector functions and become part of a memory pool. The priming of T cells occurs through an immunological synapse formed between the T cells and an antigen-presenting cell (APC). By disrupting synaptic stability at different times, we found that the differentiation of CD8+ T cells requires interactions between primed T cells beyond those with APCs. We identified a critical differentiation period during which T cell–T cell synapses play a crucial role in generating protective CD8+ T cell memory. These synapses allow T cells to communicate with each other and polarize the secretion of interferon-γ (IFN-γ) towards each other. The collective activation and homotypic clustering of T cells promote cytokine sharing and act as regulatory stimuli for T cell differentiation.

title: The Histone H3 Lysine-27 Demethylase Jmjd3 Links Inflammation to Inhibition of Polycomb-Mediated Gene Silencing
text:
Eprior studies have established that epigenetic chromatin modifications restrict the ability of differentiated cells to alter gene expression programs in response to environmental stimuli and to undergo transdifferentiation. Specifically, Polycomb group (PcG) proteins mediate gene silencing and repress transdifferentiation through histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3). However, the role of inflammation in modulating PcG-dependent silencing remains unclear.
Our current investigation aims to address this knowledge gap by elucidating the impact of inflammation on PcG-mediated silencing in macrophages. We demonstrate that the JmjC-domain protein Jmjd3 is a H3K27me demethylase specifically expressed in macrophages in response to bacterial products and inflammatory cytokines. Jmjd3 binds PcG target genes and regulates their H3K27me3 levels and transcriptional activity.
Our findings provide a novel link between inflammation and the reprogramming of the epigenome, which may underlie the phenomenon of macrophage plasticity and contribute to the development of differentiation abnormalities in chronic inflammation. The discovery of an inducible enzyme that erases a histone mark controlling differentiation and cell identity offers a new avenue for understanding the complex interplay between inflammation and cellular differentiation.

title: Apolipoprotein E and atherosclerosis: beyond lipid effect.
text:
In humans, the protein apolipoprotein E (apoE) is a multifunctional and polymorphic gene that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes, including lipoprotein metabolism, coagulation, oxidative processes, and cell homeostasis. The apoE gene is located on chromosome 19 and is encoded by three alleles (e2, e3, and e4) that determine six different genotypes and plasma phenotypes. The e4 allele is particularly notorious for its association with increased risk of neurodegenerative disorders and atherosclerotic arterial disease.
However, the relationship between apoE and atherosclerosis is complex and context-dependent, and the mechanisms underlying this association are not fully understood. Despite this, apoE mimetic peptides that promote LDL clearance are currently being tested in animals for potential clinical applications.
In contrast to humans, the situation is relatively simpler in animals, particularly in the mouse model, which has been useful in testing mechanisms related to apoE and atherosclerosis.
Overall, the study of apoE and its role in atherosclerosis is an ongoing and complex area of research, with many factors influencing the relationship between the two. While there is evidence to support the association between apoE and atherosclerosis, the full mechanisms underlying this relationship are still being uncovered.

title: Exploitative and Hierarchical Antagonism in a Cooperative Bacterium
text: Social organisms that cooperate with some members of their own species, such as close relatives, may fail to cooperate with other genotypes of the same species. This noncooperation can take the form of outright antagonism or social exploitation. Myxococcus xanthus, a highly social prokaryote, cooperatively develops into spore-bearing, multicellular fruiting bodies in response to starvation. In this study, the social interactions among nine developmentally proficient strains of M. xanthus isolated from distant locations were characterized. These strains were competing against each other in all possible pairwise combinations during starvation-induced development. The results showed that at least one competitor often exhibited strong antagonism towards its partner, and a majority of mixes showed bidirectional antagonism that decreased total spore production, even to the point of driving whole populations to extinction. The primary determinant of competitive superiority was not the sporulation efficiencies of unmixed populations, but rather the differential response to mixing. In some competitive pairings, the dominant partner sporulated more efficiently in mixed populations than in clonal isolation. This finding represents a novel form of exploitation in bacteria carried out by socially competent genotypes and is the first documentation of social exploitation among natural bacterial isolates. The patterns of antagonistic superiority among these strains formed a highly linear dominance hierarchy. Some competition pairs constructed chimeric, rather than segregated, fruiting bodies. The cooperative prokaryote M. xanthus has diverged into a large number of distinct social types that cooperate with clone-mates but exhibit intense antagonism towards distinct social types of the same species. This study suggests that intense mutual antagonism may be more prevalent in prokaryotes with cooperative traits than in eukaryotes such as Dictyostelium discoideum, which also exhibits multicellular development. The finding of several cases of facultative social exploitation among these natural isolates suggests that such exploitation may occur frequently in nature in many prokaryotes with cooperative traits.

title: Mental Health Conditions Among Patients Seeking and Undergoing Bariatric Surgery: A Meta-analysis.
text:
Bariatric surgery is associated with sustained weight loss and improved physical health status in severely obese individuals, but mental health conditions are also common among patients seeking this surgery. Despite the prevalence of mental health conditions among bariatric surgery candidates and recipients, the relationship between these conditions and postoperative outcomes is not well understood. This systematic review aimed to determine the prevalence of mental health conditions, evaluate the association between preoperative mental health conditions and health outcomes following bariatric surgery, and assess the impact of surgery on the clinical course of mental health conditions.
The review included 68 publications, with 59 studies reporting the prevalence of preoperative mental health conditions and 27 studies examining the association between preoperative mental health conditions and postoperative outcomes. The most common mental health conditions among bariatric surgery patients were depression (19%-25%) and binge eating disorder (17%-21%). While there was conflicting evidence regarding the association between preoperative mental health conditions and postoperative weight loss, bariatric surgery was consistently associated with postoperative decreases in the prevalence of depression (7%-74%) and the severity of depressive symptoms (40%-70%).
The findings of this review suggest that mental health conditions are common among bariatric surgery patients and that bariatric surgery may have a positive impact on the clinical course of these conditions. However, the relationship between preoperative mental health conditions and postoperative weight loss remains unclear. Further research is needed to better understand the association between mental health conditions and postoperative outcomes in bariatric surgery patients.

title: The Nuclear Effector of Wnt-Signaling, Tcf1, Functions as a T-Cell–Specific Tumor Suppressor for Development of Lymphomas
text: The transcription factor Tcf1 plays a crucial role in T-cell development in the thymus, particularly in mediating the nuclear response to Wnt signals. Tcf1-deficient mice have been previously characterized, showing developmental blocks at the CD4-CD8- double negative (DN) to CD4+CD8+ double positive transition, resulting in a small thymus. Surprisingly, a large proportion of Tcf1-deficient mice spontaneously develop thymic lymphomas with 50% of mice developing a thymic lymphoma/leukemia by 16 weeks of age. These lymphomas are clonal, highly metastatic, and paradoxically show high Wnt signaling when crossed with Wnt reporter mice, with high expression of Wnt target genes Lef1 and Axin2. In contrast to wild-type thymocytes, where Tcf1 is expressed at higher levels than Lef1, Tcf1 loss leads to an increase in Wnt activity, which is the initiating event in lymphoma development. This is further exacerbated by activating Notch1 mutations. Therefore, Notch1 and loss of Tcf1 function as collaborating oncogenic events. Tcf1 deficiency predisposes to the development of thymic lymphomas by ectopic up-regulation of Lef1 due to lack of Tcf1 repressive isoforms and frequently by cooperating activating mutations in Notch1. Tcf1 thus functions as a T-cell-specific tumor suppressor gene, in addition to its established role as a Wnt responsive transcription factor. Therefore, Tcf1 acts as a molecular switch between proliferative and repressive signals during T-lymphocyte development in the thymus.

title: Activator Control of Nucleosome Occupancy in Activation and Repression of Transcription
text:
The relationship between chromatin structure and gene expression is a topic of intense research, with a particular focus on the role of nucleosomes in transcriptional regulation. While it is known that the universal transcriptional activator Gal4 removes promoter nucleosomes as it triggers transcription, the mechanisms underlying this process have remained unclear. In contrast, the reverse process of repression has often been correlated with the presence of nucleosomes. However, it is not clear whether nucleosomes are required for this effect.
To investigate these processes, we have developed a new quantitative assay that allows us to monitor the fraction of DNA molecules in the population that bear a nucleosome at any given instant. This has enabled us to follow the time courses of nucleosome removal and reformation in wild-type and mutant cells upon activation and repression of the GAL genes of yeast. Our results show that upon being freed of its inhibitor Gal80 by the action of galactose, Gal4 quickly recruits SWI/SNF to the genes, leading to the removal of promoter nucleosomes. In the absence of SWI/SNF, Gal4's action also results in nucleosome removal and the activation of transcription, but this process is significantly delayed. Addition of glucose to cells growing in galactose represses transcription, but if galactose remains present, Gal4 continues to work, recruiting SWI/SNF and maintaining the promoter nucleosome-free despite repression. This requirement for galactose is obviated in a mutant in which Gal4 works constitutively.
Our findings demonstrate how an activator's recruiting function can control chromatin structure both during gene activation and repression. We show that promoter nucleosome removal invariably accompanies activation, but reformation of nucleosomes is not required for repression. These results clarify our understanding of the early events of gene activation and correct earlier reports that SWI/SNF plays no role in GAL gene induction. Additionally, our findings contradict the widely held idea that nucleosomes are required for repression, as we show that repression sets in as efficiently whether or not promoter nucleosomes are allowed to reform.
The development of our nucleosome occupancy assay has provided a powerful tool for studying other outstanding issues in the field, and we believe it will prove useful in elucidating the complex interplay between chromatin structure and gene expression.

title: Contractile forces sustain and polarize hematopoiesis from stem and progenitor cells.
text: Self-renewal and differentiation of stem cells are regulated by asymmetric division and polarized motility processes, which are modulated by nonmuscle myosin-II (MII) forces and matrix mechanics. Using mass spectrometry-calibrated intracellular flow cytometry in human hematopoiesis, we found that MIIB is a major isoform that is strongly polarized in hematopoietic stem cells and progenitors (HSC/Ps) and downregulated in differentiated cells through asymmetric division. In contrast, MIIA is constitutive and activated by dephosphorylation during cytokine-triggered differentiation of cells grown on stiff, endosteum-like matrices, but not soft, marrow-like matrices. In vivo, MIIB is essential for the generation of blood, while MIIA is required for sustained HSC/P engraftment.
