This phosphorylation event precedes and is essential for ATM autophosphorylation at Ser 1981, and activates ATM kinase activity. The Cdk5-ATM signaling pathway regulates the phosphorylation and function of ATM targets, including p53 and H2AX. Inhibition of the Cdk5-ATM pathway attenuates DNA-damage-induced neuronal cell cycle re-entry and the expression of p53 targets, PUMA and Bax, protecting neurons from death. Therefore, activation of Cdk5 by DNA damage serves as a critical signal to initiate the ATM response and regulate ATM-dependent cellular processes.

title: Nerve-induced release of nitric oxide in the rabbit gastrointestinal tract as measured by in vivo microdialysis.
text:
Introduction:
Nitric oxide (NO) has been proposed as a gastrointestinal neurotransmitter, mediating the relaxation of the gastric mucosa and the peristaltic reflex. The aim of the present study was to measure in vivo nerve-induced NO formation in the gastrointestinal tract using a novel methodological procedure.
Methods:
Microdialysis probes were inserted into the wall of the stomach and proximal colon of anesthetized rabbits, and nitrite and nitrate concentrations in the dialysate were measured by capillary electrophoresis during bilateral vagal nerve stimulation. The effect of intravenous administration of the NO synthase inhibitor N omega-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) on nerve-induced NO formation was also investigated.
Results:
During bilateral vagal nerve stimulation, there was an increase in nitrite and nitrate formation in the stomach and colon, respectively. This increase was inhibited by L-NAME, which significantly increased nerve-induced gastric and colonic contractions, as well as spontaneous colonic contractions.
Discussion:
The present study provides evidence that NO is released in the stomach and colonic wall during vagal nerve activity, at concentrations able to cause inhibition of smooth muscle contractions in vivo. The novel methodological procedure used in this study allows for the quantification of small changes in NO formation in vivo, and highlights the importance of NO in the regulation of gastrointestinal function.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, the present study demonstrates the release of NO in the gastrointestinal tract during vagal nerve activity, and provides evidence for the role of NO in the regulation of gastrointestinal function. The novel methodological procedure used in this study provides a valuable tool for the study of NO formation in vivo, and highlights the importance of NO in the regulation of gastrointestinal function.

title: Screening for concomitant diseases in peripheral vascular patients. Results of a systematic approach.
text:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing arterial surgery often have a high prevalence of coexistent cardiovascular and other diseases, which can impact operative risk and survival. To address this, we developed a systematic workup strategy using non-invasive diagnostic techniques to detect these coexistent conditions in vascular surgical patients.
METHODS: We evaluated 200 consecutive patients admitted to our department of vascular surgery in an academic teaching hospital to determine the total incidence of relevant concomitant disorders, the extent to which this screening yielded new diagnostic information, and its impact on short-term (one year) survival.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed that coronary artery disease was present in 46% of patients, with 22% having active ischemia diagnosed for the first time in 5.5%. Impaired cardiac function was identified in 37% of patients, including 12% with severely impaired function and 27% with new diagnoses. Carotid artery disease was present in 32% of patients, with critical stenoses detected in 9% and new diagnoses in 29.9%. Aortic aneurysms were found in 7% of patients, with 5% being newly diagnosed. Severe renal artery stenosis was present in 5% of patients, with 3.5% being newly diagnosed. Additionally, 16% of patients had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with 3.5% being newly diagnosed, and 4.5% had unexpected disorders, all of which were new diagnoses. Overall, new diagnoses were made in 64.5% of patients, affecting therapeutic strategy in 21% of cases. The presence of coronary artery disease and cardiac failure were significantly related to one-year survival.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that a systematic screening strategy using non-invasive techniques can effectively detect coexistent diseases in vascular surgical patients. Notably, new diagnoses were made in one out of every five patients, which had a significant impact on surgical management and patient prognosis.

title: Archetypal trajectories of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress in family care givers of patients with lung cancer: secondary analysis of serial qualitative interviews
text:
Objective: To investigate whether family caregivers of patients with lung cancer experience similar patterns of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress as the patients themselves, from diagnosis to death.
Design: Secondary analysis of serial qualitative interviews conducted every three months for up to a year or until bereavement.
Setting: South East Scotland.
Participants: 19 patients with lung cancer and their 19 family caregivers, resulting in 88 interviews (42 with patients and 46 with caregivers).
Results: Caregivers exhibited patterns of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress that mirrored the experiences of the patients they were caring for, with some caregivers also experiencing deterioration in physical health, which impacted their ability to care. Psychological and spiritual distress were particularly prevalent, with carers experiencing personal reflections on the meaning and purpose of life in response to witnessing suffering. Key time points in the illness that proved particularly problematic for both carers and patients included diagnosis, initial treatment, recurrence, and the terminal stage.
Conclusions: Family caregivers share a significant portion of the illness experience of the dying patient, with the multidimensional distress experienced by patients with lung cancer reflected in the suffering of their caregivers in the social, psychological, and spiritual domains. Caregivers may require support throughout the illness period, rather than solely during the terminal phase and bereavement, as is currently the case.

title: HER-2/neu induces p53 ubiquitination via Akt-mediated MDM2 phosphorylation
text:
Her-2/neu amplification or overexpression can render cancer cells resistant to programmed cell death (apoptosis) and promote their growth. The tumor suppressor protein p53 plays a crucial role in regulating cell growth and apoptosis, but it is often mutated or deleted in various types of tumors. Interestingly, even in tumors with a wild-type p53 gene, the function of p53 can be impaired due to oncogenic signals.
Our study investigates the mechanism by which Her-2/neu-mediated resistance to DNA-damaging agents involves the activation of the Akt protein. Akt phosphorylates and enhances the ubiquitination and degradation of p53 through its interaction with the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2. Specifically, Akt phosphorylates MDM2 at Ser166 and Ser186, leading to increased nuclear localization and interaction with the coactivator p300, and decreased interaction with the tumor suppressor p19ARF. These changes result in enhanced p53 degradation, thereby conferring resistance to DNA-damaging drugs in tumor cells with wild-type p53.
Our findings suggest that inhibiting the Akt pathway, which is activated by Her-2/neu, may increase the cytotoxic effect of DNA-damaging drugs in tumor cells with wild-type p53. This provides a potential therapeutic strategy for overcoming resistance to chemotherapy in such tumors.

title: T cell memory.
text: T cell memory induced by prior infection or vaccination offers enhanced protection against subsequent microbial infections. Recent technological advances have helped scientists better understand the processes involved in generating and maintaining T cell memory. T cells develop in response to a specific set of signals, starting with antigen-loaded, activated antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and inflammatory mediators triggered by the innate immune response. As the immune response wanes towards homeostasis, additional signals are received, regulating the persistence of resting memory T cells. Cytokines play a crucial role in this process. This chapter explores recent findings on how memory T cells develop to confer long-term protective immunity.

title: The impact of organisational change on outcome in an intensive care unit in the United Kingdom
text:
Objective: To evaluate the impact of introducing a resident medical staff team and a "closed" organisational format on patient outcomes in an intensive care unit (ICU).
Design: Retrospective database review of prospectively collected data.
Setting: ICU of a postgraduate teaching hospital.
Subjects: 1134 ICU admissions over a 3-year period, of whom 476 (42%) underwent elective surgery.
Main outcome measure: Hospital mortality corrected for illness severity using the APACHE II scoring system.
Results: The crude hospital mortality rate decreased from 28% before the changes to 20% after (P=0.01). After adjusting for case-mix factors, the probability of death was reduced by almost half (OR 0.51; CI 0.32, 0.82, P=0.005).
Conclusion: The implementation of a resident medical staff team and a "closed" organisational format in the ICU was associated with improved patient outcomes, as evidenced by a significant decrease in hospital mortality.

title: Monitoring effectiveness and safety of Tafamidis in transthyretin amyloidosis in Italy: a longitudinal multicenter study in a non-endemic area
text: Tafamidis is a TTR stabilizer that prevents TTR tetramer dissociation, with encouraging studies on its efficacy in early-onset inherited transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) due to Val30Met mutation. However, its efficacy in later disease stages and non-Val30Met mutations is less clear. To investigate, we conducted a multi-center observational study on symptomatic ATTR patients treated with Tafamidis. We followed patients for up to 3 years, assessing them every 6 months using a standardized protocol that included general medical, cardiological, and neurological evaluations. Sixty-one patients (42 males) were enrolled, with only 28% carrying the common Val30Met mutation, and a late age of onset (59 years) and 18% in advanced disease stage at study entry. Tafamidis was well-tolerated, and one-third of patients showed no significant disease progression over 36 months, regardless of mutation type or disease stage. Neurological function worsened in the first 6 months but slowed thereafter, while autonomic function remained stable in 33%, worsened in 56%, and improved in 10%. Fifteen percent of patients experienced cardiac disease progression, and 30% developed new-onset cardiomyopathy. Unfortunately, Tafamidis was unable to prevent functional progression of the disease in 23 (43%) subjects, including 16 patients who worsened in their walking ability and 12 patients who reached a higher NYHA score during the follow-up period. Interestingly, a higher baseline mBMI was associated with better preservation of neurological function. In conclusion, despite treatment with Tafamidis, neuropathy and cardiomyopathy progressed in a significant proportion of patients. However, the rate of neurological function worsening slowed after the first 6 months, and subjects with more advanced neuropathy, as well as those with non-Val30Met mutations, benefited from treatment. Body weight preservation was also identified as a favorable prognostic factor.

title: The Spliceosome: Design Principles of a Dynamic RNP Machine
text: Ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) play a crucial role in cellular functions such as gene expression and regulation. Unlike most RNP enzymes, which maintain a stable composition and preformed active sites, the spliceosome, which removes non-coding introns from precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs), employs unique strategies to achieve accuracy in recognizing reactive splice sites and flexibility in choosing splice sites during alternative splicing. To accomplish this, the spliceosome exhibits exceptional compositional and structural dynamics during substrate-dependent complex assembly, catalytic activation, and active site remodeling.

title: Blimp-1 attenuates Th1 differentiation by repression of ifng, tbx21, and bcl6 gene expression.
text: Deletion of Blimp-1 in T cells leads to abnormal T cell homeostasis and function, resulting in spontaneous, fatal colitis in mice. To investigate the role of Blimp-1 in Th1/Th2 differentiation, we analyzed Blimp-1 mRNA and protein expression in Th1 and Th2 cells. Our findings revealed that Blimp-1 is more highly expressed in Th2 cells compared to Th1 cells, and that Blimp-1 attenuates interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) production in CD4 cells activated under non-polarizing conditions. Although Blimp-1-deficient T cells differentiate normally to Th2 cytokines in vitro, we found that Blimp-1 is required in vivo for normal Th2 humoral responses to NP-KLH immunization. The lack of Blimp-1 in CD4 T cells leads to increased IFN-γ, T-bet, and Bcl-6 mRNA expression. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation, we found that Blimp-1 binds directly to a distal regulatory region in the ifng gene and multiple sites in the tbx21 and bcl6 genes. Our data suggest that Blimp-1 functions in Th2 cells to reinforce Th2 differentiation by repressing critical Th1 genes.

title: CX3CR1 is required for airway inflammation by promoting T helper cell survival and maintenance in inflamed lung
text: Asthma is a T helper type 2 (T(H)2)-dominated disease of the lung, and in people with asthma, a fraction of CD4(+) T cells express the CX3CL1 receptor, CX3CR1. When exposed to an allergen, the expression of CX3CL1 increases in airway smooth muscle, lung endothelium, and epithelium. Our findings show that mice lacking the CX3CR1 gene or treated with CX3CR1-blocking reagents have reduced lung disease upon allergen sensitization and challenge. Transferring CD4(+) T cells from wild-type (WT) mice into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored the characteristic features of asthma, and CX3CR1-blocking reagents prevented airway inflammation in CX3CR1-deficient recipients injected with WT T(H)2 cells. We discovered that CX3CR1 signaling promotes T(H)2 cell survival in the inflamed lungs, and injecting B cell leukemia/lymphoma-2 protein (BCl-2)-transduced CX3CR1-deficient T(H)2 cells into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored asthma. Additionally, we found that CX3CR1-induced survival is observed for T(H)1 cells upon airway inflammation but not under homeostatic conditions or upon peripheral inflammation. These findings suggest that targeting CX3CR1 and CX3CL1 may be a promising therapeutic strategy for asthma.

title: TRPC6 is a glomerular slit diaphragm-associated channel required for normal renal function
text:
Progressive kidney failure due to genetic and clinical heterogeneity is a complex group of disorders. Podocyte foot processes and the interposed glomerular slit diaphragm are critical components of the kidney's permeability barrier. Mutations in genes encoding podocyte structural proteins can lead to the development of proteinuria, resulting in progressive kidney failure and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
In this study, we investigated the role of the canonical transient receptor potential 6 (TRPC6) ion channel in podocytes and its involvement in the glomerular slit diaphragm. We identified five families with autosomal dominant focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, in which disease segregated with mutations in the TRPC6 gene on chromosome 11q. Of particular interest, we found that two of the TRPC6 mutants exhibited increased current amplitudes, suggesting that TRPC6 channel activity at the slit diaphragm is essential for proper regulation of podocyte structure and function.
In conclusion, our findings provide evidence that TRPC6 channels play a critical role in maintaining the integrity of the glomerular barrier and suggest that dysfunction of these channels may contribute to the development of progressive kidney failure. Further research into the mechanisms underlying TRPC6-mediated podocyte function may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of kidney diseases.

title: Usefulness of high mobility group box 1 protein as a plasma biomarker in patient with peripheral artery disease.
text: Atherosclerosis is often linked to chronic vascular inflammation, and high-mobility group box 1 protein (HMGB1) plays multiple roles, including as a transcriptional regulator in the nucleus and as an inflammatory mediator. Previous research suggested that fibrinogen may be a crucial factor in the progression of atherosclerosis. To investigate the relationship between HMGB1 and atherosclerosis, we analyzed the levels of plasma HMGB1 protein in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) and atherosclerosis. Our study included 24 patients with PAD and atherosclerosis and 10 healthy controls. We found that the concentrations of HMGB1 were significantly higher in the plasma of patients with atherosclerosis, and there were strong correlations between plasma HMGB1 and fibrinogen levels. These findings suggest that plasma HMGB1 may play a key role in the development and progression of atherosclerosis.

title: Functional specialization of Piwi proteins in Paramecium tetraurelia from post-transcriptional gene silencing to genome remodelling
text: Proteins of the Argonaute family, which are small RNA-carrying molecules, play a crucial role in regulating gene expression by guiding regulatory complexes to their target sites. This family is divided into two main subclades, Ago and Piwi. Members of the Ago subclade are present in most eukaryotic phyla and bind different types of small RNAs, regulating gene expression at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. In contrast, Piwi subclade members, which are found primarily in metazoa, bind to piRNAs and play essential roles in sexual reproduction. Interestingly, Piwi proteins are also present in ciliates, which are unicellular organisms that harbor both germline micronuclei and somatic macronuclei. Here, we report phylogenetic and functional analyses of the 15 Piwi genes from Paramecium tetraurelia. Our findings show that four constitutively expressed Piwi proteins are involved in siRNA pathways that mediate gene silencing throughout the life cycle of the organism. Additionally, two other Piwi proteins, specifically expressed during meiosis, are required for the accumulation of scnRNAs during sexual reproduction and for programmed genome rearrangements during the development of the somatic macronucleus. Our results suggest that Paramecium Piwi proteins have evolved to perform both vegetative and sexual functions through a range of mechanisms, including post-transcriptional mRNA cleavage and epigenetic regulation of genome rearrangements.

title: A parasomnia overlap disorder involving sleepwalking, sleep terrors, and REM sleep behavior disorder in 33 polysomnographically confirmed cases.
text:
Over an 8-year period, a series of 33 patients with combined sleepwalking, sleep terrors, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (viz. "parasomnia overlap disorder") were studied. The patients underwent clinical and polysomnographic evaluations, and the results showed:
* The average age of the patients was 34 +/- 14 years (SD), with a range of 1-66 years.
* Seventy percent (n = 23) of the patients were males.
* An idiopathic subgroup (n = 22) had a significantly earlier age of parasomnia onset (9 +/- 7 years) compared to a symptomatic subgroup (n = 11) (27 +/- 23 years, p = 0.002), whose parasomnia began with either neurological disorders (such as congenital Mobius syndrome, narcolepsy, multiple sclerosis, brain tumor, and treatment, brain trauma, or indeterminate disorder (exaggerated startle response/atypical cataplexy)), nocturnal paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, posttraumatic stress disorder/major depression, chronic ethanol/amphetamine abuse and withdrawal, or mixed disorders (schizophrenia, brain trauma, substance abuse).
* The rate of DSM-III-R (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, 3rd edition, revised) Axis 1 psychiatric disorders was not elevated.
* Group scores on various psychometric tests were not elevated.
* Forty-five percent (n = 15) of the patients had previously received psychologic or psychiatric therapy for their parasomnia, without benefit.
* Treatment outcome was available for n = 20 patients, and 90% (n = 18) had substantial parasomnia control with bedtime clonazepam (n = 13), alprazolam and/or carbamazepine (n = 4), or self-hypnosis (n = 1).

In conclusion, "parasomnia overlap disorder" is a treatable condition that emerges in various clinical settings and can be understood within the context of current knowledge on parasomnias and motor control/dyscontrol during sleep.

title: How can health care organizations be reliably compared?: Lessons from a national survey of patient experience.
text:
Background: Patient experience is increasingly used to evaluate organizational performance, particularly in public reporting and pay-for-performance schemes. However, conventional approaches using 95% confidence intervals may result in unreliable comparisons between organizations.
Methods: We analyzed data from 2.2 million patients who completed the 2009 General Practice Patient Survey in England, which included 45 patient experience questions across 6 care domains (access, continuity of care, communication, anticipatory care planning, out-of-hours care, and overall care satisfaction). We calculated unadjusted and case-mix adjusted (for age, sex, and ethnicity) organization-level reliability and intraclass correlation coefficients for each question.
Results: The mean responses per organization ranged from 23 to 256 for primary care questions and from 1454 to 2758 for out-of-hours care questions. Adjusted and unadjusted reliability values were similar, with 26 questions having excellent reliability (≥0.90). Seven nurse communication questions had very good reliability (≥0.85), but 3 anticipatory care planning questions had lower reliability (<0.70). Reliability was typically <0.70 for questions with <100 mean responses per practice, indicating questions that only a subset of patients were eligible to answer. Nine questions had both excellent reliability and high intraclass correlation coefficients (≥0.10), indicating both reliable measurement and substantial performance variability.
Conclusions: High reliability is a crucial property of indicators used to compare healthcare organizations. By analyzing the English General Practice Patient Survey data, we demonstrate how reliability and intraclass correlation coefficients can be used to select measures that support robust organizational comparisons and to design surveys that provide high-quality measurement while minimizing survey costs.

title: Conservation of methylation reprogramming in mammalian development: aberrant reprogramming in cloned embryos.
text: In early embryonic development, mouse embryos undergo genome-wide demethylation, followed by remethylation. We investigate whether this process is conserved in other mammalian species and examine the effect of highly methylated somatic donor nuclei on epigenetic reprogramming in cloned embryos. Our findings show that demethylation occurs in normal zygotes from bovine, rat, and pig, suggesting active demethylation. In bovine embryos, methylation levels decrease during cleavage stages and then increase by the 16-cell stage, while cloned embryos exhibit reduced methylation similar to demethylation, but no further demethylation occurs. Instead, cloned embryos undergo de novo methylation and reorganization of methylation patterns resembling those of differentiated cells. Cloned morulae have highly methylated nuclei in all blastomeres, similar to the donor cells. Our study reveals that epigenetic reprogramming occurs abnormally in most cloned embryos, and incomplete reprogramming may contribute to the low efficiency of cloning.

title: Intracellular transport of fat-soluble vitamins A and E.
text:
Vitamins are essential compounds that support the normal growth, reproduction, and function of the human body. Of the 13 known vitamins, vitamins A, D, E, and K are classified as fat-soluble due to their lipophilic nature. These vitamins are transported and metabolized by intracellular carrier proteins, including retinoid-binding proteins, to exert their effects. Vitamin A and its derivatives, known as retinoids, are solubilized by intracellular proteins such as cellular retinol-binding protein (CRBP), cellular retinoic acid-binding protein (CRABP), and cellular retinal-binding protein (CRALBP). These proteins act as chaperones, regulating the metabolism, signaling, and transport of retinoids. CRALBP-mediated intracellular retinoid transport is crucial for vision in humans.
α-Tocopherol, the primary form of vitamin E found in the body, is transported by α-tocopherol transfer protein (α-TTP) in hepatic cells. Defects in α-TTP can lead to vitamin E deficiency and neurological disorders in humans. Recent research has shown that the interaction of α-TTP with phosphoinositides plays a critical role in the intracellular transport of α-tocopherol and is associated with familial vitamin E deficiency.
In this review, we summarize the mechanisms and biological significance of the intracellular transport of vitamins A and E, highlighting the role of intracellular carrier proteins in their metabolism and function.

title: Reduced Cytokine Release in Ex Vivo Response to Cilengitide and Cetuximab Is a Marker for Improved Survival of Head and Neck Cancer Patients
text: Targeting αVβ3 and αVβ5 integrins with cilengitide may reduce the growth of solid tumors, including head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Preclinical studies suggest that combining cilengitide with other treatment modalities may have increased activity. The only published trial in HNSCC, ADVANTAGE, investigated cisplatin, 5-fluorouracil, and cetuximab (PFE) without or with once (PFE+CIL1W) or twice weekly cilengitide (PFE+CIL2W) in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC. Although the cilengitide arms showed good tolerability and fewer adverse events compared to PFE, the trial did not demonstrate a significant improvement in overall survival as expected based on preclinical data. However, a short-time ex vivo assay called FLAVINO revealed that only a subset of HNSCC had a suppressive effect of cilengitide-containing combination therapies on colony formation of epithelial cells (CFec) and release of pro-angiogenetic and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while the remaining HNSCC failed to respond. These findings suggest that response to αVβ3 and αVβ5 integrin targeting by cilengitide can classify HNSCC regarding outcome. The FLAVINO data support the further development of cilengitide plus cetuximab for the treatment of a subgroup of HNSCC potentially identified by the FLAVINO assay using a set of biomarkers for response evaluation.

title: Genes required for mycobacterial growth defined by high density mutagenesis.
text: Despite over a century of research, tuberculosis remains a major infectious disease killer worldwide. As drug resistance to Mycobacterium tuberculosis increases, identifying genes essential for its growth can provide new targets for designing effective antibiotics. Here, we employ transposon site hybridization (TraSH) to comprehensively identify the genes required for optimal growth of M. tuberculosis. These genes include essential pathways and many of unknown function. Notably, the genes crucial for M. tuberculosis growth are conserved in the degenerate genome of Mycobacterium leprae, indicating that non-essential functions have been selectively lost since the leprosy bacillus diverged from other mycobacteria. In contrast, a significant proportion of these genes lack identifiable orthologues in other bacteria, suggesting that the minimal gene set required for survival varies greatly between organisms with different evolutionary histories.

title: Production of de novo cardiomyocytes: human pluripotent stem cell differentiation and direct reprogramming.
text: Cardiovascular disease is a significant global health concern, accounting for a substantial proportion of mortalities worldwide. The limited capacity of heart tissue to regenerate has prompted the development of innovative methods for generating de novo cardiomyocytes, both in vitro and in vivo. These methodological advancements have the potential to not only enhance cell replacement therapy but also find applications in drug testing, drug discovery, and disease modeling. Recently, there has been an expansion of approaches for generating cardiomyocytes, with three primary sources of starting cells: human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), adult heart-derived cardiac progenitor cells (CPCs), and reprogrammed fibroblasts. This review focuses on the state-of-the-art methods for generating de novo cardiomyocytes from hPSCs and reprogrammed fibroblasts, highlighting potential applications and future challenges.

title: Within the hemopoietic system, LAR phosphatase is a T cell lineage-specific adhesion receptor-like protein whose phosphatase activity appears dispensable for T cell development, repertoire selection and function.
text: The expression of the receptor-type tyrosine phosphatase LAR was investigated in cells of the murine hemopoietic system. The gene is expressed in all cells of the T cell lineage, but not in cells of any other hemopoietic lineage. The level of expression in T cells is developmentally regulated, with low levels observed in immature thymocytes and high levels in mature T cells. In contrast, uncommitted c-kit(+)B220(+)CD19(-) precursors in the bone marrow express low levels of LAR, while committed B cell lineage precursors do not. Interestingly, PAX-5-deficient pre-BI cells, which are committed to the B cell lineage, express LAR, suggesting that PAX-5-mediated commitment to the B cell lineage results in the suppression of LAR. During differentiation of PAX-5-deficient pre-BI cells into non-T cell lineages, expression of LAR is turned off, but it is up-regulated during differentiation into thymocytes. These findings suggest that LAR is a T cell lineage-specific receptor-type phosphatase within the hemopoietic system. However, surprisingly, truncation of its phosphatase domains has no obvious effect on T cell development, repertoire selection, or function.

title: Competition and the evolution of reproductive restraint in malaria parasites.
text:
All living organisms must balance the allocation of resources between different life processes that determine their survival and reproduction. Malaria parasites, for instance, replicate asexually within their hosts but must produce sexual stages to transmit between hosts. Due to the specialized nature of these life-history components, the allocation of resources between them poses a key challenge for natural selection to resolve. Despite their significant medical and economic importance, the reproductive strategies of these parasites remain poorly understood and often seem counterintuitive.
To investigate this phenomenon, we tested recent theories suggesting that in-host competition influences how parasites allocate resources between in-host replication and between-host transmission. Our findings, across multiple genotypes, reveal that Plasmodium chabaudi parasites detect the presence of competing genotypes and adjust their investment in sexual stages accordingly to maximize their competitive ability. Moreover, we show that genotypes adjust their allocation to sexual stages based on the availability of exploitable red blood cell resources.
Our findings are in line with evolutionary theory developed to explain life-history trade-offs in more traditionally studied multicellular organisms and suggest that the reason why few transmission stages are produced in natural infections is that heavy investment in reproduction may compromise in-host survival. In other words, the parasite's allocation of resources between in-host replication and between-host transmission is a delicate balance that must be struck to ensure both survival and reproduction.

title: [Neutrophils and macrophages related to the pathogenesis and disease development of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease by the inflammatory reaction].
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory disorder characterized by obstruction of airflow, which cannot be fully reversed with treatment. The initial stages of COPD are believed to involve inflammatory changes in the peripheral airways, particularly those with diameters less than 2mm (known as small airway disease). It is clear that neutrophils and macrophages play a crucial role in the development of these lesions. Bronchoalveolar lavage studies have shown an increase in neutrophil numbers and the neutrophil chemoattractant interleukin-8. Recent research has also demonstrated that neutrophils and macrophages are abundant in these lesions and contain a variety of proteases, which are involved in cell infiltration and activation. To gain a deeper understanding of the role of neutrophils and macrophages in COPD and to identify potential therapeutic targets, studies using gene-engineered animals and anti-cytokine treatment are being conducted.

title: Piezo1 Is as a Novel Trefoil Factor Family 1 Binding Protein that Promotes Gastric Cancer Cell Mobility In Vitro
text: Trefoil factor family 1 (TFF1) is a member of the TFF-domain peptide family involved in epithelial restitution and cell motility. Recently, we identified Piezo1 as a candidate TFF1-binding protein through a screening process. Our aim was to confirm the interaction between TFF1 and Piezo1 and to investigate its role in mediating gastric cancer cell mobility. Using co-immunoprecipitation and co-localization techniques, we confirmed the interaction between TFF1 and Piezo1 in GES-1 cells. To further investigate the significance of this interaction, we employed stable RNA interference to knockdown Piezo1 protein expression and restored the expression of TFF1 in gastric cancer cell lines SGC-7901 and BGC-823. Cell motility was evaluated using invasion and migration assays in vitro. Additionally, we detected the expression levels of integrin subunits β1, β5, α1, as well as β-catenin and E-cadherin by Western blot. Our findings revealed that TFF1 interacts specifically with the C-terminal portion of Piezo1 in the cytoplasm. Restoring TFF1 expression in gastric cancer cells led to enhanced cell mobility, which was attenuated by knockdown of Piezo1. Furthermore, Western blots showed decreased expression of integrin β1 in Piezo1-knockdown cells. Our study demonstrates that Piezo1 is a novel TFF1 binding protein that plays a crucial role in TFF1-mediated cell migration, and suggests that targeting this interaction may be a promising therapeutic strategy for the invasion and metastasis of gastric cancer.

title: A conditionally lethal yeast mutant blocked at the first step in glycosyl phosphatidylinositol anchor synthesis.
text: Glycosyl phosphatidylinositols (GPIs) play a crucial role in anchoring proteins to the surface of eukaryotic cells, and may also serve as sorting signals or participate in signal transduction. To investigate the importance of GPIs in the unicellular eukaryote Saccharomyces cerevisiae, we isolated a GPI anchoring mutant, gpi1, using a colony screen for cells that exhibited reduced incorporation of [3H]inositol into proteins. The gpi1 mutant is defective in the synthesis of N-acetylglucosaminyl phosphatidylinositol, the first intermediate in GPI synthesis, and is also temperature-sensitive for growth. Our findings suggest that completion of the first step in GPI assembly is essential for the growth of S. cerevisiae, making GPI synthesis a potential target for antifungal or antiparasitic agents.

title: Beyond pattern recognition: five immune checkpoints for scaling the microbial threat
text:
The innate immune system's ability to recognize patterns enables the detection of microorganisms, but the process by which the level of microbial threat is evaluated is not as well understood. New research has revealed that the immune system can detect features of microbial viability and respond accordingly, inducing robust responses that are not warranted for dead microorganisms. To better understand this process, we propose five immune checkpoints that collectively determine the severity of microbial encounters. These checkpoints include:
1. Cellular viability: The ability of microorganisms to maintain cellular viability and function, even in the face of immune pressure.
2. Metabolic activity: The ability of microorganisms to maintain metabolic activity, such as the production of ATP, which can indicate their level of activity and potential to cause harm.
3. Morphological changes: The ability of microorganisms to undergo changes in shape or structure, which can indicate their level of activity and potential to cause harm.
4. Biochemical signals: The ability of microorganisms to produce biochemical signals, such as lipopolysaccharides, which can activate the immune response and indicate their level of threat.
5. Host-microbe interactions: The ability of microorganisms to interact with the host immune system, including the ability to evade or subvert immune responses, which can indicate their level of threat.
By understanding these five immune checkpoints, we can better appreciate the complex and dynamic nature of the immune response to microbial encounters, and how it can be modulated to minimize inflammatory tissue damage while still effectively combating infection.

title: Macrophages induce COX-2 expression in breast cancer cells: role of IL-1β autoamplification.
text: In this study, the authors investigated the relationship between tumor-associated macrophages and high levels of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in breast cancer patients, and whether macrophages regulate COX-2 expression in breast cancer cells. The study found that coculture of THP-1 cells (a type of macrophage cell line) with breast cancer cells (HCC1954) led to increased COX-2 expression and elevated prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) levels in the conditioned media. Similar results were observed when THP-1 cells were incubated with other breast cancer cells (HCC1937) or when human monocyte-derived macrophages were cocultured with HCC1954 cells. The coculture triggered the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in HCC1954 cells, which in turn induced COX-2 expression. The study also found that the induction of COX-2 was blocked when cells were preincubated with an inhibitor of NADPH oxidase or when the expression of p67PHOX, a subunit of NADPH oxidase, was silenced. Additionally, the study showed that ROS production triggered the activation of Src and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), and that blocking these pathways or the activator protein-1 (AP-1) transcription factor attenuated COX-2 induction in HCC1954 cells. The study also found that macrophage-induced COX-2 expression was blocked when HCC1954 cells were preincubated with an interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) or anti-IL-1β IgG, suggesting that macrophages contribute to COX-2 induction through IL-1β-mediated signaling. Overall, the study suggests that macrophages play a role in the progression of breast cancer by inducing COX-2 expression in breast cancer cells through IL-1β-mediated signaling, and that targeting this pathway may be a potential therapeutic strategy in breast cancer treatment.

title: A graphene-based platform for induced pluripotent stem cells culture and differentiation.
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold great promise for regenerative medicine, yet their culture, maintenance of pluripotency, and induction of differentiation remain challenging. In contrast, graphene (G) and graphene oxide (GO) have garnered significant attention in the fields of materials science, physics, chemistry, and nanotechnology. In this study, we investigate the potential of G and GO to support the culture and differentiation of mouse iPSCs. Our findings reveal that both G and GO surfaces support the spontaneous differentiation of iPSCs into ectodermal and mesodermal lineages, with distinct cell proliferation and differentiation characteristics. Notably, iPSCs cultured on G surfaces exhibited similar degrees of cell adhesion and proliferation as those on the GO surface, while iPSCs on the GO surface adhered and proliferated at a faster rate. Furthermore, G maintained the iPSCs in an undifferentiated state, while GO expedited differentiation. Interestingly, G suppressed iPSC differentiation towards the endodermal lineage, while GO augmented endodermal differentiation. These findings suggest that the unique surface properties of G and GO govern the behavior of iPSCs and highlight the potential of graphene-based materials as a platform for iPSCs culture and diverse applications.

title: Aerobic capacity in black adolescent girls.
text: The aim of our study was to determine the aerobic capacities (VO2max) of a group of black female adolescents (aged 11.4-15.8 years) selected randomly from a single urban school. Of the 91 girls selected, 64 completed an incremental treadmill running test to volitional exhaustion and had their VO2max measured through expired gas analysis. Other measures included height, weight, and skinfold measurements for body fat percentage estimation. Additionally, the girls were asked if they had reached menarche. Our findings showed that VO2max averaged 37.3 +/- 6.2 ml.kg-1 x min-1 and was significantly correlated with height (-0.32, p < 0.01), body mass index (-0.63, p < 0.001), and body fat percentage (-0.65, p < 0.001), but not with age (-0.16, p > 0.10). Postmenarchal girls were found to be taller and older than premenarchal girls. Contrary to previous studies, our subjects' VO2max values were not related to their biological age. Our findings showed that the girls' VO2max values averaged 14% lower than those of non-black U.S. female adolescents reported in the literature. This difference in VO2max was primarily due to body weight. Our study suggests that overweight in adult black women may develop during early adolescence, highlighting the importance of aerobic fitness in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in black adolescent girls. Future longitudinal studies should be designed to investigate the effects of aerobic fitness on cardiovascular risk factor reduction in black adolescent girls.

title: Acetylation controls Notch3 stability and function in T-cell leukemia
text: The post-translational modifications of Notch3 and their functional implications in T-cell leukemia remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify a novel property of Notch3, which is acetylated and deacetylated at lysines 1692 and 1731 by p300 and HDAC1, respectively. The balance between these modifications is disrupted by HDAC inhibitors (HDACi), leading to hyperacetylation of Notch3. Using HDACi and a non-acetylatable Notch3 mutant carrying K/R1692−1731 mutations in the intracellular domain, we demonstrate that Notch3 acetylation primes ubiquitination and proteasomal-mediated degradation of the protein. Consequently, Notch3 protein expression and its transcriptional activity are decreased both in vitro and in vivo in Notch3 transgenic (tg) mice, thereby impairing downstream signaling upon target genes. Notably, HDACi-induced Notch3 hyperacetylation inhibits in vivo growth of T-cell leukemia/lymphoma in Notch3 tg mice. Our findings suggest a novel level of Notch signaling control, where the Notch3 acetylation/deacetylation process serves as a key regulatory switch. This finding provides a druggable target for Notch3-sustained T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia therapy.

title: Hypoglycemia: incidence and clinical predictors in a large population-based sample of children and adolescents with IDDM.
text:
Objective: To determine the frequency of moderate and severe hypoglycemic episodes and identify clinical predictors associated with their occurrence in a large population-based sample of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).
Design and Methods: A prospective study over 3 years, including 657 patients (age 12.1 ± 4.4 years, mean ± SD) with T1DM, resulting in 1,449 patient-years of data. Patients and caregivers recorded episodes of significant hypoglycemia (moderate and severe events) at each 3-month clinic visit, along with HbA1c levels. Data were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models fitted with the exchange correlation structure.
Results: The overall incidence of severe hypoglycemic events was 4.8/100 patient-years, and of moderate events was 13.1/100 patient-years. Over 3 years, severe events occurred in 8.5% of children, and moderate events occurred in 26.9%. Significant hypoglycemia was rare in the first 12 months after diagnosis. Rates of hypoglycemia were higher in children < 6 years of age compared to > 6 years of age (40.9 vs. 16.6/100 patient-years, P < 0.001). Rates of hypoglycemia doubled when HbA1c levels fell below 8%, and children with HbA1c < 7% had a threefold increase in both moderate and severe hypoglycemia (e.g., severe episodes 14.9 vs. 4.1/100 patient-years, HbA1c < or = 7% vs. HbA1c > 7%, P < 0.001). Most severe events were seizures, and 75% of them occurred at night. The majority of events were related to missed meals or increased activity, but in 38% no predisposing factor was evident.
Conclusions: Newly diagnosed children appear to be protected from severe hypoglycemia. Rates increase with lower glycated hemoglobin, especially when mean HbA1c is < 8.0%. Younger children, who may be more susceptible to the adverse effects of neuroglycopenia, are at a particular risk of significant hypoglycemia.

title: Efficacy of a 6-month versus 9-month intermittent treatment regimen in HIV-infected patients with tuberculosis: a randomized clinical trial.
text:
The study compared the efficacy of two different antituberculosis treatment regimens in HIV-infected patients with newly diagnosed pulmonary or extrapulmonary tuberculosis. The regimens were:
* Reg6M: an intermittent 6-month regimen consisting of ethambutol, isoniazid, rifampicin, and pyrazinamide for 2 months, followed by isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 months.
* Reg9M: a 9-month regimen consisting of ethambutol, isoniazid, rifampicin, and pyrazinamide for the entire 9 months.
The study found that:
* The outcome of the 6-month regimen was similar to the 9-month regimen in terms of favorable responses at the end of treatment.
* However, the 9-month regimen had a significantly lower bacteriological recurrence rate compared to the 6-month regimen.
* All 19 patients who failed treatment developed acquired rifamycin resistance (ARR), with baseline isoniazid resistance being the main risk factor.
* Neither mortality nor ARR was altered by lengthening TB treatment.
The study concluded that among antiretroviral treatment-naive HIV-infected patients with TB, a 9-month regimen resulted in a similar outcome at the end of treatment but a significantly lower bacteriological recurrence rate compared to a 6-month thrice-weekly regimen. However, acquired rifamycin resistance was high with these intermittent regimens, and neither mortality nor ARR was altered by lengthening TB treatment.

title: High prevalence of evolutionarily conserved and species-specific genomic aberrations in mouse pluripotent stem cells.
text: Mouse pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) are the most extensively studied pluripotent system and are widely regarded as the benchmark against which human PSCs are compared. However, despite the growing attention to the genomic integrity of human PSCs, the genomic stability of mouse PSCs has remained largely unexplored. The integrity of PSCs is of paramount importance, as it impacts their pluripotency, differentiation, and tumorigenicity. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the genomic integrity of 325 mouse PSC samples, including 127 induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) samples. Our findings revealed that genomic aberrations are frequent in mouse embryonic stem cells of various mouse strains and iPSCs of diverse cell origins and derivation techniques. Specifically, we identified four hotspots of chromosomal aberrations: full trisomy 11, full trisomy 8, and deletions in chromosomes 10qB and 14qC-14qE. Interestingly, the most recurrent aberration in mouse PSCs, gain 11qE2, showed synteny with the common aberration 17q25 in human PSCs, while other recurrent aberrations were found to be species-specific. In addition, analysis of chromosomal aberrations in 74 samples of rhesus macaque PSCs revealed a gain in chromosome 16q, which is syntenic to the hotspot in human 17q. These findings highlight the need to rigorously monitor the genomic integrity of PSCs from all species to ensure their proper use in biomedical research.

title: Inhibition of cell proliferation and induction of apoptosis by ExFABP gene targeting.
text: Ex-FABP, an extracellular fatty acid binding lipocalin, is expressed physiologically by differentiating chicken chondrocytes and myoblasts. Its expression is enhanced after exposure to inflammatory stimuli and repressed by anti-inflammatory agents, consistent with its classification as an acute phase protein. In vitro studies using chicken liver fragments showed that Ex-FABP expression is increased after treatment with bacterial endotoxin. To investigate the biological role of Ex-FABP, we employed stable transfection of proliferating chondrocytes with an expression vector carrying antisense-oriented Ex-FABP cDNA. Our findings revealed a significant loss of cell viability and a pronounced inhibition of cell proliferation and differentiation following Ex-FABP down-modulation. Additionally, we observed an increase in apoptotic cell number upon Ex-FABP down-modulation in chondrocytes, and extensive cell death and impaired myotube formation in myoblasts. These results suggest that Ex-FABP serves as a constitutive survival protein and that its expression and activation are essential to protect chondrocytes from cell death.

title: Profile of the Navrongo Health and Demographic Surveillance System.
text:
Located in the Kassena-Nankana districts of northern Ghana, the Navrongo Health and Demographic Surveillance System (NHDSS) was established in 1992 by the Navrongo Health Research Centre (NHRC). The NHRC is one of three research centers of the Ghana Health Service. The NHDSS monitors the health and demographic dynamics of the two Kassena-Nankana districts in northern Ghana and evaluates the morbidity and mortality impact of health and social interventions. Currently, the system is tracking the health status of 152,000 individuals residing in 32,000 households, with data updates every 4 months provided by trained field workers. The NHRC also conducts biomedical and socio-economic studies.
The NHDSS has several unique features, including the community key informant system, where trained volunteers report key events such as births and deaths as they occur in their locality, and the verbal autopsy (VA) system, which determines the probable causes of deaths that occur at the community level. The data collected by the NHDSS is shared with funders, collaborators, and partners in the INDEPTH Network. The Director of the NHDSS is the primary contact for potential collaboration and the use of its data.

title: The impact of COPD on lung health worldwide: epidemiology and incidence.
text:
Data on the prevalence of COPD was obtained from various sources, including vital statistics, health interview surveys, hospital charge records, national publications, and the World Health Organization (WHO). These data suggest that COPD is a widespread disease with significant implications for global health. In the United States, COPD is the fourth leading cause of death, with approximately 4% of the population affected. Internationally, there is significant variation in death rates, which may be due to factors such as smoking habits, tobacco processing and type, pollution, climate, respiratory management, and genetic predisposition.
The Global Obstructive Lung Disease Initiative, launched by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and the WHO, aims to raise awareness of the growing burden of COPD, reduce morbidity and mortality, promote further research into the condition, and implement programs to prevent COPD.

title: TLR activation triggers the rapid differentiation of monocytes into macrophages and dendritic cells
text: Leprosy provides an opportunity to study the mechanisms by which the innate immune system contributes to protecting the host against infection, as the disease can progress or remain limited. We found that activation of Toll-like receptors (TLRs) on human monocytes leads to the rapid differentiation of these cells into two distinct subsets: DC-SIGN+ CD16+ macrophages and CD1b+ DC-SIGN− dendritic cells. DC-SIGN+ macrophages were expanded by TLR-mediated upregulation of interleukin (IL)-15 and IL-15 receptor, while CD1b+ dendritic cells were expanded by TLR-mediated upregulation of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and its receptor, leading to increased T cell activation and proinflammatory cytokine secretion. Notably, DC-SIGN+ macrophages were detected in lesions and after TLR activation in all leprosy patients, while CD1b+ dendritic cells were not detected in lesions or after TLR activation of peripheral monocytes in individuals with the progressive lepromatous form, except during reversal reactions in which bacilli were cleared by TH1 responses. In tuberculoid lepromatous lesions, DC-SIGN+ cells were positive for macrophage markers but negative for dendritic cell markers, suggesting that TLR-induced differentiation of monocytes into either macrophages or dendritic cells plays a crucial role in shaping effective host defenses against infection in human disease.

title: Mismatch repair status and clinical outcome in endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between deficiency in mismatch repair (MMR) genes and prognosis in women with endometrial cancer is unclear. To investigate this association, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between MMR status and clinical outcomes in endometrial cancer.
METHODS: We searched major literature databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane) from 1980 to December 2011 to identify studies assessing the association between MMR status and clinical outcomes in endometrial cancer. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS).
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met our inclusion criteria, with a median sample size of 112. The majority of studies (74%) were retrospective case-series, and 70% used microsatellite instability (MSI) analysis to evaluate MMR status. However, only 22% of studies used the recommended panel of five microsatellite markers by the National Cancer Institute. Only seven studies used immunohistochemistry to define MMR deficiency, and only two of these studies evaluated the expression of all four MMR proteins. Significant associations between MMR and outcome were observed in 32% of studies, but there was marked inter-study heterogeneity for estimates of OS and DFS. Pooled analysis did not show any significant association between MMR deficiency and worse OS (6 studies, hazard ratio [HR] 2.0, p=0.11) or DFS (4 studies, HR ratio 1.31, p=0.66).
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that there is no definitive evidence of a significant association between MMR status and detrimental survival in endometrial cancer.

title: p53 induces formation of NEAT1 lncRNA-containing paraspeckles that modulate replication stress response and chemosensitivity
text: In our search for mediators of the p53 tumor suppressor pathway, which triggers diverse and often opposing cellular responses, we discovered the long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) NEAT1. NEAT1 is a crucial structural component of paraspeckle nuclear bodies, whose functional significance in disease remains unclear. Upon activation of p53, either pharmacologically or through oncogene-induced replication stress, we observed the formation of paraspeckles in mouse and human cells. Silencing NEAT1 expression in mice, which abrogates paraspeckle formation, enhanced sensitivity of preneoplastic cells to DNA damage-induced cell death and impaired skin tumorigenesis. Our findings provide mechanistic insights into the role of NEAT1 in attenuating oncogene-dependent p53 activation through a negative feedback loop. Notably, targeting NEAT1 in established human cancer cell lines resulted in synthetic lethality with genotoxic chemotherapeutics, including PARP inhibitors, and nongenotoxic activation of p53. This study establishes a key genetic connection between NEAT1-mediated paraspeckle formation, p53 biology, and tumorigenesis, and identifies NEAT1 as a promising target for enhancing cancer cell sensitivity to both chemotherapy and p53 reactivation therapy.

title: Regulation of innate immunity by NADPH oxidase.
text: NADPH oxidase is a crucial regulator of both host defense against microbial infections and inflammation. Activated by microorganisms and their byproducts in phagocytic cells, NADPH oxidase is rapidly assembled and generates reactive oxygen intermediates (ROIs) in response to infectious threats. Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), an inherited disorder of NADPH oxidase, is characterized by recurrent and severe bacterial and fungal infections, as well as pathological manifestations of excessive inflammation. Studies in CGD patients and mouse models have revealed that NADPH oxidase plays a pivotal role in modulating inflammation and tissue damage, distinct from its antimicrobial function, which has far-reaching implications for understanding the normal physiological immune response and various pathological states, such as acute lung injury and bacterial or fungal infections.

title: Protection from olanzapine-induced metabolic toxicity in mice by acetaminophen and tetrahydroindenoindole
text:
Objective: To investigate the preventive effects of acetaminophen (APAP) and tetrahydroindenoindole (THII) on metabolic changes in mice treated with the antipsychotic drug olanzapine (OLZ).
Design and Measurement: C57BL/6J mice were given either a standard diet or a high-fat (HF) diet and administered daily doses of OLZ (3 mg/kg body weight), alone or with APAP (30 mg/kg body weight) or THII (4.5 mg/kg body weight) for 10 weeks. Body composition and metabolic parameters, including glucose and insulin homeostasis and oxidative stress, were measured.
Results: OLZ treatment doubled the HF diet-induced increases in body weight and body fat. APAP and THII partially prevented these increases, while food consumption remained constant in all groups. THII also increased whole body and mitochondrial respiration. OLZ exacerbated HF diet-induced loss of glucose tolerance and insulin resistance, but APAP and THII prevented these effects. As increased body fat promotes insulin resistance through oxidative stress, we evaluated lipid peroxidation in white adipose tissue (WAT). HF diet increased lipid peroxidation, NADPH-dependent O2 uptake, and H2O2 production, which were further exacerbated by OLZ. APAP, THII, and the NADPH oxidase inhibitor, diphenyleneiodonium chloride, abolished oxidative stress in WAT.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that both APAP and THII intervene in the development of obesity and metabolic complications associated with OLZ treatment.

title: Detection of prions in blood
text: Prion diseases are caused by an unconventional infectious agent termed prion, primarily composed of misfolded prion protein (PrPSc). The development of highly sensitive assays for biochemical detection of PrPSc in blood is crucial for minimizing the spread of the disease. Here, we demonstrate that the protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA) technology can be automated and optimized for high-efficiency amplification of PrPSc. We show that 140 PMCA cycles result in a 6,600-fold increase in sensitivity compared to standard detection methods. Two consecutive rounds of PMCA cycles led to a 10 million–fold increase in sensitivity, enabling the detection of as little as 8,000 equivalent molecules of PrPSc. Notably, serial PMCA enabled the detection of PrPSc in blood samples of scrapie-afflicted hamsters with 89% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These findings represent the first time that PrPSc has been detected biochemically in blood, offering potential for developing a noninvasive method for early diagnosis of prion diseases.

title: Genetic alterations and their relationship in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt pathway in thyroid cancer.
text:
Objective: To investigate the prevalence and interrelationship of genetic alterations in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt signaling pathway in thyroid tumors and explore its potential as a therapeutic target for thyroid cancer.
Experimental Design: We analyzed the genetic alterations in the PI3K/Akt pathway, including PIK3CA copy number gain and mutation, Ras mutation, and PTEN mutation, in a large series of primary thyroid tumors.
Results: Our findings revealed that any of these genetic alterations occurred in 31% of benign thyroid adenomas (BTA), 55% of follicular thyroid cancers (FTC), 24% of papillary thyroid cancers (PTC), and 58% of anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC), with FTC and ATC showing the highest frequency. PIK3CA copy gain was associated with increased PIK3CA protein expression. A mutual exclusivity among these genetic alterations was observed in BTA, FTC, and PTC, suggesting an independent role of each alteration in the tumorigenesis of these differentiated thyroid tumors. However, coexistence of these genetic alterations increased with progression from differentiated tumors to undifferentiated ATC. Their coexistence with BRAF mutation was also frequent in PTC and ATC.
Conclusions: Our findings provide strong genetic evidence that aberrant activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway plays a significant role in thyroid tumorigenesis, particularly in FTC and ATC. The coexistence of these genetic alterations and BRAF mutation may facilitate progression from PTC to ATC. The PI3K/Akt pathway may thus be a promising therapeutic target in thyroid cancers.

title: Vitamin D and obesity: current perspectives and future directions.
text: In recent years, new roles of vitamin D have emerged beyond its traditional function in calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism, linking the fat-soluble vitamin to various non-communicable diseases. Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] < 25-30 nmol/l) and suboptimal status (25(OH)D < 50-100 nmol/l) are increasingly associated with unfavourable metabolic phenotypes, including insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease (CVD), conditions commonly linked with overweight and obesity. Early studies found poor vitamin D status in morbidly obese individuals. More recent observations suggest a graded relationship between vitamin D status and body mass index (BMI), or adiposity, exists in the general population. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain the mechanisms underlying alterations in the vitamin D endocrine system in the obese state, including sequestration in adipose tissue, volumetric dilution, or negative feedback mechanisms from increased circulating 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3. Some researchers suggest that heavier individuals may engage in less outdoor activity, cover themselves more, or limit sun exposure, leading to decreased endogenous vitamin D production in the skin. However, the relationship between BMI and vitamin D status following supplementation is inconsistent, making it unclear whether body size and adiposity should be considered when determining dietary vitamin D requirements. This review aims to evaluate the current evidence linking vitamin D status and supplementation to overweight and obesity and discuss the implications for setting dietary requirements.

title: Transcriptional regulation by p53 through intrinsic DNA/chromatin binding and site-directed cofactor recruitment.
text: The tumor suppressor protein p53 plays a crucial role in responding to cellular stress signals by regulating genes involved in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. p53 is inactive when it comes to DNA binding unless its C-terminus is modified or structurally altered. Our findings show that unmodified p53 actively binds to two sites within the chromatin-assembled p21 promoter at -1.4 and -2.3 kb, and requires the C-terminus and the histone acetyltransferase p300 for transcription. Acetylation of the C-terminus by p300 is not necessary for binding or promoter activation, but instead, p300 acetylates p53-bound nucleosomes in the p21 promoter, spreading to the TATA box. This suggests that p53 is an active DNA and chromatin binding protein that can selectively regulate its target genes by recruiting specific cofactors to structurally distinct binding sites.

title: Pleiotropic effects of statins.
text:
Statins are powerful inhibitors of cholesterol production in the body. Clinical trials have shown that statins are beneficial in both primary and secondary prevention of coronary heart disease. However, the observed benefits of statins go beyond mere cholesterol reduction, suggesting effects on various cellular processes. Recent studies have revealed that some of these non-lipid-related effects of statins include:
1. Improving endothelial function: Statins have been shown to enhance the health of the inner lining of blood vessels, which can help to prevent the formation of atherosclerosis.
2. Stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques: Statins may help to reduce the risk of plaque rupture and subsequent heart attack or stroke.
3. Reducing oxidative stress and inflammation: Statins have anti-inflammatory properties, which can help to protect against cellular damage and reduce the risk of chronic diseases.
4. Inhibiting the thrombogenic response: Statins may help to prevent the formation of blood clots, which can reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke.
5. Beneficial effects on the immune system, CNS, and bone: Statins have been shown to have a positive impact on various aspects of overall health, including the immune system, central nervous system, and bone health.
The mechanisms underlying these pleiotropic effects of statins involve inhibition of isoprenoids, which are lipids that play a crucial role in intracellular signaling pathways. In particular, inhibition of small GTP-binding proteins, such as Rho, Ras, and Rac, whose proper membrane localization and function are dependent on isoprenylation, may play an important role in mediating the non-lipid-related effects of statins.

title: Increasing the efficiency of precise genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9 by inhibition of nonhomologous end joining
text: Methods for introducing targeted double-strand breaks (DSBs) into DNA enable precise genome editing by increasing the rate at which externally supplied DNA fragments are incorporated into the genome through homologous recombination. The efficiency of these methods is limited by nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), an alternative DNA repair pathway that competes with homology-directed repair (HDR). To promote HDR at the expense of NHEJ, we targeted DNA ligase IV, a key enzyme in the NHEJ pathway, using the inhibitor Scr7. Treatment with Scr7 increased the efficiency of HDR-mediated genome editing, as demonstrated in mammalian cell lines and mice, with up to 19-fold increases in the efficiency of genome editing using the Cas9 endonuclease. This approach is likely to be applicable to other customizable endonucleases, such as zinc finger nucleases and transcription activator–like effector nucleases, as well as to nonmammalian cells with sufficiently conserved mechanisms of NHEJ and HDR.

title: Molecular mechanism of BST2/tetherin downregulation by K5/MIR2 of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus.
text: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) membrane-associated RING-CH (MARCH) ubiquitin ligase proteins K3/MIR1 and K5/MIR2 play a crucial role in immune evasion by targeting ubiquitin to immunostimulatory transmembrane proteins, thereby avoiding host immune responses. In a previous study, we identified K5 and HIV-1 immunomodulator VPU as novel host cell proteins downregulated by viral immunomodulators, suggesting that BST2 (bone marrow stromal cell antigen 2) might be a novel substrate of K5. Recent research revealed that HIV-1 virions are tethered to the plasma membrane in BST2-expressing HeLa cells, and that K5 may similarly overcome an innate antiviral host defense mechanism by targeting BST2. Our findings demonstrate that BST2 is a bona fide target of K5, which is downregulated during primary infection and reactivation of KSHV. Ubiquitination of BST2 by K5 leads to its rapid degradation, and this process is essential for K5's function. Moreover, we show that KSHV release is decreased in the absence of K5, suggesting that K5 contributes to the evasion of intracellular antiviral defense programs. Our study identifies BST2 as the first type II transmembrane protein targeted by K5 and the first example of a protein that is both ubiquitinated and GPI linked.

title: Regulation of beta catenin signaling and parathyroid hormone anabolic effects in bone by the matricellular protein periostin.
text: Periostin (Postn) is a protein primarily expressed by osteocytes and periosteal osteoblasts in response to mechanical stress and parathyroid hormone (PTH) stimulation. However, the role of periostin in bone anabolism remains unclear. To investigate, we examined the skeletal response of adult Postn-deficient (Postn(-/-) and Postn(+/+) mice) to intermittent PTH treatment. Our findings revealed that Postn(-/-) mice had lower bone mass, cortical bone volume, and strength compared to Postn(+/+) mice. PTH-stimulated bone-forming indices were significantly lower in Postn(-/-) mice, particularly at the periosteum. In vitro studies showed that PTH inhibited MEF2C and sclerostin (Sost) expression in bone and osteoblasts, while recombinant periostin suppressed Sost expression through the integrin αVβ3 receptor. Periostin-blocking antibody prevented PTH-mediated inhibition of MEF2C and Sost. Administration of a Sost-blocking antibody partially restored the PTH-mediated increase in bone mass in Postn(-/-) mice. Primary osteoblasts from Postn(-/-) mice showed decreased proliferation, mineralization, and migration, both spontaneously and in response to PTH. Osteoblastic gene expression levels confirmed a defect in Postn(-/-) osteoblast differentiation and increased osteoblast apoptosis. These findings elucidate the complex role of periostin in bone anabolism, including the regulation of Sost, Wnt-β-catenin signaling, and osteoblast differentiation.

title: Lipoprotein(a) concentration and the risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and nonvascular mortality.
text: The study investigated the relationship between the circulating concentration of lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]) and the risk of various vascular and nonvascular outcomes. The study included 126,634 participants from 36 prospective studies with a median follow-up time of 1.3 million person-years. The study found that Lp(a) concentration was weakly correlated with conventional vascular risk factors and was highly consistent within individuals over time. The study also found that higher Lp(a) concentrations were associated with an increased risk of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke, with a risk ratio of 1.16 (95% CI, 1.11-1.22) per 3.5-fold higher usual Lp(a) concentration, and 1.13 (95% CI, 1.09-1.18) following further adjustment for lipids and other conventional risk factors. The study also found that Lp(a) concentration was associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke, but not with the risk of nonvascular mortality, cancer deaths, or nonvascular deaths other than cancer. The study concluded that there are continuous, independent, and modest associations of Lp(a) concentration with risk of CHD and stroke that appear exclusive to vascular outcomes.

title: The biphasic behavior of incoherent feed-forward loops in biomolecular regulatory networks.
text: An incoherent feed-forward loop (FFL) is a ubiquitous motif in biomolecular regulatory networks, observed with remarkable frequency. Previous studies have posited that the incoherent FFL is designed to elicit a transient response characterized by 'fast activation and delayed inhibition'. However, our investigation reveals that the dynamics of various incoherent FFLs can be categorized into two distinct types: time-dependent biphasic responses and dose-dependent biphasic responses. The reasons behind the disparate dynamical roles of structurally identical incoherent FFLs remain enigmatic. Through computational analyses, we demonstrate that the dynamics of these two types of incoherent FFLs are mutually exclusive. Furthermore, our findings and additional computational results suggest that incoherent FFLs have been optimally designed to fulfill distinct biological functions, arising from different cellular contexts. Additional Supporting Information can be found in the online version of the article.

title: Antipsychotic prescribing patterns in Germany: a retrospective analysis using a large outpatient prescription database.
text: The data on prescribing practices for antipsychotics holds significant importance in evaluating the quality of care. To investigate this, we analyzed all prescriptions under the statutory health insurance claims redeemed at pharmacies in Southern Germany between July 1999 and December 2001. This database covers prescriptions for approximately 25 million people. Approximately 6% of the population was prescribed an antipsychotic at least once during the study period. The majority of prescriptions were written by non-specialists and were for conventional antipsychotics. Patients receiving second-generation antipsychotics were more likely to receive continuous antipsychotic therapy. A significant proportion of patients were found to be taking multiple antipsychotic medications, known as polypharmacy, as well as medications for somatic illnesses. In particular, drugs for the treatment of cardiovascular and metabolic disorders were frequently co-prescribed. It is essential for physicians to consider patients' cardiovascular and metabolic risk profile when selecting treatment options. Our findings suggest that the majority of antipsychotics are used for conditions other than schizophrenia. Therefore, it is crucial to educate non-specialist physicians about the indications, efficacy, and side effects of antipsychotics, as they account for the majority of antipsychotic prescriptions.

title: Structural basis for the activation of microtubule assembly by the EB1 and p150Glued complex.
text: Plus-end tracking proteins, such as EB1 and the dynein/dynactin complex, regulate microtubule dynamics by stabilizing microtubules through a poorly understood mechanism involving a plus-end complex at the growing ends of microtubules. In this study, we have determined the crystal structure of two components of the plus-end complex: the carboxy-terminal dimerization domain of EB1 and the microtubule binding (CAP-Gly) domain of the dynactin subunit p150Glued. Each EB1 dimer contains two helices that form a conserved four-helix bundle, while also providing binding sites for p150Glued in its flexible tail region. Using a combination of crystallography, NMR, and mutational analysis, we have identified the critical interacting elements of both EB1 and p150Glued, and found that mutations in these elements alter microtubule polymerization activity. Additionally, we discovered that removing the flexible tail from EB1 activates microtubule assembly by EB1 alone, suggesting that the flexible tail negatively regulates EB1 activity. Based on these findings, we propose that EB1 possesses an auto-inhibited conformation that is relieved by p150Glued as an allosteric activator.

title: Epigenetic regulation of NANOG by miR-302 cluster-MBD2 completes induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming.
text: Most somatic cells undergoing induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell reprogramming with Yamanaka factors reach stable partially reprogrammed stages, but the molecular mechanisms required for full reprogramming are still unknown. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate mRNA translation and are implicated in reprogramming, but the functional targets of miRNAs crucial for complete iPS cell reprogramming remain elusive. We discovered methyl-DNA binding domain protein 2 (MBD2) as an epigenetic suppressor that hinders full reprogramming of somatic cells to iPS cells by directly binding to the NANOG promoter elements and preventing transcriptional activation. When we overexpressed the miR-302 cluster, we observed a significant increase in the conversion of partial to fully reprogrammed iPS cells by suppressing MBD2 expression, thereby increasing NANOG expression. Our findings demonstrate that expressing exogenous miR-302 cluster (without miR-367) can efficiently achieve a fully reprogrammed iPS state in partially reprogrammed cells by relieving MBD2-mediated inhibition of NANOG expression. These studies provide a direct molecular mechanism for generating complete human iPS cell reprogramming, which can be used to study disease pathogenesis, drug screening, and potential cell-based therapies.

title: Complex physiology and compound stress responses during fermentation of alkali-pretreated corn stover hydrolysate by an Escherichia coli ethanologen.
text: The physiology of ethanologenic Escherichia coli grown anaerobically in alkali-pretreated plant hydrolysates is intricate and has not been extensively studied. To gain insights into how E. coli responds to these hydrolysates, we investigated an E. coli K-12 ethanologen fermenting a hydrolysate derived from corn stover pretreated with ammonia fiber expansion. Although the hydrolysate contained a high concentration of glucose (∼6% glucose, 3% xylose) and relatively low toxicity, E. coli growth ceased before glucose depletion. However, the cells remained metabolically active and continued to convert glucose to ethanol until all glucose was consumed. Gene expression profiling revealed complex and dynamic patterns of metabolic physiology and cellular stress responses during exponential growth, transition, and glycolytically active stationary phases. During exponential and transition phases, high cell maintenance and stress response costs were partially offset by available free amino acids in the hydrolysate. However, after most amino acids were depleted, cells entered stationary phase, and ATP derived from glucose fermentation was entirely consumed by cell maintenance in the hydrolysate. Comparative gene expression profiling and metabolic modeling of the ethanologen suggested that the high energetic cost of mitigating osmotic, lignotoxin, and ethanol stress collectively limits growth, sugar utilization rates, and ethanol yields in alkali-pretreated lignocellulosic hydrolysates.
