text: In an association analysis comparing cases and controls regarding allele frequencies at a highly polymorphic locus, a potential issue arises when using the conventional chi-squared test, particularly when dealing with large and sparse contingency tables. However, relying on statistical methods with known asymptotic distributions is no longer necessary, as Monte Carlo simulations can be employed to estimate the significance level of any test statistic. We have developed and evaluated a Monte Carlo method for four chi-squared test statistics, three of which involve combining alleles, on a real data set. Combining rare alleles to avoid small expected cell counts and considering each allele in turn against the rest can lead to a loss of power to detect a genuine association when the number of alleles is very large. Therefore, it is important to either not combine alleles at all or to combine them in a way that preserves the evidence for an association.

title: KLF4-dependent phenotypic modulation of smooth muscle cells has a key role in atherosclerotic plaque pathogenesis
text: Previous research on the role of smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and macrophages in the development of atherosclerosis has yielded conflicting results due to the use of unreliable methods for identifying these cell types. To address this limitation, we used a novel mouse model, Myh11-CreERT2 ROSA floxed STOP eYFP Apoe−/−, to perform SMC lineage tracing. Our findings reveal that traditional methods for detecting SMCs based on immunostaining for SMC markers fail to identify over 80% of SMC-derived cells within advanced atherosclerotic lesions. These unidentified cells exhibit characteristics of other cell lineages, including macrophages and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). Conditional knockout of Krüppel-like factor 4 (Klf4) in SMCs resulted in reduced numbers of SMC-derived MSC- and macrophage-like cells, a smaller lesion size, and improvements in plaque stability, including an increase in fibrous cap thickness compared to controls. In vivo ChIP-seq analyses and studies of cholesterol-treated cultured SMCs identified over 800 KLF4 target genes, including those that regulate pro-inflammatory responses in SMCs. Our findings suggest that the contribution of SMCs to atherosclerotic plaques has been significantly underestimated, and that KLF4-dependent transitions in SMC phenotype are crucial in lesion pathogenesis.

title: Late-life depression and microstructural abnormalities in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex white matter.
text:
Objective:
This study aimed to investigate whether microstructural abnormalities in the white matter of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are linked to late-life depression.
Methodology:
Seventeen elderly depressed individuals were compared to 16 non-depressed elderly controls. Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) was used to measure fractional anisotropy (FA) in the white matter of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex's superior and middle frontal gyri bilaterally and in the left occipital lobe as a control region. The authors controlled for age, sex, and comorbid medical disorders (hypertension and heart disease) when comparing the results between groups.
Results:
After controlling for age, sex, hypertension, and heart disease, the authors found significantly lower FA values in the right superior frontal gyrus white matter of depressed patients compared to the comparison subjects.

Conclusions:
The study found microstructural changes in the white matter of the right superior frontal gyrus to be associated with late-life depression. Further research is needed to determine how these changes contribute to depression outcomes.

title: Pioglitazone prevents tau oligomerization.
text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is primarily caused by Tau aggregation and Amyloid β protein (Aβ) deposition. However, recent studies have shown that Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activation can modulate Aβ production. To investigate whether PPARγ agonists can also prevent Tau aggregation in AD, we used a cellular model in which wild-type Tau protein (4R0N) is overexpressed (M1C cells) (Hamano et al., 2012) as well as primary neuronal cultures. Our results showed that the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone (PIO) reduced both phosphorylated and total Tau levels, and inactivated glycogen synthase kinase 3β, a major Tau kinase, associated with activation of Akt. Additionally, PIO decreased cleaved caspase3 and C-terminal truncated Tau species by caspase, which is expected to decrease Tau aggregation. A fractionation study showed that PIO reduced high molecular-weight (120 kDa), oligomeric Tau species in Tris Insoluble, sarkosyl-soluble fractions. Interestingly, the Tau decrease was reversed by adding GW9662, a PPARγ antagonist. Overall, our findings support the idea that PPARγ agonists may be useful therapeutic agents for AD.

title: Prognostic impact of the mean platelet volume/platelet count ratio in terms of survival in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
text:
Background:
Platelet volume indices, including mean platelet volume (MPV), have been recognized as markers of platelet activation and have been linked to various diseases, including malignant tumors. Recent studies have shown that MPV and MPV/platelet count (PC) ratio can predict long-term mortality in patients with ischemic cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to evaluate the contribution of platelet volume indices to survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
Patients and Methods:
We conducted a retrospective analysis of hematological indices in 268 patients with advanced NSCLC. The median age of the patients was 68 years (range: 31-87 years). We compared the hematological indices between the NSCLC group and an age- and sex-matched comparator group.
Results:

Our results showed that MPV was significantly decreased in the NSCLC group compared to the comparator group, while the PC was significantly increased in the NSCLC group. As a result, the MPV/PC ratio was also decreased in the NSCLC group. In receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis, the MPV/PC ratio was associated with a sensitivity of 62.3% and a specificity of 74.6% at a cutoff value of 0.408730 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.72492). Univariate analysis revealed that overall survival (OS) was significantly shorter in the group with a low MPV/PC ratio than in the other group (median survival time [MST]: 10.3 months vs. 14.5 months, log-rank, P=0.0245). Multivariate analysis confirmed that a low MPV/PC ratio was an independent unfavorable predictive factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.668, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.235-2.271, P=0.0008).


Conclusion:

Our findings demonstrate a close association between the MPV/PC ratio and survival in patients with advanced NSCLC. These data suggest that the MPV/PC ratio may be a useful predictive marker for survival in this patient population. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to determine the clinical implications of using the MPV/PC ratio as a predictive marker in NSCLC.

title: Traceability of biologicals: present challenges in pharmacovigilance.
text:
INTRODUCTION:
Traceability is a crucial aspect of postmarketing surveillance for biologicals, as changes in the manufacturing process can lead to unique risks associated with specific products or batches. With the growing biosimilar market, there is a need to improve the ability to trace individual products within pharmacovigilance databases.
AREAS COVERED:
This article discusses the current challenges in tracing biologicals during pharmacovigilance, including the processes involved in ensuring traceability. The authors explore the existing systems for recording exposure information in clinical practice, as well as the critical steps involved in transferring exposure data to various pharmacovigilance databases.
EXPERT OPINION:
Existing systems provide traceability of biologicals to the manufacturer within pharmacy records, but do not support routine batch recording. Upcoming changes in supply chain standards offer opportunities to systematically record detailed exposure information. However, spontaneous reporting systems are the most vulnerable link in ensuring traceability due to their manual data transfer process. To improve traceability, efforts should focus on encouraging health professionals and patients to record and report detailed exposure information in a systematic manner. Long-term solutions involve expanding accessibility to and increasing the electronic exchange of exposure data.

title: Regulation of self-ligands for activating natural killer cell receptors.
text: Natural killer (NK) cells are capable of selectively lysing infected and tumor cells while sparing healthy cells through recognition of disease-specific ligands. The recognition of these ligands by NK cells is mediated by a complex interplay of activating and inhibitory receptors. By examining the various signaling pathways involved in the expression of self-encoded ligands on NK cells and certain T cells, we may uncover novel therapeutic strategies for treating infections and cancer. Specifically, we will review the roles of NKG2D, DNAM-1, LFA-1, NKp30, NKp44, NKp46, NKp65, and NKp80 in the regulation of self-ligand expression and their potential as targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: A core Klf circuitry regulates self-renewal of embryonic stem cells
text:
Embryonic stem (ES) cells possess a remarkable ability to self-renew and maintain pluripotency, which is regulated by a complex interplay of transcription factors. Among these factors, Klf4 is a crucial reprogramming factor that, when combined with Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc, can reverse the highly differentiated state of somatic cells back to a pluripotent state. However, the maintenance of self-renewal and pluripotency of ES cells requires only Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc, while Klf4 is dispensable.
Interestingly, our study reveals that Krüppel-like factors (Klfs) are essential for the self-renewal of ES cells. Surprisingly, simultaneous depletion of Klf2, Klf4, and Klf5 leads to ES cell differentiation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation coupled to microarray assay (ChIP-seq) shows that these Klf proteins share many common targets of Nanog, suggesting a close functional relationship between these factors. Furthermore, expression analysis after triple RNA interference (RNAi) of the Klfs reveals that they regulate key pluripotency genes, such as Nanog.
Taken together, our findings provide new insights into how the core Klf circuitry integrates into the Nanog transcriptional network to specify gene expression that is unique to ES cells. This study highlights the importance of the Klf proteins in maintaining the pluripotent state of ES cells and suggests that they may be potential targets for therapeutic interventions aimed at reprogramming somatic cells into pluripotent stem cells.

title: A myeloid hypoxia-inducible factor 1α-Krüppel-like factor 2 pathway regulates gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.
text: Although gram-positive infections account for the majority of sepsis cases, the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects are poorly understood. To investigate, we examined how cell wall components of gram-positive bacteria contribute to sepsis development. Our findings indicate that gram-positive bacterial endotoxins induce hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) mRNA and protein expression in macrophages. Inoculation of live or heat-inactivated gram-positive bacteria with macrophages led to HIF-1 transcriptional activity in macrophages. Myeloid deficiency of HIF-1α attenuated gram-positive bacterial endotoxin-induced cellular motility and proinflammatory gene expression in macrophages. Conversely, gram-positive bacteria and their endotoxins reduced expression of the myeloid anti-inflammatory transcription factor Krüppel-like transcription factor 2 (KLF2). Sustained expression of KLF2 reduced and deficiency of KLF2 enhanced gram-positive endotoxins-induced HIF-1α mRNA and protein expression in macrophages. Moreover, KLF2 attenuated gram-positive endotoxins-induced cellular motility and proinflammatory gene expression in myeloid cells. Consistently, mice lacking myeloid HIF-1α were protected from gram-positive endotoxin-induced sepsis mortality and clinical symptoms, while myeloid KLF2-deficient mice were susceptible to gram-positive sepsis-induced mortality and clinical symptoms. These findings identify HIF-1α and KLF2 as critical regulators of gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.

title: Autophagy controls Salmonella infection in response to damage to the Salmonella-containing vacuole.
text: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) is a facultative intracellular pathogen that causes disease in various hosts. S. Typhimurium invades host cells and resides within a membrane-bound compartment called the Salmonella-containing vacuole (SCV). The bacteria manipulate the SCV using two independent type III secretion systems (TTSS), which damage eukaryotic cell membranes. S. Typhimurium has been suggested to damage the SCV using its Salmonella pathogenicity island (SPI)-1 encoded TTSS. During in vitro infection, we observed that this damage leads to an intracellular bacterial population targeted by the autophagy system. Approximately 20% of intracellular S. Typhimurium colocalized with the autophagy marker GFP-LC3 at 1 hour post-infection. Autophagy of S. Typhimurium was dependent on the SPI-1 TTSS and bacterial protein synthesis. Bacteria targeted by the autophagy system were often associated with ubiquitinated proteins, indicating their exposure to the cytosol. Surprisingly, these bacteria also colocalized with SCV markers. Autophagy-deficient (atg5-/-) cells were more permissive for intracellular growth by S. Typhimurium than normal cells, allowing increased bacterial growth in the cytosol. Our findings propose a model in which the host autophagy system targets bacteria in SCVs damaged by the SPI-1 TTSS. This serves to retain intracellular S. Typhimurium within vacuoles early after infection to protect the cytosol from bacterial colonization. Our findings support a role for autophagy in innate immunity and demonstrate that Salmonella infection is a powerful model to study the autophagy process.

title: PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis controls Th17 differentiation by regulating Gfi1 expression and nuclear translocation of RORγ.
text: The PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 signaling axis plays a crucial role in the activation, survival, and proliferation of CD4+ T cells upon TCR and CD28 stimulation. Our findings demonstrate that inhibition of this axis using p85α deletion, PI3K/mTORC1 inhibitors, or T cell-specific raptor deletion impairs Th17 differentiation in vitro and in vivo. These effects are mediated by the downregulation of Gfi1, a negative regulator of Th17 differentiation, and are accompanied by the induction of S6K2, a nuclear protein that binds RORγ and promotes its nuclear localization. These results highlight the central role of the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis in Th17 differentiation.

title: Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 and neuregulin 1 are required for the specification of oligodendrocytes and neurones in the zebrafish brain.
text:
Introduction:
Schizophrenia is a complex mental disorder that is believed to arise from subtle abnormalities in brain development, which may be influenced by genetic factors. Candidate susceptibility genes, such as Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 (DISC1) and Neuregulin 1 (NRG1), have been implicated in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia. To gain novel insights into the functions of DISC1 in brain development, we conducted a study using zebrafish models.
Methods:
We mapped the expression of zebrafish disc1 and characterized its role in early embryonic development using morpholino antisense methods. We also analyzed the roles of nrg1 and ErbB signaling in zebrafish brain development and observed similar defects in disc1 morphant embryos.
Results:
Our findings revealed a critical requirement for disc1 in oligodendrocyte development, promoting the specification of olig2-positive cells in the hindbrain and other brain regions. In addition, knock-down of disc1 or nrg1 caused near total loss of olig2-positive cerebellar neurons, but had no apparent effect on spinal motor neurons. These results suggest that disc1 and nrg1 function in common or related pathways controlling the development of oligodendrocytes and neurons from olig2-expressing precursor cells.
Discussion:
Our findings in the zebrafish embryo suggest that there may be unappreciated neurodevelopmental connections between key human schizophrenia susceptibility genes, such as DISC1 and NRG1. These connections could be investigated in Disc1 and Nrg1 mouse models and in genetically defined groups of patients to determine their relevance to the pathobiology of schizophrenia.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study provides novel insights into the functions of DISC1 in brain development and suggests that it may play a critical role in the development of oligodendrocytes and neurons in the brain. Further research into the connections between key schizophrenia susceptibility genes may lead to a better understanding of the pathobiology of this complex mental disorder.
GenBank accession number for Danio rerio disc1: EU273350.

title: Monoclonal antibody targeting of N-cadherin inhibits prostate cancer growth, metastasis and castration resistance
text: The shift from androgen-dependent to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is a lethal and poorly understood molecular event. By comparing gene expression in identical androgen-dependent and CRPC xenografts, we discovered a consistent increase in N-cadherin expression, which was also elevated in primary and metastatic tumors from individuals with CRPC. When we introduced N-cadherin into non-metastatic, androgen-dependent prostate cancer models, it caused castration resistance, invasion, and metastasis. We developed monoclonal antibodies targeting the extracellular domain of N-cadherin and tested their effects on prostate cancer cells in vitro. These antibodies significantly reduced cell proliferation, adhesion, and invasion. In vivo, the antibodies slowed the growth of established CRPC xenografts, blocked local invasion and metastasis, and, at higher doses, led to complete tumor regression. Treatment with N-cadherin-specific antibodies significantly delayed the emergence of castration resistance, altered tumor histology and angiogenesis, and reduced AKT serine-threonine kinase activity and serum interleukin-8 (IL-8) secretion. These findings suggest that N-cadherin is a crucial factor in both prostate cancer metastasis and castration resistance. Targeting this factor with monoclonal antibodies may have substantial clinical benefits.

title: PP2A regulates tau phosphorylation directly and also indirectly via activating GSK-3beta.
text:
Abnormal phosphorylation of tau protein has been implicated in the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Previous research suggests that a decrease in protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), the primary tau phosphatase in the human brain, contributes to tau hyperphosphorylation in AD. However, the specific effects of PP2A down-regulation on tau phosphorylation at different sites are not well understood.
In this study, we investigated the effects of PP2A dephosphorylation on tau phosphorylation at various sites in vitro. We found that PP2A dephosphorylated tau at several sites with different efficiencies, with Thr205, Thr212, Ser214, and Ser262 being the most favorable sites, and Ser199 and Ser404 being the least favorable sites. Inhibition of PP2A with okadaic acid in metabolically active rat brain slices led to inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3beta (GSK-3β) via an increase in its phosphorylation at Ser9. GSK-3β, in turn, phosphorylated tau at multiple sites, with Ser199, Thr205, and Ser396 being the most favorable sites in cells.
Our findings suggest that the combined effects of reduced tau dephosphorylation due to PP2A inhibition and reduced phosphorylation by GSK-3β due to its inhibition lead to alterations in tau phosphorylation. These changes may play a crucial role in neurofibrillary degeneration in AD. Our study provides new insights into the role of PP2A down-regulation in neurofibrillary degeneration in AD, highlighting the importance of site-specific tau phosphorylation in the progression of the disease.

title: Human artificial chromosomes containing chromosome 17 alphoid DNA maintain an active centromere in murine cells but are not stable.
text: Human artificial chromosomes (HACs) are autonomous molecules that can function and segregate like normal chromosomes in human cells. De novo HACs have been used as gene expression vectors to complement genetic deficiencies in human cultured cells, offering the possibility of studying the regulation and expression of large genes in various cell types from different tissues and correcting gene deficiencies caused by human inherited diseases. Complementary gene expression studies in mice, particularly in mouse models of human genetic diseases, are also crucial in determining if large human transgenes can be expressed appropriately from artificial chromosomes. To achieve this, we are establishing artificial chromosomes in murine cells as novel gene expression vectors. Initially, we transferred HAC vectors into murine cells but were unable to generate de novo HACs at a reasonable frequency. We then transferred HACs previously established in human HT1080 cells to three different murine cell types through microcell fusion, followed by positive selection. Our results show that the HACs in murine cells bound centromere protein C (CENP-C), a marker of active centromeres, and were detected under selection but rapidly lost their stability when selection was removed. These findings suggest that the HACs maintain at least a partially functional centromere complex in murine cells, but other factors are required for stability and segregation. Artificial chromosomes containing mouse centromeric sequences may be necessary for better stability and maintenance in murine cells.

title: How nascent phagosomes mature to become phagolysosomes.
text: Phagocytosis plays a crucial role in the removal of both apoptotic cells and microbial pathogens. Upon engulfment of a particle, a nascent phagocytic vacuole is formed, which lacks the microbicidal and degradative capabilities of mature phagosomes. These functions are acquired during the maturation process, a complex series of events involving the sequential fusion of the phagosomal vacuole with specialized endocytic and secretory compartments. This process culminates in the formation of phagolysosomes, which undergo continuous remodeling and fusion to maintain their structure and function. The molecular machinery that governs this metamorphosis is summarized here.

title: Purification and structural characterization of bovine cathelicidins, precursors of antimicrobial peptides.
text: Cathelicidins are a novel class of antimicrobial peptide precursors found in mammalian myeloid cells. These peptides are characterized by a conserved N-terminal region and a variable C-terminal antimicrobial domain. Four cathelicidins, proBac5, proBac7, prododecapeptide, and proBMAP-28, were simultaneously purified from bovine neutrophils using simple and rapid methods. Analysis of their ES-MS data revealed common features in their primary sequences, such as the presence of N-terminal 5-oxoproline (pyroglutamate) residues and two disulfide bridges in a 1-2, 3-4 arrangement. The N-terminal domains of the cathelicidins contain one or two Asp-Pro bonds, which are more susceptible to hydrolysis in some cases. An unexpected feature of prododecapeptide is its dimeric structure, formed by three possible combinations of its two isoforms. The isolation of a truncated, monomeric form of this protein revealed that dimerization occurs via disulfide bridge formation at the C-terminal domain, and the dodecapeptide is likely released as a dimer from its precursor. Sequence-based secondary structure predictions and CD results indicate that cathelicidins have a 30-50% content of extended conformation and <20% content of alpha-helical conformation, with the alpha-helical segment located near the N-terminus. Additionally, similarity searching and topology-based structure prediction suggest that the conserved N-terminal domain of cathelicidins is similar to cystatin-like domains, placing this family within the cystatin superfamily. When assessed against cathepsin L, three of the four cathelicidins showed only a weak inhibitory activity (Ki = 0.6-3 microM), unlike the potent cystatin inhibitors.

title: Tuberculosis mortality in England and Wales during 1982-1992: its association with poverty, ethnicity and AIDS.
text:
This study aims to investigate the association between contemporary tuberculosis (TB) in England and Wales and various potential risk factors. Using an ecological analysis of standardized annual TB mortality rates for 403 local authority districts between 1982 and 1992, the study examines the relationship between TB mortality and social, demographic, and ethnicity factors. Specifically, the study looks at the impact of overcrowding at the household level, poverty, and AIDS-related mortality on TB mortality rates among different age and sex groups.
The study found a strong association between TB mortality and overcrowding at the household level for both men and women. However, for women, no other factors improved the explanatory power of the models beyond overcrowding. In contrast, for younger men, both poverty and AIDS-related mortality explained additional variation in the model. The study also found that there was no significant relationship between ethnicity and TB notifications, and that the relationship between ethnicity and TB mortality was not observed once overcrowding had been accounted for.
The study's findings suggest that prolonged contact is required for disease transmission, and that it is the overcrowding and poverty among ethnic populations that are significant for their TB mortality. The study also provides evidence that AIDS has little influence on the level of TB mortality in the wider population, with the exception of the group most typical of AIDS patients. The study's explanations for the observed relationship include preferential certification, migration for treatment, and shortcomings in health care provision.

title: Noncognate interaction with MHC class II molecules is essential for maintenance of T cell metabolism to establish optimal memory CD4 T cell function.
text: CD4 memory T cells that survive in the absence of MHC class II molecules lose their characteristic memory function. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we analyzed the gene expression profiles of resting memory T cells isolated from MHC class II-competent or -deficient hosts. We focused on five transcripts related to T cell activation, metabolism, and survival that were found to be underexpressed in resting memory T cells from MHC class II-deficient hosts compared to MHC class II-competent hosts. Our analysis revealed that CD4 memory cells isolated from MHC class II-deficient hosts exhibit alterations in their degree of differentiation and metabolic activity, which are already present in the effector phase despite the presence of antigen-presenting dendritic cells. Our findings suggest that the absence of interactions with noncognate MHC class II molecules compromises the accumulation of signals necessary for optimal survival and fitness, leading to impaired metabolic activity and functional capacity of activated T cells. These signals, which may involve AKT-mediated coordination of survival and metabolic pathways, are critical for the successful generation of a long-lived functional memory CD4 T cell population.

title: The kinase TAK1 integrates antigen and cytokine receptor signaling for T cell development, survival and function
text: The tyrosine kinase TAK1 plays a crucial role in both innate and B cell immunity, but its function in T cells is not well understood. To investigate, we deleted the gene encoding TAK1 specifically in T cells and observed that it resulted in a reduction in the development of thymocytes, particularly regulatory T cells expressing the transcription factor Foxp3. In mature thymocytes, TAK1 was necessary for survival and activation of transcription factor NF-κB and the kinase Jnk in response to interleukin 7. In effector T cells, TAK1 was dispensable for NF-κB activation and cytokine production, but important for proliferation and p38 kinase activation in response to interleukins 2, 7, and 15. These findings suggest that TAK1 is essential for integrating T cell receptor and cytokine signals to regulate the development, survival, and function of T cells.

title: Caregiver burden in HIV-positive and HIV-negative partners of men with AIDS.
text: This research investigates the factors associated with caregiver burden in 82 HIV-positive (HIV+) and 162 HIV-negative (HIV-) partners of men with AIDS. We hypothesized that HIV+ caregivers would experience greater burden due to the strain of their disease on their resources. Surprisingly, HIV+ caregivers actually reported higher levels of burden and were more likely to be religious or spiritual, have lower incomes, and use coping strategies such as positive reappraisal and cognitive escape-avoidance to manage their emotions. In contrast, HIV- caregivers were more likely to be healthy partners of men with AIDS. When comparing HIV+ caregivers with 61 HIV+ partners of healthy men, we found that most of the differences between the two groups were due to HIV seropositivity rather than caregiving. However, of the variables associated with HIV seropositivity, only religiosity or spirituality independently contributed to burden in HIV+ caregivers, suggesting a relatively weak link between HIV seropositivity and caregiver burden. The model explained 62% of the variance in burden in HIV+ caregivers and 36% of the variance in HIV- caregivers.

title: Renal Disease and Pregnancy
text: Pregnancy in women with various kidney diseases has significant implications for both the developing fetus and the mother's health. The kidneys and urinary tract undergo adaptations during pregnancy, leading to anatomical, hemodynamic, and endocrine changes. Failure to adapt can exacerbate preexisting maternal disease and create an unfavorable environment for fetal development, increasing the risk of obstetric complications. Accurate interpretation of renal functional tests is crucial for modern obstetricians to avoid misdiagnosis of renal disease, while simultaneously detecting any underlying pathology that could worsen the mother's and baby's condition. Advances in renal pathophysiology during pregnancy have enabled pregnant women to anticipate a positive outcome, including those with renal transplants. The concept of multidisciplinary teamwork is now emphasized, with nephrologists playing a vital role as key players in the team. Obstetricians should refer pregnant women for routine check-ups of their renal status in the second or early third trimester, alongside standard blood and urine tests. Nephrologists and urologists should be involved in the management of severe medical conditions, such as preeclampsia, acute and chronic renal failure, and dialysis or renal transplant management. Pregnancy can encounter various renal diseases, some existing before pregnancy and others directly influenced by it. This chapter will provide a basic evaluation of renal status to better understand acute and chronic renal disorders during pregnancy. It will focus on the most common preexisting diseases in pregnancy, including chronic glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies (chronic pyelonephritis, renal tuberculosis), diabetes nephropathy, and unique surgical kidney. Additionally, the chapter will discuss the management of dialysis in pregnancy and pregnant women with renal transplants.

title: Integrin beta1-mediated matrix assembly and signaling are critical for the normal development and function of the kidney glomerulus.
text:
The human kidneys filter approximately 180 liters of blood every day through a complex network of tiny blood vessels called glomeruli. Within these glomeruli, there are approximately 2.5 million tiny structures called glomerular filtration apparatus, which are responsible for filtering waste products and excess fluids from the blood. The glomerular filtration apparatus is composed of three layers: the fenestrated endothelium, the specialized extracellular matrix known as the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), and the podocyte foot processes with their modified adherens junctions called the slit diaphragm (SD).
In this study, we investigated the role of podocyte beta1 integrin signaling in maintaining normal glomerular function. We used mice that lacked the integrin beta1 protein (podocin-Cre beta1-fl/fl mice) and observed that they were born normal but could not complete their postnatal renal development. These mice exhibited detectable proteinuria (excess protein in the urine) from an early age and died within a week.
We also generated mice that were deficient in the ILK protein (podocin-Cre ILK-fl/fl mice), which is a downstream mediator of integrin beta1 activity in epithelial cells. These mice developed normally but exhibited postnatal proteinuria at birth and died within 15 weeks of age due to renal failure.
Our findings suggest that podocyte beta1 integrin and ILK signaling are essential for the proper development and function of the glomerular filtration apparatus after birth. Without these signals, the glomeruli are unable to filter waste products and excess fluids from the blood effectively, leading to proteinuria and ultimately renal failure.

title: The Aging Epigenome.
text: As we age, the mechanisms that normally maintain our health and stress resistance gradually deteriorate, leading to a decline in physical and mental function, frailty, and ultimately death. While the exact timeline and causes of this decline are still unclear, research suggests that changes in transcriptional networks and chromatin state play a central role. These epigenomic changes are not only observed during aging but also significantly impact cellular function and stress resistance, contributing to the progression of aging. We propose that the dysregulation of transcriptional and chromatin networks is a fundamental component of aging. Uncovering the age-dependent epigenomic changes will provide crucial insights into how aging begins and progresses, and may lead to the development of new therapies that delay or even reverse aging and age-related diseases.

title: Cancer chemoprevention: Much has been done, but there is still much to do. State of the art and possible new approaches.
text: Over the past three decades, significant progress has been made in the search for effective cancer chemoprevention strategies. Advances in our understanding of the complex process of cellular transformation from normal to cancer cells have enabled the development of interventions aimed at modifying lifestyle habits, using natural compounds or drugs to block or reverse this process. Noteworthy successes have been achieved, particularly in the areas of breast and colorectal cancer. However, despite these achievements, these strategies have yet to be widely adopted in clinical practice. This article aims to highlight the accomplishments, challenges, and future directions necessary to enhance the efficacy and applicability of chemoprevention strategies. Key elements to be addressed include education and training for physicians to properly disseminate the goals and cultural shift of chemoprevention, improving the risk-benefit ratio by identifying minimal effective doses and intermittent schedules, developing more personalized interventions based on individual characteristics, and containing costs of public and private health prevention programs.

title: Secreted Frizzled-related Protein 5 Diminishes Cardiac Inflammation and Protects the Heart from Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury.
text: Wnt signaling has diverse effects on cardiovascular development and disease processes. The secreted frizzled-related protein 5 (Sfrp5) acts as an extracellular inhibitor of non-canonical Wnt signaling, with high levels of expression in white adipose tissue. This study aimed to investigate the role of Sfrp5 in the heart under ischemic stress. Sfrp5-knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice were subjected to ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). While Sfrp5-KO mice showed no noticeable baseline phenotype compared to WT controls, they exhibited larger infarct sizes, enhanced cardiac myocyte apoptosis, and diminished cardiac function following I/R. The ischemic lesions in Sfrp5-KO mice had greater infiltration of Wnt5a-positive macrophages and increased inflammatory cytokine and chemokine gene expression compared to WT mice. In bone marrow-derived macrophages, Wnt5a activated JNK and increased inflammatory gene expression, while treatment with Sfrp5 blocked these effects. These findings suggest that Sfrp5 functions to antagonize inflammatory responses after I/R in the heart, possibly through a non-canonical Wnt5a/JNK signaling mechanism.

title: Asymptomatic spinal cord lesions predict disease progression in radiologically isolated syndrome.
text: Background: Advances in neuroimaging technology have led to the discovery of incidental abnormalities in the central nervous system (CNS) in patients undergoing imaging for unrelated reasons. Asymptomatic spinal cord lesions are periodically identified in these patients. Objective: To determine if the presence of asymptomatic spinal cord lesions is associated with clinical progression in patients with radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS). Methods: A retrospective review of RIS cases at the University of California, San Francisco Multiple Sclerosis Center was conducted. The presence of asymptomatic cervical spinal cord lesions was analyzed as a potential predictor of clinical progression. Results: Twenty-five of 71 subjects with RIS were found to have suggestive demyelinating disease in their cervical spine. Of these, 21 (84%) progressed clinically to either clinically isolated syndrome (n = 19) or primary progressive multiple sclerosis (n = 2) over a median time of 1.6 years from the date of RIS identification (interquartile range 0.8-3.8). The sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value of an asymptomatic spinal cord lesion for subsequent development of either a first demyelinating attack or primary progressive MS were 87.5%, 91.5%, and 84%, respectively. The odds ratio of clinical progression was 75.3 (95% confidence interval 16.1-350.0, p < 0.0001), which remained significant after adjusting for potential confounders. Conclusion: These findings suggest that the presence of asymptomatic spinal cord lesions significantly increases the risk of clinical conversion to either an acute or progressive event in patients with RIS, independent of brain lesions on MRI.

title: YqhC regulates transcription of the adjacent Escherichia coli genes yqhD and dkgA that are involved in furfural tolerance
text: Previous studies have shown that silencing the adjacent genes encoding NADPH-dependent furfural oxidoreductases (yqhD dkgA) in E. coli strain EMFR9 leads to increased tolerance to furfural. According to a recent study, this silencing is now believed to result from the spontaneous insertion of an IS10 element into the coding region of yqhC, an upstream gene. YqhC shares homology with transcriptional regulators from the AraC/XylS family and was found to positively regulate the adjacent operon encoding YqhD and DkgA. Regulation was demonstrated through chromosomal deletion of yqhC, a firefly luciferase reporter plasmid for yqhC, and direct comparison of furfural resistance and NADPH-dependent furfural reductase activity. Related bacteria, such as E. coli LY180, contain yqhC, yqhD, and dkgA orthologs in the same arrangement as in E. coli EMFR9. Additionally, orthologs of yqhC are present in more distantly related Gram-negative bacteria. Disrupting yqhC provides a useful means of increasing furfural tolerance in bacteria.

title: A direct role for Met endocytosis in tumorigenesis
text: Recent research has highlighted the significance of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) endocytosis compartmentalization in determining various cellular functions. Using tumor-associated Met-activating mutations, we have demonstrated a direct relationship between endocytosis and tumorigenicity. Met mutants exhibit enhanced endocytosis/recycling activity and reduced degradation levels, leading to accumulation on endosomes, activation of the GTPase Rac1, loss of actin stress fibers, and increased cell migration. Inhibition of endocytosis in these mutants resulted in decreased anchorage-independent growth, in vivo tumorigenesis, and metastasis, while maintaining their activation. Interestingly, one resistant mutant to inhibition by a Met-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitor was sensitive to endocytosis inhibition, suggesting that altered endocytic trafficking may play a crucial role in RTK-dependent tumorigenesis. Our findings underscore the importance of endosomal signaling in regulating RTK-mediated tumorigenesis.

title: Immediate effects of droperidol
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the given text:
The subjective and behavioral responses of 20 healthy volunteers who took droperidol 5 mg as part of a cognitive challenge program were documented. All participants experienced some form of akathisia, with half feeling dysphoric. However, the dysphoria was not uniform and was influenced by various factors, resulting in a range of other effects, including sedation, dissociative experiences, alterations in sensation, and subtle changes in facial expressions. The duration of these effects varied from a few hours to over a week. In the acute phase, participants' insight into the origin of their experiences was mixed. The findings have implications for the interpretation of cognitive challenge tests, the nature of akathisia, clinical therapeutics, and drug development. © 1998 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

title: Toxicity of Nerium oleander in the monkey (Cebus apella).
text: In this study, the toxic effects of Nerium oleander were investigated in capuchin monkeys (Cebus apella) using clinical signs, hematological and serum chemical parameters, and gross and microscopic lesions. The study used dried and ground oleander leaves given to the monkeys at intervals of 48 hours in doses of 30, 7.5, and 3 mg/kg body weight. The lethal dose range for monkeys given doses of 30 and 7.5 mg/kg body weight was found to be between 30 and 60 mg/kg body weight, while monkeys given a dose of 3 mg/kg body weight (total cumulative dose: 60 mg/kg) survived. Clinical signs included vomiting, salivation, polyuria, bradycardia, vaginal hemorrhage, abortion, anorexia, constipation, loss of body weight, narcosis, restlessness, weakness, and rapid and shallow respirations. Changes in blood values included leukocytosis, neutrophilia, increased potassium, glutamic-oxalacetic transaminase, glutamic-pyruvic transaminase, blood urea nitrogen, and α-globulins; reticulo-cytopenia; and decreased calcium, glucose, total serum protein, albumin, γ-globulin levels, and hematocrit. These findings suggest that Nerium oleander can have severe toxic effects on capuchin monkeys, even at low doses.

title: Plzf regulates limb and axial skeletal patterning
text: The protein Plzf, encoded by the Zfp145 gene, belongs to the POZ/zinc-finger family of transcription factors. In this study, we generate Zfp145-deficient mice and demonstrate that Plzf is essential for proper patterning of the limb and axial skeleton. Plzf inactivation leads to defects in the patterning of all skeletal structures in the limb, including homeotic transformations of anterior skeletal elements into posterior structures. We find that Plzf acts as a growth-inhibitory and pro-apoptotic factor in the limb bud and regulates the expression of certain genes, including members of the Abdb Hox gene complex and genes encoding bone morphogenetic proteins (Bmps), in a manner independent of known patterning genes. Additionally, Zfp145-deficient mice exhibit anterior-directed homeotic transformation throughout the axial skeleton, accompanied by changes in Hox gene expression. Our findings suggest that Plzf plays a crucial role in both AP patterning of the axial and appendicular skeleton and the regulation of Hox gene expression.

title: Requirement for the ERI/DICER complex in endogenous RNA interference and sperm development in Caenorhabditis elegans.
text: Small regulatory RNAs, specifically endogenous small interfering RNAs (endo siRNAs), play a crucial role in regulating gene expression. The ERI/DICER complex, composed of ERI-1/3/5, RRF-3, and DICER, mediates endo RNAi processes in Caenorhabditis elegans. To identify additional components of the endo RNAi machinery, we conducted a genetic screen. Our screen revealed alleles of eri-9, which encodes a novel DICER-interacting protein, and a missense mutation in the helicase domain of DICER (DCR-1(G492R)). ERI-9(-) and DCR-1(G492) animals exhibit defects in endo siRNA expression and a failure to regulate mRNAs with sequence homology to these endo siRNAs, indicating that ERI-9 and the DCR-1 helicase domain are essential for the C. elegans endo RNAi pathway. We also identified a subset of Eri mutant animals (including eri-1, rrf-3, eri-3, and dcr-1, but not eri-9 or ergo-1) that exhibit temperature-sensitive, sperm-specific sterility and defects in X chromosome segregation. These mutants display multiple abnormalities in sperm development, starting with cytokinesis and continuing through terminal differentiation. These findings identify new components of the endo RNAi machinery, highlight the distinct requirements for the Eri factors in the sperm-producing germline, and begin to elucidate the functional role of the ERI/DICER complex in sperm development.

title: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia: pathogenesis, evaluation, and management.
text: Although drugs are a common trigger for acute immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in adults, the drug-induced cause is often initially overlooked. Most cases of drug-induced thrombocytopenia (DITP) are caused by drug-dependent antibodies that bind tightly to platelets via their Fab regions, but only when the drug is present. A comprehensive database of 1301 published reports detailing 317 drugs, available at www.ouhsc.edu/platelets, provides evidence for a causal link to thrombocytopenia. Typically, DITP develops 1-2 weeks after starting a new drug or suddenly after a single dose when a drug has been taken intermittently. However, severe thrombocytopenia can occur immediately after the first administration of antithrombotic agents that block fibrinogen binding to platelet GP IIb-IIIa, such as abciximab, tirofiban, and eptifibatide. Recovery from DITP usually begins within 1-2 days of stopping the drug and is typically complete within a week. Drug-dependent antibodies can persist for many years, so it is crucial to confirm the drug etiology and avoid the drug thereafter.

title: Costs and financial feasibility of malaria elimination
text: The economic benefits and drawbacks of transitioning malaria control programs from a control to an eradication goal are crucial to strategic decision-making, but empirical data is scarce. We propose a theoretical framework to evaluate the economics of eradication and analyze a key component of that framework—potential short-term to medium-term financial savings. After conducting a review that revealed a lack of existing data, we calculated the net present value of eradication in five sites and compared it with effective control. Our findings indicate that the probability of eradication being cost-saving over 50 years ranged from 0% to 42%, with only one site showing cost-savings in the base case. These results suggest that financial savings should not be the primary motivation for eradication, but that eradication may still be a worthwhile investment if total benefits outweigh marginal costs. Urgent research into these eradication benefits is necessary.

title: Expression of the angiogenic factors vascular endothelial cell growth factor, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor, tumor growth factor beta-1, platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor, placenta growth factor, and pleiotrophin in human primary breast cancer and its relation to angiogenes
text:
Angiogenesis, or the formation of new blood vessels, is a crucial process in breast cancer progression, but the underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood. In this study, we investigated the expression of multiple angiogenic polypeptides in primary human breast cancers and examined their relationship with estrogen receptor (ER) and vascular density.
We analyzed the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and its four isoforms, transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1, pleiotrophin, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor (FGF), placental growth factor, and thymidine phosphorylase (platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor) in 64 primary breast cancers using RNase protection analysis. We also measured the expression of the epidermal growth factor receptor and vascular density in these tumors.
Our results showed that all tumors expressed at least six different vascular growth factors, with VEGF being the most abundant and the transcript for the 121-amino acid form predominating. Other angiogenic factors expressed at high levels included thymidine phosphorylase and TGF-beta1. Interestingly, the expression of thymidine phosphorylase was found to be correlated with the expression of acidic FGF (P = 0.001). Similarly, TGF-beta was found to be correlated with the expression of platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (P = 0.001).
In univariate analysis, high VEGF expression was found to be associated with poor prognosis (P = 0.03), as were ER and epidermal growth factor receptor expression. Basic FGF was also found to be more highly expressed in tumors than in normal breast tissues (P = 0.01).
Our findings suggest that angiogenesis in breast cancer may involve a coordinated regulation of multiple vascular growth factors. Targeting these factors with broad-spectrum agents that block common features, such as heparin-binding activity, may be a useful approach to therapy. Inhibiting endothelial migration or directly toxic agents to the endothelium could also be effective in combination with other therapies.

title: Cnn1 inhibits the interactions between the KMN complexes of the yeast kinetochore
text: Kinetochores play a crucial role in the transmission of replicated chromosomes to daughter cells during mitosis by attaching these chromosomes to the mitotic spindle apparatus. The process of kinetochore-spindle binding and chromosome segregation is mediated by multi-copy protein complexes known as the KMN network, which consists of proteins such as KNL1Spc105, MIS12Mtw1, and NDC80Ndc80. These complexes are regulated by various kinases, including Aurora BIpl1 and MPS1Mps1, which are involved in KMN-spindle attachment. While the mechanisms underlying KMN activity during the cell cycle are not fully understood, recent studies have shed light on the role of kinetochore protein Cnn1 in promoting a functionally competent configuration of the KMN network. Cnn1 localizes to the base of the Ndc80 complex and regulates KMN activity in a spatiotemporal manner by inhibiting the interaction between its complexes. The peak activity of Cnn1 occurs in anaphase and is driven by the Cdc28, Mps1, and Ipl1 kinases.

title: Origin and functions of tissue macrophages.
text: Macrophages are dispersed throughout tissues throughout the body and play a crucial role in both homeostasis and disease. Recent research has revealed that the majority of adult tissue macrophages originate during embryonic development, rather than from circulating monocytes. Each tissue has a unique composition of embryonically derived and adult-derived macrophages, but it is unclear whether these different macrophage populations have distinct functions at steady state. This new understanding also raises questions about the role of circulating monocytes. Classical Ly6c(hi) monocytes patrol the extravascular space in resting organs, while Ly6c(lo) nonclassical monocytes patrol the vasculature. Inflammation can trigger monocytes to differentiate into macrophages, but it is unclear whether resident and newly recruited macrophages have similar functions during inflammation. Here, we discuss the tools used to identify the complex origin of tissue macrophages and the relative contributions of tissue niche and ontological origin to the regulation of macrophage functions during steady state and inflammation.

title: Treatment outcome of an unselected cohort of tuberculosis patients in relation to human immunodeficiency virus serostatus in Zomba Hospital, Malawi.
text: There is limited information available on the treatment outcomes of patients with smear-negative pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) or extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resource-limited settings. To address this gap, a prospective study was conducted in Zomba General Hospital, Malawi, to determine the treatment outcomes of an unselected cohort of TB patients. The study included 827 adult patients (451 men and 376 women) admitted between July and December 1995. The standardized treatment outcomes of treatment completion, death, default, and transfer to another district were assessed in relation to the type of TB, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) serostatus, age, and gender. The study found that 31% of the patients died by the end of treatment, with half of the deaths occurring in the first month. The death rates were highest among patients with smear-negative PTB (3.9, 95% CI 2.7-5.5) and EPTB (2.6, 95% CI 1.8-3.7) compared to smear-positive PTB patients (19%, 95% CI 14-24). The study also found that HIV-positive patients had higher death rates than HIV-negative patients (hazard ratio [HR] 2.5, 95% CI 1.6-3.8). The study highlights the need for national TB control programmes in areas of high HIV prevalence to prioritize treatment outcomes in patients with smear-negative PTB or EPTB.

title: Statin use and risk of gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy.
text: In this study, the authors aimed to investigate the association between the use of lipid-lowering medications, including statins, and the risk of developing gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy. The study used data from the UK-based General Practice Research Database and included 27,035 patients who underwent cholecystectomy and 106,531 matched controls. The authors found that current statin use, defined as 20 or more prescriptions, was associated with a decreased risk of gallstones followed by cholecystectomy, with an adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of 0.64 (95% CI: 0.59-0.70). The association remained consistent across different subgroups of patients based on age, sex, body mass index, and statin class. These findings suggest that long-term use of statins may be associated with a lower risk of gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy, which could have important implications for the prevention and treatment of this common condition.

title: Chromatin remodeling in embryonic stem cells: regulating the balance between pluripotency and differentiation.
text: Embryonic stem cells possess an extraordinary ability to self-renew, with the potential to differentiate into multiple cell lineages. These cells are pluripotent, meaning they can develop into any of the three primary germ layers: ectoderm, endoderm, and mesoderm. The maintenance of an undifferentiated state is achieved through the action of key pluripotency-specific factors, while lineage-specific factors work to promote cell specialization. In addition to these transcriptional regulators, epigenetic modifiers play a crucial role in regulating the balance between pluripotency and differentiation by altering chromatin structure.

title: The National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI) of the Republic of South Africa.
text: The South African National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG), formerly known as the National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI), was established in 1993 to provide expert advice to the National Department of Health (DoH) on matters related to vaccination. Meetings are held at least twice a year as needed, with a scope that includes vaccines, immunization, and other relevant infectious disease issues. NAGI also makes recommendations on vaccine schedules and formulations, with agendas set by the DoH and the Chairperson of NAGI. As a multidisciplinary group consisting of experts from various fields relevant to vaccines and immunization, NAGI has been a valuable resource for guiding the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in South Africa.

title: Effect of n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation in pregnancy on infants’ allergies in first year of life: randomised controlled trial
text:
Objective: To determine whether supplementing pregnant women with high-risk infants with n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCPUFA) reduces the incidence of immunoglobulin E (IgE) associated allergies in the first year of life.
Design: Follow-up of infants at high hereditary risk of allergic disease in the Docosahexaenoic Acid to Optimise Mother Infant Outcome (DOMInO) randomized controlled trial.
Setting: Adelaide, South Australia.
Participants: 706 infants at high hereditary risk of developing allergic disease whose mothers were participating in the DOMInO trial.
Interventions: The intervention group (n=368) was randomly allocated to receive fish oil capsules (providing 900 mg of n-3 LCPUFA daily) from 21 weeks' gestation until birth; the control group (n=338) received matched vegetable oil capsules without n-3 LCPUFA.
Main Outcome Measure: IgE associated allergic disease (eczema or food allergy with sensitization) at 1 year of age.
Results: No significant differences were seen in the overall percentage of infants with IgE associated allergic disease between the n-3 LCPUFA and control groups (32/368 (9%) vs 43/338 (13%); unadjusted relative risk 0.68, 95% confidence interval 0.43 to 1.05, P=0.08; adjusted relative risk 0.70, 0.45 to 1.09, P=0.12). However, the percentage of infants diagnosed as having atopic eczema (i.e., eczema with associated sensitization) was lower in the n-3 LCPUFA group (26/368 (7%) vs 39/338 (12%); unadjusted relative risk 0.61, 0.38 to 0.98, P=0.04; adjusted relative risk 0.64, 0.40 to 1.02, P=0.06). Additionally, fewer infants were sensitized to egg in the n-3 LCPUFA group (34/368 (9%) vs 52/338 (15%); unadjusted relative risk 0.61, 0.40 to 0.91, P=0.02; adjusted relative risk 0.62, 0.41 to 0.93, P=0.02), but no difference between groups in IgE associated food allergy was seen.
Conclusion: n-3 LCPUFA supplementation in pregnancy did not reduce the overall incidence of IgE associated allergies in the first year of life, although atopic eczema and egg sensitization were lower. Longer-term follow-up is needed to determine if supplementation has an effect on respiratory allergic diseases and aeroallergen sensitization in childhood.
Trial Registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12610000735055 (DOMInO trial: ACTRN12605000569606).

title: ModLoop: automated modeling of loops in protein structures.
text: ModLoop is a web-based server for automated modeling of loops in protein structures. Users can input atomic coordinates of the protein structure in Protein Data Bank (PDB) format and specify the starting and ending residues of one or more segments to be modeled, with a maximum of 20 residues in total. The server uses the loop modeling routine in MODELLER to predict the loop conformations by satisfying spatial restraints without relying on a database of known protein structures. ModLoop can run rapidly on a cluster of Linux PC computers. The server is freely accessible to academic users at <http://salilab.org/modloop>.

title: What is the best way to help caregivers in cancer and palliative care? A systematic literature review of interventions and their effectiveness.
text: Informal carers providing support to patients receiving home cancer and palliative care services often experience high levels of psychological distress and needs, yet there is a scarcity of targeted interventions to address these issues. To address this gap, a systematic review of interventions for carers of patients receiving home cancer and palliative care services was conducted. The review searched four major databases, including Medline, CancerLit, Psycinfo, and Cinahl, using the terms "carer(s)," "caregiver(s)," "palliative," and "cancer." Papers were included if they reported interventions for adults actively providing informal care for non-institutionalized cancer and palliative care patients. The review identified 22 interventions, including home nursing care (4), respite services (3), social networks and activity enhancement (2), problem-solving and education (3), and group work (10). Of these, nine interventions were targeted specifically at carers. Only six of these interventions had been evaluated, with two using a randomized controlled trial (RCT) design (grades IB), three employing a single group methodology (two prospective, grade IIIC, and one retrospective, grade IIIC), and one evaluated using facilitator feedback. The review noted a lack of outcome evaluation designs, small sample sizes, and reliance on intervention descriptions and formative evaluations. Given these methodological challenges, alternatives to RCTs may be necessary. The current evidence contributes to understanding the feasibility and acceptability of interventions, but more research is needed to determine their effectiveness. Practitioners and evaluators must prioritize the further development of intervention studies to address the psychological morbidity and needs of informal carers in cancer and palliative care.

title: Brief Internet-Based Intervention Reduces Posttraumatic Stress and Prolonged Grief in Parents after the Loss of a Child during Pregnancy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
text:
The loss of a child during pregnancy can have a profound psychological impact on women and their partners, leading to long-lasting psychiatric disorders. To address this issue, researchers compared the effectiveness of an internet-based intervention with a waiting list control group for parents who have experienced prenatal loss.
The study included 228 participants (92% female), who were randomly assigned to either the treatment group (TG) or the waiting list control (WLC) group. The TG received a 5-week cognitive behavioral intervention that included self-confrontation, cognitive restructuring, and social sharing. The intervention aimed to help participants confront their trauma, reframe their negative thoughts, and connect with others who had experienced similar losses.
The results showed that the TG had significantly lower symptoms of posttraumatic stress, prolonged grief, depression, and anxiety compared to the WLC group. Intention-to-treat analysis revealed treatment effects ranging from d = 0.84 to d = 1.02 for posttraumatic stress and prolonged grief from pre- to post-treatment time points. Additionally, significant improvement in all symptoms of PTSD and prolonged grief was found from the post-treatment evaluation to the 12-month follow-up. The attrition rate of 14% was relatively low.
The study's findings suggest that internet-based interventions can be a feasible and cost-effective treatment for parents who have experienced prenatal loss. These interventions have the potential to improve psychological support and reduce the long-term psychiatric disorders associated with this traumatic event.

title: Up-regulation of PPAR-gamma mRNA expression in the liver of obese patients: an additional reinforcing lipogenic mechanism to SREBP-1c induction.
text:
Introduction:
Triglyceride accumulation in the liver is an early hallmark of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), a multifactorial disorder that affects a significant proportion of the global population, particularly those who are obese. The underlying mechanisms of NAFLD are just beginning to be elucidated, and recent studies have implicated the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) as a key player in the development of hepatic steatosis.
Objectives:
The present study aimed to investigate the expression of PPAR-γ and sterol receptor element-binding protein 1c (SREBP-1c) in the liver of obese patients with NAFLD, as well as the relationship between these markers and insulin resistance (IR).
Methods:
We measured PPAR-γ and SREBP-1c mRNA levels in the liver of 22 obese patients with NAFLD who underwent subtotal gastrectomy with gastrojejunal anastomosis in Roux-en-Y, as well as 16 nonobese controls who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy. In addition, we determined serum levels of total adiponectin and high molecular weight (HMW) adiponectin, as well as IR using the homeostasis model assessment-IR (HOMA-IR).
Results:
Our results showed that PPAR-γ mRNA levels were significantly higher in the liver of obese patients with NAFLD compared to controls, with a 112% and 188% increase in steatosis and steatohepatitis, respectively. Concomitantly, SREBP-1c mRNA levels were also elevated, with a 70% and 62% increase in steatosis and steatohepatitis, respectively. Furthermore, PPAR-γ expression showed positive associations with SREBP-1c mRNA levels, serum insulin levels, and HOMA-IR, as well as negative correlations with total adiponectin and HMW-adiponectin levels in serum.

Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that PPAR-γ is up-regulated in the liver of obese patients with NAFLD, representing an additional lipogenic mechanism that reinforces the induction of SREBP-1c in the development of hepatic steatosis. These data provide further evidence of the complex interplay between genetic and environmental factors in the pathogenesis of NAFLD and highlight the potential role of PPAR-γ as a therapeutic target in the prevention and treatment of this common metabolic disorder.

title: Ribosomal protein S17 gene (RPS17) is mutated in Diamond-Blackfan anemia.
text: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a congenital erythroid aplasia characterized by a normochromic macrocytic anemia with a selective deficiency in red blood cell precursors in otherwise normocellular bone marrow. In approximately 40% of DBA patients, various physical anomalies are also present. Currently, two genes have been associated with the DBA phenotype: the ribosomal protein (RP) S19 mutated in 25% of DBA patients, and RPS24 mutated in approximately 1.4% of DBA patients. Our study reports the identification of a mutation in yet another ribosomal protein, RPS17. The mutation affects the translation initiation start codon, changing T to G (c.2T>G), thereby eliminating the natural start of RPS17 protein biosynthesis. RNA analysis revealed that the mutated allele was expressed, and the next downstream start codon located at position +158 should give rise to a short peptide of only four amino acids (Met-Ser-Arg-Ile). The mutation arose de novo, as all healthy family members carry wild-type alleles. The identification of a mutation in the third RP of the small ribosomal subunit in DBA patients further supports the theory that impaired translation may be the primary cause of DBA pathogenesis.

title: An overview of the effective combination therapies for the treatment of breast cancer.
text:
Breast cancer (BC) is typically classified based on the receptors overexpressed on the cell nucleus, which include hormone receptors such as progesterone (PR) and estrogen (ER), and HER2. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a type of cancer that lacks any of these three receptor proteins (ER/PR/HER2). Tumor cells exhibit drug-resistant phenotypes that reduce the effectiveness of chemotherapeutic treatments. While drug resistance often has a genetic basis, there are several mechanisms underlying it, including:
1. Efflux pumps that lower the cellular concentration of drugs
2. Alterations in membrane lipids that reduce cellular uptake of drugs
3. Increased or altered drug targets
4. Metabolic alterations of drugs
5. Inhibition of apoptosis, or programmed cell death
6. Repair of damaged DNA
7. Alteration of cell cycle checkpoints

The use of "combination therapy" is widely recognized as an effective approach to treat human diseases, particularly breast cancer. In this review, we provide examples of different nanocarriers used to co-deliver multiple therapeutics (chemotherapeutic agents and nucleic acids) to drug-resistant tumor cells. Finally, we offer our recommendations for future directions in co-delivery treatments.

title: Disturbed sleep in bipolar disorder is related to an elevation of IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.
text: Bipolar disorder is a severe mental illness characterized by recurrent changes in mood, energy, and activity levels. These changes are often accompanied by alterations in the quality, duration, and organization of sleep. Currently, there is no single theory that explains the sleep disturbances observed in individuals with bipolar disorder, and managing these changes can be challenging. However, research suggests that cytokines, such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), play a significant role in sleep regulation. Elevated levels of IL-6 have been linked to poorer sleep quality and changes in sleep architecture similar to those observed in bipolar disorder. Additionally, therapeutic administration of interferon can lead to increased levels of intrathecal IL-6, which may worsen sleep quality. Conversely, blocking IL-6 with tocilizumab in rheumatoid arthritis has been associated with improvements in sleep quality. Interestingly, individuals with bipolar disorder tend to have elevated levels of IL-6, particularly in peripheral monocytes. Based on these findings, we propose that the sleep disturbances observed in bipolar disorder are likely linked to the elevated levels of IL-6 and the resulting increased expression of mRNA coding for IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.

title: Targeted blockade of TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathways inhibits lung cancer growth promoted by bone marrow-derived myofibroblasts
text: To investigate the role of TGF-β and IL-6 in the interactions between myofibroblasts (MFs) and lung cancer cells, we used the Lewis and CTM-167 cell lines and stimulated them with IL-6, MF-conditioned medium (MF-CM), or MFs, either with or without TGF-β signaling inhibitors - SB431542 and/or JAK2/STAT3 inhibitor - JSI-124. MFs were also stimulated with TGF-β, cancer cell-conditioned medium (CCM), or cancer cells, with or without SB431542 and JSI-124. We measured cell proliferation, cytokine levels, mRNA expression, and protein production. In addition, mice bearing xenograft tumors were intraperitoneally treated with SB431542 or JSI-124 and monitored for up to 45 days. In co-culture systems, MFs produced high levels of IL-6, while cancer cells secreted high levels of TGF-β. Recombinant IL-6 and MF-CM activated STAT3 and upregulated TGF-β in cancer cells. Conversely, cancer cell-CM or TGF-β stimulated MFs to produce IL-6. Blockade of JAK2/STAT3 and TGF-β signaling by specific inhibitors significantly inhibited cell proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo of lung cancer cells. Our study demonstrated that the TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathways form a positive feedback loop that mediates the interactions between MFs and lung cancer cells. Targeted inhibition of this signaling loop could be a promising approach for lung cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Production of cloned mice and ES cells from adult somatic cells by nuclear transfer: how to improve cloning efficiency?
text:
It has been 10 years since the first cloned mammals were generated from somatic cells using nuclear transfer (NT). However, most cloned embryos still experience developmental arrest before or shortly after implantation, and the success rate for producing live offspring through cloning remains below 5%. The low success rate is believed to be due to epigenetic errors, including abnormal DNA hypermethylation, but the mechanism of "reprogramming" is unclear.
We have developed a stable NT method in mice using a piezo-actuated micromanipulator to directly inject donor nuclei into the oocyte. While only a few laboratories can produce clones from adult somatic cells in mice, cloned mice are never successfully produced from most mouse strains. However, this technique has the potential to be a valuable tool for future research in basic biology. For example, NT can be used to generate embryonic stem (NT-ES) cell lines from a patient's own somatic cells. We have shown that NT-ES cells are equivalent to ES cells derived from fertilized embryos and can be generated relatively easily from a variety of mouse genotypes and cell types of both sexes, although it may be more challenging to generate clones directly.
In general, NT-ES cell techniques are expected to be applied to regenerative medicine, but this technique can also be used to preserve the genetic resources of mouse strains instead of embryos, oocytes, and spermatozoa. This review aims to provide guidance on how to improve cloning efficiency and NT-ES cell establishment, as well as further applications.

title: Recruitment of Tat to heterochromatin protein HP1 via interaction with CTIP2 inhibits human immunodeficiency virus type 1 replication in microglial cells.
text: The Tat protein of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) plays a crucial role in inducing viral gene expression. Recently, a nuclear receptor cofactor chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor-interacting protein 2 (CTIP2) was identified as a potent inhibitor of Tat function in human microglial cells. Overexpression of CTIP2 leads to repression of HIV-1 replication by inhibiting Tat-mediated transactivation. In contrast, the related CTIP1 was unable to affect Tat function and viral replication. Using confocal microscopy, we found that overexpression of CTIP2, but not CTIP1, leads to disruption of Tat nuclear localization and recruitment of Tat within CTIP2-induced nuclear ball-like structures. Additionally, we discovered that CTIP2 colocalizes and associates with the heterochromatin-associated protein HP1alpha. The CTIP2 protein harbors two Tat and HP1 interaction interfaces, the 145-434 and the 717-813 domains. CTIP2, HP1alpha, and Tat form a three-protein complex in which the 145-434 CTIP2 domain interacts with the N-terminal region of Tat, while the 717-813 domain binds to HP1. Our findings suggest that inhibition of HIV-1 expression by CTIP2 correlates with recruitment of Tat within CTIP2-induced structures and relocalization within inactive regions of the chromatin via formation of the Tat-CTIP2-HP1alpha complex. These data reveal a novel mechanism of Tat inactivation through subnuclear relocalization, which may ultimately lead to inhibition of viral pathogenesis.

title: Cryptochrome Mediates Circadian Regulation of cAMP Signaling and Hepatic Gluconeogenesis
text:
During fasting, mammals maintain normal glucose homeostasis by stimulating hepatic gluconeogenesis through the activation of key transcriptional regulators, cAMP response element-binding protein (Creb) and dephosphorylation of the Creb-regulated transcription coactivator-2 (Crtc2). Although the underlying mechanism is not fully understood, hepatic gluconeogenesis is also regulated by the circadian clock, which coordinates glucose metabolism with changes in the external environment. The circadian clock controls gene expression through two transcriptional activators, Clock and Bmal1, which stimulate cryptochrome (Cry1 and Cry2) and Period (Per1, Per2, and Per3) repressors that feed back on Clock-Bmal1 activity.
Our study shows that Creb activity during fasting is modulated by Cry1 and Cry2, which are rhythmically expressed in the liver. Cry1 expression increases during the night-day transition, reducing fasting gluconeogenic gene expression by blocking glucagon-mediated increases in intracellular cAMP concentrations and in the protein kinase A-mediated phosphorylation of Creb. In biochemical reconstitution studies, we found that Cry1 inhibited accumulation of cAMP in response to G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation but not to forskolin, a direct activator of adenyl cyclase. Cry proteins appeared to modulate GPCR activity directly through interaction with G(s)α.
Our findings suggest that compounds that enhance cryptochrome activity may provide therapeutic benefit to individuals with type 2 diabetes, as hepatic overexpression of Cry1 lowered blood glucose concentrations and improved insulin sensitivity in insulin-resistant db/db mice.

title: Toll-like receptor 4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism in myocardial infarction: a meta-analysis of 15,148 subjects.
text: The association between the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) gene Asp299Gly (+896 A/G) polymorphism and myocardial infarction (MI) risk remains controversial. To address this, a large-scale meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the potential association between this gene variant and MI risk. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CBMdisc, CNKI, and Google Scholar yielded 9 articles involving 10 studies, which included a total of 8299 MI cases and 6849 controls. The results of the meta-analysis revealed no significant association between the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism and MI risk (G allele vs. A allele: OR=0.95, 95% CI=0.74-1.22, p=0.71; G/G vs. A/A: OR=1.03, 95% CI=0.54-1.98, p=0.93; G/G vs. A/G+A/A: OR=1.05, 95% CI=0.55-2.03, p=0.87; G/G+A/G vs. A/A: OR=0.92, 95% CI=0.75-1.13, p=0.42). Additionally, there was no significant association found in the subgroup analysis based on the source of controls. In conclusion, the present meta-analysis suggests that the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism is not associated with MI risk.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase and proinflammatory cytokine production by chondrocytes of human osteoarthritic cartilage: associations with degenerative changes.
text: Objective: To investigate the distribution of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and proinflammatory cytokines, interleukin-1beta (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα), in osteoarthritic (OA) cartilage compared to normal, age-matched articular cartilage, using immunohistochemistry. Methods: Articular cartilage samples were obtained from OA knees removed during arthroplasty and from normal, non-arthritic knees obtained at autopsy. The samples were fixed in Carnoy's fixative, processed, embedded in paraffin, sectioned, and examined by immunohistochemistry for MMP and cytokine production. In addition, human articular chondrocytes (HAC) were treated in vitro with either IL-1β, TNFα, or phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) to assess their potential to produce each of the MMPs, as determined by Western blotting and gelatin zymography. Results: Immunodetection of collagenases (MMPs 1, 8, and 13) and stromelysin 1 (MMP-3) was observed in a proportion of chondrocytes in the superficial zone of almost all OA specimens with degenerative matrix changes.
