Female migraineurs with aura were more likely to be using oral contraceptives (OR = 2.06, 95% CI = 1.05-4.06). The odds of having an elevated Framingham risk score for CHD were approximately doubled for the migraineurs with aura.
Conclusions: This study suggests that migraineurs, particularly those with aura, have a higher cardiovascular risk profile than individuals without migraine. These findings highlight the importance of monitoring cardiovascular risk factors in migraine patients and identifying strategies to reduce their risk of developing cardiovascular disease.

title: Th2-mediated host protective immunity to intestinal nematode infections.
text: Despite decades of research, there is still limited understanding of the mechanisms that govern the immune response to intestinal nematodes. Most of what is known comes from studies conducted in laboratory animals, such as mice. It is clear that when an intestinal parasite infection occurs, the immune system mounts a strong Th2-mediated response, which regulates various immune responses characteristic of helminth infections, including eosinophilia, intestinal mastocytosis, and elevated IgE production. The use of cytokine-specific monoclonal antibodies and recombinant cytokines, as well as animals with genetic disruptions in immune-related genes, have provided valuable tools for dissecting the potential effector mechanisms involved. However, the absence of a T-cell compartment in the host makes it impossible to expel the parasite, and a Th1-dominated response can compromise protective immunity almost universally. It appears that some aspect of a Th2-mediated response controls effector mechanisms, although the exact mechanisms remain unclear. While mast cells may play a role in protection through a non-specific inflammatory response, the mechanisms by which they become activated are not well understood. Studies in transgenic animals suggest that activation is not through the high-affinity receptor for IgE, and conventional interactions between effector leucocytes and antibody may not be as important as previously thought. There is little evidence to support a protective role for eosinophilia in any system, and new data suggest that other Th2 cytokines, such as IL-13, may be more important than IL-4 in mediating protection. It is likely that multiple Th2-controlled effector mechanisms, some of which may be particularly important at mucosal surfaces, remain to be explored. Overall, it is likely that the expulsion of worms is the result of a combination of multiple mechanisms, with some mechanisms being more critical for certain species of parasites than others.

title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
text:
Zebrafish fin regeneration is mediated by the formation of a blastema, a population of progenitor cells that give rise to the regenerated fin. Wnt/β-catenin signaling is crucial for the proliferation and patterning of the overlying epidermis during fin regeneration. However, our findings indicate that β-catenin signaling is not active in the epidermis or the majority of proliferative blastemal cells. Instead, tissue-specific pathway interference suggests that Wnt signaling in the nonproliferative distal blastema is required for cell proliferation in the proximal blastema, while signaling in cells lining the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation.
Our findings suggest that Wnt signaling regulates epidermal patterning, blastemal cell proliferation, and osteoblast maturation indirectly through secondary signals. Gene expression profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and functional rescue experiments indicate that Wnt/β-catenin signaling acts through Fgf and Bmp signaling to control epidermal patterning, while retinoic acid and Hedgehog signals mediate its effects on blastemal cell proliferation.
We propose that Wnt signaling orchestrates fin regeneration by defining organizing centers that instruct cellular behaviors of adjacent tissues. In conclusion, our findings provide new insights into the complex interplay of signaling pathways involved in zebrafish fin regeneration and highlight the importance of Wnt signaling in coordinating cellular behaviors during tissue regeneration.

title: The utility of cerebrospinal fluid analysis in patients with multiple sclerosis
text: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) requires ruling out other possible diagnoses. Therefore, analyzing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is crucial in patients with their first symptoms suggestive of MS. However, CSF analysis is no longer a necessary step in diagnosing relapsing-remitting MS if magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) criteria are met. Nevertheless, caution is advised when diagnosing MS in patients with negative MRI findings or without CSF analysis, as CSF investigation can help eliminate other causes of disease. The detection of oligoclonal IgG bands in CSF has potential prognostic value and can inform clinical decision-making. Moreover, CSF analysis is important for research into the pathogenesis of MS, as it has provided valuable insights into the inflammatory and neurodegenerative processes involved in the disease. Novel CSF biomarkers, although not yet validated, have been identified for MS diagnosis and monitoring disease activity, prognosis, and treatment response. This Review summarizes CSF findings that aid in differentiating MS from other conditions and highlights the potential of emerging biomarkers to advance understanding of MS pathophysiology.

title: Expression of circadian genes correlates with liver metastasis and outcomes in colorectal cancer.
text: Circadian rhythms are the daily fluctuations in various biological processes, generated by the interplay of eight core circadian genes: Period1 (Per1), Period2 (Per2), Period3 (Per3), Cryptochrome1 (Cry1), Cryptochrome2 (Cry2), Clock, Bmal1, and Casein Kinase I ε (CKIε). Recent studies have suggested that these genes may also play a role in the development and progression of cancer. To investigate this further, we conducted a study examining the correlation between circadian gene expression and clinicopathological factors, as well as outcomes, in patients with colorectal cancer. We analyzed surgical specimens of cancer tissue and adjacent normal mucosa from 202 patients with untreated colorectal cancer, measuring the relative expression levels of the circadian genes using quantitative real-time, reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction. Our results showed that the expression of the Clock gene and the CKIε gene in cancer tissue was significantly higher than in adjacent normal mucosa, while the expression of the Per1 and Per3 genes was significantly lower in cancer tissue. We also found that high expression of the Bmal1 gene and low expression of the Per1 gene were associated with liver metastasis, and that high expression of the Per2 gene was associated with better outcomes. These findings suggest that overexpression of the Bmal1 gene and reduced expression of the Per1 gene may serve as predictors of liver metastasis, while reduced expression of the Per2 gene may be a predictor of outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer.

title: The Danish prescription registries.
text: The computerization of Danish pharmacies has enabled the creation of two large prescription databases: the Odense University Pharmacoepidemiological Database (OPED) and the Pharmacoepidemiological Prescription Database of North Jutland (PDNJ). These databases contain information on the prescriptions of approximately one million people, which represents 18% of the Danish population. The databases are stable and representative of the population, covering all reimbursed medication at the individual user level. A unique personal identifier allows for the creation of longitudinal drug histories and the linking of prescription data to other population-based Danish registries. The completeness of the Danish prescription registries is excellent for reimbursed prescription drugs, and a small number of studies have shown high validity of the register information. These databases provide a valuable new resource for pharmacoepidemiological research.

title: Oridonin, a diterpenoid purified from Rabdosia rubescens, inhibits the proliferation of cells from lymphoid malignancies in association with blockade of the NF-kappa B signal pathways.
text: This study discovered that oridonin, a natural compound extracted from Rabdosia rubescens, inhibited the growth of multiple myeloma (MM) cells (U266 and RPMI8226), acute lymphoblastic T-cell leukemia (Jurkat) cells, and adult T-cell leukemia (MT-1) cells with an effective dose that inhibited 50% of target cells (ED50) ranging from 0.75 to 2.7 microg/mL. The study also found that oridonin caused apoptosis of MT-1 cells in a time-dependent manner, and down-regulated levels of Mcl-1 and BCL-x(L), but not Bcl-2 protein, in both MT-1 and RPMI8226 cells. Additionally, oridonin inhibited nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) DNA-binding activity in these cells as measured by luciferase reporter gene, ELISA-based, and electrophoretic mobility shift assays. Furthermore, oridonin blocked tumor necrosis factor-alpha- and lipopolysaccharide-stimulated NF-κB activity in Jurkat cells as well as RAW264.7 murine macrophages. Notably, oridonin decreased survival of freshly isolated adult T-cell leukemia (three samples), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (one sample), chronic lymphocytic leukemia (one sample), non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (three samples), and MM (four samples) cells from patients in association with inhibition of NF-κB DNA-binding activity. However, oridonin did not affect survival of normal lymphoid cells from healthy volunteers. Therefore, the study suggests that oridonin may be useful as an adjunctive therapy for individuals with lymphoid malignancies, including the lethal disease adult T-cell leukemia.

title: Uncertainty in integrative structural modeling.
text:
Integrative structural modeling involves the use of multiple types of input information and progresses through four stages:
1. Gathering Information: In this stage, uncertainty arises from data that are limited, noisy, ambiguous, or sourced from diverse populations.
2. Designing Model Representation and Converting Information into a Scoring Function: Uncertainty can stem from a representation that is too simplistic for the available information or a scoring function that does not accurately capture the information.
3. Sampling Good-Scoring Models: The major source of uncertainty in this stage is insufficient sampling, which can lead to a biased or incomplete representation of the population.
4. Analyzing Models and Information: In the final stage, clustering, cross-validation, and other techniques are used to estimate the precision and accuracy of the models and information.

title: Moist occlusive dressing (Aquacel(®) Ag) versus moist open dressing (MEBO(®)) in the management of partial-thickness facial burns: a comparative study in Ain Shams University.
text:
INTRODUCTION:
The face is the most distinctive feature of a person, conveying emotions and feelings through facial expressions. Facial burns are a common occurrence and can have severe physical, emotional, and psychosocial consequences. Partial thickness facial burns are particularly prevalent, especially among children. This study aims to compare the effectiveness of standard moist open dressing technique and moist closed dressing technique in managing partial thickness burns of the face.
PATIENTS AND METHODS:
The study included patients with partial thickness facial burns admitted to the burn unit of Ain Shams University, Cairo, Egypt, between April 2009 and December 2009. The patients were divided into two groups: those treated with open dressing using MEBO(®) (n=20) and those treated with closed dressing using Aquacel(®) Ag (n=20). The demographic characteristics (age, gender, ethnicity, total body surface area, burn area), length of hospital stay (LOS), rate of infections, time to total healing, frequency of dressing changes, pain, cost-benefit ratio, and patient discomfort were compared between the two groups. The long-term outcome (incidence of hypertrophic scarring) was assessed up to 6 months follow-up.
RESULTS:
There were no significant differences in demographic characteristics between the two groups. The mean time for re-epithelialization was significantly shorter in the Aquacel(®) Ag group (10.5 days) compared to the MEBO(®) group (12.4 days, p<0.05). The frequency of dressing changes, pain, and patient discomfort were significantly lower in the Aquacel(®) Ag group. The cost-benefit ratio was not significantly different between the two groups. The scar quality improved in the Aquacel(®) Ag treatment group. Follow-up assessments were conducted at 3 and 6 months, and the long-term outcomes were recorded in both groups.
CONCLUSION:
The results of this study suggest that the use of moist closed dressing (Aquacel(®) Ag) significantly improves the management and healing rate of partial thickness facial burns compared to the standard moist open dressing (MEBO(®)). The improved outcomes in the Aquacel(®) Ag group include faster re-epithelialization, reduced pain and discomfort, and better long-term scar quality. These findings support the use of moist closed dressing for the management of partial thickness facial burns.

title: Feedback upregulation of HER3 (ErbB3) expression and activity attenuates antitumor effect of PI3K inhibitors.
text: In this study, we investigated the effects of an inhibitor of PI3K, XL147, on human breast cancer cell lines with constitutively activated PI3K. Treatment with XL147 resulted in dose-dependent inhibition of cell growth and levels of pAKT and pS6, which are key signaling proteins in the PI3K/AKT/TOR pathway. Interestingly, inhibition of PI3K in HER2-overexpressing cells led to the up-regulation of expression and phosphorylation of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases, including HER3. We found that knockdown of FoxO1 and FoxO3a transcription factors, which are known to regulate the expression of these receptor tyrosine kinases, suppressed the induction of HER3, InsR, IGF1R, and FGFR2 mRNAs upon inhibition of PI3K. In HER2-positive cells, knockdown of HER3 using siRNA or cotreatment with the HER2 inhibitors trastuzumab or lapatinib enhanced XL147-induced cell death and inhibition of pAKT and pS6. Trastuzumab and lapatinib also synergized with XL147 to inhibit pAKT and the growth of established BT474 xenografts. These findings suggest that PI3K antagonists may have limited clinical activity when used as single agents, but combining them with HER2/HER3 antagonists may be a more effective strategy in patients with HER2-overexpressing breast cancer.

title: Developmental RacGAP α2-Chimaerin Signaling Is a Determinant of the Morphological Features of Dendritic Spines in Adulthood.
text: The morphological characteristics of dendritic spines are believed to play a crucial role in cognitive function, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying the fine-tuning of spine morphology during development are not fully understood. Moreover, it remains unclear whether these developmental mechanisms contribute to the normal adult spine morphological features. To address these questions, we investigated the involvement of α2-isoform of Rac-specific GTPase-activating protein α-chimaerin (α2-chimaerin) in spine morphological refinement during late postnatal development. Using a series of mice with global and conditional knock-out (KO) of α-chimaerin isoforms (α1-chimaerin and α2-chimaerin), we found that disruption of α2-chimaerin leads to an increase in the size (and density) of spines in the hippocampus. In contrast, overexpression of α2-chimaerin in developing hippocampal neurons results in a decrease in spine size. Furthermore, we showed that disruption of α2-chimaerin suppresses EphA-mediated spine morphogenesis in cultured developing hippocampal neurons. Interestingly, disruption of α2-chimaerin that begins during the juvenile stage leads to an increased size of spines in the hippocampus, while spine morphologies are unaltered when α2-chimaerin is deleted only in adulthood. These findings suggest that α2-chimaerin signaling during late postnatal development contributes to the determination of the morphological features of adult spines and the establishment of normal cognitive ability. Our results provide compelling evidence for the involvement of α2-chimaerin in spine morphological refinement and suggest that disruptions in this process may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying spine morphogenesis and their contribution to cognitive function.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of amitriptylinoxide in the treatment of chronic tension-type headache: a multi-centre controlled study.
text: In a double-blind, parallel-group trial involving 197 patients with chronic tension-type headache, the efficacy and tolerability of 60-90 mg amitriptyline hydrochloride (AO) were compared to 50-75 mg amitriptyline (AM) and placebo (PL). The primary study endpoint was a reduction of at least 50% in the product of headache duration and frequency, and a reduction of at least 50% in headache intensity. The results showed that there was no significant difference between the three groups in terms of the primary study endpoint. Treatment response occurred in 30.3% of the AO group, 22.4% of the AM group, and 21.9% of the PL group. A reduction in headache duration and frequency of at least 50% was found in 39.4% of the AO group, 25.4% of the AM group, and 26.6% of the PL group. Additionally, a reduction in headache intensity of at least 50% was found in 31.8% of the AO group, 26.9% of the AM group, and 26.6% of the PL group. Trend analysis revealed a superior effect of AO in reducing headache intensity and the product of headache duration and frequency. The results suggest that amitriptyline hydrochloride is the medication of first choice in the treatment of chronic tension-type headache.

title: Downregulation of Superoxide Dismutase Activity and Gene Expression in Cultured Rat Brain Astrocytes after Incubation with Vitamin C
text: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) have been linked to neurodegenerative changes in the central nervous system (CNS). Epidemiological studies have shown that supplementation with antioxidants can have a beneficial effect on these changes. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) is an endogenous enzyme that can scavenge ROS. This study investigated the effect of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) supplementation on SOD activity and gene expression in cultured neurological cells. Rat brain astrocytes (RBA-1 cells) were incubated with vitamin C at concentrations of 40, 80, and 160 µmol/l for 2 and 7 days. After incubation, SOD activity, SOD mRNA levels, and SOD protein amounts were measured. The results showed that short-term (2 days) and long-term (7 days) incubation with vitamin C resulted in a decrease in SOD activity in a concentration-dependent manner. Specifically, the activity of Mn-SOD decreased from 14.8 ± 1.2 to 13.2 ± 0.5 U/mg protein and Cu/Zn-SOD decreased from 64.8 ± 1.2 to 51.7 ± 0.9 U/mg protein. Additionally, vitamin C attenuated the mRNA level of Mn-SOD from 100 to 86.3 ± 6.7% and Cu/Zn-SOD from 100 to 84.7 ± 4.8%. These findings suggest that incubation with relatively high concentrations of vitamin C for 2 and 7 days may downregulate the activity and gene expression of SOD in cultured RBA-1 cells.

title: Lateral Hypothalamic Area Glutamatergic Neurons and Their Projections to the Lateral Habenula Regulate Feeding and Reward.
text:
Introduction:
The global obesity epidemic has been linked to the overconsumption of highly palatable, calorically dense foods. However, the neural circuits that regulate hedonic feeding remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the role of lateral hypothalamic area (LHA) glutamatergic neurons and their projections to the lateral habenula (LHb) in regulating feeding behavior.
Methods:
We used genetic ablation to examine the effect of LHA glutamatergic neuron loss on feeding behavior in mice. We also used optogenetic techniques to selectively stimulate or inhibit the LHA-LHb circuit in vivo.
Results:
Our results show that LHA glutamatergic neurons play a critical role in regulating feeding behavior. Genetic ablation of these neurons led to increased daily caloric intake and weight gain in mice with access to a high-fat diet. Optogenetic stimulation of the LHA-LHb circuit resulted in increased firing of LHb neurons, while inhibition of this circuit produced a real-time place preference. Furthermore, optogenetic inhibition of the LHA-LHb circuit acutely increased the consumption of a palatable liquid caloric reward.
Discussion:
Our findings demonstrate that LHA glutamatergic neurons are well situated to bidirectionally regulate feeding behavior via their functional circuit connectivity with the LHb and potentially other brain regions. These results provide new insights into the neural circuits that underlie feeding behavior and have important implications for the development of novel treatments for obesity.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study provides the first characterization of the functional connectivity and behavioral relevance of the LHA-LHb circuit within the context of feeding and reward-related behavior. These findings highlight the critical role of LHA glutamatergic neurons in regulating feeding behavior and suggest new avenues for the treatment of obesity.

title: Glucose Metabolism Inhibits Apoptosis in Neurons and Cancer Cells by Redox Inactivation of Cytochrome c
text: Neurons and cancer cells exhibit an unusual reliance on glucose, yet the underlying reason for this adaptation remains unclear. These two seemingly unrelated cell types also display an enhanced regulation of the apoptotic pathway, allowing them to survive for extended periods. Our research reveals that both neurons and cancer cells tightly restrict cytochrome c-mediated apoptosis through a mechanism that depends on glucose metabolism. We found that the pro-apoptotic activity of cytochrome c is influenced by its redox state, and that increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) following an apoptotic insult lead to the oxidation and activation of cytochrome c. In healthy neurons and cancer cells, cytochrome c is reduced and inactivated by intracellular glutathione (GSH), generated as a result of glucose metabolism through the pentose phosphate pathway. These findings uncover a striking similarity in apoptosis regulation between neurons and cancer cells and provide insight into the adaptive advantage offered by the Warburg effect for cancer cell evasion of apoptosis and for long-term neuronal survival.

title: mTORC2 Regulates Amino Acid Metabolism in Cancer by Phosphorylation of the Cystine-Glutamate Antiporter xCT.
text: Mutations in cancer cells lead to a reprogramming of amino acid metabolism, which in turn promotes tumor growth. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To investigate these mechanisms, we employed an unbiased proteomic screen, which identified mTORC2 as a critical regulator of amino acid metabolism in cancer. Specifically, we found that mTORC2 phosphorylates the cystine-glutamate antiporter xCT at serine 26 in the cytosolic N-terminus, thereby inhibiting its activity. Inhibition of mTORC2 or mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) kinase activity leads to increased glutamate secretion, cystine uptake, and incorporation into glutathione. These findings reveal an unexpected mechanism by which cancer cells adapt to changing environmental conditions through amino acid uptake and utilization, which is linked to growth factor receptor signaling.

title: Bayesian models leveraging bioactivity and cytotoxicity information for drug discovery.
text: Identifying unique leads in drug discovery is a daunting task, particularly in neglected diseases such as tuberculosis. To address this challenge, we have leveraged public high-throughput screening (HTS) data to validate a virtual screening approach using Bayesian models. We employed two models: a single-event model built with bioactivity information and a dual-event model that incorporates both bioactivity and cytotoxicity information. By virtually screening a commercial library, we experimentally confirmed active compounds with hit rates significantly higher than typical HTS results. This initial dual-event Bayesian model identified compounds with antitubercular whole-cell activity and low mammalian cell cytotoxicity from a published set of antimalarials. The most potent hit demonstrated both in vitro activity and in vitro/in vivo safety profiles comparable to those of a drug lead. These Bayesian models offer substantial time and cost savings in drug discovery.

title: A role for interleukin-1β in determining the lineage fate of embryonic rat hippocampal neural precursor cells.
text:
Neurogenesis occurs in the hippocampus of both developing and adult brains due to the presence of multipotent stem cells and restricted precursor cells at different stages of differentiation. The potential benefit of these cells for use in cell transplantation approaches for neurodegenerative disorders and trauma has been proposed. However, prolonged release of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) from activated microglia has a detrimental effect on hippocampal neurons and is implicated in the impaired neurogenesis and cognitive dysfunction associated with aging, Alzheimer's disease, and depression.
This study investigated the effect of IL-1β on the proliferation and differentiation of embryonic rat hippocampal neural progenitor cells (NPCs) in vitro. Our findings revealed that IL-1R1 is expressed on proliferating NPCs, and IL-1β treatment decreased cell proliferation and neurosphere growth. When NPCs were differentiated in the presence of IL-1β, a significant reduction in the percentages of newly born neurons and post-mitotic neurons and a significant increase in the percentage of astrocytes were observed in these cultures. These effects were attenuated by IL-1 receptor antagonist.
These results demonstrate that IL-1β exerts an anti-proliferative, anti-neurogenic, and pro-gliogenic effect on embryonic hippocampal NPCs, which is mediated by IL-1R1. The present findings highlight the detrimental consequences of an inflammatory environment during NPC development and suggest that strategies to inhibit IL-1β signaling may be necessary to facilitate effective cell transplantation approaches or in conditions where endogenous hippocampal neurogenesis is impaired.

title: Bone disease in pediatric patients undergoing dialysis with CAPD or CCPD.
text:
The histological features of renal osteodystrophy and the prevalence of bone aluminum deposition in children undergoing regular dialysis have not been previously described. In this study, 44 pediatric patients undergoing continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD) or cycling peritoneal dialysis (CCPD) had bone biopsies and deferoxamine (DFO) infusion tests. All patients were receiving oral calcitriol. The study found that:
* Osteitis fibrosa (OF) was present in 39% of patients, mild lesions (M) in 25%, normal histology (NH) in 16%, aplastic lesions (AP) in 11%, and osteomalacia (OM) in 9%.
* Bone surface aluminum (SA) was present by histochemical staining in 10 out of 20 patients given aluminum-containing phosphate-binding agents and in 0 of 24 treated with calcium carbonate (chi 2 = 15.5, P less than 0.0001).
* Serum biochemistries and DFO infusion tests failed to predict bone histology, but plasma aluminum levels were markedly elevated and bone aluminum content was highest in patients with OM.
* Bone formation rate (BFR) correlated with serum parathyroid hormone (PTH), r = 0.55, P less than 0.001; BFR was inversely related to bone aluminum content (r = -0.42, P less than 0.01), even in patients with OF (r = -0.66, P less than 0.05).
* All patients with SA greater than 30% had normal or reduced BFR when compared to those with SA less than 30%; chi 2 = 12.2, P less than 0.005.
* Based on SA greater than 30%, six patients were classified as aluminum-related bone disease: three OM, one AP, and two NH.
* Two-thirds of pediatric patients undergoing CAPD/CCPD have persistent hyperparathyroidism despite treatment with calcitriol, but aluminum can adversely affect BFR when SA exceeds 30% regardless of histologic lesion or serum PTH level.
In summary, this study found that bone aluminum deposition is a common feature in children undergoing regular dialysis, and that bone formation rate is adversely affected by high levels of bone aluminum, regardless of the histological lesion or serum parathyroid hormone level.

title: Disruption of the immune-checkpoint VISTA gene imparts a proinflammatory phenotype with predisposition to the development of autoimmunity.
text: The VISTA protein, a negative checkpoint regulator, suppresses T-cell activation and immune responses. Previous studies using a VISTA-neutralizing antibody showed that blocking VISTA enhances T-cell activation. This study investigates the effects of deleting the VISTA gene in mice. Young mice lacking VISTA appear to have normal hematopoiesis, but exhibit an accumulation of spontaneously activated T cells, accompanied by the production of various inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Enhanced T-cell responsiveness was also observed after immunization with a neoantigen. Interestingly, aged VISTA-deficient mice did not develop systemic or organ-specific autoimmune diseases despite the presence of chronic inflammation. Interbreeding of VISTA-deficient mice with 2D2 T-cell receptor transgenic mice, which are prone to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, significantly increased disease incidence and severity. The enhanced disease was associated with increased activation of encephalitogenic T cells in the periphery and infiltration into the central nervous system. Overall, these findings suggest that VISTA functions as a negative checkpoint regulator, and its loss of function lowers the threshold for T-cell activation, leading to an increased proinflammatory phenotype and higher frequency and intensity of autoimmunity in susceptible individuals.

title: Molecular mechanisms that funnel RNA precursors into endogenous small-interfering RNA and microRNA biogenesis pathways in Drosophila.
text:
In the fruit fly Drosophila, three types of endogenous small RNAs - microRNAs (miRNAs), PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), and endogenous small-interfering RNAs (endo-siRNAs or esiRNAs) - function as triggers in RNA silencing. Although piRNAs are produced independently of Dicer, the enzyme responsible for processing miRNAs and esiRNAs, the biogenesis pathways for these small RNAs require Dicer1 and Dicer2, respectively. Recent studies have shown that two isoforms of the Loquacious protein, Loqs-PB and Loqs-PD, are involved in the processing of miRNAs and esiRNAs, respectively. However, the mechanisms by which these isoforms function in their respective small RNA biogenesis pathways remain unclear.
Our study reveals that Loqs-PD associates specifically with Dicer2 through its C-terminal domain. The Dicer2-Loqs-PD complex contains another known Dicer2 partner, R2D2, and excises both exogenous siRNAs and esiRNAs from their corresponding precursors in vitro. Interestingly, Loqs-PD, but not R2D2, enhances Dicer2 activity. The Dicer2-Loqs-PD complex processes esiRNA precursor hairpins with long stems, resulting in the production of AGO2-associated small RNAs. Notably, small RNAs derived from terminal hairpins of esiRNA precursors are loaded onto AGO1, suggesting that they are a new subset of miRNAs. These findings suggest that the precursor RNA structure determines the biogenesis mechanism of esiRNAs and miRNAs, with hairpin structures with long stems serving as intermediates in the evolution of Drosophila miRNA.

title: Neutralizing antibody responses in acute human immunodeficiency virus type 1 subtype C infection.
text: The investigation of the evolution and specificities of neutralizing antibodies during the course of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection may lead to the discovery of potential targets for vaccine design. In this study, we examined the autologous and heterologous neutralization responses of 14 HIV-1 subtype C-infected individuals, using envelope clones obtained within the first 2 months post-infection. Our findings reveal that potent but relatively strain-specific neutralizing antibodies develop within 3 to 12 months of HIV-1 infection. The magnitude of this response was associated with shorter V1-to-V5 envelope lengths and fewer glycosylation sites, particularly in the V1-V2 region. Antibodies against membrane-proximal external region (MPER) were detected in 4 of 14 individuals within a year of infection, while antibodies to CD4-induced (CD4i) epitopes developed to high titers in 12 participants, in most cases before the development of autologous neutralizing antibodies. However, neither MPER nor CD4i antibody specificity conferred neutralization breadth. These findings provide insights into the kinetics, potency, breadth, and epitope specificity of neutralizing antibody responses in acute HIV-1 subtype C infection.

title: The cell cycle in polyploid megakaryocytes is associated with reduced activity of cyclin B1-dependent cdc2 kinase.
text: The megakaryocyte precursor undergoes endomitosis, a process of DNA replication without cell division, resulting in polyploidy. We used a megakaryocytic cell line, MegT, derived from transgenic mice expressing temperature-sensitive simian virus 40 large T antigen, to investigate the mechanisms of endomitosis. Our findings reveal that endomitosis consists of a series of S phases interrupted by gaps, rather than a continuous phase of DNA synthesis. Upon inactivation of large T antigen, the cells shift from a mitotic cell cycle to an endomitotic cell cycle characterized by elevated levels of G1/S cyclins, cyclin A and cyclin D3, but reduced levels of mitotic cyclin, cyclin B1. In contrast, immortalized fibroblasts lacking cyclin B1 do not display reduced levels of this protein upon shifting to high temperatures, indicating that reduced cyclin B1 is a specific property of megakaryocytes. Our results suggest that cellular programming during endoreduplication in megakaryocytes is associated with decreased levels of cyclin B1.

title: Ghrelin secretion stimulated by {beta}1-adrenergic receptors in cultured ghrelinoma cells and in fasted mice.
text: Ghrelin, an octanoylated peptide hormone produced in the stomach, experiences a dramatic increase in plasma levels during chronic severe calorie deprivation, a crucial mechanism for survival. Despite its importance, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. To investigate the regulation of ghrelin secretion, we studied ghrelin-producing cells derived from mice harboring ghrelinomas induced by a tissue-specific SV40 T-antigen transgene in tissue culture. Our findings revealed that these cells exhibit high levels of mRNA encoding beta(1)-adrenergic receptors. Exposure to norepinephrine or epinephrine in the culture medium significantly enhanced ghrelin secretion, which was blocked by the selective beta(1)-adrenergic antagonist atenolol. When mice were treated with reserpine to deplete adrenergic neurotransmitters from sympathetic neurons, the fasting-induced increase in plasma ghrelin was aborted. Similar results were observed following atenolol administration. Our findings suggest that ghrelin secretion during fasting is mediated by adrenergic agents released by sympathetic neurons, which act directly on beta(1) receptors on the ghrelin-producing cells of the stomach.

title: Dominance relationships between S-alleles in self-incompatible Brassica campestris L.
text: For 249 out of 276 possible pair-wise combinations of 24 S-alleles from two natural populations of Brassica campestris (from Turkey and Japan), dominance relationships were studied. Each F1 hybrid was crossed reciprocally with its parental S-homozygotes to determine dominance relationships between the pair of S-alleles it contained. The 24 S-alleles were grouped into two categories on the stigma side and three categories on the pollen side. In the stigma, codominance occurred frequently, and dominance or recessiveness appeared depending on the combination of S-alleles. In the pollen, codominance was less common, and a hierarchical pattern of dominance relationships emerged, although dominance appeared with specific S-allele combinations. Interactions among the 24 S-alleles differed between the stigma and pollen. Weakening of S-alleles was observed between 20 pairs in the pollen, but only two in the stigma. This interaction was found to be correlated with the recessiveness of S-alleles.

title: MicroRNA-203 inhibits cellular proliferation and invasion by targeting Bmi1 in non-small cell lung cancer.
text: MicroRNAs are believed to play a crucial role in regulating the progression and invasion of tumors, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the expression levels of miR-203 in NSCLC and its clinical significance have yet to be fully understood. In this study, we investigated the association between miR-203 and B-cell-specific moloney murine leukemia virus insertion site 1 (Bmi1) in NSCLC. Our findings demonstrated that miR-203 acts as a tumor suppressor by regulating the expression of Bmi1. We found that miR-203 expression levels were downregulated in NSCLC tissues, while Bmi1 expression was upregulated in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. Furthermore, we discovered that downregulating Bmi1 or enhancing miR-203 expression inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion in vitro. Additionally, a dual-luciferase reporter assay identified Bmi1 as a novel target of miR-203. Our study suggests that miR-203 functions as a tumor suppressor and may be a promising therapeutic target for NSCLC.

title: Characterization of the interaction between retinoic acid receptor/retinoid X receptor (RAR/RXR) heterodimers and transcriptional coactivators through structural and fluorescence anisotropy studies.
text: The retinoid receptors RARs and RXRs are transcription factors that regulate gene expression by recruiting coregulator complexes to specific promoters upon ligand binding. To investigate the mechanisms underlying coactivator recruitment, we determined the crystal structure of the RARβ/RXRα heterodimer complexed with a ligand and an LXXLL-containing peptide (NR box 2) derived from the nuclear receptor interaction domain (NID) of the coactivator SRC-1. Simultaneously, we measured the binding affinities of the NR box 2 peptide or the full-length NID of SRC-1 to retinoid receptors in the presence of various ligands. Our analysis of the three-dimensional structure and fluorescence data revealed that heterodimerization does not significantly affect the structure of individual subunits or their ability to interact with NR box 2. Moreover, we found that the ability of a protomer to recruit NR box 2 is not influenced by the ligand binding status of the partner receptor. In contrast, the strength of the association between the heterodimer and the full-length SRC-1 NID is dependent on the combinatorial action of RAR and RXR ligands, with the simultaneous presence of both receptor agonists being required for maximum binding affinity. We identified an LXXLL peptide-driven mechanism that generates an "aromatic clamp" that locks the RXR activation helix H12 into the transcriptionally active conformation. Additionally, we showed how variations in helix H11-ligand interactions can alter the communication pathway linking helices H11, H12, and the connecting loop L11-12 to the coactivator-binding site. Overall, our findings reveal molecular and structural features that influence the ligand-dependent interaction of the RAR/RXR heterodimer with nuclear receptor coactivators.

title: PRC2 complexes with JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 in ES cells to modulate ES cell pluripotency and somatic cell reprogramming.
text:
Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) has been implicated in the maintenance of embryonic stem (ES) cell pluripotency, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Previous studies assumed that ES cells possess PRC2 with the same subunit composition as in HeLa cells and Drosophila embryos. However, our current investigation reveals that PRC2 in mouse ES cells comprises at least three additional subunits: JARID2, MTF2, and a novel protein designated esPRC2p48. Notably, these subunits are highly expressed in mouse ES cells compared to differentiated cells.
Our findings demonstrate that knockdowns of JARID2, MTF2, or esPRC2p48 result in altered levels of PRC2-mediated histone H3K27 methylation and the expression of differentiation-associated genes in ES cells. Interestingly, co-expression of JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48, but not individual knockdowns, enhances the reprogramming of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) into induced pluripotent stem cells, while knockdown or knockout of these subunits significantly inhibits reprogramming. Moreover, we demonstrate that JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 modulate H3K27 methylation and repress lineage-associated gene expression when transduced into MEFs, and synergistically stimulate the histone methyltransferase activity of PRC2 in vitro.
Our results identify JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 as crucial regulatory subunits of PRC2 in ES cells and reveal their essential functions in modulating PRC2's activity and gene expression in both ES cells and during somatic cell reprogramming. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying pluripotency maintenance and reprogramming, and highlight the importance of considering the complex composition of chromatin-modifying complexes in stem cell biology.

title: General and abdominal adiposity and risk of death in Europe.
text:
Background: Previous studies have primarily relied on body mass index (BMI) to assess the association between adiposity and the risk of death. However, few studies have investigated whether the distribution of body fat contributes to the prediction of death.
Methods: We examined the association between BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-hip ratio with the risk of death among 359,387 participants from nine countries in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC). We used a Cox regression analysis, with age as the time variable, and stratified the models according to study center and age at recruitment, with further adjustment for educational level, smoking status, alcohol consumption, physical activity, and height.
Results: During a mean follow-up of 9.7 years, 14,723 participants died. The lowest risks of death related to BMI were observed at a BMI of 25.3 for men and 24.3 for women. After adjustment for BMI, waist circumference and waist-to-hip ratio were strongly associated with the risk of death. Among men and women in the highest quintile of waist circumference, the relative risks were 2.05 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.80 to 2.33) and 1.78 (95% CI, 1.56 to 2.04), respectively, and in the highest quintile of waist-to-hip ratio, the relative risks were 1.68 (95% CI, 1.53 to 1.84) and 1.51 (95% CI, 1.37 to 1.66), respectively. BMI remained significantly associated with the risk of death in models that included waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio (P<0.001).
Conclusions: These findings suggest that both general adiposity and abdominal adiposity are associated with the risk of death and support the use of waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio in addition to BMI in assessing the risk of death.

title: Phosphorylation of the autophagy receptor optineurin restricts Salmonella growth.
text: Selective autophagy can be mediated through receptor molecules that connect specific cargoes to the autophagosomal membrane, which is decorated with ubiquitin-like microtubule-associated protein light chain 3 (LC3) modifiers. Although several autophagy receptors have been identified, little is known about the mechanisms that control their functions in vivo. In this study, we discovered that the phosphorylation of an autophagy receptor, optineurin, promotes selective autophagy of ubiquitin-coated cytosolic Salmonella enterica. The protein kinase TANK binding kinase 1 (TBK1) phosphorylates optineurin on serine-177, enhancing the binding affinity of LC3 and accelerating the autophagic clearance of cytosolic Salmonella. Conversely, mutants of optineurin that bind ubiquitin or LC3, or the silencing of optineurin or TBK1, impair Salmonella autophagy, leading to increased intracellular bacterial proliferation. We propose that the phosphorylation of autophagy receptors may serve as a general mechanism for regulating cargo-selective autophagy.

title: PKD1 Inhibits AMPKα2 through Phosphorylation of Serine 491 and Impairs Insulin Signaling in Skeletal Muscle Cells.
text:
AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is an energy-sensing enzyme whose activity is suppressed in conditions of insulin resistance. Recent studies have shown that exposure to high glucose concentrations leads to increased phosphorylation of AMPK at Ser(485/491) of its α1/α2 subunit, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Our investigation aimed to determine whether protein kinase C (PKC) or protein kinase D1 (PKD1) are involved in the inhibition of AMPK by phosphorylating Ser(485/491) in skeletal muscle cells.
We used C2C12 myotubes and treated them with the PKC/D1 activator phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), which mimics diacylglycerol (DAG) and activates PKC and PKD1. Our results showed that PMA caused dose- and time-dependent increases in AMPK Ser(485/491) phosphorylation, which was associated with a ∼60% decrease in AMPKα2 activity. We found that expression of a phosphodefective AMPKα2 mutant (S491A) prevented the PMA-induced reduction in AMPK activity. Inhibition of Serine phosphorylation and AMPK activity by PMA was partially prevented by the broad PKC inhibitor Gö6983 and fully prevented by the specific PKD1 inhibitor CRT0066101. Additionally, genetic knockdown of PKD1 also prevented Ser(485/491) phosphorylation of AMPK. Interestingly, inhibition of previously identified kinases that phosphorylate AMPK at this site (Akt, S6K, and ERK) did not prevent these events. PMA treatment also caused impairments in insulin signaling through Akt, which were prevented by PKD1 inhibition. Finally, recombinant PKD1 phosphorylated AMPKα2 at Ser(491) in cell-free conditions, confirming PKD1's role in AMPK phosphorylation.
Our findings identify PKD1 as a novel upstream kinase of AMPKα2 Ser(491) that plays a negative role in insulin signaling in muscle cells. These results provide new insights into the regulation of AMPK activity and its implications for insulin resistance and metabolic disorders.

title: Accuracy of ICD-9-CM codes for identifying cardiovascular and stroke risk factors.
text:
Objective:
This study aimed to identify which ICD-9-CM codes in Medicare Part A data are associated with cardiovascular and stroke risk factors.
Design and Participants:
This cross-sectional study compared ICD-9-CM data to structured medical record review from 23,657 Medicare beneficiaries aged 20 to 105 years with atrial fibrillation.
Measurements:
Quality improvement organizations used standardized abstraction instruments to determine the presence of 9 cardiovascular and stroke risk factors. The accuracy of ICD-9-CM codes in identifying these risk factors was assessed using chart abstractions as the gold standard.
Main Results:
ICD-9-CM codes for all risk factors had high specificity (>0.95) but low sensitivity (< or =0.76). The positive predictive values were greater than 0.95 for 5 common, chronic risk factors-coronary artery disease, stroke/transient ischemic attack, heart failure, diabetes, and hypertension. The sixth common risk factor, valvular heart disease, had a positive predictive value of 0.93. For all 6 common risk factors, negative predictive values ranged from 0.52 to 0.91. The rare risk factors-arterial peripheral embolus, intracranial hemorrhage, and deep venous thrombosis-had high negative predictive value (> or =0.98) but moderate positive predictive values (range, 0.54-0.77) in this population.
Conclusions:
Using ICD-9-CM codes alone, heart failure, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and stroke can be ruled in but not necessarily ruled out. Where feasible, review of additional data (eg, physician notes or imaging studies) should be used to confirm the diagnosis of valvular disease, arterial peripheral embolus, intracranial hemorrhage, and deep venous thrombosis.

title: Modulation of cellular and viral promoters by mutant human p53 proteins found in tumor cells.
text: Recent research has shown that wild-type p53 represses transcription from various cellular and viral promoters. Given that p53 mutations are the most common genetic alteration in human cancers, studying the effects of these mutations on promoter function is crucial. To investigate, we examined the effects of wild-type and mutant human p53 on the human proliferating-cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) promoter and several viral promoters, including the herpes simplex virus type 1 UL9 promoter, the human cytomegalovirus major immediate-early promoter-enhancer, and the long terminal repeat promoters of Rous sarcoma virus and human T-cell lymphotropic virus type I. HeLa cells were co-transfected with a wild-type or mutant p53 expression vector and a plasmid containing a chloramphenicol acetyltransferase reporter gene under viral (or cellular) promoter control. Our findings showed that expression of wild-type p53 inhibited promoter function, while expression of a p53 mutant at positions 175, 248, 273, or 281 correlated with a significant increase in PCNA promoter activity (2-11-fold). The viral promoters were also activated, although to a lesser extent. We also found that activation by a mutant p53 requires a minimal promoter containing a single TATA box, and a more significant increase (25-fold) in activation occurs when the promoter contains a binding site for the activating transcription factor or cyclic AMP response element-binding protein. Using Saos-2 cells that do not express p53, we showed that activation by a mutant p53 is a direct enhancement. These findings suggest that the mutant forms of p53 found in cancer cells may play a functional role in activating important loci, including PCNA, leading to increased cell proliferation.

title: Valvular interstitial cells suppress calcification of valvular endothelial cells.
text:
Background: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most common heart valve disease in the Western world. Previously, we proposed that valvular endothelial cells (VECs) replenish injured adult valve leaflets through endothelial-to-mesenchymal transformation (EndMT); however, the role of EndMT in valvular calcification remains unclear. We hypothesized that aortic VECs undergo osteogenic differentiation via an EndMT process that can be inhibited by valvular interstitial cells (VICs).
Approach and Results: To investigate the role of EndMT and VICs in valve homeostasis, we isolated VEC clones and derived VICs from the same valve leaflets. We then cultured VECs with or without VICs and examined the expression of EndMT markers, osteogenic genes, and the inhibitory effect of VICs on VEC osteogenesis. Our results showed that VECs underwent EndMT upon TGF-β1 stimulation, as evidenced by increased expression of α-SMA, MMP-2, and Slug. In contrast, the presence of VICs inhibited VEC EndMT and osteogenesis, as shown by decreased expression of osteocalcin and osteopontin. Time-course analysis revealed that EndMT precedes osteogenesis, with an initial increase in EndMT markers followed by an increase in osteogenic genes.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that EndMT may play a crucial role in valve homeostasis, and VICs play a critical role in regulating VEC EndMT and osteogenesis. These results provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying valvular calcification and may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of CAVD.

title: The HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor simvastatin activates the protein kinase Akt and promotes angiogenesis in normocholesterolemic animals.
text: Recent research has suggested that statins may protect the vasculature in ways unrelated to their ability to lower lipids. Our study found that statins rapidly activate the protein kinase Akt/PKB in endothelial cells. As a result, simvastatin enhanced the phosphorylation of the endogenous Akt substrate endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) in an Akt-dependent manner, inhibited cell death, and accelerated the formation of new blood vessels in vitro. Similarly, both simvastatin administration and enhanced Akt signaling in the endothelium promoted angiogenesis in ischemic limbs of normocholesterolemic rabbits, similar to the effects of VEGF treatment. These findings suggest that activation of Akt may contribute to some of the beneficial side effects of statins, such as promoting new blood vessel growth.

title: Varenicline, an alpha4beta2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor partial agonist, selectively decreases ethanol consumption and seeking.
text: Alcohol dependence affects millions of people worldwide, and while there has been some progress in developing pharmacotherapies, there is still a pressing need for novel and additional therapeutic approaches. Interestingly, alcohol and nicotine are often abused together, and research suggests that neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) play a role in both substance dependencies. Varenicline, a partial agonist at the alpha4beta2 nAChRs, has been approved as a smoking cessation aid and has shown promise in reducing nicotine intake. In this study, we investigated the potential of varenicline in modulating ethanol consumption using three different animal models of drinking. Our findings indicate that acute administration of varenicline, in doses that reduce nicotine reward, selectively reduced ethanol but not sucrose seeking in an operant self-administration drinking paradigm. Additionally, chronic varenicline administration decreased ethanol consumption without resulting in a rebound increase in ethanol intake when the varenicline was no longer administered. These results suggest that the alpha4beta2 nAChRs may play a role in ethanol-seeking behaviors in animals chronically exposed to ethanol. The selectivity of varenicline in decreasing ethanol consumption, combined with its reported safety profile and mild side effects in humans, suggests that it may prove to be a valuable treatment for alcohol dependence.

title: Targeting TLR4 signaling by TLR4 Toll/IL-1 receptor domain-derived decoy peptides: identification of the TLR4 Toll/IL-1 receptor domain dimerization interface.
text: The dimerization of TLR4 Toll/IL-1R (TIR) domains upon agonist stimulation initiates intracellular signaling, making the identification of the TLR4-TIR dimerization interface a crucial step in the design of therapeutics that block TLR4 signaling. To achieve this, a library of cell-permeating decoy peptides was created, each representing a non-fragmented patch of the TLR4 TIR surface. These peptides were synthesized in tandem with a cell-permeating Antennapedia homeodomain sequence and tested for their ability to inhibit early cytokine mRNA expression and MAPK activation in LPS-stimulated primary murine macrophages. Five peptides were identified that potently inhibited TLR4 signaling without affecting TLR2 signaling. Further investigation using time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy revealed that the peptides 4R1, 4BB, and 4αE bound directly to the TLR4 TIR domain, with the area between the BB loop and the fifth helical region mediating TLR4 TIR dimerization. These findings demonstrate the utility of the decoy peptide approach, which involves probing for the ability of peptides representing various surface-exposed segments of a protein to inhibit protein function, and then identifying their specific targets using Förster resonance energy transfer to define recognition sites in signaling proteins that may be targeted therapeutically to disrupt functional transient protein interactions.

title: A paediatric case of sideroblastic anaemia. Ultrastructural studies of erythroblasts cultured from marrow BFU-E in a methylcellulose micromethod.
text: We investigated the morphological and functional characteristics of erythroblasts derived from bone marrow erythroid progenitor cells grown in a methylcellulose microculture from a female child with rare, atypical sideroblastic anemia (SA) that was partially responsive to pyridoxine. In comparison to normal cells, colony formation was within the normal range in three consecutive cultures (median values: 82.25 CFU-E and 16.4 BFU-E derived colonies/6.6 x 10^4 cells). We evaluated in vitro differentiation of erythroid cells by measuring the activity of uroporphyrinogen I synthase (UROS), an enzyme involved in the heme pathway, in cytosolic extracts from the erythroid colonies. The UROS values in the erythroid colonies from SA marrow were at the lower end of the normal range (median values: 6.7 +/- 0.3 and 14.4 +/- 3.8 pmol uroporphyrinogen/h in CFU-E and BFU-E-derived colonies, respectively, versus 17.4 +/- 7.3 and 25 +/- 7.2 pmol/h in CFU-E and BFU-E colonies from normal subjects). Ultrastructural examination of both non-cultured bone marrow and cultured BFU-E revealed the characteristic deposition of iron in mitochondria around the nucleus of most cells (ringed sideroblasts). However, the majority of cultured cells displayed marked dyserythropoietic features, including bilobulated or trilobulated erythroblasts, multiple cytoplasmic vacuoles, abnormalities of the nucleus, and excessive membrane material beneath the plasma membrane, which were difficult to observe in non-cultured marrow.

title: Innate lymphoid cells: emerging insights in development, lineage relationships, and function.
text: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) are a unique subset of immune cells that lack a specific antigen receptor, yet possess the capacity to produce a diverse array of effector cytokines, comparable to those produced by T helper cell subsets. ILCs play a crucial role in the development and maintenance of lymphoid organs, tissue remodeling, antimicrobial immunity, and inflammation, particularly at mucosal surfaces. Their exceptional ability to rapidly respond to insults inflicted by stress-induced microorganisms suggests that ILCs are indispensable in the initial lines of immunological defense. In this review, we will delve into the current understanding of the developmental requirements, lineage relationships, and effector functions of two distinct subtypes of ILCs: (a) Rorγt-expressing cells, which are involved in the formation of lymphoid tissues, mucosal immunity, and inflammation, and (b) type 2 ILCs, which are essential for helminth immunity. Additionally, we will explore the potential roles of ILCs in the pathogenesis of immune-mediated inflammatory and infectious diseases, including allergies.

title: No net renal extraction of homocysteine in fasting humans.
text:
BACKGROUND: The underlying pathophysiological mechanism of hyperhomocysteinemia in chronic renal failure in humans remains unknown. Previous studies have suggested that the kidneys may play a role in removing excess homocysteine from the bloodstream, but this has not been definitively proven. To investigate this further, we examined homocysteine extraction in the normal human kidney.
METHODS: We measured plasma total (free and protein-bound) and free homocysteine (tHcy and fHcy, respectively) levels in arterial and renal venous blood samples collected from 20 fasting patients with normal renal function during cardiac catheterization. Renal homocysteine extraction was calculated as the arteriovenous difference divided by the arterial levels multiplied by 100%.
RESULTS: We found no significant net renal uptake of homocysteine in these patients, with a calculated extraction rate of 0.9% (standard deviation 5.8%, 95% confidence interval -1.8 to +3.6) for total homocysteine and -0.2% (standard deviation 11.0%, 95% CI -5.4 to +4.9) for free homocysteine.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on our findings, we conclude that the kidneys do not play a significant role in removing excess homocysteine from the bloodstream in fasting humans with normal renal function. Therefore, the observed increase in homocysteine levels in patients with renal failure cannot be attributed to a loss of renal homocysteine uptake.

title: Traditional Chinese acupuncture in tension-type headache: a controlled study.
text:
In this study, 30 patients with tension-type headaches were randomly assigned to receive either traditional Chinese acupuncture or sham acupuncture for 8 weeks, followed by a 12-month follow-up. Five measures were used to assess symptom severity and treatment response, including the intensity, duration, and frequency of headache episodes, as well as headache index and analgesic intake. These measures were assessed at baseline, after 4 and 8 weeks of treatment, and 1, 6, and 12 months later. Before the start of the study, each patient completed the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI).
Using split-plot analysis of variance (ANOVA), the study found that compared to baseline, the frequency of headache episodes, analgesic consumption, and headache index significantly decreased over time at 1 month after the end of treatment and the 12-month follow-up. However, there was no significant difference between acupuncture and placebo treatment in terms of these outcomes. Additionally, the study found that no single MMPI scale predicted treatment response, but the mean MMPI profile of acupuncture non-responders showed the presence of "Conversion V."

title: TCR stimulation with modified anti-CD3 mAb expands CD8+ T cell population and induces CD8+CD25+ Tregs.
text: Modified anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are emerging as a potential means of inducing immunological tolerance in various settings, including transplantation and autoimmune diseases such as type 1 diabetes. In a trial of a modified anti-CD3 mAb (hOKT3gamma1(Ala-Ala)) in patients with type 1 diabetes, we identified clinical responders based on an increase in the number of peripheral blood CD8+ cells following treatment with the mAb. Our findings show that the anti-CD3 mAb triggered the activation of CD8+ T cells in both in vitro and in vivo settings, leading to the induction of regulatory CD8+CD25+ T cells. These cells inhibited the responses of CD4+ cells to the mAb and to antigen, and required direct cell-to-cell contact for their inhibitory effects. Additionally, we observed the induction of Foxp3 on CD8+ T cells in patients during mAb treatment, suggesting a potential mechanism for the anti-CD3 mAb's immune-modulatory effects involving the induction of a subset of regulatory CD8+ T cells.

title: Interactions between Non-Physician Clinicians and Industry: A Systematic Review
text:
BACKGROUND: As restrictions on physician-industry interactions increase, the pharmaceutical industry may shift its marketing efforts towards other healthcare professionals. Recent health policy developments highlight the importance of non-physician clinicians' decision-making in clinical practice. This systematic review aims to investigate the types and implications of non-physician clinician-industry interactions in clinical practice.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a systematic search of MEDLINE and Web of Science from January 1, 1946, to June 24, 2013, following PRISMA guidelines. Non-physician clinicians eligible for inclusion were registered nurses, nurse prescribers, physician assistants, pharmacists, dieticians, and physical or occupational therapists, with trainee samples excluded. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were qualitatively synthesized into eight outcome domains: nature and frequency of industry interactions, attitudes towards industry, perceived ethical acceptability of interactions, perceived marketing influence, perceived reliability of industry information, preparation for industry interactions, reactions to industry relations policy, and management of industry interactions. Non-physician clinicians reported interacting with the pharmaceutical and infant formula industries, with clinicians across disciplines meeting with pharmaceutical representatives regularly and relying on them for practice information. Clinicians frequently received industry "information," attended sponsored "education," and distributed similar materials targeted at patients. Clinicians generally regarded these interactions as ethical and beneficial, and were able to detect "promotion" while benefiting from industry "information." Free samples were among the most common ways clinicians interacted with industry. The studies were observational and varied in methodological rigor, so these findings may not be generalizable. This review provides the first descriptive analysis of this literature.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-physician clinicians' generally positive attitudes towards industry interactions, despite recognition of issues related to bias, suggest that industry interactions are normalized in clinical practice across non-physician disciplines. Consistent implementation of industry relations policy across all disciplines is necessary to mitigate conflicts of interest and address the potential impact of industry interactions on patient care.

title: Emtricitabine-tenofovir concentrations and pre-exposure prophylaxis efficacy in men who have sex with men.
text: Drug concentrations associated with protection against HIV-1 acquisition have not been established. In a substudy of the iPrEx trial, we evaluated drug concentrations among men who have sex with men. This randomized, placebo-controlled trial used daily oral doses of emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in men who have sex with men. We found that drug concentrations were lower in blood plasma and viable cryopreserved peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in HIV-infected individuals compared to controls at the time of HIV diagnosis (8% vs 44%; P < 0.001) and 90 days prior (11% vs 51%; P < 0.001). An intracellular concentration of the active form of tenofovir, tenofovir-diphosphate (TFV-DP), of 16 fmol per million PBMCs was associated with a 90% reduction in HIV acquisition relative to the placebo arm. In a separate study, directly observed dosing yielded TFV-DP concentrations that, when analyzed using the iPrEx model, corresponded to an HIV-1 risk reduction of 76%, 96%, and 99% for two, four, and seven doses per week, respectively. These findings suggest ways to optimize PrEP regimens for this population, with prophylactic benefits observed across a range of doses and drug concentrations.

title: Clinical outcomes following institution of the Canadian universal leukoreduction program for red blood cell transfusions.
text:
A number of countries have implemented policies of universal leukoreduction for their blood supply, but the effectiveness of this approach in reducing postoperative mortality and infection is unclear. To investigate this, we conducted a retrospective cohort study in 23 hospitals across Canada, comparing clinical outcomes before and after the introduction of a national universal prestorage leukoreduction program for blood transfusions.
We enrolled 14,786 patients who received red blood cell transfusions after cardiac surgery, repair of a hip fracture, or who required intensive care following a surgical intervention or multiple trauma. Of these, 6,982 patients were enrolled during the control period and 7,804 patients were enrolled after the introduction of leukoreduction.
Our results showed that unadjusted in-hospital mortality rates were significantly lower after the introduction of leukoreduction compared to the control period (6.19% vs 7.03%, respectively; P = 0.04). After adjusting for potential confounding variables, we found that the odds of death were reduced with leukoreduction (odds ratio [OR], 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75-0.99), but the rate of serious nosocomial infections did not decrease (adjusted OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.87-1.09). We also observed a significant decrease in posttransfusion fevers (adjusted OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.79-0.94) and antibiotic use (adjusted OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.99) following leukoreduction.
Our findings suggest that a national universal leukoreduction program may be associated with decreased mortality as well as decreased fever episodes and antibiotic use after red blood cell transfusion in high-risk patients.

title: Failure of continuous venovenous hemofiltration to prevent death in paraquat poisoning.
text: Paraquat poisoning is characterized by multiorgan failure and pulmonary fibrosis with respiratory failure, leading to early death within 3 days of ingestion in many cases. Recent studies have suggested that continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH) may play a role in treating multiorgan failure by promoting hemodynamic stability. To investigate the effectiveness of prophylactic CVVH in paraquat poisoning, we evaluated 80 patients (August 1996 to February 1999) who ingested 2.1 +/- 1.0 mouthfuls of paraquat (as 20% concentrate). All patients were treated with hemoperfusion (HP) within 24 hours of ingestion and then randomly assigned to the HP-alone or HP-CVVH group. Forty-four patients underwent HP only, while 36 patients underwent CVVH (duration, 57.4 +/- 31.3 hours; ultrafiltration volume, 40.2 +/- 4.8 L/d) after HP. Although the time to death after ingestion was significantly longer in the HP-CVVH than HP group (5.0 +/- 5.0 versus 2.5 +/- 2.1 days; P < 0.05), there was no difference in mortality rates between the two groups (66.7% versus 63.6%; P = 0.82). In the HP group, early circulatory collapse was a major cause of death, while in the HP-CVVH group, late respiratory failure was a major cause of death. Our findings suggest that prophylactic CVVH after HP can prevent early death caused by circulatory collapse, but it cannot prevent late death caused by respiratory failure and does not provide a survival benefit in acute paraquat poisoning.

title: The antidiabetic effect of mesenchymal stem cells is unrelated to their transdifferentiation potential but to their capability to restore Th1/Th2 balance and to modify the pancreatic microenvironment.
text:
Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic metabolic disease caused by the immune-mediated destruction of insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. In animal models of T1DM, the intravenous administration of multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) has been shown to result in the regeneration of pancreatic islets. However, the mechanisms underlying this effect are not fully understood.
Our study aimed to investigate whether MSCs differentiate into pancreatic β-cells and modify systemic and pancreatic pathophysiologic markers of T1DM. We found that after the intravenous administration of 5 × 105 syngeneic MSCs, mice with T1DM reversed their hyperglycemia and did not show any donor-derived insulin-producing cells. In contrast, MSCs were engrafted into secondary lymphoid organs 7 and 65 days post-transplantation, which correlated with a systemic and local reduction in the abundance of autoaggressive T cells and an increase in regulatory T cells. Additionally, in the pancreas of mice with T1DM treated with MSCs, we observed a shift from a proinflammatory to an anti-inflammatory cytokine profile, as well as a recovery of local expression and increased circulating levels of epidermal growth factor, a pancreatic trophic factor.
Our data suggest that the antidiabetic effect of MSCs is not related to their transdifferentiation potential but rather to their ability to restore the balance between Th1 and Th2 immunological responses, along with the modification of the pancreatic microenvironment. These findings have important implications for the design of clinical trials aimed to evaluate MSC transplantation in patients with T1DM, as the presence of endogenous precursors may be critical for restoring glycemic control.

title: Tmem27: a cleaved and shed plasma membrane protein that stimulates pancreatic beta cell proliferation.
text: The mechanisms that regulate the replication of terminally differentiated beta cells are currently unknown. In this study, we have identified and characterized a transmembrane protein called Tmem27 (also known as collectrin) in pancreatic beta cells. Our findings show that the expression of Tmem27 is reduced in mice lacking the transcription factor Tcf1, and increased in mice with hypertrophy of the endocrine pancreas. Interestingly, Tmem27 forms dimers and its extracellular domain is glycosylated, cleaved, and shed from the plasma membrane of beta cells, a process that is unique to beta cells. Overexpression of full-length Tmem27 leads to increased cell replication, while silencing of Tmem27 using RNAi results in a decrease in cell replication. Furthermore, mice with increased expression of Tmem27 in pancreatic beta cells exhibit increased beta cell mass. Our study identifies a novel transmembrane protein that regulates cell growth of pancreatic islets, providing new insights into the mechanisms that control beta cell replication.

title: The ATM missense mutation p.Ser49Cys (c.146C>G) and the risk of breast cancer.
text: Homozygous mutations in the ATM gene are associated with ataxia telangiectasia, while heterozygous mutation carriers may be at increased risk of breast cancer. In a study of 22 ATM variants, we found that a missense mutation (Ser49Cys, c.146C>G, p. S49C) carried by approximately 2% of individuals was more common in breast cancer cases than controls in both a large U.S. population-based study and a Polish study. The combined odds ratio (OR) for this mutation was 1.69 (95% CI, 1.19-2.40; P=0.004). Another missense mutation (Phe858Leu, c.2572T>C, p. F858L) was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer in the U.S. study but not in Poland, with a combined OR of 1.44 (95% CI, 0.98-2.11; P=0.06). These findings provide the most convincing evidence to date that missense mutations in ATM, particularly p. S49C, may be breast cancer susceptibility alleles. However, due to their low frequency, larger sample sizes are needed to more firmly establish these associations.

title: A diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging study of corpus callosum from adult patients with migraine complicated with depressive/anxious disorder.
text:
Objective:
This study aimed to investigate potential microstructural abnormalities in the corpus callosum (CC) of adult patients with migraine without aura, who also experienced depressive/anxious disorder.
Background:
Migraine patients are at a higher risk of developing depressive/anxious disorders, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

Methods:
Diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging was performed on 12 adult patients with simple migraine (without aura and without depressive/anxious disorder) (S-M group), 12 adult patients with complicated migraine (without aura but complicated with depressive/anxious disorder) (Co-M group), and 12 age- and sex-matched healthy subjects (Control group). Fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient were measured at the genu, body, and splenium of the CC, respectively.

Results:
Significant differences in FA values were observed among the three groups at all CC locations. The FA values from both the SM and Co-M groups were significantly lower than the control (P < .05 and P < .01, respectively). The FA values from the Co-M group were significantly lower than the SM group (P < .01). The apparent diffusion coefficient values of the above regions showed no significant differences among the groups (P > .05). Negative correlations were found between FA values of the genu of the CC and disease course, as well as FA values of the genu and body of the CC and headache frequency (P < .05). Additionally, negative correlations were found between FA values at all CC locations and Hamilton anxiety and Hamilton depression scores (both P < .05).


Conclusions:

These findings suggest that there may be changes in the integrity of neurofibrotic microstructures in the CC of migraine patients complicated by depressive/anxious disorder, which could serve as a possible neuroanatomical basis for these disorders.

title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists for the Prevention of Adverse events following percutaneous coronary Revascularization--results of the PPAR study.
text:
BACKGROUND Patients with metabolic syndrome are at a higher risk of developing cardiovascular complications. We aimed to determine whether peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists have any beneficial effects on patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS A total of 200 patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI were randomly assigned to receive either rosiglitazone or a placebo for 1 year. We measured carotid intima-medial thickness (CIMT), inflammatory markers, lipid levels, brain natriuretic peptide, and clinical events at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months.
RESULTS There was no significant difference in CIMT between the two groups. However, the 12-month composite end point of death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or any recurrent ischemia was numerically lower in the rosiglitazone group (31.4% vs 30.2%, P = .99). The rate of death, MI, or stroke at 12 months was also lower in the rosiglitazone group (11.9% vs 6.4%, P = .19). Additionally, there was a trend towards greater decreases in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein values compared with baseline in the rosiglitazone group at 6 months (-35.4% vs -15.8%, P = .059) and 12 months (-40.0% vs -20.9%, P = .089), as well as higher changes in high-density lipoprotein (+15.5% vs +4.1%, P = .05) and lower triglycerides (-13.9% vs +14.9%, P = .004) in the rosiglitazone arm. Furthermore, there was a trend towards fewer new onset diabetes in the rosiglitazone group (0% vs 3.3%, P = .081) and no episodes of symptomatic hypoglycemia. Finally, there was no excess of new onset of clinical heart failure in the rosiglitazone group, nor was there a significant change in brain natriuretic peptide levels.
CONCLUSIONS Patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI are at increased risk of subsequent cardiovascular events. Our study found that rosiglitazone treatment for 12 months did not significantly affect CIMT in this population, although it had beneficial effects on inflammatory markers, lipid levels, and triglycerides. Further research on peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonism in patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI may be warranted.

title: Accumulation of hydroxyethyl starch in human and animal tissues: a systematic review
text: To conduct a systematic review of clinical and preclinical data on hydroxyethyl starch (HES) tissue storage, we searched MEDLINE (PubMed) and included articles based on defined criteria. A total of 48 studies were identified, consisting of 37 human studies with 635 patients and 11 animal studies. The most common indication for HES fluid infusion was surgery, accounting for 282 patients (45.9%).
