HES was shown to accumulate in various tissues, including skin, kidney, liver, and bone marrow, with the highest measured tissue concentration in the kidney. HES uptake into intracellular vacuoles was observed within 30 minutes of infusion, and storage was found to be cumulative, increasing in proportion to dose. However, in 15% of patients, storage and associated symptoms were demonstrated at the lowest cumulative doses (0.4 g/kg). Some HES deposits were found to be extremely long-lasting, persisting for up to 8 years in skin and 10 years in kidney. Pruritus and renal dysfunction were commonly reported symptoms associated with HES storage. In one randomized trial, HES infusion produced osmotic nephrosis-like lesions and increased the need for renal replacement therapy. The tissue distribution of HES was similar in both animals and humans. Overall, HES tissue storage is widespread, rapid, cumulative, frequently long-lasting, and potentially harmful.

title: Cationic host defense (antimicrobial) peptides.
text: Members of the cationic host defense (antimicrobial) peptide family are found throughout nature, from insects to plants to mammals and non-mammalian vertebrates. Although many of these peptides demonstrate direct antimicrobial activity against bacteria, fungi, eukaryotic parasites, and viruses, it is now recognized that they also play a crucial modulatory role in the innate immune response. Recent research has shown that host defense peptides are effective adjuvants, synergize with other immune effectors, polarize the adaptive response, and support wound healing. As our understanding of the mechanisms of action of these peptides grows, we are better equipped to harness their therapeutic potential.

title: A mental health intervention for schoolchildren exposed to violence: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
No randomized controlled studies have been conducted to date on the effectiveness of psychological interventions for children who have witnessed or been exposed to violence and are experiencing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). To address this gap in knowledge, a randomized controlled trial was conducted among sixth-grade students in two large middle schools in Los Angeles who reported exposure to violence and had clinical levels of PTSD symptoms.
The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a collaboratively designed school-based intervention in reducing children's symptoms of PTSD and depression. The intervention consisted of a 10-session standardized cognitive-behavioral therapy (Cognitive-Behavioral Intervention for Trauma in Schools) delivered by trained school mental health clinicians. Students were randomly assigned to either an early intervention group (n=61) or a wait-list delayed intervention comparison group (n=65).
The primary outcome measures included child-reported symptoms of PTSD (Child PTSD Symptom Scale), depression (Child Depression Inventory), parent-reported psychosocial dysfunction (Pediatric Symptom Checklist), and teacher-reported classroom problems using the Teacher-Child Rating Scale (acting out, shyness/anxiousness, and learning problems). The study found that compared to the wait-list delayed intervention group, students who were randomly assigned to the early intervention group had significantly lower scores on symptoms of PTSD, depression, and psychosocial dysfunction after 3 months of intervention. However, there were no significant differences between the two groups in teacher-reported classroom problems at 3 or 6 months.
The findings suggest that a standardized 10-session cognitive-behavioral group intervention can significantly decrease symptoms of PTSD and depression in students who are exposed to violence and can be effectively delivered on school campuses by trained school-based mental health clinicians.

title: Knowledge gaps and misconceptions about coronary heart disease among U.S. South Asians.
text: BACKGROUND: Despite being at a higher risk for coronary heart disease (CHD) than most other racial/ethnic groups in the US, very little research has been conducted to address this disparity among South Asians. PURPOSE: As a first step towards developing culturally tailored CHD prevention messages for this rapidly growing community, this study aimed to examine South Asians' knowledge and beliefs about CHD. METHODS: In 2009, data from a cross-sectional study of 270 South Asian adults in Illinois were analyzed. The study used a standardized questionnaire conducted in English, Hindi, or Urdu to gather information on participants' knowledge and attitudes towards CHD. Multivariate regression models were used to identify associations between sociodemographics and CHD knowledge and beliefs about preventability. RESULTS: Eighty-one percent of respondents reported having one or more CHD risk factors. The majority (89%) of participants reported having little or no knowledge about CHD. Stress was the most frequently cited risk factor (44%), followed by lack of knowledge about controlling blood pressure (11%), cholesterol (10%), and diabetes (5%). Only 53% of participants believed that heart attacks are preventable. Lower education level, being interviewed in Urdu or Hindi, and lower acculturation levels were associated with lower knowledge and beliefs about preventability. CONCLUSIONS: The study findings suggest that a majority of South Asians in the study believed that CHD is not preventable and had low awareness of modifiable risk factors. As a first step, culturally tailored CHD education programs should target the knowledge gaps that may hinder risk factor control and behavior change. Educational messages may need to be tailored to subgroups (e.g., by education and language) to be most effective.

title: Innate host defense requires TFEB-mediated transcription of cytoprotective and antimicrobial genes.
text: Animal defense against infection depends on the timely and proper expression of defense genes. Uncovering the mechanisms behind this control requires identifying the transcription factors involved. Using an unbiased approach in the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans, we discovered that HLH-30 (equivalent to TFEB in mammals) is a crucial transcription factor for host defense. Upon Staphylococcus aureus infection, HLH-30 is activated and regulates the expression of nearly 80% of host response genes, including antimicrobial and autophagy genes essential for the host's tolerance of infection. Similarly, in murine macrophages, TFEB is rapidly activated upon S. aureus infection and plays a critical role in the transcriptional induction of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Our findings suggest that TFEB is an evolutionarily ancient transcription factor in the host response to infection, highlighting its importance in maintaining proper defense mechanisms.

title: DAP kinase regulates JNK signaling by binding and activating protein kinase D under oxidative stress
text: The stress-activated kinase, JNK, plays a crucial role in mediating cellular responses to oxidative stress. Recent studies have shown that DAP kinase (DAPk), a Ser/Thr protein kinase involved in cell death, plays a primary role in oxidative stress-induced JNK signaling. In this investigation, we identify protein kinase D (PKD) as a novel substrate of DAPk and demonstrate that DAPk physically interacts with PKD in response to oxidative stress. Furthermore, we show that DAPk activates PKD in cells and that induction of JNK phosphorylation by ectopically expressed DAPk can be attenuated by reducing PKD expression or inhibiting its catalytic activity. Additionally, knockdown of DAPk expression leads to a significant decrease in JNK activation under oxidative stress conditions, indicating that DAPk is essential for the activation of JNK signaling in this context. Lastly, we demonstrate that DAPk is required for cell death under oxidative stress, which exhibits characteristics of caspase-independent necrotic cell death. These findings collectively suggest that DAPk and its specific interaction with PKD play a pivotal role in regulating the JNK signaling network under oxidative stress conditions.

title: The changes of antioxidant defense system caused by quercetin administration do not lead to DNA damage and apoptosis in the spleen and bone marrow cells of rats.
text: The study aimed to investigate the anti- and pro-oxidant effects of quercetin in rat bone marrow and spleen cells. The experimental rats were administered quercetin at doses of 8 or 80mg/kg body weight via gavage for 40 days. The researchers measured the intracellular redox state by assessing the ferric ion reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) levels and malondialdehyde (MDA) concentrations. Additionally, the expression of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) mRNA was examined using real-time PCR, and the extent of DNA damage was determined through the alkaline-labile comet assay. Furthermore, the researchers evaluated the potential pro-apoptotic effects of quercetin using the FITC-Annexin V kit. The quercetin and isorhamnetin concentrations in serum were analyzed using high-performance liquid chromatography-electrochemical detection (HPLC-ECD). The results showed that quercetin treatment significantly decreased MDA levels and increased FRAP values in the spleen and bone marrow cells at the higher dose of 80mg/kg b.w., compared to the control group. Quercetin also dose-dependently upregulated the expression of HO-1 mRNA in the bone marrow cells. However, quercetin administration did not induce DNA damage or pro-apoptotic activity in the examined cells. Overall, the study demonstrated that quercetin's antioxidant effects do not lead to DNA damage or pro-apoptotic activity in vivo.

title: Mutated KRAS results in overexpression of DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase, in rectal carcinomas.
text: Mutations in the KRAS oncogene have been found to be predictive of resistance to treatment with antibodies targeting the epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR) in patients with colorectal cancer. To address this therapeutic challenge, potential strategies could involve inhibiting signaling pathways activated by KRAS mutations. To identify such pathways comprehensively, we profiled pretreatment biopsies and normal mucosa from 65 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, of which 30 had KRAS mutations. Using global gene expression microarrays, we identified a total of 22,297 features that were differentially expressed between normal mucosa and cancer, including several novel potential rectal cancer genes. We then used this comprehensive transcriptome analysis as a baseline for identifying KRAS-dependent alterations. Our findings revealed a significant correlation between the presence of activating KRAS mutations and upregulation of 13 genes, including DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase. Previous studies have shown that inhibiting the expression of these genes using MEK1 inhibitor PD98059 and the antibacterial compound Novobiocin, respectively, may provide a potential approach to overcome resistance to EGFR-targeting therapies in KRAS-mutant rectal carcinomas.

title: Clinicopathological and prognostic significance of Bmi-1 expression in human cervical cancer.
text:
Objective: To investigate the clinical significance of Bmi-1 expression as a prognostic marker for cervical cancer.
Design: A retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort.
Setting: Jiangsu Province Hospital.
Population: Eighty-eight women diagnosed with cervical carcinoma between 2000 and 2003.
Methods: RT-PCR assay was performed to determine Bmi-1 mRNA expression in 18 cervical cancer and noncancerous tissue samples, and immunohistochemistry was used to detect Bmi-1 protein expression in 88 cervical cancer samples. The correlation between Bmi-1 expression and clinicopathological factors was analyzed. Additionally, statistical analyses were applied to test for prognostic associations. RNA interference was used to downregulate Bmi-1 expression in a cervical cancer cell line (HeLa). In vitro cytotoxicity was measured by the methylthiazoletetrazolium and colony formation assays. Effects of Bmi-1 inhibition on in vivo growth of cancer cells were detected by the tumorigenicity assay. Cell cycle distribution and cell apoptosis were measured by flow cytometry.
Main Outcome Measures: The levels of Bmi-1 mRNA and protein expression in tissues were evaluated by RT-PCR and Western Blot assays.
Results: The level of Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer tissues was significantly higher than that in corresponding noncancerous tissues. High Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis. Patients with high Bmi-1 expression showed shorter overall survival than those with low expression. Univariate and multivariate analyses showed that high Bmi-1 expression was an independent prognostic factor.
Conclusions: RNA interference-mediated Bmi-1 inhibition could inhibit in vitro and in vivo growth, enhance apoptosis, and induce cell cycle arrest of cervical cancer cells. Bmi-1 might be an independent prognostic marker for cervical cancer patients.

title: Dexamethasone decreases vomiting by children after tonsillectomy.
text: In a randomized, stratified, blocked, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, we evaluated the effect of dexamethasone on vomiting in 133 healthy children aged 2-12 years after elective tonsillectomy. The study used general anesthesia induced by inhalation of N2O and halothane or intravenously with propofol, and maintained with N2O and halothane. Dexamethasone (150 micrograms/kg up to a maximum dose of 8 mg) or placebo was administered intravenously before surgery. All patients received 1.5 mg/kg codeine intramuscularly intraoperatively. Standardized perioperative IV fluids, emesis management, postoperative pain management, and hospital discharge criteria were used. The results showed that dexamethasone significantly reduced the overall incidence of vomiting from 72% (placebo) to 40% (P < 0.001). Prophylactic administration of dexamethasone decreased both in-hospital and postdischarge vomiting, with each episode of in-hospital vomiting prolonging discharge by 13 ± 2 minutes (P < 0.001). In conclusion, our study demonstrated that dexamethasone significantly decreased vomiting in healthy children after elective tonsillectomy in an ambulatory hospital setting.

title: A Conserved Histidine in the RNA Sensor RIG-I Controls Immune Tolerance to N1-2'O-Methylated Self RNA.
text: The cytosolic helicase retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a crucial role in initiating immune responses to most RNA viruses by recognizing and responding to 5'-triphosphorylated RNA (pppRNA) from these viruses. However, endogenous mRNA, which is also 5'-triphosphorylated, is not recognized by RIG-I due to modifications to its backbone and the presence of a specific cap structure. In this study, we investigate the role of the 5'-terminal nucleotide (N1) of endogenous capped mRNA in preventing RIG-I activation. Specifically, we identify a conserved amino acid (H830) in the RIG-I RNA binding pocket that mediates steric exclusion of N1-2'O-methylated RNA. Mutation of this amino acid (RIG-I(H830A)) restores binding of N1-2'O-methylated pppRNA, leading to activation of the mutant protein in the absence of exogenous stimuli. Similarly, knockdown of the endogenous N1-2'O-methyltransferase results in increased RIG-I activation. Our findings reveal a novel mechanism by which viruses, such as yellow-fever-virus, exploit this process to evade RIG-I-mediated immune responses. Overall, our data highlight a previously unappreciated role for cap N1-2'O-methylation in RIG-I tolerance of self-RNA.

title: lumi: a pipeline for processing Illumina microarray.
text:
The Illumina microarray platform has gained popularity in recent years due to the BeadArray technology developed by Illumina, which offers distinct preprocessing and quality control procedures compared to other microarray technologies. Unfortunately, many analyses have failed to capitalize on the unique features of the BeadArray system, instead adopting preprocessing methods originally designed for Affymetrix microarrays. To address this gap, the lumi package was developed as a Bioconductor tool specifically designed to process Illumina microarray data.
The lumi package encompasses various components, including data input, quality control, variance stabilization, normalization, and gene annotation. Of particular note is the variance-stabilizing transformation (VST) algorithm integrated into the package, which exploits the technical replicates present on every Illumina microarray. Additionally, various normalization method options and multiple quality control plots are provided. To further enhance the annotation of Illumina data, a vendor-independent nucleotide universal identifier (nuID) was created to identify the probes of Illumina microarrays. The nuID annotation packages and output of lumi-processed results can be seamlessly integrated with other Bioconductor packages to construct a comprehensive statistical data analysis pipeline for Illumina data.
The lumi package is freely available for download on the Bioconductor website, located at <https://www.bioconductor.org/>.

title: Large scale replication and meta-analysis of variants on chromosome 4q25 associated with atrial fibrillation.
text: A recent genome-wide association study identified a haplotype block on chromosome 4q25 as a potential risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF). To further investigate this association, we replicated the findings in four independent cohorts of European descent. Our results confirm the association between AF and non-coding single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) rs2200733 and rs10033464, with odds ratios ranging from 1.37 to 2.52 across the four cohorts. A meta-analysis of the current and prior AF studies revealed a strong association between these SNPs and AF, with an odds ratio of 1.90 for rs2200733 and 1.36 for rs10033464. These findings suggest that intergenic variants on chromosome 4 may play a significant role in the development of AF.

title: Ecological analysis of ethnic differences in relation between tuberculosis and poverty.
text:
Objective: To investigate the relationship between ethnicity and the association between tuberculosis (TB) and deprivation in Birmingham, UK.
Design: Retrospective ecological study comparing the incidence of TB among white and South Asian residents of 39 electoral wards in Birmingham, using ethnic-specific indices of deprivation.
Setting: Birmingham, 1989-1993.
Subjects: 1516 notified cases of TB.
Main Outcome Measures: TB rates and measures of deprivation.
Results: Univariate analysis revealed significant associations between TB rates for the entire population and several indices of deprivation (P<0.01) and with the proportion of the population of South Asian origin (P<0.01). All deprivation covariates were positively associated with each other, but on multiple regression, higher levels of overcrowding were independently associated with TB rates. For the white population, overcrowding was associated with TB rates independently of other variables (P=0.0036). No association between deprivation and TB was found for the South Asian population in either single or multivariable analyses.
Conclusions: Poverty is significantly associated with TB in the white population, but no such relation exists for those of Asian ethnicity. These findings suggest that causal factors and potential interventions may differ by ethnic group.

title: Reduced expression of oestrogen receptor beta in invasive breast cancer and its re-expression using DNA methyl transferase inhibitors in a cell line model.
text: To gain insights into the potential role of oestrogen receptor beta (ERβ) in breast cancer development, immunohistochemical analysis of ERβ was conducted on 512 breast tissue samples, including normal (n = 138), pure ductal carcinoma in situ (n = 16), invasive cancers (n = 319), lymph node metastases (n = 31), and recurrences (n = 8). Real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was also used to investigate the methylation status of the ERβ gene in ERβ-negative breast cancer cell lines, SkBr3 and MDA-MB-435. The results showed a gradual decrease in ERβ expression during the transition from normal and pre-invasive lesions to invasive cancers, with ERβ loss occurring in 21% of cases. This decrease was more pronounced in invasive ductal carcinomas than in lobular carcinomas, with a higher proportion of ERβ-positive cases in the latter (74% vs 91%, p = 0.0004). Additionally, examination of paired primary cancers and their axillary lymph node metastases revealed that if ERβ was present in the primary tumor, it persisted in the metastasis. Treatment of ERβ-negative cell lines with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors restored ERβ expression, providing experimental evidence that silencing of ERβ in breast carcinomas may be due to promoter hypermethylation. These findings suggest that loss of ERβ expression is a hallmark of breast cancer development and may be a reversible process involving methylation.

title: Atopy risk in infants and children in relation to early exposure to fish, oily fish, or long-chain omega-3 fatty acids: a systematic review.
text: There are two main categories of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), n-6 and n-3. While it has been suggested that n-6 PUFA intake may be associated with an increased risk of allergic diseases, there are biological mechanisms that could explain this relationship. Fish and fish oils are rich in long-chain n-3 PUFAs, which have the opposite effect of n-6 PUFAs and may protect against allergic sensitization and clinical manifestations. Epidemiological studies have consistently shown that maternal fish intake during pregnancy, lactation, and infancy is associated with a lower risk of atopic outcomes in offspring. However, the evidence for the effect of fish intake during childhood is inconsistent, with some studies showing a protective effect and others not. Fish oil supplementation during pregnancy, lactation, and infancy has been shown to increase the n-3 PUFA status in offspring and may also have immunological effects in cord blood that persist. While the evidence suggests that fish oil supplementation may reduce the risk of allergic diseases in infants and children, more research is needed to fully understand the immunological and clinical effects of increased n-3 PUFA provision in this population.

title: Dietary quality among men and women in 187 countries in 1990 and 2010: a systematic assessment
text:
The article discusses the findings of a systematic assessment of global dietary patterns from 1990 to 2010. The study aimed to characterize global changes in dietary patterns across different regions, ages, sexes, and income levels. The analysis was based on consumption data from 325 surveys covering 88.7% of the global adult population. Two types of dietary patterns were assessed: one based on consumption of healthy items and the other based on consumption of unhealthy items.
The study found that global diets based on healthy items improved by 2.2 points from 1990 to 2010, while diets based on unhealthy items worsened by 2.5 points. However, there was substantial heterogeneity across regions and countries, with better diets observed in older adults, women, and high-income nations. The study also found that middle-income countries showed the largest improvement in dietary patterns based on healthy items, but the largest deterioration in dietary patterns based on unhealthy items.
The study highlights the importance of addressing the global burden of poor diet quality, which is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and prioritize the need for targeted interventions to improve dietary patterns globally. The study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and Medical Research Council.

title: The epidemiology of major depressive disorder: results from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R).
text:
The article discusses the prevalence and correlates of major depressive disorder (MDD) in the United States, based on data from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R). The study found that:
* The prevalence of MDD according to the World Health Organization's (WHO) Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI) was 16.2% for lifetime and 6.6% for 12-month.
* Almost all 12-month cases were classified as clinically significant using the Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology Self-Report (QIDS-SR).
* The mean episode duration was 16 weeks.
* Role impairment was substantial, with 59.3% of 12-month cases having severe or very severe role impairment.
* The majority of cases (72.1% for lifetime and 78.5% for 12-month) had comorbid CIDI/DSM-IV disorders, with MDD rarely being the primary disorder.
* Although 51.6% of 12-month cases received health care treatment for MDD, treatment was adequate in only 41.9% of these cases, resulting in 21.7% of 12-month MDD being adequately treated.
* Sociodemographic correlates of treatment were less common than those of prevalence.

The study highlights the need for improved screening and treatment quality to address the inadequate treatment of MDD.

title: The Pain Catastrophizing Scale: Further Psychometric Evaluation with Adult Samples
text: Previous research with undergraduate students has supported the reliability and three-factor structure of a new scale, the Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS). In this study, we examined the reliability and validity of the PCS in adult community and pain outpatient samples. Our findings indicate that the PCS exhibited high internal consistency in both groups. Using data from the community sample, confirmatory factor analysis revealed that the PCS taps a single construct composed of three related dimensions. Additionally, we found significant gender differences on the PCS total score in both the community and outpatient samples. Furthermore, the analyses revealed notable differences between the community and outpatient samples on the PCS total and subscales. Overall, our results provide strong evidence of criterion-related, concurrent, and discriminant validity for the PCS in the community sample. However, limitations of the study are also discussed.

title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma.
text:
Background: Interferon alfa is a widely used treatment for metastatic renal-cell carcinoma, but its efficacy and tolerability are limited. Temsirolimus, a specific inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin kinase, may offer a better therapeutic option for these patients.
Methods: In this multicenter, phase 3 clinical trial, we randomly assigned 626 patients with poor-prognosis metastatic renal-cell carcinoma to receive one of three treatments: intravenous temsirolimus at a dose of 25 mg per week, subcutaneous interferon alfa at a dose of 3 million units three times per week, or combination therapy with 15 mg of temsirolimus per week plus 6 million units of interferon alfa three times per week. The primary endpoint of the study was overall survival, which was compared between the temsirolimus group and the combination-therapy group in relation to the interferon group.
Results: Our findings showed that patients who received temsirolimus alone had significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.92; P=0.008) and progression-free survival (P<0.001) than patients who received interferon alone. In contrast, overall survival in the combination-therapy group did not differ significantly from that in the interferon group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.20; P=0.70). The median overall survival times in the interferon group, the temsirolimus group, and the combination-therapy group were 7.3, 10.9, and 8.4 months, respectively. Adverse events were more common in the temsirolimus group, including rash, peripheral edema, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia. In contrast, asthenia was more common in the interferon group. There were fewer patients with serious adverse events in the temsirolimus group than in the interferon group (P=0.02).
Conclusion: Our study suggests that temsirolimus improves overall survival among patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma and a poor prognosis, compared to interferon alfa. The addition of temsirolimus to interferon did not improve survival. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00065468 [ClinicalTrials.gov].)

title: Macrophage Diversity Enhances Tumor Progression and Metastasis
text: There exists a compelling body of clinical and experimental evidence indicating that macrophages play a significant role in the initiation and progression of cancer. During the early stages of tumor formation, macrophages create an inflammatory environment that fosters mutagenesis and promotes cell growth. As tumors progress to malignancy, macrophages stimulate angiogenesis, enhance tumor cell migration and invasion, and suppress anti-tumor immunity. At metastatic sites, macrophages prepare the target tissue for the arrival of tumor cells and then a distinct subpopulation of macrophages promotes tumor cell extravasation, survival, and subsequent growth. The existence of specialized subpopulations of macrophages may represent a novel therapeutic target.

title: Ankle brachial index as a predictor of cognitive impairment in the general population: ten-year follow-up of the Edinburgh Artery Study.
text:
Objective: To investigate the association between ankle brachial index (ABI) and cognitive impairment in older adults over a 10-year period.
Design: Cohort study (Edinburgh Artery Study)
Setting: Eleven general practices in Edinburgh, Scotland.
Participants: Seven hundred seventy-one men and women aged 55-74 from the general population, followed for 10 years.
Measurements: ABI was measured at baseline, and major cognitive functions, including premorbid function using the National Adult Reading Test (NART), were tested after 10 years.
Results: After adjusting for age and sex, a low ABI was associated with lower scores on Raven's Matrices (bottom tertile vs top tertile; odds ratio (OR) =1.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) =1.0-2.6), Verbal Fluency (OR =1.8, 95% CI =1.1-3.0), and Digit Symbol Test (OR =2.3, 95% CI =1.3-4.2), indicating that the ABI is predictive of poorer performance in nonverbal reasoning, verbal fluency, and information processing speed. The association between ABI and the Digit Symbol Test remained significant after further adjusting for premorbid cognitive function (tested using the NART), suggesting that the ABI is also predictive of decline in information processing speed (from premorbid ability to that measured here in older age).
Conclusion: The ABI may be useful in identifying older individuals at higher risk of cognitive impairment. Future preventive measures should consider measures to reduce vascular-related cognitive decline as well as cardiovascular events, in an effort to reduce the incidence and consequences of subsequent cognitive impairment and dementia.

title: PTEN Regulates PI(3,4)P2 Signaling Downstream of Class I PI3K
text: The PI3K signaling pathway regulates cell growth and movement, and is frequently mutated in cancer. Class I PI3Ks produce the lipid messenger PI(3,4,5)P3. PI(3,4,5)P3 can be dephosphorylated by 3- or 5-phosphatases, with the latter producing PI(3,4)P2. The PTEN tumor suppressor is thought to primarily function as a PI(3,4,5)P3 3-phosphatase, limiting activation of this pathway. However, our findings show that PTEN also functions as a PI(3,4)P2 3-phosphatase, both in vitro and in vivo. PTEN is a major PI(3,4)P2 phosphatase in Mcf10a cytosol, and loss of PTEN and INPP4B, a known PI(3,4)P2 4-phosphatase, leads to synergistic accumulation of PI(3,4)P2, which correlates with increased invadopodia in EGF-stimulated cells. Deletion of PTEN increases PI(3,4)P2 levels in a mouse model of prostate cancer, and it inversely correlates with PI(3,4)P2 levels across several EGF-stimulated prostate and breast cancer lines. These results suggest a role for PI(3,4)P2 in the phenotype caused by loss-of-function mutations or deletions in PTEN.

title: Genetic analysis of an ARS element from the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
text: Autonomously replicating sequence (ARS) elements are DNA fragments that can serve as origins of DNA replication in yeast. In this study, we conducted a fine-scale analysis of ars1, an ARS element from the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Our characterization of a series of nested deletion mutations revealed that the minimal DNA fragment encompassing ars1 is surprisingly large, with no fragment smaller than 650 base pairs (bp) retaining significant ARS activity. Through a detailed analysis of deletion and substitution mutations spanning the entire minimal ars1, we identified a single essential 50-bp fragment (segment 1) that is required for efficient ARS function. Additionally, we found that a second, larger region of the ars1 sequence is tolerant of internal structural alterations. Higher resolution analysis of segment 1 revealed a critical 30-bp A/T-rich segment that appears to contain redundant genetic elements. Interestingly, while Schizosaccharomyces pombe ars1 promoted high-frequency transformation in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, this heterologous activity was not dependent on segment 1, suggesting that the functional elements required for ARS function in these two species are distinct.

title: N terminus of Swr1 binds to histone H2AZ and provides a platform for subunit assembly in the chromatin remodeling complex.
text:
Variant histone H2AZ-containing nucleosomes play a crucial role in regulating gene expression, particularly in the yeast species Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The process of chromatin deposition of histone H2AZ in S. cerevisiae is mediated by the SWR1 complex, a fourteen-subunit enzyme that catalyzes ATP-dependent exchange of nucleosomal histone H2A for H2AZ. Previous studies have identified the functional roles of seven SWR1 subunits (Swr1 ATPase, Swc2, Swc3, Arp6, Swc5, Yaf9, and Swc6) in maintaining complex integrity and H2AZ histone replacement activity.
In this study, we aimed to investigate the functional roles of three additional SWR1 subunits, bromodomain-containing Bdf1, actin-related protein Arp4, and Swc7, in the SWR1 complex. We analyzed affinity-purified mutant SWR1 complexes to examine the effects of depletion or loss of these subunits on complex integrity and H2AZ histone replacement activity. Our findings revealed that depletion of Arp4 (arp4-td) significantly impaired the association of Bdf1, Yaf9, and Swc4, while loss of either Bdf1 or Swc7 had minimal effects on overall complex integrity. Furthermore, we found that the basic H2AZ histone replacement activity of SWR1 in vitro required Arp4, but not Bdf1 or Swc7.
Our results suggest that three out of fourteen SWR1 subunits, Bdf1, Swc7, and previously identified Swc3, have auxiliary roles in the SWR1 complex beyond the basic histone replacement activity. The N-terminal region of the Swr1 ATPase subunit was found to be necessary and sufficient to direct the association of Bdf1, Swc7, Arp4, Act1, Yaf9, and Swc4. Interestingly, this region contains an additional H2AZ-H2B specific binding site, distinct from the previously identified Swc2 subunit. These findings imply that one SWR1 enzyme might be capable of binding two H2AZ-H2B dimers, providing further insight into the hierarchy and interdependency of molecular interactions within the SWR1 complex.

title: Role of the cytoskeleton during leukocyte responses
text: The cytoskeleton is a complex network of molecules within cells that plays a crucial role in regulating various cellular functions related to the immune response. This network consists of structural, adaptor, and signaling molecules that work together to control processes such as migration, extravasation, antigen recognition, activation, and phagocytosis by different types of white blood cells, including leukocytes. Recently, a significant number of regulatory elements and structural components of the leukocyte cytoskeleton have been identified, providing valuable insights into its composition and function. In this review, we will delve into the composition and regulation of these cytoskeletal elements and their crucial role in immune responses.

title: Integration of mental health into primary healthcare in low-income countries: avoiding medicalization.
text:
Since 2008, the World Health Organization (WHO) has been working through its mental health Gap Action Programme to revitalize efforts to integrate mental health into primary healthcare. While this has sparked renewed interest in this approach, it has also faced criticism. Some concerns include that it may lead to the medicalization of social and psychological problems and neglect other levels of the healthcare system, such as community-based care and care on district levels. This paper identifies seven key elements that are crucial to preventing a narrow biomedical approach to mental healthcare when integrating mental health into non-specialized healthcare:
1. Using task shifting approaches within a stepped care system,
2. Ensuring primary mental healthcare includes brief psychotherapeutic interventions,
3. Promoting community-based recovery-oriented interventions for people with disabling chronic mental disorders,
4. Conceptualizing training as a continuous process of strengthening clinical competencies through supervision,
5. Engaging communities as partners in psychosocial interventions,
6. Embedding shifts to primary mental healthcare within wider health policy reforms, and
7. Promoting inter-sectoral approaches to address social determinants of mental health.

title: Comparison of clomiphene citrate, metformin, or the combination of both for first-line ovulation induction and achievement of pregnancy in 154 women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
text:
Objective: To compare the effectiveness of clomiphene citrate (CC) and metformin in ovulation induction and pregnancy achievement in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients, and to identify potential patient characteristics associated with a better response to therapy.
Design: Observational comparative study.
Setting: Fertility clinic.
Patients: One hundred fifty-four infertile women with oligomenorrhea and hyperandrogenism.
Intervention: Group 1 (56 patients) received CC 50 mg from days 5-9 of the cycle. Group 2 (57 patients) received 500 mg of metformin 3 times a day. Group 3 (41 patients) received both medications.
Main Outcome Measures: Ovulation and pregnancy.
Results: Patients receiving metformin alone had a higher ovulation rate compared to those receiving CC alone (75.4% vs. 50%). The ovulation rates were similar in the metformin and combination groups (75.4% vs. 63.4%). Pregnancy rates were equivalent in the three groups. The response to metformin was independent of body weight and dose, and nonsmoking was associated with a better ovulatory response overall and lower fasting glucose for CC, and lower androgens for metformin.
Conclusion: Metformin is more effective than CC alone for ovulation induction in PCOS patients, and the response to metformin is independent of body weight and dose. Metformin can be used as a first-line medication for ovulation induction in PCOS patients regardless of their weight and insulin levels due to its efficacy and known safety profile.

title: Pulmonologist involvement, stage-specific treatment, and survival in adults with non-small cell lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
text: The study examined the relationship between pulmonologist management and the likelihood of receiving appropriate treatment and survival in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who also have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The study found that patients who received pulmonologist management were more likely to receive the recommended stage-specific treatment (surgical resection for early-stage NSCLC and chemotherapy for advanced-stage NSCLC) and had better overall survival compared to those who did not receive pulmonologist management. Specifically, the study found that among patients with early-stage NSCLC, 58.5% of those with pulmonologist management received surgical resection, compared to 41.5% of those without pulmonologist management. Similarly, among patients with advanced-stage NSCLC, 43.6% of those with pulmonologist management received chemotherapy, compared to 27.4% of those without pulmonologist management. The study also found that pulmonologist management was associated with reduced mortality risk for patients with early-stage NSCLC, but not for patients with advanced-stage NSCLC. These findings suggest that pulmonologist management may play an important role in improving outcomes for patients with NSCLC and COPD.

title: Divalent cations differentially regulate integrin alphaIIb cytoplasmic tail binding to beta3 and to calcium- and integrin-binding protein.
text:
In this study, we investigated the in vitro complexation and ligand binding capacity of recombinant or synthetic alphaIIb and beta3 integrin cytoplasmic peptides using surface plasmon resonance. Our results showed that alpha.beta heterodimerization occurred in a 1:1 stoichiometry with a weak dissociation constant (KD) in the micromolar range, indicating that the association between the two subunits is weak but stable. The presence of divalent cations did not significantly affect the association between the alphaIIb and beta3 subunits, but did stabilize the complex by decreasing the dissociation rate. We found that mutations in the alphaIIb subunit, specifically the R995A substitution and the KVGFFKR deletion, impaired alpha.beta complexation, while the beta3 subunit mutation (S752P) did not have any significant effect.
We also investigated the binding of recombinant calcium- and integrin-binding protein (CIB) to the alphaIIb cytoplasmic peptide. Our results showed that CIB bound to the alphaIIb peptide in a Ca2+- or Mn2+-independent, one-to-one reaction with a dissociation constant (KD) value of 12 microM. In contrast, the binding of CIB to intact alphaIIbbeta3 occurred preferentially with Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3 conformers, as evidenced by enhanced coimmunoprecipitation of CIB with PAC-1-captured Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3. These findings suggest that Mn2+ activation of intact alphaIIbbeta3 induces the exposure of a CIB-binding site, which is not present in the free alphaIIb peptide. Our results indicate that CIB does not regulate alphaIIbbeta3 inside-out signaling, but rather is involved in a post-receptor occupancy event.

title: Lethal autoimmune myocarditis in interferon-gamma receptor-deficient mice: enhanced disease severity by impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase induction.
text:
Background: Interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) is a crucial cytokine in the regulation of inflammatory responses in autoimmune diseases. However, its role in inflammatory heart disease remains poorly understood.
Methods and Results: We investigated the role of IFN-gamma in inflammatory heart disease by using IFN-gamma receptor-deficient mice (IFN-gammaR(-/-)) on a BALB/c background, which were immunized with a peptide derived from cardiac alpha-myosin heavy chain. Our results showed that IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice developed severe myocarditis with high mortality, which subsided in wild-type mice after 3 weeks. In contrast, IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice showed persistent inflammation, accompanied by robust in vitro CD4 T-cell responses and impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression, as well as evidence of impaired nitric oxide production in IFN-gammaR(-/-) hearts. Treatment of wild-type mice with the nitric oxide synthetase inhibitor N:-nitro-l-arginine-methyl-ester (NNA) enhanced in vitro CD4 T-cell proliferation and prevented healing of myocarditis.
Conclusions: Our findings provide evidence that IFN-gamma protects mice from lethal autoimmune myocarditis by inducing the expression of iNOS, followed by the downregulation of T-cell responses.

title: Association between CYP2D6 polymorphisms and outcomes among women with early stage breast cancer treated with tamoxifen.
text: The study investigated the relationship between the activity of the CYP2D6 enzyme, which is responsible for metabolizing the breast cancer drug tamoxifen, and clinical outcomes in women treated with adjuvant tamoxifen for early-stage breast cancer. The study included 1325 patients from Germany and the US, with diagnoses between 1986 and 2005, and found that the presence of nonfunctional or reduced-function CYP2D6 alleles was associated with worse clinical outcomes, including increased risk of recurrence and poorer event-free and disease-free survival. In contrast, the presence of two functional CYP2D6 alleles was associated with better clinical outcomes. These findings suggest that genetic variation in the CYP2D6 gene may be a useful predictor of response to tamoxifen therapy and could potentially be used to personalize treatment strategies for breast cancer patients.

title: Long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment of injurious parasomnias and other disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep in 170 adults.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the efficacy, dose stability, safety, and abuse potential of long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment for chronic disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep, including injurious sleepwalking and sleep terrors, rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, chronic severe insomnia, and restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movement disorder.
Patients and Methods: Over a 12-year period, one author treated 170 adult patients with nightly benzodiazepine therapy for longstanding, sleep-disruptive disorders for at least 6 months. The patients included 69 with injurious sleepwalking and sleep terrors, 52 with rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, 25 with chronic severe insomnia, and 24 with restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movement disorder.
Results: Complete or substantial control of the sleep disorders was achieved in 146 patients (86%), with 8% experiencing adverse effects requiring medication changes, 2% relapsing into alcohol or chemical abuse requiring hospitalization, and 2% misusing their medications. Of the 136 patients who received clonazepam nightly, the mean dose remained stable over 3.5 years, with no significant difference between the initial and final mean doses (0.77 mg ± 0.46 vs 1.10 mg ± 0.96). Similar results were observed in patients treated with chronic alprazolam and other benzodiazepine treatments.
Conclusion: Long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment of injurious parasomnias and other disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep resulted in sustained efficacy in most cases, with low risk of dosage tolerance, adverse effects, or abuse. However, the study's findings on the treatment of chronic, severe insomnia are not generalizable to typical insomnia patients.

title: Decreased proteasomal activity causes age-related phenotypes and promotes the development of metabolic abnormalities.
text: The proteasome is a multifunctional enzyme complex responsible for the degradation of both normal and damaged proteins, and age-related decline in its activity has been linked to various age-related diseases. However, the exact relationship between decreased proteasomal activity and aging remains unclear due to the lack of suitable animal models. To address this gap, we generated a transgenic (Tg) mouse model with reduced proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity. Tg mice exhibited a shorter lifespan and developed age-related phenotypes, including the accumulation of polyubiquitinated and oxidized proteins, altered expression of cellular proteins such as Bcl-xL and RNase L, and elevated levels of adipose differentiation-related protein (ADRP) in the liver. When Tg mice were fed a high-fat diet, they exhibited more pronounced obesity and hepatic steatosis than wild-type mice, and aged Tg mice had even higher levels of ADRP, suggesting that the metabolic abnormalities in Tg mice mimic those in aged mice. Our findings provide the first in vivo evidence that decreased proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity affects longevity and exacerbates age-related metabolic disorders, such as obesity and hepatic steatosis.

title: Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression suppresses cell proliferation via attenuation of the store-operated calcium influx-mediated signalling pathway in A549 lung cancer cells.
text:
Background: Orai1/CRACM1 is a critical component of store-operated calcium channels, which play a crucial role in regulating calcium influx in response to various stimuli. Store-operated calcium influx is closely linked to inflammatory responses, immune regulation, and cell proliferation. Epidermal growth factor (EGF), a key player in cell proliferation, can activate store-operated calcium channels. However, the consequences of Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression in EGF-mediated lung cancer cell growth remain unclear.
Methods: To investigate the role of Orai1/CRACM1 in EGF-mediated lung cancer cell proliferation, Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids were transfected into cells using lipofection. Cell proliferation was monitored using a cell proliferation assay, immunofluorescence staining, flow cytometry, and real-time polymerase chain reaction. Calcium influx signals were examined using a fluorescent-based calcium assay.
Results: Transfection of Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids inhibited EGF-mediated cell proliferation, accompanied by reduced phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and Akt. The cell cycle modulator p21 was induced, while cyclin D3 expression was decreased. Flow cytometry analysis revealed G0/G1 cell cycle arrest in Orai1/CRACM1-overexpressing cells. Furthermore, Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression significantly attenuated EGF-mediated store-operated calcium influx. Notably, application of 2-APB, a store-operated calcium channel inhibitor, also inhibited EGF-mediated cancer cell proliferation.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression attenuates store-operated calcium influx, which in turn blocks EGF-mediated proliferative signaling and leads to cell cycle arrest. These results provide new insights into the role of Orai1/CRACM1 in lung cancer cell growth and highlight the potential of targeting store-operated calcium channels in cancer therapy.

title: Oxidative stress in cancer associated fibroblasts drives tumor-stroma co-evolution: A new paradigm for understanding tumor metabolism, the field effect and genomic instability in cancer cells.
text: Loss of stromal fibroblast caveolin-1 (Cav-1) is a powerful predictor of poor prognosis in breast cancer patients, associated with early tumor recurrence, lymph node metastasis, and tamoxifen resistance. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we developed a novel co-culture system, proposing a new paradigm to explain the prognostic value of stromal Cav-1. Cancer cells induce oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, aerobic glycolysis, and DNA damage in cancer cells. Specifically, we found that an acute loss of Cav-1 expression in cancer-associated fibroblasts leads to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and aerobic glycolysis. Moreover, defective mitochondria are removed by autophagy/mitophagy induced by oxidative stress. Cancer-associated fibroblasts provide nutrients, such as lactate, to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism in adjacent cancer cells, a phenomenon we term the "Reverse Warburg Effect." Oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts is sufficient to induce genomic instability in adjacent cancer cells, potentially increasing their aggressive behavior, via a bystander effect. We also found that nitric oxide (NO) over-production, secondary to Cav-1 loss, is the root cause of mitochondrial dysfunction in cancer-associated fibroblasts. Treatment with anti-oxidants or NO inhibitors reversed many of the cancer-associated fibroblast phenotypes. Our findings suggest that cancer cells use oxidative stress in adjacent fibroblasts as an "engine" to fuel their own survival and drive their mutagenic evolution towards a more aggressive phenotype. The "field effect" in cancer biology may also be related to the stromal production of ROS and NO species. eNOS-expressing fibroblasts can downregulate Cav-1 and induce mitochondrial dysfunction in adjacent fibroblasts, creating an "oncogenic/mutagenic" field that promotes widespread DNA damage.

title: Telomeres and telomerase: more than the end of the line
text: Early investigations into telomerase suggested that telomeres were maintained through a straightforward yet highly conserved mechanism involving telomerase-mediated replication. However, as research has progressed, it has become evident that this mechanism is not as straightforward as initially thought. It is also clear that, although many species share similar or identical DNA sequences in their telomeres, each species exhibits its own unique characteristics in the way it regulates these sequences and potentially performs additional functions through its telomeric DNA. The striking similarities between telomeres across different species have provided valuable insights into chromosome ends, while the differences have raised equally intriguing questions. This review aims to explore recent studies, the insights they offer, and the questions they raise regarding the complex and diverse nature of telomeres.

title: Reduced osteoblastic population and defective mineralization in osteopetrotic (op/op) mice.
text: Osteopetrotic (op/op) mice exhibit a defect in osteoclast formation due to a lack of macrophage colony-stimulating factor, leading to impaired bone remodeling. In this study, we investigated the femora of op/op mice to determine whether the osteoblastic population and bone mineralization are involved in osteoclasts or their bone resorption. Our findings revealed that the op/op mice exhibited an expanded meshwork of trabecular bones in the chondro-osseous junction to the diaphyseal region. In the femoral metaphyses of op/op mice, intense alkaline phosphatase (ALPase)-positive osteoblasts were observed on the metaphyseal bone in close proximity to the erosion zone of the growth plates. Von Kossa's staining revealed scattered mineralized nodules and a fine meshwork of mineralized bone matrices in the wild-type littermates, while the op/op mice displayed flattened osteoblasts with weak ALPase-positivity and bone surfaces without a covering by osteoblasts. These results suggest that the osteoblastic population and activity were reduced in the op/op diaphyses. Additionally, von Kossa's staining demonstrated patchy unmineralized areas in the op/op diaphyses, indicating that a lower population and/or the activity of osteoblasts resulted in defective mineralization in the bone. Transmission electron microscopy revealed few osteoblasts on the diaphyseal bones, and instead, bone marrow cells and vascular endothelial cells were often attached to the unmineralized bone. Osteocytes were embedded in the unmineralized bone matrix. These findings suggest that osteoclasts are involved in the osteoblastic population and activity as well as subsequent bone mineralization.

title: Interleukin 18 function in atherosclerosis is mediated by the interleukin 18 receptor and the Na-Cl co-transporter
text: Interleukin-18 (IL18) plays a role in atherogenesis through various mechanisms, and its inhibition can reduce atherosclerosis in mice. Our study found that the absence of the IL18 receptor (IL18r) does not affect atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient (Apoe−/−) mice, nor does it affect IL18 cell surface binding or signaling in endothelial cells. Initially, we identified IL18's interaction with the Na-Cl co-transporter (NCC; also known as SLC12A3), a 12-transmembrane-domain ion transporter protein primarily expressed in the kidney. NCC is expressed in atherosclerotic lesions and colocalizes with IL18r. In Apoe−/− mice, combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC, but not single deficiency of either protein, protects mice from atherosclerosis. Peritoneal macrophages from Apoe−/− mice or from Apoe−/− mice lacking IL18r or NCC show IL18 binding and induction of cell signaling and cytokine and chemokine expression, but macrophages from Apoe−/− mice with combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC have a blunted response. An interaction between NCC and IL18r on macrophages was detected by co-immunoprecipitation. IL18 binds to the cell surface of NCC-transfected COS-7 cells, which do not express IL18r, and induces cell signaling and cytokine expression. This study identifies NCC as an IL18-binding protein that collaborates with IL18r in cell signaling, inflammatory molecule expression, and experimental atherogenesis.

title: Notch promotes survival of pre–T cells at the β-selection checkpoint by regulating cellular metabolism
text:
Notch signals are crucial for the functional outcomes of T cell receptor β-selection, including differentiation, proliferation, and rescue from apoptosis. However, the underlying mechanism for this requirement remains unknown. Our study shows that Notch receptor and Delta-like 1 ligand interactions promote the survival of CD4−CD8− pre–T cells by maintaining cell size, glucose uptake, and metabolism. Furthermore, the trophic effects of Notch signaling are mediated by the phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase (PI(3)K) and Akt pathway, which allows expression of active Akt to overcome the requirement for Notch in β-selection. Our results demonstrate the involvement of Notch receptor–ligand interactions in the regulation of cellular metabolism, thereby enabling the autonomous signaling capacity of the pre–T cell receptor complex.
Note: In the initial online version of the article, the term "Atk" was misspelled in the abstract. The correct term is "Akt." Additionally, in the second paragraph of the introduction, the name of the second kinase mentioned, "PI(3)K-dependent kinase 1," was incorrect. The correct name is "phosphoinositide-dependent kinase 1." These errors have been corrected in the HTML and print versions of the article.

title: Blood pressure, salivary cortisol, and inflammatory cytokine outcomes in senior female cancer survivors enrolled in a tai chi chih randomized controlled trial
text:
Older cancer survivors are a vulnerable population due to their heightened risk of developing chronic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, compounded by the effects of cancer treatment and declines in physical functioning. Therefore, interventions that target chronic disease risk factors, such as blood pressure, chronic inflammation, and cortisol levels, are crucial in this population. While tai chi chih (TCC) has been shown to reduce chronic disease risk factors in the general population, its effectiveness in older cancer survivors remains unexplored.
In a feasibility randomized controlled trial, we investigated the impact of TCC on secondary outcomes, including blood pressure, salivary cortisol, and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-4) in older female cancer survivors with physical functioning limitations. Sixty-three participants (mean age: 67 years, SD: 7.15) were randomized to either 12-weeks of TCC or Health Education control (HEC) classes. Resting blood pressure, 1-day salivary cortisol samples, and fasting plasma samples for cytokine multiplex assays were collected at baseline and 1-week post-intervention.
Our findings revealed significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and cortisol area-under-curve (AUC) in the TCC group compared to the HEC group, with SBP decreasing by 10 mmHg (p = 0.002) and cortisol AUC decreasing by 25% (p = 0.02) at post-intervention. However, there was no intervention effect on inflammatory cytokines (p's > 0.05). These results suggest that TCC may be an effective intervention for reducing chronic disease risk factors in older cancer survivors.
While these findings are promising, larger, definitive trials are needed to confirm these results and establish the long-term safety and efficacy of TCC in this population. Nevertheless, our study highlights the potential of TCC as a non-pharmacological intervention to reduce chronic disease risk factors in older cancer survivors, thereby improving their overall health and quality of life.

title: Heart failure admissions in adults with congenital heart disease; risk factors and prognosis.
text:
Background: Heart failure (HF) is a major complication and leading cause of death in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). To determine the frequency of HF-admissions and identify risk factors for both HF-admission and mortality, we analyzed data from the Dutch CONCOR registry linked with hospital discharge and mortality registries.
Methods: We analyzed data from 10,808 adult patients with CHD, with a median follow-up period of 21 years. Risk factors for HF-admission and mortality were assessed using Cox regression models.
Results: Of the total population, 274 patients (2.5%) were admitted for HF during the study period. The incidence of first HF-admission was 1.2 per 1000 patient-years, but the actual incidence of HF is likely higher. Main defect, multiple defects, and surgical interventions in childhood were identified as independent risk factors for HF-admission. Patients admitted for HF had a five-fold higher risk of mortality than patients not admitted (hazard ratio (HR)=5.3; 95% confidence interval 4.2-6.9). One- and three-year mortality after first HF-admission were 24% and 35%, respectively. Independent risk factors for three-year mortality after first HF-admission were male gender, pacemaker implantation, admission duration, non-cardiac medication use, and high serum creatinine.
Conclusions: The incidence of HF-admission in adults with CHD is 1.2 per 1000 patient-years, and mortality risk is significantly increased after HF-admission. Identifying patients at high risk of HF-admission may help with closer follow-up and earlier medical interventions. The presented risk factors may facilitate surveillance and improve patient outcomes.

title: New pathologic classification of lung cancer: relevance for clinical practice and clinical trials.
text:
In 2011, the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC), in collaboration with the American Thoracic Society (ATS) and the European Respiratory Society (ERS), released a new classification system for lung adenocarcinoma. This classification was developed by an international core panel of experts representing IASLC, ATS, and ERS, including oncologists/pulmonologists, pathologists, radiologists, molecular biologists, and thoracic surgeons. The new system aimed to address the significant challenges associated with the diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer, particularly the lack of clear morphological features in tumors previously classified as non-small-cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified.
To address these challenges, the classification system introduced a new approach to small biopsies and cytology, with specific terminology and criteria for distinguishing squamous cell carcinoma from adenocarcinoma, as well as molecular testing for EGFR mutations and ALK rearrangement. In addition, the terms "bronchioloalveolar carcinoma" and "mixed subtype adenocarcinoma" were discontinued, and tumors were classified further using a limited immunohistochemical workup to preserve tissue for molecular testing.
For resected adenocarcinomas, the classification system introduced new concepts of adenocarcinoma in situ and minimally invasive adenocarcinoma, which define patients who, if they undergo complete resection, will have 100% disease-free survival. Invasive adenocarcinomas were classified by predominant pattern after comprehensive histologic subtyping, including lepidic, acinar, papillary, and solid patterns, with the addition of micropapillary as a new histologic subtype with poor prognosis. Former mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinomas were reclassified as "invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma."
The new classification system provides a much-needed standard for pathologic diagnosis not only for patient care but also for clinical trials and TNM classification, as the field of lung cancer is rapidly evolving with new advances occurring frequently, particularly in the molecular arena.

title: Polymorphisms in EGFR and IL28B are associated with spontaneous clearance in an HCV-infected iranian population
text: Although most individuals infected with hepatitis C virus (HCV) will develop chronic infection, approximately 25% are able to clear the virus without any treatment. The aim of the current study was to identify genetic markers associated with spontaneous HCV clearance in a population of Iranian patients. We genotyped 110 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 59 candidate genes in a cohort of 107 individuals who spontaneously cleared HCV infection and 176 individuals whose infection persisted. Three SNPs were found to be associated with HCV outcome (P-values <0.03). Specifically, the SNPs rs11506105 in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene, rs11881222 in the interferon-λ3 (IL28B) gene, and rs12979860 in the IL28B gene were associated with HCV clearance. Using multivariate logistic regression, we found that the A/A genotype in both rs11506105 and rs11881222, and the C/C genotype in rs12979860 were associated with HCV clearance (recessive model: odds ratio = 2.06, 95% confidence interval = 1.09-3.88, P = 0.025; odds ratio = 2.09, 95% confidence interval = 1.23-3.60, P = 0.007; and odds ratio = 1.95, 95% confidence interval = 1.15-3.35, P = 0.014 for rs11506105, rs12979860 and rs11881222, respectively). In conclusion, the EGFR and IL28B SNPs are strong independent predictive markers of spontaneous viral clearance.

title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing variables reflect the degree of diastolic dysfunction in patients with heart failure-normal ejection fraction.
text:
The purpose of the present study was to compare the diagnostic accuracy of echocardiography with tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in patients with heart failure (HF) and normal ejection fraction (NEF). The study included 32 patients with HF-NEF who underwent both echocardiography with TDI and CPX to measure various variables, including the ratio of mitral early velocity to mitral annular velocity (E/E'), ejection fraction, left ventricular (LV) mass, LV end-systolic volume, peak oxygen uptake (VO2), ventilatory efficiency, partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (P(ET)CO2) at rest and peak exercise, and heart rate recovery at 1 minute (HRR1).
The results of the study showed that there was a significant correlation between E/E' and peak VO2, ventilatory efficiency slope, resting P(ET)CO2, peak P(ET)CO2, and HRR1. In contrast, LV mass and LV end-systolic volume were not correlated with any CPX variable. Ejection fraction was correlated with HRR1. An HRR1 threshold of less than 16 beats per minute (higher value positive) was found to effectively identify subjects with an E/E' > 10, which suggests that E/E' provides an accurate reflection of LV filling pressure and insight into diastolic function. The study suggests that CPX provides valuable insight into cardiac dysfunction in patients with HF-NEF and may eventually prove to be a valuable and accepted clinical assessment.

title: Radical prostatectomy for pathological Gleason 8 or greater prostate cancer: influence of concomitant pathological variables.
text:
In this study, we evaluated the long-term outcomes of patients with pathological Gleason score 8 or higher prostate cancer who underwent radical prostatectomy. We analyzed the prognostic significance of various pathological variables, including tumor stage, grade, and DNA ploidy.
Our results showed that overall and progression-free survival at 10 years were 67% and 36%, respectively, and cancer-specific survival was 85%. Adjuvant treatment, pathological stage, preoperative PSA, and pathological grade were significant univariate predictors of progression-free survival. Pathological stage, margin status, and ploidy were also associated with cancer-specific survival. The multivariate analysis revealed that pathological grade (p=0.02), preoperative PSA (p <0.0001), adjuvant therapy (p <0.0001), and pathological stage (p=0.036) were independent predictors of progression-free survival.
Our findings suggest that high-grade prostate cancer can be controlled with radical prostatectomy in some patients with disease confined pathologically, and 10-year cancer-specific survival is 96%. The predictors of outcome in patients with Gleason 8 disease or higher are similar to established predictors derived by using all grades. Although adjuvant hormonal therapy appears to improve disease progression rates after radical prostatectomy, it may not affect prostate cancer death rates within 10 years in patients with high-grade cancer.

title: Successful establishment of long-term bone marrow cultures in 103 patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
text: In this study, we employed bone marrow biopsies instead of mononuclear cells to establish long-term cultures from 103 patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), spanning all five sub-categories, as well as 12 normal controls. By week 4, confluency levels of 30-50% were achieved and maintained for up to 12 weeks with 100% confluency. The predominant cell types observed were fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelial cells, and adipocytes, which were confirmed through immunohistochemical and electron microscopic analysis. Notably, normal hematopoiesis was adequately supported by the MDS stroma. Furthermore, neither the FAB nor cytogenetic classification was found to be correlated with the growth potential of the stroma. Our findings suggest that MDS stroma appears to be both morphologically and functionally normal.

title: [Acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking therapy for post stroke depression:a randomized controlled trial].
text:
Objective: To evaluate the clinical effects of acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking in treating post-stroke depression (PSD).
Methods: Sixty patients with PSD were randomly assigned into two groups: acupuncture plus auricular application (combination group) and medication group, with 30 cases in each. The medication group received 20 mg paroxetine hydrochloride orally once a day for 8 weeks. The combination group received 30-minute acupuncture at specific points (Baihui, Sishencong, Shenting, Yintang, Shenmen, Neiguan, Taichong, Hegu, Zusanli, Sanyinjiao, and Fenglong) once a day and three times a week. Auricular point sticking therapy was applied at Shenmen, Pizhixia, Xin, and Gan for 8 weeks, with pressing 3 times a day and once 3-5 days. Hamilton's Depression Scale (HAMD) scores and Asberg's Antidepressant Side-Effect Rating Scale (SERS) were used to assess the clinical effects before and after treatment.
Results: After treatment, both groups showed a significant decrease in HAMD scores compared to before treatment (P<0.05), with better results in the combination group (P<0.05). The combination group's HAMD scores after treatment were lower than those in the medication group for the anxiety/somatization, sleep disturbance, and hopelessness factors (all P<0.05). The total effective rate of the combination group was 86.7% (26/30), which was higher than the medication group's 66.7% (20/30) (P<0.05). The SERS score of the combination group was also lower than that of the medication group (P<0.05).
Conclusions: Acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking is effective and safe for treating PSD. The combination therapy showed better clinical symptoms and a higher total effective rate than medication alone.

title: Selective enhancement of endothelial BMPR-II with BMP9 reverses pulmonary arterial hypertension
text: Genetic evidence suggests that the loss of bone morphogenetic protein type II receptor (BMPR-II) signaling in the endothelium is an initial factor in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, targeting this signaling pathway directly using BMP ligands has yet to be explored as a therapeutic approach. In this study, we identify BMP9 as the preferred ligand for preventing cell death and enhancing monolayer integrity in both pulmonary arterial endothelial cells and blood outgrowth endothelial cells from individuals with PAH who carry mutations in the BMPR-II gene. We generated a mouse model of PAH by introducing a heterozygous knock-in allele of a human BMPR2 mutation, R899X, which resulted in spontaneous development of PAH. Administration of BMP9 reversed established PAH in these mice, as well as in two other experimental PAH models, in which PAH develops in response to either monocrotaline or VEGF receptor inhibition combined with chronic hypoxia. These findings demonstrate the potential of directly enhancing endothelial BMP signaling as a new therapeutic strategy for PAH.

title: Coordinated actions of SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 for Holliday junction resolution in human cells.
text: Holliday junctions (HJs), four-way DNA intermediates that arise during homologous recombination, are crucial for proper chromosome segregation. The efficient resolution of HJs is essential for maintaining genome stability. Recent studies have identified three structure-selective endonucleases, specifically SLX1-SLX4, MUS81-EME1, and GEN1, that define two distinct pathways for HJ resolution in human cells. The first pathway is mediated by GEN1, while the second pathway, termed SLX-MUS, is orchestrated by the combination of SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1. Depletion of cells lacking the SLX-MUS or GEN1 pathway proteins leads to severe defects in chromosome segregation and reduced survival. Intriguingly, these endonucleases associate with each other in response to CDK-mediated phosphorylation, forming a stable SLX-MUS holoenzyme that can be reconstituted in vitro. Biochemical investigations have revealed that SLX-MUS is a HJ resolvase that coordinates the active sites of two distinct endonucleases during HJ resolution, resulting in a more efficient and orchestrated cleavage reaction compared to the SLX1-SLX4 pathway. Notably, the SLX-MUS pathway exhibits a more precise and targeted cleavage mechanism, as it relies on the coordinated action of two endonucleases to cleave the HJ. In contrast, the SLX1-SLX4 pathway displays a more promiscuous nickase activity that can act on various DNA secondary structures.

title: Prevalence of frequent headache in a population sample.
text: In this study, we aimed to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of frequent headaches in the general population in Baltimore County, Maryland. We conducted a telephone-based survey among 13,343 individuals aged 18-65, and found that 4.1% of the population experienced frequent headaches, with a higher prevalence among Caucasians (4.4%) than African Americans (3.3%). The prevalence of frequent headaches was highest among individuals with the lowest level of education. Among those who experienced frequent headaches, 52% and 56% of females and males, respectively, met the criteria for chronic tension-type headache, while 33% and 25% of females and males, respectively, met the criteria for frequent headache with migrainous features. The remaining 15% of females and 19% of males were unclassified. Notably, 30% of females and 25% of males who experienced frequent headaches met the International Headache Society (IHS) criteria for migraine (with or without aura). Our findings suggest that frequent headache is a common condition in the general population, with variations in prevalence and characteristics among different demographic groups.

title: HTLV-I/II associated disease in England and Wales, 1993-7: retrospective review of serology requests.
text: Besides HIV, two other retroviruses, human T cell leukemia viruses type I (HTLV-I) and type II (HTLV-II), infect humans. HTLV-I is prevalent in Japan, the Caribbean, Africa, and Melanesia, and is found among immigrants from these regions in Europe. HTLV-I infection is associated with a 1-5% lifetime risk of adult T cell leukemia/lymphoma, a 0.25% lifetime risk of HTLV-I associated myelopathy, and other inflammatory conditions such as uveitis, alveolitis, and arthritis. HTLV-II is endemic in some native American and African populations and among injecting drug users, and has been linked to neurological disease. Between 1986 and 1992, 100 cases of HTLV-I associated myelopathy and 44 cases of adult T cell leukemia/lymphoma were diagnosed in the United Kingdom. Adult T cell leukemia/lymphoma was first described in 1977, and patients with this condition have a mean life expectancy of only six months, so most of the 44 cases were likely incident cases.

title: Lentiviral vector design and imaging approaches to visualize the early stages of cellular reprogramming.
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) can be generated from somatic cells by introducing reprogramming transcription factors through gene transfer. The efficiency of iPSC formation is influenced by the expression levels of these factors, but additional stochastic cell-intrinsic factors also play a role. In this study, we developed engineered lentiviral vectors that co-express reprogramming factors with a strong retroviral promoter, which is rapidly silenced in iPSCs. We used fluorescence microscopy and long-term single cell tracking to analyze the conversion of fibroblasts to iPSCs, and found that vector silencing typically occurs before or simultaneously with the induction of the Oct4-EGFP pluripotency marker. Around 7 days post-transduction, a subfraction of cells in clonal colonies expressed Oct4-EGFP and rapidly expanded. Single cell tracking of iPSC colonies revealed that stochastic epigenetic changes are necessary for reprogramming. Additionally, we found that iPSC colonies may emerge as a genetic mosaic originating from different clusters. The use of improved vector design with continuous cell tracking provides a powerful tool to explore the subtle dynamics of early reprogramming events.

title: EIF2AK3, encoding translation initiation factor 2-α kinase 3, is mutated in patients with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome
text: Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS) is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by insulin-dependent diabetes that occurs in infancy or early childhood, along with other multisystemic manifestations such as epiphyseal dysplasia, osteoporosis, growth retardation, hepatic and renal dysfunction, mental retardation, and cardiovascular abnormalities. Based on analysis of two consanguineous families, we mapped the WRS gene to a region of less than 3 cM on chromosome 2p12, with highest linkage evidence and homozygosity at four microsatellite markers within an interval of approximately 1 cM. The gene encoding the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2-α kinase 3 (EIF2AK3) resides in this interval, and we identified distinct mutations of EIF2AK3 that segregated with the disorder in each of the families. The first mutation results in a truncated protein lacking the entire catalytic domain, while the other mutation affects an highly conserved amino acid in the catalytic domain of the protein.
