Our findings provide evidence for the role of EIF2AK3 in WRS and may offer insights into the etiology of more common forms of diabetes and other manifestations of the disorder.

title: Beta oscillations in a large-scale sensorimotor cortical network: directional influences revealed by Granger causality.
text: Previous studies have shown that synchronized beta frequency (14-30 Hz) oscillations in the primary motor cortex are involved in maintaining steady contractions of contralateral arm and hand muscles. However, little is known about the role of postcentral cortical areas in motor maintenance and their patterns of interaction with motor cortex. To investigate these questions, we conducted a study in which two monkeys performed a visual discrimination task while we recorded the activity of neurons in the pre- and postcentral areas of their brain. Using power and coherence spectral analysis, we identified a beta-synchronized large-scale network linking pre- and postcentral areas. We then used Granger causality spectra to measure the directional influences among recording sites. Our results showed that primary somatosensory cortex exerted strong Granger causal influences on both motor cortex and inferior posterior parietal cortex, while motor cortex had weak Granger causal influences on postcentral sites in one monkey, and no Granger causal influences in the other. These findings are the first to demonstrate in awake monkeys that synchronized beta oscillations bind multiple sensorimotor areas into a large-scale network during motor maintenance behavior and carry Granger causal influences from primary somatosensory and inferior posterior parietal cortices to motor cortex.

title: Aging, frailty and age-related diseases
text: The concept of frailty has evolved over time based on the clinical experience of geriatricians, and is now recognized as a distinct medical syndrome. Frailty is a state of vulnerability that reflects multisystem physiological changes, which may not always lead to a specific life-threatening illness. Current thinking suggests that both physical, psychological, cognitive, and social factors contribute to frailty, and must be taken into account in its definition and treatment. These signs and symptoms are thought to reflect a reduced functional reserve and decreased adaptation (resilience) to stressors, leading to increased risk of physical and cognitive decline, disability, and death. The characteristics of frailty can be applied to the aging process itself, and there is little consensus in the literature on the specific physiological/biological pathways associated with frailty. However, it is widely accepted that heightened chronic systemic inflammation plays a major role in the development of frailty. This review will examine the relationship between aging, frailty, and age-related diseases, and will explore possible interventions to reduce the occurrence and impact of frailty in elderly individuals.

title: A case of paraquat intoxication caused by intravenous injection.
text: Paraquat intoxication is a life-threatening condition, and most cases occur through oral ingestion. However, we report a fatal case of paraquat intoxication following intravenous injection. There is limited clinical data on the effects of parenteral paraquat exposure, and we describe this case and its tragic outcome. Toxic symptoms and severe organ dysfunction developed rapidly after injection. Despite aggressive treatment with repeated activated charcoal hemoperfusion, pulse steroids, cyclophosphamide, and antioxidants, the patient tragically succumbed to multiple organ failure just three days after intoxication. This case highlights the extreme danger of paraquat intoxication via intravenous injection, even in small amounts, and underscores the need for urgent medical attention in such situations.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and CR1 associated with Alzheimer's disease
text: The gene encoding apolipoprotein E (APOE) on chromosome 19 is the only confirmed susceptibility locus for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. To identify additional risk loci, we conducted a large genome-wide association study of 2,032 individuals from France with Alzheimer's disease (cases) and 5,328 controls. Markers outside APOE with suggestive evidence of association (P < 10−5) were examined in collections from Belgium, Finland, Italy, and Spain, totaling 3,978 Alzheimer's disease cases and 3,297 controls. Two loci showed replicated evidence of association: one within CLU (also called APOJ), encoding clusterin or apolipoprotein J, on chromosome 8 (rs11136000, OR = 0.86, 95% CI 0.81–0.90, P = 7.5 × 10−9 for combined data), and the other within CR1, encoding the complement component (3b/4b) receptor 1, on chromosome 1 (rs6656401, OR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.14–1.29, P = 3.7 × 10−9 for combined data). Previous biological studies support roles for CLU and CR1 in the clearance of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptide, the primary component of amyloid plaques, which are one of the major brain lesions of individuals with Alzheimer's disease.

title: Identification and characterization of subpopulations in undifferentiated ES cell culture.
text: Embryonic stem (ES) cells are derived from the inner cell mass (ICM) and epiblast and are characterized by the expression of Oct3/4 and Rex1 genes, which are used as markers to identify undifferentiated cells. To investigate whether ES cells constitute a homogeneous population or a heterogeneous mixture of cells at different stages of differentiation, we generated knock-in ES cell lines with fluorescent protein genes inserted into the Rex1 and Oct3/4 gene loci. Our findings revealed that undifferentiated ES cells consist of at least two distinct populations, Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells and Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells. These populations can convert into each other in the presence of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF). We found that Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells predominantly differentiate into primitive ectoderm and contribute to chimera formation, while Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells differentiate into somatic cell types more efficiently and have poor ability to contribute to chimera formation. These results confirm that undifferentiated ES cell cultures contain subpopulations corresponding to ICM, epiblast, and primitive ectoderm.

title: Isolation of intact nuclei of high purity from mouse liver.
text:
Current methods of nuclear isolation from liver involve disrupting the plasma membrane via homogenization and separating the nuclei through high centrifugal force (HCF) gradients of sucrose or other substances for up to 80 minutes. However, prolonged use of HCF can lead to nuclear damage and degradation by endogenous proteases. To address this limitation, we compared four modified nuclear isolation methods:
1. Gently crushing mouse liver through a fine mesh without in vivo perfusion with collagenase.
2. Gently crushing mouse liver through a fine mesh with in vivo perfusion with collagenase.
3. Centrifuging the cell suspension at moderate centrifugal force (MCF, 16,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
4. Centrifuging the cell suspension at high centrifugal force (HCF, 70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
We evaluated the purity of the isolated nuclei using biological and morphological analyses of representative marker proteins for nuclei and cytoplasm. Our results showed that MCF and no collagenase provided the highest nuclear integrity and purity, while MCF with collagenase is a viable option if yield is prioritized. This method is particularly suitable for small sample sizes and should facilitate studies with human liver biopsies and livers from mice, the most commonly used species for gene targeting.

title: Two structurally independent domains of E. coli NusG create regulatory plasticity via distinct interactions with RNA polymerase and regulators.
text: NusG is a conserved protein that modulates transcription by interacting with elongation complexes (ECs) of RNA polymerase, DNA, and RNA. In Escherichia coli, NusG suppresses pausing and increases elongation rate, enhances termination by E. coli rho and phage HK022 Nun protein, and promotes antitermination by lambdaN and in ribosomal RNA operons. Using NMR studies, we found that E. coli NusG consists of two largely independent structural domains, NTD and CTD, respectively. Our in vivo and in vitro experiments revealed that NTD alone is sufficient to suppress pausing and enhance transcript elongation, while neither domain alone can enhance rho-dependent termination or support antitermination. We propose that the two domains of NusG mediate distinct interactions with ECs, with the NTD interacting with RNA polymerase and the CTD interacting with rho and other regulators, allowing NusG to effect different regulatory outcomes.

title: Cytochemistry and C-values: the less-well-known world of nuclear DNA amounts.
text:
In the plant sciences, two main techniques are used to measure nuclear DNA content: Feulgen absorbance cytophotometry and flow cytometry (FCM). While FCM has gained popularity among plant scientists, traditional absorbance-cytophotometric methods are gradually losing ground. This narrowing of the methodological repertoire is undesirable and can lead to a loss of valuable data. Both techniques have their advantages, but static cytophotometry faces instrumental difficulties and material-based problems, which can result in less reliable data than FCM.
The purpose of this article is to provide a selective overview of the field of nuclear DNA content measurement, with a focus on the technical challenges posed by the characteristics of the biological material and the photometric aspects of the work. For over 20 years, it has been known that plant polyphenols can interfere with Feulgen DNA cytophotometry, leading to unreliable results. However, little is known about the chemical classes of plant metabolites that can interfere with DNA staining and the mechanisms of their inhibition. Plant slimes are another source of concern.
Recently, research has begun to uncover the effects of secondary metabolites on FCM results. In particular, the analysis of intraspecific genome size variation requires a stringent methodology that accounts for inhibitors. FCM tests for inhibitory effects of endogenous metabolites should become obligatory. Using dry seeds for harvesting embryo and endosperm nuclei for FCM and Feulgen densitometry may provide a means of circumventing staining inhibitors. The importance of internal standardization is highlighted. The goal of this article is to improve our understanding of phytochemical/cytochemical interactions in plant DNA photometry, which is essential for the growing list of plant genome sizes.

title: Integrins and cell proliferation: regulation of cyclin-dependent kinases via cytoplasmic signaling pathways.
text: Cell cycle progression in mammalian cells is tightly regulated by both integrin-mediated adhesion to the extracellular matrix and by growth factor binding to their receptors. This regulation is mediated by G1 phase cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs), which are downstream of signaling pathways that are under the coordinated control of both integrins and growth factor receptors. Recent discoveries have revealed a remarkable diversity of integrin-dependent signals that are channeled into the regulation of G1 phase CDKs. The regulation of cyclin D1 by the ERK pathway may serve as a paradigm for elucidating how cell adhesion influences cell cycle progression.

title: Interplay between microtubule bundling and sorting factors ensures acentriolar spindle stability during C. elegans oocyte meiosis
text: In various species, oocyte meiosis occurs without the presence of centrioles. As a result, the mechanisms of microtubule organization, spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation are distinct and unique. In this study, we investigate the underlying principles of this specialized form of cell division by examining the kinesin-14 family of proteins, specifically KLP-15 and KLP-16, in the acentriolar oocyte spindle of C. elegans. These proteins promote microtubule bundling during spindle assembly, but following depletion, microtubule bundles collapse into a disorganized array. However, surprisingly, microtubules are able to reorganize during anaphase and form a bundled array that facilitates chromosome segregation. This phenomenon allows us to identify factors that promote microtubule organization during anaphase, whose contributions are normally undetectable in wild-type worms. We find that SPD-1 (PRC1) bundles microtubules and KLP-18 (kinesin-12) sorts those bundles into a functional orientation capable of mediating chromosome segregation. Our studies reveal an interplay between distinct mechanisms that together promote spindle formation and chromosome segregation in the absence of structural cues such as centrioles.

title: Development of a questionnaire to measure heart disease risk knowledge in people with diabetes: the Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire.
text: This paper presents a questionnaire designed to assess heart disease risk knowledge in individuals with diabetes. The Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire (HDFQ) is a 25-item survey that taps into respondents' knowledge of major risk factors for developing coronary heart disease (CHD). Approximately half of the items specifically address diabetes-related CHD risk factors. Based on pilot data, the current study analyzed responses from 524 individuals with diabetes to evaluate the psychometric properties of the HDFQ. The questionnaire is readable for an average 13-year-old and imposes minimal burden, with good content and face validity. It demonstrates adequate internal consistency (Kuder-Richardson-20 formula = 0.77) and good item-total correlations. Item analysis revealed a desirable range of P-values, and discriminant function analyses showed that HDFQ scores differentiated respondents based on their knowledge of their own cardiovascular health, use of lipid-lowering medications, health insurance status, and educational attainment, indicating good criterion-related validity. The HDFQ is a brief, understandable, and easy-to-administer measure of heart disease risk knowledge, with potential for use in both research and practice. Future research should establish norms and investigate the questionnaire's test-retest reliability and predictive validity.

title: Prevalence of Multiple Sclerosis in Isfahan, Iran
text: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence varies globally, with Iran considered to have a low prevalence. Objective: To estimate the period prevalence and risk factors of MS in Isfahan, central Iran. Methods: A cross-sectional case register study conducted from 2004 to 2005 included all patients with definite MS in Isfahan, identified through the Isfahan MS Association and provincial records. Demographic and case-related data were collected through interviews and questionnaires. Population data were obtained from the 1999 Iran Census. Participants' mean age was 32.5 years (9.3), with a mean disease duration of 6.4 years for men and 6.9 years for women. Results: The period prevalence of MS was 35.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 33.6–37.3) in a population of 3,923,255, with a higher prevalence in women (54.5%, 95% CI: 51.1–57.8) compared to men (14.9%, 95% CI: 13.3–16.6). The female/male ratio was 3.6 (95% CI: 3.2–4.1). The direct age-adjusted period prevalence was 59.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 44.8–75.2) for women and 17.0 per 100,000 (95% CI: 8.9–25.1) for men. MS rates were highest among 30- to 39-year-olds and decreased with increasing age. Sensory and visual disturbances were the most common initial presentations, with a prevalence of 51.1% (95% CI: 48.4–53.7) and 47.0% (95% CI: 44.4–49.7), respectively. Conclusion: Isfahan has a medium to high risk of MS, contrasting with the gradient hypothesis.

title: A kinetochore-independent mechanism drives anaphase chromosome separation during acentrosomal meiosis
text: Although the assembly of acentrosomal meiotic spindles has been extensively studied, little is known about the separation of chromosomes on these spindles. In this study, we investigate the role of the kinetochore protein KNL-1 in directing the assembly of meiotic kinetochores in Caenorhabditis elegans oocytes. Our findings reveal that, unlike mitosis, chromosome separation during meiotic anaphase is kinetochore-independent. Prior to anaphase, meiotic kinetochores and spindle poles disassemble, along with the microtubules on the poleward side of chromosomes. During anaphase, microtubules then form between the separating chromosomes. Our functional analysis implicates a set of proteins that localize to a ring-shaped domain between kinetochores during pre-anaphase spindle assembly and anaphase separation. These proteins are localized by the chromosomal passenger complex, which regulates the loss of meiotic chromosome cohesion. Therefore, meiotic segregation in C. elegans is a two-stage process, where kinetochores orient chromosomes, but are then dispensable for their separation. We propose that separation is controlled by a meiosis-specific chromosomal domain to coordinate cohesin removal and chromosome segregation.

title: Association between the Medicare Modernization Act of 2003 and patient wait times and travel distance for chemotherapy.
text:
Background: The Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003 (MMA) altered reimbursements for outpatient chemotherapy drugs and drug administration services. Anecdotal reports suggest that these adjustments may have negatively affected access to chemotherapy for Medicare beneficiaries. This study aims to compare patient wait times and travel distances for chemotherapy before and after the enactment of the MMA.
Methods: This study analyzed a nationally representative 5% sample of claims from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for the period 2003 through 2006. The study population consisted of Medicare beneficiaries with incident breast cancer, colorectal cancer, leukemia, lung cancer, or lymphoma who received chemotherapy in inpatient hospital, institutional outpatient, or physician office settings. The main outcome measures were days from incident diagnosis to first chemotherapy visit and distance traveled for treatment, controlling for age, sex, race/ethnicity, cancer type, geographic region, comorbid conditions, and year of diagnosis and treatment.
Results: The study included 5082 incident cases of breast cancer, colorectal cancer, leukemia, lung cancer, or lymphoma in 2003; 5379 cases in 2004; 5116 cases in 2005; and 5288 cases in 2006. Approximately 70% of patients received treatment in physician office settings in each year. Although the distribution of treatment settings in 2004 and 2005 was not significantly different from 2003 (P = .24 and P = .72, respectively), there was a small but significant change from 2003 to 2006 (P = .02). The proportion of patients receiving chemotherapy in inpatient settings decreased from 10.2% in 2003 to 8.8% in 2006 (P = .03), and the proportion in institutional outpatient settings increased from 21.1% to 22.5% (P = .004). The proportion in physician offices remained at 68.7% (P = .29). The median time from diagnosis to initial chemotherapy visit was 28 days in 2003, 27 days in 2004, 29 days in 2005, and 28 days in 2006. In multivariate analyses, average wait times for chemotherapy were 1.96 days longer in 2005 than in 2003 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.11-3.80 days; P = .04) but not significantly different in 2006 (0.88 days; 95% CI, -0.96 to 2.71 days; P = .35). Median travel distance was 7 miles (11.2 km) in 2003 and 8 miles (12.8 km) in 2004 through 2006. After adjustment, average travel distance remained slightly longer in 2004 (1.47 miles [2.35 km]; 95% CI, 0.87-2.07 miles [1.39-3.31 km]; P < .001), 2005 (1.19 miles [1.90 km]; 95% CI, 0.58-1.80 miles [0.93-2.88 km]; P < .001), and 2006 (1.30 miles [2.08 km]; 95% CI, 0.69-1.90 miles [1.10-3.04 km]; P < .001) compared with 2003.
Conclusion: This study found no major changes in travel distance and patient wait times for chemotherapy in the Medicare population since 2003, the year before MMA-related changes in reimbursement. These findings suggest that the MMA may not have had a significant impact on access to chemotherapy for Medicare beneficiaries.

title: 20-year outcomes following conservative management of clinically localized prostate cancer.
text:
The appropriate treatment for men with clinically localized prostate cancer remains uncertain, as a recent study suggests an increasing prostate cancer mortality rate for men who are alive more than 15 years following diagnosis. To investigate this further, we conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using data from the Connecticut Tumor Registry, supplemented by hospital records and histology reviews of 767 men aged 55 to 74 years with clinically localized prostate cancer diagnosed between January 1, 1971, and December 31, 1984. These men were treated with either observation or immediate or delayed androgen withdrawal therapy, with a median observation time of 24 years. Our main outcome measures were the probability of mortality from prostate cancer or other competing medical conditions, based on a patient's age at diagnosis and tumor grade.
Our results showed that the prostate cancer mortality rate was 33 per 1000 person-years during the first 15 years of follow-up (95% confidence interval [CI], 28-38) and 18 per 1000 person-years after 15 years of follow-up (95% CI, 10-29). These mortality rates were not statistically different after adjusting for differences in tumor histology (rate ratio, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.6-1.9). Men with low-grade prostate cancers (Gleason score of 2-4) had a minimal risk of dying from prostate cancer during 20 years of follow-up (6 deaths per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 2-11). In contrast, men with high-grade prostate cancers (Gleason score of 8-10) had a high probability of dying from prostate cancer within 10 years of diagnosis (121 deaths per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 90-156). Men with Gleason score of 5 or 6 tumors had an intermediate risk of prostate cancer death.
Our findings suggest that the annual mortality rate from prostate cancer appears to remain stable after 15 years from diagnosis, which does not support aggressive treatment for localized low-grade prostate cancer.

title: Role of beta adrenergic receptor polymorphisms in heart failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: Heart Failure (HF) is a prevalent condition characterized by significant morbidity and mortality. The beta adrenergic receptor (betaAR) pathway plays a crucial role in regulating cardiac function, and chronic activation of the beta(1)AR subtype has been implicated in the development and progression of HF. betaAR blockade has been shown to improve survival in patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Variations in the genes encoding beta adrenergic receptors (ADRB) have been associated with HF phenotypes and pharmacogenetic interactions with beta blockers. However, these associations have not been consistently replicated. A meta-analysis of three studies examining the effect of the ADRB1 Arg389Gly polymorphism on left ventricular remodeling with beta blockers found a 5% improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction in homozygous Arg389 individuals. This study provides evidence of a different functional response to beta blockers associated with this polymorphism. As more molecular evidence emerges, it may be possible to identify patients who are at increased risk of developing HF, whose HF will progress rapidly, or who are unlikely to benefit from beta blockers. Such patients may benefit from targeted, aggressive therapy.

title: New development of the yolk sac theory in diabetic embryopathy: molecular mechanism and link to structural birth defects.
text: Maternal diabetes mellitus poses a significant risk for structural birth defects, including congenital heart defects and neural tube defects, due to the rising prevalence of type 2 diabetes and obesity among women of childbearing age. In vitro and in vivo studies have shown that high glucose levels damage the cells and organelles of the yolk sac, leading to injuries that impair nutrient transportation and increase the risk of birth defects. Recent studies have identified key molecular intermediates involved in diabetic yolk sac vasculopathy, including hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1, and its inhibitor thioredoxin-1, c-Jun-N-terminal kinases, nitric oxide, and nitric oxide synthase. Dietary supplementation with fatty acids has been shown to reduce diabetes mellitus-induced malformations. While the role of the human yolk in embryogenesis is less extensive than in rodents, human embryonic vasculogenesis is still affected negatively by maternal diabetes mellitus. Mechanistic studies have identified potential therapeutic targets for future intervention against yolk sac vasculopathy, birth defects, and other complications associated with diabetic pregnancies.

title: Hepatitis B and C in HIV-infected patients. Prevalence and prognostic value.
text:
BACKGROUND/AIMS:
There is limited information on the prevalence and impact of coinfection with hepatitis B or C on the clinical course of patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
METHODS: We conducted a follow-up study in 232 HIV-infected patients (age 37±8 years, CD4 count 167±167 microl; 46% had AIDS) and investigated their samples for markers of HBV and HCV infection (HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV-DNA, Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, anti-HCV, HCV-RNA).
RESULTS: Our results showed that 23% of the patients were anti-HCV positive, and 9% suffered from chronic HBV infection (HBsAg positive). Of these, 82% had detectable HBeAg and 86% had HBV-DNA. The presence of HCV-RNA, HBeAg, and amount of HBV-DNA were found to be related to the degree of immunodeficiency. In contrast to the control group without HBV or HCV infection, patients infected with HIV and either HBV or HCV showed a direct correlation between a reduction in CD4 counts and decreased cholinesterase activity. In patients with AIDS, coinfection with HBV or HCV was associated with a reduced survival compared to controls (HBV: 212 days, 95%CI, 106-317; HCV: 267, 95%CI, 112-396; controls: 439 days, 95%CI, 364-513).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that coinfection of HIV and HBV or HCV is common and is associated with a reduced survival rate in HIV-infected patients, particularly in those with AIDS.

title: Requirement of endogenous stem cell factor and granulocyte-colony-stimulating factor for IL-17-mediated granulopoiesis.
text: IL-17 is a novel cytokine that specifically targets CD4+ T cells and stimulates hematopoiesis, leading to an increase in mature granulocytes in vivo. In this study, we found that IL-17-mediated granulopoiesis requires the release of G-CSF and the presence or induction of the transmembrane form of stem cell factor (SCF) for optimal granulopoiesis. However, IL-17 also protects mice from G-CSF neutralization-induced neutropenia, suggesting that there is a SCF/G-CSF-independent effect of IL-17 on splenic granulopoiesis. Interestingly, while G-CSF neutralization completely reversed IL-17-induced BM progenitor expansion, the reduction in splenic CFU-GM/CFU-granulocyte-erythrocyte-megakaryocyte-monocyte colonies was only 50% in both Sl/Sld and littermate control mice, indicating that there is a significant SCF/G-CSF-independent effect of IL-17 on splenic granulopoiesis. These findings suggest that IL-17 may have potential as a therapeutic agent for modulating hematopoiesis and host defense.

title: The expression of immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) is differentially induced by retinoic acids in NB4 and KG1 cells: possible implication in the distinct phenotype of retinoic acid-responsive and -resistant leukemic cells
text: In a cell-type and stimulus-specific manner, the early response gene immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) is involved in growth regulation and modulation of apoptosis. The current study demonstrates that, in two acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) cell lines, NB4 and KG1, exhibiting distinct sensitivity to retinoic acids (RAs), IEX-1 expression is rapidly induced (within 30-60 minutes) by all-trans- or cis-RA, independently of other signal transduction mediators, such as TNFα, NF-κB, or MAP kinases. In NB4 cells (expressing PML-RARα), this increase in IEX-1 expression is transient and completely reversible, accompanied by a cell cycle arrest, ongoing differentiation, and reduced sensitivity to anti-cancer drug-induced apoptosis. In contrast, the RA-induced IEX-1 expression in KG1 cells (expressing PLZF-RARα) persists over several days, along with continued cell cycle progression and enhanced apoptotic sensitivity. Furthermore, two functional RA response elements in the IEX-1 promoter were identified through gel shift and luciferase reporter gene assays. IEX-1 may be a unique transcriptional target of the two X-RARα fusion receptors, which exhibit distinct responsiveness to RAs. Following different time courses of direct transcriptional induction by PML-RARα and PLZF-RARα in NB4 and KG1 cells, respectively, IEX-1 expression may be involved in the distinct actions of these receptors and the phenotypes of APL cells.

title: Comorbidity between ADHD and obesity: exploring shared mechanisms and clinical implications.
text: Recent studies suggest a connection between Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and obesity. In this review, we systematically examine and critically evaluate the available evidence on the prevalence of ADHD in obese individuals and the weight status of those with ADHD. We searched PubMed, PsychInfo, and ISI Web of Science for relevant articles from January 1980 to June 2010. Our findings indicate that there is a high prevalence of ADHD in clinical samples of individuals seeking treatment for obesity. Moreover, available studies show that individuals with ADHD have higher-than-average body mass index (BMI) z scores and/or a significantly higher prevalence of obesity compared to those without ADHD. Three possible mechanisms underlying the association between ADHD and obesity have been proposed: 1) it is possible that obesity and/or factors associated with it (such as sleep-disordered breathing) manifest as ADHD-like symptoms; 2) ADHD and obesity share common biological dysfunctions; and 3) ADHD contributes to obesity. Our findings suggest that screening for ADHD in patients with obesity and looking for abnormal eating behaviors as possible contributing factors of obesity in patients with ADHD may be noteworthy. Additionally, appropriate treatment of ADHD may improve the weight status of individuals with both obesity and ADHD, based on preliminary findings.

title: Rapamycin treatment augments motor neuron degeneration in SOD1(G93A) mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
text: Abnormal protein misfolding may contribute to the development of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but the underlying mechanisms are still unclear. Our previous research has shown that autophagy is altered in the mouse model of ALS. In this study, we investigated the correlation between autophagic alterations and motor neuron (MN) degeneration in ALS mice. We found that the autophagic protein marker LC3-II is significantly increased in the spinal cord MNs of ALS mice, and electron microscopy and immunochemistry studies revealed the accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in dystrophic axons of spinal cord MNs. These changes were observed in ALS mice at 90 days of age, when they display mild clinical symptoms, and became more pronounced at 120 days. The clinical symptoms were found to correlate with the progression of MN degeneration. Interestingly, we also found that the autophagy-related protein p62/SQSTM1 accumulates progressively in the spinal cord of ALS mice, suggesting impaired autophagic flux. Surprisingly, treatment with autophagy enhancer rapamycin accelerated MN degeneration, shortened the lifespan of ALS mice, and had no effect on SOD1 aggregate accumulation. Moreover, rapamycin treatment in ALS mice led to more severe mitochondrial impairment, higher Bax levels, and greater caspase-3 activation, suggesting that selective degeneration of MNs is associated with impairment of the autophagy pathway and that rapamycin treatment may exacerbate the pathological process through apoptosis and other mechanisms in ALS mice.

title: Improvements in survival and clinical benefit with gemcitabine as first-line therapy for patients with advanced pancreas cancer: a randomized trial.
text:
The purpose of this clinical trial was to compare the effectiveness of gemcitabine and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) in treating advanced pancreas cancer, with a focus on improving disease-related symptoms and survival.
One hundred twenty-six patients with advanced pancreas cancer were enrolled in the study and underwent a lead-in period to stabilize their pain levels. They were then randomly assigned to receive either gemcitabine (1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 weeks, followed by a rest period, and then weekly for 3 cycles every 4 weeks) or 5-FU (600 mg/m2 weekly). The primary outcome measure was clinical benefit response, which involved assessments of pain (analgesic consumption and pain intensity), Karnofsky performance status, and weight. Other measures of efficacy included response rate, time to progressive disease, and survival.
The results showed that gemcitabine was more effective than 5-FU in improving disease-related symptoms. Specifically, 23.8% of gemcitabine-treated patients experienced clinical benefit response compared to 4.8% of 5-FU-treated patients (P = 0.0022). Additionally, gemcitabine-treated patients had a median survival duration of 5.65 months, compared to 4.41 months for 5-FU-treated patients (P = 0.0025). The 12-month survival rate was 18% for gemcitabine patients and 2% for 5-FU patients. Treatment was generally well tolerated.
In conclusion, this study suggests that gemcitabine is more effective than 5-FU in improving symptoms and survival in patients with advanced pancreas cancer. These findings support the use of gemcitabine as a treatment option for this patient population.

title: Endothelial-myofibroblast transition contributes to the early development of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice.
text:
Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of chronic kidney disease. Myofibroblasts play a crucial role in the production and secretion of extracellular matrix in diabetic renal fibrosis. Recent evidence suggests that endothelial cells may undergo a transformation into myofibroblasts under both normal and abnormal conditions. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate whether endothelial-myofibroblast transition occurs in diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis and contributes to its development.
To induce diabetes, we used streptozotocin in Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP mice, a genetically modified mouse line that allows us to trace endothelial cells. We also studied the endothelial-myofibroblast transition in MMECs (a mouse pancreatic microvascular endothelial cell line) and primary cultures of CD31+/EYFP- (enhanced yellow fluorescent protein) endothelial cells isolated from adult normal alpha-smooth muscle actin promoter-driven-EYFP (alpha-SMA/EYFP) mouse kidneys.
Using confocal microscopy, we found that 10.4 ± 4.2 and 23.5 ± 7.4% of renal interstitial myofibroblasts (alpha-SMA+) in 1- and 6-month streptozotocin-induced diabetic kidneys were of endothelial origin (EGFP+/alpha-SMA+ cells), compared to only 0.2 ± 0.1% of myofibroblasts in vehicle-treated Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP mice (P < 0.01). Additionally, real-time PCR and confocal microscopy showed that transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 induced de novo expression of alpha-SMA and loss of expression of VE-cadherin and CD31 in MMECs and primary cultures of renal endothelial cells in a time- and dose-dependent fashion.
Our findings demonstrate that the endothelial-myofibroblast transition occurs and contributes to the early development and progression of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis. These results suggest that targeting the endothelial-myofibroblast transition may be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of diabetic nephropathy.

title: Effect of phosducin silencing on the photokinetic motile response of Blepharisma japonicum.
text: The coloured ciliate Blepharisma japonicum exhibits changes in swimming velocity (positive photokinesis) and elongation of its body in response to prolonged illumination. Recently, we proposed that alterations in the phosphorylation level of the ciliate phosducin (Pdc) may be involved in light-induced cell elongation, which in turn affects the interaction of βγ-dimer of G-proteins (Gβγ) with β-tubulin and subsequent cytoskeletal remodeling. The cellular mechanism underlying the photokinetic effect in this ciliate remains unelucidated. In the present study, we employed real-time PCR to investigate the levels of ciliate Pdc mRNA in cells treated with Pdc-RNAi, compared to control cells fed with bacteria carrying the empty vector. Western immunoblotting was used to confirm that Pdc-RNAi-treated cells expressed lower levels of the Pdc protein. The assay also revealed that in ciliates treated with Pdc-RNAi and exposed to light, the cytosolic level of Gβ (~36 kDa) was reduced, while the level of Gβ localized to the membrane (~32 kDa) was increased compared to control cells. Additionally, behavioral analysis of the cells indicated a significant reduction in photokinesis. The findings of this study provide further characterization of the functional properties of the ciliate Pdc protein and suggest a likely role for this phosphoprotein in the photokinetic phenomenon of the ciliate protist Blepharisma.

title: Alzheimer’s disease and NGF signaling
text: Age-related degeneration of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (BFCNs) occurs early and significantly contributes to cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Proper function and morphology of BFCNs rely on the supply of nerve growth factor (NGF) from the cortex and hippocampus. A wealth of experiments have demonstrated that decreased NGF supply at the level of BFCN cell bodies leads to loss of neuronal markers and shrinkage, mimicking the hallmarks of AD. The delivery of sufficient NGF to BFCN cell bodies depends on various factors, including adequate synthesis and release of NGF, expression of NGF receptors by BFCNs, normal signaling and retrograde transport of NGF-receptor complex, and effective gene expression induction by NGF. Recent research has shown that decreased NGF levels in BFCN cell bodies are primarily due to impaired retrograde transport rather than decreased synthesis, binding, or expression of NGF receptors in BFCN terminals. We will discuss in vivo evidence supporting this conclusion in a mouse model of BFCN degeneration and compare these findings to our postmortem human AD brain studies. We will speculate on the possible mechanisms underlying failed NGF retrograde transport and its relationship to AD pathology.

title: Echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular hypertrophy: comparison to necropsy findings.
text: In this study, the accuracy of echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) dimension and mass for detecting and quantifying LV hypertrophy was evaluated. The study included 55 patients who underwent echocardiography before death, and LV mass was measured at necropsy using the Penn and American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) conventions. The results showed that the Penn-cube LV mass correlated closely with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.92, p < 0.001) and overestimated it by only 6%. The ASE-cube LV mass correlated similarly to necropsy LV mass (r = 0.90, p < 0.001), but systematically overestimated it by a mean of 25%. This overestimation could be corrected by the equation: LV mass = 0.80 (ASE-cube LV mass) + 0.6 g. The use of ASE measurements in the volume correction formula systematically underestimated necropsy LV mass by a mean of 30%. In a subset of 9 patients with technically adequate echocardiograms, 2-dimensional echocardiographic (echo) LV mass measurements were also significantly related to necropsy LV mass (r = 0.68, p < 0.05 and r = 0.82, p < 0.01). The study found that only measurement of myocardial cross-sectional area was acceptably accurate for quantitation of LV mass (r = 0.80, p < 0.001) or diagnosis of LV hypertrophy (sensitivity = 72%, specificity = 94%).

title: R93W mutation in Orai1 causes impaired calcium influx in platelets.
text: The intracellular calcium concentration of many non-excitable cells is regulated by calcium store release and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). In platelets, STIM1 was recently identified as the primary calcium sensor expressed in the endoplasmic reticulum. To investigate the role of the SOC channel moiety, Orai1, in platelet SOCE, we generated mice expressing a mutated, inactive form of Orai1 in blood cells only (Orai1(R93W)). Platelets expressing Orai1(R93W) exhibited significantly reduced SOCE and impaired agonist-induced increases in intracellular calcium. These platelets also showed reduced integrin activation and impaired degranulation when stimulated with low agonist concentrations under static conditions. However, the ability of Orai1(R93W) platelets to aggregate or adhere to collagen under arterial flow conditions ex vivo was not significantly affected. In contrast, these adherent Orai1(R93W) platelets were defective in surface phosphatidylserine exposure, indicating that Orai1 is essential for the platelets' procoagulant response rather than other calcium-dependent cellular responses.

title: [Efficacy on post-stroke depression treated with acupuncture at the acupoints based on ziwuliuzhu and prozac].
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effects of a comprehensive approach combining acupuncture at specific points based on the midnight-noon ebb-flow theory (ziwuliuzhu) with oral administration of fluoxetine hydrochloride (Prozac) on post-stroke depression, compared to acupuncture based on ziwuliuzhu alone and oral administration of Prozac alone.
Methods: Ninety-three patients were randomized into three groups: a comprehensive group, a ziwuliuzhu group, and a Prozac group. In the comprehensive group, acupuncture based on ziwuliuzhu was combined with oral administration of Prozac. In the ziwuliuzhu group, acupuncture was applied to specific points based on the midnight-noon ebb-flow theory, once a day, 5 times a week. In the Prozac group, oral administration of Prozac was given once a day, 20 mg each time. The treatment lasted for 6 sessions. Clinical efficacy and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) scores were compared among the three groups.
Results: The total effective rate was 96.8% (30/31) in the comprehensive group, significantly higher than in the ziwuliuzhu group (83.9%, 26/31) and the Prozac group (80.6%, 25/31), P<0.05. In each of the 4, 12, and 24-week treatment periods, HAMD scores were significantly lower than before treatment in all three groups, and the scores in the comprehensive group were consistently lower than in the other two groups. In the 4- and 12-week treatment periods, there were no significant differences in HAMD scores between the ziwuliuzhu group and the Prozac group (P>0.05). However, in the 24-week treatment period, HAMD scores in the ziwuliuzhu group were significantly lower than in the Prozac group (P<0.05). The comprehensive group had fewer adverse reactions (2 cases) compared to the Prozac group (6 cases) and the ziwuliuzhu group (0 case).
Conclusion: The comprehensive therapy of acupuncture at specific points based on ziwuliuzhu and oral administration of Prozac is more effective and safer than either simple oral administration of Prozac or acupuncture based on ziwuliuzhu alone in treating post-stroke depression. While the clinical efficacy of simple ziwuliuzhu acupuncture is not significantly different from simple oral administration of Prozac, the long-term HAMD scores and safety of the comprehensive approach are superior.

title: Linkage with methadone treatment upon release from incarceration: a promising opportunity.
text: Individuals who inject drugs (IDUs) are disproportionately affected by HIV, viral hepatitis, and tuberculosis, and make up over a quarter of the incarcerated population in the United States. Methadone maintenance treatment for opioid addiction has been shown to significantly reduce drug use, criminal activity related to drug use, and the risk of HIV transmission. Recently released inmates are particularly vulnerable to overdose and disease transmission, making immediate linkage to methadone treatment upon release a crucial opportunity to combat disease transmission, facilitate reentry into the community, and reduce recidivism.

title: The Diabetes Prevention Program: baseline characteristics of the randomized cohort. The Diabetes Prevention Program Research Group.
text:
Objective:
The Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) is a 27-center randomized clinical trial aimed at evaluating the safety and efficacy of interventions that may delay or prevent the onset of diabetes in individuals at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
Research Design and Methods:
The study included 3,234 participants aged 25 years or older with a BMI of 24 kg/m2 or higher (or 22 kg/m2 or higher for Asian Americans) and impaired glucose tolerance, with a fasting plasma glucose level of 5.3-6.9 mmol/l (or < 6.9 mmol/l for American Indians). Participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups: intensive lifestyle modification, standard care plus metformin, or standard care plus placebo. Baseline data for the three groups were collected over a period of 2.7 years.
Results:
Of the 3,234 participants, 55% were Caucasian, 20% were African American, 16% were Hispanic, 5% were American Indian, and 4% were Asian American. The average age of the participants at entry was 51 +/- 10.7 years, and 67.7% were women. The study also found that 16% of the participants were younger than 40 years old, and 20% were older than 60 years old. Among the women, 48% were postmenopausal. The study also found that men and women had similar frequencies of history of hypercholesterolemia (37% and 33%, respectively) or hypertension (29% and 26%, respectively). Additionally, 66% of men and 71% of women had a first-degree relative with diabetes. The average BMI of the participants was 34.0 +/- 6.7 kg/m2, with 57% of the men and 73% of the women having a BMI of > or = 30 kg/m2. The average fasting plasma glucose level in men was 6.0 +/- 0.5 mmol/l, which was comparable to the level in women (5.9 +/- 0.4 mmol/l).
Conclusions:
The DPP has successfully randomized a large cohort of participants with a wide range of ages, obesity levels, and ethnic and racial backgrounds who are at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes. The study will examine the effects of interventions on the development of diabetes.

title: Chronic Helicobacter pylori infections induce gastric mutations in mice.
text:
BACKGROUND & AIMS:
Helicobacter pylori is a significant etiological factor in the development of gastric cancer. The aim of this study was to investigate the role of H. pylori infections in inducing mutagenic events in gastric epithelial cells, as well as the effect of a high-salt diet as a genotoxic risk factor.
METHODS:
Big Blue transgenic male mice (C57Bl/6) were inoculated with H. pylori (strain SS1) or Helicobacter felis (strain CS1) for 6 and 12 months. The frequency and spectrum of mutations at the stomach level were assessed using molecular biology techniques. Inflammatory host response and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression were evaluated using reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry analysis.
RESULTS:
After 6 months, the gastric mutant frequency was found to be 4-fold and 1.7-fold higher in mice infected with H. pylori and H. felis, respectively, compared to uninfected mice. This increase in mutations was associated with a high frequency of transversions (AT --> CG and GC --> TA), which are known to result from oxidative damages. Helicobacter-infected mice exhibited severe gastritis and a high level of iNOS messenger RNA expression. Hyperplasia developed 12 months after inoculation, and both the mutagenic effects and iNOS expression decreased in H. pylori- and H. felis-infected mice. No synergistic effects of a high-salt diet and Helicobacter infection were observed regarding the frequency of gastric mutation.
CONCLUSIONS:
The present study demonstrates a direct gastric mutagenic effect due to H. pylori infection in the Big Blue transgenic mouse model, which can be attributed to oxidative DNA damage involving the inflammatory host response. The findings suggest that H. pylori infection may play a significant role in the development of gastric cancer, and that a high-salt diet may exacerbate this effect.

title: A minimal Tat system from a gram-positive organism: a bifunctional TatA subunit participates in discrete TatAC and TatA complexes.
text: The Tat system facilitates the transport of folded proteins across bacterial and thylakoid membranes. In Gram-negative organisms, a TatABC substrate-binding complex and separate TatA complex are believed to cooperate to form an active translocon, with all three subunits essential for translocation. In contrast, most Gram-positive organisms lack a tatB gene, indicating significant differences in organization and potential modes of action. Here, we investigated Tat complexes encoded by the tatAdCd genes of Bacillus subtilis. Expression of tatAdCd in an Escherichia coli tat null mutant resulted in efficient export of a large, cofactor-containing E. coli Tat substrate, TorA. Our findings suggest a bifunctional role for the tatAd gene in B. subtilis, as it complements E. coli mutants lacking either tatAE or tatB. Additionally, we identified and characterized two distinct Tat complexes in B. subtilis: a TatAdCd complex of approximately 230 kDa and a separate TatAd complex of approximately 270 kDa. The latter is a discrete entity unlike the highly heterogeneous E. coli TatA complex, which ranges in size from approximately 50 kDa to over 600 kDa. The singular nature of the B. subtilis TatAd complex suggests that discrete TatAC and TatA complexes may form a single form of translocon.

title: A systemic granulomatous response to Schistosoma mansoni eggs alters responsiveness of bone-marrow-derived macrophages to Toll-like receptor agonists.
text: Macrophages play a crucial role in both innate and acquired immune responses to Schistosoma mansoni. Within these cells, there are two distinct activation states: classical (M1) or alternative (M2). The former is characterized by the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while the latter is associated with the production of anti-inflammatory cytokines. In the present study, we investigated the impact of systemic Th2-type cytokine polarization on macrophage differentiation and activation. To achieve this, we analyzed bone marrow-derived macrophages from mice with S. mansoni egg-induced pulmonary granulomas and unchallenged (or naïve) mice to determine their activation state and response to specific TLR agonists, including S. mansoni egg antigens. Our findings revealed that macrophages from Th2-polarized mice constitutively expressed higher levels of "found in inflammatory zone-1" (FIZZ1) and ST2 (M2 markers) and lower levels of NO synthase 2, CCL3, MIP-2, TNF-alpha, and IL-12 (M1 markers) compared to naïve macrophages. Additionally, Th2-polarized macrophages exhibited enhanced responses to TLR agonists, resulting in significantly higher levels of gene and protein expression for M2 and M1 markers in these cells. These data suggest that signals received by bone marrow precursors during S. mansoni egg-induced granuloma responses dynamically alter the development of macrophages and enhance their TLR responsiveness, which may have a significant impact on the pulmonary granulomatous response.

title: Orai1 and STIM reconstitute store-operated calcium channel function.
text:
The two membrane proteins, STIM1 and Orai1, have been shown to be crucial for the activation of store-operated channels (SOCs), but the mechanisms by which they interact are not fully understood. In this study, we investigate the functional interaction between STIM1 and Orai1 and find that coexpression of these proteins leads to a significant increase in store-dependent Ca2+ entry in human embryonic kidney 293 cells and rat basophilic leukemia cells.
When expressed alone, Orai1 reduces store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) in human embryonic kidney 293 cells and rat basophilic leukemia cells, but when coexpressed with STIM1, Orai1 enhances SOCE by up to 103-fold, making it entirely store-dependent. This entry is completely blocked by the SOC blocker, 2-aminoethoxydiphenylborate. Additionally, coexpression of Orai1 and STIM1 leads to a large gain in the Ca2+ release-activated Ca2+ current (I(CRAC)) in rat basophilic leukemia cells.
Interestingly, the close STIM1 homologue, STIM2, inhibits SOCE when expressed alone, but coexpression with Orai1 leads to substantial constitutive (store-independent) Ca2+ entry. STIM proteins are known to mediate Ca2+ store-sensing and endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane coupling with no intrinsic channel properties. Our results suggest that Orai1 contributes the PM channel component responsible for Ca2+ entry, and the suppression of SOC function by Orai1 overexpression likely reflects a required stoichiometry between STIM1 and Orai1.
In summary, our findings reveal a powerful gain in SOC function dependent on the presence of both Orai1 and STIM1, and provide insight into the functional interaction between these two proteins in the regulation of Ca2+ entry.

title: Tet and TDG mediate DNA demethylation essential for mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition in somatic cell reprogramming.
text: Recently discovered mammalian epigenetic modification, Tet-mediated DNA oxidation, remains poorly understood in its functional role in cell-fate transitions. To investigate, we generated mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) lacking all three Tet genes and examined their capacity for reprogramming into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Surprisingly, Tet-deficient MEFs were unable to undergo reprogramming due to a block in the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) step. Similarly, reprogramming of MEFs lacking the TDG gene was also impaired. We found that the block in reprogramming was caused, at least in part, by defective activation of key microRNAs (miRNAs), which depends on oxidative demethylation promoted by Tet and TDG. Reintroduction of either the affected miRNAs or catalytically active Tet and TDG restored reprogramming in the knockout MEFs. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the role of epigenetic barriers in cell-lineage conversion.

title: The last and the next hundred years of malariology.
text:
The founding fathers of malariology were visionaries who combined scientific rigor, tenacity, and social consciousness in their research. A century later, despite significant progress in understanding and controlling malaria, the global burden of the disease remains daunting. To tackle the complex challenges of malaria in the next century, research must strike a balance between specialization and interdisciplinary collaboration, leveraging cutting-edge techniques and tools to inform control efforts.
Advances in molecular biology, epidemiology, and genetics have allowed for a more nuanced understanding of the malaria life cycle, including the analysis of stage-specific antigens, disease cycles, and population genetics of parasites, vectors, and humans. This comprehensive understanding provides a robust framework for developing effective control strategies, including drug resistance management, vaccine development, insecticidal and net control, and socio-economic interventions.
The emergence of large-scale changes in malaria distribution and transmission patterns, enabled by advances in remote sensing and spatial analysis, allows for more accurate predictions of epidemics and the tailoring of control efforts to local contexts. Moreover, the interplay between environmental changes and human activities underscores the need for a holistic approach to malaria control, integrating research findings into the broader health system.
In light of the ongoing challenges in low- and middle-income countries, where the burden of malaria remains disproportionately high, it is essential that research findings are translated into practical support and interventions. A coherent understanding of the biomedical and socio-economic aspects of malaria, informed by the legacy of the founding fathers of malariology, must feed into the renewed efforts to control and eliminate the disease. This includes the Roll Back Malaria initiative and beyond, as we embark on a new century of research and control.

title: Activation of AMP-activated protein kinase suppresses oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced macrophage proliferation.
text: Macrophage-derived foam cells play a crucial role in the progression of atherosclerosis, and previous studies have shown that ERK1/2-dependent granulocyte/macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) expression is important for oxidized low density lipoprotein (Ox-LDL)-induced macrophage proliferation. In this study, we investigated the potential of activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) to suppress macrophage proliferation. We found that Ox-LDL-induced proliferation of mouse peritoneal macrophages was significantly inhibited by the AMPK activator 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR) and restored by dominant-negative AMPKalpha1, suggesting that AMPK activation suppresses macrophage proliferation. AICAR also partially suppressed Ox-LDL-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and GM-CSF expression, suggesting that another mechanism is involved in the AICAR-mediated suppression of macrophage proliferation. Interestingly, AICAR suppressed GM-CSF-induced macrophage proliferation without suppressing p38 MAPK/Akt signaling. GM-CSF, on the other hand, suppressed p53 phosphorylation and expression and induced Rb phosphorylation. Overexpression of p53 or p27(kip) suppressed GM-CSF-induced macrophage proliferation. AICAR induced cell cycle arrest, increased p53 phosphorylation and expression, and suppressed GM-CSF-induced Rb phosphorylation via AMPK activation. Moreover, AICAR induced p21(cip) and p27(kip) expression via AMPK activation, and small interfering RNA (siRNA) of p21(cip) and p27(kip) restored AICAR-mediated suppression of macrophage proliferation. In conclusion, our findings suggest that AMPK activation suppresses Ox-LDL-induced macrophage proliferation by suppressing GM-CSF expression and inducing cell cycle arrest. These effects of AMPK activation may represent therapeutic targets for atherosclerosis.

title: Evaluation of cortical bone by peripheral quantitative computed tomography in renal transplant recipients.
text:
Background: Renal transplant patients have an increased risk of fractures, with an absolute risk that is three times higher than that of matched controls. Most of these fractures occur in the peripheral bones, suggesting a greater compromise of cortical bone. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) is a noninvasive imaging technique that allows for separate evaluations of cortical and trabecular bones. This study aimed to investigate cortical bone using pQCT in renal transplant patients and compare the results with those of normal controls.
Methods: pQCT was performed on the distal radius of the nondominant forearm in 12 renal transplant patients (seven men and five women) and 27 normal controls. The following bone parameters were evaluated: total and cortical bone mineral density (TBMD, cBMD), total (cross-sectional) and cortical area (TA, cA), cortical thickness (cThk), endosteal and periosteal circumferences, and the buckling ratio (r/cThK).
Results: Compared to normal controls, transplant patients as a whole showed a significant increase in total area (TA), endosteal circumference, and the buckling ratio, along with a significant reduction in cortical thickness (cThk). Female patients had a marked decrease in cortical area (cA) and cortical thickness (cThk), while male patients also showed a decrease in cortical thickness (cThk) and an increase in endosteal perimeter. Total time on dialysis prior to renal grafting correlated negatively with cortical thickness (r = .62; P < .01).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that a significant thinning of cortical bone may contribute to the increased incidence of peripheral fractures among renal transplant patients.

title: Ataxia, dementia, and hypogonadotropism caused by disordered ubiquitination.
text:
Background:
The combination of ataxia and hypogonadism has been described for over a century, but the genetic basis of this syndrome has remained elusive.
Methods:
We performed whole-exome sequencing in a patient with ataxia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, followed by targeted sequencing of candidate genes in similarly affected patients. We also characterized the neurological and reproductive endocrine phenotypes in detail. The effects of sequence variants and the presence of an epistatic interaction were tested in a zebrafish model.
Results:
Digenic homozygous mutations in RNF216 and OTUD4, which encode a ubiquitin E3 ligase and a deubiquitinase, respectively, were identified in three affected siblings in a consanguineous family. Additional screening identified compound heterozygous truncating mutations in RNF216 in an unrelated patient and single heterozygous deleterious mutations in four other patients. Knockdown of rnf216 or otud4 in zebrafish embryos induced defects in the eye, optic tectum, and cerebellum, and combinatorial suppression of both genes exacerbated these phenotypes, which were rescued by nonmutant, but not mutant, human RNF216 or OTUD4 messenger RNA. All patients had progressive ataxia and dementia, with neuronal loss observed in cerebellar pathways and the hippocampus. Defects were also detected at the hypothalamic and pituitary levels of the reproductive endocrine axis.
Conclusions:
Our findings demonstrate that the syndrome of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, ataxia, and dementia can be caused by inactivating mutations in RNF216 or by the combination of mutations in RNF216 and OTUD4. These results highlight the importance of disordered ubiquitination in neurodegeneration and reproductive dysfunction, and demonstrate the power of whole-exome sequencing in combination with functional studies to uncover genetic interactions that cause disease. (Funded by the National Institutes of Health and others.)

title: Combination cancer immunotherapies tailored to the tumour microenvironment
text: Cancer immunotherapy is poised to play a significant role in combination treatment plans for many cancer patients in the near future. Research has identified various immune processes involving different types of immune cells, including T-cells and myeloid cells, as well as tumour cells' strategies to evade the immune response. The tumour microenvironment can also influence which immune suppressive pathways are activated, leading to restrained antitumour immunity. To overcome these challenges, therapeutic approaches targeting immune checkpoint receptors and other inhibitory mechanisms have shown promise in inducing durable antitumour responses in patients with advanced cancers, including melanoma. However, many patients do not respond well to monotherapy and alternative strategies are needed to achieve optimal therapeutic benefit. These strategies include eliminating the bulk of tumour cells to stimulate antigen release and APC function, using adjuvants to enhance APC function, and enhancing effector-cell activity. In this review, we discuss the stratification of the tumour microenvironment based on tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes and PD-L1 expression in the tumour, and how this stratification can inform the design of personalized combination cancer therapies.

title: Cyclic AMP-dependent phosphorylation of thromboxane A(2) receptor-associated Galpha(13).
text: Although it is well established that cAMP inhibits platelet activation induced by all agonists, the thromboxane A2 signal transduction pathway was found to be particularly sensitive to such inhibition. Therefore, we investigated whether cAMP-dependent kinase mediates phosphorylation of the thromboxane A2 receptor-G-protein complex. Our findings showed that cAMP induces protein kinase A-dependent [gamma-(32)P]ATP labeling of solubilized membrane proteins in the region of Galpha subunits, specifically 38-45 kDa. Moreover, ligand affinity chromatography purification of thromboxane A2 receptor-G-protein complexes from these membranes revealed that 38-45-kDa phosphoproteins co-purify with thromboxane A2 receptors. Immunoprecipitation of the affinity column eluate with a Galpha13 antibody demonstrated that 8-Br-cAMP increased phosphorylation of thromboxane A2 receptor-associated Galpha13 by 87 +/- 27%. In separate experiments, immunopurification of Galpha13 on microtiter wells coated with a different Galpha13 antibody revealed that 8-Br-cAMP increased Galpha13 phosphorylation by 53 +/- 19%. Finally, treatment of [32]P-labeled whole platelets with prostacyclin resulted in a 90 +/- 14% increase in phosphorylated Galpha13, which was abolished by pretreatment with the adenylate cyclase inhibitor MDL-12. These results provide the first evidence that protein kinase A mediates phosphorylation of Galpha13 both in vitro and in vivo and provide a basis for the preferential inhibition of thromboxane A2-mediated signaling in platelets by cAMP.

title: Tet proteins can convert 5-methylcytosine to 5-formylcytosine and 5-carboxylcytosine.
text:
5-methylcytosine (5mC) plays a crucial role in gene expression, genomic imprinting, and the suppression of transposable elements in DNA. The enzyme Tet (ten eleven translocation) converts 5mC to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) through an enzymatic activity-dependent process. Our study reveals that the Tet proteins can generate two additional cytosine derivatives, 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC), from 5mC in an enzymatic activity-dependent manner. These findings suggest that the genomic content of 5hmC, 5fC, and 5caC can be modulated through the overexpression or depletion of Tet proteins. Our study identifies two previously unknown cytosine derivatives in genomic DNA as the products of Tet proteins, raising the possibility that DNA demethylation may occur through Tet-catalyzed oxidation followed by decarboxylation.
In this study, we investigate the role of Tet proteins in the generation of cytosine derivatives in genomic DNA. Our findings reveal that Tet proteins can convert 5mC to 5hmC, as well as generate 5fC and 5caC from 5mC through an enzymatic activity-dependent process. The presence of these cytosine derivatives in genomic DNA of mouse embryonic stem cells and mouse organs is also observed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the genomic content of 5hmC, 5fC, and 5caC can be modulated through the overexpression or depletion of Tet proteins. Our study provides new insights into the mechanisms of DNA demethylation and highlights the importance of Tet proteins in this process.

title: Long-term use of aspirin and age-related macular degeneration.
text:
The study examines the association between regular aspirin use and the incidence of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in a population-based cohort of older adults. The study included 4926 participants aged 43-86 years who underwent examinations every 5 years over a 20-year period. Participants were asked if they had regularly used aspirin at least twice a week for more than 3 months. The main outcome measures were the incidence of early AMD, late AMD, and two subtypes of late AMD (neovascular AMD and pure geographic atrophy).
The study found that regular aspirin use 10 years prior to retinal examination was associated with an increased risk of incident late AMD and neovascular AMD, but not early AMD. Specifically, the estimated incidence of late AMD was 1.76% in regular aspirin users and 1.03% in non-users, and the estimated incidence of neovascular AMD was 2.20% in regular aspirin users and 1.20% in non-users. However, aspirin use 5 years or 10 years prior to retinal examination was not associated with incident early AMD.
The study suggests that regular aspirin use may have a small but statistically significant increase in the risk of incident late and neovascular AMD, but the overall incidence of AMD remains low. However, the study highlights the importance of considering aspirin use when evaluating patients for ocular surgery or assessing risk factors for AMD.

title: Growth control and ribosomopathies.
text: Ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis are two of the most energy-intensive processes in a growing cell, consuming a significant portion of the cell's resources. Any disruptions to these processes can have a profound impact on the cell's ability to express genes, leading to a range of developmental defects and diseases. It is therefore unsurprising that cells have evolved a complex surveillance system to monitor the status of the translational machinery, ensuring that any deviations from normal function are quickly identified and addressed. Recent discoveries of genetic mutations and deletions associated with ribosome biogenesis have led to the classification of these defects as ribosomopathies. Over the past decade, significant progress has been made in understanding the interplay between growth control and ribosome biogenesis, including the identification of extra-ribosomal functions of certain ribosome proteins and their regulation of p53 levels. However, evidence suggests that p53 and/or Hdm2-independent pathways may also be involved in these processes. In this review, we will summarize the current state of knowledge regarding the mechanisms underlying ribosomopathies and explore the relationship between ribosome production and tumorigenesis.

title: Tunable signal processing through modular control of transcription factor translocation.
text: Signaling pathways can lead to diverse transcription factor (TF) activation dynamics. We investigated how TFs process signaling inputs to generate varied responses. The budding yeast general stress-responsive TF Msn2 served as a versatile signal processor, capable of tracking, filtering, or integrating signals in an input-dependent manner. This adaptable signal processing originates from dual regulation of both nuclear import and export by phosphorylation, with mutants sustaining only one function. Msn2's versatile signal processing is crucial for generating distinct dynamic responses to various environmental stresses. Our findings reveal how complex signal-processing functions are integrated into a single molecule and provide insights for designing TFs with "programmable" signal-processing capabilities.

title: Killing by bactericidal antibiotics does not depend on reactive oxygen species.
text: Traditionally, bactericidal antibiotics were believed to kill by modulating their respective targets. However, recent studies have challenged this view, proposing an alternative mechanism of killing involving the production of toxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the presence of antibiotics. Our findings contradict this theory, as we found no correlation between an individual bacterial cell's probability of survival in the presence of antibiotics and its level of ROS. In fact, the addition of a ROS quencher, thiourea, protected cells from the harmful effects of antibiotics at low concentrations, regardless of whether the conditions were aerobic or anaerobic. These results suggest that ROS do not play a role in the killing of bacterial pathogens by antibiotics.

title: A naturally occurring mouse model of X-linked congenital stationary night blindness.
text: Objective: To describe a naturally occurring X-linked recessive mutation, nob, that disrupts visual transmission between photoreceptors and second-order neurons in mice. Methods: Affected mice were identified by measuring the light-evoked response of the retina using electroretinography (ERG). To evaluate visual transmission, cortical potentials were recorded with a scalp electrode. The inheritance pattern of nob was determined by breeding nob animals with normal mice. Retinal histology was examined using light microscopy. Results: Although the photoreceptor-mediated ERG component (a-wave) was normal in nob mice, the major response component reflecting postreceptoral neuronal activity (b-wave) was absent. Visually-driven cortical activity was also abnormal in nob animals. At the light microscopic level, the nob retina appeared to have a normal cytoarchitecture. Conclusions: These findings suggest that the nob defect disrupts the transmission of visual information through the retina, making these mice a useful model for studying outer retinal synaptic function. Additionally, the nob mutant mouse may provide an animal model for complete congenital stationary night blindness, a human disorder characterized by a profound loss of rod-mediated visual sensitivity.

title: Differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and embryonic stem cells into steroidogenic cells using steroidogenic factor-1 and liver receptor homolog-1.
text:
In a previous study, we demonstrated that mesenchymal stem cells could be converted into steroidogenic cells through treatment with steroidogenic factor-1 (SF-1) and 8-bromo-cAMP. We also found that the use of liver receptor homolog-1 (LRH-1), another member of the nuclear receptor 5A family, in combination with 8-bromo-cAMP, could also direct the differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells into steroid-producing cells. However, these approaches were not effective in differentiating other types of undifferentiated cells, such as embryonic stem cells or embryonal carcinoma cells, as over-expression of the nuclear receptor 5A family was cytotoxic to these cells.
To overcome this limitation, we generated embryonic stem cells carrying a tetracycline-regulated SF-1 gene at the ROSA26 locus. The embryonic stem cells were first differentiated into a mesenchymal cell lineage by culturing on collagen IV-coated dishes and treating with pulse exposures of retinoic acid before expression of SF-1. While untreated embryonic stem cells were unable to be converted into steroidogenic cells by expression of SF-1 in the absence of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF), the differentiated cells could successfully be converted into steroidogenic cells when expression of SF-1 was induced. These cells exhibited characteristics of adrenocortical-like cells and produced a large amount of corticosterone. These results suggest that pluripotent stem cells can be differentiated into steroidogenic cells by the nuclear receptor 5A family of proteins via the mesenchymal cell lineage, providing a potential source of cells for gene therapy for diseases caused by steroidogenesis deficiencies.

title: Chronic daily headache. A clinical and psychological profile before and after treatment.
text: To investigate the clinical and personality characteristics of patients with chronic daily headache (CDH) before and after treatment, 20 patients were assessed using the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) and the Strait and Trait Anxiety Index 1,2 (STAI). The study found that the patients were divided into two groups based on their MMPI scores: group 1 (n = 6) had elevated scores on hypochondria and hysteria scales, while group 2 (n = 13) had elevated scores on depression and other MMPI scales. STAI scores were high in both groups. The study also found that almost all patients experienced psychosomatic symptoms and migraine features. After treatment, there was a significant improvement in headache occurrence, severity, and duration, as well as a decrease in MMPI and STAI scores. However, 12 of the 20 patients still had a "conversion V" configuration after treatment, indicating that CDH was often transformed migraine in most cases and accompanied by anxiety levels in all patients and hysteric traits in some. The study suggests that these patients may develop a depressive disorder over time, and that hysterical traits may still be present after treatment, although at a lower level in those who had them before treatment and may be unmasked in those who had depression.

title: Potassium channel structure and function as reported by a single glycosylation sequon.
text:
Inwardly rectifying potassium (K+) channels, specifically the IRK family, are crucial for maintaining the resting membrane potential and cell volume. These integral membrane proteins are frequently N-glycosylated, with the attached carbohydrate residing extracellularly and potentially influencing channel function. However, the molecular-level dynamics of glycosylation have yet to be elucidated. ROMK1, a member of the IRK family, is an ideal candidate for studying glycosylation due to its single N-glycosylation consensus sequence (Ho et al., 1993).
We demonstrate that ROMK1 is expressed in a functional state in the plasma membrane of an insect cell line (Spodoptera frugiperda, Sf9) and exists in two forms: glycosylated and unglycosylated. To investigate functionality, we abolished glycosylation through an N117Q mutation or treatment with tunicamycin. Whole-cell currents were significantly reduced in both unglycosylated forms compared to wild-type, while single-channel currents revealed a dramatic decrease in opening probability, po. These findings support the notion that the N-glycosylation sequon is located extracellularly, in agreement with current topological models of IRKs, and suggest that sequon occupancy by carbohydrate stabilizes the open state of ROMK1.

title: Role of the novel Th17 cytokine IL-17F in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): upregulated colonic IL-17F expression in active Crohn's disease and analysis of the IL17F p.His161Arg polymorphism in IBD.
text:
Background: Interleukin (IL)-17F, produced by IL-23R-expressing Th17 cells, is a novel member of the IL-17 cytokine family. Given the association of IL23R with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we investigated the role of IL-17F in IBD, including its intestinal gene expression and the effect of the IL17F p. His161Arg polymorphism on disease susceptibility and phenotype. Additionally, we analyzed the IL17F p. His161Arg polymorphism for potential epistasis with IL23R and NOD2/CARD15 variants.
Methods: We measured intestinal IL-17F mRNA expression in inflamed colonic lesions and uninflamed biopsies from 499 patients with Crohn's disease (CD) and 216 patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR). We also genotyped 1682 individuals (CD: n = 499; UC: n = 216; controls: n = 967) for the presence of the IL17F p. His161Arg polymorphism, as well as 3 NOD2 variants (p. Arg702Trp, p. Gly908Arg, and p. Leu1007fsX1008) and 10 CD-associated IL23R variants.
Results: Intestinal IL-17F mRNA expression was found to be 4.4-fold increased in inflamed colonic lesions compared to uninflamed biopsies in CD (P = 0.016), but not in UC. However, the mean intestinal IL-17F mRNA expression was higher in UC than in CD (P < 0.0001). The IL17F p.
