His161Arg substitution was observed with similar frequencies in IBD patients and controls and was not associated with a certain disease phenotype. There was also no evidence for epistasis between the IL17F p. His161Arg polymorphism and IBD-associated single nucleotide polymorphisms within the IL23R gene.
Conclusions: Intestinal IL17F gene expression is increased in active CD. The IL17F p. His161Arg polymorphism is not associated with IBD susceptibility and has no epistatic interaction with CD-associated IL23R variants.

title: Targeting brain cancer: advances in the molecular pathology of malignant glioma and medulloblastoma
text: Malignant brain tumors continue to have a disproportionate impact on morbidity and mortality across various populations. The most common types in adults and children, malignant glioma and medulloblastoma, have been the focus of extensive research over the past two decades, leading to significant advances in understanding their basic biology and pathogenesis. This Review summarizes these developments in the context of the evolving field of molecular pathology and explores the implications for the design of new treatment regimens.

title: Rapid helper T-cell recovery above 200 × 106/l at 3 months correlates to successful transplant outcomes after allogeneic stem cell transplantation
text: The current study investigates the role of quantitative measurement of peripheral lymphocyte subsets, particularly CD4+ helper T-cell recovery, in predicting post-transplant outcomes, including overall survival (OS) and non-relapse mortality (NRM), in allogeneic stem cell transplantation. A total of 69 allogeneic recipients with various diagnoses, including acute myeloid leukemia (42), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (5), chronic myeloid leukemia (15), non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (5), and high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (2), were included in the study. Peripheral lymphocyte subset counts, including CD3+ T cells, CD3+4+ helper T cells, CD3+8+ cytotoxic T cells, CD19+ B cells, and CD56+ natural killer cells, were measured at 3, 6, and 12 months post-transplant. The study found that CD4+ helper T-cell reconstitution at 3 months was strongly correlated with OS (P<0.0001), NRM (P=0.0007), and opportunistic infections (P=0.0108) at the cutoff value of 200 × 106/l CD4+ helper T cells. Rapid CD4+ helper T-cell recovery was also associated with a higher CD4+ helper T-cell transplant dose (P=0.006) and donor type (P<0.001). Additionally, an early CD4+ helper T-cell recovery at 3 months correlated with a subsequent faster helper T-cell recovery until 12 months, but not with B-cell recovery. In a multivariate analysis, rapid recovery of CD4+ helper T cells at 3 months was identified as a favorable prognostic factor, along with higher CD34+ cell transplant dose, in terms of OS (P=0.001) and NRM (P=0.005).

title: Generating an iPSC bank for HLA-matched tissue transplantation based on known donor and recipient HLA types.
text: The likelihood of immunological rejection of Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA)-mismatched induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hinders their therapeutic potential. However, we have discovered a solution to overcome this limitation. By utilizing a tissue bank of 150 HLA-typed volunteers, we have found that 93% of the UK population can be matched, with a minimal requirement for immunosuppression. Our approach provides a practical solution for generating an iPSC stem cell bank using existing HLA-typed samples, thereby avoiding the need to type a large number of individuals prospectively.

title: Promiscuous gene expression and the developmental dynamics of medullary thymic epithelial cells.
text: Thymic epithelial cells (TEC) play a crucial role in shaping the T cell repertoire by providing a structured and functional microenvironment. In addition, they display a unique feature called promiscuous gene expression (pGE), which involves the expression of numerous tissue-restricted antigens (TRA) on a subset of TEC. However, the regulation of pGE in TEC is not well understood, particularly in terms of their turnover and developmental interrelationships. Our study shows that pGE is primarily a property of mature medullary TEC (mTEC), which differentiate from immature CD80neg TEC. This differentiation process occurs continuously in the postnatal thymus, with mature mTEC undergoing turnover every 2-3 weeks while immature mTEC maintain a smaller cycling and larger non-cycling pool. The latter pool may serve as a reservoir of committed precursors that sustain the renewal process. Our findings demonstrate that mTEC are a highly dynamic cell population, and that the availability and display of TRA in the thymus undergoes a continuous temporal and spatial reorganization.

title: Evaluation of HER-2/neu amplification and other biological markers as predictors of response to neoadjuvant anthracycline-based chemotherapy in primary breast cancer: the role of anthracycline dose intensity.
text:
OBJECTIVES: The debate continues regarding the value of HER-2/neu status as a predictor of response to anthracycline-based chemotherapy. To investigate this further, we evaluated the contribution of HER-2/neu gene amplification and other biomarkers in predicting response to different doses of neoadjuvant anthracycline-based chemotherapy.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical and pathological records of 115 primary breast cancer patients who received neoadjuvant anthracycline-based chemotherapy. The patients were divided into two groups based on the dose intensity of anthracyclines: high-dose (doxorubicin ≥20 mg/m2/week or epirubicin ≥30 mg/m2/week) and moderate-low dose (doxorubicin or epirubicin <20 mg/m2/week). The HER-2/neu status was determined by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) on tumor samples before chemotherapy.
RESULTS: HER-2/neu amplification was observed in 25% (29/115) of the tumors, with a similar distribution in the high-dose (11/48, 23%) and moderate-low-dose (18/67, 27%) groups. In the univariate analysis, a high Ki67 index (>20%) and positive clinical axillary nodes were predictive of an objective tumor response (P = 0.033 and 0.001, respectively). In the multivariate analysis, Ki67 was the only factor predictive of response (OR = 3.08, 95% CI = 1.1-8.5, P = 0.03). HER-2/neu status and hormonal receptor status (HR) were not significant predictors of response to different anthracycline dose intensities.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that HER-2/neu status is not a significant predictor of response to different doses of neoadjuvant anthracycline-based chemotherapy in breast cancer patients. The only significant predictor of response was the Ki67 index, which highlights the importance of this marker in predicting treatment response. These results suggest that other biomarkers may be more useful in predicting response to chemotherapy than HER-2/neu status.

title: Radioactive labeling of mitochondrial translation products in cultured cells.
text: The mammalian mitochondrial genome encodes 37 genes, of which 13 are responsible for the synthesis of polypeptide subunits within the enzyme complexes of the oxidative phosphorylation system. These genes are exclusively located in the mitochondrial matrix and are dedicated to the translation of these subunits. The remaining genes encode ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) and transfer RNAs (tRNAs) necessary for the translation of these polypeptides. Mitochondrial disease in humans is often associated with defects in mitochondrial translation, which can result in a global decrease in mitochondrial protein synthesis, a decrease in the synthesis of specific polypeptides, the synthesis of abnormal polypeptides, or alterations in the stability of specific translation products. These changes in mitochondrial translation can be detected using a straightforward technique that exploits the insensitivity of the mitochondrial translation machinery to antibiotics that inhibit cytoplasmic translation. By specifically labeling mitochondrial translation products with radioactive markers, their distribution on gradient gels can be visualized. This analysis is useful for studying disease-causing mutations in both the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes in cultured cells derived from patient biopsies.

title: Caenorhabditis elegans cyclin A- and B-type genes: a cyclin A multigene family, an ancestral cyclin B3 and differential germline expression.
text: We have isolated cDNA clones for Caenorhabditis elegans cyclins A1, B, and B3. While cyclins A1 and B are most closely related to A- or B-type cyclins found in other organisms, cyclin B3 is less similar to these cyclins. However, our discovery of a C. elegans homologue suggests that cyclin B3 has been conserved throughout evolution. Cyclin A1 is a member of an A-type multigene family, but the cyclin A1 cDNA only detects a single band on northern blots. In contrast, three different transcripts are observed for the cyclin B cDNA. Using RNA from germline-defective mutants and populations enriched for males, we found that one cyclin B transcript is specifically expressed in the paternal germline. The other two cyclin B transcripts, as well as the cyclin A1 and cyclin B3 transcripts, are most abundant in the maternal germline and are only present at low levels in other tissues. Additionally, the 3' untranslated regions of each C. elegans cyclin cDNA contain several copies of potential translational control elements found in Xenopus and Drosophila maternal cyclin mRNAs, which are involved in oogenesis and early embryogenesis.

title: A comparison of pharmacological (amitriptyline HCL) and nonpharmacological (cognitive-behavioral) therapies for chronic tension headaches.
text: Forty-one individuals with recurrent tension headaches were randomly assigned to either cognitive-behavioral therapy (delivered in a predominantly home-based treatment protocol) or amitriptyline therapy, with dosages tailored to 25, 50, or 75 mg/day. Both treatments showed significant improvements in headache activity, as measured by patient daily records (56% reduction in headache index with cognitive-behavioral therapy and 27% reduction with amitriptyline) and neurologist ratings of clinical improvement (94% and 69% of patients rated at least moderately improved, respectively). When comparing treatment effectiveness, cognitive-behavioral therapy yielded slightly more positive outcomes than amitriptyline in terms of headache index, somatic complaints, and perceived control of headache activity. However, neither treatment completely eliminated headache problems.

title: Homeostasis model assessment: insulin resistance and β-cell function from fasting plasma glucose and insulin concentrations in man
text: The steady-state basal plasma glucose and insulin concentrations are determined by a feedback loop, with a computer-based model used to predict the homeostatic concentrations that arise from varying degrees of β-cell deficiency and insulin resistance. By comparing a patient's fasting values with the model's predictions, a quantitative assessment of the contributions of insulin resistance and deficient β-cell function to fasting hyperglycaemia (homeostasis model assessment, HOMA) can be made. The accuracy and precision of the estimate were determined by comparing it with independent measures of insulin resistance and β-cell function obtained through hyperglycaemic and euglycaemic clamps and an intravenous glucose tolerance test. The correlation between the estimate of insulin resistance obtained through HOMA and those obtained through euglycaemic clamp (Rs = 0.88, p < 0.0001), fasting insulin concentration (Rs = 0.81, p < 0.0001), and hyperglycaemic clamp (Rs = 0.69, p < 0.01) was found to be high. Similarly, the correlation between the estimate of deficient β-cell function obtained through HOMA and those derived through hyperglycaemic clamp (Rs = 0.61, p < 0.01) and intravenous glucose tolerance test (Rs = 0.64, p < 0.05) was also significant. However, the low precision of the estimates from the model (coefficients of variation: 31% for insulin resistance and 32% for β-cell deficit) limits its use. Nevertheless, the correlation of the model's estimates with patient data supports the hypothesis that basal glucose and insulin interactions are primarily determined by a simple feedback loop.

title: Clinical benefits and considerations of bisphosphonate treatment in metastatic bone disease.
text: Patients with metastatic bone disease are at risk of developing skeletal-related events that can negatively impact their quality of life, leading to loss of autonomy and functional capabilities. To address this issue, bisphosphonates have become a crucial component of treatment for patients with bone metastases, as they delay the onset and reduce the risk of skeletal-related events, while also providing pain relief in multiple cancer types. Among bisphosphonates, zoledronic acid has proven to be highly effective and safe in treating bone lesions from various cancer types, including breast cancer, prostate cancer, lung cancer, and multiple myeloma. Recent studies suggest that early treatment with zoledronic acid (before the onset of bone pain) may offer additional clinical benefits and positive effects on survival in certain patient subgroups, particularly those with elevated levels of N-telopeptide of type I collagen (NTX), a marker of bone resorption. In patients with breast cancer, prostate cancer, lung cancer, or other solid tumors, normalization of elevated NTX levels was observed in the majority of those who received zoledronic acid. Moreover, normalization of NTX values was found to correlate with extended survival.

title: Distinct memory CD4+ T cells with commitment to T follicular helper- and T helper 1-cell lineages are generated after acute viral infection.
text: CD4(+) T follicular helper (Tfh) cells play a crucial role in facilitating long-lasting antibody responses by providing the necessary signals to B cells during germinal center reactions. However, it remains unclear whether CD4(+) memory T cells retain their commitment to the Tfh cell lineage after antigen clearance. To investigate this, we employed adoptive transfer of antigen-specific memory CD4(+) T cell subpopulations in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model. Our findings reveal that there are distinct memory CD4(+) T cell populations with commitment to either Tfh- or Th1-cell lineages. Through gene expression profiling, epigenetic studies, and phenotypic and functional analyses, we demonstrate that CD4(+) memory T cells retain their previous effector lineage after antigen clearance, with the ability to reacquire their lineage-specific effector functions upon antigen reencounter. These findings have significant implications for vaccine design, as enhancing the generation and engagement of memory Tfh cells could be a strategy to improve vaccine-induced protective immunity.

title: Control of synapse development and plasticity by Rho GTPase regulatory proteins
text:
Synapses are specialized cell-cell connections that enable communication between neurons. Most excitatory synapses in the brain are formed on dendritic spines, small protrusions made of actin filaments that extend from dendrites. During development and in response to environmental stimuli, spines undergo significant changes in shape and number, which are thought to be involved in processes such as learning and memory. Abnormalities in spine development have been linked to various brain disorders, highlighting the importance of understanding the mechanisms that regulate spine formation and plasticity.
Rho-family GTPases, which play a crucial role in shaping the actin cytoskeleton, are essential for the development and remodeling of spines and synapses. The proper regulation of Rho GTPase activity is critical for their function, as aberrant signaling can lead to spine and synapse defects and cognitive impairments. Rho GTPases are activated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) and inhibited by GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs).
We propose that Rho-family GEFs and GAPs provide the necessary spatiotemporal regulation and signaling specificity for proper Rho GTPase function. These proteins possess distinct features, including multiple GEFs and GAPs per Rho GTPase, developmentally regulated expression, discrete localization, the ability to bind to and organize specific signaling networks, and tightly regulated activity. Recent studies have identified several Rho-family GEFs and GAPs that contribute to spinogenesis and synaptogenesis, and we highlight several of these proteins and their distinct biochemical niches in the brain.
Understanding the mechanisms that regulate Rho GTPases and their downstream effects on spine formation and plasticity is crucial for elucidating the underlying causes of brain disorders and developing effective treatments. By shedding light on the complex interplay between Rho GTPases, GEFs, GAPs, and other signaling molecules, we can gain valuable insights into the intricate processes that govern cognition and neural function.

title: Rate and molecular spectrum of spontaneous mutations in the bacterium Escherichia coli as determined by whole-genome sequencing.
text:
Understanding the rate and nature of spontaneous mutations is crucial for comprehending evolutionary and molecular processes. In this report, we investigate the accumulation of spontaneous mutations over thousands of generations in both wild-type Escherichia coli and a derivative lacking the mismatch repair (MMR) system, the primary mechanism for correcting replication errors. Our key findings are as follows:
1. The mutation rate of a wild-type E. coli strain is approximately 1 x 10(-3) mutations per genome per generation.
2. Mutations in the wild-type strain exhibit a mutational bias towards G:C > A:T transitions, but this bias shifts to A:T > G:C mutations in the absence of MMR.
3. During replication, A:T > G:C transitions preferentially occur with A templating the lagging strand and T templating the leading strand, while G:C > A:T transitions preferentially occur with C templating the lagging strand and G templating the leading strand.
4. There is a strong bias towards transition mutations occurring at 5'ApC3'/3'TpG5' sites (where bases 5'A and 3'T are mutated) and, to a lesser extent, at 5'GpC3'/3'CpG5' sites (where bases 5'G and 3'C are mutated).
5. Although the rate of small (≤4 nt) insertions and deletions is high at repeat sequences, these events occur at only 1/10th the genomic rate of base-pair substitutions.

Our findings suggest that MMR activity is genetically regulated, and bacteria isolated from nature often lack MMR capacity, indicating that modulation of MMR can be adaptive. Comparing the results from the wild-type and MMR-defective strains can provide a deeper understanding of the factors that determine mutation rates and spectra, how these factors may differ among organisms, and how they may be shaped by environmental conditions.

title: Apolipoprotein E4 as a predictor of outcomes in pediatric mild traumatic brain injury.
text:
The epsilon4 allele of the apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene has been linked to unfavorable outcomes in adults with traumatic brain injury (TBI), with preliminary evidence suggesting a similar pattern in children. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the APOE epsilon4 allele and outcomes in children with mild TBI.
Participants were 99 children aged 8-15 who were admitted to two large children's hospitals with mild TBI. The study was prospective and longitudinal, with outcomes assessed acutely in the Emergency Department and at follow-ups at 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months post-injury. Of the 99 participants, 28 had at least one epsilon4 allele.
The results showed that children with an epsilon4 allele were more likely to have a lower Glasgow Coma Scale score, but the groups did not differ on any other measures of injury severity. Interestingly, children with an epsilon4 allele performed better than those without on a test of constructional skill, but the groups did not differ on any other neuropsychological tests. Additionally, there were no significant differences between the two groups on measures of post-concussive symptoms.
Overall, the findings suggest that the APOE epsilon4 allele is not consistently related to the outcomes of mild TBI in children. This suggests that other factors may be more important in determining the severity of mild TBI in children.

title: Do physicians follow systemic treatment and funding policy guidelines?
text:
BACKGROUND: The use of bisphosphonates for the prevention of skeletal-related events in women with bone metastases from breast cancer has been well established. To evaluate the use of bisphosphonates in clinical practice, we conducted a retrospective review of patient charts and electronic files at three Canadian cancer centers. In addition, we assessed whether physicians at these centers are following their local treatment guidelines and funding policies.
METHODS: We reviewed the charts and electronic files of patients who had received clodronate or pamidronate at any time between January 2000 and December 2001 at three Canadian cancer centers.
RESULTS: Our findings showed a significant improvement in the time between the diagnosis of bone metastases and the commencement of bisphosphonates, from a median of 155 days in 1998 to 24 days in 2001. However, despite a local funding policy requiring that oral clodronate be the first bisphosphonate used, this was the case in only 67% of patients. Furthermore, despite one centre's guidelines recommending that bisphosphonates be stopped once the patient was progressing, 90% of their patients remained on bisphosphonates until they died.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that while a significant amount of effort is spent on creating evidence-based treatment guidelines, funding agencies often develop policies that are more restrictive than the guidelines suggest. It is clear that physicians are managing a substantial proportion of patients outside of funding policies, but within evidence-based recommendations. Therefore, there is a need for either the creation of guidelines and policies that physicians will follow or the implementation of methods to ensure that restrictive policies are actually followed.

title: Increased resting energy expenditure and weight loss are related to a systemic inflammatory response in lung cancer patients.
text:
Purpose: To investigate the relationship between increased resting energy expenditure (REE) and weight loss in lung cancer patients, and their association with a systemic inflammatory response.
Materials and Methods: REE was measured using indirect calorimetry in 87 patients with primary non-small-cell lung cancer. Levels of soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor 55 (sTNF-R55), soluble intercellular adhesion molecule (sICAM)-1, soluble E (sE)-selectin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-binding protein (LBP), interleukin (IL)-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) were measured using sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). C-reactive protein (CRP) was measured by turbidimetry. A cross-sectional study was conducted to compare inflammatory mediators between hypermetabolic (REE/Harris Benedict [HB] equation ≥ 110%) versus normometabolic (REE/HB < 110%) patients and between patients who lost weight (≥ 10% loss of preillness weight) versus those whose weight remained stable.
Results: Eighty-seven patients with primary non-small-cell lung cancer were included in the study. The mean REE expressed as a percentage of the HB reference values was 118% ± 12%; 67 patients were considered hypermetabolic. Twenty-six patients had a substantial loss of more than 10% of their preillness weight. Hypermetabolic patients had significantly increased levels of sTNF-R55, sE-selectin, LBP, and CRP compared with normometabolic patients. Weight loss was associated with increased levels of the sTNF-Rs, sICAM-1, IL-6, LBP, and CRP.
Conclusion: Hypermetabolism and weight loss in lung cancer patients are related to the presence of a systemic inflammatory response, as reflected by elevated levels of inflammatory mediators and acute phase proteins.

title: Exercise capacity and body mass as predictors of mortality among male veterans with type 2 diabetes.
text:
Objective: To investigate the relationship between exercise capacity and mortality in a population of male veterans with type 2 diabetes, while also examining the role of body mass index (BMI) in this association.
Design and Methods: A total of 831 male patients with type 2 diabetes (mean age 61 ± 9 years) referred for exercise testing for clinical reasons between 1995 and 2006 were included in the study. Exercise capacity was measured using a maximal exercise test and categorized into three groups based on BMI (18.5-24.9, 25.0-29.9, and ≥30 kg/m2). The association between exercise capacity, BMI, and other clinical variables with all-cause mortality was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Study participants were followed up for mortality until June 30, 2006.
Results: During a mean follow-up of 4.8 ± 3.0 years, 112 patients died, resulting in an average annual mortality rate of 2.2%. Each 1-MET increase in exercise capacity was associated with a 10% survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.90 [95% CI 0.82-0.98]; P = 0.01), but BMI was not significantly associated with mortality after adjusting for age, ethnicity, examination year, BMI, presence of cardiovascular disease (CVD), and CVD risk factors. In contrast, patients who achieved <5 maximal METs were 70% more likely to die than those who achieved ≥5 maximal METs after adjusting for these variables.
Conclusion: There was a strong inverse association between exercise capacity and mortality in this cohort of men with type 2 diabetes, and this relationship was independent of BMI. These findings suggest that exercise capacity may be a more important predictor of mortality than BMI in this population.

title: Impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia: a review.
text: Impaired awareness of hypoglycaemia (IAH) is an acquired complication of insulin therapy that affects individuals with type 1 and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes mellitus, characterized by a diminished or absent ability to perceive the onset of hypoglycaemia. This condition is often accompanied by deficiencies in the counter-regulatory hormonal responses to hypoglycaemia, further increasing the risk of severe hypoglycaemia. To identify individuals at risk of severe hypoglycaemia, clinicians have developed scoring systems that can be applied in the clinical setting. The cornerstone of treatment for IAH is the strict avoidance of hypoglycaemia.

title: A chikungunya fever vaccine utilizing an insect-specific virus platform
text: Historically, vaccine development has involved balancing act between immunogenicity and safety. Live-attenuated vaccines typically offer rapid and durable immunity, but have reduced safety compared to inactivated vaccines. In contrast, inactivated vaccines' inability to replicate enhances safety at the cost of immunogenicity, often requiring multiple doses and boosters. To overcome these trade-offs, we developed the insect-specific alphavirus, Eilat virus (EILV), as a vaccine platform. To combat the chikungunya fever (CHIKF) pandemic, we created a chimeric virus containing CHIKV structural proteins by using an EILV cDNA clone. The recombinant EILV/CHIKV was structurally identical to wild-type CHIKV at the 10 Å level, as determined by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, and mimicked the early stages of CHIKV replication in vertebrate cells from attachment and entry to viral RNA delivery. However, the recombinant virus remained completely incapable of productive replication, providing a high degree of safety. A single dose of EILV/CHIKV produced in mosquito cells elicited rapid (within 4 days) and long-lasting (>290 days) neutralizing antibodies that provided complete protection in two different mouse models. In nonhuman primates, EILV/CHIKV elicited rapid and robust immunity that protected against viremia and telemetrically monitored fever. Our EILV platform represents the first structurally native application of an insect-specific virus in preclinical vaccine development and highlights the potential application of such viruses in vaccinology.

title: Molecular elements of low-oxygen signaling in plants.
text: Oxygen and its limitations are becoming increasingly recognized as a crucial factor in plant fitness, growth, and development. Recent research has uncovered the mechanisms by which plants perceive and respond to oxygen levels. For example, some plant cells use an oxygen-mediated branch of the N-end rule pathway for protein degradation, which involves the degradation of specific ethylene responsive transcription factors (ERF-VII) when oxygen levels are low. Additionally, an ERF-VII protein is sequestered at the plasma membrane under aerobic conditions and released upon hypoxia, triggering a response that helps protect the plant from oxidative stress. When oxygen is completely absent, plants transiently accumulate reactive hydrogen peroxide and induce additional genes involved in both signaling and attenuation of oxidative stress. Furthermore, hypoxic environments created by dense cell packing in maize anthers can determine cell fate, while limited oxygen delivery in bulky fruit or tuber tissues growing in aerobic conditions can stimulate anaerobic-like responses. These advances highlight the importance of considering hypoxia in agricultural practices and breeding programs.

title: Purification, characterization, and sequence analysis of a potential virulence factor from Porphyromonas gingivalis, peptidylarginine deiminase.
text:
The progression and initiation of adult-onset periodontitis have been linked to the infection of the gingival sulcus by Porphyromonas gingivalis, a bacterium that employs various virulence factors to establish itself as a dominant pathogen in periodontal pockets. One such factor is the production of ammonia, which provides a protective effect during acidic cleansing cycles in the mouth. Additionally, ammonia production by P. gingivalis has been proposed as a virulence factor due to its negative impact on neutrophil function.
In this study, we report the first purification of a peptidylarginine deiminase (PAD) from a prokaryote. PAD displays biochemical characteristics and properties that suggest it may be a virulence agent. PAD deiminates the guanidino group of carboxyl-terminal arginine residues on various peptides, including the vasoregulatory peptide-hormone bradykinin, resulting in the formation of ammonia and a citrulline residue. The soluble protein has an estimated mass of 46 kDa, while the DNA sequence predicts a full-length protein of 61.7 kDa. PAD is most active at 55°C, stable at low pH, and exhibits the greatest activity above pH 9.0. Notably, in the presence of stabilizing factors, PAD is resistant to limited proteolysis and retains significant activity after brief exposure to boiling.
We propose that PAD, working in conjunction with arginine-specific proteinases from P. gingivalis, promotes the growth of the pathogen in the periodontal pocket, initially by enhancing its survivability and then by aiding the organism in evading host humoral defenses.

title: Traumatic encephalopathy: review and provisional research diagnostic criteria.
text:
Objective:
To determine the frequency of neurobehavioral signs and symptoms in published cases of traumatic encephalopathy (TE) in order to develop clinical diagnostic criteria with predictive validity.
Introduction:
Since 1928, cases of persistent or progressive neurological or neurobehavioral changes following head injuries have been reported. This condition is referred to as traumatic encephalopathy (TE). However, no diagnostic criteria have been established or accepted for the clinical diagnosis of TE. Provisional research diagnostic criteria are necessary for meaningful diagnosis and to facilitate research on the epidemiology, etiology, course, prognosis, imaging and biomarkers, neuropathological features, and potentially effective treatments of TE.
Methods:
All 436 published cases of TE were reviewed, and all symptoms and signs reported were classified and enumerated. Ninety-seven cases met inclusion criteria based on sufficient documentation of history and neurobehavioral examination. Provisional research diagnostic criteria for clinically probable and clinically possible TE were developed based on the most frequently reported clinical features.
Results:
Conclusion:
The provisional diagnostic criteria for TE presented here are the first published criteria for this condition based on a systematic analysis of its clinical characteristics. This is a crucial step towards scientifically derived consensus criteria, which are essential to accelerate progress in the investigation of this important condition.

title: Hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus infection.
text: In the United States, an estimated 200,000 individuals are infected with both hepatitis C virus (HCV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). As HIV-infected individuals have experienced prolonged life expectancy due to highly active antiretroviral therapy (ART), liver disease has emerged as a significant cause of morbidity and mortality. HIV infection appears to exacerbate all stages of HCV infection, leading to increased viral persistence and accelerated progression of HCV-related liver disease. Conversely, hepatitis C can complicate the management of HIV infection by increasing the incidence of liver toxicity caused by antiretroviral medications. The management of hepatitis C in HIV-infected individuals remains contentious due to the complexity of both infections and potential drug interactions, as well as the lack of published information. However, the high burden of liver disease warrants prompt management of HIV/HCV-coinfected patients, which must be based on data from studies conducted on individuals without HIV and an understanding of both infections. Properly designed studies of therapy in HIV/HCV-coinfected individuals are necessary to guide management of these patients in the future.

title: Role of the vascular endothelial growth factor pathway in tumor growth and angiogenesis.
text: New blood vessel formation (angiogenesis) is a crucial process in the growth and spread of tumors, making it a key area of research in cancer studies. The molecular mechanisms underlying tumor angiogenesis have been extensively investigated, with the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) pathway emerging as a major regulator of this process. The VEGF/VEGF-receptor axis involves multiple ligands and receptors with distinct binding specificities, expression patterns, and functions. Activation of this pathway triggers a network of signaling processes that promote endothelial cell growth, migration, and survival, as well as vessel permeability. Recent studies have also highlighted the role of VEGF in mobilizing endothelial progenitor cells from the bone marrow to sites of neovascularization. The well-established role of VEGF in promoting tumor angiogenesis and the pathogenesis of human cancers has led to the development of agents that target this pathway. Preclinical studies have shown that these agents can potently inhibit angiogenesis and tumor growth. In a significant breakthrough, an anti-VEGF antibody (bevacizumab) was found to improve survival and response rates in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer when used in combination with chemotherapy, validating VEGF pathway inhibitors as a promising new treatment approach in cancer therapy.

title: Frozen robust multiarray analysis (fRMA).
text:
Robust Multiarray Analysis (RMA) is the most widely used preprocessing algorithm for Affymetrix and Nimblegen gene expression microarrays. RMA performs background correction, normalization, and summarization in a modular fashion, with the last two steps requiring multiple arrays to be analyzed simultaneously. The ability to borrow information across samples provides RMA several advantages, including the ability to detect outliers more accurately through the use of a parametric model that accounts for probe effects, which are assumed to be fixed across arrays. Additionally, residuals obtained from the fitted model can be used to create useful quality metrics.
However, there are two drawbacks to the RMA method. Firstly, it cannot be used in clinical settings where samples must be processed individually or in small batches. Secondly, data sets preprocessed separately are not comparable.
To address these limitations, we propose a preprocessing algorithm called Frozen RMA (fRMA), which allows for the analysis of microarrays individually or in small batches. This is achieved by utilizing information from large publicly available microarray databases to estimate probe-specific effects and variances, which are then frozen. With new data sets, these estimates are used in conjunction with information from the new arrays to normalize and summarize the data.
We find that fRMA is comparable to RMA when the data are analyzed as a single batch, and outperforms RMA when analyzing multiple batches. The methods described here are implemented in the R package fRMA and are currently available for download from the software section of <http://rafalab.jhsph.edu>.

title: Hypoxia in relation to vasculature and proliferation in liver metastases in patients with colorectal cancer.
text: Purpose: To investigate the expression of hypoxia markers, including pimonidazole binding, glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1), and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX), in liver metastases of colorectal cancer, and to compare the expression of these markers in primary tumors. Methods: Twenty-five patients with liver metastases of colorectal cancer undergoing metastasectomy were included in the study. The hypoxia marker pimonidazole and proliferation marker iododeoxyuridine were administered before surgery, and the frozen metastases were then analyzed for pimonidazole binding, vascularity, and proliferation using immunofluorescent staining. Thirteen paraffin-embedded primary tumors were stained immunohistochemically for GLUT1 and CA-IX expression, and the expression was analyzed semiquantitatively in both primary tumors and corresponding liver metastases. Results: In liver metastases, pimonidazole binding showed a pattern consistent with diffusion-limited hypoxia, with a mean pimonidazole-positive fraction of 0.146 and a mean distance from vessels to pimonidazole-positive areas of 80 microm. Co-localization was observed between pimonidazole binding and GLUT1 or CA-IX expression in some areas, but mismatches were also observed. No correlation was found between the level of pimonidazole binding and GLUT1 or CA-IX expression. In some patients, a large fraction (up to 30%) of proliferating cells was present in pimonidazole-stained areas. Expression of CA-IX in primary tumors and metastases showed a significant correlation, which was absent for GLUT1 expression. Conclusions: Compared to other tumor types, liver metastases of colorectal cancer contain large amounts of hypoxic cells. The lack of correlation between pimonidazole binding and GLUT1 or CA-IX expression suggests that these markers may not be reliable endogenous markers of hypoxia in liver metastases.

title: Unmet needs mediate the relationship between symptoms and quality of life in breast cancer survivors
text:
This study aimed to investigate the symptoms, unmet needs, and quality of life (QoL) reported by women at different time points following breast cancer surgery and adjuvant treatment. Specifically, the study compared the symptoms, unmet needs, and QoL reported by women at 6 months to <2 years and 2 to 5 years after treatment. The study also evaluated the relationships among symptoms, unmet needs, and QoL using structural equation modeling.
The study included 113 and 137 breast cancer survivors who completed the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale, the Supportive Care Needs Survey-34, and the Medical Outcomes Study 12-item Short Form Health Survey version 2.0 during their medical follow-up. The results showed that the mean number of symptoms and unmet needs were higher among survivors at <2 years compared to those at 2 to 5 years after treatment. The most common reported symptoms were related to physical domains. No significant differences were found between the two survivor groups on the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale scores. However, survivors at <2 years reported higher scores in Psychological and Health Care System/Information needs, and lower composite scores in physical and mental QoL compared to those at 2 to 5 years post-treatment.
The study also found significant direct and indirect effects of symptom burden on survivors' physical and mental QoL through unmet needs, after adjusting for survival time. The models showed a good fit. These findings suggest that breast cancer survivors continue to experience many symptoms, regardless of the survivorship period, and that unmet needs play a mediating role in the relationship between symptom burden and QoL.

title: Phagocytosis and deposition of vascular beta-amyloid in rat brains injected with Alzheimer beta-amyloid.
text: The presence of extracellular beta-amyloid deposits in the brain is a defining feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). To investigate the impact of beta-amyloid in an animal model, the authors injected isolated beta-amyloid cores from AD brains into the cortex and hippocampus of rats. To control for any potential effects of the injection process, they also injected a contaminant called lipofuscin into the contralateral side of the brain. Rats were sacrificed at various time points after injection and the distribution of beta-amyloid was analyzed using four different histochemical techniques. The results showed that beta-amyloid and lipofuscin both moved from the injection site into unaffected neural tissue, persisted for at least one month, and were associated with increased levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein and microglia (OX-42) staining. By one week, many of the beta-amyloid cores had been engulfed by phagocytes, and some of the internalized beta-amyloid was found in vessels and ventricles. These findings suggest that phagocytic cells can internalize exogenous beta-amyloid and attempt to clear it from the central nervous system (CNS), indicating that the observed distribution of beta-amyloid may not necessarily reflect the initial site of deposition.

title: Specific sites in the C terminus of CTCF interact with the SA2 subunit of the cohesin complex and are required for cohesin-dependent insulation activity.
text: Recent studies have elucidated the crucial role of the protein CTCF in the organization of chromatin within the eukaryotic nucleus, particularly in the context of insulation and large-scale chromatin structure. CTCF's dependence on the cohesin complex for both activities has been demonstrated, and our findings reveal that the interaction between CTCF and cohesin involves direct contacts between the cohesin subunit SA2 and specific regions of the C-terminal tail of CTCF. Notably, all other cohesin components are recruited through their interaction with SA2. In vivo expression of CTCF mutants lacking the C-terminal domain or bearing mutations within it, which are required for SA2 binding, leads to disrupted expression profiles of imprinted genes IGF2-H19 and a loss of insulator function. Our results unequivocally demonstrate that specific regions on the C terminus of CTCF are essential for cohesin binding and insulator function. Furthermore, the observation that the only direct interaction between CTCF and cohesin involves contact with SA2, which is located external to the cohesin ring, suggests that SA2 may bind to CTCF first, followed by the assembly of the cohesin ring.

title: Interleukin 6 plays a key role in the development of antigen-induced arthritis.
text: To investigate the direct role of interleukin (IL-6) in the development of rheumatoid arthritis, IL-6-deficient (IL-6 -/-) mice were backcrossed for eight generations into C57BL/6 mice, a strain prone to antigen-induced arthritis (AIA). Both histological and immunological comparisons were made between IL-6-deficient (IL-6 -/-) mice and their wild-type (IL-6 +/+) littermates after the induction of AIA. While all IL-6 +/+ mice developed severe arthritis, only mild arthritis was observed in IL-6 -/- mice. Safranin O staining revealed that articular cartilage was well preserved in IL-6 -/- mice, whereas it was completely destroyed in IL-6 +/+ mice. Additionally, comparable mRNA expression for IL-1β and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), but not for IL-6, was detected in the inflamed joints of IL-6 -/- mice, suggesting that IL-6 may play a more crucial role in cartilage destruction than either IL-1β or TNF-α. In immunological comparisons, both antigen-specific in vitro proliferative response in lymph node cells and in vivo antibody production were elicited in IL-6 -/- mice, but they were reduced to less than half of that found in IL-6 +/+ mice. Lymph node cells from IL-6 -/- mice produced more Th2 cytokines than did IL-6 +/+ mice with either antigen-specific or nonspecific stimulation in in vitro culture. These results suggest that IL-6 may play a key role in the development of AIA at both the inductive and effector phases, and blocking IL-6 may be beneficial in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Relation between renal function within the normal range and central and peripheral arterial stiffness in hypertension.
text: In this study, we investigated the relationship between renal function and arterial stiffness in patients with never-treated essential hypertension. We found that glomerular filtration rate (GFR), estimated using the Mayo clinic equation, was inversely correlated with large-artery stiffness, as assessed by aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV), and with peripheral artery stiffness, as assessed by upper-limb PWV. In a multivariate linear regression analysis, aortic PWV was independently predicted by age, mean arterial pressure, and GFR, while upper-limb PWV was predicted by GFR and mean arterial pressure. These findings suggest that in hypertensive patients with normal renal function, there is an inverse relationship between GFR and stiffness of both central elastic and peripheral muscular arteries, which is independent of confounding factors such as age, sex, and blood pressure values.

title: Comparative gene expression profiling of in vitro differentiated megakaryocytes and erythroblasts identifies novel activatory and inhibitory platelet membrane proteins.
text: To identify previously uncharacterized platelet receptors, we compared the transcriptomes of in vitro differentiated megakaryocytes (MKs) and erythroblasts (EBs). We obtained RNA from purified, biologically paired MK and EB cultures and analyzed them using cDNA microarrays. Bioinformatic analysis of MK-up-regulated genes revealed 151 transcripts encoding transmembrane domain-containing proteins. While many of these were known platelet genes, we also identified several previously unidentified or poorly characterized transcripts. These included G6b, G6f, LRRC32, LAT2, and the G protein-coupled receptor SUCNR1. These proteins have structural features or functions that suggest they may play a role in modulating platelet function. We confirmed the presence of these proteins in platelets through immunoblotting and flow cytometric analysis. Through comparative analysis of expression in platelets and other blood cells, we found that G6b, G6f, and LRRC32 are specifically expressed in the platelet lineage, while LAT2 and SUCNR1 were also detected in other blood cells. The identification of the succinate receptor SUCNR1 in platelets is particularly interesting, as physiologically relevant concentrations of succinate were shown to potentiate the effect of low doses of various platelet agonists.

title: Topographic mapping of VMH → arcuate nucleus microcircuits and their reorganization by fasting
text: In the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC), pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons are inhibitory, while neuropeptide-Y (NPY) neurons are stimulatory. In a study, we investigated whether neurons in the ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus (VMH), a known satiety center, activate anorexigenic neuronal pathways in the ARC by projecting either excitatory or inhibitory inputs to POMC and NPY neurons. Using laser scanning photostimulation in brain slices from transgenic mice, we found that POMC and NPY neurons, which are interspersed in the ARC, are regulated by distinct synaptic inputs. POMC neurons receive strong excitatory input from the medial VMH (mVMH), while NPY neurons do not receive any inhibitory input from within the ARC. Instead, NPY neurons receive weak inhibitory input from the mVMH. The strength of the excitatory input from the mVMH to POMC neurons was found to be diminished by fasting. These findings identify a new molecularly defined circuit that is dynamically regulated by nutritional state in a manner consistent with the known role of the VMH as a satiety center.

title: The human immunodeficiency virus type 1 nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor resistance mutation I132M confers hypersensitivity to nucleoside analogs.
text:
In a previous study, we identified a rare mutation in the reverse transcriptase (RT) gene of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), specifically the I132M mutation, which confers resistance to non-nucleoside RT inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as nevirapine and delavirdine. In this follow-up study, we further investigated the role of this mutation in viral replication capacity and resistance to other RT inhibitors. Surprisingly, our findings showed that I132M actually confers increased sensitivity to nucleoside analogs such as lamivudine (3TC) and tenofovir, both at the virus and enzyme levels.
Using subunit-selective mutagenesis and transient kinetic analyses, we found that the mutation in the p51 subunit of RT was responsible for the increased sensitivity to these drugs. Specifically, the mutation decreases the enzyme's affinity for the natural dCTP substrate but increases its affinity for 3TC-triphosphate. Additionally, we observed that the replication capacity of HIV-1 containing the I132M mutation is significantly impaired. However, this decrease in viral replication capacity can be partially or completely compensated for by the A62V or L214I mutation, respectively.
Overall, these results provide insight into the mechanisms by which a single mutation outside of the polymerase active site and inside of the p51 subunit of RT can influence nucleotide selectivity and viral replication capacity. These findings may help explain the infrequent selection of I132M in patients for whom NNRTI regimens are failing and may have implications for the development of new antiretroviral therapies.

title: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs
text:
The AFF (AF4/FMR2) protein family functions as scaffolding proteins, linking two transcription elongation factors, P-TEFb and ELL1/2, in super elongation complexes (SECs), thereby regulating gene transcription. However, the role of AFF1 and AFF4 in the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of AFF1 and AFF4 depletion on MSC osteogenic differentiation using siRNA-mediated depletion and overexpression techniques.
Our findings indicate that AFF1 depletion leads to increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, enhanced mineralization, and upregulated expression of osteogenic-related genes in MSCs. Conversely, AFF4 depletion significantly inhibits MSC osteogenic potential. Furthermore, we found that overexpression of AFF1 and AFF4 differentially affects osteogenic differentiation in vitro and MSC-mediated bone formation in vivo.
Our mechanistic studies revealed that AFF1 regulates the expression of DKK1 via binding to its promoter region. Depletion of DKK1 in HA-AFF1-overexpressing MSCs abrogates the impairment of osteogenic differentiation. Additionally, we found that AFF4 is enriched in the promoter region of ID1. AFF4 knockdown blunts the BRE luciferase activity, SP7 expression, and ALP activity induced by BMP2 treatment.
In conclusion, our data demonstrate that AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying osteogenic differentiation and have important implications for the development of therapeutic strategies for bone-related disorders.

title: Markers of myocardial damage and inflammation in relation to long-term mortality in unstable coronary artery disease. FRISC Study Group. Fragmin during Instability in Coronary Artery Disease.
text:
In patients with unstable coronary artery disease, there is a correlation between short-term risk of death and blood levels of troponin T (a marker of myocardial damage) and C-reactive protein and fibrinogen (markers of inflammation). By analyzing data from an extension of the follow-up period in the Fragmin during Instability in Coronary Artery Disease trial, we investigated the usefulness of these markers and other indicators of risk as predictors of long-term risk of death from cardiac causes.
We evaluated the levels of C-reactive protein and fibrinogen at enrollment and the maximum level of troponin T during the first 24 hours in 917 patients with unstable coronary artery disease. The patients were followed for a mean of 37.0 months (range, 1.6 to 50.6). During follow-up, 1.2% of the 173 patients with troponin T levels of less than 0.06 microg/liter died of cardiac causes, compared to 8.7% of the 367 patients with levels of 0.06 to 0.59 microg/liter and 15.4% of the 377 patients with levels of at least 0.60 microg/liter (P=0.007 and P=0.001, respectively). Similarly, the rates of death from cardiac causes were 5.7% among the 314 patients with C-reactive protein levels of less than 2 mg/liter, 7.8% among the 294 with levels of 2 to 10 mg/liter, and 16.5% among the 309 with levels of more than 10 mg/liter (P=0.29 and P=0.001, respectively). The rates of death from cardiac causes were 5.4% among the 314 patients with fibrinogen levels of less than 3.4 g/liter, 12.0% among the 300 with levels of 3.4 to 3.9 g/liter, and 12.9% among the 303 with levels of at least 4.0 g/liter (P=0.004 and P=0.69, respectively).
In a multivariate analysis, levels of troponin T and C-reactive protein were independent predictors of the risk of death from cardiac causes. These markers were found to have a strong correlation with the long-term risk of death from cardiac causes, and their effects were additive with respect to each other and other clinical indicators of risk.
In conclusion, elevated levels of troponin T and C-reactive protein are strongly related to the long-term risk of death from cardiac causes in patients with unstable coronary artery disease. These markers are independent risk factors, and their effects are additive with respect to each other and other clinical indicators of risk.

title: Loss of lamin B1 results in prolongation of S phase and decondensation of chromosome territories.
text: Nuclear lamin B1 (LMNB1) plays a crucial role in the structural organization of the lamina mesh within interphase nuclei. To investigate the functional significance of LMNB1 in colon cancer cells, we employed RNA interference-mediated silencing of LMNB1 in the DLD-1 cell line. Our findings revealed a pronounced redistribution of histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) from the periphery to a more homogeneous distribution throughout the nucleus. Concomitantly, we observed telomere shortening, increased frequencies of micronuclei and nuclear blebs, and altered chromosome territory morphology as visualized by 3D-fluorescence in situ hybridization (3D-FISH). These changes were accompanied by a prolonged G1 phase due to the activation of checkpoint kinase 1 (Chk1). Furthermore, LMNB1 silencing led to extensive alterations in alternative splicing patterns of multiple genes and an increased number of enlarged nuclear speckles. Taken together, our results provide evidence for the essential role of the nuclear lamina in maintaining genome integrity, proper gene splicing, and chromosome organization during interphase.

title: Human artificial chromosomes with alpha satellite-based de novo centromeres show increased frequency of nondisjunction and anaphase lag.
text: Human artificial chromosomes have been employed to model the requirements for human chromosome segregation and to investigate the nature of sequences capable of functioning as centromeres. Normal human centromeres require specialized chromatin composed of alpha satellite DNA complexed with epigenetically modified histones and centromere-specific proteins. Although various types of alpha satellite DNA have been utilized to construct de novo centromeres in artificial chromosome assays, the extent to which they recapitulate normal centromere function has not been thoroughly examined. In this study, we utilized two types of alpha satellite DNA, DXZ1 (derived from the X chromosome) and D17Z1 (derived from chromosome 17), to generate human artificial chromosomes. Surprisingly, when we examined the segregation of these artificial chromosomes in individual cell divisions using an anaphase assay, we observed more segregation errors than natural human chromosomes (P < 0.001). Additionally, naturally occurring, but abnormal small ring chromosomes derived from chromosome 17 and the X chromosome also exhibited increased missegregation compared to normal chromosomes, suggesting that overall chromosome size and/or structure may play a role in the fidelity of chromosome segregation. Furthermore, our data indicate that variable centromeric DNA content and/or epigenetic assembly can influence the mitotic behavior of artificial chromosomes, with different artificial chromosomes exhibiting a fivefold range of missegregation.

title: Identification of a human HLA-E-restricted CD8+ T cell subset in volunteers immunized with Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi strain Ty21a typhoid vaccine.
text: Our previous research in volunteers immunized with Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi) has suggested a crucial role for CD8+ T cells in host defense. In this study, we identified a novel subset of nonclassical human HLA-E-restricted S. Typhi-specific CD8+ T cells derived from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of Ty21a typhoid vaccinees. These CD3+CD8+CD4-CD56- T cells were able to kill S. Typhi-infected targets without requiring classical HLA class I molecules, using a FAS-independent, granule-dependent mechanism that involved the release of granzyme B and the blocking effects of concanamycin and strontium ions. We also found that the expression of HLA-E antigens on the surface of S. Typhi-infected targets made them susceptible to lysis, and that anti-HLA-E antibodies partially blocked these responses. Additionally, we demonstrated that presentation of S. Typhi antigens via HLA-E could stimulate interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) production, with increased frequencies of IFN-gamma-producing cells observed when targets were coated with peptides containing S. Typhi GroEL HLA-E binding motifs. These findings suggest that HLA-E binds to nonamer peptides derived from bacterial proteins and triggers CD8+-mediated lysis and IFN-gamma production when exposed to infected targets, which could contribute to host defense against intracellular bacterial infections.

title: Costs and cost-effectiveness of alternative tuberculosis management strategies in South Africa--implications for policy.
text:
Objective: To conduct an economic analysis of the Hlabisa community-based directly observed therapy management strategy for tuberculosis and to estimate the costs of three alternative strategies.
Setting: Hlabisa health district, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
Methods: An economic analysis was conducted to compare the current tuberculosis management strategy in Hlabisa with three alternative strategies (the pre-1991 strategy based on hospitalization, the national strategy, and sanatorium care) in terms of costs to both the health service and patients, as well as cost-effectiveness.
Results: The current Hlabisa strategy was found to be the most cost-effective, with a total cost of R3799 per patient cured, compared to R98307 for the pre-1991 strategy, R9940 for the national strategy, and R11145 for sanatorium care. The majority of treatment costs (71-88%) are borne by the health service, with hospitalization (R119 per day) being the most expensive item. Prolonged hospitalization is expensive, but community care is cheaper (R28 for a community clinic visit, R7 for a community health worker visit). The total cost of supervising a patient in the community under the current Hlabisa strategy was R503, equivalent to 4.2 days in hospital. Drug costs (R157) are equivalent to just 1.3 days in hospital.
Conclusion: The findings of this study suggest that using community-based directly observed therapy for tuberculosis can significantly reduce costs to both the health service and patients, making it a cost-effective strategy in Hlabisa. These findings have important national implications and support the goals of the new tuberculosis control programme.

title: Interleukin-18 null mutation increases weight and food intake and reduces energy expenditure and lipid substrate utilization in high-fat diet fed mice
text:
Objective: The pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-18 (IL-18) has been implicated in the regulation of food intake and energy metabolism, but its effects on high-fat diet-fed animals remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the hypothesis that IL-18 modulates weight gain, energy intake, whole-body energy expenditure, and lipid fuel utilization in high-fat diet-fed mice.
Methods: The study compared the food intake, whole-body metabolism, and motor activity of IL-18 knockout mice with their wildtype littermates. The anorectic effects of intracerebroventricular IL-18 administration were also compared between IL-18 receptor knockout, IL-18/IL-18R knockout, and wildtype mice.
Results: Chow-reared IL-18 knockout mice were found to be overweight at 6 months of age and gained excess weight on both low-fat and high-fat diets. They also consumed more high-fat food and showed reduced whole-body energy expenditure and increased respiratory exchange ratios. These reductions in energy expenditure were observed across various conditions, including fasting and feeding, low- and high-fat diets, and different times of day. Additionally, the circadian amplitude of energy expenditure was blunted in IL-18 knockout mice, but not food intake, motor activity, or respiratory exchange ratio. Central IL-18 administration reduced high-fat diet intake in wildtype mice, but not in mice lacking the IL-18 receptor.
Conclusion: The loss-of-function results support the hypothesis that endogenous IL-18 suppresses appetite and promotes energy expenditure and lipid fuel substrate utilization not only during sickness, but also in healthy adults consuming high-fat diets.

title: Notch activation promotes cell proliferation and the formation of neural stem cell-like colonies in human glioma cells
text: Given the crucial role of Notch signaling in stem cells and oncogenesis, we hypothesized that the Notch pathway might play a role in cancer stem cells and cells with a stem cell phenotype in cancer. To investigate this, we examined the potential functions of the Notch pathway in the formation of cancer stem cells using human glioma. Using RT-PCR, we found that most human astrogliomas of different grades expressed moderate to high levels of Notch receptors and ligands, including Hes5 but not Hes1, which are downstream molecules of the Notch pathway. In human glioma cell lines BT325, U251, SHG-44, and U87, we detected mRNA encoding different types of Notch receptors, but only the active form of Notch1 (NIC) was detected in SHG-44 and U87 cells by Western blot. Interestingly, these two cell lines showed faster proliferation than the other two lines in which NIC was not detected. To evaluate the effects of Notch signaling on glioma cells, we over-expressed NIC in SHG-44 cells through constitutive transfection. Our results showed that over-expression of NIC in SHG-44 cells promoted the growth and colony-forming activity of these cells. Moreover, over-expression of NIC increased the formation of neurosphere-like colonies in the presence of growth factors, which expressed the stem cell marker nestin and could be induced to express neuron-, astrocyte-, or oligodendrocyte-specific markers, consistent with the phenotype of neural stem cells. These findings suggest that Notch signaling promotes the formation of cancer stem cell-like cells in human glioma.

title: Rodent models in bone-related research: the relevance of calvarial defects in the assessment of bone regeneration strategies.
text:
In vivo research using animal models has long been a preferred experimental system in bone-related biomedical research, as it allows for the collection of relevant data regarding physiological and pathological conditions that can inform the development of more effective clinical interventions. Animal models, and specifically rodent models, have been widely used and have made significant contributions to the development and refinement of translational approaches aimed at bone tissue regeneration. However, the use of certain types of defects in animal models, such as critical size defects that are unable to spontaneously heal, has been the subject of controversy.
This work aims to review the advantages and limitations of using rodent models in bone-related biomedical research, with a particular focus on the problematic issues surrounding the use of calvarial critical and subcritical size defects. Additionally, the surgical protocols for establishing both types of defects in rat calvarial bone will be described, as well as the most commonly used techniques for accessing the bone tissue repair process.
The use of animal models in bone-related research has several advantages, including the ability to study the progression of bone tissue repair in a controlled and reproducible manner, the ability to test the efficacy of new treatments in a preclinical setting, and the ability to identify potential therapeutic targets and mechanisms. However, there are also limitations to the use of animal models, including the potential for variability in the repair process between individual animals, the difficulty of directly translating findings from animal models to humans, and the ethical considerations surrounding the use of animals in research.
In the context of calvarial defects, the use of critical size defects has been controversial due to the inability of these defects to spontaneously heal. While these defects allow for the study of the later stages of bone tissue repair, they may not accurately reflect the healing process in humans. Subcritical size defects, on the other hand, are able to spontaneously heal, but may not be as representative of the later stages of bone tissue repair.
In conclusion, the use of rodent models in bone-related biomedical research is a valuable tool for understanding the mechanisms of bone tissue repair and for developing new treatments. However, it is important to carefully consider the advantages and limitations of using animal models, and to select the most appropriate type of defect for the research question being addressed. Additionally, the development of new techniques and technologies, such as 3D printing and tissue engineering, may provide alternative approaches to studying bone tissue repair that can address some of the limitations of animal models.

title: The transcriptional responses of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to inhibitors of metabolism: novel insights into drug mechanisms of action.
text: To investigate the transcriptional response of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to various drugs and growth-inhibitory conditions, a dataset of 430 microarray profiles was generated. Unsupervised clustering of these profiles accurately predicted the mechanism of action of previously uncategorized agents, such as pyridoacridones and phenothiazines, through biochemical validation. Analysis of the data set revealed 150 coordinately regulated gene clusters, providing the first glimpse into the full metabolic potential of M. tuberculosis. A subset of these gene clusters was sufficient to classify all known agents according to their mechanism of action. Transcriptional profiling of both crude and purified natural products can provide valuable insights into mechanism and detoxification, guiding the drug discovery process. Notably, the transcriptional profile of a crude marine natural product recapitulated the mechanistic prediction based on the pure active component, while the underlying gene clusters provided fundamental insights into the metabolic response of bacteria to drug-induced stress and the selection of critical metabolic targets for screening for new agents with improved activity against M. tuberculosis.

title: Electron microscopic studies of macrophages in early human yolk sacs.
text: In this study, the distribution and fine structure of macrophages were investigated in 10 human embryos at 6-7 weeks of gestation (5.5-12 mm in crown-rump length). Macrophages were found in both extravascular mesenchymal tissues and intravascular spaces, long before the appearance of bone marrow and lymphatic tissues. In addition to macrophages, fibroblastic cells and cells of the erythropoietic series were also present in the extravascular space. Macrophages exhibited various stages of maturity, with immature cells lacking heterophagolysosomes and mature cells showing avid phagocytosis of primitive erythroblasts and occasional platelets. Macrophages were positively stained for lysosomal enzymes and had numerous pleomorphic heterophagolysosomes, indicating digestion of phagocytized blood cells. The origin of intravascular macrophages may be due to either migrated extravascular macrophages or phagocytic endothelial cells. The phagocytosis and degradation of erythroblasts appeared to be a primary function of yolk sac macrophages. The presence of macrophages in mitosis suggested their proliferation in situ.

title: Urban malaria and anaemia in children: a cross-sectional survey in two cities of Ghana.
text:
Objective: To investigate the epidemiology of urban malaria in sub-Saharan Africa, with a specific focus on Ghana.
Methodology: Cross-sectional surveys were conducted in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana, to identify risk factors for malaria infection and anemia in children aged 6-60 months.
Findings: Malaria prevalence rates varied widely between urban communities, ranging from 2% to 33%. A significant proportion of children, 47.1%, were found to be anemic (Hb<11.0 g/dl). The study identified low socio-economic status, age, and anemia as key factors associated with malaria prevalence. The attributable risks of anemia and severe anemia (Hb<8.0 g/dl) caused by malaria were estimated to be 5% and 23%, respectively.
Conclusion: The study highlights the complexity and heterogeneity of malaria in urban areas, which differs from the rural environment. The findings underscore the importance of targeting specific areas or districts when designing malaria control measures, with a particular focus on the urban poor. A comprehensive assessment of the malaria risk pattern in any city is crucial to guide an integrated control program.

title: Nitrite infusions to prevent delayed cerebral vasospasm in a primate model of subarachnoid hemorrhage.
text: In this study, the authors investigated the effect of sodium nitrite infusions on the development of delayed cerebral vasospasm in anesthetized cynomolgus monkeys after subarachnoid hemorrhage. The study found that sodium nitrite infusions increased the levels of nitrite and methemoglobin in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid without causing systemic hypotension. Moreover, the infusions prevented the development of vasospasm in the cerebral arteries, as evidenced by a significant reduction in the area of vasospasm in the treated monkeys compared to the control group. The study also found a negative correlation between the concentration of nitrite in the cerebrospinal fluid and the degree of vasospasm. These findings suggest that sodium nitrite infusions may be a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing delayed cerebral vasospasm in patients after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

title: Developmental gene networks: a triathlon on the course to T cell identity
text: Cells attain their final identities by activating specific combinations of transcription factors, leading to the expression of genes specific to each cell type. The development of T cells involves three critical phases, each characterized by distinct transcription factor ensembles that regulate progenitor cell recruitment to the thymus, proliferation, lineage commitment, and responsiveness to T cell receptor signals. These phases are essential for proper T cell development, and the mechanisms that define their boundaries are equally important. Failure to properly regulate these processes can lead to leukemic transformation.

title: A tumor necrosis factor-α–mediated pathway promoting autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
text: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is caused by heterozygous mutations in either the PKD1 or PKD2 genes, which encode polycystin-1 and polycystin-2, respectively. Our findings demonstrate that tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), an inflammatory cytokine present in the cystic fluid of humans with ADPKD, disrupts the localization of polycystin-2 to the plasma membrane and primary cilia through a scaffold protein, FIP2, which is induced by TNF-α. Treatment of mouse embryonic kidney organ cultures with TNF-α led to the formation of cysts, and this effect was amplified in Pkd2+/− kidneys. Moreover, TNF-α stimulated cyst formation in vivo in Pkd2+/− mice, while treatment with the TNF-α inhibitor etanercept prevented cyst formation. These data uncover a pathway connecting TNF-α signaling, polycystins, and cystogenesis, which may lead to the ADPKD cellular phenotype by reducing the functional polycystin-2 below a critical threshold.

title: Inappropriate inhaler use: assessment of use and patient preference of seven inhalation devices. EDICI.
text:
Inefficient inhaler technique is a prevalent issue that can lead to suboptimal drug delivery, inadequate disease control, and increased inhaler use. The aim of this study was to investigate patients' preferences for different inhaler devices and determine whether patient preference is associated with ease of use and current inhaler use. Additionally, the study aimed to identify the most appropriate method of selecting an inhaler for a patient based on observed technique and device cost.
One hundred patients received instruction on the use of seven different inhaler devices in a randomized manner. After instruction, patients were evaluated using predetermined criteria for their inhaler technique. Patients were then asked to select their top three preferred inhalers and which, if any, they currently used. The results showed that patients had better technique when using breath-actuated inhalers, such as the Easi-Breathe and Autohaler, with 91% of patients demonstrating good technique. In contrast, the pressurized metered dose inhaler (pMDI) performed poorly, with only 79% of patients showing good technique, despite being the most commonly prescribed. The Easi-Breathe was the most popular device among patients, followed by the Autohaler, Clickhaler, and Accuhaler. Interestingly, despite the majority of patients (55%) currently using the pMDI, it did not score highly for preference or technique. In fact, only 79% of patients could use the pMDI effectively even after expert instruction, highlighting the importance of proper training and device selection.
These findings have significant implications for drug delivery and disease control. Prescribing a patient's preferred inhaler device can increase cost, but it may also improve efficiency and be cost-effective in the long term. Using an inexpensive device (pMDI) when technique is good and the patient's preferred inhaler device when not can help optimize delivery and potentially reduce costs.
In conclusion, this study highlights the importance of proper inhaler technique and device selection to ensure effective drug delivery and disease control. By taking into account patient preferences and device cost, healthcare providers can optimize drug delivery and improve patient outcomes.

title: Hemoperfusion-hemodialysis ineffective for paraquat removal in life-threatening poisoning?
text:
Introduction:
We report on a patient who was treated with hemoperfusion-hemodialysis (HP-HD) for severe paraquat poisoning. The rationale behind this treatment was the belief that the combination of adsorption and dialysis may improve overall drug removal.
Methods:
The patient was admitted to the hospital after ingesting paraquat, and conventional treatment was initiated. HP-HD was initiated within 3 hours of admission and lasted for 5 hours. Blood samples were collected during and after HP-HD. The samples were taken before the charcoal column, between the charcoal column and the artificial kidney, and after the artificial kidney.
Results:
The blood clearance of paraquat during HP-HD was 116 +/- 32 ml/min (n=6) for the charcoal column (HP), 90 +/- 54 ml/min (n=6) for the artificial kidney (HD), and 151 +/- 37 ml/min (n=6) for the combined systems (HP-HD). After HP-HD, a limited rebound of blood paraquat levels was observed. Renal and hepatic failure developed one day after admission, and the patient died 5 days later. Tissue paraquat levels were measured in various organs, including skeletal muscle, pancreas, prostate, thyroid, lungs, bone marrow, kidney, spleen, adrenal, heart, liver, stomach, and testis. The levels were as follows: skeletal muscle, 9.4 micrograms/g wet tissue; pancreas, 6.0 micrograms/g wet tissue; prostate, 5.6 micrograms/g wet tissue; thyroid, 4.2 micrograms/g wet tissue; lungs, 4.0 micrograms/g wet tissue; bone marrow, 4.0 micrograms/g wet tissue; kidney, 3.1 micrograms/g wet tissue; spleen, 2.9 micrograms/g wet tissue; adrenal, 2.9 micrograms/g wet tissue; heart, 2.8 micrograms/g wet tissue; liver, 2.3 micrograms/g wet tissue; stomach, <1.0 microgram/g wet tissue; testis, <1.0 microgram/g wet tissue. Measurements of blood levels demonstrated the efficient clearance of paraquat from the central (plasma) compartment with HP-HD. However, the present results confirmed previous findings that the efficiency of short HP-HD in treating severe paraquat poisoning is questionable, as paraquat levels in the peripheral (tissue) compartment remain elevated.
Discussion:
The present study demonstrates the potential of HP-HD in removing paraquat from the central compartment. However, the limited clearance of paraquat from the peripheral compartment suggests that HP-HD may not be effective in treating severe paraquat poisoning. The results of this study are consistent with previous findings, which have shown that the efficiency of short HP-HD in treating severe paraquat poisoning is questionable.
