Further research is needed to determine the optimal duration and technique of HP-HD for treating severe paraquat poisoning.

title: Cancer treatment and survivorship statistics, 2014.
text: The number of cancer survivors is increasing due to the aging and growth of the population, as well as improvements in early detection and treatment. To better serve these individuals, the American Cancer Society and the National Cancer Institute collaborated to estimate the number of current and future cancer survivors using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program registries. The study found that nearly 14.5 million Americans with a history of cancer were alive on January 1, 2014, and this number is expected to increase to nearly 19 million by January 1, 2024. The most common cancers among males are prostate cancer (43%), colorectal cancer (9%), and melanoma (8%), while among females, the most common cancers are breast cancer (41%), uterine corpus cancer (8%), and colon and rectum cancer (8%). The age distribution of survivors varies significantly by cancer type, with prostate cancer survivors being predominantly aged 70 years or older, while only a third of melanoma survivors are in this age group. It is essential for clinicians to understand the unique medical and psychosocial needs of cancer survivors and to proactively assess and manage these issues. There are a growing number of resources available to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers navigate the various phases of cancer survivorship.

title: Massive activation of archaeal defense genes during viral infection.
text: Archaeal viruses exhibit remarkable genetic and structural diversity, which has contributed significantly to our understanding of viral evolution. The Sulfolobus islandicus rod-shaped virus 2 (SIRV2) is a valuable model for investigating virus-host interactions in Archaea. It is a lytic virus that employs a unique mechanism of egress through the formation of pyramidal structures on the host cell envelope. By using whole-transcriptome sequencing, we have generated a comprehensive map of host and viral gene expression during the infection cycle of SIRV2 in its thermophilic host S. islandicus LAL14/1. This information, combined with a yeast two-hybrid analysis of SIRV2 protein interactions, has advanced our understanding of viral gene functions. As a result of SIRV2 infection, more than one-third of S. islandicus genes were found to be differentially regulated. Specifically, genes involved in cell division were downregulated, while genes involved in antiviral defense were upregulated on a large scale. The study also highlighted the specific activation of genes belonging to toxin-antitoxin and CRISPR-Cas systems. The differential activation of these systems underscores their specialized functions. The knowledge gained from this study is expected to aid future investigations into the intricate interactions between these systems in vivo.

title: Impact of human immunodeficiency virus infection on the histological features of chronic hepatitis C: a case-control study. The MULTIVIRC group.
text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is commonly found in individuals infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) due to shared transmission routes. Previous studies suggested that HIV infection may accelerate the progression of chronic hepatitis C to cirrhosis, but these studies did not consider the impact of HIV on chronic hepatitis C progression in relation to risk factors for liver fibrosis progression, such as alcohol consumption, sexual transmission, age of infection, and duration of HCV infection. To investigate this further, we analyzed liver biopsy samples from 58 patients infected with both HCV and HIV or HCV alone, and matched the groups according to these risk factors. Our findings showed that HIV-positive patients had higher METAVIR activity compared to HIV-negative patients, and cirrhosis was more frequent in HIV-positive patients with lower CD4 cell counts (45% vs 10%, P = 0.003). Additionally, cirrhosis was more common in HIV-positive patients with lower CD4 cell counts compared to those with higher CD4 cell counts (45% vs 17%, P = 0.04). These differences may be related to enhanced HCV replication during HIV infection or other immune mechanisms that require further investigation.

title: Relation of plasma leptin concentrations to sex, body fat, dietary intake, and peak oxygen uptake in young adult women and men.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between leptin and various metabolic and dietary factors in college-age adults. A total of 32 young adult men and women were recruited and underwent testing for body mass index (BMI), body composition, peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak), dietary intake, and plasma levels of leptin and insulin. The results showed that leptin levels were significantly higher in women than in men (2.1 vs. 1.2 ng/mL, respectively). This difference remained significant even after adjusting for fat mass and fat-free mass as covariates in separate analyses. In contrast, VO2peak was higher in men than in women, and this difference remained significant after adjusting for differences in fat-free mass and total body mass. Significant correlations were found between leptin levels and indicators of fat mass in both men and women, with stronger correlations observed in men. Specifically, there were positive correlations between leptin levels and body mass index (BMI), percentage of body fat, and fat mass in men, and negative correlations in women. Additionally, leptin levels showed an inverse relationship with VO2peak in men only. After adjusting for body fat mass using partial correlations, leptin levels were not significantly associated with any of the measured variables. However, when normalizing leptin levels using fat mass as the divisor, men showed statistically significant correlations between leptin and dietary intake and VO2peak. These findings suggest that leptin levels are associated with metabolic and dietary factors in men, but not in women.

title: Expression of a human cytomegalovirus latency-associated homolog of interleukin-10 during the productive phase of infection.
text: The human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) UL111A region is active during both the productive and latent phases of infection. During productive infection, the virus expresses ORF79, a protein with oncogenic properties, and cmvIL-10, a functional homolog of human IL-10. However, during the latent phase of infection in myeloid progenitor cells, an alternately spliced variant of cmvIL-10, termed latency-associated (LA) cmvIL-10, has been identified. To determine whether LAcmvIL-10 transcription occurs during productive infection, we performed 5' and 3' RACE to map UL111A-region transcripts in productively infected human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs). This analysis revealed the presence of a singly spliced UL111A-region transcript that encodes LAcmvIL-10. This transcript was expressed in HFFs with early (β) kinetics, which differs from the expression of ORF79 (α kinetics) and cmvIL-10 (γ kinetics). These findings identify and map a transcript encoding a latency-associated homolog of IL-10, which is expressed by the virus during the productive phase of infection.

title: Kruppel-like factor 4 is essential for inflammatory monocyte differentiation in vivo.
text: The Kruppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors plays a crucial role in the differentiation, survival, and trafficking of various blood and immune cell types. In this study, we investigate the role of KLF4 in hematopoietic cells using in vivo loss-of-function experiments. We demonstrate that hematopoietic cells from KLF4-deficient fetal livers (FL) maintain normal numbers of functional hematopoietic progenitor cells, are radioprotective, and perform equally well as KLF4-expressing cells in competitive repopulation assays. However, hematopoietic chimeras generated by transplanting KLF4-deficient fetal liver cells into lethally irradiated wild-type mice lack circulating inflammatory (CD115(+)Gr1(+)) monocytes and have reduced numbers of resident (CD115(+)Gr1(-)) monocytes. Although peritoneal macrophages in KLF4-deficient chimeras are normal, bone marrow monocytic cells from these chimeras exhibit lower levels of key trafficking molecules and are more apoptotic. These findings demonstrate that KLF4 is essential for the differentiation of mouse inflammatory monocytes and is involved in the differentiation of resident monocytes. Additionally, inducible expression of KLF4 in the HL60 human acute myeloid leukemia cell line stimulates monocytic differentiation and enhances 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol 13-acetate-induced macrophage differentiation, but blocks all-trans-retinoic acid-induced granulocytic differentiation of HL60 cells. The inflammation-selective effects of loss-of-KLF4 and the gain-of-KLF4-induced monocytic differentiation in HL60 cells identify KLF4 as a key regulator of monocytic differentiation and a potential target for translational immune modulation.

title: A population-based, case–control study of green tea consumption and leukemia risk in southwestern Taiwan
text: This study examined the relationship between green tea consumption and leukemia. A total of 252 cases (90.3% response rate) and 637 controls (53.4% response rate) were enrolled, with controls matched to cases based on age and gender. Information on participants' living habits, including tea consumption, was collected, and green tea was used to estimate total catechin consumption. Tea consumption was categorized into four levels. Conditional logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between leukemia and catechin consumption among subjects aged 0-15 and 16-29 years. A significant inverse association was found between green tea consumption and leukemia risk in individuals aged 16-29 years, while no significant association was observed in younger age groups. For the older group with higher amounts of tea consumption (>550 units of catechins), the adjusted odds ratio (OR) compared to the group without tea consumption was 0.47 (95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.23-0.97). After adjusting for smoking status and medical irradiation exposure, the overall OR for all participants was 0.49 (95% CI = 0.27-0.91), indicating an inverse relationship between high levels of catechins and leukemia. Drinking sufficient amounts of tea, particularly green tea, which contains more catechins than oolong tea and black tea, may reduce the risk of leukemia.

title: Specific HDV RNA-templated transcription by pol II in vitro.
text: RNA polymerase II is involved in the RNA-templated RNA synthesis during the replication of viroids and Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV), although the specific requirements for this process are not well understood. To investigate, we developed an in vitro transcription system using HeLa cell nuclear extract (NE) and a segment of antigenomic RNA corresponding to the left-hand tip region of the HDV rod-like structure as a template for efficient and highly specific RNA synthesis. Our results showed that the accumulation of the unique RNA product is highly sensitive to alpha-amanitin in HeLa NE, but only partially sensitive in NE from PMG cells that contain an allele of the alpha-amanitin-resistant subunit of pol II. This suggests that pol II is involved in this reaction. Further analysis of the RNA product revealed that it is a chimeric molecule composed of a newly synthesized transcript covalently attached to the 5' half of the RNA template. The selection of the start site for transcription is specific and depends on the secondary structure of the RNA template, rather than its primary sequence. Some features of this reaction resemble the RNA cleavage-extension process observed for pol II-arrested complexes in vitro. Our findings suggest that this reaction may play a role in HDV replication.

title: Pulmonary vascular lesions in end-stage idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Histopathologic study on lung explant specimens and correlations with pulmonary hemodynamics.
text:
In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), the blood vessels in the affected areas show distinct modifications, but the condition of the vessels in the remaining, healthier tissue is less clear. The relationship between blood vessel abnormalities and blood flow in the lungs is also not well understood. To address this gap in knowledge, we conducted a retrospective study on lung tissue samples from 26 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of IPF who had undergone lung transplantation. Our objectives were to:
1. Describe the vascular abnormalities in both fibrotic and preserved lung areas.
2. Examine the correlation between vascular lesions and pulmonary hemodynamics. In areas of dense fibrosis, we observed thickening of the arterial and venous walls, along with severe narrowing of the blood vessels. In contrast, architecturally preserved lung zones showed occlusion of venules and small pulmonary veins in approximately 65% of patients, although there were only mild changes in the muscular pulmonary arteries. We found a significant correlation between the extent of lung fibrosis and mean pulmonary artery pressure, but we did not detect a link between mean pulmonary artery pressure and venous/venular abnormalities in non-fibrotic areas. Our study suggests that in many cases of IPF, non-fibrotic lung tissue exhibits an occlusive venopathy, the significance of which remains unclear.

title: Maternal and perinatal outcome in severe pregnancy-related liver disease.
text: Over a 10-year period, 46 pregnant women (median age 30 years, range 17-41 years) were transferred to a Liver Failure Unit due to severe hepatic dysfunction during the third trimester of pregnancy. Of these, 70% were nulliparous and 5 had twin pregnancies, with a median gestational age of 35 weeks (range 24-40 weeks). At admission, 70% of the patients were preeclamptic and 46% were encephalopathic and/or ventilated. Clinical features and laboratory values consistent with Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy (AFLP) were present in 70% of the patients, while 15% had the HELLP syndrome. One patient had preeclamptic liver rupture requiring liver transplantation. In contrast to previous studies, this large series showed a relatively favorable maternal and perinatal outcome in severe AFLP and HELLP syndrome. To improve outcomes further, prevention of bleeding and infectious complications associated with these disorders is crucial.

title: Circadian rhythms and the regulation of metabolic tissue function and energy homeostasis.
text: Circadian rhythm regulators are crucial for synchronizing physiological processes with the recurring changes in the external environment. Recent clinical and molecular research suggests that circadian biology may have a significant impact on the regulation of metabolic tissue functions, including adipose tissue. In this discussion, we propose the hypothesis that disruptions in circadian rhythms may contribute to the development of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome.

title: Large-scale gene function analysis with the PANTHER classification system
text: The PANTHER (Protein Annotation through Evolutionary Relationships) classification system (<http://www.pantherdb.org/>) is a comprehensive platform that integrates gene function, ontology, pathways, and statistical analysis tools to enable biologists to analyze large-scale, genome-wide data from sequencing, proteomics, or gene expression experiments. The system is constructed using 82 complete genomes organized into gene families and subfamilies, with their evolutionary relationships captured in phylogenetic trees, multiple sequence alignments, and statistical models (hidden Markov models or HMMs). Genes are classified based on their function through various methods, including ontology terms (Gene Ontology (GO) and PANTHER protein class), and sequence assignment to PANTHER pathways. The PANTHER website provides a suite of tools for browsing and querying gene functions, as well as analyzing large-scale experimental data with various statistical tests. It is widely used by bench scientists, bioinformaticians, computer scientists, and systems biologists. In the 2013 release of PANTHER (v.8.0), the data content was updated, and the website interface was redesigned to improve both user experience and analytical capability. This protocol provides a detailed guide on how to analyze genome-wide experimental data with the PANTHER classification system.

title: Periostin, a novel marker of intramembranous ossification, is expressed in fibrous dysplasia and in c-Fos-overexpressing bone lesions.
text:
Fibrous dysplasia is a benign bone disorder caused by a mutation in the gene for the stimulatory guanine nucleotide-binding protein Gs alpha, leading to elevated levels of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP). Histologically, fibrous dysplasia is characterized by the production of fibrous tissue, accompanied by the deposition of ectopic type I collagen and other bone-associated extracellular matrix proteins, as well as irregular woven intramembranous bone onto which type I collagen-containing Sharpey fibers are often attached. Fibrous dysplasia is also characterized by high levels of c-Fos/c-Jun, known targets of cAMP signaling.
In this study, we investigated the expression of the bone-related extracellular matrix protein periostin and its known receptor, integrin alpha v beta 3 (CD51/61), in normal bones and fibrous dysplasia. Immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization studies revealed that periostin is expressed in the extracellular matrix during intramembranous but not endochondral ossification, as well as in the fibrous component of fibrous dysplasia. All cells adjacent to periostin-positive regions expressed CD51/61. Importantly, periostin was abundantly localized to Sharpey fibers.
To further investigate the role of c-Fos in fibrous dysplasia, we examined transgenic mice overexpressing c-Fos, which develop sclerotic lesions resembling those found in fibrous dysplasia. In all lesions, transformed osteoblasts expressed high levels of periostin, whereas normal osteoblasts did not. Our results suggest that periostin is a novel marker for intramembranous ossification and may be a useful diagnostic tool and/or therapeutic target in fibrous dysplasia. Moreover, the Gs alpha-cAMP-c-Fos pathway may represent one mechanism of periostin up-regulation in fibrous dysplasia, leading to altered collagen fibrillogenesis characteristic of this disease.

title: FGF-2 enhances intestinal stem cell survival and its expression is induced after radiation injury.
text:
Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) have the ability to stimulate cell growth and division in a wide range of cell types, including those of mesenchymal, neuronal, and epithelial origin. During normal embryonic development, FGFs play a crucial role in regulating various events. Additionally, they are involved in angiogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. While FGF-2 is expressed in many adult tissues, its effects on intestinal epithelial stem cells during normal epithelial renewal or regeneration are not well understood.
In this study, we investigated the expression of FGF-2 in the mouse small intestine after irradiation and examined the effect of exogenous FGF-2 on crypt stem cell survival after radiation injury. We found that expression of FGF-2 mRNA and protein increased significantly at 12 hours after irradiation, reaching peak levels between 48 and 120 hours. The higher molecular mass isoform (approximately 24 kDa) of FGF-2 was the predominant form expressed in the small intestine. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that FGF-2 was primarily found in the mesenchyme surrounding regenerating crypts.
Our results also showed that exogenous recombinant human FGF-2 (rhFGF-2) significantly enhanced crypt stem cell survival when given before irradiation. These findings suggest that expression of FGF-2 is induced by radiation injury, and that rhFGF-2 can enhance crypt stem cell survival after subsequent injury.
In summary, our study demonstrates that FGF-2 plays a crucial role in the regulation of intestinal epithelial stem cell survival after radiation injury, and that exogenous FGF-2 can enhance crypt stem cell survival. These findings have important implications for the understanding of the mechanisms of radiation-induced damage to the intestinal epithelium and the development of strategies for protecting against this damage.

title: Caspase inhibitors promote alternative cell death pathways.
text: The use of caspase inhibitors has revealed the existence of backup cell death programs for apoptosis, which can be modulated by broad-spectrum caspase inhibitors like zVAD-fmk. This compound can block apoptotic cell death, sensitize cells to necrotic cell death, and induce autophagic cell death. Recent studies have shown that the kinase RIP1 and the adenosine nucleotide translocator (ANT)-cyclophilin D (CypD) complex play crucial roles in necrotic cell death, and the mechanism of zVAD-fmk-mediated sensitization involves the inhibition of caspase-8-mediated proteolysis of RIP1 and disruption of the ANT-CypD interaction. Additionally, caspase inhibitors and knockdown studies have revealed negative roles for catalase and caspase-8 in autophagic cell death. These findings suggest that the pathways of necrotic and autophagic cell death are interconnected, with RIP1 playing a positive role in both and caspase-8 having a negative role in both. Necrotic cell death is a rapid response to cellular insults, including mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and decreased adenosine triphosphate concentration, whereas autophagic cell death begins as a survival attempt to clean up ROS-damaged mitochondria. However, when this process occurs in excess, autophagy can become cytotoxic and lead to autophagic cell death. A better understanding of these alternative cell death pathways may provide therapeutic tools to combat cell death associated with neurodegenerative diseases, ischemia-reperfusion pathologies, and infectious diseases, as well as alternative cytotoxic strategies in cancer treatment.

title: Nucleosome stability mediated by histone variants H3.3 and H2A.Z.
text: Nucleosomes containing the histone variant H3.3 are observed to be clustered in vivo near transcriptionally active genes and regulatory elements. However, it has remained unclear whether H3.3-containing nucleosomes possess distinct properties that could impact transcription. In this study, we investigate the stability of H3.3 nucleosomes isolated from vertebrates in the presence of salt, which can disrupt nucleosome structure. Our results reveal that H3.3 nucleosomes, regardless of their association with H2A or H2A.Z, are unusually sensitive to salt-dependent disruption, resulting in the loss of H2A/H2B or H2A.Z/H2B dimers. Immunoprecipitation studies of nucleosome core particles (NCPs) further reveal that NCPs containing both H3.3 and H2A.Z are less stable than those containing H3.3 and H2A, while NCPs containing H3 and H2A.Z are at least as stable as those containing H3 and H2A. These findings establish an hierarchy of stabilities for native nucleosomes carrying different variants and suggest that H2A.Z may play different roles depending on its partners within the NCP. Additionally, the results are consistent with the idea that H3.3 plays an active role in maintaining accessible chromatin structures in enhancer regions and transcribed regions, as promoters and enhancers at transcriptionally active genes and coding regions at highly expressed genes exhibit nucleosomes carrying both H3.3 and H2A.Z, which should be highly sensitive to disruption.

title: Increased growth after long-term oral 1alpha,25-vitamin D3 in childhood renal osteodystrophy.
text: In this study, we evaluated the effectiveness of oral 1,25-vitamin D3 in treating renal osteodystrophy in six prepubescent children who had previously been treated with vitamin D2. The children received daily doses of 14 to 41 ng of 1,25-vitamin D3 per kilogram of body weight to correct hypocalcemia and reverse bone disease. We measured the serum levels of 1,25-vitamin D3 before and after treatment and found that they increased significantly, from an initial level of 15 +/- 5 pg/mL to 54 +/- 13 pg/mL after 26 months of treatment. Additionally, we observed a significant increase in serum calcium levels, from 7.5 +/- 1.6 mg/dL to 9.8 +/- 0.6 mg/dL after one month of treatment, and a decrease in alkaline phosphatase activity from 536 +/- 298 to 208 +/- 91 IU/L after 12 months of treatment. Furthermore, we found that serum immunoreactive parathyroid levels decreased from 900 +/- 562 to 411 +/- 377 microliter/mL after 26 months of treatment. The healing of rickets and subperiosteal erosions was also observed, and remineralization of bone was demonstrated using a photon absorption technique. In terms of growth, we found that the growth velocity of the children increased significantly, from 2.6 +/- 0.8 to 8.0 +/- 3.2 cm/year, and the growth velocity per year increased from less than the third percentile to the 10th to 97th percentile after treatment. The height increment ranged from 27 to 113 percent of the expected change in chronologic age and 40 to 114 percent of the expected change in bone age after treatment. Overall, this trial demonstrates that oral 1,25-vitamin D3 can effectively reverse renal bone disease and increase growth in uremic children.

title: Rapid progression of familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy: a multinational natural history study.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the relationship between the severity of neuropathy and disease stage in patients with familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy (FAP) across different countries, and to estimate the rate of neuropathy progression using a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a multinational population.
Methods:
We analyzed data from 283 patients with FAP in France, the United States, Portugal, and Italy, assessing neuropathy severity using Neuropathy Impairment Scores (NIS), time from symptom onset to NIS measurement, polyneuropathy disability (PND) scores, FAP disease stage, and manual grip strength data. We used Loess Fit and Gompertz Fit models to estimate neuropathy progression.
Results:
Our findings showed significant intercountry genotypic variation in the transthyretin (TTR) mutation, with the majority of patients in Portugal (92%) having early-onset Val30Met-FAP. There was also significant intercountry variation in PND score, FAP stage, and TTR stabilizer use. Neuropathy Impairment Scores (NIS) were associated with PND score (NIS 10 and 99 for scores I and IV, respectively; p < 0.0001) and FAP stage (NIS 14 and 99 for stages 1 and 3, respectively; p < 0.0001). Additionally, there was an association between NIS and TTR genotype. The estimated rate of NIS progression for a population with a median NIS of 32 was 14.3 points/year; the corresponding estimated rate for the modified NIS+7 is 17.8 points/year.

Conclusion:
Our study demonstrates rapid neuropathic progression in patients with FAP across different countries, and highlights the association between the severity of neuropathy and disease stage. These findings have important implications for the management and monitoring of FAP patients, particularly in the context of TTR stabilizers, which have been shown to slow neuropathy progression in some studies.

title: The BRRF1 early gene of Epstein-Barr virus encodes a transcription factor that enhances induction of lytic infection by BRLF1.
text: The switch from a latent to a lytic form of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is mediated by the expression of viral immediate-early (IE) proteins, BZLF1 (Z) and BRLF1 (R). An EBV early protein, BRRF1 (Na), encoded by the opposite strand of the BRLF1 intron, plays a previously unknown role in the viral life cycle. Here, we demonstrate that Na enhances the R-mediated induction of lytic EBV infection in 293 cells latently infected with a recombinant EBV (R-KO) defective in both R and Na expression. Na also enhances R-induced lytic infections in a gastric carcinoma line (AGS) carrying the R-KO virus, although it has no effect in a Burkitt lymphoma line (BL-30) stably infected with the same mutant virus. We show that Na is a transcription factor that increases the ability of R to activate Z expression from the R-KO viral genome in 293 cells and that Na can activate the Z promoter (Zp) in EBV-negative cells. Na activation of Zp requires a CRE motif (ZII), and a consensus CRE motif is sufficient to transfer Na responsiveness to the heterologous E1b promoter. Additionally, we find that Na enhances the transactivator function of a Gal4-c-Jun fusion protein but does not increase the transactivator function of other transcription factors (including ATF-1, ATF-2, and CREB) known to bind CRE motifs. Our results suggest that Na is a transcription factor that activates the EBV Zp IE promoter through its effects on c-Jun and indicate that Na cooperates with BRLF1 to induce the lytic form of EBV infection in certain cell types.

title: Stromal p16 expression differentiates endometrial polyp from endometrial hyperplasia
text:
Endometrial polyps are common benign growths in the lining of the uterus, but their exact cause is not well understood. Recent studies suggest that these polyps may be a type of benign stromal neoplasm. However, it can be challenging to distinguish endometrial polyps from endometrial hyperplasia, a condition where the lining of the uterus grows abnormally, on a biopsy or curettage sample. Currently, there is no reliable immunohistochemical marker to help with this distinction.
In this study, we examined the expression of the protein p16 in 35 endometrial polyps and 33 cases of endometrial hyperplasia. We found that stromal p16 expression was significantly higher in endometrial polyps (89%) compared to endometrial hyperplasia (3%). The percentage of p16-positive stromal cells ranged from 10 to 90% (mean 47%) and were mostly found around glands. Interestingly, all six cases of endometrial hyperplasia within an endometrial polyp showed stromal p16 expression. There was no significant difference in glandular p16 expression between endometrial polyps (94%) and hyperplasia (82%). The p16-immunoreactivity was mostly confined to metaplastic epithelial cells in both groups.
Our findings suggest that stromal p16 expression may be a distinct characteristic of endometrial polyps and could potentially serve as a useful marker for their diagnosis, particularly in fragmented samples from biopsy or curettage. It is possible that stromal p16 expression is a reflection of p16-induced cellular senescence, which has been documented in several benign mesenchymal neoplasms.

title: A systematic review of mortality in schizophrenia: is the differential mortality gap worsening over time?
text:
Despite improvements in mental health services over the past few decades, it remains unclear whether the risk of mortality in individuals with schizophrenia has changed over time. To investigate this, we conducted a comprehensive review of studies that examined mortality rates in people with schizophrenia.
Our analysis included 37 studies from 25 different countries, which provided data on mortality rates in over 100,000 individuals with schizophrenia. We found that the standardized mortality ratio (SMR) for all-cause mortality was 2.58 (95% CI: 1.18-5.76), with a corresponding pooled SMR of 2.50 (95% CI: 2.18-2.43) across all individuals. We did not observe any significant sex differences in mortality rates. However, we found that suicide was associated with the highest SMR (12.86). Additionally, we found that the SMRs for all-cause mortality have increased over time (P = 0.03).
Our findings suggest that there is a substantial gap in mortality rates between individuals with schizophrenia and the general population. This differential mortality gap has worsened over recent decades, highlighting the urgent need to address the general health of individuals with schizophrenia. In light of the potential for second-generation antipsychotic medications to further adversely influence mortality rates in the coming decades, optimizing the general health of people with schizophrenia is crucial.

title: Antioxidant Defenses in the Rat Placenta in Late Gestation: Increased Labyrinthine Expression of Superoxide Dismutases, Glutathione Peroxidase 3, and Uncoupling Protein 21
text: The role of oxidative stress in placenta-related disorders, such as preeclampsia (PE) and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), is significant. Oxidative stress occurs when there is an accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which can damage DNA, proteins, and lipids. The mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) may also play a role in limiting oxidative stress by reducing ROS production. In this study, we investigated the placental antioxidant defenses during normal gestation and following glucocorticoid-induced IUGR. We analyzed the expression of several genes encoding antioxidant enzymes (Sod1, Sod2, Sod3, Cat, Gpx3, Txn1, Txnrd1, Txnrd2, and Txnrd3) and Ucp2 in the labyrinth (LZ) and junctional zones (JZ) of the placenta. Our results showed that the expression of Sod1 and Ucp2 mRNAs and the activity of xanthine oxidase, a source of ROS, increased from Days 16 to 22 in both placental zones. In contrast, Sod2 and Gpx3 increased only in the rapidly growing LZ. Dexamethasone treatment reduced fetal-placental growth and LZ expression of Ucp2, but increased JZ expression of Txn1. Our findings suggest that the rat placenta is protected from oxidative stress by the dynamic zone- and stage-dependent expression of antioxidant defense genes.

title: Emerging role of bisphosphonates in the clinic--antitumor activity and prevention of metastasis to bone.
text: Bisphosphonates are currently used to treat bone metastases, and emerging evidence suggests they may also have antitumor properties. Preclinical studies have shown that zoledronic acid can inhibit angiogenesis, invasion, and adhesion of tumor cells, and slow down overall tumor progression. Recent clinical data in patients with metastatic bone disease have found that basal levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a key factor in angiogenesis, were significantly reduced in those receiving zoledronic acid, suggesting that zoledronic acid may have clinically relevant antiangiogenic properties. Early clinical trials in patients with breast cancer have yielded promising results with the use of clodronate, an earlier-generation bisphosphonate, in preventing bone metastases. Currently, trials are underway to assess the efficacy of clodronate in this setting. Additionally, small pilot studies have demonstrated zoledronic acid's activity in preventing bone metastases in patients with high-risk solid tumors, with an overall survival advantage observed in patients receiving zoledronic acid compared to those receiving standard treatment alone in a separate 5-year trial involving patients with multiple myeloma. These encouraging early clinical results have supported the initiation of larger randomized trials that are currently ongoing.

title: LIF/STAT3 controls ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency by a Myc-dependent mechanism.
text: Murine embryonic stem (ES) cells can be maintained as a pluripotent, self-renewing population through LIF/STAT3-dependent signaling. However, the downstream effectors of this pathway have remained unidentified until now. In this study, we investigate the key target of the LIF self-renewal pathway by showing that STAT3 directly regulates the expression of the Myc transcription factor. ES cells exhibit elevated levels of Myc, which collapse upon LIF withdrawal and result in the phosphorylation of Myc on threonine 58 (T58). This phosphorylation triggers its GSK3β-dependent degradation, leading to maintained self-renewal and pluripotency independence from LIF. Conversely, expression of a dominant negative form of Myc inhibits self-renewal and promotes differentiation. Our findings establish a mechanism for how LIF and STAT3 regulate ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency, highlighting the crucial role of transcriptional control by STAT3 and suppression of T58 phosphorylation in maintaining Myc activity and pluripotency.

title: Chronic renal failure accelerates atherogenesis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice.
text:
Cardiovascular mortality is 10 to 20 times higher in patients with chronic renal failure (CRF) compared to the general population. This increased risk is due to the presence of numerous risk factors for atherosclerosis in patients with CRF. However, the underlying mechanisms of cardiovascular disease in CRF remain unclear. To investigate this, we examined the effect of CRF on the development of atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient male mice.
Seven-week-old mice underwent 5/6 nephrectomy (CRF, n = 28), unilateral nephrectomy (UNX, n = 24), or no surgery (n = 23). Twenty-two weeks later, CRF mice showed significantly increased aortic plaque area fraction, aortic cholesterol content, and aortic root plaque area compared to no-surgery mice. UNX mice showed intermediate values. The plaques from uremic mice contained CD11b-positive macrophages and showed strong staining for nitrotyrosine. Systolic BP and plasma homocysteine concentrations were similar in uremic and non-uremic mice. Plasma urea and cholesterol concentrations were elevated 2.6-fold and 1.5-fold, respectively, in CRF compared to no-surgery mice. Both variables correlated with aortic plaque area fraction and with each other. On multiple linear regression analysis, only plasma urea was a significant predictor of aortic plaque area fraction.
Our findings suggest that uremia significantly accelerates atherogenesis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice. This effect cannot be fully explained by changes in BP, plasma homocysteine levels, or total plasma cholesterol concentrations. Therefore, the CRF apolipoprotein E-deficient mouse is a valuable new model for studying the pathogenesis of accelerated atherosclerosis in uremia.

title: Left ventricular function and exercise capacity.
text: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between left ventricular function, as assessed by echocardiography, and exercise capacity in a large cohort of patients undergoing exercise echocardiography. The study found that diastolic dysfunction, as measured by echocardiography, was strongly and inversely associated with exercise capacity. Specifically, patients with moderate or severe resting diastolic dysfunction had significantly lower exercise capacity compared to those with normal diastolic function. Additionally, the study found that left ventricular filling pressures, as measured by resting and post-exercise E/e' ratio, were also associated with a reduction in exercise capacity. The study also found that age, sex, and body mass index were independent correlates of exercise capacity. The study suggests that assessing left ventricular function by echocardiography may be useful in predicting exercise capacity and identifying individuals at risk of reduced exercise capacity, particularly in older adults and women.

title: A dynamic population model to investigate effects of climate on geographic range and seasonality of the tick Ixodes scapularis.
text:
A dynamic population model of Ixodes scapularis, the vector of several tick-borne zoonoses in North America, was developed to simulate the effects of temperature on tick survival and seasonality. The model took into account the temperature-dependent development rates of ticks, as well as the impact of temperature on host-finding success. By using data from meteorological stations near endemic populations of I. scapularis, the model reached repeatable, stable, cyclical equilibria with seasonal activity of different instars that were similar to observations in the field. In simulations run using data from central and eastern Canada, the maximum equilibrium numbers of ticks declined as the station location became more northern, and simulated populations died out at the northernmost stations. The decline in tick populations at northern latitudes was due to a gradual increase in mortality of all life stages with decreasing temperature, rather than a specific threshold event in the phenology of one life stage.
To investigate the relationship between temperature conditions and tick populations, the authors used mean annual numbers of degree-days >0 degrees C (DD>0 degrees C) as a readily available index of temperature conditions at the meteorological stations providing temperature data for the model. The results showed that maximum numbers of ticks at equilibrium were strongly associated with the mean DD>0 degrees C, with the Province of origin of the meteorological station being a significant factor (Quebec>Ontario, beta=103, P<0.001). The intercepts of the regression models provided theoretical limits for the establishment of I. scapularis in Canada, which were mapped to suggest that the range of southeast Canada where temperature conditions are currently suitable for the tick is much wider than the existing distribution of I. scapularis, indicating potential for spread. The authors concluded that the model could be used to investigate the impact of climate change on I. scapularis populations and to inform public health strategies for tick-borne disease control.

title: Inflammatory cytokines in depression: neurobiological mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
text:
Increasing evidence suggests that inflammatory cytokines play a role in the development of depression in both medically ill and healthy individuals. Cytokines are essential for brain development and function, and can influence neurocircuitry and neurotransmitter systems to produce behavioral changes. Acute exposure to inflammatory cytokines can lead to adaptive behavioral responses that conserve energy to combat infection or recover from injury. However, chronic exposure to elevated inflammatory cytokines and persistent alterations in neurotransmitter systems can contribute to the development of neuropsychiatric disorders, including depression.
The mechanisms by which cytokines affect behavior involve activation of inflammatory signaling pathways in the brain, leading to changes in monoamine, glutamate, and neuropeptide systems, and decreases in growth factors such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor. Inflammatory cytokines may also act as mediators of environmental and genetic factors that contribute to depression's development, such as childhood trauma, obesity, stress, and poor sleep.
This review explores the idea that specific gene polymorphisms and neurotransmitter systems can confer protection from or vulnerability to specific symptom dimensions of cytokine-related depression. Additionally, potential therapeutic strategies that target inflammatory cytokine signaling or the consequences of cytokines on neurotransmitter systems in the brain to prevent or reverse cytokine effects on behavior are discussed.
In summary, mounting evidence suggests that inflammatory cytokines play a role in the development of depression, and that targeting these cytokines or the consequences of their action on the brain may provide a promising avenue for the prevention or treatment of depression.

title: Sputum inflammation predicts exacerbations after cessation of inhaled corticosteroids in COPD.
text:
The GOLD guidelines advise against initiating inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in patients with mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, many patients already use ICS, and withdrawal is associated with worsening lung function and increased exacerbation rates. Unfortunately, it is unclear which patients can safely stop ICS treatment. This study aimed to identify predictors of COPD exacerbations after ICS withdrawal.
Methods:
During ICS treatment, post-bronchodilator spirometry, body plethysmography, and health status assessment were performed in 68 COPD patients. Additionally, sputum cell differentials, supernatant leukotriene B(4), eosinophilic cationic protein, and myeloperoxidase, serum C-reactive protein, and soluble intracellular adhesion molecule, and urinary desmosine were assessed. Sputum was also analyzed for mRNA levels of hemoxygenase-1, tumor necrosis factor-α, RANTES, interleukin 5 (IL-5), IL-10, IL-12, IL-13, transforming growth factor-β, and interferon-γ.
Results:
Higher sputum % eosinophils, higher sputum myeloperoxidase/neutrophil level, longer duration of COPD symptoms, <40 packyears smoking, and ICS withdrawal in November, December, or January were significant hazards (all p<0.05) for experiencing a COPD exacerbation after ICS withdrawal in a monovariate model. In a multivariate model, all factors proved independent predictors except for sputum myeloperoxidase/neutrophil level.
Conclusions:
Assessing sputum inflammation, particularly eosinophil numbers, next to packyears smoking, season, and duration of COPD symptoms, can help facilitate decisions on whether or not ICS can be safely withdrawn in mild-to-moderate COPD patients.

title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha activation decreases metastatic potential of melanoma cells in vitro via down-regulation of Akt.
text:
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) play a crucial role in regulating lipid and glucose metabolism, but recent studies have also highlighted their anticancer properties. In our previous work, we demonstrated the antimetastatic activity of the PPARα ligand, fenofibrate, against melanoma tumors in vivo. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-metastatic action of fenofibrate.
We employed a variety of experimental approaches, including monolayer cultures of mouse (B16F10) and human (SkMell88) melanoma cell lines, soft agar assays, and cell migration assays. Additionally, we examined PPARα expression and its transcriptional activity in response to fenofibrate using Western blots and a luciferase-based reporter system.
Our results showed that fenofibrate inhibited the migration of B16F10 and SkMel188 cells in Transwell chambers and colony formation in soft agar. These effects were reversed by a PPAR inhibitor, GW9662. Western blot analysis revealed a time-dependent down-regulation of Akt and extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) phosphorylation in fenofibrate-treated cells. Interestingly, a B16F10 cell line stably expressing a constitutively active Akt mutant was resistant to the anti-metastatic effects of fenofibrate, while Akt gene silencing with siRNA mimicked the fenofibrate action and reduced the migratory ability of B16F10 cells. Furthermore, fenofibrate strongly sensitized B16F10 cells to the pro-apoptotic drug staurosporine, suggesting that the down-regulation of Akt function contributes to the anti-metastatic effects of fenofibrate in this experimental model.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that the PPAR-dependent antimetastatic activity of fenofibrate involves the down-regulation of Akt phosphorylation. These results provide evidence that supplementation with this drug may enhance the effectiveness of melanoma chemotherapy.

title: PHC3, a component of the hPRC-H complex, associates with E2F6 during G0 and is lost in osteosarcoma tumors
text: Polyhomeotic-like 3 (PHC3) is a ubiquitously expressed member of the polycomb gene family and a component of the human polycomb complex hPRC-H. Our findings reveal that in normal cells, PHC3 associates with both hPRC-H complex components and the transcription factor E2F6. In differentiating and confluent cells, PHC3 and E2F6 exhibit nuclear colocalization in a punctate pattern resembling the binding of polycomb bodies to heterochromatin. This punctate pattern is not observed in proliferating cells, suggesting that PHC3 may be part of an E2F6-polycomb complex that occupies and silences target promoters in G0. Previous loss of heterozygosity (LoH) analyses have shown that the region containing PHC3 undergoes frequent LoH in primary human osteosarcoma tumors. In examining normal bone and human osteosarcoma tumors, we found that PHC3 is lost in 36 of 56 osteosarcoma tumors, and sequence analysis revealed that PHC3 is mutated in nine of 15 primary osteosarcoma tumors. These findings suggest that loss of PHC3 may contribute to tumorigenesis by disrupting the ability of cells to remain in G0.

title: Germinal center T follicular helper cell IL-4 production is dependent on signaling lymphocytic activation molecule receptor (CD150).
text: CD4 T cell help is crucial for the formation and maintenance of germinal centers (GCs), and T follicular helper (T(FH)) cells are the CD4 T cell subset responsible for this process. The expression of signaling lymphocytic activation molecule (SLAM)-associated protein (SAP [SH2D1A]) in CD4 T cells is essential for GC development. However, SAP-deficient mice only have a mild defect in T(FH) differentiation, as evidenced by the presence of common T(FH) surface markers. GC-associated T follicular helper (GC T(FH)) cells can be identified by their coexpression of CXCR5 and the GL7 epitope, allowing for the analysis of T(FH) and GC T(FH) populations. GC T(FH) cells are a functionally distinct subset of further polarized T(FH) cells, with enhanced B cell help capacity and a unique ability to produce IL-4 in a T(H)2-independent manner. Surprisingly, SAP-deficient mice lack the GC T(FH) cell subset, and SAP(-) T(FH) cells are defective in IL-4 and IL-21 production. We further demonstrate that SLAM (Slamf1, CD150), a surface receptor that utilizes SAP signaling, is specifically required for IL-4 production by GC T(FH) cells. GC T(FH) cells require IL-4 and -21 production for optimal help to B cells. These findings reveal the intricate nature of SAP-dependent SLAM family receptor signaling, highlighting a prominent role for SLAM receptor ligation in IL-4 production by GC CD4 T cells but not in T(FH) cell and GC T(FH) cell differentiation.

title: High cardiovascular mortality in Russia cannot be explained by the classical risk factors. The Arkhangelsk study 2000
text: Since the 1990s, Russia has experienced a severe public health crisis marked by high mortality rates and a significant decrease in life expectancy. Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of death. Only a limited number of large-scale population studies have been conducted in Russia during this period. A total of 1968 men and 1737 women aged 18-75 years participated in a health survey in Arkhangelsk, Russia, between 1999 and 2000. The survey included the assessment of classic cardiovascular risk factors (family history, smoking, blood pressure, and blood lipids) as well as general health variables. The paper presents sex-specific data on risk factors for coronary heart disease. Although cardiovascular mortality is high in Russia, the calculated risk for coronary heart disease (using the Framingham risk score and the Norwegian risk score) was lower in all age groups of men and women in Arkhangelsk compared to studies in Western Europe and the USA. Our findings suggest that the high cardiovascular mortality in Russia may not be solely attributed to classic risk factors for coronary heart disease.

title: Wnt7a/Fzd7 Signalling Directly Activates the Akt/mTOR Anabolic Growth Pathway in Skeletal Muscle
text: Wnt7a signals through its receptor Fzd7 to promote the expansion of satellite stem cells in skeletal muscle, leading to enhanced repair. In differentiated myofibers, Wnt7a binding to Fzd7 activates the Akt/mTOR growth pathway, causing myofiber hypertrophy. This process is independent of IGF-receptor activation and requires the presence of Gα(s) and PI(3)K components in the Fzd7 receptor complex. These findings demonstrate that Wnt7a-Fzd7 activation of the Akt/mTOR pathway is a distinct non-canonical anabolic signaling pathway in skeletal muscle, highlighting the complex regulation of myogenic lineage progression.

title: Four newly located pseudouridylate residues in Escherichia coli 23S ribosomal RNA are all at the peptidyltransferase center: analysis by the application of a new sequencing technique.
text: A novel technique has been developed for the efficient identification of pseudouridylate (psi) residues in any RNA molecule. This method combines two established modification procedures that uniquely identify U residues that have been converted to psi. The first step involves treating all U-like and G-like residues with N-cyclohexyl-N'-beta-(4-methylmorpholinium)ethylcarbodiimide p-tosylate (CMC), followed by alkaline removal of all CMC groups except those linked to the N3 of psi. This process stops reverse transcription, resulting in a gel band that identifies the U residue. The second procedure is uridine-specific hydrazinolysis, which cleaves the RNA chain at all U residues and produces a gel band upon reverse transcription. However, psi residues are resistant to hydrazinolysis and do not stop reverse transcription, resulting in the absence of a band at these positions. By combining these two methods, the technique can also distinguish psi from other modified bases such as 5-methyluridine, 4-thiouridine, uridine-5-oxyacetic acid, and 2-thio-5-methylaminomethyluridine. Using this method, four new sites for psi in Escherichia coli 23S RNA were discovered, and one was disproven. The four new sites are located at positions 2457, 2504, 2580, and 2605, while the erroneous site is located at position 2555. These newly identified psi residues are situated near the peptidyltransferase center and are likely to play a functional or structural role in this region.

title: Pharmacological characterization of 1-(5-chloro-6-(trifluoromethoxy)-1H-benzoimidazol-2-yl)-1H-pyrazole-4-carboxylic acid (JNJ-42041935), a potent and selective hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor.
text:
The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) enzymes represent potential targets for the treatment of anemia, ulcerative colitis, and ischemic and metabolic diseases, among others. We have identified a novel small-molecule inhibitor of PHD, 1-(5-chloro-6-(trifluoromethoxy)-1H-benzoimidazol-2-yl)-1H-pyrazole-4-carboxylic acid (JNJ-42041935), through structure-based drug design methods.
The pharmacology of JNJ-42041935 was investigated in enzyme, cellular, and whole-animal systems, and was compared to other compounds described in the literature as PHD inhibitors. JNJ-42041935 was found to be a potent (pK(I) = 7.3-7.9), 2-oxoglutarate competitive, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes.
To further evaluate the potential of JNJ-42041935, we compared the effect of selective inhibition of PHD to intermittent, high doses (50 μg/kg i.p.) of an exogenous erythropoietin receptor agonist in an inflammation-induced anemia model in rats. JNJ-42041935 (100 μmol/kg, once a day for 14 days) was effective in reversing inflammation-induced anemia, whereas erythropoietin had no effect. These results demonstrate that JNJ-42041935 is a valuable new pharmacological tool that can be used to investigate PHD inhibition and highlight the potential of PHD inhibitors for the treatment of inflammation-induced anemia.

title: Three-Dimensional Modeling and Quantitative Analysis of Gap Junction Distributions in Cardiac Tissue
text: Gap junctions play a crucial role in intercellular communication within cardiac tissue. Various heart diseases, including hypertrophy and ischemia, are associated with alterations in the spatial arrangement of gap junctions. Previous studies used two-dimensional optical and electron microscopy to visualize gap junction arrangements. In this study, we expanded these methods to create three-dimensional reconstructions of gap junction distributions using high-resolution scanning confocal microscopy and image processing. We developed quantitative methods to characterize gap junction distributions based on the analysis of intensity profiles along the principal axes of myocytes. These methods included the measurement of gap junction polarization at cell ends and higher-order statistical image moments of intensity profiles. We tested these methods in rat ventricular myocardium and obtained novel quantitative data on gap junction distributions. Specifically, our analysis revealed significant variability in gap junction polarization, skewness, and kurtosis. We propose that this methodology provides a valuable alternative to current qualitative approaches and has applications in the characterization of both healthy and diseased myocardium. Additionally, we suggest that these data could improve computational modeling of cardiac conduction.

title: Clonally derived human embryonic stem cell lines maintain pluripotency and proliferative potential for prolonged periods of culture.
text: Human embryonic stem (ES) cell lines derived from blastocysts have the potential to form derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers even after prolonged culture. We describe the clonal derivation of two human ES cell lines, H9.1 and H9.2, from a parental ES cell line, H9, that had been cultured for 6 months. Following an additional 8 months of culture, H9.1 and H9.2 ES cell lines continued to exhibit high levels of telomerase expression and normal karyotypes. Telomere lengths were maintained between 8 and 12 kilobases in high-passage H9.1 and H9.2 cells. Both cell lines formed teratomas in SCID-beige mice that included differentiated derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers. These findings demonstrate the pluripotency of single human ES cells, their ability to maintain pluripotency over an extended period of culture, and the long-term self-renewing properties of cultured human ES cells. The remarkable developmental potential, proliferative capacity, and karyotypic stability of human ES cells distinguish them from adult cells.

title: Autosomal dominant lateral temporal epilepsy: two families with novel mutations in the LGI1 gene.
text:
Introduction:
Mutations in the leucine-rich, glioma-inactivated gene (LGI1) have recently been identified in a small number of families with autosomal dominant lateral temporal epilepsy (ADLTE). ADLTE is characterized by partial seizures with symptoms suggestive of a lateral temporal onset, including frequent auditory aura. In this study, we report the results of clinical and genetic analyses of two newly identified families with ADLTE.
Methods:
We identified two families whose seizure semiology was consistent with ADLTE. A detailed history and neurological examination were conducted, and DNA was collected from affected individuals. The coding sequence of the LGI1 gene was analyzed for mutations in both families.
Results:
Each patient in the study had a history of partial seizures, often with secondary generalization earlier in the course. Approximately two-thirds of affected patients in each family reported auditory aura. Novel mutations in the LGI1 gene were detected in both families, including a heterozygous single-nucleotide deletion at position 329 (del 329C) in one family and a nonsynonymous variation corresponding to C435G in the second family.
Conclusion:
Our findings support the notion that LGI1 mutations should be considered in patients with a history of partial seizures if the semiology of seizures is consistent with the onset in the lateral temporal lobe. The identification of these mutations in two additional families with ADLTE further highlights the importance of genetic testing in this clinical context.

title: Identification of Senescent Cells in the Bone Microenvironment.
text:
Cellular senescence is a fundamental mechanism by which cells cease dividing and undergo distinct phenotypic alterations, including upregulation of p16Ink4a, profound secretome changes, telomere shortening, and decondensation of pericentromeric satellite DNA. As cells accumulate in multiple tissues with aging, these cells and the dysfunctional factors they secrete, termed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutic targets to prevent age-related degenerative pathologies, including osteoporosis. However, the cell type(s) within the bone microenvironment that undergoes senescence with aging in vivo has remained poorly understood, largely because previous studies have focused on senescence in cultured cells.
To investigate this, we measured senescence and SASP markers in vivo in highly enriched cell populations rapidly isolated from bone/marrow without in vitro culture in young (age 6 months) and old (age 24 months) mice. Our results showed that p16Ink4a expression was significantly higher with aging in B cells, T cells, myeloid cells, osteoblast progenitors, osteoblasts, and osteocytes. In addition, in vivo quantification of senescence-associated distension of satellites (SADS), ie, large-scale unraveling of pericentromeric satellite DNA, revealed significantly more senescent osteocytes in old compared with young bone cortices (11% versus 2%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, primary osteocytes from old mice had sixfold more (p < 0.001) telomere dysfunction-induced foci (TIFs) than osteocytes from young mice. Corresponding with the age-associated accumulation of senescent osteocytes was significantly higher expression of multiple SASP markers in osteocytes from old versus young mice, several of which also showed dramatic age-associated upregulation in myeloid cells.
Our findings suggest that with aging, a subset of cells of various lineages within the bone microenvironment become senescent, although senescent myeloid cells and senescent osteocytes predominantly develop the SASP. Given the critical roles of osteocytes in orchestrating bone remodeling, our findings suggest that senescent osteocytes and their SASP may contribute to age-related bone loss. These data provide new insights into the mechanisms of age-related bone loss and highlight the potential of targeting senescent cells and their SASP as a therapeutic strategy to prevent or treat age-related bone disorders.

title: Changes in white blood cells and platelets in children with falciparum malaria: relationship to disease outcome.
text: Little is known about the changes in white blood cells and platelets in children with falciparum malaria in endemic areas. To investigate, we measured the white blood cell count (WCC) and platelet levels of 230 healthy children from the community, 1369 children hospitalized with symptomatic malaria, and 1461 children with other medical conditions. Our findings showed that children with malaria had higher WCC compared to community controls, and leucocytosis was strongly associated with younger age, deep breathing, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and death. However, a positive blood culture was not associated with WCC. In children with malaria, high lymphocyte counts and low monocyte counts were independently associated with mortality. Additionally, we found that 56.7% of children with malaria had a platelet count of less than 150 x 109/l, which was associated with age, prostration, and parasite density, but not with bleeding problems or mortality. Furthermore, we observed that the mean platelet volume was higher in children with malaria compared to other medical conditions. This may indicate that early release from the bone marrow in response to peripheral platelet destruction occurs in children with malaria. Our findings suggest that leucocytosis is associated with both severity and mortality in children with falciparum malaria, regardless of bacteremia, while thrombocytopenia, although common, is not associated with adverse outcomes.

title: Microenvironmental regulation of biomacromolecular therapies
text: There is currently a growing interest in developing molecular therapies to treat various diseases, and this has led to significant efforts to deliver bioactive macromolecules, such as proteins, antibodies, DNA, and small interfering RNA, in a targeted and controlled manner. However, the influence of the microenvironment in which the target cell resides has been underappreciated, particularly with regards to the extracellular matrix (ECM) component of the cellular niche. Many diseases and injuries disrupt the normal ECM architecture, affecting cell adhesion and subsequent cellular activities. This review will highlight the importance of the ECM and ECM-cell interactions on the cell response to bioactive macromolecules and suggest new criteria for the design of novel drug delivery systems.

title: Homocysteine Induces Trophoblast Cell Death with Apoptotic Features1
text:
Abstract:
Hyperhomocysteinemia has been implicated as a potential risk factor for various pregnancy complications, including habitual abortions, placental abruption or infarcts, preeclampsia, and intrauterine growth retardation. However, the underlying mechanisms by which homocysteine contributes to these complications are not well understood. The present study aimed to investigate the in vitro effects of homocysteine on trophoblast cell function and viability.
Using primary human trophoblast cells, we found that exposure to homocysteine (20 μmol/L) resulted in cellular flattening, enlargement, and extension of pseudopodia, as well as cellular vacuolization and detachment. Apoptosis and necrosis were also observed, as evidenced by DNA degradation, cytochrome c release from mitochondria to the cytosol, and DNA cleavage in agarose gel. In contrast, cysteine had no significant effects on trophoblast cell function.
Our findings suggest that trophoblast cell death may play a pathogenic role in the development of pregnancy complications associated with placental diseases. These results provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying the adverse effects of hyperhomocysteinemia on pregnancy outcomes.

title: Intrahippocampal administration of an androgen receptor antagonist, flutamide, can increase anxiety-like behavior in intact and DHT-replaced male rats.
text:
Testosterone (T) and its 5alpha-reduced metabolite, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), have been shown to decrease anxiety-like behavior in male rats. However, the underlying mechanisms for these effects have not been fully elucidated. To investigate, we posed two hypotheses:
1. If T reduces anxiety-like behavior through the actions of DHT, then gonadectomy (GDX) should increase anxiety-like behavior, which would be reversed by systemic administration of DHT.
2. If T and DHT reduce anxiety-like behavior through actions at intracellular androgen receptors in the hippocampus, then direct administration of an androgen receptor antagonist, flutamide, to the hippocampus should increase anxiety-like behavior in GDX rats, but not in intact or DHT-replaced rats.
To test these hypotheses, we applied empty or flutamide-containing inserts directly to the dorsal hippocampus of intact, GDX, or GDX and DHT-replaced rats 2 hours prior to testing in the open field, elevated plus maze, or defensive freezing tasks. Our findings showed that GDX rats exhibited significantly more anxiety-like behaviors than intact or DHT-replaced rats, while intact and DHT-replaced rats administered flutamide to the hippocampus displayed significantly more anxiety-like behavior than intact and DHT-replaced controls. However, flutamide alone did not increase anxiety-like behavior in GDX rats. These results suggest that androgens, including DHT, can decrease anxiety-like behavior in male rats through actions at androgen receptors in the hippocampus.

title: Cardiovascular risk and events in 17 low-, middle-, and high-income countries.
text:
Background: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low-income and middle-income countries. However, the reasons for this disparity are unclear.
Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study among 156,424 individuals from 628 urban and rural communities in 17 countries (3 high-income, 10 middle-income, and 4 low-income countries). We used the INTERHEART Risk Score, a validated tool for assessing cardiovascular risk based on a combination of risk factors, to quantify the risk-factor burden of each participant. Participants were followed for incident CVD and death for a mean of 4.1 years.
Results: Our findings revealed a significant gradient in the risk-factor burden across the three income groups, with the highest burden in high-income countries, intermediate burden in middle-income countries, and lowest burden in low-income countries. However, despite having a lower risk-factor burden, low-income countries had higher rates of major CVD events (death from CVD, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure) and case fatality rates than high-income countries. Urban communities had a higher risk-factor burden than rural communities but lower rates of CVD events and case fatality rates. The use of preventive medications and revascularization procedures was significantly more common in high-income countries than in middle- or low-income countries.
Conclusions: Our study suggests that the high burden of risk factors in high-income countries may be mitigated by better control of risk factors and more frequent use of proven pharmacologic therapies and revascularization. However, the substantially higher rates of CVD and death in low-income countries highlight the need for targeted interventions to address the underlying causes of this disparity.

title: Increased density of tumor-associated macrophages is associated with decreased survival in advanced thyroid cancer.
text: The study aimed to investigate the density of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in well-differentiated thyroid cancers (WDTC), poorly differentiated thyroid cancers (PDTC), and anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC) and evaluate their correlation with clinicopathologic parameters. The study included 33 WDTC, 37 PDTC, and 20 ATC tissue samples, which were analyzed using immunohistochemistry for macrophage-specific markers. The study also collected electronic medical records for PDTC patients, which provided follow-up information for up to 12 years. The results showed that the density of CD68(+) TAMs was significantly higher in PDTC (54%) and ATC (95%) compared to WDTC (27%). Increased TAM density in PDTC was associated with capsular invasion, extrathyroidal extension, and decreased cancer-related survival. These findings suggest that TAMs may play a role in facilitating thyroid cancer progression. As novel therapies targeting thyroid tumor cells are being developed, the potential role of TAMs as modulators of thyroid cancer behavior will need to be considered.

title: Blockade of Tim-1 and Tim-4 Enhances Atherosclerosis in Low-Density Lipoprotein Receptor-Deficient Mice.
text:
Objective: T cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain (Tim) proteins are expressed by various immune cells and play a crucial role in the clearance of apoptotic cells and the regulation of T cell responses. In this study, we investigate the modulation of Tim-1 and Tim-4 proteins as a potential therapeutic approach for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
Methods: We fed low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient (ldlr(-/-) mice a high-fat diet for 4 weeks and treated them with control rat immunoglobulin G1, anti-Tim-1 (3D10) or anti-Tim-4 (21H12) monoclonal antibodies. We evaluated the impact of these treatments on atherosclerosis by analyzing aortic CD4+ T cells, efferocytosis, and phosphatidylserine expression.
Results: Our results show that both anti-Tim-1 and anti-Tim-4 treatments enhanced atherosclerosis by 45% compared to controls, likely due to impaired efferocytosis and increased aortic CD4+ T cells. In contrast, anti-Tim-4 treatment increased the percentages of activated T cells and late apoptotic cells in the circulation. In vitro blockade of Tim-4 inhibited efferocytosis of oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced apoptotic macrophages. Furthermore, combined blockade of Tim-1 and Tim-4 increased atherosclerotic lesion size by 59%.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that blockade of Tim-4 aggravates atherosclerosis by preventing phagocytosis of phosphatidylserine-expressing apoptotic cells and activated T cells by Tim-4-expressing cells. In contrast, Tim-1-associated effects on atherosclerosis are related to changes in Th1/Th2 balance and reduced circulating regulatory T cells. Modulation of Tim-1 and Tim-4 proteins may provide a potential therapeutic approach for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.

title: Genetic and physical analysis of double-strand break repair and recombination in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: We have investigated the process of double-strand break (DSB) recombination and repair in a LACZ duplication plasmid in yeast, using the HO endonuclease-induced DSB as a site for recombination. A 117-bp MATa fragment, embedded within one copy of LACZ, served as the site for DSB initiation when HO endonuclease was expressed. The DSB could be repaired using wild-type sequences located on a second, promoterless, copy of LACZ on the same plasmid. Unlike normal mating-type switching, crossing-over associated with gene conversion occurred at least 50% of the time. The proportion of conversion events accompanied by exchange was greater when the two copies of LACZ were in direct orientation (80%), compared to when they were inverted (50%). Additionally, the fraction of plasmids lost was significantly greater in the inverted orientation. The kinetics of appearance of intermediates and final products were also monitored, revealing that the repair of the DSB is a slow process, taking at least an hour from the detection of the HO-cut fragments to completion of repair. Interestingly, the appearance of the two reciprocal products of crossing over did not occur with the same kinetics, with the HO-induced formation of a large circular deletion product not being accompanied by the appearance of a small circular reciprocal product when the two LACZ sequences were in direct orientation. These differences may reflect two kinetically separable processes, one involving only one cut end and the other resulting from the concerted participation of both ends of the DSB.

title: Nitroxergic nerves mediate vagally induced relaxation in the isolated stomach of the guinea pig.
text: Here we demonstrate that the relaxation induced by stimulation of the vagus nerve in the presence of cholinergic (muscarinic) and adrenergic blockade in the isolated stomach of the guinea pig is mediated by nitric oxide (NO). This conclusion is supported by the inhibition of vagal relaxation by NG-monomethyl-L-arginine, an inhibitor of NO synthesis. The effect of NG-monomethyl-L-arginine was partially reversed by coincubation with L-arginine but not with D-arginine. NO activates soluble guanylate cyclase, and relaxation of the stomach induced by vagal stimulation was prevented by an inhibitor of soluble guanylate cyclase, methylene blue, further supporting our findings. Additionally, the relaxant effect of vagal stimulation was ablated by hexamethonium, an inhibitor of ganglionic nicotinic receptors, indicating that ganglionic transmission does not rely on NO release from preganglionic neurons. However, hexamethonium did not inhibit the gastric relaxation brought about by increasing the intragastric pressure, which is also mediated by NO, as previously described by us. The selective inhibition by hexamethonium of only the vagally mediated relaxation but not of the pressure-induced relaxation of the stomach suggests the existence of at least two distinct neuronal pathways capable of generating NO and contributing to gastric accommodation of food or fluid.

title: Efficient T cell activation requires an optimal dwell-time of interaction between the TCR and the pMHC complex
text: Cytotoxic T cell (CTL) activation requires the specific recognition of peptide-major histocompatibility class I (pMHC) molecules on the surface of target cells by the T cell receptor (TCR). To investigate the impact of mutations in the antigen-binding site of a Kb-restricted TCR on T cell activation, we examined the effects of these mutations on T cell activation, antigen binding, and dissociation from antigen. Similarly, we studied variants of a Kd-restricted peptide that was recognized by a CTL clone. Our findings reveal that T cell activation can be impaired by mutations that either increase or decrease the binding half-life of the TCR-pMHC interaction. Our data suggest that efficient T cell activation occurs within a specific dwell-time range of the TCR-pMHC interaction, which is consistent with the exclusion of either low or high affinity T cells from the expanded population during immune responses.

title: Crystal structure of human insulin-regulated aminopeptidase with specificity for cyclic peptides.
text: Insulin-regulated aminopeptidase (IRAP), also known as oxytocinase, is a membrane-bound zinc-metallopeptidase that plays a crucial role in the brain's memory function. By cleaving neuroactive peptides, IRAP enhances memory performance when inhibited. Through crystal structure determination, we have revealed the unique arrangement of IRAP's four domains, including a large, buried cavity near the active site. This structure provides insight into IRAP's specificity for cyclic peptides, such as oxytocin and vasopressin, and allows us to understand the molecular basis of its cognitive-enhancing effects. Computational docking of IRAP-specific cognitive enhancers into the crystal structure has provided a framework for developing new classes of cognitive enhancers to treat memory disorders like Alzheimer's disease.

title: Glutathione and glutathione-dependent enzymes represent a co-ordinately regulated defence against oxidative stress.
text: Increased levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) within cells can lead to oxidative stress, a potentially harmful insult that can cause cellular damage, including DNA damage and protein inactivation. Chronic oxidative stress has been linked to various diseases, such as cancer, arthritis, and neurodegenerative disorders. Glutathione, a tripeptide molecule, plays a crucial role in protecting cells against oxidative stress through its multiple detoxification mechanisms. Glutathione participates in detoxification at various levels, including scavenging free radicals, reducing peroxides, and conjugating with electrophilic compounds. This article discusses the integrated functioning of glutathione biosynthesis, glutathione peroxidases, glutathione S-transferases, and glutathione S-conjugate efflux pumps in responding to oxidative stress. The antioxidant responsive element (ARE) plays a crucial role in coordinating this response, and its activation is mediated by transcription factors such as Nrf and small Maf proteins. The identification of the intracellular sensor(s) for ROS and thiol-active chemicals that induce genes through the ARE has significant medical implications, as it may help to explain acquired resistance of tumors to cancer chemotherapeutic drugs.

title: Does socioeconomic status matter? A meta-analysis on parent training effectiveness for disruptive child behavior.
text:
Disadvantaged families' socioeconomic status (SES) is often believed to hinder the effectiveness of parent training programs. However, the impact of SES on program effectiveness has been overlooked, with a focus on initial problem severity instead.
