In this meta-analysis, we examined whether SES affects parent training program effectiveness at both immediate post-treatment and 1-year follow-up, while controlling for initial problem severity. We analyzed 75 studies on parent training programs aimed at reducing disruptive child behavior. Our findings reveal that:
1. Immediately post-treatment, disadvantaged families benefited less from parent training when they had low levels of initial problem severity.
2. At follow-up, disadvantaged families benefited less from parent training regardless of initial problem severity.
3. Initial problem severity was a strong predictor of effect sizes both immediately post-treatment and at follow-up.
4. Parent training programs were found to be equally effective for disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged families immediately post-treatment, provided initial problems were severe.
5. However, maintenance of treatment gain seemed more challenging for disadvantaged families, suggesting that sustained family support may be necessary.
In summary, while disadvantaged families may benefit less from parent training programs at immediate post-treatment, this gap narrows or disappears at follow-up, and initial problem severity remains a crucial factor in determining program effectiveness. Providing sustained support to disadvantaged families may be essential to ensure long-term treatment gains.

title: Infectiousness of malaria-endemic human populations to vectors.
text: Despite its crucial role in determining the stability and intensity of malaria transmission, the infectiousness of human populations to mosquitoes has rarely been quantified. Traditionally, field-based analyses of malaria transmission have relied on the prevalence of asexual parasites or gametocytes as proxies for infectiousness. Here, we present empirical data on human infectiousness from Africa and Papua New Guinea, covering a wide range of transmission intensities. Our findings reveal a surprising lack of relationship between the infectiousness of human populations to vector mosquitoes and mosquito-to-human transmission intensity. We also compare these data with the predictions of a stochastic simulation model of Plasmodium falciparum epidemiology. The model predicted little variation in human infectiousness across entomologic inoculation rates (EIRs) greater than approximately 10 infectious bites per year, suggesting that the lack of relationship between EIR and human infectiousness can be explained without invoking acquired transmission-blocking immunity. However, the near absence of field data from areas with low EIR values precluded validation of the model predictions for these scenarios. Our results suggest that interventions aimed at reducing mosquito-to-human transmission will have little or no impact on human infectiousness in most rural areas of sub-Saharan Africa, unless very large reductions in transmission can be achieved. Therefore, measures to prevent mosquito-to-human transmission should be complemented with interventions that reduce the density or infectiousness of blood stage parasites.

title: Molecular analysis of circulating tumour cells—biology and biomarkers
text: Growing evidence highlights the limitations of single-site biopsies in capturing the full genomic landscape of a tumor. As more targeted therapies enter the clinic, it is essential to screen tumors for genetic abnormalities and investigate resistance mechanisms during disease progression. However, obtaining multiple biopsies at different spatial and temporal locations is impractical, uncomfortable for patients, and carries risks. To address this challenge, we explore the potential of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) captured through a minimally invasive blood test. CTCs can provide valuable insights into intratumor heterogeneity and tumor evolution, although their clinical usefulness remains to be determined. Various technologies, such as the validated CellSearch® system, are available for detecting and isolating CTCs. Recent discoveries on CTCs also align with mechanisms of hematological spread described in preclinical models, including evidence for epithelial-mesenchymal transition, collective cell migration, and tumor-initiating cells in the circulation. Advances in single-cell molecular analysis are enhancing our understanding of metastasis mechanisms, and the combination of CTC and cell-free DNA assays is expected to offer valuable blood-borne biomarkers for real-time patient monitoring and treatment stratification.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress contributes to beta cell apoptosis in type 2 diabetes
text: Increased lipid levels can lead to beta cell death, which may contribute to the reduction of beta cell mass in type 2 diabetes. To investigate the role of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in this process, we examined the expression of genes involved in ER stress in insulin-producing MIN6 cells exposed to elevated lipids, as well as in islets from an animal model of diabetes (db/db mice) and in human pancreas tissue from type 2 diabetes subjects. We found that the pro-apoptotic fatty acid palmitate triggers a comprehensive ER stress response in MIN6 cells, which was absent in cells treated with the non-apoptotic fatty acid oleate. Time-dependent increases in the mRNA levels of activating transcription factor 4 (Atf4), DNA-damage inducible transcript 3 (Ddit3, also known as C/EBP homologous protein [Chop]), and DnaJ homologue (HSP40) C3 (Dnajc3, also known as p58) were observed in palmitate-treated cells, but not in oleate-treated cells. Overproduction of the ER chaperone heat shock 70 kDa protein 5 (HSPA5, previously known as immunoglobulin heavy chain binding protein [BIP]) in MIN6 cells protected against lipid-induced apoptosis. Similarly, in islets of db/db mice, a variety of marker genes of ER stress were upregulated, and increased processing (activation) of X-box binding protein 1 (Xbp1) mRNA was observed, confirming the existence of ER stress. Finally, we observed increased islet protein production of HSPA5, DDIT3, DNAJC3, and BCL2-associated X protein in human pancreas tissue from type 2 diabetes subjects. Our findings provide evidence that ER stress occurs in type 2 diabetes and is required for aspects of the underlying beta cell failure.

title: Coactivator SRC-2-dependent metabolic reprogramming mediates prostate cancer survival and metastasis.
text: Metabolic pathway reprogramming is a fundamental aspect of cancer cell growth and survival, allowing these rapidly dividing cells to meet their anabolic and energetic demands. While the underlying regulators of the tumor metabolic program are not yet fully understood, identifying and targeting these factors could provide a promising avenue for cancer therapy. In this study, we investigated the role of the oncogenic transcriptional coregulator steroid receptor coactivator 2 (SRC-2), also known as NCOA2, in cancer metabolism. Our findings revealed that SRC-2 drives glutamine-dependent de novo lipogenesis in tumor cells, which supports their survival and eventual metastasis. We found that SRC-2 was highly elevated in a variety of tumors, with particularly high levels in prostate cancer, where it was amplified and overexpressed in 37% of metastatic tumors examined. In prostate cancer cells, SRC-2 stimulated reductive carboxylation of α-ketoglutarate to generate citrate via retrograde TCA cycling, promoting lipogenesis and reprogramming of glutamine metabolism. Glutamine-mediated nutrient signaling activated SRC-2 via mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation, which then triggered downstream transcriptional responses by coactivating SREBP-1, leading to enhanced lipogenic enzyme expression. Metabolic profiling of human prostate tumors revealed a striking increase in the SRC-2-driven metabolic signature in metastatic tumors compared to localized tumors, further implicating SRC-2 as a key coordinator of cancer metastasis. In addition, inhibition of SRC-2 in murine models significantly attenuated the survival, growth, and metastasis of prostate cancer cells. These findings suggest that targeting the SRC-2 pathway may be a promising therapeutic strategy for prostate cancer.

title: In vitro substrate specificity of protein tyrosine kinases
text: Synthetic peptides, such as P60stc autophosphorylation site peptides and angiotensin, are randomly phosphorylated by protein tyrosine kinases. This observation has led to the widespread belief that protein tyrosine kinases are highly promiscuous, showing little in vitro site specificity. However, recent studies have challenged this view by demonstrating the existence of highly specific protein tyrosine kinases that phosphorylate specific substrates with high activity. For example, synthetic peptides with high substrate activity for specific protein tyrosine kinases have been identified, and modifications to these peptides have revealed that kinase substrate determinants reside with specific amino acid residues proximal to the target tyrosine. Additionally, several protein kinases have been shown to be regulated by tyrosine phosphorylation at specific sites by highly specific protein tyrosine kinases. These and other biochemical studies are contributing to an evolving understanding of the in vitro substrate specificity of protein tyrosine kinases.

title: Relative effectiveness of clinic and home blood pressure monitoring compared with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in diagnosis of hypertension: systematic review
text:
Objective: To compare the accuracy of clinic and home blood pressure measurements with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring as a reference standard for the diagnosis of hypertension.
Design: Systematic review with meta-analysis and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) models.
Data Sources: Medline (from 1966), Embase (from 1980), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, DARE, Medion, ARIF, and TRIP up to May 2010.
Eligibility Criteria: Studies examining the diagnosis of hypertension in adults of all ages using home and/or clinic blood pressure measurements compared with those made using ambulatory monitoring with clearly defined thresholds to diagnose hypertension.
Results: Of the 20 eligible studies, only seven (clinic) and three (home) could be directly compared with ambulatory monitoring. Compared to ambulatory monitoring thresholds of 135/85 mm Hg, clinic measurements had mean sensitivity and specificity of 74.6% (95% CI: 60.7%-84.8%) and 74.6% (47.9%-90.4%), respectively, while home measurements had mean sensitivity and specificity of 85.7% (78.0%-91.0%) and 62.4% (48.0%-75.0%).
Conclusions: Neither clinic nor home blood pressure measurements had sufficient sensitivity or specificity to be recommended as a single diagnostic test. If ambulatory monitoring is taken as the reference standard, treatment decisions based on clinic or home blood pressure alone may result in substantial overdiagnosis. Ambulatory monitoring before the start of lifelong drug treatment may lead to more appropriate targeting of treatment, particularly around the diagnostic threshold.

title: Purification and characterization of mouse hematopoietic stem cells.
text: Researchers isolated mouse bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells using various phenotypic markers. These cells have the ability to proliferate and differentiate with high efficiency into myelomonocytic cells, B cells, or T cells. In fact, just 30 of these stem cells are enough to save 50% of lethally irradiated mice and reconstitute all blood cell types in the survivors.

title: Regulation of arabinose and xylose metabolism in Escherichia coli.
text: Bacteria such as Escherichia coli often consume one sugar at a time when fed multiple sugars, a process known as carbon catabolite repression. For example, E. coli will first consume glucose before consuming lactose. In addition, glucose also represses the consumption of other sugars, including arabinose and xylose. In this study, we characterized a second hierarchy in E. coli, where arabinose is consumed before xylose when grown in a mixture of the two pentoses. We found that the expression of the xylose metabolic genes is repressed in the presence of arabinose, and this repression is dependent on the protein AraC. Our results demonstrate that sugar utilization in E. coli involves multiple layers of regulation, where cells consume glucose first, then arabinose, and finally xylose. These findings may be relevant in the metabolic engineering of E. coli strains capable of producing chemicals and biofuels from mixtures of hexose and pentose sugars derived from plant biomass.

title: MicroRNA expression profiling of human metastatic cancers identifies cancer gene targets.
text: Small non-coding microRNAs (miRNAs) have been implicated in the development and progression of cancer, with their expression patterns differing between normal tissues and cancers. However, the specific role of miRNAs in the metastatic process remains unclear. To identify a miRNA expression signature characteristic of metastatic cancer, we performed a microarray analysis on 43 paired primary tumors (ten colon, ten bladder, 13 breast, and ten lung cancers) and one of their corresponding metastatic lymph nodes. Our analysis revealed a metastatic cancer miRNA signature comprising 15 overexpressed and 17 underexpressed miRNAs, which were validated through qRT-PCR analysis. Of note, several of these miRNAs have been previously linked to cancer progression, including miR-10b, miR-21, miR-30a, miR-30e, miR-125b, miR-141, miR-200b, miR-200c, and miR-205. To further elucidate the relationship between miRNAs and cancer metastasis, we conducted an immunohistochemical analysis of three well-defined miRNA gene targets (PDCD4, DHFR, and HOXD10) in a small series of paired colon, breast, and bladder cancers, and one of their metastatic lymph nodes. Our findings showed a significant correlation between the immunohistochemical expression of these targets and the corresponding miRNA deregulation, suggesting that specific miRNAs may play a direct role in cancer metastasis and potentially serve as a novel diagnostic tool for characterizing metastatic cancer gene targets.

title: Circos: an information aesthetic for comparative genomics.
text: We developed a visualization tool called Circos to aid in the identification and analysis of similarities and differences that arise from comparisons of genomes. Our tool is effective in displaying variations in genome structure and, more broadly, any other type of positional relationships between genomic intervals. This data is commonly produced through sequence alignments, hybridization arrays, genome mapping, and genotyping studies. Circos utilizes a circular ideogram layout to facilitate the display of relationships between pairs of positions using ribbons, which encode the position, size, and orientation of related genomic elements. Circos can display data in various formats, including scatter plots, line plots, histograms, heat maps, tiles, connectors, and text. Additionally, Circos can create bitmap or vector images from GFF-style data inputs and hierarchical configuration files, making it suitable for rapid deployment in data analysis and reporting pipelines.

title: Pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and clinical profile of novel antiplatelet drugs targeting vascular diseases.
text: Platelet inhibitors are the cornerstone of treatment for patients suffering from vascular diseases. The current gold standard antiplatelet agent, clopidogrel, has several pharmacological and clinical limitations that have prompted the search for more effective and efficient platelet antagonists. A plethora of candidates are being investigated, including various blockers of the purinergic P2Y12 receptor such as prasugrel, an oral and irreversible thienopyridine; ticagrelor, an oral and reversible analogue; elinogrel, a direct-acting and reversible P2Y12 receptor inhibitor, the only antiplatelet compound that can be administered both intravenously and orally; BX 667, an orally active and reversible small-molecule P2Y12 receptor antagonist; SCH 530348, SCH 205831, SCH 602539, and E5555, highly selective and orally active antagonists on the protease-activated receptor 1. Additionally, there are novel drugs that target new targets, such as terutroban, an oral, selective, and specific inhibitor of the thromboxane receptor; ARC1779, a second-generation, nuclease-resistant aptamer that inhibits von Willebrand factor-dependent platelet aggregation; ALX-0081, a bivalent humanized nanobody targeting the GPIb binding site of von Willebrand factor, and AJW200, an IgG4 monoclonal antibody of von Willebrand factor. The pharmacology and clinical profiles of these new platelet antagonists suggest that they offer more consistent, rapid, and potent platelet inhibition compared to existing agents. However, their efficacy in clinical settings will require further evaluation through properly powered, randomized, controlled trials.

title: BLM is required for faithful chromosome segregation and its localization defines a class of ultrafine anaphase bridges.
text: Mutations in the gene encoding the protein Bloom Syndrome (BLM) are associated with Bloom's syndrome, a disorder characterized by an increased risk of cancer and chromosomal instability. To investigate the role of BLM in ensuring faithful chromosome segregation during cell division, we examined the behavior of BLM-defective cells during mitosis. Our findings revealed that these cells display a higher frequency of anaphase bridges and lagging chromatin compared to isogenic corrected derivatives that ectopically express the BLM protein. In normal cells, BLM localizes to anaphase bridges, where it interacts with its cellular partners, including topoisomerase IIIalpha and hRMI1 (BLAP75). Using BLM staining as a marker, we identified a novel class of ultrafine DNA bridges in anaphase, which we termed BLM-DNA bridges. These bridges frequently link centromeric loci and are present at an elevated frequency in BLM-deficient cells. Based on these observations, we propose that sister-chromatid disjunction is often incomplete in human cells even after the onset of anaphase, and we present a model for the action of BLM in ensuring complete sister chromatid decatenation during anaphase.

title: Association Between High Serum Soluble Corin and Hypertension: A Cross-Sectional Study in a General Population of China.
text:
Background: Corin has been suggested to be associated with hypertension based on cellular and animal studies. However, there is a lack of population-based evidence to support this association, which hinders the translation of basic research findings into clinical and preventive practice. This study aimed to investigate the association between serum corin levels and hypertension in a general population of China.
Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2,498 participants aged 30 years or older residing in Gusu district of Suzhou from January to May 2010. Serum soluble corin and blood pressure were measured.
Results: The study found that participants with hypertension had higher levels of serum corin compared to those without hypertension (median (interquartile range): 1,836.83 (1,497.85-2,327.87) pg/ml vs. 1,579.14 (1,322.18-1,956.82) pg/ml, P < 0.001). Furthermore, higher serum corin levels were positively associated with the prevalence of hypertension (odds ratio (OR) = 2.01, P < 0.001). In multiple logistic regression analysis, participants in the third (OR = 1.43, P = 0.007) and fourth (OR = 1.96, P < 0.001) quartiles had significantly increased odds of hypertension compared to those in the lowest quartile of serum corin. The ORs of hypertension positively and significantly increased with serum corin levels (P for trend <0.001). Subgroup analysis revealed that the association between serum corin and hypertension remained significant in various subgroups defined by age, body mass index, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and fasting plasma glucose (all P < 0.05).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that hypertensive participants had higher levels of serum corin compared to non-hypertensive participants, which implies that corin may play a role in the pathophysiology of hypertension. This study provides population-based evidence supporting the association between corin and hypertension, which may have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for hypertension.

title: Shared and distinct genetic variants in type 1 diabetes and celiac disease.
text:
Two inflammatory conditions, type 1 diabetes and celiac disease, frequently occur together in populations, indicating a shared genetic origin. Since both diseases are linked to the HLA class II genes on chromosome 6p21, we investigated whether other non-HLA loci are also associated with these conditions.
We analyzed the genetic association between type 1 diabetes and eight loci related to the risk of celiac disease in 8064 patients with type 1 diabetes, 9339 control subjects, and 2828 families providing 3064 parent-child trios (consisting of an affected child and both biological parents). Additionally, we examined 18 loci associated with type 1 diabetes in 2560 patients with celiac disease and 9339 control subjects.
Our results showed that three celiac disease loci - RGS1 on chromosome 1q31, IL18RAP on chromosome 2q12, and TAGAP on chromosome 6q25 - were also associated with type 1 diabetes (P<1.00x10(-4)). A 32-bp insertion-deletion variant on chromosome 3p21 was identified as a new type 1 diabetes locus (P=1.81x10(-8)) and was also associated with celiac disease, along with PTPN2 on chromosome 18p11 and CTLA4 on chromosome 2q33, bringing the total number of shared loci to seven, including SH2B3 on chromosome 12q24. The effects of the IL18RAP and TAGAP alleles provide protection in type 1 diabetes and susceptibility in celiac disease. Loci with distinct effects in the two diseases included INS on chromosome 11p15, IL2RA on chromosome 10p15, and PTPN22 on chromosome 1p13 in type 1 diabetes and IL12A on 3q25 and LPP on 3q28 in celiac disease.
Our findings suggest that there may be a common genetic basis for both type 1 diabetes and celiac disease, involving shared alleles. This suggests that common biological mechanisms, such as autoimmunity-related tissue damage and intolerance to dietary antigens, may be etiologic features of both diseases.

title: Promotion of tumorigenesis by heterozygous disruption of the beclin 1 autophagy gene.
text: Malignant cells often exhibit defects in the autophagy pathway, an evolutionarily conserved mechanism for degrading long-lived proteins and cytoplasmic organelles. However, there is currently no genetic evidence to suggest a role for autophagy genes in tumor suppression. Interestingly, approximately 40-75% of cases of human sporadic breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer exhibit monoallelic deletion of the beclin 1 autophagy gene. To investigate the potential role of beclin 1 in tumorigenesis, we generated a targeted mutant mouse model and found that heterozygous disruption of beclin 1 leads to an increased frequency of spontaneous malignancies and accelerated development of hepatitis B virus-induced premalignant lesions. Molecular analysis of tumors in beclin 1 heterozygous mice revealed that the remaining wild-type allele is neither mutated nor silenced. Moreover, beclin 1 heterozygous disruption resulted in enhanced cellular proliferation and reduced autophagy in vivo. These findings demonstrate that beclin 1 is a haplo-insufficient tumor-suppressor gene and provide genetic evidence that autophagy is a novel mechanism of cell-growth control and tumor suppression. Therefore, mutations in beclin 1 or other autophagy genes may contribute to the development of human cancers.

title: Treatment-related mortality with bevacizumab in cancer patients: a meta-analysis.
text:
Background: Angiogenesis inhibitors, such as bevacizumab, have been widely used in cancer treatment, particularly in combination with chemotherapy. However, fatal adverse events (FAEs) have been reported in some studies, and the role of bevacizumab in treatment-related mortality remains unclear. Objective: To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to determine the overall risk of FAEs associated with bevacizumab in combination with chemotherapy or biological therapy.
Methods: PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases, as well as abstracts presented at American Society of Clinical Oncology conferences from January 1966 to October 2010, were searched to identify relevant studies. Eligible studies included prospective RCTs in which bevacizumab was compared with chemotherapy or biological therapy alone. Summary incidence rates, relative risks (RRs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models.
Results: A total of 10,217 patients from 16 RCTs were included in the analysis. The overall incidence of FAEs with bevacizumab was 2.5% (95% CI, 1.7%-3.9%). Compared with chemotherapy alone, the addition of bevacizumab was associated with an increased risk of FAEs, with an RR of 1.46 (95% CI, 1.09-1.94; P = .01; incidence, 2.5% vs 1.7%). This association varied significantly with chemotherapeutic agents (P = .045) but not with tumor types (P = .13) or bevacizumab doses (P = .16). Bevacizumab was associated with an increased risk of FAEs in patients receiving taxanes or platinum agents (RR, 3.49; 95% CI, 1.82-6.66; incidence, 3.3% vs 1.0%) but was not associated with increased risk of FAEs when used in conjunction with other agents (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.25-2.88; incidence, 0.8% vs 0.9%). The most common causes of FAEs were hemorrhage (23.5%), neutropenia (12.2%), and gastrointestinal tract perforation (7.1%).
Conclusion: In a meta-analysis of RCTs, bevacizumab in combination with chemotherapy or biological therapy, compared with chemotherapy alone, was associated with increased treatment-related mortality. These findings suggest that bevacizumab may increase the risk of FAEs in certain patient populations, and further research is needed to determine the optimal use of this agent in cancer treatment.

title: Quiescent and active hippocampal neural stem cells with distinct morphologies respond selectively to physiological and pathological stimuli and aging.
text: New neurons are generated in the adult hippocampus throughout life by neural stem/progenitor cells (NSCs), and neurogenesis is a plastic process that is responsive to external stimuli. Our findings demonstrate that canonical Notch signaling through RBP-J is essential for hippocampal neurogenesis. Notch signaling distinguishes distinct subpopulations of Sox2(+) NSCs, and within these pools, subpopulations can exhibit either mitotically active or quiescent properties. Radial and horizontal NSCs respond selectively to neurogenic stimuli, and physical exercise activates the quiescent radial population, while epileptic seizures induce the expansion of the horizontal NSC pool. Interestingly, reduced neurogenesis in aged mice is associated with a loss of active horizontal NSCs rather than a total loss of stem cells, and the transition to a quiescent state is reversible, leading to the rejuvenation of neurogenesis in the brain. The discovery of multiple NSC populations with Notch dependence and selective responses to stimuli, as well as their reversible quiescence, has significant implications for the mechanisms of adaptive learning and regenerative therapy.

title: Low serum vitamin D is associated with high risk of diabetes in Korean adults.
text: In this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between vitamin D levels and glucose metabolism in a large population-based survey of Korean adults. We found that individuals with lower vitamin D levels had a higher risk of developing diabetes mellitus, after adjusting for various confounding factors. Specifically, the odds ratio (OR) for diabetes mellitus was 1.73, 1.30, and 1.40 for serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) concentrations <25 nmol/L, 25 to <50 nmol/L, and 50 to <75 nmol/L, respectively. Additionally, we found that a lower vitamin D concentration was associated with higher insulin resistance, as measured by homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and quantitative insulin sensitivity check index (QUICKI), in overweight or obese participants. These findings suggest that vitamin D may play a role in glucose metabolism and that maintaining adequate vitamin D levels may help reduce the risk of diabetes mellitus in Korean adults.

title: When NK cells overcome their lack of education.
text: The immune system's cells have developed diverse molecular mechanisms to detect their surroundings and respond to alterations in self. Among these cells are natural killer (NK) cells, which are a type of lymphocyte with both effector and regulatory functions that are particularly adept at adapting to changes in self. In a recent study published in this issue of the Journal of Clinical Investigation (JCI), Tarek and colleagues report the successful use of an innovative monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based therapy to manipulate NK cell adaptation to self in the treatment of neuroblastoma (NB). This groundbreaking therapeutic approach has the potential to stimulate further research into NK cell therapies.

title: Toll-like receptor-3 mediates HIV-1 transactivation via NFκB and JNK pathways and histone acetylation, but prolonged activation suppresses Tat and HIV-1 replication.
text: Research has implicated TLR3 in the pathogenesis of various viral infections, including SIV and HIV-1-induced inflammation and AIDS. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood, and it is unclear whether HIV interacts with TLR3 to affect the disease process. To investigate this, we examined the effects of TLR3 ligands on HIV-1 transactivation in primary human macrophages and cells containing integrated copies of the HIV-1 promoter. Our findings demonstrate that TLR3 activation leads to the upregulation of transcription factors, including c-Jun, CEBPA, STAT-1, STAT-2, RELB, and NFκB1, which are known to regulate HIV promoter activity. Additionally, we found that TLR3 activation increases HIV-1 transactivation through the JNK and NFκB signaling pathways. These effects were associated with epigenetic modifications, such as decreased histone deacetylase activity, increased HAT activity, and increased acetylation of histones H3 and H4 at specific sites in the HIV-1 promoter. However, prolonged TLR3 activation resulted in decreased HIV-1 transactivation, HAT activity, and Tat transcription, as well as suppressed viral replication. Overall, our findings suggest that TLR3 can function as a viral sensor to mediate viral transactivation, cellular signaling, innate immune response, and inflammation in HIV-infected individuals. Our study provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying these TLR3-mediated effects.

title: Patent ductus arteriosus: are current neonatal treatment options better or worse than no treatment at all?
text: Although a moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) typically needs to be closed by the age of 1-2 years, there is a lack of consensus among neonatologists regarding the optimal time for closure in infants who do not require mechanical ventilation. While 95% of neonatologists believe that a moderate-sized PDA should be closed if it persists in infants born before 28 weeks who still require mechanical ventilation, the number of neonatologists who treat a PDA in infants who do not require mechanical ventilation varies widely. The uncertainty surrounding PDA closure is further compounded by the high likelihood of spontaneous ductus closure and the absence of randomized controlled trials specifically addressing the risks and benefits of neonatal ductus closure. New evidence suggests that early pharmacologic treatment may have several important short-term benefits for preterm newborns, while ductus ligation may have its own set of potential morbidities that could counteract the benefits of ductus closure.

title: A conserved phosphatase cascade that regulates nuclear membrane biogenesis.
text: A newly identified family of phosphatases, belonging to the haloacid dehalogenase superfamily, contains the catalytic motif DXDX(T/V). One member of this family, Dullard, was recently shown to play a role in regulating neural tube development in Xenopus. Our study demonstrates that Dullard and a yeast protein, Nem1p, have similar functions in both mammalian and yeast cells. Both proteins share similarities in primary structure, domain composition, and substrate preferences, and localize to the nuclear envelope. Additionally, we show that human Dullard can rescue the abnormal nuclear envelope morphology of nem1Delta yeast cells, effectively replacing Nem1p. Furthermore, Nem1p has been shown to dephosphorylate the yeast phosphatidic acid phosphatase, Smp2p, and we find that Dullard dephosphorylates the mammalian phosphatidic acid phosphatase, lipin. These findings suggest that Dullard is involved in a unique phosphatase cascade that regulates nuclear membrane biogenesis, which is conserved from yeast to mammals.

title: Increased expression of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 in ovarian/peritoneal endometriotic lesions.
text:
Endometriosis is a disease that affects up to 10% of premenopausal women and is dependent on estrogen. Recent studies have shown that different endometriosis sites have varying levels of estrogen concentration, which may be due to unique local estrogen metabolism. To investigate this further, we analyzed the expression of enzymes responsible for oxidative estrogen metabolism in biopsy samples and endometrial and endometriotic stromal cells.
We used a cross-sectional study design to evaluate the mRNA and protein expressions of cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A1 and CYP1B1 in 58 premenopausal women who were not under hormonal treatment. Our results showed that superficial lesions (ovarian and peritoneal) had increased CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 mRNA expression compared to healthy endometrium. Interestingly, we found a similar pattern of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 expression in in vitro stromal cells isolated from ovarian lesions, rectal lesions, and eutopic endometrium. However, there was an increased half-life of estradiol (measured by HPLC-MS-MS) in ovarian endometriotic stromal cells compared to paired eutopic stromal endometrial cells.
Our findings suggest that there is a site-dependent regulation of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 in ovarian/peritoneal lesions and ovarian endometriotic stromal cells, while a slower metabolism occurs in these cells. These findings may have implications for the development of new treatments for endometriosis.

title: Eset partners with Oct4 to restrict extraembryonic trophoblast lineage potential in embryonic stem cells.
text: The histone H3 Lysine 9 (H3K9) methyltransferase Eset is an epigenetic regulator crucial for the development of the inner cell mass (ICM) in embryonic stem cells. Although ICM-derived embryonic stem cells are normally incapable of contributing to the trophectoderm (TE) in blastocysts, depletion of Eset using short hairpin RNAs (shRNAs) leads to differentiation and the formation of trophoblast-like cells, as well as the induction of trophoblast-associated gene expression. Through chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and sequencing (ChIP-seq) analyses, we identified Eset target genes with Eset-dependent H3K9 trimethylation. Our findings revealed that genes preferentially expressed in the TE, such as Tcfap2a and Cdx2, are bound and repressed by Eset. Using single-cell PCR analysis, we observed that the expression of Cdx2 and Tcfap2a is also induced in Eset-depleted morula cells. Notably, Eset-depleted cells can incorporate into the TE of a blastocyst and, subsequently, placental tissues. Coimmunoprecipitation and ChIP assays further demonstrated that Eset interacts with Oct4, which in turn recruits Eset to silence these trophoblast-associated genes. Our results suggest that Eset restricts the extraembryonic trophoblast lineage potential of pluripotent cells and links an epigenetic regulator to key cell fate decisions through a pluripotency factor.

title: Suicides after pregnancy in Finland, 1987-94: register linkage study.
text:
Objective: To determine the rates of suicide associated with different stages of pregnancy in the Finnish population.
Design: Register linkage study.
Setting: Nationwide data from Finland.
Subjects: Women who committed suicide in 1987-94.
Results: A total of 73 suicides were associated with pregnancy, representing 5.4% of all suicides in women in this age group. The mean annual suicide rate was 11.3 per 100,000. The suicide rate associated with birth was significantly lower (5.9), while the rates associated with miscarriage (18.1) and induced abortion (34.7) were significantly higher than in the general population. The risk associated with birth was higher among teenagers, while the risk associated with abortion was increased in all age groups. Women who had committed suicide tended to come from lower social classes and were more likely to be unmarried than other women who had had a completed pregnancy.
Conclusions: The findings suggest that the increased risk of suicide after an induced abortion may be due to common risk factors or harmful effects of induced abortion on mental health.

title: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis: a rare or very rare clinical entity?
text:
Lactic acidosis associated with biguanide therapy, including metformin, is a well-known complication that can be serious. Although the incidence of metformin-associated lactic acidosis (MALA) is lower than that associated with phenformin, it is still being reported sporadically, raising concerns for clinicians. In this review, we examine the current global data on the prevalence of MALA, risk factors for its development, and practical guidelines for metformin use to minimize the risk of this potential hazard.
METHODS:
We conducted an extensive literature search using Medline and Ovid databases (1965-1998) for articles containing the following keywords: 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'oral hypoglycemic drugs', 'biguanides', 'metformin-associated lactic acidosis', and 'renal impairment'.
RESULTS:
MALA is a rare clinical entity, 20 times less common than phenformin-associated lactic acidosis. Renal impairment is the major precipitating factor for MALA in metformin-treated patients. In some cases, no precipitating factors could be identified, and the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Based on previous reports, practical recommendations for metformin use to minimize the risk of MALA have been listed.
CONCLUSIONS:
The low prevalence of MALA is comparable to the prevalence of sulphonylurea-induced hypoglycaemia. Metformin has numerous beneficial metabolic effects in the management of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Provided that recommended guidelines for metformin use are strictly adhered to, its widespread use will be safe, and the incidence of MALA will further reduce.

title: Inborn errors of human JAKs and STATs.
text: Inborn errors of the genes encoding two of the four human JAKs (JAK3 and TYK2) and three of the six human STATs (STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5B) have been identified. We review the disorders caused by mutations in these five genes, highlighting how the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying these conditions have been elucidated by the discovery of inborn errors of cytokines, hormones, and their receptors, including those interacting with JAKs and STATs. Although the functions of JAKs and STATs are largely conserved between mammals, significant phenotypic differences have emerged between mice and humans carrying biallelic null alleles of JAK3, TYK2, STAT1, or STAT5B. Moreover, the high degree of allelic heterogeneity at the human JAK3, TYK2, STAT1, and STAT3 loci has revealed a wide range of immunological and clinical phenotypes, which were not anticipated.

title: Mental health problems of homeless children and families: longitudinal study.
text:
Objective: To assess the mental health needs of homeless children and families before and after rehousing, and to identify local strategies for addressing these needs.
Design: Cross-sectional and longitudinal study.
Setting: City of Birmingham.
Population: 58 rehoused families with 103 children aged 2-16 years and 21 comparison families of low socioeconomic status in stable housing, with 54 children.
Main Outcome Measures: Mental health problems in children and mothers, including level of communication, social support, and history of abuse and poor social integration.
Results: Mental health problems were significantly higher in rehoused mothers and their children than in the comparison group, with 26% of mothers and 39% of children experiencing mental health problems compared to 5% and 11%, respectively, in the comparison group (P = 0.04 and P = 0.0003). Homeless mothers also had significantly less social support at follow-up. Mothers with a history of abuse and poor social integration were more likely to have children with persistent mental health problems.
Conclusions: Homeless families have a high level of complex needs that cannot be met by conventional health services and arrangements. Local strategies for rapid rehousing into permanent accommodation, effective social support and health care for parents and children, and protection from violence and intimidation should be developed and implemented to address these needs.

title: The flip side of perception-action coupling: locomotor experience and the ontogeny of visual-postural coupling.
text: The potential impact of motor development on psychological function has recently gained renewed attention, with a shift in focus from predicting long-term psychological outcomes based on early motor abilities, to understanding how the acquisition of motor skills influences psychological changes. This paper explores the relationship between the acquisition of prone locomotion and the development of an infant's ability to regulate posture based on visual information. It is argued that the onset of prone locomotion prompts infants to differentiate and control spatially defined regions of visual flow to effectively perform subtasks within the larger task of locomotion, such as steering, attending to the surface of support, and maintaining postural control. The paper presents a research program aimed at determining whether locomotor experience directly improves the ability to utilize peripheral visual flow for postural control, or if it simply forecasts maturational improvements. Additionally, a hypothesis is proposed that links the emergence of a fear of heights to an infant's ability to regulate posture based on visual flow. The paper's central theoretical idea is the principle of probabilistic epigenesis, which suggests that one developmental acquisition can lead to a multitude of new developmental changes in the same and different domains.

title: Crystal structure of the first plant urease from jack bean: 83 years of journey from its first crystal to molecular structure.
text: Urease, a nickel-dependent metalloenzyme, is synthesized by plants, bacteria, and fungi, and catalyzes the hydrolysis of urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide. Although the amino acid sequences of plant and bacterial ureases are similar, there are notable differences in their biological activities. Plant ureases possess insecticidal properties independent of their ureolytic activity, whereas bacterial ureases do not. To date, the structural information available only for bacterial ureases, although the jack bean urease (Canavalia ensiformis; JBU), the first plant urease to be crystallized in 1926, has been studied. To better understand the biological properties of plant ureases, including their insecticidal mechanism, we initiated structural studies on some plant ureases. Here, we report the crystal structure of JBU, the first plant urease structure, at 2.05 Å resolution. The active-site architecture of JBU is similar to that of bacterial ureases, containing a bi-nickel center. JBU has a bound phosphate and covalently modified residue (Cys592) by beta-mercaptoethanol at its active site, and the concomitant binding of multiple inhibitors (phosphate and beta-mercaptoethanol) is not observed in bacterial ureases. By correlating the structural information of JBU with available biophysical and biochemical data on insecticidal properties of plant ureases, we hypothesize that the amphipathic beta-hairpin located in the entomotoxic peptide region of plant ureases might form a membrane insertion beta-barrel, similar to beta-pore-forming toxins.

title: Studies of nuclear and cytoplasmic behaviour during the five mitotic cycles that precede gastrulation in Drosophila embryogenesis.
text:
Using differential interference contrast optics and cinematography, we have investigated the morphological changes that occur in the living, syncytial embryo of Drosophila from stages 10 to 14 of embryogenesis, just prior to and during the formation of the cellular blastoderm. To supplement these studies, we have also collected data from fixed, stained, whole embryos. Our findings include:
* The average duration of nuclear cycles 10, 11, 12, and 13 is approximately 9, 10, 12, and 21 minutes, respectively, at 25°C.
* During these four cycles, the duration of the mitotic period without a discrete nuclear envelope is 3, 3, 3, and 5 minutes, respectively.
* The length of nuclear cycle 14 varies positionally throughout the embryo, with the shortest cycles lasting approximately 65 minutes.
* In living embryos, syncytial blastoderm nuclei enter and leave mitosis in two waves that originate simultaneously from the opposite anterior and posterior poles of the embryo and terminate in the midregion. These waves take approximately half a minute to travel across the embryonic surface from pole to equator.
* Yolk nuclei, which remain in the core of the embryo while the rest of the nuclei migrate to the periphery, divide in synchrony with the migrating nuclei at nuclear cycles 8 and 9, and just after the now peripherally located nuclei at nuclear cycle 10. After cycle 10, these yolk nuclei cease dividing and become polyploid.
* The syncytial embryo has at least three distinct levels of cytoskeletal organization: structured domains of cytoplasm are organized around each blastoderm nucleus; radially directed tracks orient colchicine-sensitive saltatory transport throughout the peripheral cytoplasm; and a long-range organization of the core of the embryo makes possible coherent movements of the large inner yolk mass in concert with each nuclear cycle. This highly organized cytoplasm may be involved in providing positional information for the important process of nuclear determination that occurs during these stages.

title: Activation of liver X receptors and retinoid X receptors prevents bacterial-induced macrophage apoptosis.
text:
The interactions between microbes and macrophages play a crucial role in the development of various infections. Some bacterial pathogens have been shown to induce macrophage apoptosis, which can help them evade the host's innate immune response. Our study reveals that activating liver X receptors (LXRs) and retinoid X receptors (RXRs) in macrophages can inhibit their apoptotic responses to various stimuli, including the withdrawal of macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) and exposure to inducers of apoptosis.
We found that LXR and RXR agonists induced the expression of antiapoptotic regulators, such as AIM/CT2, Bcl-X(L), and Birc1a, while inhibiting the expression of proapoptotic regulators and effectors, including caspases 1, 4/11, 7, and 12; Fas ligand; and Dnase1l3. Combining LXR and RXR agonists was more effective than using either agonist alone at inhibiting apoptosis in response to various inducers of apoptosis. Additionally, inhibition of AIM/CT2 expression in response to LXR/RXR agonists partially reversed their antiapoptotic effects.
Our findings suggest that LXRs and RXRs play unexpected roles in controlling macrophage survival and raise the possibility that LXR/RXR agonists may be exploited to enhance innate immunity to bacterial pathogens that induce apoptotic programs as a strategy for evading host responses.

title: p53 binding to nucleosomal DNA depends on the rotational positioning of DNA response element.
text: The specific binding of p53 to DNA is essential for its tumor suppressor function. To investigate the constraints on p53-DNA recognition due to nucleosomal organization, we examined the binding of the p53 DNA binding domain (p53DBD) and full-length wild-type p53 protein to a single p53 response element (p53RE) located near the nucleosomal dyad in six different rotational configurations. Our results show that the strongest p53 binding occurs when the p53RE in the nucleosome is bent in the same direction as observed in solution and co-crystal structures. However, if the orientation of the binding site in the core particle is changed by approximately 180 degrees, the p53RE becomes inaccessible, indicating that the orientation of the binding sites on a nucleosome may play a significant role in the initial p53-DNA recognition and subsequent cofactor recruitment.

title: Diminished sympathetic nervous system activity in genetically obese (ob/ob) mouse.
text: The genetically obese (ob/ob) mouse exhibits impaired thermoregulatory responses to cold exposure, which has been attributed to abnormalities in intracellular metabolism or insensitivity of peripheral tissues to the thermogenic effects of catecholamines. However, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is also subject to feedback regulation, suggesting that a peripheral impairment in thermogenesis should be associated with an increase in SNS activity. To investigate SNS activity in the ob/ob mouse, norepinephrine (NE) turnover was measured in heart and interscapular brown adipose tissue (IBAT) of ob/ob and lean mice. The results showed that SNS activity was reduced by 33-56% in heart and by 45-73% in IBAT in ob/ob mice compared to lean controls at ambient temperature (22°C). However, during cold exposure (4°C), NE turnover increased in heart and IBAT to a similar extent in both ob/ob and lean mice, but NE turnover rates in heart, and probably in IBAT as well, remained lower in the obese mice than in the lean despite the gradual development of hypothermia in the ob/ob mice during this period. Administration of naltrexone, a long-acting opiate antagonist, failed to reverse the suppression of SNS activity observed in the ob/ob mice. These findings suggest that diminished SNS activity may be an additional factor contributing to the defective thermogenesis characteristic of ob/ob mice.

title: Quality of life of young adults with idiopathic short stature: effect of growth hormone treatment. Dutch Growth Hormone Working Group.
text: The study aimed to investigate the impact of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment on the quality of life of young adults diagnosed with idiopathic short stature (ISS) during childhood. The study included 89 subjects, with 24 treated with rhGH from childhood and 65 never treated. At the time of the interview, all subjects had reached their final height, and the treated subjects were found to have a lower rate of having a partner compared to the control subjects, although there were no significant differences in general health state or personality between the two groups. The subjects reported experiencing negative events related to their height, but only a minority were willing to trade-off their height for increased growth. The parents of the treated subjects were found to have a high satisfaction rate with the treatment, with an estimated gain of 12-13 cm in final height. However, the actual gain in height was significantly lower, at 3.3 cm. Overall, the study concluded that rhGH treatment does not appear to have a significant impact on the quality of life of young adults with ISS.

title: Neighborhood Racial/Ethnic Concentration, Social Disadvantage, and Homicide Risk: An Ecological Analysis of 10 U.S. Cities
text: Homicide is a leading cause of death among African American and Hispanic men in the United States. To investigate the role of neighborhood characteristics in explaining racial/ethnic homicide gaps, we examined the relationship between these factors in 10 US cities. Our hypotheses were that higher concentrations of African Americans and Hispanics would be associated with higher homicide rates, and that adjusting for neighborhood characteristics such as unemployment, median household income, low educational attainment, and female headship would attenuate this relationship. We used separate Poisson regression models to test these hypotheses, controlling for spatial autocorrelation. Our findings revealed that homicide rates were significantly higher in neighborhoods with higher concentrations of African Americans and Hispanics compared to other groups, and that the association between racial/ethnic concentration and homicide was reduced after adjusting for neighborhood social disadvantage variables, particularly the percentage of female heads of household and percentage of individuals with less than a high school education. Additionally, we found that the relationship between neighborhood racial/ethnic concentration and homicide was more strongly explained by social disadvantage variables in some cities than in others. Based on our findings, policy makers may consider implementing policies that expand early childhood education programs and higher education opportunities, as well as encourage economic and community development initiatives in socially disadvantaged neighborhoods.

title: Preterm patent ductus arteriosus: A continuing conundrum for the neonatologist?
text: The management of preterm patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) remains a puzzle. On one hand, the physiological and statistical associations with adverse outcomes suggest that it is a pathological condition. However, clinical trials of treatment strategies have failed to demonstrate any long-term benefits. Recent ultrasound studies have suggested that the hemodynamic impact of PDA may occur earlier after birth than previously thought, within the first few hours after delivery. Despite this knowledge, it is still unclear when to treat PDA. Historical studies of symptomatic or pre-symptomatic treatment have not tested the effect of no treatment, and prophylactic treatment is the best-studied regimen. However, improvements in some short-term outcomes do not necessarily translate to longer-term benefits. Neonatologists have been hesitant to participate in trials that test treatment against a never-treat approach. Early postnatal hemodynamic significance suggests that targeting treatment based on the early postnatal constrictive response of the duct may optimize benefits. A pilot trial of this strategy showed a reduction in pulmonary hemorrhage incidence, but more trials are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Political and economic aspects of the transition to universal health coverage.
text:
Countries have achieved universal health coverage through diverse paths and health systems, yet they share common features in their journey towards UHC. These common features include:
1. A politically driven process fueled by various social forces to create public programs or regulations that expand access to care, improve equity, and distribute financial risks.
2. A growth in incomes and corresponding increase in health spending, which enables the purchase of more health services for a larger population.
3. An increase in the proportion of health spending that is pooled rather than paid out-of-pocket by households. This pooled share is often mobilized through taxes and channelled through government programs that provide or subsidize care, or through mandatory insurance schemes.
While pooled spending is a necessary condition for achieving UHC, it is not sufficient on its own. This paper examines common patterns in countries that have successfully achieved universal access to healthcare and considers how economic growth, demographics, technology, politics, and health spending have converged to bring about this significant advancement in public health.

title: Wedelolactone protects human bronchial epithelial cell injury against cigarette smoke extract-induced oxidant stress and inflammation responses through Nrf2 pathway.
text:
Cigarette smoke is the leading cause of various lung diseases, including lung cancer, by triggering oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, which can lead to cellular lesions in the normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) cells. Interestingly, Wedelolactone (WEL), a natural compound derived from Eclipta prostrata L., has been found to have inhibitory effects on cancer cell growth and proliferation. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of WEL on NHBE cell injury induced by cigarette smoke extract (CSE) in vitro.
Our results showed that pre-treatment with WEL (2.5-20 μM) significantly protected NHBE cells from 10% CSE-induced cell death. The pre-treatment with WEL also dose-dependently reversed the activities of antioxidant enzymes, such as superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), glutathione (GSH), and malondialdehyde (MDA), to their normal levels. Additionally, WEL significantly reduced the expressions of inflammatory markers, including cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), compared to CSE treatment alone. Furthermore, WEL also reduced the expressions of antioxidant enzymes, including NAD(P)H dehydrogenase:quinone 1 (NQO1) and heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), and these effects were further enhanced by the addition of an Nrf2 inhibitor, all-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA).
Our findings suggest that WEL protects NHBE cells against CSE-induced injury by modulating the Nrf2 pathway. These results indicate that WEL may be a promising new agent for protecting against cigarette smoke-induced lung injury.

title: IL-17 promotes tumor development through the induction of tumor promoting microenvironments at tumor sites and myeloid-derived suppressor cells.
text: The study investigates the role of immune responses in tumor development, specifically focusing on the cytokine IL-17. Although IL-17-producing cells are found in cancer patients and tumor-bearing mice, their role in tumor growth is controversial and mechanisms are not fully understood. The researchers found that mice lacking the IL-17 receptor (IL-17R) had reduced tumor growth, while those deficient in both IL-17R and another receptor (IFN-gammaR) had slower tumor growth compared to wild-type mice. Neutralizing IL-17 with antibodies inhibited tumor growth in wild-type mice, while systemic administration of IL-17 promoted tumor growth. The IL-17R deficiency increased CD8 T cell infiltration and reduced myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) infiltration in tumors, while administration of IL-17 had the opposite effects. The study suggests that IL-17-mediated responses promote tumor development by inducing tumor-promoting microenvironments at the tumor site, and that IL-17-mediated regulation of MDSCs is a primary mechanism for its tumor-promoting effects. These findings have significant implications for targeting IL-17 in cancer treatment.

title: Circulating tumor cells and [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography for outcome prediction in metastatic breast cancer.
text: The purpose of this study was to compare the prognostic value of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) monitoring during systemic therapy for metastatic breast cancer (MBC). The study analyzed 115 MBC patients who underwent CTC counts and FDG-PET/CT scans at baseline and during therapy (midtherapy). The patients were categorized based on their midtherapy CTC counts as favorable (<5 CTCs/7.5 mL blood) or unfavorable (≥5 CTCs/7.5 mL blood). The study found that midtherapy CTC levels correlated with FDG-PET/CT response in 68% of evaluable patients. In univariate analysis, midtherapy CTC counts and FDG-PET/CT response predicted overall survival (OS) (P < .001 and P = .001, respectively). FDG-PET/CT predicted OS in 31 (91%) of 34 discordant patients who had fewer than 5 CTCs at midtherapy. Only midtherapy CTC levels remained significant in a multivariate analysis (P = .004). The study concluded that detection of 5 or more CTCs during therapeutic monitoring can accurately predict prognosis in MBC beyond metabolic response. FDG-PET/CT deserves a role in patients who have fewer than 5 CTCs at midtherapy. Prospective trials should evaluate the most sensitive and cost-effective modality for therapeutic monitoring in MBC.

title: Phylogenetic analysis of Portuguese Feline Immunodeficiency Virus sequences reveals high genetic diversity.
text: Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV) is a Lentivirus responsible for an immunodeficiency disease in domestic cats. Based on the genetic diversity of the V3-V5 region of the env gene, FIV is classified into five phylogenetic subtypes (A, B, C, D, and E) with a worldwide distribution. To investigate the subtype diversity of FIV in Portugal, a serological survey was conducted over a one-year period at the Veterinary Faculty Hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, to identify seropositive animals. Two viral genomic regions were amplified using nested PCR, sequenced, and the phylogenetic relationships between 24 newly obtained Portuguese FIV sequences and previously published FIV isolates were assessed. The introduction of these sequences resulted in subclustering within subtype B, which includes most of the new Portuguese sequences. Additionally, a new cluster emerged, consisting of two highly divergent new sequences that may represent a new subtype. The study of these new FIV isolates revealed the presence in Portugal of a unique viral population subclustering within subtype B and of sequences distinct from the five known subtypes, contributing to the understanding of FIV's genetic diversity.

title: Aire deficiency promotes TRP-1-specific immune rejection of melanoma.
text: The thymic transcription factor autoimmune regulator (Aire) plays a crucial role in preventing autoimmunity by promoting the expression of tissue-specific self-antigens, including many cancer antigens. For instance, individuals lacking Aire are predisposed to vitiligo, an autoimmune disease that targets melanocytes, which can sometimes be triggered by effective immunotherapies against melanoma. Consequently, we hypothesized that Aire deficiency in mice might enhance immune responses to cancer and provide insights into how such responses might be triggered. In this study, we found that Aire deficiency leads to decreased thymic expression of TRP-1 (TYRP1), a self-antigen specific to melanocytes and a cancer antigen in melanomas. Aire deficiency also impairs negative selection of TRP-1-specific T cells without affecting the number of regulatory T cells in the thymus. As a result, Aire-deficient mice exhibit elevated immune responses against melanoma, which are associated with suppressed melanoma outgrowth. Moreover, transplantation of Aire-deficient thymic stroma into an otherwise Aire wild-type host leads to more effective immune rejection of melanoma. Overall, our findings demonstrate how Aire deficiency can boost immune responses against melanoma and highlight the potential of manipulating TRP-1-specific T-cell negative selection as a strategy to enhance immune rejection of melanoma.

title: Mass screening programmes and trends in cervical cancer in Finland and the Netherlands.
text: With respect to cervical cancer management, Finland and the Netherlands share similar characteristics, such as fertility rate, age of mother at first birth, and a national screening program for several years. The aim of this study is to compare trends in incidence of and mortality from cervical cancer in Finland and the Netherlands in relation to the introduction and intensity of their screening programs. Therefore, incidence and mortality rates were calculated using cancer registries in both countries. Data on screening intensity were obtained from the Finnish Cancer Registry and the Dutch evaluation center at ErasmusMC-Rotterdam. Women aged 30-60 have been screened every 5 years in Finland since 1992 and in the Netherlands since 1996. Screening protocols for smear taking and referral to the gynecologist are similar. Incidence and mortality rates have declined more in Finland. In 2003, age-adjusted incidence and mortality in Finland were 4.0 and 0.9 per 100,000 woman-years, respectively, compared to 4.9 and 1.4 per 100,000 woman-years in the Netherlands. Excess smear use in the Netherlands was estimated to be 24 per 1,000 women during a 5-year interval, while in Finland it was 121 per 1,000 women. The decline in mortality in Finland seems to be almost entirely related to the screening program, while in the Netherlands it was initially thought to be a natural decline. Differences in risk factors, such as population density and percentage of immigrants and female smokers, may also play a role. The greater excess smear use in Finland may also have influenced incidence.

title: Biochemical characterization of the Ran-RanBP1-RanGAP system: are RanBP proteins and the acidic tail of RanGAP required for the Ran-RanGAP GTPase reaction?
text: RanBP proteins have been shown to enhance the efficiency of the RanGAP-mediated GTPase reaction on Ran. Despite the structure of the Ran-RanBP1-RanGAP complex indicating that RanBP1 is located away from the active site, we reinvestigated the reaction using fluorescence spectroscopy under pre-steady-state conditions. Our findings reveal that RanBP1 does not influence the rate-limiting step of the reaction, which involves the cleavage of GTP and/or the release of product P(i). However, RanBP1 does affect the dynamics of the Ran-RanGAP interaction, significantly stimulating the association reaction (4.5 x 10(8) M(-1) s(-1)) to the point that it is under diffusion control. By establishing a valuable kinetic system for the interaction analysis, we found that the highly conserved acidic C-terminal end of RanGAP is not essential for the switch-off reaction. In contrast to previous findings, our results demonstrate that the acidic tail of RanGAP plays a crucial role in microtubule organization during mitosis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We propose that the acidic tail of RanGAP is involved in a process during mitosis.

title: Concomitant induction of CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in volunteers immunized with Salmonella enterica serovar typhi strain CVD 908-htrA.
text: The study investigated the role of Type 1 cell-mediated immunity in protecting against typhoid fever by evaluating the immune response to Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi) strain CVD 908-htrA, a leading live oral typhoid vaccine candidate. The study found that immunization with CVD 908-htrA elicited both CD4+ and CD8+ S. Typhi immune responses, including potent cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) responses and interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) secretion. The study showed that CTL responses were observed in six out of eight vaccinees, with strong CD4+ T cell responses also observed. Increases in IFN-gamma production to soluble S. Typhi flagella (STF) occurred in 82% and 38% of the volunteers in the high and low dose groups, respectively. The study found robust correlations between volunteers who responded with IFN-gamma-secreting cells to stimulation with S. Typhi-infected cells and IFN-gamma released in response to stimulation with STF Ags (r = 0.822, p < 0.001) and between CTL and IFN-gamma production to STF (r = 0.818, p = 0.013). These findings suggest that Type 1 immunity plays a significant role in controlling typhoid infection and support the continued evaluation of CVD 908-htrA as a typhoid vaccine candidate.

title: The diverse functions of GAPDH: views from different subcellular compartments.
text: Recent studies have revealed multiple roles for glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) beyond its cytoplasmic location under basal conditions. GAPDH is also found in nucleus, mitochondria, and small vesicular fractions. Upon exposure to stressors, GAPDH undergoes dynamic subcellular redistribution. This review focuses on the multifunctional properties of GAPDH, including its oligomerization, posttranslational modification, and subcellular localization. We also discuss how S-nitrosylation of GAPDH under oxidative stress can lead to cell death/dysfunction through nuclear translocation of GAPDH, which is counteracted by a cytosolic protein called GOSPEL. Additionally, GAPDH has been implicated in various diseases such as neurodegenerative disorders and cancers, and therapeutic strategies based on molecular understanding of GAPDH are discussed.

title: Exercise-induced asthma: a practical guide to definitions, diagnosis, prevalence, and treatment.
text: Exercise-induced asthma is characterized by an intermittent narrowing of the airways, leading to a decrease in airflow, which triggers symptoms such as wheezing, chest tightness, coughing, and difficulty breathing. This condition is most commonly experienced by individuals with chronic asthma, but can also affect those without a prior diagnosis of asthma. A definitive diagnosis requires demonstrating a drop in airflow rate of over 13-15% in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) and over 15-20% in peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) after exercise, accompanied by symptoms. According to prevalence data, this condition is quite common among recreational athletes and highly competitive athletes, with at least 12-15% of unselected athletes exhibiting positive exercise challenges. Treatment for exercise-induced asthma involves a combination of non-pharmacological measures, such as utilizing the refractory period after exercise and prewarming air, as well as medications like beta-agonists, cromolyn, and nedocromil. With proper treatment, individuals with exercise-induced asthma can potentially participate and compete at the highest levels of performance.

title: Effect of sample quality on the sensitivity of endoscopic biopsy for detecting gastric and duodenal lesions in dogs and cats.
text:
Background: The quality of histopathology slides from endoscopic biopsies of dogs and cats varies, and the impact of biopsy quality on diagnostic accuracy is unknown.
Hypothesis: The ability to detect histological lesions in the stomach or duodenum of dogs and cats is influenced by the quality of endoscopic biopsy samples submitted. More samples are required to diagnose lesions in poor-quality tissue specimens.
Methods: Histopathology slides from 99 dogs and 51 cats were evaluated as clinical cases at 8 veterinary institutions or practices in 5 countries. The quality of the histological section of tissue (inadequate, marginal, adequate), type of lesion (lymphangiectasia, crypt lesion, villus blunting, cellular infiltrate), and severity of lesion (normal, mild, moderate, severe) were determined. The sensitivity of different quality tissue samples for detecting various lesions was also determined.
Results: Fewer samples were required to diagnose lesions in dogs as the quality of the sample improved from inadequate to marginal to adequate. Duodenal lesions in cats showed a similar trend, except for moderate duodenal infiltrates, for which quality of tissue sample had no effect. Gastric lesions in dogs and mild gastric lesions in cats followed a similar pattern, while the number of tissue samples needed to diagnose moderately severe gastric lesions in cats was not affected by sample quality.
Conclusions and Clinical Importance: The quality of endoscopically obtained tissue samples has a significant impact on their sensitivity for detecting certain lesions, and there are differences in the quality required for biopsies of canine and feline tissues.

title: G-quadruplexes significantly stimulate Pif1 helicase-catalyzed duplex DNA unwinding.
text:
The evolutionarily conserved G-quadruplexes (G4s) are inherited faithfully and play a multifaceted role in cellular processes, including telomere maintenance, gene regulation, DNA replication initiation, and epigenetic regulation. Unlike the Watson-Crick base-pairing found in duplex DNA, G4s are formed through Hoogsteen base pairing, resulting in highly stable and compact DNA structures. Failure to resolve G4s in the cell can hinder DNA-based transactions and lead to genome instability. Cells have evolved specialized helicases to unwind G4 structures.
In this study, we employed a recombinant form of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Pif1 helicase to investigate its ability to unwind DNA substrates mimicking stalled lagging strand synthesis due to G4s, which resemble a replication origin and a G4-structured flap in Okazaki fragment maturation. Our findings reveal that the presence of G4s can significantly enhance the unwinding activity of Pif1. Further analysis revealed that this stimulation is due to G4-mediated Pif1 dimerization, which is essential for duplex DNA unwinding. These findings provide new insights into the properties and functions of G4s and their potential regulatory role in the rapid rescue of stalled lagging strand synthesis by facilitating the recognition and activation of replication origins, as well as the rapid removal of G4-structured flaps during Okazaki fragment maturation.

title: Diffusion tensor imaging detects and differentiates axon and myelin degeneration in mouse optic nerve after retinal ischemia.
text: Both axon and myelin degeneration have a significant impact on the long-term disability of patients with white matter disorders, but the clinical manifestations of the neurological dysfunction caused by these disorders are not sufficient to determine the origin of the neurological deficits. A noninvasive biological marker that can detect and differentiate axon and myelin degeneration would be a valuable addition to the current diagnostic tools. Previous studies have proposed directional diffusivities derived from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) as potential biological markers for detecting and differentiating axon and myelin degeneration. To further investigate this hypothesis, the optic nerve was examined serially using DTI in a mouse model of retinal ischemia. The results showed a significant decrease in the lambdaparallel diffusion marker, which is consistent with histological findings of axonal degeneration, 3 days after ischemia, without any concurrent changes in the lambdaperpendicular marker, which is consistent with myelin degeneration. These findings support the hypothesis that lambdaparallel and lambdaperpendicular can serve as specific markers of axonal and myelin injury, respectively, and that the coexistence of axonal and myelin degeneration does not confound their utility.

title: Direct isolation and identification of promoters in the human genome.
text: Transcriptional regulatory elements play a crucial role in gene expression during animal development and cellular responses to environmental cues, yet our understanding of these regions in the human genome remains limited despite the availability of the complete genome sequence. Promoters, which mark the initiation of every transcript, are a crucial class of regulatory elements. The assembly of a large, complex protein structure known as the pre-initiation complex (PIC) on all active promoters distinguishes them from other sequences in the genome. By isolating promoters directly from human cells as protein-DNA complexes and identifying the resulting DNA sequences using genomic tiling microarrays, we uncovered 252 PIC-binding sites in 44 semirandomly selected human genomic regions, comprising 1% (30 megabase pairs) of the human genome. Of these, nearly 72% overlap or immediately flank 5' ends of known cDNA sequences, while the remainder is found in other genomic regions that likely harbor putative promoters of unannotated transcripts. Molecular analysis of the RNA isolated from one cell line revealed transcripts initiated from over half of the putative promoter fragments, and transient transfection assays revealed promoter activity for a significant proportion of fragments when fused to a luciferase reporter gene. These results demonstrate the specificity of a genome-wide analysis method for mapping transcriptional regulatory elements and highlight the fact that a significant number of human genes remain to be discovered.

title: Attempted suicide in Europe: rates, trends and sociodemographic characteristics of suicide attempters during the period 1989-1992. Results of the WHO/EURO Multicentre Study on Parasuicide.
text: The World Health Organization/EURO Multicentre Project on Parasuicide is part of the efforts to achieve Target 12 of the WHO's "Health for All by the Year 2000" program for the European region. Sixteen centers in 13 European countries are involved in the project's monitoring aspect, which assesses trends in the epidemiology of suicide attempts. The project found significant variations in the average male and female age-standardized rates of suicide attempts across the participating countries. For example, Helsinki, Finland had the highest rate (314/100,000) among males, while Guipuzcoa, Spain had the lowest rate (45/100,000). Similarly, Cergy-Pontoise, France had the highest rate among females (462/100,000), while Guipuzcoa had the lowest rate (69/100,000). Interestingly, with the exception of Helsinki, the person-based suicide attempt rates were higher among women than among men. Additionally, the highest rates were observed in the younger age groups, while the rates among individuals aged 55 years or over were generally the lowest. The project also found that the majority of suicide attempters made more than one attempt, with nearly 20% of second attempts occurring within 12 months of the first attempt. Furthermore, the methods used were primarily "soft" (poisoning) or cutting. Notably, suicide attempters were more likely to belong to social categories associated with social destabilization and poverty compared to the general population.

title: Recurrent outbreaks of Salmonella Enteritidis infections in a Texas restaurant: phage type 4 arrives in the United States.
text: In recent years, infections caused by Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) phage type 4 have spread across Europe, but have been rare in the USA. However, there have been two notable outbreaks of this strain in the USA, both of which were linked to a Chinese restaurant in El Paso, Texas. The first outbreak occurred in April 1993, with no source identified, while the second outbreak occurred in September 1993. To investigate the cause of the second outbreak, we compared the food exposures of the 19 patients with those of two control groups. Our findings revealed that egg rolls were the only item significantly associated with illness in both analyses, with an odds ratio of 8.2 in the first control group and 13.1 in the second control group. Retrospective analysis of the April outbreak also implicated egg rolls, with an odds ratio of 32.4. It is likely that these two outbreaks could have been prevented by using pasteurized eggs and safe food preparation practices.

title: Strand-specific mismatch correction in nuclear extracts of human and Drosophila melanogaster cell lines.
