The FBC evaluations consisted of baseline spirometry, actual or simulated competition, and spirometry tests at 5, 10, and 15 minutes post-exercise. In contrast to self-reported symptoms, the study found that only 48% of athletes who tested positive for EIA reported symptoms, with post-race cough being the most common symptom. The study also found that baseline spirometry was similar for both groups, and that a lower limit reference range of forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) for controls suggested that post-exercise decrements of greater than approximately -7% indicate abnormal airway response in this population. Additionally, the study found that exercise time duration did not affect bronchial reactivity, and that 78% of FBC PFT positives were PFT normal after undergoing a laboratory-based challenge. Overall, the study suggests that self-reported symptoms are not reliable in identifying EIA, and that reference range criteria for FEV1 decrement in elite athletes post-exercise differ from current recommended guidelines. The study also highlights the potential for false negatives in this population if EIA screening is performed with inadequate exercise and environmental stress.

title: Use of a targeted oncolytic poxvirus, JX-594, in patients with refractory primary or metastatic liver cancer: a phase I trial.
text:
In this study, the researchers aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of intratumoral injection of JX-594, a targeted oncolytic poxvirus, in patients with refractory primary or metastatic liver cancer. The study was conducted as a phase I dose-escalation trial at Dong-A University Hospital in South Korea, and 14 patients were enrolled between January 2006 and July 2007.
The primary objectives of the study were to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of JX-594 and to assess its safety profile. The researchers also evaluated the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of JX-594.
The study results showed that intratumoral injection of JX-594 was generally well-tolerated, with all patients experiencing mild to moderate flu-like symptoms and four patients experiencing transient grade I-III dose-related thrombocytopenia. Grade III hyperbilirubinaemia was observed as a dose-limiting toxicity, and the MTD was determined to be 1x10(9) pfu.
In addition, the researchers found that JX-594 replication-dependent dissemination in the blood led to infection of non-injected tumour sites, and GM-CSF expression resulted in grade I-III increases in neutrophil counts in four of six patients at the MTD. Tumour responses were observed in both injected and non-injected tumours, with three patients experiencing partial response, six patients having stable disease, and one patient experiencing progressive disease.
Overall, the study suggests that intratumoral injection of JX-594 is a promising approach for treating refractory primary or metastatic liver cancer, with a generally acceptable safety profile and evidence of anti-tumoral effects against several types of carcinomas. Phase II trials are currently underway to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of JX-594 in this patient population.

title: PTH Signaling in Osteoprogenitors Is Essential for B-Lymphocyte Differentiation and Mobilization.
text: Cells of the osteoblast lineage play a crucial role in supporting the development of B lymphocytes in the bone marrow (BM). Parathyroid hormone (PTH) signaling through its receptor (PPR) regulates hematopoietic stem cells, but its function in B lymphopoiesis is not well understood. Our study shows that deleting PPR in osteoprogenitors leads to a significant loss of trabecular and cortical bone. PPR signaling in osteoprogenitors, but not in mature osteoblasts or osteocytes, is essential for B-cell precursor differentiation through IL-7 production. Interestingly, despite a reduction in B-cell progenitors in the BM of mice lacking PPR in osteoprogenitors, there is an increase in mature IgD(+) B cells in the BM. This retention of mature B cells is associated with increased expression of vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM1) by PPR-deficient osteoprogenitors, and treatment with VCAM1 neutralizing antibody increases mobilization of B lymphocytes from mutant BM. Our findings demonstrate that PPR signaling in early osteoblasts is necessary for B-cell differentiation via IL-7 secretion and for B-lymphocyte mobilization via VCAM1.

title: Snail coordinately regulates downstream pathways to control multiple aspects of mammalian neural precursor development.
text:
The Snail transcription factor plays a crucial role in regulating various developmental processes, but it is not believed to play a role in mammalian neural precursors. However, our study has shown that Snail does indeed regulate the survival, self-renewal, and differentiation of radial glial precursor cells in the embryonic murine cortex. We have identified two distinct and separable target pathways through which Snail regulates these processes.
Firstly, Snail promotes cell survival by inhibiting a p53-dependent death pathway. When p53 is knocked down, survival deficits caused by Snail knockdown are rescued. This suggests that Snail acts to protect these cells from death.
Secondly, we found that the cell cycle phosphatase Cdc25b is regulated by Snail in radial precursors. When Cdc25b is co-expressed with Snail, the decreased proliferation and differentiation of radial precursors observed upon Snail knockdown are rescued. This suggests that Snail regulates the cell cycle progression of these cells through Cdc25b.
Taken together, our findings indicate that Snail acts via both p53 and Cdc25b to coordinate multiple aspects of mammalian embryonic neural precursor biology. This provides new insights into the role of Snail in regulating the development of the nervous system.

title: Endothelial KLF2 links local arterial shear stress levels to the expression of vascular tone-regulating genes.
text:
Lung Krüppel-like factor (LKLF/KLF2) is an endothelial transcription factor that plays a crucial role in murine vasculogenesis and is specifically regulated by flow in vitro. Recent studies have shown a correlation between local flow variations in the adult human vasculature and LKLF expression. Specifically, decreased LKLF expression was observed at the bifurcation of the aorta to the iliac and carotid arteries, an area where neointima formation occurs. In vitro studies have demonstrated that shear stress directly regulates the expression of LKLF, with high shear stresses inducing a 4- to 30-fold increase in LKLF expression.
In vitro experiments have also shown that steady flow and pulsatile flow induce basal LKLF expression at shear stresses greater than approximately 5 dyne/cm2, while cyclic stretch has no effect. Prolonged LKLF induction in the absence of flow leads to changes in the expression of angiotensin-converting enzyme, endothelin-1, adrenomedullin, and endothelial nitric oxide synthase to levels similar to those observed under prolonged flow. Furthermore, LKLF repression by siRNA suppresses the flow response of endothelin-1, adrenomedullin, and endothelial nitric oxide synthase (P < 0.05).
These findings demonstrate that endothelial LKLF is regulated by flow in vivo and acts as a transcriptional regulator of several endothelial genes that control vascular tone in response to flow.

title: Synapsin I Cre transgene expression in male mice produces germline recombination in progeny.
text: The Cre/LoxP system can temporarily disable gene function in specific cell types, such as neurons, by using a transgenic mouse line that expresses the Cre enzyme under the control of a specific promoter. For instance, a Synapsin I promoter-driven Cre (SynCre) transgene has been widely used in studies to achieve neuronal-specific Cre expression. Interestingly, our findings show that Cre expression can also be observed in SynCre mice in the testes after breeding them with a floxed transgenic mouse line. This results in recombination of the floxed substrate in the testes, with the majority of male progeny inheriting a germline-recombined floxed allele. In contrast, this phenomenon is never observed in female progeny. This observation highlights the potential for confounding in studies using these mice and provides a means to employ male germ cell "deletor" strategies.

title: Hospital mortality, length of stay, and preventable complications among critically ill patients before and after tele-ICU reengineering of critical care processes.
text: The study aimed to investigate the association between a tele-intensive care unit (ICU) intervention and hospital mortality, length of stay, and preventable complications in an academic medical center. The study was a prospective stepped-wedge clinical practice study conducted over a period of two years, from April 26, 2005, to September 30, 2007, in 7 ICUs across two campuses of an 834-bed academic medical center. The study included 6290 adult patients admitted to medical, surgical, or cardiovascular ICUs. The tele-ICU intervention involved electronically supported and monitored processes for best practice adherence, care plan creation, and clinician response times to alarms. The study found that the tele-ICU intervention was associated with a significantly lower adjusted odds of mortality (odds ratio [OR] 0.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.31-0.52), shorter hospital length of stay (hazard ratio for discharge 1.44, 95% CI 1.33-1.56), and lower rates of preventable complications such as ventilator-associated pneumonia and catheter-related bloodstream infection. The results were similar across medical, surgical, and cardiovascular ICUs. The study concluded that implementation of a tele-ICU intervention was associated with improved patient outcomes, including reduced mortality and shorter hospital stay, as well as improved adherence to best practices and lower rates of preventable complications.

title: CD11b+ monocytes abrogate Th17 CD4+ T cell-mediated experimental autoimmune myocarditis.
text: Experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) serves as a Th17 T cell-mediated mouse model of post-inflammatory heart disease. In BALB/c wild-type mice, EAM is a self-limiting disease that peaks 21 days after alpha-myosin heavy chain (MyHC-alpha) peptide/complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) immunization and largely resolves thereafter. However, in IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice, EAM is exacerbated and exhibits a chronic progressive disease course. We found that this progressive disease course parallels persistently elevated interleukin-17 (IL-17) release from T cells infiltrating the hearts of IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice 30 days after immunization. In fact, IL-17 promotes the recruitment of CD11b(+) monocytes, the predominant heart-infiltrating cells in EAM. In turn, CD11b(+) monocytes suppress MyHC-alpha-specific Th17 T cell responses in an IFN-gamma-dependent manner in vitro. In vivo, injection of IFN-gammaR(+/+)CD11b(+) monocytes, but not IFN-gammaR(-/-)CD11b(+), monocytes, suppresses MyHC-alpha-specific T cells and abrogates the progressive disease course in IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice. Finally, co-injection of MyHC-alpha-specific, but not ovalbumin (OVA)-transgenic, IFN-gamma-releasing CD4(+) Th1 T cell lines, together with MyHC-alpha-specific Th17 T cells, protects RAG2(-/-) mice from EAM. In conclusion, CD11b(+) monocytes play a dual role in EAM: as a major cellular substrate of IL-17-induced inflammation and as mediators of an IFN-gamma-dependent negative feedback loop that confines disease progression.

title: The cytokine RANKL produced by positively selected thymocytes fosters medullary thymic epithelial cells that express autoimmune regulator.
text: The thymic medulla harbors a unique microenvironment that supports the development of self-tolerance through the expression of autoimmune regulator and diverse tissue-restricted genes by medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs). Positive selection is crucial for the formation of the thymic medulla, but the mechanisms underlying this process are not fully understood. Our study reveals that the cytokine RANK ligand (RANKL) produced by positively selected thymocytes plays a pivotal role in regulating the cellularity of mTECs and promoting thymic medulla formation. We found that RANKL production by thymocytes is essential for the formation of the thymic medulla in mice lacking positive selection, while disrupting RANKL function impairs medulla formation. These findings suggest that RANKL produced by positively selected thymocytes is the key factor in establishing central tolerance by fostering thymic medulla formation.

title: Fibrosis and adipogenesis originate from a common mesenchymal progenitor in skeletal muscle.
text: In muscular dystrophies, there is an accumulation of adipocytes and collagen type-I-producing cells (fibrosis), which was previously unknown in terms of their origin. Recently, we identified mesenchymal progenitors positive for platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRα) as the source of adipocytes in skeletal muscle. However, the origin of muscle fibrosis remains unidentified. In this study, clonal analyses revealed that PDGFRα(+) cells can also differentiate into collagen type-I-producing cells. In fact, PDGFRα(+) cells were found in fibrotic areas of the diaphragm in the mdx mouse, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Furthermore, mRNA of fibrosis markers was expressed exclusively in the PDGFRα(+) cell fraction in the mdx diaphragm. Interestingly, transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) isoforms, known to be potent profibrotic cytokines, induced expression of fibrosis markers in PDGFRα(+) cells but not in myogenic cells. Transplantation studies showed that fibrogenic PDGFRα(+) cells mainly originated from pre-existing PDGFRα(+) cells, and the contribution of PDGFRα(-) cells and circulating cells was limited. These findings indicate that mesenchymal progenitors are the primary source of both fat accumulation and fibrosis in skeletal muscle.

title: The pecking order of free radicals and antioxidants: lipid peroxidation, alpha-tocopherol, and ascorbate.
text: Free radicals exhibit a wide range of thermodynamic properties, from highly oxidizing to highly reducing. These properties can be used to predict a hierarchical order for free radical reactions. Using one-electron reduction potentials, the predicted order is in agreement with experimentally observed free radical electron transfer reactions, including those involving hydrogen atoms. These potentials are also consistent with experimental data that demonstrate the cooperative protection of lipids and lipid structures against peroxidation by vitamin E, the primary lipid-soluble antioxidant, and vitamin C, the terminal water-soluble antioxidant. Although vitamin E is located in membranes and vitamin C is located in aqueous phases, vitamin C is able to recycle vitamin E by repairing its tocopheroxyl (chromanoxyl) radical, allowing it to function again as a chain-breaking antioxidant. This review covers:

title: Mitochondrial respiration in subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue from patients with morbid obesity.
text: Adipose tissue plays a crucial role in endocrine and metabolic functions, yet its bioenergetics are not well characterized in humans, particularly in terms of regional differences. To investigate this, we used high-resolution respirometry to measure mitochondrial respiration in human abdominal subcutaneous and intra-abdominal visceral (omentum majus) adipose tissue obtained from 20 obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery. We also determined mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) using the PCR technique to estimate mitochondrial density. Adipose tissue samples were permeabilized and respirometric measurements were performed in duplicate at 37°C. We found that visceral fat contained more mitochondria per milligram of tissue than subcutaneous fat, but the cells were smaller in size. Robust and stable oxygen fluxes were observed in both tissues, and coupled state 3 (GMOS(D)) and uncoupled respiration were significantly higher in visceral (0.95 ± 0.05 and 1.15 ± 0.06 pmol O2 s1 mg1, respectively) compared to subcutaneous (0.76 ± 0.04 and 0.98 ± 0.05 pmol O2 s1 mg1, respectively) adipose tissue. Moreover, expressed per mtDNA, visceral adipose tissue had significantly lower mitochondrial respiration. Substrate control ratios were higher and uncoupling control ratio was lower (P < 0.05) in visceral compared to subcutaneous adipose tissue. These findings suggest that visceral fat is more bioenergetically active and more sensitive to mitochondrial substrate supply than subcutaneous fat, with higher relative activity of oxidative phosphorylation in visceral adipose tissue.

title: Endogenous gamma-H2AX-ATM-Chk2 checkpoint activation in Bloom's syndrome helicase deficient cells is related to DNA replication arrested forks.
text: The Bloom syndrome helicase (BLM) plays a crucial role in maintaining genomic stability, and a deficiency in BLM activity leads to the development of Bloom syndrome (BS), a cancer-predisposing condition. In this study, we investigate the effects of BLM deficiency on the DNA damage response in cell lines and primary fibroblasts. We find that BLM-deficient cells exhibit an endogenously activated DNA double-strand break checkpoint response, characterized by prominent levels of phosphorylated histone H2AX (gamma-H2AX), Chk2 (p(T68)Chk2), and ATM (p(S1981)ATM) colocalizing in nuclear foci. Interestingly, the mitotic fraction of gamma-H2AX foci does not appear to be higher in BLM-deficient cells, suggesting that these lesions form transiently during interphase. Using iododeoxyuridine pulse labeling and immunofluorescence microscopy, we observe the colocalization of gamma-H2AX, ATM, and Chk2 with replication foci, which are also costained for Rad51, indicating homologous recombination at these replication sites. To further investigate replication in BS cells, we use a single molecule approach on combed DNA fibers. We find that BS cells display a higher frequency of replication fork barriers, a reduced average fork velocity, and a global reduction of interorigin distances, indicative of an elevated frequency of origin firing. These findings suggest that the lack of BLM engages the cells in a state similar to precancerous tissues with replication stress. Our study is the first to report high ATM-Chk2 kinase activation and its linkage to replication defects in a BS model.

title: Impact of TNF-alpha and IL-6 levels on development of cachexia in newly diagnosed NSCLC patients.
text:
Background: Cachexia is a complex syndrome characterized by unexplained weight loss in patients with cancer. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) are cytokines that have been implicated in the development of cachexia. This study aimed to investigate the role of TNF-alpha and IL-6 in the development of cachexia in newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients.
Methods: We evaluated 44 NSCLC patients (21 males and 23 females) and 12 age-matched healthy smokers. The NSCLC patients were divided into two groups based on their weight loss: cachectic (n=23) and non-cachectic (n=21). The levels of TNF-alpha and IL-6 were measured in the serum of these patients.
Results: Our results showed that the body mass index (BMI) of cachectics was significantly lower than that of non-cachectics and controls (P=0.02). Serum TNF-alpha levels did not differ between cachectic and non-cachectic patients, but were significantly higher in NSCLC patients compared to controls (P=0.03). Serum IL-6 levels did not differ between the three groups, but there was a significant correlation between IL-6 and TNF-alpha, as well as between IL-6 and BMI (P=0.006 and P=0.03, respectively). Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) also correlated significantly with TNF-alpha (P=0.003) and BMI (P=0.03). The survival of 12 and 17 patients was recorded in cachectics and non-cachectics, respectively, but there was no significant difference in survival between the two groups.
Discussion: Our findings suggest that TNF-alpha and IL-6 play a role in the development of cachexia in NSCLC patients, but the levels of these cytokines do not necessarily distinguish between cachectic and non-cachectic patients. The significant correlation between IL-6, BMI, and TNF-alpha suggests that these cytokines act as cofactors in weight loss. The lack of significant difference in survival between the two groups suggests that BMI and cytokine levels may not be useful predictors of survival in NSCLC patients. However, the significant correlation of ESR with TNF-alpha suggests that ESR could provide valuable clues for considerable weight loss in the follow-up of NSCLC patients.
Conclusion: In conclusion, our study suggests that TNF-alpha and IL-6 play a role in the development of cachexia in NSCLC patients, but the levels of these cytokines do not necessarily distinguish between cachectic and non-cachectic patients. Further studies are needed to determine the clinical usefulness of measuring these cytokines in the follow-up of NSCLC patients.

title: Treatment of antidepressant-associated sexual dysfunction with sildenafil: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
Background: Sexual dysfunction is a common adverse effect of antidepressants, leading to noncompliance with treatment. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of sildenafil citrate in improving sexual function in men taking selective and nonselective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SRI) antidepressants.
Methods: This was a prospective, parallel-group, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at three US university medical centers between November 1, 2000, and January 1, 2001. A total of 90 male outpatients (mean age, 45 years) with major depression in remission and sexual dysfunction associated with SRI antidepressant treatment were randomly assigned to receive either sildenafil (n=45) or placebo (n=45). Participants took the study drug at a flexible dose starting at 50 mg and adjustable to 100 mg before sexual activity for 6 weeks. The primary outcome measure was the Clinical Global Impression-Sexual Function (CGI-SF) score, with secondary measures including scores on the International Index of Erectile Function, Arizona Sexual Experience Scale, Massachusetts General Hospital-Sexual Functioning Questionnaire, and Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAM-D).
Results: Of the 90 randomized patients, 83 (89%) took at least one dose of study drug and 76 (85%) completed the 6-week end-point assessments. At a CGI-SF score of 2 or lower, 54.5% of sildenafil-treated patients were much or very much improved compared to 4.4% of placebo patients (P<.001). Significant improvements were also observed in erectile function, arousal, ejaculation, orgasm, and overall satisfaction domain measures in the sildenafil group compared to the placebo group. Mean depression scores remained consistent with remission (HAM-D score < or =10) in both groups throughout the study duration.
Conclusion: This study found that sildenafil citrate effectively improved sexual function in men taking selective and nonselective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SRI) antidepressants. These improvements may enable patients to maintain adherence with effective antidepressant treatment.

title: Noncoding transcription at enhancers: general principles and functional models.
text: Mammalian genomes exhibit extensive transcriptional activity outside of protein-coding gene regions. Recent genome-wide studies have shown that cis-regulatory elements, such as enhancers and locus-control regions, are major sites of extragenic noncoding transcription. Enhancer-templated transcripts contribute a small fraction to the total amount of nonribosomal RNA in the cell, yet the possibility that enhancer transcription and resulting enhancer RNAs may have functional roles in certain cases, rather than simply representing transcriptional noise at accessible genomic regions, is supported by a growing body of experimental evidence. In this review, we will summarize the current understanding of enhancer transcription and its potential functional implications.

title: Microarray analysis of pneumococcal gene expression during invasive disease.
text: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a preeminent pathogen responsible for invasive bacterial infections. This study employed whole-genome microarrays from The Institute for Genomic Research to investigate the in vivo expression of S. pneumoniae genes. Total RNA was isolated from pneumococci isolated from blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and bacteria attached to a pharyngeal epithelial cell line in vitro. Microarray analysis of pneumococcal genes expressed in these models revealed body site-specific patterns of expression for virulence factors, transporters, transcription factors, translation-associated proteins, metabolism, and genes with unknown function. The study confirmed the contributions of several unknown genes to virulence through insertion duplication mutagenesis and challenge of mice with mutants. Additionally, the results were cross-referenced with previous studies that employed signature-tagged mutagenesis and differential fluorescence induction to identify genes that may be essential for invasive disease across a broad range of pneumococcal strains.

title: Integration of Smad and MAPK pathways: a link and a linker revisited.
text: Cells develop by responding to a combination of signals, with the highly dynamic processes of embryogenesis relying on swift decision-making in response to well-coordinated growth factor combinations. Understanding how diverse signaling pathways are integrated is crucial for comprehending physiology, and this requires identifying key nodes that operate in vivo. A recent study sheds light on the relevance of one such node by investigating the integration of the Smad and Ras/MAPK pathways during neural induction in Xenopus. The study found that two growth factors, FGF8 and IGF2, favor neural differentiation and mesoderm dorsalization by inhibiting BMP signaling. BMP induces differentiation of ectoderm into epidermal cell fates at the expense of neural fates, and it ventralizes the mesoderm at the expense of dorsal fates. The study also showed that neural differentiation and dorsal mesoderm formation are favored when BMP signaling is attenuated. Interestingly, the neuralizing effect of BMP inhibitors is somehow tied to FGF and IGF signaling, and the study suggests that FGF8 and IGF2 activate MAPK, which in turn inhibits the BMP signal-transduction factor Smad1. Smads are transcription factors that mediate gene responses to the entire TGF family, and they have two conserved globular domains involved in DNA binding and cytoplasmic retention. Receptor-mediated phosphorylation of Smads enables their nuclear accumulation and association with the shared partner Smad4 to form transcriptional complexes that are interpreted by the cell as a function of the context. The study highlights the importance of understanding how diverse signaling pathways are integrated in vivo and the relevance of key nodes in this process.

title: A brief analysis of clinical pharmacy interventions undertaken in an Australian teaching hospital.
text: During a 30-day period, clinical pharmacists recorded and analyzed 67 interventions they had made in response to drug-related problems. After initial review, 28 intervention reports were excluded, leaving 39 for further analysis. Of the remaining interventions, 20 patients were under the care of a medical unit, and cardiovascular/antithrombotic agents accounted for 17 reports (43.5%). The majority of interventions (64%) were implemented during inpatient medication order review by the clinical pharmacist. The most common drug-related problem addressed in the interventions was the prescription of inappropriately high doses of the correct drug for the patient (43.6%). Technical knowledge deficiencies accounted for less than 25% of all cases.

title: Lethal complications of typhoid-cholera-vaccination. (Case report and review of the literature).
text: Simultaneous administration of typhoid and cholera vaccines resulted in death due to anaphylactic or endotoxic shock in a 36-year-old male. At autopsy, characteristic features of shock were observed, along with chronic interstitial myocarditis. Additionally, fresh histiocytic and lymphocytic nodules were found in the liver, heart, and meninges. A review of the literature revealed that debilitated individuals (those with emaciation, stress, or cold) are at an increased risk of fatal complications following parenteral typhoid vaccinations, and most fatalities occurred in individuals with pre-existing cardiovascular problems, such as the case presented here. Cardiac failure, Landry's paralysis, renal failure, and disturbances of skin, joints, and intestines may also occur, but are usually not fatal. The patients in this case had several conditions that exacerbated the situation and led to a lethal outcome. The review of this case and the subsequent discussion highlight the importance of only administering parenteral typhoid vaccines to healthy individuals. It is hoped that presenting this information will help prevent similar fatalities in the future.

title: Functional genomics and proteomics approaches to study the ERBB network in cancer.
text: Advances in functional genomics and proteomics have significantly expanded the scope of biomedical research. The near-complete sequencing of the human genome has revealed the intricate complexity of gene regulation and provided new insights into the mechanisms underlying biological processes. The development of cutting-edge technologies, such as RNA interference (RNAi) and protein arrays, has enabled researchers to gather comprehensive data on gene function beyond single gene analysis. In addition, systems biology approaches, which integrate qualitative and quantitative data on the components of biological processes, are increasingly being used to model these processes, predict the effects of perturbations, and refine these models through experimental validation. Here, we explore the potential of applying functional genomics and proteomics to the ERBB family of growth-factor receptors, which play a crucial role in cancer signaling networks, to gain a deeper understanding of the signaling network and its impact on cancer.

title: Evaluation of spatial filters to create smoothed maps of health data.
text: Spatial filters have been employed as a straightforward and intuitive method for creating smoothed disease maps. Using birth weight data from New York State in 1994 and 1995, we compare the effectiveness of traditional filter types with fixed geographical sizes against filters with constant or nearly constant population sizes. The latter are more suitable for mapping diseases in areas with varying population densities, such as New York State. We assess the merits of different population sizes for the filter, the degree of smoothing, the ability to detect genuine spatial patterns, and the ability to reduce random spatial noise.

title: Glucose tolerance and blood pressure: long term follow up in middle aged men.
text:
Objective: To investigate the relationship between glucose tolerance and the development of hypertension in a group of middle-aged men over a 13-year period.
Design: Retrospective analysis of data from a health check-up conducted in the late 1960s and follow-up examinations in 1979 and 1986.
Setting: Institute of Occupational Health, Helsinki, Finland, and the second department of medicine, University of Helsinki.
Subjects: In total, 3490 men born between 1919 and 1934 participated in the health check-up in the late 1960s. Of these, 1815 clinically healthy men were entered into a primary prevention trial for cardiovascular disease in 1974, and 1222 were considered at high risk of cardiovascular disease based on clinical examination.
Interventions: By 1979, 103 men were taking antihypertensive drugs, and by 1986, 131 were taking antihypertensive drugs and 12 were taking drugs for hyperglycaemia.
Main Outcome Measures: Blood glucose concentration one hour after a glucose load, blood pressure, and body weight were measured in 1968, 1974, and 1979. In 1986, blood pressure and body weight were recorded.
Results: Men who were hypertensive in 1986 had significantly higher blood pressures (p < 0.0001) and significantly higher blood glucose concentrations one hour after a glucose load at all examinations compared to those who were normotensive in 1986. Regression analysis showed that the higher the blood glucose concentration after a glucose load in 1968, the higher the blood pressure during the following years. Men in the second and third tertiles of blood glucose concentration in 1968 had a significantly higher risk of developing hypertension (odds ratio 1.71, 95% confidence interval 1.05 to 2.77) compared to those below the first tertile.
Conclusion: Men who developed hypertension tended to have shown an increased intolerance to glucose up to 18 years before the clinical manifestation of their disorder. Blood glucose concentration one hour after a glucose load was an independent predictor of future hypertension.

title: At the gates of death.
text: Apoptosis that occurs through the mitochondrial pathway involves the permeabilization of the outer mitochondrial membrane (MOMP), which releases cytochrome c and other proteins from the intermembrane space. This crucial step is regulated and mediated by proteins from the Bcl-2 family. Proapoptotic proteins like Bax and Bak are necessary for MOMP, while antiapoptotic Bcl-2 proteins, including Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1, and others, prevent MOMP. Recent research has shown that different proapoptotic BH3-only proteins can disrupt the function of antiapoptotic Bcl-2 members or activate Bax and Bak, leading to MOMP and apoptosis. An emerging view, proposed by Certo et al. in this issue of Cancer Cell, suggests that these interactions result in MOMP and apoptosis.

title: Structure of human RNase H1 complexed with an RNA/DNA hybrid: insight into HIV reverse transcription.
text: In this study, we present the crystal structures of human RNase H1 complexed with both RNA and DNA substrates. In contrast to the RNase H1 enzyme from Bacillus halodurans, the human enzyme possesses a basic protrusion that forms a DNA-binding channel and, in conjunction with the conserved phosphate-binding pocket, confers specificity for the B form and 2'-deoxy DNA substrates. The RNA strand is recognized by four consecutive 2'-OH groups, which are cleaved by a two-metal ion mechanism. Although RNase H1 has a net positive charge, the substrate interface is neutral to acidic in character, which is thought to contribute to the enzyme's catalytic specificity. The positions of the scissile phosphate and the two catalytic metal ions are interdependent and highly coupled. Furthermore, modeling of HIV reverse transcriptase (RT) with RNA/DNA in its RNase H active site suggests that the substrate cannot simultaneously occupy the polymerase active site and must undergo a conformational change to toggle between the two catalytic centers. The region that accommodates this conformational change represents a potential target for the development of HIV-specific inhibitors.

title: A diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging study of brain tissue from patients with migraine.
text:
Objective:
To assess the extent of pathological damage to normal appearing brain tissue (NABT) in patients with migraine using diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging (DT-MRI).
Methods:
DT-MRI scans of the brain were obtained from 34 patients with migraine and 17 sex and age-matched healthy volunteers. Mean diffusivity (MD) and fractional anisotropy (FA) histograms of the NABT were obtained from all subjects, and the peak heights and average NABT MD and FA were measured. When present, average MD and FA values of T2 visible lesions were also measured.
Results:
Compared to healthy volunteers, patients with migraine had lower peak heights of MD histograms of the NABT (p=0.02). No significant differences were found in FA histogram derived metrics between migraine patients and healthy subjects. No significant differences were found in MD and FA histogram derived metrics between migraine patients with and without brain MRI lesions, and between patients with and without aura.

Conclusions:
This study suggests that, although brain damage may extend beyond T2 weighted abnormalities in patients with migraine, the severity of these "occult" changes is relatively mild compared to other diseases associated with white matter abnormality.

title: Determination of chloramphenicol residues in milk by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay: improvement by biotin-streptavidin-amplified system.
text: A novel biotin-streptavidin amplified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (BA-ELISA) method was developed for the detection of chloramphenicol residues in milk. The biotin-streptavidin system was employed to enhance the sensitivity of the assay, resulting in a detection limit of 0.042 +/- 0.006 ng/mL, which is 8-fold more sensitive than the traditional competitive ELISA using the same antibody and coating antigen. The amplification mechanism of the biotin-streptavidin system and the key factors influencing sensitivity were investigated. This method was successfully applied to milk samples using a simple and rapid extraction procedure, resulting in good recoveries (85.66-109.67%). The results suggest that the biotin-streptavidin system may be a valuable tool for the specific detection of trace veterinary drug residues and could be widely used for routine monitoring of food samples.

title: Wedelolactone exhibits anti-fibrotic effects on human hepatic stellate cell line LX-2.
text:
Wedelolactone, a major coumarin derived from Eclipta prostrata, has been shown to prevent liver damage. However, the anti-fibrotic effects of wedelolactone on activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) remain unexplored. To investigate the anti-fibrotic effects of wedelolactone and its underlying mechanisms, we employed MTT assay, Hoechst staining, real-time quantitative PCR, and western blot analysis on the LX-2 HSC line.
Our results demonstrated that wedelolactone exhibited a time- and dose-dependent reduction in the cellular viability of LX-2 cells. Additionally, the expressions of collagen I and α-smooth muscle actin, two biomarkers of LX-2 activation, were significantly decreased after treatment with wedelolactone. Furthermore, wedelolactone-induced apoptosis in LX-2 cells was accompanied by a decrease in the expression of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 and an increase in the expression of pro-apoptotic Bax.
Furthermore, our findings showed that wedelolactone up-regulated the phosphorylated status of extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), but not p38. Moreover, wedelolactone significantly repressed the level of phosphorylated inhibitor of nuclear factor κB (IκB) and p65 in the nucleus, even in the presence of tumor necrosis factor-α stimulation.
In conclusion, our study demonstrates that wedelolactone can significantly inhibit the activation of LX-2 cells through mechanisms involving inducing Bcl-2 family involved apoptosis, up-regulating phosphorylated status of ERK and JNK expressions, and inhibiting NF-κB mediated activity. These findings suggest that wedelolactone may serve as a useful tool for the prevention and treatment of hepatic fibrosis.

title: Adipose stem cells originate from perivascular cells.
text: Recent research has revealed that adipose tissues contain a rich supply of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). However, the origin and location of these stem cells within adipose tissue remain unknown, hindering their further purification and study. To investigate the origins of adipose stem cells, we used transgenic mice that express green fluorescent protein (GFP) under the control of the α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) gene. We harvested adipose stromal cells (ASCs) from these mice and sorted them into GFP-positive and GFP-negative cells using flow cytometry. We then evaluated the pluripotent ability of these cells using multilineage differentiation tests. Immunofluorescent staining was used to identify the GFP-positive cells and assess their expression of α-SMA and platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGF-Rβ). We found that all GFP-positive cells in adipose tissue were located near blood vessels, while the GFP-negative cells could only differentiate in an adipogenic direction. The GFP-positive cells maintained expression of α-SMA during multilineage differentiation and could promote the vascularization of endothelial cells in both in vitro and in vivo cultures. Our findings suggest that adipose stem cells originate from perivascular cells in adipose tissue and gather around blood vessels.

title: Interferon alpha and zidovudine therapy in adult T-cell leukaemia lymphoma: response and outcome in 15 patients.
text: Adult T-cell leukemia-lymphoma (ATLL) is a severe disease caused by the human T-lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-I), with a poor prognosis. While responses to interferon alpha (IFN-alpha) and zidovudine (AZT) have been documented, long-term follow-up data are limited. We treated 15 ATLL patients with IFN and AZT, with promising results. The main findings included organomegaly (14 patients), skin lesions (10 patients), elevated white blood cell count (11 patients), and hypercalcaemia (9 patients). Eleven patients had previously received chemotherapy, and one patient had undergone an autograft. At the time of the study, seven patients had progressive disease, while eight patients were in partial or complete clinical remission. Responses (PR) lasting 2-44 months were observed in 67% of patients, while 26% did not respond (NR). One patient was not evaluable. Hypercalcaemia was a predictor of poor outcome, but the difference was not statistically significant. Eight of the 15 patients have died within 3-41 months of diagnosis, with a median survival time of 18 months. Of the non-responder patients (NR), survival ranged from 4-20 months, while six patients who achieved a PR are still alive 8-82 months after diagnosis. The difference in survival between the NR and PR groups was statistically significant (P = 0.002). In conclusion, the combination of IFN and AZT improves the outcome of ATLL patients and helps maintain responses.

title: Replisome stalling and stabilization at CGG repeats, which are responsible for chromosomal fragility
text: Expanded CGG repeats in the human genome are associated with chromosomal fragility and hereditary neurological disorders. In primate cells and yeast, replication forks stall at CGG repeats in a length-dependent manner, hindering the progression of DNA replication. Two proteins, Tof1 and Mrc1 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, play a crucial role in facilitating replication fork progression through CGG repeats. Interestingly, Mrc1's fork-stabilizing function does not rely on its checkpoint activity, suggesting that chromosomal fragility may arise when stalled forks at expanded CGG repeats evade the S-phase checkpoint.

title: Direct reprogramming of fibroblasts into neural stem cells by defined factors.
text: Recent research has revealed that specific combinations of transcription factors can directly convert differentiated somatic cells into other cell types without passing through a pluripotent state. However, the resulting cells have limited potential for use in certain applications due to their restricted proliferative and lineage potential. In this study, we demonstrate that a combination of transcription factors (Brn4/Pou3f4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc, and E47/Tcf3) can induce mouse fibroblasts to directly acquire a neural stem cell identity, which we term induced neural stem cells (iNSCs). The reprogramming process is gradual, resulting in the silencing of the donor transcriptional program over time. iNSCs exhibit characteristics similar to those of wild-type neural stem cells, including cell morphology, gene expression, epigenetic features, differentiation potential, and self-renewing capacity. These findings suggest that differentiated cells can be directly reprogrammed into specific somatic stem cell types using defined sets of transcription factors, expanding the scope of their potential applications.

title: Epigenetics in lung fibrosis: from pathobiology to treatment perspective.
text:
The purpose of this review is to elucidate the role of epigenetics in the development and progression of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a fatal disease characterized by limited treatment options and extensive gene expression changes in the lung parenchyma. Multiple lines of evidence suggest that epigenetic factors play a crucial role in the dysregulation of gene expression in IPF lung tissue. Notably, risk factors associated with IPF, such as age, sex, cigarette smoke exposure, and genetic variants, have been shown to influence epigenetic marks in the lung. This review aims to summarize recent findings on the association of DNA methylation and histone modifications with the presence of disease and fibroproliferation in IPF lung tissue.
Recent studies have demonstrated widespread changes in DNA methylation patterns in IPF lung tissue, with a significant impact on gene expression. Moreover, genetic loci associated with IPF have been found to contain differentially methylated regions, suggesting a complex interplay between genetic and epigenetic factors in the dysregulation of gene expression in IPF lung.
In conclusion, while the field of epigenetics in IPF is still in its early stages, the potential for the use of epigenetic marks as biomarkers and therapeutic targets is substantial. Further research in this area may lead to improved prognostication and treatment of this fatal disease.

title: Novel roles for KLF1 in erythropoiesis revealed by mRNA-seq.
text: KLF1 (previously known as EKLF), a transcription factor, regulates the development of erythroid cells from bi-potent progenitor cells by activating a diverse set of genes through transcriptional mechanisms. Mice lacking KLF1 die in utero before E15 due to severe anemia resulting from inadequate expression of genes involved in hemoglobin production, cell membrane and cytoskeletal integrity, and cell cycle regulation. Recently, we identified the full range of KLF1 binding sites in vivo by performing KLF1 ChIP-seq on primary erythroid tissue (E14.5 fetal liver). In this study, we investigate the KLF1-dependent erythroid transcriptome by comparing mRNA-seq data from Klf1(+/+) and Klf1(-/-) erythroid tissue. This approach revealed novel target genes that could not be identified through traditional microarray technology, providing new insights into KLF1's function as a transcriptional activator. We identify a cis-regulatory module bound by KLF1, GATA1, TAL1, and EP300 that regulates a core set of erythroid genes. Additionally, we describe a novel set of erythroid-specific promoters that drive high-level expression of otherwise ubiquitously expressed genes in erythroid cells. Our study also identifies two novel long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) that are dynamically expressed during erythroid differentiation, and reveals a role for KLF1 in directing apoptotic gene expression to drive the terminal stages of erythroid maturation.

title: Self-assembling peptides optimize the post-traumatic milieu and synergistically enhance the effects of neural stem cell therapy after cervical spinal cord injury.
text:
INTRODUCTION:
After a spinal cord injury (SCI), the hostile environment can hinder the effectiveness of regenerative therapies. We hypothesized that optimizing this environment with QL6 self-assembling peptides (SAPs) before transplanting neural precursor cells (NPCs) would enhance their survival, differentiation, and functional recovery.
METHODS:
We conducted a study in which 90 Wistar rats received a clip-compression SCI at C7. The animals were then randomized into five groups: NPCs, SAPs, NPCs + SAPs, vehicle, and sham. SAPs were injected into the spinal cord 1 day after injury, and NPCs were injected 14 days later. The animals received growth factors over a period of 7 days and were immunosuppressed. The rats were sacrificed at 4 weeks, and sections of the cervical spinal cord were prepared for immunohistochemistry. Neurological function was assessed weekly for 8 weeks using a battery of behavioral tests. At 9 weeks post-SCI, the corticospinal tract was evaluated using fiber-tracking in a second study arm.
RESULTS:
Our results showed that SAP-treated animals had significantly more surviving NPCs that differentiated into neurons and oligodendrocytes more effectively than controls. SAPs alone or in combination with NPCs resulted in smaller intramedullary cysts and larger volumes of preserved tissue compared to other groups. The combined treatment group showed reduced astrogliosis and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan deposition. Synaptic connectivity was increased in the NPC and combined treatment groups. Behavioral outcomes improved with combinatorial treatment, and corticospinal tract preservation was also observed.
CONCLUSION:
Our findings suggest that injecting SAPs after SCI enhances the survival, integration, and differentiation of NPCs and improves functional recovery. This approach has the potential to improve the efficacy of regenerative therapies for spinal cord injuries. By creating a supportive environment for repair and regeneration, SAPs can help optimize the effects of NPC transplantation, leading to better outcomes for individuals with spinal cord injuries.

title: A direct role for IFN-gamma in regulation of Th1 cell development.
text: IL-12 and IFN-gamma have been shown to play a crucial role in the differentiation of CD4 cells to a Th1 phenotype. While IL-12 has been identified as a major cytokine in this process, the role of IFN-gamma is controversial. To investigate the interrelationship between IL-12 and IFN-gamma in promoting Th1 responses, we used naive CD4 cells reactive with pigeon cytochrome c from TCR transgenics and memory CD4 cells derived by in vivo priming with KLH. We found that without exogenous IL-12 or IFN-gamma, primary and memory effectors induced by Ag or anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 produced variable levels of IL-2 and IFN-gamma. The level of IFN-gamma produced by effectors correlated with the endogenous IFN-gamma produced in primary cultures, and anti-IFN-gamma largely inhibited the development of effectors producing IFN-gamma. Interestingly, with optimal TCR stimulation and costimulation, endogenous IFN-gamma, without IL-12, was sufficient to elicit Th1 cells via an autocrine mechanism. However, when stimulation was suboptimal, exogenous rIFN-gamma or rIL-12 was required for Th1 development, with rIL-12 being more effective than rIFN-gamma. The synergistic actions of both cytokines were found to be necessary for optimal Th1 development. Our findings suggest that the extent of differentiation to a Th1 phenotype may depend on the availability of both APC-derived IL-12 and autocrine IFN-gamma, which are influenced by the strength of T cell stimulation.

title: Neuregulin 1 promotes excitatory synapse development and function in GABAergic interneurons.
text: Neuregulin 1 (NRG1) and its receptor ErbB4 have been identified as susceptibility genes for schizophrenia, but the underlying mechanisms of their dysfunction are not well understood. Although ErbB4 is enriched in GABAergic interneurons, the role of NRG1 in excitatory synapse formation in these neurons is poorly understood. Our study found that NRG1 increases the number and size of PSD-95 puncta and the frequency and amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) in GABAergic interneurons, suggesting that NRG1 promotes the formation of new synapses and strengthens existing ones. In contrast, NRG1 treatment had no effect on excitatory synapses in glutamatergic neurons, indicating that its synaptogenic effect is specific to GABAergic interneurons. Treatment with ecto-ErbB4, a protein that mimics the activity of ErbB4, diminished both the number and size of excitatory synapses, suggesting that endogenous NRG1 may be essential for basal synapse formation. Our findings suggest that NRG1 may stabilize PSD-95 in a manner that requires the tyrosine kinase activity of ErbB4. Additionally, deletion of ErbB4 in parvalbumin-positive interneurons led to reduced frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs, providing in vivo evidence that ErbB4 is important in excitatory synaptogenesis in interneurons. Together, our findings provide insight into the potential pathological mechanism of schizophrenia, which is associated with the dysfunction of the GABAergic system.

title: Tolerance rather than immunity protects from Helicobacter pylori-induced gastric preneoplasia.
text:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Chronic infection with the bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori is a major risk factor for gastric disorders, including chronic gastritis and gastric adenocarcinoma. However, not all infected individuals will develop overt disease, with some remaining asymptomatic despite lifelong colonization. This study aimed to investigate the factors that contribute to differential susceptibility to H pylori infection across and within populations.
METHODS: The authors established a C57BL/6 mouse model of H pylori infection using a strain that can deliver the virulence factor cytotoxin-associated gene A (CagA) into host cells through the activity of a Cag-pathogenicity island-encoded type IV secretion system.
RESULTS: The study found that mice infected at 5-6 weeks of age with CagA(+)H pylori rapidly developed gastritis, gastric atrophy, epithelial hyperplasia, and metaplasia in a type IV secretion system-dependent manner. In contrast, mice infected during the neonatal period were protected from preneoplastic lesions, with this protection attributed to the development of H pylori-specific peripheral immunologic tolerance. This tolerance required transforming growth factor-β signaling and was mediated by long-lived, inducible regulatory T cells, which controlled the local CD4(+) T-cell responses that trigger premalignant transformation. The authors found that tolerance to H pylori developed in the neonatal period due to a biased ratio of T-regulatory to T-effector cells, and that prolonged low-dose exposure to antigen favored its development.
CONCLUSIONS: The study's findings suggest that the age at initial infection may play a crucial role in determining an individual's susceptibility to H pylori-associated disease manifestations. The use of a novel CagA(+)H pylori infection model allowed the authors to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the development of tolerance to H pylori, which may have implications for the prevention and treatment of gastric cancer.

title: Impaired mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and insulin resistance in aging: novel protective role of glutathione.
text:
The study investigated the role of glutathione (GSH) in the aging process and its impact on mitochondrial function, insulin resistance, and fasted oxidation of nonesterified fatty acids (NEFA). The research consisted of three experiments:
1. In aged mice (82 weeks old), the effect of naturally occurring GSH deficiency and its restoration on mitochondrial (13) C1 -palmitate oxidation and glucose metabolism was compared with young mice (22 weeks old).
2. In young mice (20 weeks old), the effect of GSH depletion on mitochondrial oxidation of (13) C1 -palmitate and glucose metabolism was studied.
3. The effect of GSH deficiency and its restoration on fasted NEFA oxidation and insulin resistance was studied in GSH-deficient elderly humans and compared with GSH-replete young humans.
The results showed that chronic GSH deficiency in old mice and elderly humans was associated with decreased fasted mitochondrial NEFA oxidation and insulin resistance, and these defects were reversed with GSH restoration. Acute depletion of GSH in young mice resulted in lower mitochondrial NEFA oxidation, but did not alter glucose metabolism. These data suggest that GSH is a novel regulator of mitochondrial NEFA oxidation and insulin resistance in aging. Chronic GSH deficiency promotes impaired NEFA oxidation and insulin resistance, and GSH restoration reverses these defects. Supplementing diets of elderly humans with cysteine and glycine to correct GSH deficiency could provide significant metabolic benefits.

title: Control of central and peripheral tolerance by Aire.
text: The negative selection of self-reactive thymocytes relies on the expression of tissue-specific antigens by medullary thymic epithelial cells. The protein autoimmune regulator (Aire) plays a crucial role in activating these antigens, and the absence of even one Aire-induced tissue-specific antigen in the thymus can lead to autoimmunity in the target organ. Recently, Aire protein has been detected in peripheral lymphoid organs, suggesting that peripheral Aire plays a complementary role in regulating tissue-specific antigens. In these peripheral sites, Aire regulates the expression of a distinct group of tissue-specific antigens compared to those expressed in the thymus. Additionally, transgenic antigen expression in extrathymic Aire-expressing cells (eTACs) can mediate deletional tolerance, but the immunological relevance of Aire-dependent, endogenous tissue-specific antigens remains to be determined.

title: Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism: A Trait Shared by Several Complex Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
text: The reproductive system's function is regulated by the gonadotropic axis, which is controlled by a complex neural network in the hypothalamus. This network's primary function is to regulate the secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). The development of this endocrine network is not complete at birth and goes through several stages of activation and inactivation to mature normally. After birth, the maturation of the GnRH network is controlled by a neurodevelopmental program that lasts until puberty. Disruptions to this program can lead to congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH), which is characterized by the absence of puberty. For many years, research has focused on the genetics of isolated CHH. However, recent advances in genomics have revealed genetic defects in rare syndromes in which CHH is associated with complex neurological problems. Here, we review the clinical features and genetic defects linked to these syndromic CHH, highlighting the connection between the ubiquitin pathway, synaptic proteins, and CHH, as well as unexpected mutations in genes encoding nucleolar proteins.

title: Elevated expression of miR-24-3p is a potentially adverse prognostic factor in colorectal adenocarcinoma.
text:
Objectives:
Several microRNAs (miRNAs) have been found to be aberrantly expressed in cancer, including colorectal adenocarcinoma. miR-24-3p, in particular, has been implicated in various cancer-related cellular processes, such as cell cycle control, cell growth, proliferation, and apoptosis. This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic and prognostic significance of miR-24-3p expression in colorectal adenocarcinoma.
Design and Methods:
Total RNA was isolated from 182 colorectal adenocarcinoma specimens and 86 paired non-cancerous colorectal mucosae. After polyadenylation of 2μg total RNA and reverse transcription into first-strand cDNA using an oligo-dT-adapter primer, miR-24-3p expression was quantified using an in-house-developed reverse-transcription real-time quantitative PCR method, based on the SYBR Green chemistry. SNORD43 (RNU43) was used as a reference gene.
Results:
miR-24-3p levels did not significantly differ between colorectal adenocarcinoma and non-cancerous colorectal mucosae, indicating that miR-24-3p expression cannot be used for diagnostic purposes. However, high miR-24-3p expression was found to predict poor disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) of colorectal adenocarcinoma patients. Multivariate Cox regression analysis confirmed that miR-24-3p overexpression is a significant predictor of relapse in colorectal adenocarcinoma and that its prognostic significance is independent of other established prognostic factors and treatment of patients. Of note, miR-24-3p overexpression retains its unfavorable prognostic value in the subgroup of patients with advanced yet locally restricted colorectal adenocarcinoma (T3) and in those without distant metastasis (M0). Moreover, miR-24-3p overexpression is a potentially unfavorable prognosticator for patients who were not treated with radiotherapy.
Conclusions:
Strong expression of miR-24-3p predicts poor DFS and OS of colorectal adenocarcinoma patients, independently of clinicopathological parameters that are currently used for prognosis in this human malignancy. These findings suggest that miR-24-3p may serve as a useful biomarker for prognosis in colorectal adenocarcinoma.

title: Reforming the health sector in developing countries: the central role of policy analysis.
text:
Policy analysis has long been a well-established discipline in industrialized countries, yet its application to developing nations has been limited, particularly in the health sector. Despite a recognized crisis in health systems and numerous recommendations for policy reforms, little attention has been paid to the actual process of implementing these reforms, including the actors involved, the processes required for change, and the context in which policies are developed. This paper argues that the focus on policy content often distracts from understanding the processes that prevent desired policy outcomes from materializing.
The paper is organized into four sections. The first section sets the stage by highlighting the shift from consensus to conflict in health policy and the need for a greater emphasis on policy analysis. The second section defines policy analysis and its significance. The third section examines what other disciplines have contributed to the field of policy analysis, providing a framework for analysis. Finally, the fourth section explores how policy analysis can not only analyze the policy process but also inform policy planning.

title: The processing of Holliday junctions by BLM and WRN helicases is regulated by p53.
text: BLM, WRN, and p53 are integral components of the homologous DNA recombination pathway. These proteins play a crucial role in unwinding Holliday junctions (HJ), a process that helps to prevent inappropriate homologous recombination during DNA replication. Our findings demonstrate that purified, recombinant p53 interacts with BLM and WRN helicases in vitro, and attenuates their ability to unwind synthetic HJ. Interestingly, the p53 248W mutant reduces the ability of both BLM and WRN to bind HJ, while the p53 273H mutant loses this ability. Furthermore, full-length p53 and a C-terminal polypeptide (residues 373-383) inhibit the BLM and WRN helicase activities, although phosphorylation at Ser(376) or Ser(378) completely abolishes this inhibition. After blocking DNA replication, Ser(15) phospho-p53, BLM, and RAD51 colocalize in nuclear foci at sites likely to contain DNA replication intermediates in cells. Our results provide evidence for a novel mechanism of p53-mediated regulation of DNA recombinational repair, involving post-translational modifications and functional protein-protein interactions with BLM and WRN DNA helicases.

title: Trim and fill: A simple funnel-plot-based method of testing and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis.
text: We investigate novel non-parametric techniques for estimating the number of unpublished studies that may have influenced the outcome of a meta-analysis. These methods are based on simple rank-based data augmentation techniques, which leverage funnel plots to formalize the estimation process. Our findings demonstrate that these techniques provide effective and relatively powerful tests for detecting publication bias. After adjusting for missing studies, we observe that the estimated overall effect size is generally accurate, and the coverage of the confidence intervals for the effect size is significantly improved, often recovering the nominal confidence levels. We apply the trim and fill method to existing meta-analyses in clinical trials and psychometrics to illustrate its utility.

title: Familial Barrett's esophagus associated with adenocarcinoma.
text: A family with six instances of Barrett's esophagus spanning three generations has been reported. Interestingly, this condition only affected males in the family, and there were three instances of associated adenocarcinomas. The inheritance pattern is consistent with an autosomal dominant model with nearly complete penetrance. This familial case of Barrett's esophagus with associated adenocarcinomas is notable when compared to other case reports in the literature.

title: Development of an insect model for the in vivo pathogenicity testing of yeasts.
text: In vivo assays to determine the relative pathogenicity of yeast isolates have traditionally relied on the use of mammalian species. The present study aimed to investigate the potential of using the insect Galleria mellonella as a model system for in vivo pathogenicity testing. The haemolymph of G. mellonella larvae was inoculated with PBS containing different concentrations of stationary phase yeasts of the genus Candida via injection at the last pro-leg. The larvae were then incubated at 30 degrees C for 72 hours. The results demonstrated that G. mellonella is susceptible to infection and killing by both pathogenic Candida species, including Candida albicans, and a range of other Candida species. However, the larvae were less susceptible to infection and killing by the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The kill kinetics for larvae inoculated with clinical and laboratory isolates of C. albicans indicated that the former class of isolates were more pathogenic. This study suggests that G. mellonella may be employed as a model system to evaluate the relative pathogenicity of a range of Candida species, and may potentially reduce the need for mammalian testing while minimizing animal suffering.

title: Use of TLS parameters to model anisotropic displacements in macromolecular refinement.
text: An essential aspect of macromolecular refinement is selecting model parameters that accurately describe experimental data while maintaining a reasonable ratio of data to parameters. This is particularly crucial when it comes to choosing atomic displacement parameters, as the transition from individual isotropic to individual anisotropic refinement involves a sixfold increase in the number of required parameters. To reduce the number of refinement parameters, collective variables can be used instead of individual atomic variables, and one of the simplest examples of this is the TLS (Translation, Lipulation, and Screw-rotation) parameterization for describing the translational, librational, and rotational displacements of a pseudo-rigid body. This article describes the implementation of TLS parameterization in the macromolecular refinement program REFMAC. The derivatives of the residual with respect to the TLS parameters are expanded in terms of the derivatives with respect to individual anisotropic U values, which are calculated using a fast Fourier transform technique. As a result, TLS refinement is fast and can be performed routinely. Examples of TLS refinement are provided for glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) and a transcription activator GerE, for which there is data available only to 2.0 Å resolution, making individual anisotropic refinement impractical. GAPDH was refined with one to four TLS groups in the asymmetric unit, while GerE was refined with six TLS groups. In both cases, the inclusion of TLS parameters led to improved refinement statistics, including an increase in R and free R values of several percent. Additionally, GAPDH and GerE have two and six molecules in the asymmetric unit, respectively, and the displacement parameters differ significantly between molecules. The TLS parameterization effectively accounts for these differences, resulting in residual local displacements that are similar between molecules and can be subjected to NCS restraints.

title: Sequence features surrounding the translation initiation sites assigned on the genome sequence of Synechocystis sp. strain PCC6803 by amino-terminal protein sequencing.
text: To investigate the sequence features surrounding translation initiation sites on the genome of Synechocystis sp. strain 6803, total proteins were separated by two-dimensional electrophoresis, and the amino-terminal sequences of the most abundant protein spots were determined. By comparing the determined amino-terminal sequences with the entire genome sequence, the translation initiation sites of 72 proteins were successfully identified. The sequence features found near the initiation sites included: (1) In addition to the commonly used initiation codons ATG, GTG, and TTG, evidence was obtained that the rare codon ATT was also used. (2) The core sequences (GAGG, GGAG, and AGGA) of the Shine-Dalgarno sequence were identified in 48.6% of the 35 initiation sites preceding them. (3) A specific sequence surrounding the initiation codons, consisting of 5'-YY[...]R-3', where Y and R represent pyrimidine and purine nucleotides, respectively, and three dots represent the initiation codons, was found. This study's findings will improve gene-finding software, and the approach used can be applied to comprehensively analyze the expression profiles of cellular proteins.

title: Deregulated DNA polymerase beta induces chromosome instability and tumorigenesis.
text: To achieve the genetic alterations characteristic of cancer, tumor cells must undergo increased mutability due to a malfunction of the network of genome stability systems, such as cell cycle arrest, DNA repair, and high accuracy of DNA synthesis during DNA replication. A common genetic change observed in many types of solid tumors is numeric chromosomal imbalance, or aneuploidy. Our study reveals that ectopic expression of DNA polymerase beta, an error-prone enzyme frequently over-regulated in human tumors, leads to aneuploidy, abnormal centrosome localization of the gamma-tubulin protein during mitosis, a weakened mitotic checkpoint, and promotion of tumorigenesis in nude immunodeficient mice. These findings suggest that altered polymerase beta expression can induce significant genetic changes associated with a malignant phenotype.

title: Combinatorial signaling by Sonic hedgehog and Wnt family members induces myogenic bHLH gene expression in the somite.
text: In our previous work, we showed that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex can synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in undetermined somites. In this study, we investigate the role of Sonic hedgehog (Shh) and Wnt family members in myogenesis. We find that Shh, which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in the dorsal regions of the neural tube, can mimic the muscle-inducing activity of these tissues. In combination, Shh and either Wnt-1 or Wnt-3 are sufficient to induce myogenesis in somitic tissue in vitro. Based on these findings, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.

title: Advances in osteoclast biology: old findings and new insights from mouse models
text: The preservation of adequate bone mass relies on the controlled and timely removal of old, damaged bone through a specialized process carried out by the multinucleated osteoclast. Over the past 15 years, significant progress has been made in understanding the origins, differentiation pathways, and activation stages involved in normal osteoclast function. This knowledge has primarily come from the development and analysis of genetically modified mouse models, which have revealed important insights into the mechanisms underlying osteoclast function. For example, these models have shown that the RANK-RANKL-OPG system plays a central role in osteoclastogenesis, and have provided details on the ion transport and cellular attachment mechanisms involved in resorptive activity. Additionally, the importance of matrix-degrading enzymes in maintaining bone integrity has been highlighted. This review focuses on the key observations in osteoclast biology derived from genetic mouse models, and highlights emerging concepts that suggest how the osteoclast may contribute to maintaining adequate bone mass and integrity throughout life.

title: DNA methylation in embryonic stem cells.
text: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) are unique, self-renewing cells with the ability to differentiate into any cell type in the body. These cells hold great promise for applications such as cell therapy, drug development, disease modeling, and the study of cellular differentiation. Understanding the intricate interplay between epigenetics, genetics, and gene expression in the control of pluripotency and differentiation is crucial for unlocking the full potential of ESCs. One of the most well-known epigenetic mechanisms is DNA methylation, which plays a crucial role in regulating gene expression. This phenomenon is particularly evident in imprinted genes and X-chromosome inactivation, where DNA methylation of promoter regions leads to repression of gene expression. Interestingly, studies have shown that the differential methylation of pluripotence-associated genes such as Nanog and Oct4/Pou5f1 is observed between pluripotent and differentiated cells. It is clear that tight regulation of DNA methylation is essential for normal development. As more associations between aberrant DNA methylation and disease are reported, the demand for high-throughput approaches for DNA methylation analysis has increased. In this article, we will highlight these methods and discuss recent DNA methylation studies on ESCs.

title: Reserves, functional, immunoregulatory, and cytogenetic properties of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the impact of myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) on the bone marrow (BM) stroma, specifically the mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). The study compared the reserves, functional properties, and cytogenetic characteristics of MSCs in patients with de novo MDS (n = 13) to those in normal controls (n = 20). The study found that:
1. The number of MSCs and their differentiation potential towards adipocytes, chondrocytes, and osteoblasts were similar between patient and normal MSCs.
2. Patient MSCs did not show any abnormalities in the production of proinflammatory or growth-promoting cytokines.
3. Patient MSCs did not harbor the cytogenetic abnormalities present in hematopoietic cells.
4. Occasional patient and normal MSC cultures developed irrelevant chromosomal alterations (trisomies 5 and 7) with uncertain pathophysiologic significance.
5. Compared to controls, patient MSCs displayed impaired proliferative and clonogenic potential with passages, which might represent a nonspecific abnormality associated with the chronic inflammatory process present in patients' BM.

The study suggests that BM MSCs from MDS patients do not belong to the abnormal clone and do not primarily contribute to the inflammatory marrow microenvironment. These findings imply that MSCs may play a less significant role in the pathophysiology of MDS than previously thought.

title: Symmetric signalling within asymmetric dimers of the Staphylococcus aureus receptor histidine kinase AgrC.
text: The virulence of Staphylococcus aureus is largely regulated by the accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum-sensing system, which involves the AgrC receptor histidine kinase. When the AgrC receptor detects its autoinducing peptide (AIP) ligand, it generates an intracellular signal that leads to the secretion of virulence factors. Although the agr system has been well-studied, the mechanism of AgrC activation remains poorly understood. Using co-immunoprecipitation analysis and intermolecular complementation of receptor mutants, we found that AgrC forms ligand-independent dimers that undergo trans-autophosphorylation upon interaction with AIP. Surprisingly, addition of specific AIPs to AgrC mutant dimers with only one functional sensor domain resulted in symmetric activation of both kinase domains, regardless of the sensor asymmetry. Additionally, mutant dimers containing one constitutive protomer showed ligand-independent activity, regardless of which protomer was kinase deficient. These findings suggest that signaling through either individual AgrC protomer leads to symmetric activation of both kinase domains, which may be an important mechanism for dimeric quorum-sensing receptors to rapidly respond to signals upon detection.

title: Attachment of the ubiquitin-related protein Urm1p to the antioxidant protein Ahp1p.
text: Urm1p is a protein that plays a crucial role in post-translational modification of other proteins by ubiquitination. The Urm1p-mediated ubiquitination process has been linked to various cellular processes, including the budding process and nutrient sensing. In this study, we identified the first in vivo target of the urmylation pathway, which is the antioxidant protein Ahp1p. The attachment of Urm1p to Ahp1p requires the E1 enzyme Uba4p, which is a crucial component of the urmylation pathway. Interestingly, loss of urmylation pathway components leads to sensitivity to thiol-specific oxidants, suggesting that urmylation plays a role in an oxidative stress response. Moreover, treatment of cells with thiol-specific oxidants affects the abundance of Ahp1p-Urm1p conjugates, further supporting the idea that the conjugation of Urm1p to Ahp1p regulates the function of Ahp1p in antioxidant stress response in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

title: Sulfasalazine in the treatment of spondylarthropathy. A randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of sulfasalazine (SSZ) in the treatment of spondylarthropathy.
Methods: This was a 6-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter study involving patients with spondylarthropathy who had not responded to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Participants were randomly assigned to receive either SSZ (3 g/day) or placebo. The primary outcome measures were assessed by both physicians and patients, including pain, morning stiffness, and overall disease activity. Secondary outcomes included laboratory markers of inflammation and the number of inflamed joints.
Results: Of the 351 enrolled patients, 263 (75%) completed the 6-month treatment period. The withdrawal rates were 35 (20%) and 53 (30%) in the placebo and SSZ groups, respectively. In the intent-to-treat analysis, the between-group difference in primary outcome variables was statistically significant only for the patient's overall assessment of disease activity, with 60% of SSZ-treated patients improving by at least 1 point on a 5-point scale, compared to 44% of placebo-treated patients. Laboratory markers of inflammation also showed a statistically significant change in favor of SSZ.
