In uncontrolled studies, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV) was found to be useful in avoiding endotracheal intubation in patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF) caused by severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). To further investigate this, we conducted a prospective, randomized study comparing standard treatment plus NPPV delivered through a face mask to standard treatment alone in patients with severe CAP and ARF.
Patients meeting the American Thoracic Society criteria for severe CAP were included if they had ARF (refractory hypoxemia and/or hypercapnia with acidosis). Exclusion criteria included severe hemodynamic instability, requirement for emergent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, home mechanical ventilation or oxygen long-term supplementation, concomitant severe disease with a low expectation of life, inability to expectorate, or contraindications to the use of the mask. Fifty-six consecutive patients (28 in each arm) were enrolled, and the two groups were similar at study entry. The use of NPPV was well tolerated, safe, and associated with a significant reduction in respiratory rate, need for endotracheal intubation (21% versus 50%; p = 0.03), and duration of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (1.8 ± 0.7 d versus 6 ± 1.8 d; p = 0.04). The two groups had a similar intensity of nursing care workload, time interval from study entry to endotracheal intubation, duration of hospitalization, and hospital mortality. Among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), those randomized to NPPV had a lower intensity of nursing care workload (p = 0.04) and improved 2-mo survival (88.9% versus 37.5%; p = 0.05). We conclude that in selected patients with ARF caused by severe CAP, NPPV was associated with a significant reduction in the rate of endotracheal intubation and duration of ICU stay. A 2-mo survival advantage was seen in patients with COPD.

title: Smallest angiosperm genomes found in lentibulariaceae, with chromosomes of bacterial size.
text: Nuclear holoploid genome sizes (C-values) have been estimated to exhibit a vast range of variation among angiosperms, with the smallest C-value of 157 Mbp recorded in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, recent studies have revealed that three taxa within the carnivorous family Lentibulariaceae possess significantly smaller genome sizes: Genlisea margaretae with a C-value of 63 Mbp, G. aurea with a C-value of 64 Mbp, and Utricularia gibba with a C-value of 88 Mbp. Notably, the smallest mitotic anaphase chromatids in G. aurea have a size of approximately 2.1 Mbp, which is comparable to that of bacteria (NB: E. coli has a genome size of approximately 4 Mbp). Additionally, several Utricularia species have genome sizes that are either similar to or lower than those of A. thaliana, indicating a range of genome sizes among this group. The highest C-value recorded among Lentibulariaceae was found in Genlisea hispidula with a C-value of 1510 Mbp, resulting in approximately 24-fold variation among Genlisea and the Lentibulariaceae. These findings suggest that genome miniaturization may be a common phenomenon in angiosperms, particularly in plants with terminal positions in the eudicot phylogeny, such as Genlisea and Utricularia. Furthermore, the Genlisea-Utricularia clade exhibits one of the highest mutational rates in several genomic regions among angiosperms, which may be linked to specialized patterns of genome evolution. In contrast, the C-values in the sister group Pinguicula vary only 1.7-fold from 487 to 829 Mbp, indicating a much lower level of genome variation in this group.

title: Parasite multiplication potential and the severity of Falciparum malaria.
text: Researchers compared the multiplication rates and invasiveness of Plasmodium falciparum parasites isolated from adult Thai patients hospitalized with uncomplicated malaria (n=34) and those from individuals with severe malaria (n=42). To simulate severe malaria and account for host factors, in vitro cultures were adjusted to 1% parasitemia using the same red blood cell donor. The study found that P. falciparum isolates from patients with severe malaria had significantly higher initial cycle multiplication rates in vitro compared to those from uncomplicated malaria (median [95% CI]: 8.3 [7.1-10.5] vs. 2.8 [1.7-3.9]; P<0.001). Additionally, parasites causing severe malaria showed unrestricted invasion of red blood cells, whereas those from uncomplicated malaria were restricted to a geometric mean of 40 (31%-53%) of red blood cells. Notably, P. falciparum parasites causing severe malaria were less selective and multiplied more at higher parasitemias than those causing uncomplicated malaria.

title: PHD3-dependent hydroxylation of HCLK2 promotes the DNA damage response.
text: The DNA damage response (DDR) is a complex regulatory network crucial for maintaining genome integrity. Post-translational modifications are widely employed to control the flow of signals with precise spatiotemporal regulation, but the DDR's response to environmental cues, such as changes in oxygen levels, remains poorly understood. We discovered that an essential component of the ATR/CHK1 signaling pathway, the human homolog of the Caenorhabditis elegans biological clock protein CLK-2 (HCLK2), interacts with and is hydroxylated by prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 3 (PHD3). HCLK2 hydroxylation is necessary for its interaction with ATR and the subsequent activation of ATR/CHK1/p53. Inhibiting PHD3, either using a pan-hydroxylase inhibitor (DMOG) or by reducing oxygen levels, prevents the activation of the ATR/CHK1/p53 pathway and reduces apoptosis induced by DNA damage. Consistently, mice lacking PHD3 are resistant to the effects of ionizing radiation and have decreased thymic apoptosis, a marker of genomic integrity. Our identification of HCLK2 as a PHD3 substrate reveals the mechanism by which hypoxia inhibits the DDR, suggesting that hydroxylation of HCLK2 may be a potential therapeutic target for regulating the ATR/CHK1/p53 pathway.

title: Economic implications of nighttime attending intensivist coverage in a medical intensive care unit.
text:
Objective: To assess the financial implications of changing the intensive care unit (ICU) staffing model from on-demand presence to mandatory 24-hour in-house critical care specialist presence.
Design: A pre-post comparison was conducted among prospectively assessed cohorts of patients admitted to our medical ICU over a one-year period, before and after the staffing model change. Data were stratified by Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation III (APACHE III) quartile and whether patients were admitted during the day or night. Costs were modeled using a generalized linear model with log-link and γ-distributed errors.
Setting: A large academic center in the Midwest.
Patients: All patients admitted to the adult medical ICU on or after January 1, 2005 and discharged on or before December 31, 2006, excluding those receiving care under both staffing models.
Intervention: Changing the ICU staffing model from on-demand presence to mandatory 24-hour in-house critical care specialist presence.
Measurements and Main Results: Total cost estimates of hospitalization were calculated for each patient from admission to discharge. Adjusted mean total cost estimates were 61% lower in the post period compared to the pre period for patients admitted during night hours (7 pm to 7 am) in the highest APACHE III quartile. No significant differences were seen at other severity levels. Unadjusted ICU length of stay decreased in the post period compared to the pre period (3.5 vs. 4.8 days), with no change in non-ICU length of stay.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that 24-hour ICU intensivist staffing reduces lengths of stay and cost estimates for the sickest patients admitted at night. The cost of implementing such a staffing model should be weighed against the potential total savings generated for these patients in smaller ICUs, particularly those that primarily care for lower-acuity patients.

title: GENOTYPING OF THALASSEMIA IN MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC ANEMIA PATIENTS FROM SOUTHWEST REGION OF IRAN
text:
Objective: To determine the frequency of α-gene, s-gene, and hemoglobin variant numbers in individuals with microcytic hypochromic anemia in Southwest Iran.
Methodology: In a study of 850 individuals with microcytic hypochromic anemia (MCV <80fl; MCH <27pg) from the Southwest region of Iran, including 340 subjects with known genetic disorders, we performed gap-PCR genotyping for -α 3.7, -α 4.2, -α PA, -α 5NT, and -med genes. Additionally, we conducted direct mutation analysis using ARMS for 23 of the most common s-gene mutations.
Results: The overall frequency of -α 3.7 deletion was 20% in 325 individuals. The most common s-gene mutations were CD 36/37, IVS II-I, and IVS I-110, occurring at frequencies of 9.7%, 11.7%, and 3.5%, respectively, in 340 patients. There were statistically significant differences in MCV and MCH indices between Beta-thalassemia trait and Beta-thalassemia Major, as well as between Beta-thalassemia trait and Hb Variants.
Conclusion: The study found that α-gene and s-gene mutations are common in the Southwest region of Iran, and molecular genotyping can help diagnose unexplained microcytosis and prevent unnecessary iron supplementation.

title: Systemic biomarkers in exacerbations of COPD: the evolving clinical challenge.
text:
BACKGROUND Exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain a significant cause of mortality and morbidity, despite advances in our understanding of their pathophysiology. The clinical presentation of ECOPD can be variable and challenging to predict, making it difficult to assess these episodes accurately. In recent years, a large number of biomarkers have been investigated for their potential role in the diagnosis, severity assessment, and treatment guidance of ECOPD.
METHODS An extensive online search was conducted using a combination of keywords related to ECOPD, biomarkers, and sampling methods, until December 2010. The biomarkers were evaluated based on their potential to establish and confirm the diagnosis of ECOPD, evaluate etiology and severity, predict prognosis, and guide treatment decisions.
RESULTS Several systemic biomarkers have been measured in the context of ECOPD, with most showing increased levels at the onset of exacerbations and decreased levels during the course of the episode. Correlations among these biomarkers have been reported, but direct associations with clinical variables have been more challenging to establish. Although there are several limitations that need to be addressed, some biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein for the identification of ECOPD and procalcitonin for antibiotic guidance, may provide clinically relevant information.
CONCLUSIONS While no single biomarker has gained widespread acceptance, the evaluation of these biomarkers in large, decision-making studies is expected to become an area of intense investigation in the near future.

title: Preoperative Predictors of Weight Loss Following Bariatric Surgery: Systematic Review
text: Obesity affects approximately 32% of adults in the United States, and bariatric surgery can lead to substantial weight loss. However, studies have shown that up to 20-30% of patients do not achieve successful weight loss after surgery. To identify preoperative psychosocial factors that may predict weight loss following bariatric surgery, we conducted a systematic literature review of articles published in PubMed® and the Cochrane Database of Reviews of Effectiveness between 1988 and April 2010. Our analysis included 115 studies that met our inclusion criteria, which included preoperative predictors of weight loss such as body mass index (BMI), preoperative weight loss, eating disorders, and psychiatric disorders/substance abuse. Our findings revealed that mandatory preoperative weight loss may be positively associated with weight loss after surgery, while preoperative BMI, super-obesity, and personality disorders may be negatively associated with weight loss. Additionally, we found that super-obese patients experienced a decrease of 10.1% excess weight loss (EWL) (95% confidence interval (CI) [3.7–16.5%]), while patients with binge eating at 12 months after surgery experienced an increase of 5.9% EWL (95% CI [1.9–9.8%]). Our findings suggest that identifying preoperative factors that predict weight loss after bariatric surgery may improve patient selection and help develop interventions targeting specific needs of patients. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to identify additional predictive factors.

title: The tumor necrosis factor receptor stalk regions define responsiveness to soluble versus membrane-bound ligand.
text: The family of tumor necrosis factor receptors (TNFRs) and their ligands form a complex signaling network that regulates immune responses. Despite their similarity, different members of this receptor family exhibit distinct responses to soluble and membrane-bound ligands. However, the underlying mechanisms behind this diversity are not yet fully understood. To investigate, we employed a well-established system of chimeric TNFRs and novel ligand variants mimicking the bioactivity of membrane-bound TNF (mTNF). Our findings reveal that the membrane-proximal extracellular stalk regions of TNFR1 and TNFR2 play a crucial role in determining responsiveness to soluble TNF (sTNF). Specifically, we found that the stalk region of TNFR2, in contrast to TNFR1, inhibits both receptor clustering in particular cell membrane regions and ligand-independent homotypic receptor preassembly, thereby preventing sTNF-induced signaling. These findings have implications not only for other TNFR family members but also provide potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: A bird's-eye view of sex chromosome dosage compensation.
text: Intensive research on a limited number of genetically tractable species with XX/XY sex chromosomes has led to generalizations about the process of sex chromosome dosage compensation that do not accurately reflect the sex chromosome system of birds (ZZ/ZW). The inherent imbalance in the dose of sex chromosome genes in birds has resulted in the evolution of sex-chromosome-wide mechanisms to balance gene dosage between the sexes and relative to autosomal genes. Recent advances in our understanding of avian genomes have prompted a reevaluation of sex-specific dosage compensation (SSDC) in birds, which is less effective than in known XX/XY systems. Insights into the mechanisms of SSDC in birds also highlight similarities and differences with those in XX/XY species. The study of SSDC in birds provides new opportunities to investigate dosage compensation in a ZZ/ZW system, shedding light on the evolution of SSDC more broadly.

title: The role of CHMP2BIntron5 in autophagy and frontotemporal dementia.
text: Charged multivesicular body protein 2B (CHMP2B) - a crucial component of the endosomal complex required for transport-III (ESCRT-III) - plays a vital role in the deformation of membranes in autophagy and endolysosomal trafficking. A dominant mutation in CHMP2B, specifically the intron 5 mutation (CHMP2BIntron5), has been linked to a subset of heritable frontotemporal dementia (FTD-3). ESCRT-III recruits Vps4, an AAA-ATPase that abscises the membrane during various cellular processes, including autophagy and intraluminal vesicle formation. The CHMP2BIntron5 mutation results in a C-terminus truncation, removing an important Vps4 binding site and eliminating the normal autoinhibitory resting state of CHMP2B. CHMP2B is expressed in most cell types, but its importance is particularly pronounced in neurons, where it plays a crucial role in maintaining proper function. The CHMP2BIntron5 mutation leads to a range of phenotypes, including misregulation of transmembrane receptors, accumulation of multilamellar structures, abnormal lysosomal morphology, downregulation of a brain-specific microRNA (miRNA-124), abnormal dendritic spine morphology, decrease in dendritic arborization, and cell death. To better understand the diverse phenotypes and develop therapeutic approaches, transgenic fly, mouse, and human cell lines are being used in current research. This article is part of a Special Issue entitled SI: Autophagy.

title: Restless legs syndrome and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a review of the literature.
text:
Study Objective: To conduct a systematic review of the literature on the association between restless legs syndrome (RLS) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), with a focus on elucidating the potential underlying mechanisms and evaluating the potential for common pharmacological treatments when co-occurring.
Methodology: A comprehensive search of PubMed was conducted to identify studies investigating the association between RLS and ADHD. Relevant articles were selected based on predetermined inclusion criteria, and data were extracted and synthesized using a standardized format.
Results: The search yielded several clinical studies that reported on the prevalence of RLS and ADHD in each disorder. The results showed that up to 44% of subjects with ADHD have been found to have RLS or RLS symptoms, while up to 26% of subjects with RLS have been found to have ADHD or ADHD symptoms. Several potential mechanisms were identified that may explain the observed association between RLS and ADHD, including sleep disruption associated with RLS leading to inattentiveness, moodiness, and paradoxical overactivity, as well as diurnal manifestations of RLS mimicking ADHD symptoms. Additionally, there is evidence to suggest that a subset of subjects with ADHD may share a common dopamine dysfunction with subjects with RLS.
Conclusion: While the evidence is still limited, the findings of the present study suggest an association between RLS and ADHD or ADHD symptoms. Further clinical studies using standardized criteria and procedures are needed to better estimate the degree of association. Epidemiological studies are also required to assess the relationship between ADHD and RLS symptoms in non-clinical populations. Further research should aim to elucidate the underlying mechanisms underlying the association between RLS and ADHD, and to evaluate the potential for common pharmacological treatments when co-occurring. Notably, the absence of randomized and blinded controlled studies precludes evidence-based recommendations at present.

title: Impact of the KU80 pathway on NHEJ-induced genome rearrangements in mammalian cells.
text: Using a substrate with an I-SceI-excised fragment, we investigated the impact of non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) on mammalian chromosome rearrangements. We observed that deletion was 2- to 8-fold more efficient than inversion, regardless of the structure of the DNA ends. The Ku80 protein controls accurate rejoining, while in its absence, microhomology-mediated repair occurs efficiently. In cells with both NHEJ and homologous recombination (HR) substrates containing a third I-SceI site, we found that NHEJ was at least 3.3-fold more efficient than HR. Additionally, we observed translocation of the I-SceI fragment from the NHEJ substrate locus into the HR-I-SceI site, but this occurred much less frequently than deletion. Deletions and translocations showed both accurate and inaccurate rejoining, suggesting that they involve a combination of KU-dependent and KU-independent processes. These findings suggest that NHEJ and HR are prominent pathways for DNA damage-induced genetic instability in mammalian cells.

title: The multi-zinc finger protein ZNF217 contacts DNA through a two-finger domain.
text: Classical C2H2 zinc finger proteins are ubiquitous transcription factors in eukaryotes, and their mechanisms of recognizing target genes have been extensively studied. In general, a tandem array of three fingers separated by characteristic TGERP links is necessary for sequence-specific DNA recognition. However, a significant proportion of zinc finger proteins lack this typical three-finger structure, raising questions about their DNA binding capabilities. We investigated the multi-finger protein ZNF217, which contains eight classical zinc fingers. ZNF217 has been implicated as an oncogene and in repressing the E-cadherin gene. Our study shows that two of its zinc fingers, 6 and 7, can interact with DNA. We examined the putative recognition site in the E-cadherin promoter and found that it is a suboptimal binding site. Using NMR analysis and mutagenesis, we characterized the DNA binding surface of ZNF217 and evaluated its specificity through fluorescence anisotropy titrations. Additionally, our sequence analysis revealed that many multi-finger proteins contain two-finger units, suggesting that these may represent a distinct subclass of DNA recognition motifs.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, risk perception, and cancer screening behaviors among cancer survivors.
text:
Background:
Little is known about the knowledge, attitudes, and risk perceptions of cancer survivors regarding second primary cancer (SPC) screening, and how these factors impact their screening practices. This study aimed to investigate these aspects and their association with screening behavior in cancer survivors.
Methods:
A total of 326 cancer survivors who had completed primary treatment for cancer over a year ago were recruited from six oncology care outpatient clinics in the Republic of Korea. Participants' knowledge, attitudes, perceived risk, and screening practices were assessed along with sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical characteristics. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify behavioral factors associated with completing all appropriate SPC screening tests according to national guidelines.
Results:
Approximately 37.7% of survivors had undergone all appropriate SPC screening tests. Survivors had a high perceived risk of SPC, high perceived benefits of screening, and positive attitudes towards cancer screening. However, they had limited knowledge regarding SPC screening tests and few had received a recommendation from a physician to undergo SPC screening. Although there was no association found between perceived risk and positive attitudes with screening behavior, higher knowledge was noted to be significantly associated with the completion of all appropriate SPC screening (adjusted odds ratio, 1.81; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-3.33).

Conclusions:

The current study found that cancer survivors had limited knowledge regarding SPC screening tests, which may have contributed to lower rates of completion of screening practices in this population. Higher knowledge was found to be significantly associated with the completion of all appropriate SPC screening tests, highlighting the importance of educating cancer survivors about SPC screening. Further research is needed to identify effective strategies for improving knowledge and screening practices in this population.

title: Ria1p (Ynl163c), a protein similar to elongation factors 2, is involved in the biogenesis of the 60S subunit of the ribosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
text:
RIA1 (YNL163c) is a quasi-essential gene that encodes a protein with significant similarity to elongation factors 2. Deletions of the protein's C-terminus can lead to a severe growth defect, which can be suppressed by intragenic mutations within the RIA1 gene or dominant extragenic mutations in TIF6. The latter is thought to play a role in the biogenesis of the 60S subunit of the ribosome. Dominant TIF6 alleles can also suppress the phenotype associated with a complete deletion of the RIA1 gene.
Depletion of Ria1p leads to a dramatic alteration in the polysome profile, characterized by a significant reduction in the levels of 80S monosomes, an imbalance in the 40S/60S ratio, and the appearance of halfmers. Dissociation of monosomes and polysomes in Ria1p-depleted cells revealed a specific reduction in the amount of 60S subunits. Localization experiments using HA-tagged derivatives of Ria1p did not reveal any stable association of Ria1p with ribosome subunits, 80S monosomes, or polysomes. Cell fractionation experiments showed that Ria1p is present in both the cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions. These findings suggest that Ria1p is involved in the biogenesis of the 60S subunit of the ribosome.

title: The Intestinal Immune System in Obesity and Insulin Resistance.
text: Obesity and insulin resistance are linked to chronic inflammation in metabolic tissues such as adipose tissue and the liver. Recent research has shown that the immune system in the digestive tract plays a crucial role in the development of metabolic disease. Obesity can lead to alterations in the immune system of the digestive tract, including changes to the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, and the number and type of immune cells in the gut. These changes can contribute to systemic inflammation and insulin resistance, which are major factors in the development of metabolic disease. This review aims to provide an overview of the emerging field of intestinal immunity in obesity-related insulin resistance and its potential as a novel therapeutic target for treating metabolic disease.

title: Human placental lactogen and unconjugated estriol concentrations in twin pregnancy: monitoring of fetal development in intrauterine growth retardation and single intrauterine fetal death.
text: In this study, the concentrations of human placental lactogen and unconjugated estriol were evaluated in 100 uneventful twin pregnancies and compared to those in 16 twin pregnancies with intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR) or single intrauterine fetal death (SIFD). In pregnancies with IUGR (n = 8), human placental lactogen levels were at the lower limit of normal range for singleton pregnancies, while estriol levels were normal in most cases. However, when one of the fetuses had died before week 33 of pregnancy (n = 5), both human placental lactogen and estriol levels were low and almost identical to those in singleton pregnancies. In contrast, when intrauterine fetal death occurred after week 36 of pregnancy (n = 3), both hormone levels remained normal until term. These findings suggest that human placental lactogen rather than estriol is a better indicator of IUGR in twin pregnancies. Both hormones are also useful for monitoring the surviving fetus in the case of SIFD.

title: Low antioxidant enzyme gene expression in pancreatic islets compared with various other mouse tissues.
text: Using a sensitive Northern blot hybridization technique, the expression of superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, and glutathione peroxidase was investigated in pancreatic islets and compared to other mouse tissues (liver, kidney, brain, lung, skeletal muscle, heart muscle, adrenal gland, and pituitary gland). Gene expression of these antioxidant enzymes was generally in the range of ±50% of that in the liver, with the exception of pancreatic islets, where gene expression was significantly lower. Specifically, the levels of cytoplasmic Cu/Zn SOD and mitochondrial Mn SOD gene expression were found to be around 30-40% of those in the liver, while glutathione peroxidase gene expression was only 15%, and catalase gene expression was undetectable in pancreatic islets. These low levels of antioxidant enzyme gene expression may provide an explanation for the unique sensitivity of pancreatic beta cells to cytotoxic damage by diabetogenic compounds and their involvement in the development of human and animal diabetes.

title: Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase isozymes expressed in mouse skeletal muscle.
text: To investigate changes in cyclic nucleotide metabolism in muscle diseases, the expression of phosphodiesterase (PDE) isozymes was examined in normal mouse leg muscle. Four subcellular fractions were generated through differential centrifugation at 10,000 x g and 100,000 x g, and PDE activity was found to be predominantly in the soluble fractions for cAMP, while cGMP PDE activity was more evenly distributed between soluble and particulate fractions. Using pharmacological inhibitors, it was found that PDE4 represents the major cAMP hydrolyzing activity and PDE2 represents the major cGMP hydrolyzing activity in mouse leg muscle. Low levels of PDE1 were expressed, while PDE3 and PDE5 had intermediate expression. Between 20 and 40% of total PDE activity remained in the presence of inhibitors for PDE1-PDE5, indicating that other PDE families contribute to the total PDE pool. Reverse-transcription PCR with family-specific primers showed expression of mRNA for PDE7-PDE9, supporting this conclusion. Total PDE activity was found to be elevated in tissue extracts from a mouse model of Duchenne's muscular dystrophy.

title: Exercise-induced asthma.
text: The impact of exercise on lung function was investigated in 7 patients with asthma. Three of the patients exhibited a significant decrease in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) after exercise. The degree of hyperventilation induced by exercise correlated with the post-exercise decrease in FEV1. Voluntary hyperventilation at rest also led to a decrease in FEV1 in all patients with asthma. Inhaling 5.6% carbon dioxide during voluntary hyperventilation resulted in a larger ventilation and greater decrease in FEV1 compared to breathing room air. Neither exercise nor voluntary hyperventilation had a significant effect on FEV1 in normal subjects or patients with chronic bronchitis. Both exercise-induced and hyperventilation-induced decreases in FEV1 were inhibited by prior administration of isoproterenol but not by atropine. It is suggested that exercise-induced asthma is likely to be a form of hyperventilation-induced asthma. Several possible underlying mechanisms for the production of airway obstruction are proposed.

title: An antimicrobial protein of the gut symbiont Bacteroides fragilis with a MACPF domain of host immune proteins.
text: Bacteroidales are the most prevalent Gram-negative bacteria within the human intestinal microbiota, comprising over half of the bacterial population in many individuals. While some of the factors that enable these bacteria to thrive in this environment are beginning to be elucidated, the ecological dynamics of competition, particularly interference competition, where one organism hinders the growth of another, remain understudied. To investigate the relevance of this ecological principle in the context of these abundant gut bacteria and the factors that may promote interference competition, we screened Bacteroides fragilis for the production of antimicrobial molecules. Our findings indicate that the production of extracellularly secreted antimicrobial molecules is widespread in this species. Specifically, we identified a molecule termed BSAP-1, which contains a membrane attack complex/perforin (MACPF) domain similar to that of host immune molecules, and mutations in key residues of this domain abrogated its activity. BSAP-1 is secreted from the cell through outer membrane vesicles and does not require additional proteins for its secretion, processing, or immunity of the producing cell. This study provides the first insight into secreted molecules that promote competitive interference among Bacteroidales strains within the human gut microbiota.

title: Directional perception of distributed sound sources.
text: In two listening experiments conducted in anechoic conditions, the perception of spatially distributed sound sources was investigated. The experiments involved 13 loudspeakers evenly distributed in the frontal horizontal plane emitting incoherent noise signals. In the first experiment, pink noise was emitted by widely distributed sound sources with gaps in their distribution. The results showed that the exact loudspeaker distribution could not be perceived accurately, and the width of the distribution was perceived to be narrower than it was in reality. Up to three spatially distributed loudspeakers that were simultaneously emitting sound could be individually perceived. Additionally, the number of loudspeakers indicated as emitting sound was smaller than the actual number. In the second experiment, the perceived spatial difference was rated for reference cases with 13 loudspeakers and test cases with fewer loudspeakers. The effect of noise bandwidth was of particular interest, and noise with different bandwidths centered around 500 and 4000 Hz was used. The results showed that as the number of loudspeakers increased from four to seven, the perceived auditory event was very similar to that perceived with 13 loudspeakers at all bandwidths. However, the perceived differences were larger in wideband noise than in narrow-band noise.

title: Adoptive T cell transfer for cancer immunotherapy in the era of synthetic biology.
text: Adoptive T cell transfer for cancer and chronic infection is an emerging field that holds great promise, as demonstrated by recent clinical trials. The engineering of T lymphocytes through synthetic biology techniques to express high-affinity antigen receptors has the potential to overcome immune tolerance, which has been a significant limitation in immunotherapy-based strategies. Advances in cell engineering and culture approaches have enabled the efficient gene transfer and ex vivo cell expansion, facilitating the broader evaluation of this technology, and positioning adoptive transfer as a mainstream technology. However, the field currently faces a major challenge in increasing the specificity of engineered T cells for tumors, as targeting shared antigens can lead to on-target off-tumor toxicities, as observed in recent clinical trials. As the field matures, the major engineering challenge lies in the development of automated cell culture systems, which will be essential to extend the approach beyond specialized academic centers and make it widely available.

title: Bruce treadmill test in children: normal values in a clinic population.
text: The Bruce treadmill protocol is suitable for young children aged 4 years and above. Maximal endurance time can be used as the sole indicator of exercise capacity, with established normal values based on 327 children with innocent heart murmurs. In boys, mean endurance time increased from 10.4 minutes at age 4 to 14.1 minutes at age 13-15 years, while in girls, it increased from 9.5 minutes at age 4 to 12.3 minutes at age 10-12 years. The mean maximal heart rate ranged from 193 to 206 beats/min, with small age differences in mean maximal and submaximal heart rates. There were negative correlations between endurance time and the ratio of weight to height, as well as between heart rates at treadmill stages 1-3 and endurance times. Notably, the correlation coefficient between endurance time and maximal oxygen uptake was 0.88, suggesting that endurance time alone can be a satisfactory indicator of exercise performance for clinical purposes.

title: Immunoproteasome and LMP2 polymorphism in aged and Alzheimer's disease brains.
text: In this investigation, we examined the presence and function of the immunoproteasome and its LMP2 subunit polymorphism at codon 60 in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The immunoproteasome was detected in various brain regions, including the hippocampus and cerebellum, and was primarily localized within neurons, astrocytes, and endothelial cells. Our findings revealed that the expression of immunoproteasome was significantly higher in the brains of AD patients compared to non-demented elderly individuals, with minimal or undetectable expression in young brain tissue. Additionally, we observed a partial decrease in proteasome trypsin-like activity in AD-affected regions. The study of LMP2 polymorphism (R/H) revealed that it did not influence LMP2 expression (either at the mRNA or mature protein level) in brain tissue. However, we did observe an interesting phenomenon where brain areas from AD patients carrying the RR genotype exhibited enhanced proteasome activity compared to RH carriers. To investigate whether this genotype-related effect might be linked to AD onset, we conducted a genetic study that allowed us to rule out any association between LMP2 codon 60 polymorphism and AD onset, despite its impact on proteasome activity in human brain.

title: The centrosome and its mode of inheritance: the reduction of the centrosome during gametogenesis and its restoration during fertilization.
text: The restoration of the centrosome during fertilization and its reduction during gametogenesis are crucial events in development, yet their mechanisms are not fully understood. While it is known that both the sperm and egg contribute haploid genomes during fertilization, the relative contributions of the centrosome by each gamete are still a topic of debate. Boveri once proposed that the ripe egg possesses all the elements necessary for development except for an active division center, while the sperm possesses such a center but lacks the protoplasmic substratum. The union of the egg and sperm restores the missing element necessary for further development. This article reviews evidence gathered from 11 experimental strategies used to test this theory, including the introduction of the centrosome by the sperm at fertilization, the de novo formation of centrosomes in unfertilized eggs, and the retention of the maternal centrosome during oogenesis and the paternal centrosome during spermatogenesis. Models of the centrosome and speculative mechanisms for its cloaking during oogenesis and retention during spermatogenesis are proposed. Additionally, the importance of proteins essential for microtubule nucleation, such as gamma-tubulin, in the restoration of the zygotic centrosome at fertilization is discussed. It is suggested that the attraction of maternal centrosomal components, including gamma-tubulin and the 25S "gamma-some" particle, to the paternal reproducing element, along with post-translational modifications, creates a functional zygote centrosome by blending both maternal and paternal constituents. title: Aggregation of vascular risk factors and risk of incident Alzheimer disease.
text:
Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is becoming more prevalent in the elderly population, and vascular risk factors may increase its risk.
Objective: To investigate the association between the accumulation of vascular risk factors and the development of AD.
Methods: The study followed 1,138 individuals without dementia (mean age 76.2) for a median of 5.5 years. The presence of vascular risk factors was analyzed in relation to the incidence of possible and probable AD.
Results: Four risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and current smoking) were found to be associated with an increased risk of AD (p < 0.10) when analyzed individually. The risk of AD increased with the number of risk factors, and the adjusted hazards ratio for probable AD was 3.4 (95% CI: 1.8, 6.3; p for trend < 0.0001) for the presence of three or more risk factors compared to no risk factors. Diabetes and current smoking were the strongest risk factors when analyzed separately or in combination, but hypertension and heart disease also showed a significant association with AD when clustered with diabetes, smoking, or each other.
Conclusions: The risk of AD increases with the number of vascular risk factors. Diabetes and current smoking are the strongest risk factors, but clusters including hypertension and heart disease also contribute to the development of AD. These associations are unlikely to be due to misclassification of the outcome, as strong associations are observed when only probable AD is considered.

title: Hotspot mutations in H3F3A and IDH1 define distinct epigenetic and biological subgroups of glioblastoma.
text: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor with a poor prognosis and significant heterogeneity. Recent research has identified recurrent H3F3A mutations in approximately one-third of pediatric GBM cases, affecting two crucial amino acids (K27 and G34) on histone H3.3. Our findings show that each H3F3A mutation defines a distinct epigenetic subgroup of GBM, characterized by a unique global methylation pattern. These subgroups are mutually exclusive with IDH1 mutations, which define a third subgroup of GBM. Additionally, we identified three further epigenetic subgroups that are enriched for hallmark genetic events common in adult GBM and/or established transcriptomic signatures. Furthermore, we found that the two H3F3A mutations segregate GBMs into different anatomical compartments, with distinct regulation of transcription factors OLIG1, OLIG2, and FOXG1, which may indicate different cellular origins.

title: Glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide for paraquat-induced lung fibrosis.
text:
Background: Paraquat is a widely used herbicide, but it can also be lethally toxic to humans. In many developing countries, paraquat is readily available and affordable, which can make poisoning prevention challenging. Most cases of paraquat poisoning are intentional, with individuals taking the substance as a means of suicide. Standard treatments for paraquat poisoning involve removing the poison from the body through hemoperfusion or hemodialysis. However, these treatments are limited in their effectiveness. The immune system plays a significant role in exacerbating paraquat-induced lung fibrosis. Therefore, immunosuppressive therapy using glucocorticoid and cyclophosphamide in combination is being investigated as a potential treatment.
Objectives: To assess the effectiveness of glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide in reducing mortality in patients with paraquat-induced lung fibrosis.
Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on this topic, searching multiple databases including Cochrane Injuries Group's Specialized Register, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, EMBASE, ISI Web of Science, Chinese Biomedical Literature and Retrieval System, Chinese Medical Current Contents, and Chinese Medical Academic Conference. We included RCTs that involved patients with moderate to severe paraquat poisoning and received standard care plus the intervention or control.
Results: Our review included three RCTs with a total of 164 participants. Patients who received glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide in addition to standard care had a lower risk of death at final follow-up compared to those receiving standard care only (risk ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.59-0.89).

Conclusion: Based on the findings of three small RCTs, glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide in addition to standard care may be a beneficial treatment for patients with paraquat-induced lung fibrosis. Further study is needed to confirm these findings and to determine the optimal dosage and duration of treatment.

title: Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) versus other fluid therapies: effects on kidney function.
text: Background: Hydroxyethyl starches (HES) are commonly used for fluid resuscitation, but controversy exists regarding their impact on kidney function. Objectives: To compare the effects of HES on kidney function with other fluid resuscitation therapies in different patient populations. Methods: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-RCTs was conducted, searching multiple databases and reference lists. Studies were included if they compared HES to an alternative fluid therapy for the prevention or treatment of intravascular volume depletion. Primary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), author-defined kidney failure, and acute kidney injury (AKI) as defined by the RIFLE criteria. Secondary outcomes included serum creatinine and creatinine clearance. Data extraction and quality assessments were performed by two authors using standardized forms, and authors were contacted for incomplete data. Subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the risk of AKI in septic versus non-septic patients. Results: Thirty-four studies (2607 patients) were included in the review. Overall, the risk of author-defined kidney failure was 1.50 (95% CI 1.20 to 1.87; n = 1199) and 1.38 for requiring RRT (95% CI 0.89 to 2.16; n = 1236) in HES-treated individuals compared to other fluid therapies. Subgroup analyses suggested an increased risk in septic patients compared to non-septic (surgical/trauma) patients. However, non-septic patient studies were smaller and had lower event rates, which may have limited the ability to detect differences. Limited data were obtained for analysis of kidney outcomes using the RIFLE criteria. Overall, the methodological quality of the studies was good, but subjective outcomes were potentially biased due to unblinding. Conclusions: The potential for increased risk of AKI should be considered when evaluating the use of HES for volume resuscitation, particularly in septic patients. Large, adequately powered studies are needed to evaluate the renal safety of HES products in non-septic patient populations. The use of the RIFLE criteria in future studies will help to provide more accurate assessments of kidney function. There is currently inadequate clinical data to support claims of safety differences between different HES products.

title: Dietary fat and obesity: evidence from epidemiology.
text: The epidemiological evidence suggesting a high-fat diet promotes obesity is suggestive but not conclusive. This paper aims to review various epidemiological methods used to investigate this association and provide an updated summary of existing evidence. Ecological studies examining dietary fat intake and obesity at the population level have yielded mixed results due to confounding and data quality issues. Cross-sectional studies generally show a positive association between dietary fat and relative weight. Prospective studies of diet and weight change have inconsistent results, which may be due to behavioral factors such as dieting in response to weight gain, or the interaction between genetic predisposition and dietary fat. Intervention studies in free-living subjects provide evidence of short-term weight loss on low-fat diets, although biological mechanisms remain controversial. Future epidemiological research could focus on the following areas:

title: Uncoupling of leading- and lagging-strand DNA replication during lesion bypass in vivo.
text: Numerous agents, such as oxidative stress, UV radiation, and chemicals, attack DNA, causing damage that hinders normal replication. To overcome these obstacles, specialized DNA polymerases temporarily replace the regular replicative polymerase and copy the damaged regions, leading to mutations, which are a primary initiator of cancer. We investigated the kinetics of DNA replication in Escherichia coli, focusing on the replication of both strands of DNA molecules containing a single blockage in either the leading or lagging strand. Surprisingly, despite a blockage in the leading strand, lagging-strand synthesis continued further, indicating a temporary disconnection between the concurrent strand synthesis. Replication through the lesion requires specialized DNA polymerases and is accomplished with similar kinetics and efficiencies in both strands.

title: Phosphoinositide 3-kinase signalling--which way to target?
text:
Abstract:
Phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) play a crucial role in regulating cell growth, proliferation, and survival, and are implicated in the progression of tumors by activating phosphoinositide-dependent kinase, protein kinase B, and the target of rapamycin. In addition to these well-established functions, PI3Ks have been shown to modulate other cellular processes, including cell motility and the control of cardiovascular parameters. Current research suggests that targeting PI3Ks may be a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of various diseases, including cancer, chronic inflammation, allergy, and cardiovascular failure. However, it is important to consider the potential consequences of PI3K inhibition on vital cellular processes, such as metabolic control and nutrient uptake. This review summarizes recent mechanistic data and mouse phenotypic analyses, and discusses the potential success of therapeutic inhibition of distinct PI3K isoforms.

title: Determination of the time course of capacitation in mouse spermatozoa using a chlortetracycline fluorescence assay.
text: The heads of mouse spermatozoa obtained 5 minutes after being released from the excised caudae epididymides exhibited a characteristic fluorescence pattern in the presence of the fluorophore chlortetracycline (CTC). Specifically, there was uniform fluorescence across the entire head, with about half of the sperm population showing a brighter line of fluorescence across the equatorial segment, which was designated "F". After incubation in culture medium (CM) containing 2% bovine serum albumin for 90 minutes, most of the sperm heads showed a dark band of non-fluorescence over the equatorial and postequatorial segment, while the anterior portion of the head remained brightly fluorescent. This fluorescence pattern was designated "B". The time course for the disappearance of pattern F matched the time course of the appearance of pattern B, with a half-time of 30 minutes. The transformation was complete in 90 minutes. At longer times of incubation in CM, the percentage of spermatozoa showing pattern B declined, and fluorescence over the entire head was lost, characteristic of the pattern for acrosome-reacted sperm. Mouse sperm showing pattern B were able to undergo the acrosome reaction, either spontaneously or by induction with acid-solubilized zonae pellucidae from mouse eggs. The latter reaction was blocked by its specific inhibitor 3-quinuclidinyl benzilate (QNB). Mouse sperm showing pattern F could not be induced to undergo the acrosome reaction by exposure to solubilized zonae. These results imply that the change from fluorescence pattern F to fluorescence pattern B corresponds with changes in the sperm that make them susceptible to undergo the acrosome reaction. This change occurs during the time interval previously determined to be needed for capacitation of mouse sperm in vitro in CM. These findings suggest that spermatozoa showing CTC fluorescence pattern B can be considered to be capacitated, and that a functional definition for capacitation is the acquired ability to undergo the acrosome reaction rapidly when treated with acid-solubilized zonae pellucidae. The CTC fluorescence assay provides for the first time a means to monitor the time course of epididymal mouse sperm capacitation in vitro.

title: [Detection of CRISPR and its relationship to drug resistance in Shigella].
text:
Objective: To detect the presence of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) in Shigella and analyze its relationship to drug resistance.
Methods: We used four pairs of primers to detect CRISPR structures in 60 Shigella strains. The primers were designed based on sequences in the CRISPR database. We also used CRISPR Finder to analyze the CRISPR loci and determined the susceptibility of Shigella strains to antibiotics using the agar diffusion method. Additionally, we investigated the relationship between drug resistance and the CRISPR locus CRISPR-S4.
Results: Our results showed that 95% of the Shigella strains had convincing CRISPR structures. We identified 12 different spectral patterns (A-L) among the CRISPR loci, with all except one containing convincing CRISPR structures. We also discovered a new repeat and 12 new spacers. The multi-drug resistance rate was 53.33%. We found no significant difference in the CRISPR-S4 locus between drug-resistant and non-drug-resistant strains. However, the repeat sequence of CRISPR-S4 in multi- or TE-resistant strains was mainly R4.1 with AC deletions in the 3' end, and the spacer sequences of CRISPR-S4 in multi-drug resistance strains were mainly Sp5.1, Sp6.1, and Sp7.
Conclusion: CRISPR is prevalent in Shigella, and variations in repeat sequences and spacer sequences may be related to drug resistance in these bacteria.

title: The helicase DDX41 senses intracellular DNA mediated by the adaptor STING in dendritic cells
text: The identification of DNA-sensing proteins is crucial for triggering antiviral responses within cells. In this study, we discovered DDX41, a DEXDc family helicase, as an intracellular DNA sensor in myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs). When DDX41 expression was suppressed using short hairpin RNA, mDCs were unable to mount type I interferon and cytokine responses to DNA and DNA viruses. Conversely, overexpressing both DDX41 and the membrane-associated adaptor STING resulted in a synergistic increase in Ifnb promoter activity. DDX41 bound both DNA and STING and localized together with STING in the cytosol. Furthermore, knockdown of DDX41 expression blocked the activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase TBK1 and transcription factors NF-κB and IRF3 in response to B-form DNA. Our findings suggest that DDX41 is another DNA sensor that relies on STING to detect pathogenic DNA.

title: Radiotherapy plus concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide for glioblastoma.
text:
Glioblastoma, the most common primary brain tumor in adults, is typically a rapidly fatal disease. The current standard of care for newly diagnosed glioblastoma involves surgical resection to the extent feasible, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. In this trial, we compared the efficacy and safety of radiotherapy alone versus radiotherapy plus temozolomide in patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma.
Methods:
We randomly assigned 573 patients from 85 centers to receive either radiotherapy alone (fractionated focal irradiation in daily fractions of 2 Gy given 5 days per week for 6 weeks, for a total of 60 Gy) or radiotherapy plus continuous daily temozolomide (75 mg per square meter of body-surface area per day, 7 days per week from the first to the last day of radiotherapy), followed by six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide (150 to 200 mg per square meter for 5 days during each 28-day cycle). The primary end point was overall survival.
Results:
At a median follow-up of 28 months, the median survival was 14.6 months in the radiotherapy plus temozolomide group and 12.1 months in the radiotherapy alone group. The unadjusted hazard ratio for death in the radiotherapy-plus-temozolomide group was 0.63 (95% confidence interval, 0.52 to 0.75; P<0.001 by the log-rank test). The two-year survival rate was 26.5% in the radiotherapy plus temozolomide group and 10.4% in the radiotherapy alone group. Concurrent treatment with radiotherapy plus temozolomide resulted in grade 3 or 4 hematologic toxic effects in 7% of patients.
Conclusions:
Our findings suggest that the addition of temozolomide to radiotherapy results in a clinically meaningful and statistically significant survival benefit with minimal additional toxicity in patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma. These results provide evidence for the use of this combination as a new standard of care for this disease.

title: Drug interactions between oral contraceptives and antibiotics.
text: Objective: To evaluate the evidence on potential drug interactions between antibiotics and oral contraceptives (OCs) that may lead to OC failure. Data Sources: Medline and Lexis/Nexis Medical Library searches for 1966-1999 using the keywords "oral contraceptives," "antibiotics," "adverse effects," and "pregnancy," and a MEDLINE search using the additional MeSH term "drug interactions." Study Selection: A total of 167 articles were retrieved for analysis, and an additional 32 articles were identified by reviewing the references cited in these publications. Articles were selected based on their ability to provide information on the relationship between antibiotic therapy and OC efficacy in otherwise compliant users. Methods: The study analyzed case reports, clinical surveys, and retrospective surveys to identify pregnancies occurring in women taking OCs and antibiotics, particularly rifampin. Information from adverse event reporting databases and retrospective surveys were also reviewed. Results: At least 30 cases of pregnancies occurring in women taking OCs and antibiotics have been reported, with approximately 20% of pregnant women reporting concomitant use of OCs and antibiotics. Pharmacokinetic studies of other antibiotics have not shown any systematic interaction between antibiotics and OC steroids, but individual patients have been identified who experienced significant decreases in the plasma concentration of OC components and appeared to ovulate. Conclusion: Rifampin impairs the effectiveness of OCs, and a cautious approach is advised. While pharmacokinetic studies of other antibiotics have not shown any systematic interaction between antibiotics and OC steroids, individual patients may experience large decreases in the plasma concentrations of ethinyl estradiol when taking certain other antibiotics, notably tetracycline and penicillin derivatives.

title: Male Japanese quails with female brains do not show male sexual behaviors.
text:
During embryonic development, gonadal steroid hormones (androgens and estrogens) are believed to play a crucial role in organizing the sexual differentiation of the brain in higher vertebrates, with the heterogametic sex (males in mammals, females in birds) being more susceptible to hormonal influences. In contrast, the homogametic sex (females in both mammals and birds) is thought to develop without the need for hormonal intervention. In the Japanese quail, for example, female brain organization is believed to arise through estrogen-mediated demasculinization of a default male brain phenotype.
To investigate the mechanisms underlying brain sexual differentiation, we performed isotopic, isochronic transplantation of the forebrain primordium in Japanese quail embryos before gonadal differentiation had occurred. The chimeras were then allowed to develop into adulthood, at which point we observed their sexual behavior and hormone levels. Our findings revealed that chimeras with a genetic male host (MM, FF, and MF) exhibited sexual behavior that was typical of their genetic sex, while chimeras with a genetic female host (FM) showed no mounting or crowing behavior, despite producing both testosterone and estrogen. Furthermore, FM chimeras had low levels of testosterone in adulthood and displayed reduced or absent reproductive behaviors, along with morphological abnormalities in the medial preoptic nucleus, a sexually dimorphic brain area. These results suggest that there is a brain-intrinsic, genetically determined component that organizes the production of gonadal hormones in adulthood, and that the mechanisms underlying brain sexual differentiation may be more complex than previously thought.

title: DNA joint dependence of pol X family polymerase action in nonhomologous end joining.
text: DNA double strand breaks (DSBs) can be repaired through the nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) pathway, which requires the action of nucleases and polymerases to accurately repair the damage. Previous research has shown that the Pol X family polymerase Pol4 is necessary for some, but not all, NHEJ events in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. In this study, we systematically analyzed the configurations of DSB ends and found that the presence of gaps on both strands and the polarity of the overhangs determine whether Pol4 is required for repair. DSBs with 3'-overhangs and a gap on each strand rely heavily on Pol4 for repair, while DSBs with 5'-overhangs of the same sequence do not. However, DSBs with 3'-overhangs containing a gap on only one strand can be repaired without Pol4. Additionally, we found that Pol4 is specific to NHEJ and is not required for the rejoining of DSBs that utilize recessed microhomology or bear 5'-hydroxyls. Furthermore, mammalian Pol X polymerases can complement a pol4 mutation in yeast, indicating that these polymerases can participate in NHEJ with distinct properties.

title: ABC of burns. Introduction.
text:
Burns are one of the most severe medical conditions encountered in healthcare, affecting individuals of all ages and backgrounds. The injury inflicts harm not only on the physical body but also on the psychological well-being of the patient, causing immense pain and distress. Burns can occur in both developed and developing countries and pose a significant challenge to medical and paramedical staff. Proper management of burn injuries requires a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach that addresses all aspects of the patient's care, from initial resuscitation and intensive care to rehabilitation and recovery. This series provides an overview of the key aspects of burn injuries and their management for hospital and non-hospital healthcare workers.
Figure 1 illustrates the severity of burn injuries, showing a child with 70% full-thickness burns who required extensive debridement and skin grafting. Despite the initial challenges, the child made a remarkable recovery, as shown in the image on the left, taken one year later at a burns camp. This example highlights the possibility of a good outcome for burn patients with proper care and management.

title: DNA methylation is a critical cell-intrinsic determinant of astrocyte differentiation in the fetal brain.
text: Astrocyte differentiation, which occurs later in brain development, is largely dependent on the activation of a transcription factor called STAT3. Our findings show that astrocytes, as identified by the protein glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), never emerge from neural precursor cells on embryonic day (E) 11.5, even when STAT3 is activated, in contrast to E14.5 neural precursor cells. Interestingly, we found that a specific DNA sequence within the GFAP promoter called a CpG dinucleotide is highly methylated in E11.5 neural precursor cells, which makes it inaccessible to STAT3 and prevents astrocyte differentiation. However, when STAT3 is activated, the methylation of this CpG sequence is demethylated, allowing STAT3 to bind to the promoter and induce GFAP expression. Our findings suggest that the methylation of a cell type-specific gene promoter is a crucial event in regulating the fate of cells in the developing brain.

title: DNMT1 Inhibition Reprograms Pancreatic Cancer Stem Cells via Upregulation of the miR-17-92 Cluster.
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and other carcinomas are organized in a hierarchical manner, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) residing at the apex of the hierarchy. CSCs are responsible for driving tumor progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance. Although CSCs and non-CSCs share a common genetic background, differences in epigenetic mechanisms are thought to account for the distinct functional properties of these cell populations. Epigenetic regulators, such as DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs), play a crucial role in maintaining pluripotency and directing the differentiation of stem cells. However, the role of DNA methylation in pancreatic CSCs remains unclear.
In this study, we aimed to investigate the genome-wide DNA methylation profile of PDAC CSCs and to elucidate the importance of DNMTs in CSC maintenance and tumorigenicity. Using high-throughput methylation analysis, we found that sorted CSCs exhibited higher levels of DNA methylation compared to non-CSCs, regardless of the heterogeneity or polyclonality of the CSC populations present in the tumors analyzed. Mechanistically, CSCs expressed higher levels of DNMT1 compared to non-CSCs. Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of DNMT1 in CSCs resulted in a reduction in their self-renewal and in vivo tumorigenic potential, thereby identifying DNMT1 as a potential therapeutic target for CSCs. The inhibitory effect was found to be mediated, in part, through the epigenetic reactivation of previously silenced microRNAs (miRNAs), with a particular focus on the miR-17-92 cluster.
Our findings suggest that DNA methylation plays a crucial role in CSC biology and provide a rationale for the development of epigenetic modulators to target CSC plasticity and improve the poor prognosis of PDAC patients.
Cancer Research; Vol. 76, No. 15; 4546-458. ©2016 AACR.

title: Mutation spectrum in the nephrin gene (NPHS1) in congenital nephrotic syndrome.
text: Congenital nephrotic syndrome, Finnish type (CNF or NPHS1), is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by excessive proteinuria and the development of nephrotic syndrome shortly after birth. This disease is most prevalent in Finland, but it has also been identified in other populations worldwide. The condition is caused by mutations in the gene for nephrin, a crucial component of the glomerular ultrafilter and the podocyte slit diaphragm. To date, a total of 30 mutations have been identified in the nephrin gene in patients with congenital nephrotic syndrome globally. In the Finnish population, two prevalent nonsense mutations account for over 94% of all mutations. In contrast, non-Finnish patients typically harbor missense, nonsense, splice site, deletion, and insertion mutations. This update summarizes the previously reported nephrin mutations and describes 20 novel mutations discovered in our laboratory.

title: The HSA domain binds nuclear actin-related proteins to regulate chromatin-remodeling ATPases
text: We have identified the helicase-SANT–associated (HSA) domain as the primary binding platform for nuclear actin-related proteins (ARPs) and actin. Through the use of individual HSA domains from chromatin remodelers (RSC, yeast SWI-SNF, human SWI-SNF, SWR1, and INO80) or modifiers (NuA4), we have reconstituted their respective ARP–ARP or ARP–actin modules. In RSC, the HSA domain is located on the catalytic ATPase subunit Sth1. Our findings indicate that the Sth1 HSA is essential in vivo, and its absence leads to the specific loss of ARPs and a moderate reduction in ATPase activity. Genetic selections for arp suppressors have yielded specific gain-of-function mutations in two new domains in Sth1, the post-HSA domain and protrusion 1, which are essential for RSC function in vivo but not ARP association. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of the role of the HSA domain and offer insight into the regulatory relationship between the ARP–HSA module and two newly identified functional domains conserved in remodeler ATPases that contain ARPs.

title: Increased dendritic complexity and axonal length in cultured mouse cortical neurons overexpressing methyl-CpG-binding protein MeCP2
text: Rett syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding the methyl DNA-binding protein MeCP2, is associated with diminished brain mass and neuronal complexity. To investigate the potential role of MeCP2 in neuronal maturation and synaptogenesis, we examined the effect of MeCP2 overexpression on the morphology of developing neurons in cultured mouse neurons. Our findings revealed that overexpression of MeCP2β (MECP2A) led to the development of more complex neuronal morphologies, marked by longer axonal and dendritic processes, and an increased number of axonal and dendritic terminal endings. To further elucidate the mechanisms underlying MeCP2's effects, we evaluated the impact of overexpressing a mutant form of MeCP2β lacking its carboxyl terminus on neuronal morphology. Surprisingly, while neurons overexpressing this mutant failed to enhance axonal and dendritic process elongation, the complexity of their axonal and dendritic processes remained significantly elevated. These findings support the hypothesis that MeCP2 directly regulates neuronal maturation and/or synaptogenesis, and suggest that MeCP2 may exert its effects on neuritic elongation and process branching through distinct mechanisms.

title: Folate affects apoptosis in human trophoblastic cells.
text: Folate deficiency has been shown to significantly increase the rate of apoptosis in human cytotrophoblastic cells in vitro. In a study investigating the effects of folate deficiency on apoptosis in these cells, cytotrophoblastic cells were cultured in control medium, folate-free medium, or folate-free medium supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum. Apoptosis was determined in each group, and the results showed that the rate of apoptosis was significantly higher in cells cultured in mediums 2 and 3 compared to those in the control medium (P<0.02 and P<0.03, respectively). These findings suggest that folate deficiency may play a role in pregnancy complications. Possible explanations for this association include the increased rate of apoptosis in cytotrophoblastic cells, which are critical for the implantation and development of the placenta during pregnancy.

title: Role of KRAS and EGFR as biomarkers of response to erlotinib in National Cancer Institute of Canada Clinical Trials Group Study BR.21.
text: Purpose: To investigate the impact of KRAS and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) genotype on the response to erlotinib treatment in the BR.21, placebo-controlled trial. Methods: We analyzed 206 tumors for KRAS mutation, 204 tumors for EGFR mutation, and 159 tumors for EGFR gene copy by fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH). We reanalyzed EGFR deletion/mutation using two highly sensitive techniques that detect abnormalities in samples with 5% to 10% tumor cellularity. KRAS mutation was analyzed by direct sequencing. Results: Thirty patients (15%) had KRAS mutations, 34 (17%) had EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutations, and 61 (38%) had high EGFR gene copy (FISH positive). Response rates were 10% for wild-type and 5% for mutant KRAS (P = .69), 7% for wild-type and 27% for mutant EGFR (P = .03), and 5% for EGFR FISH-negative and 21% for FISH-positive patients (P = .02). Significant survival benefit from erlotinib therapy was observed for patients with wild-type KRAS (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.69, P = .03) and EGFR FISH positivity (HR = 0.43, P = .004) but not for patients with mutant KRAS (HR = 1.67, P = .31), wild-type EGFR (HR = 0.74, P = .09), mutant EGFR (HR = 0.55, P = .12), and EGFR FISH negativity (HR = 0.80, P = .35). In multivariate analysis, only EGFR FISH-positive status was prognostic for poorer survival (P = .025) and predictive of differential survival benefit from erlotinib (P = .005). Conclusion: EGFR mutations and high gene copy number are predictive of response to erlotinib. EGFR FISH is the strongest prognostic marker and a significant predictive marker of differential survival benefit from erlotinib.

title: Immune dysregulation in major depression: a critical review of existing evidence.
text: It is widely accepted that depression is linked to immune system dysfunction. However, it remains unclear whether this dysfunction contributes to the development of major depression or simply makes depressed individuals more susceptible to immune-related disorders. This article provides a comprehensive review of the existing evidence for immune dysregulation in major depression, including changes in white blood cell movement, lymphocyte function, and markers of immune activation. We also briefly discuss potential mediators of immune dysregulation in major depression. Finally, we critically evaluate the relationship between major depression and various medical conditions, such as infections, allergies, autoimmune disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and AIDS.

title: Regulation of E2Fs and senescence by PML nuclear bodies.
text: The tumor suppressor protein PML (promyelocytic leukemia protein) regulates two critical cellular processes: terminal differentiation and cellular senescence, which involve a permanent exit from the cell cycle. Our study reveals that PML achieves this by recruiting E2F transcription factors and the retinoblastoma (Rb) protein to nuclear bodies enriched in heterochromatin proteins and protein phosphatase 1α. When we blocked the functions of the Rb protein family or added back E2Fs to PML-expressing cells, we observed a rescue of E2F-dependent gene expression and cell proliferation, which inhibited the senescent phenotype. In benign prostatic hyperplasia, a neoplastic disease characterized by senescence, PML was found to be up-regulated and forming nuclear bodies. In contrast, PML bodies were rarely observed in prostate cancers. Our findings define a novel PML/Rb/E2F pathway, which may help distinguish benign tumors from cancers, and suggest E2F target genes as potential targets to induce senescence in human tumors.

title: The International Classification of Headache Disorders.
text: A collection of related medical disorders without a standardized classification system and diagnostic criteria is like a society without a functional legal framework. This lack of organization leads to confusion and chaos, making it difficult to provide accurate diagnoses and appropriate treatments. In contrast, the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD) has been a groundbreaking achievement in headache medicine over the past 50 years. The ICHD systematically categorizes over 100 different types of headaches in a logical and hierarchical manner, providing clear diagnostic criteria for each disorder. The widespread acceptance of the ICHD has facilitated both clinical research and clinical care in headache medicine, leading to a significant acceleration of progress in the field despite limited resources. In summary, the ICHD has become the standard reference for headache disorders, providing a much-needed framework for diagnosis and treatment.

title: Call to Develop a Standard Acquisition Charge Model for Kidney Paired Donation
text:
We are proposing a Medicare Demonstration Project to establish a standardized acquisition charge for kidney paired donation. Currently, Medicare and commercial insurance providers may not directly cover the costs associated with living donor expenses intended to lead to the transplantation of a beneficiary from a different insurance provider. This is similar to the challenges faced in the recovery and placement of deceased donor organs before the 1970s, when organ procurement organizations were empowered to act as financial intermediaries and cover upfront recovery expenses for deceased donor kidneys before knowing the identity of the recipient.
Similarly, kidney paired donation requires the evaluation of living donors before identifying their recipient, which incurs additional financial barriers, including tissue typing, crossmatching, and transportation costs. Moreover, organizations that identify and coordinate kidney paired donation transplantation incur administrative expenses that need to be reimbursed. To expand access to kidney paired donation for more patients, we propose a model that would reimburse paired donation expenses using a proven strategy that has been successful for over 30 years in paying for deceased donor solid organ transplantation in the United States.

title: Oxidant stress promotes disease by activating CaMKII.
text: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) is activated by the oxidation of specific methionine residues located in its regulatory domain. Once activated, oxidized CaMKII (ox-CaMKII) has been implicated in a variety of diseases, including cardiovascular and pulmonary disorders, as well as cancer. This review aims to summarize the current understanding of the role of ox-CaMKII in disease, identify knowledge gaps, and suggest new areas for research.

title: Genetic diagnosis and prognosis of Alzheimer's disease: challenges and opportunities.
text: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common form of dementia affecting Western societies, is a complex and multifaceted disease with a significant genetic component. Recent advances in high-throughput genome technologies have enabled the rapid analysis of millions of polymorphisms in thousands of individuals, significantly expanding our knowledge of the genomic factors contributing to AD susceptibility. Over the past five years, genome-wide association, whole-exome, and whole-genome sequencing studies have identified more than 20 genetic loci associated with AD, providing valuable insights into the molecular pathways involved in the disease's pathogenesis and suggesting potential new therapeutic targets. This review article discusses the challenges and opportunities of using genomic information to diagnose and predict AD.

title: WNT5A regulates adipose tissue angiogenesis via antiangiogenic VEGF-A165b in obese humans.
text:
Experimental studies have suggested that Wingless-related integration site 5A (WNT5A) is a pro-inflammatory secreted protein that plays a role in metabolic dysfunction in obesity. Specifically, impaired angiogenesis in fat depots has been linked to the development of adipose tissue capillary rarefaction, hypoxia, inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction. Recently, we demonstrated that impaired adipose tissue angiogenesis is associated with overexpression of anti-angiogenic factor VEGF-A165b in both human fat and the systemic circulation. In the present study, we investigated the role of WNT5A in regulating VEGF-A165b expression in human obesity.
We biopsied subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue from 38 obese individuals (BMI: 44 ± 7 kg/m2, age: 37 ± 11 years) during planned bariatric surgery and analyzed depot-specific protein expression of VEGF-A165b and WNT5A using Western blot analysis. We found that VEGF-A165b expression strongly correlated with WNT5A protein expression in both subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue (r = 0.9, P < 0.001). In subcutaneous adipose tissue, where angiogenic capacity is greater, exogenous human recombinant WNT5A increased VEGF-A165b expression in both whole adipose tissue and isolated vascular endothelial cell fractions (P < 0.01 and P < 0.05, respectively). This was associated with blunted angiogenic capillary sprout formation in human fat pad explants. Moreover, recombinant WNT5A increased secretion of soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, a negative regulator of angiogenesis, in the sprout media (P < 0.01).
We also investigated the effect of WNT5A on angiogenic capillary sprout formation using VEGF-A165b-neutralizing antibody and secreted frizzled-related protein 5, which acts as a decoy receptor for WNT5A. Both neutralizing antibody and secreted frizzled-related protein 5 significantly improved capillary sprout formation and reduced soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 production (P < 0.05).
Our findings demonstrate a significant regulatory nexus between WNT5A and anti-angiogenic VEGF-A165b in adipose tissue of obese subjects, which is linked to angiogenic dysfunction. Elevated WNT5A expression in obesity may function as a negative regulator of angiogenesis. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying metabolic dysfunction in obesity and may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of obesity-related metabolic disorders.

title: At least 1400 base pairs of 5'-flanking DNA is required for the correct expression of the HO gene in yeast.
text: Homothallic yeast cells undergo a specific pattern of mating-type switching that is initiated by an endonuclease encoded by the HO gene. The expression of HO is influenced by various factors, including cell type (a, alpha, and a/alpha), cell age (mother or daughter), and the cell cycle. To investigate the sequences involved in HO transcription, this paper employs an in vitro mutation approach to replace genomic DNA with mutated copies.
