The study reveals that a region between -1000 and 1400 (designated URS1) is essential for transcription, in addition to a "TATA"-like region at -90. Interestingly, the 900 bp of DNA separating URS1 from the "TATA" box is not necessary for transcription or a/alpha repression, but it plays a crucial role in mother/daughter control and cell cycle regulation.

title: Inflammation and its role in neuroprotection, axonal regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury.
text: Trauma to the central nervous system (CNS) leads to inflammation within the brain itself, known as intraparenchymal inflammation. This inflammation activates the body's immune system, which can either exacerbate or repair damaged tissue, depending on the context. Despite the complexity of these mechanisms, immune-based therapies are gaining attention as a potential treatment approach. This review will delve into the intricacies of post-traumatic neuroinflammation, particularly in the spinal cord, and discuss current therapies aimed at modulating neuroinflammatory pathways.

title: Order of intron removal influences multiple splice outcomes, including a two-exon skip, in a COL5A1 acceptor-site mutation that results in abnormal pro-alpha1(V) N-propeptides and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type I.
text: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) type I (the classical variety) is a dominantly inherited, genetically heterogeneous connective tissue disorder. Mutations in the COL5A1 and COL5A2 genes, which encode type V collagen, have been identified in individuals with EDS type I. These mutations typically affect either the triple-helical domain of the protein or the expression of one COL5A1 allele. In one patient with EDS type I, we identified a novel splice-acceptor mutation (IVS4-2A-->G) in the N-propeptide-encoding region of COL5A1. This mutation resulted in a complex outcome, with multiple products being produced due to the skipping of exons 5 and 6 in the major product, as well as the inclusion of a small amount of a product in which only exon 5 was skipped and an even smaller amount of a product in which cryptic acceptor sites within exon 5 were used. All of these products were in frame. The mutation led to dramatic alterations in collagen fibril structure. Our findings suggest that the order of intron removal plays a crucial role in the outcome of splice-site mutations and provide a model for understanding why multiple products can arise from a single mutation at a single splice site.

title: Kruppel-like factor KLF10 targets transforming growth factor-beta1 to regulate CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regulatory cells.
text: CD4(+)CD25(+) regulatory T cells (T regs) play a crucial role in maintaining self-tolerance and immune suppression, although the mechanisms underlying T reg development and function are not fully understood. Our study reveals that Kruppel-like factor 10 (KLF10/TIEG1) is a critical regulator of T regulatory cell suppressor function and CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell activation, involving distinct mechanisms involving transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 and Foxp3. Overexpression of KLF10 in CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells leads to increased TGF-beta1 and Foxp3 expression, resulting in reduced T-Bet (Th1 marker) and Gata3 (Th2 marker) mRNA expression. Conversely, KLF10 deficiency in CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells leads to enhanced differentiation along both Th1 and Th2 pathways, resulting in higher levels of Th1 and Th2 cytokines. Additionally, KLF10-deficient CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell effectors are unable to be appropriately suppressed by wild-type T regs. Interestingly, KLF10-deficient T reg cells have reduced suppressor function, independent of Foxp3 expression, with decreased expression and elaboration of TGF-beta1. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that KLF10 can transactivate both TGF-beta1 and Foxp3 promoters in response to TGF-beta1, suggesting a positive feedback loop that may promote cell-intrinsic control of T cell activation. Finally, KLF10-deficient CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells promote atherosclerosis in ApoE(-/-)/scid/scid mice by approximately 2-fold, with increased leukocyte accumulation and peripheral pro-inflammatory cytokines. Overall, our findings highlight KLF10 as a critical regulator in the transcriptional network controlling TGF-beta1 in both CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regs, and suggest a role for KLF10 in regulating atherosclerotic lesion formation in mice.

title: Synchrotron radiation solution X-ray scattering study of the pH dependence of the quaternary structure of yeast pyruvate decarboxylase.
text: The pH-dependent structure of pyruvate decarboxylase from yeast was investigated in the range of 6.2 pH units less than the midpoint (pH 7.5) between tetramers and dimers. The enzyme's catalytic activity depends on the proportion of tetramers. This equilibrium may provide an additional regulatory mechanism beyond substrate activation, as accumulation of pyruvate would lower the pH and increase the concentration of the active tetramer form. Radiation damage during X-ray scattering experiments altered this equilibrium, leading to the formation of octamers. To circumvent these effects, specialized experimental and data analysis techniques were employed, which can be applied to other radiation-sensitive systems. The low-resolution shapes of the dimers and tetramers were determined from the scattering curves using spherical harmonics. The results suggest that a conformational change occurs in the dimers upon formation of the tetramers, in agreement with previous circular dichroism measurements.

title: Enhancement of anxiety-like responsiveness to the cannabinoid CB(1) receptor agonist HU-210 following chronic stress.
text: The impact of chronic unpredictable stress on the anxiety-like response elicited by the cannabinoid receptor agonist HU-210 (3-(1,1-dimethylheptyl)-(-)-11-hydroxy-delta 8-tetrahydrocannabinol) was investigated in male Long-Evans rats. The rats were either unstressed or subjected to a 21-day stress regimen, and then divided into three testing groups (vehicle, 10, and 50 microg/kg of HU-210). The elevated plus maze was used to assess anxiety-like behavior. The results showed that in unstressed animals, a low dose of HU-210 produced an anxiolytic response, while a high dose induced an anxiogenic response. In contrast, in stressed animals, both low and high doses of HU-210 induced an anxiogenic response. These findings suggest that chronic stress enhances the responsiveness of cannabinoid receptors or interacting systems involved in emotional states.

title: Cardiac glycosides inhibit TNF-α/NF-κB signaling by blocking recruitment of TNF receptor-associated death domain to the TNF receptor
text: Digitoxin and other cardiac glycoside drugs potently obstruct the activation of the TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway. Our hypothesis is that this mechanism may be uncovered by systematically searching for selective inhibitory action throughout the entire pathway. We report that these drugs consistently block the TNF-α-dependent binding of TNF receptor 1 to TNF receptor-associated death domain. This drug action can be observed in native cells, such as HeLa, and in reconstituted systems prepared in HEK293 cells. In turn, this initial upstream signaling event appears to be the root cause of all other anti-inflammatory effects of digitoxin on NF-κB and c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways.

title: Zinc supplementation during lactation: effects on maternal status and milk zinc concentrations.
text: The impact of a zinc supplement on the zinc status of lactating women and their milk zinc concentrations was investigated over a period of at least 7 months. Seventy-one lactating women were randomly assigned to receive either a daily 15-mg zinc supplement (ZS group, n = 40) or a placebo (NZS group, n = 31). The study was double-blind and the participants' zinc intakes were monitored. The overall mean zinc intake for the NZS group was 13.0 +/- 3.4 mg/day, while the ZS group had a mean intake of 25.7 +/- 3.9 mg/day (including the supplement). The plasma zinc concentrations of the ZS group were significantly higher than those of the NZS group (P = 0.05). However, milk zinc concentrations did not change significantly over the course of the study for either group. The study found that a daily zinc supplement of 15 mg can increase the plasma zinc concentrations of lactating women, but it did not affect milk zinc concentrations. The study suggests that a dietary zinc intake of at least 13 mg/day is sufficient to maintain normal maternal zinc status and milk zinc concentrations through at least 7 months of lactation. Further studies are needed to determine the impact of lower zinc intakes on milk zinc concentrations in less well-nourished populations.

title: DMSO as a vehicle for central injections: tests with feeding elicited by norepinephrine injected into the paraventricular nucleus.
text: Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is gaining popularity as a vehicle for central injections, particularly for solubilizing substances that are insoluble in water. The aim of the present study was to investigate whether the vehicle used for solubilization (75% DMSO and 25% artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF)) affects the well-established stimulatory response to norepinephrine (NE) injected into the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) over short-term food intake. To evaluate its suitability, we compared the effects of repeated unilateral injections of NE dissolved in two different vehicles (100% aCSF or 75% DMSO, 25% aCSF) in separate groups of animals every 48 hours over a 30-day period. NE (40 nmol) significantly increased food intake by approximately sevenfold compared to either vehicle alone, and the stimulatory effect was similar regardless of whether aCSF or 75% DMSO was used as a vehicle. Moreover, the NE-induced feeding did not vary in magnitude across multiple tests. These findings suggest that 75% DMSO is a suitable vehicle for administering NE (and likely other water-insoluble substances) in small volumes (0.3 microl) into specific brain regions.

title: Dodecameric structure and ATPase activity of the human TIP48/TIP49 complex.
text: TIP48 and TIP49 are two highly conserved eukaryotic AAA(+) proteins that play an essential role in various cellular pathways, including those linked to cancer. These proteins are found in multiple highly conserved chromatin-modifying complexes together with other proteins. While they share some sequence similarity with the bacterial RuvB protein, the mechanisms and nature of their biochemical function remain unknown. To investigate their activity, recombinant human TIP48 and TIP49 were assembled into a stable high molecular mass complex and tested for ATPase activity in vitro. The results showed that TIP48/TIP49 complex formation resulted in a synergistic increase in ATPase activity, but no stimulation of ATP hydrolysis was observed in the presence of single-stranded, double-stranded, or four-way junction DNA, nor could any DNA helicase or branch migration activity be detected. The presence of catalytic defects in either TIP48 or TIP49 completely abolished ATPase activity, indicating that both proteins within the complex are essential for ATP hydrolysis. The structure of the TIP48/TIP49 complex was further investigated using negative stain electron microscopy, which revealed that the complex consisted of two stacked hexameric rings with C6 symmetry. Interestingly, TIP48 formed oligomers in the presence of adenine nucleotides, while TIP49 did not. These findings suggest that there may be biochemical differences between TIP48 and TIP49, which could be important for their specialized functions.

title: Associations between work-related factors and specific disorders of the shoulder--a systematic review of the literature.
text:
Objective:
Our study aimed to conduct a quantitative assessment of the relationships between work-related physical and psychosocial factors and the occurrence of specific shoulder disorders in occupational populations.
Methods:
We conducted a systematic review of the literature to investigate the associations between work factors and the occurrence of tendinitis of the biceps tendon, rotator cuff tears, subacromial impingement syndrome (SIS), and suprascapular nerve compression. We used odds ratio (OR) or relative risk (RR) to quantify the associations between work factors and shoulder disorders.
Results:
Our findings showed that the occurrence of SIS was associated with work factors such as force requirements exceeding 10% of maximum voluntary contraction (MVC), lifting weights greater than 20 kg more than 10 times per day, and high levels of hand force usage for more than 1 hour per day (OR 2.8-4.2). Repetitive movements of the shoulder, repetitive motion of the hand/wrist for more than 2 hours per day, hand-arm vibration, and working with the hand above shoulder level also showed an association with SIS (OR 1.04-4.7). Additionally, upper-arm flexion exceeding 45 degrees for more than 15% of the time or duty cycle of forceful exertions exceeding 9% of time or duty cycle of forceful pinch were also associated with SIS (OR 2.43). High psychosocial job demands were also linked to SIS (OR 1.5-3.19). Jobs in the fish processing industry had the highest risk for both tendinitis of the biceps tendon and SIS (OR 2.28 and 3.38, respectively). Work in a slaughterhouse and as a betel pepper leaf culler were associated with the occurrence of SIS only (OR 5.27 and 4.68, respectively). None of the included articles described the association between job title/risk factors and the occurrence of rotator cuff tears or suprascapular nerve compression.

title: Altered TCR signaling from geometrically repatterned immunological synapses.
text: The immunological synapse, a specialized cell-cell junction characterized by large-scale spatial patterns of receptors and signaling molecules, has remained largely mysterious in terms of its formation and function. To shed light on this enigmatic process, we employed supported bilayer membranes and nanometer-scale structures fabricated on the underlying substrate to impose geometric constraints on immunological synapse formation. By analyzing the resulting alternatively patterned synapses, we discovered a direct relationship between the radial position of T cell receptors (TCRs) and signaling activity, with prolonged signaling from TCR microclusters that had been mechanically trapped in the peripheral regions of the synapse. These findings support a model of the synapse in which the spatial translocation of TCRs serves as a direct mechanism of signal regulation.

title: Molecular regulation of histone H3 trimethylation by COMPASS and the regulation of gene expression.
text: The Set1-containing complex COMPASS, which shares homology with the human MLL complex, plays a crucial role in the mono-, di-, and trimethylation of lysine 4 on histone H3. To further elucidate the function of COMPASS in histone trimethylation, we conducted a comprehensive global proteomic screen. Our findings indicate that both Cps60 and Cps40 components of COMPASS are essential for proper histone H3 trimethylation, but not for the regulation of telomere-associated gene silencing. Interestingly, purified COMPASS lacking Cps60 can mono- and dimethylate histone H3, but is unable to trimethylate it. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) analysis revealed that the loss of COMPASS subunits required for histone trimethylation does not affect the localization of Set1 to chromatin for the genes examined. These results suggest a molecular requirement for multiple components of COMPASS for proper histone H3 trimethylation and regulation of telomere-associated gene expression, highlighting the diverse roles of different forms of histone methylation mediated by COMPASS.

title: Mitosis-specific anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes by pericentrin controls spindle organization and mitotic entry.
text:
Centrosomes play a crucial role in microtubule nucleation, with centrosomal microtubule nucleation primarily mediated by gamma tubulin ring complexes (gamma TuRCs). However, little is known about the molecules that anchor these complexes to centrosomes. This study investigated the role of the centrosomal coiled-coil protein pericentrin in anchoring gamma TuRCs at spindle poles.
Our findings show that pericentrin silencing in somatic cells disrupts gamma tubulin localization and spindle organization during mitosis, but has no effect on gamma tubulin localization or microtubule organization in interphase cells. Overexpression of the GCP2/3 binding domain of pericentrin also disrupts the endogenous pericentrin-gamma TuRC interaction and perturbs astral microtubules and spindle bipolarity. When added to Xenopus mitotic extracts, this domain uncouples gamma TuRCs from centrosomes, inhibits microtubule aster assembly, and induces rapid disassembly of preassembled asters. These phenotypes were significantly reduced in a pericentrin mutant with diminished GCP2/3 binding and were specific to mitotic centrosomal asters.
Furthermore, pericentrin silencing or overexpression induced G2/antephase arrest followed by apoptosis in many but not all cell types. These results suggest that pericentrin anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes at centrosomes in mitotic cells is essential for proper spindle organization, and that loss of this anchoring mechanism triggers a checkpoint response that prevents mitotic entry and leads to apoptotic cell death.
In summary, this study provides evidence that pericentrin plays a crucial role in anchoring gamma tubulin complexes at centrosomes during mitosis, and that disruption of this anchoring mechanism leads to a checkpoint response that prevents mitotic entry and triggers apoptotic cell death.

title: High levels of viral replication contrast with only transient changes in CD4(+) and CD8(+) cell numbers during the early phase of experimental infection with simian immunodeficiency virus SIVmnd-1 in Mandrillus sphinx.
text: Early stages of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections are believed to reflect the host's ability to control the infection. To investigate this, we studied early virus and host parameters during the early phase of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIVmnd-1) infection in its natural host, the mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx). Four mandrills were experimentally infected with a primary SIVmnd-1 strain derived from a naturally infected mandrill, while two non-infected control animals were monitored in parallel. Blood and lymph nodes were collected at three time points before infection, twice a week during the first month, and at days 60, 180, and 360 post-infection (p.i.). Antibodies against SIVmnd-1 were detected starting from day 28 to 32 p.i., but neither elevated temperature nor increased lymph node size were observed. The viral load in plasma peaked between days 7 to 10 p.i. (2 x 10(6) to 2 x 10(8) RNA equivalents/ml), then decreased 10- to 1,000-fold, reaching the viral set point between days 30 to 60 p.i. The levels during the chronic phase of infection were similar to that in the naturally infected donor mandrill (2 x 10(5) RNA equivalents/ml). CD4(+) cell numbers and percentages in blood and lymph nodes decreased slightly (<10%) during primary infection, and CD8(+) cell numbers increased transiently. All values returned to pre-infection levels by day 30 p.i. However, CD8(+) cell numbers or percentages in peripheral blood and lymph nodes did not increase during the 1-year follow-up period. Our findings suggest that SIVmnd-1 has the capacity for rapid and extensive replication in mandrills, but CD4(+) and CD8(+) cell numbers remained stable in the post-acute phase of infection, raising questions about the susceptibility of mandrill T cells to activation and/or cell death in response to SIVmnd-1 infection in vivo.

title: Vascular endothelial growth factor stimulates bone repair by promoting angiogenesis and bone turnover.
text: Throughout the process of fracture repair, various growth factors are expressed in distinct temporal and spatial patterns. Of these, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) stands out due to its ability to induce neovascularization, or angiogenesis. To determine the role of VEGF in bone repair, we experimentally inhibited its activity during two different types of fracture healing: secondary bone healing in a cartilage intermediate (endochondral ossification) and direct bone repair (intramembranous ossification) in a novel mouse model. Our findings showed that treatment with a soluble, neutralizing VEGF receptor decreased angiogenesis, bone formation, and callus mineralization in femoral fractures. Inhibition of VEGF also significantly hindered healing of a tibial cortical bone defect, which supports our discovery of a direct autocrine role for VEGF in osteoblast differentiation. In separate experiments, exogenous VEGF enhanced blood vessel formation, ossification, and new bone (callus) maturation in mouse femur fractures, and promoted bony bridging of a rabbit radius segmental gap defect. Our results at specific time points during the course of healing highlight the role of VEGF in endochondral versus intramembranous ossification, as well as skeletal development versus bone repair. The responses to exogenous VEGF observed in two distinct model systems and species suggest that a slow-release formulation of VEGF, applied locally at the site of bone damage, may prove to be a viable therapy to promote human bone repair.

title: Psychiatric comorbidity in chronic daily headache.
text: According to clinical evidence, chronic daily headaches (CDH) are often associated with psychological disorders. Previous studies have primarily focused on migraines, but our study aimed to evaluate this association more comprehensively. We analyzed a population of 88 patients (18 males and 70 females) with CDH (mean duration of 7.4 ± 8.7 years) using the DSM-IIIR criteria. We found that psychiatric disorders were present in a staggering 90% of this population. The most common diagnosis was a comorbidity of anxiety and mood disorders. This comorbidity has significant implications for treatment approaches.

title: An Expanded Oct4 Interaction Network: Implications for Stem Cell Biology, Development, and Disease
text: The transcription factor Oct4 plays a pivotal role in maintaining the stem cell identity of embryonic cells and reprogramming them towards a pluripotent state. Understanding the molecular interactions that govern Oct4's function is crucial for elucidating the mechanisms underlying pluripotency and development. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of Oct4-binding proteins in mouse embryonic stem cells and identified a significantly expanded set of proteins associated with Oct4. Our findings reveal that Oct4 interacts with a diverse range of proteins, including transcriptional regulators and modulators of its function. Notably, half of these proteins are transcriptionally regulated by Oct4 or other stem cell transcription factors, while one-third exhibit altered expression upon cell differentiation. Interestingly, most of the Oct4-associated proteins identified to date display an early lethal phenotype when mutated, underscoring the critical role of Oct4 in maintaining cell viability. Furthermore, a subset of human orthologs of these proteins have been implicated in inherited developmental disorders or cancer, highlighting the potential of the Oct4 interactome as a resource for uncovering mechanisms of pluripotency and development, as well as identifying additional reprogramming factors.

title: Reproductive and lifestyle determinants of anti-Müllerian hormone in a large population-based study.
text:
The article discusses the influence of reproductive and lifestyle factors on anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) levels in a large population-based cohort of premenopausal women. The study aimed to investigate the role of these factors on AMH levels, which are increasingly used as a prognostic and diagnostic tool in clinical practice.
The study included 2,320 premenopausal women from the general community participating in the Doetinchem Cohort study. The researchers calculated age-specific AMH percentiles using general linear modeling with the Cole and Green, Lambda, Mu, and Sigma (CG-LMS) method. They found that women who currently used oral contraceptives (OCs), had menstrual cycle irregularity, or were pregnant had significantly lower age-specific AMH percentiles compared to women with a regular menstrual cycle. However, age at menarche and age at first childbirth were not associated with AMH levels. Higher parity was associated with 2 percentiles higher age-specific AMH percentiles.
The study also investigated the association between lifestyle factors and AMH levels. Current smoking was found to be associated with 4 percentiles lower age-specific AMH percentiles, regardless of smoking dose. However, body mass index, waist circumference, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, and socioeconomic status were not significantly associated with AMH levels.
The study's findings suggest that several reproductive and lifestyle factors are associated with AMH levels, and these effects may be reversible. The study highlights the importance of considering these factors when interpreting AMH levels in a clinical setting and basing patient management on AMH.

title: Primary care and health insurance among women released from New York City jails.
text: In a study conducted among 511 women released from jail in New York City between 1997 and 2001, researchers examined the factors associated with primary care utilization and health insurance coverage. One year after release, approximately half of the sample reported primary care utilization (47%) and health insurance coverage (56%). The study found that neither having diabetes, asthma, or depression increased the likelihood of primary care utilization or health insurance coverage. Instead, factors such as receiving public benefits, having health insurance coverage, moderate social support, avoiding illegal activities, and being HIV seropositive were associated with higher rates of primary care utilization. Additionally, health insurance coverage was found to be associated with receipt of public benefits, hospitalization, primary care, and avoiding re-arrest. These findings suggest that a majority of women leaving jail, including those with chronic diseases, lack access to primary care. The study highlights the need for continuity of care from corrections to the community and suggests that providing health benefits and social support can help facilitate this.

title: The effects of prion protein proteolysis and disaggregation on the strain properties of hamster scrapie.
text: Native mammalian prions are composed of self-propagating strains that display distinct clinical, pathological, and biochemical characteristics. Despite the association between prion strain diversity and variations in the conformational structure of the PrP(Sc) molecule, the specific physical properties of the PrP(Sc) molecules required to encode mammalian prion strain phenotypes remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of proteinase K digestion or sonication on prion-infected brain homogenates from three different hamster scrapie strains, and inoculated the modified samples into normal hamsters. Our results show that the strain-specific clinical features and neuropathological profiles of inoculated animals were not affected by either treatment. Similarly, the strain-dependent biochemical characteristics of the PrP(Sc) molecules, including electrophoretic mobility, glycoform composition, conformational stability, and susceptibility to protease digestion, were unchanged by either proteolysis or sonication of the original inocula. These findings suggest that the infectious strain properties of native prions are not altered by PrP(Sc) disaggregation, and that maintenance of such properties does not rely on the N-domain (residues 23-90) of the protease-resistant PrP(Sc) molecules or protease-sensitive PrP(Sc) molecules.

title: Methylation of histone H3 lysine-79 by Dot1p plays multiple roles in the response to UV damage in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: Various proteins have been found to play roles in both the repair of UV-damaged DNA and heterochromatin-mediated silencing in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Specifically, factors involved in the methylation of lysine-79 on histone H3 by Dot1p have been implicated in both processes, suggesting a bipartite function for this modification. Our findings show that a dot1 null mutation and a histone H3 point mutation at lysine-79 result in increased sensitivity to UV radiation, indicating that lysine-79 methylation is crucial for efficient repair of UV damage. Epistasis analysis with various UV repair genes reveals that lysine-79 methylation plays overlapping roles in the nucleotide excision, post-replication, and recombination repair pathways, as well as RAD9-mediated checkpoint function. In contrast, epistasis analysis with a histone H3 lysine-79 point mutation suggests that this allele disrupts a specific subset of lysine-79 methylation functions within the nucleotide excision and post-replication repair pathways. These findings indicate the existence of distinct and separable roles of histone H3 lysine-79 methylation in the response to UV damage, potentially coordinating the various repair processes.

title: Unmet need for personal assistance with activities of daily living among older adults.
text:
This study investigated the prevalence, correlates, and negative consequences of unmet need for personal assistance with activities of daily living (ADLs) among older adults.
METHODS: The authors analyzed cross-sectional data from the 1994 National Health Interview Survey's Supplement on Aging. The data were weighted to be representative of the noninstitutionalized population aged 70 years and older.
RESULTS: Overall, 20.7% of individuals who required help with 1 or more ADLs reported receiving inadequate assistance. The prevalence of unmet need varied across individual ADLs, ranging from 10.2% (eating) to 20.1% (transferring). Lower household income, multiple ADL difficulties, and living alone were associated with a higher likelihood of having unmet needs. Nearly half of those with unmet needs reported experiencing negative consequences, such as being unable to eat when hungry, as a result of their unmet need.
IMPLICATIONS: These findings suggest that greater, targeted efforts are needed to reduce the prevalence and consequences of unmet need for ADL assistance in elderly persons.

title: Multi-stage chemical carcinogenesis in mouse skin: Fundamentals and applications
text: For over 60 years, researchers have used the chemical induction of tumors in mouse skin to investigate the mechanisms of epithelial carcinogenesis and evaluate modifying factors. In the traditional two-stage skin carcinogenesis model, the initiation phase involves applying a sub-carcinogenic dose of a carcinogen to the skin, followed by repeated treatments with a tumor-promoting agent to elicit tumor development. This process can be completed within 1-3 hours, depending on the number of mice used. The promotion phase requires twice weekly treatments (1-2 hours) and weekly tumor palpation (1-2 hours) for the duration of the study. Using this protocol, a highly reproducible papilloma burden is expected within 10-20 weeks, with a portion of the tumors progressing to squamous cell carcinomas within 20-50 weeks. In contrast to complete skin carcinogenesis, the two-stage model allows for a greater yield of premalignant lesions, as well as separation of the initiation and promotion phases.

title: Preventing deaths by drowning in children in the United Kingdom: have we made progress in 10 years? Population based incidence study.
text: Detailed information on drowning in children is rarely collected by national statistics offices. Few studies have been conducted in the United Kingdom, and none have focused on British children abroad. In 1988-9, two authors (AMK and JRS) combined data from national statistical offices, police forces, and a press cutting service to conduct a comprehensive analysis of drowning deaths in children. This analysis found that 149 children drowned in the United Kingdom during 1998-9. The analysis also identified a safety agenda, which focused on young children in garden ponds and pools and older children swimming without supervision. Over the past 10 years, there have been various initiatives aimed at improving children's safety in water, particularly through swimming programs. To determine whether these efforts have resulted in any changes, we obtained similar data for 1998-9.

title: Hypoxic heterogeneity in human tumors: EF5 binding, vasculature, necrosis, and proliferation.
text: We investigated the levels and distribution of hypoxia in 31 human tumors using fluorescent immunohistochemical detection of binding by the 2-nitroimidazole, EF5. Hypoxia was found to be a heterogeneous property of human tumors, with necrosis often occurring adjacent to areas of high EF5 binding within an individual patient's tumor. However, hypoxia can occur independently of necrosis. In the tumors studied, the most common relationship between blood vessels (PECAM/CD31) and EF5 staining was consistent with diffusion-limited hypoxia, with acute hypoxia occurring infrequently. Within a given patient's tumor, there was an inverse correlation between regions of proliferation (Ki-67) and regions of hypoxia. However, the absence of proliferation does not predict the presence of hypoxia in a given patient. The relationships between hypoxia and other biological endpoints are complex, but within a given tumor's spatial relationships, they are in accordance with known physiological principles. Therefore, our data emphasize that the relationships between hypoxia and other biological parameters vary between patients. Necrosis, proliferation, and blood vessel distribution cannot predict the level or presence of hypoxia in an individual patient's tumor.

title: The Sp1-like protein BTEB3 inhibits transcription via the basic transcription element box by interacting with mSin3A and HDAC-1 co-repressors and competing with Sp1.
text: Sp1-like proteins are characterized by three conserved C-terminal zinc finger motifs that bind to GC-rich sequences in the promoters of essential genes for mammalian cell homeostasis. These proteins act as either transcriptional activators or repressors, although the mechanisms of repression for Sp1-like repressors are less understood. In this study, we investigate the functional characterization of BTEB3, a ubiquitously expressed Sp1-like transcriptional repressor. Our results show that the N-terminal region of BTEB3 contains repressor domains that can act directly on target genes. We also find that BTEB3 interacts with the co-repressor mSin3A and the histone deacetylase protein HDAC-1. Using gel shift assays, we demonstrate that BTEB3 specifically binds to the BTE site, a well-characterized GC-rich DNA element, with an affinity similar to that of Sp1. Furthermore, we show that BTEB3 can also mediate repression by competing with Sp1 for BTE binding in Chinese hamster ovary cells. Our findings expand the repertoire of BTEB-like members of the Sp1 family involved in transcriptional repression and suggest a mechanism of repression involving direct repression by the N-terminal region of BTEB3 through interaction with mSin3A and HDAC-1, as well as competition with Sp1 via the DNA-binding domain.

title: Perceptual limits in a simulated "Cocktail party".
text: In a series of experiments, the ability of listeners to accurately judge the number of talkers in simultaneous conversations was examined. In each experiment, listeners were asked to report the number of talkers they heard, with the number varying from 1 to 13. The experiments manipulated various factors, including the spatial location of the talkers (1 or 6 locations), the duration of the talker voices (0.8 seconds, 5.0 seconds, and 15.0 seconds), and the gender arrangement of the talkers (mixed or same gender). The results showed that the proportion of correct numerosity judgments decreased as the number of talkers increased, with perceptual limits (the number of talkers at which the proportion of correct judgments is 0.5) ranging from 3 to 5 talkers depending on the listening conditions. The results also showed that average response times for numerosity judgments increased monotonically over a range of one to four talkers. These findings suggest that listeners perceptually segregate talkers before counting them to make numerosity judgments, and that the functional auditory world for simultaneous voices may consist of no more than three to five talkers in most listening situations. The study discusses possible causes for these perceptual limits.

title: The MOS social support survey.
text: This paper outlines the development and evaluation of a brief, multidimensional, self-administered social support survey designed for patients in the Medical Outcomes Study (MOS), a two-year study of individuals with chronic conditions. The survey aimed to comprehensively capture recent thinking on various dimensions of social support. To achieve this, the survey was carefully crafted to differentiate itself from other related measures. The authors present a summary of the key conceptual issues considered when selecting items for the social support battery, describe the items, and provide findings based on data from 2987 patients aged 18 and older. Multitrait scaling analyses supported the dimensionality of four functional support scales (emotional/informational, tangible, affectionate, and positive social interaction) and the construction of an overall functional social support index. These support measures differ from structural measures of social support and related health measures, and exhibit strong reliability (all Alphas greater than 0.91) and stability over time. Additionally, selected construct validity hypotheses were supported.

title: Can hematological parameters discriminate malaria from nonmalarious acute febrile illness in the tropics?
text: Background: Malaria is a leading differential diagnosis for acute fever in tropical regions, and alterations in hematological parameters have been observed in patients with malaria. Objective: To determine if specific hematological parameters can increase the likelihood of malaria in patients with acute fever. Methods: Prospective cohort study of consecutive patients with fever of less than 7 days duration at a hospital. Exclusion criteria included patients with a known localizing cause for fever. Hematological parameters (hemoglobin, red blood cell distribution width (RDW), leukocyte count, and platelet count) were measured using automated counters, and peripheral smear examination was used as the gold standard for malaria diagnosis. Statistical analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of these parameters. Results: A total of 184 patients were included, and 70 (38%) had a positive peripheral smear for malarial parasites. Thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 150,000/mm3) was a significant predictor of malaria (sensitivity 60%, specificity 88%, LR+ 5.04), and when combined with anemia (Hb < 10 g/dl), it was the next best parameter (sensitivity 69%, specificity 74%, LR+ 2.77). RDW and leukocyte count were not predictive. Conclusion: The presence of thrombocytopenia in a patient with acute fever increases the probability of malarial infection.

title: 14q deletions are associated with trisomy 12, NOTCH1 mutations and unmutated IGHV genes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma.
text: Deletions of the long arm of chromosome 14 (del(14q)) are uncommon but frequently observed in mature B-cell neoplasms, particularly in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). To further elucidate this aberration, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of 81 cases with del(14q), including 54 CLL and 27 SLL patients, the largest reported series to date. Using karyotype and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), we identified the most common additional abnormalities, which were trisomy 12 (tri12) in 28/79 (35%) cases, followed by del13q14 in 12/79 (15%), delTP53 in 11/80 (14%), delATM in 5/79 (6%), and del6q21 in 3/76 (4%). The IGHV genes were unmutated in 41/53 (77%) patients, with a high frequency of IGHV1-69 (21/52, 40%). NOTCH1 gene mutations were detected in 14/45 (31%) patients. Our findings revealed no significant differences in cytogenetic and molecular abnormalities between CLL and SLL. Using FISH and SNP-array analysis, we observed the heterogeneity of 14q deletions, but a distinct group of patients with the same del(14)(q24.1q32.33) was identified in 48% of cases. In this subgroup, tri12 and NOTCH1 mutations were significantly more frequent than in the remaining patients. The median treatment-free survival (TFS) in CLL patients with del(14q) was 27 months. In conclusion, del(14q) is associated with tri12 and pejorative prognostic factors, including unmutated IGHV genes (with over-representation of the IGHV1-69 repertoire), NOTCH1 mutations, and short TFS.

title: Rapid DNA methylation changes after exposure to traffic particles.
text:
RATIONALE: Exposure to particulate air pollution has been linked to increased hospitalization and mortality, particularly due to cardiovascular disease. Lower levels of DNA methylation have been observed in genes related to cardiovascular outcomes, such as oxidative stress, aging, and atherosclerosis.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate whether exposure to particulate air pollution affects DNA methylation in heavily methylated regions of the human genome.
METHODS: We measured DNA methylation levels of long interspersed nucleotide element (LINE)-1 and Alu repetitive elements in 1,097 blood samples from 718 elderly participants in the Boston area Normative Aging Study. We used covariate-adjusted mixed models to account for within-subject correlation in repeated measures. We estimated the effect of ambient particulate pollutants (black carbon, particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 microm [PM2.5], or sulfate) on DNA methylation in multiple time windows (4 hours to 7 days) before the examination. We calculated standardized regression coefficients (β) representing the fraction of a standard deviation change in DNA methylation associated with a standard deviation increase in exposure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Repetitive element DNA methylation showed variability in association with time-related variables, such as day of the week and season. LINE-1 methylation decreased after recent exposure to higher levels of black carbon (β = -0.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.18 to -0.04; P = 0.002) and PM2.5 (β = -0.13; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.06; P < 0.001 for the 7-day moving average). In two-pollutant models, only black carbon, a tracer of traffic particles, was significantly associated with LINE-1 methylation (β = -0.09; 95% CI, -0.17 to -0.01; P = 0.03). No association was found with Alu methylation (P > 0.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that exposure to traffic particles is associated with decreased methylation of repetitive elements in the human genome. Further research is needed to determine whether this decrease in methylation mediates the adverse health effects of air pollution exposure.

title: Incidence of adverse drug events and potential adverse drug events. Implications for prevention. ADE Prevention Study Group.
text:
Objective:
To determine the incidence and preventability of adverse drug events (ADEs) and potential ADEs in hospitalized patients.
Design: Prospective cohort study.
Participants: All 4031 adult admissions to a stratified random sample of 11 medical and surgical units in two tertiary care hospitals over a 6-month period.
Main Outcome Measures: Adverse drug events and potential ADEs.
Methods: Incidents were detected through stimulated self-report by nurses and pharmacists and daily review of all charts by nurse investigators. Incidents were classified as ADEs or potential ADEs based on severity and preventability, and were subsequently reviewed by two independent reviewers.
Results: Over 6 months, 247 ADEs and 194 potential ADEs were identified, resulting in an extrapolated event rate of 6.5 ADEs and 5.5 potential ADEs per 100 non-obstetrical admissions. Of these, 1% were fatal and 12% life-threatening, with 30% being serious and 57% significant. Twenty-eight percent of ADEs were judged preventable. Of the life-threatening and serious ADEs, 42% were preventable, compared to 18% of significant ADEs. Errors resulting in preventable ADEs occurred most often at the stages of ordering (56%) and administration (34%), with transcription (6%) and dispensing errors (4%) being less common. Errors were more likely to be intercepted if they occurred earlier in the process, with 48% of errors being intercepted at the ordering stage and 0% at the administration stage.
Conclusion: Adverse drug events were common and often preventable, with most resulting from errors at the ordering stage. However, many errors also occurred at the administration stage. Prevention strategies should target both stages of the drug delivery process.

title: Induction of galactokinase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: kinetics of induction and glucose effects.
text: The study investigated the synthesis of galactokinase in whole yeast cells, specifically examining the effects of different carbon sources on induction. The researchers found that the response of uninduced cells to galactose was dependent on the type of carbon source used to grow the cells prior to exposure to galactose. Cells grown on glucose had a delayed response to galactose, while cells grown on lactate exhibited induced synthesis within 8 minutes. The optimal concentration for induction was found to be 0.5% galactose. The addition of glucose to yeast cultures growing on galactose resulted in a temporary repression of synthesis, followed by a resumed rate of synthesis characteristic of a weaker, permanent catabolite repression. The study also showed that 2-deoxygalactose and fucose did not act as inducers or substrates for galactokinase.

title: Gene--nutrition interactions in coronary artery disease: correlation between the MTHFR C677T polymorphism and folate and homocysteine status in a Korean population.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Elevated levels of plasma total homocysteine have been identified as a significant risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Methyltetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is a key enzyme involved in homocysteine metabolism, and a common mutation in the MTHFR gene, specifically the C677T allele, has been associated with increased homocysteine levels and decreased folate levels. In this study, we aimed to investigate the frequency of the MTHFR C677T allele in a Korean population, determine the genotype-specific threshold levels of folate or vitamin B12 required to maintain normal homocysteine levels, and evaluate the relationship between the TT genotype and the risk of CAD.
MATERIALS AND METHODS
We recruited a total of 163 CAD patients and 50 healthy control subjects for this study. The MTHFR C677T polymorphism was genotyped using real-time PCR with melting point analysis. Plasma homocysteine, folate, and vitamin B12 levels were also measured. We defined the genotype-specific threshold values of folate and vitamin B12 required to maintain normal homocysteine levels for individuals of each MTHFR C677T genotype.
RESULTS
Our findings revealed that the frequency of the TT genotype was significantly higher in the patient group (26%) compared to the control group (18%) (P<0.05). Individuals homozygous for the TT genotype had significantly elevated homocysteine levels compared to the CC or CT genotypes (P<0.05). The genotype-specific folate threshold level was significantly higher in TT individuals than in the CC or CT genotypes. The odds ratio (OR) of individuals with low folate status and the TT genotype to estimate the relative risk of CAD was 2.2, and the OR of those with high folate status and the TT genotype was 1.5 (95% CI, 0.5-9.6 and 0.7-3.2, respectively).
CONCLUSION
Our study demonstrates a gene-nutrient interaction where individuals with the TT genotype require higher folate levels to maintain normal homocysteine levels. These findings suggest that a higher risk of CAD may be associated with specific threshold folate levels required by different MTHFR C677T genotypes in a Korean population.

title: Human bone marrow adipocytes block granulopoiesis through neuropilin-1-induced granulocyte colony-stimulating factor inhibition.
text: Adipocytes, a component of the hematopoietic microenvironment, have been subject to debate regarding their role in hematopoiesis. Previous studies have shown that the accumulation of fat cells in the femoral bone marrow (BM) is associated with increased expression of neuropilin-1 (NP-1). In contrast, NP-1 expression is relatively low in hematopoietic iliac crest BM. Based on these observations, we hypothesized that adipocytes may exert a negative effect on hematopoiesis through NP-1. To investigate this, we established a BM adipocyte model differentiated into fibroblast-like fat cells (FLFCs), which share similarities with primitive unilocular fat cells. Our findings revealed that FLFCs constitutively produce macrophage colony stimulating factor and induce CD34(+) cell differentiation into macrophages independently of cell-to-cell contact. However, granulopoiesis was inhibited by cell-to-cell contact, but could be restored in transwell culture conditions, along with granulocyte colony stimulating factor production. Both functions were also recovered when FLFCs were cultured in contact with CD34(+) cells and treated with an antibody neutralizing NP-1, which confirmed its critical role in contact inhibition. The modulation of FLFC properties by inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1 beta or dexamethasone also restored granulopoiesis. Our study provides the first evidence that primary adipocytes play a regulatory role in hematopoiesis, which may be implicated in certain pathological processes. Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest can be found at the end of this article.

title: The transcriptome profile of human embryonic stem cells as defined by SAGE.
text: Human embryonic stem (ES) cell lines with the capacity to self-renew and differentiate into specific cell types have been developed. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes are still poorly understood. To investigate, we analyzed the transcriptome profiles of two proprietary human ES cell lines (HES3 and HES4, ES Cell International) and compared them to those of murine ES cells and other human tissues. Our findings revealed both similarities and differences between human and mouse ES cells, including an inactive leukemia inhibitory factor pathway and a higher expression of genes such as POU5F1 and SOX2 in human ES cells. We identified a list of genes that are specifically expressed in human ES cells, including known ES-specific genes and new candidates that could serve as markers for human ES cells and contribute to their "stemness" phenotype. Notably, we found that the expression of DNMT3B and LIN28 mRNAs is downregulated during ES cell differentiation. The similarities and differences in gene expression profiles between human and mouse ES cells provide a foundation for a detailed and concerted analysis of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying their pluripotency, directed differentiation into specific cell types, and extended ability for self-renewal.

title: Small-molecule antagonists of p53-MDM2 binding: research tools and potential therapeutics.
text: The tumor suppressor protein p53 plays a crucial role in protecting normal tissues from the development of tumors, which can arise from various forms of stress. In the absence of stress, p53's growth suppressive and pro-apoptotic activity is inhibited by MDM2, which binds to p53 and negatively regulates its activity and stability. Recently, researchers have identified potent and selective low molecular weight inhibitors of MDM2-p53 binding, known as Nutlins. These molecules activate the p53 pathway and suppress tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, representing valuable new tools for studying the p53 pathway and its defects in cancer. Notably, Nutlins induce p53-dependent apoptosis in human cancer cells but remain cytostatic towards proliferating normal cells, suggesting that MDM2 antagonists may have clinical utility in treating tumors with wild-type p53. The potent activity of Nutlins against osteosarcoma xenografts further supports the potential of MDM2 antagonists as a cancer treatment approach.

title: Slipped (CTG)•(CAG) repeats can be correctly repaired, escape repair or undergo error-prone repair
text: The expansion of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats, a underlying cause of 14 or more diseases, is believed to arise from the improper repair of slipped DNA. We investigated the fidelity of slipped-DNA repair in human cell extracts and DNA samples with slip-outs of (CAG)20 or (CTG)20. Our findings revealed three possible outcomes: correct repair, escaped repair, and error-prone repair. The choice of repair path depended on the location of the nick and the composition of the slip-out (CAG or CTG). We also detected a new form of error-prone repair, where excess repeats were incompletely excised, leading to the generation of expansions but not deletions. Neuron-like cell extracts showed each of the three repair outcomes, suggesting that these processes play a role in (CTG)•(CAG) instability in patient post-mitotic brain cells. Our findings also indicate that MMR and NER proteins, such as hMSH2, hMSH3, hMLH1, XPF, XPG, and polymerase β, are not essential for the instability of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats, suggesting that their role in this process may occur before or independently of slip-out processing. The differential processing of slipped repeats may explain the differences in mutation patterns between various disease loci or tissues.

title: High Dub3 expression in mouse ESCs couples the G1/S checkpoint to pluripotency.
text: The molecular mechanism underlying the bypass of the G1/S checkpoint in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) remains unexplored. DNA damage inhibits the entry into S phase by CDK2 kinase, which is destroyed by its activator, Cdc25A phosphatase. Surprisingly, we discovered high levels of Cdc25A in G1 phase in mouse ESCs, which persist even after DNA damage. Additionally, we found elevated expression of Dub3, a deubiquitylase that regulates Cdc25A protein abundance. Interestingly, we discovered that the Dub3 gene is a direct target of Esrrb, a key transcription factor involved in the self-renewal machinery. Our findings indicate that Dub3 expression is downregulated during neural conversion, preceding Cdc25A destabilization. Moreover, forced expression of Dub3 in ESCs leads to lethality upon differentiation, concurrent with cell-cycle remodeling and lineage commitment. Finally, knockdown of either Dub3 or Cdc25A triggers spontaneous differentiation of ESCs. These findings integrate the self-renewal machinery with cell-cycle control through a deubiquitylase in ESCs.

title: Paracrine effects of direct intramyocardial implantation of bone marrow derived cells to enhance neovascularization in chronic ischaemic myocardium.
text:
Objective: To determine the optimal bone marrow (BM) cell types and their potential mechanisms of action for promoting neovascularization in chronic ischaemic myocardium.
Methods: In a swine model of chronic ischaemic myocardium, the functional effects, angiogenic potential, and cytokine expression of direct intramyocardial implantation of autologous BM CD31-positive endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs), BM mononuclear cells (MNCs), and saline were compared. Autologous BM cells were harvested and catheter-based electromechanical mapping-guided direct intramyocardial injection was performed to target ischaemic myocardium. After 12 weeks, cardiac function, capillary density, and mRNA expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and angiopoietin-2 were evaluated.
Results: Injection of BM-MNCs resulted in significant improvements in left ventricular dP/dt, left ventricular pressure, and regional microsphere myocardial perfusion over ischaemic endocardium and epicardium compared to BM-EPCs and saline. Capillary density and VEGF mRNA expression in ischaemic myocardium were significantly greater in the BM-MNC group than the saline group. The capillary density in ischaemic myocardium demonstrated a significant positive correlation with VEGF expression.
Conclusion: Catheter-based direct intramyocardial injection of BM-MNCs enhanced angiogenesis more effectively than BM-EPCs or saline, possibly via a paracrine effect, with increased expression of VEGF that subsequently improved cardiac performance of ischaemic myocardium.

title: Endogenous miRNA sponge lincRNA-RoR regulates Oct4, Nanog, and Sox2 in human embryonic stem cell self-renewal.
text: The regulatory circuitry controlling embryonic stem cell (ESC) transcription and epigenetics is complex, involving multiple layers of control. Core transcription factors (TFs), posttranscriptional modifier microRNAs (miRNAs), and other regulators all play a role. However, the function of large intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) in this circuitry and their underlying mechanisms are still unknown. Here, we investigate the role of a lincRNA, linc-RoR, in this regulatory network. We find that linc-RoR may function as a key competing endogenous RNA, linking the network of miRNAs and core TFs, such as Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog. linc-RoR shares miRNA-response elements with these core TFs and prevents them from being suppressed by miRNAs. This feedback loop between linc-RoR, core TFs, and miRNAs regulates ESC maintenance and differentiation. These findings provide new insights into the interactions between genetic components during development and may lead to new therapies for many diseases.

title: Foxp3(+) T cells regulate immunoglobulin a selection and facilitate diversification of bacterial species responsible for immune homeostasis.
text: Foxp3(+) T cells play a crucial role in maintaining immune tolerance by promoting the diversification and selection of gut microbiota. In mice, these cells contribute to the expansion of beneficial bacteria, particularly those belonging to the Firmicutes phylum. The control of indigenous bacteria by Foxp3(+) T cells involves both regulatory functions outside and inside germinal centers (GCs), including the suppression of inflammation and regulation of immunoglobulin A (IgA) selection in Peyer's patches. The diversified and selected IgAs help maintain a balanced and diverse microbiota, which in turn supports the expansion of Foxp3(+) T cells, the induction of GCs, and IgA responses in the gut through a symbiotic regulatory loop. This process demonstrates the adaptive immune system's role in mediating host-microbial symbiosis by controlling the richness and balance of bacterial communities required for homeostasis.

title: The isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding phospholipid-specific inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase.
text: In this study, we report the cloning and characterization of a novel human inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase (5-phosphatase), designated as type IV. Unlike previously described members of this gene family, which hydrolyze water-soluble inositol phosphates, this enzyme specifically targets lipid substrates, including phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate. The cDNA isolated comprises 3110 base pairs and encodes a protein product of 644 amino acids with a molecular mass (M(r)) of 70,023. We found that type IV 5-phosphatase is a highly basic protein (pI = 8.8) with the highest affinity towards phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate among known 5-phosphatases, with a Ki value of 0.65 micrometer, which is approximately 1/10 that of SHIP (5.95 micrometer). The enzyme activity is sensitive to the presence of detergents in the in vitro assay, with the enzyme hydrolyzing lipid substrates in the absence of detergents or in the presence of n-octyl beta-glucopyranoside or Triton X-100, but not in the presence of cetyltriethylammonium bromide. Interestingly, SHIP, a previously characterized 5-phosphatase that hydrolyzes only substrates with d-3 phosphates, also showed activity towards phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the presence of n-octyl beta-glucopyranoside, but not cetyltriethylammonium bromide. Using antibodies raised against a peptide predicted by the cDNA, we were able to identify the type IV 5-phosphatase enzyme in human tissues and found high levels of expression in the brain, as determined by Western blotting. We also detected expression in the brain, testes, and heart, as well as lower levels of expression in other tissues, in both human and mouse tissues using Western blotting. mRNA was also detected in many tissues and cell lines using Northern blotting.

title: Lack of Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) expression in tumor cells is closely associated with poor survival in colorectal cancer patients.
text: Functional studies on colorectal cancer cells have suggested that the interferon-inducible DNA sensor Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) plays a protective role in cancer progression. Previous studies found that a high mutation rate and low AIM2 expression were present in a subset of colorectal cancers. To investigate the association between AIM2 expression in tumor cells and patient prognosis, we analyzed a tissue microarray of 476 matched tissue pairs (colorectal tumor and adjacent normal colon epithelium) from 62 patients. Our results showed that 279 (67.4%) of the tumor samples had reduced AIM2 expression compared to their normal counterparts. Thirty-eight patients (9.18%) had completely lost AIM2 expression in their tumor cells. After adjusting for various factors, including sex, age, cancer stage, tumor site, tumor grade, and chemotherapy, we found that complete lack of AIM2 expression was associated with a 3-fold increase in overall mortality (HR=2.40, 95% CI=1.44-3.99) and disease-specific mortality (HR=3.14, 95% CI=1.75-5.65) compared to AIM2-positive tumor samples. Our findings strongly suggest that lack of AIM2 expression is associated with poor outcome in colorectal cancer. These results provide evidence that AIM2 may be a useful biomarker for identifying colorectal cancer patients with poor prognosis. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to determine the potential therapeutic implications of AIM2 expression in colorectal cancer.

title: VSL#3 probiotic upregulates intestinal mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase and reduces inflammation.
text:
Background: Alkaline sphingomyelinase, an enzyme found exclusively in the bile and intestinal brush border, hydrolyzes sphingomyelin into ceramide, sphingosine, and sphingosine-1-phosphate, leading to epithelial apoptosis. Decreased levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase have been observed in premalignant and malignant intestinal epithelial tissues and in ulcerative colitis tissue. Probiotic bacteria, such as VSL#3, have the potential to increase sphingomyelinase levels.
Objective: To investigate the effect of VSL#3 probiotic therapy on mucosal levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase in both a mouse model of colitis and in patients with ulcerative colitis.
Methods: Interleukin-10 gene-deficient (IL10KO) mice and wild-type control mice were treated with VSL#3 (10(9) colony-forming units per day) for three weeks, after which alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was measured in ileal and colonic tissue. Additionally, 15 patients with ulcerative colitis were treated with VSL#3 (900 billion bacteria twice daily for five weeks). Alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was measured through biopsies, and disease activity index scores were compared before and after treatment.
Results: Lowered alkaline sphingomyelinase levels were observed in the colon and ileum of IL10KO mice compared to controls. Treatment of these mice with VSL#3 resulted in upregulation of mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity in both the colon and ileum. VSL#3 treatment of human patients with ulcerative colitis led to a significant decrease in mean (+/- SEM) ulcerative colitis disease activity index scores from 5.3+/-1.8946 to 0.70+/-0.34 (P=0.02) and an increase in mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity.
Conclusion: Mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity is reduced in the intestine of IL10KO mice with colitis and in humans with ulcerative colitis. VSL#3 probiotic therapy upregulates mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity, suggesting a potential therapeutic role for probiotics in the treatment of inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: Nodal/Activin signaling predicts human pluripotent stem cell lines prone to differentiate toward the hematopoietic lineage.
text: The differentiation potential of human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) varies among different lines, making it crucial to identify which lines have the highest potential for a specific lineage. In this study, we compared the hematopoietic potential of 14 hESC/induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines and observed significant differences in their ability to differentiate into blood cells. While some lines showed good blood differentiation potential, others had limited capacity. Correlation studies revealed that the colony-forming unit (CFU) potential robustly correlated with hemogenic progenitors and primitive blood cells, but not mature blood cells. Microarray analysis showed distinct gene expression profiles between hPSCs with good and poor hematopoietic potential, with downregulation of neuroectoderm-associated genes and upregulation of Nodal/Activin signaling in the former. Loss- and gain-of-function functional assays confirmed that Nodal/Activin signaling predicts hPSC lines with good hematopoietic differentiation potential. Our findings reinforce the importance of prospective comparative studies to determine lineage-specific differentiation potential among different hPSCs and highlight the potential of Nodal/Activin signaling as a predictive marker for hematopoietic differentiation.

title: Addition of a Gastrointestinal Microbiome Modulator to Metformin Improves Metformin Tolerance and Fasting Glucose Levels.
text:
BACKGROUND: Adverse effects of metformin, such as gastrointestinal (GI) intolerance, can limit the dose of the medication or cause patients to discontinue it altogether. Some of these side effects may be due to changes in the GI microbiome. To investigate whether a GI microbiome modulator (GIMM) could alleviate these side effects, we conducted a study in which patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who experienced GI intolerance to metformin were given either GIMM or placebo in combination with metformin.
METHODS: We used a 2-period crossover study design with 2 treatment sequences. In the first period, patients took 500 mg of metformin along with either GIMM or placebo, and in the second period, they took 500 mg of metformin t.i.d. (three times a day) with either GIMM or placebo. Patients were allowed to discontinue metformin if they experienced intolerable side effects. We measured the tolerance to metformin and fasting glucose levels during both periods.
RESULTS: The combination of metformin and GIMM resulted in significantly better tolerance to metformin than the placebo combination (6.78 ± 0.65 vs. 4.45 ± 0.69, P = .0006). Fasting glucose levels were also significantly lower with the metformin-GIMM combination (121.3 ± 7.8 mg/dl) compared to the metformin-placebo combination (151.9 ± 7.8 mg/dl, P < .02).
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that combining a GI microbiome modulator with metformin may allow for greater use of this medication in T2D patients and improve treatment of the disease.

title: Diverse tumorigenic pathways in ovarian serous carcinoma.
text: In this study, we aimed to investigate genetic alterations in 108 sporadic serous ovarian neoplasms to gain insights into the mechanisms of ovarian serous carcinogenesis. Our findings reveal that approximately 50% of serous borderline tumors (SBTs), non-invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas (MPSCs), and invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas harbor K-ras mutations, indicating a morphological continuum of tumor progression. Moreover, we observed a progressive increase in the degree of allelic imbalance of chromosomes 1p, 5q, 8p, 18q, 22q, and Xp across different tumor types, with high-grade (conventional serous carcinoma) tumors showing a high frequency of allelic imbalance even in small (early) primary tumors. Based on these findings, we propose a dualistic model for ovarian serous carcinogenesis, involving two distinct pathways: one involving a stepwise progression from SBT to non-invasive and invasive MPSC, and the other characterized by rapid progression from the ovarian surface epithelium or inclusion cysts to a conventional (high-grade) serous carcinoma.

title: Tissue-inherent fate of GPI revealed by GPI-anchored GFP transgenesis.
text: To investigate the fate of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) in mammals, we created a fusion protein consisting of enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) and GPI. We introduced this protein into cultured cells and observed that it was correctly sorted to plasma membranes and microsomes based on GPI biosynthesis. Transgenic mice carrying the EGFP-GPI fusion protein showed widespread expression of the transgene. Histological analysis revealed a distinctive polarized localization of the EGFP-GPI protein in various epithelial tissues, including the nervous system, liver, and exocrine glands, as well as non-polarized presence in non-epithelial tissues. This study provides insight into the tissue-specific sorting of GPI in mammals.

title: Essential role for the SANT domain in the functioning of multiple chromatin remodeling enzymes.
text: The SANT domain is a novel motif discovered in various eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory proteins, which was identified due to its similarity to the DNA binding domain of c-myb. Our study reveals that the SANT domain is crucial for the in vivo functions of yeast Swi3p, Ada2p, and Rsc8p, components of three distinct chromatin remodeling complexes. Additionally, we find that the Ada2p SANT domain is essential for the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity of native, Gcn5p-containing HAT complexes. Furthermore, our kinetic analyses suggest that an intact SANT domain is necessary for an Ada2p-dependent enhancement of histone tail binding and enzymatic catalysis by Gcn5p. Our results support a general role for SANT domains in interacting with histone N-terminal tails, leading to functional consequences.

title: Mechanisms of pancreatic beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: many differences, few similarities.
text: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes are characterized by progressive beta-cell failure, with apoptosis being the primary form of beta-cell death in both conditions. While the mechanisms of beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes share some similarities, there are also significant differences. In type 1 diabetes, invading immune cells produce cytokines such as IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IFN-gamma, which induce beta-cell apoptosis through the activation of beta-cell gene networks controlled by transcription factors NF-κB and STAT-1. These cytokines lead to the production of nitric oxide (NO) and chemokines, as well as the depletion of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) calcium, ultimately resulting in the execution of beta-cell death through activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases, ER stress, and the release of mitochondrial death signals. In contrast, chronic exposure to elevated levels of glucose and free fatty acids (FFAs) in type 2 diabetes causes beta-cell dysfunction and may induce beta-cell apoptosis through different mechanisms. While high glucose initially triggers "glucose hypersensitization," it can later induce apoptosis through mechanisms that are distinct from those in type 1 diabetes. High glucose does not activate IL-1beta, NF-κB, or inducible nitric oxide synthase in beta-cells, suggesting that different pathways are involved in the death of beta cells in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Similarly, FFAs may cause beta-cell apoptosis through ER stress, which is NF-κB and NO independent. These findings argue against a unifying hypothesis for the mechanisms of beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes and suggest that different approaches may be needed to prevent beta-cell death in each condition.

title: Health-related quality of life among children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text: The study aimed to evaluate the health-related quality of life (HRQL) of children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and identify specific areas for improvement. The study included two groups: ALL patients aged 5 and older participating in a multi-center clinical trial, and a general population control group. HRQL was assessed using the Health Utilities Index Mark 2 (HUI2) and Mark 3 (HUI3) during all four phases of active treatment and approximately 2 years after treatment. The results showed that HRQL scores increased from induction through the post-treatment phase, but there were no significant demographic or treatment effects on HRQL except for the type of asparaginase used during continuation therapy. Compared to controls, patients lost approximately 0.2 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) during active treatment, with disability evident in mobility/ambulation, emotion, self-care, and pain. The study suggests that new treatment protocols are needed to reduce disabilities in these areas without compromising survival.

title: JUVENILE MORTALITY INCREASES WITH CLUTCH SIZE IN A NEOTROPICAL BIRD
text: The variation in avian clutch size with latitude is a well-known example of geographic variation in a vertebrate life-history trait, with tropical birds typically having smaller clutches than birds from higher latitudes. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this pattern, including nest predation, limited food availability for nestlings, and post-fledging juvenile mortality. To test these hypotheses, we manipulated the clutch size of Spotted Antbirds (Hylophylax naevioides) in central Panama. Our results showed that parental activity at nests and the ability of parents to feed nestlings in larger broods were not factors that influenced nest predation or post-fledging mortality. While larger broods produced the most fledged juveniles, these individuals were less likely to survive to dispersal than juveniles from smaller broods. Consequently, nest productivity did not vary with clutch size. Instead, differences in the allocation of parental investment per juvenile among differently sized broods appeared to influence juvenile survival probability. These findings suggest that parental care during the post-fledging period may play a crucial role in shaping the evolution of small clutch size in tropical birds.

title: Diagnosis of rotator cuff tears.
text: Rotator cuff tears are responsible for nearly half of all significant shoulder injuries, yet they can be challenging to diagnose. To address this issue, we conducted a prospective study comparing the results of 23 clinical tests from 400 patients with and without rotator cuff tears. Our findings revealed that three simple tests are highly predictive of rotator cuff tears: supraspinatus weakness, weakness in external rotation, and impingement. When all three of these tests are positive, or if two tests are positive and the patient is 60 years or older, the likelihood of a rotator cuff tear is 98%. Conversely, the absence of these features eliminates the possibility of a rotator cuff tear diagnosis.

title: Increased susceptibility to UV-induced skin carcinogenesis in polymerase eta-deficient mice.
text: XPV patients with mutations in the DNA polymerase eta (Pol eta) gene are highly sensitive to sunlight and have a heightened risk of developing skin cancer due to their inability to efficiently repair UV light-induced DNA damage. In contrast, Pol eta-deficient mice are viable and fertile, but exhibit increased sensitivity to UV light-induced killing and mutagenesis. Fibroblasts derived from these mice are also more susceptible to UV light-induced killing. Notably, all Pol eta-deficient mice develop skin tumors after UV irradiation, whereas wild-type littermate controls do not. These findings, along with biochemical studies of translesion synthesis by mouse Pol eta, suggest that Pol eta-dependent bypass of cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers can suppress UV light-induced skin cancer in mice. Furthermore, 37.5% of Pol eta heterozygous mice also developed skin cancer after 5 months of UV light exposure, indicating that individuals who are heterozygous for Pol eta mutations may also have an increased risk of skin cancer.

title: Hydrogen sulfide interacts with nitric oxide in the heart: possible involvement of nitroxyl.
text:
The present study aims to investigate the interaction between nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S), two important gaseous mediators, in rat hearts. The study employed intracellular calcium measurement using Fura-2 and myocyte contractility measurement with a video edge system to investigate the effects of H2S on NO-induced changes in myocyte contraction.
The results showed that H2S had no significant effect on the resting calcium level or myocyte contractility in isolated cardiomyocytes. However, stimulating endogenous NO production with l-arginine or exogenous application of NO donors decreased myocyte twitch amplitudes accompanied by slower velocities of both cell contraction and relaxation. Interestingly, H2S reversed the negative inotropic and lusitropic effects of these NO-increasing agents. Furthermore, the mixture of sodium nitroprusside (SNP) and H2S increased, whereas SNP alone decreased, the resting calcium level and the amplitudes of electrically induced calcium transients. The study also showed that three thiols (N-acetyl-cysteine, l-cysteine, and glutathione) abolished the effects of H2S on myocyte contraction. Finally, the study found that the effects of H2S were cAMP/PKA- or cGMP/PKG-independent, suggesting a novel mechanism of action.
In conclusion, the study suggests that H2S may interact with NO to form a thiol-sensitive molecule (probably HNO) that produces positive inotropic and lusitropic effects. These findings may provide new insights into the interaction of NO and H2S and shed light on potential therapeutic strategies for cardiovascular diseases.

title: A novel mechanism of rapid nuclear neutrophil extracellular trap formation in response to Staphylococcus aureus.
text: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are web-like structures composed of DNA and antimicrobial molecules that play a crucial role in the innate immune response. Previous studies have shown that NETs form through an oxidant-dependent process that requires the death of neutrophils, taking around 3-4 hours to develop. In this study, we discovered a novel mechanism of NET formation that does not involve neutrophil lysis or breach of the plasma membrane. Instead, the multilobular nucleus rapidly condenses and separates into vesicles, which are filled with nuclear DNA and extruded into the extracellular space.
