Conclusion: Overall, most tests for rotator cuff pathology were inaccurate and cannot be recommended for clinical use. At best, suspicion of a rotator cuff tear may be heightened by a positive palpation, combined Hawkins/painful arc/infraspinatus test, Napoleon test, lift-off test, belly-press test, or drop-arm test, and it may be reduced by a negative palpation, empty can test, or Hawkins-Kennedy test.

title: Skeletal muscle interleukin‐6 regulates metabolic factors in iWAT during HFD and exercise training
text:
Objective: To investigate the role of skeletal muscle interleukin-6 (SkM IL-6) in the regulation of adipose tissue metabolism.
Methods: Muscle-specific IL-6 knockout (IL-6 MKO) and IL-6 (loxP/loxP) (Floxed) mice were subjected to a standard rodent diet (Chow), high-fat diet (HFD), or HFD in combination with exercise training (HFD ExTr) for 16 weeks.
Results: Total fat mass increased in both genotypes with HFD, but HFD IL-6 MKO mice had lower inguinal adipose tissue (iWAT) mass than HFD Floxed mice. Additionally, iWAT glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) protein content, 5'AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) (Thr172) phosphorylation, and fatty acid synthase (FAS) mRNA content were lower in IL-6 MKO than Floxed mice on Chow. Furthermore, iWAT AMPK (Thr172) and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) (Ser565) phosphorylation, as well as perilipin protein content, was higher in HFD IL-6 MKO than HFD Floxed mice, and pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α (PDH-E1α) protein content was higher in HFD ExTr IL-6 MKO than HFD ExTr Floxed mice.
Conclusions: These findings suggest that SkM IL-6 affects iWAT mass through the regulation of glucose uptake capacity as well as lipogenic and lipolytic factors.

title: Risk of hospitalization or death from ischemic heart disease among British vegetarians and nonvegetarians: results from the EPIC-Oxford cohort study.
text: Background: Few previous studies have investigated the association between a vegetarian diet and incident ischemic heart disease (IHD) risk. Objective: To examine the relationship between a vegetarian diet and the risk of incident (nonfatal and fatal) IHD in a large prospective cohort study. Design: A total of 44,561 men and women from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)-Oxford study, of whom 34% consumed a vegetarian diet at baseline, were included in the analysis. Incident IHD cases were identified through linkage with hospital records and death certificates. Serum lipids and blood pressure measurements were available for 1519 non-cases, who were matched to IHD cases by sex and age. The association between vegetarian status and IHD risk was estimated using multivariate Cox proportional hazards models. Results: After an average follow-up of 11.6 years, there were 1235 IHD cases (1066 hospital admissions and 169 deaths). Compared to non-vegetarians, vegetarians had a lower mean body mass index (BMI) (-1.2 kg/m(2); 95% CI: -1.3, -1.1), non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentration (-0.45 mmol/L; 95% CI: -0.60, -0.30), and systolic blood pressure (-3.3 mm Hg; 95% CI: -5.9, -0.7). Vegetarians had a 32% lower risk of IHD (HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.58, 0.81) compared to non-vegetarians, which was only slightly attenuated after adjustment for BMI and did not differ materially by sex, age, BMI, smoking, or the presence of IHD risk factors. Conclusion: Consuming a vegetarian diet was associated with lower IHD risk, a finding that is likely mediated by differences in non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and systolic blood pressure.

title: The Supporting Independent Immunization and Vaccine Advisory Committees (SIVAC) initiative: a country-driven, multi-partner program to support evidence-based decision making.
text: The need for evidence-based decision making in immunization programs is heightened by multiple health priorities, limited human resources, and logistical capacities, as well as the cost of expensive vaccines and limited funds. The Supporting Independent Immunization and Vaccine Advisory Committees (SIVAC) Initiative aims to support countries in establishing or strengthening National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) that provide recommendations on immunization policies and programs, such as vaccination schedules, improving routine immunization coverage, and introducing new vaccines. SIVAC, a program funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, takes a country-driven, step-by-step approach that is tailored to each country's needs and emphasizes the sustainability of NITAGs. SIVAC provides support to NITAGs by reinforcing their scientific and technical secretariat and offering specific activities that are developed in consultation with the country and other international partners. Additionally, SIVAC has created an electronic platform, the NITAG Resource Center, which provides information, tools, and briefings to NITAGs and the immunization community.

title: Redox-relevant aspects of the extracellular matrix and its cellular contacts via integrins.
text:
The extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a crucial role in multicellular organisms, providing a mechanical scaffold and environmental cues to cells. Upon cell attachment, the ECM signals into the cells through reactive oxygen species (ROS) physiologically used as signaling molecules. Recent advances have shown that ECM attachment influences ROS production in cells, which in turn affects the production, assembly, and turnover of the ECM during wound healing and matrix remodeling. Abnormalities in ROS levels lead to excess ECM production and increased tissue contraction in fibrotic disorders and desmoplastic tumors.
Integrins are cell adhesion molecules that mediate cell adhesion and force transmission between cells and the ECM. Redox-regulation of integrins has been identified, with cysteine-based redox modifications affecting integrin binding activity. In a molecular model, long-range disulfide bridges within the integrin β-subunit and disulfide bridges within the genu and calf-2 domains of the integrin α-subunit may control the transition between the bent/inactive and upright/active conformation of the integrin ectodomain. These thiol-based intramolecular cross-linkages occur in the stalk domain of both integrin subunits, while the ligand-binding integrin headpiece is apparently unaffected by redox-regulation.
Understanding the underlying mechanism of redox-regulation of integrins may provide new prospects for the treatment of fibrotic disorders. Future directions may involve investigating the role of redox-regulation in other cellular processes and exploring the potential of targeting redox-regulation in disease treatment.

title: Prevalence of hypertension and pre-hypertension among adolescents.
text:
Objective: To determine the prevalence of hypertension and pre-hypertension among adolescents based on the 2004 National High Blood Pressure Education Program Working Group guidelines using a school-screening population.
Study Design: Cross-sectional assessment of blood pressure (BP) in 6790 adolescents (11-17 years) in Houston schools from 2003 to 2005. Initial measurements included height, weight, and 4 oscillometric BP readings. Repeat measurements were obtained on students with persistently elevated BP. Final prevalence was adjusted for loss to follow-up, and logistic regression was used to assess risk factors.
Results: BP distribution at initial screen was 81.1% normal, 9.5% pre-hypertension, and 9.4% hypertension (8.4% Stage 1; 1% Stage 2). After 3 screenings, prevalence was 81.1% normal, 15.7% pre-hypertension, and 3.2% hypertension (2.6% Stage 1; 0.6% Stage 2). Hypertension and pre-hypertension increased with increasing body mass index. Sex, race, and classification as either at-risk for overweight or overweight were independently associated with pre-hypertension. Only classification as overweight was associated with hypertension.
Conclusions: Application of new classification guidelines for adolescents with elevated BP reveals approximately 20% are at risk for hypertension. Further research is needed to determine the significance of each BP category and to refine definitions to account for BP variability.

title: Increased short- and long-term risk of inflammatory bowel disease after salmonella or campylobacter gastroenteritis.
text:
Background and Aims:
The etiology of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) is complex and involves the interplay of genetic and environmental factors. Commensal enteric and potentially pathogenic bacteria may play a role in the pathogenesis of IBD. This study aimed to investigate the association between Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis and the risk of developing IBD in a population-based cohort.
Methods:
We conducted a cohort study in North Jutland and Aarhus counties, Denmark, from 1991 to 2003. We identified 13,324 patients with Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis from laboratory registries and 26,648 age- and gender-matched unexposed controls. The study cohort included 176 exposed patients with IBD before the infection, 352 unexposed controls with IBD, and 80 unexposed individuals without IBD. The final study cohort consisted of 13,148 exposed and 26,216 unexposed individuals, who were followed up for a maximum of 15 years (mean, 7.5 years).
Results:
A first-time diagnosis of IBD was observed in 107 exposed individuals (1.2%) and 73 unexposed individuals (0.5%). By age, gender, and comorbidity-adjusted Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, the hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) for IBD was 2.9 (2.2-3.9) for the entire study period and 1.9 (1.4-2.6) if the first year after the Salmonella/Campylobacter infection was excluded. The increased risk of IBD was observed throughout the 15-year observation period and was similar for Salmonella and Campylobacter infections and for first-time diagnoses of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
Conclusions:
Our population-based cohort study found an increased risk of IBD in individuals notified in laboratory registries with an episode of Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis. These findings suggest that commensal enteric and potentially pathogenic bacteria may play a role in the pathogenesis of IBD. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

title: Establishment of a cell line (NPC/HK1) from a differentiated squamous carcinoma of the nasopharynx.
text: A long-term cell culture of epithelioid cells was established from a recurrent squamous carcinoma of the nasopharynx of a Chinese male, who had received radiation therapy 17 years and 6 months prior to the establishment of the cell line. The cell line, designated NPC/HK1, has been passaged 72 times over a period of 1 year. Microscopic examination of the cells revealed them to be of the squamous epithelial type. When the cells were subcutaneously transplanted into the backs of athymic nude BALB/c (nu/nu) mice, tumors developed at the sites of inoculation, which upon histological examination were found to be well-differentiated squamous carcinomas, similar in morphology to the recurrent human tumor from which they were derived. Karyotypic analysis of the cells revealed an aneuploid human karyotype with a modal chromosome number of 74, along with both numerical and structural chromosomal aberrations. The presence of viral particles or Epstein-Barr viral nuclear antigen (EBNA) was not demonstrated in the cells from the primary culture or several of the subcultures tested. Infection of subcultured cells with EBV from P3HR1 and B95-8 cells was also unsuccessful.

title: Effect of lipid restriction on mitochondrial free radical production and oxidative DNA damage.
text: Numerous studies have demonstrated that a 40% reduction in caloric intake (caloric restriction) leads to a decrease in mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in rodents. Recently, we discovered that 7 weeks of 40% protein restriction without significant caloric restriction also lowers ROS levels in rat liver. This is intriguing, as it has been reported that protein restriction can extend lifespan in rodents. In the current study, we investigated the potential role of dietary lipids in the effects of caloric restriction on mitochondrial oxidative stress. Using semipurified diets, we reduced lipid intake by 40% in male Wistar rats compared to controls, while maintaining the same levels of other dietary components. After 7 weeks of treatment, liver mitochondria from lipid-restricted animals showed increased oxygen consumption with complex I-linked substrates (pyruvate/malate and glutamate/malate). Additionally, we found that neither mitochondrial H(2)O(2) production nor oxidative damage to mitochondrial or nuclear DNA was altered in lipid-restricted animals. However, mitochondrial DNA damage was found to be approximately 10 times higher than nuclear DNA damage in both dietary groups. These results suggest that lipids do not play a significant role in the decrease in mitochondrial ROS production and DNA damage caused by caloric restriction, and instead reinforce the possible role of dietary proteins in this process.

title: Kruppel-like factor 2 is a transcriptional regulator of chronic and acute inflammation.
text: Although myeloid cell activation is essential for an optimal innate immune response, it must be tightly regulated to prevent unintended damage to host tissues. Kruppel-like factor 2 (KLF2) plays a crucial role in regulating myeloid cell proinflammatory activation, and studies have shown that reduced KLF2 levels are associated with acute or chronic inflammatory disorders in humans. To investigate the role of KLF2 in inflammation, we studied the biological response to inflammation in KLF2-deficient mice. Our findings show that partial deficiency of KLF2 modulates the in vivo response to acute (sepsis) and subacute (skin) inflammatory challenges. We also uncovered that KLF2 inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity, providing mechanistic insights into its anti-inflammatory effects. These observations offer biologically relevant insights into KLF2-mediated modulation of inflammatory processes, which could potentially be exploited for therapeutic gain.

title: Simian immunodeficiency viruses replication dynamics in African non-human primate hosts: common patterns and species-specific differences.
text: METHODS: To identify potential common features of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections in different naturally infected host species, we compared the dynamics of viral replication in 31 African green monkeys (10 sabeus, 15 vervets, and seven Caribbean AGMs), 14 mandrills, and three sooty mangabeys (SMs) that were experimentally infected with their species-specific viruses. RESULTS: After infection, these SIVs replicated rapidly, reaching viral loads (VLs) of 105-109 copies/ml of plasma between days 9-14 post-infection (p.i.). A set point viremia was established between days 42 and 60 p.i., with levels of approximately 105-106 copies/ml in SM and mandrills, and lower levels (103-105 copies/ml) in AGMs. The VL during the chronic phase did not correlate with viral genome structure: SIVmnd-2 (a vpx-containing virus) and SIVmnd-1 (which does not contain vpu or vpx) replicated to similar levels in mandrills. VL was dependent on virus strain: vervets infected with three different viral strains showed different patterns of viral replication. The pattern of viral replication of SIVagm.sab, which uses both CCR5 and CXCR4 co-receptors, was similar to those of the other viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate a common pattern of SIV replication in naturally and experimentally infected hosts, similar to that observed in pathogenic SIV infection of macaques. This suggests that differences in clinical outcome between pathogenic and non-pathogenic infections rely on host responses rather than the characteristics of the virus itself.

title: The role of the transcription factor KLF2 in vascular development and disease.
text: The zinc finger transcription factor KLF2 converts the mechanical forces generated by blood flow into molecular signals that regulate a wide range of biological processes. Initially identified as a flow-sensitive endothelial transcription factor, KLF2 is now recognized as a ubiquitous factor that is expressed in various cell types and plays a crucial role in multiple physiological processes, including endothelial homeostasis, vasoregulation, vascular growth and remodeling, and inflammation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of KLF2's role in vascular biology.

title: Implementation of contemporary oral antiplatelet treatment guidelines in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a report from the GReek AntiPlatelet rEgistry (GRAPE).
text: The study aimed to assess the implementation of contemporary oral antiplatelet treatment guidelines in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The study, known as the Greek AntiPlatelet rEgistry (GRAPE), was a prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study that evaluated the appropriateness of P2Y12 inhibitor selection in 1434 patients. The study found that appropriate selection of P2Y12 inhibitors was initially made in 45.8% of patients and at discharge in 64.1%. The selection of clopidogrel was most commonly less preferable, both initially and at discharge. The study also found that the selection of newer agents was high initially, with a further increase at discharge. Inappropriate selection of the newer agents was 17.2%-20.8% initially, decreasing to 10.2%-10.6% at discharge. The study identified certain factors that predicted appropriate P2Y12 selection, including age ≥75 years, conditions and co-medications related to increased bleeding risk, and regional trends. The study concluded that adherence with the recently released guidelines on oral antiplatelet therapy was satisfactory, with clopidogrel being most commonly used as a less preferable selection, and prasugrel or ticagrelor selection being mostly appropriate.

title: Comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders in chronic daily headache and its subtypes.
text:
Objective: To investigate the frequency of depressive and anxiety disorders in patients with chronic daily headache.
Background: There is a lack of data in the literature on the extent of psychiatric comorbidity in patients with different subtypes of chronic daily headache.
Methods: We recruited consecutive patients with chronic daily headache seen in a headache clinic from November 1998 to December 1999. The subtypes of chronic daily headache were classified according to the criteria proposed by Silberstein et al. A psychiatrist evaluated the patients according to the structured Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview to assess the comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders.
Results: Two hundred sixty-one patients with chronic daily headache were recruited, with a mean age of 46 years and 80% being women. Transformed migraine was diagnosed in 152 patients (58%), and chronic tension-type headache in 92 patients (35%). Seventy-eight percent of patients with transformed migraine had psychiatric comorbidity, including major depression (57%), dysthymia (11%), panic disorder (30%), and generalized anxiety disorder (8%). Sixty-four percent of patients with chronic tension-type headache had psychiatric diagnoses, including major depression (51%), dysthymia (8%), panic disorder (22%), and generalized anxiety disorder (1%). The frequency of anxiety disorders was significantly higher in patients with transformed migraine after controlling for age and sex (P =.02). Both depressive and anxiety disorders were significantly more frequent in women.
Conclusion: Psychiatric comorbidity, especially major depression and panic disorders, was highly prevalent in patients with chronic daily headache seen in a headache clinic. These results demonstrate that women and patients with transformed migraine are at higher risk of psychiatric comorbidity.

title: The precursor form of IL-1alpha is an intracrine proinflammatory activator of transcription.
text: Although most cytokines are traditionally studied for their biological effects after binding to specific cell surface receptors, recent evidence suggests that some cytokines, such as IL-1alpha, may also function within the nucleus. In this study, we overexpressed the precursor form of IL-1alpha in various cells and evaluated its activity in the presence of saturating concentrations of IL-1 receptor antagonist to prevent receptor signaling. We found that IL-1alpha precursor translocated to the nucleus after activation by endotoxin, a Toll-like receptor ligand. The precursor form, but not the mature form, activated the transcriptional machinery in the GAL4 system by 90-fold, with a 50-fold increase observed using only the IL-1alpha propiece. This suggests that transcriptional activation is localized to the N terminus, where the nuclear localization sequence resides. Under conditions of IL-1 receptor blockade, intracellular overexpression of the precursor and propiece forms of IL-1alpha was sufficient to activate NF-κB and AP-1. Stable transfectants overproducing precursor IL-1alpha released the cytokines IL-8 and IL-6 and exhibited a lower threshold of activation to subpicomolar concentrations of tumor necrosis factor alpha or IFN-gamma. These findings suggest that intracellular functions of IL-1alpha may play an unforeseen role in the genesis of inflammation, and that reducing its intracellular functions might be beneficial in some inflammatory conditions.

title: Three-dimensional structure of the AAH26994.1 protein from Mus musculus, a putative eukaryotic Urm1.
text: Using NMR spectroscopy, we have determined the solution structure of protein AAH26994.1 from Mus musculus and propose that it represents the first three-dimensional structure of a ubiquitin-related modifier 1 (Urm1) protein. Amino acid sequence comparisons indicate that AAH26994.1 belongs to the Urm1 family of ubiquitin-like modifier proteins, which have only a weak sequence similarity to ubiquitin. Our findings suggest that ubiquitin and ubiquitin-related proteins may have evolved from a protein-based sulfide donor system of the molybdopterin synthase type, as the structure of AAH26994.1 shares a signature ubiquitin secondary structure fold with the structures of three bacterial MoaD proteins with 14%-26% sequence identity to AAH26994.1. However, the structures of AAH26994.1 and the MoaD proteins differ significantly from ubiquitin in regions outside of the fold, bolstering the hypothesis that ubiquitin and ubiquitin-related proteins have a distinct evolutionary origin.

title: Concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia: a Gynecologic Oncology Group study.
text: The aim of this study was to estimate the prevalence of concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH). The study included 306 women who underwent hysterectomy within 12 weeks of being diagnosed with AEH. The study pathologists reviewed the biopsy specimens and found that 25.6% of the specimens were diagnosed as less than AEH, 39.8% were diagnosed as AEH, and 29.1% were diagnosed as endometrial carcinoma. In 5.5% of the specimens, there was no consensus on the biopsy diagnosis. The rate of concurrent endometrial carcinoma was found to be 42.6%, with 30.9% of the carcinomas being myoinvasive and 10.6% involving the outer 50% of the myometrium. Among women who had hysterectomy specimens with carcinoma, 18.9% had a study panel biopsy consensus diagnosis of less than AEH, 39.1% had a consensus diagnosis of AEH, and 64.3% had a consensus diagnosis of carcinoma. Among women who had no consensus in their biopsy diagnosis, 62.5% had carcinoma in their hysterectomy specimens. These findings suggest that the prevalence of concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of AEH is high, and that clinicians and patients should consider this when making management decisions.

title: The prevalence and clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors in an English adult population.
text:
Background: This study aimed to investigate the clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors (smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, inadequate fruit and vegetable intake, and physical inactivity) among the English adult population, and to examine the variation in clustering across different socio-demographic groups.
Methods: The study population consisted of 11,492 individuals from the 2003 Health Survey for England. Clustering was analyzed by comparing observed and expected prevalence of different combinations of risk factors. A multinomial multilevel regression model was used to examine socio-demographic variations in clustering.
Results: The study found that, based on British health recommendations, a majority of the English population had multiple lifestyle risk factors simultaneously. Clustering was observed at both ends of the lifestyle spectrum, with more pronounced clustering among women than men. Multiple risk factors were more common among men, lower socioeconomic households, singles, and economically inactive individuals, but less common among homeowners and older age groups.
Conclusions: The clustering of multiple risk factors supports the use of multiple-behavior interventions rather than single-behavior interventions.

title: Cutting edge: interleukin 17 signals through a heteromeric receptor complex.
text: Interleukin-17 (IL-17) is a pro-inflammatory cytokine produced primarily by a distinct subset of CD4 T cells, which plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of various autoimmune diseases. The IL-17 receptor (IL-17RA) is ubiquitously expressed and essential for the biological activity of IL-17. However, the activity of IL-17 is primarily defined by its ability to induce the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and other mediators in stromal cells. Interestingly, mouse stromal cells lacking IL-17RA fail to respond to human IL-17RA, suggesting the presence of an obligate ancillary component whose activity is species-specific. This component is IL-17RC, a distinct member of the IL-17 receptor family. Therefore, the biological activity of IL-17 is dependent on a complex composed of IL-17RA and IL-17RC, which challenges the traditional understanding of the interactions between the expanding family of IL-17 ligands and their receptors.

title: Long non-coding RNAs with low expression levels in cells are enriched in secreted exosomes.
text:
Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play a crucial role in regulating various cellular processes, including chromatin modifications, gene transcription, mRNA translation, and protein function. Recently, we reported a significant variation in the basal expression levels of a panel of lncRNAs in HeLa and MCF-7 cells, and their differential response to DNA damage induction. Here, we hypothesized that lncRNA molecules with different cellular expression may have a differential abundance in secreted exosomes, and their exosome levels would reflect cellular response to DNA damage.
To investigate this, we characterized the expression of MALAT1, HOTAIR, lincRNA-p21, GAS5, TUG1, and CCND1-ncRNA in exosomes secreted from cultured cells. Our findings revealed a distinct expression pattern of lncRNAs in exosomes compared to cells, with RNA molecules with low expression levels (lincRNA-p21, HOTAIR, ncRNA-CCND1) showing a high enrichment in exosomes. TUG1 and GAS5 levels were moderately elevated in exosomes, while MALAT1, which was the most abundant molecule in cells, was present at levels comparable to its cellular levels. LincRNA-p21 and ncRNA-CCND1 were the main molecules, and their exosome levels best reflected the change in their cellular levels upon exposure of the cells to bleomycin-induced DNA damage.
Our findings provide conclusive evidence that lncRNAs have a differential abundance in exosomes, indicating a selective loading. This selective loading of lncRNAs in exosomes may play a crucial role in cellular communication and the response to DNA damage. These findings have important implications for our understanding of the mechanisms of lncRNA function and their role in various cellular processes.

title: Olanzapine depot exposure in male rats: Dose-dependent lipogenic effects without concomitant weight gain.
text:
Treatment with second-generation antipsychotic agents, such as olanzapine, frequently leads to metabolic adverse effects in both male and female patients, including hyperphagia, weight gain, and dyslipidemia. Despite extensive research, the molecular mechanisms underlying these metabolic side effects are still not fully understood. Animal studies, particularly in rodents, have been instrumental in exploring these mechanisms. However, a significant limitation of these studies is that antipsychotics induce weight gain in female rats but not male rats, which limits the validity of the rodent model.
Olanzapine, a long-acting antipsychotic, has been shown to yield clinically relevant plasma concentrations in female rats after a single intramuscular injection. In the current study, we investigated the effects of depot injections of olanzapine in male rats. Our results showed that clinically relevant plasma olanzapine concentrations were achieved in male rats as well, and surprisingly, olanzapine resulted in weight loss rather than weight gain. This was accompanied by a slight increase in thermogenesis markers in brown adipose tissue, although the mechanism behind the olanzapine-related weight loss remains unclear. Additionally, we found that olanzapine doses of 200mg/kg or higher led to significantly elevated plasma cholesterol levels and pronounced activation of lipogenic gene expression in the liver, indicating that olanzapine stimulates lipogenic effects independently of weight gain. These findings suggest that endocrine factors may play a role in the gender-specific metabolic effects of antipsychotics in the rat, highlighting the need for further research in this area.

title: Glutamate mediates the function of melanocortin receptor 4 on Sim1 neurons in body weight regulation.
text: The melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) is a well-established regulator of body weight homeostasis, yet the neurotransmitters that modulate its function remain largely unexplored, thereby limiting our understanding of the second-order neurons within the MC4R neural pathway. Specifically, the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH), which houses Sim1-expressing brain regions, plays a crucial role in mediating melanocortin action. To investigate the neurotransmitter(s) responsible for MC4R function, we conditionally restored MC4R expression in Sim1 neurons of Mc4r-null mice. Our findings demonstrated a dramatic reduction in obesity in these mice, which was completely reversed by selective disruption of glutamate release from the same Sim1 neurons. This reversal was accompanied by decreased energy expenditure and hyperphagia, corroborating previous studies that have shown selective disruption of glutamate release from adult PVH neurons leads to rapid obesity development through reduced energy expenditure and hyperphagia. Therefore, this study unequivocally establishes glutamate as the primary neurotransmitter mediating MC4R function within the Sim1 neurons of the body weight regulatory system.

title: Intracellular sterol dynamics.
text: In this study, we delve into the cellular mechanisms involved in cholesterol transport and distribution. Recent investigations have provided novel insights into the distribution of sterols within cells, including the analysis of their transbilayer distribution. The interaction between cholesterol and other lipids, as well as its engagement in various trafficking processes, determines its optimal concentration in a specific membrane, leading to an uneven distribution of cholesterol among intracellular organelles. Cholesterol plays a crucial role in membrane structure and function, as well as in various cellular events such as signal transduction and protein trafficking. The movement of cholesterol between cellular organelles is a dynamic process that can occur through both vesicular and non-vesicular mechanisms. Recent studies have shed light on the proteins involved in these processes, providing new information on the relative importance of these two trafficking pathways in cholesterol transport. Although still inadequately characterized in many cases, several potential sterol transport proteins have been described in detail, allowing us to begin to appreciate the molecular mechanisms underlying sterol transport among membranes.

title: A plasma membrane component able to bind and alter virions of poliovirus type 1: studies on cell-free alteration using a simplified assay.
text: Intact HeLa cells can bind and convert poliovirus type 1 virions into altered particles through incubation at 37°C. Altered particles have slower sedimentation rates, lack VP-4, and are disrupted by sodium dodecyl sulfate, but retain their RNA integrity. Using a simple assay procedure, the binding and alteration processes can be quantitatively measured. The binding-altering activity can be localized to plasma membranes, and pure membranes can be shown to carry out the alteration process. The membrane-bound activity is inhibited by proteases and nonionic detergents. Only altered particles are formed through membrane-bound processes, and RNA release is not caused by membranes but rather by intact cells. Binding and alteration are closely associated processes, and it is possible that alteration is a consequence of multiple receptor binding in a fluid membrane.

title: Resequencing studies of nonmodel organisms using closely related reference genomes: optimal experimental designs and bioinformatics approaches for population genomics.
text: The decreasing costs of next-generation sequencing (NGS) have made it possible to study a wide range of genomic questions in non-model organisms. However, the lack of genomic resources for these organisms presents a challenge in experimental design and analysis of NGS data. In this work, we investigate the performance of alternative experimental designs and bioinformatics approaches in estimating variability and neutrality tests based on the site-frequency-spectrum (SFS) from individual resequencing data. We specifically address the challenges faced in studying non-model organisms, including the absence of a species-specific reference genome, and compare the performance of three bioinformatics approaches: genotype calling, genotype-haplotype calling, and direct estimation without calling genotypes. Our results show that relying on genotype calls provides biased estimates of population genetic statistics at low to moderate read depth, while genotype-haplotype calling returns more accurate estimates regardless of the divergence to the reference genome. Direct estimation without calling genotypes returns the most accurate estimates of variability and SFS tests, including at low read depth. Our findings suggest that studies without a species-specific reference genome should aim for low read depth and avoid genotype calling whenever individual genotypes are not essential. Alternatively, aiming for moderate to high depth at the expense of the number of individuals, and using genotype-haplotype calling, may be recommended.

title: Thalassemia and malaria: new insights into an old problem.
text: The hemoglobinopathies are likely the most common genetic disorders worldwide, with the World Health Organization estimating that at least 5% of the population are carriers of one of the more severe forms, including alpha- and beta-thalassemias and structural variants hemoglobins S, C, and E, which are found at frequent mutations in many countries. These hemoglobinopathies are believed to offer protection against malaria, a theory first proposed 50 years ago by J.B.S. Haldane. Epidemiological studies conducted in the 1950s on hemoglobin S in Africa supported the "malaria hypothesis," but it has proven challenging to verify this theory for the thalassemias until recently. The application of molecular methods has provided new opportunities to investigate this old question. Population and molecular genetic analysis of thalassemia variants and microepidemiological studies of the relationship between alpha-thalassemia and malaria in the southwest Pacific have provided conclusive evidence for protection. Interestingly, some of this protection appears to stem from the enhanced susceptibility of very young thalassemic children to both Plasmodium falciparum and, particularly, P. vivax, and this early exposure may provide the basis for better protection in later life.

title: Endocrine control of spermatogenesis: Role of FSH and LH/ testosterone.
text:
Evaluation of testicular function, including the production of sperm and androgens, is a crucial aspect of preclinical safety assessment. Testicular toxicity is significantly more common than ovarian toxicity, and this chapter focuses on the histological changes that occur in the reproductive organs of rats, dogs, and nonhuman primates due to disturbances in reproductive endocrinology.
The chapter covers two main topics:
1. The histological sequelae of disturbed reproductive endocrinology in rat, dog, and nonhuman primates, including the effects on different types of germ cells and spermatogenic stages. It is noted that the end-stage spermatogenic involution is more pronounced in dog and primates compared to rodents.
2. A review of the current understanding of the roles of gonadotropins and androgens in testicular function, including the relative importance of luteinizing hormone (LH)/testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in quantitatively normal spermatogenesis, with a focus on the differences between rodents and primates.
Overall, the chapter highlights the importance of evaluating testicular function in preclinical safety assessments and provides a comprehensive overview of the endocrine factors that control testicular function in different species.

title: Extravasation injuries on regional neonatal units.
text: This study of regional neonatal intensive care units found that approximately 38 out of every 1000 newborns (38%) sustained an extravasation injury that led to skin necrosis. The majority of these injuries occurred in infants who were 26 weeks gestation or younger, and were caused by the administration of parenteral nutrition through intravenous cannulae. Treatment for these injuries typically involved exposing the wounds to air, infiltrating them with hyaluronidase and saline, and applying occlusive dressings.

title: Nonstructural protein 3-4A: the Swiss army knife of hepatitis C virus.
text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) nonstructural protein 3-4A (NS3-4A) is a complex composed of NS3 and its cofactor NS4A, which harbors both serine protease and NTPase/RNA helicase activities. This complex plays a crucial role in HCV replication, including polyprotein processing, RNA replication, and virion formation. Inhibitors of the NS3-4A protease have been shown to significantly improve sustained virological response rates in patients with chronic hepatitis C when combined with pegylated interferon-α and ribavirin. Additionally, NS3-4A has been found to target cellular proteins, interfering with innate immune pathways and growth factor signaling, contributing to the persistence and pathogenesis of HCV. This review provides an update on the biochemical and structural aspects of NS3-4A, its role in chronic hepatitis C, and the clinical development of NS3-4A protease inhibitors.

title: Phase 2 safety trial targeting amyloid beta production with a gamma-secretase inhibitor in Alzheimer disease.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, and amyloid beta (Aβ) response to the gamma-secretase inhibitor LY450139 in patients with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease.
Design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled trial.
Setting: Community-based clinical research centers.
Patients: Fifty-one individuals with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease were randomized to receive placebo (n=15) or LY450139 (100 mg [n=22] or 140 mg [n=14]), with 43 completing the treatment phase.
Intervention: The LY450139 groups received 60 mg/d for 2 weeks, then 100 mg/d for 6 weeks, and then either 100 or 140 mg/d for 6 additional weeks.
Main Outcome Measures: Primary outcome measures included adverse events, plasma and cerebrospinal fluid Aβ levels, vital signs, electrocardiographic data, and laboratory safety test results. Secondary outcome measures included the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale cognitive subscale and the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study Activities of Daily Living Scale.
Results: Group differences were seen in skin and subcutaneous tissue concerns (P=.05), including 3 possible drug rashes and 3 reports of hair color change in the treatment groups. There were 3 adverse event-related discontinuations, including 1 transient bowel obstruction. The plasma Aβ(40) concentration was reduced by 58.2% for the 100-mg group and 64.6% for the 140-mg group (P<.001). No significant reduction was seen in cerebrospinal fluid Aβ levels. No group differences were seen in cognitive or functional measures.
Conclusions: LY450139 was generally well tolerated at doses of up to 140 mg/d for 14 weeks, with several findings indicating the need for close clinical monitoring in future studies. Decreases in plasma Aβ concentrations were consistent with inhibition of gamma-secretase. Trial Registration: clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT00244322.

title: Reduction in skin grafting after the introduction of hydrofiber dressings in partial thickness burns: a comparison between a hydrofiber and silver sulphadiazine.
text:
The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical outcomes of children with scald burns treated with a hydrofiber dressing (Aquacel®, Convatec Inc.) versus the traditional standard of care with silver sulfadiazine (Flammazine®; Solvay Pharmaceuticals), taking into account the need for surgical intervention and length of stay (LOS) in hospital.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study of all consecutive children aged zero to four years who were admitted to the Burn Centre of the Maasstad Hospital Rotterdam with primary scald burns covering up to 10% of their body surface area. Data were collected using a prospective computerized database. The study period was divided into two periods: 1987-1999 (period 1) and 1999-2010 (period 2).
RESULTS: During the entire study period, 27.3% of the 502 patients treated with silver sulfadiazine (Ag-SD) underwent surgery, while before the introduction of hydrofiber dressings (HFD), 30.5% of the 338 Ag-SD-treated patients were operated on. After the introduction of HFD, 20.7% of the 164 patients treated with Ag-SD eventually underwent skin grafting, which is a significantly lower proportion than the 11.6% of the 302 patients whose wounds were dressed with HFD (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared to silver sulfadiazine treatment, a lower number of surgical interventions were observed in children aged 0-4 years with mixed partial thickness scald burns covering up to 10% of their body surface area after the introduction of hydrofiber dressings. Additionally, the use of HFD limited the length of stay in hospital.

title: Induction of the heat-shock response by carbon dioxide in Chironomus thummi.
text: The impact of various stress treatments on gene expression in Chironomus thummi salivary gland cells has been investigated. Of the treatments examined, only the recovery from carbon dioxide exposure showed a response similar to that previously observed after heat-shock treatment, namely the induction of heat-shock puffs and the synthesis of heat-shock polypeptides. In these conditions, puffing and transcription of telomeric regions were observed, leading to the appearance of the temperature-inducible telomeric Balbiani ring T-BR-III. Conversely, other treatments failed to elicit a heat-shock response in C. thummi larvae or salivary gland cells, despite exposing them to real stress conditions.

title: Candida albicans-Staphylococcus aureus polymicrobial peritonitis modulates host innate immunity.
text:
Despite advances in medical device fabrication and antimicrobial treatment therapies, fungal-bacterial polymicrobial peritonitis remains a significant complication for surgery patients, those on peritoneal dialysis, and critically ill individuals. Using a mouse model of peritonitis, we have demonstrated that monomicrobial infections with Candida albicans or Staphylococcus aureus are non-fatal. However, coinfection with these microorganisms leads to a 40% mortality rate and increased microbial burden in the spleen and kidney by day 1 post-infection.
We have also identified a unique subset of innate pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, keratinocyte chemoattractant, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, and macrophage inflammatory protein-1α) that are significantly increased during polymicrobial versus monomicrobial peritonitis, leading to increased inflammatory infiltration into the peritoneum and target organs. Treatment of coinfected mice with the cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitor indomethacin reduces the infectious burden, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and inflammatory infiltrate while simultaneously preventing any mortality.
Further experiments demonstrated that the immunomodulatory eicosanoid prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) is synergistically increased during coinfection compared to monomicrobial infection; indomethacin treatment also decreased elevated PGE2 levels. Moreover, adding exogenous PGE2 into the peritoneal cavity during infection overrode the protection provided by indomethacin and restored the increased mortality and microbial burden. These studies highlight the ability of fungal-bacterial coinfection to modulate innate inflammatory events with devastating consequences for the host.

title: Techniques and probes for the study of Xenopus tropicalis development.
text: The African clawed frog, Xenopus laevis, has provided valuable insights into developmental and cellular processes. However, its allotetraploid genome hinders its use in forward genetic analysis. An alternative species, Xenopus (Silurana) tropicalis, with a diploid genome and shorter generation time, can be used for genetic analysis. Here, we demonstrate that many tools developed for X. laevis can be applied to X. tropicalis. Using the developmental staging system of Nieuwkoop and Faber, we find that X. tropicalis embryos develop at similar rates to X. laevis, although they are more tolerant of temperature fluctuations. We also show that many analytical reagents, such as whole-mount in situ hybridization to mRNA transcripts and antibodies against X. laevis proteins, can be successfully transferred to X. tropicalis. Additionally, X. laevis probes often work in X. tropicalis, eliminating the need to clone X. tropicalis orthologs before initiating developmental studies. Furthermore, antisense morpholino oligonucleotides (MOs) can be used to study loss of gene activity during development in X. tropicalis. Finally, X. tropicalis offers the possibility for forward genetics and genomic analysis.

title: Requirement of c-myb in T cell development and in mature T cell function.
text: Prior studies have suggested that the proto-oncogene c-myb plays a role in T cell development within the thymus and mature T cell proliferation. To further investigate this, we generated two T cell-specific c-myb knockout mouse models, myb/LckCre and myb/CD4Cre. Our findings demonstrate that c-myb is essential for the development of thymocytes at the DN3 stage, for the survival and proliferation of double-positive thymocytes, for the differentiation of single-positive CD4 and CD8 T cells, and for the proliferative responses of mature T cells. Additionally, our data indicate that c-myb is directly involved in the formation of double-positive CD4+CD8+CD25+, CD4+CD25+, and CD8+CD25+ T cells, developmental processes that may suggest a role for c-myb in autoimmune dysfunction.

title: Effect of losartan on ambulatory short-term blood pressure variability and cardiovascular remodeling in hypertensive patients on hemodialysis.
text:
OBJECTIVE: Previous studies have shown that increased ambulatory short-term blood pressure (BP) variability is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. In this study, we investigated whether treatment with an angiotensin II type 1 receptor blocker, losartan, would improve ambulatory short-term BP variability in hypertensive patients undergoing hemodialysis.
METHODS: Forty hypertensive patients undergoing hemodialysis were randomly assigned to either the losartan treatment group (n=20) or the control treatment group (n=20). Ambulatory BP monitoring was performed at baseline and 6 and 12 months after treatment, along with echocardiography, measurements of brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), and biochemical parameter assessments.
RESULTS: After 6 and 12 months of treatment, nighttime short-term BP variability, as measured by the coefficient of variation of ambulatory BP, was significantly decreased in the losartan group compared to the control group. Additionally, losartan significantly reduced left ventricular mass index (LVMI), baPWV, and plasma levels of brain natriuretic peptide and advanced glycation end products (AGE). Multiple regression analysis revealed significant correlations between changes in LVMI and changes in nighttime short-term BP variability, as well as between changes in LVMI and changes in plasma levels of AGE.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that losartan is beneficial in suppressing pathological cardiovascular remodeling through its inhibitory effect on ambulatory short-term BP variability during nighttime.

title: Interleukin-17 mRNA expression in blood and CSF mononuclear cells is augmented in multiple sclerosis.
text: Myelin-directed autoimmunity is believed to play a crucial role in the development of multiple sclerosis (MS). Studies have shown that both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines are overproduced in MS patients. Interleukin-17 (IL-17), a cytokine produced exclusively by activated memory T cells, has been found to induce the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines from parenchymal cells and macrophages. To investigate the role of IL-17 in MS, in situ hybridization was used to detect and count IL-17 mRNA-expressing mononuclear cells (MNC) in blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from MS patients and control individuals. Our results showed that the numbers of IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC were significantly higher in patients with MS and acute aseptic meningoencephalitis (AM) compared to healthy individuals. Additionally, higher numbers of IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC were detected in MS patients during clinical exacerbations compared to remission. Notably, there was a significant increase in the numbers of IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC in CSF from MS patients compared to blood, and this increase was not observed in patients with AM. These findings suggest that IL-17-producing MNC play a key role in the pathogenesis of MS, with higher numbers present in CSF during clinical exacerbations.

title: A European perspective on population studies of dementia.
text: The shift in global demographics and the projected increase in age-related diseases, including dementia, pose a significant public health challenge. Both the United States and Europe have dedicated significant research efforts to comprehend the underlying causes and prevalence of dementia. This article provides an overview of the historical development of dementia research in Europe and compares it to the situation in the United States. The review highlights the shared concerns and strategies employed by researchers in both regions, emphasizing the need for improved harmonization of methodologies to maximize the value of global research initiatives.

title: The cost of providing comprehensive HIV treatment in PEPFAR-supported programs.
text:
In recent years, there has been a significant investment from organizations such as the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), national governments, and other stakeholders to provide HIV treatment in developing countries. To better understand the costs associated with this treatment, a study was conducted in 2006-2007 at 43 PEPFAR-supported outpatient clinics in Botswana, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, and Vietnam.
The study collected data on HIV treatment costs over a consecutive 6-month period for all patients receiving treatment and care at the study sites, which included 62,512 antiretroviral therapy (ART) patients and 44,394 pre-ART patients. The results showed that the median annual economic costs were US$ 202 (2009 USD) for pre-ART patients and US$ 880 for ART patients, excluding antiretrovirals. The per patient ART costs were US$ 298, and the costs for newly initiated ART patients were 15-20% higher than for established patients. However, the per patient costs dropped rapidly as the sites matured, with a 46.8% decrease between the first and second 6-month periods after the beginning of scale-up, and an additional 29.5% decrease the following year.
The study found that PEPFAR provided 79.4% of funding for service delivery, while national governments provided 15.2%. The study concluded that while treatment costs may decrease over time, programs must balance the need to improve services for current patients with the need to expand coverage to new patients.

title: A sperm cytoskeletal protein that signals oocyte meiotic maturation and ovulation.
text: Caenorhabditis elegans oocytes, like those of most other animals, undergo a temporary arrest during the prophase stage of meiosis. The resumption of meiosis and the subsequent ovulation are promoted by sperm, which also cause the contraction of smooth muscle-like gonadal sheath cells. We have discovered that the major sperm cytoskeletal protein (MSP) serves as a bifunctional signaling molecule for both oocyte maturation and sheath contraction. In addition, MSP has been found to play a role in sperm locomotion, analogous to the function of actin in other organisms. These findings suggest that during evolution, MSP has acquired both extracellular signaling and intracellular cytoskeletal functions for the purpose of reproduction. Interestingly, proteins with MSP-like domains have been identified in other organisms, including plants, fungi, and other animals, suggesting that related signaling functions may exist in other phyla.

title: Unmet need for mental health care among U.S. children: variation by ethnicity and insurance status.
text: This study aimed to provide national estimates of unmet mental health needs among children and adolescents in the United States. The authors analyzed data from three nationally representative household surveys conducted between 1996 and 1998, including the National Health Interview Survey, the National Survey of American Families, and the Community Tracking Survey. The study found that only a small proportion of children and adolescents (2%-3% of 3-5 year olds and 6%-9% of 6-17 year olds) received mental health services in a 12-month period, despite a significant proportion of children being in need of mental health evaluation (nearly 80% of children and adolescents 6-17 years old). The study also found that certain groups, such as Latino children and uninsured children, had higher rates of unmet need compared to other children. The study highlights the need for policy and clinical programs to address the low rates of mental health service use among children and adolescents, particularly among vulnerable populations.

title: Conditional economic incentives for reducing HIV risk behaviors: integration of psychology and behavioral economics.
text:
Objective: This article reviews the integration of psychology and behavioral economics in HIV prevention, specifically in the context of conditional economic incentive (CEI) programs. The review aims to examine the effectiveness of these approaches in reducing HIV risk behaviors.
Methods: The article first provides an overview of the history of HIV prevention strategies, highlighting the limitations of traditional psychological theories. It then provides an overview of the theoretical tenets of behavioral economics relevant to HIV prevention, and utilizes CEIs as an example of how psychological frameworks and behavioral economics can be combined. The article also presents findings from illustrative CEI programs, showing the mixed but generally promising effects of economic interventions on HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevalence, HIV testing, HIV medication adherence, and drug use.
Results: The review finds that behavioral economic interventions can complement psychological frameworks for reducing HIV risk by providing unique insights into the conditions under which risky decisions can be influenced. The findings from CEI programs show that economic interventions can have mixed but generally positive effects on HIV and STI prevalence, HIV testing, HIV medication adherence, and drug use.
Conclusions: The article concludes that CEI programs can complement psychological interventions for HIV prevention and behavioral risk reduction. To maximize program effectiveness, CEI programs must be designed according to contextual and population-specific factors that may determine intervention applicability and success.

title: ALDH1 is a marker of normal and malignant human mammary stem cells and a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
text: The application of stem cell biology to breast cancer research has been hindered by the lack of straightforward methods for identifying and isolating normal and malignant stem cells. By utilizing in vitro and in vivo experimental systems, our study demonstrates that normal and cancerous human mammary epithelial cells with elevated aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) activity possess stem/progenitor properties. These cells comprise the subpopulation of normal breast epithelium with the broadest differentiation potential and highest growth capacity in a xenotransplant model. In breast carcinomas, high ALDH activity identifies the tumorigenic cell fraction, capable of self-renewal and tumor generation that recapitulate the heterogeneity of the parental tumor. In a series of 577 breast carcinomas, immunostaining for ALDH1 correlated with poor prognosis. These findings provide a valuable new tool for studying normal and malignant breast stem cells and facilitate the clinical application of stem cell concepts.

title: Interleukin-6 and interleukin-8 levels in serum and synovial fluid of patients with osteoarthritis.
text: Concentrations of interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 in serum and synovial fluid samples obtained from patients with osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee were measured using the chemiluminescence-ELISA (CL-ELISA) method, which offers a sensitivity of 100-1,000 times greater than the conventional ELISA method. The results were compared with those obtained from patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and healthy controls. The mean IL-6 and IL-8 levels in synovial fluid were found to be higher in RA than in OA. Additionally, the IL-6 and IL-8 levels in serum were significantly higher in both RA and OA compared to controls. In OA patients who exhibited remarkable improvement in hydrarthrosis, the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels at initial examination were relatively higher, and were significantly decreased after treatment with sodium hyaluronate (NaHA). In contrast, among those who did not show improvement in hydrarthrosis, the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels at initial examination were relatively lower, and hydrarthrosis was not significantly improved even after treatment with NaHA. Furthermore, there was a tendency for the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels to decrease as hyaluronic acid (HA) levels increased. X-ray findings revealed that the IL-6 levels in synovial fluid at initial examination were significantly higher in low-grade cases than in high-grade cases. In low-grade cases, as determined by X-ray findings, there was a significant decrease in IL-6 levels in synovial fluid after treatment with NaHA.

title: Inhibition of SRC expression and activity inhibits tumor progression and metastasis of human pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells in an orthotopic nude mouse model.
text: The non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase Src is overexpressed in approximately 70% of pancreatic adenocarcinomas. In this study, we investigated the effect of reducing Src expression on the growth, incidence, and metastasis of pancreatic tumor cells in an orthotopic model. We used stable expression of a plasmid encoding small interfering RNA (siRNA) to target c-Src in L3.6pl human pancreatic tumor cells. Reducing Src expression resulted in a >80% reduction in Src protein levels without affecting the expression of related kinases c-Yes and c-Lyn, or proliferation rates. Additionally, phosphorylation of Akt and p44/42 Erk mitogen-activated protein kinase, as well as production of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) in culture supernatants, were all reduced (P < 0.005). When varying cell numbers of the siRNA-treated cells were implanted into nude mice, tumor incidence was unchanged, but large tumors failed to develop, and the incidence of metastasis was significantly reduced in the siRNA-treated mice. To further investigate this, animals bearing established wild-type tumors were treated with the Src/Abl-selective inhibitor BMS-354825 (dasatinib). Treatment resulted in a decrease in tumor size and a significant reduction in the incidence of metastases compared to controls. These findings suggest that Src activation plays a critical role in pancreatic tumor progression in this model, making Src a potential target for targeted therapy.

title: Eicosapentaenoic acid is converted via ω-3 epoxygenation to the anti-inflammatory metabolite 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid.
text:
Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) has many beneficial effects in treating inflammatory conditions. In a recent study, researchers found that EPA was converted into a different compound called 17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (17,18-EpETE) in the peritoneum of mice. This compound was then broken down into even more powerful anti-inflammatory metabolites, including 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-OH-17,18-EpETE).
The researchers found that 12-OH-17,18-EpETE has a strong anti-inflammatory effect, blocking the movement of white blood cells called neutrophils into the peritoneum. They also discovered that 12-OH-17,18-EpETE inhibits the production of a chemical called leukotriene B4, which can cause inflammation.
The researchers were able to identify the exact structure of two natural forms of 12-OH-17,18-EpETE and compare them to synthetic versions. They found that the natural forms were much more effective at reducing inflammation than the synthetic versions. These findings suggest that 17,18-EpETE, which is found in fish and other foods, may play a role in the body's natural anti-inflammatory processes.

title: Scrapie in mice. Agent-strain differences in the distribution and intensity of grey matter vacuolation.
text: Five different strains of the scrapie agent were used to inoculate the brains of two inbred mouse strains, C57BL and VM, as well as their F1 hybrid offspring. The degree of brain damage in specific regions of the brain, as measured by the degree of vacuolation, varied significantly between the different strains of scrapie agent. Using either mouse strain, it was possible to distinguish any of the five strains with a very high degree of accuracy based solely on the histological parameters of brain damage. The severity of brain damage was not affected by the dose of the agent, as demonstrated by using different doses of the ME7 strain in C57BL mice. The genetic background of the mice had a significant impact on the overall degree of brain damage and the shape of the lesion profile, with some agents causing more damage in certain areas of the brain depending on the mouse strain used. The F1 hybrid offspring of C57BL and VM mice showed either more or less brain damage in certain areas depending on the strain of scrapie agent used, compared to their parental genotypes. The complexity of the genetic control of the lesion profile made it impossible to conduct further analysis in these data.

title: Cyclin A2 is an RNA binding protein that controls Mre11 mRNA translation
text: Cyclin A2 exerts a multifaceted regulatory role in DNA replication, as it activates cyclin-dependent kinases Cdk1 and Cdk2 and is expressed at elevated levels from S phase until early mitosis. Our findings indicate that mutant mice lacking cyclin A2 are prone to chromosomal instability and tumorigenesis. Underlying this phenomenon is a failure to up-regulate the meiotic recombination 11 (Mre11) nuclease in S phase, leading to impaired resolution of stalled replication forks, inadequate repair of double-stranded DNA breaks, and improper segregation of sister chromosomes. Notably, cyclin A2 controls Mre11 abundance through a C-terminal RNA binding domain, which selectively and directly binds Mre11 transcripts to mediate polysome loading and translation. These data reveal cyclin A2 as a mechanistically diverse regulator of DNA replication, combining both kinase-dependent and kinase-independent functions to ensure adequate repair of common replication errors.

title: Cluster sampling to assess immunization coverage: a review of experience with a simplified sampling method.
text: The Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) utilizes a simplified cluster sampling method, involving the random selection of 210 children from 30 clusters of 7 children each, to estimate immunization coverage levels. This study analyzes the results of this method in both actual and simulated surveys. A total of 60 actual surveys were conducted in 25 countries, providing 446 sample estimations of immunization coverage. Findings reveal that 83% of the sample results had 95% confidence limits within + or - 10%, and none exceeded + or - 13%. To further evaluate the method's precision, 12 hypothetical population strata with immunization coverage rates ranging from 10%-99% were established for computer simulation, and 10 hypothetical communities were allocated various proportions of each stratum. The results of these simulated surveys showed that over 95% of the results were within + or - 10% of the actual population mean. Based on the findings of both actual and simulated surveys, the precision of the EPI method is considered satisfactory for the requirements of the program. Among the actual surveys, the proportion of results with confidence limits exceeding + or - 10% was highest (50%) when immunization coverage in the sample was 45%-54%.

title: Gender differences in the utilization of health care services.
text:
Background: Previous studies have consistently shown that women utilize more healthcare services than men. To investigate these gender differences and their associated costs, we analyzed data from a cohort of new adult patients at a university medical center.
Methods: We randomly assigned 509 patients to primary care physicians at the medical center and monitored their healthcare use and costs for one year. We collected self-reported health status data using the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 (SF-36) and controlled for health status, sociodemographic information, and primary care physician specialty in our statistical analyses.
Results: Our findings revealed significant gender differences in healthcare utilization and costs. Women had lower self-reported health status and lower levels of education and income compared to men. They also had a higher mean number of visits to their primary care clinic and diagnostic services, resulting in higher mean charges for primary care, specialty care, emergency treatment, diagnostic services, and annual total charges. After controlling for health status, sociodemographics, and clinic assignment, women still had higher medical charges for all categories of charges except hospitalizations.
Conclusions: Our study confirms that women have higher healthcare service utilization and associated costs than men. While the appropriateness of these differences remains to be determined, these findings have important implications for healthcare policy and resource allocation.

title: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor administered as a 24-hour intravenous infusion. A phase I and pharmacologic study.
text: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor (rH-TNF) is a cytokine with direct antitumor properties. In a phase I trial, we continuously infused rH-TNF for 24 hours in 50 patients, administering a total of 115 courses of therapy at doses ranging from 4.5 to 645 micrograms per square meter. While systemic toxicity, including fever, chills, fatigue, and hypotension, increased with dose, the highest doses (greater than 454 micrograms per square meter) caused severe lethargy and fatigue that precluded hospital discharge at the end of therapy. The dose-limiting toxicity was hypotension, and five patients treated at the two highest dose levels required dopamine treatment. Organ-specific toxicity was generally mild and resolved spontaneously within 48 hours. The 24-hour infusions of rH-TNF were associated with significant decreases in serum cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein levels. Pharmacokinetic studies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay showed peak plasma rH-TNF levels of 90-900 pg/mL, but no steady-state level was achieved. Based on these results, the recommended phase II dose for rH-TNF as a 24-hour continuous infusion is 545 micrograms per square meter.

title: Detection and comparison of epidermal growth factor receptor mutations in cells and fluid of malignant pleural effusion in non-small cell lung cancer.
text: Cells or cell-free fluid from malignant pleural effusions in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients may serve as valuable clinical specimens for detecting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. However, their utility in mutation detection has not been extensively studied. In this investigation, we enrolled 26 East Asian NSCLC patients with malignant pleural effusion and evaluated the EGFR mutation status in both cell and cell-free fluid using sequencing and mutant-enriched PCR. Our findings indicate that both cell and cell-free fluid may be suitable clinical specimens for EGFR mutation detection in unresectable NSCLC, provided that sensitive genotyping assays are employed. Direct sequencing may miss a significant portion of mutations in these heterogeneous specimens, highlighting the need for more sensitive methods such as mutant-enriched PCR and gene scan to provide reliable mutational information.

title: Materials and Methods Figs. S1 to S15 References Supporting Online Materials
text: Endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLRs) 7 and 9 are crucial for recognizing viral pathogens and initiating signaling pathways that lead to the activation of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB)-dependent proinflammatory cytokines and interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7)-dependent type I interferons (IFNs). TLR9 recognizes viral nucleic acids through a process that involves its cleavage in the endolysosomal compartment. Our study demonstrates that TLR9 signals leading to the activation of type I IFN, but not proinflammatory cytokine genes, require TLR9 trafficking from endosomes to a specialized lysosome-related organelle. Furthermore, we identify adapter protein-3 as the protein complex responsible for the trafficking of TLR9 to this subcellular compartment. Our findings reveal a novel intracellular mechanism for the bifurcation of TLR9 signals within the endosomal system, which allows for the selective activation of different signaling pathways in response to viral infection.

title: Sedimentation velocity method in the analytical ultracentrifuge for the study of protein-protein interactions.
text: Sedimentation analysis in the analytical ultracentrifuge can be used to detect macromolecular interactions by measuring the change in mass of the interacting molecules. When two molecules interact, the resulting complex has a greater mass than the individual molecules, and this difference in mass is reflected in the sedimentation behavior. In this chapter, we explore how this phenomenon can be used to determine quantitative parameters of an interaction. As an example, we examine the interaction between a single-stranded DNA binding protein and a subunit of DNA polymerase III holoenzyme, providing a detailed explanation of the related theory and a description of the algorithms used to evaluate the data.

title: Structural trends in the aging femoral neck and proximal shaft: analysis of the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry data.
text:
In this study, the authors analyzed hip scans from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) to measure bone mineral density (BMD) and other parameters in a non-Hispanic white subgroup of 2,719 men and 2,904 women. The study focused on two regions of the femur: a cortical region across the proximal shaft 2 cm distal to the lesser trochanter and a mixed cortical/trabecular region across the narrowest point of the femoral neck. The authors investigated age trends in BMD and section modulus in both regions by sex after correcting for body weight.
The results showed that BMD declined with age in both regions, but the rate of decline was different between sexes. In females, BMD in the narrow neck region declined at a similar rate as in the Hologic neck region, while in males, the section modulus in the narrow neck region declined modestly until the fifth decade and then remained nearly constant. In contrast, the shaft region section modulus declined at a slower rate than BMD in both sexes.
The authors also found that the apparent age trends in BMD and section modulus were influenced by a linear expansion in subperiosteal diameter in both sexes and in both regions, which tended to mechanically offset net loss of medullary bone mass. These findings suggest that aging loss of bone mass in the hip does not necessarily mean reduced mechanical strength, as the section modulus in the elderly was found to be within 14% of young values in females and within 6% in males.

title: Turning blood into brain: cells bearing neuronal antigens generated in vivo from bone marrow.
text: Bone marrow stem cells have the ability to generate a diverse range of hematopoietic cell types and replenish the blood supply throughout adulthood. Our research demonstrates that, in a specific strain of mice incapable of producing myeloid and lymphoid cells, transplanted adult bone marrow cells migrated to the brain and differentiated into cells expressing neuron-specific markers. These findings suggest that bone marrow-derived cells may serve as a potential alternative source of neurons for patients with neurodegenerative diseases or central nervous system injuries.

title: A negative staining method for high resolution electron microscopy of viruses.
text: A novel technique has been devised for the visualization of virus particles using electron microscopy. By mixing virus preparations with 1% phosphotungstic acid adjusted to pH 7.5 and spraying directly onto electron microscope supporting films made from evaporated carbon, high contrast and good preservation are achieved. This technique has been applied to study the external form and structure of tobacco mosaic virus and turnip yellow mosaic virus, allowing for the resolution of structural details previously suggested by X-ray diffraction methods.

title: Nef induces multiple genes involved in cholesterol synthesis and uptake in human immunodeficiency virus type 1-infected T cells.
text: Recent studies have suggested that cholesterol may play a crucial role in the replication of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). To investigate this further, we used microarrays to examine the effects of HIV-1 infection on cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake in both transformed T-cell lines and primary CD4(+) T cells. Our findings revealed that HIV-1 significantly increased the expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis in both cell types. Consistent with these results, we observed increased incorporation of (14)C-labeled mevalonate and acetate in HIV-1-infected cells. Additionally, we found that the changes in cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake were only observed when the Nef protein was functional, suggesting that increased cholesterol synthesis may contribute to the enhanced infectivity and replication of the virus through the Nef protein.

title: Long noncoding RNA as modular scaffold of histone modification complexes
text:
Long intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) play a crucial role in regulating chromatin states and epigenetic inheritance. Recent studies have shown that lincRNAs can act as scaffolds for histone modification complexes, facilitating the assembly of these complexes on specific genomic regions. In this study, we investigate the function of the lincRNA HOTAIR as a scaffold for at least two distinct histone modification complexes.
Our results demonstrate that the 5' domain of HOTAIR binds to polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), while the 3' domain of HOTAIR interacts with the LSD1/CoREST/REST complex. The ability of HOTAIR to tether these two complexes enables RNA-mediated assembly of PRC2 and LSD1, leading to coordinated targeting of PRC2 and LSD1 to chromatin for coupled histone H3 lysine 27 methylation and lysine 4 demethylation. These findings suggest that lincRNAs may serve as scaffolds by providing binding surfaces for the assembly of select histone modification enzymes, thereby specifying the pattern of histone modifications on target genes.
In summary, our study provides evidence that lincRNAs can act as scaffolds for histone modification complexes, allowing for the precise regulation of chromatin states and epigenetic inheritance. These findings have important implications for our understanding of the mechanisms underlying gene regulation and cellular differentiation.

title: Therapeutic Clearance of Amyloid by Antibodies to Serum Amyloid P Component.
text:
Background: Amyloid fibril deposits in systemic amyloidosis are composed of the non-fibrillar protein serum amyloid P component (SAP). The drug (R)-1-[6-[(R)-2-carboxy-pyrrolidin-1-yl]-6-oxo-hexanoyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (CPHPC) efficiently depletes SAP from the plasma, but some SAP remains in amyloid deposits, which can be specifically targeted by therapeutic IgG anti-SAP antibodies. In murine amyloid A type amyloidosis, the binding of these antibodies to the residual SAP in amyloid deposits activates the complement system and triggers the rapid clearance of amyloid by macrophage-derived multinucleated giant cells.
