title: Vegetarian vs. conventional diabetic diet – A 1-year follow-up
text:
Abstract:
Our previous 6-month randomized study demonstrated the beneficial effects of a vegetarian diet (V) compared to a conventional diet (C) on cardiovascular risk factors for patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), including increased insulin sensitivity, reduced body weight, reduced visceral and subcutaneous fat, decreased LDL-cholesterol, and improved oxidative stress markers and adipokines. To determine whether these improved outcomes persisted after the end of the study, we conducted post-trial monitoring on 62 subjects who completed the study. Results showed that 44 patients (71%) attended the follow-up appointment, and hypoglycemic agents were increased by 14% in the vegetarian group and by 26% in the conventional group. Insulin therapy was introduced in 5% of the vegetarian group and 13% of the conventional group within one year after the end of the intervention. Additionally, neither weight nor waist circumference changed significantly in either group. HbA1c levels increased similarly in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while blood lipids did not change in either group. Our findings suggest that the positive effects of a vegetarian diet on cardiovascular risk factors persisted to some extent one year after the end of the intervention.

title: Alcohol, wine, and health
text:
Over the past two decades, numerous epidemiological studies have investigated the relationship between alcohol consumption and various disease states. These studies have consistently shown that moderate alcohol consumption is associated with a reduced risk of mortality, as well as lower rates of arteriosclerotic vascular diseases, hypertension, cancers, peptic ulcers, respiratory infections, gallstones, kidney stones, age-related macular degeneration, bone density, and cognitive function compared to abstainers.
A review of these articles reveals that each study has compared the outcomes of individuals at different levels of alcohol consumption to those of abstainers. The results of these analyses have consistently shown a U-shaped or J-shaped curve of reduced relative risk for each disease state compared to abstinence.
Based on these findings, a clear definition of moderate alcohol consumption can be established: for men, it should not exceed 2 to 4 drinks per day, and for women, it should not exceed 1 to 2 drinks per day.
While alcohol consumption by itself has favorable effects on high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels and platelet aggregation inhibition, wine, particularly red wine, stands out due to its high levels of phenolic compounds, which have a positive impact on various biochemical systems. These compounds include increased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, antioxidant activity, decreased platelet aggregation and endothelial adhesion, cancer cell growth suppression, and nitric oxide production promotion.
In conclusion, the evidence from these studies suggests that moderate alcohol consumption, particularly red wine consumption, may have favorable effects on overall health and disease risk.

title: Contraceptive practices of women requesting termination of pregnancy : A study from China
text: In order to develop a program for preventing unplanned pregnancies, we conducted a survey of 1520 women seeking abortion at eight hospitals in Zheng Zhou City, Henan Province, China, from March to May 1996. Our findings revealed that the most common cause of unplanned pregnancy was contraceptive failure (71.9%), with 61.7% of these pregnancies being potentially predictable due to non-use of contraception or recognition of contraceptive failures. The most common contraceptive failures were condom mishaps (29.7%), IUD failures (23.5%), and rhythm miscalculation (15.9%). The majority of abortion seekers (77.1%) had used some contraceptive methods previously, but only 19.7% had used a method at their first sexual encounter. Among those who had used condoms, 50.9% had experienced at least one instance of condom mishap. The rhythm method had been used by 31.7% of abortion seekers, with 59.1% of these users experiencing at least one instance of rhythm failure. Of those who had used pills, 58.0% had experienced pill failures. User failure (46.4% for condom users and 56.0% for pill users) was the most common category for contraceptive failures. Our findings also showed that 56.4% of the women had experienced at least one previous abortion, and 5.3% had experienced two or more previous abortions. Only 10 subjects had utilized emergency contraception prior to their current pregnancy.

title: Oncologists' perceptions of the effects of cancer patients' companions on physician-patient interactions
text: To gain insight into the views of physicians regarding the impact of cancer patients' companions on their communication, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 oncologists (6 medical, 4 surgical, and 2 radiation) from a pool of 21 oncologists. The physicians estimated that approximately three-quarters of their patients brought companions to consultations, which they found to be more challenging for them. The behaviors of the companions varied from dominating the conversation to passively taking notes, with young professional men or older women accompanying their husbands being the most vocal and inquisitive. The physicians observed various coalitions during medical visits, with the companions and patients often having different agendas. The physicians also noted differences in the companions' behaviors based on their gender and whether they lived in rural or urban areas.

title: Wolff's Headache and Other Head Pain.
text: There has never been a book on headaches that comes close to the late Harold Wolff's groundbreaking work. The second edition, published 10 years ago, is a masterpiece of writing, providing an exhaustive and engrossing account of Wolff's extensive study and understanding of headaches. The new edition, revised by Dalessio, updates certain aspects of headache treatment, primarily focusing on drug therapy. However, the emphasis on total therapy rather than solely drug therapy has been maintained. While Dalessio has made some changes to the book's format, the new chapters on cluster headache and trigeminal neuralgia are simply reorganized sections from the original work. The main part of the book, on migraines, has been revised with some anecdotal material removed, but little new content has been added. It is noteworthy that the section on observations of methysergide (UML-491 in Wolff's original work) has been slightly altered.

title: Ansichten von Hausärzten zur Versorgung von unheilbar kranken Patienten am Lebensende - Ergebnisse einer Befragung in Niedersachsen
text:
Background: Family doctors play a crucial role in providing care to terminally ill patients. However, the current level of palliative care in Germany has been criticized, and there is a lack of empirical data, particularly regarding family doctors' attitudes.
Methods: To address this gap, semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with 257 family doctors in four representative regions of Lower Saxony as part of a larger health system research report.
Results: Of the 257 doctors surveyed, 71 (28%) participated in the interviews. On average, they cared for four palliative patients with cancer and eight patients with other diseases at the time of the interview. Many doctors reported being available for their patients around the clock, particularly in the final stages of illness. The main area for improvement identified by doctors was psychosocial support, rather than pain therapy, which is often the focus. Additionally, there was a strong expression of openness to the establishment of new palliative care structures.
Conclusion: Family doctors are highly motivated to provide palliative care and are open to improvements. However, it is important to respect and consider the diversity of opinion among professions and disciplines regarding the current situation and future development of palliative care.

title: Novel Risk Factors for Systemic Atherosclerosis: A Comparison of C-Reactive Protein, Fibrinogen, Homocysteine, Lipoprotein(a), and Standard Cholesterol Screening as Predictors of Peripheral Arterial Disease
text: In this study, the authors aimed to compare the predictive value of 11 lipid and nonlipid biomarkers as risk factors for the development of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD) in a nested case-control design. The study included 14,916 initially healthy US male physicians aged 40-84 years, of whom 140 developed symptomatic PAD over an average 9-year follow-up period. The authors found that plasma levels of total cholesterol, LDL-C, triglycerides, apo B-100, fibrinogen, and CRP were significantly higher at baseline among men who developed PAD compared to those who remained free of vascular disease. In contrast, HDL-C and apo A-I levels were lower among cases. In multivariable analyses, the total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio and CRP were the strongest lipid and nonlipid predictors of risk, respectively. Additionally, the authors found that the addition of CRP to standard lipid screening significantly improved risk prediction models. These findings suggest that the total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio and CRP may be useful for identifying individuals at high risk of developing PAD, and that incorporating CRP into lipid screening may improve risk prediction.

title: Assessment of older people: Self-maintaining and instrumental activities of daily living.
text: The use of standardized formal devices for assessing function is becoming the norm in agencies serving the elderly, as highlighted in the Gerontological Society's recent contract study on functional assessment (Howell, 1968). The study gathered a wide range of rating scales, checklists, and other techniques used in practical settings. Currently, it seems that each investigator or practitioner feels an internal drive to create their own scale and criticize existing ones for not fitting their specific setting. However, the authors join this group by presenting two scales that have been standardized on their own population (Lawton, 1969). They take comfort in the fact that one of the scales, the Physical Self-Maintenance Scale (PSMS), has been developed and used by other investigators (Lowenthal, 1964), which was adapted for use in their institution. The second scale, the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale (IADL), taps a level of functioning that has been inadequately represented in previous attempts to assess everyday functional competence. Both scales have been tested in various types of institutions and facilities serving community-resident older people. Before delving into the specific behaviors measured by these scales, the authors will briefly describe the competence schema into which these behaviors fit (Lawton, 1969). Human behavior is viewed as varying in complexity, with the lowest level being life maintenance, followed by increasingly complex levels of functioning in various tasks.

title: Diabetes in pregnancy: management of diabetes and its complications from preconception to the postnatal period (NG3)
text:
In February 2015, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) released new guidance (NG3) on managing diabetes during pregnancy. Healthcare providers must be aware of this guidance and implement its recommendations. The guidelines include:
* Preconception care with an HbA1c target of 48 mmol/mol.
* Women at risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should undergo a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT).
* Diagnostic criteria for GDM have been revised to include a fasting glucose level of 5.6 mmol/L or higher or a 2-hour glucose level of 7.8 mmol/L or higher.
* Glycemic targets in all diabetic pregnancies have been revised to include a fasting glucose level below 5.3 mmol/L (or 4-5.2 mmol/L if on insulin) and a 1-hour postprandial glucose level below 7.8 mmol/L if achievable without compromising safety.
* Continuous glucose monitoring and insulin pump therapy should not be used routinely but can be employed if glycemic control is challenging.
* Capillary ketone testing should be performed routinely on women with type 1 diabetes when hyperglycemic and on all women with diabetes, including those with GDM, when acutely unwell.
* There is more flexibility in the recommended delivery timing, with a range of 37+0 weeks to 38+6 weeks for women with types 1 and 2 diabetes, and prior to 40+6 weeks in GDM (and earlier if complications arise).
* Postnatal testing following GDM should be performed by fasting glucose (not OGTT) at 6-13 weeks postpartum. Testing later than this can use HbA1c.

These changes will likely result in an increase in the number of women diagnosed with GDM, and they will also have resource implications.

title: Mental health difficulties across childhood and mental health service use: findings from a longitudinal population-based study.
text:
Over the past two decades, there has been a lack of change in the prevalence of mental disorders among children and adolescents in high-income countries, despite increased investment in mental health services. Insufficient contact with mental health professionals may be a contributing factor, but it is unclear what proportion of children receive adequate treatment. This study aimed to investigate the level of mental healthcare received by Australian children aged 4-14 years.
Using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, the study mapped the trajectories of mental health symptoms in children. Health professional attendances and psychotropic medications dispensed were identified from linked national Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme records. The study found four distinct trajectories of mental health symptoms: low, high-decreasing, moderate-increasing, and high-increasing.
The majority of children with mental health symptoms had few MBS mental health attendances, and only a minority received care meeting the study's criteria for minimally adequate treatment. Children in the high-increasing and moderate-increasing trajectories were more likely to access care, but there was no evidence of improvement in symptoms.
The study highlights the importance of ensuring that children and adolescents with mental health problems receive treatment that meets minimal practice guidelines. Further research is needed to identify the quality of care currently provided to children with mental health difficulties and how clinicians can be best funded and supported to provide care meeting minimal practice guidelines.
The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

title: Rembrandt Scholz
text: This study examines the potential impact of changes in medical care on mortality rates in Lithuania, Hungary, and Romania, with west Germany included for comparison. The research focuses on deaths from conditions that should not occur with timely and effective healthcare (amenable mortality) and calculates the contribution of these deaths to changes in life expectancy between birth and age 75. The study finds that temporary life expectancy improved consistently in west Germany, with men gaining 2.7 years and women gaining 1.6 years. In contrast, gains were relatively small in the other countries, except for Hungarian women, who gained 1.3 years. Romanian men, however, lost 1.3 years. In the 1980s, falling infant mortality made a significant contribution to improvements in temporary life expectancy in all countries, with about a quarter to half a year's worth of gains attributed to amenable conditions. At older ages, falling amenable mortality contributed about 40% among those aged over 40 in Germany and, to a lesser extent, Hungary, while causing a loss of life expectancy in Romania. In the 1990s, improvements in infant mortality continued to benefit Lithuania and Hungary, but had little impact in either Germany or Romania. Among adults, improvements in amenable mortality continued to benefit Hungarians and west Germans. In Lithuania, up to two-thirds of the gain in temporary life expectancy were attributable to falling mortality from ischaemic heart disease, while medical care had a negative impact. Romanian men and women experienced increases in amenable mortality that contributed up to half of the overall loss of life expectancy. The study suggests that changes in medical care had a significant impact on mortality rates in the selected central and eastern European countries, both positively and negatively, over the past 20 years.

title: The Women's Interagency HIV Study
text: The Women's Interagency HIV Study (WIHS) is the largest cohort of HIV-seropositive women in the United States to date, consisting of 2,058 participants. This cohort is complemented by a comparison cohort of seronegative women, which consists of 568 participants. The study's methodology, training procedures, and quality assurance activities are detailed in this text. The study population is diverse, with participants from across the United States, and the cohort has been followed over an extended period of time, providing valuable insights into the natural history of HIV infection in women.

title: Prevalence of the Metabolic Syndrome Among Us Adults: Findings From the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
text:
Metabolic syndrome is diagnosed when an individual exhibits three or more of the following criteria:
* Abdominal obesity (waist circumference exceeding 102 cm in men and 88 cm in women)
* Hypertriglyceridemia of 150 mg/dl or higher
* Low levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (less than 40 mg/dl in men and 50 mg/dl in women)
* Blood pressure of 130/85 mm Hg or higher
* Fasting glucose of at least 110 mg/dl
Individuals with metabolic syndrome are more likely than others to develop diabetes and cardiovascular disease and have a higher mortality rate from all causes, including cardiovascular disease.
The investigators analyzed data from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) conducted between 1988 and 1994, which included 8814 men and women aged 20 years or older in the non-institutionalized civilian American population.
The overall age-adjusted prevalence of metabolic syndrome was 23.7%. The prevalence increased from 6.7% in those aged 20-29 to 42% in those aged 70 years and older. There was little difference in prevalence rates between gender for the combined racial groups. Metabolic syndrome was most common in Mexican Americans and least common in whites, African Americans, and "others." Among both African Americans and Mexican Americans, women had higher prevalence rates than men.
Using age-specific prevalence rates and US census data from 2000, it is estimated that 47 million US residents have metabolic syndrome. Given its prevalence, it is important to estimate the direct medical costs of metabolic syndrome. In most cases, the primary causes are poor nutrition and insufficient physical activity, highlighting the importance of controlling obesity and promoting physical activity in the US.

title: Baseline cytology, human papillomavirus testing, and risk for cervical neoplasia: A 10-year cohort analysis
text:
The study investigated whether women at higher risk for cervical cancer could be identified by testing for the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cervical smears. The study included 23,702 women who underwent annual Pap smears between April 1989 and November 1990. Of these, 20,810 had satisfactory cervical smears with sufficient samples for HPV testing. The study found that:
* Most women (83.6%) had at least one follow-up smear during the study period, but women with atypical squamous cells (ASC) or worse had more smears than women with normal results (mean, 4.4 vs. 3.3).
* Follow-up was conducted more or less annually for a total period of 122 months. HPV results were not used in deciding patient management.
* Ninety-six percent of the 20,810 baseline Pap smears were diagnosed as negative (N = 20,156). Thirteen percent of these patients tested positive for HPV.
* The baseline smears of 654 of the 20,810 women (3.1%) were classified as ASC or worse. Of these 654 smears, 417 (63.8%) were positive for HPV.
* One hundred seventy-eight women had a cytologic diagnosis of a low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse; of these, 143 (80.3%) tested positive for HPV.
* During the 10 years of follow-up, 171 patients developed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 3 or cervical cancer. The baseline smear was normal in 112 of these women and ASC or worse in 59 (34.5%).
* Only half (49.2%) of the 58 patients diagnosed within the first 45 months of follow-up had an abnormal baseline smear.
* During this first 45 months, 7.85% of the women whose initial Pap test was at least ASC were diagnosed with CIN 3 or cancer.
* The cumulative incidence at 10 years of follow-up was 10.2%.
* Sixty of the 171 women with CIN 3 or cervical cancer had a negative baseline HPV test. Of the 118 women who were diagnosed during the first 45 months of follow-up, 89 (79.4%) were HPV positive initially.
* The cumulative incidence of CIN 3 or cancer among the group with a positive baseline HPV test was 6.92% over 10 years but only 1.73% at 45 months.
* The risk of developing CIN 3 or cancer remained elevated throughout the study in those women with a positive baseline HPV test.
* The predictive ability of the baseline Pap smear diminished as the follow-up interval increased.
* Fifteen percent of the patients (N = 3216) had a positive Pap smear, a positive HPV test, or both at the initial examination.
* One hundred twenty-three (71.9%) were among the 171 women who developed CIN 3 or cancer.
* Eighty-six percent (102 of 123) of the patients who were diagnosed within the first 45 months were positive with at least one of the screening studies.
* The cumulative incidence over 45 months for women who had positive HPV testing and/or abnormal Pap smear results was 4.54%.
* Women with negative results in both screening tests had a cumulative risk of 0.16% for the same period.
* At 10 years the cumulative risk incidence for these two groups was 6.83% and 0.79%, respectively, yielding a negative predictive value of 99.1% for combined testing.

title: Preconception Care and the Risk of Congenital Anomalies in the Offspring of Women With Diabetes Mellitus: A Meta-Analysis
text: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of preconception care (PCC) in minimizing the risk of congenital birth defects in offspring of women with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). The study conducted a meta-analysis of published studies on PCC in women with DM from 1970 to 2000. Two reviewers independently abstracted the data, and the rate and relative risk (RR) of major and minor malformations were pooled from eligible studies using a random effects model. Early first-trimester glycosylated hemoglobin values were also recorded. Eight retrospective and eight prospective cohort studies were included, conducted in Europe, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Israel. Most participants had type 1 DM, but three studies included women with type 2 DM. Women who received PCC were found to be around 2 years older on average than those who did not. The methods of PCC varied, but most centers provided some maternal education on the pregnancy risks associated with poor glycemic control. In seven studies reporting early gestational glycosylated hemoglobin values, mean levels were consistently lower in PCC patients. The pooled rate for major and minor anomalies was 2.4% in the PCC group and 7.7% in non-PCC recipients, with a pooled RR of 0.32. Among 2104 offspring, major malformations were less prevalent in the PCC group (2.1 vs. 6.5%; pooled RR = 0.36). Similar results were obtained when only prospective studies were analyzed and in studies where the infant examiners were unaware of the mothers' PCC status. The lowest risk of major anomalies was found in a study that administered folic acid periconceptionally to its PCC recipients; the RR was 0.11. This meta-analysis, which included both retrospective and prospective studies, demonstrated an association between PCC and a significantly lower risk of congenital anomalies in the offspring of women with established DM. The lowered risk was accompanied by significantly lower glycosylated hemoglobin values in the first trimester in recipients of PCC.

title: Behçet's disease associated with a lymphoproliferative disorder, mixed cryoglobulinemia, and an immune complex mediated vasculitis.
text:
A 59-year-old woman has been monitored for 13 years, during which time she has experienced various manifestations of Behcet's disease, including:
* Aphthous stomatitis
* Genital ulcers
* Uveitis causing blindness
* Recurrent erythema nodosum
* Synovitis

In 1970, a poorly differentiated diffuse lymphocytic lymphoma developed and was treated with radiation therapy.

In 1976, she experienced a mixed cryoglobulinemia and an immune complex-mediated vasculitis, characterized by purpura and neuropathy, which improved with treatment using prednisone and chlorambucil.
The subsequent course of her lymphoproliferative disorder suggests that it was in fact benign.

title: Older People at the End of Life: Delivery of Care and Needs for Improvement from the Perspective of Bereaved Relatives
text:
BACKGROUND As the population ages and experiences an increase in chronic illnesses and multimorbidity, the importance of palliative care for geriatric patients has grown significantly. This study aimed to explore the perspectives of bereaved relatives regarding their experiences and expectations regarding the delivery of care for older people in the last phase of life.
METHODS Qualitative interviews were conducted with 12 relatives of deceased older patients (aged 60 years or older). The interviews were recorded, transcribed, coded, and analyzed using qualitative content analysis according to Mayring.
RESULTS Bereaved relatives perceived that the care for geriatric patients in the last phase of life was inadequate in various aspects. They criticized overtreatment (e.g., unnecessary skin cancer diagnoses) as well as unmet needs (e.g., inadequate pain management, patient-centered care, and poor communication). Family doctors were identified as the primary contact persons in the healthcare system.
CONCLUSIONS From the perspective of bereaved relatives, care for older people in the last phase of life has significant deficiencies. They criticize an inappropriate prioritization and the neglect of palliative care. Improved communication and information exchange between patients, relatives, and healthcare providers are essential to address these issues. Enhancing the role of generalist palliative care, particularly provided by family doctors and community nurses, may help to address these concerns.

title: Role of Computerized Physician Order Entry Systems in Facilitating Medication Errors
text:
According to a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association, the implementation of a computer-alert program significantly reduced the rates of deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism among hospitalized patients at risk. The study found that compared to a control group, the computer-alert program reduced the risk of deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism by 41% (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% confidence interval, 0.43 to 0.81; P < 0.001).
The study included 103 patients in the intervention group and 103 patients in the control group. The computer-alert program notified physicians when their patients were at increased risk for venous thromboembolism, which led to an increase in the use of appropriate prophylactic measures. The study found that the computer-alert program increased the likelihood of freedom from deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism at 90 days to 94.1% (95% confidence interval, 92.5 to 95.4%) and 90.6% (95% confidence interval, 88.7 to 92.2%), respectively (P < 0.001).
The study's findings suggest that computer-alert systems can be an effective tool in improving the quality of care and reducing the incidence of venous thromboembolism. Urologists can learn two important lessons from this study: first, many urology patients are at increased risk for venous thromboembolism, and appropriate prophylaxis should be used; second, computer-alert systems may become more common in the future, and clinicians should expect to see more of them.

title: Beta-band oscillations--signalling the status quo?
text: In this review, we explore the potential functional role of beta-band oscillations, which is currently not well understood. We examine evidence from recent studies on top-down mechanisms involved in cognitive processing, the motor system, and the pathophysiology of movement disorders, which suggests a unifying hypothesis: beta-band activity appears to be related to the maintenance of the current sensorimotor or cognitive state. We propose that beta oscillations and/or coupling in the beta-band are more pronounced when maintaining the status quo is intended or predicted, compared to when a change is expected. Furthermore, we suggest that pathological enhancement of beta-band activity may lead to an abnormal persistence of the status quo and a decline in flexible behavioral and cognitive control.

title: Safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of IMCgp100, a first-in-class soluble TCR-antiCD3 bispecific t cell redirector with solid tumour activity: Results from the FIH study in melanoma.
text:
Background: T cell-based bispecific agents have shown promise in the treatment of hematologic cancers, but their efficacy in solid tumors remains limited. IMCgp100 is a bispecific biologic that combines an affinity-enhanced T cell receptor (TCR) specific for gp100 with an anti-CD3 scFv. In vitro studies have shown that IMCgp100 can bind to gp100-expressing melanoma cells and redirect cytotoxicity, leading to potent immune effects.
Methods: In this Phase I study, we evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and efficacy of IMCgp100 in HLA-A2+ patients with advanced melanoma. The study was conducted in a 3+3 design, with patients receiving IMCgp100 intravenously (iv) weekly (Arm 1) or daily (4QD3W, Arm 2) to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). The recommended Phase 2 regimen (RP2D-QW) was defined based on the results of the dose escalation phase.
Results: In the dose escalation phase, 31 patients received doses ranging from 5 ng/kg to 900 ng/kg of IMCgp100. Dose-limiting toxicity of grade 3 or 4 hypotension was observed in Arm 1, associated with rapid trafficking of peripheral lymphocytes to the skin and tumor. The MTD was determined to be 600 ng/kg QW. IMCgp100 exhibited a dose-proportional pharmacokinetic profile with a plasma half-life (T1/2) of approximately 5-6 hours at the RP2D-QW dose.
Conclusion: While the efficacy of IMCgp100 in solid tumors remains to be determined, these results suggest that it may be a promising approach for the treatment of melanoma. Further study is needed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of IMCgp100 in this patient population.

title: The Bitterest Pills: The Troubling Story of Antipsychotic Drugs
text: © Joanna Moncrieff 2013. All rights reserved. A groundbreaking reevaluation of the history of antipsychotics, uncovering how they were transformed from toxic neurological substances into miraculous cures, their advantages overstated and their harmful effects downplayed or disregarded.

title: Variables Affecting Kinetics of Minimal Residual Disease Clearance in Children with Lymphoblastic Leukaemia; Results of the United Kingdom Medical Research Council (UK MRC) Protocols ALL97, ALL97/99 and ALL2003.
text: In this study, we investigated the influence of various factors on the clearance of Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) in children with lymphoblastic leukemia treated with an intensive risk-stratified approach. We analyzed data from three clinical trials: UK MRC protocol ALL97 (1997-1999), ALL97/99 (1999-2002), and ALL2003 (2003). The trials compared the efficacy and toxicity of different treatments, including dexamethasone (DEX) versus prednisolone (PRED), and 6-thioguanine (TG) versus 6-mercaptopurine (MP). We evaluated the potential influence of various factors on MRD status at the end of induction (EOI), including NCI risk, asparaginase intensity, DEX versus PRED, and marrow response at day 8/15 of induction. MRD was assessed using either a semi-quantitative sequence-specific PCR (ALL97) or Real-Time Quantitative PCR (ALL99 and ALL2003) of antigen receptor gene rearrangements at EOI. We found that the proportions of patients with MRD NEG, POS, or POQR did not significantly differ between steroid or NCI sub-groups. However, we observed a significant difference in the proportions of patients who were MRD POS when receiving ERW Asparaginase compared to E.Coli Asparaginase. Our results suggest that patients with undetectable MRD at EOI have a low risk of relapse.

title: Chromosome numbers in certain Indian species ofUtricularia L. (Lentibulariaceae)
text:

title: Detection of [Ca2+]I Changes In Sub-Plasma Membrane Micro Domains in A Single Living Cell By an Optical Fiber-Based Nanobiosensor
text: An optical fiber-based nanobiosensor, designed to detect subtle changes in intracellular calcium ion concentrations ([Ca2+]i) within single living cells, has been developed. The nanobiosensor consists of a silver-coated probe, followed by immobilization of Calcium Green-1 Dextran, a calcium ion-sensitive dye, on the distal end. This construct enables the detection of ultra-low and local [Ca2+]i concentrations within the nanomolar range, which is comparable to the physiological level of free cytosolic calcium ion in a single living cell. The response time of the nanobiosensor is less than milliseconds, allowing for the detection of transient calcium ion signaling events associated with microdomains. The effects of stimuli such as high potassium buffer solution and norepinephrine solution were also investigated, demonstrating the versatility and sensitivity of the nanobiosensor. This advanced nano-diagnostic platform has the potential to revolutionize the field of cellular calcium ion signaling and real-time in vivo diagnosis.

title: Construction of plant bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) libraries: an illustrated guide.
text:
Journal of Agricultural Genomics, 5 | ABSTRACT
Bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) libraries have become essential tools in plant genetic research. However, novice researchers often encounter difficulties in creating plant BAC libraries de novo due to the lack of detailed protocols and the unique features of plant cells, which make the isolation of high-molecular-weight DNA challenging. To address this issue, we present a comprehensive, step-by-step protocol for constructing plant BAC libraries. This protocol is designed to be user-friendly and accessible to both new and experienced investigators. By simplifying the process of BAC cloning in plants, we aim to accelerate progress in plant genomics and foster new discoveries in the field.

title: Activation by IKKα of a second, evolutionary conserved, NF-κB signaling pathway
text: In mammals, the canonical nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling pathway, activated in response to infections, relies on the degradation of inhibitors IκB. This pathway depends on the IκB kinase (IKK), which consists of two catalytic subunits, IKKα and IKKβ. While IKKβ is essential for inducible IκB phosphorylation and degradation, IKKα is not. Our findings show that IKKα is required for B cell maturation, formation of secondary lymphoid organs, increased expression of certain NF-κB target genes, and processing of the NF-κB2 (p100) precursor. Interestingly, IKKα preferentially phosphorylates NF-κB2, and this activity requires its phosphorylation by upstream kinases, one of which may be NF-κB–inducing kinase (NIK). Therefore, IKKα plays a pivotal role in a second NF-κB activation pathway based on regulated NF-κB2 processing rather than IκB degradation.

title: Identification and transmission of Piper yellow mottle virus and Cucumber mosaic virus infecting black pepper (Piper nigrum) in Sri Lanka
text:
Sri Lankan black pepper exhibiting symptoms of yellow mottle disease contained a mixture of viruses, including:
* Piper yellow mottle virus (PYMV) particles (average size: 30 × 130 nm)
* Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) particles (average size: 30 nm in diameter, isometric shape)
* Unidentified, isometric virus-like particles (average size: 30 nm in diameter)
An effective purification procedure was developed for PYMV. Immunosorbent and conventional electron microscopy were used to detect badnavirus particles in partially purified extracts, with successful detection of PYMV. It was determined that PYMV was the cause of the disease, with the other two viruses appearing to play no role in producing symptoms. PYMV was transmitted through grafting, by the insect vectors Planococcus citri and Diconocoris distanti, but not through mechanical inoculation or seed transmission. The CMV isolate was transmitted to indicator plants through mechanical inoculation and by the vector Aphis gossypii, but not through Myzus persicae; neither mechanical nor insect transmission of CMV to black pepper was successful. A sensitive polymerase chain reaction assay was developed to detect PYMV in black pepper.

title: A forkhead-domain gene is mutated in a severe speech and language disorder
text: Individuals with developmental disorders of speech and language face significant challenges in acquiring expressive and/or receptive language skills, even with adequate intelligence and opportunities. While genetic factors are thought to play a significant role in these disorders, studies of twins have not identified a single "speech and language disorder gene." Instead, most families exhibit complex patterns of inheritance. We have investigated a unique three-generation pedigree, KE, in which a severe speech and language disorder is inherited in an autosomal-dominant manner. Previous work has mapped the responsible locus, SPCH1, to a 5.6-cM interval on chromosome 7 (region 7q31). We have also identified an unrelated individual, CS, with speech and language impairments associated with a chromosomal translocation involving the SPCH1 interval. Our findings suggest that the gene FOXP2, which encodes a transcription factor with a polyglutamine tract and forkhead DNA-binding domain, is directly disrupted by the translocation breakpoint in CS. Additionally, we have identified a point mutation in affected members of the KE family that alters an invariant amino-acid residue in the forkhead domain. These findings implicate FOXP2 in the developmental process leading to speech and language.

title: The Growth and Sporulation of the Benign and Malignant Tertian Malarial Parasites in the Culture Tube and in the Human Host

title: Innate immunity to a facultative intracellular bacterial pathogen.
text: The traditional view of the mouse response to Listeria monocytogenes as a model of T-cell-mediated immunity has been challenged by recent discoveries. Contrary to expectations, T-cell-deficient mice have been shown to be capable of surviving a L. monocytogenes infection. This shift in understanding has been driven by advances in our knowledge of the cellular and molecular mechanisms of infection, revealing a more complex and nuanced picture of the immune response to this pathogen.

title: Diversity and Evenness: A Unifying Notation and Its Consequences
text: Three commonly used measures of diversity - Simpson's index, Shannon's entropy, and the total number of species - are connected to Renyi's generalization of entropy. A unified concept of diversity is proposed, which reveals a continuum of possible diversity measures. In essence, these measures provide estimates of the actual number of species present, and they differ only in their tendency to emphasize or ignore less abundant species. The distinction between the diversity of a community and a sample is explored, and it is related to the asymptotic form of the species-abundance curve. A novel and plausible definition of evenness is derived.

title: Guide to yeast genetics and molecular biology
text: This volume and its companion, Volume 350, are tailored to meet the requirements of graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and experts in the field by offering a comprehensive collection of cutting-edge techniques for studying genes in yeast. The book provides step-by-step instructions for setting up a yeast laboratory and mastering fundamental manipulations, making it accessible to novices. Additionally, relevant background information and reference materials are provided for each procedure, serving as a valuable resource for developing customized protocols across various disciplines. The book covers a range of topics, including cytology, biochemistry, cell fractionation, and cell biology, providing a thorough understanding of the subject matter.

title: Cutadapt removes adapter sequences from high-throughput sequencing reads
text: When small RNA is sequenced on current sequencing machines, the resulting reads are typically longer than the RNA itself, containing parts of the 3' adapter. To accurately map these reads, the adapter must be identified and removed from each read using an error-tolerant approach. While previous methods may be difficult to use or lack essential features, such as support for color space data, we have developed the command-line tool cutadapt as a user-friendly alternative. Cutadapt supports 454, Illumina, and SOLiD data (color space), offers two adapter trimming algorithms, and includes additional useful features. The source code, licensed under MIT, is available for download at <http://code.google.com/p/cutadapt/>.

title: Reproductive physiology of marsupials
text:
Preface:
The breeding biology of marsupials is a fascinating and complex field of study that has garnered significant attention from researchers in recent years. This chapter provides an overview of the historical introduction of marsupials, their breeding biology by family, sexual differentiation and development, male anatomy and spermatogenesis, the female urogenital tract and oogenesis, ovarian function and control, pregnancy and parturition, lactation, neuroendocrine control of seasonal breeding, and the evolution of mammalian reproduction.
Historical Introduction:
Marsupials are a unique group of mammals characterized by their ability to carry their young in a pouch on their body. The first marsupials appeared around 100 million years ago, and since then, they have evolved into a diverse group of species found in various parts of the world. Despite their diversity, marsupials share several common breeding behaviors and reproductive strategies that are unique among mammals.
Breeding Biology of Marsupials by Family:
Marsupials are divided into two main families: the Didelphimorphia and the Peramelemorphia. The Didelphimorphia includes opossums, rat-kangaroos, and wombats, while the Peramelemorphia includes bandicoots, bilbies, and peramelemorphs. Each of these families has distinct breeding behaviors and reproductive strategies. For example, opossums are solitary animals that breed seasonally, while bilbies are social animals that breed year-round.
Sexual Differentiation and Development:
Sexual differentiation and development in marsupials are complex and involve the interaction of genetic and environmental factors. In many marsupial species, males have larger testes than females, indicating that they invest more in reproduction. However, some species, such as the tamandua, have reversed sexual size dimorphism, with females having larger testes than males. The development of reproductive structures in marsupials is also unique, with the formation of the genital tubercle in the embryo, which eventually develops into the male or female reproductive system.
Male Anatomy and Spermatogenesis:
Male marsupials have a unique reproductive system that is adapted to their pouched lifestyle. The testes are located in the inguinal region and are suspended in the scrotum by a cord-like structure called the spermatic cord. The epididymis, a structure that stores and transports sperm, is also located in the inguinal region. Spermatogenesis in marsupials is similar to that in other mammals, with the formation of spermatozoa in the testes and their transport to the epididymis for maturation.
Female Urogenital Tract and Oogenesis:
The female urogenital tract in marsupials is also unique and is adapted to the pouched lifestyle. The uterus is located in the pelvic region and is connected to the pouch through a narrow opening called the vulval opening. The ovaries are located on either side of the uterus and produce eggs that are released into the uterus during breeding. Oogenesis in marsupials is similar to that in other mammals, with the formation of ova in the ovaries and their release into the uterus for fertilization.
Ovarian Function and Control:
The ovaries of marsupials play a crucial role in reproductive function, and their function is regulated by a complex interplay of hormonal and environmental factors. The ovaries produce eggs, which are released into the uterus during breeding, and they also produce hormones that regulate the reproductive cycle. The hormonal regulation of ovarian function is unique in marsupials and is influenced by factors such as temperature, humidity, and social status.
Pregnancy and Parturition:
Pregnancy and parturition in marsupials are complex and involve the interaction of hormonal and environmental factors. Marsupials have a unique reproductive strategy called embryonic diapause, which allows them to delay implantation of the embryo until the environment is favorable for reproduction. This allows them to avoid breeding during times of food scarcity or other environmental stressors. Parturition in marsupials is also unique, with the young being born in a premature state and then completing their development in the pouch.
Lactation:
Lactation in marsupials is a complex process that involves the production of milk in the mammary glands and its transport to the young in the pouch. Marsupials have a unique mammary gland structure that allows them to produce milk in a highly efficient manner. The milk is rich in nutrients and antibodies, which help the young to grow and develop.
Neuroendocrine Control of Seasonal Breeding:
Marsupials have a unique reproductive strategy called seasonal breeding, which is regulated by a complex interplay of hormonal and environmental factors. The neuroendocrine system plays a crucial role in regulating reproductive function in marsupials, with the hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and adrenal gland all playing important roles. The hypothalamus produces hormones that regulate the reproductive cycle, while the pituitary gland produces hormones that stimulate the production of milk in the mammary glands. The adrenal gland produces hormones that help to regulate the reproductive cycle and prepare the female for breeding.
Evolution of Mammalian Reproduction:
The evolution of mammalian reproduction in marsupials has been shaped by a complex interplay of genetic and environmental factors. Marsupials have evolved unique reproductive strategies that allow them to survive and thrive in a variety of environments. The pouched lifestyle has allowed marsupials to develop a unique reproductive system that is adapted to their environment, and their reproductive strategies have evolved to optimize reproduction in these environments.

title: Stage-Specific and Differential Notch Dependency at the αβ and γδ T Lineage Bifurcation
text: Notch signaling plays a crucial role in the differentiation of T cells, specifically in the specification and differentiation of αβ T lineage cells. However, the role of Notch signals during the decision to differentiate into αβ versus γδ T lineage cells remains unclear. To address this question, we employed a clonal analysis of CD4-CD8- (DN) progenitor potential to determine the timing of the divergence of αβ and γδ T cell lineages. Our findings show that Notch signals are critical for the transition of DN cells to CD4+CD8+ (DP) cells, regardless of the identity of the inducing T cell receptor complex. In contrast, γδ T cells develop independently of Notch ligand interaction. These findings demonstrate a stage-specific requirement for Notch receptor-ligand interactions in the differentiation of αβ and γδ T cells from T cell progenitors.

title: Investigating the Intron Recognition Mechanism in Eukaryotes
text: According to recent studies, it appears that introns and the complex splicing mechanism to remove them were present early in the evolution of eukaryotic organisms. This study aims to investigate the intron recognition mechanism by analyzing intron and exon characteristics from whole genome annotations. The study contrasts exon definition, which uses the exon as the unit of recognition and places length constraints on exons but not introns, with intron definition, which uses the intron itself as the unit of recognition and removes constraints on internal exon length. The study shows that it is possible to recover valid intron and exon information from genome annotations and compares internal intron and exon information from a range of eukaryotic genomes to investigate evolutionary length constraints on introns and exons and their impact on the intron recognition mechanism. The results suggest that exon definition-based mechanisms may predominate in vertebrates, although the exact system in fish is expected to show some differences with the better characterized system from mammals. The study also raises the possibility that the last common ancestor of plants and animals contained some type of exon definition, which was replaced in some genes and lineages by intron definition, possibly as a result of intron loss and/or intron shortening.

title: BRAF mutation predicts for MEK-dependence in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
text:
Introduction:
Constitutive ERK signaling is a common feature of human cancer, particularly in melanoma, colon, and thyroid cancers, and is often caused by activating mutations in BRAF, RAS, and upstream receptor tyrosine kinases. Among these mutations, missense BRAF kinase domain mutations are frequently observed in melanoma, colon, and thyroid cancers, and less frequently in lung and other cancer types. The majority of these mutations (>90%) involve a glutamic acid for valine substitution at codon 600 (V600E), which leads to increased BRAF kinase activity. In addition to V600E mutations, intermediate and impaired kinase activity mutations have also been identified, most frequently in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
Methods:
Using the potent and selective MEK1/2 inhibitor PD0325901 (Pfizer), we examined a panel of NSCLC cell lines with mutant EGFR, KRAS, and/or low, intermediate, and high-activity BRAF kinase domain mutations for MEK dependence. The IC50 values of MEK inhibition were determined for each cell line, and the proliferation of cells with non-V600E mutations was also evaluated.
Results:
Our results showed that NSCLC cells with V600E BRAF mutation were exquisitely sensitive to MEK inhibition, with an IC50 value of 2nM. In contrast, the proliferation of cells with non-V600E mutations was MEK dependent, with IC50 values ranging between 2.7 and 80 nM. Inhibition of MEK in these cells resulted in downregulation of cyclin D1 and G1 growth arrest, with variable induction of apoptosis. Interestingly, despite high basal ERK activity, NSCLC tumor cells with EGFR mutation were uniformly resistant to MEK inhibition, even at high doses (up to 500nM). Tumor cells with RAS mutation had a more variable response, with some cell lines demonstrating sensitivity, while others were completely resistant. There was no correlation between basal ERK activity and sensitivity to MEK inhibition. Furthermore, we observed a strong inverse correlation between Akt activity and PD0325901 sensitivity.
Discussion:
Our findings suggest that MEK inhibition may be a useful therapeutic strategy in tumors with V600E and non-V600E BRAF kinase domain mutations. However, the results also indicate that inhibition of both MEK and Akt signaling may be required in NSCLC tumors with high basal AKT activity. The results of this study have important implications for the development of targeted therapies for NSCLC, and highlight the complexity of the signaling pathways involved in cancer development and progression.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, our study provides new insights into the role of MEK signaling in NSCLC and highlights the potential of MEK inhibition as a therapeutic strategy in this disease. Further research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms underlying MEK inhibition and to identify the most effective strategies for targeting these pathways in NSCLC.

title: THE REGULATION OF NUMBERS OF TROPICAL OCEANIC BIRDS
text: The article examines the limitations on the numbers of tropical sea birds, focusing on food availability as the primary factor. However, it is argued that food shortages alone are unlikely to exert a density-dependent control on bird mortality outside the breeding season. The author rejects Wynne-Edwards' hypothesis that sea bird colonies can regulate their numbers by controlling the output of young, as unproven and improbable. Instead, the article suggests that as bird populations increase, competition for food becomes more intense, leading to a density-dependent control on the output of young and a regulation of bird numbers. The author also considers the adaptations of long-lived sea birds, such as clutches of one and deferred maturity, and suggests that these are not evolved to lower reproductive rates but rather to enable birds to raise single chicks in competition-ridden environments. Finally, the article explores the implications of this hypothesis for conservation and exploitation of sea bird populations in higher latitudes.

title: Induced pluripotent stem cell lines derived from human somatic cells.
text: Somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) enables trans-acting factors present in the mammalian oocyte to reprogram somatic cell nuclei to a pluripotent state. We demonstrate that four factors (OCT4, SOX2, NANOG, and LIN28) are sufficient to reprogram human somatic cells into pluripotent stem cells that exhibit the essential characteristics of embryonic stem (ES) cells. These induced pluripotent human stem cells have normal karyotypes, express telomerase activity, express cell surface markers and genes that characterize human ES cells, and retain the developmental potential to differentiate into advanced derivatives of all three primary germ layers. These induced pluripotent human cell lines have the potential to be used in the production of new disease models and in drug development, as well as for applications in transplantation medicine, once technical limitations such as viral integration-induced mutations are overcome.

title: Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum): A Review of Health Beneficial Physiological Effects
text: Among the esoteric spices used to enhance flavor and color in food, fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) also has the ability to modify the texture of food. In addition to its culinary uses, fenugreek has been employed in traditional medicine systems for its antibacterial, gastric stimulant, anorexia-fighting, and galactogogue properties. In recent years, numerous health-promoting physiological attributes of fenugreek seeds have been observed in both animal studies and human trials. These include antidiabetic, hypocholesterolemic, antioxidant, digestive stimulant, and hepatoprotective effects. Of these, the antidiabetic and hypocholesterolemic properties of fenugreek, which are primarily due to its dietary fiber content, hold the most promise for nutraceutical value. This article provides an overview of the experimental evidence supporting the nutraceutical potential of fenugreek seeds.

title: The Rat Brain in Stereotaxic Coordinates
text:
The Fifth Edition of "The Rat Brain in Stereotaxic Coordinates" has cemented its position as the second most cited book in science, following years of research and dedication to providing users with an updated and improved atlas of the rat brain. This latest edition features a completely new set of coronal sections from a single rat brain, offering significantly improved resolution through the addition of a third section level compared to previous editions. Moreover, numerous new nuclei and structures have been identified and included in the atlas.
To enhance usability, the drawings are presented in two colors, providing a clearer contrast between different structures. The accompanying CD-ROM contains all of the drawings from the atlas, as well as the corresponding color micrographs, which are not included in the printed book. This comprehensive and convenient resource continues the legacy of this major neuroscience publication, serving as a valuable guide for students and scientists studying the rat brain.
The atlas contains 161 coronal diagrams based on a single brain, each spaced at constant 120 m intervals for high resolution and ease of use. Blue color lines and black labels are used to facilitate the extraction of information. The stereotaxic grid was derived using the same techniques as previous editions, ensuring accuracy and consistency. Over 1000 structures are identified for the first time in this edition, making it an invaluable resource for researchers and students alike.

title: The Self-Incompatibility Genes of Brassica: Expression and Use in Genetic Ablation of Floral Tissues
text:
INTRODUCTION
Self-incompatibility is a crucial aspect of plant reproduction, ensuring that pollen from one plant cannot fertilize the ovules of another. This process is mediated by genetic differences between plants, which result in the inability of compatible pollen and ovules to combine. Understanding the genetic basis of self-incompatibility is essential for crop improvement, as it can be used to develop new varieties with improved fertility and reproductive success.
POLLINATION AND POLLEN TUBE GROWTH
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther of one plant to the stigma of another, and it is a critical step in the reproduction of plants. The growth and development of pollen tubes are essential for successful pollination, and any defects in this process can result in reduced fertility. Understanding the genetic basis of pollen tube growth and development can help identify genes involved in self-incompatibility and improve crop fertility.
INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE MALE GAMETOPHYTE AND PISTIL
The male gametophyte and pistil are the reproductive organs of plants, and they interact in a complex manner during pollination. The male gametophyte produces pollen grains, which are transferred to the stigma of the pistil during pollination. The pistil, in turn, receives the pollen grains and develops an ovule, which will eventually contain the fertilized egg cell. Understanding the interactions between these two organs is essential for understanding the genetic basis of self-incompatibility.
SELF-INCOMPATIBILITY SYSTEMS: GAMETOPHYTIC AND SPORO PHYTIC DETERMINATION OF POLLEN PHENOTYPE
Self-incompatibility is a complex trait that is determined by multiple genes, including both gametophytic and sporophytic genes. The gametophytic genes are responsible for the development of the male reproductive organs, while the sporophytic genes are responsible for the development of the female reproductive organs. Understanding the genetic basis of self-incompatibility can help identify genes involved in this process and improve crop fertility.
DEVELOPMENTAL STUDIES OF REPRODUCTIVE STRUCTURES
The development of reproductive structures in plants is a complex process that involves the interaction of multiple genes and hormones. Understanding the genetic basis of reproductive structure development can help identify genes involved in self-incompatibility and improve crop fertility.
MOLECULAR ANALYSIS OF SELF-INCOMPATIBILITY
Molecular analysis of self-incompatibility can help identify genes involved in this process and improve crop fertility. The S-M ultigene family of Brassica is one example of a self-incompatible system that has been studied using molecular techniques.
EXPRESSION OF THE SLG GENE IN PISTILS AND ANTERS
The SLG gene is involved in the self-incompatibility response in plants, and its expression in pistils and anthers can help identify genes involved in this process. The expression of the SLG gene in transgenic plants can also be used to study the genetic basis of self-incompatibility.
GENETIC INTERACTIONS IN SELF-INCOMPATIBILITY RESPONSES
Genetic interactions play a crucial role in the self-incompatibility response, and understanding these interactions can help identify genes involved in this process. The analysis of self-compatible lines and transgenic plants can help identify genes involved in self-incompatibility and improve crop fertility.
GENETIC ABLATION OF FLORAL TISSUES
The ablation of floral tissues can be used as a tool for studying plant development and improving crop fertility. The genetic ablation of floral tissues can help identify genes involved in the development of reproductive structures and improve crop fertility.
In conclusion, self-incompatibility is a complex trait that is determined by multiple genes, including both gametophytic and sporophytic genes. Understanding the genetic basis of self-incompatibility can help identify genes involved in this process and improve crop fertility. The use of molecular techniques, such as expression analysis and genetic ablation, can help identify genes involved in self-incompatibility and improve crop fertility.

title: The Ulp1 SUMO isopeptidase distinct domains required for viability, nuclear envelope localization, and substrate specificity
text: The ubiquitin-like SUMO protein is modified by the enzyme Ulp1 in many cellular regulatory mechanisms. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, both sumoylating and desumoylating activities are essential for viability. Of its two known desumoylating enzymes, Ulp1 and Ulp2/Smt4, Ulp1 is specifically required for cell cycle progression. The Ulp domain (UD) of Ulp1, a 200-residue segment, is conserved among Ulps and contains a core cysteine protease domain that is even more widespread. Here, we demonstrate that the Ulp1 UD can support wild-type growth rates and act as an independent protease in vitro, cleaving SUMO from substrates. However, in cells expressing only the UD of Ulp1, many SUMO conjugates accumulate to high levels, indicating that the non-essential NH2-terminal domain of Ulp1 is important for activity against a substantial fraction of sumoylated targets. The NH2-terminal domain also includes sequences necessary and sufficient to concentrate Ulp1 at nuclear envelope sites. Interestingly, NH2-terminally deleted Ulp1 variants are able to suppress defects in cells lacking the divergent Ulp2 isopeptidase, suggesting that the NH2-terminal regulatory domain of Ulp1 restricts Ulp1 activity towards certain sumoylated proteins while enabling the cleavage of others. These data define key functional elements of Ulp1 and highlight the importance of subcellular localization in determining SUMO isopeptidase specificity.

title: Gastropathies in the Lundehund
text: In this study, the mucin profiles of the gastric mucosa in Lundehunds with intestinal lymphangiectasia were compared to those in control dogs from other breeds. A previous study had shown that all examined Lundehunds had gastritis and approximately 30% had gastric carcinoma. The study used the periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Alcian blue (pH 2.5) periodic acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) methods to identify neutral and acid mucins. The acid mucins were then divided into sialomucins and sulfomucins based on their reaction with high-iron diamine Alcian blue, pH 2.5 (HID-AB). In Lundehunds with chronic atrophic gastritis in the fundic and body regions, the surface and foveolar epithelium showed a predominantly normal mucin profile, although some Lundehunds had a reduced mucin content. The mucous neck cells extended from below the gastric foveolae towards the muscularis mucosae. Morphometric examination showed that the abnormal presence of mucous neck cells occupied 41% of the height of the gastric mucosa in Lundehunds compared to only 19% in the control dogs (p<0.05). Of the four Lundehunds with gastric carcinoma, two possessed neoplastic cells that contained minimal or no mucins. The amount and type of mucin in the neoplastic cells of the remaining two Lundehunds varied both between individuals and within a neoplasm. The study found that the abnormal presence of mucous neck cells and the associated pseudopyloric metaplasia were the predominant changes in the gastric mucin profiles of Lundehunds.

title: MicroRNAs: small RNAs with a big role in gene regulation
text:
MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a family of small non-coding RNAs that play a crucial role in regulating gene expression. The founding members of the miRNA family, lin-4 and let-7, were initially identified in Caenorhabditis elegans through genetic screens for defects in larval development. Since then, hundreds of miRNAs have been identified in various metazoan genomes, including worms, flies, plants, and mammals. These miRNAs exhibit complex and temporally regulated expression patterns during various developmental and physiological processes.
Most miRNAs have been shown to regulate protein synthesis from their target mRNAs, while plant miRNAs typically direct the cleavage of their targets. The degree of complementarity between a miRNA and its target determines the regulatory mechanism. In animals, miRNAs are processed sequentially by two RNase-III enzymes, Drosha and Dicer, into a small, imperfect dsRNA duplex (miRNA:miRNA*) that contains both the mature miRNA strand and its complementary strand (miRNA*). The asymmetric assembly of the mature miRNA into the effector complex, the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC), is mediated by Ago proteins, which are present in multiple homologues in various metazoan genomes.
Bioinformatic prediction of miRNA targets has provided an important tool for exploring the functions of miRNAs. However, the overall success rate of such predictions remains to be determined by experimental validation. In summary, the discovery of miRNAs has significantly expanded our understanding of complex gene regulatory networks and their role in various biological processes.

title: Molecular mechanisms of invadopodium formation: the role of the N-WASP–Arp2/3 complex pathway and cofilin
text: Invadopodia are protrusions on the cell membrane rich in actin, with the ability to degrade the surrounding matrix, formed by invasive cancer cells. Through molecular analysis, we have investigated the mechanisms of invadopodium formation in metastatic carcinoma cells. Inhibition of the epidermal growth factor (EGF) receptor kinase in serum-rich conditions blocks invadopodium formation, while EGF stimulation of serum-starved cells induces their formation. RNA interference and dominant-negative mutant expression analyses revealed that the necessary components for invadopodium formation include neural WASP (N-WASP), Arp2/3 complex, and their upstream regulators, Nck1, Cdc42, and WIP. Time-lapse analysis showed that invadopodia are formed de novo at the cell periphery and have lifetimes ranging from minutes to several hours, with short-lived invadopodia being motile and long-lived invadopodia tending to be stationary. Interestingly, suppressing cofilin expression through RNA interference inhibited the formation of long-lived invadopodia, resulting in the formation of only short-lived invadopodia with reduced matrix degradation activity. These findings suggest that EGF receptor signaling regulates invadopodium formation through the N-WASP–Arp2/3 pathway, and cofilin is essential for the stabilization and maturation of invadopodia.

title: Genome downsizing in polyploid plants
text: All else being equal, polyploids are expected to have larger amounts of DNA in their unreplicated gametic nuclei (C-values) than their diploid ancestors, with the increase in C-value directly proportional to the level of ploidy. However, some polyploid series exhibit C-values that are lower than expected, suggesting that loss of DNA occurs during polyploid formation, leading to a phenomenon known as genome downsizing. The availability of the Angiosperm DNA C-values database has allowed researchers to investigate this phenomenon across a wide range of angiosperms and has revealed interesting patterns. Specifically, the mean 1C DNA amount does not increase linearly with ploidy, and the mean DNA amount per basic genome (calculated by dividing the 2C value by ploidy) tends to decrease with increasing ploidy. These findings suggest that genome downsizing may be a widespread and significant evolutionary phenomenon, with important implications for our understanding of the molecular events that occur during polyploid formation. Recent advances in our understanding of these processes, combined with new data on DNA amount changes, provide valuable insights into how genome downsizing may occur. The evolutionary forces driving DNA loss are also discussed.

title: Construction of an antisense CYP86MF gene plasmid vector and production of a male-sterile Chinese cabbage transformant by the pollen-tube method
text: A plant expression vector, pBIA9-AMF, was constructed by fusing an antisense fragment of the CYP86MF gene with the tapetum-specific A9 promoter. This vector was introduced into Chinese cabbage (Brassica campestris ssp. chinensis) and flowering Chinese cabbage (B. campestris ssp. chinensis var. parachinensis) using floral-dipping and pollen-tube transformation methods. The results showed that KanR seedlings could be obtained through germination tests of T1 progeny seeds using the pollen-tube method, but not through the floral-dipping method. One of the two KanR seedlings was further analyzed using PCR amplification and Southern blotting, which confirmed that the antisense fragment of the CYP86MF gene was integrated into the Chinese cabbage genome. Northern hybridization also indicated that the CYP86MF gene, under the A9 promoter, was inhibited in the transformant, and self-infertility was found in the transformed plants.

title: Stem Cells,Cancer and Cancer Stem Cells
text: Stem cells are characterized by their ability to both extensively self-renew and differentiate into various progenitor cells. Recent research has revealed that cancer patients harbor more resilient stem cells than common cancer cells. Identifying these differences could lead to the development of more effective classification, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for cancer.

title: Characterization and culture of human embryonic stem cells
text:
Objective:
To investigate the in vitro maintenance and characterization of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
Methods:
hESCs were cultured on a feeder layer using ES culture medium, which consists of 20% Knockout Serum Replacement, Knockout DMEM, and 10 ng/mL bFGF. The undifferentiated status of hESCs was evaluated through cell morphology and the expression of cell surface markers SSEA-1, SSEA-3, and TRA-1-60. Karyotype analysis was performed using the G banding technique. Pluripotency was evaluated through in vitro embryoid body (EB) formation and in vivo teratoma formation.
Results:
Most of the cells maintained their undifferentiated properties throughout extended culture periods, as evidenced by their normal karyotype and positive immunoreactivity to SSEA-3, SSEA-4, and TRA-1-60. In vitro EB formation and in vivo teratoma formation demonstrated the pluripotency of human ES cells.
Conclusion:
The maintenance of undifferentiated status and pluripotency are essential requirements for human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) in research and clinical applications. Our results demonstrate the potential of hESCs for these purposes.

title: Detection of Sugarcane bacilliform virus isolate and its influence on yield and quality of cane in Yunnan
text: Sugarcane bacilliform virus (SCBV) was detected through polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in sugarcane samples from Kaiyuan, Yunnan Province, showing symptoms of chlorosis and mottling. The replicase gene of the isolate SCBV-Kaiyuan was partially sequenced, revealing high levels of similarity between the virus and isolates from Australia (73.2%-74.0% at the nucleotide level and 83.1%-84.1% at the amino acid level), Morocco (66.7%-68.4% at the nucleotide level and 65.6%-67.7% at the amino acid level), and SCBV-Kaiyuan itself (589 bp shared identities of 73.2%-74.0% and 83.1%-84.1% at the nucleotide and amino acid levels). The quality and yield of sugarcane infected with SCBV-Kaiyuan were also investigated, revealing decreases in juice extraction, sucrose content, gravity purity, and average stalk weight, as well as an increase in reducing sugar content of 0.21% in infected plants.

title: Mitotic chromosomes fold by condensin-dependent helical winding of chromatin loop arrays
text: During mitosis, chromosomes transform into compact, rod-shaped structures. By combining imaging and Hi-C analysis of synchronized DT40 cell cultures with polymer simulations, we aimed to elucidate how interphase chromosomes are converted into compressed arrays of loops characteristic of mitotic chromosomes. Our findings reveal that interphase organization is disassembled within minutes of prophase entry, and by late prophase, chromosomes have already folded into arrays of consecutive loops. During prometaphase, this array reorganizes to form a helical arrangement of nested loops, as revealed by polymer simulations. These simulations suggest that Hi-C data are inconsistent with a solenoidal coiling of the entire chromatid, instead proposing a centrally located helically twisted axis from which consecutive loops emanate, similar to a spiral staircase. As mitosis progresses, chromosomes shorten through progressive helical winding, with the number of loops per turn increasing, resulting in larger helical turns. Condensin is essential for disassembling interphase chromatin structure, and our analysis of mutants revealed distinct roles for condensin I and II during these processes. Both condensins can mediate formation of loop arrays, but condensin II is specifically required for helical winding during prometaphase, while condensin I modulates the size and arrangement of loops within the helical turns. These findings uncover a mitotic chromosome morphogenesis pathway where folding of linear loop arrays produces long, thin chromosomes during prophase, which then shorten through progressive growth of loops and helical winding during prometaphase.

title: REVIEW ON CLINICALLY DEVELOPING ANTIBIOTICS
text:
The global antibiotic crisis is escalating, with a severe shortage of new drugs in development. Between 1940 and 1962, over 20 new classes of antibiotics were introduced to the market. However, since then, only two additional classes have been developed. This lack of innovation has led to a critical shortage of new antibiotics to combat the growing threat of antibiotic resistance, particularly among gram-negative bacteria, which are becoming increasingly resistant to existing treatments.
This review focuses on the antibiotics currently in late-stage clinical development, which offer hope for addressing this crisis. Most of these drugs belong to established antibiotic classes, but a few novel compounds with a narrow spectrum of activity are directed against novel targets.
Unfortunately, the history of antibiotic discovery and development has been marked by numerous failures, which have contributed to the current shortage. These failures have been caused by a range of factors, including the high cost of drug development, the lack of investment in antibiotic research, and the challenges of developing drugs that can effectively target multi-drug resistant bacteria.
To address these challenges and attract much-needed investment to fund the discovery of new antibiotics, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of antibiotic development, including the reasons for past failures and potential strategies for moving forward. By shining a light on the current landscape and highlighting the need for innovation, we hope to stimulate renewed interest and investment in this critical area of research.

title: Improved Au/Zn/Au ohmic contacts for p-type InP
text: In this study, an innovative Si3N4 layer was proposed as an out-diffusion barrier layer for the Au/Zn/Au contact system in p-type InP. The approach involved depositing a 200Å thick Si3N4 layer on the Au(200Å)/Zn(700Å)/Au(200Å) structure, followed by removal of the Si3N4 layer using HF and deposition of a 2000Å layer of pure gold to facilitate wire bonding. The resulting contact resistance dropped to a minimum value of 6×10-7 Ω•cm2 (for an acceptor concentration of about 3×1018 cm-3) and the contact became perfectly Ohmic. Additionally, the Si3N4 layer was found to be an excellent passivation layer and antireflection coating in InP/InGaAs/InP (p-i-n) photodiodes.

title: The reclamation of brine generated from desalination process by bipolar membrane electrodialysis
text:
Abstract:
This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) for the treatment of industrial saline water through techno-economic analyses and environmental impact evaluations. However, despite proving the technology's feasibility, some unsolved application-oriented problems hinder its implementation, such as the requirement for specific feed solutions, the availability of produced acids and bases, high salt concentrations in the effluent, and low desalination efficiency and capacity. To overcome these challenges, a novel hybrid process was designed by coupling conventional electrodialysis with monovalent selective cation-exchange membranes in a constant-voltage mode. The response surface methodology was employed to establish empirical models for understanding the influence of initial operating conditions on BMED performance. The BMED-based reclamation scheme was confirmed through a continuous BMED experiment on real solutions, with a focus on investigating the effects of product concentration on current efficiency and energy consumption. The results showed acceptable current efficiency and energy consumption when the product concentration was set at 0.9 M, which is suitable for the regeneration of ion-exchange resins.
Keywords: bipolar membrane electrodialysis, industrial saline water, reclamation, hybrid process, response surface methodology, ion-exchange process, current efficiency, energy consumption.

title: Process analysis and economic evaluation for Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) production by fermentation
text: Several processes for the production and recovery of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) were designed and analyzed using computer-aided bioprocess design, based on previously reported data. The processes were evaluated based on PHB productivity, content, and yield, which significantly impacted the final price of PHB. The annual production of 2,850 tonnes of purified PHB resulted in the lowest price of $5.58/kg when using Alcaligenes eutrophus with the recovery method of surfactant-hypochlorite digestion.
