As the production scale increased to one million tonnes per year, the price of PHB decreased to $4.75/kg. The use of agricultural wastes, such as whey and molasses, as carbon substrates can significantly lower the overall economics of large-scale production.

title: Modification in the chemical bath deposition apparatus, growth and characterization of CdS semiconducting thin films for photovoltaic applications
text:
In this study, we investigate the growth and characterization of CdS thin films using the Chemical Bath Deposition (CBD) technique. We modify a commonly available CBD system to achieve precise control over the pH of the solution during deposition at 90°C. Our findings reveal that the pH of the solution plays a crucial role in determining the quality of the CBD-CdS films.
We analyze the structural, optical, and electrical properties of the as-deposited and annealed films using X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and other techniques. Our results show that varying the cadmium ion concentration in the bath leads to changes in the crystallization of the CdS films, resulting in a transition from a cubic phase with (1 1 1) predominant orientation to a hexagonal phase with (0 0 2) predominant orientation. These structural changes also affect the optical and electrical properties of the films.
We observe that the optimum electrical resistivity, band gap, and refractive index values are achieved for the annealed films deposited at a cadmium ion concentration of 0.8 M. These films are suitable for solar cell applications. Furthermore, annealing the samples at 350°C in H2 for 30 min leads to an increased diffraction intensity and shifts in the peak towards lower scattering angles, resulting in an increase in the lattice parameters and a narrowing of the band-gap values. Our results are compared with previous work in the field.
In summary, our study demonstrates the importance of pH control in the CBD technique for growing high-quality CdS thin films with desired optical and electrical properties. The modified CBD system allows for precise control over the pH of the solution during deposition, enabling the growth of CdS films with optimized properties for various applications.

title: Combined sampler robot and high-performance liquid chromatography: a fully automated system for biological small-angle X-ray scattering experiments at the Synchrotron SOLEIL SWING beamline
text:
Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) for macromolecules in solution has gained popularity in structural biology as a complement to high-resolution structure determination obtained through X-ray crystallography or NMR. With the advent of third-generation synchrotron sources, there is a growing interest in developing sample environments and automation. The need for sample monodispersity has led to the development of an online purification system, which has been optimized at the SWING beamline of Synchrotron SOLEIL in France.
In the sample changer mode, a few microliters of sample can be injected between two air bubbles and circulated at a controlled speed of typically 40 µl min−1. This allows for the measurement of up to 14 samples per hour through remote control of the sample injections.
In the HPLC mode, an initially polydisperse sample can be separated into its individual components before immediate data acquisition. The sample cell is thermostatted, and offers visualization control and online UV–Vis absorption monitoring. This mode allows for the separation of macromolecules based on their size and charge, resulting in a more accurate representation of the sample's structure.
Overall, the combination of SAXS and HPLC at the SWING beamline provides a powerful tool for studying the structure and properties of macromolecules in solution, and has the potential to greatly enhance our understanding of these important biological molecules.

title: Feasibility assessment of desalination application in Australian traditional agriculture
text: Abstract: This paper provides an initial assessment of areas in Australia with potential for implementing desalination technologies to supply water for agriculture, subject to certain limitations. Using a set of criteria, areas were identified within a national scale that are suitable for desalination based on distance from existing irrigated agriculture and feedlots, town sites, and environmental protection areas. The study found that industries involved in high-value crop production are most likely to benefit from desalinated water due to their more efficient irrigation practices and highest gross value of irrigated agricultural production. Groundwater was identified as the most feasible feedwater source for cost-effective desalination, which is consistent with global trends. However, brine disposal remains a crucial factor in the overall cost-effectiveness of desalination. When feedwater salinity is relatively low, mixing permeate with feedwater can increase water production and reduce costs. The study estimated that Australian farmers are unlikely to pay more than AU$1.2/kL for agricultural water. While desalinated water is generally more expensive than water from other sources, there may be situations where the costs are comparable.

title: Development of a specific monoclonal antibody assay and a rapid testing strip for the detection of apramycin residues in food samples
text:
Abstract:
A monoclonal antibody (MAb) specific to apramycin (AP) was produced and utilized to develop an indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (idcELISA) and a rapid testing strip for the detection of AP residues in foods. The MAb exhibited minimal cross-reactivity with other aminoglycosides. Under optimized conditions in 0.01 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), the half maximum inhibitory concentration (IC50) of the MAb was 0.41 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.15 ng/mL. The ELISA results were obtained within 90 minutes. The mean recoveries from all spiked food samples were within the range of 79.02% to 105.49%, with coefficients of variation in the range of 2.21% to 11.4%. The strip test results obtained within 5 minutes had visual LODs in the range of 2.5 μg/kg to 5 μg/kg (ng/mL) for all food samples tested. Therefore, the developed strip test represents a rapid and convenient method for detecting AP residues in foods.

title: Utilization of Desalination Brine for Sodium Hydroxide Production: Technologies, Engineering Principles, Recovery Limits, and Future Directions
text: As global desalination capacity continues to expand rapidly, the need to minimize the adverse environmental impacts of brine discharge also increases. Although modern brine outfall designs have significantly reduced these impacts, they are still costly. Recovering valuable components and chemical derivatives from brine could address both environmental and economic concerns. In this article, we examine methods for producing sodium hydroxide (NaOH) from seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) brine for internal reuse, which typically involve brine purification, concentration, and sodium chloride electrolysis. We evaluate the energy consumption of these processes and compare them to thermodynamic minimum energy consumption and maximum NaOH production rates. By reviewing the latest technologies, we identify five existing facilities that are benchmarked against these standards.

title: Training toddlers seated on mobile robots to drive indoors amidst obstacles
text: The primary objective of this research is to train young children seated on mobile robots to drive purposefully and safely within indoor environments. Our previous studies have demonstrated that infants can acquire the ability to drive directly to a target using conventional joysticks within approximately six weeks of training. However, these children are unable to develop the advanced skill of avoiding obstacles while driving, which limits their mobility and hinders their cognitive and social development in the critical early years. To address this issue, we have designed an obstacle course for toddlers to drive a robot through, while utilizing algorithms based on artificial potential fields to create a force field on the joystick that trains them to navigate safely around obstacles. In this 'assist-as-needed' approach, if the child steers the mobile robot outside of a force tunnel centered around the desired direction, the driver experiences a bias force on the hand. Our findings suggest that the use of force-feedback joysticks leads to faster learning compared to conventional joysticks.

title: Coming soon to a Wal-Mart near you
text: According to the website of the Association for Automatic Identification and Data Capture Technologies (AIM Global), "RFID technology enables the automatic collection of product, place, and time or transaction data without human intervention or error, providing real-time supply chain visibility. RFID technology has the potential to track everything from crates of disposable razors to individual peanut-butter jars on store shelves. Promoters of RFID technology, such as C. Humer (2003), believe that 'RF tags are to this decade what the Internet was to the 1990s - a promise of radical change in the way business is done.' However, several hurdles must be overcome before the full potential of RFID technology can be realized, including reliability, cost, lack of standards, and security. As these hurdles are gradually addressed, Wal-Mart has publicly embraced the technology."

title: Innovative beneficial reuse of reverse osmosis concentrate using bipolar membrane electrodialysis and electrochlorination processes
text:
Reverse osmosis (RO) is a widely used and rapidly growing desalination technology, but it has a significant drawback: the concentrate produced by the RO process, which can make up to 25% of the feed stream, is a polluting stream that can pose a significant challenge for its implementation, particularly for inland communities without the option of ocean disposal. An environmentally benign approach to disposal could be beneficial reuse of the waste stream. This study presents two innovative beneficial reuse strategies for RO concentrate produced by an integrated membrane system (IMS) from a wastewater reclamation facility.
The technologies evaluated in this study include bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) for converting RO concentrate into mixed acid and mixed base streams, and electrochlorination (EC) for on-site chlorine generation. Bench-scale studies showed that BMED can desalt the RO concentrate while producing mixed acids and mixed bases with concentrations as high as 0.2N. Similarly, the EC process can produce a 0.6% hypochlorite solution from RO concentrate. The acids and bases, as well as the hypochlorite, can be directly applied to the RO process and upstream pre-treatment processes.
A preliminary economic evaluation was conducted to assess the viability of these two approaches. Rough order of magnitude cost estimates were based on the bench-scale performance of these processes on RO concentrate. The comparison of the overall costs of an Integrated Membrane System utilizing these innovative reuse strategies with conventional disposal options and thermal zero liquid discharge treatment indicates that a reuse approach might be economically viable for inland wastewater reuse facilities that utilize RO membranes and have limited options for concentrate disposal.

title: Amplification of siRNA in Caenorhabditis elegans generates a transgenerational sequence-targeted histone H3 lysine 9 methylation footprint
text: Exogenous double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) has been shown to exert effects on both the stability of target mRNA and chromatin structure. Using the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans as a model organism, we investigated the generality, scope, and longevity of dsRNA-targeted chromatin effects, as well as their dependence on components of the RNAi machinery. Using high-resolution genome-wide chromatin profiling, we found that a diverse set of genes can be induced to acquire locus-specific enrichment of histone H3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me3) with modification footprints extending several kilobases from the site of dsRNA homology. Genetic analysis revealed that factors responsible for secondary siRNA production during RNAi were necessary for effective targeting of chromatin. Temporal analysis showed that H3K9me3 can be maintained in the absence of dsRNA for at least two generations before being lost, implying that dsRNA-triggered chromatin modification in C. elegans defines a programmable and locus-specific response that can persist through generational boundaries.

title: Physicians' initial management of acute low back pain versus evidence-based guidelines. Influence of sciatica.
text:
The study aimed to assess the consistency of physicians' management decisions with evidence-based guidelines for acute low back pain, and to examine how physician characteristics and patient presentations (i.e., sciatica) influenced compliance.
The study was a cross-sectional survey of randomly selected physicians from internal medicine, family practice, general practice, emergency medicine, and occupational medicine specialties. Participants were asked to provide recommendations for two case scenarios, one representing a patient without sciatica and the other with sciatica.
The results showed that only 26.9% of physicians fully complied with the guideline for the case without sciatica, and only 4.3% complied for the case with sciatica. The odds of guideline noncompliance increased by 1.03 times for each year of practice, and the greatest odds of noncompliance were observed in general practice, internal medicine, and emergency medicine. For the case with sciatica, internal medicine had the highest odds of noncompliance (6.93, 95% CI=1.47 to 32.78), followed by family practice and emergency medicine.
The study found that sciatica significantly influenced clinical decision-making, leading to increased noncompliance with evidence-based guidelines. The authors suggest that physicians' misunderstanding of sciatica's natural history and belief that more intensive initial management is indicated may contribute to this observation.
In summary, the study found that a majority of primary care physicians continue to be noncompliant with evidence-based back pain guidelines, with sciatica significantly influencing clinical decision-making. The study highlights the need for ongoing education and training to improve physician understanding of sciatica and its management.

title: Appropriate Critical Values When Testing for a Single Multivariate Outlier by Using the Mahalanobis Distance
text: The Mahalanobis distance is a widely used criterion for detecting outliers in multivariate data, but there is ongoing debate about the appropriate critical values to use. This paper compares the Mahalanobis distance with Wilks's method and shows that the previously recommended critical values, {p(n-1)/(n-p)}Fp,n−p, are not suitable for detecting a single outlier. Instead, the correct critical values are p(n-1)2Fp,n−p−1/n(n−p−1+pFp,n−p−1). These critical values are illustrated through an example using clinical laboratory data from 10 patients and five variables. Additionally, the paper discusses the jackknifed Mahalanobis distance and provides relevant critical values. Finally, the paper discusses upper bounds for the usual Mahalanobis distance and the jackknifed version.

title: How to calculate sample size in animal studies
text: "Before starting any animal study, it is crucial for researchers to determine the appropriate sample size. This is essential to detect even small significant differences between groups. A small sample size can lead to insignificant results and less power in the study. Calculating sample size involves complex statistical methods, but there are simplified approaches that can help non-statisticians conduct the calculation. By doing so, researchers can ensure their study has adequate statistical power to produce reliable and meaningful results."

title: On the Theory and Computation of Evolutionary Distances
text: This paper provides a rigorous definition of the biological concept of evolutionary distance and a computational algorithm to compute it. For any set of finite sequences of varying lengths, this distance is a real-valued function on the Cartesian product $S \times S$, and it is shown to satisfy the properties of a metric under a broad range of conditions that are relevant to biological applications. The algorithm introduced here is easily implementable in computer programs and offers a computationally efficient method for computing evolutionary distance that is more effective than existing methods.

title: Over 30% efficient InGaP/GaAs tandem solar cells
text:
A novel two-terminal monolithic InGaP/GaAs tandem solar cell with an unprecedented efficiency record of 30.28% has been developed, covering a practical large area of 4 cm². This achievement was accomplished under one-sun air-mass 1.5 global illumination. To enhance the performance of the tandem cell, we introduced a double-hetero (DH) structure, where InGaP layers are sandwiched between high band gap AlInP barriers. This DH structure not only boosts the peak current of the InGaP tunnel junction but also effectively reflects minority carriers in the top cell using the AlInP barrier located directly beneath the InGaP top cell, which serves as a back surface field (BSF) layer.
The AlInP BSF layer acts as a high potential barrier, preventing the diffusion of zinc from a high-doped tunnel junction towards the top cell during epitaxial growth. Moreover, the InGaP tunnel junction reduces the absorption loss that occurs in a GaAs tunnel junction, while increasing the photogenerated current. This results in a significant improvement in the overall efficiency of the tandem solar cell.

title: Electrical, optical, and structural properties of indium-tin-oxide thin films for organic light-emitting devices
text: High-quality indium-tin-oxide (ITO) thin films (200-850 nm) were grown using pulsed laser deposition (PLD) on glass substrates without a post-deposition annealing treatment. The structural, electrical, and optical properties of these films were investigated as a function of target composition, substrate deposition temperature, background gas pressure, and film thickness. Films were deposited from various target compositions containing 0-15 wt% SnO2, with the optimum composition for high conductivity found to be 5 wt% SnO2 + 95 wt% In2O3. Deposition was performed at substrate temperatures ranging from room temperature to 300 °C in O2 partial pressures of 1-100 mTorr. The films were deposited using a KrF excimer laser (248 nm, 30 ns full width at half maximum) at a fluence of 2 J/cm2. For a 150-nm-thick ITO film grown at room temperature in an oxygen pressure of 10 mTorr, the resistivity was 4×10−4 Ω cm and the average transmission in the visible range (400-700 nm) was 85%. For a 170-nm-thick film grown at 300 °C in an oxygen pressure of 10 mTorr, the resistivity was 1×10−4 Ω cm and the average transmission in the visible range was 90%.

title: Disaster Management and Community Planning, and Public Participation: How to Achieve Sustainable Hazard Mitigation
text:
The paper begins by providing a brief historical overview of disaster management planning, before moving on to examine the current state of research in Australia and America. These findings suggest that the field of disaster management should shift its focus from response and recovery to sustainable hazard mitigation, and that this shift requires integrating disaster management and community planning. Unfortunately, current practice often fails to reflect this synthesis, which is one reason why hazard awareness is often absent from local decision-making processes.
The paper then argues that successful implementation of mitigation strategies requires public participation at the local decision-making level. To illustrate this point, the paper concludes with a case study of California's Portola Valley, which demonstrates how public participation can be successfully integrated into disaster management planning and community planning, leading to sustainable hazard mitigation.

title: A second generation of homogenized Canadian monthly surface air temperature for climate trend analysis
text: This study presents a second-generation dataset for analyzing Canadian climate trends. The dataset includes monthly mean surface air temperatures at 338 locations across Canada, with adjustments made to account for changes in observing times and non-climatic shifts. Two techniques were used to detect and adjust for these discontinuities: a multiple linear regression-based test and a penalized maximal t-test. The adjusted data were then analyzed to estimate temperature trends for Canada (1950-2010) and Southern Canada (1900-2010). The results show that temperature has increased at most locations, with an average annual increase of 1.5°C over Canada from 1950 to 2010, and a greater warming in the minimum temperature compared to the maximum temperature. Similarly, for Southern Canada, the warming is more pronounced in the minimum temperature over the period 1900-2010.

title: Prevention of radiographic-contrast-agent-induced reductions in renal function by acetylcysteine.
text:
Background: Radiographic contrast agents have been shown to cause a decrease in renal function, which may be attributed to the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). The efficacy of antioxidants in preventing this reduction in renal function is currently unknown.
Methods: In a prospective study, we evaluated 83 patients with chronic renal insufficiency (mean serum creatinine concentration, 2.4±1.3 mg/dL [216±116 micromol/L]) undergoing computed tomography with a nonionic, low-osmolality contrast agent. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either oral acetylcysteine (600 mg twice daily) and 0.45% saline intravenously before and after contrast agent administration or placebo and saline.
Results: Ten of the 83 patients (12%) experienced an increase in serum creatinine concentration of at least 0.5 mg/dL (44 micromol/L) within 48 hours of contrast agent administration: 1 of 41 patients (2%) in the acetylcysteine group and 9 of 42 patients (21%) in the control group (P=0.01; relative risk, 0.1; 95% CI, 0.02-0.9). In the acetylcysteine group, the mean serum creatinine concentration decreased significantly (P<0.001), from 2.5±1.3 to 2.1±1.3 mg/dL (220±118 to 186±112 micromol/L) 48 hours after contrast agent administration, whereas in the control group, the mean serum creatinine concentration increased nonsignificantly (P=0.18), from 2.4±1.3 to 2.6±1.5 mg/dL (212±114 to 226±133 micromol/L) (P<0.001 compared to the control group).
Conclusions: Prophylactic oral administration of acetylcysteine, along with hydration, prevents the reduction in renal function induced by contrast agents in patients with chronic renal insufficiency.

title: Sample size calculation in epidemiological studies
text:
Determining the appropriate sample size for an epidemiological study is a crucial step in the statistical design of the project. The sample size depends on the type of study, such as descriptive, observational, or randomized controlled trial. In this article, we will discuss the formulas used to estimate sample size in epidemiological trials and provide examples from clinical practice to illustrate the concept.
An adequate sample size is essential to ensure that the study yields reliable information, regardless of whether the results show a clinically important difference between treatments or measure the accuracy of a diagnostic test or disease incidence. Unfortunately, many studies published in medical literature have inadequate sample sizes, making it difficult to interpret negative results. Conducting a study with an insufficient sample size is not only futile but also unethical, as it exposes patients to unnecessary risks.
The question of how many individuals to study is commonly asked by clinical investigators and highlights one of the many issues that need to be addressed before conducting a study. Consultation with a statistician is valuable in addressing study design issues, but a statistician may not always be readily available.
Sample size (n) is the number of individuals in a study group. A larger sample size provides greater precision and power to detect an effect of a given size. For statisticians, an n > 30 is usually sufficient for the Central Limit Theorem to hold, allowing for normal theory approximations to be used for measures such as the standard error of the mean. However, this sample size (n = 30) is unrelated to the clinician's objective of detecting biologically significant effects, which determines the specific sample size needed for a particular study.

title: Tammarniit (Mistakes): Inuit Relocation in the Eastern Arctic, 1939-63
text:
Preface:
Introduction
Chapter 1: Are Inuit Indians?: Exploring Relief, Jurisdiction, and Government Responsibility
Chapter 2: Social Welfare and Social Crisis in the Eastern Arctic: An Overview
Chapter 3: Planning for Relocation in the Eastern Arctic: A Critical Examination
Chapter 4: Recolonizing the Arctic Islands: The 1953 Relocations to Resolute Bay and Craig Harbour
Chapter 5: The Ennadai Lake Relocations, 1950-60: A Study in Forced Migration
Chapter 6: The Garry Lake Famine: A Tragic Chapter in Inuit History
Chapter 7: The Whale Cove Relocation: A Case Study in Government Intervention
Chapter 8: Relocation and Responsibility, 1955-63: A Legal and Ethical Analysis

Notes
Bibliography
Index

title: Levels of selection in evolution
text: Since the groundbreaking work of George Williams, W. D. Hamilton, and Richard Dawkins, evolutionary biologists have recognized that natural selection operates at various levels, including the individual, cell, and gene. However, the question remains as to how these different levels of selection can coexist without compromising the common interests gained through cooperation. To address this issue, twelve prominent scientists in this volume explore the current state of theoretical and empirical research in evolutionary biology, examining the mechanisms that prevent conflict between different levels of selection. Editor Laurent Keller aims to bridge the gap between molecular and organismal biologists by bringing together leading researchers from various disciplines to discuss potential conflicts and their resolution. The chapters in this book follow a rigorous theoretical framework, providing a unique synergy that is characteristic of multi-authored works. The contributors, including the editor, are H. Charles J. Godfray, Edward Allen Herre, Dawn M. Kitchen, Egbert Giles Leigh, Jr., Catherine M. Lessells, Richard E. Michod, Leonard Nunney, Craig Packer, Andrew Pomiankowski, H. Kern Reeve, John Maynard Smith, and Eors Szathmary.

title: A psychometric evaluation of the Beck Depression Inventory–II.
text: This article offers psychometric insights into the second edition of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II; A. T. Beck, R. A. Steer, & G. K. Brown, 1996), focusing on internal consistency, factorial validity, and gender differences. Both versions of the inventory demonstrated strong internal reliability in the overall student sample. The findings revealed significant disparities between the mean BDI and BDI-II scores, leading to the development of new cutoffs for analogous research on the BDI-II. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses revealed that a 2-factor solution best represented the data for both versions of the inventory, accounting for approximately 41% and 46% of the shared variance in BDI and BDI-II responses, respectively. These factor solutions were reliably cross-validated, with each factor displaying varying importance across gender groups. The authors conclude that the BDI-II is a more robust instrument than the BDI in terms of its factor structure.

title: Why people feel crowded: An examination of objective and subjective crowding
text: Previous studies have found only a limited connection between the physical density of a space and people's perception of crowding, which goes against common sense and previous research. Using data from a representative sample of Bangkok, Thailand, where households are four times more crowded than in Western societies, we investigate possible explanations for this discrepancy. By examining seven different measures of objective crowding, our analysis reveals that the modest relationship observed in previous studies is not due to measurement errors. Contrary to expectations, our findings suggest that the relationship between objective and subjective crowding is nonlinear, with a ceiling effect that limits the impact of increased objective crowding. Additionally, we find that part of the perceived crowding can be attributed to household-specific factors, such as the degree of control individuals have over the use of household space.

title: Self-Report and Tests of Memory Aging
text: Despite a lack of correlation between memory complaints and objective tests of memory, self-report questions that assess everyday memory processes have been found to be well-correlated with both self-report and performance measures. In a study of 60 volunteers aged 21-84 years, self-report ratings of memory competence were categorized into four processes and found to be moderately correlated with performance measures on six tests of verbal, faces, story, and nonverbal memory, both of which declined with age in parallel. Interestingly, older participants were more accurate in their self-report ratings than younger participants, but this difference was not observed across all tests. Additionally, some participants' performance appeared to be influenced by their expectations, with poorer performance in certain tests.

title: Code of the Street: Decency, Violence, and the Moral Life of the Inner City
text: Inner-city black America is often associated with senseless street violence, but this is not a random act. In fact, violence is regulated through an informal yet well-known code of the street. The way one dresses, talks, makes eye contact, and understands the social hierarchy can have life-or-death consequences, particularly for young people. This code is a response to the lack of well-paying jobs, racial stigma, drug use, alienation, and hopelessness. The police have little control, and an individual's safety and self-worth are determined by how much respect they can command in public. This is based on physical and psychological control, as well as an implied threat of violence. The strong, loving, and decent family is the most powerful force counteracting this code, but the culture of the street often overshadows decency, entangling individuals with better aspirations in its grasp.

title: A generic measure of relationship satisfaction.
text: In today's diverse society, there is a need for brief and reliable measures of relationship satisfaction that can be applied to various types of close relationships. This article aims to develop such a measure. Study I involved 125 individuals who identified themselves as "in love" and administered the 7-item Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS). The results revealed a unifactorial scale structure, significant factor loadings, and moderate interitem correlations. The scale also correlated with measures of love, sexual attitudes, self-disclosure, commitment, and investment in a relationship. Study II involved 57 couples in ongoing relationships and supported a single factor, alpha reliability of .86, and significant correlations with relevant relationship measures. The RAS also correlated .80 with a longer criterion measure, the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (Spanier, 1976), and both scales were effective in distinguishing between couples who remained together and those who broke up. The RAS is a brief, psychometrically sound, and generic measure of relationship satisfaction.

title: ECONOMIC RESTRUCTURING AND SUBURBANIZATION IN CHINA
text: Similar to other countries, suburbanization in China emerged after urban areas experienced a prolonged period of industrial and population growth. This study focuses on suburbanization in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenyang, and Dalian. As a result of economic restructuring, the urban core witnessed net population loss from 1982 to 1990 due to decentralization, while the inner suburbs experienced growth. The forces driving suburbanization included marketization of urban land, shift of industrial land to tertiary uses, improved transportation, availability of foreign and domestic capital, housing rehabilitation in the city, and new housing construction in the suburbs. While there are some similarities between American and Chinese suburbanization, there are also notable differences. Unlike the current metropolitan landscape in the United States, where suburban growth has led to a polycentric spatial structure, suburbanization in China is still in its early stages of development, with suburbs dominated by centralized commercial and residential areas.

title: The Assumption of Caregiving: Grandmothers Raising the Children of the Crack Cocaine Epidemic:
text: In this study, researchers examined the experiences of 71 African American women who have taken on the role of sole caregiver for their grandchildren or great-grandchildren due to their parents' involvement in crack cocaine use. Through in-depth interviews and participant observation, the study identified three distinct patterns of caregiving: sudden assumption, negotiated assumption, and inevitable assumption of the permanent caregiver role. Each pattern is characterized by six dimensions: forewarning, initiation, the trigger event, the caregiver's goal, her assumed trajectory of the caregiving period, and her perceived influence on her own destiny. These findings offer valuable insights for professionals working with families and individuals affected by the crack cocaine epidemic, as well as a unique perspective on the consequences of drug addiction on families.

title: The effect of information related to fat content and taste on consumer responses to a reduced-fat frankfurter and a reduced-fat chocolate bar
text: In a study to investigate the impact of product information on consumer preferences, researchers compared sensory and hedonic ratings of frankfurter sausages and chocolate bars in two conditions: blind tasting and tasting with information present. Additionally, the effect of information alone was examined by asking subjects to rate the expected sensory and hedonic intensities of the products based on packages with different claims. Three groups of subjects were tested, each receiving different information: a basic group with no added claims (n = 31), a reduced-fat group with products claimed to have reduced fat (n = 29), and a flavorful group with products claimed to have full meat/chocolate flavor (n = 31). The study found that product information significantly increased the perceived pleasantness of the frankfurters in all three information groups compared to blind ratings. However, the information did not affect the pleasantness of the chocolate bars. The reduced-fat group rated the expected attribute intensities of the frankfurters and chocolates lower than the other groups. The study suggests that the impact of product information is more pronounced in ratings of sensory attributes than in pleasantness ratings.

title: Transnationalism and identity
text: Transnationalism and identity are intrinsically linked concepts, as many individuals' and groups' transnational connections are based on a shared sense of identity. Conversely, people's identities are often shaped within social contexts that span multiple locations. This introductory article will explore the transnational perspective on migration studies, followed by critiques and outstanding questions. The final section will summarize the key points raised by the contributing authors of the main articles in this themed issue of JEMS, with a focus on how transnational settings and dynamics influence the construction, negotiation, and reproduction of identities.

title: Social Isolation and Social Support: An Applied Perspective
text: There is considerable empirical evidence highlighting the significance of social networks and support for the health and well-being of older adults. However, more research is needed before effective interventions can be widely implemented to positively impact an elderly person's social network. This article discusses the importance of social support and isolation from an applied perspective, drawing on presentations originally given at a National Institute on Aging-sponsored symposium on applied gerontology in 1992. The authors make general observations about the field of applied social relations in later life, discuss the mental health aspects of these relations, outline fundamental principles and existing technology in this field, describe the use of a brief screening instrument for social isolation developed by one of the authors (Lubben), and explore various domains of knowledge concerning elder social relations. Finally, the authors conclude by identifying areas that require further attention and research in order to improve the well-being of older adults.

title: Wine and health: faraway concepts?
text:
Purpose: This study aims to investigate consumers' perceptions and beliefs regarding the health benefits of wine and their consumption patterns.
Design/Methodology/Approach: A face-to-face in-store survey was conducted among 402 wine consumers, which was analyzed using two-step cluster analysis. ANOVA confirmed differences among the groups. Subsequent chi-square significance analysis was conducted to profile the groups. A multivariate binary logistic regression was used to estimate the influence of wine consumption on healthiness perceptions.
Findings: The study identified four distinct consumer groups: two health-oriented groups (optimistic and medical) and two non-health-oriented groups (unintentional drinker and unconvinced). Notably, these groups did not differ significantly in terms of socio-economic factors. The study found that wine consumption behavior significantly influenced health orientation, with monthly and wine drinkers showing a stronger preference for health-enhancing wine compared to weekly and other alcohol drinkers. Health-oriented consumers were more willing to pay a premium for wine with perceived health benefits. Consumers believed that wine could enhance their overall health, particularly cardiovascular health, and were more likely to associate wine with positive health benefits than negative ones.
In summary, the study revealed that consumers' perceptions and beliefs about the health benefits of wine are complex and influenced by various factors, including consumption patterns and socio-demographic characteristics. The findings provide valuable insights for wine producers and marketers seeking to capitalize on the growing demand for health-enhancing products.

title: The Changing Problem of Overcrowded Housing
text: Overcrowding in the United States has experienced a sudden and significant increase after decades of decline, with some areas and ethnic groups being disproportionately affected. The nature of this issue and its definition for policy purposes are evolving, with important implications for how it is addressed. We investigate the unique characteristics of overcrowded areas, where they are located, and the factors contributing to the resurgence of overcrowding. Ethnicity, age, immigration, and poverty play a significant role in the incidence of crowding, but housing market conditions are less important. Additionally, we highlight that the standard used to determine overcrowding is relative and has varied over time, and that social norms differ among ethnic groups. The issue of overcrowding may serve as an example of the challenges in implementing uniform standards in a diverse, multiethnic society. To better target worst-case housing needs in highly impacted areas, we suggest allowing for more "place diversity" in the setting of standards.

title: Best response dynamics and socially stable strategies
text:
An evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS), as first introduced by Maynard Smith and Price in Nature (London) in 1973, is a strategy that is resistant to small perturbations or "invasions" of mutants. In other words, an ESS is a strategy that can withstand the emergence of a small number of mutants that deviate from the dominant strategy.
The concept of ESS has been further developed by Gilboa and Matsui in Econometrica in 1991, who proposed a stability concept based on a dynamic process known as best response dynamics. In this process, the frequency of a strategy increases only if it is the best response to the current distribution of strategies.
This paper demonstrates the equivalence between two different stability concepts: the static concept and the dynamic one. The set-valued versions of these concepts always exist, and examples are provided to illustrate their usefulness in analyzing forward induction and preplay communication.
In summary, this paper explores the relationship between two different stability concepts in the context of evolutionarily stable strategies, and demonstrates their equivalence through a dynamic process known as best response dynamics.

title: From youth to adult homelessness
text: Governments have shown interest in early intervention strategies to prevent youth homelessness, but critics argue that these programs lack clear outcomes. This study investigates the consequences of not implementing early intervention measures and how young people fare when they transition to adult homelessness. The study tests the 'social adaptation' hypothesis, which suggests that the longer a person is homeless, the more they adapt to it as a way of life. The study examines data from 1,677 individuals who became homeless before the age of 18, of which three-quarters had progressed to adult homelessness (defined as 25 or older) and one-quarter were young adults aged 19 to 24. The findings reveal that the longer a person is homeless, the more challenging it becomes to escape homelessness. However, the social adaptation hypothesis overstates the extent to which people accept homelessness as a permanent lifestyle. With long-term support, people can transition back to conventional accommodation. The study concludes with three policy recommendations.

title: Urban spatial development in the land policy reform era: evidence from Beijing
text: This study examines the characteristics of urban spatial development in Beijing and assesses the extent to which these characteristics can be attributed to the emerging land market in Beijing, as well as the impact of land policy reform. Using empirical analysis of land use rights granted from 1993 to the first half of 2000 in the built-up area of Beijing, the study finds that both land prices and land development density decrease with distance to the city core. Additionally, the study reveals that the slope of the land rent curve depends on land use types. These findings suggest that the land market plays a significant role in shaping land development decisions and urban form. The study also shows that the slope of the land rent curve and the elasticity of land-capital substitution change over time. Specifically, the former decreases, likely due to Beijing's massive investments in transportation, which have reduced transport costs and shifted the land rent curve. Conversely, the latter increases, indicating a greater price effect on land development density. These changes in the land rent function and the elasticity of land-capital substitution suggest that the Beijing land market is maturing. It is important to note, however, that there are significant land developments outside of the formal land market (land development on administratively allocated land), which can distort urban land use patterns and affect the findings of this study.

title: The Mismatch Argument: The Construction of a Housing Orthodoxy in Australia
text:
In Australia, the housing policy discourse is characterized by a number of entrenched beliefs or "orthodoxies." While these orthodoxies are not universally accepted within the discourse, they hold significant symbolic authority and shape the way policy discussions unfold. One of the most influential orthodoxies in Australia is the notion of a "mismatch" between the available housing stock and the size of households, resulting in underutilization and underoccupation of housing. This mismatch argument is often taken for granted in housing policy discussions, and criticism of it can take various forms, including empirical, conceptual, and discursive.
The discursive critique of the mismatch orthodoxy focuses less on the empirical relationship between households and dwellings, and more on the statements made about this relationship. By examining the construction of the mismatch orthodoxy over time, this paper aims to uncover how it arose, how it has been maintained, and its impact on housing discourse.
The analysis reveals that the orthodoxy has been constructed through a series of structural and discursive processes, beginning in the early 1970s and solidifying in national and state housing policy research by the early 1990s. Despite empirical and conceptual criticisms of the mismatch orthodoxy, it has remained entrenched in the discourse, with significant consequences for how people are perceived and treated who are deemed to be underutilizing their dwellings. Moreover, the orthodoxy has shaped policy interpretations, such as occupancy standards, in ways that reinforce the mismatch narrative.
In conclusion, the study highlights the importance of examining the construction and maintenance of orthodoxies in housing policy discourse, and the need to challenge and critique them in order to promote more inclusive and equitable housing policies.

title: Citizen Participation and Citizen Evaluation in Disaster Recovery
text: In April 1997, the twin cities of Grand Forks, North Dakota, and East Grand Forks, Minnesota, faced a devastating flood that left both cities in ruins. However, while both cities have been recognized by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) as textbook examples of success, their paths have diverged significantly in the aftermath of the disaster. East Grand Forks embraced citizen participation initiatives, leading to political stability and high citizen satisfaction. In contrast, Grand Forks relied primarily on bureaucratic guidance, resulting in changes in government structure, turnover of elected and appointed officials, and less positive citizen evaluations. This study aims to investigate the impact of perceptions of citizen participation on citizens' assessments of the success of the recovery effort.

title: Population growth, urban sprawl and landscape integrity of Beijing City
text:
The detailed landscape pattern within the 6th ring road area of Beijing City was identified using airborne remote sensing data acquired between 1997 and 2002. Landscape indices were computed at the landscape level using Fragstats 3.3, and changes in land use/cover types in Beijing during the same period were examined. The results indicate that there were significant changes in the urban built area (UBA) and farmland within the 6th ring road. Specifically, farmland was replaced by UBA, resulting in an increase of 106.6% in the number of patches and a decrease of 51.6% in the mean patch area. The splitting index increased by 94.3%, and the landscape diversity index increased by 17.8%. These changes indicate that the landscape pattern within the 6th ring road became more fragmented and diversified over the five-year period.
The main drivers of these landscape changes were the increasing demand for land due to Beijing's growing population, unreasonable urban growth, and improvements in housing standards. These factors led to rapid urbanization, which had a negative impact on the urban environment. The changes in the landscape pattern within the 6th ring road area of Beijing are a reflection of the broader challenges facing the city in managing its rapid growth and development.

title: Drink Choice: Factors Influencing the Intention to Drink Wine
text: This study investigates why consumers prefer wine over other alcoholic beverages, with a focus on the beliefs and attitudes surrounding wine drinking. The research findings indicate that while both attitudes and social pressure play a role in wine consumption, attitudes are more predictive of intentions to drink wine. However, both attitudinal and normative factors are necessary to fully understand wine consumption. Although the study found that health concerns were a significant factor in the qualitative phase, the subsequent quantitative research revealed that drinking wine for its purported health benefits was not a significant attitudinal or behavioral driver. On the other hand, the enjoyment of wine's diverse flavors and pairing capabilities with food were found to be more important reasons for drinking wine. These findings suggest that promotional efforts emphasizing the health benefits of wine drinking may have limited effectiveness.

title: Application of growth technologies in enhancing food security and sustainability
text:
For over 50 years, anabolic steroids have been widely used in the beef cattle industry as safe and effective growth-promoting agents. Today, more than 90% of feedlot cattle in the US receive some type of steroidal implant during their lifetime, as approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). These implants have been shown to increase growth rate by 8-28%, improve feed efficiency by 5-20%, and enhance lean tissue mass of the carcass by 3-10%. This improvement in production efficiency has numerous benefits, including reducing production costs, land requirements, and greenhouse gas emissions, while also providing a year-round, affordable supply of beef at reduced prices.
In addition to steroidal implants, a newer class of orally active growth promotants, known as beta-adrenergic agonists (BAA), have been approved for use in finishing beef cattle in the last decade. These products provide similar production benefits as steroidal implants, but differ in application and mode of action. BAA are fed during the last 20-42 days of the cattle finishing period, depending on the specific product. The purpose of this paper is to explain how anabolic implants and BAA work and their benefits to beef cattle production.

title: Metabolic modifiers as performance-enhancing technologies for livestock production
text: With the projected surge in global population and consumption of food, there will be a corresponding rise in competition for land, water, and energy. This will have a profound impact on food production, as well as the urgent need to reduce the environmental footprint of food systems. Globalization has fueled trade in livestock inputs and products, leading to growth in the industry, but this has also resulted in a challenge for livestock producers, who must meet increasing demand with dwindling resources. The only solution is to significantly improve efficiency. As incomes rise in emerging economies, there will be a corresponding increase in demand for high-quality animal proteins such as meat, milk, and eggs, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. However, recent technological advancements in the animal industries have the potential to help these sectors prosper in the face of these challenges. To fully utilize these technologies, such as metabolic modifiers, immunization against gonadotropin-releasing factor, orally active dietary additives, and more, further emphasis is needed on their acceptance and development. These advancements have benefited producers through improved production efficiencies and meat packers through increased lean meat yield, making meat leaner and less expensive for consumers. However, there are concerns that the focus on increasing production efficiency and lean meat yield has come at the expense of meat quality. Despite the apparent need for these technologies, external factors such as market differentiation and trade barriers, as well as consumer resistance, pose challenges to their adoption. This article argues that to meet the increased global demand for animal protein, it is crucial to continue developing and adopting technologies to improve livestock efficiency, while being aware of these potential barriers to acceptance.

title: Assessment of hemodynamic efficacy and safety of 6% hydroxyethylstarch 130/0.4 vs. 0.9% NaCl fluid replacement in patients with severe sepsis: The CRYSTMAS study
text: Inadequate initial treatment and delayed hemodynamic stabilization (HDS) can significantly increase the risk of death in patients with severe sepsis. To compare the hemodynamic efficacy and safety of 6% hydroxyethyl starch (HES) 130/0.4 and normal saline (NaCl) 0.9% for HDS in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with severe sepsis, we conducted a prospective, multicenter, active-controlled, double-blind, randomized study. Of the 196 enrolled patients, 174 reached HDS (88 and 86 patients for HES and NaCl, respectively). We found that significantly less HES was required to reach HDS compared to NaCl (mean difference = -331 ± 1,033, 95% CI -640 to -21, P = 0.0185). The time to reach HDS was also shorter for HES (11.8 ± 10.1 hours) than for NaCl (14.3 ± 11.1 hours). However, the total quantity of study drug infused over four consecutive days, ICU and hospital length of stay (LOS), and area under the curve of Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score were comparable between the two groups. Acute renal failure occurred in 24 (24.5%) and 19 (20%) patients for HES and NaCl, respectively (P = 0.454). There was no significant difference in mortality, coagulation, or pruritus between the two groups up to 90 days after treatment initiation. Our findings suggest that HES may require significantly less volume to achieve HDS in the initial phase of fluid resuscitation in severe sepsis patients without compromising safety. The study was registered at NCT00464204.

title: Comparisons between different polychemotherapy regimens for early breast cancer: meta-analyses of long-term outcome among 100,000 women in 123 randomised trials.
text: The study aimed to investigate the differences in efficacy between various adjuvant chemotherapy regimens for breast cancer, as these differences could significantly impact treatment decisions. The researchers conducted individual-patient-data meta-analyses of randomized trials that compared different chemotherapy regimens, including any taxane-plus-anthracycline-based regimen versus the same or more non-taxane chemotherapy (n=44,000), one anthracycline-based regimen versus another or versus cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, and fluorouracil (CMF; n=18,000), and polychemotherapy versus no chemotherapy (n=32,000). The study found that adding four separate cycles of a taxane to a fixed anthracycline-based control regimen resulted in a significant reduction in breast cancer mortality (RR 0·86, SE 0·04, two-sided significance [2p]=0·0005). In contrast, trials with four extra cycles of a taxane counterbalanced in controls by extra cycles of other cytotoxic drugs did not show a significant difference in breast cancer mortality (RR 0·94, SE 0·06, 2p=0·33). The study also found that standard 4AC and standard CMF were equivalent in terms of breast cancer mortality (RR 0·98, SE 0·05, 2p=0·67), but that anthracycline-based regimens with higher cumulative dosage than standard 4AC (e.g., CAF or CEF) were superior to standard CMF (RR 0·78, SE 0·06, 2p=0·0004). Additionally, trials versus no chemotherapy suggested greater mortality reductions with CAF (RR 0·64, SE 0·09, 2p<0·0001) than with standard 4AC (RR 0·78, SE 0·09, 2p=0·01) or standard CMF (RR 0·76, SE 0·05, 2p<0·0001). The study found that the proportional risk reductions were little affected by age, nodal status, tumour diameter or differentiation (moderate or poor; few were well differentiated), oestrogen receptor status, or tamoxifen use. The study concluded that some taxane-plus-anthracycline-based or higher-cumulative-dosage anthracycline-based regimens (not requiring stem cells) reduced breast cancer mortality by, on average, about one-third, and that these regimens were effective across a range of patient subgroups, including older patients and those with poorer prognostic factors. The study also found that the absolute benefits of these regimens depended on the absolute risks without chemotherapy, and that low absolute risks implied low absolute benefits. The study was funded by Cancer Research UK, the British Heart Foundation, and the UK Medical Research Council.

title: Invariant NKT cells modulate the suppressive activity of IL-10-secreting neutrophils differentiated with serum amyloid A.
text: Neutrophils play a crucial role in inflammation, but they can also regulate excessive inflammation by producing anti-inflammatory cytokines. However, the mechanisms that govern their ability to switch between these roles are not fully understood. Our study reveals that systemic serum amyloid A 1 (SAA-1) regulates the plasticity of neutrophil differentiation. SAA-1 not only induces anti-inflammatory interleukin 10 (IL-10)-secreting neutrophils but also promotes the interaction between invariant natural killer T cells (iNKT cells) and these neutrophils, which limits the suppressive activity of the neutrophils by reducing IL-10 production and enhancing IL-12 production. Since SAA-1-producing melanomas can induce the differentiation of IL-10-secreting neutrophils, harnessing iNKT cells could be a potential therapeutic strategy by reducing the frequency of immunosuppressive neutrophils and restoring tumor-specific immune responses.

title: Body-mass index and cause-specific mortality in 900 000 adults: collaborative analyses of 57 prospective studies.
text: The study aimed to investigate the associations between body mass index (BMI) and overall and cause-specific mortality by analyzing data from numerous prospective studies. The study included 57 studies with over 894,000 participants, mostly from western Europe and North America. The analysis was adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, and study. The findings showed that mortality was lowest at a BMI of around 22.5-25 kg/m2, and above this range, there were positive associations with several specific causes of death, such as vascular mortality, diabetic, renal, and hepatic mortality. In contrast, there were inverse associations with none. The study found that each 5 kg/m2 higher BMI was associated with about 30% higher overall mortality, with the highest excess mortality observed for vascular mortality (40%), diabetic, renal, and hepatic mortality (60-120%), and neoplastic mortality (10%). In contrast, there was a 20% excess mortality for respiratory and all other causes of death. The study also found that below the range of 22.5-25 kg/m2, BMI was associated inversely with overall mortality, mainly due to strong inverse associations with respiratory disease and lung cancer. The study suggests that BMI is a strong predictor of overall mortality both above and below the apparent optimum of about 22.5-25 kg/m2, and that the progressive excess mortality above this range is due mainly to vascular disease. The study also found that the definite excess mortality below 22.5 kg/m2 is due mainly to smoking-related diseases, and is not fully explained.

title: Targeting metabolic remodeling in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: A significant difference between cancer cells and normal, differentiated cells is altered metabolism, which allows cancer cells to retain proliferation, survive in unfavorable environments, and invade surrounding tissues. One notable biochemical adaptation is the metabolic shift towards aerobic glycolysis, regardless of oxygen availability, a phenomenon known as the "Warburg Effect". This results in high glucose uptake, low oxygen consumption, and increased production of lactate, which provides a survival advantage and generates necessary substrates, such as fatty acids, amino acids, and nucleotides, in rapidly proliferating cells. This review focuses on the role of key metabolic enzymes in modulating the "Warburg Effect" in Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), an aggressive, highly glycolytic, and deadly brain tumor. Targeting these enzymes may offer a novel therapeutic approach, either alone or in combination with existing treatments, in GBMs.

title: Signaling architectures that transmit unidirectional information despite retroactivity
text:
A signaling pathway conveys information from an upstream system to downstream systems in a unidirectional manner, ideally. However, retroactivity, or the additional reaction flux that affects a system due to interactions with downstream systems, poses a significant challenge to unidirectional transmission. This raises the question of whether signaling pathways have evolved specialized architectures to overcome retroactivity and transmit unidirectional signals.
To address this question, we propose a general mathematical analysis procedure. Using this procedure, we investigate the ability of various signaling architectures to transmit one-way signals as key biological parameters are adjusted. Our findings reveal a design trade-off in single-stage phosphorylation and phosphotransfer systems that hinders their ability to overcome retroactivity. Interestingly, cascades of these architectures, which are prevalent in nature, can overcome this trade-off and enable unidirectional transmission. In contrast, phosphotransfer systems, as well as single and double phosphorylation cycles that transmit signals from a substrate, are unable to mitigate retroactivity effects, even when cascaded, and are therefore not well-suited for unidirectional information transmission.
Our results identify signaling architectures that can successfully transmit unidirectional signals, thereby conserving their input/output behavior across multiple contexts. These findings can be used to decompose natural signal transduction networks into modular components and establish a library of devices that can be employed in synthetic biology to facilitate modular circuit design.

title: Association between pre-diabetes, type 2 diabetes and trabecular bone score: The Vietnam Osteoporosis Study.
text: The present study aimed to investigate the association between type 2 diabetes (T2D) and trabecular bone score (TBS) in adult Vietnamese men and women. As part of the Vietnam Osteoporosis Study, 2702 women and 1398 men aged ≥30 years were recruited from the general community in Ho Chi Minh City. HbA1c levels were measured using the ADAMS™ A1c HA-8160 (Arkray, Kyoto, Japan) and classified into three groups: normal (HbA1c <5.7%), pre-diabetes (5.7 to 6.4%), and diabetes (>6.4%). TBS was evaluated using iNsight Software, version 2.1 (Medimaps, Merignac, France) on lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD) scans (Hologic Horizon). The study found that the prevalence of pre-diabetes and diabetes in men and women was 30.2% and 8.3%, respectively. In women, TBS was significantly lower in pre-diabetes (-0.02, P < 0.001) and diabetes (-0.02, P < 0.001) compared to normal individuals. In contrast, there was no statistically significant difference in TBS between diabetic status in men. Furthermore, TBS was inversely correlated with HbA1c levels in women (P = 0.01), but not in men (P = 0.89). These findings suggest that diabetes and pre-diabetes are associated with deterioration of bone microarchitecture, with a greater impact on women than men.

title: Adhesion molecules and chemokines: relation to anthropometric, body composition, biochemical and dietary variables
text:
Introduction: Obesity is a complex metabolic disorder characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation, which is mediated by various cell adhesion molecules and chemokines. Among these, Pselectin, E-selectin, VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and MCP-1 have been implicated in the pathogenesis of obesity. These molecules play a crucial role in cell adhesion, endothelial integrity, and can be modulated by body composition and dietary patterns.
Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the correlation between anthropometric, body composition, dietary, and biochemical markers and the levels of cell adhesion molecules and chemokines in obesity.
Methods: A systematic search of scientific databases was conducted using specific keywords and no time restrictions. The selected papers were analyzed for their association with obesity-related markers.
Results: The analysis revealed that all cell adhesion molecules and chemokines were positively correlated with anthropometric markers, but controversial results were found for ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. Visceral fat was found to be more strongly associated with E-selectin and MCP-1 levels. Weight loss was observed to reduce the levels of these molecules, except for VCAM-1. A Western dietary pattern, excessive consumption of saturated and trans fats, and low intake of w-3 fatty acids were associated with increased levels of cell adhesion molecules and chemokines. Conversely, a healthy dietary pattern, high calcium intake, and high dairy consumption were found to decrease these molecules. Biochemical parameters showed an inverse relationship with HDLC and a positive relationship with total cholesterol, triglycerides, blood glucose, fasting insulin, and insulin resistance.
Conclusion: The present study demonstrates that normal anthropometric indicators, body composition, biochemical parameters, and eating pattern positively modulate the subclinical inflammation associated with obesity by reducing the levels of cell adhesion molecules and chemokines. These findings highlight the importance of a healthy lifestyle and diet in reducing inflammation and improving metabolic health in obesity.
